functions.name: __iterator(_Parent&, _OuterIter)
functions.prose_contract: Constructor of join_with_view<_View,_Pattern>::__iterator<_Const>, only available when the base is a forward_range. Precondition: __parent refers to a live join_with_view that outlives the iterator, and __outer is an iterator into its base range (or its end). Postcondition: stores a non-owning pointer to __parent and moves __outer into __outer_it_. If __outer is not ranges::end(base), __inner_it_ is set to alternative 1 holding ranges::begin of the inner range of *__outer and then __satisfy() runs; __satisfy() may leave the iterator on a pattern element (alternative 0), on an inner-range element (alternative 1), or advance __outer to the end of the base, in which case __inner_it_ is reset to alternative 0 only when the inner range type is a reference (__ref_is_glvalue) and otherwise stays at alternative 1. If __outer is the end of the base, __inner_it_ is left default-initialised (alternative 0) and __satisfy() is not called. Exceptions from the underlying iterator or range operations propagate; nothing is returned.

functions.name: __iterator(_Parent&)

Precondition: __parent refers to a live join_with_view whose cached outer iterator __parent->__outer_it_ is engaged (begin() emplaces it before calling this constructor); the iterator is dereferenced by __get_outer() with no check. Postcondition: stores a non-owning pointer to __parent (the outer iterator lives in the parent, not in this object). If *__parent->__outer_it_ is not ranges::end(base), __inner_it_ is set to alternative 1 holding ranges::begin of the inner range of *outer and __satisfy() runs; as in the forward constructor __satisfy() may leave the iterator on a pattern element (alternative 0), on an inner element (alternative 1), or move the shared outer iterator to the end of the base (resetting __inner_it_ to alternative 0 only when the inner range type is a reference). If the outer iterator is already at the end, __inner_it_ stays default-initialised and __satisfy() is not called. Because the outer iterator is shared state in the parent, advancing it here changes the parent.

functions.name: operator+(__iterator __i, difference_type __n)

Postcondition: returns a new __iterator built from *__i.__parent_ (the new iterator again points at the same parent view object; the parent is not copied) and the underlying position __i.__current_ + __n. The by-value parameter __i is a copy, so the caller's iterator is not modified; overflow or out-of-range results are the underlying iterator's concern and are not checked here.

functions.name: vector<_Tp,_Allocator>::__move_assign(vector& __c, true_type)
functions.prose_contract: Move-assignment helper used when the allocator propagates on move assignment; declared noexcept(is_nothrow_move_assignable<allocator_type>). Precondition: *this and __c are distinct valid vectors. Steps: __vdeallocate() destroys the elements and frees the buffer of *this (when it has one) and sets begin, end and capacity pointers to null; then __move_assign_alloc(__c) assigns the allocator (a throw here propagates, leaving *this empty with no buffer and __c untouched); then *this takes __c's begin, end and capacity pointers and __c's three pointers are set to nullptr. After a normal return *this owns the buffer previously owned by __c and __c is empty with no buffer.

functions.name: vector<_Tp,_Allocator>::assign(size_type __n, const_reference __u)
functions.prose_contract: Replaces the contents with __n copies of __u. If __n <= capacity(): the first min(__n, size()) existing elements are assigned from __u with fill_n; then if __n > size() the remaining __n - size() copies are constructed at the end, otherwise the elements from begin()+__n to the old end are destroyed; no allocation occurs and __u may refer to an element of the vector in this branch. If __n > capacity(): the old buffer is destroyed and freed first (__vdeallocate), then __vallocate(__recommend(__n)) allocates a new one (length_error from __recommend or bad_alloc may propagate, leaving *this empty with no buffer) and __n copies of __u are constructed; here __u must not refer to an element of the old buffer, since it is gone. A throw from a copy assignment or construction propagates and leaves the vector in a partially modified but not necessarily unchanged state; this function does not give a strong guarantee. On normal return size() == __n.

functions.name: vector<_Tp,_Allocator>::erase(const_iterator __position)
functions.prose_contract: Erases the element at __position. Precondition: __position is a dereferenceable iterator of this vector (not end()); this is only checked by an assertion macro when assertions are enabled. Steps: computes the position p, move-assigns the elements after p one place left with std::move, then destroys the tail (the last element) with __destruct_at_end. Returns an iterator at the same index, which refers to the element that followed the erased one, or end() if the erased one was last. No allocation occurs. If a move assignment throws, the exception propagates before __destruct_at_end runs, so size() is unchanged and the elements from p onward are in a partly moved state.

functions.name: vector<_Tp,_Allocator>::erase(const_iterator __first, const_iterator __last)
functions.prose_contract: Erases the range [__first, __last). Precondition: it is a valid range of this vector with __first <= __last (checked only by an assertion macro). If __first != __last, elements from __last to the end are move-assigned down to __first with std::move and the now-surplus elements at the end are destroyed, so size() decreases by __last - __first; if the range is empty nothing is modified. Returns an iterator at the index of __first, which is the element after the erased range or end() if the range reached the end. No allocation occurs. A throw from a move assignment propagates before the destruction step, leaving size() unchanged and the elements from __first onward partly moved.

functions.name: vector<_Tp,_Allocator>::insert(const_iterator __position, const_reference __x)
functions.prose_contract: Inserts a copy of __x before __position and returns an iterator to the inserted element. Precondition: __position is in [begin(), end()]. Three paths: (a) size() < capacity() and __position == end(): constructs the copy at the end (__emplace_back_assume_capacity); (b) size() < capacity() and __position != end(): __move_range shifts [p, end) up by one, then assigns *p = *xr where xr points at __x, advanced by one element if __x lies inside [p, end) so an aliasing __x is read from its shifted location; (c) size() == capacity(): builds a __split_buffer of capacity __recommend(size()+1) (length_error if the new size exceeds max_size(), bad_alloc from allocation), emplaces the copy of __x into it, and __swap_out_circular_buffer relocates the old elements around it and swaps buffers; the returned pointer is the position of the new element. A throw from an allocation, a copy or a move propagates; in path (b) the vector may be left with some elements shifted or assigned, so there is no strong exception guarantee for that path. Iterators and references are invalidated in path (c) and for elements at or after __position in the other paths.

functions.name: vector<_Tp,_Allocator>::insert(const_iterator __position, value_type&& __x)
functions.prose_contract: Inserts __x by move before __position and returns an iterator to the inserted element. Precondition: __position is in [begin(), end()]. Paths: (a) size() < capacity() and __position == end(): move-constructs the element at the end; (b) size() < capacity() and __position != end(): __move_range shifts [p, end) up one place and then *p = std::move(__x); __x is not adjusted for aliasing, so __x must not refer to an element in [p, end) (it would be read after the shift); (c) size() == capacity(): a __split_buffer of capacity __recommend(size()+1) is allocated (length_error if size()+1 exceeds max_size(), or bad_alloc), __x is moved into it, and __swap_out_circular_buffer relocates the old elements around it; returns the new element's position. Throws from allocation, element move or relocation propagate; in path (b) the vector may be left partly shifted/assigned, so there is no strong exception guarantee there. __x is moved-from on success.

functions.name: vector<_Tp,_Allocator>::emplace(const_iterator __position, _Args&&... __args)
functions.prose_contract: Constructs a new element from __args before __position and returns an iterator to it. Precondition: __position is in [begin(), end()]. Paths: (a) size() < capacity() and __position == end(): constructs in place at the end via __emplace_back_assume_capacity; (b) size() < capacity() and __position != end(): first constructs a temporary value from __args (__temp_value, so __args may refer into the vector), then __move_range shifts [p, end) up one place and *p = std::move(temporary); (c) size() == capacity(): allocates a __split_buffer of capacity __recommend(size()+1) (length_error if the size would exceed max_size(), or bad_alloc), constructs the element in it from __args, and __swap_out_circular_buffer relocates the old elements around it. Exceptions from allocation, construction, move or relocation propagate; in path (b) the vector may be left partly shifted or assigned (no strong guarantee). In path (c) __args are used after the buffer is allocated but before old elements are relocated, so they may refer to old elements.

functions.name: vector<_Tp,_Allocator>::insert(const_iterator __position, size_type __n, const_reference __x)
functions.prose_contract: Inserts __n copies of __x before __position and returns an iterator to the first inserted element, or to __position's index unchanged when __n == 0 (nothing is done and size() is unchanged). Precondition: __position is in [begin(), end()]. If __n <= capacity() - size(): when __n exceeds the number of elements after the insertion point, the surplus __n - (end - p) copies are constructed at the end first (__construct_at_end); then, if any copies remain, __move_range shifts the elements at the insertion point up by the original count and the remaining copies are written by fill_n from a pointer to __x that is advanced by the original __n when __x lies inside [p, end) so aliasing is handled. Otherwise a __split_buffer of capacity __recommend(size()+__n) is allocated (length_error / bad_alloc may be thrown), __n copies are constructed in it, and __swap_out_circular_buffer relocates the old elements around them. Exceptions propagate; in the in-place branch the vector can be partially modified (copies already constructed at the end, elements shifted), so there is no strong guarantee. size() grows by __n on normal return.

functions.name: __get_sys_info_rule
functions.prose_contract: Static helper in libc++ time_zone.cpp: computes the sys_info for a continuation whose rules come from a named rule set. Precondition: __rules is non-empty (an assertion at the top checks that a first rule exists; without assertions an empty set is undefined behaviour). It first clamps __time to be at least __continuation_begin, then walks the rules in order starting with the first rule and returns, as the value alternative of __sys_info_result (an expected), a __sys_info holding a sys_info plus a bool can_merge. All returns shown yield the value alternative; the unexpected (time-to-retry) alternative is never produced by this function. Returns: (1) __time before the first rule begin: if the continuation starts at the minimum time or more than 12h earlier, a sys_info starting at __continuation_begin with offset stdoff, save 0 and the abbreviation using the letters before the first rule, ending at rule_begin if the first rule's save is nonzero, otherwise at the next rule time (can_merge false); otherwise a sys_info starting at __continuation_begin, ending at min(continuation UNTIL for that save, next rule time), offset stdoff+save, can_merge true exactly when the end equals the continuation UNTIL. (2) first rule save is 0 and __time is before the next rule: sys_info [continuation_begin, next rule time) with save 0, can_merge false (this end is not capped at the continuation UNTIL). (3) first rule save nonzero, continuation_begin >= rule_begin - save and __time before the next rule: [continuation_begin, next rule time) with offset stdoff+save, can_merge false (also not capped at UNTIL). (4) in the walk, the interval of the rule containing __time (or when the next rule time reaches the continuation end): [max(continuation_begin, rule_begin), min(UNTIL, next rule time)) with can_merge true exactly when the end equals the UNTIL; (5) when the rules run out: [max(continuation_begin, rule_begin), UNTIL) can_merge true. The returned interval need not contain __time; the caller handles that.

functions.name: __remove_all
functions.prose_contract: Windows/MVS variant of __remove_all (compiled when REMOVE_ALL_USE_DIRECTORY_ITERATOR is defined): ErrorHandler clears *ec when ec is non-null, then remove_all_impl(p, mec) runs with a local error code. remove_all_impl takes __symlink_status(p) (a failure sets mec and returns (uintmax_t)-1); for a directory it iterates it with directory_iterator, calls itself on each entry and adds the result to count; any error code set in a child, in the iterator constructor or in increment stops with -1; finally it calls __remove(p) which returns false for any failure and, for ENOENT, leaves the error code clear. Results of __remove_all: if mec is set and equals no_such_file_or_directory it returns 0 and no error is reported, which covers a missing p but also an ENOENT produced by a nested entry or by opening the directory after it vanished; any other mec is reported through ErrorHandler, giving (uintmax_t)-1 with *ec set, or a thrown filesystem_error when ec is null; if mec is clear it returns count, which is (uintmax_t)-1 with *ec clear when the removal of p itself failed with ENOENT. A nested entry whose own removal failed with ENOENT also returns -1 with mec clear, and the parent then adds that value to count (wraps by one). Entries may already have been deleted whenever an error or -1 is returned. A symlink to a directory is removed as a link (symlink status).

functions.name: __remove_all
functions.prose_contract: openat/unlinkat variant of __remove_all (the non-Windows variant): ErrorHandler clears *ec if non-null; remove_all_impl(AT_FDCWD, p, mec) runs; if mec is set it returns err.report(mec), which is (uintmax_t)-1 with *ec set to mec, or a thrown filesystem_error when ec is null; otherwise it returns count. remove_all_impl: if openat(parent, p, O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW) succeeds it wraps the fd in a DIR stream (fdopendir failure sets ec and returns 0, closing the fd), reads entries skipping '.' and '..', recursing on each, summing counts, and stops at the end of the directory or when readdir sets ec; then unlinkat(AT_REMOVEDIR) on the directory: failure sets ec and returns count, success returns count + 1. If the open fails with ENOENT the error is cleared and it returns 0 (a missing path, at any depth, is not an error); if it fails with ENOTDIR, ELOOP or EMLINK the entry is removed with unlinkat (success returns 1, failure sets ec and returns 0); any other open failure leaves ec set and returns 0. Note that posix_readdir clears ec at each call, so an error set while removing a child is erased by the next readdir call in the parent loop and is not propagated directly; it usually surfaces as the parent's AT_REMOVEDIR failing (typically ENOTEMPTY), which is then reported at the top level only if it is the top-level path. Entries may have been removed when -1 is returned.

functions.name: locale::__imp::__imp(const __imp& other)
functions.prose_contract: Copy constructor of locale::__imp. Allocates a facets_ table of size max(N, other.facets_.size()), copies other's facet pointers into it (vector assignment), copies other.name_, and then calls __add_shared() once on each non-null facet pointer in the new table so that the new object shares ownership with other. It does not install, replace or release any facet and has no return value. If allocation or the copy throws, the exception propagates before any reference has been added.

functions.name: locale::__imp::__imp(const __imp& other, const string& name, locale::category c)
functions.prose_contract: Constructs a locale implementation from other with the facets of the categories in c replaced by new by-name facets for `name`. The facets_ table starts with N entries, name_ is build_name(other.name_, name, c) (a throw here propagates before any reference is taken), the table is assigned from other's and each non-null facet gets __add_shared(). Then, inside a try block, for each category bit set in c (collate, ctype, monetary, numeric, time, messages) it creates the corresponding *_byname facets for `name` with new and calls install on each (the codecvt_byname set belongs to ctype; wide-character and char8_t facets only when those features are compiled in). install takes its own reference on the new facet, grows the table if needed, releases the reference currently held for any facet already at that id (for other's facets this is the reference just added by this constructor) and stores the new facet; so facets of the selected categories are no longer shared with other, while all other facets are. If any construction or install throws, the catch block calls __release_shared() on every non-null facet in the table (including already-installed new ones) and rethrows.

functions.name: locale::__imp::__imp(const __imp& other, const __imp& one, locale::category c)
functions.prose_contract: Constructs a locale implementation from other with the facets of the categories in c taken from `one`. The facets_ table starts with N entries, name_ is build_name(other.name_, one.name_, c), the table is assigned from other's and every non-null facet gets __add_shared(). Then, inside a try block, for each category bit in c it calls install_from<F>(one) for the facets of that category (a larger set than the by-name constructor, e.g. money_get/money_put, num_get/num_put as well). install_from fetches one.use_facet(id), which throws bad_cast if `one` has no facet at that id, and install()s it: install takes a reference, grows the table if needed, releases the reference held at that id and stores the facet. When the facet from `one` is the same object that other already had at that id, the net count is unchanged and the facet stays shared; otherwise other's facet loses the reference added by this constructor and the new one gains a reference. If anything throws (including bad_cast) the catch block calls __release_shared() on every non-null facet in the table and rethrows.

functions.name: locale::__imp::__imp(const __imp& other, facet* f, long id)
functions.prose_contract: Constructs a locale implementation from other plus facet f at index id; name_ is "*". Precondition: f is non-null (it is dereferenced) and is the facet whose id is `id`. Steps: the facets_ table starts with max(N, other.size()+1) entries; f->__add_shared() is called and the reference is held by a unique_ptr with the releaser deleter; the table is assigned from other's and each non-null facet gets __add_shared(); then install(f, id) adds another reference to f, grows the table if needed, releases the reference held at index id if there was a facet there, and stores f; when the constructor ends the temporary holder releases its reference to f. Net: every facet of other at an index other than id gains one reference, f gains one reference held by the table, and a facet of other at index id is not retained by the new table (if that facet is f itself the table still holds f at id). This constructor has no try/catch: if install throws (the table resize), the references added to the copied facets are not released.

functions.name: operator new(size_t size, const std::nothrow_t&) noexcept
functions.prose_contract: Weak nothrow allocation function. Declared noexcept. With exceptions enabled it calls the (replaceable) throwing ::operator new(size) inside try { } catch (...) { } and returns its result, or nullptr if any exception was thrown. With exceptions disabled it returns operator_new_impl(size), which treats size 0 as 1, calls malloc in a loop and on failure calls the installed new_handler (if any) and retries, ending with nullptr when malloc fails and no handler is installed; in that build, if overridden-function detection (_LIBCPP_CAN_DETECT_OVERRIDDEN_FUNCTION) is enabled, an assertion fails when operator new(size_t) has been overridden. The caller owns a non-null result and releases it with operator delete.

functions.name: operator new[](size_t size, const std::nothrow_t&) noexcept
functions.prose_contract: Weak nothrow array allocation function, declared noexcept. With exceptions enabled it calls ::operator new[](size) inside try/catch(...) and returns its result or nullptr if anything was thrown; with exceptions disabled it returns operator_new_impl(size) (size 0 treated as 1; malloc loop calling the new_handler on failure; nullptr when malloc fails and no handler exists), and an assertion fires there when overridden-function detection is on and operator new[](size_t) was overridden (the assertion text checks operator new[]). The caller owns a non-null result and releases it with operator delete[].

functions.name: operator delete(void* ptr, size_t) noexcept
functions.prose_contract: Weak sized deallocation function (the second parameter is unnamed and ignored). Declared noexcept; calls ::operator delete(ptr), which calls std::free(ptr); a null pointer is accepted by free and does nothing. ptr must be null or a pointer obtained from the non-aligned operator new family. The caller gives up ownership; nothing is returned.

functions.name: _LIBCPP_OVERRIDABLE_FUNCTION(void*, operator new, (std::size_t size, std::align_val_t alignment)) _THROW_BAD_ALLOC
functions.prose_contract: Replaceable throwing aligned allocation function. Calls operator_new_aligned_impl(size, alignment): size 0 is treated as 1, an alignment smaller than sizeof(void*) is raised to sizeof(void*), and __libcpp_aligned_alloc(alignment, size) is called in a loop; when it returns null and a new_handler is installed the handler is called and the allocation retried (an exception from the handler propagates), and when null with no handler the loop ends with null. If the result is null it throws std::bad_alloc through __throw_bad_alloc_shim; otherwise it returns the non-null aligned block. alignment must be a value __libcpp_aligned_alloc accepts (not checked here). The caller owns the block and releases it with an aligned operator delete. Only compiled when _LIBCPP_HAS_LIBRARY_ALIGNED_ALLOCATION.

functions.name: operator new(size_t size, std::align_val_t alignment, const std::nothrow_t&) noexcept
functions.prose_contract: Weak nothrow aligned allocation function, declared noexcept. With exceptions enabled it calls ::operator new(size, alignment) in try/catch(...) and returns its result or nullptr on any exception. With exceptions disabled it returns operator_new_aligned_impl(size, alignment) (size 0 as 1, alignment raised to at least sizeof(void*), allocation retried via the new_handler until it succeeds or no handler remains, nullptr then); in that build an assertion fires if overridden-function detection is on and the throwing aligned operator new has been overridden. The caller owns a non-null result and releases it with an aligned operator delete.

functions.name: _LIBCPP_OVERRIDABLE_FUNCTION(void*, operator new[], (size_t size, std::align_val_t alignment)) _THROW_BAD_ALLOC
functions.prose_contract: Replaceable throwing aligned array allocation function: it returns ::operator new(size, alignment), so its result and its exceptions are those of the aligned scalar operator new (possibly user-replaced): a non-null block of at least size bytes (0 treated as 1) aligned to at least alignment (raised to sizeof(void*)), or std::bad_alloc when the allocation fails with no new_handler, or whatever the new_handler throws. The caller owns the block and releases it with an aligned operator delete[]. No assertion is made here.

functions.name: operator new[](size_t size, std::align_val_t alignment, const std::nothrow_t&) noexcept
functions.prose_contract: Weak nothrow aligned array allocation function, declared noexcept. With exceptions enabled it calls ::operator new[](size, alignment) in try/catch(...) and returns its result or nullptr on any exception. With exceptions disabled it returns operator_new_aligned_impl(size, alignment), and an assertion fires if overridden-function detection is on and the throwing aligned operator new[] has been overridden. The caller owns a non-null result and releases it with an aligned operator delete[].

functions.name: operator delete(void* ptr, std::align_val_t) noexcept
functions.prose_contract: Weak aligned deallocation function: calls std::__libcpp_aligned_free(ptr), which frees ptr; ptr must be null or a block from an aligned operator new (nothing in this function checks for null; whether null is accepted depends on __libcpp_aligned_free). The alignment parameter is unnamed and unused. Declared noexcept; no return value; ownership passes to the allocator.

functions.name: operator delete(void* ptr, std::align_val_t alignment, const std::nothrow_t&) noexcept
functions.prose_contract: Weak aligned nothrow deallocation function: calls ::operator delete(ptr, alignment), the aligned deallocation function; ptr must be null or a block from an aligned operator new. Declared noexcept; no return value; ownership passes to the allocator.

functions.name: operator delete(void* ptr, size_t, std::align_val_t alignment) noexcept
functions.prose_contract: Weak sized aligned deallocation function: the size_t parameter is unnamed and ignored; calls ::operator delete(ptr, alignment). ptr must be null or a block from an aligned operator new. Declared noexcept; no return value; ownership passes to the allocator.

functions.name: Registers_ppc::setRegister
functions.prose_contract: Sets one saved register in a Registers_ppc object from regNum and value (uint32_t). UNW_REG_IP stores value in __srr0 and UNW_REG_SP in __r1; UNW_PPC_R0 to R31 store value in the corresponding __rN field; UNW_PPC_MQ, LR, CTR, VRSAVE and XER store value in __mq, __lr, __ctr, __vrsave and __xer. For UNW_PPC_CR0 to CR7 the matching 4-bit nibble of __cr is cleared and replaced with the same nibble of value (for CR0 the bits value & 0xF0000000, for CR7 value & 0x0000000F), the other 28 bits of __cr stay. For UNW_PPC_AP, UNW_PPC_VSCR and UNW_PPC_SPEFSCR the call returns without storing anything. For any other regNum it reaches _LIBUNWIND_ABORT("unsupported ppc register") after the switch. Returns nothing.

functions.name: _Unwind_VRS_Pop
functions.prose_contract: Pops registers from the stack addressed by the context's SP and loads them into the context, according to regclass. Common failure results: it returns _UVRSR_FAILED if the representation is not the one required for the class, or if _Unwind_VRS_Get of SP or any _Unwind_VRS_Set that it checks fails. CORE class (and WMMXC when __ARM_WMMX is defined): representation must be _UVRSD_UINT32; for each bit i in 0..15 set in discriminator it reads a word from the stack and sets register i (a Set failure returns FAILED, with earlier registers already set and SP not updated); if bit 13 (SP) was not among the popped registers it then returns the result of setting SP to the advanced pointer, otherwise it returns _UVRSR_OK and SP keeps the popped value. VFP class (and WMMXD with __ARM_WMMX): representation must be _UVRSD_VFPX or _UVRSD_DOUBLE; first = discriminator >> 16 and count = discriminator & 0xffff registers starting at first are loaded from pairs of 32-bit words (combined per endianness), a failed Set returns FAILED, VFPX skips one extra padding word, and the result of setting SP is returned. PSEUDO class: representation must be _UVRSD_UINT32 and discriminator must be 0 (otherwise FAILED); it reads one word (the return-address authentication code) from the stack, advances SP via _Unwind_VRS_Set ignoring that call's result, and returns the result of setting the PSEUDO register 0 to the word. Any other class (and WMMX classes when __ARM_WMMX is not defined) reaches _LIBUNWIND_ABORT("unsupported register class"). The stack memory is read without any bounds check.

functions.name: unwind_phase1
functions.prose_contract: ARM EHABI phase 1 (search): initialises the cursor from uc itself (__unw_init_local), so the caller need not initialise it, then loops over frames. For each iteration it calls __unw_get_proc_info (failure returns _URC_FATAL_PHASE1_ERROR); if the frame has a personality routine it fills exception_object->pr_cache (fnstart, ehtp, additional) and calls it with _US_VIRTUAL_UNWIND_FRAME. _URC_HANDLER_FOUND returns _URC_NO_REASON (the personality is expected to have filled the barrier cache); _URC_CONTINUE_UNWIND continues the loop; _URC_FAILURE returns _URC_FAILURE; any other personality result, including _URC_END_OF_STACK, returns _URC_FATAL_PHASE1_ERROR. This function does not call __unw_step; advancing to the next frame is left to the personality routine, and a frame whose handler is 0 simply repeats the loop on the same cursor state. The final return _URC_NO_REASON after the loop is reached only if handlerNotFound became false, which does not happen without the earlier return. It does not itself return _URC_END_OF_STACK.

functions.name: unwind_phase2_forced
functions.prose_contract: ARM EHABI forced-unwind phase 2. Initialises the cursor from uc (__unw_init_local), then loops until endOfStack is set. Each iteration: __unw_get_proc_info failure returns _URC_FATAL_PHASE2_ERROR; the stop function is called with _UA_FORCE_UNWIND|_UA_CLEANUP_PHASE and any result other than _URC_NO_REASON returns _URC_FATAL_PHASE2_ERROR; if the frame has a handler the personality is called with _US_FORCE_UNWIND|_US_UNWIND_FRAME_STARTING: _URC_CONTINUE_UNWIND continues the loop, _URC_INSTALL_CONTEXT calls __unw_resume(cursor) (which transfers control; if it returns the loop simply continues), _URC_END_OF_STACK sets endOfStack, and any other value returns _URC_FATAL_PHASE2_ERROR. A frame without a handler repeats the loop with no step in this function. After the loop the stop function is called once more with _UA_FORCE_UNWIND|_UA_CLEANUP_PHASE|_UA_END_OF_STACK, its result is ignored, and the function returns _URC_FATAL_PHASE2_ERROR. So every return of this function is _URC_FATAL_PHASE2_ERROR; successful forced unwinding leaves through __unw_resume or the stop function's own transfer of control.

functions.name: _Unwind_RaiseException
functions.prose_contract: Entry point called by __cxa_throw. It captures a context (__unw_getcontext), sets exception_object->unwinder_cache.reserved1 to 0 (marking a non-forced unwind), runs unwind_phase1 and returns its code if it is not _URC_NO_REASON (which can be _URC_FAILURE or _URC_FATAL_PHASE1_ERROR), otherwise returns the result of unwind_phase2(..., resume=false). When a handler is found, phase 2 normally transfers control to the landing pad through __unw_resume and does not return here; phase 2 returns _URC_FATAL_PHASE2_ERROR on its failure paths and calls abort() when a personality returns _URC_FAILURE. So this function returns only with _URC_FAILURE, _URC_FATAL_PHASE1_ERROR or _URC_FATAL_PHASE2_ERROR; it does not return _URC_END_OF_STACK. Precondition: exception_object points to a valid _Unwind_Exception; the reserved1 field is written by this function, not required beforehand.

functions.name: _GCC_specific_handler
functions.prose_contract: Windows SEH language-specific handler used by libunwind/mingw. Returns an EXCEPTION_DISPOSITION. (1) If ms_exc->ExceptionCode is STATUS_GCC_UNWIND: when the unwind flag marks a target unwind, it stores ms_exc->ExceptionInformation[3] into the second return register slot of disp->ContextRecord (Rdx on x86_64, R1 on arm, X1 on aarch64, nothing on other targets); in every case of this branch it returns ExceptionContinueSearch. (2) Else if the code is STATUS_GCC_THROW it takes the _Unwind_Exception from ExceptionInformation[0] and, when not unwinding and NumberParameters > 1, takes ctx and action from ExceptionInformation[1] and [2]; any other exception code returns ExceptionContinueSearch. (3) If ctx is still null it initialises a local cursor from disp->ContextRecord, attaches disp, sets the IP register to disp->ControlPc and derives action: not unwinding gives _UA_CLEANUP_PHASE|_UA_FORCE_UNWIND for a GCC throw with parameters and _UA_SEARCH_PHASE otherwise; unwinding gives _UA_CLEANUP_PHASE|_UA_HANDLER_FRAME when the throw's ExceptionInformation[1] equals frame, else _UA_CLEANUP_PHASE. (4) It calls the personality routine pers(1, action, exception_class, exc, ctx) and switches on the result: _URC_CONTINUE_UNWIND aborts if action has _UA_HANDLER_FRAME, else returns ExceptionContinueSearch; _URC_HANDLER_FOUND returns 4 (ExceptionExecuteHandler) for a GCC throw with parameters, aborts if the exception flags say unwinding, otherwise records frame in exc->private_[1] (and for a GCC throw sets NumberParameters = 4 and ExceptionInformation[1] = frame) and calls RtlUnwindEx, which does not return normally (the code aborts if it does); _URC_INSTALL_CONTEXT returns 4 for a GCC throw in the non-unwinding case with parameters, aborts during phase 1, otherwise stores the landing pad and return registers into exc->private_[2..3], turns ms_exc into a STATUS_GCC_UNWIND record and calls RtlUnwindEx (abort if it returns); any other result returns ExceptionContinueExecution. Only the STATUS_GCC_UNWIND branch writes through disp->ContextRecord directly.

functions.name: UnwindCursor<A, R>::stepWithSEHData
functions.prose_contract: Windows SEH step: calls RtlVirtualUnwind(UNW_FLAG_UHANDLER, ImageBase, ControlPc, FunctionEntry, ContextRecord, &HandlerData, &EstablisherFrame, NULL) on the cursor's _dispContext, storing the returned language handler in _dispContext.LanguageHandler (it may be null) and letting the call update ContextRecord, HandlerData and EstablisherFrame. Then it sets _info.lsda to the HandlerData pointer value (reinterpret_cast of the pointer, not the address of the field) and _info.handler to the address of __libunwind_seh_personality when LanguageHandler is non-null, or 0 otherwise. Its only return is UNW_STEP_SUCCESS; no error from RtlVirtualUnwind is checked. Precondition: _dispContext.ImageBase, ControlPc, FunctionEntry and ContextRecord have been set up by an earlier lookup.

functions.name: UnwindCursor<A, R>::stepWithEHABI
functions.prose_contract: ARM EHABI step, compiled only for _LIBUNWIND_ARM_EHABI. _info.unwind_info is the encoded exception-handling-table word, not decoded data: it calls decode_eht_entry(unwind_info, &off, &len), which for the generic model (top bit clear) takes the unwind opcodes after the personality word with a length from the size byte, for the ARM compact model (top bit set) derives off/len from the format (SU16, LU16, LU32) and for any other format returns nullptr. It then calls _Unwind_VRS_Interpret(this as _Unwind_Context*, ehtp, off, len); if that returns anything other than _URC_CONTINUE_UNWIND the function returns UNW_STEP_END, otherwise UNW_STEP_SUCCESS. A null ehtp from decode_eht_entry is passed on to _Unwind_VRS_Interpret without a check here. Registers in the cursor are updated by the interpreter.

functions.name: unwind_phase2_forced
functions.prose_contract: Forced-unwind phase 2 (libunwind UnwindLevel1.c). Initialises the cursor from uc itself (__unw_init_local), so the caller need not. It then loops while __unw_step_stage2(cursor) > 0: __unw_get_proc_info failure returns _URC_FATAL_PHASE2_ERROR; the stop function is called with action _UA_FORCE_UNWIND|_UA_CLEANUP_PHASE and any result other than _URC_NO_REASON returns _URC_FATAL_PHASE2_ERROR; if the frame has a personality routine it is called with that action: _URC_CONTINUE_UNWIND continues, _URC_INSTALL_CONTEXT calls __unw_phase2_resume(cursor, framesWalked) (normally does not return; if it does the loop continues) and any other result returns _URC_FATAL_PHASE2_ERROR. When the loop ends because __unw_step_stage2 returned 0 or negative (end of stack or step error; the code does not distinguish them), the stop function is called once more with _UA_END_OF_STACK added to the action, its result is ignored, and the function returns _URC_FATAL_PHASE2_ERROR. So every return is _URC_FATAL_PHASE2_ERROR; the early failure returns do not make the final stop call. Successful completion happens through the resume or the stop function transferring control.

functions.name: operator<(const GHashCell &l, const GHashCell &r)
functions.prose_contract: Friend comparison of two GHashCell values: returns l.data < r.data, an unsigned 64-bit comparison of the packed cell words. The word layout is bit 63 = isItem, bits 62 to 32 = tpiSrcIdx + 1, bits 31 to 0 = ghashIdx, so cells with isItem == 0 compare less than cells with isItem == 1, then ties are ordered by (tpiSrcIdx + 1) and then by ghashIdx; an empty cell (data == 0) is the smallest. Pure function of its arguments, no side effects.

functions.name: elf::createTaggedSymbols
functions.prose_contract: AArch64 MTE global-tagging pass over ctx.objectFiles; precondition (assert only) hasMemtag(ctx). Pass 1: for each ObjKind file and each non-null, non-discarded section of type SHT_AARCH64_MEMTAG_GLOBALS_STATIC, addTaggedSymbolReferences walks its relocations (a REL-format section reports an error but the walk continues over rels.relas): each relocation's target symbol that is not STT_OBJECT is skipped, a local symbol is marked tagged immediately, any other symbol has its count in a local DenseMap incremented; the section is then marked dead. Pass 2: for each Binary or Obj file and each symbol in it (declarations and definitions alike) that is STT_OBJECT and non-local and present in the map, if its remaining count is already 0 the entry is erased (the symbol is used by more declarations/definitions than tagged marks, so it stays untagged), otherwise the count is decremented. If the map is still non-empty and ctx.arg.writeAddends is set, an error about --apply-dynamic-relocs and MTE globals is reported (ErrAlways, processing continues). Finally every symbol still in the map is marked tagged (setIsTagged(true)); the code asserts its count is 0 (debug builds only). Locals are tagged unconditionally. No value is returned.

functions.name: AArch64::relocate
functions.prose_contract: Applies one relocation to the bytes at loc, switching on rel.type with val the computed value. Range and alignment checks (checkInt, checkUInt, checkIntUInt, checkAlignment) only report an error through the linker's diagnostics when the value does not fit or is misaligned; they do not stop the write that follows. Groups: ABS16/PREL16 write 16 bits and ABS32/PREL32 write 32 bits (checkIntUInt), PLT32/GOTPCREL32 write 32 bits (checkInt). ABS64 writes 64 bits: val, or -rel.addend when rel.sym is tagged and the addend is negative or at least the symbol size. PREL64 writes 64 bits. AUTH_ABS64 writes a 32-bit value only if val fits in a signed 32-bit integer (isInt<32>); otherwise the location is left unchanged. ADR/ADRP page relocations check a 33-bit range (the _NC variant does not) and write the page value val >> 12; ADR_PREL_LO21 checks 21 bits. JUMP26 first overwrites the whole instruction word with 0x14000000 and then falls into CALL26, which checks a 28-bit range and writes the masked word offset. CONDBR19/LD_PREL_LO19-style relocations check 4-byte alignment and a 21-bit range. The LDSTn/LD64 low-12 relocations check alignment of n bytes and write the shifted 12-bit immediate; MOVW_UABS/SABS/PREL/TPREL relocations check ranges (not for the _NC and G3 variants) and write the 16-bit immediate from the matching bit group; TSTBR14 checks 16 bits; the TLSLE ADD relocations write the high 12 bits (checkUInt 24) or the low 12 bits; TLSDESC writes val to loc + 8. Any other rel.type reaches llvm_unreachable. Returns nothing.

functions.name: AMDGPU::calcEFlags
functions.prose_contract: Computes the ELF e_flags for the output of an AMDGPU link from ctx.objectFiles. Returns 0 if there are no object files. Otherwise it reads the ABI version from the first object's header and dispatches: HSA_V2/V3 to calcEFlagsV3 (returns the first file's e_flags if all files have identical e_flags, else reports an error with ErrAlways and returns 0); HSA_V4/V5 to calcEFlagsV4 (compares mach across files, reports Err and returns 0 on mismatch, combines xnack and sramecc by the ANY/UNSUPPORTED rules, reporting Err and returning 0 on incompatibility, else returns mach|xnack|sramecc); HSA_V6 to calcEFlagsV6 (computes the V4 flags, then compares the generic version bits across files, reporting ErrAlways and returning 0 on mismatch, otherwise ORs the first file's generic version into the V4 result, so after a V4 incompatibility error the V4 value 0 still gets the generic version OR-ed in and a nonzero value can be returned); any other ABI version reports Err 'unknown abi version' and returns 0. Errors are reported through the diagnostics and execution continues to return a value.

functions.name: X86_64::deleteFallThruJmpInsn
functions.prose_contract: Tries to delete a trailing direct jmp (5 bytes, opcode 0xe9) at the end of input section `is` when it falls through to the next section nextIS. Returns false without changes if nextIS is null, if the section is shorter than 5 bytes, if no live relocation (expr != R_NONE) sits at offset size-4, if the byte before that offset is not 0xe9, or if the relocation does not make the jump target equal to the start of nextIS (relocation must be PLT32, PC32 or PC8). If it is a fall-through jump it turns the relocation into R_NONE with offset 0, drops the last 5 bytes of the section, sets is.nopFiller and returns true. Otherwise, if the section is at least 11 bytes (5 + a 6-byte jcc), it looks for a relocation of a conditional jump right before the final jmp; the jcc opcode must be one of the known conditional types with an inverse, and its relocation must target nextIS; then it records a JumpInstrMod that inverts the conditional jump, copies the final jmp's expr/type/addend/symbol into the conditional jump's relocation, turns the final jmp's relocation into R_NONE, drops the last 5 bytes, sets nopFiller and returns true; any failed check on this second path returns false. Mutates is only on the true paths.

functions.name: X86_64::relaxOnce
functions.prose_contract: One linker-relaxation pass for GOT-relative relocations. It computes minVA and maxVA over allocated output sections and returns false immediately if maxVA fits in an unsigned 31-bit value, or if maxVA-minVA fits in 31 bits and the output is PIC. Otherwise, for every relocation in executable output sections whose expr is R_RELAX_GOT_PC or R_RELAX_GOT_PC_NOPIC (the code asserts addend == -4 in debug builds) it computes the target virtual address with the matching addend; if the value fits in a signed 32-bit integer the relocation is left relaxed; otherwise, if the symbol has no aux entry yet (auxIdx == 0), it allocates one, adds a GOT entry and sets changed = true; in both of those not-fitting cases rel.expr is changed to R_GOT_PC. Returns changed, which is true only if at least one new GOT entry was created, so it can return false even though some relocations were converted to R_GOT_PC for symbols that already had an aux entry. The pass argument is not used.

functions.name: EhReader::getFdeEncoding
functions.prose_contract: Parses a CIE and returns the FDE pointer encoding byte. It reads the augmentation via getAugmentation: skips 8 bytes, reads the version (must be 1 or 3, else an error is reported and an empty string results), reads the augmentation string, skips two LEB128 values and reads one byte (version 1) or skips a LEB128 (version 3). It then scans the augmentation characters: 'R' returns the next byte (0 if the buffer is empty, after an error report), 'z' skips a LEB128, 'L' reads a byte, 'P' calls skipAugP, 'B', 'S' and 'G' are ignored, and any other character reports an error and stops the scan. If no 'R' is reached it returns DW_EH_PE_absptr. Parse problems are reported through errOn (Err, non-fatal) and do not stop the scan, except the unknown-character case; so an error reported for an earlier 'P' or truncated field can still be followed by a returned 'R' byte. skipAugP reports an error for DW_EH_PE_aligned, for an unknown size, and also when the encoded size is greater than or equal to the remaining bytes.

functions.name: EhReader::hasLSDA
functions.prose_contract: Parses a CIE and returns true if its augmentation string contains 'L'. It uses getAugmentation (skip 8 bytes, version 1 or 3, read the string, skip two LEB128s, read a byte or skip a LEB128) and then scans the characters: 'L' returns true at once; 'z' skips a LEB128; 'P' calls skipAugP; 'R' reads a byte; 'B', 'S', 'G' are ignored; any other character reports an error and stops the scan; after the scan it returns false (also when getAugmentation failed with an empty string). Errors are reported through errOn (non-fatal) and do not stop the scan, so it can return true after reporting an error from an earlier 'P' or truncated field.

functions.name: elf::hasLSDA
functions.prose_contract: Free function wrapper: constructs an EhReader over the section piece's section and data (EhReader(p.sec, p.data())) and returns EhReader::hasLSDA(). So it returns true if the CIE augmentation string of the piece contains 'L' before an unknown character stops the scan, false otherwise; parse problems are reported through the reader's non-fatal errOn diagnostics and do not by themselves change the result. No state of p is modified.

functions.name: SharedFile::parse<ELFT>
functions.prose_contract: Parses a shared library (ELF DSO) input: collects dynamic tags and the versym/verdef/verneed section headers from the section table, then creates symbols. It allocates the symbols array (numSymbols entries) first. Early exits that do not process any symbol: SHT_GNU_versym present with numSymbols == 0 reports ErrAlways and returns; a DT_NEEDED or DT_SONAME value beyond the string table reports Err and returns (dtNeeded may already hold earlier entries); if another shared file with the same soname is already registered in ctx.symtab->soNames, this file's isNeeded is OR-ed into that earlier entry and the function returns without adding symbols; otherwise the file is appended to ctx.sharedFiles. It then parses verdefs and verneeds, parseGnuAndFeatures, builds a versym table (default VER_NDX_GLOBAL, filled from the versym section when present) and walks the global ELF symbols: a STB_LOCAL symbol in the global part gets Err and is skipped; an undefined symbol with a version other than local/global takes its name from the verneed table as name@version (a verneed index out of range reports ErrAlways and skips the symbol), is added as Undefined with isExported = true and, when it is not weak and unresolvedSymbolsInShlib is not Ignore, is pushed to requiredSymbols; a defined symbol whose version is VER_NDX_LOCAL or whose index is beyond verdefs is skipped (silently for MIPS _gp_disp, otherwise with ErrAlways); for the remaining defined symbols the unversioned SharedSymbol is added only when the symbol's version equals its index (i.e. the hidden bit is not set), and when the version is not VER_NDX_GLOBAL a second SharedSymbol named name@verdefname is added; both set dsoDefined and set versionId only when the symbol's file is this file. A hidden-version defined symbol therefore appears only under its versioned name. Returns nothing.

functions.name: SymbolTable::scanVersionScript
functions.prose_contract: Applies the version-script patterns in ctx.arg.versionDefinitions to the symbol table, in three passes, then calls handleDynamicList(). Pass 1 (definitions in order): for each non-wildcard pattern of a version's non-local list it calls assignExactVersion with the version id/name, then again for the name `pattern@versionname` (includeNonDefault); non-wildcard local patterns do the same with VER_NDX_LOCAL and the name "local". If neither call found a symbol and ctx.arg.undefinedVersion is false, it reports Err (an error, not a warning): version script assignment ... failed: symbol not defined; so the error is suppressed when the `pattern@version` form matched even if the plain pattern matched nothing. Pass 2 (definitions in reverse order): every wildcard pattern other than "*" is passed to assignWildcardVersion (plain and with `@version` form), non-local with the version id and local with VER_NDX_LOCAL; no message is produced for an unmatched wildcard. Pass 3 (reverse order): patterns that are exactly "*" are assigned the same way; while no warning has been issued and the pattern is local or its version id is above VER_NDX_LOCAL, it warns once (Warn, sets asteriskReported) if '*' is used for both local and global scopes or for multiple version definitions, otherwise it records which scope has been seen. Nothing is returned; the result is stored in the symbols' versionId and versionScriptAssigned fields by the callees.

functions.name: Writer<ELFT>::createPhdrs
functions.prose_contract: Builds the list of program headers (PhdrEntry) for one partition when the linker script has no PHDRS command. isMain is partNo == 1. Unless -n/-N: a PT_PHDR (main partition: the program headers output; otherwise the partition's program-headers section), a PT_INTERP for a .interp section of that partition, and, for the main partition, a first PT_LOAD containing the ELF header and program headers. It builds a PT_GNU_RELRO candidate from the partition's relro sections (ErrAlways if a relro section is not contiguous once the relro run has ended). The PT_LOAD loop visits every output section that needs a PT_LOAD: sections of other partitions are skipped, except that for the main partition a section of partition 255 gets its own PT_LOAD; for sections of this partition it computes newFlags (computeFlags), treats the flags as incompatible when they differ from the current load's flags (ignoring X when !W and singleRoRx, ignoring R when !W and singleXoRx), and extends the current PT_LOAD (OR-ing p_flags) only if one exists, the section is not the relro end, memRegion is the same, the LMA region matches (and the section has no lmaExpr) or the load's last section is the program headers, and either a SECTIONS command exists, the section is NOBITS, or the load's last section is not NOBITS; otherwise it starts a new PT_LOAD. Then it adds PT_TLS (if any TLS sections), PT_DYNAMIC, PT_GNU_RELRO (if non-empty), PT_GNU_EH_FRAME (when eh_frame and its header exist), OpenBSD-specific headers when the OSABI is OpenBSD and the sections exist, PT_GNU_STACK unless -z nognustack (RW, plus X for exec stack, p_memsz = stack size), PT_OPENBSD_NOBTCFI / PT_OPENBSD_WXNEEDED from options, PT_GNU_PROPERTY from .note.gnu.property, and PT_NOTE headers: consecutive allocatable SHT_NOTE sections of the partition share one PT_NOTE, a new one starts when there is none, when the section has an lmaExpr, or when its alignment differs from the previous note's last section; any other section in the partition ends the current PT_NOTE group. Returns the vector.

functions.name: kmp_topology_t::filter_hw_subset
functions.prose_contract: Applies the user's KMP_HW_SUBSET to the detected topology and restricts the affinity masks accordingly. Returns false without filtering when no subset is set (__kmp_hw_subset null), when validation fails (each case issues a warning through KMP_AFF_WARNING or __kmp_msg: a requested layer type has no equivalent in the topology, two requested layers are equivalent, a count + offset exceeds the available count for a non-absolute subset, core attributes used on a non-hybrid machine with more than one attribute, core type and efficiency mixed, an invalid efficiency value, a core attribute count too large, an attribute missing or repeated), or when every hardware thread would be filtered out. Before validating it sorts and canonicalizes __kmp_hw_subset and rewrites each item's type to the equivalent topology type, so the subset is modified even on failure; a single core-attribute item on a non-hybrid machine is only warned about and ignored. Otherwise it allocates filtered_mask with KMP_CPU_ALLOC, copies __kmp_affin_fullMask into it, walks all hardware threads maintaining per-level sub-ids (absolute counters when the subset is absolute or core attributes are used) and clears a thread's os_id bit when any subset item rejects it (unknown id, sub-id outside [offset, offset+num), or core type/efficiency not listed), then calls restrict_to_mask(filtered_mask) and returns true. This function itself does not free filtered_mask.

functions.name: __kmp_affinity_create_cpuinfo_map
functions.prose_contract: Builds __kmp_topology from /proc/cpuinfo-style data (platform-specific variants exist for AIX and others). Returns bool; *msg_id is set to kmp_i18n_null at entry and, on failure, to an error id. First it counts 'processor' records (and node_N id lines for the index range); false with NoProcRecords if none (:3266), TooManyProcRecords if more than __kmp_xproc, CantRewindCpuinfo if it cannot rewind the file. It allocates the threadInfo table (num_records+1 rows) and then parses line by line: a line longer than the buffer gives LongLineCpuinfo, a field line without ':' or number gives MissingValCpuinfo, a repeated field in one record gives DuplicateFieldCpuinfo (except where the code allows repeated processor lines on AArch64), a record end with num_avail == __kmp_xproc gives TooManyEntries, a record without a processor id gives MissingProcField; records whose os id is not in __kmp_affin_fullMask are skipped when affinity is capable. A package id missing for any record is filled from core siblings lists or gives MissingPhysicalIDField. It sorts the records, derives per-level counts, sets __kmp_nThreadsPerCore, nCoresPerPkg, nPackages and __kmp_ncores, and if affinity is not capable returns true at that point (with no __kmp_topology built; the code asserts affinity type is none). Otherwise it detects non-unique ids at a level (PhysicalIDsNotUnique, false), allocates __kmp_topology, fills each hardware thread, frees the temporary tables, sorts ids, fills missing thread ids, and if check_ids() fails deallocates __kmp_topology, sets it to nullptr, sets PhysicalIDsNotUnique and returns false; otherwise returns true. The temporary threadInfo rows are freed on the failure paths shown (CLEANUP_THREAD_INFO).

functions.name: __kmp_aux_unset_affinity_mask_proc
functions.prose_contract: Removes processor `proc` from an affinity mask given through mask (a pointer to a kmp_affin_mask_t pointer). Returns -1 if affinity is not capable (KMP_AFFINITY_CAPABLE() false) or if proc < 0 or proc >= __kmp_aux_get_affinity_max_proc(); returns -2 if proc is not set in __kmp_affin_fullMask; otherwise clears the bit with KMP_CPU_CLR and returns 0. With __kmp_env_consistency_check enabled a null mask or null *mask calls KMP_FATAL (AffinityInvalidMask) before the range checks; without that option mask and *mask are dereferenced unchecked. In debug trace builds it also prints the mask. No other state is modified.

functions.name: ATOMIC_XCHG_WR(fixed4, wr, kmp_int32, 32, =, KMP_ARCH_X86)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function void __kmpc_atomic_fixed4_wr(ident_t *id_ref, int gtid, kmp_int32 *lhs, kmp_int32 rhs) (macro ATOMIC_XCHG_WR over ATOMIC_BEGIN). It asserts __kmp_init_serial in debug builds. When KMP_GOMP_COMPAT is compiled in, the GOMP flag (KMP_ARCH_X86, true only on 32-bit x86 builds) is non-zero and __kmp_atomic_mode == 2, it takes the generic atomic lock path (OP_GOMP_CRITICAL with op '=': get the gtid if needed, perform the store under the lock, return). Otherwise it performs KMP_XCHG_FIXED32(lhs, rhs), an atomic exchange whose old value is discarded, so *lhs becomes rhs. Returns nothing. Precondition: lhs points to a suitably aligned kmp_int32.

functions.name: ATOMIC_XCHG_SWP(fixed4, kmp_int32, 32, KMP_ARCH_X86)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function kmp_int32 __kmpc_atomic_fixed4_swp(ident_t *id_ref, int gtid, kmp_int32 *lhs, kmp_int32 rhs) (macros ATOMIC_XCHG_SWP over ATOMIC_BEGIN_SWP). It asserts __kmp_init_serial in debug builds. When the GOMP flag (KMP_ARCH_X86) is non-zero and __kmp_atomic_mode == 2 it uses the generic lock (CRITICAL_SWP(0)): acquire the lock, old_value = *lhs, *lhs = rhs, release, return old_value. Otherwise old_value = KMP_XCHG_FIXED32(lhs, rhs), an atomic exchange, and it returns old_value. In both cases the returned value is the previous *lhs and *lhs equals rhs afterwards. Precondition: lhs points to an aligned kmp_int32.

functions.name: ATOMIC_CRITICAL_CPT_WRK(cmplx4, add_cpt, kmp_cmplx32, +, 8c, 1)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function void __kmpc_atomic_cmplx4_add_cpt(ident_t *id_ref, int gtid, kmp_cmplx32 *lhs, kmp_cmplx32 rhs, kmp_cmplx32 *out, int flag). It asserts __kmp_init_serial in debug builds. When KMP_GOMP_COMPAT is compiled in, the flag argument 1 is set and __kmp_atomic_mode == 2, it takes the generic lock (LCK_ID 0) and does the capture below under it; otherwise it takes the 8c complex lock (ATOMIC_LOCK8c). Under the lock: if flag is non-zero, *lhs += rhs and *out = *lhs (the new value); if flag is zero, *out = *lhs (the old value) and then *lhs += rhs. The lock is released and the function returns void. It is a lock-based update, not a hardware atomic. Precondition: lhs and out point to valid kmp_cmplx32 objects; nothing in the code checks that they differ.

functions.name: __kmp_init_hierarchical_barrier_thread
functions.prose_contract: Refreshes this thread's hierarchical-barrier state in thr_bar for team/nproc/tid and returns whether the team-related state changed. Let uninitialized = (thr_bar->team == NULL), team_changed, team_sz_changed (nproc differs from thr_bar->nproc) and tid_changed (tid differs from old_tid). If uninitialized or team_sz_changed it calls __kmp_get_hierarchy(nproc, thr_bar). If uninitialized, team_sz_changed or tid_changed it recomputes my_level and parent_tid (primary thread: my_level = depth-1, parent_tid = -1), offset, old_tid, wait_flag = KMP_BARRIER_NOT_WAITING, team and parent_bar (the parent_bar assignment indexes team->t.t_threads[parent_tid], which is index -1 for the primary thread; I did not verify that slot is valid). If uninitialized, team_changed or tid_changed it sets team and parent_bar again and sets the return value true. If uninitialized, team_sz_changed or tid_changed it sets nproc, recomputes leaf_kids (0 for level 0, clipped so tid + leaf_kids + 1 <= nproc) and leaf_state. It returns true exactly when uninitialized, team_changed or tid_changed was true; a pure team-size change returns false. Argument gtid is unused.

functions.name: sqrt_newton_approx
functions.prose_contract: Approximates the square root of the unsigned 64-bit x with Newton's iteration in double precision: it starts with sqrt_new = (double)x and repeats sqrt_old = sqrt_new; sqrt_new = (sqrt_old + x / sqrt_old) / 2 while sqrt_old - sqrt_new > 0.1, then returns sqrt_new. The return value is the last iterate, which for x >= 1 comes from above (Newton iteration from x downwards) and, by the standard error bound for this iteration (derived, not tested), lies between sqrt(x) and sqrt(x) + 0.1 up to rounding error; for x == 1 it returns exactly 1.0. For x == 0 the first step computes 0.0/0.0, giving NaN, and the comparison with NaN is false, so it returns NaN. x is converted to double, so for x above 2^53 the input is rounded. No state is read or written.

functions.name: __kmpc_end_serialized_parallel
functions.prose_contract: Leaves a serialized parallel region for the calling thread (gtid global_tid). If loc is non-null and has KMP_IDENT_AUTOPAR set it returns immediately without doing anything else. Otherwise it validates gtid, initialises the parallel runtime if needed, resumes from a soft pause, and if the thread's task team has found proxy tasks or hidden-helper tasks it waits on that task team. It asserts (KMP_ASSERT) that serial_team->t.t_serialized is non-zero. With OMPT enabled and the thread state not 'overhead' it issues implicit-task end and parallel-end callbacks and unlinks the lightweight task team. If the control-stack top's serial_nesting_level equals t_serialized it copies those ICVs back, pops and frees that entry. It pops the dispatch buffer stack (frees the top buffer), pops the task team node when t_serialized > 1, restores th_def_allocator, and decrements t_serialized. If t_serialized reaches 0 it restores the floating-point control state when saved (x87 and MXCSR), pops the current task, fires an OMPD breakpoint, restores th_team to the parent team, th_info.ds.ds_tid, the cached team nproc/master/serialized values and the dispatch pointer, marks the current task as executing, restores the task state and task team when tasking is enabled (not immediate-exec), and resets the root init mask when the team level is 0 and affinity reset is set; otherwise (still nested) it only traces. Finally it decrements serial_team->t.t_level, pops the parallel construct when the consistency check is on, and with OMPT sets the thread state to work_serial or work_parallel. Returns nothing.

functions.name: __kmp_dispatch_next<T>
functions.prose_contract: Returns non-zero if the calling thread was given another chunk of a dynamically scheduled loop, 0 when no more work remains. Outputs: *p_lb and *p_ub receive the chunk bounds, *p_st (when non-null in the serialized paths) the stride, and *p_last (when p_last is non-null) whether this is the last chunk, with the exceptions below. Serialized team (team->t.t_serialized): pr is the top dispatch buffer. If pr->u.p.tc == 0 the function sets *p_lb = *p_ub = 0, *p_st = 0 when non-null, pops the workshare when consistency checking is on, and returns 0 without touching *p_last. For a nomerge loop it hands out chunks of size parm1 by incrementing pr->u.p.count; when the chunk index is past the last it behaves like the tc == 0 case, otherwise it sets *p_lb/*p_ub (scaled by the stride), *p_last, *p_st and the ordered bounds when ordered. Otherwise (merged loop) it hands out the whole range once: sets tc = 0, *p_lb = lb, *p_ub = ub, last_upper, *p_last = TRUE when non-null and *p_st when non-null, and returns the earlier status (1). Active team: the status comes from the hierarchical scheduler when pr->flags.use_hier is set, otherwise from __kmp_dispatch_next_algorithm with the thread's team size and tid (p_st is passed through there without a null check in this function). If the status is 0, the shared num_done counter is atomically incremented, use_hier is cleared when hierarchical scheduling is compiled in, and the last thread to finish (num_done == team size - 1) resets the shared buffer: for static_steal it resets each thread's buffer steal_flag to UNUSED and frees 8-byte-type steal locks, then sets num_done = 0, iteration = 0, ordered_iteration = 0 only when the loop is ordered, and adds __kmp_dispatch_num_buffers to sh->buffer_index (it is advanced, not reset); every thread with status 0 pops the workshare when consistency checking is on and clears th_deo_fcn, th_dxo_fcn, th_dispatch_sh_current and th_dispatch_pr_current. If the status is non-zero and the chunk is the last, pr->u.p.last_upper = pr->u.p.ub. *p_last = last is written only when p_last is non-null and status != 0. In all paths OMPT dispatch/work-end callbacks and statistics are done before returning status.

functions.name: __kmp_dispatch_init_algorithm<T>
functions.prose_contract: Initialises the private dispatch info pr for a loop with bounds lb, ub, stride st, requested schedule and chunk, for team size nproc and thread tid. It records nomerge and ordered flags from the schedule value (ordered forces monotonic), resolves kmp_sch_static to __kmp_static, kmp_sch_runtime to the team's runtime schedule (chunk from the team's schedule, *cur_chunk updated when non-null), kmp_sch_guided_chunked to __kmp_guided, kmp_sch_auto to __kmp_auto, a non-positive explicit chunk to KMP_DEFAULT_CHUNK, kmp_sch_dynamic_chunked with non-monotonic to kmp_sch_static_steal, guided_analytical with more than 2^20 threads to guided_iterative (with a warning), and the runtime_simd cases to static_balanced_chunked or guided_simd (chunk multiplied by the team's chunk). It reports an error for st == 0 when the consistency check is on, computes the trip count tc from lb/ub/st (0 for an empty range), stores lb, ub, st, tc, count = 0, last_upper = ub + st, and for an active ordered loop resets the ordered bookkeeping. It then sets the per-schedule parameters in pr->u.p: static_steal splits chunks among threads and claims the buffer only when nproc > 1 and the chunk count is at least nproc, otherwise it switches to dynamic_chunked; static_balanced computes per-thread lb/ub; static_balanced_chunked always changes the schedule to static_greedy (parm1 = tc rounded up to chunk multiples per thread, or tc when nproc == 1); guided_simd/iterative falls back to dynamic_chunked when (2*chunk+1)*nproc >= tc and to static_greedy when nproc == 1; guided_analytical computes the cross-over point similarly (also falling back to dynamic_chunked or static_greedy); static_greedy and static_chunked/dynamic_chunked set parm1/parm2 (chunk clamped to 1..tc), trapezoidal sets parm1 to parm4, and any other schedule calls __kmp_fatal. Finally it stores the (possibly changed) schedule in pr->schedule. Returns nothing.

functions.name: __kmp_dispatch_deo<UT>
functions.prose_contract: Template entry for an `ordered` region start in a dynamically scheduled loop; gtid is read from *gtid_ref (cid_ref unused). With __kmp_env_consistency_check on and pr->pushed_ws != ct_none it pushes a ct_ordered_in_pdo construct onto the consistency stack (this function contains no pop; any matching pop is elsewhere). If the team is not serialized: pr and sh come from the thread's dispatch current pointers; when KMP_GOMP_COMPAT is not defined and consistency checking is on, it reports CnsMultipleNesting if pr->ordered_bumped is set (that check only runs here in the non-serialized case); it then spin-waits (__kmp_wait with __kmp_ge) until sh->u.s.ordered_iteration >= pr->u.p.ordered_lower. In a serialized team it does nothing except the optional consistency push. Returns nothing.

functions.name: __kmp_check_sync
functions.prose_contract: Consistency checking before entering a synchronization construct of type ct (OpenMP runtime consistency-check mode). It first grows the construct stack (__kmp_expand_cons_stack) when it is full, so stack storage may change even when no error is found. Then: for ct_ordered_in_parallel / ct_ordered_in_pdo, if the thread is not inside a worksharing construct (w_top <= p_top) it reports CnsBoundToWorksharing (or, with BUILD_PARALLEL_ORDERED, only asserts ct == ct_ordered_in_parallel); if inside one whose type is not ordered it reports CnsNoOrderedClause; and if the innermost sync construct (s_top above both p_top and w_top) is a critical, or an ordered with an ident flagged KMP_IDENT_KMPC, it reports CnsInvalidNesting. For ct_critical, only when lck is non-null and its owner is this thread (the same named critical is already held) it reports CnsNestingSameName with the matching stack entry. For ct_master / ct_masked / ct_reduce it reports CnsInvalidNesting when inside a worksharing construct, and for ct_reduce also when inside another sync construct. It does not check a critical nested inside a differently named critical or inside an ordered region. Returns nothing; errors go through __kmp_error_construct / __kmp_error_construct2, which I did not read.

functions.name: int FTN_STDCALL KMP_EXPAND_NAME(FTN_GET_NESTED)(void)
functions.prose_contract: Generated Fortran/C entry point for omp_get_nested (the name comes from KMP_EXPAND_NAME(FTN_GET_NESTED)). In a KMP_STUB build it returns __kmps_get_nested(). Otherwise it gets the calling thread with __kmp_entry_thread(), emits a deprecation notice (KMP_INFORM APIDeprecated, naming omp_get_max_active_levels), and returns 1 if the thread's max-active-levels ICV is greater than 1, otherwise 0.

functions.name: int FTN_STDCALL KMP_EXPAND_NAME(FTN_IN_PARALLEL)(void)
functions.prose_contract: Generated entry point for omp_in_parallel. Stub build: returns 0. Otherwise it gets the calling thread; if the thread is inside a teams construct (th_teams_microtask non-null) it returns 1 when the current team's t_active_level is non-zero, else 0; if not, it returns FTN_TRUE when the root's r_in_parallel is non-zero and FTN_FALSE otherwise.

functions.name: int FTN_STDCALL KMP_EXPAND_NAME(FTN_GET_ACTIVE_LEVEL)(void)
functions.prose_contract: Generated entry point for omp_get_active_level. Stub build: returns 0. Otherwise returns __kmp_entry_thread()->th.th_team->t.t_active_level, the active parallel nesting level of the calling thread's current team; it reads thread/team state (the thread pointer comes from __kmp_entry_thread()) and modifies nothing.

functions.name: int FTN_STDCALL KMP_EXPAND_NAME(FTN_GET_LEVEL)(void)
functions.prose_contract: Generated entry point for omp_get_level. Stub build: returns 0. Otherwise returns __kmp_entry_thread()->th.th_team->t.t_level, the nesting level (active or serialized) of the calling thread's current team; reads state only.

functions.name: int FTN_STDCALL KMP_EXPAND_NAME(FTN_GET_ANCESTOR_THREAD_NUM)(int KMP_DEREF level)
functions.prose_contract: Generated entry point for omp_get_ancestor_thread_num. Stub build: returns -1 if level is non-zero and 0 if it is zero. Otherwise it returns __kmp_get_ancestor_thread_num(__kmp_entry_gtid(), level) (level is dereferenced for the Fortran variant); the result, including -1 for an invalid level, is decided by that callee, which I did not read.

functions.name: int FTN_STDCALL KMP_EXPAND_NAME(FTN_GET_TEAM_SIZE)(int KMP_DEREF level)
functions.prose_contract: Generated entry point for omp_get_team_size. Stub build: returns -1 if level is non-zero and 1 if it is zero. Otherwise it returns __kmp_get_team_size(__kmp_entry_gtid(), level); the value (including any -1 for an invalid level) is decided by that callee, which I did not read.

functions.name: int FTN_STDCALL KMP_EXPAND_NAME(FTN_GET_THREAD_LIMIT)(void)
functions.prose_contract: Generated entry point for omp_get_thread_limit. Stub build: returns 1. Otherwise: if __kmp_init_serial is not set it calls __kmp_serial_initialize(); it takes the calling thread's current task ICVs and returns task_thread_limit if that is non-zero, otherwise the thread_limit ICV.

functions.name: int FTN_STDCALL KMP_EXPAND_NAME(FTN_IN_FINAL)(void)
functions.prose_contract: Generated entry point for omp_in_final. Stub build: returns 0. Otherwise returns 0 if __kmp_init_parallel is not set (before the runtime is initialised); else it returns the `final` flag of the calling thread's current task (td_flags.final).

functions.name: int FTN_STDCALL KMP_EXPAND_NAME(FTN_GET_NUM_PLACES)(void)
functions.prose_contract: Generated entry point for omp_get_num_places. Returns 0 in a stub build or when affinity is not supported at compile time. Otherwise it runs __kmp_middle_initialize() if not yet done, returns 0 if affinity is not capable at run time, and, when __kmp_affinity.flags.reset is not set and the calling thread's team level is 0, calls __kmp_assign_root_init_mask(); it returns __kmp_affinity.num_masks.

functions.name: int FTN_STDCALL KMP_EXPAND_NAME(FTN_GET_PLACE_NUM_PROCS)(int place_num)
functions.prose_contract: Generated entry point for omp_get_place_num_procs. Returns 0 in a stub build or without affinity support. Otherwise it runs __kmp_middle_initialize() if needed, returns 0 if affinity is not capable, optionally assigns the root init mask (as in get_num_places), returns 0 if place_num < 0 or >= __kmp_affinity.num_masks, and otherwise returns the number of processors that are set both in that place's mask and in __kmp_affin_fullMask.

functions.name: LOOP_START_ULL(func, schedule)
functions.prose_contract: Macro that generates the GOMP unsigned-long-long loop start entry points (GOMP_loop_ull_static_start, dynamic, guided and the nonmonotonic variants): int func(int up, unsigned long long lb, unsigned long long ub, unsigned long long str, unsigned long long chunk_sz, unsigned long long *p_lb, unsigned long long *p_ub). It computes the signed stride str2 = up ? (long long)str : -(long long)str and obtains the global thread id. The loop is entered only if (str > 0) ? (lb < ub) : (lb > ub); since str is unsigned, str > 0 holds for every non-zero str, so the test is lb < ub unless str == 0, and the direction comes from `up` only through str2. If the test is true it calls KMP_DISPATCH_INIT_ULL with the macro's schedule, lb, upper bound ub - 1 (str2 > 0) or ub + 1, stride str2, chunk_sz and a final argument (schedule != kmp_sch_static), then KMP_DISPATCH_NEXT_ULL to fill *p_lb and *p_ub; when that returns non-zero it adds 1 to *p_ub if str > 0 and subtracts 1 otherwise (again by the unsigned test), and returns the status. If the test is false it returns 0 and does not write *p_lb or *p_ub. In debug builds an assertion checks the returned stride equals str2.

functions.name: LOOP_RUNTIME_START_ULL(func, schedule)
functions.prose_contract: Macro that generates the GOMP unsigned-long-long runtime-schedule loop start entry points (GOMP_loop_ull_runtime_start and the maybe-nonmonotonic / nonmonotonic runtime variants): int func(int up, unsigned long long lb, unsigned long long ub, unsigned long long str, unsigned long long *p_lb, unsigned long long *p_ub). It has no chunk argument: chunk_sz is a local 0. Otherwise it behaves like LOOP_START_ULL: str2 = up ? str : -str; the loop is entered only if (str > 0) ? (lb < ub) : (lb > ub) (for unsigned str this is lb < ub unless str == 0); then KMP_DISPATCH_INIT_ULL(schedule, lb, ub - 1 or ub + 1 depending on str2 > 0, str2, chunk_sz 0, TRUE) and KMP_DISPATCH_NEXT_ULL fill *p_lb and *p_ub, and on a non-zero status *p_ub is adjusted by +1 if str > 0, else -1; it returns the status. If the range test fails it returns 0 and leaves *p_lb and *p_ub unwritten.

functions.name: __kmp_test_adaptive_lock
functions.prose_contract: Tries to acquire an adaptive (speculative) lock without blocking; returns 1 on success and 0 on failure. If __kmp_should_speculate (acquire_attempts & badness == 0) holds, it first tries __kmp_test_adaptive_lock_only, a hardware-transactional (RTM) attempt: on _XBEGIN_STARTED it checks the underlying queuing lock is free (aborting the transaction if not) and returns 1, meaning the lock is held speculatively inside the transaction, not actually acquired; after soft aborts it retries up to max_soft_retries, a hard abort stops retrying, and when speculation fails the badness is stepped ((badness << 1) | 1, unchanged if that would exceed max_badness) and 0 is returned to this function. If speculation is not tried or fails, acquire_attempts is incremented (a plain, non-atomic increment) and __kmp_test_queuing_lock on the underlying queuing lock decides: 1 (and a non-speculative-acquire statistic) if it was acquired, else 0. So a failing call can change acquire_attempts and badness; the lock itself is not changed on failure.

functions.name: __kmp_test_adaptive_lock_with_checks
functions.prose_contract: Checked variant of the adaptive-lock test used for omp_test_lock. If lck->lk.qlk.initialized does not equal the lock's queuing-lock pointer it calls KMP_FATAL(LockIsUninitialized, "omp_test_lock"). It then calls __kmp_test_adaptive_lock (which may change acquire_attempts and badness even on failure); if that returns non-zero it stores gtid + 1 in lck->lk.qlk.owner_id (also after a speculative success) and returns the value; on 0 it returns 0 without changing owner_id. It does not check for a nestable lock used as a simple lock (unlike the plain queuing-lock checked variant).

functions.name: __kmp_serial_fork_call
functions.prose_contract: Handles a fork when the region is to be serialized; its two returns (lines 1923 and 1931) both return FALSE, so it never reports a real fork. It calls __kmpc_serialized_parallel(loc, gtid) (and under OMPD sets the serial team's t_pkfn). Then by call_context: fork_context_intel: sets the serial team's t_ident; if ap is null it reverts the level increment (t_level--) and invokes the microtask with the parent team's argv, bracketing it with OMPT lightweight-taskteam link, implicit-task begin/end, parallel-end callbacks and unlink; if the microtask is __kmp_teams_master it uses the current (serial) team, sets t_invoke, copies argc arguments from the va_list into its argv, decrements t_level and calls invoker(gtid), then fires OMPT implicit-task end and parallel-end callbacks (no lightweight taskteam is linked or unlinked on this branch); otherwise it copies the arguments from the va_list into a local array and invokes the microtask with the same OMPT bracketing as the first case. fork_context_gnu: with OMPT enabled it initialises and links a lightweight taskteam (exit frame cleared) and returns FALSE without invoking the microtask and without firing OMPT callbacks, leaving the unlink to the caller. Any other call_context hits KMP_ASSERT2. After the intel branches it executes a memory barrier and returns FALSE.

functions.name: __kmp_join_call
functions.prose_contract: Ends a parallel region for the primary thread (join). Normal path: records th_ident and, with OMPT, sets the overhead state (not for a serialized GNU region); unless exit_teams it joins the team with __kmp_internal_join and releases ITT stack ids, while with exit_teams it only sets th_task_state = 0 (so a join barrier is not run for exit_teams). Early return 1 (team serialized): if the thread is in a teams construct it increments t_level when level == th_teams_level or t_serialized when level == th_teams_level + 1 (increments, not decrements), then calls __kmpc_end_serialized_parallel; with OMPT it unlinks the lightweight taskteam for the GNU context and restores state; returns. Early return 2 (teams construct, not exit_teams, team's microtask is not __kmp_teams_master, and t_level == th_teams_level + 1): ends the OMPT implicit task and unlinks the lightweight taskteam, decrements t_level and t_active_level and the root's r_in_parallel, enlarges t_nproc and the workers' th_team_nproc up to the teams size when th_team_nproc is smaller (initialising barrier state and task state of the added threads), fires the OMPT join callback, and returns with the team intact (it is not freed and the primary thread is not moved to the parent team). Otherwise (full join): restores the primary thread's tid, this_construct and dispatch pointer, takes __kmp_forkjoin_lock, decrements r_in_parallel only if not in a teams construct or t_level > th_teams_level, ends the OMPT implicit task, pops the current task, restores the default allocator and HW floating-point control, restores r_active when it differs, frees the team with __kmp_free_team (which frees worker threads), moves th_team, th_team_nproc, th_team_master, th_team_serialized to the parent team, frees and replaces the serial team if the parent is a serialized team other than the thread's serial team or the root team, restores task state and task team when tasking is enabled, marks the current task executing, releases the lock, resets the root init mask when the new level is 0 and affinity reset is set, and fires the OMPT join callback. Returns nothing.
