functions.name: __kmp_join_call
functions.prose_contract: Ends a parallel region for the primary thread (join). Normal path: records th_ident and, with OMPT, sets the overhead state (not for a serialized GNU region); unless exit_teams it joins the team with __kmp_internal_join and releases ITT stack ids, while with exit_teams it only sets th_task_state = 0 (so a join barrier is not run for exit_teams). Early return 1 (team serialized): if the thread is in a teams construct it increments t_level when level == th_teams_level or t_serialized when level == th_teams_level + 1 (increments, not decrements), then calls __kmpc_end_serialized_parallel; with OMPT it unlinks the lightweight taskteam for the GNU context and restores state; returns. Early return 2 (teams construct, not exit_teams, team's microtask is not __kmp_teams_master, and t_level == th_teams_level + 1): ends the OMPT implicit task and unlinks the lightweight taskteam, decrements t_level and t_active_level and the root's r_in_parallel, enlarges t_nproc and the workers' th_team_nproc up to the teams size when th_team_nproc is smaller (initialising barrier state and task state of the added threads), fires the OMPT join callback, and returns with the team intact (it is not freed and the primary thread is not moved to the parent team). Otherwise (full join): restores the primary thread's tid, this_construct and dispatch pointer, takes __kmp_forkjoin_lock, decrements r_in_parallel only if not in a teams construct or t_level > th_teams_level, ends the OMPT implicit task, pops the current task, restores the default allocator and HW floating-point control, restores r_active when it differs, frees the team with __kmp_free_team (which frees worker threads), moves th_team, th_team_nproc, th_team_master, th_team_serialized to the parent team, frees and replaces the serial team if the parent is a serialized team other than the thread's serial team or the root team, restores task state and task team when tasking is enabled, marks the current task executing, releases the lock, resets the root init mask when the new level is 0 and affinity reset is set, and fires the OMPT join callback. Returns nothing.

functions.name: __kmp_get_ancestor_thread_num
functions.prose_contract: Returns the thread number of the calling thread's ancestor at nesting level `level`, for global thread id gtid (assumed valid). Returns 0 if level == 0; -1 if level < 0; -1 if level is greater than the current team's t_level. Inside a teams construct (th_teams_microtask set) with level <= th_teams_level it first adjusts the local level counter ii (by +2 when ii == th_teams_level, else +1). If ii == level it returns the calling thread's own tid (__kmp_tid_from_gtid(gtid)). Otherwise it walks up parent teams, tracking the serialized depth dd, until the level is reached, and returns 0 if dd > 1, else that team's t_master_tid (the tid of the primary thread of the child region in the parent). Reads thread and team state only.

functions.name: __kmp_parse_affinity_proc_id_list
functions.prose_contract: Parses a processor-id list string (GOMP_CPU_AFFINITY / explicit proclist style) starting at env; var names the variable for warnings. Sets *proclist = NULL first. Accepts comma-separated items with optional blanks: a decimal number n, a range n-m with an optional :stride (stride may be negative), or a braced set {n,n,...} (the first number after '{' is required). Returns FALSE after a KMP_WARNING on: a missing digit where one is required (AffSyntaxError), including a first token that is neither digit nor '{' when nothing has been parsed yet, stride 0 (AffZeroStride), start > end with positive stride (AffStartGreaterEnd), start < end with negative stride (AffStrideLessZero), or (end - start) / stride > 65536 (AffRangeTooBig); on FALSE *nextEnv is not written and *proclist stays NULL. Scanning stops at end of string or at a non-digit following at least one valid item (not an error). On TRUE it sets *nextEnv to the position where parsing stopped and *proclist to a newly allocated (__kmp_allocate) NUL-terminated copy of env[0 .. stop); an empty string yields TRUE with an empty copy. Numbers are parsed with __kmp_str_to_int; the code asserts they are non-negative.

functions.name: __kmp_stg_parse_allocator
functions.prose_contract: Parses the OMP_ALLOCATOR environment value (name, value) into the global __kmp_def_allocator; returns nothing. is_memalloc is true when the value contains neither "mem_space" nor ':'. Predefined-allocator form: omp_high_bw_mem_alloc and omp_large_cap_mem_alloc set __kmp_def_allocator to that allocator and return when __kmp_hwloc_available or __kmp_memkind_available is set, otherwise they warn OmpNoAllocator; omp_const/low_lat/cgroup/pteam/thread_mem_alloc warn OmpNoAllocator; omp_default_mem_alloc and every case that did not return then set __kmp_def_allocator = omp_default_mem_alloc, warn StgInvalidValue when nothing was consumed or text remains, and return. Memory-space form (value has a ':' or 'mem_space'): the memory space name (default, large_cap, const, high_bw, low_lat) is read, an unknown name sets the default allocator, warns if nothing/extra text and returns; if a ':' is present it then parses comma-separated trait=value pairs (sync_hint, alignment as a power of two, access, pool_size, fallback, pinned, partition, and fb_data= for a predefined fallback allocator). An unrecognised key, an invalid value (non-digit, non-power-of-two alignment, negative pool_size) skips that pair with a StgInvalidValue warning and reduces ntraits. At the end it calls __kmpc_init_allocator(gtid, memspace, ntraits, traits) and sets __kmp_def_allocator to the result, or omp_default_mem_alloc if that is omp_null_allocator. Not verified by running: if the value names a memory space with no ':' and non-blank text remains after it, the loop body does not advance the scan pointer on later iterations.

functions.name: __kmp_release_deps
functions.prose_contract: Called when task `task` finishes, to release its dependences. With OMPX_TASKGRAPH, if the task belongs to a task graph that is not being recorded it decrements the predecessor counter of each recorded successor and calls __kmp_omp_task for a successor whose counter reaches 0 and whose task pointer is non-null, then returns at once, skipping the lock release, dephash free and node handling below. Otherwise: if the task's depnode exists and mtx_num_locks < 0 it makes the count positive and releases the mutexinoutset locks in reverse order; if the task has a dependence hash it frees it (__kmp_dephash_free) and clears the pointer; if there is no depnode it returns. Otherwise it acquires the depnode lock, sets node->dn.task = NULL (not done for a task-graph task that is being recorded) and releases it, then for each successor in node->dn.successors: atomically decrements its predecessor count and, if that reached 0 and the successor has a task, queues it: on a hidden-helper thread a successor that is not itself a hidden-helper task is handed to its encountering thread with __kmpc_give_task, otherwise __kmp_omp_task; on other threads __kmp_omp_task. Each list element is dereferenced and freed, and finally the task's own depnode is dereferenced. Returns nothing.

functions.name: __kmp_task_finish<ompt>
functions.prose_contract: Finishes execution of an explicit task `task` on thread gtid; resumed_task is the task to resume afterwards (NULL allowed for serialized tasks, then the parent is used). Pops the tied-task stack when that debug feature is built. For an untied task it atomically decrements td_untied_count and, if parts remain (count > 0), restores th_current_task to the resumed task, marks it executing and returns without completing or freeing the task. Otherwise it runs the compiler's destructor thunk if flagged. For a detachable task whose completion event is still pending (checked under the event lock) the task is marked proxy, executing is cleared and completed is false; for a task with a target async handle it is re-queued with __kmpc_give_task (signalling the hidden-helper worker when on a hidden-helper thread) and completed is false. If completed: it sets complete and onced, and when __kmp_track_children_task(taskdata) is true it releases dependences, atomically decrements the parent's incomplete-child count and the taskgroup count; otherwise, if the task team has found proxy or hidden-helper tasks, it releases dependences only; the children and taskgroup counts are not decremented in that case. Then it clears executing (after release_deps) and decrements the unexecuted hidden-helper count for hidden-helper tasks. Afterwards it sets th_current_task = resumed_task, calls __kmp_free_task_and_ancestors only if completed, marks the resumed task executing, and for task-graph tasks decrements the taskgroup count. Returns nothing; the OMPT finish callbacks are issued only when the ompt template argument is true.

functions.name: __kmp_invoke_task
functions.prose_contract: Executes task `task` on thread gtid with `current_task` as the task to resume. If the task is a proxy and already complete, it runs __kmp_bottom_half_finish_proxy and returns, skipping everything below. Otherwise: with OMPT it saves the thread's OMPT info and sets a work state; unless the task is a proxy it calls __kmp_task_start. If cancellation is enabled and the task's taskgroup has a cancel request or the team has t_cancel_request == cancel_parallel, the task is discarded (OMPT cancel callback, statistics) and its routine is not run. Otherwise (not discarded): an untied task copies td_last_tied from current_task; statistics/OMPT/OMPD/ITT bookkeeping is done; if the task has a target async handle it calls tgt_target_nowait_query on that handle instead of running the routine; else if task->routine is non-null it calls it, as routine(shareds) for a native task or routine(gtid, task). Afterwards, unless the task is a proxy, it restores the saved OMPT info (clearing the exit frame for tied tasks) and calls __kmp_task_finish (also for a discarded task); for a proxy task it only runs OMPT task-finish with ompt_task_switch when OMPT is enabled and the task has the target flag, and does not restore the OMPT state. Returns nothing.

functions.name: lua_gc
functions.prose_contract: Lua C API: performs the garbage-collector operation `what` with extra arguments from the variable-argument list; returns an int. If the collector has been stopped internally (g->gcstp has GCSTPGC) it returns -1 immediately, before taking the state lock, for every option. Otherwise it takes lua_lock and handles: LUA_GCSTOP (set stopped by user; res 0), LUA_GCRESTART (debt 0, clear stop flags; 0), LUA_GCCOLLECT (full collection; 0), LUA_GCCOUNT / LUA_GCCOUNTB (total bytes >> 10, and the low 10 bits), LUA_GCSTEP (optional int argument; a basic step when 0 or adds data*1024 to the debt and checks the GC; returns 1 if a cycle finished, else 0), LUA_GCSETPAUSE / LUA_GCSETSTEPMUL (returns the old parameter and sets the new from the int argument), LUA_GCISRUNNING (gcrunning), LUA_GCGEN and LUA_GCINC (return the previous mode, update parameters that are non-zero, and change mode), and any other value returns -1 (after having locked and then unlocking). The function releases the lock (lua_unlock) before returning on all paths that took it.

functions.name: luaG_traceexec
functions.prose_contract: Called before each Lua opcode when debugging hooks may be active; pc points at the instruction being executed in the current Lua function. If the hook mask has neither the line nor the count bit, it clears ci->u.l.trap and returns 0. Otherwise it increments pc to refer to the next instruction and saves it in ci->u.l.savedpc, decrements L->hookcount only when the count mask is set and treats a result of 0 as a count event (reset by resethookcount). If it is not a count event and the line mask is not set it returns 1. If the previous hook yielded (CIST_HOOKYIELD) it clears that flag and returns 1 without calling hooks. It corrects L->top when the instruction does not use the top, calls the count hook (LUA_HOOKCOUNT) if due, and for the line mask calls the line hook (LUA_HOOKLINE) when the new pc index is not after the old one (a backward jump) or the line changed, then stores the new pc index in L->oldpc (L->oldpc is treated as 0 if invalid). If a hook yielded (L->status == LUA_YIELD) it undoes the count decrement (hookcount = 1 if a count event), marks CIST_HOOKYIELD and throws LUA_YIELD, so it does not return in that case. Otherwise returns 1 (keep the trap set).

functions.name: singlestep
functions.prose_contract: Performs one incremental step of the Lua garbage collector and returns the amount of work done (lu_mem); the collector must not be running (asserted). It sets g->gcstopem = 1, then by g->gcstate: GCSpause: restart the collection, state becomes GCSpropagate, work 1; GCSpropagate: if the gray list is empty the state becomes GCSenteratomic (work 0), otherwise it traverses one gray object (propagatemark) and the state stays GCSpropagate; GCSenteratomic: runs atomic(), then entersweep, records the first GCestimate; the sweeping states run sweepstep, which advances to the next sweep state only when its sweep list is exhausted (not on every call); GCSswpend: checkSizes, state GCScallfin, work 0; GCScallfin: if objects remain to be finalized and not in emergency mode it clears gcstopem and runs up to GCFINMAX finalizers (state stays GCScallfin, work scaled by GCFINALIZECOST), otherwise the state becomes GCSpause with work 0. At the end it resets gcstopem to 0 and returns the work, except that an invalid state hits lua_assert(0) and returns 0 without resetting gcstopem. So the state is not advanced on every call.

functions.name: fullinc
functions.prose_contract: Performs a full garbage collection in incremental mode. If the collector invariant is being kept (keepinvariant(g), meaning black objects may exist) it calls entersweep to turn them white. It then runs luaC_runtilstate until GCSpause (finishing any sweep in progress), runs until GCSpropagate (starts a new cycle), sets g->gcstate = GCSenteratomic directly (so the propagate phase is skipped), runs until GCScallfin (atomic phase and sweeping; the debug-only lua_assert then checks GCestimate equals the total bytes), runs until GCSpause (calls pending finalizers and finishes), and finally calls setpause(g). Finalizers run in the last step, so allocations they make may happen after that assertion point. Returns nothing.

functions.name: fts_read
functions.prose_contract: BSD fts compat: returns the next FTSENT of the traversal (fts_cur), or NULL at the end or on a fatal condition. It returns NULL at once if fts_cur is NULL or FTS_STOP is set. It saves and clears the current node's instruction. If the current node is a directory in pre-order (FTS_D): when the instruction is FTS_SKIP or the device changed under FTS_XDEV it frees any pending children, sets FTS_DP and returns the node for its post-order visit; otherwise it uses pending children or calls fts_build; if fts_build returns NULL it returns NULL when FTS_STOP is set, or else returns the same directory node with whatever fts_info fts_build left (FTS_DNR with fts_errno when opendir failed, FTS_DP for an empty directory, FTS_ERR on memory errors with STOP set, so the first two cases are a normal return, not an error stop); otherwise it makes the first child current, builds its path and returns it. For other nodes it moves to the next sibling (freeing the finished node): a root-level next calls fts_load and returns it; a sibling with FTS_SKIP is skipped; otherwise its path is built and it is returned. With no sibling it moves to the parent (freeing the node): the root parent ends the traversal (frees it, sets errno = 0, returns NULL); otherwise the path is truncated and the parent is returned with fts_info FTS_ERR if it has a recorded fts_errno, else FTS_DP (normal post-order visit).

functions.name: getline
functions.prose_contract: POSIX getline replacement: reads a line from fp into *buf, growing it as needed; returns the number of characters read including the newline (excluding the NUL), or -1. If buf or bufsz is NULL it sets errno = EINVAL and returns -1. If *buf is NULL it sets *bufsz = 0, else it stores a NUL in **buf (so a non-NULL *buf must be at least one byte). It reads with fgetc; before each byte it reallocates (doubling *bufsz, or BUFSIZ from 0) whenever pos + 1 >= *bufsz, so the buffer is kept as is when it is already large enough; if realloc fails it returns -1 (earlier contents stay in the old buffer). Every stored byte is followed by a NUL. On a newline it returns the length; on EOF it NUL-terminates and returns the length if at least one character was read and feof(fp) is true, otherwise -1 (also for a read error). Bytes equal to NUL are stored and counted.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Entry point of mandoc / man / apropos / whatis / help. It sets the program name and, for a name beginning with mandocdb or equal to the makewhatis name, returns mandocdb(argc, argv) at once. It selects the argument mode from the program name, parses options with getopt (a usage error calls usage(), which exits), and handles option errors for -I, -K, -T, -W and -O by printing a message and returning mandoc_msg_getrc() directly, without freeing the configuration (so these early returns skip manconf_free). It resolves the output mode, applies -O (either as search output key or as manconf_output settings), decides on pager use and terminal width, and applies pledge when available. For man-style modes it applies quirks (help page default argument, a leading section argument, MACHINE for the architecture). Unless in file mode (it also does this in file mode when the message level minimum is MANDOCERR_STYLE) it fills defpaths from `manpath -q` when -M is not given and calls manconf_parse. In man mode it resolves each name separately (mansearch then fs_search), warns when nothing matches, and for first-match output picks the best section by priority; with no names and -w it prints the manpath and returns; apropos/whatis do one mansearch (usage() when it fails, 'nothing appropriate' when it finds nothing); file mode builds one entry per file argument (or stdin). Output modes -w and -l print file names or name lists and jump to cleanup; otherwise it allocates parser state, processes each result with process_onefile, reports an unused -O tag, frees the formatter data, and at `out:` frees the search results and, unless in file mode, the configuration, closes tag files and may run the pager or print the message summary. It returns mandoc_msg_getrc().

functions.name: print_man_node
functions.prose_contract:
HTML output of one man(7) node n. It returns immediately, printing nothing, for a comment node or a node flagged NODE_NOPRT. Otherwise it sets the fill mode from NODE_NOFILL (and may end the line in no-fill mode). Text nodes: an empty string prints an end-of-line and returns; otherwise a leading blank at the start of an input line emits a
(unless HTML_NONEWLINE), a delimiter-closing flag sets no-space, the tag's refcount is incremented and the text is printed. Equation nodes are printed with print_eqn. Table nodes are printed with print_tbl and the function returns. For other nodes it closes any font scope, closes an open table, increments the current tag's refcount, and if the token is a roff request (n->tok < ROFF_MAX) it calls roff_html_pre, restores the refcount, closes tags with print_stagq and returns without printing children; otherwise it calls the macro's pre handler (when present), whose result decides whether the children are printed. After the children it decrements the refcount; for IP/TP/TQ blocks it finds the enclosing DL/UL tag and closes the whole list if no further item of that type follows, else only the item. Returns nothing. The early returns for comments/NOPRT, empty text, tables and roff requests skip the final refcount decrement and tag closing.

functions.name: manconf_output
functions.prose_contract: Parses one -O style output option string cp into the manoutput structure conf; fromfile is non-zero when it comes from the config file. Returns 0 on success and -1 after printing a message on error. It matches cp against the tokens includes, man, paper, style, indent, width, outfilename, tagfilename, tag, fragment, noval, toc (a token must be followed by a blank, '=' or the end), skips an '=' and following blanks, and handles: the first eight need a non-empty value (otherwise BADVAL_MISS, -1); fragment, noval and toc must have no value (otherwise BADVAL, -1); an unknown option gives BADARG_BAD, -1. Setting rules: includes, man, paper, style, outfilename, tagfilename and tag store a copy of the value when not yet set; if already set, the old value is kept, and the call returns 0 silently when fromfile, or reports BADVAL_DUPE and returns -1 otherwise. indent (0..1000) and width (1..1000) use strtonum and report BADVAL_BAD with -1 for bad numbers; they are treated as already set only when the stored value is non-zero. fragment, noval and toc just set their flag to 1 and return 0, with no duplicate detection.

functions.name: args
functions.prose_contract: Static tokenizer in mdoc_argv.c that scans the next argument of an mdoc macro line from buf at *pos and returns an enum margserr, storing the argument start in *v (a local dummy when v is NULL). If at end of line it returns ARGS_EOLN, first warning ARG_QUOTE and clearing PHRASELIT if a quoted literal is still open outside a phrase, and clearing PHRASEQL. With flag ARGSFL_DELIM and a line whose remaining words are a close delimiter followed only by delimiters it returns ARGS_PUNCT. With ARGSFL_TABSEP it takes the field up to the next tab (or to the end of the line), updates PHRASEQL/PHRASEQN, skips blanks after the tab and trailing blanks, NUL-terminates in place and returns ARGS_PHRASE. If a quoted literal is open (MDOC_PHRASELIT) or the phrase flag is set and the word begins with '"', it parses a quoted literal in place: the opening quote is skipped, doubled quotes collapse to one, an unescaped closing quote ends it and is replaced by NUL; if the line ends first it warns ARG_QUOTE (unless in a phrase) and leaves PHRASELIT set; in all these quoted cases it returns ARGS_WORD, after skipping following blanks and warning SPACE_EOL if the line then ends. Otherwise it takes the word with roff_getarg (a newly allocated string, freed here when v was NULL), converts PHRASEQL to PHRASEQF after the last word of a phrase, and returns ARGS_ALLOC (the caller must free *v).

functions.name: print_word
functions.prose_contract: Writes the word s to standard output for the man(7) generator, using the file-level flags outflags and counter TPremain. If any pending break flag (MMAN_PP, sp, br, nl) is set it prints the corresponding request line (.PP with .PD bookkeeping, .sp, .br or a plain newline), clears those flags and MMAN_spc, prints '.br' if TPremain == 1, sets TPremain = 0, and prints no space before the word. Otherwise, if MMAN_spc is set, it prints a space (preceded by a backslash for a non-suspended Bk word) only if the space is forced, s is empty, s does not start with one of .,:;)]?! or s is longer than one character; a printed space decrements TPremain if non-zero. It then recomputes MMAN_spc (set when MMAN_Sm is on and s is not a lone '(' or '['), clears the force and Bk-suspend flags, and prints the characters: ASCII_NBRSP as '\ ', ASCII_HYPH as '-', ASCII_BREAK as '\:', a blank as '\ ' when MMAN_nbrword is set, else the character; TPremain is decremented (if non-zero) once per input character of s, not per output character. Finally it clears MMAN_nbrword. Returns nothing.

functions.name: print_node
functions.prose_contract: Recursive man(7) output for one mdoc node. It returns immediately for a node flagged NODE_NOPRT. It sets MMAN_nl when a space is pending, the node starts a line and is not transparent, and clears NODE_ENDED on the node at entry (so already-ended nodes are processed). Equation and table nodes print a notice that -T man does not support them and return. Text nodes get a leading '\&' when a line starts with '.' or ''', spacing flags are adjusted for delimiters and Sm, and the text is printed with print_word. Other nodes: a roff request (n->tok < ROFF_MAX) is handled by roff_man_acts and the function returns without visiting children or running post handlers; an mdoc macro looks up its action, evaluates its condition, runs its pre handler when the condition holds and (n->end == ENDBODY_NOT or the node has children), whose result decides whether children are visited. The children are visited recursively. If NODE_ENDED has been set on the node by then (e.g. by an enclosing block end) it returns without running the post handler or marking the body; otherwise it runs the post handler when the condition held and, for an end-of-body node (n->end != ENDBODY_NOT), sets NODE_ENDED on n->body. Returns nothing.

functions.name: state_sh
functions.prose_contract: mdoc state handler for the Sh macro. It does nothing unless n is the head of the block (n->type == ROFFT_HEAD). If the node is not yet marked NODE_VALID it determines the section: a head with exactly one text child maps through mdoc_a2sec, otherwise SEC_CUSTOM; it stores that in the parent block's sec and sets it with setsec(n, sec). Regardless of NODE_VALID it then sets mdoc->lastsec = n->sec; if that is SEC_SYNOPSIS it sets the roff register nS to 1 and the MDOC_SYNOPSIS flag, otherwise it sets nS to 0 and clears that flag. Returns nothing.

functions.name: termp_sh_pre
functions.prose_contract: Terminal renderer pre-handler for the Sh macro; returns 1 in all branches except the head, where it returns the result of termp_bold_pre. For the block it calls term_vspace(p) unless the previous sibling is an Sh whose body is empty (a previous Sh with an empty body suppresses the vertical space). For the head it sets p->fontibi = 1 and returns termp_bold_pre(p, pair, meta, n). For the body it sets p->tcol->offset = term_len(p, p->defindent), resets the tab stops (term_tab_set NULL, then "T" and ".5i"), and for the AUTHORS section clears the TERMP_SPLIT and TERMP_NOSPLIT flags. Other node types change nothing.

functions.name: tblcalc_number
functions.prose_contract: Computes and records the width of one numeric table cell in out.c. Returns 0 for a null or empty cell string. Otherwise totsz is the printed width of the string (tbl->slen). If col is NULL it returns totsz without touching any column. With a column it looks for the last digit and the last decimal point adjacent to a digit (the \& alignment mark overrides both); if there is no digit it treats the cell as a literal string, raises col->width to totsz when smaller and returns totsz. Otherwise it measures the integer part width intsz up to the decimal point (or after the last digit); if intsz exceeds col->decimal it increases col->nwidth by the difference and sets col->decimal = intsz, else it adds col->decimal - intsz to totsz; then it raises col->nwidth to totsz and col->width to col->nwidth when smaller, and returns totsz (including the alignment padding).

functions.name: ps_end
functions.prose_contract: Finishes PostScript/PDF output for the mandoc terminal renderer. It first calls ps_plast (flush the pending last character) and ps_pclose (close an open text string). If PS_NEWPAGE is not set in p->ps->flags, meaning a page is still open, it asserts the flags and last-character state are clear and calls ps_closepage, which writes the pending page (margins, then showpage for PostScript, or the stream length, resource and page objects for PDF) and sets PS_NEWPAGE. For PostScript it then prints the %%Trailer, %%Pages count and %%EOF and returns. For PDF it writes the Pages node, the Catalog, the cross-reference table, trailer and %%EOF. All output goes through ps_printf, which writes to stdout (or into the growable margin buffer while PS_MARGINS is set) and updates pdfbytes; pdf_obj and ps_growbuf can reallocate the object table or the margin buffer, so the function can allocate memory. Returns nothing.

functions.name: ps_pclose
functions.prose_contract:
Closes an open text string in the PostScript/PDF renderer. If PS_INLINE is not set in p->ps->flags it returns immediately without output. Otherwise: for PDF output it prints ") Tj
ET
"; for PostScript, if the current row equals lastrow it prints ")c
", else it prints ")s
" and sets lastrow to the current row. Then it clears PS_INLINE. Returns nothing.

functions.name: GEN_FIELD_ATTR_SET_FCT(fore)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function int set_field_fore(FIELD *field, chtype attr) (macro GEN_FIELD_ATTR_SET_FCT(fore), documented as setting the field's foreground attribute). It starts with the result E_BAD_ARGUMENT. If attr is A_NORMAL or consists only of attribute bits (attr & A_ATTRIBUTES) == attr, it replaces a NULL field argument by the default field (Normalize_Field), so a NULL field modifies the default field instead of failing; then if the stored fore attribute differs from attr it stores attr and returns _nc_Synchronize_Attributes(field), which can return E_OK, E_BAD_ARGUMENT or the result of Display_Field (for example E_SYSTEM_ERROR); if the stored value already equals attr it returns E_OK without synchronising. For an attr containing non-attribute bits nothing is changed and E_BAD_ARGUMENT is returned.

functions.name: GEN_FIELD_ATTR_SET_FCT(back)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function int set_field_back(FIELD *field, chtype attr) (macro GEN_FIELD_ATTR_SET_FCT(back), documented as setting the field's background attribute). It starts with the result E_BAD_ARGUMENT. If attr is A_NORMAL or consists only of attribute bits (attr & A_ATTRIBUTES) == attr, it replaces a NULL field argument by the default field (Normalize_Field), so a NULL field modifies the default field instead of failing; then if the stored back attribute differs from attr it stores attr and returns _nc_Synchronize_Attributes(field), which can return E_OK, E_BAD_ARGUMENT or the result of Display_Field (for example E_SYSTEM_ERROR); if the stored value already equals attr it returns E_OK without synchronising. For an attr containing non-attribute bits nothing is changed and E_BAD_ARGUMENT is returned.

functions.name: set_current_field
functions.prose_contract: Public libnform call that makes `field` the current field of `form`. Returns E_BAD_ARGUMENT if form or field is NULL; E_REQUEST_DENIED if the field belongs to another form or is not selectable. If the form is not posted it just stores the field as current and sets curpage from the field's page, and returns E_OK without hooks. If posted: E_BAD_STATE while the driver is running (_IN_DRIVER); if the field is already current nothing happens and the result is E_OK; otherwise it validates the current field with _nc_Internal_Validation (failure gives E_INVALID_FIELD and no change), then calls the field-term hook, moves to the new field either through _nc_Set_Form_Page (when the page differs, with the form-term and form-init hooks around it) or _nc_Set_Current_Field, calls the field-init hook and refreshes the current field, returning the error code of the move; hooks and the refresh run even if the move reported an error, and a failed move can leave the form's current field or window changed.

functions.name: _nc_Set_Current_Field
functions.prose_contract: Makes `newfield` the current field of `form`, creating the field's display window. Returns E_BAD_ARGUMENT if form or newfield is NULL or newfield belongs to another form; E_BAD_STATE if the driver is running; E_NOT_CONNECTED if the form has no fields. If newfield is already current and the form is posted it skips the window work and goes straight to the final step, so E_OK can be returned without creating a new window. Otherwise: if there is a current field with a window that is visible and on the current page it calls _nc_Unset_Current_Field on it; it then creates a new pad (field with invisible parts) or a derived window for the field, returning E_SYSTEM_ERROR if that fails (at that point the previous current field has already been unset but form->current and form->w are unchanged); on success it sets form->current, deletes the old form->w, installs the new window, clears _WINDOW_MODIFIED, applies the field's window attributes and redraws buffer contents. In all successful paths it sets currow, curcol, toprow and begincol to 0 and returns E_OK.

functions.name: IFN_Next_Word
functions.prose_contract: Intra-field navigation: moves the cursor to the start of the next word in the current field. It synchronises the buffer itself (Synchronize_Buffer), so the caller need not. It finds the first whitespace after the cursor position and then the start of data after it, and moves the cursor there with Adjust_Cursor_Position, returning E_OK. In this build FRIENDLY_PREV_NEXT_WORD is defined as 1, so when there is no next word (the two positions coincide) it still returns E_OK and the cursor is moved to the position found, which is the end of the data, not the start of a word; the E_REQUEST_DENIED return exists only when FRIENDLY_PREV_NEXT_WORD is 0.

functions.name: IFN_Previous_Word
functions.prose_contract: Intra-field navigation: moves the cursor to the start of the previous word in the current field. It synchronises the buffer itself. It finds the end of data before the cursor (After_End_Of_Data); if the cursor was inside a word (that position equals the cursor) it repeats the search once more from before that word's start; it then finds the position after the last whitespace before it and moves the cursor there with Adjust_Cursor_Position, returning E_OK. With FRIENDLY_PREV_NEXT_WORD defined as 1 (as in this file) a missing previous word does not yield E_REQUEST_DENIED: the function still returns E_OK, with the cursor moved to the position found (the start of the buffer region examined) rather than to a real previous word.

functions.name: FE_New_Line
functions.prose_contract: Field-editing request for a new line in the current field. Let Last_Row be true when the cursor is on the field's last data row. Overlay mode (_OVLMODE): if Last_Row and the field is not growable-and-multi-line, it returns E_REQUEST_DENIED unless the form has O_NL_OVERLOAD, in which case it clears to end of line, sets _WINDOW_MODIFIED and returns the result of Inter_Field_Navigation(FN_Next_Field). Otherwise (not last row, or a growable multi-line field) it grows the field by one row first when on the last row (E_SYSTEM_ERROR if that fails), clears to end of line, increments currow, sets curcol = 0, sets _WINDOW_MODIFIED and returns E_OK. Insert mode: if Last_Row and not growable-multi-line it returns E_REQUEST_DENIED without O_NL_OVERLOAD, else the Inter_Field_Navigation result; otherwise it needs room for a line or a growable field (E_REQUEST_DENIED if neither; E_SYSTEM_ERROR if growing fails) and splits the line at the cursor: clears to end of line, moves to the next row at column 0, inserts a line and writes the rest of the old line there, sets _WINDOW_MODIFIED and returns E_OK. So the Inter_Field_Navigation result is returned only on the overload path, and a last-row growable multi-line field grows instead of navigating.

functions.name: FE_Insert_Character
functions.prose_contract: Field-editing request that inserts a blank at the cursor. It starts with E_REQUEST_DENIED and proceeds only if Check_Char accepts a blank (C_BLANK) for the field's type; if it does not accept it, E_REQUEST_DENIED is returned with no change. If there is room in the line, or the field is single-line and growable, it grows the field when there is no room (E_SYSTEM_ERROR if growing fails) and otherwise inserts the blank with winsch and returns the result of Wrapping_Not_Necessary_Or_Wrapping_Ok, which may be E_OK or an error such as E_REQUEST_DENIED or E_SYSTEM_ERROR; when wrapping fails the inserted character has been put into the window and is then deleted again, so the window is modified and restored rather than untouched. If there is no room and the field is not growable single-line, it returns E_REQUEST_DENIED.

functions.name: _nc_Internal_Validation
functions.prose_contract: Validates the current field of `form`; returns TRUE (non-zero) if the field is accepted or needs no check, FALSE if the field-type check rejects the contents. It first calls Synchronize_Buffer(form). It checks the field only if the form has _FCHECK_REQUIRED set or the field does not have the O_PASSOK option: then Check_Field must succeed (otherwise it returns FALSE with no further change); on success it clears _FCHECK_REQUIRED on the form, sets _CHANGED on the field and synchronises linked fields. When O_PASSOK is set and _FCHECK_REQUIRED is not, it skips the check and these updates and returns TRUE. A current field must exist (form->current is dereferenced).

functions.name: Data_Entry
functions.prose_contract: Handles the typing of one character c into the current field of `form`. Returns E_REQUEST_DENIED unless the field has O_EDIT (and O_ACTIVE when FIX_FORM_INACTIVE_BUG is built); the window and buffer are then untouched. If the field has O_BLANK, the cursor is at the first position and neither _FCHECK_REQUIRED nor _WINDOW_MODIFIED is set, the window is erased. In overlay mode it writes the character with waddch; in insert mode it requires room in the line or a growable single-line field (else E_REQUEST_DENIED), grows the field if needed (E_SYSTEM_ERROR on failure) and inserts with winsch. It then calls Wrapping_Not_Necessary_Or_Wrapping_Ok; only if that returns E_OK it records whether the cursor is at the field's end (and sets move_after_insert for O_EDGE_INSERT_STAY), sets _WINDOW_MODIFIED, and: if at the end of a non-growable field with O_AUTOSKIP it returns the result of Inter_Field_Navigation(FN_Next_Field); else if at the end of a growable field and growing fails it returns E_SYSTEM_ERROR; else it moves to the next character position (unless a multibyte character is still incomplete) and returns E_OK. If wrapping returns an error, that error is returned and _WINDOW_MODIFIED is not set.

functions.name: form_driver
functions.prose_contract: Public libnform driver: processes request or character c for form. It first sets the file-level move_after_insert to TRUE. Returns E_BAD_ARGUMENT for a NULL form and E_NOT_CONNECTED when the form has no fields or no current field (both checked before any other work). The special value FIRST_ACTIVE_MAGIC sets form->current to the first active field and returns E_OK. Then E_BAD_STATE if the driver is running and E_NOT_POSTED if the form is not posted. If c is a form command whose binding matches, the command's generic method (page, field, scrolling or editing wrapper, or none) is run, giving E_SYSTEM_ERROR when the method index is out of range or the command function is missing; otherwise the command's result. With mouse support, KEY_MOUSE events are mapped to field/page requests or selection of a field under the click (E_REQUEST_DENIED when the click is not usable). For a regular character, if it is printable (and, in the non-wide build, accepted by Check_Char) it calls Data_Entry; otherwise the result stays E_UNKNOWN_COMMAND. After all paths that reach the end it calls _nc_Refresh_Current_Field and returns the result.

functions.name: set_form_sub
functions.prose_contract: Sets the subwindow used to display a form. If form is non-NULL and posted it returns E_POSTED without change. Otherwise Normalize_Form replaces a NULL form argument by the default form (so the default form is modified), and the subwindow is set: in builds with NCURSES_SP_FUNCS, form->sub = win if win is non-NULL, else the screen's standard window; in builds without it, form->sub = win, which may be NULL. Returns E_OK in both builds.

functions.name: post_menu
functions.prose_contract: Posts a menu. Returns E_BAD_ARGUMENT for NULL, E_BAD_STATE if the menu driver is running (_IN_DRIVER), E_POSTED if already posted, and E_NOT_CONNECTED if the menu has no items. Otherwise it creates a pad menu->win sized for the menu and a subpad menu->sub; if newpad fails it returns E_SYSTEM_ERROR, and if subpad fails it also returns E_SYSTEM_ERROR but leaves menu->win allocated (menu->sub is NULL), so the menu is changed. Then it relinks items if _LINK_NEEDED, sets _POSTED, clears each item's value when O_ONEVALUE is not set, draws the menu, calls the menu-init and item-init hooks, shows the menu and returns E_OK.

functions.name: waddch_literal
functions.prose_contract: Stores one literal character cell at the window cursor (the wide-character build is described). It applies CHECK_POSITION, renders the character with the window's background (render_char) and marks the cell changed. If an incomplete multibyte sequence is pending or the character is not a single byte, _nc_build_wch assembles it: a complete character replaces ch; if the sequence is still incomplete the function returns OK without storing anything; on an encoding error (len == -1) an 8-bit character whose unctrl form is longer than one character is output as that expansion through waddch (returning the first failure), otherwise it returns waddch(win, ' ' | attr). Then by display width: width 0 (non-spacing) is added to the previous cell's character list (the previous line's last cell at column 0), no new cell is written and the cursor stays; width greater than 1: if wider than the window it returns ERR, if it does not fit on the line the rest of the line is blank-filled and the cursor wraps (ERR if wrapping fails), orphaned cells are blanked, and the width cells are written; width 1: the cell is stored and x advances. Finally if x is past the last column it returns wrap_to_next_line(win), else it sets the cursor column and returns OK.

functions.name: _nc_background
functions.prose_contract: Common implementation of wbkgd (narrow) and wbkgrnd (wide) background setting for window win with background character ch. It returns ERR if the screen (SP) is NULL or win is NULL. Otherwise it forms the new background (colour info is dropped on a terminal without colour pairs, a null character becomes a blank with the same attributes). If the new background is identical to the current one it returns OK at once without changing anything. Otherwise it sets the window background (wbkgrndset), sets the window attributes (and the colour pair when the old and new pair are equal and non-zero), then visits every cell of the window: cells whose character equals the old background character get the new background character; every cell's attributes and colour pair are recomputed (old background attributes removed, new ones added, depending on its colour pair), not only the cells that matched the old background; finally it touches the whole window, calls _nc_synchook and returns OK. In the narrow call a non-charable new background keeps the old character.

functions.name: endwin
functions.prose_contract: Ends curses mode for the screen and restores the shell terminal mode. In builds with NCURSES_SP_FUNCS the public endwin() simply returns the screen-pointer version called with CURRENT_SCREEN (lines 79-83); the logic described here is in lines 48-76 (in other builds this is endwin itself). The result starts as ERR. If the screen pointer is non-NULL: when the screen is not already in the suspended state it sets the suspended state, runs the terminal-driver or mouse/screen/mvcur wrap-up and sets the result to OK; then, whether or not it was already suspended, it calls reset_shell_mode, and if that returns ERR the result becomes ERR. So the result is OK only when this call performed the suspend and reset_shell_mode succeeded; a NULL screen, a second endwin without refresh, or a reset_shell_mode failure gives ERR.

functions.name: fifo_push
functions.prose_contract: Reads one more input key and appends it to the screen's key fifo; returns the key stored, ERR, or KEY_EVENT. Static helper in lib_getch.c, with several configuration-dependent branches. It returns ERR immediately if tail < 0 (the fifo has no room, nothing is stored). With event support, if an event list is given (or a mouse fd exists) it checks mouse/event activity; an event result makes it ungetch KEY_EVENT and return KEY_EVENT without storing to the fifo. A pending GPM or sysmouse (or terminal-driver mouse) event is handled by calling the mouse-event routine and the key becomes KEY_MOUSE. Otherwise it blocks reading one byte from the input (through the driver, console read or read()), and a read result of -1 or 0 makes the key ERR. It then stores the key at sp->_fifo[tail], clears _fifohold, sets head and peek to tail when the fifo was empty (head == -1), advances tail with t_inc and returns the key; this storing path is the same for mouse keys and ERR, so ERR is also pushed in that case.

functions.name: allow_gpm_mouse
functions.prose_contract: Decides whether ncurses may use the GPM mouse library (compiled only with USE_GPM_SUPPORT); returns bool, starting from FALSE. With weak-symbol support, if the GPM function Gpm_Wgetch is already linked in or loaded, it skips the remaining checks and returns FALSE (it reads sp->_mouse_gpm_loaded only to trace whether ncurses loaded it). Otherwise, if stdout is a terminal: when the environment variable NCURSES_GPM_TERMS is set the result is TRUE only if TERM is set and matches that list (_nc_name_match with separators "|:"); when it is not set the result is TRUE only if TERM is set and contains "linux". If stdout is not a terminal it returns FALSE. It only reads the environment and sp; nothing else is modified.

functions.name: NCURSES_SP_NAME(resize_term)
functions.prose_contract: Resizes the terminal model of `sp` to ToLines x ToCols. Returns ERR at once, before taking the lock, if sp is NULL or either size is not positive. Otherwise it locks the global curses lock and computes the number of stolen (ripped-off) lines; only if is_term_resized reports that the size differs does it resize windows: it increases line count first (increase_size), then column count, then decreases if either target is smaller (decrease_size), each stopping with ERR if a window adjustment fails. If all succeeded, in that branch it updates the stored screen size (and the terminal driver's size or the lines/columns variables), sets _lines_avail, and frees and clears the old and new hash arrays (oldhash and newhash). If the size is unchanged it does none of this and the hash arrays stay allocated. Whenever the result is OK, including the unchanged case, it also updates LINES and COLS (minus stolen lines), then unlocks and returns the result (OK or ERR).

functions.name: resize_term
functions.prose_contract: Public resize_term(ToLines, ToCols) in builds with NCURSES_SP_FUNCS: takes the global curses lock (_nc_sp_lock_global), calls the screen-pointer version with CURRENT_SCREEN and the same sizes, releases the lock and returns the result. So the argument and NULL-screen checks are made inside that callee (ERR), after this wrapper has locked.

functions.name: _nc_merge_entry
functions.prose_contract: Merges the capabilities of source entry into target entry (both ENTRY structures); returns void. It returns immediately if source, target or their term types are NULL. With extended names (NCURSES_XNAMES) it copies the source term type, aligns the extended capability tables of target and the copy, and rebuilds both string tables: all names and string capabilities of the copy and of the target are copied into one newly malloc'ed table (the program aborts through _nc_err_abort when malloc fails), the target's pointers are repointed into it and the old target table and the copy's table are freed; the extended-name strings get the same treatment. Then, for each source capability within the target's counts: booleans: if the target value is not CANCELLED, a source CANCELLED sets it FALSE, a source TRUE sets it TRUE, and a source FALSE or ABSENT leaves it unchanged; numbers: if the target is not CANCELLED, a source CANCELLED makes it ABSENT, a source that is not ABSENT replaces it, and ABSENT leaves it; strings: the same rule with CANCELLED_STRING/ABSENT_STRING (a present source string replaces the target string, pointing into the new table). The temporary copy arrays are freed at the end.

functions.name: _nc_get_token
functions.prose_contract: Terminfo/termcap lexer: reads the next token from the input set up by the compiler and returns its type (NAMES, BOOLEAN, CANCEL, NUMBER, STRING, EOF or UNDEF), filling _nc_curr_token. If a token was pushed back it restores it (_nc_set_type with the pushed name), clears the pushback and returns its type. If the stream is at its end it returns EOF and clears tk_name if that pointed at tok_buf. Otherwise it skips blanks and newlines (tracking a newline for the termcap warning), handles an optional leading '.' (commented-out entry: it parses the token and then returns the result of a recursive call for the next one), and skips illegal leading characters through _nc_panic_mode, warning unless silent. At the start of an entry line it reads the name field up to the separator, deciding between termcap (':') and terminfo (',') syntax; running out of input inside that name line calls _nc_err_abort(MSG_NO_INPUTS) and does not return. It sets tk_name to tok_buf and returns NAMES. Elsewhere it reads an identifier and then by the next character: ',' or ':' returns BOOLEAN (a separator that does not match the syntax calls _nc_err_abort 'Separator inconsistent with syntax'); '@' returns CANCEL; '#' reads digits into a number buffer, returns NUMBER with tk_valnumber, and when not silent warns on missing, negative or oversized values and clamps the value to the NCURSES_INT2 maximum; '=' translates the string with _nc_trans_string and returns STRING with tk_valstring; end of input or a full buffer gives EOF; any other character gives UNDEF with a warning when not silent. Warnings do not change the return value.

functions.name: _nc_timed_wait
functions.prose_contract: Waits for input, mouse or event activity on the screen's file descriptors for up to `milliseconds` (negative means no timeout); mode is a bitmask (TW_INPUT, TW_MOUSE, TW_EVENT); returns a bitmask of the ready sources, 0 on timeout, error or interruption, or TW_NONE if the poll descriptor array cannot be allocated in an event build. With events, a pending event timeout shorter than the requested wait replaces it. It records a start time, then uses poll (descriptors for the input fd, the mouse fd and readable event files), or a BeOS loop, or select, to wait; event results are recorded in the event list. It then reduces `milliseconds` by the elapsed time and decrements event timeouts, and with PRECISE_GETTIME and nanosleep, if nothing happened and more than 100 ms remain, it sleeps 100 ms and repeats the wait. If timeleft is non-NULL it stores the remaining milliseconds in *timeleft. A positive poll/select result is turned into the bits for the ready descriptors (poll: the bit position is the slot index for each of the first MIN_FDS slots with POLLIN set and the bit present in mode; select: TW_MOUSE and TW_INPUT by FD_ISSET), a zero or negative result becomes 0, and the TW_EVENT bit is added when the event list reports activity. A malloc'ed poll array is freed before returning.

functions.name: TransformLine
functions.prose_contract: Updates terminal line `lineno` from the new screen image (newLine) to the current screen image (oldLine) with as little output as possible; returns void. It first copies the new line's hash into the old hash. With colour, cells that differ only in colour pair number but whose pairs are the same colours get the new pair number in oldLine. If the terminal has ceol_standout_glitch and clr_eol and any cell's attributes changed, it moves to column 0, clears to end of line and rewrites the whole line. Else, if magic_cookie_glitch > 0 (USE_XMC_SUPPORT) it writes the line cell by cell with PutChar, skipping cells that would hold cookies. Otherwise it finds the first differing cell (optionally using clr_bol for leading blanks) and returns without output if there is none; when the last cell cannot be cleared with a blank it writes the range of differing cells and copies it into oldLine before returning; otherwise it compares the last non-blank cells and chooses between clearing to end of line, rewriting a range, inserting characters (InsStr) or deleting characters (DelChar), using the cost estimates. After the chain of cases (including the attribute-change and magic-cookie cases) it copies newLine[firstChar..] into oldLine, so oldLine matches newLine afterwards in those branches too.

functions.name: _nc_is_charable
functions.prose_contract: Reports whether the wide character ch is a single-byte character in the current locale whose byte value equals the code point. With wctob available it returns wctob((wint_t) ch) == (int) ch, which is true only when wctob maps ch to the same value (for example ASCII, or Latin-1 in a Latin-1 locale) and false when ch is not a single byte (wctob returns EOF) or maps to a different byte value; without wctob it returns _nc_to_char(ch) >= 0, i.e. whenever ch converts to some single byte. It has no side effects beyond the locale's conversion state.

functions.name: _nc_to_char
functions.prose_contract: Converts the wide character ch to a single byte of the current locale and returns it as an int in 0..255, or a negative value when it is not representable as one byte. With wctob it returns wctob(ch) (EOF, normally -1, when ch has no single-byte form). Without wctob it calls wctomb into a local buffer and returns the unsigned first byte if exactly one byte was produced, else -1. No other state changes except the multibyte conversion state.

functions.name: NCURSES_SP_NAME(term_attrs)
functions.prose_contract: Returns the highlight attributes supported by the terminal as a wide attr_t mask. If the screen pointer is NULL it returns 0. Otherwise it starts from termattrs() for that screen and, in wide-character builds where the terminfo has the horizontal-highlight capabilities, ORs in WA_HORIZONTAL, WA_LEFT, WA_LOW, WA_RIGHT, WA_TOP and WA_VERTICAL for each corresponding enter_*_hl_mode capability that is set. The public term_attrs() (SP builds) calls this with CURRENT_SCREEN. Reads terminal capabilities only.

functions.name: show_entry
functions.prose_contract: Writes the accumulated terminfo/termcap entry text outbuf to stdout and returns the number of characters in outbuf.used afterwards. If outbuf.used != 0 it trims the end first: scanning backwards from the last character (index > 0), a newline is skipped without trimming, a whitespace character truncates the buffer to that index (removing it), in termcap mode a backslash also truncates to that index, and a delimiter (',' for terminfo, ':' for termcap) not preceded by a backslash sets the length to just after it; any other character stops the scan. The scan continues after the delimiter case, so whitespace before a delimiter can be removed together with the delimiter. It then NUL-terminates at outbuf.used (outbuf.text is dereferenced, so it must be non-NULL when used != 0). Finally, if outbuf.text is non-NULL it prints it followed by a newline. A trailing newline preceded by a non-space character is not removed.

functions.name: decode_tabs
functions.prose_contract: Parses a tab-stop specification such as "1,10,16,36,72" or "+8" into a newly allocated int array terminated by 0, or returns NULL. It allocates strlen(tab_list) + max_cols ints (failed() on allocation failure) and treats a negative margin as 0. For each character: a digit accumulates a value (limited to max_cols); ',' stores value + prior + margin as the next stop, and if this stop is not greater than the previous stop it prints 'tab-stops are not in increasing order', frees the array and returns NULL; '+' sets prior to the previous stop (if there is one) so the next number is relative; other characters are ignored. After the loop, if there was only a single number (no comma) it is treated as a step: stops 1+margin, 1+margin+step, ... are generated for up to max_cols - 1 entries. Finally the last value (value + prior + margin) is appended and a 0 terminator is stored; this final value is not checked against the previous stop's order. Stops generated or appended are not clamped to max_cols beyond the per-number limit on the digits.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Entry point of the tabs utility. It takes the terminal name from -T or $TERM (default "ansi+tabs") and parses options: predefined tab lists (-a, -a2, -c, -c2, -c3, -f, -p, -s, -u), -d (debug), -n (no operation), -V (print version and exit successfully), a numeric list, +mN margin and further tab-list words (collected with add_to_tab_list); an unknown option calls usage(). It saves the tty settings, calls setupterm, sets max_cols from the terminal width (80 if none) minus the margin, and then: if the terminal has no clear_all_tabs it prints 'cannot reset tabs'; else if it has no set_tab it prints 'cannot set tabs'; else if the list is legal it defaults to "8" when no list was given and, unless -n was given, switches off OCRNL when stdout is a tty (changing the tty settings), and clears the old tabs; it sets the margin when requested, decodes the list with decode_tabs, and if the list decoded it sets the tab stops with do_tabs unless -n was given and prints a ruler and tab list when -d was given; with -n it does not clear or set tabs and does not change or restore the tty settings; it restores the tty if it changed it, and exits with EXIT_SUCCESS in that branch (even when decode_tabs returned NULL and only an error message was printed). In the 'cannot reset/set tabs' or illegal-list cases the exit status is EXIT_FAILURE.

functions.name: unconfigure_cgd
functions.prose_contract: Test helper in t_cgd_aes.c: unconfigures the cgd (cryptographic disk) device open on descriptor fd by calling rump_sys_ioctl(fd, CGDIOCCLR, &ci) and returning its result (0 on success, -1 with errno set on failure). The ioctl argument ci is an uninitialised local struct cgd_ioctl, which the code passes without setting any field. fd must be an open cgd device descriptor.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(ymdhms_to_secs, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body (function ymdhms_to_secs_body) for clock_ymdhms_to_secs. For every entry in the clock_tests table it calls clock_ymdhms_to_secs on the entry's broken-down time and checks with ATF_CHECK_EQ_MSG (a non-fatal check that records a failure and continues) that the result equals the entry's expected seconds value, printing both values on mismatch. It returns nothing and modifies no global state.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(secs_to_ymdhms, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body (function secs_to_ymdhms_body) for clock_secs_to_ymdhms. For every entry in the clock_tests table it converts the entry's seconds value into a struct clock_ymdhms and checks, with non-fatal ATF_CHECK_EQ_MSG, that year, mon, day, wday, hour, min and sec each equal the entry's expected fields. Returns nothing.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(getdents, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body for reading the kernfs root directory. It calls mountkernfs() (rump_init, mkdir /kern, mount kernfs; any failure fails the test), opens /kern read-only and calls getdents into an 8192-byte buffer, failing the test on an error from either call. It then requires (ATF_REQUIRE_STREQ, fatal) that the first three directory entries are named ".", ".." and "boottime" in that order. The directory descriptor is not closed.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(hostname, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body checking that /kern/hostname reflects and changes the system hostname. It mounts kernfs and opens /kern/hostname read-write; it reads the file (failing the test on error), cuts it at the first newline, and requires it to equal the hostname obtained through sysctl(KERN_HOSTNAME). It then writes "turboton roos-berg" at offset 0 with pwrite (failing unless all bytes are written) and requires the sysctl hostname to equal that string. The read buffer is not NUL-terminated after the read, so the first-newline search relies on the file content ending with a newline; the descriptor is not closed.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(utypefit, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body (function utypefit_body) that checks the __type_fit macro for unsigned types with fatal ATF_REQUIRE checks. For unsigned char, short, int and long long it requires __type_fit to be 0 for -1, 1 for 1, 1 for the values up to the type's maximum (0x7f, 0x80, 0xff for char, 0x7fff-0xffff for short, 0x7fffffff-0xffffffff for int, 0x7fff...-0xffff... for long long) and 0 for a value that needs more bits: 0x1ff for char, 0x1ffff for short, 0x1ffffffffLL for int (not the maximum plus one); there is no overflow case for unsigned long long. Returns nothing; a failed check ends the test.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(bits_49, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body for 49-bit bitstrings: it calls one_check(tc, 49), which opens a file named "out" for writing (ATF_REQUIRE that fopen succeeds), runs calculate_data(out, 49) to write the results of the bit_set, bit_clear, bit_test, bit_nset and bit_nclear operations on a 49-bit bitstring, closes it, and runs `diff -u <srcdir>/d_bitstring_49.out out` through system(); if diff does not exit with success the test fails with 'Test failed; see output for details'. It leaves the file "out" in the working directory and depends on the reference file in the srcdir config variable.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(bits_64, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body for 64-bit bitstrings: it calls one_check(tc, 64), which opens a file named "out" for writing (ATF_REQUIRE that fopen succeeds), runs calculate_data(out, 64) to write the results of the bit_set, bit_clear, bit_test, bit_nset and bit_nclear operations on a 64-bit bitstring, closes it, and runs `diff -u <srcdir>/d_bitstring_64.out out` through system(); if diff does not exit with success the test fails with 'Test failed; see output for details'. It leaves the file "out" in the working directory and depends on the reference file in the srcdir config variable.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(bits_67, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body for 67-bit bitstrings: it calls one_check(tc, 67), which opens a file named "out" for writing (ATF_REQUIRE that fopen succeeds), runs calculate_data(out, 67) to write the results of the bit_set, bit_clear, bit_test, bit_nset and bit_nclear operations on a 67-bit bitstring, closes it, and runs `diff -u <srcdir>/d_bitstring_67.out out` through system(); if diff does not exit with success the test fails with 'Test failed; see output for details'. It leaves the file "out" in the working directory and depends on the reference file in the srcdir config variable.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(int8, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body (function int8_body). It runs one non-fatal check, ATF_CHECK(INT8_MIN < UINT8_MAX), which compares the constants -128 and 255 and passes in normal C integer arithmetic. It reads no state and changes nothing; a failed check would only be recorded and the test would continue.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(int16, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body (function int16_body). It runs one non-fatal check, ATF_CHECK(INT16_MIN < UINT16_MAX), comparing the constants -32768 and 65535; it passes in normal C integer arithmetic. No state is read or changed.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(check_sdp_put_str, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body (function check_sdp_put_str_body) for sdp_put_str. It sets up a 512-byte buffer and an sdp_data_t (next at the start, end at the end), then with ATF_REQUIRE (fatal on failure) puts four strings: "Hello World!" with length 5, "Hello\0World" with length 11, "Hello World!" with length -1 and "Hello\0World" with length -1 (the last two use the C string length). It then sets end = next and next = buf and requires the encoded length to equal the expected array (str8 headers 0x25 with lengths 5, 11, 12 and 5 followed by the data bytes); finally it compares the bytes with ATF_CHECK(memcmp(...) == 0), which is non-fatal, so a byte mismatch is recorded but the test continues; a length mismatch is fatal.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(check_sdp_put_url, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body (function check_sdp_put_url_body) for sdp_put_url. With a 512-byte buffer and an sdp_data_t over it it requires (fatal) that sdp_put_url succeeds for "http://www.netbsd.org/" with length 21 (dropping the trailing slash) and with length -1 (the whole string). It then sets end = next and next = buf, requires the encoded size to equal the expected array (url8 header 0x45 with lengths 0x15 and 0x16 plus the characters), and compares the bytes with ATF_CHECK(memcmp(...) == 0), which only records a failure.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(libbpfjit_ldx_imm1, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Each of these ATF bodies builds a static BPF program, checks it with bpf_validate (ATF_CHECK, non-fatal), compiles it with bpfjit_generate_code (ATF_REQUIRE that the result is not NULL), runs it through the jitcall helper (which fills a bpf_args_t with the packet, wirelen and buflen and calls the compiled function with a NULL context) and frees the code with bpfjit_free_code. Program: X = UINT32_MAX - 5 (BPF_LDX+BPF_W+BPF_IMM), A += X, return A. Since A starts at 0 the check is jitcall(code, pkt, 1, 1) == UINT32_MAX - 5; the one-byte packet is not read.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(libbpfjit_ldx_imm2, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Each of these ATF bodies builds a static BPF program, checks it with bpf_validate (ATF_CHECK, non-fatal), compiles it with bpfjit_generate_code (ATF_REQUIRE that the result is not NULL), runs it through the jitcall helper (which fills a bpf_args_t with the packet, wirelen and buflen and calls the compiled function with a NULL context) and frees the code with bpfjit_free_code. Program: X = 5, A = 5, if A == X skip the next instruction, return 7, return UINT32_MAX. The check is jitcall(code, pkt, 1, 1) == UINT32_MAX (the equal case skips the 'return 7').

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(libbpfjit_ldx_len1, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Each of these ATF bodies builds a static BPF program, checks it with bpf_validate (ATF_CHECK, non-fatal), compiles it with bpfjit_generate_code (ATF_REQUIRE that the result is not NULL), runs it through the jitcall helper (which fills a bpf_args_t with the packet, wirelen and buflen and calls the compiled function with a NULL context) and frees the code with bpfjit_free_code. Program: X = packet length (BPF_LEN), A += X, return A. For i = 1..4 it checks jitcall(code, pkt, i, 1) == i and jitcall(code, pkt, i + 1, i) == i + 1, i.e. the result equals the wirelen argument, independent of buflen; the packet bytes are not read.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(libbpfjit_ldx_len2, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Each of these ATF bodies builds a static BPF program, checks it with bpf_validate (ATF_CHECK, non-fatal), compiles it with bpfjit_generate_code (ATF_REQUIRE that the result is not NULL), runs it through the jitcall helper (which fills a bpf_args_t with the packet, wirelen and buflen and calls the compiled function with a NULL context) and frees the code with bpfjit_free_code. Program: X = packet length, A = 5, if A == X skip the next instruction, return 7, return UINT32_MAX. Checks jitcall(code, pkt, 5, 1) == UINT32_MAX (wirelen 5 equals A) and jitcall(code, pkt, 6, 5) == 7 (wirelen 6 differs).

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(libbpfjit_ldx_msh, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Each of these ATF bodies builds a static BPF program, checks it with bpf_validate (ATF_CHECK, non-fatal), compiles it with bpfjit_generate_code (ATF_REQUIRE that the result is not NULL), runs it through the jitcall helper (which fills a bpf_args_t with the packet, wirelen and buflen and calls the compiled function with a NULL context) and frees the code with bpfjit_free_code. Program: X = 4 * (pkt[1] & 0xf) (BPF_LDX+BPF_B+BPF_MSH with offset 1), A += X, return A. With pkt = {0, 0x7a} the check is jitcall(code, pkt, 2, 2) == 40 (0x7a & 0xf = 10, times 4).

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(libbpfjit_misc_tax, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Each of these ATF bodies builds a static BPF program, checks it with bpf_validate (ATF_CHECK, non-fatal), compiles it with bpfjit_generate_code (ATF_REQUIRE that the result is not NULL), runs it through the jitcall helper (which fills a bpf_args_t with the packet, wirelen and buflen and calls the compiled function with a NULL context) and frees the code with bpfjit_free_code. Program: A = 3, X = A (BPF_MISC+BPF_TAX), A = byte at pkt[X + 2], return A. With pkt = {0, 11, 22, 33, 44, 55} the check is jitcall(code, pkt, 6, 6) == 55 (pkt[5]).

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(libbpfjit_misc_txa, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Each of these ATF bodies builds a static BPF program, checks it with bpf_validate (ATF_CHECK, non-fatal), compiles it with bpfjit_generate_code (ATF_REQUIRE that the result is not NULL), runs it through the jitcall helper (which fills a bpf_args_t with the packet, wirelen and buflen and calls the compiled function with a NULL context) and frees the code with bpfjit_free_code. Program: X = 391, A = X (BPF_MISC+BPF_TXA), return A. The check is jitcall(code, pkt, 1, 1) == 391; the one-byte packet is not read.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(libbpfjit_st1, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Each of these ATF bodies builds a static BPF program, checks it with bpf_validate (ATF_CHECK, non-fatal), compiles it with bpfjit_generate_code (ATF_REQUIRE that the result is not NULL), runs it through the jitcall helper (which fills a bpf_args_t with the packet, wirelen and buflen and calls the compiled function with a NULL context) and frees the code with bpfjit_free_code. Program: A = packet length, store A in scratch M[0] (BPF_ST), A += 1, A = M[0] (BPF_LD+BPF_MEM), return A. For i = 1..16 with a 16-byte packet it checks jitcall(code, pkt, i, 16) == i, i.e. the stored length is returned, not length + 1.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(fexecve, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body for fexecve (function ATF_TC_BODY_fexecve). It forks (ATF_REQUIRE). The child opens /usr/bin/touch read-only (exiting with EXIT_FAILURE through err() if that fails) and calls fexecve(fd, {"touch","test"}, empty environment); if fexecve returns -1 the child closes fd and exits with status 76 when errno is ENOSYS, otherwise EXIT_FAILURE. The parent waits (ATF_REQUIRE the wait succeeds), fails the test if the child did not exit normally, and if the status is 76 calls atf_tc_expect_fail("fexecve not implemented"); otherwise it requires the exit status to be EXIT_SUCCESS. In all non-failed paths it then requires access("test", F_OK) == 0, i.e. that the touched file "test" exists in the current directory. With status 76 that last requirement is normally expected to fail, but if a file named "test" already exists it passes and the expected failure becomes an unexpected pass. The test also depends on /usr/bin/touch being executable and openable.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(floatunditf, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body checking uint64 to long double conversion. Without __HAVE_LONG_DOUBLE it calls atf_tc_skip and the loop is not built. On FreeBSD/i386 it first declares an expected failure (atf_tc_expect_fail). Otherwise, for each of the table's entries (a 64-bit unsigned value and the exactly expected long double) it uses ATF_CHECK_MSG (non-fatal) that (long double)u64 == the expected value, printing the index and both values with %.20Lf on mismatch. It returns nothing.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(fpsetmask_basic, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body for fpsetmask/fpgetmask. After FPU_PREREQ() it reads the current mask msk = fpgetmask(). For each of FP_X_INV, FP_X_DZ, FP_X_OFL and FP_X_UFL it sets the mask to msk | bit and checks with ATF_CHECK (non-fatal) that fpgetmask() has the bit set, then sets the mask to msk & ~bit and checks the bit is clear. The last step leaves the mask as msk & ~FP_X_UFL, so the original mask is not restored (an FP_X_UFL bit that was set originally ends up cleared). Failed checks are recorded and the test continues.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(sethostname_basic, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body for sethostname/gethostname; its first statement is atf_tc_skip("screws up the test host's hostname on FreeBSD"), which ends the test as skipped, so the rest is not reached in this file. The code after it would, for each of four hostnames in the hosts table (MAXHOSTNAMELEN-sized arrays), clear a name buffer, set the hostname (on FreeBSD with length sizeof - 1 after size sanity checks, elsewhere with the full array size), read it back with gethostname and require equality with strcmp, and finally restore the saved hostname. The test requires root.

functions.name: ATF_TC_CLEANUP(sethostname_basic, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF cleanup routine: restores the hostname saved at test-program start by calling sethostname(host, sizeof(host)); the result is cast away and ignored. `host` is the static buffer filled by gethostname when the tests are registered.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(sethostname_limit, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body checking that a too long hostname is rejected. It zero-fills a buffer of MAXHOSTNAMELEN + 1 bytes and requires (fatal) that sethostname(name, sizeof(name)) returns -1. Runs as root (require.user = root).

functions.name: ATF_TC_CLEANUP(sethostname_limit, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF cleanup routine. On FreeBSD it first requires (ATF_REQUIRE) that sethostname(host, MAXHOSTNAMELEN - 1) returns 0 and sethostname(host, MAXHOSTNAMELEN) returns -1; on every platform it then restores the saved hostname with sethostname(host, sizeof(host)), ignoring that result. So on FreeBSD the cleanup can itself fail a requirement.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(sethostname_perm, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body checking that an unprivileged user cannot set the hostname (require.user = unprivileged). It sets errno = 0 and requires (ATF_REQUIRE_ERRNO) that sethostname(host, sizeof(host)) returns -1 with errno EPERM.

functions.name: ATF_TC_CLEANUP(sethostname_perm, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF cleanup routine: calls sethostname(host, sizeof(host)) to restore the saved hostname and ignores the result.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(mbrtowc_internal, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body that runs h_ctype2(t, false) for each entry of the tests table (C, en_US.UTF-8, ja_JP.ISO2022-JP2, ja_JP.SJIS, ja_JP.eucJP) until an entry with data == NULL. h_ctype2 sets the locale (fatal on NetBSD if missing; on other systems it prints 'Locale not found' and returns, skipping that entry), then for chunk sizes n = 9 down to 1 decodes the entry's data with mbrtowc using the internal state (stp = NULL), requires an initial state, checks each wide character and byte width against the table (atf_tc_fail on mismatch or an invalid sequence), requires the terminating character 0 and the expected length, and finally checks mbsrtowcs over the whole string. Returns nothing.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(mbrtowc_object, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body identical to mbrtowc_internal except that it calls h_ctype2(t, true), so the mbrtowc and mbsrtowcs calls use an explicit, zero-initialised mbstate_t object instead of the internal state; it iterates over every table entry until data == NULL and fails through the helper's checks.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(wctomb, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body that runs h_wctomb(t, TC_WCTOMB) for each entry of the tests table until data == NULL. h_wctomb sets the locale (fatal on NetBSD if missing; on other systems it prints 'Locale not found' and returns without testing that entry), converts the entry's data to wide characters with mbsrtowcs (requiring the expected count and a terminating 0), and then for each of the wclen + 1 characters calls wctomb(cs, wcs[i]) and compares the returned byte count with the expected mblen[i], calling atf_tc_fail at the first mismatch. It first prints a heading.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(wcrtomb_state, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body that runs h_wctomb(t, TC_WCRTOMB_ST) for each entry of the tests table until data == NULL. h_wctomb sets the locale (fatal on NetBSD if missing; on other systems it prints 'Locale not found' and returns without testing that entry), converts the entry's data to wide characters with mbsrtowcs (requiring the expected count and a terminating 0), and then for each of the wclen + 1 characters calls wcrtomb(cs, wcs[i], &st) with a zero-initialised mbstate_t object and compares the returned byte count with the expected mblen[i], calling atf_tc_fail at the first mismatch. It first prints a heading.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(wcrtomb, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body that runs h_wctomb(t, TC_WCRTOMB) for each entry of the tests table until data == NULL. h_wctomb sets the locale (fatal on NetBSD if missing; on other systems it prints 'Locale not found' and returns without testing that entry), converts the entry's data to wide characters with mbsrtowcs (requiring the expected count and a terminating 0), and then for each of the wclen + 1 characters calls wcrtomb(cs, wcs[i], NULL), i.e. with the internal state and compares the returned byte count with the expected mblen[i], calling atf_tc_fail at the first mismatch. It first prints a heading.

functions.name: efind
functions.prose_contract: Static helper in the regex test driver: converts a regerror error name (the part after "REG_") to its numeric code. It formats "REG_<name>" into a static 100-byte buffer with sprintf (the length assertion comes after the write, so an over-long name overflows before it is checked), sets re.re_endp to that buffer, calls regerror(REG_ATOI, &re, efbuf, sizeof(efbuf)), which writes the decimal code of the named error into efbuf, and returns atoi(efbuf). What it returns for an unknown name depends on regerror, which was not read.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(test04, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body for fmemopen in append modes. For each mode in "a", "ab", "a+", "ab+", "a+b" it fills a BUFSIZ buffer with the byte 0x01, opens it with fmemopen(buf, sizeof(buf), mode) and checks (ATF_CHECK, non-fatal; an assert when the standalone macros are used) that the stream is non-NULL and that buf[0] is still 0x01 (append mode does not truncate); on non-glibc systems it also checks that ftello(fp) equals sizeof(buf) (position at the end, because the buffer holds no NUL) and that after fseeko(fp, 0, SEEK_END) the position is again sizeof(buf); then it checks fclose(fp) == 0.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(clearenv_basic, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body for a user clearing the environment directly. It sets 1024 variables crap0..crap1023 with setenv (each ATF_CHECK that the call does not return -1), then sets *environ = NULL (so the environment becomes empty without using clearenv), sets crap0 again, and checks that getenv("crap0") is "0" and that getenv("crap1") and getenv("crap2") are NULL. Checks are non-fatal.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(getenv_basic, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body for setenv/getenv/unsetenv. It sets EVIL to "very=bad" (ATF_CHECK success), checks getenv("EVIL") equals "very=bad", checks that getenv("EVIL=very") is NULL, and unsets EVIL, checking the call succeeds. Checks are non-fatal.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(putenv_basic, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body for putenv.
