It builds "crap=true" in a local array and calls putenv on it, checks getenv("crap") is "true", then changes string[1] to 'l' and checks getenv("clap") is "true" and getenv("crap") is NULL (the environment entry aliases the caller's array), restores string[1] to 'r', unsets crap and checks it is gone. It then checks that putenv(NULL), putenv("val") and putenv("=val") return -1 with errno EINVAL (ATF_CHECK_ERRNO). Checks are non-fatal.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(setenv_basic, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body (timeout 600 s) for setenv/getenv/unsetenv at scale. It picks a random offset and sets 8192 variables var0..var8191 in a permuted order to random values with overwrite 1, checks that setenv(name, "foo", 0) does not overwrite (getenv still returns the random value); then in another permuted order it unsets each variable, checks getenv returns NULL and that unsetting again succeeds. It then checks that setenv with a NULL name, an empty name and a name containing '=' return -1 with errno EINVAL; on FreeBSD it expects a SIGSEGV for the next check (setenv("var", NULL, 1) is not validated there); it checks setenv("var", NULL, 1) returns -1 with EINVAL, and that setenv("var", "=val", 1) returns 0 and getenv("var") is "=val". Checks are non-fatal.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(setenv_mixed, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body mixing setenv, putenv and unsetenv on one variable, mixedcrap. It copies "mixedcrap=putenv" into a local array; sets mixedcrap=setenv and checks getenv returns "setenv", calls putenv(string) and checks it returns "putenv", unsets it and checks it is NULL; then repeats in the other order (putenv, then setenv, then unsetenv) with the same checks. All checks are non-fatal.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(strtod_underflow, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body checking underflow detection in strtod. It parses a decimal string of the form 0.000...0002 with several hundred zeros after the point (a value far below the smallest double), after setting errno = 0, and calls atf_tc_fail (fatal) unless the result is exactly 0 and errno equals ERANGE.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(strtod_gherman_bug, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body for a strtod rounding bug reported by Geza Herman. It sets errno = 0, parses the string "1.8254370818746402660437411213933955878019332885742187" and checks with ATF_CHECK (non-fatal) that the result equals the hexadecimal double constant 0x1.d34fd8378ea83p+0 exactly.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(strtoi_signed, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body for signed parsing in strtoi(3), table-driven. For each entry of the table of fourteen cases (strings such as " -3", "--1", "+-2", "-1 3", "-1.3", "+33.", "30x0") it sets errno = 0, calls strtoi(str, &end, base 0, INTMAX_MIN, INTMAX_MAX, &e), calls atf_tc_fail if errno changed (note that the message prints e rather than errno), and calls check(), which uses atf_tc_fail_nonfatal to compare the returned value, the status code e (0, ECANCELED for a bad sign sequence, ENOTSUP for trailing garbage) and the end pointer with the table's expectations. Returns nothing.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(memccpy_simple, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body for memccpy. It fills a 100-byte buffer with ' ' and then checks (ATF_CHECK, non-fatal): memccpy(buf, "foo bar", ' ', 100) returns non-NULL (stops after copying the first blank, index 3) and buf[4] is still ' ' (the fill); memccpy(buf, "foo bar", '\0', 99) returns non-NULL (stops after the terminating NUL) and buf[8] is still ' '; memccpy(buf, "foo bar", 'x', 7) returns NULL (no 'x' in 7 bytes) and the first 7 bytes of buf equal "foo bar"; memccpy(buf, "xxxxxxx", 'r', 7) returns NULL (no 'r') and the first 7 bytes of buf now equal "xxxxxxx", i.e. buf is overwritten by the copy.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(fchroot_perm, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body (compiled only where the fchroot tests are enabled, i.e. NetBSD; requires root) checking that an unprivileged user cannot fchroot. It gets the current directory with getcwd (ATF_REQUIRE), looks up user "nobody" with getpwnam, opens the directory read-only (ATF_REQUIRE fd >= 0 and pw != NULL) and forks (ATF_REQUIRE). The child calls setuid(nobody) (result ignored), sets errno = 0 and calls fchroot(fd): it exits with EXIT_FAILURE if the call succeeded or if errno is not EPERM, and with EXIT_SUCCESS otherwise. The parent waits (result ignored) and calls atf_tc_fail unless the child exited normally with EXIT_SUCCESS. The descriptor is not closed. If setuid failed the child would still run with the original (root) credentials.

functions.name: INVALID_UCONTEXT(amd64, pc_too_high, "instruction pointer outside userland address space")
functions.prose_contract: Helper generated by the INVALID_UCONTEXT macro for amd64: static void amd64_pc_too_high(ucontext_t *uc) sets the saved instruction pointer uc->uc_mcontext.__gregs[_REG_RIP] to VM_MAXUSER_ADDRESS, the first address above the user address space, and returns nothing. It is called by the generated test lwp_create_amd64_fail_pc_too_high, which does getcontext, sets uc_flags = _UC_CPU, applies the helper, and requires (fatal) that _lwp_create(&uc, 0, &lid) returns non-zero with errno EINVAL. Only compiled for __amd64__.

functions.name: ATF_TC_CLEANUP(mkfifo_stat, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF cleanup routine for the mkfifo_stat test: calls unlink(path) on the relative path "fifo" and casts the result to void, so any error (for example the file not existing because the test already removed it, or a permission error) is ignored. Afterwards the path is gone only if it existed and unlink succeeded.

functions.name: ATF_TC_CLEANUP(mlock_err, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF cleanup routine for mlock_err, compiled only on FreeBSD (inside #ifdef __FreeBSD__): it calls restore_vm_max_wired(), which is declared at the top of the file and defined elsewhere (not read), to undo the set_vm_max_wired(INT_MAX) done by the test body. It has no return value. On other systems the test has no cleanup routine.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(mmap_truncate, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body checking that ftruncate works while a file is mapped. It opens (creating if needed, mode 0700) the file named by the static `path`; if the open fails the body returns silently without failing. Otherwise it requires (fatal) ftruncate(fd, page) == 0, maps one page of the file read-write and private (requiring MAP_FAILED not returned), writes 'x' to each byte of the page, then requires six more ftruncate calls, with sizes 0, page/8, page/4, page/2, page/12 and page/64, to succeed (seven ftruncate calls in total), unmaps (result ignored) and requires close(fd) == 0. The cleanup routine unlinks the file.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(msgrcv_nonblock, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body for msgrcv with IPC_NOWAIT (timeout 10 s). It creates a System V message queue with key 1234 (IPC_CREAT, mode 0600; ATF_REQUIRE id != -1), sends 10 identical messages of type 0x41 with IPC_NOWAIT (each ATF_REQUIRE success), and forks. The child receives 10 messages of that type with IPC_NOWAIT and _exit(EXIT_FAILURE) as soon as a msgrcv returns -1, else _exit(EXIT_SUCCESS). The parent waits (result ignored) and calls atf_tc_fail if the child was killed by a signal (or WTERMSIG equals SIGKILL), meaning msgrcv blocked, and calls atf_tc_fail 'msgrcv(2) failed' only if WIFEXITED(sta) == 0 and WEXITSTATUS(sta) != EXIT_SUCCESS; since that condition requires the child not to have exited normally, a child that exited normally with EXIT_FAILURE does not fail the test. Finally it requires msgctl(id, IPC_RMID, 0) == 0. The cleanup routine removes the queue if it exists.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(wait3_options, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body that loops over option combinations produced by get_options4 (it stops when that helper returns -1), printing each value, and for each requires (ATF_REQUIRE_ERRNO, fatal) that wait3(NULL, o | TWAIT_OPTION, NULL) returns -1 with errno ECHILD, because the process has no children. TWAIT_OPTION (0 or WNOHANG, set by the file that includes this one) is OR-ed into the options. Returns nothing.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(wait4_options, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body that loops over option combinations produced by get_options4 (it stops when that helper returns -1), printing each value, and for each requires (ATF_REQUIRE_ERRNO, fatal) that wait4(WAIT_ANY, NULL, o | TWAIT_OPTION, NULL) returns -1 with errno ECHILD, because the process has no children. TWAIT_OPTION (0 or WNOHANG, set by the file that includes this one) is OR-ed into the options. Returns nothing.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(wait6_options, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body that loops over option combinations produced by get_options6 (it stops when that helper returns -1), printing each value, and for each requires (ATF_REQUIRE_ERRNO, fatal) that wait6(P_ALL, 0, NULL, o | TWAIT_OPTION, NULL, NULL) returns -1 with errno ECHILD, because the process has no children. TWAIT_OPTION (0 or WNOHANG, set by the file that includes this one) is OR-ed into the options. Returns nothing.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(waitid_options, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body that loops over option combinations produced by get_options6 (it stops when that helper returns -1), printing each value, and for each requires (ATF_REQUIRE_ERRNO, fatal) that waitid(P_ALL, 0, NULL, o | TWAIT_OPTION) returns -1 with errno ECHILD, because the process has no children. TWAIT_OPTION (0 or WNOHANG, set by the file that includes this one) is OR-ed into the options. Returns nothing.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(waitpid_options, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body that loops over option combinations produced by get_options4 (it stops when that helper returns -1), printing each value, and for each requires (ATF_REQUIRE_ERRNO, fatal) that waitpid(WAIT_ANY, NULL, o | TWAIT_OPTION) returns -1 with errno ECHILD, because the process has no children. TWAIT_OPTION (0 or WNOHANG, set by the file that includes this one) is OR-ed into the options. Returns nothing.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(t_tls_static, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body for thread-local variables in static binaries. If __HAVE_NO___THREAD is defined it calls atf_tc_skip, which does not return, so the rest is not executed. Otherwise it calls testf(NULL) in the main thread and then twice creates a thread running testf and joins it (the pthread_create results are not checked). testf checks (ATF_CHECK_EQ, non-fatal) that the thread-local var1 is 1 and var2 is 0, calls the external helper testf_helper(), and then checks both are -1. Each new thread starts from the initial values, so every run begins with var1 == 1 and var2 == 0.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(asinf_inrange, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body comparing asinf with reference values. For each of the eight table entries (x = -1, -0.9, -0.5, -0.1, 0.1, 0.5, 0.9, 1 with their double results, converted to float) it computes whether |(asinf(x) - y) / y| <= FLT_EPSILON and, if not, calls atf_tc_fail_nonfatal with the values and the error in ulp; the loop continues, so every failing entry is reported, not just the first. On NetBSD, for |x| == 0.5 it first calls atf_tc_expect_fail (known ~2 ulp error); on every platform, after the check for |x| == 0.5, it calls atf_tc_expect_pass(), which resets the expectation. So for the +-0.5 entries these ATF expectation calls are made even when no entry fails, and atf_tc_expect_pass() is also called on non-NetBSD systems.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(asinf_zero_neg, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body checking asinf(-0.0) == -0.0. It computes y = asinf(-0.0f) and calls atf_tc_fail_nonfatal("asinf(-0.0) != -0.0") if fabsf(y) > 0.0 or the sign bit of y is clear, so only a negative zero passes; a NaN result passes the magnitude test but fails only through the sign-bit test if its sign is clear.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(asinf_zero_pos, tc)

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(casinh, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body for casinh special values. For each entry of the table (ten entries when __HAVE_NANF is defined, otherwise the first four) of cases of input real/imaginary and expected real/imaginary parts (including infinities and NaNs) it builds the input and expected complex numbers and uses ATF_COMPLEX_EQUAL, which computes casinh(input) and checks with ATF_CHECK_MSG (non-fatal) that the real and imaginary parts are each crudely equal to the expected ones: equal as doubles (so -0 equals +0) or both NaN (only when __HAVE_NANF is defined). functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(replace, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body for ppath_replace_idx and ppath_replace_key. After checking that no paths or components are extant (non-fatal checks), it creates an empty path p and checks (ATF_CHECK_EQ) that replacing an index or a key on the empty path returns NULL. It then pushes PPATH_MAX_COMPONENTS index components 0.. into p (checking each push returns p), copies p to cp, pops the last component of cp and pushes the key "key" onto it, and replaces the last component of p with index 0 (return value ignored). It checks that p's last component has index 0 and its other components have indices 0..MAX-2, that cp's first MAX-1 components have indices 0..MAX-2, and that cp's last component is the key "key" (this last check uses atf_tc_fail, fatal). Both paths are released and it checks no paths or components remain extant. Failed ppath_create/ppath_push/prop internalize calls use atf_tc_fail (fatal); the value comparisons use ATF_CHECK_EQ/ATF_CHECK_STREQ, which are non-fatal and only record a failure. Creation or component lookup failures call atf_tc_fail.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(copyset_object_twice_success, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body for two back-to-back ppath_copyset_* calls. It internalizes the personnel dictionary d, copies it to od, and calls atf_tc_fail if they differ at the start (fatal). It builds three paths: p = John Doe / u.s. citizen, p2 = John Doe / children / [0], p3 = John Doe. It checks (non-fatal) that ppath_get_bool(d, p) is 0 with value true and ppath_get_string(d, p2) is 0 with "Jane Doe". It calls ppath_copyset_bool(d, &nd, p, false) to create the new dictionary nd and records the John Doe object r from nd; then ppath_copyset_string(d, &nd, p2, "Martha Doe") and checks that nd is the same dictionary pointer (the second call modifies the existing copy) and that the John Doe object is the same pointer r. It checks nd has u.s. citizen false and child 0 "Martha Doe". It then uses atf_tc_fail if the original d differs from od, or nd equals od; applies the same two changes directly to od with ppath_set_bool/ppath_set_string and calls atf_tc_fail if od then differs from nd. Finally it releases the paths and dictionaries and checks nothing is extant. Failed ppath_create/ppath_push/prop internalize calls use atf_tc_fail (fatal); the value comparisons use ATF_CHECK_EQ/ATF_CHECK_STREQ, which are non-fatal and only record a failure.

It checks that ppath_get_bool(nd, p) now returns ENOENT and leaves v true. It calls atf_tc_fail if d differs from od or nd equals od; applies ppath_delete_bool and ppath_delete_string to od and calls atf_tc_fail if od then differs from nd. It releases everything and checks nothing is extant. Failed ppath_create/ppath_push/prop internalize calls use atf_tc_fail (fatal); the value comparisons use ATF_CHECK_EQ/ATF_CHECK_STREQ, which are non-fatal and only record a failure.

functions.name: signal_wait_race_threadfunc
functions.prose_contract: Thread function of the signal_wait_race test (the argument is unused). It locks static_mutex (PTHREAD_REQUIRE, fatal on failure). While the shared count is positive it decrements count, increments total, sets toggle = 0, signals static_cond, and waits on static_cond (releasing static_mutex) until toggle == 1; when the loop ends it unlocks static_mutex and returns NULL. So it returns with the mutex unlocked, and if the loop ran at least once toggle is 1 at return (the wait loop only ends when it is 1), not reset to 0.

functions.name: bar
functions.prose_contract: Thread function of the pthread FPU test (argument unused). It computes d = mul3(mul3(2,3,5), mul3(7,11,13), mul3(17,19,23)) (mul3 yields x*y*z after a sched_yield that must succeed), and requires (fatal) that d == 223092870.0. It then increments the shared recursion_depth under recursion_depth_lock (taking the old value rc). If rc < N_RECURSE (10) it calls recurse(), which creates another thread running bar and sleeps 20 seconds; otherwise it calls atf_tc_pass(), which ends the test and does not return. Only after recurse() returns (after the sleep) does it return NULL; in the pass branch it does not return.

It disables core dumps (setrlimit RLIMIT_CORE to 0, result ignored), creates a thread running an empty function (never joined), blocks SIGUSR1 with pthread_sigmask(SIG_SETMASK), installs the handler for SIGSEGV with SIGUSR2 in sa_mask and no flags, and requires sigsetjmp(env, 1) == 0 (true on the direct call). It then reads the signal mask and requires that SIGSEGV and SIGUSR2 are not members and SIGUSR1 is a member; the checks are fatal.

The library's efun implementation was not read.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(pingsize, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body for test case pingsize, generated by the ATF_TC_BODY(pingsize, tc) macro. It calls fork(), then rump_init() and netcfg_rump_makeshmif("jippikaiee", ifname) in whichever process(es) get that far. switch on the fork result: -1 calls atf_tc_fail_errno("fork failed") (source falls through to case 0 textually, relying on that call not returning); 0 (child) configures 1.1.1.10/255.255.255.0 on the interface, calls pause(), and after pause() returns falls out of the switch into the code below, so a child that is woken would run the parent code too; any other value (parent) just leaves the switch. Code after the switch configures 1.1.1.20/255.255.255.0, then sums doping("1.1.1.10", 1, i) over sizes i = 0..IP_MAXPACKET-60001 step 1, then i = IP_MAXPACKET-60000 step 1000 while i < IP_MAXPACKET-100, then i = IP_MAXPACKET-100 step 10 while i < IP_MAXPACKET (sampled sizes, not every size). It prints "got succ/IP_MAXPACKET" and calls kill(cpid, SIGKILL). Returns nothing; success or failure is only reported through the ATF calls (no explicit check of succ).

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(OOSIOCGIFBRDADDR, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body for test case OOSIOCGIFBRDADDR, generated by the ATF_TC_BODY macro. It zeroes a local struct oifreq, calls rump_init(), then rump_pub_shmif_create("bus", &ifnum); a nonzero return calls atf_tc_fail with the strerror text. It formats the interface name "shmif%d" into ifreq.ifr_name and calls netcfg_rump_if(name, "1.7.64.10", "255.255.0.0"). It then calls atf_tc_expect_fail("PR kern/51610: rump does not include COMPAT_43"), opens an AF_INET SOCK_DGRAM socket and issues ioctl OOSIOCGIFBRDADDR on it, each wrapped in RL (which reports an error if the call fails). It then casts &ifreq.ifr_broadaddr to struct sockaddr_in and requires sin_addr.s_addr == htonl(0x0107ffff) with ATF_REQUIRE_EQ, and finally calls rump_sys_close(fd). Because of atf_tc_expect_fail, a failure from the ioctl or the comparison is recorded by ATF as an expected failure, and the close is not reached if either of those calls aborts the test. No explicit return value.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(at_print, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body for test case at_print, generated by the ATF_TC_BODY macro. With a local buf[ATALK_ADDRSTRLEN]: for each entry of the tst table (2 entries) it calls at_print(buf, sizeof(buf), &tst[i].ia) and uses ATF_REQUIRE_STREQ(buf, tst[i].str) and ATF_REQUIRE_EQ(r, tst[i].len), which end the test on mismatch. It then sets l = 4 and for each entry calls at_print(buf, 4, ...); it checks strncmp(buf, str, 3) == 0 with ATF_CHECK (a failure is recorded but the test continues), requires buf[3] == '\0' only if r > 4 (r > (int)l), and requires r == tst[i].len with ATF_REQUIRE_EQ. Returns nothing.

It then sets l = 8 and for each entry calls in_print(buf, 8, ...), checks strncmp(buf, str, 7) == 0 with ATF_CHECK (a mismatch is recorded but the test continues), then requires buf[7] == '\0' and r == tst[i].len with ATF_REQUIRE_EQ (the return value is compared to the full untruncated length). Returns nothing.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(uvm_physseg_unplug, tc)
functions.prose_contract: ATF test body for test case uvm_physseg_unplug, generated by the ATF_TC_BODY macro. It mallocs a vm_page slab of npages1+npages2+npages3 entries without checking the result, calls setup(), and requires uvm_physseg_plug(atop(0), atop(1MB), NULL) to return true and uvm_physseg_get_entries() to be 1. It calls uvm_physseg_find on the 256KB page and requires the returned pa to equal that page, and requires uvmexp.npages == 0. If VM_PHYSSEG_MAX == 1 it first calls atf_tc_expect_signal(SIGABRT, ...) for the fragmenting unplug. It then requires uvm_physseg_unplug(atop(256KB), atop(512KB)) to return true, requires that find now leaves pa == 0, calls uvm_page_init_fake(slab, n1+n2+n3), and checks uvmexp.npages == atop(512KB) with ATF_CHECK_EQ (non-fatal; this is the only npages check after the initial one). It then requires 2 entries, finds the segment at 256KB+512KB, requires it valid, unplugs (256KB+512KB, 256KB) requiring true, requires that handle to be no longer valid and 1 entry. It then unplugs (128KB, 128KB) and (0, 64KB), each requiring true and 1 entry afterwards. functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Program entry of the nc (netcat) utility, main(int argc, char *argv[]), defined at netcat.c:157; it ends the process through exit() or through err/errx/usage, and its end (line 594) is exit(ret) rather than a return. Local ret starts at 1. It ignores SIGPIPE and parses options with getopt_long; bad option values, unsupported combinations (e.g. -l with -s, -p or -z, -k or --lb without -l, --sctp with -u or -U, --tun without -u, proxy with -u/-l/-U/IPv6/-s) and a failed tun open end the process with errx(1,...), and a missing or wrong number of host/port arguments calls usage(1); option h calls help(), which calls usage(0). Option x does strdup of the proxy string, which is not freed anywhere in main. For unix-domain datagram connect it picks the temporary socket path (-s value or a mktemp name). Listen mode (-l) sets ret = 0, creates the unix socket (or calls local_listen each loop for non-unix), and exits with err(1) on listen, recvfrom, connect or accept errors; it then serves the connection (UDP with -k just readwrite, UDP without -k peeks the peer with recvfrom, connects, readwrite; TCP accepts then readwrite and close), closes s for non-unix, and repeats only if -k is set; otherwise falls to the final cleanup. Unix connect mode (non-listen, -U) sets ret = 0 and calls unix_connect; if it returns a value > 0 and -z is not set it does readwrite and close, otherwise ret = 1; it then unlinks the temporary socket if -u and calls exit(ret) directly, without closing tun_fd. Otherwise (inet connect mode) it builds the port list and for each port closes any previous s if nonzero, connects directly or via socks_connect, skips to the next port if the connect fails (s < 0) without changing ret, sets ret = 0 on a connected port, and with -v or -z (for UDP a failed udptest sets ret = 1 and continues) prints the 'succeeded' message, then does fdpass with -F or readwrite unless -z. After the loop the shared tail closes s if nonzero (so listen mode may close an already closed s) and closes tun_fd if open, then exit(ret): ret is 1 if no port got past the connect check, otherwise the value set by the last port that did (0 or 1 from udptest).

functions.name: jsmn_parse
functions.prose_contract: jsmn_parse(parser, js, len, tokens, num_tokens) scans js from parser->pos while pos < len and js[pos] is not NUL, and returns the count of tokens seen (a jsmnerr_t used as int count) or a negative error. It dispatches per character: '{' and '[' increment count and, only if tokens is non-NULL, allocate a token via jsmn_alloc_token (NULL result returns JSMN_ERROR_NOMEM), bump the parent's size, set type/start and make it the current super token. '}' and ']' do nothing when tokens is NULL; otherwise they search back for the innermost open token (start set, end unset), return JSMN_ERROR_INVAL if its type does not match or (in the non-JSMN_PARENT_LINKS build) if no open token exists, and set its end and the new super token. '"' calls jsmn_parse_string and ':' sets toksuper to the last token. ',' with tokens non-NULL moves toksuper back to the enclosing array or object. Whitespace is skipped. Under JSMN_STRICT, a digit, '-', 't', 'f' or 'n' returns JSMN_ERROR_INVAL if tokens is non-NULL and the current super token is an object or a string that already has size; other unexpected characters return JSMN_ERROR_INVAL; without JSMN_STRICT any other character is treated as a primitive. Strings and primitives each count++ and bump the super token's size if tokens is non-NULL; any negative result from jsmn_parse_string or jsmn_parse_primitive is returned unchanged (their bodies were not read, so which codes they produce is not stated here). After the loop, if tokens is non-NULL and any token has start set but end unset, JSMN_ERROR_PART is returned; otherwise count is returned. On an early error return parser->pos is left at the current character (not advanced) and toknext/toksuper as modified so far; the function takes no locks and does not free anything.

functions.name: ntpcal_leapyears_in_years
functions.prose_contract: ntpcal_leapyears_in_years(years) takes an int32_t number of elapsed years and returns an int32_t count of leap years using the 4/100/400 rule. It takes sf32 = int32_sflag(years) (the sign mask, used to flip all bits for negative input), forms uyear = (uint32_t)years ^ sf32 (so uyear = years for years >= 0 and -years-1 for years < 0), computes sum = uyear/4 - uyear/100 + uyear/400 by chained division, and returns uint32_2cpl_to_int32(sf32 ^ sum). For years >= 0 the result is years/4 - years/100 + years/400. For years < 0 the result is the one's complement of that sum for uyear = -years-1, that is -1 - (u/4 - u/100 + u/400) with u = -years-1 (for example years = -1 gives -1). Pure arithmetic on its argument; no locks, memory or globals are touched.
functions.contract: /*@ requires true; ensures (years >= 0 ==> result == years/4 - years/100 + years/400) && (years < 0 ==> result == -1 - ((-years-1)/4 - (-years-1)/100 + (-years-1)/400)); */

functions.prose_contract: Static function fmtflt(str, len, size, fvalue, width, precision, flags, overflow) at snprintf.c:1091-1378 appends a formatted floating-point conversion to str through OUTCHAR, returning nothing. (The sign and thousands-separator settings are not parameters: sign is derived from fvalue and the PLUS/SPACE flags, and separators from flags & PRINT_F_QUOTE.) A precision of -1 becomes 6. If fvalue is NaN or infinite it builds the sign plus "nan"/"inf" (uppercase with PRINT_F_UP) in iconvert, passes it to fmtstr with the width and flags, and returns. For E and G conversions it computes the decimal exponent; precision is capped at 9, 19 or 38 depending on sizeof(UINTMAX_T). If cast(ufvalue) of the scaled magnitude equals UINTMAX_MAX it sets *overflow = 1 and returns without appending anything. functions.prose_contract: Static input handler gps_input(parseio, ch, tstamp), clk_meinberg.c:593-733, consumes one received byte for the Meinberg GPS framing state machine kept in the msg_buf stored at parseio->parse_pdata. functions.name: Strncmp
functions.prose_contract: Static function Strncmp(s, t, n) in parsestreams.c:173-191 compares up to n characters of two C strings with an int result. It returns 0 immediately if s or t is NULL or s == t. Otherwise it runs while (n-- && !(c = *s++ - *t++) && *s && *t): the loop stops when n reaches 0 (n == 0 compares nothing and returns 0; a negative n is nonzero, so the count never stops the loop), when a character pair differs (then c, the difference of the two chars, is returned, negative if the s character is smaller), or after an equal pair when either next character is NUL; in that last case c is 0, so the function returns 0 for strings where one is a proper prefix of the other (e.g. "ab" against "abc"), and also returns 0 when both strings end together. An empty string against a nonempty one returns the nonzero difference of the first characters. Note that after an equal pair of NUL characters the loop reads *s and *t one byte past the terminators (the post-increment at 187 runs before the *s && *t test), so for two distinct empty strings and n > 0 the strings must have a readable byte after the NUL. No memory is allocated or freed.

functions.prose_contract: crypto_xmit(peer, xpkt, rbufp, start, ep, cookie), ntp_crypto.c:1082-1407, builds one extension field in the transmit packet at byte offset start and returns an int length, not an XEVNT code. functions.name: crypto_recv
functions.prose_contract: crypto_recv(peer, rbufp), ntp_crypto.c:419-1062, walks the extension fields of a received NTP packet and returns an XEVNT_* code (int). If opening fails it deletes the new endpoint and selects wildipv4 or wildipv6 by the family of addr (ep becomes NULL if neither): when found it stores *addr in that wildcard endpoint's bcast and logs an error, otherwise it logs "No multicast socket available" and returns without adding anything to the address list. In either of the two successful cases it then sets one_ep = ep, calls socket_multicast_enable(ep, addr) exactly once on that endpoint (new or wildcard), logs "Joined ..." if it returns nonzero, and finally calls add_addr_to_list(addr, one_ep). In the MULTICAST_NONEWSOCKET build it sets one_ep to wildipv4 (for an IPv4 addr) or else wildipv6, then loops over ep_list, skipping endpoints that are ignored, of a different address family, lack INT_MULTICAST or have INT_LOOPBACK or INT_WILDCARD; for each remaining endpoint it sets one_ep to it, calls socket_multicast_enable(ep, addr) and logs "Joined ..." on nonzero; then calls add_addr_to_list(addr, one_ep), so one_ep is the last eligible endpoint, or the wildcard endpoint if none was eligible. No locks are taken in this function.

functions.name: leapsec_add
functions.prose_contract: Static function leapsec_add(pt, now64, insert), ntp_leapsec.c:930-974, returns a boolean int. It returns FALSE with errno = ERANGE if *now64 is earlier than pt->head.expire (equal to expire passes this test) or if the table is non-empty and *now64 is not later than pt->info[0].ttime (equal is rejected). It converts *now64 to calendar fields and returns FALSE with errno = EINVAL when the day of month is 1 and the hour is 0 (first hour of the first day of a month); that case is handled by the code, not a precondition. Otherwise it sets the calendar to the first day, 00:00:00 of the month containing now64 (starttime) and to the same time one month later via month++ (ttime), builds a leap_info_t with ttime, stime = low 32 bits of ttime - starttime, taiof = (newest entry's taiof if the table has entries, else head.base_tai) + 1 when insert is nonzero or - 1 when it is zero, and dynls = 1, and returns add_range(pt, &li). add_range (read at 725-767) shifts the entries down and inserts the new one at index 0 (dropping the oldest when the table is full), invalidates cached limits through reset_times, and returns TRUE; it does not set errno. No locks.

functions.name: loop_config
functions.prose_contract: loop_config(item, freq), ntp_loopfilter.c:1256-1398, returns void and switches on item. LOOP_DRIFTINIT does nothing when LOCKCLOCK is defined; otherwise, with KERNEL_PLL, it breaks out immediately if mode_ntpdate is set (skipping everything below, including set_freq, rstclock and loop_started), else calls start_kern_loop() first; then it clamps init_drift_comp/1e6 to the range -NTP_MAXFREQ..NTP_MAXFREQ, calls set_freq on it, calls rstclock(EVNT_FSET, 0) if freq_set is nonzero or rstclock(EVNT_NSET, 0) otherwise, and sets loop_started = TRUE. LOOP_KERN_CLEAR does nothing (its body is under #if 0). LOOP_ALLAN stores (u_char)freq in allan_xpt; LOOP_CODEC stores freq/1e6 in clock_codec; LOOP_PHI stores freq/1e6 in clock_phi; LOOP_FREQ stores init_drift_comp = freq and freq_set = 1; LOOP_NOFREQ sets both to 0; LOOP_PANIC stores clock_panic; LOOP_MINSTEP stores max(freq, CLOCK_MINSTEP) in clock_minstep; LOOP_TICK calls set_sys_tick_precision(freq). LOOP_HUFFPUFF raises freq to at least HUFFPUFF, sets sys_hufflen = (int)(freq / HUFFPUFF), allocates sys_huffpuff with eallocarray (the previous array is not freed here), fills it with 1e9 and sets sys_mindly = 1e9. LOOP_MAX sets both clock_max_fwd and clock_max_back to freq; LOOP_MAX_BACK sets clock_max_back and LOOP_MAX_FWD sets clock_max_fwd; in the three cases select_loop(FALSE) is called when freq is 0 or above 0.5 (LOOP_MAX), or, for the two single-direction cases, when either clock_max_back or clock_max_fwd is 0 or above 0.5. LOOP_LEAP and any other value log "loop_config: unsupported option %d" at LOG_NOTICE. No locks are taken.

functions.name: local_clock
functions.prose_contract: local_clock(peer, fp_offset), ntp_loopfilter.c:452-933, applies a new clock offset to the discipline loop and returns an int. It returns 0 after only calling record_loop_stats if ntp_enable is false. It returns -1 (after report_event EVNT_SYSFAULT) when |fp_offset| exceeds clock_panic, clock_panic > 0 and allow_panic is not set; otherwise allow_panic is cleared. In mode_ntpdate it steps (step_systime) when the offset exceeds the forward/backward step threshold, else slews (adj_systime), logs, records stats and calls exit(0), so it does not return. With a huff-n-puff table it adjusts fp_offset by half the delay excess. It then clamps sys_poll to the peer's minpoll..maxpoll, computes mu = current_time - clock_epoch and sets rval = 1. If the offset exceeds clock_max_fwd or clock_max_back (when those are > 0) or force_step_once is set, it switches on state: EVNT_SYNC reports EVNT_SPIK, sets state = EVNT_SPIK and returns 0; EVNT_FREQ returns 0 if mu < clock_minstep, otherwise computes direct_freq and goes on to the SPIK case; EVNT_SPIK returns 0 if mu < clock_minstep, otherwise falls to the default case; the default case (also NSET and FSET) reports EVNT_CLOCKRESET, steps the clock, reinits the timer, sets tc_counter = 0, clock_jitter to the precision, sets rval = 2, and if the state was EVNT_NSET calls rstclock(EVNT_FREQ, 0) and returns 2 at once, otherwise calls rstclock(EVNT_SYNC, 0) and continues. Early returns of 0 happen without calling record_loop_stats. If the offset is inside the step threshold, it updates clock_jitter and by state: EVNT_NSET slews with adj_systime and calls rstclock(EVNT_FREQ, fp_offset); EVNT_FREQ returns 0 if mu < clock_minstep, otherwise computes direct_freq and falls through (as the default path); default (including SYNC and FSET) adjusts clock_frequency (Allan/PLL terms when freq_cnt == 0) and calls rstclock(EVNT_SYNC, fp_offset), resetting freq_cnt if |fp_offset| < CLOCK_FLOOR. Both non-returning paths then, if the kernel loop is enabled and freq_cnt == 0, build an ntp_adjtime request (offset, constant, status, leap flags, PPS flags), call it, and read back clock_offset and clock_frequency, setting loop_tai if changed. Finally it logs if |clock_frequency| exceeds NTP_MAXFREQ, stores drift_comp clamped to +/-NTP_MAXFREQ, updates clock_stability and the tc_counter/sys_poll hysteresis (calling poll_update if sys_poll changed), calls record_loop_stats and returns rval, which is 2 after a step and 1 otherwise.

functions.name: receive
functions.prose_contract: receive(rbufp), ntp_proto.c:626-2553, is the NTP packet input routine; it returns void and most outcomes are early returns. It increments sys_received first (line 686, before any return) and looks up the restriction mask. It then drops the packet, each time with a different counter, as follows: sys_badlength for a bogus port or length, an old-version or invalid-mode or invalid-poll packet, or a bad length at several MAC/extension-length checks; sys_restricted for RES_IGNORE, private (mode 7) packets without ntp_mode7 or with RES_NOQUERY, control packets with RES_NOQUERY, RES_DONTSERVE, RES_FLAKE, RES_DONTTRUST with no MAC, and for several later access-denied cases; sys_limitrejected when RES_LIMITED is set and the rate is exceeded (the code at 957-977 returns in that case, depending on KOD handling); sys_declined in several association-setup cases; sys_badauth in an autokey MAC-length failure and at a later authentication failure. Control and private packets are handed to process_control or process_private and the function returns. sys_newversion or sys_oldversion is incremented for packets passing the version test. A crypto-NAK that is invalid (valid_NAK returns INVALIDNAK) calls report_event, increments peer->badNAK when peer is non-NULL, logs, and returns without incrementing any sys_* counter (lines 1039-1046). A packet without a MAC is not dropped by authentication: it is accepted with is_authentic = AUTH_NONE (and RES_MSSNTP cleared); a valid crypto-NAK gets AUTH_CRYPTO; otherwise the MAC is checked with authdecrypt giving AUTH_OK or AUTH_ERROR. An existing peer whose keyid differs from the packet's key id, or whose MAC fails authentication, is dropped with sys_restricted. The function then dispatches on the association match code (fast_xmit replies for AM_FXMIT, newpeer creation for manycast/broadcast-client/passive cases, several sys_declined or sys_restricted drops, and AM_PROCPKT/AM_ERR handling). For an existing peer it increments peer->received, does the on-wire/timestamp checks (bogus or old packets return after incrementing peer->bogusorg or peer->oldpkt), kiss-o'-death handling, authentication-failure handling (peer->badauth), autokey checks via crypto_recv, and finally calls process_packet(peer, pkt, rbufp->recv_length) and, if the packet tests pass, poll_update and the nextdate adjustment for flipped peers.

functions.name: alloc_res6
functions.prose_contract: Static function alloc_res6(void), ntp_restrict.c:250-273, takes no parameters; the block size is the constants cb = V6_SIZEOF_RESTRICT_U and count = INC_RESLIST6. It first unlinks the head of the global free list resfree6 with UNLINK_HEAD_SLIST; if that yielded an entry it returns it. Otherwise it allocates count entries of cb bytes with eallocarray (the NTP allocator wrapper, not read here), links entries count-1 down to 1 of the new block onto resfree6, and returns the first entry (the block start, which the DEBUG_INSIST at line 270 expects the loop to end on). The returned entry is not on the free list. restrictcount and the restriction list are not touched.

functions.name: check_leapsec
functions.prose_contract: Static function check_leapsec(now, tpiv, reset), ntp_timer.c:550-732, returns void. It first calls leapsec_electric(pll_control && kern_enable) (or leapsec_electric(0) without KERNEL_PLL; not under SYS_WINNT), and sets leap_smear.enabled under LEAP_SMEAR. If reset is nonzero it sets lsprox = LSPROX_NOWARN, calls leapsec_reset_frame and zeroes lsdata; sys_tai is not changed on this path. Otherwise it calls leapsec_query(&lsdata, now, tpiv). If the query reports a full hit (fired) it computes the clock warp: for a negative warp it steps the clock (step_systime) only when clock_max_back > 0 and smaller than the warp magnitude, otherwise only logs a slew message; for a positive warp likewise against clock_max_fwd; it logs the chosen message, calls report_event(EVNT_LEAP), sets lsprox and the global leapsec to LSPROX_NOWARN and sys_tai to lsdata.tai_offs. If not fired it sets lsprox = lsdata.proximity and sys_tai = lsdata.tai_offs (noting a change of sys_tai for autokey). With LEAP_SMEAR it also maintains the smear interval and offset. Then, unless the red-alert guard blocks it ((leapsec > 0 or lsprox < LSPROX_ALERT) and leapsec < lsprox), a rise of the proximity level sets leapsec = lsprox, reporting PEVNT_ARMED with sys_peer when lsdata.dynamic or EVNT_ARMED otherwise, only when the level crosses from below LSPROX_SCHEDULE to at or above it; a fall of the level (leapsec > lsprox) reports EVNT_DISARMED when crossing below LSPROX_SCHEDULE and sets leapsec = lsprox. It then sets leapdif = lsdata.tai_diff when leapsec >= LSPROX_SCHEDULE, else 0, calls check_leap_sec_in_progress(&lsdata) (which recomputes leap_sec_in_progress and calls set_sys_leap(sys_leap) when it changed), and under AUTOKEY calls crypto_update_taichange() if sys_tai changed or the leap fired.

functions.name: simulate_server
functions.prose_contract: int simulate_server(serv_addr, inter, rpkt), ntpsim.c:255-377, is the simulator's server model, called with the client request rpkt. It zeroes a reply packet and receive buffer, scans simulation.servers[0..num_of_servers-1] and takes the first entry whose addr memcmp-equals *serv_addr (so with duplicates the first one wins), prints a "Received packet" line to stderr, and calls abortsim("Server with specified address not found!!!") if none matched; it relies on abortsim (defined outside this file, not read) not returning, since server->curr_script is dereferenced straight after at line 293, and curr_script is never checked for NULL. It builds a stratum-1 reply with refid "GPS", ppoll/precision copied from the request, org = the request's xmt, and delays d1, d3 = poisson(curr_script->prop_delay, curr_script->jitter), d2 = poisson(curr_script->proc_delay, 0); t1 is the request transmit time, t2 = server->server_time + d1, t3 = t2 + d2 (stored as rec and xmt), t4 = t1 + d1 + d2 + d3. It fills a recvbuf (receiver = receive, length LEN_PKT_NOMAC, dstadr = inter, source address copied from *serv_addr), creates a PACKET event at t4 with event(t4, PACKET), copies the buffer into it and enqueues it on event_queue. If curr_script->duration > simulation.sim_time and HEAD_PFIFO(server->script) is NULL it prints "Hello" and unlinks curr_script from the server's script FIFO (no free). It then returns 0; the only way out other than the abortsim path is this return 0.

functions.name: teljjy_conn_send
functions.prose_contract: Static function teljjy_conn_send(peer, pp, up), refclock_jjy.c:3346-3440, sends the next command of the TELJJY command sequence and returns TELJJY_CHANGE_CLOCK_STATE or TELJJY_STAY_CLOCK_STATE. If up->iClockCommandSeq > 0 and teljjy_command_sequence[up->iClockCommandSeq].command is NULL it returns TELJJY_CHANGE_CLOCK_STATE immediately. Otherwise, for sequence 0 with peer->ttl == 100 it sets iClockCommandSeq to TELJJY_COMMAND_START_SKIP_LOOPBACK; for sequence 0 with ttl != 100 it resets iLoopbackCount and clears bLoopbackTimeout[]; for sequence > 0 with ttl != 100, a current entry whose expected reply type is TELJJY_REPLY_LOOPBACK and iLoopbackCount < MAX_LOOPBACK it calls teljjy_setDelay and increments iLoopbackCount. It then increments iClockCommandSeq and reads the new entry's command and length. If that command is NULL it returns TELJJY_CHANGE_CLOCK_STATE (nothing written). Otherwise it write()s the command to pp->io.fd, calling refclock_report(CEVNT_FAULT) if the byte count differs from the length (it still carries on); for a loopback-type command it records the send time in sendTime[iLoopbackCount] and sets bLoopbackMode when iLoopbackCount < MAX_LOOPBACK, else logs a bug message and clears bLoopbackMode; for other commands it clears bLoopbackMode. It writes clockstats, and returns TELJJY_CHANGE_CLOCK_STATE if the entry after the new one has a NULL command, else TELJJY_STAY_CLOCK_STATE.

functions.name: modem_control
functions.prose_contract: Static function modem_control(peer, pp, up), refclock_jjy.c:3969-4005, returns void. It calls the handler pModemHandler[up->iModemEvent][up->iModemState](peer, pp, up) and keeps its result rc. Only if rc == CHANGE_MODEM_STATE does it read iPostEvent = iModemPostEvent[event][state] (using the old event and state), and, only if the next state iModemNextState[event][state] differs from the current state, reset up->iModemSilentCount, up->iModemStateTimer and up->iModemCommandSeq to 0; it then sets up->iModemState to the next-state table entry. If rc is not CHANGE_MODEM_STATE, iPostEvent stays MODEM_EVENT_NULL and neither the state nor the counters change. If iPostEvent is not MODEM_EVENT_NULL (possible only after a state change), it sets up->iModemEvent = iPostEvent and calls modem_control recursively. In every case it ends by setting up->iModemEvent = MODEM_EVENT_NULL (the recursive call does this too before returning). No locks or memory are involved; the table indices are not range checked here.

functions.name: wwv_endpoc
functions.prose_contract: Static function wwv_endpoc(peer, epopos), refclock_wwv.c:1382-1593, is called once per second with the second-comb-filter epoch maximum position and returns void; it keeps its state in function statics (median filter, scount, syncnt, maxrun, zepoch, zcount, avgcnt, avginc and so on) and in the wwvunit. It increments scount, then if up->epomax < STHR or up->eposnr < SSNR it clears the SSYNC and FGATE status bits, sets avgcnt, syncnt and maxrun to 0 and returns. If neither SELV nor SELH is set it returns with nothing else changed (scount was already incremented). Otherwise it pushes epopos through a 3-entry median filter to get tepoch, computes tmp2 = (tepoch - xepoch) % WWV_SEC; when tmp2 is 0 it increments syncnt and, if syncnt > SCMP, MSYNC is set and (FGATE is set or scount - zcount <= up->avgint), it sets SSYNC and up->yepoch = tepoch; when tmp2 is nonzero and syncnt >= maxrun it records the run (maxrun, mcount, mepoch) and clears syncnt. With CLK_FLAG4 and no MSYNC it writes a clockstats line. It increments avgcnt and, if avgcnt < up->avgint, saves xepoch = tepoch and returns (so no frequency or interval adjustment on that call, even though SSYNC and yepoch may already have been set above). At the end of the averaging interval it updates the longest run, sets xepoch, and computes dtemp = (mepoch - zepoch) % WWV_SEC; if FGATE is set and |dtemp| < MAXFREQ*MINAVG it adjusts up->freq (clamped to +/-MAXFREQ) and, when |dtemp| < MAXFREQ*MINAVG/2, moves the avginc ratchet up and doubles up->avgint (if below MAXAVG) after avginc reaches 3; if FGATE is set and |dtemp| is larger, it moves the ratchet down and halves up->avgint (if above MINAVG) after avginc reaches -3, so avgint can be reduced in that case. It then optionally writes clockstats, sets FGATE, saves zepoch = mepoch and zcount = mcount, and resets avgcnt, syncnt and maxrun to 0. When FGATE was not set the freq and avgint adjustment block is skipped.

functions.name: wwvb_receive
functions.prose_contract: Static function wwvb_receive(rbufp), refclock_wwvb.c:247-443, returns void. It reads a line with refclock_gtlin(rbufp, pp->a_lastcode, BMAX, &trtmp). If that returns 0 (empty line) it stores trtmp in up->laststamp only when up->prev_eol_cr was false, toggles up->prev_eol_cr, and returns. Otherwise it sets pp->lencode to the length, pp->lastrec to the old up->laststamp, up->laststamp to trtmp and up->prev_eol_cr to TRUE, and returns if pp->lastrec is zero. It then initialises the sync, quality, leap and dst characters to ' ' and parses a_lastcode by pp->lencode: LENWWVB0 and LENWWVB2 and LENWWVB3 each use a sscanf format (format 0: sync, day, hour, minute, second, dst, tz, 8 fields, nsec = 0; format 2: sync, quality, year, day, h:m:s.msec, leap, 9 fields, nsec = msec * 1e6; format 3: sync, year, month, day, h/m/s, dst, leap, 8 fields, day from ymd2yd, nsec = 0). A short sscanf or any other length goes to the bad-format path: when up->linect > 0 it decrements linect and records the line in clockstats, otherwise it reports CEVNT_BADREPLY, then returns. After a successful parse it sets pp->disp from the quality character (' ' gives .001 and also sets pp->lastref = pp->lastrec; 'A' .01; 'B' .1; 'C' .5; 'D' MAXDISPERSE; any other character gives MAXDISPERSE and reports CEVNT_BADREPLY), and sets pp->leap to LEAP_NOTINSYNC if the sync character is not ' ', else LEAP_ADDSECOND if the leap character is 'L', else LEAP_NOWARNING. Under HAVE_PPSAPI it increments up->tcount and returns if the peer has FLAG_PPS. Otherwise it calls refclock_process_f(pp, pp->fudgetime2) and reports CEVNT_BADTIME if that returns false. Formats 0 and 3 leave the quality character at ' ', so they take the ' ' branch.

functions.name: ntpqmain
functions.prose_contract: ntpqmain(argc, argv), ntpq.c:502-657 (compiled unless BUILD_AS_LIB), is the body of the ntpq program; the wrapper main at ntpq.c:490-497 (built unless NO_MAIN_ALLOWED) just returns ntpqmain(argc, argv), but the code in this slice is ntpqmain itself. It sets the default delay, calls init_lib, ssl_applink and init_auth, falls back to AF_INET as the default family if IPv6 does not work, rewrites the description and comment of the built-in "keytype" command from list_digest_names() (INSISTing that the command is found), and processes the command line with ntpOptionProcess, then sets debug, address family, interactive, numeric/wide display, old_rv and drefid from the options. With no remaining arguments it adds the default host; otherwise every argument is added as a host, except that arguments starting with "-4" or "-6" only set the address family. It turns interactive mode on when there are no command-line commands (defcmds == 0) and both stdin and stderr are terminals. It installs the ctrl-C hook (and push_ctrl_c_handler(abortcmd) when interactive). If command-line commands were given (numcmds > 0) it opens each host with openhost and, for each host that opened, runs each command with docmd (printing blank-line separators), then frees the command strings. If defcmds == 0 it opens the first host (ignoring the result) and runs getcmds() for the interactive loop. It then returns 0; the ntpq-specific functions it calls may exit the process themselves, which was not checked.

functions.name: translate_option_strings
functions.prose_contract: Static function translate_option_strings(void), ntpsnmpd-opts.c:503-539 (compiled only with ENABLE_NLS), takes no parameters; it works on the file-scope ntpsnmpdOptions (taken as a local const pointer opts) and on option_xlateable_txt. If option_xlateable_txt.field_ct is 0 it does nothing (one-shot guard at line 512). Otherwise it first walks the field_ct pointers that follow the field count in option_xlateable_txt and replaces each with AO_gettext(*ppz); then sets field_ct to 0 (which also disables the "libopts" gettext domain lookup inside AO_gettext); then replaces opts->pzCopyright, pzCopyNotice, pzFullVersion, pzUsageTitle, pzExplain and pzDetail, and the pzText of each of the opts->optCt option descriptors, with AO_gettext of the old pointer. AO_gettext returns NULL for NULL, returns the same pointer when no translation exists, and otherwise returns a strdup copy of the translation (nothing frees the old string here, and the function exits the process with NTPSNMPD_EXIT_FAILURE if that strdup fails). It returns void and takes no locks.

functions.name: arc4random_uniform
functions.prose_contract: arc4random_uniform(upper_bound), arc4random.c:512-545 (compiled unless ARC4RANDOM_NOUNIFORM), returns an unsigned int below upper_bound. It returns 0 at once, without calling the generator, if upper_bound < 2. Otherwise it computes min = 2^32 mod upper_bound: when unsigned int is wider than 32 bits (UINT_MAX > 0xffffffffUL) as 0x100000000UL % upper_bound; otherwise, avoiding 64-bit math, as 1 + ~upper_bound for upper_bound > 0x80000000 and ((0xffffffff - upper_bound*2) + 1) % upper_bound for smaller values. It then loops, calling arc4random() until a draw r >= min (the loop has no iteration limit in the code), and returns r % upper_bound. The result is less than upper_bound; it is uniform over that range to the extent that arc4random() is uniform over 32 bits. Each arc4random() call advances the shared generator state (and may reseed), so the function is not free of global-state effects.

functions.name: evbuffer_read
functions.prose_contract: evbuffer_read(buf, fd, howmuch), buffer.c:2283-2412, reads from fd into the evbuffer and returns an int. It takes the buffer lock with EVBUFFER_LOCK (a no-op when the buffer has no lock) and releases it at the done label on every return. It returns -1 immediately if buf->freeze_end is set. Otherwise it asks get_n_bytes_readable_on_socket (FIONREAD, or EVBUFFER_MAX_READ when unavailable), uses EVBUFFER_MAX_READ if that is <= 0 or above the maximum, and sets howmuch to that value if howmuch is negative or larger. It then makes room: with iovecs via evbuffer_expand_fast_ (return -1 on failure) and readv/WSARecv into the chain space, or without iovecs via evbuffer_expand_singlechain (return -1 on NULL) and read/recv into that chain. This expansion can allocate or add chains before the read, so on the following -1 or 0 returns the buffer contents and total_len are unchanged but its capacity may have grown. If the read returns -1 (or WSARecv fails with an error other than WSAECONNABORTED) the result is -1; a return of 0 (or WSAECONNABORTED) gives 0, with no change to total_len or callbacks. For n > 0 it advances the chain offsets (and last_with_datap) by n, adds n to total_len and n_add_for_cb, calls evbuffer_invoke_callbacks_ and returns n.

functions.name: evbuffer_run_callbacks
functions.prose_contract: Static function evbuffer_run_callbacks(buffer, running_deferred), buffer.c:455-511, returns void; the caller must hold the buffer lock (ASSERT_EVBUFFER_LOCKED at line 478). It chooses a flag mask and a pending-counter policy: when running_deferred is nonzero it runs callbacks that have EVBUFFER_CB_ENABLED set and EVBUFFER_CB_NODEFER clear (the deferred ones) and clears the counters; when running_deferred is zero and buffer->deferred_cbs is set it runs only callbacks with both ENABLED and NODEFER set and does not clear n_add_for_cb and n_del_for_cb; otherwise it runs every ENABLED callback (NODEFER not examined) and clears the counters. If the callback list is empty it sets both counters to 0 and returns (also when deferral is on). If both counters are already 0 it returns with no callbacks run. Otherwise it fills a cb_info with total_len, the added and deleted counts and orig_size = total_len + n_del_for_cb - n_add_for_cb, clears the counters when the policy says to, and for each entry matching the mask calls the obsolete-style callback (EVBUFFER_CB_OBSOLETE, with orig_size and new size) or the normal callback with the info; the next pointer is read before each call.

functions.name: evbuffer_launch_read_
functions.prose_contract: evbuffer_launch_read_(buf, at_most, ol), buffer_iocp.c:245-309 (Windows overlapped I/O), starts an overlapped WSARecv and returns 0 or -1 (r starts at -1). It returns -1 at once, before taking the lock, if upcast_evbuffer(buf) is NULL. Otherwise it takes the buffer lock and asserts that no write is in progress (EVUTIL_ASSERT aborts in debug builds). If buf->freeze_end is set or a read is already in progress it jumps to done and returns -1; no other fields were changed yet. Past that check it resets first_pinned and n_buffers and memsets the buffers array, which stays reset on any later failure. If evbuffer_expand_fast_(buf, at_most, MAX_WSABUFS) fails it returns -1. Otherwise it freezes the end of the buffer with evbuffer_freeze(buf, 0) (not the front), builds WSABUFs from evbuffer_read_setup_vecs_, records first_pinned and n_buffers, pins every chain from the first one onward with EVBUFFER_MEM_PINNED_R (asserting the pinned count equals nvecs) and takes an extra reference with evbuffer_incref_. If WSARecv fails with an error other than WSA_IO_PENDING it releases the pins, unfreezes the end, drops the reference with evbuffer_free and returns -1; otherwise (success or WSA_IO_PENDING) it sets read_in_progress = 1 and returns 0. The lock is released at done on every path after it was taken.

functions.name: dnsname_to_labels
functions.prose_contract: Static function dnsname_to_labels(buf, buf_len, j, name, name_len, table), evdns.c:1614-1678, encodes the dotted name into DNS length-prefixed labels in buf starting at offset j and returns the new offset (off_t) or a negative error. It returns -2 at once if name_len > 255. functions.name: gen_mvkey
functions.prose_contract: gen_mvkey(id, evpars), ntp-keygen.c:1554-1958, generates MV (mutual-verification) parameters and keys and returns an EVP_PKEY pointer. With n = nkeys it prints progress to stderr, allocates BIGNUMs and a DSA object, generates n distinct primes s1[1..n] of modulus2/n bits (retrying on duplicates, no bound on retries), forms q = product of the s1 and p = 2q + 1, regenerating one s1 at a time until p is prime (BN_is_prime_ex), then picks g with gcd(g, p-1) = 1 and g^q mod p = 1 (also unbounded retries) and stores p, q, g in the DSA. It chooses n zeros x[1..n] coprime to q, builds polynomial coefficients a[0..n] mod q, computes gs[i] = g^a[i] mod p, and runs a self-check: for every j it computes the product over i of g^(a[i] * x[j]^i) mod p (the code uses g and the exponent a[i]*x[j]^i, not gs[i]); if any product is not 1 it prints "Confirm ... no" and returns NULL immediately, before opening the key file or writing evpars, without freeing the BIGNUMs, DSA or BN_CTX. Otherwise it computes biga, a random group key b (coprime to q) and its inverse b1, the per-client keys xbar[j], xhat[j], the enabling key s, bige, gbar and ghat, opens the output file with fheader("MVta", "mvta", groupname), and writes three kinds of PKCS8 PEM keys through PEM_write_PKCS8PrivateKey: the trusted-authority key (assigned to the DSA, stored as evpars[0] and the value to return), the server key (a new DSA built from BN_dup copies) and n client keys, each stored in evpars in turn; for each client key it checks a relation and, if it is not 1, prints "Revoke key j" and continues (the key has already been written and stored). It terminates evpars with NULL, closes the file, frees a[i] and gs[i] for i in 0..n and x[j], xbar[j], xhat[j], s1[j] for j in 1..n, and returns the trusted-authority key evpars[0]. The remaining BIGNUMs (u, v, w, b, b1, s, biga, bige, gbar, ghat, p, q, g, priv_key, pub_key where not owned by a DSA) and the BN_CTX are not freed.
