Otherwise it sets exist = db_exist(sp, TMAP->lno + 1), saves the cursor with gp->scr_cursor, and for each screen map entry from HMAP to TMAP skips entries that are not first screen lines (with O_LEFTRIGHT only entries with coff == 0 qualify, otherwise only entries with soff == 1). For a qualifying entry it stops the loop (break) when smp->lno != 1, exist is zero and db_exist(sp, smp->lno) is false; otherwise it moves to that row, formats the line number with O_NUMBER_FMT and draws it with gp->scr_addstr. After the loop it moves the cursor back to the saved position and returns 0. Return values of scr_move, scr_addstr and db_exist-based breaks do not produce a nonzero return.

functions.name: vs_sm_fill
functions.prose_contract: vs_sm_fill(sp, lno, pos), vs_smap.c:172-286, rebuilds the screen map and returns 0 or 1. It first flushes every SMAP entry (sp->t_rows entries from HMAP) and sets SC_SCR_REDRAW. By pos: P_FILL decides by distance (vs_sm_nlines against HALFTEXT) between anchoring line 1 at the top (lno set to 1, goto top), anchoring the last line (from db_last, return 1 if it fails) at the bottom, and the middle. P_TOP anchors HMAP at lno with coff 0 and soff 1, or, when lno is OOBLNO, keeps the current HMAP line and resets soff to 1 if the line now has fewer screens than HMAP->soff, then fills downward over the map with vs_sm_next (each entry from the previous). P_MIDDLE puts lno in the entry t_rows / 2, fills upward with vs_sm_prev (on failure it sets lno = 1 and goes to the top case) and then downward with vs_sm_next. P_BOTTOM anchors TMAP at lno (or leaves TMAP when lno is OOBLNO) and fills upward with vs_sm_prev (on failure falls back to the top case with lno = 1). Any other pos calls abort(). A vs_sm_next failure in the downward fills goes to err, which restarts the map from line 1 (HMAP = line 1, filled downward with vs_sm_next) and returns 0 if that succeeds or 1 if even that fails. A normal fill returns 0.

functions.name: vs_sm_down
functions.prose_contract: Static function vs_sm_down(sp, rp, count, scmd, smp), vs_smap.c:807-952, scrolls the screen map down (towards earlier lines) and sets the cursor mark; it returns 0 or 1. It returns 1 after v_sof if HMAP is already line 1 at its first screen (or O_LEFTRIGHT) and scmd is CNTRL_Y or Z_CARAT or smp == HMAP. cursor_set starts as scmd == CNTRL_Y. For a small screen (IS_SMALL): if count >= sp->t_maxrows or scmd is CNTRL_B it erases the screen, steps back count lines with vs_sm_prev (stopping at line 1), refills with vs_sm_fill(OOBLNO, P_TOP) and returns the result of vs_sm_position(sp, rp, 0, P_BOTTOM), returning 1 on any failure; otherwise it sets cursor_set = (scmd == CNTRL_Y) || vs_sm_cursor(...), grows t_rows with vs_sm_1down up to t_maxrows (stopping at line 1), sets rp from the saved cursor entry when cursor_set is false, and returns 0 if count reached 0. The main loop scrolls one line at a time with vs_sm_1down (return 1 on failure, stop at line 1), moving smp for CNTRL_Y (setting ychanged when smp is already at TMAP) and Z_CARAT. After it, if scmd is not CNTRL_Y and cursor_set is true it returns 0 without setting rp in this part of the function. Then by scmd: CNTRL_B picks the last existing line on the map when count was exhausted (else falls into CNTRL_U), CNTRL_U moves smp up by count entries (clamped to HMAP), CNTRL_Y sets rp from smp only if ychanged and returns 0 (so rp can be left unset when ychanged is 0), Z_CARAT leaves smp, anything else calls abort(). For the remaining cases it calls vs_line on smp if its cache is not valid (return 1 on failure), sets rp->lno = smp->lno and rp->cno to 0 or the saved column, and returns 0.

functions.name: vs_vsplit
functions.prose_contract: vs_vsplit(sp, new), vs_split.c:203-286, splits sp vertically into sp and new and returns 0 or 1. If sp->cols / 2 <= MINIMUM_SCREEN_COLS it queues an error message and returns 1 without changing anything (so a split needs sp->cols / 2 > MINIMUM_SCREEN_COLS). Otherwise it calls vs_resolve(sp, NULL, 1), allocates new's screen map (CALLOC; return 1 if it fails) and initialises its first entry to line sp->lno, coff 0, soff 1. It sets cols = sp->cols / 2, new->cols = sp->cols - cols - 1, sp->cols = cols, new->coff = sp->coff + cols + 1 and sp->cno = 0, copies rows, t_rows, t_maxrows, t_minrows, roff and defscroll from sp to new, sets new's TMAP to the last entry, inserts new in the screen list with vs_insert, calls gp->scr_split(sp, new) (result ignored), sets SC_SCR_REFORMAT | SC_STATUS on sp, and sets SC_SCR_REFORMAT | SC_STATUS plus the SC_EX, SC_VI, SC_SCR_VI, SC_SCR_EX and SC_READONLY bits copied from sp on new. It returns 0.

functions.name: vs_resize
functions.prose_contract: vs_resize(sp, count, adj), vs_split.c:795-905, moves rows between sp and a neighbouring screen and returns 0 or 1. It returns 0 immediately, changing nothing, if count is 0, or if adj is A_SET and count equals sp->t_maxrows; for other A_SET it becomes A_DECREASE or A_INCREASE with count set to the difference from t_maxrows. It finds next, the first later screen in the list that overlaps sp horizontally, and prev likewise before sp, and sets either to NULL unless it has exactly sp's coff and cols. For A_DECREASE (a negative count is negated) s = sp: if sp->t_maxrows < MINIMUM_SCREEN_ROWS + count it queues "The screen can only shrink to %d rows" and returns 1; g = prev with s_off = count, else g = next with g_off = -count, and if neither exists it queues "The screen cannot shrink" and returns 1. For A_INCREASE g = sp: s = next if next is large enough (s_off = count), otherwise s = prev (if none: "The screen cannot grow" and return 1; if prev is too small the 'can only shrink' message and return 1) with g_off = -count. Then s->rows -= count and s->roff += s_off, g->rows += count and g->roff += g_off (so with A_DECREASE where g is next, s_off is 0 and sp->roff is unchanged), g's t_rows, t_maxrows and TMAP grow by count (t_minrows too when it equalled t_maxrows), s's t_rows and t_maxrows shrink by count (t_minrows clamped), TMAP of s is moved back, and both get SC_SCR_REFORMAT | SC_STATUS. It calls gp->scr_discard(0, list) with g and s (result ignored) and returns 0.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: main(argc, argv) of iblinkinfo, iblinkinfo.c:589-769, ends the process with exit() on every path I read (the last statement is exit(rc) at line 768); it does not return. It parses options with ibdiag_process_opts (which may itself exit), opens the IB port with mad_rpc_open_port (exit(1) with a message if that fails), sets the mkey and timeout, opens the node name map, and exits 1 if both dr_path and load_cache_file are set (after closing the port). With dr_path or guid_str it resolves the port id with resolve_portid_str and only warns ("attempting full scan") if that fails. It queries the local Node Info with smp_query_via and exits 1 if that fails, then closes the MAD port. It loads diff_cache_file and filterdownports_cache_file when given, calling IBEXIT (not read, assumed to terminate) if loading fails; with load_cache_file it loads that fabric (exit(1) on failure); otherwise, if the port was resolved, it tries a partial scan (max_hops defaulting to 1) and warns if it fails, then if there is still no fabric it does a full ibnd_discover_fabric; failure there prints "discover failed", sets rc = 1 and goes to close_port. With a fabric, if not -a and guid_str is set (or, similarly, dr_path using the port GUID from the local node info) it looks the port up with ibnd_find_port_guid and, if found and matching only_type when only_flag is set, prints it (or diffs it against diff_fabric); if the port is not found or filtered out it only prints "Failed to find port" to stderr (exit status stays 0). Otherwise it prints or diffs every node (filtered by type when only_flag is set). It destroys the fabrics, closes the node name map and calls exit(rc), where rc is 0 except after the failed full discovery (1).

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Tail of main(argc, argv) of saquery, saquery.c:1738-1984 (the packet name saquery_main_dispatch does not exist; this slice, 1875-1984, and the lines just before it are the part described here). After option parsing it skips the options (argc -= optind), sets query_type from the first argument (via find_query, else IB_SA_ATTR_NODERECORD) when no query type was given and the command is a plain query, and stores the next argument as the requested lid, guid or name depending on node_print_desc. It prints an error and calls ibdiag_show_usage (not read, assumed not to return) when a name is required (LID_ONLY, UNIQUE_LID_ONLY, GUID_ONLY) but missing, when NAME_OF_LID has no lid flag or a zero lid, or when NAME_OF_GUID has no guid flag. It calls umad_init (IBEXIT on failure) and sa_get_handle (IBPANIC if NULL). With params.with_grh it resolves the GID (resolve_self and sm_pr_query when the destination GID is all zero, else copies it) and calls sa_set_handle, jumping to error with the failing status on any failure. It opens the node name map, converts src_lid and dst_lid with get_lid when non-empty, and, if the class-port-info command, CLASS_PORT_INFO query or switch-info query needs it, calls query_sa_cpi (goto error with its status on failure). It then dispatches by command: node records, class port info (dump_class_port_info and status 0), ISSM records, multicast groups or members, or, for other commands, the matching query handler found with find_query_by_type (an unknown query prints "Unknown query type" and sets status = EINVAL). At the error label it frees src_lid if it is non-NULL (so it must be NULL or heap memory), frees the SA handle, calls umad_done and close_node_name_map, and returns status (0 on success, otherwise the status of the failing step or handler).

functions.name: bnxt_re_dbr_thread
functions.prose_contract: bnxt_re_dbr_thread(arg), db.c:542-571, is the doorbell-recovery thread body for the bnxt_re_context passed in arg; it never returns normally. It loops: ibv_get_cq_event on cntx->dbr_ev_chan; if that returns nonzero it prints "Failed to get cq_event" to stderr and calls pthread_exit(NULL). It then sets epoch = cntx->db_recovery_page and epoch_ack = epoch + 1; if epoch is NULL (epoch_ack, being epoch + 1, is then not NULL) it prints "DB reovery page is NULL" and calls pthread_exit(NULL), without acking the event it just received. If *epoch equals *epoch_ack it acks the event with ibv_ack_cq_events(ev_cq, 1) and continues. Otherwise it saves usr_epoch = *epoch, calls bnxt_re_db_recovery(cntx), stores usr_epoch in *epoch_ack, and then acks the event and continues the loop.

functions.name: poll_cq
functions.prose_contract: Static function poll_cq(wq, cq, cqe, cqe_flushed, cookie, credit), cq.c:345-549 (Chelsio T4), reaps one completion queue entry and returns 0, -EAGAIN or the error from t4_next_cqe. It first sets *cqe_flushed = 0 and *credit = 0 (credit is not set to any other value in this function), then calls t4_next_cqe(cq, &hw_cqe) and returns that error at once, consuming nothing, if it is nonzero. If wq is NULL it skips the CQE (ret = -EAGAIN). For a FW_RI_READ_RESP opcode it skips with -EAGAIN for an egress-error read response (setting the wq in error when the status is nonzero), for a WRID_STAG of 1, or when the oldest read is not signaled (after advance_oldest_read); otherwise it synthesises a read-request CQE and advances the oldest read. A FW_RI_TERMINATE opcode is skipped with -EAGAIN. If the CQE status is nonzero or the wq is in error it sets *cqe_flushed to (status == T4_ERR_SWFLUSH), sets wq->error and processes the CQE. For an RQ-type CQE it sets the wq in error and skips with -EAGAIN if the RQ is empty, and marks a T4_ERR_MSN status when the MSN differs from wq->rq.msn. An SQ CQE whose index is not the SQ consumer index and is not a software CQE is recorded as complete in sw_sq and skipped with -EAGAIN after flush_completed_wrs. In the processing step it copies the CQE to *cqe; for an SQ CQE it updates in_use and cidx, sets *cookie to the work request id and consumes the SQ entry, then runs flush_completed_wrs; for an RQ CQE it sets *cookie to the RQ work request id and consumes the RQ entry. At skip_cqe it consumes the software or hardware CQE (t4_swcq_consume or t4_hwcq_consume) and returns ret, which is 0 after a processed CQE and -EAGAIN after every skip path. The BUG_ON checks mean some inconsistent states abort rather than return.

functions.name: mad_rpc
functions.prose_contract: mad_rpc(port, rpc, dport, payload, rcvdata), rpc.c:221-284, sends one MAD and returns rcvdata on success or NULL. For MAD RPC version 1 classes it first sets rpcv1->error = 0. In a loop it zeroes the send buffer and builds the packet with mad_build_pkt (a negative result returns NULL, leaving rpcv1->error at 0 and rpc->rstatus unchanged), then calls _do_madrpc with the class agent, timeout and retries; if that returns a negative value it copies the local error variable into rpcv1->error (version 1 only; what _do_madrpc stores in it was not read), logs a warning and returns NULL, again without setting rpc->rstatus. It reads the reply status from the MAD header; if the status equals IB_MAD_STS_REDIRECT it calls redirect_port and repeats the loop when that returns 0, otherwise (redirect_port nonzero, or any non-redirect status) it leaves the loop. After the loop, for version 1 classes it sets rpcv1->error = error (the value from the last _do_madrpc call), and it sets rpc->rstatus = status. If status is nonzero (including a redirect that could not be followed) it logs the error, sets errno = EIO and returns NULL. Otherwise it optionally dumps the data when ibdebug is set, copies rpc->datasz bytes from the reply at offset rpc->dataoffs into rcvdata if rcvdata is non-NULL, and returns rcvdata (so NULL on success when rcvdata is NULL).

functions.name: group_nodes
functions.prose_contract: group_nodes(fabric), chassis.c:1237-1344 (the packet name was an unnamed enclosing function), groups the fabric's nodes into chassis and returns 0 on success or -1 on failure. It starts with an empty local chassis_scan and chassisnum = 0. Pass 1 walks fabric->switches: for a Voltaire vendor id it calls fill_voltaire_chassis_record and for a Mellanox vendor id fill_mellanox_chassis_record, jumping to cleanup if either returns nonzero. Pass 2 walks the switches again: for each Voltaire node that has ch_found set, is a spine (is_spine) and does not already have a chassis with a chassisnum, it calls add_chassis (cleanup on failure), gives the new current chassis the next chassisnum and calls build_chassis (cleanup on failure). Pass 3 walks fabric->nodes, skipping Voltaire nodes: for each node with a nonzero System GUID it looks up an existing chassis with find_chassisguid and increments its nodecount, or else calls add_chassis (cleanup on failure), records get_chassisguid(node) and nodecount 1 on the new chassis and sets fabric->chassis to the first chassis if it is still NULL. Pass 4 walks fabric->nodes again, skipping Voltaire nodes: for a node with a nonzero System GUID whose chassis has nodecount > 1 it assigns the next chassisnum to the chassis if it has none, then, if the node is not yet marked ch_found, marks it and calls add_node_to_chassis, or, if it is already marked and is a Mellanox node, calls insert_mellanox_line_and_spine. On success it sets fabric->chassis = chassis_scan.first_chassis and returns 0. At cleanup it frees every chassis in the local list starting at chassis_scan.first_chassis (only the chassis structures themselves), sets fabric->chassis = NULL and returns -1; failures of the fill_* and build_chassis calls therefore also lead to -1, not only add_chassis.

functions.name: mlx5_start_poll
functions.prose_contract: Static inline function mlx5_start_poll(ibcq, attr, lock, stall, cqe_version), cq.c:831-894 (mlx5 extended CQ polling), starts a poll and returns 0, EINVAL, ENOENT or an error from mlx5_parse_lazy_cqe. It returns EINVAL at once if attr->comp_mask is nonzero. If stall is nonzero it first stalls before taking the lock: in adaptive mode, if cq->stall_last_count is nonzero it calls mlx5_stall_cycles_poll_cq with last count plus stall_cycles; in the other mode, if cq->stall_next_poll is set it clears it and calls mlx5_stall_poll_cq. If lock is nonzero it takes cq->lock, then sets cq->cur_rsc and cq->cur_srq to NULL and calls mlx5_get_next_cqe. If that returns CQ_EMPTY it releases the lock if it took it, and when stall is nonzero updates the stall state (adaptive: stall_cycles = max(stall_cycles - mlx5_stall_cq_dec_step, mlx5_stall_cq_poll_min) and stall_last_count set to the current cycle count; otherwise stall_next_poll = 1), then returns ENOENT. For any other result it sets MLX5_CQ_FLAGS_FOUND_CQES when stall is nonzero and calls mlx5_parse_lazy_cqe. If that returns an error it releases the lock if it took it and, when stall is nonzero, in adaptive mode lowers stall_cycles the same way and sets stall_last_count = 0 (the non-adaptive mode changes no stall counter), and in both modes clears FOUND_CQES; it returns the parse result, so on success (0) the lock stays held for the matching end_poll.

functions.name: sq_overhead
functions.prose_contract: Static function sq_overhead(qp_type), verbs.c:773-820, returns the per-WQE send-queue header size in bytes for the QP type (converted from size_t to int), or -EINVAL. It reads no state and has no side effects. With mw_bind_size = sizeof(umr_ctrl_seg) + sizeof(mkey_context_seg) + max(sizeof(umr_klm_seg), 64) it returns: for IBV_QPT_RC, sizeof(ctrl_seg) + max(sizeof(atomic_seg) + sizeof(raddr_seg), mw_bind_size); for IBV_QPT_UC, sizeof(ctrl_seg) + max(sizeof(raddr_seg), mw_bind_size); for IBV_QPT_UD, sizeof(ctrl_seg) + sizeof(datagram_seg); for IBV_QPT_XRC_SEND, the larger of sizeof(ctrl_seg) + mw_bind_size and sizeof(ctrl_seg) + sizeof(xrc_seg) + sizeof(raddr_seg) (it falls through into the XRC_RECV case); for IBV_QPT_XRC_RECV, exactly sizeof(ctrl_seg) + sizeof(xrc_seg) + sizeof(raddr_seg) with no mw_bind term; for IBV_QPT_RAW_PACKET, sizeof(ctrl_seg) + sizeof(eth_seg); any other qp_type returns -EINVAL.

functions.name: rdma_migrate_id
functions.prose_contract: rdma_migrate_id(id, channel), cma.c:2255-2308 (the packet name ucma_migrate_id is rdma_migrate_id in the file), moves an rdma_cm_id to another event channel and returns 0 or an error. It returns ERR(EINVAL) if id_priv->sync is set and channel is NULL (a synchronous id cannot move to a new private channel). If channel is NULL it creates a private channel with rdma_create_event_channel (sync = 1) and returns -1, not ENOMEM, if that fails. It builds a MIGRATE_ID command with the id handle and the current channel's fd (id->channel->fd) and writes it to channel->fd; if the write does not return the full command size it destroys the channel it created when sync is set and returns ERR(ENODATA) for a short non-negative count or -1 for a negative result. On success, if id_priv->sync was set it acks and clears id->event when present and destroys the old id->channel. It then takes id_priv->mut, sets id_priv->sync = sync and id->channel = channel, waits on id_priv->cond while id_priv->events_completed < resp.events_reported, releases the mutex and returns 0.

functions.name: server_open
functions.prose_contract: Static function server_open(rs, msg), rcopy.c:229-271, handles a received CMD_OPEN and returns an int status. It prints "opening: ". If the global file_addr is non-NULL or the global fd is greater than 0 it prints a message and goes to out with ret = EBUSY. Otherwise it sets len = msg->len - sizeof *msg, mallocs a path buffer of len bytes (goto out with ENOMEM if that fails), and receives the path with _recv(rs, path, len); if _recv returns anything other than len it prints an error and goes to out with ret equal to _recv's value (which may be 0, a partial count or a negative number), without opening a file. Otherwise it prints the path and calls open(path, O_RDWR | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC, msg->data) into the global fd; if that fails it prints a message and stores errno in ret, but line 264 then sets ret = 0 unconditionally, so the function reports 0 even when the open failed (fd stays negative). At out it frees path if allocated, calls msg_send_resp(rs, msg, ret) and returns ret. The path buffer is not NUL-terminated by this function (printf of it assumes the sender included the NUL).

functions.name: copysockopts
functions.prose_contract: Static function copysockopts(dfd, sfd, dapi, sapi), preload.c:447-474, copies a few socket settings from sfd to dfd using the two socket_calls tables, and returns 0 or the failing call's nonzero result. It reads sfd's file status flags with sapi->fcntl(sfd, F_GETFL); if the result is positive it sets them on dfd with dapi->fcntl(dfd, F_SETFL, flags) and uses that call's result; a nonzero final result (including a negative F_GETFL result) is returned at once, while a result of 0 from F_GETFL continues without copying flags. It then reads SO_REUSEADDR from sfd with getsockopt and, if the value is nonzero and the getsockopt returned 0, sets it on dfd with setsockopt; a nonzero result is returned. The same is done for TCP_NODELAY at the IPPROTO_TCP level. The tested value param is read even when getsockopt failed (the test is param && !ret, so param is uninitialised on the first failure path but ret is then returned anyway). A zero option value is not copied. It returns 0 if none of the attempted calls failed. The returned failure value is whatever the socket_calls entry returned (typically -1), not an errno code.

functions.name: rsocket
functions.prose_contract: rsocket(domain, type, protocol), rsocket.c:1130-1170, creates an rsocket and returns its index, or a negative value. It returns ERR(ENOTSUP) if domain is not AF_INET, AF_INET6 or AF_IB, type is not SOCK_STREAM or SOCK_DGRAM, a SOCK_STREAM protocol is nonzero and not IPPROTO_TCP, or a SOCK_DGRAM protocol is nonzero and not IPPROTO_UDP (ERR is a macro that was not read; it is assumed to set errno and return a negative value). It calls rs_configure and rs_alloc(NULL, type), returning ERR(ENOMEM) if that fails. For SOCK_STREAM it calls rdma_create_id (RDMA_PS_TCP), sets the cm_id's source address family to domain and uses the event channel fd as the index; for SOCK_DGRAM it calls ds_init(rs, domain) and uses rs->udp_sock as the index. A nonzero rdma_create_id or ds_init result, or a negative rs_insert(rs, index) result, goes to err, which calls rs_free(rs) and returns that value. On success it returns rs->index.

functions.name: rbind
functions.prose_contract: rbind(socket, addr, addrlen), rsocket.c:1172-1193, binds an rsocket and returns the underlying call's result. It looks the socket up with idm_lookup and returns ERR(EBADF) if it is not registered. For a SOCK_STREAM rsocket it calls rdma_bind_addr(rs->cm_id, addr) and, if that returns 0, sets rs->state = rs_bound; it returns rdma_bind_addr's result. For a datagram rsocket, if rs->state is rs_init it first calls ds_init_ep(rs) and returns its nonzero result at once (without binding); it then calls bind(rs->udp_sock, addr, addrlen) and returns its result. The function itself only sets the state in the stream case; any state change made by ds_init_ep (it may leave the datagram rsocket in a different state even if the following bind fails) was not read.

functions.name: rlisten
functions.prose_contract: rlisten(socket, backlog), rsocket.c:1195-1212, starts listening and returns an int. It returns ERR(EBADF) if idm_lookup does not find the socket. If rs->state is not rs_listening it calls rdma_listen(rs->cm_id, backlog), sets rs->state = rs_listening when that returns 0, and returns rdma_listen's result; if the state already is rs_listening it returns 0 without calling anything. The function does not check the rsocket type itself (the cm_id is used directly).

functions.name: raccept
functions.prose_contract: raccept(socket, addr, addrlen), rsocket.c:1226-1282, accepts a connection on a listening rsocket and returns the new rsocket index or a failing value. It returns ERR(EBADF) if the socket is not registered and ERR(ENOMEM) if rs_alloc(rs, rs->type) fails. It then calls rdma_get_request(rs->cm_id, &new_rs->cm_id), rs_insert on the new cm_id's channel fd, and checks the connection data version; failures go to err (the negative rs_insert result, ERR(ENOTSUP) if creq->version != 1, or rdma_get_request's result). If the listening rsocket has O_NONBLOCK it sets O_NONBLOCK on the new cm_id's channel fd. It calls rs_create_ep (error goes to err), saves the connection data, builds the accept parameters with the response connection data and calls rdma_accept: a result of 0 sets new_rs->state = rs_connect_rdwr; a nonzero result with errno EAGAIN or EWOULDBLOCK sets new_rs->state = rs_accepting and is treated as success; any other nonzero result goes to err (and the value returned is rdma_accept's, typically -1). If addr and addrlen are both non-NULL it fills them with rgetpeername (result ignored). It returns new_rs->index. At err it calls rs_free(new_rs) and returns ret; the listening rsocket's state is not changed here.

functions.name: rs_poll_cq
functions.prose_contract: Static function rs_poll_cq(rs), rsocket.c:1900-1986, drains the receive completion queue (rs->cm_id->recv_cq) one completion at a time and returns 0 or a negative value. For a receive completion with a non-success status it skips it (not counted). For a successful one it increments rcnt and takes the message from the immediate data or from the receive buffer area, then by operation: RS_OP_SGL sets rs->sseq_comp; RS_OP_IOMAP_SGL and RS_OP_WRITE do nothing; RS_OP_CTRL with RS_CTRL_DISCONNECT sets rs->state = rs_disconnected and returns 0 at once; with RS_CTRL_SHUTDOWN it clears rs_readable if the rsocket is writable, otherwise sets rs_disconnected and returns 0 at once; any other operation is appended to the rmsg ring at rmsg_tail. The two immediate returns skip the reposting of receive buffers and leave later completions unread. For a send completion it updates counters by the operation (SGL: ctrl_max_seqno++; CTRL: ctrl_max_seqno++ and, for RS_CTRL_DISCONNECT, state = rs_disconnected without returning; IOMAP_SGL and other ops: sqe_avail++ and sbuf_bytes_avail adjusted), and if the status is not success while the state has rs_connected it sets state = rs_error and err = EIO, then continues the loop. After the loop (ret is ibv_poll_cq's last result: 0 when the queue is empty, negative on error), if the state still has rs_connected it reposts rcnt receive buffers with rs_post_recv while ret is 0 (so none are reposted after a negative poll result), and if ret is nonzero it sets state = rs_error and err = errno. It returns ret.

functions.name: __osmv_dispatch_rmpp_rcv
functions.prose_contract: Static function __osmv_dispatch_rmpp_rcv(h_bind, p_mad, p_txn, p_mad_addr), osm_vendor_mlx_dispatcher.c:484-637 (the earlier hit at line 83 is the prototype), handles one received RMPP segment of an existing transaction and returns an ib_api_status_t (initially IB_SUCCESS). An RMPP ACK is logged and dropped (returns IB_SUCCESS). An ABORT or STOP from the peer returns IB_REMOTE_ERROR. Otherwise it calls __osmv_dispatch_accept_seg and switches on its status: IB_SUCCESS computes is_last1 from the segment's last flag and is_last2 from the accumulated byte count against the size announced in the first segment; if they differ it sends an ABORT/BAD_LEN NAK and returns IB_ERROR; otherwise it sends an ACK (__osmv_dispatch_send_ack) and continues. IB_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES (an out-of-order segment) sends an ACK and returns IB_SUCCESS without accepting it. IB_INSUFFICIENT_MEMORY sends a STOP/RESX NAK and returns IB_INSUFFICIENT_MEMORY. Any other status triggers CL_ASSERT(FALSE) and then falls out of the switch with the unexpected status, which is returned unchanged at the end (after the not-last check). If the segment is not the last one it logs that assembly continues and returns the current status (IB_SUCCESS in the normal case). For the last segment it takes the size from the first segment or, if that was 0, from the last, allocates a MADW with osm_mad_pool_get (NULL gives IB_INSUFFICIENT_MEMORY without any NAK), reassembles the MAD (a failure returns that status and does not release the MADW just allocated), calls osmv_txn_done unless the transaction was initiated by the peer and the response is a multi-response, restores the original transaction id in the MAD and calls p_bo->recv_cb(p_new_madw, cb_context, p_req_madw). It then returns the status, IB_SUCCESS after a delivered message.

functions.name: ni_rcv_process_new
functions.prose_contract: Static function ni_rcv_process_new(sm, p_madw), osm_node_info_rcv.c:657-838, processes a NodeInfo reply from a newly discovered node and returns void. If the SM state is master it sets port->is_new = 1. For a router node it creates a router object with osm_router_new and inserts it in rtr_guid_tbl; failures are only logged. It then inserts the node into node_guid_tbl: if another entry with that GUID is already there (a discovery race) it logs that, deletes the new node, sets the links on the existing node with ni_rcv_set_links and returns; otherwise it sets the links on the new node, increments its discovery_count, calls ni_rcv_get_node_desc, and calls ni_rcv_process_new_ca_or_router for CA and router nodes or ni_rcv_process_new_switch for switches; any other node type logs "Unknown node type". functions.name: sa_mad_ctrl_process
functions.prose_contract: Static function sa_mad_ctrl_process(p_ctrl, p_madw, is_get_request), osm_sa_mad_ctrl.c:95-271, routes a received SA MAD to a dispatcher message and returns void. It then maps the MAD's attribute id to a message id (class port info, node, portinfo, link, sminfo, service, path, mcmember, inform info, vlarb, slvl, pkey table, lft, guidinfo, inform info record, switch info, mft, and with VENDOR_RMPP_SUPPORT and DUAL_SIDED_RMPP the multipath record); for an unsupported attribute it logs ERR 1A01 and dumps the MAD, leaving msg_id as CL_DISP_MSGID_NONE. functions.name: osm_mpr_rcv_process
functions.prose_contract: osm_mpr_rcv_process(context, data), osm_sa_multipath_record.c:1533-1672 (the packet name osm_mpr_rcv does not exist), handles a MultiPathRecord SA request, with context the osm_sa_t and data the MAD wrapper; it returns void and its alias-guid array, counts and path list are locals, not caller storage. functions.name: osm_pkey_rec_rcv_process
functions.prose_contract: osm_pkey_rec_rcv_process(ctx, data), osm_sa_pkey_record.c:212-316 (the packet name sa_pkey_record_query does not exist), handles a P_KeyTableRecord SA request and returns void. If the MAD's sm_key differs from opt.sa_key (the request is not trusted) it logs, sends IB_SA_MAD_STATUS_REQ_INVALID and returns, again without the lock. Otherwise it takes sa->p_lock (cl_plock_acquire), finds the requester's physical port from the MAD address and, if not found, releases the lock, logs ERR 4604 and returns with no reply. It releases the lock and always sends a reply with osm_sa_respond(sa, p_madw, sizeof(ib_pkey_table_record_t), &rec_list), including when the list is empty because the LID was not found.

functions.name: osm_pir_rcv_process
functions.prose_contract: osm_pir_rcv_process(ctx, data), osm_sa_portinfo_record.c:506-608 (the packet name osm_sa_pir_rcv does not exist), handles a PortInfoRecord SA request and returns void. It asserts the attribute id. If the method is neither GET nor GETTABLE it logs, sends IB_MAD_STATUS_UNSUP_METHOD_ATTR and returns before taking the lock. Otherwise it takes sa->p_lock (cl_plock_acquire) and finds the requester's physical port; if not found it releases the lock, logs an error and returns without replying. functions.name: osm_sr_rcv_lease_cb
functions.prose_contract: osm_sr_rcv_lease_cb(context), osm_sa_service_record.c:724-802 (the packet name sa_sr_trim does not exist), is the service-record lease timer callback (context is the osm_sa_t); it returns void. It starts with trim_time = 20 and takes sa->p_lock exclusively. For each record in sa->p_subn->sa_sr_list: records whose service_lease is 0xFFFFFFFF are left alone; otherwise it computes elapsed seconds since modified_time (at least 1); if elapsed is less than the record's lease_period it subtracts elapsed from lease_period, sets modified_time to now and lowers trim_time to the remaining lease (but not below 1); otherwise (lease expired) it removes the record from the database with osm_svcr_remove_from_db and deletes it with osm_svcr_delete. After the list it releases the lock and calls cl_timer_trim(&sa->sr_timer, trim_time * 1000) if trim_time is not 0xFFFFFFFF; since trim_time starts at 20 and is only ever reduced (to no less than 1), that test is always true, and the timer is re-armed for 1 to 20 seconds.

functions.name: osm_smir_rcv_process
functions.prose_contract: osm_smir_rcv_process(ctx, data), osm_sa_sminfo_record.c:170-328 (the packet's unnamed handler), handles an SMInfoRecord SA request and returns void. Then, if the LID named a port other than the local one, it looks that port's GUID up in sm_guid_tbl and, if found, adds its remote-SM record with sa_smir_by_comp_mask (a log message otherwise); if no LID was given at all (p_port is NULL) it applies sa_smir_by_comp_mask_cb to every entry of sm_guid_tbl. functions.name: osm_vlarb_rec_rcv_process
functions.prose_contract: osm_vlarb_rec_rcv_process(ctx, data), osm_sa_vlarb_record.c:206-305 (the packet's 'unnamed SA handler'), handles a VLArbitrationTableRecord SA request and returns void (it does not return a status and does not expect the caller to hold the lock). functions.name: sm_mad_ctrl_rcv_callback
functions.prose_contract: Static function sm_mad_ctrl_rcv_callback(p_madw, bind_context, p_req_madw), osm_sm_mad_ctrl.c:605-692, is the QP0 MAD receive callback (bind_context is the osm_sm_mad_ctrl_t, p_req_madw is the matching request MAD, if any); it returns void. It then dispatches on the SMP method: GET_RESP calls sm_mad_ctrl_process_get_resp(p_ctrl, p_madw, p_req_madw) and TRAP_REPRESS calls sm_mad_ctrl_process_trap_repress, each asserting that p_req_madw is non-NULL; GET, TRAP and SET call sm_mad_ctrl_process_get, _trap and _set, asserting p_req_madw is NULL (the asserts are CL_ASSERT, compiled only in assert builds). functions.name: osm_sm_state_mgr_process
functions.prose_contract: osm_sm_state_mgr_process(sm, signal), osm_sm_state_mgr.c:272-499, applies a state-manager signal to the SM state machine and returns an ib_api_status_t (IB_SUCCESS unless set otherwise). It takes sm->state_lock (a spinlock) for the whole transition and releases it just before returning; sm->p_lock is taken and released inside individual cases. By sm->p_subn->sm_state: in DISCOVERING, DISCOVERY_COMPLETED sets MASTER and (under p_lock exclusively) first_time_master_sweep = TRUE and master_sm_base_lid = sm_base_lid; MASTER_OR_HIGHER_SM_DETECTED sets STANDBY, clears ignore_existing_lfts and starts polling; HANDOVER queues OSM_SIGNAL_SWEEP; in STANDBY, POLLING_TIMEOUT and DISCOVER set DISCOVERING, set coming_out_of_standby and queue a sweep, DISABLE sets NOTACTIVE, HANDOVER sets master_sm_base_lid, force_first_time_master_sweep, state MASTER and queues a sweep, and ACKNOWLEDGE only breaks; in NOTACTIVE, STANDBY sets state STANDBY and starts polling; in MASTER, POLLING_TIMEOUT and HANDOVER (shared block) clear polling_sm_guid, set force_first_time_master_sweep and queue a sweep, HANDOVER_SENT sets STANDBY and starts polling, WAIT_FOR_HANDOVER starts polling, and DISCOVER sets DISCOVERING. Each state change calls osm_report_sm_state. In every state, a signal that is not listed calls sm_state_mgr_signal_error and sets status = IB_INVALID_PARAMETER. An unrecognised sm_state value only logs an error (status stays IB_SUCCESS). The listed actions are my reading of the code; log message details and the exact comments are not included.

functions.name: state_mgr_is_sm_port_down
functions.prose_contract: Static function state_mgr_is_sm_port_down(sm), osm_state_mgr.c:434-490, returns a boolean_t TRUE when the SM's own port is considered down. It reads port_guid = sm->p_subn->sm_port_guid. If that is 0 it logs ERR 3308 and treats the state as IB_LINK_DOWN without taking sm->p_lock. Otherwise it takes sm->p_lock (CL_PLOCK_ACQUIRE) and looks the port up with osm_get_port_by_guid; if there is none it logs ERR 3309, treats the state as IB_LINK_DOWN and releases the lock. If the port exists it sets state = IB_LINK_ACTIVE when its node is a switch whose switch_info is not an enhanced port 0 (a base switch port 0), otherwise state = osm_physp_get_port_state(port's physp); then, if p_port->discovery_count is 0 it logs ERR 330A and sets state = IB_LINK_DOWN; it releases the lock. It returns state == IB_LINK_DOWN. So it returns TRUE for a zero SM port GUID, an unknown port, a port with discovery_count 0, or a non-base-port-0 port whose physical state is IB_LINK_DOWN, and FALSE otherwise; the lock is taken and released only on the paths that reach the lookup.

functions.name: link_srcsink
functions.prose_contract: link_srcsink(t, i, j, k), osm_torus.c:1665-1806, moves a fabric switch's source/sink ports into the torus switch's SRCSINK port group and returns bool. It canonicalizes i, j and k against the torus dimensions and looks up tsw = t->sw[i][j][k]; if there is none it returns true. It takes fsw = tsw->tmp; if fsw is NULL or fsw->osm_switch is NULL it logs ERR 4E1C and returns false. Otherwise it sets the port group at index 2 * TORUS_MAX_DIM to type SRCSINK and transfers the osm_switch from fsw to tsw (tsw->osm_switch = fsw->osm_switch, its priv set to tsw, fsw->osm_switch set to NULL); this transfer happens before the port loop, so it also takes place on the later false returns. For each fsw port: a port of type SRCSINK is moved into the group (attached to tsw, group port count incremented, fsw->port[p] cleared); a PASSTHRU port whose link has a SRCSINK (CA) end is converted: the link is examined, and if the far end is not SRCSINK it is skipped. If the group already has portgrp_sz ports it logs ERR 4E1D or 4E1E and the function returns false; a CA end with a NULL osm_port logs ERR 4E1F and returns false; if alloc_tlink returns NULL that port is skipped (the CA link is not moved and the function still can return true); otherwise a new torus link is filled, added to the group, the CA's osm_port is handed to the new link, t->ca_cnt is incremented, and the fabric endpoint is cleared. After the loop it returns true. Earlier ports stay moved when a later port makes it return false.

functions.name: new_size
functions.prose_contract: Static function new_size(size), st.c:150-171, returns the next table size from the static primes[] array for a requested bin count. In the compiled (#else) branch it starts with newsize = MINSIZE (8) and i = 0 and, for each i up to the number of entries in primes[] (29, the last entry being 0), tests newsize > size, doubling newsize each step; it returns primes[i] for the first i where 8 << i exceeds size. primes[i] is (8 << i) plus a small offset, e.g. primes[0] = 11 (for size up to 7), primes[1] = 19 (8 to 15), primes[2] = 37, primes[3] = 67, primes[17] = 1048583 (1048576 + 7, for size up to 1048575 and above 524287), and so on up to primes[27] = 1073741909 (1073741824 + 85) for sizes from 536870912 up to 1073741823. For a negative size it returns primes[0]. If no entry qualifies (size at least 1073741824, or the int newsize shift overflows) it falls out of the loop and returns 0 (the comment says it should raise an exception); the int doubling past 2^30 is signed overflow in C, so the exact behaviour for such sizes is not defined by the language. The #if 0 branch (a power-of-two version returning -1) is not compiled.

functions.name: regexpr
functions.prose_contract: regexpr(), lex.c:561-592, scans the body of a /regular expression/ in the awk lexer and returns REGEXPR (via the RET macro). It uses a static heap buffer buf (initially 500 bytes, allocated on first use with FATAL "out of space for reg expr" if malloc fails) that is reused across calls. It reads characters with input() until a '/' or end of input (0). Before storing each character it calls adjbuf to make room (FATAL if that fails). A newline ends the scan: it terminates the buffer, reports SYNTAX "newline in regular expression", pushes the newline back with unput and breaks out of the loop. A backslash stores itself and the next input() character (the next character is stored without further checks, including a newline or 0). Any other character is stored. After the loop it terminates the buffer; if the loop ended on end of input (c == 0) it reports SYNTAX "non-terminated regular expression". It then sets yylval.s to tostring(buf), a fresh heap copy that the caller owns, calls unput('/') so the next input() returns '/', and returns REGEXPR. In the newline case the '/' is therefore read before the pushed-back newline. FATAL (malloc, adjbuf, tostring) ends the program, and unput may itself call FATAL if its pushback buffer is full (not read, so not verified); SYNTAX reports an error and the function carries on.

functions.name: get_str_val
functions.prose_contract: Static function get_str_val(vp, fmt), tran.c:424-513, returns vp->sval for the awk Cell vp, converting a number to a string when needed; fmt points to the OFMT or CONVFMT format-string pointer. If neither NUM nor STR is set in vp->tval it calls funnyvar (not read). If vp is a field and fields have not been split yet it calls fldbld(), else if it is the record and the record is not built it calls recbld(). If vp is not a string (isstr is false) it converts with the update_str_val macro: frees the old sval if freeable, then formats fval as "+inf"/"-inf"/"+nan"/"-nan" for non-finite values (get_inf_nan), as "%.30g" if the value is integral, otherwise with *fmt into a 256-byte buffer; stores a tostring copy in sval, clears DONTFREE and sets STR; then it sets CONVO (clearing CONVC) when fmt == OFMT or CONVC (clearing CONVO) otherwise, and vp->fmt = *fmt. If vp is already a string it returns the existing string unchanged when it is DONTFREE, is not numeric (isnum false) or is a field. Otherwise (a string that is also numeric, not DONTFREE, not a field) it reconverts with update_str_val when the cached conversion was made with the other kind of format (for fmt == OFMT: CONVC set, or CONVO set with vp->fmt != *fmt; for the CONVFMT case: CONVO set, or CONVC set with vp->fmt != *fmt), updating the CONV flag and vp->fmt, and does nothing otherwise. It returns vp->sval in all cases.

functions.name: swap_audit_file
functions.prose_contract: Takes no arguments. It reads the globals lastfile and audit_review_gid (audit_review_gid is only passed along, not assigned) and the cached audit state. It returns -1 if getTSstr fails, and returns -1 if auditd_swap_trail returns any error other than ADE_ACTL (an ADE_ACTL error is only logged and processing continues); on these -1 returns lastfile and the cached state are not changed by this function. If lastfile is non-NULL and its last path component starts with the new timestamp, it logs a debug message and returns 0 before auditd_swap_trail is called, leaving lastfile and the cached state unchanged and closing nothing. Otherwise, if the cached state is AUD_STATE_ENABLED it calls close_lastfile(TS) and ignores the result (close_lastfile can return -1 early if strdup fails, leaving the old trail unrenamed; otherwise it tries to rename lastfile, unlinks the 'current' link only if the rename succeeds, frees lastfile and sets it to NULL); it then sets the cached state to AUD_STATE_ENABLED, calls auditd_new_curlink(newfile) (a failure is only logged), stores newfile in lastfile and returns 0. I did not read the bodies of auditd_swap_trail, auditd_new_curlink or getTSstr.

functions.name: wait_for_fd
functions.prose_contract: Takes a descriptor fd and a timeout in seconds (-1 means no timeout is passed to select). It loops: builds an fd_set with only fd, calls select for writability with a fresh timeval each iteration, and if select returns 0 returns ETIMEDOUT; if select returns -1 with errno EINTR it retries the loop (so EINTR is not returned and the timeout restarts from the full value); if select returns -1 with another errno it returns that errno; if select returns a positive count it returns 0 (after PJDLOG_ASSERTs that fd is set). It opens, closes and locks nothing and allocates no memory; behaviour for an fd outside the range an fd_set can hold is not handled by this code.

functions.name: receiver_open
functions.prose_contract: Opens or creates the trail file named by filename for the current adhost; it reads and may update adhost->adh_trail_fd and adh_trail_name and renames or opens files through adhost->adh_trail_dirfd. Returns ADIST_ERROR_WRONG_ORDER, leaving everything unchanged, if adh_trail_fd is already not -1 (the previous file was not closed); ADIST_ERROR_INVALID_NAME if trail_validate_name rejects the name; then switches on trail_name_compare(filename, adh_trail_name). TRAIL_RENAMED: if the current trail name is not an unterminated trail it returns ADIST_ERROR_INVALID_NAME, if renameat fails it returns ADIST_ERROR_RENAME, otherwise the file has been renamed on disk and it falls through to the open-existing case. TRAIL_IDENTICAL (and the fall-through): openat with O_WRONLY|O_APPEND|O_NOFOLLOW, ADIST_ERROR_OPEN if it fails (a rename already done is not undone). TRAIL_NEWER: openat with O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW mode 0600, ADIST_ERROR_CREATE on failure. TRAIL_OLDER returns ADIST_ERROR_OPEN_OLD; any other compare result aborts via PJDLOG_ABORT. On success it copies filename into adh_trail_name (PJDLOG_VERIFY that it fits), stores the new descriptor in adh_trail_fd and returns 0. On the error returns listed above no new descriptor is stored in adh_trail_fd.

functions.name: auditfilterd_conf_apply
functions.prose_contract: Void. Takes a list of freshly parsed modules and reconciles the global filter_list with it in three passes, matching modules by am_modulename with strcmp. Pass 1: every module in filter_list with no same-named entry in the new list is removed, detached and freed. Pass 2: for every module present in both lists, the argc/argv of the two entries are swapped, auditfilter_module_reinit is called on the old (filter_list) entry; if reinit fails that entry is removed from filter_list, detached and freed, and then the new-list twin is removed from the new list and freed in either case (note the loop then continues from the freed entry's link, a use-after-free if reinit failed). Pass 3: for each remaining new-list entry that is not in filter_list, the entry is removed from the new list and auditfilter_module_attach is called; if attach fails it is freed without a detach, otherwise it is inserted at the head of filter_list (inserting rewrites the entry's list link, so the foreach over the new list then continues through the old filter_list entries, which all match and are skipped, and any later new-list entries are not visited by this pass). Finally if the new list is still non-empty it only warns. So after the call filter_list is not guaranteed to equal the new configuration: modules whose reinit or attach failed are absent, and entries skipped by the pass 3 iteration quirk stay in the new list.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Program entry of auditreduce; slice cut the head. It parses options "Aa:b:c:d:e:f:g:j:m:o:r:u:vz:" with getopt, recording options in opttochk. For -a, -b it uses strptime/mktime on the argument; -d sets both the start and end time of that day and rejects use together with -a or -b by calling usage; for -a/-b the usage call is made if the same option repeats. For -e, -f, -g, -r, -u a non-numeric argument is looked up as a user or group name and, if the lookup fails, the option is silently skipped (break) without setting its flag. -c calls usage if getauditflagsbin fails; -m grows the p_evec array (32 entries initially, doubling) and exits with err(1) if malloc or realloc fails, and calls usage if the argument is neither a number nor a known event name; unknown options call usage. With no file operands it optionally (HAVE_CAP_ENTER) calls cap_enter (exiting with EXIT_FAILURE on failure other than ENOSYS), runs select_records(stdin), exits with errx(EXIT_FAILURE) if that returns -1 and otherwise exit(EXIT_SUCCESS). With file operands it opens each file (errx EXIT_FAILURE if fopen fails); in a HAVE_CAP_ENTER build it forks a child that cap_enters and runs select_records and the parent waits and exits EXIT_FAILURE if the child's exit status is nonzero (the fork result is not checked); otherwise it runs select_records in-process with errx(EXIT_FAILURE) on -1; then fclose, and after all files exit(EXIT_SUCCESS). It does not return normally. I did not read select_records, usage or parse_object_type.

functions.name: DecoderMngrBase<P,Pt,Pc>::attachPktMonitor
functions.prose_contract:
Template member that attaches a raw-packet monitor to a decoder component. It picks pComponent->getAssocComponent() when that is non-NULL, otherwise pComponent itself, and dynamic_casts it to TrcPktProcBase; if the cast fails it returns OCSD_ERR_INVALID_PARAM_TYPE. It then dynamic_casts pPktRawDataMon to IPktRawDataMon

; if that fails (including a NULL pointer) it returns OCSD_ERR_INVALID_PARAM_TYPE. Otherwise it returns the result of calling replace_first with that monitor on the packet processor's raw-packet-monitor attach point (the value is whatever replace_first returns; I did not read it). pComponent itself is dereferenced without a NULL check. The function takes no ownership and frees nothing.

functions.name: TraceComponent::setComponentOpMode
functions.prose_contract: Stores op_flags ANDed with m_supported_op_flags into m_op_flags (flags the component does not support are silently cleared) and returns OCSD_OK. It does not return an error for unsupported flags even though the header comment in trc_component.h (line 77) says it does; the only return statement is OCSD_OK.

functions.name: EtmV3PktProcImpl::OnISyncPacket
functions.prose_contract: Void. Builds the current ETMv3 I-sync packet from m_currPacketData, starting with m_currPktIdx set to 1 (its previous value is discarded). If m_bIsync_got_cycle_cnt is set it reads a cycle count with extractCycleCount, stores it and marks the I-sync as having a cycle count. If m_config.CtxtIDBytes() is non-zero it reads the context ID with extractCtxtID and updates it. Then it reads one info byte: bits 6:5 give the I-sync reason, bit 3 updates the NS flag, bit 1 updates the Hyp flag only if hasVirtExt(), bit 4 is J, and bit 2 is AltISA only if MinorRev() >= 3 (otherwise AltISA is 0). If isInstrTrace() it reads four bytes little endian as the instruction address, takes bit 0 as the T flag, clears it, updates the 32-bit address, sets ISA to jazelle if J, else to tee if T and AltISA, else to thumb2 if T, else to arm; if m_bIsync_get_LSiP_addr is also set it reads a branch-style address with extractBrAddrPkt and updates the data address first with the main address (32 bits) then with the LSiP address (LSiPBits bits). If isInstrTrace() is false it marks the packet as having no address (no address or ISA update). Finally it calls SendPacket(). m_currPktIdx is left after the consumed bytes; the function does not bounds-check the data it indexes. I did not read extractCycleCount, extractCtxtID or extractBrAddrPkt.

functions.name: TrcPktDecodeEtmV4I::processException
functions.prose_contract: Returns an ocsd_err_t. It takes the exception element off the back of m_P0_stack (a TrcStackElemExcept is assumed, not checked) and pops it. If the exception came from the ETE PE-reset packet it skips the address handling; otherwise it looks at the next element, pops it if it is a context element (remembering it), and requires the following element to be an address element: if it is not, it returns the result of handlePacketSeqErr(OCSD_ERR_BAD_PACKET_SEQ, ...) with the popped elements still pending deletion. The address element itself is read but not popped. If the exception's previous-same flag (branch target) is set, the current instruction address and ISA (aarch64 or arm from the context SF bit or current ISA; thumb2 if the address element's ISA is nonzero) are set from the address and m_need_addr is cleared. It then adds an output element (returns that error if addElem fails); if a context element was found it calls updateContext into it (return value ignored) and adds another element. Unless this was a PE reset, if the current instruction address differs from the return address it calls traceInstrToWP: on error it returns that error (additionally setting m_need_addr and m_need_ctxt and logging a warning for OCSD_ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ISA, or logging an error for other codes); a found waypoint, or a partial range with different start and end, yields a trace-range element (followed by a new element), and a missing waypoint sets m_need_addr; if the walk reported inaccessible memory it fills an ADDR_NACC element at the current address and adds another element. Finally it fills the current element as OCSD_GEN_TRC_ELEM_EXCEPTION with its end address set to the return address (0 for PE reset), its exception-return-address flag set to 1, the branch-target flag and the exception number, calls m_P0_stack.delete_popped() and returns the last value of err (OCSD_OK at that point, because each addElem or traceInstrToWP failure returns before this line). Error returns leave popped elements undeleted.

functions.name: TrcPktProcEtmV4I::onReset
functions.prose_contract: If m_isInit is false it returns OCSD_RESP_FATAL_NOT_INIT and changes nothing. Otherwise it calls InitProcessorState and returns OCSD_RESP_CONT. InitProcessorState clears the buffered packet data (m_currPacketData), calls initNextPacket on the current packet, sets m_update_on_unsync_packet_index to 0, sets the packet function to iNotSync, the packet index to 0, m_is_sync, m_first_trace_info and m_sent_notsync_packet to false, m_process_state to PROC_HDR and calls initStartState on the current packet.

functions.name: TrcPktProcEtmV4I::onFlush
functions.prose_contract: If m_isInit is false it returns OCSD_RESP_FATAL_NOT_INIT; otherwise it returns OCSD_RESP_CONT. In both cases it changes no member state and does not look at or emit any buffered packet data (the code comment says full packets are sent immediately and only a partial packet may be pending).

functions.name: TrcPktProcEtmV4I::BuildIPacketTable
functions.prose_contract: Void. Fills the 256-entry m_i_table: all entries are first set to ETM4_PKT_I_RESERVED with the iPktReserved handler, then the header bytes that have defined packets get their pkt_type and handler (extension, trace info, timestamp, exception, cycle count, speculation, conditional, event, context, address, Q and atom packets and others). Several entries depend on m_config: 0x05 (function return) gets the no-payload handler only for a Cortex-M profile with a v8 architecture and FullVersion >= 0x42, otherwise its handler stays iPktReserved; 0x07 (exception return) gets iPktNoPayload for MajVersion < 5, and for MajVersion >= 5 gets either the ignore type with the no-payload handler (if ETE_TRACE_ERET_AS_IGNORE is defined at compile time) or iPktInvalidCfg (if not); with MajVersion >= 5, 0x0A and 0x0B get the transaction start/commit types and 0x09 the ITE packet only if MinVersion >= 3; entries 0x70 (ignore) need FullVersion >= 0x43, 0x88 (timestamp marker) FullVersion >= 0x46, and 0xB0-0xB9 (source address packets) FullVersion >= 0x50; Q packets are enabled only if hasQElem(), with certain Q type codes left reserved; many data-trace and conditional-trace entries use iPktInvalidCfg when their feature is not enabled. It returns nothing and has no failure path. Partly read: I only checked the middle table entries (about 1344-1500) and the atom loops by pattern, not entry by entry.

functions.name: TrcPktProcEtmV4I::iPktCycleCntF123
functions.prose_contract: Void. Called for each byte of a cycle-count packet with the newest byte in lastByte; it uses m_curr_packet.type (F1, F2 or F3) and the number of bytes in m_currPacketData. When the packet has 1 byte it first sets m_count_done and m_commit_done to false and m_has_count to true; then for F3 it sets the commit-element count to bits 3:2 of the byte plus 1 only if commitOpt1 is false, sets the cycle count to getCCThreshold() plus bits 1:0, and sets m_process_state to SEND_PKT; for F1 with bit 0 set it clears m_has_count and sets m_count_done, and if commitOpt1 is true it sets m_commit_done (F2 with one byte only gets the flag reset). When the packet is F2 with 2 bytes it sets the cycle count to getCCThreshold() plus bits 3:0, the commit-element count to bits 7:4 plus (MaxSpecDepth-15 if bit 0 is set, else 1), and SEND_PKT. Otherwise (any other size, F1 continuation bytes) it sets m_commit_done from the cleared bit 7 if commit is not yet done, else m_count_done likewise. After that, for F1 only, if both m_commit_done and m_count_done are set it parses the buffer: if commitOpt1 is false it extracts a commit field from index 1 and sets the commit elements; if m_has_count it extracts the count field and sets the cycle count to that value plus getCCThreshold(), else sets the cycle count to 0; and sets SEND_PKT. Otherwise the cycle count and process state are left unchanged.

functions.name: T_FUNC(empty_policy, "empty policy")
functions.prose_contract: Generated function t_empty_policy_func (static, from the T_FUNC macro; both arguments are unused). It creates a temporary policy file containing only the comment line "# empty policy", calls pam_start on it with a scripted conversation, and if pam_start does not return PAM_SUCCESS it prints the code and returns 0 without closing the temporary file or calling pam_end. Otherwise it calls pam_authenticate, pam_setcred, pam_acct_mgmt, pam_chauthtok, pam_open_session and pam_close_session with flags 0, prints each result, and returns nonzero only if all six returned PAM_SYSTEM_ERR (the results are ANDed). Before returning it calls pam_end with the last status and closes the temporary file.

functions.name: T_FUNC(mod_return, "module return value")
functions.prose_contract: Generated function t_mod_return_func (static, from the T_FUNC macro; arguments unused). For each entry of the static table t_pam_return_cases (currently one entry: PAM_AUTH facility, PAM_SM_AUTHENTICATE, two PAM_REQUIRED modules both returning PAM_SUCCESS) it creates a temporary policy file with two lines of the form "facility control-flag pam_return_so error=name" (pam_return_so comes from the PAM_RETURN_SO environment variable), calls pam_start on it, and if that fails prints the code, closes the file and moves to the next case. Otherwise it calls the pam primitive selected by the table's primitive field (a switch without a default, so pam_err keeps its pam_start value for an unknown primitive), prints its return value, calls pam_end, prints "here" and closes the file. It then returns 1 whether or not the primitive's result matched the table's result field, which the function does not read (nothing in its body compares against it).

functions.name: T_FUNC(empty_input, "empty input")
functions.prose_contract: Generated function t_empty_input_func (static, from the T_FUNC macro; arguments unused). It creates an empty temporary file and calls orw_expect with expected word NULL, 0 lines, EOF expected and EOL not expected, closes the file, and returns orw_expect's result. orw_expect runs openpam_readword on the file and returns 1 only if no word was returned, the line counter stayed 0, the stream is at EOF, and the next character read is not a newline; it also calls err(1, ...) if the stream is in an error state. No data is written, so no rewind is done.

functions.name: T_FUNC(single_quoted_comment, "single-quoted comment")
functions.prose_contract: Generated function t_single_quoted_comment_func (static, from the T_FUNC macro; arguments unused). It writes the line " '# comment'" (a leading space, then a single-quoted text starting with a hash) to a temporary file, rewinds it, and calls orw_expect expecting the word "# comment", 0 lines advanced, EOF not reached and the next character a newline. It closes the file and returns orw_expect's result: 1 only if openpam_readword returned exactly that word, did not count a line, did not reach EOF and left the newline unread.

functions.name: T_FUNC(final_percent, "template ends with %")
functions.prose_contract: Generated function t_final_percent_func (static, from the T_FUNC macro; arguments unused). It calls openpam_subst(NULL, buf, &bufsize, template) with the template "test%" (the array holds more bytes after its first NUL, which I did not check openpam_subst against) and a 20-byte buffer holding "Squeamish Ossifrage", then returns nonzero only if the call returned PAM_SUCCESS, bufsize equals sizeof("test%") (6) and the buffer contains "test%" (the three checks are ANDed; t_compare_sz and t_compare_str report mismatches). It touches no files or global PAM state.

functions.name: pamk5_authenticate
functions.prose_contract: Takes args and returns a PAM status; slice cut the head and the real function is pamk5_authenticate, not pam_sm_authenticate. If use_authtok is set without force_first_pass it logs an error and sets force_first_pass. It calls pamk5_context_new (any non-success status is returned through the exit code, which calls pamk5_context_free), and returns PAM_USER_UNKNOWN if pamk5_should_ignore says to ignore the user. It then calls pamk5_password_auth. If that returns PAM_NEW_AUTHTOK_REQD: with fail_pwchange it becomes PAM_AUTH_ERR; with defer_pwchange it sets ctx->expired and becomes PAM_SUCCESS; with force_pwchange it prints an info message, moves PAM_AUTHTOK into PAM_OLDAUTHTOK when available, clears PAM_AUTHTOK, sets use_first_pass and returns the result of pamk5_password_change; with none of those flags the status PAM_NEW_AUTHTOK_REQD is kept. Any status other than PAM_SUCCESS is logged and returned. It then calls pamk5_authorized (non-success returned), sets PAM_USER to ctx->name unless expired or no_update_user (errors only logged), logs the authentication, and calls pam_set_data("pam_krb5", ctx, pamk5_context_destroy): on failure it logs, calls pamk5_context_free and returns PAM_SERVICE_ERR (the common exit code then calls pamk5_context_free again; I did not check whether that second call is a harmless no-op). On success it records that the context is stored, and unless no_ccache is set or the context is expired it returns the result of pamk5_cache_init_random with the obtained credentials. At the exit label the credentials are freed only if both creds and ctx are non-NULL; args->ctx is set to NULL only if the context was stored; and on any non-success status the stored context is cleared with pam_set_data(NULL) if this call stored it, otherwise pamk5_context_free is called.

functions.name: pamk5_password
functions.prose_contract: Takes args and only_auth and returns a PAM status. If ignore_root is set or minimum_uid > 0 and pam_get_user succeeds and pamk5_should_ignore says to ignore that user, it returns PAM_IGNORE; before that, only when only_auth is false, it frees and clears the configured banner and calls pamk5_password_prompt (result ignored), and with only_auth true it touches neither. Otherwise, if args->config->ctx is NULL it calls pamk5_context_new and registers the new context with pam_set_data("pam_krb5", ..., pamk5_context_destroy): either failure returns PAM_AUTHTOK_ERR, and on a pam_set_data failure the newly created context is left in args->config->ctx unregistered and not freed here; on success it records the context as registered and sets args->ctx to NULL at exit. If the context is expired and has no creds and neither force_first_pass nor use_first_pass is set it shows a "Password expired" message. It then returns the result of pamk5_password_change(args, only_auth) immediately when only_auth is true; otherwise, if that succeeded and the context is expired, it sets force_first_pass, calls pamk5_password_auth (a non-success status is returned), logs the principal, clears ctx->expired, returns the result of pamk5_cache_init_random and frees the credentials. In all exits a non-success status of PAM_SERVICE_ERR, PAM_AUTH_ERR or PAM_AUTHINFO_UNAVAIL is changed to PAM_AUTHTOK_ERR and other statuses are returned unchanged. The local pass buffer is never assigned, so its cleanup does nothing.

functions.name: LOG_FUNCTION(crit,   LOG_CRIT)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function putil_crit(pargs, fmt, ...), a printf-style logger at priority LOG_CRIT. It starts a va_list, calls log_vplain(pargs, LOG_CRIT, fmt, args) and ends the va_list; it returns nothing. log_vplain does not suppress messages at this priority; with pargs non-NULL and pargs->user set it formats the message and logs "(user NAME) MSG" via pam_syslog, with pargs non-NULL and no user it uses pam_vsyslog on pargs->pamh, and with pargs NULL it formats the message and logs it with syslog and LOG_AUTHPRIV (a formatting failure logs a critical syslog line and drops the message).

functions.name: LOG_FUNCTION(err,    LOG_ERR)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function putil_err(pargs, fmt, ...), the same as putil_crit but at priority LOG_ERR: it calls log_vplain(pargs, LOG_ERR, fmt, args) and returns nothing. The message is logged through pam_syslog (with a "(user NAME) " prefix when pargs->user is set), pam_vsyslog when pargs has no user, or plain syslog with LOG_AUTHPRIV when pargs is NULL; no priority filtering happens at this level.

functions.name: LOG_FUNCTION(notice, LOG_NOTICE)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function putil_notice(pargs, fmt, ...), the same as putil_crit but at priority LOG_NOTICE: it calls log_vplain(pargs, LOG_NOTICE, fmt, args) and returns nothing; nothing is suppressed at this level and routing (pam_syslog with a user prefix, pam_vsyslog, or syslog with LOG_AUTHPRIV when pargs is NULL) is as in log_vplain.

functions.name: LOG_FUNCTION(debug,  LOG_DEBUG)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function putil_debug(pargs, fmt, ...), which calls log_vplain(pargs, LOG_DEBUG, fmt, args) and returns nothing. log_vplain returns without logging anything when pargs is NULL or pargs->debug is false; otherwise the message is logged as for the other levels (pam_syslog with a "(user NAME) " prefix if pargs->user is set, else pam_vsyslog).

functions.name: LOG_FUNCTION(crit,   LOG_CRIT)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function putil_crit_pam(pargs, status, fmt, ...) from the same macro invocation, at priority LOG_CRIT. It starts a va_list and calls log_pam(pargs, LOG_CRIT, status, fmt, args), returns nothing. log_pam formats the message (and returns silently after a critical syslog line if formatting fails); with pargs NULL it logs the message via log_plain with no PAM error text; with pargs non-NULL it logs the message alone if status is PAM_SUCCESS, otherwise the message followed by ": " and pam_strerror(pargs->pamh, status), and frees the formatted message.

functions.name: LOG_FUNCTION(err,    LOG_ERR)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function putil_err_pam(pargs, status, fmt, ...) from the same macro invocation, at priority LOG_ERR: it calls log_pam(pargs, LOG_ERR, status, fmt, args) and returns nothing. The message is logged alone if pargs is NULL or status is PAM_SUCCESS, otherwise followed by ": " and pam_strerror(pargs->pamh, status); formatting failure drops the message after a critical syslog line.

functions.name: LOG_FUNCTION(notice, LOG_NOTICE)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function putil_notice_pam(pargs, status, fmt, ...) from the same macro invocation, at priority LOG_NOTICE: it calls log_pam(pargs, LOG_NOTICE, status, fmt, args) and returns nothing, logging the message alone if pargs is NULL or status is PAM_SUCCESS, otherwise followed by ": " and pam_strerror(pargs->pamh, status).

functions.name: LOG_FUNCTION(debug,  LOG_DEBUG)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function putil_debug_pam(pargs, status, fmt, ...) from the same macro invocation, at priority LOG_DEBUG: it calls log_pam(pargs, LOG_DEBUG, status, fmt, args) and returns nothing. log_pam returns without logging if pargs is NULL or pargs->debug is false; otherwise it logs the formatted message, followed by ": " and pam_strerror(pargs->pamh, status) when status is not PAM_SUCCESS.

functions.name: test_print_range
functions.prose_contract: Prints a number range to stdout and returns a count. With first, last, chars (characters already on the line) and limit it first computes needed: the decimal digits of first (0 digits if first is 0), plus, only if last > first, the digits of last plus 1, plus 2 if chars > 0. If limit > 0 and chars + needed > limit: if chars <= limit it prints ", " (only when chars > 0) followed by "..." and returns 5 when chars > 0 or 3 when chars == 0; if chars > limit it prints nothing and returns 0. Otherwise (limit is 0 or the text fits) it prints ", " when chars > 0, then "first-" when last > first, then last, and returns needed. When last < first it prints only last but the returned count is the digit count of first (plus 2 if chars > 0), so the return value equals the printed length only when last >= first or the digit counts match.

functions.name: pam_sm_chauthtok
functions.prose_contract: Takes pamh, flags, argc, argv and returns a PAM status. It copies the default params and calls parse (a non-success status is returned). flags must contain PAM_PRELIM_CHECK or PAM_UPDATE_AUTHTOK, otherwise it returns PAM_SERVICE_ERR; the matching ask-old-password option (prelim or update) decides whether to ask. If asking and getuid() != 0 it prompts for the old password and stores it with pam_set_item(PAM_OLDAUTHTOK) (any failure, or an empty reply giving PAM_AUTHTOK_RECOVERY_ERR, is returned). With PAM_PRELIM_CHECK it then returns the current status (PAM_SUCCESS here) without choosing or setting any new password. Otherwise it fetches PAM_USER and PAM_OLDAUTHTOK (failures returned), builds a fake passwd for non-UNIX users or calls getpwnam (PAM_USER_UNKNOWN if the user does not exist) and, if the check-old-password option is set and getuid() != 0, verifies oldpass against the password or shadow hash with crypt (PAM_AUTH_ERR if oldpass is missing or does not match); in the getpwnam case it zeroes pw_passwd afterwards and returns any error status. With the use_authtok option it reads PAM_AUTHTOK and returns PAM_AUTHTOK_ERR if it is missing or too long under enforcement, runs the strength check and, if the password is weak, says so and returns PAM_AUTHTOK_ERR only when enforcement applies (the say result is ignored), and on this branch it does not set a new token. Otherwise it loops: it prints introduction/explanation messages (a failed say there is returned), generates a random password (if generation fails and only random passwords are allowed it says so, ignoring the say result, and returns PAM_AUTHTOK_ERR; a failed say about the random password only discards it), prompts for the new password (failure or empty reply returns PAM_AUTHTOK_ERR after wiping the random password; if strdup fails it returns the current status, which is PAM_SUCCESS at that point, without setting anything), checks length and strength (with enforcement failures set PAM_AUTHTOK_ERR and request a retry; messages from say are ignored), prompts a second time and compares (a mismatch prints a message and gives PAM_AUTHTOK_ERR with a retry only if the say succeeded; an empty reply gives PAM_AUTHTOK_ERR), and on success calls pam_set_item(PAM_AUTHTOK, newpass), whose result becomes the status. It overwrites the typed and random passwords and frees newpass. If a retry was requested and retries remain it says the retry message and loops if that say succeeded, otherwise returns the say status; the final return is the current status.

functions.name: isolation_protocol
functions.prose_contract: Takes no arguments and returns an int. It calls send_Initiation_LFSR, writes 0x04 to PNP_CONFIG_CONTROL (reset the CSN of all cards), then loops csn from 1 while csn < PNP_MAX_CARDS: each iteration sets the global logdevs to 0, writes PNP_WAKE 0, writes the global rd_port to PNP_SET_RD_DATA, writes PNP_SERIAL_ISOLATION to the address port, busy-waits about 1 ms with DELAY(1000), then calls get_serial(data); if it succeeds it calls dump_resdata(data, csn) (which sets logdevs for that card and, per the reviewer, mallocs and frees resource buffers; I did not read dump_resdata beyond locating malloc/free at pnpinfo.c:495-514), and if it fails the loop breaks. It returns csn - 1: the number of iterations that succeeded before the first get_serial failure, or PNP_MAX_CARDS - 1 if none failed. On return logdevs is 0 if the loop ended on a get_serial failure, else the value left by the last dump_resdata. The function itself allocates nothing and takes no locks.

functions.name: cnd_wait
functions.prose_contract: Static inline wrapper in the POSIX threads shim. If cnd or mtx is NULL it returns thrd_error. Otherwise it calls pthread_cond_wait(&cnd->cond, &mtx->mutex) (which releases the mutex while waiting and reacquires it before returning, and may wake spuriously) and returns thrd_error if that call returned a nonzero error code, else thrd_success. It allocates or frees nothing.

functions.name: pt_blk_event
functions.prose_contract: Returns -pte_invalid if decoder or uevent is NULL and -pte_bad_query if decoder->process_event is clear. Otherwise it switches on the type of decoder->event: enabled sets variant.enabled.resumed when decoder->ip equals the event ip and calls pt_blk_process_enabled; async_disabled returns -pte_bad_query unless decoder->ip equals variant.async_disabled.at (this check does not look at ip_suppressed) and then, like disabled, calls pt_blk_process_disabled; async_branch returns -pte_bad_query unless decoder->ip equals variant.async_branch.from (also without checking ip_suppressed) and calls pt_blk_process_async_branch; async_paging, async_vmcs, exec_mode and tsx return -pte_bad_query when the event ip is not suppressed and does not match decoder->ip, then call the paging, vmcs, exec_mode or tsx process function (paging and vmcs events themselves skip the check); overflow and stop call their process functions; exstop and mwait return -pte_bad_query on an IP mismatch (only when the ip is not suppressed and the decoder is enabled) and otherwise clear process_event; pwre, pwrx, ptwrite, tick, cbr and mnt just clear process_event; an event type with no case falls out of the switch unchanged. Any negative status from a process function is returned immediately, before the event is copied to the user. After the switch it copies min(size, sizeof(event)) bytes of the event to uevent and returns the result of pt_blk_proceed_trailing_event(decoder, NULL) (a status or negative error; I did not read it). The process_* helpers are not read here, so whether they clear process_event is not claimed.

functions.name: pt_df_fetch
functions.prose_contract: Selects the decoder function for the packet at pos. It returns -pte_internal if dfun or config is NULL; otherwise it sets *dfun to NULL first (so *dfun is NULL on the -pte_nosync and -pte_eos returns below). It returns -pte_nosync if pos is NULL, before config->begin or after config->end, and -pte_eos if pos equals config->end. It reads the opcode byte and picks a static decoder function, storing it in *dfun and returning 0: masked opcodes tnt_8, cyc, tip, fup, tip_pge and tip_pgd (checked in that order), pad, mode, tsc, mtc, otherwise pt_decode_unknown. For the extended opcode it returns -pte_eos if there is no following byte, then selects on that byte: ptw (masked), psb, ovf, tnt_64, psbend, cbr, pip, tma, stop, vmcs, exstop (either form), mwait, pwre, pwrx, or pt_decode_unknown for others; for ext2 it returns -pte_eos if the next byte is missing and selects mnt or pt_decode_unknown. It reads only the input bytes, writes only *dfun, and allocates nothing.

functions.name: pt_enc_next
functions.prose_contract: Slice shows only the first half of pt_enc_next. Encodes one packet into the encoder's buffer: it returns -pte_invalid if encoder or packet is NULL; otherwise it switches on packet->type. For most types it first calls pt_reserve (a negative result, for example -pte_eos when the packet does not fit before config.end or -pte_internal if encoder->pos is NULL, is returned and nothing is written), writes the bytes at encoder->pos, stores the advanced position in encoder->pos and returns the number of bytes written. Types fup, tip, tip_pge and tip_pgd return the result of pt_encode_ip. tnt_8 returns -pte_bad_packet if bit_size >= 7, checked before pt_reserve. tnt_64 calls pt_reserve first and then returns -pte_invalid if bit_size >= pt_pl_tnt_64_bits or the payload has bits at or above the stop bit. mode returns -pte_bad_packet after the reservation for a leaf other than exec or tsx. tma returns -pte_bad_packet after the reservation if fc has bits outside pt_pl_tma_fc_mask. cyc returns -pte_bad_packet before the reservation if the value needs more than pt_pl_cyc_max_size bytes. ptw returns pt_ptw_size's negative error before the reservation. ppt_unknown, ppt_invalid and any unlisted type return -pte_bad_opc. encoder->pos is only assigned just before a successful return, so on the error returns made by this function itself it is unchanged and no bytes are published (pt_encode_ip's own behaviour was not read).

functions.name: pt_enc_next
functions.prose_contract: Encodes one packet into the encoder's buffer and returns the number of bytes written (positive) on success, or a negative error code. It returns -pte_invalid if encoder or packet is NULL. The caller does not need to reserve space: each packet case calls pt_reserve itself, and returns its negative result (-pte_eos if the bytes would pass config.end, -pte_internal if encoder->pos is NULL) without writing. The packet types pad, psb, psbend, ovf, tnt_8, tnt_64, mode, pip, tsc, cbr, tma, mtc, cyc, stop, vmcs, mnt, exstop, mwait, pwre, pwrx and ptw write their opcode and payload bytes at encoder->pos; fup, tip, tip_pge and tip_pgd return pt_encode_ip's result. Invalid payloads: tnt_8 bit_size >= 7 gives -pte_bad_packet (before the reservation); tnt_64 with bit_size >= pt_pl_tnt_64_bits or payload bits at or above the stop bit gives -pte_invalid (after the reservation; not -pte_bad_packet); a mode leaf other than exec or tsx gives -pte_bad_packet; tma fc outside pt_pl_tma_fc_mask gives -pte_bad_packet; a cyc value needing more than pt_pl_cyc_max_size bytes gives -pte_bad_packet; a ptw plc for which pt_ptw_size is negative returns that negative value; ppt_unknown, ppt_invalid and any other type give -pte_bad_opc. encoder->pos is advanced only on the success path, so it stays unchanged on the error returns made by this function itself (pt_encode_ip's own behaviour was not read).

functions.name: pt_insn_event
functions.prose_contract: Returns -pte_invalid if decoder or uevent is NULL and -pte_bad_query if decoder->process_event is clear.
