It then steps a nondeterministic automaton character by character while characters remain and the next state set is non-empty, handling the operations MATCH, ATSTART, ANY, WORD, NOTWORD, DIGIT, NOTDIGIT, SPACE, NOTSPACE, BOUNDARY, ANYSTAR, FORK, GOTO, ACCEPT, and character classes (CC_INC and CC_EXC with values and ranges); ACCEPT ends the scan with success. After the loop, if the remaining state set contains an ACCEPT (after following GOTOs) it returns 1; otherwise 0.

functions.name: lookupName
functions.prose_contract: Static function lookupName (sqlite3.c:108312-108888) resolves a column reference expression against the name contexts and returns a Walker code. It searches the FROM tables (and joins with USING/NATURAL columns, rowid aliases, trigger new/old rows, the RETURNING and alias lists, and outer name contexts) counting matches in cnt. Partly read: I read the counting logic and the exits, not each lookup branch. If cnt is not exactly 1 at the end it deletes the partial full-join match list when relevant and reports an error with sqlite3ErrorMsg: "no such column" when cnt is 0 or "ambiguous column name" when more than one match, with the db/table/column qualifiers or, for a double-quoted name that matched nothing, a message suggesting a string literal, and records the error offset; in this case the function ends through the common exit and returns WRC_Abort (the error is set here, not left for the caller). A misused aliased aggregate, aliased window function or row value also sets an error message and returns WRC_Abort at once. If exactly one match is found it converts the expression in place (it frees pLeft and pRight of the expression and turns it into a TK_COLUMN or related node), updates the matching table's colUsed bits, calls the authorizer read hook if configured, propagates usage counts through the enclosing name contexts, and returns WRC_Prune. The special handling of a bare name that matches no column (the block at 108750-108779, which includes a TK_NULL conversion for some rowid cases) was not read, so I make no claim on it.

functions.name: resolveExprStep

functions.name: sqlite3CodeSubselect
functions.prose_contract: sqlite3CodeSubselect(pParse, pExpr) (sqlite3.c:114085-114203) generates code for a scalar subquery (TK_SELECT) or EXISTS (TK_EXISTS) and returns the register holding the result, or 0 on failure. functions.name: sqlite3CreateIndex
functions.prose_contract: sqlite3CreateIndex(pParse, pName1, pName2, pTblName, pList, onError, pStart, pPIWhere, sortOrder, ifNotExist, idxType) (sqlite3.c:126926-127516) creates an index or the implied index of a constraint; it returns nothing. functions.name: sqlite3CreateIndex
functions.prose_contract: Same function as the previous entry (sqlite3CreateIndex, sqlite3.c:126926-127516); this slice (127367-127628) covers its tail and the start of the next function (sqlite3DropIndex), so the head was cut. functions.prose_contract: Static function multiSelectOrderBy(pParse, p, pDest) (sqlite3.c:148352-148666; the packet name did not mention the function but it is in the file) implements a compound SELECT (UNION, EXCEPT, INTERSECT) with an ORDER BY by running each side as a co-routine and merging. functions.name: sqlite3SelectPrep

functions.name: sqlite3RunVacuum
functions.prose_contract: sqlite3RunVacuum(pzErrMsg, db, iDb, pOut) (sqlite3.c:157275-157540; VACUUM and VACUUM INTO) returns an SQLite result code. It returns SQLITE_ERROR with an error message, before changing anything, if the connection is not in autocommit mode ("cannot VACUUM from within a transaction"), if other statements are active (nVdbeActive > 1), or if pOut is given and is not text; these preconditions apply to both plain VACUUM and VACUUM INTO. functions.name: whereOmitNoopJoin
functions.prose_contract: Static function whereOmitNoopJoin(pWInfo, notReady) (sqlite3.c:170833-170904; the packet name sqlite3WhereOmitNoopJoin does not exist) marks the loops of LEFT JOIN tables whose columns are unused as omitted, so no code is generated for them, and returns the updated notReady bitmask. functions.name: sqlite3WhereBegin
functions.prose_contract: Builds the code-generation plan and the VDBE loop code for a WHERE clause over pTabList and returns a newly allocated WhereInfo (the return at sqlite3.c:171765, after the codegen loop at 171718-171760), or returns a null pointer in the failure cases below. Return 0 at 171182: pTabList->nSrc is greater than BMS; it raises the error "at most %d tables in a join" through sqlite3ErrorMsg first, and no WhereInfo has been allocated yet. All other failures go to the label whereBeginError (171768), which, if pWInfo is non-null, restores pParse->nQueryLoop from pWInfo->savedNQueryLoop, frees it with whereInfoFree and returns 0. The gotos are: db->mallocFailed after the WhereInfo allocation (171204, where pWInfo is freed and set to 0 first, so only the return remains), pParse->nErr after the WHERE-term analysis (171295), a nonzero rc from whereLoopAddAll (171383, 171402), db->mallocFailed after wherePathSolver (171408, 171412), pParse->nErr after the optimiser stage (171430), db->mallocFailed before the code-generation loop (171712), and pParse->nErr or db->mallocFailed inside the loop (171722, 171749). functions.name: sqlite3_test_control
functions.prose_contract: Variadic dispatcher for the SQLITE_TESTCTRL_* test hooks (this slice covers the part of the function starting inside its switch). In a build with SQLITE_UNTESTABLE it does nothing and returns 0 (186793-186794, 187355-187356). Otherwise it reads the extra arguments for op with va_arg (types must match what the chosen case reads), runs that case, and then returns rc at the single return at 187356. rc starts at 0 (186792) and is set only by these cases: BITVEC_TEST (the result of sqlite3BitvecBuiltinTest, 186884), FAULT_INSTALL (sqlite3FaultSim(0), 186910), PENDING_BYTE (the PENDING_BYTE value, 186943), ASSERT (the int argument x, 186967; x stays 0 if assert is compiled out), ALWAYS (ALWAYS(x) when x is nonzero, else 0, 187024), BYTEORDER (SQLITE_BYTEORDER*100 + SQLITE_LITTLEENDIAN*10 + SQLITE_BIGENDIAN, 187040), ISINIT (SQLITE_ERROR when sqlite3GlobalConfig.isInit is 0, 187174), PARSER_COVERAGE (SQLITE_ERROR when sqlite3ParserCoverage(out) is nonzero, 187222, only when YYCOVERAGE is defined) and TUNE (SQLITE_NOTFOUND when id is 0 or outside plus or minus SQLITE_NTUNE, 187326, only when SQLITE_DEBUG is defined and SQLITE_OMIT_WSD is not). There is no default case, so an unrecognized op also leaves rc at 0. IMPOSTER holds db->mutex while it looks up the schema name and updates db->init, and leaves the mutex before break (187197-187207). SEEK_COUNT writes sqlite3BtreeSeekCount of the main database to *pn (187255).

functions.name: sqlite3_test_control
functions.prose_contract: Variadic dispatcher for the SQLITE_TESTCTRL_* test hooks (this slice covers the tail of the function, from TRACEFLAGS to the end). In a build with SQLITE_UNTESTABLE it does nothing and returns 0. Otherwise it reads the arguments for the chosen op with va_arg, runs the matching case and returns rc at the single return (187356). rc starts at 0 and is changed only by BITVEC_TEST, FAULT_INSTALL, PENDING_BYTE, ASSERT, ALWAYS, BYTEORDER, ISINIT, PARSER_COVERAGE (when YYCOVERAGE is defined) and TUNE; no other case assigns it, and there is no default case, so an unrecognized op returns 0. In this tail: RESULT_INTREAL calls sqlite3ResultIntReal on the sqlite3_context argument (187238-187239) and keeps rc; SEEK_COUNT stores sqlite3BtreeSeekCount(db->aDb->pBt) in *pn (187255); TUNE writes Tuning(id) from *piValue for 0<id<=SQLITE_NTUNE, writes *piValue from Tuning(-id) for -SQLITE_NTUNE<=id<0, and otherwise sets rc to SQLITE_NOTFOUND (187321-187326); these TUNE and JSON_SELFCHECK bodies exist only when SQLITE_DEBUG is defined and SQLITE_OMIT_WSD is not, and JSON_SELFCHECK with those options reads *pOnOff and either stores the current bJsonSelfcheck into it when it is negative, or sets bJsonSelfcheck to its low 8 bits (187344-187349); without them it does nothing.

functions.name: sqlite3Fts3MsrCancel
functions.prose_contract: If pExpr->bEof is nonzero on entry, returns SQLITE_OK without touching pExpr (194872, 194880). Otherwise it saves pExpr->iDocid, calls fts3EvalRestart, and then, while rc is SQLITE_OK and pExpr->iDocid differs from the saved value, calls fts3EvalNextRow and sets rc to FTS_CORRUPT_VTAB whenever pExpr->bEof is set after that call (194873-194878). That check runs after each advance, so FTS_CORRUPT_VTAB is returned if the end is reached on an advance even if the docid then happens to equal the saved one, and the result is also an error code from fts3EvalRestart or fts3EvalNextRow if they report one. It returns SQLITE_OK when the loop exits with rc unchanged, which includes when restart already leaves iDocid equal to the saved value. The single return is at 194880.

functions.name: sqlite3Fts3EvalPhrasePoslist
functions.prose_contract: Looks up the position list of phrase pExpr for column iCol in the current row and stores a pointer into *ppOut; *ppOut is set to 0 at 195118 before anything else. It returns SQLITE_OK with *ppOut still 0 when the phrase is restricted to a different column (195120-195121), when the phrase is not below an OR node while its docid does not match pCsr->iPrevId or it is at EOF (195147), when no position list is found (195218), or when the column list ends before iCol is reached (195228). If pExpr->iDocid equals pCsr->iPrevId and pExpr->bEof is zero, the phrase's current doclist pointer is used directly. Otherwise, for a phrase below an OR node it takes the nearest non-deferred ancestor pRun of the topmost NEAR ancestor pNear (or of pExpr itself when it has no NEAR ancestor), and, if pPhrase->bIncr is set, restarts pRun and advances it until it reaches the saved docid or hits EOF (195157-195168); if any ancestor was at EOF it advances pRun to EOF (195169-195173). Errors from fts3EvalRestart/fts3EvalNextRow are returned (195174), and FTS_CORRUPT_VTAB is returned when pRun->bEof differs from its value before the restart (195165-195167). It then scans the phrases in the NEAR chain, moving each one's cached OR poslist/docid until it reaches pCsr->iPrevId, and uses its own cached poslist only if every phrase matches that docid (195176-195216). Finally it skips column lists until it reaches iCol and sets *ppOut to the list only if the column found equals iCol, else 0 (195226-195237).

functions.name: sqlite3Fts3Incrmerge
functions.prose_contract: Performs incremental merging on the FTS3 table p, with a work quota nMerge (leaf pages to write) and a minimum segment count nMin that is raised to at least 2 in the level query (204395). It allocates one block holding the cursor, filter and writer and returns SQLITE_NOMEM if that fails (204377). Otherwise it loads the merge hint from the %_stat table and loops while rc is SQLITE_OK and nRem is positive (204382). Each pass finds the absolute level with the smallest number of segments that is at least MAX(2,nMin) via SQL_FIND_MERGE_LEVEL, optionally replaces it with the next entry popped from the hint when no such level exists or the hint's level is not later in the level order (204415-204426), and leaves the loop if the resulting segment count nSeg is not positive (204437). It returns FTS_CORRUPT_VTAB if the level number is negative or above nMod<<32 (204440-204442). Otherwise it merges the oldest nSeg segments of that level into one segment using the incremental writer, subtracts the pages written plus one from nRem, and records the remaining segments in the hint (204499-204505). A SegReaderStep result that is neither SQLITE_OK nor SQLITE_ROW finishes the cursor, leaves the loop and is returned (204476-204478). The loop ends without error when nRem is exhausted or no level qualifies; running out of hint entries alone does not end it. After the loop it writes the hint back to %_stat if it was changed and rc is SQLITE_OK (204522-204523), frees the block and the hint buffer, and returns rc (204526-204528); on errors rc is the first error code recorded by the helpers, which are not individually read here.

functions.name: jsonErrorFunc
functions.prose_contract: Generated SQL function json_error_position(X) (the scalar function jsonErrorFunc, argc==1). Builds a JsonParse s with s.db set to the connection (212538-212539). If argv[0] is a JSONB blob (jsonArgIsJsonb) the result value is whatever jsonbValidityCheck(&s,0,s.nBlob,1) returns. Otherwise it takes the text of argv[0] via sqlite3_value_text; if that is NULL (an SQL NULL argument or an out-of-memory failure) the function returns at once without setting a result and without calling jsonParseReset (212543-212544). Otherwise it converts the text to JSONB with jsonConvertTextToBlob: if that succeeds the position stays 0; if it fails with s.oom set the position becomes -1, and if it fails otherwise the position is one plus the number of non-UTF-8-continuation bytes among the first s.iErr bytes of the text, i.e. a 1-based character offset (212546-212557). After that it calls jsonParseReset(&s) and sets the SQL result with sqlite3_result_error_nomem when the position is negative, else with sqlite3_result_int64 of the position (212560-212564).

functions.name: rtreeBestIndex
functions.prose_contract: xBestIndex for the R-Tree virtual table. It first scans all constraints, including unusable ones, and sets bMatch if any has op SQLITE_INDEX_CONSTRAINT_MATCH (215500-215504); that scan is complete before the second loop begins, so a MATCH constraint that comes later in the array also sets bMatch. In the second loop, if bMatch is 0 and a constraint is usable, has iColumn<=0 and op SQLITE_INDEX_CONSTRAINT_EQ (a rowid lookup), it clears argvIndex and omit for all earlier constraints, sets idxNum=1, argvIndex=1 and omit=1 for that constraint, sets estimatedCost=30.0, estimatedRows=1 and idxFlags=SQLITE_INDEX_SCAN_UNIQUE, and returns SQLITE_OK at once (215510-215532). Otherwise a usable constraint on a coordinate column (1<=iColumn<=nDim2) or a usable MATCH constraint with op EQ, GT, LE, LT, GE or MATCH appends two characters (the operator and the column digit) to zIdxStr, sets its argvIndex to the running count and sets omit to 0 for EQ, GT and LT and to 1 for LE, GE and MATCH (215535-215555); other ops are skipped. The loop stops early when the local zIdxStr buffer is full (215507). After the loop it sets idxNum=2 and needToFreeIdxStr=1, and when iIdx>0 allocates idxStr with sqlite3_malloc and returns SQLITE_NOMEM if that fails (215559-215566); otherwise it copies the string, sets estimatedRows to pRtree->nRowEst >> (iIdx/2) and estimatedCost to 6.0 times that, and returns rc, which is SQLITE_OK as initialised (215573).

functions.name: rbuSetupCheckpoint
functions.prose_contract: Void helper that prepares an RBU handle for the checkpoint stage, working through p->rc and p->eStage. If pState is NULL it first sets p->eStage to 0, even if p->rc is already an error, and when p->rc is SQLITE_OK it runs "SELECT * FROM sqlite_schema" on p->dbMain and stores the result in p->rc (224308-224313). If p->rc is SQLITE_OK it then sets p->eStage to RBU_STAGE_CAPTURE and runs "PRAGMA main.wal_checkpoint=restart"; its result goes into p->rc unless it is SQLITE_NOTICE, which is ignored (224343-224348). If p->rc is still SQLITE_OK and p->nFrame>0 it sets p->eStage to RBU_STAGE_CKPT, p->nStep to pState->nRow (or 0 when pState is NULL), allocates p->aBuf of p->pgsz bytes with rbuMalloc, and sets p->iWalCksum from rbuShmChecksum (224350-224355). If p->rc is still SQLITE_OK after that, then when p->nFrame is 0, or pState is non-NULL and its iWalCksum differs from p->iWalCksum, it sets p->rc to SQLITE_DONE and p->eStage to RBU_STAGE_DONE; otherwise it computes p->nPagePerSector from the target file's sector size (at least 1) and calls xSync on the WAL file, storing the result in p->rc (224357-224378). With an earlier error in p->rc and a non-NULL pState nothing is changed. On a failure in the checkpoint step eStage can stay RBU_STAGE_CAPTURE, and p->iWalCksum is not set when nFrame is 0.

functions.name: rbuMoveOalFile
functions.prose_contract: Void helper for the MOVE stage of an RBU update; asserts p->eStage is RBU_STAGE_MOVE and p->rc is SQLITE_OK with p->zErrmsg zero (224531-224532). It builds the names "<f>-oal" and "<f>-wal", where f is the main database filename of p->dbMain, or of p->dbRbu when rbuIsVacuum(p) (224520-224529). If either allocation fails it sets p->rc to SQLITE_NOMEM, sets no error message, and leaves the connections and files alone (224533-224534). Otherwise it applies rbuFileSuffix3 to both names, finalizes the object iterator, closes p->dbRbu and p->dbMain and sets both pointers to 0 (224544-224552). It then opens a new handle on p->zTarget with rbuOpenDbhandle and, if that returned a handle, takes its lock with rbuLockDatabase, storing the result in p->rc (224554-224558). If p->rc is SQLITE_OK it renames oal to wal with p->xRename (224560-224562); a rename is therefore attempted even when no handle was opened as long as p->rc is still OK. The new handle is closed and cleared if p->rc is an error, or the update is a vacuum, or rbuExclusiveCheckpoint(dbMain)==0 (224564-224570). If p->rc is OK it then calls rbuOpenDatabase(p, dbMain, 0) and rbuSetupCheckpoint(p, 0) (224572-224575). Both name strings are freed on every path (224578-224579).

functions.name: sqlite3rbu_step
functions.prose_contract: Performs one unit of work for an RBU handle and returns p->rc, or SQLITE_NOMEM when p is NULL (224968, 225085-225087). It switches on p->eStage. RBU_STAGE_OAL: for a vacuum with p->nProgress==0 and p->rc OK it first creates the target schema and copies user_version and application_id (224975-224979). It then loops over the object iterator while p->rc is SQLITE_OK: for an iterator in cleanup state it deletes the rbu_tmp table rows when the update is not a vacuum and pIter->abIndexed is set; otherwise it prepares the statements, steps the SELECT, and if a row was returned increments p->nProgress and p->nStep and returns rbuStep(p) directly (224981-225001); if no row was returned it resets the SELECT into p->rc and sets p->nStep to 0, and the iterator advances (225003-225008). The cleanup and table-advance paths do not increment nProgress. When the loop ends with p->rc OK it saves the state with RBU_STAGE_MOVE, increments the schema cookie, commits on dbMain and dbRbu while rc stays OK, and sets eStage to RBU_STAGE_MOVE (225011-225021). RBU_STAGE_MOVE: if p->rc is OK it calls rbuMoveOalFile and increments p->nProgress (225027-225029). RBU_STAGE_CKPT: if p->rc is OK, when p->nStep>=p->nFrame it syncs the target file, maps shared memory and writes p->iMaxFrame to word 24, and on success sets eStage to RBU_STAGE_DONE and p->rc to SQLITE_DONE (225036-225054); otherwise it checkpoints frames one sector at a time (225066-225075); nProgress is incremented after either branch (225077). Other stages do nothing. The return value is the p->rc held at that point.

functions.name: fts5yy_reduce
functions.prose_contract: Parser-generated reduce step of the FTS5 query grammar parser (Lemon). The slice cuts the head; the function starts at 237523. It starts from the stack top fts5yymsp = fts5yypParser->fts5yytos (237537), then runs the semantic action of rule fts5yyruleno through a large switch (for example case 0 calls sqlite3Fts5ParseFinished(pParse, ...) at 237551; the default case does nothing, 237690-237691). After the switch it takes the rule's left-hand-side symbol fts5yygoto from fts5yyRuleInfoLhs and fts5yysize from fts5yyRuleInfoNRhs, which is zero or a negative number (minus the length of the right-hand side), looks up the new state with fts5yy_find_reduce_action on the state found fts5yysize entries below the top (237695-237697), moves the local pointer by fts5yysize+1 entries, stores it back into fts5yypParser->fts5yytos, sets that entry's stateno and major to the new state and the left-hand-side symbol, traces the shift, and returns the new state (237706-237711). The effect on the stack is that the right-hand-side entries are replaced by one entry (it is not an explicit destroy of each popped entry apart from whatever the rule action itself does), and for an empty right-hand side the stack grows by one entry. The function does not check stack room itself; sqlite3Fts5Parser grows the stack before calling it for a rule whose right-hand side is empty. It has a single return, at 237711.

functions.name: sqlite3Fts5Parser
functions.prose_contract: Feeds one token (fts5yymajor, fts5yyminor; major 0 means end of input) to the FTS5 expression parser fts5yyp, a Lemon-generated driver, and returns nothing; it processes only this token, not a whole input. It loops: it finds the action for the token in the current state (237843); if that is a reduce, then for a rule with an empty right-hand side it first grows the stack when the top is at the stack end and, if growing fails, calls fts5yyStackOverflow and leaves the loop (237867-237880), then calls fts5yy_reduce and loops again with the returned action (237882); if it is a shift (or shift-reduce), it calls fts5yy_shift and leaves the loop (237883-237888); if it is the accept action, it pops the top, calls fts5yy_accept and returns immediately (237889-237892); any other action is a syntax error. In this file fts5YYNOERRORRECOVERY is defined (sqlite3.c:236557) and no error symbol is defined, so the compiled error branch is the NOERRORRECOVERY one, which calls fts5yy_syntax_error, destroys the token and leaves the loop (237959-237969); the other error branches (error-symbol recovery at 237904 and the default one at 237970-237991, which calls fts5yy_parse_failed at end of input) are compiled out here. The error counter is not touched in this configuration (237885-237887 are compiled out). When it leaves the loop it prints the stack in debug builds and returns (237995-238007).

functions.name: fts5MultiIterNew
functions.prose_contract: Builds a multi-segment iterator over an FTS5 index and stores it in *ppOut; it returns nothing and reports problems through p->rc. The slice cuts the head; the function starts at 248148. It asserts that either pTerm==0 and nTerm==0, or iLevel<0 (248164), so a non-NULL pTerm is expected only when iLevel<0. If p->rc is SQLITE_OK it counts the segments: for iLevel<0 all pStruct->nSegment segments plus one for the in-memory hash when p->pHash is set and FTS5INDEX_QUERY_SKIPHASH is not in flags, otherwise MIN(nSeg of that level, nSegment) (248167-248174). It always assigns *ppOut = fts5MultiIterAlloc(p, nSeg) (248176); if that is NULL it goes to the end label, leaving *ppOut 0 (the assert at 248178 expects p->rc to be an error). Otherwise it copies bRev, bSkipEmpty and pColset from flags and arguments and sets the output callback unless FTS5INDEX_QUERY_NOOUTPUT is set (248181-248186). If p->rc is still OK it initializes one segment iterator for the hash (if counted) and one for every segment of every level (a term seek when pTerm is non-NULL), or for the first nSeg segments of the named level in reverse order, and asserts that iIter equals nSeg (248189-248214). If p->rc is still OK after that it calls fts5MultiIterFinishSetup; otherwise it frees the new iterator and sets *ppOut to 0 (248221-248226). At the end label the assert says *ppOut is non-NULL or p->rc is an error (248229).

functions.name: fts5StorageDeleteFromIndex
functions.prose_contract: Removes the index contributions of row iDel in an FTS5 storage object. It asserts bSaveRow is 0 or 1 and that bSaveRow is 1 only with apVal==0 (258102-258103), so with bSaveRow==0 apVal may be NULL or point to the row's nCol values. If apVal is NULL it reads the row through a statement: when bSaveRow is set and p->pSavedRow exists it takes over that saved statement (258107-258109); otherwise it gets the lookup statement, binds iDel and steps; if there is no row it returns sqlite3_reset(pSeek) without any change to totals (258111-258116), and a failure to get the statement is returned at 258112. Then for each column that is not marked unindexed it takes the value (from the statement row or from apVal), decodes the locale value or copies a non-text value, and tokenizes the text with sqlite3Fts5Tokenize and fts5StorageInsertCallback (258139-258166). After each column it subtracts the counted size ctx.szCol from p->aTotalSize and sets rc to FTS5_CORRUPT if the total went negative while rc was SQLITE_OK (258167-258170). After the loop, if rc is OK and p->nTotalRow<1 it sets rc to FTS5_CORRUPT, and otherwise it decrements p->nTotalRow by one, which also happens when rc already held an error (258176-258180). Finally, if rc is OK and bSaveRow is set, the statement is stored in p->pSavedRow without being reset; otherwise the statement is reset and its result becomes rc if rc was OK (258182-258188). The result is returned at 258189.

functions.name: afpLock
functions.prose_contract: Lock method for the AFP (Apple Filing Protocol) VFS: tries to raise the file's lock level to eFileLock. If pFile->eFileLock is already at least eFileLock it returns SQLITE_OK at once, before taking the inode mutex (41810-41814). Otherwise it asserts the lock order (a first lock must be SHARED, the requested level is not PENDING, RESERVED is requested only from SHARED; asserts only, 41821-41823), enters pInode->pLockMutex (41828) and leaves it on every path before returning (41964). Returns SQLITE_BUSY without changing any lock state when another unixFile on the inode holds a different level and either the inode is at PENDING or above or a level above SHARED is requested (41833-41837). A SHARED request when the inode already holds SHARED or RESERVED just records the SHARED level in pFile and increments pInode->nShared and nLock (41844-41852). Otherwise, for a SHARED request, or an EXCLUSIVE request from below PENDING, it first takes the PENDING byte lock through afpSetLock, and returns the failure code if that fails (41859-41867). For a SHARED request it then locks a random shared byte, releases the PENDING byte, returns the first error code from either step if one is a lock error, or the busy-style code from the shared-byte lock without recording the lock, and on success sets pFile->eFileLock to SHARED, nShared to 1 and increments nLock (41873-41906). An EXCLUSIVE request with pInode->nShared>1 gives SQLITE_BUSY (41907-41910). Otherwise a RESERVED or EXCLUSIVE request takes the reserved byte if needed, and for EXCLUSIVE drops its shared byte and tries the whole shared range, restoring the shared byte if that fails and returning SQLITE_IOERR_LOCK or failed2 when it cannot (41916-41949). If the code reaches 41955 with rc SQLITE_OK, pFile and pInode record the new level; if it reaches it with an error from an EXCLUSIVE request, both are set to PENDING_LOCK (41955-41961); the gotos at 41837, 41852, 41866, 41896, 41899 and 41944 skip this update.

functions.name: afpLock
functions.prose_contract: Lock method for the AFP (Apple Filing Protocol) VFS: tries to raise the file's lock level to eFileLock. If pFile->eFileLock is already at least eFileLock it returns SQLITE_OK at once, before taking the inode mutex (41810-41814). Otherwise it asserts the lock order (a first lock must be SHARED, the requested level is not PENDING, RESERVED is requested only from SHARED; asserts only, 41821-41823), enters pInode->pLockMutex (41828) and leaves it on every path before returning (41964). An EXCLUSIVE request with pInode->nShared>1 gives SQLITE_BUSY (41907-41910). Otherwise a RESERVED or EXCLUSIVE request takes the reserved byte if needed, and for EXCLUSIVE drops its shared byte and tries the whole shared range, restoring the shared byte if that fails and returning SQLITE_IOERR_LOCK or failed2 when it cannot (41916-41949). functions.name: sqlite3_os_init
functions.prose_contract: Unix-VFS initialization (this is the definition at sqlite3.c:46992-47113, the slice cut the head). It registers each entry of the local static array aVfs[] with sqlite3_vfs_register: "unix" (with the finder chosen by platform), "unix-none", "unix-dotfile", "unix-excl", plus "unix-namedsem", "unix-posix", "unix-flock", "unix-afp", "unix-nfs" and "unix-proxy" only when the matching compile-time options are set (47045-47070). The registration return values are not checked. Whether an entry becomes the default VFS is decided by the second argument: when SQLITE_DEFAULT_UNIX_VFS is defined it is true for the entry whose name equals that string, otherwise for index 0 (47078-47085). With SQLITE_OS_KV_OPTIONAL it also calls sqlite3KvvfsInit. It then assigns unixBigLock = sqlite3MutexAlloc(SQLITE_MUTEX_STATIC_VFS1) without checking the result (47089), asserts some shared-memory constants when WAL is compiled in, calls unixTempFileInit (47110), and returns SQLITE_OK at its only return (47112).

functions.name: winLock
functions.prose_contract: Win32 VFS lock method: tries to raise the lock level of pFile (a winFile) to locktype. It returns SQLITE_OK immediately if pFile->locktype is already at least locktype (50664-50666), and SQLITE_IOERR_LOCK if the file is read-only (WINFILE_RDONLY) and locktype is RESERVED_LOCK or higher (50671-50672). It asserts the lock order (first lock must be SHARED, no PENDING request, RESERVED only from SHARED; asserts only, 50677-50679). For a SHARED request, or an EXCLUSIVE request made from RESERVED, it tries to lock the PENDING byte with LockFileEx up to three times, sleeping 1 ms between failed attempts, and returns SQLITE_IOERR_LOCK immediately (without changing pFile->locktype) if the failure is ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE (50686-50725). With the pending byte held (or not needed) it then, depending on locktype: acquires the shared lock by winGetReadLock and records SHARED (50730-50742); locks the RESERVED byte and records RESERVED (50746-50754); for EXCLUSIVE sets the recorded level to PENDING_LOCK (this happens even when the request started at SHARED and no pending byte was locked, 50758-50760) and then unlocks the shared lock, locks the whole shared range, records EXCLUSIVE on success, or tries to re-take the shared lock on failure (50765-50776). A pending byte taken for a SHARED request is released again (50781-50783). At the end it returns SQLITE_OK if the last step succeeded (res nonzero), otherwise it stores the last error in pFile->lastErrno and returns SQLITE_BUSY; in both cases pFile->locktype is set to the new level reached so far, which can be SHARED, RESERVED or PENDING_LOCK after a failed request (50788-50799).

functions.name: sqlite3PCacheSetDefault
functions.prose_contract: Registers the built-in page cache implementation: it calls sqlite3_config(SQLITE_CONFIG_PCACHE2, &defaultMethods), where defaultMethods is a static const sqlite3_pcache_methods2 table whose entries are the pcache1Init, pcache1Shutdown, pcache1Create, pcache1Cachesize, pcache1Pagecount, pcache1Fetch, pcache1Unpin, pcache1Rekey, pcache1Truncate, pcache1Destroy and pcache1Shrink functions (sqlite3.c:57301-57316). The call is unconditional, so it replaces any page cache implementation already configured, and the return value of sqlite3_config is ignored. The function returns nothing and has no other statements.

functions.name: writeSuperJournal
functions.prose_contract: Appends the super-journal (master journal) name record to the rollback journal file; the packet name pager_write_superjournal does not exist, the function is writeSuperJournal (sqlite3.c:59760-59823; the slice cut the head). It returns SQLITE_OK without writing anything, and without setting pPager->setSuper, if zSuper is NULL, the journal mode is PAGER_JOURNALMODE_MEMORY, or the journal file is not open (59770-59775). Otherwise it sets pPager->setSuper to 1, computes the checksum as the sum of the name bytes, and in full-sync mode first moves journalOff to the next sector boundary via journalHdrOffset (59776-59790). It then writes, starting at the current journal offset, the 4-byte page number PAGER_SJ_PGNO, the name bytes, the name length, the checksum and the 8-byte journal magic, and returns the first nonzero error code from those writes (59796-59804); on that failure journalOff has not been advanced past the record and setSuper stays 1. On success it advances journalOff by nSuper+20 (59805) and, if the file size is readable and larger than journalOff, truncates the journal file to journalOff, returning the result of sqlite3OsFileSize or sqlite3OsTruncate (59817-59822). It asserts that setSuper was 0 and that WAL is not in use on entry (59767-59768).

functions.name: pager_end_transaction
functions.prose_contract: Ends the current write transaction of a pager; the real function is pager_end_transaction at 60097-60225 (slice cut the head). If pPager->eState is below PAGER_WRITER_LOCKED and pPager->eLock is below RESERVED_LOCK it returns SQLITE_OK at once and does nothing (60116-60118). Otherwise it releases all savepoints and, if the journal file is open, finishes the journal according to its mode: an in-memory journal is closed; truncate mode truncates to 0 when journalOff is nonzero and syncs it when fullSync is set, then sets journalOff to 0; persist mode, or exclusive mode below WAL, calls zeroJournalHdr and sets journalOff to 0; any other mode closes the journal and deletes the journal file with sqlite3OsDelete only when the pager is not a temp file (60124-60167), the result going into rc. It then frees pInJournal and clears nRec (60181-60183). If rc is SQLITE_OK it cleans all dirty pages when the database is in memory or flush-on-commit applies and otherwise clears their writable flags, and truncates the page cache to dbSize (60184-60191). With WAL it calls sqlite3WalEndWriteTransaction into rc2 (asserted to be SQLITE_OK, 60198-60199); without WAL, on commit when rc is OK and the file is longer than dbSize, it truncates the file (60200-60209). If rc is OK and bCommit is set it sends SQLITE_FCNTL_COMMIT_PHASETWO and treats SQLITE_NOTFOUND as success (60211-60214). If the pager is not in exclusive mode (and, for WAL, sqlite3WalExclusiveMode(...,0) is true) it drops to a SHARED lock with pagerUnlockDb, storing the result in rc2 (60216-60220). It sets eState to PAGER_READER and setSuper to 0 and returns rc if rc is not SQLITE_OK, else rc2 (60221-60224).

functions.name: pager_playback_one_page
functions.prose_contract: Reads one record (page number and page image) from the main journal or a sub-journal and writes the page back to the database file and/or the page cache; the function is at sqlite3.c:60343-60545 (slice cut the head). It reads the page number and the page data from the journal at *pOffset and returns the error code of either read at once (60382-60385); after a successful read it advances *pOffset by the page size plus 4 (plus 4 more for the main journal checksum, 60386). It returns SQLITE_DONE without playing back if pgno is 0 or the super-journal marker page number (60393-60395); returns SQLITE_OK without playing back if pgno is beyond pPager->dbSize or its bit is already set in pDone (60397-60399); for the main journal it reads the checksum and returns the read error, or SQLITE_DONE if the checksum of a non-savepoint record does not match (60400-60405). If pDone is non-NULL it sets the page's bit and returns the error (such as SQLITE_NOMEM) if that fails; with pDone NULL nothing is recorded (60411-60413). For page 1 it restores pPager->nReserve from byte 20 of the image (60417-60418). It looks up the page in the cache unless WAL is in use (60456-60460). If the database file is open, the state is WRITER_DBMOD or OPEN, and the journal data counts as synced (for a main-journal record that is when pPager->noSync is set or *pOffset is not beyond journalHdr; for a sub-journal record when the page is not cached or lacks PGHDR_NEED_SYNC, 60467-60471), it writes the image to the database file, storing the write result in rc without checking it yet, raises dbFileSize if needed and updates a backup (60467-60493). Otherwise, for a sub-journal record whose page is not cached, it gets the page with sqlite3PagerGet while SPILLFLAG_ROLLBACK is set, returns the error if that fails, and marks the page dirty (60494-60518). If a cached page exists (even when the file write failed) it copies the image into it, calls xReiniter, restores dbFileVers for page 1 and releases it (60520-60543). It returns rc at 60544, which is the file write result when that write ran, else SQLITE_OK.

functions.name: pager_playback
functions.prose_contract: Rolls back the contents of the hot or ordinary journal into the database file (sqlite3.c:60857-61062; slice cut the head). It gets the journal size (error goes to end_playback with that rc, 60874-60877), then reads the super-journal name into pTmpSpace and, if a name is present, checks that the file exists; an error from either step, or a missing super-journal file (res==0), jumps to end_playback without replaying any page (60891-60898). Otherwise it sets journalOff to 0 and loops over journal headers: readJournalHdr returning SQLITE_DONE ends the loop with rc SQLITE_OK, any other nonzero code ends it with that code (60912-60918); it adjusts nRec for the 0xffffffff and empty-header cases, truncates the database to mxPg and updates dbSize and mxPgno at the first header (60925-60961), and plays back each record with pager_playback_one_page, calling pager_reset first when isHot (60966-60971). A SQLITE_DONE from a page stops that header's records and sets journalOff to the journal size, SQLITE_IOERR_SHORT_READ ends playback with rc SQLITE_OK, and other errors end it with that error (60975-60993). At end_playback, if rc is SQLITE_OK it restores the original page size with sqlite3PagerSetPagesize (61001-61003), sets changeCountDone to tempFile (61022), and if rc is still OK re-reads the super-journal name, syncs the database when the state is WRITER_DBMOD or higher or OPEN, calls pager_end_transaction, and, when a super-journal name exists, the file existed and rc is OK, calls pager_delsuper (61024-61050). It logs a recovery notice when isHot and pages were replayed (61051-61054), calls setSectorSize, which recomputes the sector size from the file (it does not restore a saved one), and returns rc (61060-61061).

functions.name: pager_incr_changecounter
functions.prose_contract: Increments the file change counter in page 1 when the pager has not yet done so in this transaction. The slice (62330-62591) does not contain this function; it is defined at sqlite3.c:64358-64432, so this prose is written from that definition. It asserts the pager is in PAGER_WRITER_CACHEMOD or PAGER_WRITER_DBMOD state (64361-64363). If changeCountDone is already set or dbSize is 0 it does nothing and returns SQLITE_OK (64384). Otherwise (asserting that the pager is not a temp file and its file is open, 64387) it fetches page 1 with sqlite3PagerGet into pPgHdr (64390). Unless direct mode applies (only possible when SQLITE_ENABLE_ATOMIC_WRITE is defined; otherwise DIRECT_MODE is 0 and isDirectMode is asserted to be 0) it makes page 1 writable with sqlite3PagerWrite (64398-64400). If rc is SQLITE_OK it updates the counter in the page image with pager_write_changecounter (64404); in direct mode it then writes page 1 to the file at offset 0, counts the write, and on success copies the counter bytes at offset 24 into pPager->dbFileVers and sets changeCountDone to 1 (64407-64422), whereas in the normal mode it just sets changeCountDone to 1 (64424). It releases the page reference with sqlite3PagerUnref (64429) and returns rc, which is the error code of the page fetch, the page-write or (direct mode) the file write when one of them fails, in which case changeCountDone stays 0 (64431).

functions.name: pager_write_pagelist
functions.prose_contract: Writes a list of dirty pages (linked through pDirty) to the database file; defined at sqlite3.c:62470-62551. It asserts that WAL is not in use, the pager is a temp file or in DBMOD state, it holds an EXCLUSIVE lock, and the file is open unless the list has no further dirty pages (62474-62477). If the file is not open (only a temp file may be in that state) it opens it with pagerOpentemp and the result becomes rc (62483-62486). If rc is SQLITE_OK, dbHintSize is below dbSize and the list has more pages or its first page lies beyond dbHintSize, it sends SQLITE_FCNTL_SIZE_HINT with the final file size and sets dbHintSize to dbSize (62492-62499). Then, while rc is SQLITE_OK and the list is not exhausted, for each page whose number is at most dbSize and which is not marked PGHDR_DONT_WRITE it writes the page content to its offset (with the change counter updated first for page 1), refreshes dbFileVers when page 1 was written, raises dbFileSize if the page is beyond it, counts the write and notifies backups; other pages are skipped (62501-62545). Each visited page gets pager_set_pagehash and the loop moves to pList->pDirty (62546-62547). It returns rc, which is the error from pagerOpentemp or the last sqlite3OsWrite, or SQLITE_OK (62550); the write result is checked only by the loop condition, so the page whose write failed is still processed (dbFileVers, dbFileSize, statistics and backup updates) before the loop ends.

functions.name: sqlite3PagerCommitPhaseOne
functions.prose_contract: First phase of a commit: syncs the journal and writes the dirty pages, or writes them to the WAL; defined at sqlite3.c:64506-64725. It returns pPager->errCode if that is set (64521), SQLITE_IOERR on a simulated fault (64524), and SQLITE_OK without doing anything when eState is below PAGER_WRITER_CACHEMOD (64530). If pagerFlushOnCommit(pPager,1) is false (an in-memory database or nothing to write) it only restarts any backup (64534-64538) and falls to the exit. Otherwise, with WAL in use, it takes the dirty list (or page 1 if the list is empty, since the commit frame needs a page), writes the frames with pagerWalFrames as a commit, releases page 1 and, if rc is SQLITE_OK, marks all pages clean (64541-64558); in this path it does not touch the database file and does not sync it. Without WAL it increments the change counter (pager_incr_changecounter; with the atomic-write or batch-atomic options compiled in it may use the direct or batch paths), writes the super-journal name with writeSuperJournal, syncs the journal with syncJournal, writes the dirty list with pager_write_pagelist (unless the batch-atomic path did it), marks pages clean, truncates the file when dbSize exceeds dbFileSize, and, unless noSync is set, calls sqlite3PagerSync (64631-64715). Any error in these steps jumps to commit_phase_one_exit with that rc. At the exit, if rc is SQLITE_OK and WAL is not in use, it sets eState to PAGER_WRITER_FINISHED (64720-64723); it returns rc at 64724.

functions.name: walIndexReadHdr
functions.prose_contract: Reads the wal-index header into pWal->hdr, running recovery if the header is invalid; defined at sqlite3.c:68518-68621 (slice cut the head). It obtains page 0 of the wal-index with walIndexPage; any error other than SQLITE_READONLY_CANTINIT is returned at once (68527-68545). On SQLITE_READONLY_CANTINIT it sets pWal->bShmUnreliable to 1, sets the heap-memory exclusive mode and sets *pChanged to 1 (68540-68542). If page 0 is mapped it tries to read the header with walIndexTryHdr, otherwise the header counts as bad (68558). On a bad header: if the shared memory is reliable and mapped read-only it takes and releases a shared WAL_WRITE_LOCK and, if that succeeded, sets rc to SQLITE_READONLY_RECOVERY, or else leaves the lock error in rc (68564-68568); in the other case it holds or takes the exclusive write lock (a lock failure is left in rc), retries the header, and if it is still bad runs walIndexRecover, sets *pChanged to 1 and stores the recover result in rc, then drops the write lock if it was taken here (68570-68595). When the header was read successfully but its version is not WALINDEX_MAX_VERSION, rc becomes SQLITE_CANTOPEN_BKPT (68604-68606). If bShmUnreliable is set, then on a nonzero rc it closes the wal-index, clears bShmUnreliable and turns SQLITE_IOERR_SHORT_READ into WAL_RETRY, and in all cases it sets exclusiveMode back to WAL_NORMAL_MODE (68607-68618). It returns rc at 68620; *pChanged is written by walIndexTryHdr (not read here) and at 68542 and 68589.

functions.name: walRestartLog
functions.prose_contract: Called before a writer appends to the WAL: if the connection holds the WAL_READ_LOCK(0) read lock (pWal->readLock==0), it tries to restart the log, then replaces its read lock; defined at sqlite3.c:69730-69770 (slice cut the head). If pWal->readLock is not 0 it does nothing and returns SQLITE_OK (69734, 69769). Otherwise, when pInfo->nBackfill is greater than 0, it gets a random salt and takes exclusive locks on WAL_READ_LOCK(1) through the last reader slot: on success it calls walRestartHdr(pWal, salt1) and releases those locks (69737-69752); SQLITE_BUSY is ignored and nothing is restarted; any other lock error is returned immediately with the read lock still held (69753-69755). In every case that reaches 69757 it releases the shared WAL_READ_LOCK(0), sets pWal->readLock to -1, and repeatedly calls walTryBeginRead(pWal, ..., useWal=1) until it stops returning WAL_RETRY (69757-69763). It returns the result of that last walTryBeginRead call, which is SQLITE_OK with a new read lock held or another error code with readLock left at -1 (69769). walRestartHdr, which changes the salt values and mxFrame in the header (the reviewer's point), is not itself read here.

functions.name: sqlite3BtreeOpen
functions.prose_contract: Opens a B-tree on a database file (or temp or memory database) and stores the new Btree in *ppBtree; defined at sqlite3.c:74081-74374 (slice cut the head). It computes isTempDb (no filename) and isMemdb (":memory:", an in-memory temp database or SQLITE_OPEN_MEMORY), sets BTREE_MEMORY in flags for a memory database, and turns a main-database open of a temp or memory database into a temp-database open (74097-74126). It returns SQLITE_NOMEM_BKPT, leaving *ppBtree unchanged, if the Btree allocation fails (74127-74130). For a shareable database (shared-cache flag, not temp) it builds the full pathname (failure other than SQLITE_OK_SYMLINK is returned after freeing p and the name; an allocation failure returns SQLITE_NOMEM_BKPT) takes the open mutex and the shared-cache list mutex, and searches the shared list for a BtShared on the same file and VFS; if the same BtShared is already used by another database of this connection it returns SQLITE_CONSTRAINT after leaving the mutexes and freeing p (74143-74198), otherwise it reuses the match and increments nRef (74191-74192). If no BtShared was found it allocates one, opens the pager, reads the file header, sets read-only, secure-delete, page-size, reserved-size and auto-vacuum fields from the header, calls sqlite3PagerSetPagesize, sets nRef to 1, and, if shareable, allocates a mutex and links the new object into the shared list (74226-74307); failures there set rc and go to btree_open_out. If shareable it then links the new Btree into the per-connection sorted sibling list (74316-74340) and stores p in *ppBtree (74342). It returns 0 after printing "TLV contents go past end of message" when the TLV length plus 4 exceeds msg_tlen (258-261). It prints the TLV type, length and its unknown-forward flags, advances past the 4-byte header and switches on the type (266-277). For the types it knows (common hello, IPv4 and IPv6 transport address, configuration sequence number, address list, common session, FEC with its wildcard, prefix, host address and Martini VC cases, generic label, status, FT session, MTU) it first requires a minimum remaining length with the TLV_TCHECK macro: if the remaining TLV length is smaller, that macro prints a bracketed message and an invalid marker and jumps to the invalid label, which returns tlv_len+4 (231-236, 545-546). A failed prefix decode with code -2 jumps to the trunc label, which calls nd_trunc_longjmp and does not return to the caller (364, 374, 542-543). A Martini VC FEC with VC-info-length below 4 prints a note and returns tlv_len+4 directly (416-419). The other listed types (hop count, path vector, ATM and FR labels, extended status, returned PDU or message, session parameters, label request message id) and unknown types only hexdump the value when ndo_vflag is at most 1 (524-538). In the normal case the function returns tlv_len+4 (540).

functions.name: lisp_print
functions.prose_contract: Prints a LISP control packet (Map-Register or Map-Notify); the packet name lisp_map_register_print does not exist, the function is lisp_print at print-lisp.c:227-390 and the slice cut its head. It sets the protocol name, requires MAP_REGISTER_HDR_LEN bytes to be captured (ND_TCHECK_LEN, which goes to the trunc label), prints the type through lisp_hdr_flag, and returns without printing more when the type is neither Map-Register nor Map-Notify (248-257). It then computes whether xTR data is present, reads the authentication data length and the record count (260-266). With -v it prints the record count, the authentication type looked up from the key-id field (not the key id itself) and the authentication data as hex; without -v it prints only the record count (268-277). If the record count is 0 it goes to the invalid label, which calls nd_print_invalid (280-281, 388-389). For each EID record while bytes remain (284-364) it requires the fixed record bytes to be captured, prints TTL, action and map version in verbose mode, prints the EID address for IPv4 or IPv6 and returns silently for any other address family (304-323); it then prints each locator (address for IPv4/IPv6, nothing for other families, priorities and flags in verbose mode, 327-363). After the records it prints the xTR-ID and site ID when the xTR bit is set, going to invalid if fewer than 24 bytes are available (371-376); otherwise it hex-prints any remaining bytes as data (379-382). It returns at 384; trunc prints a truncation message and returns (385-387).

functions.name: llc_print
functions.prose_contract: Prints an IEEE 802.2 LLC header and dispatches on the SAPs; defined at print-llc.c:148-403 (slice cut the head). The return value is a header length: positive when the payload was printed by a dissector or the LLC frame was fully described, negative or zero otherwise. It requires 3 captured and 3 total bytes, and prints a truncation marker plus the default hex print and returns caplen or length respectively if either is below 3 (157-166). The control field is one byte for unnumbered frames (hdrlen 3), where the check is for 3 bytes; for every other frame the control field is two bytes (hdrlen 4) and fewer than 4 captured or total bytes give the same truncation return (178-206). A frame with both SAPs global is passed to ipx_print and returns 0 (208-228). With -e it prints the LLC header fields (234-248). It then advances past the header and tries the dissectors: SNAP via snap_print returns hdrlen+5 when snap_print reports the payload printed and -(hdrlen+5) when not (257-273); STP, IP, IPX, NetBEUI and ISO CLNS with their SAP pairs print the payload and return hdrlen (275-328). Otherwise it prints the SAP names (without -e) and describes the frame: for an unnumbered frame it prints the command and flags and, for XID, handles an empty or truncated XID body with an early return of hdrlen (353-385); a supervisory frame returns hdrlen with no payload (387-393); an information frame, or an unnumbered frame that did not return earlier, ends with return -hdrlen (402).

functions.name: snap_print
functions.prose_contract: Prints a SNAP header (OUI plus protocol id) and dispatches to the protocol dissector; defined at print-llc.c:420-608 (slice cut the head). It returns 1 after printing a truncation marker when fewer than 5 bytes are captured or present (ND_TCHECK_5 and the length check, 430-432, 605-607). It reads the 3-byte OUI and 2-byte protocol id, prints them with -e, and skips the 5 bytes (433-451). By OUI: encapsulated Ethernet and Cisco-90 call ethertype_print and return its result if nonzero (454-465); AppleTalk with ethertype ATALK does the same (467-481); Cisco CDP, DTP, UDLD, VTP, PVST and VLAN-bridge protocol ids call the matching printer and return 1 (483-503); for RFC 2684 the Ethernet, 802.5, FDDI and BPDU protocol ids skip the bridge padding (and one more byte for FDDI), call ether_print, token_print, fddi_print or stp_print and return 1 (506-573); the padding checks ND_TCHECK_LEN(p, bridge_pad) at 518, 539 and 560 jump to trunc, which prints a truncation message and returns 1 when the padding bytes are not captured. If nothing matched it prints an addresses and SNAP summary line (without -e) and returns 0 (576-603).

functions.name: lspping_print
functions.prose_contract: Prints an MPLS LSP-Ping packet (common header, then its TLVs); defined at print-lspping.c:488-1074 (slice cut the head), returning nothing. It jumps to the tooshort label (prints "packet is too short") if fewer bytes than the common header are present (528-529, 1072-1073), requires the header to be captured (ND_TCHECK_SIZE goes to trunc), and returns after printing a message if the version is not LSPPING_VERSION (535-539). Without -v it prints a one-line summary and returns (542-548). Otherwise it prints version, message type, reply mode, return code (with the subcode for return codes 3, 4, 8, 10, 11 and 12), sender handle, sequence number and the sent and received timestamps (553-597). It then loops over the TLVs while bytes remain: a remaining length below the TLV header size, or a TLV whose length plus header exceeds the remaining length, goes to tooshort (606-607, 631-632); a TLV of length 0 is skipped (621-625); the value must be captured (ND_TCHECK_LEN at 634). The Target FEC Stack TLV is parsed sub-TLV by sub-TLV: too little data for a sub-TLV header or its length sets tlv_hexdump and goes to tlv_tooshort (641-657); a sub-TLV of unexpected length for its type, and unknown sub-TLV types, are printed as hex through subtlv_hexdump (676, 690, 704, ..., 855); after the sub-TLV a too-short padded length prints "TLV is too short" and returns (865-871). The downstream-mapping TLV and the other TLV types are handled in the code after 878 (too-short TLV values set tlv_hexdump and go to tlv_tooshort, 880-882 and later); unknown TLV types are hex-dumped when -v is at most 1 (1044-1051). At tlv_tooshort it hex-dumps the value when -vv or tlv_hexdump applies, pads the length to a multiple of 4, goes to tooshort if the padded TLV exceeds what is left, and advances (1054-1069). It returns at 1071.

functions.name: rsvp_obj_print
functions.prose_contract: Prints a sequence of RSVP objects from tptr (tlen bytes) for a message with the given common header; defined at print-rsvp.c:675-1915 (slice cut the head). It returns 0 at 1902 after the loop, or -1 on any error. While at least an object header remains it requires the header to be captured (ND_TCHECK_LEN, which goes to trunc), and returns -1 after printing an error when the object length is not a multiple of 4, is smaller than the header, or exceeds the remaining length (699-739). It prints the object class and class type, then switches on the class number and for known classes parses the value (session, confirm, notify request, labels, style, templates, label request, ERO/RRO, XRO, hello, restart capability, capability, session attribute, generalized UNI, RSVP hop, time values, TSPEC/ADSPEC/FLOWSPEC, filter spec, fast reroute, detour, class type, error spec, properties, message ids, integrity, admin status, label set and others, 749-1878); the many goto obj_tooshort exits (for example 753, 767, 1160) print "object is too short" and return -1 (1906-1908), goto subobj_tooshort prints "sub-object is too short" and returns -1 (1310, 1316, 1338, 1903-1905), goto invalid calls nd_print_invalid and returns -1 (1112, 1119, 1132, 1261, 1301, 1909-1911), trunc calls nd_print_trunc and returns -1 (1912-1914), and a property TLV shorter than 2 returns -1 at 1717. In the ERO/RRO IPv4 loop a sub-object whose length exceeds the remaining object length prints an error and only breaks out of that loop, and a zero length does the same (1096-1104); neither returns -1. Unknown classes are hex-dumped when -v is at most 1 (1889-1892). After each object the value is hex-dumped when -vv or the hexdump flag applies (1895-1897) and tptr and tlen advance by the object length (1899-1900).

functions.name: sliplink_print
functions.prose_contract: Prints the direction and link-level type of a SLIP packet; defined at print-sl.c:108-168. It reads the direction byte at p+SLX_DIR and prints "I " for incoming, "O " for outgoing, or "Invalid direction %d " and sets dir to -1 (116-131). It then switches on the high nibble of the byte at p+SLX_CHDR. TYPE_IP prints "ip <length+SLIP_HDRLEN>: " (134-136). TYPE_UNCOMPRESSED_TCP reads the connection id from the ip_p field of the copy at p+SLX_CHDR into the global lastconn, prints "utcp <id>: ", and returns if dir is -1; otherwise it requires the ip header and the TCP header to be captured (ND_TCHECK_SIZE, 150-152), and stores the data length (length minus the header words) in the global lastlen[dir][lastconn] (144-154). Any other type returns if dir is -1; else if TYPE_COMPRESSED_TCP is set it calls compressed_sl_print (which itself reads the compressed header and the ip and TCP headers and updates lastconn and lastlen) and prints ": ", and otherwise it prints "slip-%u!: " with the byte value (157-166). It returns nothing.

functions.name: slow_oam_print
functions.prose_contract: Prints an IEEE 802.3 Slow Protocols OAM PDU; defined at print-slow.c:478-735 (slice cut the head), returning nothing. It jumps to tooshort (prints a "too short" message, 733-735) if fewer than the 3-byte common header (flags and code) remain (511-512), requires it to be captured (ND_TCHECK_SIZE), advances past it and prints the flags and code (513-522). Then it switches on the code. Information PDUs (code INFO) and event notification PDUs loop over TLVs: a TLV header that does not fit goes to tooshort (528-529, 625-626); an end-of-TLV type prints a marker and returns (538-544, 635-641); a TLV length below the header size prints a message and returns (547-551, 644-648); a TLV longer than the remaining bytes goes to tooshort and the TLV bytes are captured-checked with ND_TCHECK_LEN (553-555, 650-652). For local and remote information TLVs and the four link-event TLV types it compares the length field stored inside the TLV (info_length or event_length) with the size of the structure, hex-dumps the TLV on mismatch (563-568, 662-667) and otherwise reads and prints the structure fields; this check uses the stored field and not the TLV length, so the TLV length is not itself checked against the structure size. Organization-specific and unknown TLVs are hex-dumped (593-599, 683-689), and -vv hex-dumps every TLV (604-607, 694-697). Event notifications first skip a 2-byte sequence number after requiring 2 bytes (616-620). Loopback control requires the structure to fit (else tooshort), prints the command and skips one byte (704-716). Variable request, response, private and unknown codes are hex-dumped when -v is at most 1 (722-729). It returns at 731.

functions.name: tcp_print
functions.prose_contract: Prints a TCP header, its options, and hands the payload to a port-specific printer; defined at print-tcp.c:160-854 (slice cut the head), returning nothing. It sets the protocol name and, if the destination port field is not captured, prints a truncated source/destination summary with nd_print_trunc and returns (177-196). It prints the ports (with addresses for IPv4/IPv6), requires the fixed header to be captured (ND_TCHECK_SIZE, which goes to trunc), and returns after a message if the header length (data offset times 4) is below the fixed header size (226-234). With -q it prints the length and returns early (241-247). Otherwise it prints flags, sequence and acknowledgement (with relative values), window and urgent pointer, and, when the header is longer than the fixed one, walks the options while bytes remain (456-709): the length byte of a non-zero-length option must be at least 2 and not exceed the remaining header bytes, otherwise it goes to bad (474-475); MSS, window scale, SACK, timestamp, signature, SCPS, TCP-AO, UTO, MPTCP, Fast Open and experimental options are decoded, with LENCHECK jumping to bad when an option claims more than the header holds (482); a SACK length that is not a multiple of 8 and the invalid signature or TCP-AO cases are reported inside the option text and the walk continues (503-505, 562, 592-593); an option whose observed length differs from the stated one prints "[len N]" (700-705) and the walk ends after an EOL option (707-708). After the options it prints the length, returns if the segment has no payload (718-719), checks that the whole header is captured (nd_trunc_longjmp if not, 729-733), skips the header, handles RST segments through print_tcp_rst_data or a captured-length check and returns (735-741), and, for a forced packet type, calls zmtp1/resp/domain printers and returns (743-756). Otherwise it dispatches on the source or destination port to the application printers (FTP, SSH, telnet, SMTP, whois, DNS, HTTP, NetBIOS, BGP, RPKI-RTR, SMB, RTSP, MSDP, LDP, RESP, BEEP, OpenFlow) or, for NFS ports with at least 4 captured bytes, to the RPC printers (759-843), and returns at 844. The bad label prints "[bad opt]" and returns (845-849) and the trunc label prints a truncation message (850-853).

functions.name: vsock_if_print
functions.prose_contract: Link-layer printer for Linux vsockmon captures: it sets the protocol name to "vsock" (251) and, when the captured length h->caplen is smaller than the vsockmon header, prints a truncation marker, adds the caplen to ndo->ndo_ll_hdr_len and returns (253-257). Otherwise it adds the header size to ndo->ndo_ll_hdr_len and calls vsock_hdr_print(ndo, cp, caplen) (258-259). It returns nothing. The packet name af_vsockmon_print does not exist in print-vsock.c; the slice (253-260) is the tail of vsock_if_print, which starts at print-vsock.c:245-246.

functions.name: open_interface
functions.prose_contract: Opens a pcap capture handle for device and returns it, or NULL when the device does not exist; defined at tcpdump.c:1294-1517 (slice cut the head); the behaviour depends on compile-time options. With HAVE_PCAP_OPEN, a device name starting with an rpcap URL prefix is opened with pcap_open: on failure it returns NULL if the error text contains "No such device" or "The system cannot find the device specified", and calls error() (which does not return) for any other failure; on success it warns if ebuf is non-empty and returns the handle (1306-1331). With HAVE_PCAP_CREATE, other devices go through pcap_create and a sequence of setting calls (timestamp precision, immediate mode, snaplen, promiscuous mode, monitor mode, timeout, buffer size, timestamp type), each of which calls error() on failure; pcap_create failing returns NULL only if the error text contains "No such device" (the Windows text is not tested on this path, 1343-1344) and otherwise calls error() (1335-1410). Then pcap_activate: a negative status closes the handle and returns NULL, after calling error() for most error codes (PCAP_ERROR, permission denied with a message, capture-not-supported with a message, rfmon-not-supported on a wlan device, and any other status), except that PCAP_ERROR_NO_SUCH_DEVICE copies a message into ebuf and does not call error() (1417-1467); a positive status prints a warning only (1468-1483). It then sets the direction if requested (error() on failure, 1485-1490). Without HAVE_PCAP_CREATE it defaults the snaplen to MAXIMUM_SNAPLEN if 0 and uses pcap_open_live, returning NULL for "No such device" and calling error() for other failures (1492-1511). In the pcap_create and pcap_open_live paths a non-empty ebuf after success produces a warning only for the open_live path (1512-1513), and the common return pc is at 1516.

functions.name: e_inc_search
functions.prose_contract: Incremental history search in tcsh's line editor (ed.chared.c:1058-1259): dir is the initial search direction, F_UP_SEARCH_HIST or its forward counterpart. It returns CC_ERROR at once if the edit buffer has too little room for the prompt (1074-1075). It then loops (1077-1257). Each pass, if the pattern buffer is empty, sets the static pchar to ':' and appends '*' to the pattern (1079-1082); this resets pchar before any search has been done. It appends a prompt line ("bck" or "fwd", pchar, and the pattern) to the input buffer, refreshes the display, and reads a character; if reading fails it returns e_send_eof(0) (1101-1102). The character is handled: inserting characters append to the pattern (beep if there is no room); the incremental forward and back commands change newdir and set redo; the delete-previous command ends the search with done set when the pattern is longer than 1, else beeps; control-G sets CC_ERROR and done; control-W appends the next word at the cursor to the pattern; any other key is pushed back as a macro and ends the search with CC_REFRESH (1104-1177). It then removes the prompt line (1179-1181). If the search is not done, and the pattern has more than one character with no unmatched '[', it searches (moving the cursor on a repeated search, appending '*', calling c_search_line and, if that fails, the up or down history search), then restores the pattern length; on failure it beeps, restores the old history line and cursor, and sets pchar to '?', otherwise pchar is ':' (1183-1230); a failure to restore the history line returns CC_ERROR (1220-1224). It then calls itself recursively with newdir, and turns CC_ERROR into CC_NORM when pchar is '?' and the outer pchar was ':' (1232-1237). If the result is CC_NORM, or CC_ERROR with an initially empty pattern, it restores pchar, the pattern length, the history number (returning CC_ERROR if GetHistLine fails) and the cursor, and refreshes after an error (1241-1253). It returns ret if done is set or ret is not CC_NORM; otherwise the loop continues (1254-1255).

functions.name: MakeLiteral
functions.prose_contract: Finds or adds a literal string in tcsh's global literal buffer litptr (ed.refresh.c:109-156) and returns its index with the LITERAL bit set, or '?' on failure. The text is addlit's text followed by str[0..len): when addlit is nonzero and has the LITERAL bit set, addlit's text is the NUL-terminated string at litptr+(addlit&~LITERAL)*LIT_FACTOR, when it has no LITERAL bit it is the single character addlit, and when addlit is 0 only str is used (113-125). It scans the entries (spaced LIT_FACTOR characters apart) for one with the same text followed by a NUL and returns (i/LIT_FACTOR)|LITERAL for the first match without changing the buffer (121-123, 126-128). If there is none and the buffer lacks room it grows litptr with xrealloc by 256 characters, doubled until the new text fits, updates litalloc, and re-points addlitptr when it pointed into the old buffer; a NULL result from xrealloc returns '?' (130-141). It also returns '?' when the new index litlen/LIT_FACTOR is not below LITERAL or equals CHAR_DBWIDTH (143-145). Otherwise it appends the addlit text, the str text and NUL characters until litlen is a multiple of LIT_FACTOR (at least one NUL), and returns the new index with the LITERAL bit (146-155).

functions.name: pgetty
functions.prose_contract: Called in a child after fork to set up its process group and, optionally, the controlling terminal; defined at sh.proc.c:1992-2057, and its body exists only when BSDJOBS is defined (1994-2056), otherwise it does nothing. With POSIXJOBS and wanttty>0 it blocks SIGTSTP and SIGTTIN, saving the old mask in oset and registering a cleanup (2007-2013). Without POSIXJOBS and wanttty>0 it calls setttypgrp(pgrp) first (2016-2019). If wanttty is not negative it calls setpgid(0, pgrp); if that fails and POSIXJOBS is defined it retries with the child's own pid as group, and if that also fails (or without POSIXJOBS) it prints a "setpgid child" system error and calls xexit(0); if the retry works it sets wanttty to the new group id, so wanttty then counts as positive (2027-2041). With POSIXJOBS and wanttty>0 (including that case) it gives the terminal to pgrp with setttypgrp and runs cleanup_until(&oset), which restores the signal mask (2044-2048). In the case that wanttty was 0 on entry and the first setpgid failed, the signals were not blocked at the start (2007 requires wanttty>0) but this cleanup is still run on oset, which was never set on that path. Finally, if the global tpgrp is positive it sets it to 0 (2054-2055). It returns nothing.

functions.name: auto_lock
functions.prose_contract: tcsh's terminal lock for the auto-lock timeout (tc.func.c:691-795); returns nothing. Unless NO_CRYPT is defined it looks up the effective user's stored password hash, from getauthuid, from getspnam (retrying while errno is EINTR) or from pw_passwd, depending on the platform, and if none is found it calls auto_logout() and returns (693-748). Otherwise it cancels the alarm, prints a newline and, up to 5 times, prompts "Password:" with xgetpass and compares the encrypted answer (through the platform's crypt wrapper) with the stored hash (the AFS build also accepts a Kerberos-style AFS authentication, whose user name comes from the shell variable afsuser, else the AFSUSER environment variable, else pw_name, 752-779). On a match it zeroes the typed password, redraws the input line if GettingInput is set and just_signaled is not, clears just_signaled and returns (781-789); on a mismatch it prints "Incorrect passwd for <user>" (791). After 5 failures, or with NO_CRYPT defined, it calls auto_logout() at the end (794).

functions.name: xwcwidth
functions.prose_contract: Returns the display width of a Unicode code point as an int; defined at tc.nls.c:38-52. If wchar is at most 0xffff it returns wcwidth((wchar_t)wchar), the library's width for that character (42-43). Otherwise it subtracts 0x10000, builds a UTF-16 surrogate pair (high 0xd800 | (v>>10), low 0xdc00 | (v&0x3ff)) in a two-element local array and returns wcswidth(ws, 2) (48-51). It writes no state of its own, and the results depend on the C library's wcwidth and wcswidth and the current locale; for inputs above 0x10ffff the pair formed is not a valid surrogate pair.

functions.name: STRBUF##_alloc(void)
functions.prose_contract: Generated functions strbuf_alloc(void) and Strbuf_alloc(void) (from DO_STRBUF(strbuf, char, strlen) and DO_STRBUF(Strbuf, Char, Strlen), tc.str.c:628, 709-710). Each returns xcalloc(1, sizeof(struct strbuf)) (or struct Strbuf) (630-634), so the fields come back zeroed (len 0, size 0, s NULL) as long as xcalloc zero-fills as calloc does; the possibility of a NULL return depends on xcalloc, which was not read. The caller owns the result and releases its buffer with the _cleanup function or the whole object with the _free function.

functions.name: STRBUF##_store1(struct STRBUF *buf, CHAR c)
functions.prose_contract: Generated static functions strbuf_store1 and Strbuf_store1 (tc.str.c:636-648). If buf->size equals buf->len it first grows buf->s with xrealloc, to 64 entries if size was 0 and otherwise to double the size, and stores the new size (639-645). It then asserts that buf->s is non-NULL (646, assert only) and writes c at buf->s[buf->len] (647); buf->len is not changed. When size differs from len, buf->s must already be a valid buffer of at least len+1 entries; this function does not check that.

functions.name: STRBUF##_terminate(struct STRBUF *buf)
functions.prose_contract: Generated functions strbuf_terminate and Strbuf_terminate (tc.str.c:651-655): they call STRBUF##_store1(buf, '\0'), which grows the buffer if size equals len and writes a NUL at buf->s[buf->len]; buf->len is not changed, so the NUL is not counted.

functions.name: STRBUF##_appendn(struct STRBUF *buf, const CHAR *s, size_t len)
functions.prose_contract: Generated functions strbuf_appendn and Strbuf_appendn (tc.str.c:664-676). If buf->size is smaller than buf->len + len, it sets size to 64 if it was 0 and doubles it until it is at least buf->len + len, then reallocates buf->s with xrealloc (667-673). It copies len characters from s to buf->s+buf->len with memcpy and increases buf->len by len (674-675). The caller must supply len readable characters in s, and no overflow check is made on buf->len + len or on the size doubling. No NUL is added.

functions.name: STRBUF##_append(struct STRBUF *buf, const CHAR *s)
functions.prose_contract: Generated functions strbuf_append and Strbuf_append (tc.str.c:678-682): each calls STRBUF##_appendn(buf, s, STRLEN(s)) with STRLEN being strlen for strbuf and Strlen for Strbuf, so it appends the characters of the NUL-terminated string s, without the terminating NUL, and grows the buffer as appendn does.

functions.name: STRBUF##_finish(struct STRBUF *buf)
functions.prose_contract: Generated functions strbuf_finish and Strbuf_finish (tc.str.c:684-689): they append a NUL with STRBUF##_append1(buf, 0), which increments buf->len so that it counts the NUL, and return xrealloc(buf->s, buf->len * sizeof(*buf->s)), the buffer shrunk or grown to exactly len entries. buf->s is not updated with the returned pointer, so if xrealloc moved the block buf->s is left pointing to the old block; the buffer is meant to be handed to the caller and the Strbuf not used again.

functions.name: STRBUF##_cleanup(void *xbuf)
functions.prose_contract: Generated functions strbuf_cleanup and Strbuf_cleanup (tc.str.c:691-698): they treat xbuf as a struct strbuf (or Strbuf) pointer and call xfree(buf->s); the struct is not freed, buf->s is not set to NULL, and len and size are not changed.

functions.name: STRBUF##_free(void *xbuf)
functions.prose_contract: Generated functions strbuf_free and Strbuf_free (tc.str.c:700-705): they call STRBUF##_cleanup(xbuf), which frees buf->s, and then xfree(xbuf), which frees the struct itself; afterwards both the struct and its s pointer are dangling.

functions.name: watch_login
functions.prose_contract: tcsh's check of the utmp file for logins and logouts of users named in the "watch" variable (tc.who.c:195-453, slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It disables interrupts with a cleanup registered (221-222) and every early return runs cleanup_until(&pintr_disabled). It returns at once if "watch" is unset and force is 0, or if less than the interval has passed since the last check (224-242). It then stats the utmp file; a failed stat prints a message (unless force) and returns, an unchanged modification time (stlast) returns, otherwise stlast is advanced to the new time before the file is read (248-260). Without getutent support, if the open fails it prints a message (unless force) and returns after stlast has already been advanced, so no scan happens (264-271). Otherwise it marks every entry in the status list OFFLINE|CLEARED and reads the utmp records, skipping non-user records, updating the matching tty entry (offline, online-announced, or changed) or inserting a new one in sorted order (279-388). If force is set or no watch list exists it returns here (396-399); otherwise for each user/terminal pair of the watch list it announces, unless firsttime, the entries that went offline, came online or changed, and updates their names and ANNOUNCE flags (405-451), then it releases the cleanup and returns (452).

functions.name: tw_result
functions.prose_contract: Maps a completion action string act (from a tcsh "complete" definition) to a TW_* look-up code and an optional pattern; defined at tw.comp.c:266-396 (slice cut the head). It frees the static result buffer res left by an earlier call (272-273). It switches on act[0] with the QUOTE bit masked off: letters select a single look-up kind, for example 'X' completion, 'S' signal, 'a' alias, 'b' binding, 'c' command, 'C' path-and-command, 'd' directory, 'D' path-and-directory, 'e' environment variable, 'f' file, 'F' (and 'p' when COMPAT is defined) path-and-file, 'g' group, 'j' job, 'l' limit, 'n' none, 's' shell variable, 't' text, 'T' path-and-text, 'v' variable, 'u' user, 'x' explain (276-341). '$' stores a copy of the rest of act in *pat and res, strips it and returns TW_VARLIST (343-346); '(' stores the text up to a ')' in *pat and returns TW_WORDLIST (348-353); '`' copies act, makes sure descriptors 0 to 2 are set up if needed, runs globone on the command text and returns TW_WORDLIST with the result in *pat, or TW_ZERO if it gives NULL (355-376). Any other first character raises the stderror ERR_COMPCOM and returns TW_ZERO (378-380). For the letter cases it then looks at act[1] with the QUOTE bit masked off: '\0' (including a QUOTE-masked end) returns the look-up code, ':' stores a stripped copy of the text after it in *pat and returns the code, and any other character gives the ERR_COMPCOM error and TW_ZERO (383-394).

functions.name: t_search
functions.prose_contract: Searches for completions of the word in tcsh's tab completion; defined at tw.parse.c:1510-1827 (slice cut the head) and returns an item count (or -1, 0 or 2 in special cases) in res. It clears the previous items, splits word into directory and name parts (1528-1534) and decides the kind of look-up: a word starting with '~' and containing no '/' becomes TW_LOGNAME, and a name with an unbraced '$' and no '/' becomes TW_VARIABLE (1542-1556). With TW_PATH set it builds the directory from pat and the typed directory (1561-1567). It then handles some kinds before collecting: TW_NONE returns -1 (1572-1574), TW_EXPLAIN prints the explanation for LIST and returns 2 (1601-1609), and other kinds set flags (1571-1618). It opens or expands the directory as the kind requires; failures return -1 (expand_dir results returned as they are, a failed opendir prints an error and returns -1, unknown kind prints an internal error and returns -1, 1624-1771). For the SPELL command on a name that is already a valid user it returns 0 (1748-1753). It then calls tw_collect, and if that returns -1 the function returns -1 (1775-1778); otherwise it acts on command: the recognize commands fix the word and add a suffix when exactly one item matched, LIST lists the items, SPELL fixes the word, and any other command value prints "Bad tw_command" and sets numitems to 0, so the function returns 0 rather than -1 in that case (1780-1821). The result is numitems (1822-1823) and the cleanup happens at err_dir (1824-1826).

functions.name: cfb64_is
functions.prose_contract: Telnet encryption suboption handler for the DES CFB64 mode (enc_des.c:233-236): it returns fb64_is(data, cnt, &fb[CFB]), so everything it does and returns is what fb64_is does for the CFB entry of the fb[] table.

functions.name: ofb64_is
functions.prose_contract: Telnet encryption suboption handler for the DES OFB64 mode (enc_des.c:239-242): it returns fb64_is(data, cnt, &fb[OFB]), so everything it does and returns is what fb64_is does for the OFB entry of the fb[] table.

functions.name: fb64_is
functions.prose_contract: Handles an incoming encryption suboption for the DES feedback modes (enc_des.c:245-307). It takes the current decrypt state fbp->state[DIR_DECRYPT-1] into a local variable. If cnt is below 1 it goes to the failure label with the state unchanged (250-251). If the first byte is FB64_IV and the remaining length is not sizeof(Block) it sets the local state to FAILED and goes to failure (255-260). If the length matches, it installs the IV into the decrypt stream with fb64_stream_iv, builds an ENCRYPT_REPLY with the FB64_IV_OK suboption, sends it with net_write (after printsub) and sets both the stored state and the local state to IN_PROGRESS (268-280).
