Any other first byte prints a debug message when encrypt_debug_mode is set and falls into the failure code (282-289). The failure code builds an ENCRYPT_REPLY with the FB64_IV_BAD suboption and writes it to the network (295-302). All paths end with fbp->state[DIR_DECRYPT-1] = state and return that value (306), so a failure with a bad size stores FAILED, and the other failures store the unchanged previous state.

functions.name: encrypt_keyid
functions.prose_contract: Processes a key identifier received for an encryption direction (encrypt.c:711-752); it returns nothing. It clamps len to MAXKEYLEN (717-718) and gets the current encryption type through kp->getcrypt. When no type is available: len==0 returns at once, otherwise kp->keylen is set to 0 (720-723). When the new length is 0 (an empty option, meaning failure): it returns at once if the stored keylen is already 0, otherwise clears keylen and, if the type has a keyid callback, calls it (724-733). When the length or the contents differ from the stored key id it stores the new id and calls the keyid callback if there is one (734-742). In those three non-returning cases it ends by sending the key id back with encrypt_send_keyid (751). When the id is unchanged it returns without sending anything: it calls the keyid callback if there is one and keeps ret = 0 when there is none, and if ret is 0, the direction is DIR_ENCRYPT and autoencrypt is set it starts output with encrypt_start_output (743-748).

functions.name: kerberos5_reply
functions.prose_contract: Handles a Kerberos V5 telnet authentication reply (kerberos5.c:568-654, slice cut the head); it returns nothing and keeps a static mutual_complete flag. It returns at once if cnt is below 1 (572-573) and switches on the first byte. KRB_REJECT prints the refusal (with the reason text if any), calls auth_send_retry and returns (575-582). KRB_ACCEPT: if mutual authentication was required and mutual_complete is not set it prints a message, calls auth_send_retry and returns (588-593); otherwise it prints the acceptance, fetches the local subkey (or the key if that fails), and if that fetch fails it prints the error, calls auth_send_retry and returns (599-610); on success it passes the 8-byte key to encrypt_session_key, frees the key block, calls auth_finished(ap, AUTH_USER), and forwards credentials with kerberos5_forward when OPTS_FORWARD_CREDS is set, then leaves the switch (612-620). KRB_RESPONSE with mutual authentication runs krb5_rd_rep: on failure it prints the error, calls auth_send_retry and returns, on success it sets mutual_complete to 1; both then return (622-641). KRB_FORWARD_ACCEPT and KRB_FORWARD_REJECT print a message and return (642-648); an unknown byte prints a debug message when auth_debug_mode is set and returns (649-652).

functions.name: sra_is
functions.prose_contract: Handles an incoming SRA telnet authentication suboption on the server side (sra.c:151-238). If cnt is below 1 it goes to the bad label (156-157). SRA_KEY: if fewer than HEXKEYBYTES bytes follow it sends SRA_REJECT, calls auth_finished(ap, AUTH_USER) and returns (161-168); otherwise it sends the server public key, returns if there is not enough room to send it, and stores the client key in pkb and calls common_key before returning (171-179). SRA_USER: more than 512 bytes breaks out to the bad code (183-184); otherwise it decodes the user name with pk_decode, calls auth_encrypt_user(user), sends SRA_CONTINUE and returns (185-191). SRA_PASS: more than 512 bytes breaks to the bad code (194-195); otherwise it decodes the password and calls check_user; if valid it sends SRA_ACCEPT, installs the session key, sets sra_valid to 1 and calls auth_finished(ap, AUTH_VALID); if not valid it sends SRA_CONTINUE (202-228); both return. Any other option prints a debug message when auth_debug_mode is set and falls to the bad code (230-233). The bad code sends SRA_REJECT, sets sra_valid to 0 and calls auth_finished(ap, AUTH_REJECT) (234-237).

functions.name: sourceroute
functions.prose_contract: Builds an IP or IPv6 source-route option from the text arg (a list such as @host1,host2 or !@host...), storing it in *cpp and its length in *lenp; defined at commands.c:2852-3017 (slice cut the head). It returns -1 if cpp or lenp is NULL (2869-2870), and when *cpp is already a buffer it returns -1 if the buffer is smaller than the minimum for the address family, but this test reads res->ai_family before res has been assigned in this function (2871-2885). It uses the caller's buffer or its own static 1024-byte buffer (2890-2896). For IPv6 it calls inet6_rth_init and returns -1 on failure or if arg does not start with '@' (2901-2908); for IPv4 it writes the LSRR or SSRR option header after a '!' or default, returning -1 if arg does not start with '@' (2917-2929). It then loops over the comma- or '@'-separated host names, resolving each with getaddrinfo (first as numeric, then as a name if EAI_NONAME): on a resolution error it prints the error, sets *cpp to the text of that host and returns 0, which does not involve any addrinfo result (2964-2976). Each address is added with inet6_rth_add (returning 0 if that fails) or copied into the IPv4 option (2977-2988). After each address except the last it returns -1 if fewer than 4 bytes of room remain in the IPv4 buffer pointer (2996-2997, so the IPv6 path has no such room check and this return does not free the addrinfo result), otherwise it frees the result and continues (2998). At the end the IPv6 case sets the header length and *lenp, the IPv4 case stores the option length and returns -1 after setting *cpp and *lenp to 0 if the route has no address (3001-3011), pads with a NOP and sets *lenp (3012-3013). It frees the last result and returns 1 (3015-3016).

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Entry point of the BSD telnet client (telnet/main.c:113-382, slice cut the head). It turns off stdio buffering, calls tninit and TerminalSaveState, derives prompt from argv[0], sets rlogin to '~' when the program name starts with "rlog" (else _POSIX_VDISABLE), sets autologin to 1 with AUTHENTICATION or -1 without it, and turns on automatic encryption when ENCRYPTION is compiled in (123-146). It then parses the options with getopt: 4, 6, 8, B, E, K, L, N, Q, S, X, a, c, d, e, f, F, k, l, n, r, s, u, x, y and, when IPSEC is compiled in, P (153-344). In the -P handler any argument whose first two characters are "in" is stored as the input policy and, failing that, any argument whose first three characters are "out" as the output policy; other arguments call usage() (330-337), so the test is a prefix test and not an exact match. Unknown options and '?' call usage() (339-341). If autologin is still -1 it is set from rlogin (345-346). With remaining arguments, more than two calls usage(); otherwise it builds an argument list (adding -l user and the source address when given) and runs tn(): the function returns 0 if tn returns 1 and 1 otherwise, after a setjmp whose longjmp calls Exit(0) (351-375). With no arguments it sets a setjmp point and loops forever calling command(1, 0, 0) (377-380); the return 0 at 381 is not reached from the loop.

functions.name: dooption
functions.prose_contract: Handles a received TELNET DO option request (telnet.c:419-525; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It first adjusts the will_wont_resp counter for the option, decrementing it once and, if it is still positive and the option state is WILL, once more (423-427). If the counter is then 0 and we do not currently want the option, it decides whether to accept it. TELOPT_TM: it sends WILL (without marking a pending reply), sets the want and state to WONT, and returns (434-442). Binary, NAWS, terminal speed, flow control, terminal type, SGA and (with ENCRYPTION) encrypt are accepted. NEW-ENVIRON, when OLD_ENVIRON is compiled in, first sends WONT for OLD_ENVIRON if that was in state WILL, then records telopt_environ and is accepted; OLD-ENVIRON itself is not accepted (it only breaks, so a WONT is sent) if NEW-ENVIRON is in state WILL, otherwise it is recorded and accepted (456-468). Authentication is accepted when autologin is set, and XDISPLOC when the DISPLAY environment variable is set (470-480). LINEMODE sets the want and state to WILL, sends WILL, initialises the SLC table and returns (with KLUDGELINEMODE it also clears kludgelinemode and sends DO SGA first, 482-491). Other options are not accepted. For an accepted option it sets the want state to WILL, sends WILL and calls setconnmode(0); for an unaccepted one it increments will_wont_resp[option] and sends WONT (498-505). If instead we already wanted the option, only LINEMODE is handled: with KLUDGELINEMODE it clears kludgelinemode and sends DO SGA, then sets the state to WILL, initialises the SLC table, sends DO SGA again (without the pending flag) and returns (511-520). Paths that did not return earlier end with set_my_state_will(option) (524).

functions.name: complete
functions.prose_contract: tnftp command-line completion callback for libedit (complete.c:360-437; slice cut the head). It returns CC_ERROR if the edit line is as long as the global line buffer (372-373). Otherwise it copies the line into the global buffer, records the cursor position, saves the previous cursor argument number and offset in the static lastc_argc and lastc_argo, and splits the line with makeargv (370-378). It returns CC_ERROR if the offset of the cursor in its word is not smaller than the static word buffer (380-381). It sets dolist to 1 when the cursor is in the same word and offset as the previous call and the saved word still matches the text typed (so the next call lists the choices), else it copies the current word into the static buffer, and terminates the word at the cursor offset (383-391). If the cursor is in the first word (cursor_argc == 0) it returns complete_command(word, dolist) (393-394). Otherwise it looks up the command in margv[0]; an unknown or ambiguous command returns CC_ERROR (396-398), so the unknown-command error applies only when the cursor is beyond the first word. It then takes the command's completion string c_complete; if the cursor word number is beyond its length and its last letter is upper case, the number is clamped to the length, and if it is still beyond the length it returns CC_ERROR (399-407). Finally it dispatches on the letter for the cursor word: 'c' or 'C' command completion, 'l' or 'L' local file completion, 'n' or 'N' CC_ERROR, 'o' or 'O' option completion, 'r' or 'R' remote completion, which prints "Must be logged in to complete." and returns CC_REDISPLAY when not connected, and any other letter calls errx(1, ...) (409-434).

functions.name: pswitch
functions.prose_contract: Swaps the active connection state with the saved "proxy" connection state in tnftp (ftp.c:1737-1821; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It clears abrtflag and installs psabort as the SIGINT handler, saving the old handler (1762-1763). With flag nonzero it returns at once if proxy is already set; with flag zero it returns at once if proxy is not set; in both early-return cases the SIGINT handler is left as psabort (the restore at 1816 is not reached, 1764-1772). Otherwise it picks the source (ip) and destination (op) blocks from two static structures, toggles proxy, and exchanges the connection fields: connected, host name, control addresses, the in and out streams, type, current type, cpend, sunique, runique, mcase, ntflag with ntin and ntout, mapflag with mapin and mapout (1777-1815). It then restores the old SIGINT handler and, if abrtflag was set meanwhile, clears it and calls the old handler directly with SIGINT (1816-1820).

functions.name: sendrequest
functions.prose_contract: Sends a local file or command output to the server with the given FTP command (tnftp ftp.c:659-886; slice cut the head); it returns nothing and reports failure through the global code (-1) and the cleanup it runs. If proxy is set it calls proxtrans and returns (688-691). It changes the transfer type if needed, installs a sigsetjmp point for aborts (on an abort during setup it drains pending replies, sets code to -1 and goes to cleanupsend, 698-703) and signal handlers. The source is stdin when local is "-", a popen of the text after '|' (failure sets code -1 and goes to cleanupsend), or a file opened with fopen, in which case only a failed open, or a file that is not a regular file according to fstat, sets code to -1 and goes to cleanupsend (706-733); stdin and piped input are therefore not required to be regular files. It then calls initconn (failure sets code -1 and goes to cleanupsend), seeks to restart_point for STOR or APPE when set (a failed seek or REST goes to cleanupsend), sends the command and opens the data connection, going to abort if dataconn fails (734-773). It copies the data with copy_bytes for image or local types or with a CRLF-translating loop for ASCII, ignoring SIGPIPE, then closes the input and data streams, reads the final reply and prints transfer statistics when bytes is positive (786-848). The abort label restores SIGINT and, when no reply is pending, sets code to -1 and goes to cleanupsend; otherwise it closes the data descriptor and stream, reads the reply, sets code to -1 and prints the statistics (850-868). cleanupsend restores the signal handlers, closes the data descriptor, input and data streams, and resets restart_point and bytes to 0 (870-885).

functions.name: slurpstring
functions.prose_contract: Extracts the next argument from the global command string stringbase into the argument area at argbase (tnftp main.c:832-959; slice cut the head). If the next character is '!' or '$' and slrflag is 0, it increments slrflag, advances stringbase by one character (INC_CHKCURSOR, not read) and returns a static one-character string "!" or "$"; if slrflag is 1 it increments slrflag and records altarg (841-855). It then skips leading blanks and tabs, increments slrflag on the first token, and records altarg for the second token (857-881). It copies characters into the argument area until a blank, tab or NUL, handling backslash (copies the next character literally) and double-quote (copies characters up to the closing quote) (883-937); a NUL inside a quote or after a backslash ends the token. At the end it terminates the argument with a NUL if any character was copied (got_one), advances argbase past it, stores the scan position in stringbase and returns the argument pointer (939-946). If no character was copied (for example only blanks, or an empty quoted string) it returns NULL, after updating slrflag (and setting altarg to NULL when slrflag was 1), leaving stringbase at the place where the scan stopped, which can be a blank rather than the terminating NUL (947-958).

functions.name: ftp_login
functions.prose_contract: Logs in to the FTP server (tnftp util.c:379-503; slice cut the head); it returns 1 on success and 0 on failure (rval, 476, 502). It copies luser and lpass, replaces them with "anonymous" and the anonpass option in anonymous mode, and calls ruserpass; a negative result sets code to -1 and goes to cleanup without printing a warning (389-410). While no user name is set it prompts for one with get_line; an input error prints "...; login aborted." and sets code to -1 (412-428); an empty answer uses the local name. In gate mode it appends "@host" to the user name (430-441). It sends USER; if the reply is CONTINUE it prompts for a password if none is set and sends PASS (443-454). If a reply is CONTINUE again it needs an account: an empty account prints "Login failed" and goes to cleanup, else it sends ACCT (455-470). A reply that is not COMPLETE, or a failed later ACCT, prints "Login failed" and goes to cleanup (471-475). Only a CONTINUE reply to USER or PASS is not a failure by itself. On success it sets rval to 1, stores the user name, and, unless proxy is set, sets connected to -1, gets the remote info, runs the "init" macro if one exists and updates the local and remote working directories (476-492). cleanup frees and zeroes the user, password and account strings and returns rval (494-502).

functions.name: tzset_unlocked
functions.prose_contract: Re-reads the TZ environment (or the default zone) into the global local-time state unless it is already current; defined at localtime.c:1881-1947 (slice cut the head); it returns nothing. In a loop it picks the zone name: NULL when wall is true, otherwise getenv("TZ"), starts from the global lclptr, and, for a name that begins with the zoneinfo directory prefix, abbreviates it (1889-1911). If the zone data is still fresh (tz_change_interval and fresh_tzdata) and either a name is set and lcl_is_set is positive with the same stored name, or there is no name and lcl_is_set is negative, it returns without changes (1913-1917). With read-write locking it upgrades to the write lock and repeats the loop once, returning if the upgrade fails (1919-1923). It then (allocating the state if needed when ALL_STATE) calls zoneinit(sp, name, flags); on an error it loads the empty (UTC) zone and sets the abbreviation to "-00" unless name is NULL and the error was ENOENT (1930-1938). A name shorter than lcl_TZname is copied into it (1939-1943). It calls settzname and sets lcl_is_set to 1 if the name is shorter than the buffer, -1 if longer, and 0 if equal; with name NULL, namelen is the buffer size plus one, so lcl_is_set is -1 (1946, 1893). With wall true, name is NULL and zoneinit calls tzload with a NULL name, which is the default zone and not UTC; UTC is used only for an empty name or as the fallback after an error (1835-1858).

functions.name: grow_nitems_alloc
functions.prose_contract: Grows an allocation count by about half and returns the byte size of the new allocation; defined at zic.c:644-659 (slice cut the head). It computes addend = (*nitems_alloc >> 1) + 1 (646). When ckd_add and ckd_mul are available it adds addend to *nitems_alloc in place (this write happens even if the check fails later) and multiplies the new count by itemsize into a local product; if neither overflowed and the product is at most INDEX_MAX it returns the product (649-651). Otherwise (no ckd macros) it requires the old count to be at most ((INDEX_MAX - 1) / 3 * 2) / itemsize, then increases *nitems_alloc by addend and returns the new count times itemsize (653-655); that bound keeps the product below about INDEX_MAX - 1 plus itemsize, so it cannot overflow ptrdiff_t for itemsize 2, and larger item sizes were not analysed. In both builds, when the checks fail it calls memory_exhausted("integer overflow") (658), which is not shown to return, so there is no value returned on that path.

functions.name: cachedb_handle_query
functions.prose_contract: Handles a query in unbound's cachedb module (cachedb.c:794-884; slice cut the head); it returns nothing and works through qstate. It clears is_cachedb_answer. If the module is not enabled, or the query is blacklisted, says no cache lookup, or a stub or forwarder forbids caching, it sets ext_state[id] to module_wait_module and returns (802-816). It then looks in unbound's internal cache; on a hit it sets module_finished and returns (820-834). Otherwise it looks in the external cache; on a hit it stores the answer into the internal cache (844). If serve_expired is configured and the entry is expired, it drops return_msg, sets module_wait_module, clears need_refetch and returns (850-858). If need_refetch is set and serve_expired_data has a timer it drops return_msg and sets module_wait_module and returns (859-864), so this wait applies only with the serve-expired timer. Otherwise it marks the answer as a cachedb answer and sets module_finished (866-870). With no external hit, if serve_expired_data, cachedb_check_when_serve_expired and no serve_expired_client_timeout apply it sends the expired answer with mesh_respond_serve_expired (873-879), and it sets module_wait_module (883).

functions.name: cachedb_operate
functions.prose_contract: Event entry point of unbound's cachedb module (cachedb.c:921-968; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It reads the module environment and the per-query state iq. For a new or pass event with no iq it creates the state with cachedb_new, replying SERVFAIL through error_response and returning if that fails (932-939). With an iq, a new or pass event calls cachedb_handle_query and returns, and a moddone event calls cachedb_handle_response and returns (940-947). With an iq and an outbound entry (and none of the earlier events) it ignores the response and returns (948-954). An error event, whether or not an outbound entry or an iq exists, logs, replies SERVFAIL and returns (955-958); a moddone event with no iq sets ext_state[id] to module_finished and returns (960-963). Any other event logs "bad event for cachedb" and replies SERVFAIL (966-967).

functions.name: getentropy_fallback
functions.prose_contract: Fills buf with len bytes of pseudo-random data by hashing system state with SHA-512 (the real name is getentropy_fallback, getentropy_osx.c:204-417; the slice 255-417 is its tail). It saves errno and chooses the repeat count (a smaller one when the process id equals the one of the previous call, 229-237). For each chunk of up to 64 bytes it initialises a SHA512 context and, repeat times, hashes the time of day, several sysctl values, process and session ids, signal masks, addresses and the page contents of mapped memory, resource usage, file system information for "." and "/" and for descriptor 0 (stat results, and, when fstat on descriptor 0 yields -1 and the (unset) mode looks like a regular file, FIFO or socket, the statvfs, statfs and related calls on it), the child resource usage and the time of day again (HX and HD hash the values whether the call failed or not, 240-407). It finalises the digest and copies min(64, remaining) bytes into buf (409-411). After the loop it zeroes the context and the digest with explicit_bzero, restores errno and returns 0 (413-416); this is the only return in the function. Failing system calls are not treated as errors; their results are only hashed.

functions.name: remote_control_callback
functions.prose_contract: Event callback for one unbound remote-control connection (remote.c:4291-4347; slice cut the head); it returns 0 except where the handshake is still pending. For an event other than NETEVENT_NOERROR it logs a timeout when it was one, calls clean_point(rc, s) and returns 0 (4298-4303). For an SSL connection it performs SSL_do_handshake; any result other than 1 returns remote_handshake_later(rc, s, c, r, error), whose return value is passed on, so this covers both a handshake that must be retried and a failed handshake (4304-4311). After a successful handshake it clears shake_state. If certificates are not in use it logs an unauthenticated connection; if they are in use it requires the verification result X509_V_OK and a peer certificate, and otherwise cleans the connection up and returns 0 (4316-4337). Then it fills res with the SSL object and the descriptor, calls handle_req, logs completion, cleans the connection up and returns 0 (4340-4346).

functions.name: dt_msg_queue_submit
functions.prose_contract: Queues a dnstap message buffer for the writer thread (dtstream.c:235-302; the packet name dt_msg_queue_push does not exist and the slice 255-509 starts inside this function); it returns nothing and takes ownership of buf. It returns without doing anything if buf is NULL (241). It frees buf and returns if len is 0 or mq is NULL (242-253), and frees buf and returns after logging an out-of-memory message if the entry allocation fails (256-261). Otherwise it locks the queue, decides whether to start a timer (list empty or the writer is not writing) and whether to wake the writer at once (message count equal to DTIO_MSG_FOR_WAKEUP, or the size crossing 90 percent of maxsize) (267-277). If the queued size plus len would exceed maxsize it unlocks, frees buf and the entry and returns, dropping the message (279-286). Otherwise it adds len to cursize, increments msgcount, appends the entry at the end of the list and unlocks (287-297); after unlocking it calls dt_msg_queue_start_timer when a wakeup or timer start was decided (299-301).

functions.name: ipsecmod_handle_query
functions.prose_contract: Handles a query inside unbound's ipsecmod module (ipsecmod.c:386-464; slice cut the head); it returns nothing and works through qstate. If the module is not enabled or the query is not whitelisted it sets ext_state[id] to module_wait_module and returns (393-396). If the IPSECKEY lookup has not been done yet, it sets no_cache_store for an A or AAAA query, sets module_wait_module and returns (399-412). Otherwise, if an IPSECKEY rrset with data exists, it calls ipsecmod_error and returns if the data is bogus and bogus data is not ignored, and likewise returns after ipsecmod_error if the hook fails while ipsecmod_strict is set (415-433). It then finds the answer rrset of the return message and, if its TTL is above ipsecmod_max_ttl, sets the rrset TTL and all its RR TTLs to ipsecmod_max_ttl, and if the message TTL is also above the limit lowers it and recomputes (not clamps) prefetch_ttl with PREFETCH_TTL_CALC and serve_expired_ttl as the new ttl plus the configured serve_expired_ttl (436-453). It stores the reply in the cache (logging an error when that fails, which does not stop it) and sets ext_state[id] to module_finished (457-463).

functions.name: response_type_from_server
functions.prose_contract: Classifies a DNS response from a name server (unbound iterator, iter_resptype.c:108-309; slice cut the head) and returns one of the RESPONSE_TYPE_ values. It returns THROWAWAY if msg or request is NULL or the TC flag is set (116-121). For NXDOMAIN it returns REC_LAME when RA is set, AA is not and rdset is 0, CNAME if the answer section has a CNAME for the query name, else ANSWER (124-139); any other non-NOERROR rcode returns THROWAWAY (143-144). For NOERROR it takes the origin zone from dp (default root) and scans the answer section: an NS rrset for a qtype of ANY or NS below the zone returns ANSWER with AA set or REFERRAL otherwise (167-176); an answer of the query type and name returns ANSWER with AA, else leaves the loop (183-193); CNAMEs followed to their target (195-200). After the loop it returns ANSWER for qtype ANY, and CNAME if a CNAME was followed (203-210). In the authority section, an SOA at or above the query name returns REC_LAME (RA set, AA not set, rdset 0) or ANSWER (215-227). An NS rrset in the authority section: equal to the origin zone returns REC_LAME (RA, no AA, rdset 0), else THROWAWAY (no answers, no AA, rdset 0), else ANSWER, so with rdset nonzero it returns ANSWER (242-259); an NS at or above the origin zone returns THROWAWAY if rdset else LAME (263-267); an NS below it returns REFERRAL (271-281). An entirely empty message returns THROWAWAY until empty_nodata_found reaches EMPTY_NODATA_RETRY_COUNT (when that pointer is given) and ANSWER after, or ANSWER at once without the pointer (294-303). Otherwise REC_LAME with RA set, AA not set and rdset 0, else ANSWER (306-308).

functions.name: scrub_sanitize
functions.prose_contract: Removes resource record sets from a parsed DNS response that a name server for zonename should not be trusted for (unbound iter_scrub.c:974-1134; slice cut the head); it returns 1 at its only return (1133). The first rrset is allowed to stay if it is a DNAME in the answer section whose owner is a strict parent of the query name and a subdomain of the zone, even though its name differs from the query name (986-995). It then removes the following answer-section rrsets whose owner differs from the query name (997-1013). Second pass over all rrsets (1022-1132): an A or AAAA rrset is length-checked and removed if that fails (1027-1031); an A, AAAA, SVCB or HTTPS rrset is removed if priv_rrset_bad says it is bad (1035-1048); an rrset whose owner is not within the zone is removed (with its referencing additional section being flagged for removal), except that an NS rrset above the zone in a NOERROR/NODATA reply without SOA is kept for lame classification, and an out-of-zone A/AAAA is stored in the cache instead of being kept when harden_glue is off (1057-1087). NS rrsets in answer or authority sections record their owner (1088-1097); additional-section rrsets are removed when del_addi was flagged (1098-1102); overreaching NSEC rrsets are removed (1104-1109); with harden_unverified_glue, A/AAAA glue that is not below the NS owner is marked as unverified glue, cached and removed from the message (1110-1128); everything else stays.

functions.name: handle_cname_response
functions.prose_contract: Collects the CNAME and DNAME chain of a response for the iterator (iterator.c:532-579; slice cut the head); it returns 1 on success and 0 on failure. It starts with *mname and *mname_len set to the chased query name (537-538). For each answer rrset it adds a DNAME that is a parent of the current name to the prepend-answer list unless it is already there, without following it (548-554). It adds a CNAME for the current name to the list unless the list already holds it, and in that case moves *mname to the CNAME's target (556-562); a CNAME that is already in the prepend list is neither added nor followed, so *mname is not advanced for it. An out-of-memory result from iter_add_prepend_answer returns 0 at once (551-552, 560-561). It then adds every NSEC and NSEC3 rrset from the authority section to the authority prepend list, returning 0 if that fails (568-577), and returns 1 (578).

functions.name: apply_ixfr
functions.prose_contract: Applies a received IXFR (a list of deletions and additions framed by SOA records) to the zone z (unbound authzone.c:4919-5052; slice cut the head); it returns 1 on success and 0 on any failure, including the "soft failure" case. It walks the resource records of the transfer chunks; a record that cannot be read returns 0 (4937-4943). The first record must be an SOA and so must the second, otherwise it returns 0 (4947-4954). An SOA whose rdata is shorter than 22 bytes returns 0 (4957). The first SOA records its serial and sets delmode to 1, and ixfr_start_serial must succeed (checked against xfr->serial) or the function returns 0 (4959-4969); a later SOA with the same serial counts up and returns 0 if it is the second record, and when it is the third occurrence it stores the serial in xfr->serial and leaves the loop (4970-4990). Each SOA that does not end the loop then toggles delmode (4997), so the first SOA ends up in add mode. In delete mode a record is removed with az_remove_rr_decompress (a failure returns 0; a record that did not exist sets softfail); in add mode a record is inserted with az_insert_rr_decompress unless it is the first record, which is skipped, so the first SOA is not added at that point (a failure returns 0; a duplicate sets softfail) (5005-5042). After the loop, if softfail is set it returns 0 so that the full zone is fetched, otherwise it returns 1 (5047-5051).

functions.name: xfr_set_timeout
functions.prose_contract: Schedules the next probe timer of an authoritative-zone transfer task (unbound authzone.c:6994-7073; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It starts next_probe at the current time, or at xfr->lease_time when that is set and failure is 0 (7004-7006). On success it resets the backoff to 0; on failure it sets it to 3 or doubles it, capped at AUTH_TRANSFER_MAX_BACKOFF (7008-7017). If the zone exists it adds the refresh interval (or retry after a failure), or the expiry if that is smaller, adds the backoff on failure, and, if lease_time plus expiry lies before the computed time but after now, uses that instead (7019-7033). If the zone does not exist it adds only the backoff to the starting time (7034-7037). It creates the timer if needed and returns after logging if that allocation fails, leaving no timer set (7039-7050). It records the worker and env, computes the delay (zero when the time has passed), and, when lookup_only is set and masters exist, uses a zero delay and sets only_lookup on the probe task if it has no worker (7052-7064). It then logs the delay and arms the timer with comm_timer_set (7065-7072).

functions.name: doq_conn_write_streams
functions.prose_contract: Writes pending DNS-over-QUIC stream data and QUIC packets of conn through ngtcp2 (unbound listen_dnsport.c:5337-5483; slice cut the head); it returns 1 normally and 0 when it closes the connection because of an error, and stores in *err_drop (if non-NULL) whether closing failed. It loops over the connection's write-stream list starting at stream_write_first, with a final pass with stream id -1 and no data when no stream is left (5340-5383). For each stream it sets the data vectors from the not-yet-written part of the length prefix and the answer, sets the FIN flag and the MORE flag when another stream follows (5355-5389), and calls ngtcp2_conn_writev_stream. A negative result: NGTCP2_ERR_WRITE_MORE adds the written bytes to nwrite, marks the stream done when fully written, moves to the next stream and continues the loop without returning (5397-5407); NGTCP2_ERR_STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED and NGTCP2_ERR_STREAM_SHUT_WR set an application error and close the connection (doq_conn_close_error), set *err_drop to 1 if that failed, and return 0 (5408-5437); any other error logs, sets a library error, closes the connection and returns 0 the same way (5440-5454). On a nonnegative result it adds the written data to the stream and marks it done when complete (5459-5463). A result of 0 disables further writing, updates the packet transmit time and returns 1 (5464-5468). Otherwise it sends the packet with doq_send_pkt, stops the loop if a packet was blocked or max_packets (65535) were sent, and moves to the next stream (5470-5479). After the loop it updates the packet transmit time and returns 1 (5481-5482).

functions.name: mesh_attach_sub
functions.prose_contract: Creates (or finds) a sub-query state of the mesh and attaches it to qstate's state (unbound mesh.c:1260-1282; slice cut the head); it returns 1 on success and 0 on failure. It calls mesh_add_sub and returns 0 if that fails (1267-1269). It notes whether the sub-state had no super states before (super_set.count == 0), calls mesh_state_attachment to link it below qstate's mesh state and returns 0 if that fails (1270-1272). If the sub-state has no reply list and no callback list, was detached before and now has exactly one super state, it decrements mesh->num_detached_states (1274-1278). It returns 1 (1281).

functions.name: serviced_check_qname
functions.prose_contract: Compares the query name of a received packet with the query name stored in qbuf (unbound outside_network.c:3000-3046); it returns 1 if both name sequences match label for label, otherwise 0. It returns 0 at once if the packet limit is below 17 bytes (3006-3007). It walks the packet's name from offset 12 and qbuf's name from offset 10 in step. A compression pointer in the packet name is followed (after checking that the pointer's bytes and its target are inside the packet limit); more than MAX_COMPRESS_PTRS pointers return 0 (3012-3023). For a plain label it returns 0 if d2 is beyond qbuf+qbuflen, the two label lengths differ, the length exceeds LDNS_MAX_LABELLEN, the label would reach the packet limit, or the label bytes differ with memcmp (3025-3039); it then moves to the next labels. It returns 1 when both reach the end of the name (3011, 3045). The code checks d2 against qbuf+qbuflen only before a label, not that d2 plus the label length stays inside qbuf.

functions.name: serviced_tcp_callback
functions.prose_contract: Callback for a TCP (or TLS) query to an upstream server in unbound (outside_network.c:3139-3235); it always returns 0 (3182, 3234), but its effects depend on the outcome. It clears sq->pending, logs an address on error, and on success marks that TCP works for the address in the infra cache (3153-3159). With dnstap and the right logging options it sends the response message to dnstap (3160-3174). If the status is serviced_query_TCP_EDNS and the response rcode is FORMERR or NOTIMPL, it sets the status to serviced_query_TCP_EDNS_fallback, starts the query again with serviced_tcp_initiate and returns 0 without calling the callbacks (3175-3182). If the status is the EDNS fallback and the rcode is NOERROR, NXDOMAIN or YXDOMAIN, it records "no EDNS" for the server in the infra cache unless DNSSEC is wanted (logging an error if that fails) and sets the status to serviced_query_TCP (3183-3199). For tcp_upstream or ssl_upstream queries it updates the round-trip time: a failure records -1, and a success with time moving forward records the measured time in milliseconds if it is below 60000 (3200-3224). It then ensures a reply structure (using a local one if rep is NULL), copies the server address into it and calls serviced_callbacks(sq, error, c, rep) (3226-3233) before returning 0.

functions.name: outnet_serviced_query
functions.prose_contract: Finds or creates a serviced (deduplicated) outgoing query and registers a callback on it (unbound outside_network.c:3474-3597; slice cut the head); it returns the serviced_query or NULL. It obtains a region from the allocator, returning NULL if that fails (3495-3496); if qstate has an outgoing EDNS option list it copies it into that region and uses the copy while the query callbacks run, returning NULL after releasing the region if the copy fails (3497-3505). If inplace_cb_query_call fails it releases the region and returns NULL without having put the original edns_opts_back_out list back, since the restore comes only after that call (3507-3515). It then restores the original list, appends a configured client-string option if the address matches, generates the query packet in buff and looks up an existing serviced query (3517-3528). If none exists it optionally increments the rate limit counter and returns NULL with *was_ratelimited set when the rate limit applies, except for random pass-through (3531-3551); it then creates the serviced query, undoing the rate-limit count and returning NULL on failure, and allocates the callback entry in its region, undoing the rate-limit count, deleting the new query from the tree and returning NULL if that fails (3554-3577). If one exists, it releases the region and allocates a callback entry, returning NULL on failure (3580-3589). It fills the callback entry, links it at the head of sq->cblist and returns sq (3592-3596).

functions.name: outnet_tcp_take_into_use
functions.prose_contract: Takes a free pending TCP entry from the outside network and uses it for the waiting query w (unbound outside_network.c:661-832; slice cut the head); it returns 1 on success and 0 on failure. It clears two toggle flags of the comm point (670-671), returns 0 if SSL upstream is wanted but no SSL context exists (676-679), opens a TCP socket with outnet_get_tcp_fd (returns 0 on -1) and binds it to the pending entry with pick_outgoing_tcp (returns 0 on failure) (682-689), sets it non-blocking and starts connecting (a connect error other than EINPROGRESS logs if the error warrants it, closes the socket and returns 0; with fast open the plain connect is skipped for non-SSL TCP, 691-751). For TLS it creates the SSL object (on failure closes the comm point and returns 0), sets the shake state, copies the authentication name (an allocation failure frees the SSL object, closes the comm point and returns 0) and sets the name on the SSL object (a failure frees everything and returns 0) (752-791). Then it links the pending entry to w, increments num_tcp_outgoing, removes the entry from the free list, fills the reuse and comm point fields and copies the address, removing an existing tree entry first if the key is set (792-811). It records the SSL state and authentication name in the reuse structure, frees any old name, inserts the reuse entry in the tree, calls outnet_tcp_take_query_setup(s, pend, w) and returns 1 (813-831). The write timer on w is set inside outnet_tcp_take_query_setup with comm_timer_set(w->timer, &tv) built from w->timeout (outside_network.c:650-656) and not in this function.

functions.name: sldns_fget_token_l
functions.prose_contract: Reads one token from file f into token (unbound sldns parse.c:33-224; slice cut the head); it returns the token length, -1 or 0. delim defaults to LDNS_PARSE_NORMAL. It reads characters with getc, treats '\r' as a blank, tracks parentheses (a depth counter p, outside quotes and comments) and ';' comments, and a leading '"' in delim starts in quoted mode (44-60). If a ')' makes the depth negative it terminates the token and returns 0 as soon as the next character is read, without that character being counted for line_nr (82-86). Newlines inside parentheses or comments are turned into blanks and counted in *line_nr when line_nr is non-NULL (98-147), and a newline seen elsewhere increments *line_nr as it is processed (156-157, 186-189). If the token limit would be reached (limit > 0) it terminates the buffer and returns -1 (140-143, 179-182). A delimiter at depth 0 after at least one character ends the token (jump to tokenread) unless only blanks have been seen, in which case the token is restarted (155-169). At EOF it returns the number of characters read (199-201). If the loop ended with nothing read or with unbalanced parentheses it returns -1 (203-209). At tokenread it skips the following delimiter characters with sldns_fskipcs_l and returns -1 if the parentheses are unbalanced, else the token length (212-223).

functions.name: sldns_bget_keyword_data
functions.prose_contract: Reads a keyword token and then a data token from the sldns buffer b (unbound sldns parse.c:491-522; the excerpt in the packet is its tail, so the real name is sldns_bget_keyword_data). It returns -1 if strlen(keyword) is at least LDNS_MAX_KEYWORDLEN or the keyword buffer cannot be allocated (499-503). It reads the first token into that buffer with delimiter k_del and limit data_limit; if the result is 0 or -1 it frees the buffer and returns -1 (505-509). If the token starts with keyword (a strncmp over strlen(keyword) characters, so a longer token that begins with the keyword also matches) it frees the buffer and returns the result of sldns_bget_token(b, data, d_del, 0) for the data token, with no length limit (512-517); otherwise it frees the buffer and returns -1 (518-520).

functions.name: sldns_buffer_skip
functions.prose_contract: Advances the position of buffer by count bytes (sbuffer.h:258-262; slice cut the head). It asserts that buffer->_position + count <= buffer->_limit (260), where count is converted to an unsigned type, so a negative count that would move the position before the start makes the sum wrap to a huge value and the assert fails, while a negative count within the current position passes it; then it adds count to _position (261). With NDEBUG the assertion is compiled out and no check remains. It returns nothing.

functions.name: config_set_option
functions.prose_contract: Sets one unbound configuration option from the text pair (opt, val) (config_file.c:541-950; slice cut the head); it returns 1 when the option was recognised and applied and 0 when it was not or the value was rejected. It returns 0 for a NULL opt (545) and appends a ':' to opt when it has none and a copy fits in a 64-byte buffer (546-549). It then walks one long if/else chain comparing opt with the option names; most entries are macros that parse val (yes/no, a number that must be non-zero or may be zero, a string that replaces and frees the old one, a list that is replaced, appended to or inserted uniquely). Special cases include: num-threads always returns 0 (557-559); outgoing-port-permit and outgoing-port-avoid, local-zone and val-override-date return the result of cfg_mark_ports, cfg_parse_local_zone or a time conversion (560-575); tls-protocols returns 0 for an invalid value (638-641); local-data-ptr calls cfg_ptr_reverse on the option name argument opt and returns the result of cfg_strlist_insert (578-580); an unrecognised name reaches the final else and returns 0, and a successful branch falls to return 1 (947-949). Because most options are table macros, the exact fields updated are those named in the macros (for example the global mirrors of max-ttl, serve-expired and the RTT limits are updated where the option sets them).

functions.name: yylex
functions.prose_contract: Flex-generated scanner of unbound's configuration lexer (configlexer.c; YY_DECL at 4828, slice 4857-5157 is inside its body, the rules table). On first use it initialises the scanner state, defaults yyin to stdin and yyout to stdout and creates the input buffer if none exists (4834-4856). It then repeatedly matches the longest input prefix with the generated DFA tables and runs the action of the matching rule through a switch on yy_act. The rule actions in the generated code either return a token number for a configuration keyword to the parser or just update lexer state (start conditions, line counters, buffer handling); at the end-of-buffer logic it either continues scanning, finishes the last match, or, at end of file, runs the end-of-file action and returns the scanner's end token (YY_NULL) through yyterminate() (7200-7263). An internal inconsistency calls YY_FATAL_ERROR (7269, 7291, 7360), which does not return normally. The function returns an int token value each time a rule returns, and otherwise keeps scanning.

functions.name: yyparse
functions.prose_contract: Bison-generated LALR parser of unbound's configuration grammar (configparser.c; function at 2807-8270, this slice 5406-5706 is inside its reduce actions). It takes no argument, keeps its state and value stacks on the C stack (initial depth YYINITDEPTH, growing them when full, and failing with YYNOMEM if they cannot grow), and starts by asking for a token (yychar = YYEMPTY, 2846-2850). Each cycle it pushes the state, reads a token with yylex when needed, looks up the action in the tables, and either shifts the token, accepts, or reduces by a rule (yyreduce, 3030) by running that rule's semantic action; the actions in this region call the configuration-building helpers (for example handlers that set fields of the config being parsed or log a parse error) and may use YYABORT or YYERROR in their action code. A syntax error calls yyerror with "syntax error", counts it, and tries to recover by popping states until one can shift the error token; at end of input during recovery it aborts (8118-8214). It ends at yyreturnlab, which discards the lookahead symbol and the stacks, frees a heap-grown stack if any, and returns yyresult (8245-8269): 0 for accept (8221), 1 for abort (8229), and 2 for memory exhaustion (8238).

functions.name: yyparse
functions.prose_contract: Bison-generated LALR parser of unbound's configuration grammar (configparser.c; function at 2807-8270, this slice 6991-7244 is inside its reduce actions). It takes no argument, keeps its state and value stacks on the C stack (initial depth YYINITDEPTH, growing them when full, and failing with YYNOMEM if they cannot grow), and starts by asking for a token (yychar = YYEMPTY, 2846-2850). Each cycle it pushes the state, reads a token with yylex when needed, looks up the action in the tables, and either shifts the token, accepts, or reduces by a rule (yyreduce, 3030) by running that rule's semantic action; the actions in this region call the configuration-building helpers (for example handlers that set fields of the config being parsed or log a parse error) and may use YYABORT or YYERROR in their action code. A syntax error calls yyerror with "syntax error", counts it, and tries to recover by popping states until one can shift the error token; at end of input during recovery it aborts (8118-8214). It ends at yyreturnlab, which discards the lookahead symbol and the stacks, frees a heap-grown stack if any, and returns yyresult (8245-8269): 0 for accept (8221), 1 for abort (8229), and 2 for memory exhaustion (8238).

functions.name: yyparse
functions.prose_contract: Bison-generated LALR parser of unbound's configuration grammar (configparser.c; function at 2807-8270, this slice 8008-8268 covers the last reduce actions and the tail). It takes no argument, keeps its state and value stacks on the C stack (initial depth YYINITDEPTH, growing them when full, and failing with YYNOMEM if they cannot grow), and starts by asking for a token (yychar = YYEMPTY, 2846-2850). Each cycle it pushes the state, reads a token with yylex when needed, looks up the action in the tables, and either shifts the token, accepts, or reduces by a rule (yyreduce, 3030) by running that rule's semantic action and then pushing the left-hand-side state (goto yynewstate at 8112). A syntax error is counted and reported with yyerror; with an error status of 3 an unusable lookahead is discarded and end of input aborts (8123-8146), then states are popped until one accepts the error token and, when the stack is empty, the parse aborts (8175-8214). The label yyacceptlab sets yyresult to 0, yyabortlab to 1 and yyexhaustedlab to 2, and all end at yyreturnlab, which destroys the lookahead if it is still held, pops all stack entries, frees a heap-grown stack and returns yyresult (8220-8269).

functions.name: change_rrsig_rrset
functions.prose_contract: Converts an RRSIG-only rrset of a parsed message into a data rrset of type datatype, or splits the signatures into a new rrset (unbound msgparse.c:397-446; slice cut the head); it returns the data rrset or NULL on allocation failure. It first computes the hash of the data rrset (402-403). If hasother is set it creates a new rrset in the given section with new_rrset (returning NULL on failure), increments the section's rrset counter, moves the RRSIGs over with moveover_rrsigs (returning NULL on failure) and returns the new rrset (406-424). If hasother is 0 it reuses sigset itself: it removes it from its hash bucket, reinserts it under the new hash, calls change_section, sets the type and flags, and turns its records into signatures by adding rr_count to rrsig_count, linking the record list behind any existing signature list and clearing rr_first and rr_last (427-444). change_section returns at once without moving the rrset or changing the section counters when section already equals the rrset's section (msgparse.c:292-293), so in that case only the other fields change. It returns the rrset at 445.

functions.name: event_add
functions.prose_contract: Registers an event with the minimal libevent-like event base of unbound (mini_event.c:292-325; slice cut the head); it returns 0 on success and -1 if the descriptor is out of range. If the event is already added it first removes it with event_del (294-295), so that removal has happened even when the function then returns -1. It returns -1 without adding anything if the descriptor is set and not below the base's capfd (296-297); in that case the event is left removed and not added. For a read or write event with a valid descriptor it records the event in the descriptor table, sets the read and/or write bits and the content bit, clears the ready bit and raises maxfd if needed (298-310). With a timeout argument and an EV_TIMEOUT event it computes the absolute timeout from the base time plus tv (with microsecond carry) and inserts the event into the timer tree (311-322). It then sets ev->added to 1 and returns 0 (323-324).

functions.name: http_process_chunk_header
functions.prose_contract: Processes one line of an HTTP chunked-transfer header or trailer from the comm point's buffer (netevent.c:4907-4960; slice cut the head); it returns 0, 1 or 2. It returns 1 at once if no complete header line is available (4909-4910). In trailer mode (http_in_chunk_headers == 3): an empty line when tcp_byte_count is 0 empties the buffer, calls the callback with NETEVENT_DONE and returns 2 (4914-4922); an empty line otherwise switches back to chunk-header mode (1), moves the buffer content over and returns 1 (4924-4930); a non-empty trailer line returns 1 (4933). In chunk-size mode (http_in_chunk_headers == 1) it parses the line with strtol in base 16; it returns 0 if no digit was consumed, errno is set, or the value is negative, and the check is only on the start of the line, so trailing characters after the hexadecimal digits (such as chunk extensions or junk) are accepted (4936-4946). Otherwise it stores the chunk size in tcp_byte_count, leaves header mode, moves the buffer content over, flips the buffer, switches to trailer mode when the size is 0, and returns 1 (4947-4956). For any other mode it returns 1 (4959).

functions.name: autr_process_prime
functions.prose_contract: Processes a fetched DNSKEY rrset for an RFC 5011 auto-trust anchor (unbound autotrust.c:2169-2280; slice cut the head); it returns 1 normally and 0 when the trust point was removed, revoked, or its next probe could not be set. On entry it expects tp->lock held. A revoked trust point is unlocked and 0 is returned (2180-2186). It records the query time, reassembles the keys after hold-down expiry and returns 1 when that allocation fails (2189-2201). Without a DNSKEY rrset it returns 1 (2203-2210). It checks for revoked keys and, if changed, reassembles (return 1 on failure) and, when no DS and no DNSKEY rrset remain, records the success time, calls autr_tp_remove and returns 0 (2212-2225). If the DNSKEY set does not verify it increments query_failed and writes the file when there was an earlier success, and returns 1 (2228-2237). Otherwise it records success, resets query_failed, calls update_events and do_statetable (each failing with an out-of-memory log and return 1), cleans up keys, and returns 0 if set_next_probe fails (2239-2264); then it writes the file and, if changed, reassembles (return 1 on failure) and removes the trust point with autr_tp_remove and returns 0 when no DS and no DNSKEY rrset remain (2265-2276), else returns 1 (2279). autr_tp_remove unlocks tp->lock, deletes the trust point from the anchor tree and frees it only if it was still in the tree; if another thread already deleted it nothing is freed here (autotrust.c:2142-2163).

functions.name: anchors_swap_tree
functions.prose_contract: Swaps the trust anchor tree and the auto-trust probe tree between two validator anchor sets (val_anchor.c:1386-1403); the packet name anchors_swap does not exist. It returns without doing anything if either anchors or data is NULL (1392-1393). Otherwise it saves anchors->tree and anchors->autr->probe, assigns data's tree and probe to anchors, and gives the saved ones to data (1395-1402), the probe structure being copied by value. It takes no locks, so the caller must ensure exclusive access, and both autr pointers must be non-NULL because they are dereferenced.

functions.name: validate_nameerror_response
functions.prose_contract: Validates a NXDOMAIN reply with NSEC or NSEC3 proofs (unbound validator.c:1271-1372; slice cut the head); it returns nothing and reports through chase_reply->security, *rcode and *suspend. It clears *suspend and scans the authority rrsets: an NSEC that proves the name does not exist sets has_valid_nsec, one with the best closest encloser that proves no covering wildcard sets has_valid_wnsec (the flag may be cleared again by a later NSEC of the same depth), and an NSEC proving an insecure delegation sets the reply to sec_status_insecure and returns at once; an NSEC3 only marks nsec3s_seen (1287-1313). If either NSEC proof is missing and NSEC3 records were seen, it runs the NSEC3 proof: an unchecked result sets *suspend and returns, any other result that is not secure keeps that security value in chase_reply->security and returns without trying the NODATA fallback, and a secure result sets both has_valid flags (1315-1334). If the name-error proof is missing, or the wildcard proof is missing, it runs validate_nodata_response and returns after suspend; if that leaves the reply secure it changes *rcode to NOERROR, otherwise it marks the reply bogus with the DNSSEC-bogus reason (1337-1366). If both proofs hold it sets the reply secure (1370-1371).

functions.name: processFindKey
functions.prose_contract: Validator step that finds the key needed to validate the reply (unbound validator.c:2026-2185; slice cut the head); it returns 1 when validation should continue in the current invocation (the state in vq->state decides what runs next) and 0 when it is waiting for a sub-query or has finished the event, or the result of val_error on an error. If the key entry is a null key (an earlier DNSKEY lookup failed with retry) it generates a DNSKEY sub-query for the DS owner name and returns 0, or val_error if generating the request fails; this return 0 does not set vq->state (2040-2048). It picks the target key name from the signer name (or the query name) and compares it with the current key entry name; equal names set vq->state to VAL_VALIDATE_STATE and return 1 (2050-2063). If the target equals the last empty-DS name it marks the reply bogus, sets VAL_FINISHED_STATE and returns 1; otherwise that name becomes the current name (2065-2081). If the target is not below the current name it marks the reply bogus, sets VAL_FINISHED_STATE and returns 1 (2088-2093). It strips labels to find the next name (2095-2102). If a DS rrset exists for a different name than the current key it sends a DNSKEY request for it and returns 0 (2112-2121). If no DS rrset exists for the next name it processes a suspended sub-query DS reply or a cached DS reply with process_ds_response (suspension sets up a timer in VAL_FINDKEY_STATE and returns 0, or val_error if the timer fails; a processed cached reply returns 1) and otherwise sends a DS request and returns 0 (2123-2173). Otherwise it sends the DNSKEY request for the DS name and returns 0 (2177-2184).

functions.name: process_prime_response
functions.prose_contract: Handles the reply to the DNSKEY priming query for the current trust anchor (unbound validator.c:3456-3518; slice cut the head); it returns nothing and sets vq->state and vq->key_entry. It looks up the trust anchor (the anchor lock is held on success); if there is none it sets VAL_INIT_STATE, or VAL_VALIDATE_STATE when no anchor name was set, clears the anchor name and returns (3462-3471). For a NOERROR reply it finds the DNSKEY rrset in the answer section (3475-3479). For an auto-trust anchor it calls autr_process_prime and, if that returns 0, sets VAL_INIT_STATE, clears the anchor name and returns without unlocking here (3481-3488). It then builds the key entry with primeResponseToKE and unlocks the anchor (3490-3492). Only if a key entry exists: a bad entry with restarts left blacklists the origin, clears the error info, counts the restart, resets the entry and state to VAL_INIT_STATE and returns; otherwise it clears chain_blacklist, adds error info (origin and trust anchor name) and caches the entry (3493-3510). With no key entry the blacklist clearing and the error info are skipped. Finally, if the key entry is missing, null or bad, the state becomes VAL_VALIDATE_STATE (3513-3516).

functions.name: sentinel_get_keytag
functions.prose_contract: Parses the key tag out of a root-sentinel query label (unbound validator.c:593-608; slice cut the head); it returns 1 on success and 0 on failure. It allocates a zeroed buffer of SENTINEL_KEYTAG_LEN+1 bytes, returning 0 if that fails (596-598). It copies SENTINEL_KEYTAG_LEN bytes from start into it (always reading that many bytes), terminates it, stores strtol(buffer, &e, 10) cast to uint16_t into *keytag, and returns 0 if e is NULL or does not point at the terminating NUL (599-605); so non-digit characters, a leading sign or blank followed by a non-digit, and an input with no digits (for example only blanks) return 0, while an input containing a NUL early, or leading white space followed by digits that fill the string, may return 1. The buffer is freed on all paths and 1 is returned otherwise (606-607). *keytag is written before the check, so it holds a value even on the failure return.

functions.name: kernel_set_device
functions.prose_contract: Sends a WireGuard device configuration to the FreeBSD kernel (wireguard-tools ipc-freebsd.h:250-362); the packet name wg_set_device does not exist, the function is kernel_set_device. It copies the interface name, builds an nvlist for the device, counts the peers and allocates an array of peer nvlists, and adds the private key, listen port, fwmark (as "user-cookie") and replace-peers flag when the corresponding flags are set (258-278). For each peer it creates an nvlist, counts allowed IPs, adds the public key, optional preshared key, keepalive interval, endpoint (for AF_INET and AF_INET6 only), replace-allowedips and remove flags, and builds an nvlist for each allowed IP with its flags, cidr and address; the allowed-ips array is attached and the temporary nvlists freed when there is at least one (280-326). A failure while building a peer jumps to err_peer, which sets ret from errno, frees the allowed-IP nvlists and the peer nvlist and continues at err (328-335). After the loop it attaches the peers array and frees the peer nvlists (337-343), packs the device nvlist (a NULL result goes to err), frees the device nvlist, gets a datagram socket and returns -errno if that fails, and otherwise returns the result of ioctl(s, SIOCSWG, &wgd), which is 0 on success and -1 on failure, not an errno value (344-352). The packed buffer wgd.wgd_data is not freed in this function on either of those returns. At err it sets ret to -errno if it was 0, frees the peer nvlists and the device nvlist and returns ret (354-361).

functions.name: hostapd_config_read_eap_user
functions.prose_contract: Reads the hostapd EAP user database file into conf->eap_user (hostapd config_file.c:251-578; the packet name hostapd_config_read_eap_user_file does not exist). It returns 0 on success and -1 on failure. If fname starts with "sqlite:" it stores a copy of the rest in conf->eap_user_sqlite and returns 0 (or returns -1 when SQLite support is not built in) without reading any file (259-268); a file that cannot be opened returns -1 (271-275). It reads the file line by line, skipping comment lines and empty lines and stripping the newline (278-292). A "radius_accept_attr=" line after a user entry parses an attribute and appends it to that user's list, or fails (295-312). Any other line must start with '"' (a user name, up to the closing quote) or '*' (wildcard); otherwise the whole read fails (318-321). For each user it allocates an entry (allocation failure fails), parses the method list, the password or other fields and the flags, and appends it to a local list that is only installed at the end (324-558, parse errors jumping to failed). On failure it frees the current entry, sets ret to -1 and stops (561-565). After the loop it closes the file; on success it frees the previous conf->eap_user list and installs the new list, otherwise it frees the new list (568-575), and returns ret (577).

functions.name: hostapd_config_fill
functions.prose_contract: Applies one "name=value" line of a hostapd configuration file to conf and bss (hostapd config_file.c:2439-5110; slice cut the head); buf holds the option name, pos the value and line the line number used in messages. It is a single long if/else chain on os_strcmp(buf, name). Each branch parses pos for its option and stores the result in the configuration (atoi, a string copy with os_strdup or os_strlcpy, a get_u16/parse helper, a lookup table); most branches return 1 after logging an error when the value is invalid, and the function returns 0 at its end when the matched branch finished normally (5109). An unknown option logs "unknown configuration item" and returns 1 (5102-5106). A few branches return other values: ctrl_interface_group returns 0 at once when the group name is found by getgrnam (3293-3299) and 1 when it is neither a known group nor a number (3303-3307); acs_chan_bias returns -1 when parsing fails (3434-3437). In the region of the slice, rxkh_file replaces the stored file name, returns 1 if os_strdup fails, but when hostapd_config_read_rxkh_file fails it only logs the error and does not return 1 (3261-3275), so the function then returns 0; ctrl_interface frees the old string and stores os_strdup(pos) without checking the copy (3284-3286).

functions.name: hostapd_ctrl_iface_eapol_rx
functions.prose_contract: Handles the EAPOL_RX control command of hostapd (ctrl_iface.c:1770-1805; the packet name is wrong in its qualifier only, the slice cut the head): the command text is "<MAC> <hex>". It logs the command, parses the MAC address with hwaddr_aton2 and returns -1 if that fails (1779-1782), skips spaces, and returns -1 if the remaining hex text has an odd length (1784-1789). It allocates len/2 bytes (-1 if that fails), converts the hex text with hexstr2bin (freeing the buffer and returning -1 if it is invalid), calls ieee802_1x_receive(hapd, src, buf, len, FRAME_ENCRYPTION_UNKNOWN), frees the buffer and returns 0 (1792-1804).

functions.name: hostapd_cli_reconnect
functions.prose_contract: Reconnects hostapd_cli to the control interface ifname (hostapd_cli.c:155-183; slice cut the head); it returns 0 on success and -1 on failure. It first closes the current connection (159). A NULL ifname returns -1 (161-162). It stores a copy of ifname in the global ctrl_ifname (freeing the old name first, so the old name is lost even if the copy fails) and returns -1 if the copy fails (164-168). It opens a connection with hostapd_cli_open_connection into ctrl_conn and returns -1 if that fails (170-172). If the client is neither interactive nor running an action file it returns 0 without attaching (173-174). Otherwise it attaches with wpa_ctrl_attach: on success it sets hostapd_cli_attached, registers the event handler and calls update_stations; on failure it prints a warning; either way it returns 0 (175-182).

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Entry point of the hs20 OSU client (osu_client.c:3228-3473; slice cut the head). It initialises the context (return -1 on failure, 3241-3242), parses options (d, f, h, K, N, o, O, q, r, s, S, t, T, w, x) with getopt, where -h or an unknown option prints usage and calls exit(0) (3244-3297), and exits with 0 after usage when there is no command argument (3299-3302). It opens the debug file, makes stdout line buffered, removes an old result file, runs check_workarounds and then dispatches on the command name: to_tnds, to_tnds2, from_tnds, sub_rem, pol_upd, prov, sim_prov, dl_osu_ca, dl_polupd_ca, dl_aaa_ca, osu_select, signup, set_pps, get_fqdn, oma_dm_prov, oma_dm_sim_prov and the others in the tail (3316-3420). Commands that need arguments check argc - optind against a minimum and call usage and exit(0) when too few are given; the get_fqdn check is "argc - optind < 1", which cannot be true at that point (the earlier test already requires one argument), so get_fqdn with no operand does not call usage but calls cmd_get_fqdn with argv[optind + 1], which is NULL (3400-3405). oma_dm_sim_prov returns -1 from main after writing a summary when the command result is negative (3419-3421). Several commands set ret from their command function; the function returns ret at 3473.

functions.name: hostapd_set_security_params
functions.prose_contract: Derives the cipher and security-policy fields of a BSS configuration from its wpa, 802.1X, WEP and OSEN settings (ap_config.c:1607-1685; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. With CONFIG_WEP and no individual WEP key length it sets broadcast_key_idx_min to 0 (1610-1615). If WPA2 is enabled and rsn_pairwise is 0 it copies wpa_pairwise into it (1618-1619). It sets wpa_group to group_cipher when that is set, otherwise to the cipher chosen by wpa_select_ap_group_cipher, and, unless the rekey interval was set explicitly, sets wpa_group_rekey to 600 for TKIP or 86400 otherwise (1620-1628). With full_config it points the RADIUS auth and accounting server at the first configured entries (1630-1633). It then picks the security policy: WPA with 802.1X gives SECURITY_WPA and WPA without it SECURITY_WPA_PSK (1635-1638); 802.1X alone gives SECURITY_IEEE_802_1X, sets the WEP default length, sets wpa_group, wpa_pairwise and rsn_pairwise to a cipher that depends on the WEP key length only when full_config is set (otherwise to WPA_CIPHER_NONE), and sets wpa_key_mgmt only when full_config is set (1639-1658); static WEP keys give SECURITY_STATIC_WEP, set the three ciphers from the key length and, with full_config, the key management (1660-1669); OSEN sets SECURITY_OSEN with CCMP as group and rsn pairwise cipher and pairwise 0 (1671-1675); otherwise it sets SECURITY_PLAINTEXT and, only when full_config is set, sets the three ciphers and wpa_key_mgmt to none (1676-1684).

functions.name: hostapd_dfs_background_start_channel_switch
functions.prose_contract: Reacts to a radar detection when background radar detection (a dedicated radar chain) may be used (dfs.c:1319-1362; slice cut the head); it returns -1, 0 or the result of hostapd_dfs_start_channel_switch_background. It returns -1 if background radar detection is not in use (1322-1323). It returns 0 without changing anything if a channel switch announcement is already in progress (1331-1332). If the radar was reported on the background chain itself (hostapd_dfs_is_background_event) it updates the background chain with a new random channel and returns 0 (1334-1342). Otherwise it returns -1 if the background chain has no channel (1349-1350); if background CAC is still running it sets radar_background.temp_ch to 1 and returns -1 so that CAC is done on the main chain, which is a state change (1352-1358). Otherwise it returns the result of hostapd_dfs_start_channel_switch_background(iface) (1361).

functions.name: hostapd_handle_dfs
functions.prose_contract: Decides whether CAC (channel availability check) is needed on the configured channel and starts it (dfs.c:829-944; slice cut the head); it returns 1 when no DFS action is required or the check can be skipped or the background chain is used, 0 when CAC is running (or no valid channel was found), and -1 on failure. It returns 1 immediately for a 6 GHz frequency or when no current_mode is known (834-845). It clears cac_started and, in a loop, gets the start channel index (-1 returns -1), the number of used channels and the CAC time (849-861); if no channel needs radar detection it returns 1 (864-869), if all required channels are already available it returns 1 and skips CAC (872-877), and if some are unavailable it calls dfs_set_valid_channel: when that fails it sets the interface state to HAPD_IFACE_DFS and returns 0, otherwise it repeats the loop (880-890). After the loop it sets the DFS state, logs the CAC start and calls hostapd_start_dfs_cac, returning -1 if that fails (893-918). When a background radar chain is in use it records the current channel in radar_background, then selects a random channel on the dedicated chain with dfs_set_valid_channel (returning its negative result), sets radar_background.temp_ch to 1 and returns 1; this selection happens after the CAC start, not before (920-940). Otherwise it returns 0 (943).

functions.name: hostapd_acs_channel_selected
functions.prose_contract: Applies the channel chosen by the driver's ACS (automatic channel selection) to the configuration (drv_callbacks.c:1371-1509; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. With CONFIG_IEEE80211BE and a link id it switches to that link's BSS and returns if there is none (1378-1387). It returns without changes if a channel is already configured (1390-1393). It sets iface->freq to the selected primary frequency (1396), which stays set even when later checks fail. If there is no current mode it looks for the hardware mode matching acs_res->hw_mode (and containing the frequency) and, if none is found, logs "bad hw_mode", sets err and goes to out (1398-1420); a zero primary frequency or a frequency for which no channel is found also set err and go to out, before iconf->channel is touched (1423-1440). Only after those checks does it set iconf->channel and acs, derive the secondary channel offset from sec_freq (a secondary equal to the primary sets err and goes to out after channel and acs were already set, 1442-1455) and store the EDMG channel (1457). For VHT or HE it sets segment indices and channel width from ch_width 40, 80 or 160 (1459-1489), with CONFIG_IEEE80211BE it also handles a 320 MHz width and the puncture bitmap (1491-1501). At out it calls hostapd_acs_completed(hapd->iface, err) and only logs a warning if that returns nonzero (1503-1508).

functions.name: hostapd_notif_update_dh_ie
functions.prose_contract: Handles a request from the driver to update the OWE (Diffie-Hellman) information element of a peer (drv_callbacks.c:2282-2360; slice cut the head); it returns -1 for invalid arguments and 0 otherwise, with errors reported to the driver. It returns -1 if hapd or its wpa_auth is missing or peer is NULL (2290-2297). If OWE is not in the key management, or the elements cannot be parsed, or owe_validate_request returns a non-success status, it goes to err (2298-2313). It finds or adds the station: for an existing one it stops the session timeout and accounting and sets the inactivity timeout to STA_NULLFUNC; adding a new one that fails goes to err (2315-2331). It clears the WPS flags and, only when CONFIG_IEEE80211BE is compiled in and link_addr is non-NULL, fills in the station's MLD information (2332-2346). It then calls owe_process_rsn_ie and frees the station if that returns a non-success status, and returns 0 (2349-2355). The err label tells the driver the failure status through hostapd_drv_update_dh_ie (using link_addr when it is non-NULL, otherwise peer) and returns 0 (2356-2359).

functions.name: hostapd_notif_assoc
functions.prose_contract: Handles a driver association or reassociation event for station addr (drv_callbacks.c:251-910; slice cut the head). The return value is mixed: -1 on rejected or failed association (after cleanup), 0 when the event is ignored or completed, and, in some inner branches, positive WLAN_STATUS_* codes. It returns -1 if addr is NULL (272-283) and 0 if addr is a multicast, zero or the AP's own address (285-294). It parses the request elements (parse failure returns -1) and selects the WPS, RSN, WPA or OSEN element if any (302-331). It finds the existing station (stopping its session timeout and accounting) or adds a new one; if adding fails it disassociates the address and returns -1 (333-349). If WPA is enabled and an SA query is needed it sends an association response with status ASSOC_REJECTED_TEMPORARILY and a comeback time and returns 0 (352-357). The middle part (360-900) validates the WPA/RSN/OSEN/WPS elements, MBO and other options and sets up the station; several of its early exits are "goto fail" (380, 393, 412, 485, 593, 612, 627, 644, 758, 805, 832, 866) and others return WLAN_STATUS_INVALID_IE or WLAN_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED_FAILURE directly (665, 675, 679, 692, 702, 713, 720, 728) or 0 (771, 801). A normal completion returns 0 (900). The fail label sends an association response with the status when status is not negative, disassociates the station, frees it with ap_free_sta and returns -1, not 0 (902-909).

functions.name: hostapd_get_eap_user
functions.prose_contract: Finds the EAP user entry for an identity (eap_user_db.c:232-290; the packet name get_eap_user does not exist). With WPS enabled, an identity equal to the WSC enrollee identity returns a static entry (rewritten on each call) whose only method is WSC, and one equal to the WSC registrar identity returns a static entry with the WSC method and the AP PIN as password (239-258). Otherwise it scans the configured user list from conf->eap_user: for phase 1 (phase2 == 0) an entry with a NULL identity is taken as a match (261-265); an entry of the right phase with a wildcard prefix matches when identity_len is at least the stored length and the stored identity is a prefix of identity (267-273); an entry of the right phase whose identity has the same length and bytes matches (275-278). The first match ends the scan. If nothing matched and an SQLite user database is configured it returns the result of eap_user_sqlite_get (283-286); otherwise it returns the match found or NULL (289).

functions.name: handle_auth_sae
functions.prose_contract: Handles a received SAE authentication frame for station sta (ieee802_11.c:1306-1639; slice cut the head); it returns nothing and sends the reply itself. resp starts as WLAN_STATUS_SUCCESS (1310). With the reflection-attack test option and transaction 1, or the commit-override option and transaction 1, it sends the prepared reply and goes to remove_sta (1322-1343). If there is no SAE state yet, only transaction 1 with an acceptable status is allowed, otherwise resp is UNSPECIFIED_FAILURE and it replies; the state is allocated (failure goes to remove_sta) and set to SAE_NOTHING (1345-1360). Transaction 1 (commit) handling (1360-1546) checks the anti-clogging token and rejected groups, can reply with an anti-clogging request, and calls sae_sm_step; transaction 2 (confirm) goes to remove_sta if the status is not success, replies UNSPECIFIED_FAILURE if the confirm is too short, silently returns for an unexpected confirm in the ACCEPTED state, replies CHALLENGE_FAIL if sae_check_confirm fails, then calls sae_sm_step (1547-1589); any other transaction number goes to remove_sta if the status is not success, else resp becomes UNKNOWN_AUTH_TRANSACTION (1590-1598). At reply, if the station was not removed and resp is not success, it sends the failure status to the driver and sends an auth reply, clearing a stored password identifier for a rejected first commit (1601-1626). At remove_sta it removes a station that was added unassociated when resp or the frame status was not success (1628-1637) and frees the data buffer (1638).

functions.name: handle_auth
functions.prose_contract: Processes a received IEEE 802.11 Authentication management frame at the AP (ieee802_11.c:2870-3336; the packet slice 1545-1807 does not contain this function, it covers the SAE helpers before it); it returns nothing and replies through send_auth_reply. It returns without a reply when the frame is shorter than the header plus the auth body (2889-2893) or when the testing option drops it by probability (2896-2902). After the header checks (2905-3227, in the part that was scanned only by gotos and returns: a number of failures go to the fail label with a status in resp, and silent returns happen for ignored, queued or duplicate frames, at 3082, 3096, 3113, 3121, 3139), it dispatches on the authentication algorithm (3229): open system marks the station authenticated and calls mlme_authenticate_indication (3230-3238); shared key calls auth_shared_key, sets the algorithm and, for transaction 1 with a stored challenge, adds the challenge element to the reply (3241-3256); FT initialises the WPA state machine (failure goes to fail) and calls wpa_ft_process_auth, then returns (3260-3277); SAE initialises the state machine in mesh mode (failure goes to fail) and calls handle_auth_sae, which sends its own reply, then returns (3280-3298); FILS and PASN call their handlers and return (3301-3313). Paths that reach fail, or leave the switch for open or shared key, send an auth reply with resp and the optional response elements, with the transaction number plus 1 except for SAE, and remove a station that was added unassociated if resp or the send result is not success (3317-3335). The SAE-specific reply statuses such as CHALLENGE_FAIL and FINITE_CYCLIC_GROUP_NOT_SUPPORTED are produced in handle_auth_sae, not in this function.

functions.name: ieee80211_ml_process_link
