functions.prose_contract: Processes one non-association link of an MLO (multi-link) association request on the AP (ieee802_11.c:4501-4622; slice cut the head); it returns 0 on success and -1 when the final status is not success. It parses the link's elements; a parse failure sets status UNSPECIFIED_FAILURE and goes to out (4516-4520). If a station with the origin address already exists on this link BSS it fails with UNSPECIFIED_FAILURE (4522-4528); otherwise it adds one with ap_sta_add, and if that fails sets AP_UNABLE_TO_HANDLE_NEW_STA and goes to out (4530-4535). It defragments the Basic Multi-Link element; if that fails it goes to out with status still SUCCESS, which returns 0 without having completed the link processing (4537-4539). It parses the link-specific association request, runs __check_assoc_ies, copies the MLD and flag information and, unless offloaded, takes the AID from the origin station (a zero AID fails) and marks it used, shares the WPA state machine and sets flags (4541-4601), and unless offloaded calls add_associated_sta, whose failure sets AP_UNABLE_TO_HANDLE_NEW_STA (4605-4606). At out it frees the buffer, stores the status in link->status, builds the link's association response unless offloaded, and, when the status is not success, frees the new station (if any) and returns -1, else returns 0 (4607-4621).

functions.name: handle_auth_cb
functions.prose_contract: Callback after the driver has sent (or failed to send) an authentication reply (ieee802_11.c:6363-6420; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It returns if the station for the destination address is not found (6371-6377). If the frame is shorter than the auth header it sets status UNSPECIFIED_FAILURE and goes to fail (6379-6385). Otherwise it reads the algorithm, transaction and status from the frame; if the frame was not acknowledged (ok == 0) it goes to fail (6388-6397). For a successful open-system reply (transaction 2) or shared-key reply (transaction 4) it sets WLAN_STA_AUTH, updates the station flags in the driver if the station was added unassociated, and returns (6399-6407). At fail it computes success_status from the frame's status code (for SAE transaction 1 through sae_status_success) and removes a station that was added unassociated from the driver, clearing added_unassoc, only when success_status is false (6410-6419). Hence an unacknowledged reply whose own status code was SUCCESS does not remove the station.

functions.name: handle_assoc_cb
functions.prose_contract: Callback after the driver has sent (or failed to send) an association or reassociation response (ieee802_11.c:6534-6705; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It returns if the station is not found (6542-6547) and, for an MLD station, if this is not the link on which the association happened (6550-6557). A frame that is too short removes the station from the driver and returns (6560-6567). It reads the status code (6569-6572). If the frame was not acknowledged it clears WLAN_STA_ASSOC_REQ_OK, removes the station from the driver when the status was success, and jumps to handle_ml (6574-6583); a non-success status also jumps to handle_ml (6586-6587). On success it stops accounting, sets WLAN_STA_ASSOC, clears WNM sleep, authorizes the station at once for open, FILS or FT cases, calls the MLME association indication, binds the VLAN (a failure jumps to handle_ml), sets the driver flags, enables a pending WDS station, sets up a WDS interface where needed, sends the WPA association event (FT or normal), calls new_assoc_sta_cb and enables the 802.1X port (6586-6669). For FILS it sets the temporal key, disconnecting the station and returning if that fails (6672-6680). If an EAPOL frame was received just before the association (pending_eapol_rx) it processes it with ieee802_1x_receive when its age is under 200 ms and frees it in either case (6683-6701). handle_ml calls hostapd_ml_handle_assoc_cb(hapd, sta, ok) (6703-6704).

functions.name: ieee802_11_sa_query_action
functions.prose_contract: Processes a received SA Query action frame at the AP (ieee802_11_shared.c:250-362; the packet name hostapd_sa_query_action does not exist, and the slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It ignores a frame too short to hold the transaction identifier and a group-addressed frame (260-272). When the sending station uses OCV it parses the information elements and returns on a parse failure, gets the channel info (a failure returns after a warning), derives the station's transmit parameters (a failure returns), and verifies the OCI element; a verification failure logs an OCV_FAILURE message at MSG_INFO level with the frame type and error string and returns (277-316). For an SA Query request it clears the station's post_csa_sa_query flag if the station exists and sends a response with ieee802_11_send_sa_query_resp, then returns (319-324). Any action other than request or response is ignored with a debug message (326-330). For a response it needs a station with a pending SA Query (transaction ids stored); with none, or with no matching transaction id among the stored ones, it returns (339-356); otherwise it logs that the reply to the pending query was received and stops the SA query with ap_sta_stop_sa_query (358-361).

functions.name: ieee802_1x_hs20_sub_rem
functions.prose_contract: Records that HS 2.0 subscription remediation is needed for a station (ieee802_1x.c:1753-1776; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It sets sta->remediation to 1 and frees the previous remediation_url (1755-1756). If len is greater than 2 it allocates len bytes into sta->remediation_url and returns at once if that allocation fails, in which case remediation_url has been set to NULL by the failed allocation (not left dangling) and remediation_method is not updated (1757-1760). Otherwise it stores the first byte of pos as the remediation method, copies the remaining len - 1 bytes as the URL and terminates it (1761-1763), and logs it. If len is at most 2 it sets remediation_url to NULL and logs the need without URL (1769-1774).

functions.name: ieee802_1x_rekey
functions.prose_contract: Timer callback that rotates the default WEP broadcast key of the 802.1X authenticator (ieee802_1x.c:2256-2301; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It advances default_wep_key_idx: from 3 or more it wraps to 1 when individual WEP keys are configured (individual_wep_key_len > 0) and to 0 otherwise, else it increments it (2261-2265). It calls ieee802_1x_rekey_broadcast, which returns 0 without generating a key when default_wep_key_len is below 1 and otherwise replaces default_wep_key with random bytes; a failure of that call logs a warning, frees the key, clears the pointer and returns without rescheduling (2270-2277, and 2219-2241). It then sets the new key in the driver with hostapd_drv_set_key; a failure logs, frees the key, clears the pointer and returns without rescheduling (2281-2293). On success it notifies every station that a key is available and, when wep_rekeying_period is positive, registers the next timeout (2295-2300). In the case default_wep_key_len < 1 no new random key is generated and the driver call still runs with the existing key pointer and the configured length.

functions.name: vlan_newlink
functions.prose_contract: Called when a VLAN network interface appears, to put it into the right bridges (vlan_full.c:461-510; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It looks for the first configured VLAN entry of hapd that is not yet configured and has the same interface name, and returns if there is none (469-476). It marks it configured and reads its description (478-482). With no VLAN description (not notempty) and a configured bridge it adds the interface to that bridge and records DVLAN_CLEAN_WLAN_PORT on success (484-488); with an untagged VLAN id within range it builds the bridge name, makes sure the bridge exists with vlan_get_bridge and adds the interface to it, recording DVLAN_CLEAN_WLAN_PORT on success (489-496). For each tagged VLAN id (stopping at the first zero) that is not the untagged id, is in range and differs from the previous one, it creates the bridge and tagged interface with vlan_newlink_tagged (498-507). Finally it always brings the interface up with ifconfig_up(ifname) (509).

functions.name: wpa_try_alt_snonce
functions.prose_contract: Tries to verify a received EAPOL-Key message MIC with the earlier (alternate) SNonce of the station (wpa_auth.c:1292-1377; slice cut the head); it returns 0 when the MIC matches and the state was updated, -1 otherwise. It loops: for a PSK (non-SAE) key management it fetches the next PSK for the station with wpa_auth_get_psk and ends the loop if there is none, otherwise it uses sm->PMK; it derives a PTK with the alternate SNonce (failure ends the loop) and verifies the MIC; a match copies the PMK into sm->PMK if it came from elsewhere and sets ok (1306-1337); for non-PSK modes, or after a mismatch with a PSK, the loop continues only for PSK (1340-1342). Without a match it logs and goes to fail (1345-1349). On a match it clears alt_snonce_valid, applies a PSK VLAN id (failure goes to fail), stores FT keys when FT is in use and not completed, copies the alternate SNonce into SNonce and the derived PTK into sm->PTK, clears the local PTK with forced_memzero, sets PTK_valid and returns 0 (1352-1372). The fail label clears pmk_r0 and pmk_r1 with forced_memzero and returns -1; the local PTK is cleared only on the success path (1369) and not on the failure paths (1373-1376).

functions.name: __wpa_send_eapol
functions.prose_contract: Builds and sends one EAPOL-Key frame to a station (wpa_auth.c:1964-2180; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It computes the MIC length, the key descriptor version from the key management and cipher, and the key-data length with AES key-wrap padding when the data is encrypted (1981-2021), then allocates the frame with os_zalloc and returns silently if that fails (2023-2025). Only after that allocation does it fill the header and advance the replay counter: it shifts the stored counters, increments key_replay[0].counter, copies it into the frame and marks it valid (2049-2059). Therefore a frame allocation failure returns before the replay counter changes, while the later early returns (a failed buffer allocation at 2088 or 2098, encryption failures at 2119 and 2143, a missing valid PTK or MIC computation failure at 2154 and 2161) happen after it was advanced, so the counter is consumed without a frame being sent. When the frame is complete it increments the transmitted-frames counter, sends the frame through wpa_auth_send_eapol and frees it (2175-2179). With the MIC bit set and a valid PTK it computes the MIC, and for a group frame the test option can corrupt it (2148-2173).

functions.name: SM_STATE(WPA_PTK, PTKCALCNEGOTIATING)
functions.prose_contract: Generated state-machine function for the PTKCALCNEGOTIATING state of the WPA authenticator's 4-Way Handshake (macro invocation SM_STATE(WPA_PTK, PTKCALCNEGOTIATING) at wpa_auth.c:3626; the packet name wpa_ptk_PTKCALCNEGOTIATING_step does not exist); it returns nothing. It enters the state (SM_ENTRY_MA), clears EAPOLKeyReceived and update_snonce, and tries to verify message 2/4 (3649-3652). In a loop it picks a PMK: for PSK key management (not SAE) the next PSK found by wpa_auth_get_psk (no PSK ends the loop), otherwise sm->PMK or the PMKSA's key (3662-3686); it derives a PTK with the stored SNonce (failure ends the loop) and verifies the MIC of the last received EAPOL-Key (or AEAD decrypts it when there is no MIC) (3690-3713). On a successful MIC check it copies the used PMK into sm->PMK immediately, before the later checks, so a later failure leaves sm->PMK changed (3695-3704). On a mismatch it retries with the OWE SHA-256 workaround, then without the KDK, and for PSK continues with the next PSK (3717-3740). If nothing matched and a RADIUS PSK request is possible it requests it, sets waiting_radius_psk and leaves via out (3751-3762); otherwise it logs an invalid MIC, reports a PSK failure when a PSK was found, and goes to out (3764-3770). The remaining part checks the key data, RSN elements, FT and other conditions and disconnects the station with wpa_sta_disconnect on mismatches, going to out in each case (goto out at 3785-3953, disconnects at 3848, 3864, 3912, 3951, 3959).

functions.name: wpa_ft_process_auth_req
functions.prose_contract: Processes the Fast BSS Transition (FT) authentication request elements of a station on the AP (wpa_auth_ft.c:3168-3442; slice cut the head); it returns WLAN_STATUS_SUCCESS (0), a WLAN_STATUS_* failure code, or -1 when the PMK-R1 must be pulled from the R0KH asynchronously. It clears *resp_ies and the length and pmk_r1_name_valid (3187-3190) and returns UNSPECIFIED_FAILURE at once if the elements cannot be parsed (3196-3198). From there on it returns through out: INVALID_MDIE for a missing or mismatching mobility-domain element, INVALID_FTIE for a missing FT element or R0KH-ID, INVALID_PMKID for a missing PMKID (3201-3232); failures of wpa_ft_set_key_mgmt, random generation, PTK derivation and of the VLAN, identity and CUI setters leave the initial UNSPECIFIED_FAILURE (3234-3235, 3317-3320, 3372-3376, 3392-3402). It derives the PMK-R1 name and finds the PMK-R1: locally generated for FT-PSK when ft_psk_generate_local is set (a failure there gives INVALID_PMKID), else from the local cache for the allowed hash lengths, else derived from a local PMK-R0, else it asks the R0KH with wpa_ft_pull_pmk_r1: a failure of the pull gives INVALID_PMKID, and success sets the result to -1 (pending) and leaves (3240-3308). With a PMK-R1 it stores it, generates the ANonce, takes the SNonce from the FT element according to the key length (INVALID_FTIE if it is too short), derives the PTK (with a KDK when configured) and installs it, then builds the response RSN, mobility-domain and FT elements into a new buffer (3310-3430). On a build failure it frees the buffer (the pointer is not reset) with the result still UNSPECIFIED_FAILURE (3436-3437); on success it returns WLAN_STATUS_SUCCESS (3434-3441). There is no INVALID_RSNIE return in this function.

functions.name: wpa_validate_wpa_ie
functions.prose_contract: Validates the WPA or RSN information element of a station's association request and stores state on sm (wpa_auth_ie.c:613-1105; slice cut the head); it returns a WPA_* result, WPA_IE_OK on success. It returns WPA_NOT_ENABLED if wpa_auth or sm is NULL (628-629) and WPA_INVALID_IE for a missing or empty element (631-632). It parses the element and rejects an unsupported protocol version (WPA_INVALID_PROTO), a malformed element, an invalid group cipher (WPA_INVALID_GROUP), an AKM not allowed (WPA_INVALID_AKMP), a disallowed pairwise cipher (WPA_INVALID_PAIRWISE), management-frame-protection violations (WPA_MGMT_FRAME_PROTECTION_VIOLATION, WPA_INVALID_MGMT_GROUP_CIPHER), an invalid mobility-domain element when FT is used (WPA_INVALID_MDIE) and PMKID mismatches (WPA_INVALID_PMKID), plus WPA_DENIED_OTHER_REASON for other denied cases (the returns at lines 629-1059, listed by line in the source). On success it records the selected key management, ciphers and extended-key-id state in sm, copies the element into sm->wpa_ie (WPA_ALLOC_FAIL if the allocation fails) and stores or clears the RSNXE copy in sm->rsnxe (WPA_ALLOC_FAIL if that allocation fails), and returns WPA_IE_OK (1063-1104). The function has no WPA_INVALID_RSXE or WPA_INVALID_OWE_DH return: rsnxe is only copied at 1089-1100 and owe_dh does not appear in the body.

functions.name: wps_pwd_auth_fail
functions.prose_contract: Event handler for a WPS "password authentication failed" event on a BSS (wps_hostapd.c:738-787; slice cut the head); it returns 0 on every path (743, 756, 786), so the return value is always 0 here. It does nothing if the failure is not an enrollee failure, no AP PIN is configured or WPS is not running (742-743). Otherwise it increments the total and the consecutive failure counters (750-751) and returns if fewer than 3 failures have been counted in total (755-756). From the third failure it sets ap_setup_locked in the WPS state and updates the registrar's information elements (759-761). If the configuration does not itself lock AP setup: with 10 or more consecutive failures it cancels the automatic AP PIN re-enable timeout (indefinite lock) (763-769); with fewer it sets the lockout time to 60 seconds the first time, doubles it each third failure while it is under a year, cancels any pending re-enable timeout and registers a new timeout of that length for hostapd_wps_reenable_ap_pin (771-783).

functions.name: dpp_controller_rx_gas_comeback_req
functions.prose_contract: Handles a GAS comeback request received over TCP by the DPP controller (dpp_tcp.c:1492-1530; slice cut the head); it returns -1 on failure and otherwise the result of the send helper. It returns -1 if the message is empty, if there is no auth, if neither a control connection nor a configurator exists, if the authentication or reconfiguration was not successful, if no GAS comeback is in progress (1499-1510), or if the dialog token differs from the stored one (1512-1516). If no configuration response is ready yet it returns dpp_tcp_send_comeback_delay (1519-1523). Otherwise it takes ownership of auth->conf_resp_tcp by moving the pointer into a local and setting auth->conf_resp_tcp to NULL, then returns dpp_tcp_send_gas_resp(conn, WLAN_PA_GAS_COMEBACK_RESP, resp) (1527-1529); that helper frees the buffer in all cases, including when it fails to allocate the outgoing message and returns -1 (dpp_tcp.c:1346-1357, 1370), so the response buffer is consumed on this path even on failure.

functions.name: dpp_controller_rx
functions.prose_contract: Socket read callback of the DPP controller TCP connection (dpp_tcp.c:1739-1856; the packet name dpp_controller_rx_msg does not exist). It first reads the 4-byte message length: a read error or end of stream removes the connection (dpp_connection_remove) and returns; a partial length returns to wait for more; a length above 65535 removes the connection; otherwise it frees any old buffer and allocates a message buffer of that length (1748-1787). If there is no buffer it removes the connection and returns (1789-1794). It reads into the buffer's tailroom; a read error or end of stream removes the connection and returns (1799-1809); it appends the received bytes and, while the buffer still has tailroom, returns to wait (1811-1818). When the message is complete it resets msg_len_octets to 0, removes the connection if the message is empty, and otherwise dispatches on the first byte: vendor specific to dpp_controller_rx_action, GAS initial request to dpp_controller_rx_gas_req, GAS initial or comeback response to dpp_rx_gas_resp and GAS comeback request to dpp_controller_rx_gas_comeback_req, each followed by removal of the connection if the handler returns a negative value; an unknown type only logs (1820-1855). It returns nothing.

functions.name: is_punct_bitmap_valid
functions.prose_contract: Checks that a channel puncturing bitmap is valid for a bandwidth (hw_features_common.c:987-1035; slice cut the head); it returns true for a valid bitmap and false otherwise, and it only reads its arguments and constant tables. A zero punct_bitmap returns true (993-994). Otherwise it inverts the bitmap, masks it to the width of the bandwidth (4 bits for 80, 8 bits for 160, 16 bits for 320 MHz) and selects the matching table of valid patterns; any other bw returns false (996-1019). It returns false if the resulting active-channel bitmap is zero, or if the bit for the primary channel (pri_ch_bit_pos) is not set in it (1021-1027), and otherwise returns true only if the active bitmap equals one of the entries of the table for that bandwidth (1029-1034). pri_ch_bit_pos is used as a shift count without a range check.

functions.name: nan_de_next_multicast
functions.prose_contract: Computes when the next multicast NAN service discovery frame should be sent for a service (nan_de.c:423-464; slice cut the head); it returns -1 if no multicast frame is wanted, 0 if one is due now, and otherwise the time to wait in milliseconds. It returns -1 for a publish service that is not unsolicited and for a subscribe service that is not active (429-432). If no multicast frame has been sent yet (last_multicast not initialised) it returns 0 (434-435); this test comes before the publish checks that return -1 for a TTL of 0 or for a pause that has an end time set (437-442), so those checks apply only after a first multicast has been sent. It then adds the announcement period (publish) or query period (subscribe), 100 ms if 0, to last_multicast (444-450). For a publish service it returns 0 if no transmit wait is pending and the next time is already in the past, otherwise it continues with next_publish_state (452-457). It returns 0 if the computed time is before now, otherwise the difference in milliseconds (459-463).

functions.name: rijndaelKeySetupEnc
functions.prose_contract: Expands an AES cipher key into the encryption round-key schedule (aes-internal.c:779-845; the packet name is an excerpt, the function is rijndaelKeySetupEnc); it returns the number of rounds or -1. It first reads the first 16 key bytes into rk[0..3] (784-787). For keyBits 128 it writes 40 more words with ten rounds of the key schedule and returns 10 (789-799). For other values it reads 8 more key bytes into rk[4..5] and, for 192, runs the 192-bit schedule and returns 12 from inside the loop (802-818). For any value other than 128 and 192 it also reads 8 more key bytes into rk[6..7], and for 256 runs the 256-bit schedule and returns 14 from inside the loop (821-841). For every other keyBits value it returns -1 (844); in that case it has already read 32 key bytes and written rk[0..7]. The caller must provide a writable rk with room for the schedule (44, 52 or 60 words) and a key of 16, 24 or 32 bytes, and a key shorter than 32 bytes is also over-read when keyBits is not 128 or 192.

functions.name: check_ocsp_resp
functions.prose_contract: Checks the OCSP response attached to a TLS connection for the peer certificate cert (tls_openssl_ocsp.c, check_ocsp_resp at 480-840; the packet name check_ocsp does not exist, and the slice 506-763 is inside it); it returns an enum ocsp_result: OCSP_GOOD, OCSP_REVOKED, OCSP_NO_RESPONSE or OCSP_INVALID. It returns OCSP_NO_RESPONSE if no response data is attached (514-516), and OCSP_INVALID if the OCSPResponse or the BasicOCSPResponse cannot be parsed, the response status is not zero, or the response type is not basic OCSP (521-553). It then goes through the response certificates, finds the signer with ocsp_find_signer, gets its public key, verifies the signature of the response data and verifies the signer certificate against the certificate store with the OCSP helper purpose; failures in this part go to fail with the result still OCSP_INVALID (556-655), except that an untrusted signer without the OCSP-signing extended key usage sets OCSP_NO_RESPONSE (658-698). It compares the issuer information across the SingleResponse values (a difference goes to fail with OCSP_INVALID) and remembers the one that matches the peer certificate's serial number and issuer (771-792). Without a matching single response it sets OCSP_NO_RESPONSE (801-805); a response outside its validity time goes to fail with OCSP_INVALID (808-812); certificate status 1 (revoked) sets OCSP_REVOKED, any other status except 0 sets OCSP_NO_RESPONSE, and status 0 sets OCSP_GOOD (815-830). All paths from the signature check on go through the fail label, which releases the allocated objects and returns result (831-839).

functions.name: atheros_set_key
functions.prose_contract: Installs or deletes a key in the Atheros driver (driver_atheros.c:494-584; slice cut the head); it returns -1, -3, the result of atheros_del_key or the result of the SETKEY ioctl. The arguments come from the wpa_driver_set_key_params structure (alg, addr, key_idx, set_tx, key, key_len, 500-505). For WPA_ALG_NONE it returns atheros_del_key(drv, addr, key_idx) (507-508). Otherwise it maps the algorithm to an IEEE80211 cipher (WEP, TKIP, CCMP, BIP-CMAC-128, and with ATH_GCM_SUPPORT also CCMP-256, GCMP, GCMP-256, BIP-CMAC-256 and BIP-GMAC), returning -1 for any other algorithm (513-552), and returns -3 if key_len exceeds the key data field (554-557). It fills a ieee80211req_key: for a NULL or broadcast address it uses the broadcast address, the key index, and sets the default-key flag when set_tx; for a unicast address it uses that address with IEEE80211_KEYIX_NONE; it copies the key and calls set80211priv with IEEE80211_IOCTL_SETKEY, logs when the result is negative and returns that result (560-583).

functions.name: wpa_driver_ndis_get_names
functions.prose_contract: Finds the NDIS network adapter that matches drv->ifname and stores its description (driver_ndis.c:2034-2307; slice cut the head); it returns 0 on success and -1 on failure. There are two compile-time variants: with CONFIG_USE_NDISUIO (2036-2133) it queries NDISUIO bindings, and otherwise (2134-2305) it uses WinPcap's PacketGetAdapterNames. In the second variant it allocates an 8 KB buffer (returning -1 if that fails) and retries once with the length the call reports (2148-2160), splits the returned names and descriptions into arrays, and, when there are fewer descriptions than names, fills the missing ones with "stub description" (2242-2243); only if there are more descriptions than names (a count mismatch afterwards) does it free the buffer and return -1 (2245-2251). It looks for an adapter whose name contains the interface name, or whose description starts with it, and, when only the description matches, it rewrites drv->ifname with the adapter name (without the "\Device\NPF_" prefix) (2253-2274). No match returns -1 (2276-2281). Otherwise it copies the description, cut at the last " (" (2283-2297), into a new drv->adapter_desc and returns -1 if that allocation fails, else 0 (2299-2305). The names buffer is freed on those paths.

functions.name: nl80211_mgmt_subscribe_non_ap
functions.prose_contract: Registers the management frames a non-AP interface wants to receive from the nl80211 driver (driver_nl80211.c:2496-2679; slice cut the head); it returns 0 or -1. It allocates the management socket handle with nl80211_alloc_mgmt_handle and returns -1 if that fails (2502-2503). It registers authentication frames for ad-hoc mode, or for SAE when the driver has SAE but not SME (2507-2515), then registers one or more frame patterns with nl80211_register_frame or nl80211_register_action_frame for a long list of action frames (public action, WNM, fast transition, interworking, SA query, WPA/NAN/DPP vendor patterns, TDLS only when supported, RRM and others, 2519-2674). Each failed registration sets ret to -1 but registration continues; the NAN publication registration is retried without the multicast flag first (2570-2575). If the FT action registration (action category 6) succeeds and the driver does not report key management capabilities itself, it adds the FT key management flags to drv->capa (2608-2621). After all registrations it calls nl80211_mgmt_handle_register_eloop(bss) (2676), so the management socket is registered with eloop, and returns ret (2678).

functions.name: wpa_driver_nl80211_set_mode_impl
functions.prose_contract: Switches the interface to nl80211 mode nlmode (driver_nl80211.c:7353-7500; slice cut the head); it returns 0 on success and a nonzero value (-1 or the nl80211 error) on failure. It returns -1 on a forced test failure (7365-7366). It tries nl80211_set_mode; success, or a failure while the interface is already in nlmode, stores nlmode in drv->nlmode and goes to done (7368-7376); -ENODEV returns -1 (7378-7379); if nlmode equals the already stored mode the error is ignored and it goes to done with ret 0 (7381-7386). Otherwise, for up to 10 attempts, it brings the interface down (retrying after sleeps, leaving the loop on EACCES or ENODEV), optionally sets the frequency, removes an AP interface from its bridge, and retries nl80211_set_mode, delaying on -EBUSY, and keeps the last result as ret (7394-7441). A successful retry records the new mode and sets ignore_if_down_event (7443-7448); then it brings the interface up again, setting ret to -1 if that fails (7451-7456). At done a nonzero ret is returned with a log (7458-7462). Otherwise it disables or re-enables 11b rates for P2P interfaces, unsubscribes management frames, sets up the AP or tears it down when leaving AP mode (an AP setup failure returns -1), subscribes for mesh interfaces (failure returns -1), and, for a non-AP, non-mesh interface not in deinit, calls nl80211_mgmt_subscribe_non_ap, whose failure is only logged (7465-7498). It returns 0 at 7499.

functions.name: wpa_driver_roboswitch_leave
functions.prose_contract: Removes the multicast address addr for the given port mask from the Broadcom RoboSwitch address-resolution table (driver_roboswitch.c:286-354; slice cut the head); it returns 0 or -1. It converts the address to big-endian words and reads the ARL control configuration, returning -1 if that read fails or if bit 4 of it is clear (291-297). It reads the first address and vector entries, returning -1 if a read fails (299-303). If entry 1 matches both the address and the ports, it reads entry 2 (a read failure returns -1) and, when entry 2 also matches, clears bit 4 of the configuration and writes it back; when entry 2 does not match it reads entry 1 again (without checking the results of those reads) and writes it into slot 2 (305-333). If entry 1 does not match, it reads entry 2 (read failure returns -1) and, when it matches, writes it into slot 1, otherwise it returns -1 (334-351). The write calls and the re-reads inside the copy branch are not checked for errors, so those branches return 0 even if they fail. It returns 0 at 353.

functions.name: wpa_driver_wext_event_link
functions.prose_contract: Handles a link add or remove event for the wext driver (driver_wext.c:534-577; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It zeroes an event structure and copies the interface name from buf into event.interface_status.ifname; if len is larger than the buffer it is reduced to the size minus one, but a len equal to the buffer size copies the whole buffer size, leaving the name without a terminating NUL (539-542). It sets the event to interface-removed (del) or interface-added and logs it (543-549). If the name equals the driver's own interface it ignores a removal when if_removed is already set and otherwise sets if_removed, and for an addition it ignores the event if the interface does not exist (if_nametoindex is 0) or if_removed is not set, and otherwise clears if_removed (551-574). It then delivers EVENT_INTERFACE_STATUS to the upper layer with wpa_supplicant_event (576).

functions.name: eap_sim_parse_attr
functions.prose_contract: Parses a list of EAP-SIM/AKA attributes between start and end into struct eap_sim_attrs (eap_sim_common.c:495-930; the packet name was a slice-level name, the slice cut the head); it returns 0 on success and -1 on failure. It clears attr and sets id_req to NO_ID_REQ and notification, counter, selected_version and client_error_code to -1 (501-506). For each attribute it returns -1 if fewer than 2 bytes remain, if the attribute length (field times 4) runs past end, or if the length field is zero (508-524). It then switches on the attribute type; for each known type it checks the attribute length against what that type needs (RAND, AUTN, PADDING, NONCE_MT, MAC, NOTIFICATION, IDENTITY, VERSION_LIST, SELECTED_VERSION, COUNTER, COUNTER_TOO_SMALL, NONCE_S, CLIENT_ERROR_CODE, IV, ENCR_DATA, NEXT_PSEUDONYM and the AKA ones, with AT_KDF and AT_BIDDING requiring exactly 2 bytes of data), returning -1 on a wrong length, and stores pointers to or copies of the data in attr (530-908). AT_PERMANENT_ID_REQ, AT_ANY_ID_REQ and AT_FULLAUTH_ID_REQ only set attr->id_req and do not check their payload length (590-593, 614-617, 666-669). An unknown attribute with a type below 128 returns -1; one at or above 128 is skipped (910-920). It advances by the attribute length and returns 0 when all attributes are consumed (923-929).

functions.name: eap_aka_process_challenge
functions.prose_contract: Processes an EAP-AKA or AKA' Challenge request on the peer (eap_aka.c:1052-1235; slice cut the head); it returns the response buffer built by one of the helper functions, or NULL. It first verifies AT_CHECKCODE if present, returning a client error (UNABLE_TO_PROCESS_PACKET) on a mismatch (1065-1075). For AKA' it requires a non-empty AT_KDF_INPUT, stores the network name (failure or missing input returns an authentication reject) and, after the KDF negotiation and KDF-count checks, may return the KDF negotiation response (1080-1109). It then checks the other attributes, runs the USIM/UMTS authentication (a failure returns an authentication reject or a synchronization-failure response, and a NULL result is returned in the case at 1152), and verifies the MAC (a failure returns a client error) (1110-1196). For AKA' it derives the CK' and IK' and the keys including K_re, MSK and EMSK with eap_aka_prime_derive_keys (1168-1182); for plain AKA it derives the master key with eap_aka_derive_mk and the keys with eap_sim_derive_keys, which does not derive K_re (1184-1186). It then handles the result indication and the next-pseudonym and reauthentication identity attributes, moves the state to success or result-indication wait unless the state is FAILURE, and returns eap_aka_response_challenge(data, id) (1201-1234).

functions.name: eap_aka_umts_auth
functions.prose_contract: Runs the UMTS authentication for the EAP-AKA peer (eap_aka.c:282-378; slice cut the head); it returns 0 on success, -1 on error, or a value from the helper it delegates to (for example a negative resynchronisation code from the card or simulator). It returns -1 if the peer configuration is not available (288-290). With an external SIM it returns the result of eap_aka_ext_sim_result when a response is already stored in the configuration, and otherwise the result of eap_aka_ext_sim_req (292-297). With PC/SC it returns the result of scard_umts_auth, which fills res, ik, ck and auts (299-303). With CONFIG_USIM_SIMULATOR and a password it parses "K:OPc:SQN" from the password (a password shorter than 78 characters, bad hex or a missing ':' returns -1) and returns the result of milenage_check (305-337). With CONFIG_USIM_HARDCODED it fills fixed test values, returns -1 if AUTN is not the expected test value, and returns 0 (340-369); otherwise, with neither compiled in, it logs and returns -1 (371-376).

functions.name: eap_fast_process_decrypted
functions.prose_contract: Processes the decrypted Phase 2 TLVs of an EAP-FAST message on the peer (eap_fast.c:1187-1297; slice cut the head); it returns 0 or the result of eap_fast_encrypt_response, and puts the encrypted answer in *out_data. If the TLVs cannot be parsed it returns 0 without setting *out_data (1198-1199). If parsing produced a response it encrypts and returns it (1200-1202); a failure result TLV or intermediate failure result TLV gets a matching failure TLV as the response (1204-1214). Otherwise it handles the crypto-binding TLV (failure sets failed), an intermediate success result, an EAP payload TLV and a PAC TLV (a PAC with a result that is not success only sets failed), requests a tunnel PAC when authenticated provisioning needs one, prepends a final result TLV and, when the tunnel result was success, there was no failure, a crypto binding was present and phase 2 succeeded, updates the method state and decision: anonymous provisioning ends as DONE with DECISION_FAIL and expected_failure, otherwise MAY_CONT (provisioning) or DONE with DECISION_UNCOND_SUCC (1216-1287). An empty response is replaced by a one-byte buffer (1289-1293), and the function returns the result of eap_fast_encrypt_response (1295). The method state is not updated to success on paths with failed set or without a crypto-binding result.

functions.name: eap_fast_process
functions.prose_contract: Processes one EAP-FAST request on the peer (eap_fast.c:1537-1677; slice cut the head); it returns the response buffer or NULL. It calls eap_peer_tls_process_init and returns NULL if that gives nothing (1550-1553). For a Start message it handles it with eap_fast_process_start (failure returns NULL) and clears the A-ID length (1558-1563). If the TLS connection is already established and not resuming it decrypts the message and builds the Phase 2 response with eap_fast_decrypt, which returns a result in res and a response in resp; a negative result sets METHOD_DONE with DECISION_FAIL (1568-1580). Otherwise it handles a pending external certificate check (good returns the stored pending response, bad ends with DECISION_FAIL, still waiting returns NULL) (1582-1608), runs the TLS handshake with eap_peer_tls_process_helper (negative result: METHOD_DONE with DECISION_FAIL and the response it produced is returned), stores the response and returns NULL while an external check is pending (1611-1629), and when the TLS connection became established decides on anonymous provisioning and derives keys (a failure frees the response and returns NULL) (1631-1656). If res is 2 the pending Phase 2 request is stored and decrypted (1659-1667). If res is 1 it frees resp and returns a TLS ACK (1670-1673); otherwise it returns resp (1676). Application data that has been consumed does not by itself make the function return NULL: it continues through eap_fast_decrypt and returns its response.

functions.name: eap_fast_load_pac_bin
functions.prose_contract: Loads PAC entries in the binary format from a file or config blob into a list (eap_fast_pac.c:748-861; the packet name eap_fast_read_pac_bin does not exist). It returns -1 if pac_file is NULL (758-759). A name starting with "blob://" is looked up as a configuration blob and any other name is read as a file; a missing blob or an unreadable file returns 0 (no PAC entries) (761-779). An empty input returns 0 (781-785); a header shorter than 6 bytes, or with a wrong magic or format version, returns -1 (787-794). It then parses entries: for each it needs enough bytes for the type, the key, and the lengths (otherwise goes to parse_fail), allocates an entry, copies the opaque and info parts with bounds checks, derives the A-ID and appends the entry to the list (799-843). At the end it frees the file buffer (not a blob) and returns 0 (845-851). parse_fail frees the file buffer and the entry being built and returns -1, while entries already appended to *pac_root before the failure are kept (853-860).

functions.name: eap_ikev2_process
functions.prose_contract: Processes one EAP-IKEv2 request on the peer (eap_ikev2.c:328-435; slice cut the head); it returns the response buffer or NULL. It validates the EAP header; failure sets ret->ignore and returns NULL (339-343). It reads the flags (none for an empty fragment ack), checks the integrity (ICV), and the optional length field; failures set ret->ignore and return NULL (350-378). In the state WAIT_FRAG_ACK a non-empty message sets ignore and returns NULL, and an empty one moves to PROC_MSG and returns eap_ikev2_build_msg (383-392). A continuation fragment is appended with eap_ikev2_process_cont (failure sets ignore and returns NULL) (395-398), and a message with the more-fragments flag returns eap_ikev2_process_fragment (400-404). Otherwise it uses a stack buffer for an unfragmented message, runs ikev2_responder_process (on failure it sets the state to FAIL and returns NULL), and frees the input buffer only if it is not that stack buffer (406-421). If no output exists it builds it with ikev2_responder_build (NULL returns NULL) and moves to PROC_MSG, returning eap_ikev2_build_msg (423-434).

functions.name: eap_peap_decrypt
functions.prose_contract: Decrypts and processes one PEAP Phase 2 message on the peer (eap_peap.c:792-1018; slice cut the head); it returns 0 when the message was handled (a response, if any, is in *out_data), 1 when only a TLS acknowledgement is needed or there is nothing to process, and otherwise the nonzero result of the TLS helper. If an earlier Phase 2 request is pending it uses that instead of decrypting and jumps to continue_req (807-816). An empty input returns 1 with METHOD_DONE and DECISION_COND_SUCC only when sm->workaround is set and phase 2 has already succeeded (818-829); an empty input otherwise returns the result of eap_peer_tls_encrypt of an empty message (830-835). It decrypts with eap_peer_tls_decrypt and returns its result if that is nonzero (837-839); an empty decrypted message is freed and gives 1 (840-843). At continue_req it examines the inner EAP header and handles Request, Success, Failure and other codes (908-1000): on the paths shown it can return 0 early for malformed or ignored inner messages (868, 887, 896, 915, 932) or 1 (944). A response built for the inner message is encrypted with eap_peer_tls_encrypt, skipping the header strip for a TLV response and, for PEAP version 0, stripping the EAP header otherwise (995-1010), and freed; the function returns 0 (1017).

functions.name: eap_pwd_perform_confirm_exchange
functions.prose_contract: Verifies the server's Confirm message of EAP-pwd and builds the peer's Confirm (eap_pwd.c:690-881; the packet name eap_pwd_build_confirm does not exist, and the slice cut the head); it returns nothing and reports through data->outbuf, data->state and ret. It uses a single exit, fin. If data->state is not PWD_Confirm_Req it sets ret->ignore and goes to fin; a payload that is not 32 bytes long also goes to fin (701-711). Otherwise it computes the expected server confirm value as a SHA-256 hash over k, the server element, the server scalar, the peer element, the peer scalar and the cipher suite, compares it with the payload in constant time and goes to fin on a mismatch (713-796); allocation, hash or conversion failures also go to fin. It then computes its own confirm value (the same elements in the peer order), derives the MSK, EMSK and session id with compute_keys, allocates data->outbuf of 32 bytes and fills it (805-866). At fin it clears and frees the scratch buffer; if data->outbuf is NULL it sets METHOD_DONE, DECISION_FAIL and the FAILURE state, otherwise it sets the state SUCCESS_ON_FRAG_COMPLETION; a hash context left open is finalised (868-880). So a wrong state or length also ends in the FAILURE state, with ret->ignore set only for the wrong state.

functions.name: eap_sake_process_identity
functions.prose_contract: Handles an EAP-SAKE Identity request on the peer (eap_sake.c:140-180; slice cut the head); it returns the response buffer or NULL. If the state is not IDENTITY it sets ret->ignore to true and returns NULL (150-153). It parses the attributes (failure returns NULL without touching ret->ignore), requires AT_PERM_ID_REQ or AT_ANY_ID_REQ (otherwise returns NULL) (157-164), builds an Identity response with the peer id attribute and moves the state to CHALLENGE (168-177), returning NULL if the response buffer cannot be allocated (170-171).

functions.name: eap_sake_process_confirm
functions.prose_contract: Handles an EAP-SAKE Confirm request on the peer (eap_sake.c:285-367; slice cut the head); it returns the response buffer or NULL. If the state is not CONFIRM it sets ret->ignore to true and returns NULL (298-301). It parses the attributes and returns NULL if parsing fails or AT_MIC_S is missing (305-312). It computes the expected server MIC; if the computation fails or the MIC differs it sets the state to FAILURE, METHOD_DONE, DECISION_FAIL and no notifications and returns an Auth-Reject message (314-337). Otherwise it builds a Confirm response with AT_MIC_P and computes the peer MIC over it (a computation failure frees the response and returns NULL), then sets the state to SUCCESS, METHOD_DONE, DECISION_UNCOND_SUCC and no notifications, and returns the response (342-366).

functions.name: eap_sake_process
functions.prose_contract: Processes one EAP-SAKE request on the peer (eap_sake.c:370-437; slice cut the head); it returns the response buffer or NULL. It validates the EAP header and the SAKE header; a failure sets ret->ignore and returns NULL (381-385). A session id different from the stored one sets ignore and returns NULL; otherwise the session id is stored (399-406). It then sets ret->ignore to false, methodState to METHOD_MAY_CONT, decision to DECISION_FAIL and allowNotifications to true (408-411) before dispatching on the subtype: Identity, Challenge or Confirm go to their handlers (which may set ignore themselves, for example when the state is wrong), and any other subtype sets ignore and returns NULL (413-431). If the method state is METHOD_DONE afterwards it clears allowNotifications, and it returns the handler's response (433-436); a NULL response from a handler therefore does not by itself imply that ret->ignore is false.

functions.name: eap_peer_sake_register
functions.prose_contract: Registers the EAP-SAKE peer method (eap_sake.c:503-521; slice cut the head); it returns 0 on success and -1 on failure. It allocates an eap_method structure for the IETF vendor, type SAKE and the name "SAKE" and returns -1 if that fails (507-510). It sets the init, deinit, process, isKeyAvailable, getKey, getSessionId and get_emsk callbacks (512-518) and returns the result of eap_peer_method_register(eap) (520), so a registration failure is returned by that call (the allocation is not freed in this function).

functions.name: eap_teap_phase2_request
functions.prose_contract: Handles a Phase 2 EAP request inside the EAP-TEAP tunnel on the peer (eap_teap.c:404-498; slice cut the head); it returns 0 or -1 and the response in *resp. It returns -1 if the request is no longer than the EAP header or, for the expanded type, shorter than the expanded header (418-432). For an Identity request it drops the inner EAP method, builds an identity response with eap_sm_buildIdentity and returns 0 (438-442). If the requested method differs from the running one it deinitialises the inner method; when no inner method is chosen it selects one, and if that fails it builds a Nak response and returns -1 if the Nak fails, else 0 (444-457). If the inner method cannot be initialised it sets METHOD_DONE with DECISION_FAIL and returns -1 (459-467). It runs the inner method's process function on the request and records whether the inner method is done (469-474); with no response or an inner failure it sets the outer state to METHOD_MAY_CONT with DECISION_FAIL, and an inner success sets phase2_success (475-486). With no response and a pending identity, password, OTP, new-password or SIM request in the configuration it stores a copy of the request in pending_phase2_req (a failed copy leaves it NULL, unchecked) and returns 0 (488-493); with no response and nothing pending it returns -1 (494-495); otherwise it returns 0 (497).

functions.name: eap_teap_load_pac_bin
functions.prose_contract: Loads PAC entries in the binary format from a file or config blob into a list (eap_teap_pac.c:752-868; the packet name eap_teap_read_pac_bin does not exist). It returns -1 if pac_file is NULL (762-763). A name starting with "blob://" is looked up as a configuration blob and any other name is read as a file; a missing blob or unreadable file returns 0, meaning no PAC entries (765-783). An empty input returns 0 (785-789); a header shorter than 6 bytes or with the wrong magic or format version returns -1 (791-798). It then parses the entries: each needs enough bytes for type, key and the two length fields, allocates an entry, copies the opaque and info parts after bounds checks, derives the A-ID and appends the entry to the list; any shortage or allocation failure goes to parse_fail (803-846). On success it frees the file buffer (not a blob) and returns 0; parse_fail frees the buffer and the entry being built and returns -1, keeping entries already appended to the list.

functions.name: eap_wsc_build_msg
functions.prose_contract: Builds the next EAP-WSC response fragment from the pending output buffer (eap_wsc.c:310-374; slice cut the head); it returns the response or NULL. It sets ret->ignore to false and allowNotifications to true (317-319). It chooses how much of the remaining output to send: when 2 plus the remaining data exceeds the fragment size it sends fragment_size - 2 bytes with the more-fragments flag and, on the first fragment, adds the length flag and an extra 2 bytes for the total length (321-333). It allocates the EAP message and returns NULL if that fails, before ret->methodState and ret->decision are set (334-337); this failure leaves those two fields as they were. Otherwise it writes the opcode, flags, the length (first fragment) and the data, advances out_used, and sets methodState to METHOD_MAY_CONT and the decision to DECISION_FAIL (339-349). If the whole buffer has been sent it frees it and moves to FAIL (with METHOD_DONE) after an ACK in failure state, a NACK or a Done, and to MESG otherwise; if more remains it moves to WAIT_FRAG_ACK (351-371). It returns the response (373).

functions.name: eap_sm_Policy_update
functions.prose_contract: Applies a peer's Nak method list to the user's configured methods (eap_server.c:1673-1687; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It returns without effect if nak_list, sm or sm->user is NULL (1676-1677). If the user entry is a phase 2 entry it sets sm->decision to DECISION_FAILURE and returns (1679-1683). Otherwise it calls eap_sm_process_nak(sm, nak_list, len), which reads sm->user_eap_method_index and the user's method table and removes from that table, by shifting later entries down and ending with an empty entry, every method that the peer's list does not support (eap_server.c:1619-1670), so the table of sm->user is modified there.

functions.name: eap_sm_Policy_getDecision
functions.prose_contract: Decides what the EAP server should do next (eap_server.c:1722-1801; slice cut the head); it returns a DECISION_* value. With a pass-through configuration (no local EAP server), an identity and no reauthentication start it returns DECISION_PASSTHROUGH (1724-1727). If the current method (not Identity) reports success it sets update_user to true and returns DECISION_SUCCESS (1729-1735); a finished method that is not successful sets update_user and returns DECISION_FAILURE (1737-1743). If there is no user or update_user is set, an identity exists and no reauthentication starts, it looks up the user with eap_user_get: a failed lookup returns DECISION_FAILURE without changing update_user or start_reauth, and an identity request loop sets update_user and returns DECISION_FAILURE; otherwise it clears update_user (1745-1772). It then clears start_reauth (1773), returns DECISION_CONTINUE if the user still has a method at the current index (1775-1783), DECISION_INITIATE_REAUTH_START when an ERP start should be sent (1785-1790), DECISION_CONTINUE when no identity or id is known yet (1792-1796) and DECISION_FAILURE otherwise (1800).

functions.name: SM_STATE(EAP, INITIATE_RECEIVED)
functions.prose_contract: Generated state function for the EAP server state INITIATE_RECEIVED, which processes an EAP-Initiate/Re-auth message (macro invocation SM_STATE(EAP, INITIATE_RECEIVED) at eap_server.c:797-992); it returns nothing. It enters the state, clears rxInitiate, and validates the ERP header, requiring at least 4 bytes; failures go to fail, which sets sm->ignore to true (812-830, 990-991). It parses the flags, the sequence number and the TLVs, and requires a keyName-NAI of at most 253 bytes (833-862). Without a local EAP server it stores the keyName-NAI as the identity for backend authentication and returns, or goes to fail if the copy fails (864-880). With a local server it looks up the ERP key for the NAI; with no key it jumps to report_error, which calls erp_send_finish_reauth with a NULL key and the default failure flag, and that function still builds a Finish/Re-auth message (without authentication tag) in that case (882-887, 986-987, and 703-735). A replayed sequence number, too little room for the tag, a cryptosuite mismatch, a tag mismatch, no matching cryptosuite or bad TLVs go to fail (889-979). On success it stores the sequence number, clears the failure bit in the response flags and sends the Finish/Re-auth with erp_send_finish_reauth (983-987).

functions.name: eap_aka_check_identity
functions.prose_contract: Examines the identity received by the EAP-AKA server and, if it is recognised, skips the identity exchange (eap_server_aka.c:155-218; slice cut the head); it returns nothing and changes the state through helpers. It takes the identity from sm->sim_aka_permanent when that is set, otherwise from sm->identity, and extracts the user name with sim_get_username, returning if that gives NULL (159-171). If eap_aka_check_identity_reauth recognises the user name as a fast re-authentication name (result above 0) it frees the name and returns (173-180); a recognised name whose re-authentication cannot be used is handled inside that helper, whose effects (for example on data->reauth) I did not read. If a permanent identity was supplied in the IDENTITY state it copies it into data->permanent and starts the full authentication (182-189). If the user name has the pseudonym prefix of the method it looks up the permanent identity: when none is found it frees the name and returns so that the permanent identity will be requested, otherwise it copies it and starts the full authentication (192-214). The user name is freed at the end (217).

functions.name: eap_aka_buildReq
functions.prose_contract: Builds the next EAP-AKA request of the server according to its state (eap_server_aka.c:684-704; slice cut the head). It clears data->auts_reported (688) and switches on data->state: IDENTITY returns eap_aka_build_identity, CHALLENGE eap_aka_build_challenge, REAUTH eap_aka_build_reauth and NOTIFICATION eap_aka_build_notification, each returning the buffer the helper builds (689-697). Any other state logs an unexpected state and falls out of the switch, returning NULL (698-703).

functions.name: eap_server_psk_register
functions.prose_contract: Registers the EAP-PSK server method (eap_server_psk.c:506-527; the packet name eap_psk_method_register does not exist); it returns 0 on success and -1 on failure. It allocates an eap_method structure with eap_server_method_alloc for the IETF vendor, type PSK, and returns -1 if that fails (510-513). It sets the init, reset, buildReq, check, process, isDone, getKey, isSuccess, get_emsk and getSessionId callbacks (515-524) and returns the result of eap_server_method_register(eap) (526); the allocated structure is not freed in this function if registration fails.

functions.name: eap_teap_process_phase2_response
functions.prose_contract: Processes the peer's Phase 2 EAP response inside the TEAP tunnel on the server (eap_server_teap.c:1069-1214; slice cut the head); it returns nothing and starts the next inner method through eap_teap_phase2_init. It returns at once if the inner method is not initialised (1083-1087). A Nak response from the peer: with EAP_SERVER_TNC and the current inner method being TNC (a required TNC negotiation) it requests a failure and starts that, without calling eap_sm_process_nak and returns (1099-1107); otherwise it calls eap_sm_process_nak and starts the next configured method, or a failure request if none remains, then returns (1109-1124). Otherwise it calls the inner method's check, which on a rejection requests a failure with TEAP_ERROR_INNER_METHOD and returns (1129-1134), and then its process; if the method is not done it returns, and if it is done but not successful it starts a failure request (1136-1147). On success it acts on the TEAP state: in PHASE2_ID it checks the identity type and the user database (failure requests an error), then chooses the first configured method (or EAP-pwd for anonymous provisioning) and moves to PHASE2_METHOD; in PHASE2_METHOD or CRYPTO_BINDING it updates the ICMK, moves to CRYPTO_BINDING, increments the EAP sequence and may start TNC; in FAILURE it does nothing; other states are logged (1149-1211). Finally it initialises the chosen next method (1213).

functions.name: eap_tnc_process
functions.prose_contract: Processes a received EAP-TNC response on the server (eap_server_tnc.c:446-537; slice cut the head); it returns nothing and works through data->state. It returns at once, with no state change, if the EAP header is not valid, or if the message is a 1-byte ack while the state is DONE or FAIL (456-466). It reads the flags and the optional length field: a length field that is truncated, smaller than the data present or above 75000 sets the state to FAIL and returns (474-491). In the WAIT_FRAG_ACK state, more than a 1-byte message sets FAIL and returns, and otherwise the state becomes CONTINUE (495-505). A continuation fragment that cannot be appended sets FAIL (507-510); a message with the more-fragments flag is processed as a fragment and sets FAIL on error or FRAG_ACK on success, then returns (512-518); a message after FRAG_ACK sets the state CONTINUE (519-522). Otherwise it uses the received data as the input buffer (a stack buffer when there was no earlier fragment), calls tncs_process on it, and frees the input buffer unless it is the stack buffer (524-536).

functions.name: eap_ttls_buildReq
functions.prose_contract: Builds the next EAP-TTLS request of the server (eap_server_ttls.c:466-510; slice cut the head). If the TLS fragment state is FRAG_ACK it returns a TLS ACK message (470-473); if it is WAIT_FRAG_ACK it returns the next TLS fragment (475-478). Otherwise it switches on the TTLS state: START returns eap_ttls_build_start; PHASE1 changes the state to PHASE2_START when the TLS connection is established and then breaks out of the switch; PHASE2_METHOD and PHASE2_MSCHAPV2_RESP replace the pending TLS output buffer with the encapsulated inner EAP request or the MS-CHAPv2 response and break; any other state logs and returns NULL (480-505). After a break it returns eap_server_tls_build_msg for the TLS output, so in PHASE1 the TLS message is returned after the possible state transition as well (508-509).

functions.name: SM_STATE(AUTH_PAE, INITIALIZE)
functions.prose_contract: Generated state function for the AUTH_PAE state INITIALIZE of the IEEE 802.1X authenticator (macro invocation SM_STATE(AUTH_PAE, INITIALIZE) at eapol_auth_sm.c:198-214; the generated function is sm_AUTH_PAE_INITIALIZE); it returns nothing. It runs the state entry macro SM_ENTRY_MA (which logs the transition and sets sm->changed when the state differs or when not running in global mode), sets sm->portMode to Auto and clears sm->keyRun to false (200-213).

functions.name: SM_STATE(AUTH_PAE, DISCONNECTED)
functions.prose_contract: Generated state function for the AUTH_PAE state DISCONNECTED (macro invocation SM_STATE(AUTH_PAE, DISCONNECTED) at eapol_auth_sm.c:217-246); it returns nothing. Before entering the state it records whether it came from INITIALIZE, whether it is a pre-authentication logoff from ABORTING (a logoff while not authenticated) and the logoff flag, and counts an EAPOL-Logoff received in the CONNECTING or AUTHENTICATED states in the matching counter (219-229). It then runs the entry macro, sets authPortStatus to Unauthorized, calls setPortUnauthorized, clears reAuthCount and eapolLogoff (231-236). Unless it came from INITIALIZE or it is a pre-authentication logoff, it calls the finished callback of the EAPOL layer with the logoff flag and sets sm->stopped to true if the callback returns nonzero (237-245).

functions.name: SM_STATE(AUTH_PAE, RESTART)
functions.prose_contract: Generated state function for the AUTH_PAE state RESTART (macro invocation SM_STATE(AUTH_PAE, RESTART) at eapol_auth_sm.c:249-263); it returns nothing. When the previous state is AUTHENTICATED it increments the counters for re-authentications, EAPOL-Start and EAPOL-Logoff events that are pending (251-258). It then runs the entry macro and sets sm->eap_if->eapRestart to true (260-262).

functions.name: eapol_sm_notify_config
functions.prose_contract: Passes a new network configuration to the EAPOL supplicant state machine (eapol_supp_sm.c:1554-1586; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It returns without effect if sm is NULL (1558-1559). It stores the config pointer in sm->config; with CONFIG_EAP_PROXY it also sets sm->use_eap_proxy from eap_proxy_notify_config (1561-1564). It returns if conf is NULL (1566-1567). It copies accept_802_1x_keys, required_keys, fast_reauth, workaround and wps into sm->conf (1569-1573). With CONFIG_EAP_PROXY and use_eap_proxy set it returns here (1574-1578). Otherwise (including builds without proxy support) and when the EAP state machine exists, it passes fast reauthentication, the workaround, the disabled flag and external SIM setting to the EAP layer (1580-1585).

functions.name: SM_STEP(SUPP_PAE)
functions.prose_contract: Generated step function of the IEEE 802.1X supplicant PAE state machine (macro invocation SM_STEP(SUPP_PAE) at eapol_supp_sm.c:365-449); it returns nothing and may change sm->SUPP_PAE_state through SM_ENTER_GLOBAL and SM_ENTER. The global transitions are tested first, in this order: LOGOFF when a user logoff is pending and not yet sent and the port is enabled and not initializing; DISCONNECTED when the port control is Auto and the port mode differs, or initialize is set, or the port is not enabled; S_FORCE_AUTH and S_FORCE_UNAUTH when the port control asks for a forced mode that is not yet set (367-381). If none of them applies, it switches on the current state: LOGOFF goes to DISCONNECTED when the user logoff is cleared; DISCONNECTED goes to CONNECTING; CONNECTING goes to CONNECTING again, AUTHENTICATED, AUTHENTICATING, RESTART or HELD depending on startWhen, startCount, portValid, eapSuccess, eapFail and eapolEap; AUTHENTICATING may first set portValid and call eapol_done_cb when the key requirements allow it, then goes to AUTHENTICATED, HELD or CONNECTING; HELD goes to CONNECTING or RESTART; AUTHENTICATED goes to RESTART or DISCONNECTED; RESTART goes to AUTHENTICATING when eapRestart is clear; the unknown and forced states do nothing (382-448). So the state can change even when no global guard fires.

functions.name: SM_STEP(SUPP_BE)
functions.prose_contract: Generated step function of the IEEE 802.1X supplicant backend state machine (macro invocation SM_STEP(SUPP_BE) at eapol_supp_sm.c:592-661); it returns nothing and may change sm->SUPP_BE_state. If initialize or suppAbort is set it enters INITIALIZE through SM_ENTER_GLOBAL (594-595). Otherwise it switches on the state: REQUEST logs a warning if both eapResp and eapNoResp are set and goes to RESPONSE (eapResp), RECEIVE (eapNoResp), FAIL (eapFail) or SUCCESS (eapSuccess), in that order of precedence (599-626); RESPONSE goes to RECEIVE; SUCCESS, FAIL and TIMEOUT go to IDLE; IDLE goes to FAIL, REQUEST or SUCCESS when suppStart is set together with eapFail, eapolEap or eapSuccess respectively; INITIALIZE goes to IDLE; RECEIVE goes to REQUEST, FAIL, TIMEOUT (authWhile is 0) or SUCCESS (627-659). The function does not use the EAP proxy or eap_key_available fields.

functions.name: p2p_build_wps_ie
functions.prose_contract: Appends a WPS vendor-specific information element for P2P to buf (p2p_build.c:742-841; slice cut the head); it returns 0 on success and -1 on failure. It needs at least 6 bytes of tailroom, writes the element id, a length placeholder and the WFA OUI, and adds the WPS version attribute, returning -1 on any failure (748-755). When all_attr is nonzero it adds the WPS State attribute with the value "not configured" (757-763). When pw_id is not negative it adds the Device Password ID attribute (765-774). When all_attr is nonzero it also adds the Response Type, UUID-E, manufacturer, model name, model number, serial number, primary device type, device name and configuration methods attributes (776-809). It adds the WFA vendor extension (811-812) and, when all_attr is nonzero and secondary device types exist, the secondary device type list (814-824). Then it adds the configured WPS vendor extensions, skipping any that does not fit (827-836), fills in the element length and returns 0 (840). Each of the tailroom checks and attribute builders returns -1 when it fails.

functions.name: p2p_process_go_neg_resp
functions.prose_contract: Processes a received P2P Group Owner Negotiation Response (p2p_go_neg.c:1214-1484; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It returns without effect if the peer device is unknown, has no WPS method, is not the current negotiation peer, the message does not parse, no response was awaited or the dialog token differs (1225-1249); otherwise it clears the wait flag and records the peer's 6 GHz capability. A missing status attribute goes to fail with INVALID_PARAMS. A nonzero status (a failure by the peer) clears go_neg_req_sent and, for "information currently unavailable", marks the peer not yet ready and waits up to 120 s, or else reports the failure with p2p_go_neg_failed; then it calls send_action_done and returns without building a confirmation (1251-1278). For a success status it requires the intended address, a GO intent of at most 15 (shifted) and a compatible GO role determination, a group id when it is the client, and a configuration timeout, going to fail with INVALID_PARAMS or INCOMPATIBLE_PARAMS otherwise (1296-1341). A missing Capability or P2P Device Info attribute is fatal only when CONFIG_P2P_STRICT is defined; otherwise it only logs (1280-1294). It then stores peer information, checks the device password id against the WPS method (INCOMPATIBLE_PROV_METHOD on mismatch), selects the operating channel when it is the GO (failure goes to fail), checks preferred channels, sets the state GO_NEG and records the intended address (1378-1447). At fail it builds a GO Negotiation Confirmation with the status, sends it, sets the pending action state and go_state only for a success status, and calls p2p_go_neg_failed for a nonsuccess status (1449-1483).

functions.name: p2p_check_pref_chan
functions.prose_contract: Applies the driver's preferred frequency list when a P2P group is being formed (p2p_go_neg.c:694-799; the packet name is right, the slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It does nothing if the driver does not provide a preferred frequency list, if preferred channels are configured, if a frequency is forced for the peer, or if an operating channel is set in the configuration (709-711). It fetches the list into p2p->pref_freq_list and returns if the call fails or the list is empty (714-721). It then removes from that list, by shifting later entries down, every frequency that is not acceptable: one with no channel mapping, one not in the local channels (and for a client not in the client channels), or a 6 GHz frequency when 6 GHz is not allowed with this peer (723-749). It logs the remaining list and looks for the peer's operating frequency in it among the entries allowed for the role (p2p_pref_freq_allowed); if found it sets the operating class and channel and copies the configured channel set, then returns (768-783). Otherwise it calls p2p_check_pref_chan_no_recv when the message has no preferred frequency list and p2p_check_pref_chan_recv when it does (793-798).

functions.name: p2p_process_prov_disc_resp
functions.prose_contract: Processes a received P2P Provision Discovery Response (p2p_pd.c:1306-1603; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It returns without effect if the frame does not parse, or, when P2PS provisioning is active, if the P2PS validation fails (the message is freed in the second case) (1320-1326). It reads the status, the group address, the advertisement MAC and id and the connection capability (swapping group owner and client roles) (1329-1354). It returns if the peer is unknown or has no pending request, and if the dialog token differs (1360-1378). It clears the pending PD state, and when the received WPS configuration methods differ from the requested ones it reports a rejected provisioning through prov_disc_fail, frees the message and goes to out (1380-1410). The rest (1413-1560) records the accepted configuration methods in the peer flags, handles the P2PS status and password ids, may report failure through prov_disc_fail, and records the interface address. At out it clears the peer's req_config_methods and calls send_action_done; if the peer is flagged PD_BEFORE_GO_NEG it clears that flag and continues with p2p_connect_send and returns (1564-1572). Otherwise it calls prov_disc_resp for a successful non-P2PS response or the P2PS cases and, if the state is P2P_PD_DURING_FIND, stops listening and continues the find (1589-1602).

functions.name: p2p_prov_disc_req
functions.prose_contract: Starts a P2P Provision Discovery exchange with a peer (p2p_pd.c:1687-1752; slice cut the head); it returns 0, -1 or the result of p2p_send_prov_disc_req. It looks up the peer; an unknown peer, or one known only from a probe request, frees p2ps_prov and returns -1 (1694-1702). With no config methods and no P2PS provisioning it returns -1 (1707-1710). A deferred P2PS status copies the previous method (1712-1716). It then clears the peer's wps_prov_info, replaces the stored P2PS provisioning with the new one (the previous one is freed), stores the requested methods and sets or clears the join flag (1719-1727). If the P2P state is not idle, search or listen-only it logs that the request is postponed and returns 0 (1729-1735). Otherwise it records user_initiated_pd and the forced frequency, sets the retry count for a user-initiated request, advances the peer's dialog token (skipping 0) and returns p2p_send_prov_disc_req(p2p, dev, join, force_freq) (1737-1751). This function does not set pending_action_state itself.

functions.name: radius_client_retransmit
functions.prose_contract: Retransmits a RADIUS message from the client list (radius_client.c:374-545; slice cut the head); it returns 0 to keep the entry, 1 to have the caller remove it, or -1 on a TLS encryption failure. It selects the accounting or authentication side, its TLS connection and server count; if that socket is not open it initialises it and, with several servers, fails over, returning 0 when the failover removed messages (391-427). It counts a request or a timeout and retransmission for the server (408-413, 429-434). An interim accounting message is dropped: it calls the interim error callback and returns 1 (437-446). A negative socket returns 1 (448-452). If the TLS connection is not yet ready it jumps to not_ready without sending and without incrementing the attempt counters, but still reaches the code that sets next_try and doubles next_wait (455-459, 536-542). For an accounting message it updates the Acct-Delay-Time and gets a new identifier (463-489). If the accumulated attempts reached the failover limit it returns 1 (492-496). Otherwise it increments attempts and accu_attempts, encrypts the message when TLS is used (failure returns -1), sends it, and on a send error that the handler treats as fatal frees the buffer and returns 0 without setting the next try time (499-531). Then it frees the buffer, sets next_try to now plus next_wait, doubles next_wait up to RADIUS_CLIENT_MAX_WAIT and returns 0 (534-544).

functions.name: radius_server_request
functions.prose_contract: Handles a received RADIUS Access-Request on the built-in server (radius_server.c:1357-1555; slice cut the head); it returns 0, -1 or -2. It finds the session from the State attribute (or uses a forced session); a request with a State but no matching session is rejected and returns -1, and without State a new session is created (failure rejects and returns -1) (1372-1402). A retransmission (same port, identifier and authenticator as the last request) counts a duplicate, resends the stored last reply and returns 0, or returns -1 if there is no stored reply (1404-1428). Without an EAP attribute it uses MAC ACL handling when configured (a NULL reply returns -1, otherwise it jumps to send_reply), and otherwise counts a dropped packet and returns -1 (1430-1443). With EAP data it passes it to the EAP server state machine and takes a reply from it; if the method is pending it stores the message and the sender and returns -2 (1454-1475); an unusable state counts a dropped packet and returns -1 (1476-1482). It marks the session complete when the state machine succeeded or failed, builds the reply with radius_server_encapsulate_eap (1485-1497), and in send_reply counts the reply type, sends it, and stores it with the port, identifier and authenticator as the last reply (1499-1538); with no reply it only counts a dropped packet and does not set last_reply (1539-1542). When the session is complete it replaces the removal timeout with one of RADIUS_SESSION_MAINTAIN seconds (1544-1551) and returns 0 (1554).

functions.name: radius_server_eap_pending_cb
functions.prose_contract: Callback invoked when a pending EAP method of the built-in RADIUS server has a result (radius_server.c:2616-2652; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It returns if data is NULL (2622-2623). It searches all clients' sessions for the one whose eap equals ctx and which has a stored last_msg (2625-2634); if there is none it logs and returns (2636-2639). It takes the stored message out of the session (clearing last_msg), calls eap_sm_pending_cb(sess->eap) (only the EAP state machine is passed, not the message), and calls radius_server_request again with that message, the stored sender information and the session forced (2641-2648). If that returns -2 (the method is pending again) it returns and the message is kept by the request function; otherwise it frees the message (2648-2651).

functions.name: wpa_tdls_process_tpk_m1
functions.prose_contract: Processes a received TDLS Setup Request (TPK Handshake Message 1) on the responder side (tdls.c:1942-2317; the packet name is correct but the slice cut the head); it returns 0 on success and -1 on failure. It returns -1 if the frame is too short (1967-1968). It finds or adds the peer entry (a failure goes to error); for an existing peer with an established link it tears the old link down and clears the peer, and for an existing peer for which it already initiated a setup it returns -1 when its own address is lower than the sender's, otherwise it disables the link of the earlier attempt and continues (1978-2012). It then parses and checks the link identifier, RSN and other elements: many malformed or inconsistent elements go to error with a TDLS status code (goto error at 2036-2176), a missing key lifetime or a lifetime below 300 seconds gives UNACCEPTABLE_LIFETIME (2165-2177). With a valid RSN it builds the peer's RSN element, and stores the validated lifetime in peer->lifetime (2273) and derives the TPK with wpa_tdls_generate_tpk (2278); unless a testing flag skips it, it adds the peer to the driver (a failure goes to error) (2281-2289). It then sets tpk_in_progress and sends TPK Message 2; a send failure disables the link and goes to error (2294-2300). It returns 0 (2309). The error label sends a setup error response with the status and frees the peer entry, then returns -1 (2311-2316).

functions.name: wpa_tdls_process_tpk_m3
functions.prose_contract: Processes a received TDLS Setup Confirm (TPK Handshake Message 3) (tdls.c:2655-2813; slice cut the head); it returns 0 or the result of the link enabling, and -1 on failure. It finds the peer entry by address and returns -1 if there is none (2671-2679). It cancels the retry timeout for the setup response (2680). A too-short frame, a nonzero status, or a failure of any of the following element checks goes to error (2682-2790): the RSN, link identifier, fast transition and timeout (lifetime) elements are compared with those stored for the peer. It adds or sets the peer in the driver, and if the TPK handshake had not succeeded yet it enables the link; a negative result of wpa_tdls_enable_link goes to error, otherwise ret holds that result and is returned (2794-2809). The error label tears the link down with wpa_tdls_do_teardown (reason TDLS_TEARDOWN_UNSPECIFIED) and returns -1 (2810-2812).

functions.name: wpa_eapol_key_send
functions.prose_contract: Sends an EAPOL-Key frame from the supplicant (wpa.c:91-207; slice cut the head); it returns the result of wpa_sm_ether_send or -1. It takes ownership of msg and frees it at the out label on every path (204-206). If the destination and the stored BSSID are both zero it tries to read the BSSID and uses it as the destination (101-117). When a MIC is in use (mic_len nonzero) and a key_mic buffer is requested it needs a PTK with a KCK (otherwise -1) and computes the MIC, going to out with -1 if that fails (119-135). When no MIC is used (the AES-SIV case) it needs a PTK with a KEK, allocates a buffer, and encrypts the key data with aes_siv_encrypt, going to out with ret still -1 if the allocation or the encryption fails; on success it replaces msg by the encrypted frame (136-195); without CONFIG_FILS this branch goes to out with -1 (197). It then sends the frame with wpa_sm_ether_send, notifies the EAPOL state machine of the transmitted key frame, and frees msg (202-206).

functions.name: wpa_supplicant_process_3_of_4
functions.prose_contract: Processes EAPOL-Key message 3 of the 4-way handshake in the supplicant (wpa.c, wpa_supplicant_process_3_of_4 ending at 2807; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It validates the key information flags (encrypted key data, install and secure must be set), parses the key data elements, checks the GTK and IGTK elements against the key-data flags, the ANonce against the stored one and the key length against the pairwise cipher; any failure goes to the failed label, which deauthenticates with WLAN_REASON_UNSPECIFIED (2583-2770, 2805-2806). Some paths return silently (2687, 2696). When the checks pass it installs the PTK (if the install flag is set; a failure goes to failed), sets the state to WPA_GROUP_HANDSHAKE (2746), handles the GTK and IGTK (a failure goes to failed), sends message 4 (wpa_supplicant_send_4_of_4) and reports negotiation completion with wpa_supplicant_key_neg_complete, then sets rekey offload, adds a PMKSA entry for Suite B, handles a transition-disable element, sets msg_3_of_4_ok to 1 and returns (2776-2803). It does not set WPA_4WAY_HANDSHAKE on the success path.

functions.name: wpa_supplicant_get_pmk
functions.prose_contract: Finds or obtains the PMK for the current 4-way handshake (wpa.c:311-510; slice cut the head); it returns 0, -1 or -2. If a PMKID is given and no PMKSA is selected it looks the entry up in the cache; none found sets abort_cached (317-333). A PMKID that matches the selected entry installs the PMK from the cache and notifies the EAPOL layer (335-341 and the lines after it). Otherwise, for 802.1X key management, it asks the EAPOL state machine for the MSK: on success it derives and caches a PMKSA, and a new PMK that does not match the given PMKID returns -1 (a mismatch message), a match clears abort_cached (430-460). With FT key management over an FT protocol association and no PMK it logs that the handshake continues without a PMK or PMKID and changes nothing (461-464), so sm->pmk, pmk_len and cur_pmksa are not updated in that case. Otherwise a failure to get the key logs a warning, cancels a selected PMKSA (setting abort_cached) or returns -1 if none was selected and abort_cached is not set (465-479). When abort_cached remains set for plain 802.1X (not Suite B, FT or OSEN) it sends an EAPOL-Start to trigger full authentication and returns -2 (-1 if the frame cannot be allocated) (482-506). Otherwise it returns 0 (509).
