functions.name: wpa_sm_set_assoc_rsnxe
functions.prose_contract: Stores the station's own RSNXE for the association (wpa.c:4991-5020; slice cut the head); it returns 0 on success and -1 on failure. It returns -1 if sm is NULL (4993-4994). It frees the old RSNXE, then clears the stored pointer and length when ie is NULL or len is 0, otherwise it stores a copy made with os_memdup and returns -1 if the copy fails, in which case sm->assoc_rsnxe has been set to NULL by that assignment and not left dangling (4996-5008). If SSID protection is enabled and the stored RSNXE does not advertise the SSID protection capability, it disables SSID protection (5011-5017). It returns 0 (5019).

functions.name: wpa_ft_process_response
functions.prose_contract: Processes an FT (fast BSS transition) response on the supplicant (wpa_ft.c:584-777; slice cut the head); it returns 0 on success and -1 on failure. All failure paths go to fail, which frees the parsed information elements (wpa_ft_parse_ies_free) and returns ret; the same free also runs on success (774-776). For an over-the-DS action it drops the response unless an over-the-DS transition is in progress for the same target AP (603-616). It fails if FT is not enabled for the key management, if the elements cannot be parsed, or if the mobility domain element, FT element, ANonce, SNonce (which must equal the stored one), R0KH-ID, R1KH-ID, the PMKID in the RSN element or the PMF requirement do not match (618-686). It stores the R1KH-ID and ANonce, derives PMK-R1 and then the PTK (with a KDK if configured) (688-716) and the LTF key seed when needed (722-727). It generates the reassociation request elements with wpa_ft_gen_req_ies and passes them to wpa_sm_update_ft_ies (743-747), marks the peer authenticated, installs the PTK (a failure sets set_ptk_after_assoc), sets ft_completed and, for the action frame case, copies the target AP address into sm->bssid, and returns 0 (749-773).

functions.name: mp_exptmod_fast
functions.prose_contract: Computes Y = G^X mod P with a fixed-window method and a Montgomery, diminished-radix or 2^k reduction (libtommath.c:2952-3235; the packet name was truncated, the function is the static mp_exptmod_fast); it returns MP_OKAY on success or an error code. The window size is chosen from the bit length of X (capped at 5), and the table entries M[1] and M[1<<(winsize-1)] to M[(1<<winsize)-1] are initialised; a failed mp_init clears the entries made so far and returns the error (2965-3003). The reduction is chosen from redmode: 0 uses Montgomery reduction (a failed setup, or an unsupported build configuration, leaves err as the setup result or MP_VAL), 1 uses diminished-radix reduction, and any other value uses 2^k reduction, so redmode is not restricted to 0 and 1 in the code (3006-3053). It initialises res (failure goes to LBL_M, 3056-3058), builds the table and runs the exponentiation loop (3067-3211 not read in detail), does a final Montgomery reduction when redmode is 0 (3213-3223), and only on success exchanges res into Y (mp_exch) and sets err to MP_OKAY (3226-3227). Any failing step jumps to LBL_RES or LBL_M, which free res and the initialised table entries; Y is changed only by that final exchange, and the function returns err (3228-3234).

functions.name: tlsv1_server_process_handshake
functions.prose_contract: Dispatches one received TLS record to the handler of the server's current handshake state (tlsv1_server_read.c:1269-1320; slice cut the head); it returns 0 on success and -1 on failure. An alert record with fewer than 2 bytes sends a fatal decode-error alert and returns -1; any other alert sets the state to FAILED and returns -1 (1272-1283). Otherwise it switches on conn->state and calls tls_process_client_hello, tls_process_certificate, tls_process_client_key_exchange, tls_process_certificate_verify, tls_process_change_cipher_spec or tls_process_client_finished, returning -1 if the handler returns nonzero; an unexpected state logs and returns -1 (1285-1314). After a successful handler, if the record is a handshake record, it adds the buffer (buf, *len) to the handshake hash with tls_verify_hash_add (1316-1317), including when the state was CLIENT_FINISHED; the length value used is whatever the handler left in *len. It returns 0 (1319).

functions.name: x509_certificate_chain_validate
functions.prose_contract: Validates a certificate chain against a list of trusted certificates (x509v3.c:2138-2259; slice cut the head); it returns 0 if the chain is valid (or CA trust is disabled with no trusted list) and -1 otherwise, setting *reason in the failing cases. It walks the chain from the first certificate. For each certificate it first sets issuer_trusted to 0, but after the chain has been found trusted at some certificate the walk only clears issuer_trusted for the remaining certificates and does nothing else (2153-2159). A failing step returns -1 at once, leaving issuer_trusted of later certificates untouched. Unless time checks are disabled it requires the current time to lie in the validity period (2161-2171). When there is a next certificate it requires that its subject equals this one's issuer, that it is a valid issuer, that a path length constraint is not exceeded and that its signature on this certificate verifies (2173-2214). It looks up the issuer in the trusted list; if found it requires the trusted certificate to be a valid issuer and its signature on this certificate to verify, then sets this certificate's issuer_trusted to 1 and marks the chain trusted (2216-2242). If no certificate was found trusted it returns -1 when a trusted list is given, and otherwise only logs that CA validation was disabled (2245-2254); it returns 0 (2258).

functions.name: ieee80211_radiotap_iterator_next
functions.prose_contract: Advances a radiotap header iterator to the next present field (radiotap.c:234-396; slice cut the head); it returns 0 with this_arg, this_arg_index and this_arg_size set when a field is found, -ENOENT at the end of the fields, or -EINVAL for an inconsistent header. It loops over bitmap bits (237-395). It returns -ENOENT when the extension bit is not set at an index that is a multiple of 32 (243-245) or when an unknown bit is found in the radiotap namespace itself (267-270). A set bit selects alignment and size: namespace and extension bits take no data, the vendor namespace bit takes 6 bytes with alignment 2, and other bits use the current namespace table (or an override); a field of unknown size in a vendor namespace ends that namespace's data by skipping to _next_ns_data (251-284). It aligns _arg (298-302). For a vendor namespace bit it returns -EINVAL if the 6-byte vendor header lies beyond max_length, reads the OUI and sub-namespace, looks up the namespace, reads the vendor data length vnslen, sets _next_ns_data = _arg + size + vnslen, and adds vnslen to size only when the namespace is not registered (304-323); so vnslen is not checked against max_length for a registered namespace, and only the later check of _arg against max_length applies (343-346). It records the current field, advances _arg and returns -EINVAL if that passes max_length (329-346). Then it handles the namespace and extension bits (switching namespace, reading the next bitmap word) without returning a field, except that an unregistered vendor namespace is returned as a raw field (349-383); any other bit is a hit and returns 0 (384-394).

functions.name: wps_registrar_pbc_timeout
functions.prose_contract: Timer callback that ends a WPS push-button (PBC) session (wps_registrar.c:1021-1028; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It calls wps_pbc_timeout_event(reg->wps) to report the timeout and wps_registrar_stop_pbc(reg) (1026-1027). wps_registrar_stop_pbc clears selected_registrar and pbc, zeroes the P2P device address, removes the wildcard authorized MAC and informs the registrar that the selected state changed (1010-1018). This function itself does not cancel any eloop timeout; it is the callback of the timer, and other code that registers it cancels it.

functions.name: wps_build_cred
functions.prose_contract: Builds the Credential attribute for the WPS registrar's M8 message into msg (wps_registrar.c:1618-1834; slice cut the head); it returns 0 on success and -1 on failure. When the registrar has skip_cred_build set it jumps straight to skip_cred_build, so wps->cred is not filled in and no Credential attribute is added; it then only appends the registrar's extra credential, if there is one, and returns 0 (1625-1626, 1827-1833). A credential supplied in wps->use_cred is copied and used; a multi-AP backhaul station with a configured backhaul SSID gets that SSID and key; otherwise the credential is built from the AP's SSID, the enrollee's masked authentication type (WPA2-PSK, then WPA-PSK, then open; none of these returns -1) and the encryption type, key and MAC address (1629-1678, the rest 1679-1784 not read). With use_provided it optionally adds a stub credential for testing, then allocates a 200-byte buffer (return -1 if that fails), builds the credential with wps_build_credential (failure frees the buffer and returns -1), appends the attribute (type, length, data) and frees the buffer; the extra credential is appended after that, and it returns 0 (1785-1833).

functions.name: wps_registrar_get_msg
functions.prose_contract: Returns the next WPS message of the registrar side to send (wps_registrar.c:2100-2195; slice cut the head); it returns the message buffer or NULL and sets *op_code only on some paths. With UPnP and no internal registrar it takes the oldest pending UPnP message from the list (clearing the external-registrar pending state if ext_reg is above 1), sets *op_code to ACK, NACK or MSG by its type, frees the list entry, and returns the message, setting ext_reg to 1 if it was 0 (2105-2138); with an external registrar and no pending message it returns NULL (2141-2145). Otherwise it builds the message for the current state: SEND_M2 builds M2D when no device password is available and M2 otherwise, SEND_M2D builds M2D, SEND_M4, SEND_M6 and SEND_M8 build those messages, RECV_DONE builds a WSC ACK (op code ACK) and SEND_WSC_NACK builds a NACK (op code NACK); a message of type MSG sets *op_code to WSC_MSG (2148-2179). Any other state logs and returns NULL without setting *op_code (2180-2184). Only when the op code is WSC_MSG and the message was built, it replaces wps->last_msg with a copy of the message; if a build returns NULL, last_msg is not touched (2187-2192). It returns the message (2194).

functions.name: wps_process_wsc_ack
functions.prose_contract: Processes a received WSC_ACK message on the registrar (wps_registrar.c:3112-3176; slice cut the head); it returns a wps_process_res. It returns WPS_FAILURE if the message does not parse, has no message type, or the type is not WSC_ACK (3119-3131). With UPnP, an external registrar, state RECV_M2D_ACK and subscribers, it returns WPS_CONTINUE if UPnP messages are pending and otherwise WPS_PENDING, before any nonce is compared (3133-3141). It returns WPS_FAILURE if the registrar nonce or the enrollee nonce is missing or differs from the stored one (3144-3155). For the state RECV_M2D_ACK it again may return WPS_CONTINUE or WPS_PENDING when UPnP subscribers exist, and otherwise logs that the negotiation is terminated (3157-3172). The function returns WPS_FAILURE at the end for every case that did not return earlier (3175), so a valid ACK without UPnP processing also gives WPS_FAILURE.

functions.name: wps_registrar_add_nfc_pw_token
functions.prose_contract: Adds an NFC password token to the WPS registrar (wps_registrar.c:3692-3744; slice cut the head); it returns 0 on success and -1 on failure. It returns -1 if dev_pw_len exceeds WPS_OOB_DEVICE_PASSWORD_LEN, and for the connection handover password id returns -1 when no public key hash was given or it was not provided out of band (3699-3707); both checks happen before any existing token is removed. It then frees existing tokens with the same pw_id (3709), allocates a token (return -1 if that fails, with the old same-id tokens already freed), fills in the public key hash, password id, the OOB flag and the device password as an uppercase hex string (3711-3726), adds it to the list, sets selected_registrar, clears pbc, adds the wildcard authorized MAC, notifies the registrar about the selected change and restarts the selected-registrar timeout (3728-3738), and returns 0 (3743).

functions.name: event_retry
functions.prose_contract: Re-queues a failed UPnP event for the next subscriber address, or gives up (wps_upnp_event.c:117-142; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It cleans up the event's HTTP client state (event_clean) (124). When do_next_address is nonzero it increments e->retry (127-130). If e->retry is not below the length of the subscription's address list it logs "Giving up" using e->addr->domain_and_port, deletes the event, sets s->last_event_failed and, if events remain queued, schedules sending later, then returns (131-138); otherwise it adds the event back at the end of the queue and schedules sending later (140-141). In that giving-up message e->addr is dereferenced, but event_addr_failure sets e->addr = NULL (wps_upnp_event.c:197) before calling event_retry(e, 0) (209), so in that call, if the address list has become no longer than e->retry, the NULL pointer is dereferenced in the log argument (133).

functions.name: event_send_start
functions.prose_contract: Starts sending the next queued UPnP event to a subscriber (wps_upnp_event.c:270-310; slice cut the head); it returns 0 when the HTTP request was started and -1 otherwise. It returns -1 without changes if the address list is empty, an event is already current, or the event queue is empty (280-283). Otherwise it makes the dequeued event the current event and walks the address list to the entry numbered e->retry: if the list has fewer than e->retry entries it returns -1 (leaving the event as current), but when e->retry equals the list length the loop ends without a break, itry is not below e->retry, and the code goes on with e->addr left pointing at the list head position and not at a real address (288-293). It builds the message; failure calls event_addr_failure and returns -1 (295-299). It starts the HTTP client; failure frees the message, calls event_addr_failure and returns -1 (301-307); otherwise it returns 0 (309).

functions.name: advertisement_state_machine_handler
functions.prose_contract: Timer callback that sends the next SSDP advertisement message of the WPS UPnP device (wps_upnp_ssdp.c:257-327; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It asks next_advertisement for the next message and its "is last" flag and returns without rescheduling if there is none (282-284). It sends the message to the SSDP multicast address and port; if sendto fails it logs and sets the next timeout to 10 seconds (291-296). If the send worked and this was the last message of the sequence it resets the state; for a "byebye" (ADVERTISE_DOWN) sequence it switches to ADVERTISE_UP and keeps the short default delay, and for an up sequence it sets a random delay of UPNP_CACHE_SEC/4 plus up to UPNP_CACHE_SEC/4 seconds and increments advertise_count (297-318). Otherwise it increments the state (319-321). It frees the message and registers itself again with eloop_register_timeout(next_timeout_sec, next_timeout_msec, ...) (323-326); the variable next_timeout_msec, whose default is 100, is passed as the microseconds argument of that call, so the default delay is 100 microseconds rather than 100 milliseconds.

functions.name: wpa_bss_update
functions.prose_contract: Updates an existing BSS entry from a new scan result (bss.c:671-800; slice cut the head); it returns the (possibly reallocated) BSS. If the entry was already updated in this scan round it returns it unchanged when the old entry is associated or looks more current, otherwise it accepts the newer one (676-710). It computes the changes, resets the scan miss count, copies the new fields and IE lengths via wpa_bss_copy_res and removes the entry from the list (712-720). Unless a P2P IE would be lost (the IEs are then kept), it copies the new IEs in place when they fit; when they do not fit it reallocates the entry, and on success it updates the references to it (last_scan_res, current_bss, the ML probe bss and a pending connect) and copies the IEs, while on allocation failure it keeps the old entry without the new IEs and carries on (738-781). If the IEs changed it sets the HESSID and the MLD address from the multi-link element (782-794). It re-adds the entry at the list tail, calls notify_bss_changes and returns the entry; there is no early return after a failed realloc, so the notification still happens (795-799).

functions.name: wpas_ctrl_nfc_report_handover
functions.prose_contract: Handles the control-interface command that reports an NFC handover (ctrl_iface.c:1826-1940; the packet name wpa_supplicant_ctrl_iface_nfc_report_handover does not exist); it returns the result of the handler it calls or -1. It parses "<role> <type> <req-hex> <sel-hex> [freq=N]" in place: an optional " freq=" value is read into forced_freq, and a missing role, type, request or select field returns -1 (1837-1866). It converts each hex string to a buffer; an odd length, an allocation failure or invalid hex returns -1 after freeing what it allocated (1868-1905). Then, by role and type, it calls wpas_wps_nfc_report_handover (INIT, WPS), wpas_ap_wps_nfc_report_handover and, if that fails with a negative result, wpas_er_wps_nfc_report_handover (RESP, WPS), wpas_p2p_nfc_report_handover with the initiator flag (INIT, P2P) or the forced frequency (RESP, P2P); any other combination logs and gives -1 (1910-1931). It frees both buffers and returns the handler's result (1933-1939).

functions.name: ctrl_iface_get_capability_key_mgmt
functions.prose_contract: Writes the list of supported key management names into buf for the GET_CAPABILITY command (ctrl_iface.c:4255-4473; slice cut the head); it returns the number of characters in the list, 0 or -1. If res is negative: with strict it returns 0, otherwise it copies the default list "WPA-PSK WPA-EAP IEEE8021X WPA-NONE NONE" with os_strlcpy and returns its length, or -1 if it does not fit (4268-4276). Otherwise it picks key_mgmt from capa->key_mgmt_iftype[iftype] for a recognised interface type (an unknown iftype_str returns -1) or from capa->key_mgmt (4278-4287). It then appends the text of "NONE IEEE8021X" and one token for each capability bit set (WPA-EAP, WPA-PSK, WPA-NONE, FT and SHA-256 variants, SAE, SUITE-B, OWE, DPP, FILS, OSEN and others) with os_snprintf (4289-4467). When a snprintf call reports truncation the function returns pos - buf at once, which counts only the tokens written completely so far; the buffer text after that point is whatever os_snprintf left (it NUL-terminates a truncated write by its definition, which I did not read) (4290-4291, 4297-4298 and the matching lines). At the end it returns pos - buf (4472).

functions.name: wpa_dbus_mark_property_changed
functions.prose_contract: Marks a D-Bus property of an object as changed and schedules the signal flush (dbus_new_helpers.c:859-900; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It returns if iface is NULL (867-868) or if the object path has no private descriptor (870-877). It searches the object's property table for the property name and interface; for a match it sets prop_changed_flags[i] = 1 when that array exists (879-885); with no matching property it logs and returns (887-891). If no flush timeout is registered for this object it registers flush_object_timeout_handler with eloop_register_timeout(0, WPA_DBUS_SEND_PROP_CHANGED_TIMEOUT, ...) (894-899); that macro is 5000 (dbus_new_helpers.c:843) and is passed as the microseconds argument, so the delay is 5000 microseconds (5 ms), not 5 seconds. An already registered timeout is left as it is.

functions.name: wpa_dbus_introspect
functions.prose_contract: Builds the D-Bus Introspect reply for an object (dbus_new_introspect.c:253-286; the packet name introspect_reply_builder does not exist). It allocates a 30000-byte XML buffer and returns NULL if that fails (260-262). It writes the XML header and "<node>", adds the introspectable and properties interfaces, the interfaces of the object descriptor and the child nodes of the message's path, and "</node>" (264-274). It creates a method-return reply for the message; if that succeeds it appends the XML text as a string argument (276-282). It frees the buffer in every case after the allocation succeeded and returns the reply, which is NULL if the reply message could not be created (283-285).

functions.name: wpas_dpp_gas_req_handler
functions.prose_contract: GAS server callback that handles a DPP Configuration Request (dpp_supplicant.c:4191-4302; slice cut the head); it returns the response buffer or NULL. It returns NULL if there is no authentication, it has not succeeded (neither authentication nor reconfiguration), or the sender is not the peer (4200-4204). If a configurator is waiting for the ACK of the Authentication Confirm, it assumes it was received, notifies success and clears the flag, and in the test mode that stops at the confirm returns NULL (4206-4222). It logs the request, builds the response with dpp_conf_req_rx and stores resp_ctx in auth->gas_server_ctx (4225-4231). Only in builds with CONFIG_DPP2: if there is no response because a certificate is not ready, it stores resp_ctx in config_resp_ctx, sets *comeback_delay to 500 and returns NULL (4233-4239). If there is no response because the configurator is waiting for the application's configuration, it formats the peer information (name, bands, MUD URL), reports DPP_EVENT_CONF_NEEDED, restarts the initial-response timeout for 50 ms and returns NULL (4242-4292). Otherwise it stores the response in conf_resp; with no response it reports DPP_EVENT_CONF_FAILED, deinitialises the authentication and clears wpa_s->dpp_auth; it returns resp (4295-4301).

functions.name: wpas_select_network_from_last_scan
functions.prose_contract: Selects and connects to a network from the last scan results (events.c:2642-2809; slice cut the head); it returns 0, 1, 2 or -1. It returns 0 when the P2P management interface is in use or a mesh group was joined (2661-2675). It picks a network (wpa_supplicant_pick_network); if one is selected and roaming is not needed it returns 0 (after the preauth step for a new scan) (2679-2686). Otherwise it deauthenticates when switching to a different network from an authenticating state, connects and returns -1 when wpa_supplicant_connect fails, and returns 1 on a successful connect (2688-2710). If none is selected it tries to pick a new network and associates (2714-2719); otherwise, for the function's own scan request, it may trigger a 6 GHz scan and return 1 when wpas_trigger_6ghz_scan returns a negative value, which cannot happen because that function returns only 0 or 1 (2720-2723). With the P2P scan helper it can return 2 or 0, and later branches return 1 after starting an ANQP fetch, 0 after scheduling a new scan quickly for P2P provisioning, WPS or OWE transition cases, or schedule a normal scan or scheduled scan and report NETWORK_NOT_FOUND (2735-2805). The default return is 0 (2808).

functions.name: multi_ap_set_4addr_mode
functions.prose_contract: Applies the Multi-AP backhaul station checks and 4-address mode after association (events.c:3059-3088; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It does nothing if there is no current network or it is not a Multi-AP backhaul station configuration (3061-3063). If the AP did not include a valid Multi-AP element it deauthenticates with WLAN_REASON_DEAUTH_LEAVING (3065-3069, 3086-3087). If the AP does not advertise backhaul support it accepts a fronthaul-only BSS only while WPS is active for the network and returns, otherwise it deauthenticates (3071-3081). If the AP advertises backhaul support it calls wpa_supplicant_set_4addr_mode (3083).

functions.name: wpas_ml_parse_assoc
functions.prose_contract: Parses the Basic Multi-Link element of an association response into per-link information (events.c:3778-4030; the packet name ml_basic_parser does not exist, and the slice cut the head); it returns the number of links stored in ml_info or 0. It returns 0 if no valid links are set or no Basic Multi-Link element is present, or if defragmentation fails (3796-3801). Any malformed or mismatching content ends at out, which frees the defragmented buffer and returns 0: a too short element, a control field lacking the expected presence bits, a common info length different from the expected one or too large for the element, and an AP MLD address different from wpa_s->ap_mld_addr (3805-3861, 4027-4029). It clears ml_info before parsing (3808). It then reads the link id of the association link and the per-link STA profile sub-elements, recording for each link its id, BSSID and status code; a sub-element too short goes to out (3864-4023). On success it frees the buffer and returns the count i (4025-4026). On a failure after some entries were filled, ml_info keeps the entries already written, and the buffer behind ml is freed on both paths.

functions.name: wpa_supplicant_event_assoc
functions.prose_contract: Handles the driver's association event in the supplicant (events.c:4132-4460; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It has several early returns (4145, 4151, 4164, 4171, 4181, 4187, 4222, 4228, 4268) and sets the state to WPA_ASSOCIATED (4196). It records already_authorized from the association information (4274). Unless the FT handshake is complete or the port is already authorized, it clears portEnabled and portValid of the EAPOL state machine; it notifies EAP success in some key management cases (PSK, DPP, OWE, FT completed, already authorized or a driver-authorized port) and sets portEnabled (4284-4294). With no key management or WPA-NONE, or in IBSS mode, it sets WPA_COMPLETED (after setting the key and cancelling the auth timeout); otherwise, when FT is not completed, it requests a 10-second authentication timeout (4296-4316). If FT is completed it sets WPA_COMPLETED and the EAPOL success and valid-port indications (4319-4327). If the driver does the 4-way handshake for PSK, it sets WPA_COMPLETED only when the driver already authorised the port and otherwise waits for the port-authorized event; for 802.1X with a driver-side 4-way handshake it only notifies portValid (4328-4355). The rest of the function (4357-4460 and the remaining handling) applies test overrides and sets the association information, which was not read.

functions.name: wpa_supplicant_event
functions.prose_contract: Called with ctx as a struct wpa_supplicant pointer, an event code and a union wpa_event_data pointer. If wpa_s->wpa_state is WPA_INTERFACE_DISABLED and the event is none of EVENT_INTERFACE_ENABLED, EVENT_INTERFACE_STATUS, EVENT_SCAN_RESULTS or EVENT_SCHED_SCAN_STOPPED, it logs "Ignore event" and returns without dispatching (events.c:5992-6001). Otherwise it logs the event (for EVENT_RX_MGMT it reads data->rx_mgmt first, events.c:6004) and switches on the event to the per-event handling code, which updates wpa_s state, may call other wpa_supplicant modules, and has no return value; the default case logs "Unknown event". Whether data may be NULL depends on the case: some cases test data before using it (for example EVENT_STATION_OPMODE_CHANGED and EVENT_TID_LINK_MAP check it) while others such as EVENT_UNPROT_BEACON (events.c:6916) and EVENT_IBSS_PEER_LOST pass data fields on without a check, so the caller must supply data for those. A disabled interface that receives EVENT_SCHED_SCAN_STOPPED passes the first check but that case executes break right away (events.c:6770-6771) and does no handling beyond clearing sched_scanning and notifying scanning.

functions.name: ibss_rsn_process_rx_eapol
functions.prose_contract: Static helper. Takes an ibss_rsn, a peer, a buffer of len bytes and the encryption flag. It first calls ibss_rsn_eapol_dst_supp(buf, len); if that returns a negative value (frame too short, not an EAPOL-Key, bad payload length, or unknown key type) it returns -1 and has made no copy. Otherwise it duplicates the frame with os_memdup; if that fails it returns -1. For a frame addressed to the supplicant it sets IBSS_RSN_AUTH_EAPOL_BY_PEER in peer->authentication_status and calls wpa_sm_rx_eapol(peer->supp, ...) with the copy (the call's result is not examined). For a frame addressed to the authenticator, if ibss_rsn_is_auth_started(peer) is 0 it frees the copy and returns -1; otherwise it calls wpa_receive(ibss_rsn->auth_group, peer->auth, copy, len). The copy is freed after delivery and the function then returns 1. The destination is determined inside this function; no caller-supplied "supp" value is assumed.

functions.name: ibss_rsn_rx_eapol
functions.prose_contract: Takes an ibss_rsn, a sender address, a buffer of len bytes and the encryption flag. Returns -1 if ibss_rsn is NULL (ibss_rsn.c:819). If a peer for src_addr exists (ibss_rsn_get_peer), it returns whatever ibss_rsn_process_rx_eapol returns for that peer, which is 1 on delivery or -1 on the failures listed for that helper. If no peer exists and ibss_rsn_eapol_dst_supp(buf, len) is greater than 0 (a well-formed EAPOL-Key addressed to the supplicant), it creates a peer with ibss_rsn_peer_init (returning -1 if that fails), marks it authenticated with IBSS_RSN_AUTH_EAPOL_BY_US, and returns the result of ibss_rsn_process_rx_eapol on ibss_rsn->peers (the list head, which is taken to be the new peer). If no peer exists and that destination test returns 0 or a negative value (frame for the authenticator, or malformed), nothing is created or delivered and it returns 0.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Entry point of wpa_supplicant (main.c:181-410). Returns -1 right away, with no cleanup, if os_program_init() fails or the first os_zalloc of the interface array fails. Otherwise it parses options with getopt. Options -h, -L, -v and any unknown option print usage, license or version and jump to out with exitcode 0; with CONFIG_NO_STDOUT_DEBUG -d jumps to out with exitcode -1 (the initial value); a failed os_realloc_array for -N or (CONFIG_MATCH_IFACE) -M also jumps to out with -1. After parsing it sets exitcode to 0 and calls wpa_supplicant_init; if that returns NULL it sets -1 and jumps to out. It then calls fst_global_init; on failure it sets -1 and jumps to out, and in that case wpa_supplicant_deinit and fst_global_deinit are not called although the global from wpa_supplicant_init exists. It then loops over the interfaces while exitcode is 0: an interface lacking (confname or ctrl_interface) or lacking ifname ends the loop with -1 after usage(), except that when exactly one interface was given and a global ctrl_interface, a match interface or the dbus interface was requested the loop just stops with exitcode unchanged; a failed wpa_supplicant_add_iface sets -1 and stops. If exitcode is still 0 it runs wpa_supplicant_init_match (CONFIG_MATCH_IFACE) and then, if still 0, wpa_supplicant_run, whose results become the exit code. After the loop (whatever the exit code) it calls wpa_supplicant_deinit(global) and fst_global_deinit(). The out label then calls wpa_supplicant_fd_workaround(0), frees ifaces, match_ifaces (CONFIG_MATCH_IFACE) and pid_file, calls crypto_unload and os_program_deinit, and returns exitcode.

functions.name: mesh_mpm_send_plink_action
functions.prose_contract: Static function in mesh_mpm.c (file lines 208-450) that sends a mesh peering Open, Confirm or Close self-protected action frame to peer sta. It reads wpa_s->ifmsh, its bss[0] and mconf before any check, so wpa_s must have a valid ifmsh with at least one bss and a mesh configuration. If sta is NULL it returns without doing anything; if wpabuf_alloc fails it also returns with no message and nothing sent. Otherwise it builds the frame: category/action, capability info, AID (when applicable), supported rates, mesh ID, mesh config, peering management, the close reason for PLINK_CLOSE, and for non-close frames the RSN element and the HT/VHT/HE/EHT elements that are compiled in and enabled. With AMPE enabled (conf->security has MESH_CONF_SEC_AMPE) it goes to the fail label if sta->sae is NULL (logging "no SAE session") and if mesh_rsn_protect_frame fails. For a non-close frame with conf->ocv set (CONFIG_OCV), it goes to fail when wpa_drv_channel_info fails or ocv_insert_extended_oci fails, whether or not AMPE is enabled. If all steps succeed it calls wpa_drv_send_action; a negative result is only logged. Every path after the successful allocation reaches the fail label (the normal end, at mesh_mpm.c:448) which frees the buffer; the function returns no value and does not report failure to the caller.

functions.name: wpas_p2p_scan_res_join
functions.prose_contract: Static handler in p2p_supplicant.c (lines 5334-5563) for scan results of a P2P join scan; scan_res may be NULL. It first cancels the pending wpas_p2p_join_scan timeout (5341) and returns if wpa_s->global->p2p_disabled is set. If scan_res is non-NULL it feeds it to wpas_p2p_scan_res_handler. If wpa_s->p2p_auto_pd is set, it looks up whether the peer is a GO (wpas_p2p_peer_go); when that is 0 and the retry counter is below P2P_AUTO_PD_SCAN_ATTEMPTS and the peer BSS is known it increments the counter, requests another join scan at the BSS frequency and returns. Otherwise it clears p2p_auto_pd, sets pending_pd_use, calls p2p_prov_disc_req (on failure it logs P2P_EVENT_PROV_DISC_FAILURE) and returns; this auto-PD branch never reaches the join code. If p2p_auto_join is set and the peer was not found running a GO (join < 0) it logs P2P_EVENT_FALLBACK_TO_GO_NEG, calls wpas_p2p_connect and returns; if the peer GO was only found in an older scan (join == 0) it logs P2P_EVENT_FALLBACK_TO_GO_NEG_ENABLED, sets p2p_fallback_to_go_neg and continues with the join code below. The join code determines the target frequency from the P2P peer table (possibly replacing pending_join_iface_addr) and from the BSS table (possibly replacing pending_join_dev_addr). If a frequency greater than 0 was found: if wpas_check_freq_conflict reports a conflict it logs P2P_EVENT_GROUP_FORMATION_FAILURE reason=FREQ_CONFLICT, notifies and returns; otherwise it sets pending_pd_before_join and, if provisioning info for the peer already equals the expected WPS config method or p2p_prov_disc_req fails, clears pending_pd_before_join and calls wpas_p2p_join_start; if p2p_prov_disc_req succeeds it returns and waits for the PD result. If no frequency was found it re-registers a one-second wpas_p2p_join_scan timeout and calls wpas_p2p_check_join_scan_limit. The function returns no value.

functions.name: p2ps_group_capability
functions.prose_contract: Static callback in p2p_supplicant.c (lines 716-911; the slice cut the head) that picks the P2PS connection capability for a provisioning request. Inputs are ctx (struct wpa_supplicant), the peer's incoming setup value, our requested role, and optional force_freq and pref_freq pointers. It first writes 0 to each non-NULL frequency pointer; if both are non-NULL and wpas_p2p_setup_freqs returns 0 it records the own frequency preference (*force_freq if non-zero, else *pref_freq). It then looks up the existing GO group, client group and persistent GO. When the device cannot create a separate group interface (wpas_p2p_create_iface returns 0) it returns P2PS_SETUP_NONE if a client group exists; if a GO group exists it returns NONE when role is CLIENT, incoming is GROUP_OWNER or the client limit is reached, otherwise GROUP_OWNER; with a persistent GO and role NONE or NEW it returns GROUP_OWNER|CLIENT when incoming is 0 and, when incoming is NEW, CLIENT or GROUP_OWNER depending on os_get_random (CLIENT if the random call fails or the low bit is set). If a role other than 0 or NEW is required, the switch on incoming either returns directly (CLIENT when role allows client and no GO or client group exists; CLIENT or NONE for incoming GROUP_OWNER; NONE for incoming equal to a CLIENT role or any unrecognised value) or sets conncap and continues at grp_owner. Otherwise a second switch on incoming sets conncap (for incoming NONE/NEW: GROUP_OWNER if a client group exists, NEW if the GO has no members, otherwise GROUP_OWNER|CLIENT or CLIENT; CLIENT gives GROUP_OWNER; GROUP_OWNER gives CLIENT only when no client group exists, else it stays NONE; GO|NEW and GO|CLIENT give GROUP_OWNER if a client group exists, else a random pick of CLIENT or GROUP_OWNER; any other value returns NONE). At grp_owner, if conncap includes GROUP_OWNER (or incoming is 0 and conncap includes NEW) it removes the GROUP_OWNER bit when the existing GO's client limit is reached; and when no persistent GO and no GO group exist it either sets the intended address (no-group-iface devices) or adds a P2P group interface, returning P2PS_SETUP_NONE if that fails and otherwise setting pending_group_iface_for_p2ps and the intended address. It returns conncap, which can be P2PS_SETUP_NONE (0) on several paths and may be a combination such as GROUP_OWNER|CLIENT.

functions.name: wpas_p2p_completed
functions.prose_contract: Called when the data connection of a P2P group is up (p2p_supplicant.c:7850-7918). It reads ssid = wpa_s->current_ssid. If ssid is NULL or ssid->mode is not WPAS_MODE_P2P_GROUP_FORMATION it cancels the wpas_p2p_group_formation_timeout timeout registered on wpa_s->p2pdev; when the ssid is in group-formation mode the timeout is left alone. It then returns, with nothing further done, if wpa_s->show_group_started is 0 or ssid is NULL. Otherwise it clears show_group_started. Only if p2p_go_group_formation_completed is 0 and global->p2p_group_formation equals wpa_s does it set p2p_go_group_formation_completed to 1, clear global->p2p_group_formation, and zero p2p_in_provisioning, p2p_in_invitation and p2p_retry_limit. It then builds go_dev_addr (zeros, or ssid->bssid when ssid->bssid_set), determines whether the group is persistent (wpas_p2p_persistent_group), copies go_dev_addr to wpa_s->go_dev_addr, clears global->p2p_group_formation again if it still equals wpa_s, takes the frequency from current_bss or assoc_freq, and formats an ip_addr string if wpa_sm_get_p2p_ip_addr returns 0 (the string is emptied if it does not fit). It calls wpas_p2p_group_started, calls wpas_p2p_store_persistent_group on wpa_s->p2pdev if the group is persistent, and calls wpas_notify_p2p_group_started. It returns no value.

functions.name: wpas_get_est_tpt
functions.prose_contract: Returns an estimated throughput (unsigned int, the same unit as rate*500) for a BSS, given its IE buffer, a legacy rate in 500 kbit/s units, an SNR, the frequency and a pointer max_cw (scan.c:2895-3144). It first lowers rate in steps according to the SNR (for example to 2 when rate > 2 and snr < 1, down to 54*2 when rate > 108 and snr < 21), and starts with est = rate * 500. It then looks up the hardware mode for freq with get_mode_with_freq; if that is NULL no table-based estimate is added and est is returned as is. With a hardware mode it raises est to the maximum of the table estimates whose conditions hold: HT20 when the HW has HT caps and the HT Capabilities IE is present; HT40 when the HW supports the HT channel width set and the HT Operation IE shows a secondary channel offset; VHT20, VHT40, VHT80 and VHT160 (each with +1) when the HW has VHT caps and the VHT Capabilities IE is present, and the VHT Operation IE marks the width and the HW supports 160; HE20, HE40, HE80, HE160 (with +2, or +3 when the HW and the peer both advertise EHT capabilities) when the HW supports HE infra mode; and EHT 320 on 6 GHz when the EHT capability bit is set. If the HW supports HE but the HE Capabilities IE is absent or shorter than 1 + IEEE80211_HE_CAPAB_MIN_LEN it returns the est reached so far (HT/VHT estimates included) at that point; if EHT is not in use it returns after the HE estimates (scan.c:3124-3125). *max_cw is read in the VHT and HE branches, so the caller must have initialised it. It is written, not as a running maximum in every branch: the HT20 branch sets CHAN_WIDTH_20 and the HT40, VHT40, VHT80 and VHT160 branches set their width unconditionally when taken, the VHT20 and HE20 steps set 20 only if it was CHAN_WIDTH_UNKNOWN, and the HE 40/80/160 and EHT 320 steps raise it only if it was unknown or smaller. If none of those branches is taken, *max_cw is left unchanged.

functions.name: wpas_mac_addr_rand_scan_set
functions.prose_contract: Takes wpa_s, a type bit mask, and addr and mask pointers. If type is not entirely contained in wpa_s->mac_addr_rand_supported (the test (supported & type) != type) it logs and returns -1 without changing any state (scan.c:3630-3635). Otherwise it calls wpas_mac_addr_rand_scan_clear(wpa_s, type), which clears the matching bits in mac_addr_rand_enable and frees and NULLs the stored buffer of each of MAC_ADDR_RAND_SCAN, MAC_ADDR_RAND_SCHED_SCAN and MAC_ADDR_RAND_PNO that is in type. If addr is non-NULL it then allocates 2*ETH_ALEN bytes and copies addr followed by mask (mask must be readable for ETH_ALEN bytes in that case); if the allocation fails it returns -1 after the clear, so the previous setting for those types is already gone. It then stores the buffer (NULL if addr was NULL) in mac_addr_scan, mac_addr_sched_scan or mac_addr_pno only when type is exactly one of those three values. For any other supported type combination it logs, frees the temporary buffer and returns -1 after the clear. On success it sets type in mac_addr_rand_enable and returns 0, including when addr is NULL (the enable bit is then set with a NULL buffer); the buffer is owned by wpa_s afterwards.

functions.name: sme_sae_auth
functions.prose_contract: Static function in sme.c (lines 1660-1906) that handles a received SAE authentication frame (auth_transaction, status_code, data/len, external flag, sender sa, and ie_offset pointer). It returns 0, 1, -1 or -2 as follows. For transaction 1 with status ANTI_CLOGGING_TOKEN_REQ in state SAE_COMMITTED (and the required current_bss/current_ssid or ext_auth_wpa_ssid present): it returns -1 if data is shorter than 2 bytes, if the group in the frame is not allowed (sae_group_allowed), if the token cannot be allocated, or (external with ext_ml_auth) if sme_external_ml_auth fails; otherwise it replaces wpa_s->sme.sae_token, re-sends the commit (sme_send_authentication, or the external commit) and returns 0. For transaction 1 with status FINITE_CYCLIC_GROUP_NOT_SUPPORTED in state SAE_COMMITTED it records the rejected group, advances the group index, returns -1 if sme_set_sae_group finds no further group, or the external ML check fails, else sends a new commit and returns 0. For transaction 1 with status UNKNOWN_PASSWORD_IDENTIFIER it logs an event and returns -1. For any other status other than SUCCESS, SAE_HASH_TO_ELEMENT or SAE_PK it logs WPA_EVENT_AUTH_REJECT and returns -2. For a commit (transaction 1) with an acceptable status: it returns -1 if the BSS/SSID context is missing, returns 0 and ignores the frame when the SAE state is not SAE_COMMITTED, returns -1 on a status/H2E mismatch, returns 0 when sae_parse_commit reports SAE_SILENTLY_DISCARD (reflection), and returns -1 when parsing fails, peer-rejected-group checks fail or sae_process_commit fails; on success it frees and clears sae_token, sends the confirm (sme_send_authentication, or the external confirm after the optional ML check) and returns 0. For transaction 2 it returns -1 if status is not SUCCESS, the state is not SAE_CONFIRMED, sae_check_confirm fails, or the external ML check fails; otherwise it sets SAE_ACCEPTED, clears temporary SAE data and the rejected-group list, reports success to the driver when external, and returns 1. Any other transaction number returns -1. *ie_offset is set by sae_parse_commit / sae_check_confirm and is also read by the external ML-auth calls.

functions.name: sme_send_authentication
functions.prose_contract: Static function in sme.c (lines 548-1220; the slice cut the head and the earlier name sme_associate was wrong) that starts SME authentication of wpa_s towards bss with network ssid; start selects the SAE step (non-zero builds an SAE commit, 0 builds a confirm). If bss is NULL it logs, calls wpas_connect_work_done and returns (sme.c:572-577). Otherwise it fills a wpa_driver_auth_params (MLO link data when applicable, auth algorithm, FT over-the-air parameters when the mobility domain and FT keys match) and builds wpa_s->sme.assoc_req_ie from: the RSN/WPA/OSEN/WPS information (when setting the WPA suites or copying the WPA IE fails, or a WPS element does not fit, it calls wpas_connect_work_done and returns at 713-714, 727-728 or 749-750), the FT mobility domain element (added only if 5 bytes fit; otherwise skipped silently, 811-823), MFP selection, P2P/FST/RRM IEs, extended capabilities (inserted by memmove at 896-905 with no check of remaining space), max-idle, the RSNXE override, HS20 and vendor/MBO elements (the HS20 and the buf-based ones are appended only if they fit). If the temporary wpa_ie was allocated it is freed on the path that reinserts it. For WPA_AUTH_ALG_SAE with skip_auth clear it builds the SAE commit or confirm; if that returns NULL it calls wpas_connection_failed and returns. For FILS it may build FILS authentication data, with several early exits to the no_fils label that continue without FILS. With CONFIG_P2P and fewer than two concurrent channels a frequency conflict that wpas_p2p_handle_frequency_conflicts cannot resolve causes wpas_connection_failed, wpa_supplicant_mark_disassoc, freeing resp, wpas_connect_work_done and return. If skip_auth is set (reassociation to the same BSS) it frees resp and calls sme_associate instead of authenticating. Otherwise it records auth_alg and calls wpa_drv_authenticate; on failure it reports connection failure, marks disassociation, frees resp, calls wpas_connect_work_done and returns; on success it arms the SME_AUTH_TIMEOUT timer and frees resp. Returns no value; the authentication data buffer resp is freed on the paths that reach the end of the function (the early return at 1044-1045 follows resp being NULL).

functions.name: wnm_scan_process
functions.prose_contract: Processes scan results for a pending BSS Transition Management request (wnm_sta.c:1174-1247). Takes wpa_s and a pre_scan_check flag and returns int. It returns 0 at once if wpa_s->wnm_dialog_token is 0. When pre_scan_check is false and wnm_cand_valid_until is initialised and earlier than scan_trigger_time, the stored candidate list is stale and it goes to the failure exit with status WNM_BSS_TM_REJECT_UNSPECIFIED. Otherwise it calls compare_scan_neighbor_results to pick a candidate bss (and a reject reason). When pre_scan_check is true it returns 0, sending nothing and not resetting BTM state, if there is no candidate, if the candidate's last_update is 10 seconds old or older, or (unless CONFIG_NO_ROAMING) if a current BSS exists, the candidate differs from it and wpa_supplicant_need_to_roam_within_ess returns non-zero; otherwise it continues. With no candidate it goes to the failure exit with status WNM_BSS_TM_REJECT_NO_SUITABLE_CANDIDATES. The failure exit sends a BSS Transition Management response with that status and the reason only if wpa_s->wnm_reply is set, calls wnm_btm_reset and returns 0. If a candidate exists it calls wnm_bss_tm_connect(wpa_s, bss, current_ssid, 1) and returns 1.

functions.name: wpas_verify_ssid_beacon
functions.prose_contract: Static eloop timeout callback (wpa_supplicant.c:932-988); eloop_ctx is the struct wpa_supplicant and timeout_ctx is unused. It returns without doing anything further if current_ssid or current_bss is NULL, if the configured SSID is non-empty and differs from the current BSS SSID, or if wpa_state is below WPA_4WAY_HANDSHAKE, bigtk_set is false or ssid_verified is already true. Otherwise it calls wpa_supplicant_update_scan_results for wpa_s->bssid and returns if that fails, then looks up the latest BSS for wpa_s->bssid and returns if none is found. If that BSS's tsf is greater than first_beacon_tsf it increments beacons_checked; if its Beacon SSID element then matches the current BSS SSID (length and bytes) it sets ssid_verified to true and returns without rescheduling. In the remaining cases (no newer beacon, or SSID mismatch) it re-arms the wpas_verify_ssid_beacon timeout after next_beacon_check seconds and increments next_beacon_check, but only when beacons_checked is below 16. beacons_checked rises only when a newer beacon is seen, so the number of timer re-arms is not bounded by 16. Returns no value.

functions.name: wpas_transition_disable
functions.prose_contract: Handles a Transition Disable notification (wpas_glue.c:1304-1373). It first logs the bitmap with wpa_msg, then returns if wpa_s->current_ssid is NULL. It then tests four flags independently, each also requiring runtime conditions. With CONFIG_SAE: TRANSITION_DISABLE_WPA3_PERSONAL when the current and configured key management are SAE and the network does not already have protected management frames required or still allows a TKIP group cipher; and TRANSITION_DISABLE_SAE_PK when the key management is SAE, (with CONFIG_SME) the SAE state is SAE_ACCEPTED with PK in use, and the SSID does not already have sae_pk set to SAE_PK_MODE_ONLY with PMF required and no TKIP. For TRANSITION_DISABLE_WPA3_ENTERPRISE it requires 802.1X key management on the connection and the SSID and again PMF not required or TKIP allowed. For TRANSITION_DISABLE_ENHANCED_OPEN it requires the connection key management to be OWE, the SSID to allow OWE and owe_only not yet set. A matching WPA3 case calls disable_wpa_wpa2, which removes the WPA protocol and the PSK key managements (PSK, FT-PSK, PSK-SHA256), adds the RSN protocol, removes the TKIP group cipher, adds CCMP only if no CCMP, GCMP, GCMP-256 or CCMP-256 group cipher remains, and sets ieee80211w to MGMT_FRAME_PROTECTION_REQUIRED; the SAE-PK case also sets sae_pk to SAE_PK_MODE_ONLY, and the Enhanced Open case sets owe_only to 1. If any of these changed the SSID and CONFIG_NO_CONFIG_WRITE is not defined and wpa_s->conf->update_config is set, it calls wpa_config_write; a failed write is only logged. The function returns no value.

functions.name: wpa_supplicant_eapol_cb
functions.prose_contract: Static EAPOL result callback in wpas_glue.c (lines 283-377); ctx is the struct wpa_supplicant, eapol the EAPOL state machine and result the supplicant result. It first logs the result string, then returns if wpas_wps_eapol_cb(wpa_s) returns a value greater than 0 (so the debug log has already happened, but nothing after it is done). Otherwise it sets eap_expected_failure to whether result is EAPOL_SUPP_RESULT_EXPECTED_FAILURE. For any result other than SUCCESS it sets eapol_failed and calls wpa_supplicant_req_auth_timeout with 2 seconds, or 0 seconds if eapol_failed was already set; for SUCCESS it clears eapol_failed and calls ieee802_1x_notify_create_actor with last_eapol_src. It then returns if the result is not SUCCESS, if the driver flag WPA_DRIVER_FLAGS_4WAY_HANDSHAKE_8021X is not set, or if the key management is not WPA IEEE 802.1X. Otherwise it fetches the PMK from the EAPOL state machine: for FT key management (CONFIG_IEEE80211R) it reads 2*PMK_LEN bytes and uses the second half as the PMK, without FT support it fails; for other key management it reads PMK_LEN (PMK_LEN_SUITE_B_192 for SHA-384 key management) bytes and, if that fails, retries with 16 bytes. If the key could not be read it returns. Otherwise it calls wpa_drv_set_key with KEY_FLAG_PMK (a failure is only logged), then calls wpa_supplicant_cancel_scan and wpa_supplicant_cancel_auth_timeout and sets the state to WPA_COMPLETED. Returns no value.

functions.name: tuklib_wrapf
functions.prose_contract: Printf-style wrapper (tuklib_mbstr_wrap.c:248-294; the name tuklib_wrap_vfprintf does not exist in the source, the real function is tuklib_wrapf, extern int, taking stream, opt, fmt and variable arguments). It formats the message into a temporary buffer: with HAVE_VASPRINTF it calls vasprintf and returns TUKLIB_WRAP_ERR_FORMAT if that returns -1 (no buffer to free); otherwise it mallocs a 128 KiB buffer, returns TUKLIB_WRAP_ERR_FORMAT if malloc fails, calls vsnprintf, and returns TUKLIB_WRAP_ERR_FORMAT after freeing the buffer when the result is <= 0 or >= buf_size - 1. On successful formatting it calls tuklib_wraps(stream, opt, buf), frees buf, and returns whatever tuklib_wraps returned (a TUKLIB_WRAP_* status). The temporary buffer is not returned to the caller. An empty formatted result (n == 0) is treated as a format error in the fixed-buffer variant only.

functions.name: block_decode
functions.prose_contract: Static decoder step for one xz Block (block_decoder.c:64-199) with coder_ptr a lzma_block_coder; it runs a state machine over coder->sequence with cases SEQ_CODE, SEQ_PADDING and SEQ_CHECK, falling through from one to the next. SEQ_CODE: limits the input and output offered to the next (raw) decoder by the remaining compressed/uncompressed limits, calls it, adds the consumed/produced byte counts to the running sizes, and if it returned LZMA_OK returns LZMA_DATA_ERROR when both sizes already equal the Block Header values, or compressed data is complete but the output buffer is not full, or output is complete but input remains. It updates the integrity check with new output unless ignore_check is set or no output was produced. A return other than LZMA_STREAM_END from the raw decoder is returned unchanged (LZMA_OK and any error). On LZMA_STREAM_END it returns LZMA_DATA_ERROR if either final size does not satisfy is_size_valid against the header value, otherwise stores both sizes into coder->block and moves on to SEQ_PADDING. SEQ_PADDING: consumes padding bytes until compressed_size is a multiple of 4, returning LZMA_OK if input runs out and LZMA_DATA_ERROR for a non-zero padding byte; then returns LZMA_STREAM_END immediately if the Block has no check (LZMA_CHECK_NONE), otherwise finishes the check calculation (unless ignore_check) and goes to SEQ_CHECK. SEQ_CHECK: copies the stored check bytes; returns LZMA_OK while incomplete; when complete it returns LZMA_DATA_ERROR only if the check is not ignored, is supported, and differs from the computed one; otherwise LZMA_STREAM_END (so an ignored or unsupported check is not verified). LZMA_PROG_ERROR is returned only after the switch, i.e. for an unknown sequence value.

functions.name: block_encode
functions.prose_contract: Static encoder step for one xz Block (block_encoder.c:47-135) with coder_ptr a lzma_block_coder. It first returns LZMA_DATA_ERROR if the remaining input (in_size - *in_pos) would make uncompressed_size exceed LZMA_VLI_MAX. It then runs a state machine on coder->sequence (SEQ_CODE, SEQ_PADDING, SEQ_CHECK, falling through in that order). SEQ_CODE: calls the next (filter) coder, then returns LZMA_DATA_ERROR if the output it just produced would push compressed_size past COMPRESSED_SIZE_MAX (this check happens after the filter coder already ran and advanced *in_pos/*out_pos), adds the output and input byte counts to compressed_size and uncompressed_size, updates the check with the consumed input if any, and returns the filter coder's result unchanged when it is not LZMA_STREAM_END or when action is LZMA_SYNC_FLUSH (so a filter coder's LZMA_PROG_ERROR or other errors also pass through, and in the SYNC_FLUSH case block->compressed_size and uncompressed_size are not written). Otherwise (LZMA_STREAM_END with another action) it writes the two sizes to coder->block and moves to SEQ_PADDING. SEQ_PADDING: writes zero bytes until compressed_size is a multiple of four, returning LZMA_OK if the output buffer fills first; if the Block check is LZMA_CHECK_NONE it then returns LZMA_STREAM_END (raw_check is not written in that case); otherwise it finishes the check and moves to SEQ_CHECK. SEQ_CHECK: copies check bytes to the output, returns LZMA_OK while incomplete, and when complete copies the check into block->raw_check and returns LZMA_STREAM_END. Any other sequence value gives LZMA_PROG_ERROR at line 134.

functions.name: lzma_code
functions.prose_contract: Public liblzma entry point (common.c:204-376; the packet slice cut the head). It first returns LZMA_PROG_ERROR if next_in is NULL with avail_in != 0, next_out is NULL with avail_out != 0, strm->internal or its next.code is NULL, action is above LZMA_ACTION_MAX, or the coder does not list the action in supported_actions (so an unsupported action gives LZMA_PROG_ERROR here, not an error from the coder). It then returns LZMA_OPTIONS_ERROR if any reserved pointer or int field is non-zero/non-NULL or a reserved enum differs from LZMA_RESERVED_ENUM. It switches on internal->sequence: in ISEQ_RUN a SYNC_FLUSH, FULL_FLUSH, FINISH or FULL_BARRIER action moves the sequence to the matching state; in the flush, finish and barrier states it returns LZMA_PROG_ERROR if the action differs from the one in force or internal->avail_in differs from strm->avail_in; ISEQ_END returns LZMA_STREAM_END at once; ISEQ_ERROR or an unknown value returns LZMA_PROG_ERROR. Otherwise it calls next.code with the stream buffers, then advances next_in/avail_in/total_in and next_out/avail_out/total_out by the amounts used (only when non-zero), and stores avail_in in internal->avail_in. It then adjusts the result: LZMA_OK with no input consumed and no output produced becomes LZMA_BUF_ERROR if allow_buf_error was already set, otherwise it sets allow_buf_error and stays LZMA_OK, and LZMA_OK with progress clears allow_buf_error; LZMA_TIMED_OUT becomes LZMA_OK; LZMA_SEEK_NEEDED is returned and resets ISEQ_FINISH to ISEQ_RUN; LZMA_STREAM_END sets the sequence to ISEQ_RUN after a SYNC_FLUSH, FULL_FLUSH or FULL_BARRIER and to ISEQ_END otherwise; LZMA_NO_CHECK, LZMA_UNSUPPORTED_CHECK, LZMA_GET_CHECK and LZMA_MEMLIMIT_ERROR are returned unchanged with allow_buf_error cleared (and for LZMA_STREAM_END the same clearing applies by fall-through); every other result sets ISEQ_ERROR and is returned. The returned value is therefore the coder's result except for the LZMA_OK / LZMA_TIMED_OUT transformations.

functions.name: file_info_decode
functions.prose_contract: Static decoder function in file_info.c (lines 247-666; the real name is file_info_decode, the earlier name file_info_decoder_decode does not exist) that reads an .xz file backwards to build a combined Index. The out, out_pos, out_size and action parameters are unused. It first trims in_size so that input beyond the end of the file (file_size - file_cur_pos) is ignored, then loops on coder->sequence through SEQ_MAGIC_BYTES, SEQ_PADDING_SEEK, SEQ_PADDING_DECODE, SEQ_FOOTER, SEQ_INDEX_INIT, SEQ_INDEX_DECODE, SEQ_HEADER_DECODE and SEQ_HEADER_COMPARE until it returns. It returns LZMA_OK when it needs more input, LZMA_FORMAT_ERROR (magic-byte stage), LZMA_DATA_ERROR for several malformed-file cases (for example a padding or footer problem, an Index size mismatch, or an Index whose total size plus the Stream Header size is larger than the remaining offset, file_info.c:516-517), LZMA_PROG_ERROR on internal failures (for instance the lzma_index_stream_flags or lzma_index_stream_padding calls failing, or an unknown sequence value), errors from the sub-decoders and from lzma_index_cat via return_if_error, and LZMA_SEEK_NEEDED when an external seek is required, which can happen both at the Index start (file_info.c:410-412) and at the reverse seeks in the padding/header stages (through reverse_seek). In SEQ_HEADER_COMPARE it compares header and footer flags, stores the flags and padding in this_index, concatenates the previous combined index, and if file_target_pos is 0 it hands the combined index to *dest_index (ownership leaves the coder), sets *in_pos = in_size and returns LZMA_STREAM_END; otherwise it continues backwards with the next Stream.

functions.name: lzma_index_iter_locate
functions.prose_contract: Public function (index.c:1248-1289; the packet slice held only the tail) that positions an iterator at the Block containing a given uncompressed offset. iter->internal[ITER_INDEX] supplies the lzma_index and target is the uncompressed offset. If the Index's uncompressed_size is less than or equal to target it returns true at once (target at or past the end of the data) and leaves the iterator unchanged. Otherwise it locates the Stream containing the target with index_tree_locate and subtracts the Stream's uncompressed_base from target, locates the Group containing it with index_tree_locate (both lookups are asserted to be non-NULL), and binary searches the group's records[0..group->last) for the first Record whose uncompressed_sum is greater than target. It stores the stream, group and that record index in iter->internal[ITER_STREAM], [ITER_GROUP] and [ITER_RECORD] (the record index can equal group->last if none qualifies), calls iter_set_info to fill the public iterator fields, and returns false. It allocates and frees nothing and takes no locks.

functions.name: stream_encoder_update
functions.prose_contract: Static update hook of the Stream encoder (stream_encoder.c:228-282) that replaces the filter chain; it takes the coder, an allocator, the new filters and the reversed filters. It first makes a deep copy of filters into a local array with lzma_filters_copy and returns that function's error immediately if the copy fails. If coder->sequence is at or before SEQ_BLOCK_INIT it clears block_encoder_is_initialized, points block_options.filters at the copy, calls block_encoder_init (restoring block_options.filters to coder->filters afterwards), and on success sets block_encoder_is_initialized to true. If the sequence is after SEQ_BLOCK_INIT but at or before SEQ_BLOCK_ENCODE it calls the Block encoder's update function with filters and reversed_filters (the original filters, not the copy). For any later sequence value it sets the result to LZMA_PROG_ERROR. If the chosen step failed it frees the copy with lzma_filters_free and returns the error code of that step, leaving coder->filters unchanged; in the first case the failed block_encoder_init has already cleared block_encoder_is_initialized, so the Block encoder is reported as not initialised even though it was initialised before the call. On success it frees the old coder->filters, copies the new array into coder->filters (taking over the copy's allocations) and returns LZMA_OK.

functions.name: lzma_stream_encoder_mt_memusage
functions.prose_contract: Public function (stream_encoder_mt.c:1231-1278; the packet slice held only its last lines) returning an estimated memory usage in bytes for a multi-threaded Stream encoder, taking an lzma_mt pointer. It calls get_options(options, ...) and returns UINT64_MAX if that does not return LZMA_OK. It then computes the input buffer size as options->threads * block_size and the per-thread filter usage with lzma_raw_encoder_memusage(filters), returning UINT64_MAX if that is UINT64_MAX, multiplies the latter by options->threads, and gets lzma_outq_memusage(outbuf_size_max, threads), returning UINT64_MAX if that is UINT64_MAX. The multiplications threads * block_size, filters_memusage * threads and threads * sizeof(worker_thread) are not checked for overflow here. It starts the total from LZMA_MEMUSAGE_BASE + sizeof(lzma_stream_coder) + threads * sizeof(worker_thread), and adds the input-buffer usage, then the filter usage, then the output-queue usage, each addition preceded by a check that returns UINT64_MAX if the sum would exceed UINT64_MAX. Otherwise it returns the sum. It allocates nothing and takes no locks.

functions.name: lzma_lz_decoder_init
functions.prose_contract: Initialises an LZ-based decoder in an lzma_next_coder (lz_decoder.c:218-325; the packet slice began at 257, mid-function). If next->coder is NULL it allocates the lzma_coder base structure, returning LZMA_MEM_ERROR on failure, installs lz_decode and lz_decoder_end, and sets an empty dictionary (NULL buffer, size 0). It calls lz_init(&coder->lz, allocator, filters[0].id, filters[0].options, &lz_options) and returns its error code unchanged if it fails (not necessarily LZMA_MEM_ERROR; the base structure allocated just before stays owned by next). It raises lz_options.dict_size to at least 4096, returns LZMA_MEM_ERROR if dict_size is larger than SIZE_MAX - 15 - 2 * LZ_DICT_REPEAT_MAX - LZ_DICT_EXTRA, rounds dict_size up to a multiple of 16, and computes alloc_size = dict_size + 2 * LZ_DICT_REPEAT_MAX. If coder->dict.size differs from alloc_size it frees the old dictionary buffer and allocates alloc_size + LZ_DICT_EXTRA bytes (returning LZMA_MEM_ERROR if that fails, with dict.buf then NULL and the old dict.size value still stored) and sets dict.size to alloc_size. It then calls lz_decoder_reset, copies the tail (at most dict_size bytes) of a non-empty preset dictionary into the buffer, advancing dict.pos by that size and setting dict.full to it, clears next_finished, this_finished and the temp buffer positions, and returns lzma_next_filter_init(&coder->next, allocator, filters + 1).

functions.name: lzma_simple_coder_init
functions.prose_contract: Public helper (simple_coder.c:235-291; the real name is lzma_simple_coder_init, not simple_coder_init) that sets up a "simple" (BCJ-style) filter coder in next. If next->coder is NULL it allocates an lzma_simple_coder plus 2 * unfiltered_max bytes of buffer, returning LZMA_MEM_ERROR on failure; it then installs simple_code, simple_coder_end and simple_coder_update, stores the filter callback and the allocated buffer size, and, when simple_size > 0, allocates the filter-specific state, returning LZMA_MEM_ERROR if that fails (the coder is already stored in next->coder, so it stays owned by next; coder->simple is the failed NULL), or sets coder->simple to NULL when simple_size is 0. If next->coder already existed none of this is redone and the filter callback is not replaced. Then if filters[0].options is non-NULL it sets coder->now_pos to its start_offset and returns LZMA_OPTIONS_ERROR if that offset has any bit set below alignment (the test uses alignment - 1 as a mask, so alignment must be a power of two); otherwise now_pos is 0. On success it sets is_encoder, clears end_was_reached, pos, filtered and size, and returns lzma_next_filter_init(&coder->next, allocator, filters + 1), whose result (LZMA_OK or an error) it returns unchanged.

functions.name: io_open_src_real
functions.prose_contract: Static function in xz's file_io.c (lines 514-755; the slice cut the head) that opens the source file of a file_pair; it returns false on success and true on error or when the file is skipped. For standard input (src_name == stdin_filename) it sets src_fd to STDIN_FILENO, reads the file status flags with fcntl (on failure it reports an error and returns true), tries to switch stdin to O_NONBLOCK (setting restore_stdin_flags when it succeeded), issues a posix_fadvise hint if available and returns false; it does not fill pair->src_st on this path. For a named file, follow_symlinks is true when opt_stdout, opt_force or opt_keep_original is set, and reg_files_only is true when opt_stdout is not set. It opens the file (with O_NOFOLLOW when symlinks are not to be followed, or an lstat check on systems without it); if the lstat reports a symlink it warns and returns true, and if open fails it reports a symlink warning for the ELOOP-style cases or an error message and returns true. After open it calls fstat (stat on DJGPP); a failure goes to error_msg (message, close, return true). A directory, or a non-regular file when reg_files_only is set, produces a warning and the error path. When reg_files_only is set and neither --force nor --keep is in effect (that is, output goes to disk and the input will be removed), setuid/setgid files, sticky-bit files and files with more than one hard link are skipped with a warning via the error path. A non-regular file (for example a FIFO) is waited on with io_wait; any result other than IO_WAIT_MORE goes to the error path. The error path closes src_fd and returns true; on success it returns false with src_fd open and src_st describing the file. Return paths that return true before open succeeded close nothing because nothing was opened.

functions.name: gss_adat
functions.prose_contract: FTP GSSAPI ADAT handler (gssapi.c:170-256) with app_data a struct gssapi_data, buf/len the received token. If ftp_do_gss_bindings is set it mallocs channel bindings built from his_addr and ctrl_addr (calling errx(1, ...) and exiting if malloc fails), otherwise it uses no bindings. It calls gss_accept_sec_context on d->context_hdl, storing the delegated credential in d->delegated_cred_handle, and frees the bindings it allocated. If an output token was produced it base64-encodes it; if base64_encode fails it replies 535 "Out of memory base64-encoding." and returns -1 immediately, at which point the output token is not released and client_name is not released. Otherwise the output token is released. On GSS_S_COMPLETE it stores client_name in d->client_name (the local copy is then cleared), replies 235 (with "ADAT=<base64>" when there is a token, else "ADAT Complete") and sets sec_complete = 1. On GSS_S_CONTINUE_NEEDED it replies 335 (with the ADAT or "OK, need more data"). For any other major status it logs the display_status string of min_stat to syslog and replies 431 "Security resource unavailable". On these three paths it releases a remaining client_name, frees the base64 string and returns 0. gss_release_buffer on the output token is done only after a successful base64_encode of a non-empty token (on a zero-length token it is not called).

functions.name: yyparse
functions.prose_contract: Bison-generated LALR parser for the FTP server command grammar (ftpcmd.c:1507-2969, one function that spans this slice and the later tail). It parses a command line from yylex and runs the grammar action for each reduced rule; the actions in this part of the file send reply codes, call helpers such as help, and release many of the lexer's heap strings with free. Not every action frees its strings: the HELP and SITE HELP actions (cases 32 and 41, ftpcmd.c:2102-2120 and 2196-2201) pass the string to help() and do not free it, and case 31 and 40 have no string. It returns 0 when the input is accepted (YYACCEPT, at ftpcmd.c:1717-1718, 2908-2909), 1 when it aborts (YYABORT: end of input while recovering from an error at 2840-2841, error-recovery stack popped to the bottom at 2897-2898, or a stack that is still full after growing at 1662-1663), and 2 after yyerror("memory exhausted") (stack exceeds its maximum or error-message allocation fails, via yyexhaustedlab). Syntax errors call yyerror and the parser tries to recover and continue before any of these returns. At yyreturn it discards a pending lookahead through yydestruct, pops and destroys the remaining stack symbols, frees the stack and the error message buffer if they were heap-allocated, and returns the result.

functions.name: yyparse
functions.prose_contract: Bison-generated parser for the FTP server grammar (ftpcmd.c:1507-2969; this slice holds its error-recovery and exit code). It takes no arguments, uses the global yychar, yynerrs and yylval, and its own stacks (the initial arrays yyssa/yyvsa, moved to the heap when they grow). It returns 0 on YYACCEPT (also taken from error recovery when the final state is reached, 2908-2909), 1 on YYABORT (end of input during error recovery at 2840-2841, or the state stack emptied while popping for the error token at 2897-2898; the abort at 1662-1663 when the stack is still full after growing returns 1 as well), and 2 after calling yyerror("memory exhausted") through yyexhaustedlab (reached when a stack-growth or error-message allocation cannot be satisfied, including the stack-size limit check at 1630-1644 and 2823-2824). On a syntax error it calls yyerror with either a verbose message or "syntax error", sets yyerrstatus to 3, discards the offending lookahead through yydestruct unless it is end of input, and pops states until one accepts the error token. At yyreturn (reached from accept, abort and exhausted) it discards a pending lookahead (unless it is YYEOF or YYEMPTY) with yydestruct, pops the rest of the stack calling yydestruct on each symbol (not the symbols of the rule whose action triggered the accept/abort), frees the stack if it moved off the initial array, frees the error message buffer if heap-allocated, and returns the result. Whether yydestruct frees semantic values was not read; grammar actions can have side effects such as replies and file operations.

functions.name: sec_prot
functions.prose_contract: FTP client "protect" command handler (security.c:694-740; the slice cut the head), with argc/argv as the command words (argc is assumed to be at least 1; argv[0] is used only for the usage message). If argc > 3 it goes straight to usage without reading argv[1..]. If argc == 1 it calls sec_status() and returns, leaving the global code unchanged. If sec_complete is false it prints "No security data exchange has taken place." sets code = -1 and returns. Otherwise it maps the last argument argv[argc-1] to a protection level with name_to_level; an unknown name goes to usage. If the mechanism's check_prot rejects the level it prints a message, sets code = -1 and returns. If argc == 2, or argv[1] is a case-insensitive prefix of "data" (strncasecmp with the length of argv[1]), it calls sec_prot_internal(level) and sets code = -1 and returns when that is negative; else if argv[1] is a prefix of "command" it calls set_command_prot(level) with the same failure handling; any other argv[1] goes to usage. On success it sets code = 0. The usage label prints "usage: <argv[0]> [command|data] [clear|safe|confidential|private]" and sets code = -1. With argc == 2 the only argument is read as the level and the data protection is changed.

functions.name: do_login
functions.prose_contract: Final stage of the login program (login.c:315-515): given a passwd entry pwd, the short tty name and the tty device path ttyn, it prepares the session and ends by calling exec_shell(pwd->pw_shell, rootlogin); it returns void, and whether exec_shell can return was not read. Steps: for a non-root user it calls checknologin(), which ends in exit(0) (login.c:292) when the nologin file exists and is shown. It then updates utmp via update_utmp, looks up the "tty" group, and chowns the tty to the user and chmods it; failure of chown, chmod, setlogin or initgroups only warns for root but ends in exit(1) for a non-root user. A non-root user also gets the limits file read. With HAVE_SETPCRED a setpcred failure only warns. do_osfc2_magic(pwd->pw_uid) returning non-zero ends in exit(1). setgid failure warns and exits with 1 for non-root; the setuid step is treated as failing (warn, exit(1) for non-root) when setuid(pwd->pw_uid) fails or when a non-root target uid can still setuid(0) afterwards (privilege drop failed). It resets all signals to SIG_DFL, then does the platform-specific shadow, UDB/limit and capability work (a missing UDB entry or a failing capability call ends in errx/err with status 1 where those build options are on). It then chdirs to the home directory; if that fails it prints a message and tries chdir("/"), calling exit(0) if that also fails, else logging in with home "/". It starts the Kerberos session when auth is KRB5, shows welcome/motd files, sets HOME, USER, LOGNAME and SHELL in the environment and calls exec_shell.

functions.name: kerberos5_reply
functions.prose_contract: Handles a Kerberos V5 telnet authentication reply (kerberos5.c:612-700). data/cnt is the reply: if cnt < 1 it returns at once with nothing printed or changed; otherwise the first byte is the reply type and the rest (cnt-1 bytes) its payload. The function returns void. KRB_REJECT: prints a refusal (including the payload as the reason when it is non-empty), calls auth_send_retry() and returns. KRB_ACCEPT: if the authenticator requests mutual authentication and the function-static mutual_complete is 0 it prints a "didn't provide mutual authentication" error, calls auth_send_retry() and returns without printing the acceptance line; otherwise it prints the acceptance (with the payload as the user name when present), obtains the key with krb5_auth_con_getlocalsubkey, falling back to krb5_auth_con_getkey; if both fail it prints the error and calls auth_send_retry(); otherwise it builds an SK_DES session key of length 8 from the key data, calls encrypt_session_key (its result is not examined), frees the keyblock, calls auth_finished(ap, AUTH_USER), and calls kerberos5_forward(ap) when forward_flags has OPTS_FORWARD_CREDS. KRB_RESPONSE: if the mutual-authentication mode is selected it calls krb5_rd_rep on the payload; on failure it prints an error and calls auth_send_retry(); on success it frees the reply and sets mutual_complete to 1; without mutual mode it does nothing. KRB_FORWARD_ACCEPT prints a message; KRB_FORWARD_REJECT prints a refusal that includes the payload; any other type prints "Unknown Kerberos option" only when auth_debug_mode is set. mutual_complete is changed only by a successful KRB_RESPONSE in mutual mode.

functions.name: rsaencpwd_is
functions.prose_contract: Handles a received RSA-encrypted-password authentication suboption on the server side (rsaencpwd.c:193-309, old K&R definition; ap is the Authenticator, data/cnt the suboption bytes, with cnt expected to be at least 1). The first byte selects the case. RSA_ENCPWD_AUTH: copies the remaining payload into auth.dat with auth.length = cnt-1 (without a size check), opens key_file; if that fails it sends RSA_ENCPWD_REJECT "Auth failed" and calls auth_finished(ap, AUTH_REJECT), then returns. Otherwise it reads the private key (a hex length then that many bytes, into a 160-byte buffer without checking the length) and closes the file; calls accept_rsa_encpwd with the global challenge and challenge_len, and on a negative result sends REJECT and calls auth_finished(ap, AUTH_REJECT); else it calls auth_encrypt_userpwd, and if rsaencpwd_passwdok(UserNameRequested, UserPassword) returns 0 it sends REJECT "Illegal password" and calls auth_finished(ap, AUTH_REJECT); if it returns non-zero it sends RSA_ENCPWD_ACCEPT and calls auth_finished(ap, AUTH_USER). IAC: only in one-way mode (AUTH_HOW_ONE_WAY) it sets the global challenge (the time in hex when the current time is even, else the string "randchal") and challenge_len, opens key_file (failure: send REJECT and call auth_finished(ap, AUTH_REJECT), then return), skips the private key, reads the public key, builds a DER-like challenge-plus-key buffer and sends RSA_ENCPWD_CHALLENGEKEY with it, without calling auth_finished. In two-way mode the IAC case does nothing. Any other first byte sends RSA_ENCPWD_REJECT without calling auth_finished. The function returns void.

functions.name: telnetsuspend
functions.prose_contract: Static telnet client command (commands.c:1243-1270) that suspends the client and always returns 1. When SIGTSTP is defined it calls setcommandmode(), then sets err to 1 if TerminalWindowSize returns 0 (window size not obtainable) and to 0 otherwise, sends SIGTSTP with kill(0, SIGTSTP) (to the whole process group, so the process stops until it is continued), and after it resumes calls TerminalWindowSize again; if that call returns non-zero, the connection is up (connected) and either err was set or the rows or columns differ from the values taken before the suspend, it calls sendnaws().
