It then scans backwards for the last '/' before the X block: if it finds one it temporarily terminates the path there and calls stat; a stat failure returns 0 with the path left truncated at the slash (the slash is not restored) and errno from stat, and a non-directory sets errno to ENOTDIR and returns 0, also leaving the path truncated; otherwise the slash is restored. In a loop it then tries the name: if doopen is non-NULL it opens with O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_RDWR|O_BINARY, mode 0600, storing the descriptor in *doopen, and returns 1 on success, or 0 for an open error other than EEXIST (a failed open leaves *doopen negative); if doopen is NULL it calls stat and returns 1 when stat fails with ENOENT and 0 when it fails with another error, and continues when the file exists. To get the next name it steps the suffix characters starting at the first replaced position: 'z' becomes 'a' with a carry, a digit becomes 'a', any other character is incremented; when the carry runs off the end of the string it returns 0 (with errno EEXIST left from the last open in the open case, and unchanged from before the call in the stat case, since a successful stat does not set errno).

functions.name: ecb_bitrev32
functions.prose_contract: Pure helper of libev's ecb.h portion in ev.c (lines 1045-1055) that returns x with its 32 bits in reverse order (bit i of the result is bit 31 - i of x). It swaps adjacent bits, then 2-bit pairs, nibbles, bytes and finally the two 16-bit halves, using the masks 0x55555555, 0x33333333, 0x0f0f0f0f and 0x00ff00ff and a final 16-bit rotation. It accepts any uint32_t value, reads and writes nothing but its argument and returns the result.

functions.name: ecb_popcount64
functions.prose_contract: Pure helper (ev.c:1059-1064) returning the number of set bits of a 64-bit value as an int. It computes it as ecb_popcount32 of the low 32 bits (the argument converted to uint32_t) plus ecb_popcount32 of the high 32 bits (x >> 32); ecb_popcount32 itself was not read. It accepts any uint64_t value and has no side effects.

functions.name: ecb_rotl8
functions.prose_contract: Inline helper (ev.c:1075) that rotates the 8-bit value x left by count bits: it returns (x >> (8 - count)) | (x << count), converted to uint8_t on return (x is promoted to int first). It gives the left rotation for count from 0 to 8 inclusive; for count greater than 8 the shift amount 8 - count is negative, which is undefined. It has no side effects.

functions.name: ecb_rotr8
functions.prose_contract: Inline helper (ev.c:1076) that rotates the 8-bit value x right by count bits: it returns (x << (8 - count)) | (x >> count), converted to uint8_t on return (x is promoted to int first). It gives the right rotation for count from 0 to 8 inclusive; for count greater than 8 the left shift amount is negative, which is undefined. It has no side effects.

functions.name: ecb_rotl16
functions.prose_contract: Inline helper (ev.c:1077) that rotates the 16-bit value x left by count bits: it returns (x >> (16 - count)) | (x << count), converted to uint16_t on return (x is promoted to int first, so shifting by 16 is defined when int is 32 bits wide). It gives the left rotation for count from 0 to 16 inclusive; for count greater than 16 the right shift amount is negative, which is undefined. It has no side effects.

functions.name: ecb_rotr16
functions.prose_contract: Inline helper (ev.c:1078) that rotates the 16-bit value x right by count bits: it returns (x << (16 - count)) | (x >> count), converted to uint16_t on return (x is promoted to int first). It gives the right rotation for count from 0 to 16 inclusive; for count greater than 16 the left shift amount is negative, which is undefined. It has no side effects.

functions.name: ecb_rotl32
functions.prose_contract: Inline helper (ev.c:1079) that rotates the uint32_t x left by count bits: it returns (x >> (32 - count)) | (x << count). It gives the correct left rotation for count from 1 to 31; with count 0 the right shift is by 32 and with count 32 the left shift is by 32, both undefined for a 32-bit unsigned operand, and larger counts make a shift amount negative or too large. It has no side effects.

functions.name: ecb_rotr32
functions.prose_contract: Inline helper (ev.c:1080) that rotates the uint32_t x right by count bits: it returns (x << (32 - count)) | (x >> count). It gives the correct right rotation for count from 1 to 31; counts 0 and 32 and larger make a shift by the full width or a negative amount, which is undefined. It has no side effects.

functions.name: ecb_rotl64
functions.prose_contract: Inline helper (ev.c:1081) that rotates the uint64_t x left by count bits: it returns (x >> (64 - count)) | (x << count). It gives the correct left rotation for count from 1 to 63; counts 0 and 64 and larger shift by the full width or by a negative amount, which is undefined. It has no side effects.

functions.name: ecb_rotr64
functions.prose_contract: Inline helper (ev.c:1082) that rotates the uint64_t x right by count bits: it returns (x << (64 - count)) | (x >> count). It gives the correct right rotation for count from 1 to 63; counts 0 and 64 and larger shift by the full width or by a negative amount, which is undefined. It has no side effects.

functions.name: ecb_bswap16
functions.prose_contract: Byte swap of a 16-bit value in ev.c (lines 1084-1118). With GCC or clang builtins it is a macro for __builtin_bswap16 (or for __builtin_bswap32(x) >> 16 on older compilers), with MSVC it is a macro around _byteswap_ushort, and otherwise (lines 1098-1103) it is an inline function ecb_bswap16(uint16_t x) that returns ecb_rotl16(x, 8). In every variant the result is x with its two bytes exchanged (high byte and low byte swapped); the macro forms evaluate their argument as a plain expression. It has no side effects.

functions.name: ecb_bswap32
functions.prose_contract: Byte swap of a 32-bit value in ev.c (lines 1084-1118). With GCC or clang it is a macro for __builtin_bswap32, with MSVC a macro around _byteswap_ulong, and otherwise (1105-1110) an inline function ecb_bswap32(uint32_t x) returning (((uint32_t)ecb_bswap16 (x)) << 16) | ecb_bswap16 (x >> 16). In each variant the result is x with its four bytes in reverse order. It has no side effects.

functions.name: ecb_bswap64
functions.prose_contract: Byte swap of a 64-bit value in ev.c (lines 1084-1118). With GCC or clang it is a macro for __builtin_bswap64, with MSVC a macro around _byteswap_uint64, and otherwise (1112-1117) an inline function ecb_bswap64(uint64_t x) returning (((uint64_t)ecb_bswap32 (x)) << 32) | ecb_bswap32 (x >> 32). In each variant the result is x with its eight bytes in reverse order. It has no side effects.

functions.name: ecb_big_endian
functions.prose_contract: Inline function (ev.c:1159-1160) returning an ecb_bool: true when ecb_byteorder_helper() equals 0x11223344. The helper returns that constant on targets recognised at compile time as big-endian (__BYTE_ORDER__ or a list of big-endian architecture macros), returns 0x44332211 on recognised little-endian targets, and otherwise builds a union of the bytes 0x11, 0x22, 0x33, 0x44 at run time and returns the 32-bit value read from it. So it is true exactly when the byte layout reads as 0x11223344, and false for little-endian and for a target that is neither. It has no side effects.

functions.name: ecb_little_endian
functions.prose_contract: Inline function (ev.c:1161-1162) returning an ecb_bool: true when ecb_byteorder_helper() equals 0x44332211, i.e. when a 32-bit value built from the bytes 0x11, 0x22, 0x33, 0x44 in memory order reads back as 0x44332211. The helper decides this at compile time on recognised little- and big-endian targets and otherwise by a run-time union read. It is false on big-endian targets and on any target that is neither. It has no side effects.

functions.name: ecb_binary16_to_binary32
functions.prose_contract: Pure function (ev.c:1197-1227) that converts the IEEE-754 half-precision bit pattern in the low 16 bits of x to the single-precision bit pattern of the same value (higher bits of x are ignored). It takes the sign bit, the 5-bit exponent and the 10-bit mantissa; an exponent of 31 (infinity or NaN) becomes exponent 255 with the mantissa kept, an exponent of 0 with a zero mantissa (zero) becomes exponent 0, an exponent of 0 with a non-zero mantissa (subnormal) is normalised by shifting the mantissa (using ecb_ld32, not read) and adjusting the exponent, and a normal exponent is rebiased by adding 127 - 15. It returns sign | (exponent << 23) | (mantissa << 13). It has no side effects.

functions.name: ecb_binary32_to_binary16
functions.prose_contract: Pure function (ev.c:1229-1291) that converts the single-precision bit pattern x to the nearest half-precision bit pattern (returned as uint16_t). It keeps the sign. If |x| is in 0x38800000..0x477fefff (normal half range) it rounds the mantissa to 10 bits with round-half-to-even (adding 0xfff plus the lowest kept bit), bumps the exponent if rounding carries, and returns sign | (exponent << 10) | mantissa. If |x| is above 0x477fefff and up to 0x7f800000 (infinity) it returns signed infinity (0x7c00). If |x| is below 0x38800000 it returns signed zero for an exact zero or for exponents too small (e < 14 - 24), and otherwise forms a half subnormal by shifting the mantissa with the implicit bit and round-half-to-even. For |x| above 0x7f800000 (NaN) it returns sign | 0x7c00 | (mantissa >> 13), forced non-zero so the result stays a NaN. It has no side effects.

functions.name: periodic_recalc
functions.prose_contract: Static function in libev (ev.c:3366-3388, only when EV_PERIODIC_ENABLE) that recomputes the next trigger time of periodic watcher w and stores it in ev_at(w); it returns nothing and uses the global current time ev_rt_now. It first computes interval as w->interval if that exceeds MIN_INTERVAL and MIN_INTERVAL otherwise, and a starting time at = offset + interval * floor((ev_rt_now - offset) / interval) (the comment says this usually errs on the low side). While at is less than or equal to ev_rt_now it computes nat = at + w->interval (the original interval, not the clamped one); if nat equals at (the addition no longer changes the value, which includes a zero interval and floating-point resolution limits) it sets at to ev_rt_now and stops; otherwise it sets at = nat and repeats. It then stores at in ev_at(w). The result is therefore a time greater than ev_rt_now when the loop advanced it, the initial value if that already exceeded ev_rt_now, or exactly ev_rt_now in the stalled-addition case. With a negative w->interval the loop moves at backwards and ends only when the addition stops changing at; no other memory is modified.

functions.name: CLeashApp::ProbeKDC
functions.prose_contract: Windows Leash method (Leash.cpp:982-1065) that checks whether a KDC answers by trying a login for a throw-away user; it returns a BOOL (TRUE or FALSE) and takes no arguments. If the function pointer pkrb5_init_context is NULL it returns FALSE at once. Otherwise it zeroes a creds structure and tries, in order, pkrb5_init_context, pkrb5_cc_default and pkrb5_cc_get_principal; if getting the principal from the default cache fails it falls back to parsing the principal "foo" with pkrb5_parse_name, and only if that also fails does it go to cleanup. Any failure of these steps (or of pkrb5_build_principal, which builds the probe principal PROBE_USERNAME in the realm of that principal) goes to cleanup and the function returns FALSE. It fills a 16-byte password with pkrb5_c_random_make_octets; if that fails it runs a refill loop whose counter is never incremented (the for statement has no increment, line 1026), so the function does not return in that case. It NUL-terminates the password and calls pkrb5_get_init_creds_password with the probe principal, no prompter, no options. The result TRUE is returned exactly when that call returns KRB5KDC_ERR_C_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN, KRB5KDC_ERR_CLIENT_REVOKED, KRB5KDC_ERR_CLIENT_NOTYET, KRB5KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_FAILED, KRB5KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_REQUIRED or KRB5KDC_ERR_PADATA_TYPE_NOSUPP (a KDC answered); success or any other error gives FALSE. After the early NULL-pointer return, every path reaches cleanup, which clears creds.client when it equals probeprinc, frees the credentials contents, frees the principals and closes the ccache and frees the context where they are non-NULL, and returns the result.

functions.name: CLeashView::OnTrayIcon
functions.prose_contract: Windows Leash handler (LeashView.cpp:1743-1810) for tray-icon notifications; lParam carries the mouse message and wParam is not used. For WM_LBUTTONDOWN it calls OnLeashRestore when CMainFrame::m_isMinimum is set and OnLeashMinimize otherwise. For WM_RBUTTONDOWN it allocates a CMenu, creates a popup menu and appends a "Close/Open MIT Kerberos Window" item (depending on m_isMinimum), a separator and "Get Tickets"; it then waits INFINITE on ticketinfo.lockObj and throws "Unable to lock ticketinfo" if the wait does not return WAIT_OBJECT_0 (for WAIT_ABANDONED the thread has been given the mutex and the throw leaves it held; in every throwing case the already created menu is not destroyed or deleted). With the mutex held it appends "Renew Tickets", grayed unless ticketinfo.Krb5.btickets is non-zero and CLeashApp::m_hKrb5DLL is set, computes a gray flag for the Destroy item from btickets but then releases the mutex and appends "Destroy Tickets" with plain MF_STRING (the computed flag is not used, so that item is never grayed here), appends "Change Password", a separator, "Automatic Ticket Renewal" and "Expiration Alarm" (checked according to m_autoRenewTickets and m_lowTicketAlarm), a separator and "Exit". It sets ID_LEASH_RESTORE as the default item, gets the cursor position, calls SetForegroundWindow, tracks the popup at the cursor (TPM_RIGHTALIGN | TPM_RIGHTBUTTON, owner the parent frame), posts WM_NULL, destroys the menu and deletes the CMenu. WM_MOUSEMOVE and any other lParam do nothing. It returns 0 on every path that does not throw.

functions.name: CLeashView::OnObtainTGTWithParam
functions.prose_contract: Windows Leash message handler (LeashView.cpp:2277-2323) that shows the "get ticket" dialog, optionally preset from a shared-memory block; wParam is unused and lParam is either 0 or a file-mapping handle. It fills an LSH_DLGINFO_EX with the size, DLGTYPE_PASSWD, use_defaults 1 and pointers to its in.title, in.username and in.realm buffers (the structure is not zeroed first, so those buffers keep whatever bytes they had unless set below). If lParam is non-zero it maps the object with MapViewOfFile (read/write, 4096 bytes). If the mapping succeeded it reads up to four consecutive NUL-terminated strings from it, in the order title, username, realm and ccache, copying each non-empty one with strcpy_s into the dialog structure; the pointer is advanced past each string with strlen, with no check that the strings fit inside the 4096 mapped bytes. If lParam is 0 or the mapping failed it sets only the title to "MIT Kerberos: Get Ticket". If the username and realm strings are both non-empty it ORs DLGFLAG_READONLYPRINC into ldi.dlgtype. It calls pLeash_kinit_dlg_ex(m_hWnd, &ldi) and keeps its result. It then calls UnmapViewOfFile on the param pointer, which has been advanced past the strings by then, so the view that MapViewOfFile returned is not the address that is passed (the mapping is not properly unmapped on the success path), closes the lParam handle if it was non-zero, sends WM_COMMAND with ID_UPDATE_DISPLAY to its own window and returns the dialog result.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Test-file runner of libecc's arithmetic tests (arithmetic_tests.c:883-1233; the packet called it an unnamed excerpt, the function is main). It initialises seven nn values and the generic fp/nn parameter pools (failure: error path, which returns -1). With WITH_ASSERT_BACKTRACE it installs a SIGINT handler (failure returns -1). With more than 2 arguments it returns -1; with the single argument "-info" it prints WORDSIZE and NN_MAX_BASE and returns 0. It mallocs the input buffer (NULL: return -1), opens the file named by argv[1] with open (the result is not checked) or uses standard input, and reads lines with read_string. For each line it parses the test number (asserted equal to the line counter), the operation name and the parameter type string, returning -1 directly if one of those three separators is missing. It then parses each record by its type letter: 'c' (a field context: a second 'c' in the same line, or a mismatch between the imported and the computed r, r_square, mpinv, p_shift or p_reciprocal, goes to err; a mismatch of the normalised p returns -1 directly), 'f' (needs a prior context, a limit of pre-allocated fp values), 'p' (a raw pointer record whose value must be 0, else err), 'n' (more than the pre-allocated number returns -1 directly), 'u' and 's' (decimal numbers), and any other letter goes to err. It records the type string, finds the test function for the operation in the dispatch table (an unknown operation is skipped with a message), calls it, adds 1 to oktests when it returns 1, and resets the counters for the next line. After the last line it prints the number of OK tests, total tests and NOK tests, closes the file if its descriptor is non-zero, frees the buffer and returns 0, so a run with failing tests still returns 0. The err label prints a message, closes the file if non-zero, frees the buffer and returns -1; the direct -1 returns above do not close the file or free the buffer.

functions.name: GENERIC_TEST(test_name, operation_, given_string_helper, fun_name, parameters_types_, parameters_io_, parameters_string_names, fun_output, nn_out_num, fp_out_num, ...)
functions.prose_contract: Macro (arithmetic_tests.c:496-627) that generates a test function int test_<test_name>(const char *op, void **params, int test_num) and registers it in the dispatch table with ADD_TO_DISPATCH_TABLE; the packet slice ended before the tail of the body. Generated function: it asserts that op equals the operation name string; returns -1 (after a message) if the global parameter-type string global_parameters differs from the declared parameter types; runs PARAMETERS_SANITY_CHECK, which returns 0 after a message when a type is not one of c, f, n, u, s, when an I/O letter is not i, o or O, when an 'O' parameter is not of type u or s, or when more than one 'O' output is declared. It then takes the common word length n_len from the first output parameter of type 'f' or 'n' and the field context from the first 'c' parameter, declares and initialises the nn and fp output temporaries with the GENERIC_TEST_NN/FP_DECL_INIT macros (a non-zero ret goes to err, which prints a message and calls exit(-1)), asserts that fp outputs are only used when a context exists, and calls the tested function with the given arguments through CHECK_FUN_<fun_output>. It then looks up the operation's printable name and, for each parameter marked 'o', compares the computed value with the expected input value (fp_cmp for 'f', nn_cmp for 'n', direct comparison for 'u' and 's') and compares the function's return value with the 'O' parameter; at the first mismatch or failed comparison it prints "result mismatch", dumps all values with PRINT_ALL and sets mismatch. It then uninitialises the temporaries and returns !mismatch (1 when every compared value matched, 0 otherwise).

functions.name: GENERIC_TEST(test_name, operation_, given_string_helper, fun_name, parameters_types_, parameters_io_, parameters_string_names, fun_output, nn_out_num, fp_out_num, ...)
functions.prose_contract: Macro (arithmetic_tests.c:496-627; GENERIC_TEST_NN and GENERIC_TEST_FP at 629-633 wrap it) that generates int test_<test_name>(const char *op, void **params, int test_num) and registers it in the dispatch table. In the generated function: assert(memcmp(operation, op, ...) == 0); return -1 after a message if global_parameters differs from the declared parameter types; PARAMETERS_SANITY_CHECK may return 0 (bad type letter, bad I/O letter, an 'O' parameter of a type other than u or s, or more than one 'O'); it derives n_len and the field context from the parameters, initialises the nn/fp temporaries (initialisation failure prints an error and calls exit(-1)), calls the function under test, and compares each 'o' parameter (fp_cmp, nn_cmp, or direct word/int comparison) and the 'O' return value against the expected values from the test file; at the first mismatch it prints "result mismatch" and a dump of the inputs, real and expected values and stops comparing. It clears the temporaries and returns 1 when everything matched and 0 on a mismatch.

functions.name: ECDH_helper
functions.prose_contract: Non-blocking ECDH step of libecc's example (curve_ecdh.c:81-228), called once for Alice and once for Bob; the shared state is the static buffers Alice_to_Bob and Bob_to_Alice and the static per-role private scalar and result (d_Alice/d_Bob, x_Alice/x_Bob). It returns -1 or a libecc error code after MUST_HAVE or EG checks when curve_name or role is NULL, the role is neither "Alice" nor "Bob" (an error message is printed for an unknown role), the curve name is too long (length including the NUL must be below 256), the curve parameters cannot be obtained or imported, or any later libecc call fails; these checks are performed by the code, not assumed by the caller. It initialises a projective point Q. If our public buffer is all zeros it generates a random private scalar d modulo the generator order, computes Q = d*G and exports it in affine form into our public buffer; otherwise it skips key generation. If the other party's buffer is still all zeros it returns 0 (nothing more to do yet). Then, if nn_check_initialized(d) returns non-zero, which the comment on lines 190-192 says means that the shared secret was already computed, it returns 1 without computing it. Otherwise it imports the peer's affine point, computes d * peer point, converts it to unique affine coordinates, prints "ECDH shared secret computed by <role>", initialises x and copies the first coordinate Q.X into it, prints x, sets the result to 1 and then (only on this fall-through path) uninitialises Q, x and d. Every early return and every error jumps to the err label, which skips that uninitialisation, so Q and the static d and x are not released on those paths.

functions.name: sha0
functions.prose_contract: Single-call SHA-0 helper of the libecc example (sha0.c:253-264). It declares a local sha0_context, calls sha0_init, then sha0_update with input and ilen, then sha0_final with output, and returns 0 on success. Each of sha0_init and sha0_update that returns non-zero makes it skip the remaining calls and return that code; the return value of sha0_final is returned as is. On success output holds the SHA-0 digest (SHA0_DIGEST_SIZE bytes) of the ilen bytes at input; on failure the contents of output are not specified by this function. It has no other side effects and keeps nothing beyond the call (the context is local).

functions.name: shake256_final
functions.prose_contract: Finishes a SHAKE256 hash in libecc (shake256.c:41-54, compiled only when WITH_HASH_SHAKE256 is defined). First SHAKE256_HASH_CHECK_INITIALIZED(ctx, ret, err) checks the context (a NULL or not-initialised context, i.e. one whose magic is not SHAKE256_HASH_MAGIC, jumps to err with a non-zero ret, leaving the context and output untouched). Then it calls _shake_finalize on the context with output, which is where the digest (SHAKE256_DIGEST_SIZE bytes) is produced, and keeps its return value. After that call it sets ctx->magic to 0 unconditionally, whether _shake_finalize succeeded or not, so the context cannot be used again without a new shake256_init. It returns 0 on success or the error code of the check or of _shake_finalize; what output holds after a failure of _shake_finalize is determined by that function, not by this one.

functions.name: _ecgdsa_verify_finalize
functions.prose_contract: Finishes an EC-GDSA signature verification in libecc (ecgdsa.c:500-613; the real name is _ecgdsa_verify_finalize). It first calls sig_verify_check_initialized(ctx) and ECGDSA_VERIFY_CHECK_INITIALIZED on the EC-GDSA data; a failing check jumps to the cleanup with that error. It zeroes the two local points, takes the generator G, public key Y, order q and the stored signature values r and s from the context, runs hash_mapping_callbacks_sanity_check, and finalises the hash with the hash function's finalize callback into e_buf. It converts the digest to an integer e (truncating by a right shift when the digest has more bits than q), zeroes e_buf, reduces e modulo q, and computes rinv = r^-1 mod q, u = rinv * e mod q, uG = u*G, v = rinv * s mod q, vY = v*Y, W' = uG + vY, converts W' to affine coordinates and sets r' = W'.x mod q. It compares r with r' using nn_cmp and returns 0 when they are equal and -1 when they differ. Any failing internal step (the hash finalisation, local_memset, nn_init_from_buf, the shift, nn_mod, nn_modinv, nn_mod_mul, prj_pt_mul, prj_pt_add, prj_pt_unique or the comparison itself) goes to the cleanup and its error code is returned. At the err label every path, success or failure, uninitialises e, r_prime, rinv, uv, uG and vY and, when ctx is non-NULL, zeroes the whole ctx->verify_data.ecgdsa structure (including its magic), so the verification context cannot be reused without a new initialisation; the local pointers are then nullified.

functions.name: _eckcdsa_verify_finalize
functions.prose_contract: Finishes an EC-KCDSA signature verification in libecc (eckcdsa.c:692-830; the real name is _eckcdsa_verify_finalize). It checks that the context is initialised (sig_verify_check_initialized and ECKCDSA_VERIFY_CHECK_INITIALIZED; a failure jumps to the cleanup with that error), zeroes the two local points, and takes G, Y, q, the signature part r (a byte string of length r_len derived from the digest size and the bit length of q) and s from the context. After the hash callbacks sanity check it finalises the message hash into hzm, drops the leading bytes beyond r_len (buf_lshift, with shift = hsize - r_len when hsize exceeds r_len; MUST_HAVE(hsize <= sizeof(hzm))), XORs the first r_len bytes with r, converts them to the integer tmp, zeroes hzm and sets e = tmp mod q. It computes sY = s*Y, eG = e*G and W' = sY + eG, converts W' to affine coordinates, exports its x coordinate into tmp_buf as p_len bytes, hashes that with a fresh hash context (init, update, finalize into r_prime), zeroes tmp_buf and the hash context, shifts r_prime the same way and compares its first r_len bytes with r using are_equal. It returns 0 when they are equal and -1 when they differ. Any failing internal helper (hash callbacks, hash steps, buf_lshift, the nn and point operations, fp_export_to_buf, local_memset, are_equal) goes to the cleanup and its error code is returned. At err, for every path, it uninitialises sY, eG, e and tmp and, when ctx is non-NULL, zeroes ctx->verify_data.eckcdsa (so the context is unusable without reinitialisation), and nullifies or zeroes the local pointers and scalars; the arrays hzm, tmp_buf and r_prime on the stack are cleared only on the success path (lines 764, 778, 785-786).

functions.name: _ecrdsa_verify_finalize
functions.prose_contract: Finishes an EC-RDSA signature verification in libecc (ecrdsa.c:498-615; the real name is _ecrdsa_verify_finalize). It checks that the context is initialised (sig_verify_check_initialized and ECRDSA_VERIFY_CHECK_INITIALIZED; failure jumps to the cleanup with the error), zeroes the points uG and vY, takes G, Y, q, r and s from the context, zeroes h_buf for hsize bytes, runs the hash callbacks sanity check and finalises the message hash into h_buf. Unless USE_ISO14888_3_ECRDSA is defined it reverses the byte order of h_buf. It converts the digest to an integer h, zeroes h_buf, reduces h modulo q, replaces a zero value by 1 (nn_inc), and computes e = h^-1 mod q, u = e*s mod q and v = -(e*r) mod q. It computes uG = u*G, vY = v*Y and W' = uG + vY, converts W' to affine coordinates, sets r' = W'.x mod q and compares r with r' using nn_cmp, returning 0 when they are equal and -1 when they differ. Any failing internal step goes to the cleanup and its (negative) error code is returned. For every path through the err label it uninitialises h, r_prime, e, v, u, vY and uG and, when ctx is non-NULL, zeroes ctx->verify_data.ecrdsa including its magic, so the context cannot be finalised again; an error before the hash finalisation step leaves the hash unfinalised, and h_buf is cleared only after the hash was converted to h.

functions.name: _eddsa_sign_finalize_pre_hash
functions.prose_contract: Finishes a pre-hashed EdDSA signature (Ed25519ph or Ed448ph) in libecc (eddsa.c:1224-1551; the real name is _eddsa_sign_finalize_pre_hash and the packet name eddsa_sign_ph does not occur in the file). It checks that ctx is initialised and that sig is non-NULL (sig_sign_check_initialized, EDDSA_SIGN_CHECK_INITIALIZED, MUST_HAVE), clears its local buffers and points, and requires that the private and public key types match and that the hash mapping is the one for that key type. It computes the half-signature lengths r_len and s_len from the digest size and requires siglen == EDDSA_SIGLEN(hsize) == r_len + s_len; only key types EDDSA25519PH (pre-hash size hsize) and EDDSA448PH (pre-hash size 64) are accepted (any other key type fails MUST_HAVE). After the hash callbacks sanity check it finalises the message hash held in ctx into ph_hash (an error before this step leaves the hash unfinalised), derives the key hash from the private key (its size must equal hsize), restarts the hash with the domain separation prefix (dom2 or dom4 with the context data, pre-hash flag 1), feeds the second half of the key hash and the pre-hash (requiring use_message_pre_hash_hsize <= hsize), finalises it and decodes the result as the scalar r. It then multiplies the generator by r to get R (using random blinding of the scalar when compiled in, and an extra 1/4 factor for Ed448), converts R from the short Weierstrass to the Edwards form and encodes it into sig[0..r_len-1]. It then hashes dom2/dom4, the encoded R, the encoded public key and the pre-hash, finalises it, decodes and reduces the result as S, computes the secret scalar s from the key hash, forms S = (S*s + r) mod q (with blinding steps when compiled in) and encodes it into sig[r_len..siglen-1], requiring s_len <= siglen - r_len. It returns the status of the last step, 0 on success. On any failure it returns the failing step's error code and sig may be partly written. At the err label, on every path, it nullifies the local pointers, zeroes the scalars, uninitialises the points, curve and big numbers, zeroes ctx->sign_data.eddsa when ctx is non-NULL (so the signing context is unusable afterwards) and clears ph_hash.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Command dispatcher of libecc's ec_utils tool (ec_utils.c:1592-1878). If argc < 2 it sets ret to -1, calls print_help(argv[0]) and returns. Otherwise it compares argv[1] (with are_str_equal; a negative error code from that call or from local_strlen is returned as is through EG) with the sub-commands, running every matching one in turn: gen_keys (argc must be 5; calls generate_and_export_key_pair with argv[2..4]; failure prints "gen_key error"), sign (argc 8 or 9; with 9 arguments argv[8] is taken as ancillary data whose length must be at most 0xffff, enforced by MUST_HAVE with no message; calls sign_bin_file; failure prints "sign error"), verify (argc 8 or 9, same ancillary data rule; calls verify_bin_file and prints "Signature check of <file> OK" or "failed"), struct_sign (argc 10 or 11; sign_bin_file with the metadata header type and version), struct_verify (argc 7 or 8; verify_bin_file without a separate signature file) and scalar_mult (argc 6; ec_scalar_mult). A wrong argument count prints "Bad args number" together with the argument list for that sub-command and returns -1 through the err label. If no sub-command matched it prints "Bad first argument" and the help text and returns -1. On success of the matched sub-command it returns 0. The return value of a failing sub-command is -1 (the callee's error code is not passed on). The function allocates nothing of its own.

functions.name: sshpam_respond
functions.prose_contract: Keyboard-interactive response handler of OpenSSH's PAM module (auth-pam.c:984-1025); ctx is the struct pam_ctxt, num the number of responses and resp the response strings. It switches on ctxt->pam_done: a value of 1 sets sshpam_authenticated to 1 and returns 0 without sending anything; any value other than 0 or 1 returns -1; with 0 it continues. If num is not exactly 1 it logs an error and returns -1. It creates a buffer (fatal if allocation fails). If the authentication context is valid and either the user's uid is not 0 or options.permit_root_login is PERMIT_YES it puts the response *resp into the buffer; otherwise (invalid user, or uid 0 without PERMIT_YES) it puts a fake password derived from *resp (fake_password) into it, freeing the fake string afterwards. A failure to add to the buffer is fatal. It then sends the buffer as a PAM_AUTHTOK message on ctxt->pam_psock with ssh_msg_send; a send failure frees the buffer and returns -1, otherwise it frees the buffer and returns 1. The num check applies only when pam_done is 0.

functions.name: userauth_finish
functions.prose_contract: Finishes one SSH user-authentication attempt in OpenSSH's server (auth2.c:360-464) and replies to the client; ssh carries the Authctxt, authenticated is the result of the method, packet_method its name and submethod an optional sub-method. If authenticated is non-zero it calls fatal() for an invalid user, for an attempt marked postponed, or for an unknown method name, and then uses the configured method name. If the user is root and auth_root_allowed denies that method, authenticated is set to 0 (with an audit event when SSH_AUDIT_EVENTS is built). If authenticated is still set and options.num_auth_methods is non-zero, auth2_update_methods_lists decides whether more methods are required; if so authenticated becomes 0 and partial becomes 1. It logs the attempt with auth_log and, when authenticated or partial, updates the session info. If authctxt->postponed is set it returns here without sending anything. With USE_PAM and an authenticated attempt it runs the PAM account check (mm_do_pam_account), sends any login message as a banner and waits for the packet to be written, and calls fatal() with "Access denied ... by PAM account configuration" if the check failed. If authenticated is exactly 1 it stops dispatching further userauth requests, sends SSH2_MSG_USERAUTH_SUCCESS, sets authctxt->success and the log preamble (a send error is fatal). Otherwise it increments authctxt->failures only when the attempt is not partial, not a server-caused failure and not the first attempt with method "none"; if failures reach options.max_authtries it calls auth_maxtries_exceeded(ssh); then it sends SSH2_MSG_USERAUTH_FAILURE with the list of methods that may continue and the partial flag (a send error is fatal). The function returns nothing.

functions.name: channel_post_connecting
functions.prose_contract: Post-select handler (channels.c:2034-2104) for channels of type SSH_CHANNEL_CONNECTING and SSH_CHANNEL_RDYNAMIC_FINISH. It returns at once, leaving the channel unchanged, if SSH_CHAN_IO_SOCK_W is not set in c->io_ready, and calls fatal_f if the channel has no remote id. It reads the pending socket error with getsockopt(SO_ERROR) (a getsockopt failure sets err to errno and logs). If err is 0 it frees the connect context, sets the type to SSH_CHANNEL_OPEN, updates the used time and, unless the channel was an RDYNAMIC_FINISH one, sends SSH2_MSG_CHANNEL_OPEN_CONFIRMATION with the remote id, own id, local window and maximum packet size (a send error is fatal), then returns. If err is EINTR, EAGAIN or EINPROGRESS it returns without changing anything. Otherwise it logs the failure and calls connect_next on the connect context for the next address. If that returns -1 (no addresses left) it logs, frees the connect context and, for an RDYNAMIC_FINISH channel, calls rdynamic_close, or else sends SSH2_MSG_CHANNEL_OPEN_FAILURE with the remote id, SSH2_OPEN_CONNECT_FAILED and the strerror text (fatal on send error) and calls chan_mark_dead. In every case that reaches the end (a new socket or none) it then closes the old c->sock and sets c->sock, c->rfd and c->wfd to the value connect_next returned, which is -1 when the addresses were exhausted, and to the new socket otherwise.

functions.name: channel_input_data
functions.prose_contract: Handler for an SSH2_MSG_CHANNEL_DATA packet (channels.c:3402-3468); it returns 0 in every path it returns from (errors are signalled by disconnect or fatal calls). It finds the channel from the channel id in the packet (channel_from_packet_id disconnects for an unknown id, not read). For a mux-proxy channel it forwards the packet upstream and returns. If the channel type is not SSH_CHANNEL_OPEN, RDYNAMIC_OPEN, RDYNAMIC_FINISH or X11_OPEN it returns without reading the rest of the packet. It reads the data as a direct string and requires the end of the packet (failure is fatal), and sets win_len to the data length plus 4 for datagram channels. If the output state is not CHAN_OUTPUT_OPEN it only reduces local_window by win_len and increases local_consumed by it, discarding the data, and returns. If win_len exceeds local_maxpacket it logs "rcvd big packet" and returns with no window accounting and no append. If win_len exceeds local_window it adds the excess to local_window_exceeded, logs, sets local_window to 0, and calls ssh_packet_disconnect if the accumulated excess is more than local_window_max / 10; otherwise it reduces local_window by win_len and resets local_window_exceeded to 0. In both of these last cases (when it did not disconnect) it appends the data to c->output, as a length-prefixed string for datagram channels, and an append failure is fatal.

functions.name: cipher_init
functions.prose_contract: Creates and initialises a cipher context for OpenSSH (cipher.c:245-332). It sets *ccp to NULL and callocs a struct sshcipher_ctx (SSH_ERR_ALLOC_FAIL if that fails). It records whether the cipher is "none" and the direction, and returns SSH_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT if keylen is less than the cipher's key length or if iv is non-NULL and ivlen is less than the cipher's IV length. For chacha20-poly1305 it creates the chachapoly context from the key (a NULL result gives SSH_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT); for the "none" cipher it succeeds with nothing further. Without OpenSSL, an AES-CTR cipher gets the key and IV set up directly (the iv pointer is passed to aesctr_ivsetup without a NULL check) and any other cipher gives SSH_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT. With OpenSSL it allocates an EVP context (SSH_ERR_ALLOC_FAIL on failure), initialises it with the cipher type and the iv pointer (which may be NULL here, but the AEAD branch below passes iv to EVP_CIPHER_CTX_ctrl with no NULL test), sets the GCM fixed IV for ciphers with an authentication length, adjusts the key length if it differs from the EVP default (EVP_CIPHER_CTX_set_key_length), and sets the key; each OpenSSL failure gives SSH_ERR_LIBCRYPTO_ERROR. On success (ret 0) it stores the context in *ccp for the caller to free with cipher_free; on any failure it frees the EVP context and zeroes and frees the partial context, leaving *ccp NULL.

functions.name: kex_assemble_names
functions.prose_contract: Builds the final algorithm list from the user's configured string (kex-names.c:242-336). Arguments: listp (the user's list, replaced by the result), the default list def and the list of all supported names all. It returns SSH_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT if listp, def or all is NULL, leaving *listp unchanged. If *listp is NULL or the empty string it sets *listp to a strdup of def and returns 0 (SSH_ERR_ALLOC_FAIL if strdup fails, in which case *listp has already been overwritten with NULL; an original non-NULL empty string is not freed). Otherwise it takes ownership of the old string and sets *listp to NULL. A leading '-' removes the named algorithms from def: *listp is set to match_filter_denylist(def, list + 1) (which may be an empty string), the old string is freed and it returns 0, or SSH_ERR_ALLOC_FAIL if that returns NULL. A leading '+' appends the user's names to def and a leading '^' prepends them (kex_names_cat; allocation failure SSH_ERR_ALLOC_FAIL); a list without a prefix is used as it is. For a '+', '^' or plain list it then splits a copy on commas; any pattern starting with '!' gives SSH_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT; each other pattern is matched against all with match_filter_allowlist and the matches are concatenated in order into the result. An empty result gives SSH_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT; otherwise *listp is set to the new string (caller frees) and it returns 0. After the initial argument check, every failure leaves *listp NULL, frees the original list, the working copies and the partial result, and returns SSH_ERR_ALLOC_FAIL or SSH_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT as stated above.

functions.name: kex_assemble_names
functions.prose_contract: This slice (kex-names.c:252-336) is the tail of kex_assemble_names (242-336); no function called kex_names_pick exists in the file. kex_assemble_names takes listp (the user's list, replaced by the result), def and all. It returns SSH_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT for a NULL argument, sets *listp to a copy of def (0, or SSH_ERR_ALLOC_FAIL) when *listp is NULL or empty, and otherwise takes ownership of the old list and sets *listp to NULL. A leading '-' returns match_filter_denylist(def, list + 1) (freeing the old list; SSH_ERR_ALLOC_FAIL on NULL); a leading '+' joins def and the user's names with def first, a leading '^' joins them with the user's names first (kex_names_cat; allocation failure SSH_ERR_ALLOC_FAIL), and a plain list is used as is. For these three cases the tail shown here splits a copy of the list on commas: a pattern beginning with '!' gives SSH_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT; every other pattern is matched against all with match_filter_allowlist and the matches are concatenated, so the '+' and '^' lists are also filtered through all. An empty result gives SSH_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT; otherwise *listp is set to the result (caller frees) and 0 is returned. On every failure after the initial argument check *listp is NULL and the original string, copies and partial result are freed.

functions.name: kex_exchange_identification
functions.prose_contract: Exchanges the SSH protocol identification strings (kex.c:1234-1437; the slice cut the head). Our version buffer is ssh->kex->server_version for a server and client_version for a client, and the peer's is the other one; both are kept in the kex structure. It resets our buffer, treats an empty version_addendum as NULL, and formats "SSH-2.0-<version>[ <addendum>]\r\n" into it (a buffer error is returned with errno saved). It writes the whole banner to the connection output (a short write gives SSH_ERR_SYSTEM_ERROR), trims the trailing CRLF from our buffer, and duplicates it as a string (SSH_ERR_ALLOC_FAIL on failure). It then reads the peer's lines. For each line, one byte at a time with an optional wait before each read when timeout_ms > 0 (a timeout sends an error message to the peer and returns SSH_ERR_CONN_TIMEOUT; another wait error gives SSH_ERR_SYSTEM_ERROR), a read failure with EPIPE gives SSH_ERR_CONN_CLOSED and other read failures SSH_ERR_SYSTEM_ERROR. CR sets a flag that the next character must be LF; a NUL, a character after CR other than LF, or a line longer than SSH_MAX_BANNER_LEN goes to the invalid-format exit; characters are stored in the peer's version buffer. A line of more than 4 characters starting with "SSH-" ends the loop; for another line, a server treats it as invalid, and a client discards it and reads the next, giving up after SSH_MAX_PRE_BANNER_LINES lines with an error message to the peer and SSH_ERR_INVALID_FORMAT. It duplicates the peer string (fatal_f on failure), allocates a buffer for the remote version text, and parses "SSH-%d.%d-%[^\n]"; a parse failure sends "Invalid SSH identification string." and returns SSH_ERR_INVALID_FORMAT. It calls compat_banner on the remote version, accepts major version 2 (and 1 only with minor 99), otherwise sends "Protocol major versions differ." and returns SSH_ERR_NO_PROTOCOL_VERSION. A server also returns SSH_ERR_CONN_CLOSED, after logging, when the compat flags mark the peer as a probe (SSH_BUG_PROBE) or scanner (SSH_BUG_SCANNER). On success it returns 0. In all cases the temporary strings are freed, and errno is restored when the result is SSH_ERR_SYSTEM_ERROR.

functions.name: kex_ext_info_check_ver
functions.prose_contract: Static helper in kex.c (lines 410-424) that checks the version string of an SSH2_MSG_EXT_INFO extension. It returns SSH_ERR_INVALID_FORMAT (after logging an error) if memchr finds a NUL byte within the first len bytes of val, leaving kex->flags unchanged. Otherwise it logs the value, compares val with want_ver using strcmp, and if they are equal sets the bit flag in kex->flags, else only logs that the extension version is unsupported; in both of those cases it returns 0. The strcmp reads val up to a terminating NUL, so val must be NUL-terminated (at val[len] or earlier, with no NUL before len, as checked). It allocates and frees nothing.

functions.name: libcrux_sha3_generic_keccak_absorb_full_9d_f8
functions.prose_contract: Generated (Eurydice/KaRaMeL) function for SHA-3 with rate 136 and one lane (libcrux_mlkem768_sha3.h:4588-4633) that absorbs all complete 136-byte blocks of the input slice inputs[0] into the Keccak state and returns the number of trailing input bytes that were not absorbed. It first calls fill_buffer_9d_b0(self, inputs), which, when self->buf_len > 0 and buf_len + input_len >= 136, copies 136 - buf_len input bytes into self->buf, sets buf_len to 136 and returns that count (otherwise it returns 0 and changes nothing). If that count is greater than 0 it loads self->buf as a block, runs keccakf1600 and sets buf_len to 0. With buf_len equal to 136 on entry the count is 0, so the buffered block is not flushed and buf_len stays 136. It then absorbs from the input, starting after the bytes already consumed, every full 136-byte block (load_block then keccakf1600 for each) and returns remainder = (input length - consumed) mod 136, which is between 0 and 135. It does not copy the remainder anywhere; self->buf_len is 0 after a flushed buffered block and unchanged otherwise.

functions.name: libcrux_sha3_generic_keccak_absorb_9d_7b
functions.prose_contract: Generated function (libcrux_mlkem768_sha3.h:4658-4682) for SHA-3 with rate 136 and one lane that absorbs a slice into a KeccakXofState and buffers any incomplete tail; it returns nothing and reports no error. It calls absorb_full_9d_f8(self, inputs), which first completes and permutes a buffered block when buf_len > 0 and enough input is present (setting buf_len to 0) and then absorbs every full 136-byte block of the remaining input, and returns the number of remaining tail bytes. If that remainder is greater than 0 it copies the last remainder bytes of inputs[0] into self->buf at offset buf_len through buf_len + remainder and increases buf_len by the remainder; with a remainder of 0 buf_len is left as absorb_full left it (0 after a flushed buffered block, otherwise unchanged). The copy assumes buf_len + remainder <= 136, which holds for buf_len below 136; with buf_len equal to 136 on entry the slice bounds are exceeded.

functions.name: mm_answer_pwnamallow
functions.prose_contract: Privileged monitor's answer to the unprivileged child's getpwnam request (monitor.c:840-933). It calls fatal_f if authctxt->attempt was already non-zero (a second request), reads the user name as a cstring into authctxt->user (parse failure is fatal), and calls getpwnamallow(ssh, user). It sets the process title to "<user> [priv]" (or "unknown" when there is no entry) and clears the message buffer. If there is no allowed entry (pwent NULL) it puts a single byte 0 into the reply, sets authctxt->pw to fakepw() and leaves authctxt->valid unset; otherwise it sets authctxt->pw to the entry, valid to 1, and puts a byte 1, the uid and gid (and pw_change and pw_expire when the platform has them) and the strings name, "*", gecos and class (when present), dir and shell into the reply; any buffer error is fatal. It then sets the log preamble. If options.refuse_connection is set it logs "administratively prohibited connection" and calls cleanup_exit(EXIT_CONFIG_REFUSED), which ends the process. It appends the server options with mm_encode_server_options, calls auth2_setup_methods_lists (a failure is only logged at debug level), sends MONITOR_ANS_PWNAM with the reply, permits the monitor requests MONITOR_REQ_AUTHSERV and MONITOR_REQ_AUTH2_READ_BANNER (and MONITOR_REQ_PAM_START when USE_PAM and options.use_pam are set), and returns 0. MONITOR_REQ_PWNAM is not re-permitted here (it was entered with MON_ONCE).

functions.name: mm_key_allowed
functions.prose_contract: Monitor wrapper in the unprivileged sshd process (monitor_wrap.c:498-540; the real name is mm_key_allowed, with type, user, host, key, pubkey_auth_attempt and authoptp parameters) that asks the privileged monitor whether a key is allowed. If authoptp is non-NULL it first sets *authoptp to NULL. It builds a request buffer with the key type, the user (or "" for NULL), the host (or ""), the key (sshkey_puts) and the pubkey_auth_attempt flag; any buffer error is fatal. It sends MONITOR_REQ_KEYALLOWED to pmonitor->m_recvfd and waits for MONITOR_ANS_KEYALLOWED (the receive helper checks the message type, not read), then reads a 32-bit allowed value from the answer. If allowed is non-zero and type is MM_USERKEY it also deserialises the key options with sshauthopt_deserialise; a parse or deserialise failure is fatal. It frees the buffer. If authoptp is non-NULL it stores the deserialised options in *authoptp (owned by the caller), otherwise they are freed. It returns the allowed value received from the monitor; *authoptp stays NULL when the key is refused or the type is not MM_USERKEY.

functions.name: chan_send_eof2
functions.prose_contract: Static function in nchan.c (lines 183-204) that sends SSH2_MSG_CHANNEL_EOF for channel c. It logs a debug message and switches on c->istate. If the input state is CHAN_INPUT_WAIT_DRAIN it calls fatal_f when c->have_remote_id is not set, otherwise it builds and sends the packet carrying c->remote_id (a packet-building or sending error is fatal) and sets CHAN_EOF_SENT in c->flags. For any other input state it only logs "cannot send eof for istate" with an error message and changes nothing and sends nothing. It returns nothing.

functions.name: chan_send_close2
functions.prose_contract: Static function in nchan.c (lines 206-229) that sends SSH2_MSG_CHANNEL_CLOSE for channel c. If c->ostate is not CHAN_OUTPUT_CLOSED or c->istate is not CHAN_INPUT_CLOSED it only logs an error ("cannot send close for istate/ostate") and sends nothing. Otherwise, if CHAN_CLOSE_SENT is already set in c->flags it only logs "already sent close". In the remaining case it calls fatal_f if c->have_remote_id is not set (so the remote-id check applies only on this sending path), otherwise builds and sends the packet carrying c->remote_id (a packet error is fatal) and sets CHAN_CLOSE_SENT in c->flags. It returns nothing.

functions.name: process_config_line_depth
functions.prose_contract: Parses one ssh client configuration line (readconf.c:1135-2542; the real name of the function that contains this slice is process_config_line_depth, which process_config_line at 1125 wraps). This slice is a stretch of its big switch over the keyword opcode. The function returns 0 for an empty, blank or comment line and for a successfully parsed directive, and -1 (ret keeps its initial value) after logging an error for a missing argument, bad quoting, an unsupported or invalid value, an unimplemented opcode, extra trailing arguments, or other keyword-specific errors; some keywords instead call fatal. Keywords are lower-cased and looked up with parse_token; the rest of the line is split with argv_split and each case consumes its arguments with argv_next. For most options the value is stored only when *activep is true and the option is still unset (-1 or NULL), so the first value wins; IdentityFile and CertificateFile instead append to arrays when active (up to SSH_MAX_IDENTITY_FILES / SSH_MAX_CERTIFICATE_FILES, else an error); StreamLocalBindMask stores its value unconditionally, whenever it is parsed correctly (octal 0 to 0777), and not only when active and unset. Cases read in this part include time, flag, multistate and string options (via the shared parse_time, parse_flag, parse_multistate and parse_string labels), the key-file options and the known-hosts file arrays. After the switch, leftover arguments give the "extra arguments at end of line" error, otherwise ret is 0. At the out label it frees the canonical-name list, the string array and the split argument vector in every exit that reaches it.

functions.name: process_config_line_depth
functions.prose_contract: Same function as the other record (readconf.c:1135-2542), whose slice here is a later stretch of the switch. It returns 0 for an empty line, comment line or keyword-only line and for a successfully parsed directive; -1 (the initial ret) when a case jumps to out after logging an error (missing argument, bad quotes, bad or unsupported value, extra trailing arguments, unimplemented opcode, Host/Match/Include on the command line); for Include it passes on a non-zero return value; and some keywords (for example a missing channel timeout, PermitRemoteOpen, SetEnv or CanonicalDomains value, or an invalid argument for certain options) call fatal and do not return. activep NULL means a command-line directive, treated as always active, and depth is the Include nesting depth passed on to nested reads (read_config_file_depth, which itself calls fatal beyond depth 16). Most options are set only when active and still unset; the SendEnv and identity or certificate file lists append; StreamLocalBindMask stores its value unconditionally (readconf.c:2307). Host and Match can change *activep. On every exit that goes through the out label it frees the canonical-name list, the string array and the split argument vector.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Entry point of the regress netcat (netcat.c:149-519); the function never returns, it ends with exit(). It ignores SIGPIPE and parses options with getopt; invalid options or combinations end through usage(1), errx(1, ...) or err(1, ...): no host or port, a single argument without -l (for non-unix families), -l together with -s, -p or -z, -k without -l, proxy (-x) with UDP, listen, unix sockets, IPv6 or -s, a bad number, and failure of mktemp for the temporary unix datagram socket. In listen mode it sets ret to 0; for AF_UNIX it binds or listens once, and for other families it calls local_listen on every loop iteration (a negative result ends with err(1, "local_listen")). With UDP and -k it calls readwrite(s); with UDP and no -k it peeks the first datagram with recvfrom, connects to its sender, optionally reports the connection and runs readwrite(s) (recvfrom and connect failures are fatal); for TCP it accepts one connection (failure is fatal), reports it with -v, runs readwrite on it and closes it. After each iteration it closes the listening socket for non-unix families (for AF_UNIX UDP it disconnects with connect(s, NULL, 0)) and, unless -k was given, stops. In AF_UNIX client mode it sets ret to 0, calls unix_connect and, if the socket is positive and -z is not given, runs readwrite and closes it; otherwise ret is 1 (with -z and a connected socket the descriptor is not closed); with -u it unlinks the temporary socket path and exits with ret directly. In the TCP/UDP client mode it builds the port list and for each port closes the previous socket if non-zero, connects directly or through socks_connect when a proxy is set, and skips ports that failed; for a successful connection it sets ret to 0, with -v or -z it runs the UDP test (a failed udptest sets ret to 1 and continues with the next port) and prints "Connection to ... succeeded!", and then runs fdpass (-F) or, unless -z, readwrite. After the loop it closes s if non-zero and calls exit(ret); ret keeps the value set by the last port that connected (or the earlier value if later connects failed), and the initial value 1 is used if no port connected.

functions.name: fuzz_next
functions.prose_contract: Advances OpenSSH's test fuzzer to its next variant (fuzz.c:283-378); it returns nothing and works on struct fuzz (seed, slen, fuzzed, strategies bitmask, current strategy, offsets o1 and o2). If fuzz->strategy is 0 or fuzz_strategy_done reports the current strategy finished, it callocs fuzz->fuzzed (slen bytes) when it is NULL and then selects the lowest strategy bit still set in fuzz->strategies as the new strategy, clears that bit and resets o1 and o2 to 0; if no strategy bit is left it returns at once, leaving the old strategy and offsets unchanged (so after the last strategy finished the old strategy stays selected and no new variant is produced). It then asserts that fuzz->fuzzed is non-NULL (an allocation failure ends there) and, depending on the strategy, copies the seed into fuzz->fuzzed and modifies it: FUZZ_1_BIT_FLIP flips bit o1 and increments o1; FUZZ_2_BIT_FLIP flips bits o1 and o2, increments o1 and, when o1 reaches slen*8, resets it to 0 and increments o2; FUZZ_1_BYTE_FLIP inverts byte o1 and increments o1; FUZZ_2_BYTE_FLIP inverts bytes o1 and o2 and advances o1 then o2 like the bit case; FUZZ_TRUNCATE_START and FUZZ_TRUNCATE_END copy the seed unchanged and increment o1 (the truncation itself is applied by fuzz_len and fuzz_ptr); FUZZ_BASE64 replaces byte o1 with the base64 character at index o2 and advances o2, then o1 when o2 wraps. The offsets are checked with asserts. An unknown strategy value calls abort() (also in fuzz_strategy_done).

functions.name: brace_expand
functions.prose_contract: Expands the shell-style brace alternatives of an scp source pattern (scp.c:953-1016, using find_brace, emit_expansion and brace_expand_one at 788-950). It sets *patternsp to NULL and *npatternsp to 0, strdups the pattern into a worklist array "active" (return -1 if strdup or the append fails). While the worklist is not empty it pops the last entry and calls brace_expand_one on it, which looks for a brace group with find_brace and, if one is found, emits one new string per comma-separated alternative into the worklist through emit_expansion. A return of -1 from brace_expand_one (an allocation failure, or an empty or INT_MAX-or-longer pattern rejected by emit_expansion at 847-848) frees the popped string and ends with -1. If the pattern is syntactically invalid (unbalanced braces or brackets) it calls fatal_f and does not return. If the entry was expanded it is freed and the loop continues with the new entries. Otherwise it keeps only the part of the string after its last '/' (the whole string when there is no '/'), appends a copy to the "done" array (a failed append frees the entry and ends with -1) and frees the entry. At the end it hands the done array and its length to the caller (*patternsp, *npatternsp), which must free the strings and the array, and returns 0. On every exit the remaining worklist entries, the worklist and any done array not handed over are freed, so on failure *patternsp is NULL and *npatternsp 0 (a string passed to a failing append inside emit_expansion is freed there).

functions.name: match_cfg_line
functions.prose_contract: Evaluates the criteria of a Match line of sshd_config (servconf.c:1049-1271); acp and avp are the argument cursor over the tokens after "Match", full_line and line serve diagnostics, and ci is NULL for a syntax check or describes the connection under test. It starts with result 1 and counts attributes. For each token it duplicates the string. A token starting with '#' consumes all remaining arguments and ends the loop. The criterion "all" returns -1 after the error "'all' cannot be combined with other Match attributes" when it is not the first attribute or is followed by an argument that is non-empty and does not start with '#'; otherwise (also when followed by a '#' comment, which consumes the rest) it ends the loop with result 1. "invalid-user" sets result to 0 when ci is NULL or the user is not invalid. The criteria user, group, host, address, localaddress, localport, rdomain and version take their argument either from an attached "name=value" form or from the next token; a missing, empty or '#' argument gives the error "Missing Match criteria" and -1. In syntax-check mode (ci NULL) or in test mode when the needed field is absent, user, group, host, rdomain and localport set result to 0; address and localaddress first check the argument with addr_match_list(NULL, arg) and call fatal() if it is invalid, then set result 0; a connection field that is NULL outside test mode calls match_test_missing_fatal, which does not return. Otherwise user is matched with match_usergroup_pattern_list, group with match_cfg_line_group (-1 returns -1, 0 sets result 0), host with match_hostname, address and localaddress with addr_match_list (a result of -2 returns -1; 0 or -1 set result 0), localport by comparing the parsed port (an invalid port returns -1), rdomain with match_pattern_list and version against SSH_RELEASE. An unsupported attribute gives an error and -1. A mismatch only sets result to 0; the loop goes on to check the remaining attributes. After the loop, with no attributes at all it returns -1 ("One or more attributes required for Match"); otherwise it returns result, 1 only when every attribute matched. The duplicated attribute string is freed at out and at the end of each fully handled iteration, but the continue paths and the early return -1 for a comment-only line skip the free, leaking that copy.

functions.name: wait_until_can_do_something
functions.prose_contract: Static function of sshd's server loop (serverloop.c:144-252) that waits with ppoll until the connection or a channel is ready. It sets *conn_in_readyp and *conn_out_readyp to 0, initialises a timeout, calls channel_prepare_poll (which sets up the poll array and *npfd_activep, so the active count need not be set on entry), and calls fatal_f if *npfd_activep is then less than 2. It adds deadlines to the timeout: the rekey timeout when rekeying is configured and not in progress, the unused-connection expiry (recomputed while channels are open or when it is 0, with the static unused_connection_expiry), the client-alive interval (starting last_client_time when it is 0), and 100 ms when a child has terminated and little data is waiting to be written. It sets entry 0 of the poll array to connection_in for reading and entry 1 to connection_out, polling for writing only when the packet layer has data to write, and calls ppoll with sigsetp. If ppoll returns -1 it clears the revents of all active entries and, for any errno except EINTR, calls fatal_f; on EINTR it returns with both ready flags 0. Otherwise it sets the two ready flags to whether revents of entries 0 and 1 are non-zero and re-reads the monotonic time. When client-alive probing is scheduled, a ppoll timeout (ret 0) with the interval elapsed calls client_alive_check(ssh) (which sends the probe and decides whether the client is considered dead; its body, including the client_alive_count_max test, was not read) and resets last_client_time, while activity on the input descriptor resets last_client_time. If the unused-connection expiry is set, has passed and no channel is still open it logs "terminating inactive connection" and calls cleanup_exit(255). The function returns nothing.

functions.name: sftp_download
functions.prose_contract: Downloads one remote file with SFTP (sftp-client.c:1596-1888) and returns 0 on success or -1 on failure; protocol errors detected while reading replies (unexpected message types, unknown request ids, oversized data) end in fatal and do not return. If attributes a are NULL it first calls sftp_stat on remote_path (failure: return -1). It derives the local mode from the permission attribute (0666 when absent), returns -1 if the permission attribute says the file is not a regular file, takes the size from the size attribute (0 when absent), opens the remote file with send_open (failure: -1) and the local file for writing, creating it and truncating it unless resume_flag or inplace_flag is set. A local open failure, a fstat failure when resuming, or a local file larger than the remote one when resuming closes the remote handle, frees it, closes the local descriptor if open and returns -1. When resuming it starts at the existing local size. It then runs a pipelined read loop: it queues read requests up to max_req outstanding, reads each reply and handles SSH2_FXP_STATUS (any status other than EOF sets read_error; either way no more requests are queued) and SSH2_FXP_DATA (written at the request's offset with lseek and atomicio; a write failure records write_errno and stops further requests; otherwise it updates maxack and the contiguous highwater mark; short reads are re-requested). An interrupt stops the queueing. After the loop it sets highwater to maxack when there was no read error, write error or interrupt. If inplace_flag, read_error, write_error or interrupted is set it truncates the local file to highwater (the highest contiguous acknowledged offset). With a read error it closes the remote handle and fails; with a write error it prints the error, closes the remote handle and fails; otherwise it closes the remote handle (a failed sftp_close or an interrupt makes the status SSH2_FX_FAILURE), applies the mode and the access and modification times when preserve_flag is set (failures only logged) and calls fsync when fsync_flag is set and the file was modified. It closes the local descriptor, frees the buffer and the handle and returns 0 only when the final status is SSH2_FX_OK, so every failure status, including SSH2_FX_FAILURE, is returned as -1.

functions.name: srclimit_penalise
functions.prose_contract: Records a penalty against a client address in sshd's per-source penalty tables (srclimit.c:345-460); it returns nothing. It returns without changing anything when penalties are disabled (penalty_cfg.enabled false), when penalty_exempt is set and the address cannot be converted to text or matches the exempt list, when the penalty type is SRCLIMIT_PENALTY_NONE, when the masked address cannot be computed, or when the table for that address family is full and the overflow mode is DENY_ALL (it logs "penalty table full" and returns). An unknown penalty type calls fatal_f. Otherwise it picks the penalty seconds and reason from the type (crash, authfail, noauth, refuseconnection, grace exceeded), masks the address with the IPv4 or IPv6 mask length, and calls expire_penalties(now) before the full-table test, so expired entries may be removed even on the paths that then return. It allocates a new penalty with the masked address, expiry now plus the seconds and the reason. If no entry for that address exists, it inserts the new one in the by-address tree, marks it active when its seconds exceed penalty_min, inserts it in the by-expiry tree (a failure is fatal), logs it, increments the family's count and, when the count exceeds max_sources, calls srclimit_early_expire_penalties (permissive mode), then returns. If an entry already exists, it removes that entry from the by-expiry tree (a mismatch is fatal), adds the new seconds to its expiry, caps the remaining time at penalty_max, activates it if the remaining time exceeds penalty_min and it was inactive, replaces its reason, frees the new penalty and reinserts the existing one in the by-expiry tree (a failure is fatal).

functions.name: sshsk_load_resident
functions.prose_contract: Loads the resident (discoverable) security-key credentials from an SK provider (ssh-sk.c:801-892; the real function name is sshsk_load_resident, with provider_path, device, pin, and the output pointers srksp and nsrksp; the code is inside ENABLE_SK). If srksp or nsrksp is NULL it returns SSH_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT before writing anything; otherwise it sets *srksp to NULL and *nsrksp to 0. It builds the provider options from device with make_options (failure: that error), opens the provider with sshsk_open (failure: SSH_ERR_INVALID_FORMAT) and calls the provider's sk_load_resident_keys with the pin; a non-zero return is logged and converted with skerr_to_ssherr. It then walks the returned credentials and skips any whose application does not start with "ssh:" or whose algorithm is neither SSH_SK_ECDSA nor SSH_SK_ED25519. For each kept credential it sets flags to user-presence-required and resident-key (adding user-verification-required when the credential has it), builds a key with sshsk_key_from_response (failure: that error), allocates a resident-key structure that takes the key, allocates and copies the user id and appends the structure to a grown array (recallocarray); an allocation failure returns SSH_ERR_ALLOC_FAIL. On success it stores the array in *srksp and its length in *nsrksp (NULL and 0 when no credential qualified) and returns 0. Every exit after the arguments check goes through the cleanup that frees the options, the provider handle, the provider's credential list, the pending key, the pending structure and the partly built array, so on failure *srksp stays NULL and *nsrksp 0 (set at the start). The caller frees the result with sshsk_free_resident_keys.

functions.name: sshbuf_load_fd
functions.prose_contract: Reads a whole open descriptor into a new buffer (sshbuf-io.c:33-78); fd must be open for reading and blobp must be a writable pointer slot. It sets *blobp to NULL first. If fstat fails it returns SSH_ERR_SYSTEM_ERROR. When the descriptor is not a socket, character device or pipe and its reported size exceeds SSHBUF_SIZE_MAX it returns SSH_ERR_INVALID_FORMAT. It allocates the buffer with sshbuf_new (failure: SSH_ERR_ALLOC_FAIL) and loops reading 4096-byte chunks with atomicio until a read returns 0: if errno is EPIPE at that point the loop ends normally, otherwise the result is SSH_ERR_SYSTEM_ERROR. Each chunk is appended with sshbuf_put (its error is returned) and the loop returns SSH_ERR_INVALID_FORMAT as soon as the buffer length exceeds SSHBUF_SIZE_MAX. After the loop, for a descriptor that is not a socket, character device or pipe, a reported size different from the number of bytes read gives SSH_ERR_FILE_CHANGED. On success it stores the buffer in *blobp and returns 0. On every failure after the buffer was allocated the buffer is freed, *blobp stays NULL, and the stack chunk is zeroed at the out label, which both the failure paths after the allocation and the success path reach; the two early returns before the allocation skip it. A read that ends at end-of-file normally relies on errno not being EPIPE; this was not checked against atomicio's implementation.

functions.name: check_host_key
functions.prose_contract: Decides whether an SSH server host key is acceptable (sshconnect.c:966-1476; this slice 1334-1588 holds the end of this function and all of verify_host_key, which is the caller that passes RDRW and clobber_port 0). Returns 0 when the key is accepted and -1 when it is rejected; it also calls fatal in some cases and may recurse into itself. It returns 0 at once, after clearing UpdateHostkeys, when no_host_authentication_for_localhost is 1, the peer is local and no host_key_alias is set. A hostname containing special characters forces read-only mode; known-hosts files (user, system, and the optional hostfile command unless clobber_port) are loaded for the host and, when the key is not a certificate and check_host_ip is still set, for the IP address. For a key not allowed by HostkeyAlgorithms it goes to fail. The result of check_key_in_hostkeys on the host decides the case. HOST_OK accepts the key (a certificate is also checked with sshkey_cert_check_host and goes to fail if invalid), may disable UpdateHostkeys, may add a new IP entry to the user file and marks the key as trusted. HOST_NEW first retries once without the port (a nested call with ROQUIET) when a non-default port is used; if that accepts, it stops with the key accepted. Otherwise a read-only mode or a certificate goes to fail, strict checking set to yes fails, strict checking set to ask prompts the user and fails when the answer is not yes, and the key is then added to the user known-hosts file (an add failure is only logged). HOST_REVOKED fails under strict checking and otherwise continues into the unsafe path. HOST_CHANGED fails for certificates, for ROQUIET mode, and under strict checking; otherwise it falls into the unsafe path. The unsafe path disables password and keyboard-interactive authentication, agent, X11, port and tunnel forwarding and UpdateHostkeys, and calls fatal when ExitOnForwardFailure is set and any of those was cancelled. HOST_FOUND calls fatal. After the switch a check_host_ip mismatch (IP entry changed but host entry not) prompts under strict ask, fails under strict yes and only warns when strict checking is off. If the key was not trusted, UpdateHostkeys is disabled. The success path frees the strings and key lists and returns 0. The fail label, for a certificate whose status was not revoked, creates the plain key, drops the certificate and jumps back to retry with it; otherwise it frees everything and returns -1.

functions.name: load_identity_file
functions.prose_contract: Loads an identity's private key for client authentication (sshconnect2.c:1521-1598; the real name is load_identity_file, a static function taking an Identity). It returns NULL, logging "no such identity" at info or debug3 level, when stat of the identity file fails. Otherwise it loops over attempts i from 0 to options.number_of_password_prompts: attempt 0 uses an empty passphrase, later attempts read one from the user with read_passphrase and end the loop when that passphrase is empty. Each attempt calls sshkey_load_private_type. Success continues; a wrong-passphrase error sets quit in batch mode and otherwise just tries again; a system error with errno ENOENT sets quit, and any other error (including a system error with another errno) is logged and sets quit. If a key was loaded that is an authenticator-hosted key while options.sk_provider is NULL, the key is freed, the result is NULL and quit is set. When quit is not set it runs sshkey_check_rsa_length against options.required_rsa_size and on failure frees the key, sets the result to NULL and sets quit. If quit is not set, a key is present, the identity has no agent descriptor and is not an already-loaded private key, it calls maybe_add_key_to_agent. A typed passphrase is zeroed and freed (not the empty literal) and the comment is freed on each attempt; the loop ends when a key is loaded or quit is set. The function returns the loaded key (owned by the caller) or NULL when it fails, is refused, or runs out of attempts.

functions.name: ssh_keysign
functions.prose_contract: Asks the external ssh-keysign helper to sign data for host-based authentication (sshconnect2.c:2011-2125; static function with ssh, key, sigp, lenp, data and datalen; the key argument is not used in the body I read). It sets *sigp to NULL and *lenp to 0 and returns -1 (logging the error) if _PATH_SSH_KEY_SIGN does not exist, fflush(stdout) fails, either pipe() fails or fork() fails; a failure of the second pipe or of fork leaves the already created pipe descriptors open (no closes on those paths). After a successful fork it installs SIG_DFL for SIGCHLD and keeps the old handler. The child side closes the unused pipe ends, dup2's the pipes onto stdout and stdin and the connection socket onto descriptor 3, closes higher descriptors and calls execl on the helper; a dup2 or exec failure calls fatal in the child, so the child never returns from this function. The parent closes its unused pipe ends, allocates a buffer (failure is fatal), puts the socket number (as 3) and the data, sends the request with ssh_msg_send (failure is fatal), reads the reply with ssh_msg_recv, closes both remaining descriptors, and on no reply logs and goes to fail without waiting for the child. Otherwise it waits for the child with waitpid (an error other than EINTR goes to fail), fails when the child did not exit normally or exited with a non-zero status, reads a version byte (failure goes to fail), fails if that byte is not 2, and reads the signature string into *sigp and *lenp (a parse failure goes to fail). At fail it restores the old SIGCHLD handler, frees the buffer and returns -1; on success it restores the handler, frees the buffer and returns 0 with a newly allocated signature the caller must free. The state of *sigp after a failed string read was not checked.

functions.name: process_gssapi_token
functions.prose_contract: Static function of the SSH client's GSSAPI authentication (sshconnect2.c:820-885) that processes one token received from the server and returns an OM_uint32 GSS status. It reads the Gssctxt from ssh->authctxt->methoddata and calls ssh_gssapi_init_ctx with options.gss_deleg_creds and recv_tok, which yields a status, an output token and context flags. If the output token has length greater than zero it sends one packet, SSH2_MSG_USERAUTH_GSSAPI_ERRTOK when GSS_ERROR(status) is true and SSH2_MSG_USERAUTH_GSSAPI_TOKEN otherwise (a packet error is fatal) and releases the token. When the status is exactly GSS_S_COMPLETE it sends, if the context flags lack GSS_C_INTEG_FLAG, an SSH2_MSG_USERAUTH_GSSAPI_EXCHANGE_COMPLETE packet. Otherwise it allocates a buffer (failure is fatal), builds the MIC input with ssh_gssapi_buildmic from server_user, service, the string "gssapi-with-mic" and the session id, takes the mutable pointer (failure is fatal), signs it with ssh_gssapi_sign (this call overwrites status), sends SSH2_MSG_USERAUTH_GSSAPI_MIC with the MIC when the new status is not an error (a send error is fatal), frees the buffer and releases the MIC. It returns the current status: the init_ctx status, or the signing status when signing was attempted. It does not free recv_tok.

functions.name: server_accept_loop
functions.prose_contract: Static function of sshd's listener (sshd.c:934-1294) that accepts connections and starts a session child. It first calls child_alloc itself (958) and allocates the startup poll index array and the poll array, so the caller does not need to have initialised the child pool. It then loops forever: with SIGHUP, SIGCHLD, SIGINFO, SIGTERM and SIGQUIT blocked it exits the process (closing the listen sockets and unlinking the pid file) with status 0 for SIGTERM and 255 for other termination signals when received_sigterm is set; reaps exited children on SIGCHLD; shows info; updates the process title when the active child count changed; and on SIGHUP closes the listening sockets once (lameduck) and calls sighup_restart when no listening startup is left. It builds a poll set from the listen sockets and the children's startup pipes (adding POLLOUT while a config or key buffer is pending) and calls ppoll with the old signal mask; a ppoll error other than EINTR is logged, EINVAL calls cleanup_exit(1), and any -1 result continues the loop.
