It writes pending config or key buffers to ready children (on a write error other than EINTR/EAGAIN it closes the child; when the config is fully sent it sets the keys buffer from pack_hostkeys), then reads one byte from each child's startup pipe (EOF or a read error closes the child, an early read while the config is still pending kills it, byte 0 on an early child marks it as no longer early, byte 1 on a non-early child closes it, anything else is logged). For each readable listen socket it accepts (an error continues the loop), clears non-blocking mode, creates the config socketpair and applies drop_connection (each failure closes the sockets and continues). In debug mode it closes the listening sockets, sets *sock_in and *sock_out to the new socket, sends the rexec state over config_s[0], closes config_s[0], frees the poll array and returns. Otherwise it registers a child, forks and in the child closes the startup pipes and the listening sockets, sets *sock_in and *sock_out, reinitialises logging, closes config_s[0], frees the poll array and returns. In the parent (also if fork failed, which is only logged) it closes config_s[1] and the accepted socket and reseeds the random generator (a failure of RAND_bytes is fatal). The only return statements in the function are the debug-mode one and the forked-child one; the parent leaves the loop only through exit, cleanup_exit, fatal or sighup_restart (whose body was not read).

functions.name: sshkey_private_serialize_maxsign
functions.prose_contract: Serialises a private key and, for XMSS keys, advances the signature state (sshkey.c:3743-3770 with the WITH_XMSS definition; in the build without WITH_XMSS the definition at 3802-3807 ignores maxsign and printerror and just returns sshkey_private_serialize_opt with SSHKEY_SERIALIZE_DEFAULT). In the XMSS build, when maxsign is 0 or the plain type of the key is not KEY_XMSS it returns exactly what sshkey_private_serialize_opt(k, b, SSHKEY_SERIALIZE_DEFAULT) returns and does nothing else. Otherwise it runs, in order and stopping at the first non-zero result, sshkey_xmss_get_state, sshkey_private_serialize_opt with SSHKEY_SERIALIZE_STATE (the buffer receives the state before advancing) and sshkey_xmss_forward_state by maxsign. Whatever happened in those steps, including a failure of the first one, it then calls sshkey_xmss_update_state. It returns the first error from the three steps if any, and otherwise the error from sshkey_xmss_update_state, or 0 when everything succeeded. The update-state call is therefore also made after an earlier failure; its error is only returned when the earlier steps succeeded.

functions.name: sshkey_curve_nid_to_bits
functions.prose_contract: Maps an OpenSSL elliptic-curve NID to a key size in bits (sshkey.c:604-619; compiled only with WITH_OPENSSL), returning a u_int. NID_X9_62_prime256v1 (415) gives 256, NID_secp384r1 (715) gives 384, and NID_secp521r1 (716) gives 521 only when OPENSSL_HAS_NISTP521 is defined at compile time; any other value, and 716 in a build without that macro, gives 0. It reads no state, allocates nothing and has no side effects.

functions.name: sshkey_ecdsa_bits_to_nid
functions.prose_contract: Maps an ECDSA key size in bits to an OpenSSL curve NID (sshkey.c:621-636; compiled only with WITH_OPENSSL), returning an int. 256 gives NID_X9_62_prime256v1 (415), 384 gives NID_secp384r1 (715), and 521 gives NID_secp521r1 (716) only when OPENSSL_HAS_NISTP521 is defined at compile time; any other value, and 521 in a build without that macro, gives -1. It reads no state, allocates nothing and has no side effects.

functions.name: sshkey_ec_nid_to_hash_alg
functions.prose_contract: Chooses the digest used with an ECDSA curve (sshkey.c:655-670; compiled only with WITH_OPENSSL), returning an int. It computes the key size with sshkey_curve_nid_to_bits(nid); if that size is not positive (an unsupported NID, including NID_secp521r1 in a build without OPENSSL_HAS_NISTP521) it returns -1. Otherwise a size up to 256 gives SSH_DIGEST_SHA256, a size up to 384 gives SSH_DIGEST_SHA384, and any larger size gives SSH_DIGEST_SHA512; so NID 415 gives SHA256, NID 715 gives SHA384 and NID 716 (when supported) gives SHA512. The symbolic constants are SSH_DIGEST_SHA256, SHA384 and SHA512 (digest.h:27-29 defines them as 2, 3 and 4 in this tree). It allocates nothing and has no side effects.

functions.name: unpack_revinfo
functions.prose_contract: Parses a revocation-info string of the form time[,reason[,argument]] used by the ca application (apps/ca.c:2567-2676; the real name is unpack_revinfo, with output pointers prevtm, preason, phold, pinvtm and the input str; the slice shows its second half). It returns 1 on success and 0 on any failure, printing a message to bio_err. It duplicates str (failure: message and 0), splits it at the first two commas, and, when prevtm is non-NULL, allocates an ASN1 UTC time into *prevtm and sets it from the time text (an allocation or invalid-date failure returns 0, leaving the already allocated *prevtm in place for the caller, since the function does not free it). When a reason text is present it is matched case-insensitively against the table of reason names; an unmatched text gives "invalid reason code" and 0. Reason index 7 becomes OCSP_REVOKED_STATUS_REMOVEFROMCRL; index 8 (hold) needs the argument, parses it as an object identifier with OBJ_txt2obj (missing or invalid: 0) and stores it in *phold when phold is non-NULL, otherwise frees it; indices 9 and 10 need the argument as a GeneralizedTime (missing, allocation failure or invalid: 0) and become key-compromise or CA-compromise respectively. On success it stores the reason code in *preason when preason is non-NULL (it stays -1, meaning no reason, when no reason text was given), transfers the compromise time to *pinvtm when pinvtm is non-NULL, and returns 1; otherwise the compromise time is freed. The duplicate string is always freed. *preason and *pinvtm are written only on success.

functions.name: ca_main
functions.prose_contract: Middle part of the main function of the openssl ca command (apps/ca.c:311-1362, the real name is ca_main; this slice 554-807 starts after option parsing and ends in the database-update step). The function keeps ret initialised to 1 (346), sets it to 0 for -help (366) and again at 1338 before the common end label, so a path that jumps to end without setting ret returns 1. In this part it takes the remaining arguments, loads the configuration file (failure: goto end), loads modules for a non-default config, finds the CA section (the section option or the default_ca setting) and optionally the oid_file and the OID section, loads random state, reads the string mask, UTF8 setting and unique_subject setting. If a serial-status query (ser_status) was requested it loads the database, builds its index and prints an error if the status check does not return 1, then goes to end; nothing on this path (606-623) sets ret to 0, so it ends with the initial value 1 even when the lookup succeeds, which a reviewer pointed out. Otherwise it reads the passphrase option, loads the CA private key and zeros the passphrase, and unless selfsign applies without spkac, self-signed certificate file or CRL generation it loads the CA certificate and checks that it matches the key (mismatch: goto end). It then reads the preserve, msie_hack, name option, cert option and extension copy settings (a bad value goes to end), checks that the new-certs directory exists when requests are present, loads the database and validates every entry (revoked entries need a valid revocation date through make_revoked, expiry dates must have the right format, serials need an even number of hex digits), builds its index, and, when updating the database was requested, calls do_updatedb and on a change saves and rotates the index files (errors go to end). The rest of the function (extension loading, certification of requests, CRL generation) is outside this slice.

functions.name: ciphers_main
functions.prose_contract: Second half of the openssl ciphers command (apps/ciphers.c:91-287; the real function is ciphers_main, which takes argc and argv; this slice lies in its listing loop, 254-287). The function starts with ret equal to 1, sets it to 0 for -help (121), when a -convert name is printed (188) and at the end of a successful listing (277), and returns ret at 286. After option parsing it uses a single optional positional argument as the cipher list, creates an SSL_CTX, sets the minimum and maximum protocol versions, installs the dummy PSK callback or the dummy SRP setup when those options were given, sets the TLS 1.3 ciphersuites and the cipher list when given (any failure goes to err, which prints the OpenSSL error queue to bio_err and then reaches end with ret 1), creates an SSL object, and takes the cipher stack with SSL_get1_supported_ciphers when use_supported is set and SSL_get_ciphers otherwise. Without verbose it prints the cipher names separated by colons and a newline; with verbose it loops over the ciphers, skipping NULL entries, prints for Verbose (capital V) the numeric id (a short form for ids whose top byte is 0x03), prints the standard name with -stdname (UNKNOWN when none) and then the description. At end it frees the cipher stack only when use_supported is set, frees the SSL_CTX and the SSL object and returns ret; the -convert path and early option errors also reach end with ctx, ssl and sk still NULL, which the free calls tolerate.

functions.name: cmp_server
functions.prose_contract: Runs the OpenSSL cmp application's built-in mock server loop (apps/cmp.c:3286-3361; built only when sockets and HTTP are available). With the context srv_cmp_ctx it first calls http_server_init for the port and verbosity; if that returns NULL it returns 0. Otherwise, while opt_max_msgs is not positive or fewer than opt_max_msgs messages were handled, each iteration receives one HTTP request with http_server_get_asn1_req. A result of 0 (no request yet) sleeps one second and retries once; on a second such result it clears ret and goes to the label next without counting a message. A result of -1 (fatal) breaks out of the loop with ret then equal to 0 because of the post-increment at 3315. For a received message it counts it, sets ret to 0, and if a request was parsed checks the path: a path other than "" or "pkix/" sends a 404 status, logs and goes to next with ret 0. Otherwise it calls OSSL_CMP_CTX_server_perform with the global client context cmp_ctx (not srv_cmp_ctx): a NULL response sends a 500 status and breaks with ret 0; otherwise it sends the response with http_server_send_asn1_resp and sets ret to its result, and a zero result breaks out of the loop. At next, when ret is 0 (a path error, an empty request, or a retry exhausted) it clears the transaction ID and sender nonce of srv_cmp_ctx; this clearing is skipped on the two break paths (send failure and NULL response), a point a reviewer made. When ret is 0, keep-alive is off or the server transaction is not in progress it frees the connection BIO and sets it to NULL. After the loop it frees both BIOs and returns ret: 0 after any break and for an iteration that ended through next with ret 0, and the nonzero result of http_server_send_asn1_resp when the loop ended by the message limit right after a successful send.

functions.name: cmp_main
functions.prose_contract: Later part of the main function of the openssl cmp command (apps/cmp.c:3673-4013, the real name is cmp_main; this slice 3744-4008 starts after option parsing). ret starts at 0 (3679, "failure"), becomes the result of the config/option handling (the code at 3717-3737 sets it to -1 for a bad option or -help usage in lines not read in full) and is set to 0 at 3737 before this slice. It sets up the UI method (batch), loads the optional engine (failure: goto err), the log callback and verbosity, and checks the TLS and port option combinations (several incompatible combinations go to err). When no -reqout_only is given and the mock server or -port is used, it builds the server context; with -port it runs ret = cmp_server(srv_cmp_ctx) and goes to err. With -reqout_only it rejects -port, ignores some other options and sets reqout. It then sets up the client context (failure: err) and runs the command opt_repeat times: IR, KUR, CR and P10CR set ret to 1 only when a certificate is returned, RR takes the result of OSSL_CMP_exec_RR_ses, genm takes do_genm and an unknown command leaves ret unchanged. If the CMP status is below accepted it sets ret to 0, or to 1 when the request was only written for -reqout_only, and goes to err. After print_status it saves or deletes the validated server certificate (failure sets ret to 0), goes to err if ret is 0, resets ret to 0, saves the extra certs, and for the enrolment commands the new chain, certificate, CA certificates and, with centralkeygen, the new private key (each failure goes to err with ret 0), then reinitialises the context (failure: err). After the loop ret is 1 (so zero repetitions also give 1). At err it cleanses the password and secret option strings, prints the CMP error queue when ret is not 1, frees the context, mock server, certConf store, TLS info, verify params, engine and config, closes the log and returns EXIT_FAILURE only when ret is 0 and EXIT_SUCCESS for every other value, including -1 (the -help or bad-option marker) and the nonzero value returned by cmp_server.

functions.name: cms_main
functions.prose_contract: Late part of the main function of the openssl cms command (apps/cms.c:342-1395, the real name is cms_main; this slice 1077-1377 holds the encrypt/sign/verify work and the end label). Return code ret starts at 1, is set to 0 for -help (398), to 2 at 871 (the argument-loading stage), to 3 at 1045 before the CMS structure is created, to 4 at 1232 after it, and the function returns ret at 1395. In this slice the CMS structure is built by operation: data, digest, compress, encrypt (partial structure, then one recipient per certificate with optional key parameters and wrap cipher, then a secret-key recipient and a password recipient, then CMS_final unless streaming), encrypted-data encrypt, sign-receipt, or sign/resign (signers loaded one by one: a failure to load a signer certificate or key sets ret to 2, other failures keep ret 3). Any failure inside these steps goes to end with ret 3, including a NULL cms at 1227-1229. After creation ret is 4: decrypt (with secret key, private key, password), data out, uncompress, digest verify, encrypted-data decrypt, verify (a failure sets ret to verify_err + 32 when -verify_retcode is given, else stays 4; failure to save signers sets 5), verify receipt, or output. In output, with -noout it only prints when requested; otherwise it writes SMIME, PEM or DER with the matching function whose result is put into ret, and a result of 0 or less sets ret to 6 and goes to end (an unknown output format also goes to end with the current ret). A path that reaches the line ret = 0 at 1353 returns 0. At end it prints the OpenSSL error queue when ret is non-zero and frees the certificate stacks, parameters, keys, strings and objects it owns. The signer certificate and key are freed only at the end of each loop iteration or in the final cleanup, so on an error inside the loop they are released by the end code.

functions.name: cms_main
functions.prose_contract: Option-processing part of the main function of the openssl cms command (apps/cms.c:342-1395, the real name is cms_main; this slice 562-822 lies in the option switch and the checks that follow it). ret is 1 from the start, so every goto end or opthelp reached here (a missing or duplicated argument, a failed allocation or push, an invalid object identifier, an engine, key-format, certificate or config load failure, a bad digest, cipher or wrap-cipher name, or an inconsistent option combination) returns 1 after the queued OpenSSL errors are printed. The cases in this slice store the options: CA path flags, input and content files, receipt-request lists, name options, secret key and key id (hex decoded; a repeated option or a bad hex string is an error), password, content type (OBJ_txt2obj), engine, passphrase source, headers (to, from, subject), certs output, digest, signer and its key (each -signer pushes the previous pair onto the signers and keys lists; -inkey without a signer is an error), originator, key format, recipient certificate (loaded and pushed when the operation is encrypt, otherwise remembered as the recipient file), the cipher name from an unknown option, key parameters (-keyopt, with the key index computed from the signers/keys or recipient count), verify parameters, random options, provider and config options and the wrap cipher. After the loop it loads the random state, looks up the digest and ciphers, and checks the combinations: receipt recipients without signers, receipts or multiple signers or keys without -sign, and CAdES with no-attributes or with verification-disabling flags (all errors, ret 1). With signing operations it then validates -inkey/-signer pairing. The body of the checks past line 822 and the operation itself were not read here.

functions.name: set_hex
functions.prose_contract: Static helper of the openssl enc command (apps/enc.c:849-877; the real name is set_hex, not hex2bin) that decodes a hexadecimal string into a fixed-size byte buffer. It takes the string length n and the capacity size*2 hex digits. If n is larger it prints "hex string is too long, ignoring excess" to bio_err and only uses the first size*2 characters; if smaller it prints "hex string is too short, padding with zero bytes to length". It then sets all size bytes of out to zero and decodes the characters one by one: a character that is not a hex digit prints "non-hex digit" and returns 0 at once; the high nibble of each byte is stored first (out[i/2] = digit << 4, which overwrites) and the low nibble is OR-ed in. An odd number of digits leaves the last nibble in the high half of its byte. At a failure the buffer holds the zeroed bytes plus the digits already written, including a high nibble stored for the failing digit's byte only if its first digit was valid and the failing digit is the second one. It returns 1 on success (including both warning cases) and 0 on a non-hex digit. It allocates nothing and does not modify in.

functions.name: self_test_events
functions.prose_contract: Callback of the openssl fipsinstall command for provider self-test events (apps/fipsinstall.c:973-1021; the slice 808-1021 also holds the tail of fipsinstall_main). It returns an int and ignores its arg. It locates the phase, description and type parameters in params; if any of the three is missing or is not a UTF8 string it returns 0. When logging is enabled (self_test_log) it prints a line at the start phase and at the pass or fail phases (the exact text is in message lines not read). If the phase is the corrupt phase and a corruption description or type was configured, then a configured description that differs from desc, or a configured type that differs from type, makes it return 1; when every configured selector matches it returns 0 (which makes the self-test corrupt its result). In every other case, including the corrupt phase with no selector configured, other phases, and a corrupt phase whose selectors do not match, it returns 1. It allocates and frees nothing.

functions.name: process_cert_request
functions.prose_contract: Mock CMP server callback that answers a certificate request (apps/lib/cmp_mock_srv.c:298-430). It takes the custom context from srv_ctx and returns NULL, raising CMP_R_NULL_ARGUMENT, if that context, cert_req, certOut, chainOut or caPubs is NULL; the outputs are not touched in that case. If ctx->sendError is 1 or equals the body type of the request it raises an error and returns NULL, again without touching the three outputs. Otherwise it sets *certOut, *chainOut and *caPubs to NULL. If a poll count is configured and the current poll count is 0 it duplicates the request into ctx->req (NULL result on allocation failure) and returns a new status info with the waiting status; otherwise it resets the current poll count to 0 once it has reached the configured count. For a CR request that carries a certProfile entry in the general-info it requires exactly one first string equal to "profile1" (a failure or mismatch returns NULL with the outputs NULL). For a KUR with a reference certificate and a CRMF message it requires the old-certificate id and checks it against the reference (missing: NULL with CMP_R_MISSING_CERTID; mismatch: NULL with CMP_R_WRONG_CERTID). Then it duplicates ctx->certOut into *certOut when set, checks whether central key generation was requested (a negative answer goes to err), and for central key generation duplicates ctx->keyOut and installs it as the new private key in the server's CMP context, failing to err if no key is configured or either step fails. It then up-refs ctx->chainOut and ctx->caPubsOut into *chainOut and *caPubs when those are set and duplicates ctx->statusOut into the returned status info when set. A failure up to that point goes to err, which frees and NULLs all three outputs and returns NULL. If statusOut is NULL it returns NULL (si stays NULL) without going through err, so the outputs may be set (owned by the caller) with a NULL return; otherwise the returned status info and the outputs are owned by the caller.

functions.name: log_set_verbosity
functions.prose_contract: Sets the global log verbosity of the openssl apps (apps/lib/log.c:16-25) and returns an int. If level is below LOG_EMERG or above LOG_TRACE it calls trace_log_message with category -1, program name prog, level LOG_ERR and the text "Invalid verbosity level %d", leaves the stored verbosity unchanged and returns 0. Otherwise it stores level in the static variable verbosity and returns 1. The error text is only printed when the current verbosity is at least LOG_ERR: trace_log_message (71-108) returns early without output when verbosity is less than the message level, and with category -1 it does not use the trace channel.

functions.name: shacrypt
functions.prose_contract: Computes the SHA-256 or SHA-512 crypt hash of a password for openssl passwd (apps/passwd.c:501-780; the real name is shacrypt, with arguments passwd, magic and salt, all NUL-terminated strings; the slice shows its middle and end). It returns a pointer to its own static buffer out_buf (not a caller-supplied one) or NULL. It returns NULL, before touching out_buf, when magic is not exactly one character or is neither '5' (SHA-256, 32-byte digest) nor '6' (SHA-512, 64-byte digest), and when salt starts with "rounds=" but the number is not followed by '$'. A valid rounds prefix is parsed with strtoul, clamped to 1000..999999999 and marks the rounds as custom; the salt then starts after the '$'. The salt is copied truncated to 16 characters. The result string is built as "$<magic>$", then "rounds=<n>$" for a custom round count, then the salt; if that string is longer than 3 + 17 (when custom) + the salt length it goes to err and returns NULL. It then runs the standard SHA-crypt steps with two digest contexts: hash of password, salt and password; the password length of that block; the bits of the password length; the P sequence (digest of the password repeated password-length times, stretched to the password length), the S sequence (digest of 16 + first digest byte copies of the salt, stretched to the salt length) and the given number of rounds that mix the previous digest, P and S. Any failed digest call or allocation (EVP_MD_CTX_new, EVP_DigestInit_ex, EVP_DigestUpdate, EVP_DigestFinal_ex, OPENSSL_zalloc of the P and S arrays) goes to err, which frees the contexts and the arrays and returns NULL. On success it frees the contexts and arrays, appends '$' and the digest in the crypt base-64 form (43 characters for SHA-256 and 86 for SHA-512 in the fixed permutations) and returns out_buf. Since out_buf is static, a later call overwrites an earlier result. OPENSSL_zalloc is called with passwd_len and salt_len, so a zero-length password or salt asks for zero bytes; whether that allocation succeeds depends on CRYPTO_zalloc, which I did not read.

functions.name: do_passwd
functions.prose_contract: Hashes one password for openssl passwd and prints it (apps/passwd.c:782-852; it returns int, 1 on success, 0 when the random salt cannot be made). If passed_salt is 0 it chooses the salt length from mode (8 for md5, apr1 and aixmd5, 16 for sha256 and sha512; any other mode trips an assertion), allocates a buffer of that length plus one only when *salt_malloc_p is NULL (setting both *salt_p and *salt_malloc_p to it) and otherwise writes into the existing *salt_p without checking its size, so a caller-supplied buffer must hold at least saltlen+1 bytes (reviewer 15 right). It fills the salt with RAND_bytes (a failure returns 0 through end, leaving any allocated buffer for the caller) and maps each byte to the crypt alphabet with the 6 low bits, then NUL-terminates. If the password is longer than pw_maxlen it prints a warning to bio_err unless quiet is set and truncates passwd in place. It then hashes with md5crypt using magic "1" for md5, "apr1" for apr1 or "" for aixmd5, or with shacrypt using "5" or "6", on the salt at *salt_p; the hash is only checked with an assertion, so in a build without assertions a failed hash would be passed to BIO_printf as NULL. It prints "passwd<TAB>hash" when table is set and reverse is not, "hash<TAB>passwd" when both are set, and "hash" otherwise, each followed by a newline, and returns 1. The caller owns the salt buffer recorded in *salt_malloc_p.

functions.name: pkcs8_main
functions.prose_contract: Final part of the main function of the openssl pkcs8 command (apps/pkcs8.c:90-406, the real name is pkcs8_main; this slice 302-406 starts inside the encrypt branch of the -topk8 conversion). ret starts at 1 (105); it is set to 0 only for -help (123), after the topk8 branch finished its output (319) and after the normal output at 392; every goto end taken before one of those assignments, including the option-error label opthelp, returns 1. In the -topk8 branch the encryption algorithm (pbe) is built with scrypt, PBES2 or the PBE nid, a NULL one prints an error and goes to end, the password is the -passout value or is read from the terminal (failure goes to end), PKCS8_set0_pbe wraps the key (NULL: the algorithm is freed, error printed, end), and the result is written as PEM or DER; an unknown output format prints "Bad format" and goes to end (ret 1). A topk8 branch with -nocrypt writes the unencrypted PKCS#8 structure in the same way. In the other branch the input is read as PKCS#8 (-nocrypt: a PrivateKeyInfo, PEM or DER; otherwise an encrypted X509_SIG whose password comes from -passin or the terminal and which is decrypted with PKCS8_decrypt); an unsupported input format, a NULL result, a failure to read the password, a decryption failure or a failure of EVP_PKCS82PKEY goes to end with ret 1. It then opens the output file with bio_open_owner (NULL goes to end), writes the key as PEM (traditional form when requested, otherwise PKCS#8) or DER, with an unknown format going to end, and sets ret to 0. The return values of the PEM and DER write calls are not checked in any branch, so a write error still gives ret 0 (reviewer 17 right). At end it frees the X509_SIG, PKCS8 key info, key, cipher, engine, output and input BIOs and the passin and passout strings and returns ret.

functions.name: req_main
functions.prose_contract: Middle part of the main function of the openssl req command (apps/req.c:283-1108, the real name is req_main; this slice 546-826 runs from the end of option parsing to the loading of the CA files). ret starts at 1 (310), is set to 0 for -help (330) and at 991 and 1077, and the function returns it at 1108; the option-error label opthelp (325-327) prints "Use -help" and goes to end with ret still 1 (so a bad option returns 1, not 0). In this slice: extra arguments go to opthelp; random loading, passphrase options, the config template and the -addext config are loaded (any failure goes to end); the OID file and OID section are added; a given digest is checked (failure goes to opthelp), else default_md is read; the extension sections are test-added (failure goes to end); passin and passout default to the config values; the string mask and UTF8 flag are read. If -key was given the private key is loaded (failure: end); a -newkey together with -key only prints a warning. When a new request is wanted and no key is loaded it reads the key length (default if absent), creates a key generation context (NULL: end), rejects RSA, RSA-PSS or DSA keys under the minimum length (end), warns for oversized RSA or DSA keys, applies the -pkeyopt options (a failure goes to end), generates the key (NULL: end), looks up the key output file in the config when none was given and, when a key was generated or -keyout was given, writes the private key as PEM, retrying up to 3 times on a password problem (failure: end). A -subj subject is parsed (failure: end). When no new request is made it loads an existing request from -in or stdin (NULL: end); in that case pkey can remain NULL when no -key or -newkey was given (reviewer 17 right). Then the -CA/-CAkey files are loaded (failure or key mismatch: end). The rest of the function is outside this slice.

functions.name: req_main
functions.prose_contract: Final part of the main function of the openssl req command (apps/req.c:283-1108, the real name is req_main; this slice 827-1110 holds the request and certificate creation tail and the end label). ret is 1 until it is set to 0 at 991 (the -noout with nothing else requested path, which jumps to end) or at 1077 (after all output has been written). It creates the request if needed (failure goes to end), sets the subject name (failure: end), prints the subject when verbose, verifies the request when -verify is given (a negative result goes to end, 0 prints an error and goes to end), and for -noout without text, modulus, subject or pubkey returns 0 at once. It opens the output file (NULL: end), writes the public key for -pubkey, and for -text prints the certificate or request with the result stored in ret: a result of 0 means the print failed and the function goes to end with ret equal to 0, so it returns 0 (success status) after a print failure and, since ret is 0, without printing the OpenSSL error queue; a non-zero result leaves ret non-zero until it is reset at 1077, and later failures go to end with that non-zero ret (a nonzero value, normally 1). It then prints the subject, prints the RSA modulus (a missing public key or failed parameter fetch goes to end, ret then holding the earlier text result or 1), writes the request in DER or PEM (a failure goes to end) and the certificate (same), and sets ret to 0. At end it prints the OpenSSL errors when ret is non-zero, frees the configs, BIOs, keys, key context, option stacks, hash table, engines, request, subject, certificates, key and serial, frees passin and passout only when they were not config-owned, and returns ret. The older claim that every error returns 1 is wrong because of the print path; the claim that all objects are freed is right for the end label as shown.

functions.name: rsa_main
functions.prose_contract: Second half of the main function of the openssl rsa command (apps/rsa.c:137-428, the real name is rsa_main; this slice 252-428 runs from loading the key to the end label). ret starts at 1 (148) and is set to 0 only for -help (168), for -noout after the checks (327), after a successful legacy-encoding fallback (384) and after a successful OSSL_ENCODER_to_bio (418); the function returns it at 427. Every goto end before those points (including the option-error label opthelp reached from the option loop) returns 1. In this slice it rejects -check with -pubin (end), loads the public key (with a legacy PEM or ASN1 RSA format when pubin is 2) or the private key (NULL: errors printed, end), requires the key to be RSA or RSA-PSS (end otherwise), opens the output with bio_open_owner (NULL: end), and for -text prints the public or private key (a failure goes to end). For -modulus it fetches the "n" parameter and prints it with BN_print, and the return values of EVP_PKEY_get_bn_param and BN_print are not checked, so a failure there does not stop the command (reviewer 15 right). With -check it creates a key context (NULL: end), runs EVP_PKEY_check: a result of 1 prints "RSA key ok", 0 prints "RSA key not ok" and continues, and a negative result prints errors and goes to end. With -noout it ends with ret 0. Otherwise it picks the output type (DER, PEM, MSBLOB or PVK; PVK with a public key input and an unsupported format go to end) and structure, creates an encoder context for the key; when no encoder is available it uses the legacy function try_legacy_encoding for public output (success gives ret 0 and the end; failure and the private-key case return 1). It sets the cipher and passphrase when encrypting, the PVK encryption level (failure: end) and calls OSSL_ENCODER_to_bio, which on failure prints the OpenSSL errors and goes to end with ret 1. At end it frees the encoder context, engine, output, key, cipher and both password strings.

functions.name: s_server_main
functions.prose_contract: Last part of the main function of the openssl s_server command (apps/s_server.c:1110-2484; the real name is s_server_main, taking argc and argv; this slice 2226-2486 holds the context set-up tail and the end label). ret starts at 1 (1135) and is set to 0 for -help (1242) and at 2445 after the server loop; the function returns ret at 2484, so every goto end before 2445 returns 1. In this slice it finishes the DH parameters (auto DH when none was loaded; a failure of EVP_PKEY_up_ref or SSL_CTX_set0_tmp_dh_pkey goes to end), installs certificates and keys with set_cert_key_stuff for the main context, the optional second context and the second certificate (failure: end), loads a serverinfo file (failure: end), sets the not-resumable callback, the PSK server callback, a PSK identity hint (a failure goes to end) and a PSK session file (open or read failure: end), sets verify callbacks, the session id context (failure: end), cookie callbacks and the servername callbacks when a second context exists, the SRP verifier file (failure: end), client CA lists, the OCSP status callbacks, the keylog file (a non-zero result goes to end), the early-data limits, and, with cert compression, SSL_CTX_compress_certs for ctx and ctx2 where a failure only prints a message and does not stop (reviewer 17 right); it applies the RPK certificate types (failure: end). It then selects rev_body, www_body or sv_body, unlinks a unix socket path when asked, calls do_server and print_stats, and sets ret to 0 unconditionally: the return value of do_server is not used (reviewer 15 right), so the function returns 0 whenever it reached this line. At end it frees the contexts, session, keys, certificates, CRLs, chains, strings, option stacks, verify parameters, engine, and the s_out and s_msg BIOs (setting both globals to NULL) and returns ret.

functions.name: www_body
functions.prose_contract: Serves one accepted connection for the s_server -www, -WWW and -HTTP modes (apps/s_server.c:3255-3733, int www_body(int s, int stype, int prot, unsigned char *context); the slice 3029-3287 shows only the start of it, after is_retryable and init_ssl_connection). Its result variable ret is initialised to 1 at 3258 and the only other assignment in the function is ret = 1 at 3417 (end of input), so every path I found that reaches its single return at 3732 returns 1, including the error paths: failures to allocate the buffer, the SSL object, the BIOs or the early-data connection go to err with ret still 1, and a clean end of input goes to end. The paths differ only in cleanup: end calls do_ssl_shutdown(con) first, while err does not; both free the read buffer, the SSL BIO, the I/O BIO chain and the early-data BIO. Between them it allocates a buffer of the maximum size, creates the SSL object and BIO chain (buffering and SSL BIOs), optionally reads early data (any read error goes to err), then loops reading request lines; a retry is retried after a one-second sleep, a read of 0 ends with goto end, and otherwise it handles GET /reneg, GET /stats, GET / and file requests, building the reply (including the directory text with escaping) and writing it, with write errors going to the write_error label that frees the file BIO and ends the request loop. After the loop it flushes io until the flush succeeds or cannot be retried.

functions.name: smime_main
functions.prose_contract: Option-processing and input-loading part of the main function of the openssl smime command (apps/smime.c:195-745; the real name is smime_main, this slice 302-555). ret is initialised to 0 (215), not 1, and is set to 2 at 497, 3 at 612, 4 at 673, 5 at 690, 3 at 718 and 0 at 722; the function returns it at 745. So every goto end or goto opthelp taken before line 497 (option errors, a missing operation, signer or recipient, a failed random, provider, config or password step) leaves ret at 0 and returns 0 after printing the message (the opthelp label at 231 prints "Use -help" and goes to end), which is what the old prose said and what the reviewer who claimed 1 got wrong (reviewer 17 wrong). In this slice the remaining option cases store flags and strings (binary, nosigs, streaming, CRLF, random, provider, config, engine, passin, to, from and so on), the signer and key lists are built, missing -signer or recipient or file arguments go to opthelp (return 0), and app_passwd failure goes to end (0). From line 497 ret is 2: it then sets the format defaults, for encrypt it defaults the cipher to aes-256-cbc and loads each recipient certificate from the arguments (a failure goes to end with ret 2), loads the extra certificates and the decrypt recipient (failures print the OpenSSL errors and go to end with ret 2), and chooses the key file for decrypt or sign; the key itself is loaded after line 555.

functions.name: smime_main
functions.prose_contract: Operation part of the main function of the openssl smime command (apps/smime.c:195-745; the real name is smime_main, this slice 556-779 contains the work and the end label). ret is 2 on entry to this slice (set at 497), becomes 3 at 612 before the PKCS7 structure is built, 4 at 673 after it, 5 at 690, and 0 at 722; it is returned at 745. In this slice it loads the signing or decryption key when a key file is set (failure: end, ret 2), opens the input (failure: end, ret 2), for the read-type operations reads the PKCS7 as S/MIME, PEM or DER into a new structure (any failure goes to end with ret 2), reads detached content from -content when given, opens the output (failure: end, ret 2) and for verify builds the certificate store (failure: end, ret 2). Then ret is 3 and it builds the structure: encrypt with PKCS7_encrypt_ex, or sign (partial sign, certificates added when nocerts, then each signer loaded and added; a failure goes to end with ret 3) or resign, followed by PKCS7_final when not streaming; a NULL p7 goes to end with ret 3. With ret 4 it runs the operation: decrypt (failure: end, 4), verify (failure: end, 4; the signer certificates are then saved and a failure of that returns 5), pk7out (PEM write) or the writing of the result as S/MIME, PEM or DER (an unknown format goes to end with ret still 4; a write that returns 0 sets ret 3). When everything succeeds ret becomes 0. At end it prints the OpenSSL errors when ret is non-zero and frees the stacks, store, certificates, keys, digest and cipher, the PKCS7, engine, BIOs, password and config.

functions.name: process
functions.prose_contract: Static function of the openssl storeutl command (apps/storeutl.c:362-516) that opens a store URI and prints or writes every item; it returns an int that works as an error count (0 means no error found). ret starts at 1. If OSSL_STORE_open_ex fails it prints the errors and returns 1 immediately, without closing anything. If expected is non-zero and OSSL_STORE_expect fails, or a search criterion is given and the store does not support it or OSSL_STORE_find fails, it goes to end2 with ret 1. Otherwise ret is set to 0 and the loop calls OSSL_STORE_load repeatedly. A NULL item with an error indication clears the error queue when recursive is set (otherwise prints it), ends the loop if the store is at end-of-file, and otherwise adds 1 to ret and continues (so recursive load errors are cleared but still counted, reviewer 2 right). A NULL item without error ends the loop at end-of-file, or prints "returned NULL without eof or error", adds 1 and ends the loop. For each item it prints its index and type (and name and description for a name item) to bio_out, opens the global output BIO out on first use (failure: ret is incremented and it goes to end2 without freeing the current item, reviewer 15 right). For name items with recursive it adds the result of the nested process call at an indent of two more; params, public key, private key, certificate and CRL items are printed when text is set and written in PEM when noout is not set, and the return values of these print and write calls are not checked (reviewer 1 right); an unknown type adds 1 to ret. Each handled item is freed and counted. After the loop it prints "Total found" and at end2 it closes the store, adding 1 to ret and printing the errors if the close fails, and returns ret.

functions.name: print_x509v3_exts
functions.prose_contract: Static function of the openssl x509 command (apps/x509.c:1304-1365; the real name is print_x509v3_exts, with arguments bio, x and ext_names) that prints the extensions of a certificate whose short names appear in a comma-separated list. It returns an int: ret starts at 0. If the certificate has no extensions it prints "No extensions in certificate" to bio_err and returns 1. It duplicates ext_names and parses the list in place (an allocation failure returns 0; zero parsed names prints "Invalid extension names" to bio and returns 0), allocates the name array (failure: 0) and fills it. For each extension of the certificate with a known short name that equals one of the listed names it pushes the extension onto a new stack exts2 (an allocation or push failure returns 0); an extension that matches several names is pushed once per match. It then tests sk_X509_EXTENSION_num(exts2) with !: when exts2 was created and is empty this cannot happen, but when nothing matched exts2 is still NULL and OPENSSL_sk_num(NULL) is -1, so the test is false, the "No extensions matched" message is not printed, and the call X509V3_extensions_print(bio, NULL, NULL, 0, 0) runs, which returns 1 for an empty or NULL stack; so the no-match result is 1 without that message. Otherwise ret is the result of X509V3_extensions_print for the matched extensions. At end it frees the stack exts2 (not the extensions themselves), the names array and the duplicated string.

functions.name: AES_bi_ige_encrypt
functions.prose_contract: Bidirectional IGE-mode AES transform (crypto/aes/aes_ige.c:180-295; the real name is AES_bi_ige_encrypt, which returns nothing; the slice 275-295 is only the second loop of its decrypt branch). It checks with OPENSSL_assert that in, out, key and ivec are non-NULL, that enc is AES_ENCRYPT or AES_DECRYPT and that length is a multiple of the AES block size (a violation aborts). For encryption it first runs a forward IGE pass over the data from in to out starting with the pair ivec and ivec+16, then a backward pass in place on out from the last block to the first with the pair ivec+32 and ivec+48. For decryption it runs a backward pass from the last block of in to out with the pair ivec+32 and ivec+48, and then a forward pass in place over out with the pair ivec and ivec+16 (the slice). All block operations use AES_encrypt or AES_decrypt with key only: the parameter key2 is not used anywhere in the function (reviewer 17 wrong that the backward pass uses it). ivec is const and is not modified; in is only read except where it overlaps out.

functions.name: ossl_c2i_ASN1_OBJECT
functions.prose_contract: Decodes the content octets of an ASN.1 OBJECT IDENTIFIER into an ASN1_OBJECT (crypto/asn1/a_object.c:238-331; the real name is ossl_c2i_ASN1_OBJECT with arguments a, pp and len; the slice 287-380 shows its second half and then ASN1_OBJECT_new, ASN1_OBJECT_free and ASN1_OBJECT_create). It returns NULL, raising ASN1_R_INVALID_OBJECT_ENCODING, if len is not positive or exceeds INT_MAX, pp or *pp is NULL, or the last content byte has its high bit set; it also returns NULL with the same error if any sub-identifier starts with the padding byte 0x80. If the bytes match a known object (OBJ_obj2nid is not NID_undef) it returns that static object from OBJ_nid2obj, frees *a first when a is non-NULL (ASN1_OBJECT_free frees only a dynamic object) and stores the static object in *a, and advances *pp by len. Otherwise it creates a new object with ASN1_OBJECT_new when a is NULL, *a is NULL or *a is not marked dynamic (NULL on allocation failure, without an error raised here), else reuses *a. It takes the old data pointer out of the object, and when there was none or the old length is smaller than length it frees it, sets the length to 0, allocates a new length-byte buffer (failure: err) and sets the dynamic-data flag. It copies the bytes, frees the old sn and ln when the dynamic-strings flag is set and clears it, stores the new data and length, clears sn and ln, advances *pp past the bytes and stores the object in *a when a is non-NULL, and returns it. At err it raises an ASN1 error whose reason value is the local variable i (which holds length after the loop), frees the new object unless it is *a, and returns NULL; in the reuse case a failed allocation leaves *a with data NULL and length 0 and *pp not advanced.

functions.name: ASN1_item_sign_ctx
functions.prose_contract: Signs the DER encoding of an ASN.1 item with an already initialised EVP_MD_CTX (crypto/asn1/a_sign.c:146-288) and returns an int: the length of the signature stored in signature on the normal success path, and 0 on most failures with an error raised. It takes the digest and the key from the context; if the context has no key it raises ASN1_R_CONTEXT_NOT_INITIALISED and returns 0. If the key has no legacy method table (pkey->ameth is NULL, a provider key) it requires a signature operation context, asks the provider for the signature algorithm identifier (a failure or an empty identifier returns 0), decodes that identifier into algor1 and algor2 when those are non-NULL (a decode failure returns 0) and goes on to sign with rv equal to 3. If the method has an item_sign hook it calls it: a result of 1 sets outl to the signature length and returns it at once through the cleanup, without allocating or re-setting anything, so the hook has already filled signature and ASN1_item_sign_ctx only reports its length (reviewer 15 right, the unused-bits count is not set here); a result of 0 or below raises ERR_R_EVP_LIB and returns 0; a result of 2 continues with the generic code. Without a hook rv is 2. In the generic case (rv 2) it requires a digest (else error and 0), looks up the signature algorithm id from the digest and key type (not found: error, 0), and sets algor1 and algor2 when they are non-NULL (failure: 0). It then DER-encodes the item (a non-positive length raises an error and returns 0), asks EVP_DigestSign for the signature size, allocates the output buffer (failure returns 0), signs, stores the buffer into signature with ASN1_STRING_set0 and sets its unused-bits count to 0; the buffer is owned by signature after that. The cleanup at the err label clears and frees the input buffer and the output buffer (when it was not handed over). The return value is outl, which the function sets to the signature length only at the points described and to 0 on the other error paths.

functions.name: ASN1_object_size
functions.prose_contract: Returns the total encoded size of an ASN.1 element (crypto/asn1/asn1_lib.c:222-249), as an int, or -1. Arguments are constructed, length (content length) and tag. It returns -1 at once when length is negative. Otherwise it starts with a header size of 1 and, when tag is 31 or more, adds one for each base-128 digit of the tag (1 for 31 to 127, 2 up to 16383, 3 up to 2097151, 4 up to 268435455 and 5 above that); when constructed is exactly 2 (indefinite length) it adds 3 (a length octet and the two end-of-contents octets); otherwise it adds 1 for the length octet and, when length exceeds 127, one more for each byte of the length (1 up to 255, 2 up to 65535, 3 up to 16777215, 4 above). If the header size is at least INT_MAX minus length it returns -1; otherwise it returns the header size plus length. It reads no state and allocates nothing.

functions.name: asn1_item_embed_new
functions.prose_contract: Creates and initialises a new ASN.1 value for the item it (crypto/asn1/tasn_new.c:57-170; static int, with pval, it, embed, libctx and propq; the slice is the whole file start). If the item has an auxiliary callback it is kept in asn1_cb. It switches on the item type. EXTERN: if the extern functions exist, it calls asn1_ex_new_ex, or else asn1_ex_new when that exists, and a failure goes to asn1err; when there are no functions or neither callback exists it does nothing at all and returns 1 without touching *pval (reviewer 15 right). PRIMITIVE: uses asn1_template_new when the item has a template, otherwise asn1_primitive_new, with failure going to asn1err. MSTRING: asn1_primitive_new, failure to asn1err. CHOICE and SEQUENCE/NDEF_SEQUENCE: first the NEW_PRE callback, whose result 0 goes to auxerr and 2 makes the function return 1 right away with *pval untouched; then it zeroes the storage in place when embed is set, otherwise allocates it with OPENSSL_zalloc, where an allocation failure returns 0 immediately with *pval NULL and no error raised (reviewer 1 right). A CHOICE sets its selector to -1; a SEQUENCE initialises the lock (failure frees a non-embedded allocation, sets *pval to NULL and goes to asn1err), initialises the encoding cache and creates every field with asn1_template_new (a failure goes to asn1err2). The NEW_POST callback failing goes to auxerr2. The error labels: asn1err2 and auxerr2 free the partly built value with ossl_asn1_item_embed_free and then raise ERR_R_ASN1_LIB (asn1err) or ASN1_R_AUX_ERROR (auxerr) and return 0; asn1err and auxerr alone raise the error and return 0 without freeing. So partial state is freed only on the SEQUENCE field failure and on NEW_POST failure, not on EXTERN, PRIMITIVE, MSTRING or NEW_PRE failure. All other item types return 1 without doing anything. Otherwise it returns 1 after the switch.

functions.name: IMPLEMENT_ASN1_STRING_FUNCTIONS
functions.prose_contract: Macro (crypto/asn1/tasn_typ.c:16-26) that defines the item, encode functions and the allocator pair for an ASN.1 string type sname; this record is its instance for ASN1_OCTET_STRING (line 28). The generated function ASN1_OCTET_STRING_new(void) takes no arguments and returns ASN1_STRING_type_new(V_ASN1_OCTET_STRING): a newly allocated string object of that type owned by the caller, or NULL when the allocation fails. It touches no global state.

functions.name: IMPLEMENT_ASN1_STRING_FUNCTIONS
functions.prose_contract: Macro (crypto/asn1/tasn_typ.c:16-26) that defines the item, encode functions and the allocator pair for an ASN.1 string type sname; this record is the free function generated for ASN1_OCTET_STRING (line 28). ASN1_OCTET_STRING_free(ASN1_OCTET_STRING *x) returns nothing and calls ASN1_STRING_free(x) with x unchanged, so for NULL it does nothing further than what ASN1_STRING_free does with NULL (not read here), and after the call x must not be used by the caller.

functions.name: IMPLEMENT_ASN1_STRING_FUNCTIONS
functions.prose_contract: Macro (crypto/asn1/tasn_typ.c:16-26) that defines the item, encode functions and the allocator pair for an ASN.1 string type sname; this record is its instance for ASN1_INTEGER (line 29). The generated function ASN1_INTEGER_new(void) takes no arguments and returns ASN1_STRING_type_new(V_ASN1_INTEGER): a newly allocated string object of that type owned by the caller, or NULL when the allocation fails. It touches no global state.

functions.name: IMPLEMENT_ASN1_STRING_FUNCTIONS
functions.prose_contract: Macro (crypto/asn1/tasn_typ.c:16-26) that defines the item, encode functions and the allocator pair for an ASN.1 string type sname; this record is the free function generated for ASN1_INTEGER (line 29). ASN1_INTEGER_free(ASN1_INTEGER *x) returns nothing and calls ASN1_STRING_free(x) with x unchanged; after the call x must not be used by the caller, and its NULL handling is that of ASN1_STRING_free (not read here).

functions.name: buffer_ctrl
functions.prose_contract: Control function of the buffering BIO (crypto/bio/bf_buff.c:235-409; static long buffer_ctrl(BIO *b, int cmd, long num, void *ptr), the slice 302-468 also contains buffer_callback_ctrl, buffer_gets and buffer_puts, which are not described here). It reads the context from b->ptr and starts with ret equal to 1. By command: RESET clears the four buffer offsets and lengths, returns 0 when there is no next BIO and otherwise returns the next BIO's result; EOF returns 0 if buffered input remains and otherwise the next BIO's answer (the next BIO is not checked for NULL here); INFO returns the output length; GET_BUFF_NUM_LINES counts newlines in the buffered input; WPENDING and PENDING return the buffered output or input length, or, when that is 0, 0 for a missing next BIO and otherwise the next BIO's answer; SET_BUFF_READ_DATA enlarges the input buffer when num exceeds its size (a non-positive num or an allocation failure returns 0), then resets the offset, sets the length to num and copies num bytes from ptr, returning 1; SET_BUFF_SIZE takes the input size, the output size or both from ptr and num (ptr pointing to 0 selects input, other values select output, NULL selects both), allocates a new buffer only when the requested size is above DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE and differs from the current one (the first branch returns 0 for a non-positive num or an allocation failure, the second frees the first new buffer when it fails and returns 0), swaps in the new buffers, resets their offsets and lengths and updates only their size fields, and returns 1; DO_STATE_MACHINE returns 0 without a next BIO and otherwise forwards and copies the retry flags; FLUSH returns 0 without a next BIO, forwards at once when no output is pending, and otherwise writes out the pending output in a loop (a write result of 0 or less is returned as the result, with the retry flags copied) and then forwards the flush to the next BIO; DUP sets the duplicate's read and write buffer sizes and gives 0 if either fails, else 1; PEEK first calls buffer_read with a zero length to fill the buffer, limits num to the buffered input length, copies that many bytes to ptr without consuming them and returns that count; any other command returns 0 without a next BIO and otherwise the next BIO's answer.

functions.name: prefix_write
functions.prose_contract: Write method of the prefix BIO (crypto/bio/bf_prefix.c:81-149; static int prefix_write(BIO *b, const char *out, size_t outl, size_t *numwritten), returning 1 on success and 0 on failure). It takes the context from the BIO data pointer and returns 0 at once, leaving *numwritten untouched, when the context is NULL. When no prefix is set (NULL or empty) and the indent is 0 it records whether the last byte of out is a newline in ctx->linestart (only when outl is positive) and returns the result of BIO_write_ex on the next BIO, with *numwritten set by that call. Otherwise it sets *numwritten to 0 and loops while bytes remain: at the start of a line it writes the prefix (a failed prefix write returns 0 at once), then prints the indent as that many spaces with BIO_printf, whose result is not checked (reviewer 1 right), and clears linestart. It then takes the bytes up to and including the next newline (or all the rest), writes them with BIO_write_ex in a loop that handles partial writes, adding each successful count to *numwritten, and returns 0 when a write fails, so on failure *numwritten holds the total of bytes successfully written before the failing call, not the count of the last call (reviewer 15 right). After a chunk ending in a newline it sets linestart again. It returns 1 after consuming all outl bytes (also for outl equal to 0, with *numwritten 0).

functions.name: readbuffer_gets
functions.prose_contract: Gets one line (or up to size minus 1 bytes) from the read-buffering BIO (crypto/bio/bf_readbuff.c:218-291; static int readbuffer_gets(BIO *b, char *buf, int size), the real name of the function whose tail the slice 262-291 shows; there is no function buffer_read in this slice). It returns 0 when buf is NULL or size is 0, and, after reserving one byte for the terminator, when the context is NULL or there is no next BIO. It clears the retry flags and first copies already buffered bytes from ctx->ibuf up to size or the first newline, advancing the offset and reducing the buffered length; if it found a newline or the size is used up it writes the terminator and returns the count. Otherwise it calls readbuffer_resize(ctx, 1 + size) and returns 0 when that fails (buf is then not terminated, and bytes copied earlier remain in buf). It then reads from the next BIO one byte at a time into the buffer and buf, advancing ibuf_off, until size bytes are read or a newline was read; a read result of 0 or less copies the next BIO's retry flags, terminates buf and returns the number of bytes read so far if positive and otherwise that read result. Normal completion terminates buf and returns the number of bytes copied. For size equal to 1 it terminates buf and returns 0. It takes no ownership.

functions.name: BIO_lookup_ex
functions.prose_contract: Resolves a host and service into a list of address records (crypto/bio/bio_addr.c:680-968; the real name is BIO_lookup_ex, with host, service, lookup_type, family, socktype, protocol and res; the slice 803-970 is the legacy gethostbyname branch near its end). It returns an int, 1 on success and 0 on failure, starting with ret equal to 0. It first rejects, with BIO_R_UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_FAMILY and 0, any family other than AF_INET, AF_INET6 (when IPv6 is enabled), AF_UNIX (when enabled) and AF_UNSPEC. For AF_UNIX it wraps the host string as a unix address with addrinfo_wrap and returns 1 on success, or raises ERR_R_BIO_LIB and returns 0. Otherwise it calls BIO_sock_init and returns 0 if that is not 1. When AI_PASSIVE is defined (the usual case) the structure is "if (1) { getaddrinfo path } else { legacy path }", so the legacy code in the slice is never compiled in as reachable: the getaddrinfo path fills a hints structure from family, socktype and protocol (AI_ADDRCONFIG for a host with an unspecified family, AI_PASSIVE for a server lookup), calls getaddrinfo, treats 0 as success (ret 1), raises a system or BIO error for EAI_SYSTEM, EAI_MEMORY and other codes, and on another error retries once with AI_NUMERICHOST instead of AI_ADDRCONFIG. In the legacy branch (used when AI_PASSIVE is not defined) it runs the one-time lock initialisation (failure: error and 0), takes the write lock (failure: 0 with no error raised), and takes the host from a fallback address (loopback for a client lookup, any for a server lookup, an unknown lookup type asserts and raises ERR_R_INTERNAL_ERROR with ret 0) or from gethostbyname (failure raises a system error 1000 plus h_errno, or 1000 on VxWorks, or the socket error on Windows, with ret 0). It takes the port from a numeric service (1 to 65535) or, for a non-numeric service, from getservbyname with "tcp" for SOCK_STREAM, "udp" for SOCK_DGRAM or NULL otherwise; a failure of that lookup goes to the unlock with ret still 0, and a service that starts numeric but is malformed raises BIO_R_MALFORMED_HOST_OR_SERVICE, also with ret 0. It then builds a list of address records from the back of the host address list with addrinfo_wrap; on a wrap failure it frees the list, sets *res to NULL and returns 0. On success *res is the new list (to be freed with BIO_ADDRINFO_free) and ret is 1. The legacy-branch paths that acquired the lock release it at the err label (a failed lock acquisition returns before that), and the function returns ret.

functions.name: BIO_do_connect_retry
functions.prose_contract: Retries BIO_do_connect on the given BIO until it succeeds, a timeout expires or a non-retryable error occurs. Precondition: bio may be NULL (checked); timeout is in seconds (timeout <= 0 selects blocking mode, timeout > 0 sets a deadline of now+timeout, max_time 0 means no deadline); a negative nap_milliseconds is replaced by 100. Postcondition: returns -1 after raising ERR_R_PASSED_NULL_PARAMETER if bio is NULL. Otherwise it sets the BIO non-blocking flag to (timeout > 0), sets an error-queue mark and calls BIO_do_connect. If that returns > 0 it clears the mark and returns that value. If it returns <= 0 and the last error is an ERR_LIB_BIO error with reason ERR_R_SYS_LIB, BIO_R_CONNECT_ERROR or BIO_R_NBIO_CONNECT_ERROR, it calls BIO_reset and treats the failure as retryable; otherwise retryability is BIO_should_retry. If timeout >= 0 and the failure is retryable it pops the error mark and calls the static bio_wait; a positive result loops back to retry, otherwise it raises BIO_R_CONNECT_TIMEOUT (wait result 0) or BIO_R_CONNECT_ERROR and returns that wait result (0 or -1). If timeout < 0 or the failure is not retryable, it clears the mark, returns -1 and raises BIO_R_CONNECT_ERROR only when the error queue had no entry. Note that with timeout == 0 bio_wait returns 1 immediately, so a retryable failure loops without a deadline.

functions.name: acpt_state
functions.prose_contract: Runs the accept-BIO state machine on c->state until it reaches a return point. Precondition: b and c are non-NULL and c is the BIO_ACCEPT of b. Postcondition by state: ACPT_S_BEFORE fails with BIO_R_NO_ACCEPT_ADDR_OR_SERVICE_SPECIFIED (return -1) if both param_addr and param_serv are NULL, otherwise frees and NULLs the four cached name/service strings and moves to ACPT_S_GET_ADDR. ACPT_S_GET_ADDR maps accept_family to AF_INET6/AF_INET/AF_UNSPEC (unavailable or unsupported family raises an error and returns -1), calls BIO_lookup (failure returns -1) and returns -1 if the result list is empty, else moves to ACPT_S_CREATE_SOCKET. ACPT_S_CREATE_SOCKET tries BIO_socket on the current address; on failure it advances to the next address and retries, and if none remain raises BIO_R_UNABLE_TO_CREATE_SOCKET and returns -1; on success it stores the socket in c->accept_sock and b->num and moves to ACPT_S_LISTEN. ACPT_S_LISTEN calls BIO_listen and then BIO_sock_info; if either fails it closes accept_sock, sets accept_sock and b->num to INVALID_SOCKET and returns -1; on success it refreshes the cached accepting name/service, sets state ACPT_S_ACCEPT and returns 1 without accepting a connection. ACPT_S_ACCEPT: if b already has a next_bio it moves to ACPT_S_OK; otherwise it clears retry flags and cached peer strings and calls BIO_accept_ex. A negative result that BIO_sock_should_retry accepts sets the retry-special flag with retry_reason BIO_RR_ACCEPT and returns -1; any other negative result is returned as is and the listening socket is left open. On success it wraps the socket in a BIO_new_socket (BIO_CLOSE), copies b callbacks, optionally duplicates c->bio_chain and appends the socket to it, pushes the result onto b, caches the peer name/service, sets ACPT_S_OK and returns 1. Failures of BIO_new_socket, BIO_dup_chain, either BIO_push return -1 after the exit_loop cleanup, which frees the pending bio if there is one, else closes the accepted socket; when BIO_push(dbio, bio) fails the duplicated chain head dbio is not freed. ACPT_S_OK returns 1 if next_bio is set, else goes back to ACPT_S_ACCEPT. Any other state value returns 0.

functions.name: acpt_state
functions.prose_contract: Runs the accept-BIO state machine on c->state until it reaches a return point. Precondition: b and c are non-NULL and c is the BIO_ACCEPT of b. Postcondition by state: ACPT_S_BEFORE fails with BIO_R_NO_ACCEPT_ADDR_OR_SERVICE_SPECIFIED (return -1) if both param_addr and param_serv are NULL, otherwise frees and NULLs the four cached name/service strings and moves to ACPT_S_GET_ADDR. ACPT_S_GET_ADDR maps accept_family to AF_INET6/AF_INET/AF_UNSPEC (unavailable or unsupported family raises an error and returns -1), calls BIO_lookup (failure returns -1) and returns -1 if the result list is empty, else moves to ACPT_S_CREATE_SOCKET. ACPT_S_CREATE_SOCKET tries BIO_socket on the current address; on failure it advances to the next address and retries, and if none remain raises BIO_R_UNABLE_TO_CREATE_SOCKET and returns -1; on success it stores the socket in c->accept_sock and b->num and moves to ACPT_S_LISTEN. ACPT_S_LISTEN calls BIO_listen and then BIO_sock_info; if either fails it closes accept_sock, sets accept_sock and b->num to INVALID_SOCKET and returns -1; on success it refreshes the cached accepting name/service, sets state ACPT_S_ACCEPT and returns 1 without accepting a connection. ACPT_S_ACCEPT: if b already has a next_bio it moves to ACPT_S_OK; otherwise it clears retry flags and cached peer strings and calls BIO_accept_ex. A negative result that BIO_sock_should_retry accepts sets the retry-special flag with retry_reason BIO_RR_ACCEPT and returns -1; any other negative result is returned as is and the listening socket is left open. On success it wraps the socket in a BIO_new_socket (BIO_CLOSE), copies b callbacks, optionally duplicates c->bio_chain and appends the socket to it, pushes the result onto b, caches the peer name/service, sets ACPT_S_OK and returns 1. ACPT_S_OK returns 1 if next_bio is set, else goes back to ACPT_S_ACCEPT. Any other state value returns 0.

functions.name: conn_state
functions.prose_contract: Runs the connect-BIO state machine on c->state, with b the BIO and c its BIO_CONNECT, until a state returns. Precondition: b and c are non-NULL. If c->info_callback is set it is called as cb(b, c->state, ret) after each state step that ends in a plain break (a zero result from it makes the function return 0 immediately) and once more at exit_loop, whose result is returned. Initial ret is -1. BIO_CONN_S_BEFORE: both hostname and service NULL raises an error and exits with ret -1 (state unchanged), else state becomes GET_ADDR. GET_ADDR: maps connect_family to AF_INET6/AF_INET/AF_UNSPEC (unavailable or unsupported family exits), calls BIO_lookup with connect_sock_type, and exits on lookup failure or an empty result (ret -1, state unchanged); else addr_iter = addr_first and state CREATE_SOCKET. CREATE_SOCKET: BIO_socket failure raises BIO_R_UNABLE_TO_CREATE_SOCKET and exits with ret equal to the failed socket value, state unchanged; success stores the socket in b->num and moves to CONNECT. CONNECT: clears retry flags, calls BIO_connect (adding BIO_SOCK_KEEPALIVE for SOCK_STREAM). If it returns 0 and BIO_sock_should_retry, it sets the retry-special flag, state BLOCKED_CONNECT, retry_reason BIO_RR_CONNECT and exits with ret 0; if it returns 0 and another address exists it closes the socket and goes back to CREATE_SOCKET; if it returns 0 with no more addresses it raises a sys error and sets state CONNECT_ERROR. A nonzero result goes on to conn_create_dgram_bio (which, for SOCK_DGRAM only, creates c->dgram_bio from b->num and on failure sets state CONNECT_ERROR) and then state OK. BLOCKED_CONNECT: if BIO_socket_wait on b->num returns 0 it just loops; else BIO_sock_error: nonzero moves to the next address (close socket, CREATE_SOCKET) or, with none left, raises BIO_R_NBIO_CONNECT_ERROR and exits with ret 0; zero goes through dgram creation to state OK. CONNECT_ERROR raises BIO_R_CONNECT_ERROR and exits with ret 0. OK exits with ret 1. An unrecognised state exits with whatever ret holds (-1 on a fresh call).

functions.name: file_ctrl
functions.prose_contract: Control dispatcher of the file BIO. Precondition: b is non-NULL; for the seek, tell, eof and flush commands b->ptr must be a valid FILE * (or an uplink handle when BIO_FLAGS_UPLINK_INTERNAL is set); for BIO_C_SET_FILENAME ptr must be a NUL-terminated file name. The return value is a long chosen by cmd, defaulting to 1: BIO_C_FILE_SEEK and BIO_CTRL_RESET return the result of fseek(fp, num, 0) (0 on success, nonzero on failure); BIO_CTRL_EOF returns feof(fp); BIO_C_FILE_TELL and BIO_CTRL_INFO return ftell(fp) (on Windows builds -1 for a non-disk handle); BIO_C_SET_FILE_PTR calls file_free(b), sets b->shutdown to (num & BIO_CLOSE), b->ptr to ptr and b->init to 1, adjusts text/binary mode on some platforms, and returns 1; BIO_C_SET_FILENAME calls file_free(b), sets b->shutdown, builds the fopen mode from num (BIO_FP_APPEND, BIO_FP_READ, BIO_FP_WRITE) and, if no valid combination is set, raises BIO_R_BAD_FOPEN_MODE and returns 0; otherwise it calls openssl_fopen, and on failure raises sys/BIO errors and returns 0 with b->ptr and b->init not set by this call, while on success it stores the FILE in b->ptr, sets b->init to 1, clears BIO_FLAGS_UPLINK_INTERNAL and returns 1; BIO_C_GET_FILE_PTR stores b->ptr into *ptr when ptr is non-NULL and returns 1; BIO_CTRL_GET_CLOSE returns b->shutdown; BIO_CTRL_SET_CLOSE sets b->shutdown = num and returns 1; BIO_CTRL_FLUSH returns 1 if fflush does not return EOF, otherwise raises errors and returns 0; BIO_CTRL_DUP returns 1; BIO_CTRL_WPENDING, BIO_CTRL_PENDING, BIO_CTRL_PUSH, BIO_CTRL_POP and any unrecognised cmd return 0.

functions.name: BN_BLINDING_update
functions.prose_contract: Advances a BN_BLINDING after one use. Precondition: b and ctx are non-NULL. If b->A or b->Ai is NULL it raises BN_R_NOT_INITIALIZED and returns 0 (via the err label). Otherwise it sets counter to 0 if it was -1, then increments it. If the incremented counter equals BN_BLINDING_COUNTER and b->e is non-NULL and BN_BLINDING_NO_RECREATE is not set, it calls BN_BLINDING_create_param to regenerate A and Ai (return 0 if that fails). Otherwise, unless BN_BLINDING_NO_UPDATE is set, it squares Ai and A modulo b->mod (using bn_mul_mont_fixed_top when b->m_ctx is set, else BN_mod_mul), returning 0 if a multiplication fails; with NO_UPDATE set it leaves A and Ai untouched. On success it returns 1. At the err label, which both the success and failure paths reach, a counter equal to BN_BLINDING_COUNTER is reset to 0, so b->counter can change even on the NULL-A/Ai error path when the counter was already at that value.

functions.name: bn_div_fixed_top
functions.prose_contract: Schoolbook long division of num by divisor that leaves its results in fixed-top form (not normalised). Precondition: num, divisor and ctx are valid, divisor->top > 0 with a non-zero top limb (asserted only in debug builds), dv and rm each NULL or a BIGNUM. It starts a BN_CTX frame, uses dv (or a ctx temporary when dv is NULL) as quotient, copies divisor into a temporary, left-aligns it (norm_shift) and clears its sign, and left-shifts num by norm_shift into a second temporary snum; if snum is not longer than the divisor it is zero-padded to div_n+1 limbs. It then computes loop = num_n - div_n quotient limbs, each by estimating q from the top limbs of the window, multiplying and subtracting the divisor, and adding it back if the estimate was too large. The quotient gets sign (num->neg XOR divisor->neg), top = loop and BN_FLG_FIXED_TOP; the remainder (snum, sign of num, top = div_n, FIXED_TOP) is shifted back right by norm_shift into rm when rm is non-NULL. Returns 1 on success; returns 0 if any ctx allocation, BN_copy, shift, or bn_wexpand fails, or if the final right shift into rm fails, ending the ctx frame in both cases. Neither the quotient nor the remainder is stripped of leading zero limbs and divisor zero is not checked here.

functions.name: BN_mod_inverse
functions.prose_contract: Public wrapper that solves a*x == 1 (mod n) by delegating to int_bn_mod_inverse. Precondition: a and n are valid BIGNUMs, in is NULL or a caller-owned BIGNUM for the result, ctx is NULL or a valid BN_CTX. If ctx is NULL it allocates a temporary one with BN_CTX_new_ex and, if that fails, raises ERR_R_BN_LIB and returns NULL. It then calls int_bn_mod_inverse with a local flag noinv initialised to 0; if the callee leaves noinv non-zero (it sets it to 1 for n == 0 or |n| == 1, and when the gcd of a and n is not 1) the wrapper raises BN_R_NO_INVERSE. It frees the temporary ctx (if it created one) and returns the callee result unchanged: the inverse, stored in in when in is non-NULL and otherwise in a newly allocated BIGNUM, or NULL on failure. Failures other than no-inverse (allocation or arithmetic errors inside the callee) return NULL without BN_R_NO_INVERSE being raised here.

functions.name: bn_mul_fixed_top
functions.prose_contract: Multiplies a by b into r and leaves r in fixed-top form. Precondition: a, b and r are valid BIGNUMs (r may be the same object as a or b) and ctx is a valid BN_CTX. If a->top or b->top is 0 it calls BN_zero(r) and returns 1 at once, without touching ctx. Otherwise it starts a ctx frame and, when r aliases a or b, computes into a ctx temporary rr (return 0 if the temporary cannot be obtained). It picks the algorithm by size: a Comba 8x8 multiply when both have 8 limbs (BN_MUL_COMBA builds), recursive Karatsuba (bn_mul_recursive or bn_mul_part_recursive) when both are at least BN_MULL_SIZE_NORMAL limbs and differ by at most one limb (BN_RECURSION builds), else schoolbook bn_mul_normal; each path grows the result with bn_wexpand and returns 0 if that fails. The result has top = a->top + b->top (not stripped of leading zeros), sign a->neg XOR b->neg and BN_FLG_FIXED_TOP; if a temporary was used it is copied into r with BN_copy (return 0 on failure). Returns 1 on success and ends the ctx frame at the err label, which both its success and error exits reach.

functions.name: BN_mod_sqrt
functions.prose_contract: Tries to compute r with r^2 == a (mod p) by the Tonelli/Shanks method; p is expected to be prime but this is not checked beyond a few detections. Precondition: a, p valid BIGNUMs, in NULL or a caller-owned BIGNUM for the result, ctx a valid BN_CTX (used only past the first two special cases). Return: the root in in (if non-NULL) or a newly allocated BIGNUM, or NULL on failure. Early cases that do not touch ctx: if p is even or |p| == 1, then |p| == 2 gives r = (a & 1) (a mod 2 is not computed beyond testing bit 0), and any other such p raises BN_R_P_IS_NOT_PRIME and returns NULL; if a is exactly 0 or 1 the result is 0 or 1 (returned without reducing mod p). Otherwise A = a mod p is computed; with e the number of trailing zero bits of |p|-1 after the lowest: e == 1 uses a single modular exponentiation to (|p|+1)/4; e == 2 uses the Atkin formula; e > 2 searches y = 2..81 for a quadratic non-residue with BN_kronecker (small integers below 22, then random values), raising BN_R_P_IS_NOT_PRIME if the Kronecker symbol is 0 or y^q == 1 and BN_R_TOO_MANY_ITERATIONS if none is found, then runs the Shanks loop, which returns 0 when A is 0 mod p and raises BN_R_NOT_A_SQUARE when no suitable power of two exponent is found. Except for the 0-mod-p shortcut and the |p| == 2 and a in {0,1} cases, the result of the e == 1, e == 2 and Shanks paths is verified by squaring it mod p and comparing with A; a mismatch raises BN_R_NOT_A_SQUARE and returns NULL. On any failure after allocation a BIGNUM created here is freed with BN_clear_free, a caller-supplied in is not freed (but may already have been overwritten), and the ctx frame is ended.

functions.name: DEFINE_OSSL_CMP_CTX_get1_certs(newChain)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function OSSL_CMP_CTX_get1_newChain (expanded from DEFINE_OSSL_CMP_CTX_get1_certs(newChain)). Returns an owned copy of the certificate stack ctx->newChain. If ctx is NULL it raises CMP_R_NULL_ARGUMENT and returns NULL. Otherwise it returns X509_chain_up_ref(ctx->newChain): a duplicate of the stack in which every certificate has its reference count incremented, which the caller must release (for example with OSSL_STACK_OF_X509_free). If ctx->newChain is NULL the duplicate is a new empty stack, not NULL; NULL is returned only when the stack duplication or one of the reference increments fails (in which case the partial copy is released).
