functions.name: get_genm_itav
functions.prose_contract: Sends a GENM request carrying the ITAV req and returns the first ITAV of the GENP response whose infoType NID equals expected (desc names the type in log and error text). Precondition: req is an ITAV whose ownership is passed to this function; ctx is expected non-NULL with status OSSL_CMP_PKISTATUS_unspecified. If ctx is NULL (CMP_R_NULL_ARGUMENT) or its status is anything else (CMP_R_UNCLEAN_CTX), or OSSL_CMP_CTX_push0_genm_ITAV fails, it frees req and returns NULL. Once push0 succeeds ownership of req belongs to ctx, and req is not freed here on any later path. It then runs OSSL_CMP_exec_GENM_ses; if that returns NULL it returns NULL, raising CMP_R_GETTING_GENP only when ctx status is not OSSL_CMP_PKISTATUS_request (so no error is raised in that status). An empty response raises CMP_R_INVALID_GENP and returns NULL. Otherwise it shifts ITAVs off the response list one by one (logging a warning when there is more than one ITAV, and a warning for each non-matching infoType, freeing the non-matching ones); on the first match it frees the remaining ITAVs and the list and returns the matching ITAV, which the caller owns. If none matches it raises CMP_R_INVALID_GENP and returns NULL (the list is freed at the err label).

functions.name: check_msg_all_certs
functions.prose_contract: Tries to find a sender certificate that authenticates msg and passes path validation, searching three certificate sources in turn. Precondition: ctx and msg are non-NULL; mode_3gpp is 0 for normal mode or non-zero for the exceptional 3GPP mode. If ctx->permitTAInExtraCertsForIR is set and the message body type is OSSL_CMP_PKIBODY_IP it only logs which mode it is trying; otherwise, if mode_3gpp is non-zero, it returns 0 immediately. It then calls check_msg_with_certs on msg->extraCerts, then on ctx->untrusted (skipping certs already checked from extraCerts), and returns 1 as soon as one of these succeeds. A call succeeds when some acceptable cert (per cert_acceptable) has a validated path (check_cert_path against ctx->trusted in normal mode, check_cert_path_3gpp in 3GPP mode) and ossl_cmp_ctx_set1_validatedSrvCert stores it in ctx. In 3GPP mode, path validation uses a store built only from self-issued extraCerts and, for an IP message, additionally requires that the newly enrolled certificate in the response also validates against that store. If both fail and ctx->trusted is NULL it logs a warning and returns 0; otherwise it runs check_msg_with_certs over all certificates of ctx->trusted (self-issued extraCerts description in 3GPP mode), frees that temporary stack and returns the result (1 or 0).

functions.name: ossl_cms_env_asn1_ctrl
functions.prose_contract: Dispatches a CMS envelope control command (cmd) to the key-type specific handler for the recipient key. Precondition: ri is non-NULL. It selects the key: for CMS_RECIPINFO_TRANS the key is ri->d.ktri->pkey (not NULL-checked here); for CMS_RECIPINFO_AGREE it is the key of ri->d.kari->pctx, returning 0 if that pctx or its key is NULL; any other recipient type returns 0. For a DH or DHX key it returns the result of ossl_cms_dh_envelope(ri, cmd); for EC, ossl_cms_ecdh_envelope; for RSA, ossl_cms_rsa_envelope. For any other key type, if the key has no ameth or no ameth->pkey_ctrl it returns 1 without doing anything; otherwise it calls pkey_ctrl(pkey, ASN1_PKEY_CTRL_CMS_ENVELOPE, cmd, ri) and returns 0 with CMS_R_NOT_SUPPORTED_FOR_THIS_KEY_TYPE if that returns -2, 0 with CMS_R_CTRL_FAILURE if it returns <= 0 (other than -2), and 1 otherwise.

functions.name: module_init
functions.prose_contract: Initialises one configuration module instance for pmod with the given name and value, and records it in the global initialized-modules list. Precondition: pmod, name, value are non-NULL (cnf is passed through to the module init callback). It allocates a CONF_IMODULE and duplicates name and value. If pmod->init is non-NULL it is called with the new imod and cnf; a result <= 0 is treated as failure. It then runs the one-time init of the list lock (failure is a failure), takes the RCU write lock, copies the current initialized_modules stack (or creates a new one), pushes imod, increments pmod->links, publishes the new stack, and after RCU synchronisation frees the old stack copy. On success it returns pmod->init result (a value > 0) or 1 when pmod->init is NULL. Failures return -1: allocation of imod, name or value fails (no finish call, no error raised here); init returns <= 0, the lock initialisation fails, or the stack copy or push fails (the latter two raise ERR_R_CRYPTO_LIB only for the copy/push). In the failure paths after init was called it calls pmod->finish(imod) when that callback is non-NULL, then frees imod and its strings; pmod->links is not incremented on failure.

functions.name: ossl_method_construct_precondition
functions.prose_contract: Decides whether methods for an operation should be constructed. Precondition: result may be NULL (checked); cbdata points to a construct_data_st (only its force_store field is read, through is_temporary_method_store); provider must be valid whenever the store is not temporary. The store is temporary exactly when no_store is non-zero and cbdata->force_store is zero. If result is NULL it raises ERR_R_PASSED_NULL_PARAMETER and returns 0. Otherwise it sets *result to 0; if the store is not temporary (no_store == 0, or force_store set) it asks ossl_provider_test_operation_bit(provider, operation_id, result) and returns 0 if that call fails (leaving *result as set by that call or 0). It then sets *result to the logical negation of *result and returns 1. So *result is 1 (construct) for a temporary store without consulting the provider, and for a non-temporary store when the provider operation bit is not set; it is 0 when the bit is set.

functions.name: ossl_ec_GF2m_simple_oct2point
functions.prose_contract: Decodes the X9.62 octet string buf of length len into a point on a binary-field (GF(2^m)) curve. Precondition: group, point and buf are non-NULL and buf holds len bytes; ctx may be NULL (a temporary BN_CTX is then created in non-FIPS builds). Returns 0 with an error raised (EC_R_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL for len == 0) before anything else is touched. The first byte gives the form (0x00 infinity, 0x02/0x03 compressed, 0x04 uncompressed, 0x06/0x07 hybrid) and the low bit y_bit; any other form, or y_bit set with form 0 or 0x04, returns 0 (EC_R_INVALID_ENCODING). For form 0 the length must be exactly 1 and the result is EC_POINT_set_to_infinity(group, point). Otherwise len must equal 1 + field_len (compressed) or 1 + 2*field_len, with field_len = (degree+7)/8, else returns 0. It then reads x (and y for non-compressed forms) with BN_bin2bn, rejecting any coordinate with more than m bits; for compressed form it calls EC_POINT_set_compressed_coordinates with y_bit; for hybrid form it checks y_bit against x==0 (y_bit must be 0) or against the parity of y/x, returning 0 on mismatch; for uncompressed and hybrid forms it finally calls EC_POINT_set_affine_coordinates, which is relied on to check that the point is on the curve. Returns 1 only when that last step succeeds (or the infinity case), and 0 on any failure; the ctx frame and any temporary ctx are released on the paths after they were created (the early returns happen before they exist).

functions.name: ossl_ec_key_public_check
functions.prose_contract: Full public key validation of an EC_KEY (SP 800-56A 5.6.2.3.3). Precondition: eckey must be non-NULL (it is dereferenced for eckey->group on the first line, before any NULL test), and its group and pub_key should be set; ctx is passed to the arithmetic. It first calls ossl_ec_key_public_check_quick, which returns 0 (with errors raised) if eckey, its group or its pub_key is NULL, the public point is infinity, its coordinates are out of range or it is not on the curve. If the group cofactor is non-NULL and equals 1 it returns 1 at that point without the order check. Otherwise it allocates a temporary point (returning 0 without raising an error here if EC_POINT_new fails), returns 0 with EC_R_INVALID_GROUP_ORDER if the group order is zero, computes pub_key * order with EC_POINT_mul (0 with ERR_R_EC_LIB if that fails), and returns 0 with EC_R_WRONG_ORDER unless that product is the point at infinity; otherwise returns 1. The temporary point is freed at the err label, which the success and error exits after its creation reach; the key is not modified.

functions.name: EC_KEY_set_group
functions.prose_contract: Replaces the group of key with a duplicate of group. Precondition: key and group are non-NULL and key->meth is set. If key->meth->set_group exists and returns 0 it returns 0 and key is unchanged. Otherwise it releases the key old group reference with EC_GROUP_free(key->group), stores EC_GROUP_dup(group) as the new group (the result is not checked before the following step), and if that group is non-NULL and its curve name is NID_sm2 sets EC_FLAG_SM2_RANGE on the key. It then increments key->dirty_cnt unconditionally (also when the dup failed) and returns 0 if the duplicate is NULL (key->group is then NULL), else 1. The caller reference to group is not consumed; if group is the same object as key->group and the key held its only reference, freeing it before the dup happens first (line 772 before 773).

functions.name: pkey_ec_ctrl
functions.prose_contract: Control dispatcher for the legacy EC EVP_PKEY method; ctx->data is the EC_PKEY_CTX. Return value by type: PARAMGEN_CURVE_NID looks up the curve p1 (EC_R_INVALID_CURVE and 0 if unknown), frees the old gen_group, stores the new one and returns 1. PARAM_ENC returns 0 with EC_R_NO_PARAMETERS_SET if gen_group is NULL, else sets its ASN1 flag to p1 and returns 1. ECDH_COFACTOR with p1 == -2 queries: returns cofactor_mode if it is not -1, otherwise 1 or 0 according to EC_FLAG_COFACTOR_ECDH on the pkey EC key. For other p1: values outside -1..1 return -2; otherwise cofactor_mode is set to p1 first, and then for p1 != -1 it returns 0 (ERR_R_UNSUPPORTED) if the pkey is a provided key (cofactor_mode stays changed), -2 if the EC key has no group, 1 if the group cofactor is 1, 0 if duplicating the key fails, else it sets or clears EC_FLAG_COFACTOR_ECDH on the duplicate co_key and returns 1; for p1 == -1 it frees co_key and returns 1. KDF_TYPE with p1 == -2 returns the current kdf_type; values other than NONE and X9_63 return -2, else stored and 1. KDF_MD stores p2 and returns 1; GET_EC_KDF_MD writes the kdf_md pointer to *p2 and returns 1. KDF_OUTLEN returns -2 if p1 <= 0, else stores it and returns 1; GET_EC_KDF_OUTLEN writes the outlen as int to *p2 and returns 1. KDF_UKM frees the previous kdf_ukm, takes ownership of p2 (pointer stored, length p1, or 0 if p2 is NULL) and returns 1; GET_EC_KDF_UKM writes the pointer to *p2 and returns kdf_ukmlen. CTRL_MD accepts only SHA-1, ECDSA-with-SHA1, SHA-2 and SHA-3 digests and SM3 (else EC_R_INVALID_DIGEST_TYPE and 0) and stores it, returning 1; GET_MD writes md to *p2 and returns 1. PEER_KEY, DIGESTINIT, PKCS7_SIGN and CMS_SIGN return 1 and do nothing; any other type returns -2.

functions.name: decoder_process
functions.prose_contract: Recursive worker of the OSSL_DECODER chain, used both for the first call (params == NULL) and as the data callback that each decoder implementation calls with the object it decoded. Precondition: arg points to a decoder_process_data_st with valid ctx and bio. At entry it sets data->flag_next_level_called = 1 and remembers ctx->start_input_type. If params == NULL (first level) it sets current_decoder_inst_index to the number of decoders and does not touch flag_construct_called. Otherwise it picks the decoder instance at current_decoder_inst_index, clears flag_construct_called, and if ctx->construct is set calls it; a result > 0 sets flag_construct_called = 1 and the function returns 1 (end). If construct is absent or does not succeed it requires an OSSL_OBJECT_PARAM_DATA octet string in params (otherwise returns 0), wraps it in a new memory BIO, reads optional data type, data structure and input type parameters (a failed read returns 0), may overwrite ctx->start_input_type and set flag_input_structure_checked, and drops a "type-specific" data structure when a data type exists. It then returns 0 if no decoder instances remain below the current index, or if BIO_tell on the input fails or the core BIO cannot be created. Otherwise it walks the instances below the current index downwards, skipping each whose input type, data type, input structure or user-requested structure does not match; for a candidate it BIO_seek()s back to the saved position (returning the current ok value, without trying more, if BIO_tell then differs), sets a new recursion level and calls that decoder decode with decoder_process as callback, setting data->flag_construct_called from the recursive state. The loop stops after a decode that returned 0 or after a construct was called (error mark cleared), and after a decode that recursed (flag_next_level_called). The return value is the ok of the last decode attempted (so 1 can be returned when a decoder reported success without an object being constructed, and 0 when no instance matched or the last attempt failed). At the end label (which all exits go through) it frees the core BIO and the in-memory BIO it created (not the caller bio) and restores ctx->start_input_type.

functions.name: encoder_process
functions.prose_contract: Recursive worker that selects a chain of encoder instances and runs them to produce the output. Precondition: data points to a valid encoder_process_data_st; the call with data->next_encoder_inst == NULL is the top level, which sets count_output_structure to -1 (no output structure requested) or 0 and writes its output to data->bio. The return value is 1 when an encoder ran successfully, 0 when a chosen encoder or its setup failed, and -1 when the instance lookup found nothing usable at this level (the caller then treats its own encoder as the first in the chain). It scans instances from index current_encoder_inst_index-1 downward; at the top level it skips instances whose output type differs from ctx->output_type, deeper it skips instances whose output type is not the name of the next encoder; if both ctx->output_structure and the instance structure are set it skips mismatches and counts matches. For each candidate it recurses; a recursive result of 0 is skipped and the scan continues, any other result stops the scan. If the scan ends without a candidate (including when a recursive failure was the last one tried) the function returns -1. Otherwise: for a recursive result of -1 it returns 0 at once if a structure was requested but none matched (count_output_structure == 0), else calls ctx->construct to build the object (NULL gives 0) and records the encoder name as data_type; for a recursive result of 1 it builds an object abstraction from the previous output (running_output) or, if that is NULL, raises an internal error and gives 0. If ok is non-zero it then encodes: at the top level into data->bio, deeper into a new memory BIO (failure to create it or the core BIO gives 0), and calls the instance encode. Finally it frees the previous running_output, hands the memory BIO contents (when one was created) to data->running_output, frees the BIO, calls ctx->cleanup when an object was constructed, and returns ok. At the top level on success running_output is therefore NULL after return.

functions.name: ENGINE_ctrl_cmd
functions.prose_contract: Runs the named control command of an ENGINE with a numeric argument i, pointer p and function pointer f. Precondition: e and cmd_name are non-NULL, otherwise it raises ERR_R_PASSED_NULL_PARAMETER and returns 0. It resolves the command number with ENGINE_ctrl(e, ENGINE_CTRL_GET_CMD_FROM_NAME, 0, cmd_name, NULL). If e->ctrl is NULL or the lookup returns <= 0 (command unknown), then when cmd_optional is non-zero it clears the error queue and returns 1 (pretending success), and otherwise raises ENGINE_R_INVALID_CMD_NAME and returns 0. If the command is found it calls ENGINE_ctrl(e, num, i, p, f) and returns 1 if that result is > 0 and 0 otherwise; the engine own return value is not passed back. It does not check whether the command is executable.

functions.name: IMPLEMENT_LEGACY_ERR_LOAD(ASN1)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function ERR_load_ASN1_strings (from IMPLEMENT_LEGACY_ERR_LOAD(ASN1), err_all_legacy.c:53-57, compiled only when OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_3_0 is not defined). Takes no arguments. When error strings are enabled it returns the result of ossl_err_load_ASN1_strings(); when OPENSSL_NO_ERR is defined (macro at lines 47-51) it simply returns 1. ossl_err_load_ASN1_strings registers the ASN1_str_reasons table with ERR_load_strings_const only if the first reason string is not yet known (ERR_reason_error_string returns NULL), ignores the result of that registration, and returns 1. So the generated function returns 1 in both configurations and has the side effect of registering the library error strings when they are absent.

functions.name: IMPLEMENT_LEGACY_ERR_LOAD(CRYPTO)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function ERR_load_CRYPTO_strings (from IMPLEMENT_LEGACY_ERR_LOAD(CRYPTO), err_all_legacy.c:53-57, compiled only when OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_3_0 is not defined). Takes no arguments. When error strings are enabled it returns the result of ossl_err_load_CRYPTO_strings(); when OPENSSL_NO_ERR is defined (macro at lines 47-51) it simply returns 1. ossl_err_load_CRYPTO_strings registers the CRYPTO_str_reasons table with ERR_load_strings_const only if the first reason string is not yet known (ERR_reason_error_string returns NULL), ignores the result of that registration, and returns 1. So the generated function returns 1 in both configurations and has the side effect of registering the library error strings when they are absent.

functions.name: enc_ctrl
functions.prose_contract: Control dispatcher of the cipher filter BIO. Precondition: b is non-NULL; if its BIO_ENC_CTX data is NULL it returns 0 at once. Default return value is 1. BIO_CTRL_RESET sets ok = 1 and finished = 0, re-initialises the cipher keeping the current direction (returning 0 if EVP_CipherInit_ex fails) and otherwise returns the result of BIO_ctrl on the next BIO. BIO_CTRL_EOF returns 1 when ctx->cont <= 0, else the next BIO result. BIO_CTRL_WPENDING and BIO_CTRL_PENDING return buf_len - buf_off if that is positive, otherwise the next BIO result. BIO_CTRL_FLUSH first loops calling enc_write(b, NULL, 0) while buffered bytes remain, returning that call result i if it is negative or if no bytes were written in the call; then, if not yet finished, marks finished, calls EVP_CipherFinal_ex into the buffer and stores its result in ctx->ok (a result <= 0 is returned as the control result without flushing further), writes out the final bytes by repeating the loop, and finally flushes the next BIO, returning its result and copying its retry flags. BIO_C_GET_CIPHER_STATUS returns ctx->ok. BIO_C_DO_STATE_MACHINE clears retry flags, forwards to the next BIO, and copies its retry flags. BIO_C_GET_CIPHER_CTX stores ctx->cipher in *ptr, marks the BIO initialised and returns 1. BIO_CTRL_DUP allocates a cipher context in the duplicate BIO data (returning 0 if that fails), copies the cipher context into it and returns the copy result, marking the duplicate initialised if it succeeded. Any other command is forwarded to the next BIO.

functions.name: md_ctrl
functions.prose_contract: Control dispatcher of the message-digest filter BIO; ctx is the EVP_MD_CTX in the BIO data and next the following BIO. Default result is 1. BIO_CTRL_RESET: if the BIO is initialised it re-runs EVP_DigestInit_ex with the digest already in ctx, else the result is 0; if that result is positive it returns the result of BIO_ctrl on the next BIO, otherwise it returns the failed value. BIO_C_GET_MD: if initialised, stores the ctx digest pointer into *ptr (ptr is a const EVP_MD **) and returns 1, else returns 0. BIO_C_GET_MD_CTX stores ctx into *ptr (an EVP_MD_CTX **), marks the BIO initialised and returns 1. BIO_C_SET_MD_CTX: if initialised, replaces the BIO data pointer with ptr and returns 1, else returns 0. BIO_C_DO_STATE_MACHINE clears the BIO retry flags, forwards to the next BIO and copies the next BIO retry flags back, returning the next BIO result. BIO_C_SET_MD treats ptr itself as the EVP_MD and calls EVP_DigestInit_ex(ctx, ptr, NULL); the BIO is marked initialised only if that returns a positive value, and the init result is returned. BIO_CTRL_DUP copies ctx into the duplicate BIO data context (ptr is the duplicate BIO), returning 0 if the copy fails, otherwise marking b (the source BIO) as initialised and returning 1. Any other command is forwarded to the next BIO and its result returned.

functions.name: fix_ecdh_cofactor
functions.prose_contract: Translation fixup for EVP_PKEY_CTRL_EC_ECDH_COFACTOR, which serves as both setter and getter. Precondition: state is one of the translation states and ctx is the translation context; ctx->p1 is -2 to query the cofactor mode, otherwise it is the new mode. Behaviour by state: PRE_CTRL_TO_PARAMS first requires ctx->action_type == OSSL_ACTION_NONE (assert failure returns 0) and sets action GET when p1 == -2, else SET; PRE_CTRL_STR_TO_PARAMS sets action SET; PRE_PARAMS_TO_CTRL requires a non-NONE action (else returns 0); POST_PARAMS_TO_CTRL with action NONE sets action GET. It then calls default_check and returns its value if that is <= 0. For PRE_CTRL_TO_PARAMS with action SET and p1 outside -1..1 it returns -2. Then it calls default_fixup_args and returns its value if that is <= 0 (this may be negative, not just 0). Finally: in POST_CTRL_TO_PARAMS with action GET, a p1 value outside 0..1 sets p1 and the result to -1; in PRE_PARAMS_TO_CTRL with action GET it sets p1 = -2; in POST_PARAMS_TO_CTRL with action GET it sets p1 to the fixup result. It returns the last fixup result (or -1 as stated).

functions.name: fix_oid
functions.prose_contract: Translation fixup for the OID-valued controls (e.g. DH KDF OID), converting between an ASN1_OBJECT and its textual name. Precondition: ctx is the translation context. It calls default_check and returns its value if that is <= 0 (including negative values). Then, for PRE_CTRL_TO_PARAMS with action SET or POST_PARAMS_TO_CTRL with action GET, it treats ctx->p2 as an ASN1_OBJECT, writes its text form into ctx->name_buf with OBJ_obj2txt (result not checked), points p2 at that buffer and sets p1 to 0 so the default fixup works out the length. It then calls default_fixup_args and returns its value if <= 0. Finally, for PRE_PARAMS_TO_CTRL with action SET or POST_CTRL_TO_PARAMS with action GET, it replaces ctx->p2 (a name string at that point) with the ASN1_OBJECT from OBJ_txt2obj(p2, 0) (possibly NULL; the object is not freed here). It returns the value from default_fixup_args (positive).

functions.name: EVP_MD_CTX_ctrl
functions.prose_contract: Sends a control command to a digest context. Precondition: ctx may be NULL; for the provider path p1/p2 are interpreted per command. If ctx is NULL it raises ERR_R_PASSED_NULL_PARAMETER and returns 0. If ctx->digest is non-NULL and has no provider (a legacy digest) it requires ctx->digest->md_ctrl (else raises EVP_R_CTRL_NOT_IMPLEMENTED and returns 0) and passes cmd, p1 and p2 unchanged to it, whatever the cmd. Otherwise (provider digest, or ctx->digest NULL) it translates three commands to parameters: EVP_MD_CTRL_XOF_LEN (XOF length p1) and EVP_CTRL_SSL3_MASTER_SECRET (octet string p2 of length p1) are applied with EVP_MD_CTX_set_params, and EVP_MD_CTRL_MICALG (output string in p2, buffer length p1, or 9999 when p1 is 0) is fetched with EVP_MD_CTX_get_params; any other cmd on this path is unsupported. In every case a result <= 0 is returned as 0 (including the unsupported-command value and a negative legacy result), and a positive result is returned unchanged (the legacy md_ctrl positive value, or the 1 from the params call).

functions.name: s390x_aes_ccm_cipher
functions.prose_contract: Cipher entry point of the s390x hardware AES-CCM implementation, covering update, AAD and final calls depending on in/out. Precondition: ctx holds an S390X_AES_CCM_CTX. Checks in order: key not set returns -1; if tls_aad_len >= 0 (TLS mode) it returns the result of s390x_aes_ccm_tls_cipher; in == NULL with out != NULL (final call, which returns no data) returns 0; iv not set returns -1. With out == NULL: in == NULL passes the message length len to s390x_aes_ccm_setiv using ctx->iv, sets len_set and returns len; otherwise (AAD) it returns -1 if len is non-zero and the message length was not set, else processes the AAD and returns len. With out != NULL (message data): when decrypting and the tag is not set it returns -1; if the message length was not yet set it sets it from len. Encrypt: s390x_aes_ccm failing returns -1, otherwise tag_set is set to 1 and len is returned. Decrypt: the result is len only if s390x_aes_ccm succeeds and the computed tag (kmac_param.icv) equals the stored tag over m bytes (CRYPTO_memcmp), else -1 with out cleansed over len bytes; in both cases iv_set, tag_set and len_set are reset to 0 before returning.

functions.name: aes_gcm_cipher
functions.prose_contract: Generic AES-GCM cipher entry point covering update, AAD and final calls. Precondition: ctx holds an EVP_AES_GCM_CTX. Returns -1 if the key has not been set. If tls_aad_len >= 0 (TLS mode) it returns the result of aes_gcm_tls_cipher. Otherwise it needs an IV: in non-FIPS builds a missing IV returns -1; in FIPS builds a missing IV is generated inside the module when encrypting (aes_gcm_iv_generate), returning -1 if decrypting or if generation fails. If in != NULL: with out == NULL the data is AAD passed to CRYPTO_gcm128_aad (non-zero result returns -1); with out != NULL it encrypts or decrypts len bytes with the ctr32 or generic GCM routines, optionally first handling a partial block and then bulk assembly code for len >= 32 (encrypt) or len >= 16 (decrypt) where compiled in; any failing CRYPTO_gcm128_* call returns -1, otherwise it returns len. If in == NULL (final call, whatever out is): when decrypting it returns -1 if taglen < 0 or CRYPTO_gcm128_finish over the stored tag fails, else clears iv_set and returns 0; when encrypting it writes a 16-byte tag into the context buffer, sets taglen to 16, clears iv_set and returns 0.

functions.name: aes_ocb_cipher
functions.prose_contract: AES-OCB cipher entry point for AAD, data and final calls; it buffers partial blocks so the low-level OCB code only sees whole 16-byte blocks. Returns -1 if the IV or the key is not set. With in != NULL: out == NULL means AAD (buffer aad_buf), out != NULL means data (buffer data_buf; a partial overlap of out and in raises EVP_R_PARTIALLY_OVERLAPPING and returns 0). If a partial block is already buffered and the new input does not fill it, the input is appended and 0 is returned; otherwise the buffer is completed and processed (CRYPTO_ocb128_aad, _encrypt or _decrypt, a zero result returns -1), counting 16 bytes. Remaining whole blocks are processed the same way; a trailing partial block is copied into the buffer. It returns the number of bytes processed in this call (for data, the bytes written to out; for AAD, the AAD bytes consumed, nothing is written). With in == NULL (final): buffered data is encrypted or decrypted into out (-1 on failure) and counted, buffered AAD is passed to CRYPTO_ocb128_aad (-1 on failure); when decrypting it returns -1 if taglen < 0 or CRYPTO_ocb128_finish on the stored tag fails (tag mismatch), else clears iv_set and returns the number of buffered data bytes written; when encrypting it computes a 16-byte tag with CRYPTO_ocb128_tag (-1 if that does not return 1), clears iv_set and returns the buffered data bytes written.

functions.name: aesni_cbc_hmac_sha1_ctrl
functions.prose_contract: Control function of the AES-NI CBC + HMAC-SHA1 cipher. By type: EVP_CTRL_AEAD_SET_MAC_KEY (ptr holds arg key bytes): a key longer than 64 bytes is first hashed with SHA1, otherwise zero-padded; it initialises key->head with the ipad state and key->tail with the opad state, wipes the temporary key and returns 1. EVP_CTRL_AEAD_TLS1_AAD (ptr is the 13-byte TLS record header, arg must equal EVP_AEAD_TLS1_AAD_LEN else returns -1): when encrypting it stores the header payload length in key->payload_length and the TLS version in key->aux.tls_ver; if the version is at least TLS1.1 and the length is < 16 it returns 0 after those two fields were already changed, else it subtracts 16 from the length and rewrites the length bytes in the caller header buffer ptr; it then sets key->md = key->head, feeds the (possibly rewritten) header into it and returns the padding that will be added (bytes to the next 16-byte boundary after length + 20-byte digest, as a positive int). When decrypting it copies the header into key->aux.tls_aad, sets key->payload_length = arg and returns SHA_DIGEST_LENGTH (20). With multiblock support compiled in: EVP_CTRL_TLS1_1_MULTIBLOCK_MAX_BUFSIZE returns 5 + 16 + ((arg + 20 + 16) & -16); EVP_CTRL_TLS1_1_MULTIBLOCK_AAD returns -1 if arg is smaller than the param struct, if encrypting with a record version below TLS1.1 or with a non-zero inp_len absent and interleave/4 equal to 0 or above 2, and returns 0 when a given inp_len is below 4096; on success it sets key->md from head plus the 13-byte header, sets param->interleave and returns the packet length computed for the fragment layout; decrypting returns -1; EVP_CTRL_TLS1_1_MULTIBLOCK_ENCRYPT returns tls1_1_multi_block_encrypt over the param buffers. Every other type, including MULTIBLOCK_DECRYPT, returns -1.

functions.name: aesni_cbc_hmac_sha256_ctrl
functions.prose_contract: Control function of the AES-NI CBC + HMAC-SHA256 cipher. By type: EVP_CTRL_AEAD_SET_MAC_KEY (ptr holds arg key bytes) returns -1 for a negative arg; a key longer than 64 bytes is first hashed with SHA256, otherwise zero-padded; it initialises key->head (ipad state) and key->tail (opad state), wipes the temporary key and returns 1. EVP_CTRL_AEAD_TLS1_AAD (ptr is the 13-byte TLS header; arg must equal EVP_AEAD_TLS1_AAD_LEN else -1): when encrypting it stores the header length in key->payload_length and the TLS version in key->aux.tls_ver; if the version is at least TLS1.1 and the length is < 16 it returns 0 after those two fields were already changed, else it subtracts 16 from the length and rewrites the two length bytes in the caller header buffer ptr; it then sets key->md = key->head, feeds the header into it and returns the number of padding bytes (to the next 16-byte boundary after length + 32-byte digest). When decrypting it copies the header into key->aux.tls_aad, sets key->payload_length = arg and returns SHA256_DIGEST_LENGTH (32), not 1. With multiblock support compiled in: MULTIBLOCK_MAX_BUFSIZE returns 5 + 16 + ((arg + 32 + 16) & -16); MULTIBLOCK_AAD returns -1 for negative arg, for arg smaller than the param struct, when decrypting, and when encrypting with record version below TLS1.1 or (no inp_len) interleave/4 equal to 0 or above 2; it returns 0 if a given inp_len is below 4096; on success it sets key->md from head plus the 13-byte header, writes param->interleave and returns the computed packet length; MULTIBLOCK_ENCRYPT returns tls1_1_multi_block_encrypt over the param buffers. Every other type, including MULTIBLOCK_DECRYPT, returns -1.

functions.name: aria_gcm_ctrl
functions.prose_contract: Control function of the ARIA-GCM cipher; gctx is the cipher context data. Results by type: EVP_CTRL_INIT resets key_set, iv_set, iv_gen, taglen (-1) and tls_aad_len (-1), points iv at the context built-in IV, sets ivlen from the cipher and returns 1. GET_IVLEN writes ivlen into *ptr and returns 1. AEAD_SET_IVLEN returns 0 if arg <= 0; if arg exceeds both EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH and the current ivlen it frees any separately allocated IV and allocates arg bytes (returning 0 if malloc fails, with gctx->iv then NULL); otherwise it stores ivlen = arg and returns 1. AEAD_SET_TAG: returns 0 if arg is outside 1..16 or the context is encrypting, else copies arg tag bytes into the context buffer, records taglen and returns 1. AEAD_GET_TAG: returns 0 unless arg is in 1..16, the context is encrypting and taglen >= 0, else copies arg bytes of the buffer to ptr and returns 1. GCM_SET_IV_FIXED: arg == -1 copies the whole IV from ptr, sets iv_gen and returns 1; otherwise returns 0 if arg < 4 or ivlen - arg < 8; copies arg fixed bytes, and when encrypting fills the rest with RAND_bytes (returning 0 on failure after the fixed part and iv were already overwritten), sets iv_gen and returns 1. GCM_IV_GEN: returns 0 unless iv_gen and key_set, else sets the GCM IV, copies the last arg bytes of the IV (the whole IV when arg <= 0 or > ivlen) to ptr, increments the 64-bit invocation counter, sets iv_set and returns 1. GCM_SET_IV_INV: returns 0 unless iv_gen and key_set and not encrypting, else copies arg bytes into the IV tail, sets the IV, iv_set, returns 1. AEAD_TLS1_AAD: returns 0 if arg is not the TLS AAD length; it copies the AAD into the buffer and sets tls_aad_len before checking, and returns 0 if the encoded record length is too short for the explicit IV (and tag when decrypting), leaving tls_aad_len and the buffer modified; on success it rewrites the length bytes in the buffer without the explicit IV (and tag) and returns EVP_GCM_TLS_TAG_LEN. EVP_CTRL_COPY returns 0 if the source GCM key pointer is set but does not point at its own key schedule, or if allocating the copied IV fails; otherwise it re-points the copy key and IV and returns 1. Any other type returns -1.

functions.name: EVP_CIPHER_CTX_ctrl
functions.prose_contract: Sends a control command to a cipher context, translating it to provider parameters for provider ciphers or calling the legacy ctrl callback. Precondition: ctx and ctx->cipher non-NULL, otherwise it raises EVP_R_NO_CIPHER_SET and returns 0. Legacy cipher (no provider): if cipher->ctrl is NULL it raises EVP_R_CTRL_NOT_IMPLEMENTED and returns 0, else the ctrl result is used. Provider cipher: SET_KEY_LENGTH, AEAD_SET_IVLEN, CCM_SET_L (arg in 2..8, IV length 15-arg), GCM_SET_IV_INV, RC5 rounds, SET_SPEED and some others return 0 for a negative (or, for CCM_SET_L, out-of-range) arg; SET_KEY_LENGTH and AEAD_SET_IVLEN return 1 without calling the provider when the length is unchanged, and otherwise set key_len / iv_len to -1 before the provider call, a value that stays -1 if the call fails. EVP_CTRL_INIT returns 1 without doing anything. AEAD_SET_MAC_KEY returns -1 for negative arg. Commands translated to a set or get of one parameter return that params call result (get is used for RAND_KEY, GCM_IV_GEN, GET_TAG, GET_RC5_ROUNDS and GET_RC2_KEY_BITS; so the RC5/RC2 getters return the call result, not the fetched value, and the RC5 value is stored in a local unsigned int). AEAD_TLS1_AAD sets the AAD parameter and then reads the padding size, returning that size, or the failed result of either call; MULTIBLOCK_MAX_BUFSIZE, MULTIBLOCK_AAD and MULTIBLOCK_ENCRYPT (when compiled in) return the size obtained from the provider, 0 or the failed result when a call fails, and MULTIBLOCK_AAD returns 0 for arg smaller than the param struct. Unsupported types (including SET_PIPELINE_OUTPUT_BUFS and unknown values) go to end with the unsupported marker. At end, a result equal to EVP_CTRL_RET_UNSUPPORTED raises EVP_R_CTRL_OPERATION_NOT_IMPLEMENTED and returns 0; any other result is returned unchanged.

functions.name: evp_cipher_init_internal
functions.prose_contract: Common initialisation of a cipher context for encrypt or decrypt, choosing between the provider (non-legacy) path and the legacy path. Precondition: ctx valid; enc is 1, 0 or -1 (keep the earlier direction); cipher may be NULL to re-initialise the context cipher. It records ctx->encrypt (any non-zero enc becomes 1) and returns 0 with EVP_R_NO_CIPHER_SET if both cipher and ctx->cipher are NULL. A pipeline call, or the absence of an engine, an explicit impl and a method-origin cipher, selects the provider path; an engine, impl, or EVP_ORIG_METH cipher selects the legacy path (the old fetched cipher is dropped first), and an existing matching engine skips straight to the legacy init step. Provider path: a context that already holds a cipher and a new cipher given is reset (keeping encrypt and flags); a legacy cipher object is replaced by a fetched provider cipher (return 0 if the fetch fails); the fetched cipher gets a reference held in ctx->fetched_cipher; a pipeline request that the cipher cannot pipeline returns 0; algctx is allocated by newctx if absent (0 on failure); no-padding is re-applied; key-length and IV-length parameters in params are applied before init (0 with EVP_R_INVALID_LENGTH on failure). A pipeline call returns 1 here. Otherwise it returns the result of the provider einit/dinit (or the *_skey variant when no key is given and only that exists), and returns 0 with EVP_R_INITIALIZATION_ERROR if no init function is available. Legacy path: when cipher is given it resets the old state, takes an engine reference if requested (0 on failure), sets ctx->cipher, ctx->cipher_data (zero-allocated, failure returns 0 with no error raised), key_len, the wrap flag, and runs EVP_CTRL_INIT if the cipher has that flag (failure returns 0). It returns 0 if ctx->cipher is NULL, rejects wrap mode unless allowed, sets up IV state per cipher mode (EVP_R_INVALID_IV_LENGTH on bad IV size; an unsupported mode returns 0), calls cipher->init when key is set or EVP_CIPH_ALWAYS_CALL_INIT, then resets buf_len and final_used, sets block_mask and returns 1. The legacy path sets ctx->cipher and cipher_data but not ctx->algctx.

functions.name: evp_cipher_init_skey_internal
functions.prose_contract: Initialises a cipher context for encryption or decryption using an EVP_SKEY (or no key yet), with provider ciphers only and no ENGINE support. Precondition: ctx valid; enc is 1, 0 or -1 (keep the earlier direction); cipher may be NULL to reuse ctx->cipher; skey may be NULL (key supplied later). It records ctx->encrypt (enc != 0) and returns 0 with EVP_R_NO_CIPHER_SET if both ciphers are NULL, and returns 0 with EVP_R_INITIALIZATION_ERROR if the context has an engine, the cipher has EVP_ORIG_METH origin, or the cipher has no provider. Only when a new cipher is given and the context already has one: it calls the old cipher cleanup callback (a cleanup returning 0 makes the function return 0 without an error raised and without further cleaning), frees cipher_data, and resets the context while preserving encrypt and flags. It takes a reference to the cipher into ctx->fetched_cipher when different (return 0 on failure), allocates algctx via newctx if absent (0 on failure), returns 0 if skey belongs to a different provider than the cipher, and re-applies no-padding. It then calls the provider init: einit_skey/dinit_skey with skey->keydata when available; otherwise einit/dinit with the raw key bytes of skey (EVP_SKEY_get0_raw_key failing returns 0) or with no key. iv_len is treated as 0 when iv is NULL. It returns the provider init result unchanged.

functions.name: evp_cipher_param_to_asn1_ex
functions.prose_contract: Extracts the AlgorithmIdentifier parameters of the cipher context c into the ASN1_TYPE type (for the legacy EVP_CIPHER_param_to_asn1 path, here in its "set" direction). Precondition: c and c->cipher should be non-NULL (otherwise the result is -1 with EVP_R_CIPHER_PARAMETER_ERROR raised); type is dereferenced by the callbacks and, in the CMS 3DES wrap case, by ASN1_TYPE_set without a NULL check; asn1_params is passed to the AEAD helper. It selects: a legacy cipher with set_asn1_parameters uses that callback result; otherwise, if the cipher does not have EVP_CIPH_FLAG_CUSTOM_ASN1, by mode: wrap mode sets type to ASN1 NULL for the CMS 3DES wrap algorithm and returns 1 (and 1 for other wrap ciphers without touching type), GCM uses evp_cipher_set_asn1_aead_params, CCM, XTS and OCB are unsupported (-2), and any other mode uses EVP_CIPHER_set_asn1_iv; if the cipher has the custom flag and a provider, it returns the result of EVP_CIPHER_CTX_get_algor_params with a temporary X509_ALGOR whose parameter is type; otherwise unsupported (-2). On exit -2 raises EVP_R_UNSUPPORTED_CIPHER, any other result <= 0 raises EVP_R_CIPHER_PARAMETER_ERROR, and any result below -1 is returned as -1. The return value is therefore whatever the selected callback or helper returned (positive on success), which may be 0 or -1 on failure, so it is not restricted to 1 and -1.

functions.name: evp_cipher_asn1_to_param_ex
functions.prose_contract: Applies the AlgorithmIdentifier parameters in the ASN1_TYPE type to the cipher context c (the "get" direction of the legacy EVP_CIPHER_asn1_to_param path). Precondition: c and c->cipher should be non-NULL (otherwise the result is -1 with EVP_R_CIPHER_PARAMETER_ERROR raised); type and asn1_params are used by the selected helper. It selects: a legacy cipher with get_asn1_parameters uses that callback result; otherwise, if the cipher does not have EVP_CIPH_FLAG_CUSTOM_ASN1, by mode: wrap mode returns 1 doing nothing, GCM uses evp_cipher_get_asn1_aead_params, CCM, XTS and OCB are unsupported (-2), and any other mode returns 1 if EVP_CIPHER_get_asn1_iv returns >= 0 and -1 otherwise; if the cipher has the custom flag and a provider, it returns the result of EVP_CIPHER_CTX_set_algor_params with a temporary X509_ALGOR whose parameter is type; otherwise unsupported (-2). On exit -2 raises EVP_R_UNSUPPORTED_CIPHER, any other result <= 0 raises EVP_R_CIPHER_PARAMETER_ERROR, and a result below -1 is returned as -1. The result is whatever the selected callback or helper returned, so it can be 0 (for example from a custom or provider set_algor_params), 1, or -1, not only the GCM/callback cases.

functions.name: EVP_PKEY_derive
functions.prose_contract: Derives a shared secret with the key exchange set up in ctx. Precondition: ctx and pkeylen non-NULL, otherwise it raises ERR_R_PASSED_NULL_PARAMETER and returns -1; key may be NULL to query the size, in which case *pkeylen is output only. It returns -1 with EVP_R_OPERATION_NOT_INITIALIZED if ctx is not in a derive operation. For a provider key exchange (ctx->op.kex.algctx non-NULL) it returns the result of exchange->derive(algctx, key, pkeylen, key != NULL ? *pkeylen : 0) unchanged. Legacy path: if ctx->pmeth or its derive callback is NULL it raises EVP_R_OPERATION_NOT_SUPPORTED_FOR_THIS_KEYTYPE and returns -2. Otherwise, for methods with EVP_PKEY_FLAG_AUTOARGLEN the macro M_check_autoarg first returns 0 with EVP_R_INVALID_KEY when the key size is 0, returns 1 after writing the key size to *pkeylen when key is NULL, and returns 0 with EVP_R_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL when *pkeylen is smaller than the key size; if it passes (or the flag is absent) it returns the result of pmeth->derive(ctx, key, pkeylen) unchanged.

functions.name: do_sigver_init
functions.prose_contract: Common setup for EVP_DigestSignInit and EVP_DigestVerifyInit (ver selects verify). Precondition: ctx valid; pkey may be NULL when ctx->pctx already exists; type, mdname and props may be NULL. It returns 0 if freeing the old algctx or creating the EVP_PKEY_CTX (when ctx has none) fails, and returns only 0 or 1. It clears the FINALISED flag. Provider path: if the pctx is not legacy, the context is re-initialised in place (no new signature or algctx) only when it already existed, pkey is NULL, the operation is the matching SIGNCTX/VERIFYCTX and a signature and algctx are present; otherwise it discards old operation data, requires a key (EVP_R_NO_KEY_SET), asks the keymgmt for the signature name, fetches the signature (first by the pctx property query, then from the keymgmt provider) and exports the key to a matching keymgmt; failure of all attempts raises EVP_R_INITIALIZATION_ERROR and returns 0, a missing second-iteration signature falls back to the legacy path. On success of that search it stores the signature, sets operation to VERIFYCTX or SIGNCTX, creates the signature algctx with newctx (failure returns 0). Both new and reinitialised paths then record *pctx if requested, set the digest (type, or mdname, or the key default digest name for a non-reinit call; the digest is fetched, falling back to EVP_get_digestbyname, and failure raises EVP_R_INITIALIZATION_ERROR), and call the signature digest_verify_init or digest_sign_init (missing callback raises EVP_R_PROVIDER_SIGNATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED and returns 0). If that returns <= 0 and no digest name was resolved it raises NO_DEFAULT_DIGEST (if type is NULL) and PROVIDER_SIGNATURE_FAILURE and returns 0; on a positive result it applies cached ctx data via evp_pkey_ctx_use_cached_data and returns 1 if that succeeds. The error exit frees old operation data and sets operation to UNDEFINED. Legacy path: uses pmeth (return 0 with an error if none), derives the digest (explicit, from mdname, or the key default digest unless EVP_PKEY_FLAG_SIGCTX_CUSTOM; none found returns 0), then calls verifyctx_init/signctx_init and sets operation VERIFYCTX/SIGNCTX, else if digestverify/digestsign exists sets operation VERIFY/SIGN with the update callback, else calls EVP_PKEY_verify_init/sign_init; then sets the signature md, records *pctx, returns 1 for custom-sigctx methods, else calls EVP_DigestInit_ex and sets flag_call_digest_custom before finishing through the cached-data step and returning 1. The legacy path does not create a provider algctx.

functions.name: EVP_DigestVerifyFinal
functions.prose_contract: Completes a digest-and-verify operation and checks sig of length siglen. Precondition: ctx non-NULL and initialised with EVP_DigestVerifyInit. If ctx is already marked finalised it raises EVP_R_FINAL_ERROR and returns 0. Provider path (pctx has operation VERIFYCTX with a signature and algctx): returns 0 with EVP_R_PROVIDER_SIGNATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED if the signature has no digest_verify_final; otherwise, unless EVP_MD_CTX_FLAG_FINALISE is set, it works on a duplicate of the pctx (falling back to the original if the duplicate fails), calls digest_verify_final and, if it returned 0 with no error queued, raises EVP_R_PROVIDER_SIGNATURE_FAILURE. The context is marked finalised only when no duplicate was used. It returns the provider result unchanged. Legacy path: returns 0 with EVP_R_INITIALIZATION_ERROR when there is no pctx or pmeth; if flag_call_digest_custom is set it calls digest_custom (returning 0 if that fails) and clears the flag; with FINALISE set it uses verifyctx (marking the ctx finalised) or EVP_DigestFinal_ex directly on ctx, otherwise it copies the context first (returning -1 if allocating or copying fails). If a verifyctx method was used, or the digest finalisation returned 0, that result is returned; else it returns the result of EVP_PKEY_verify(pctx, sig, siglen, md, mdlen) unchanged, which can be positive, 0 or negative.

functions.name: EVP_DigestVerify
functions.prose_contract: One-shot digest-and-verify of tbs (length tbslen) against the signature sigret (length siglen). Precondition: ctx non-NULL. Returns -1 with EVP_R_INITIALIZATION_ERROR if ctx->pctx is NULL, and 0 with EVP_R_FINAL_ERROR if ctx is already finalised. If the pctx is in operation VERIFYCTX with both a signature and algctx and the signature has a digest_verify callback, it marks ctx finalised, calls it (raising EVP_R_PROVIDER_SIGNATURE_FAILURE when it returns <= 0 with nothing queued) and returns its result unchanged. Otherwise, whenever the pctx is not in that state (including operation VERIFYCTX with a missing algctx or signature) and its pmeth has a digestverify method, it returns that method result. In every remaining case (provider signature without digest_verify, or a legacy method without digestverify) it calls EVP_DigestVerifyUpdate over tbs (returning -1 if that fails) and returns the result of EVP_DigestVerifyFinal(ctx, sigret, siglen).

functions.name: EVP_PKEY_set_type_by_keymgmt
functions.prose_contract: Sets the type of pkey from the key management object keymgmt (provider-side key). Precondition: keymgmt non-NULL; pkey may be NULL (then it only validates the combination). In non-FIPS builds it first collects, with EVP_KEYMGMT_names_do_all and find_ameth, up to two keymgmt names that have a legacy ASN.1 method; if the name iteration fails or a second name is found it raises ERR_R_INTERNAL_ERROR and returns 0. It then returns the result of pkey_set_type(pkey, NULL, EVP_PKEY_NONE, name-or-NULL, length, keymgmt) (in FIPS builds name NULL, length -1). That helper returns 0 with an error when type and keymgmt are inconsistent or when neither a legacy method nor keymgmt is given, and returns 0 if EVP_KEYMGMT_up_ref fails. When pkey is non-NULL it frees any existing key data, releases engines, takes a reference to keymgmt, stores it in pkey->keymgmt, and sets the type to the legacy pkey_id when a legacy method for the name exists, else EVP_PKEY_KEYMGMT, without storing the ameth (since keymgmt is set), and returns 1. When pkey is NULL none of the pkey fields is written and it returns 1 if the lookup succeeded.

functions.name: evp_pkey_ctx_store_cached_data
functions.prose_contract: Caches an EVP_PKEY_CTX control value for later use (currently only the EVP_PKEY_CTRL_SET1_ID distinguishing identifier). Precondition: ctx non-NULL; cmd (or the OSSL param name) should map to a supported command, but this is checked here: an unsupported command raises EVP_R_COMMAND_NOT_SUPPORTED and returns -2. If keytype != -1 the ctx must match it: for a provider ctx a NULL keymgmt returns -2 and a keymgmt that is not of that key type returns -1 (EVP_R_INVALID_OPERATION); for a legacy or unknown-state ctx a NULL pmeth returns -2 and a pkey_id of a different type returns -1. If optype != -1 and ctx->operation has none of those bits it returns -1 with EVP_R_INVALID_OPERATION. For SET1_ID it frees any previously cached id, then duplicates name into cached_parameters.dist_id_name only when name is non-NULL and copies data into dist_id only when data_len > 0 (each copy failure returns 0, leaving an earlier copy such as the name in place and dist_id_set unchanged), and finally sets dist_id_set = 1 and dist_id_len = data_len and returns 1. With name NULL and data_len 0 nothing is copied but the id is still marked set with length 0.

functions.name: evp_pkey_signature_init
functions.prose_contract: Initialises ctx for a signature-type operation (SIGN, SIGNMSG, VERIFY, VERIFYMSG or VERIFYRECOVER) using a given EVP_SIGNATURE or one found automatically. Precondition: ctx may be NULL (raises ERR_R_PASSED_NULL_PARAMETER, returns -1). It frees old operation data and stores operation in ctx->operation before anything else, so ctx->operation stays set on the early returns that follow. With a pre-fetched signature: no key raises EVP_R_NO_KEY_SET and fails (error exit); the key is exported to the signature provider (if that yields no provider key it returns 0 without an error raised and without clearing the operation); the signature must accept the key type (query_key_types, or the keymgmt name / default operation name), else EVP_R_SIGNATURE_TYPE_AND_KEY_TYPE_INCOMPATIBLE and -2; then a reference is taken (failure takes the error exit). Without a signature it uses the legacy path for legacy contexts, else fetches the signature from the keymgmt operation name (twice: normal fetch, then from the keymgmt provider) and exports the key, falling back to legacy when none works. Provider path: stores the signature, creates its algctx (failure takes the error exit) and calls the matching init callback; a missing callback gives -2 (EVP_R_PROVIDER_SIGNATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED), an unknown operation takes the error exit, and a result <= 0 frees the algctx and takes the error exit. Legacy path: returns -2 without resetting the operation when pmeth is NULL or lacks sign/verify/verify_recover for the requested operation (SIGNMSG and VERIFYMSG are not handled, error exit); if the matching init callback is NULL it returns 1 at once, otherwise a result <= 0 takes the error exit. On a positive result the cached ctx data are applied via evp_pkey_ctx_use_cached_data (non-FIPS) and its result is returned. The error exit frees operation data, sets operation to UNDEFINED and returns the current ret (which can be 0, a negative provider result or -2).

functions.name: ossl_ffc_params_FIPS186_4_gen_verify
functions.prose_contract: Generates or verifies FFC (DSA/DH) domain parameters p, q, g following FIPS 186-4. Precondition: params and res non-NULL; mode FFC_PARAM_MODE_VERIFY selects verification (the checks in params->flags then apply) and any other mode generation (flags treated as 0); L and N are the bit lengths of p and q (N may be 0, then derived from the digest); libctx and cb may be NULL. It sets *res = 0 first. Return value is ok: FFC_PARAM_RET_STATUS_SUCCESS, FFC_PARAM_RET_STATUS_UNVERIFIABLE_G (when VALIDATE_G was requested but g is not canonical, so unverifiable), or FFC_PARAM_RET_STATUS_FAILED, which is also the value on every goto err path. It fetches the digest (params->mdname or a default for N, failing if none), rejects L <= N or an invalid L/N pair (*res = FFC_CHECK_BAD_LN_PAIR), and in generate mode requires p and q to be both set or both NULL (FFC_CHECK_INVALID_PQ); in verify mode it requires a seed and non-negative pcounter for VALIDATE_PQ and a g for VALIDATE_G. If params->p exists and PQ validation is not requested, it skips to the g step using params->p and params->q. Otherwise it checks the seed length, generates (or, for verify, reuses and requires) the seed, and loops generating q (generate_q_fips186_4) and then p (generate_p), comparing against params->q and params->p in verify mode (mismatch gives FFC_CHECK_Q_MISMATCH or failure, a bad pcounter FFC_CHECK_INVALID_COUNTER, a p that is not prime in verify mode FFC_CHECK_P_NOT_PRIME) and reporting progress to cb. If only PQ validation was requested it stops there with success. Otherwise it validates g (unverifiable g check or canonical g from gindex and seed, with mismatch FFC_CHECK_G_MISMATCH in verify mode) or, in generate mode, generates an unverifiable g. In generate mode it replaces params->p, q and g with duplicates, stores the seed and counter (ossl_ffc_params_set_validate_params) and sets params->h; any allocation or storing failure returns FAILED. At the end it frees temporary seed, digest and BN resources.

functions.name: ossl_ffc_params_FIPS186_2_gen_verify
functions.prose_contract: Generates or verifies DSA domain parameters p, q, g following FIPS 186-2. Precondition: params and res non-NULL; mode FFC_PARAM_MODE_VERIFY selects verification (flags from params->flags apply), anything else generation (flags 0); in verify mode with VALIDATE_PQ the seed, a non-negative pcounter and params->p are needed (the p comparison at the end dereferences params->p without a NULL check), with VALIDATE_G params->g is needed (NULL gives FFC_CHECK_INVALID_G), and when VALIDATE_PQ is not set but params->p is, params->q is used as is. It sets *res = 0, fetches the digest (failing for an unsupported N), and requires L >= 512 (FFC_CHECK_BAD_LN_PAIR) and a q size of 20, 28 or 32 bytes (FFC_CHECK_INVALID_Q_VALUE); L is rounded up to a multiple of 64. A supplied seed must be at least q bytes long (FFC_CHECK_INVALID_SEED_SIZE) and is truncated to qsize. In generate mode p and q must be both set or both NULL (FFC_CHECK_INVALID_PQ). If params->p is set and PQ validation is not requested it skips to the g step. Otherwise it loops generating q (generate_q_fips186_2) and p (generate_p), retrying with a random seed when no p is found; in verify mode a counter above 4L-1 gives FFC_CHECK_INVALID_COUNTER, and a counter or p mismatch gives FFC_CHECK_COUNTER_MISMATCH or FFC_CHECK_P_MISMATCH. With PQ-only validation it jumps to success. For g it generates an unverifiable g (generate mode) or runs the unverifiable-g check when VALIDATE_G is set (verify mode). In generate mode it then replaces params->p, q, g with duplicates, stores the seed and counter and sets params->h. The return value is FFC_PARAM_RET_STATUS_FAILED on every error exit, FFC_PARAM_RET_STATUS_UNVERIFIABLE_G when VALIDATE_G is set in flags (at pass) and FFC_PARAM_RET_STATUS_SUCCESS otherwise. Temporary BN and digest objects are freed at the end.

functions.name: OSSL_HTTP_REQ_CTX_nbio
functions.prose_contract: Non-blocking step function of the HTTP request/response state machine of rctx; each call runs as far as the BIOs allow. Precondition: rctx non-NULL (NULL raises ERR_R_PASSED_NULL_PARAMETER and returns 0) and rctx->mem, wbio and rbio non-NULL (otherwise ERR_R_SHOULD_NOT_HAVE_BEEN_CALLED and 0). It clears redirection_url. Return values: 1 when the response header is complete and a text/stream response follows (state OHS_STREAM) or when the full ASN.1 response has been received (state OHS_ASN1_DONE); -1 when a read, write, flush or request-BIO read must be retried later; 0 on error, end or redirect. In states where reading is allowed it reads either a text line (BIO_gets, falling back to BIO_get_line) or raw bytes for ASN.1, appending to the memory BIO; a read of <= 0 returns -1 if retryable, else raises HTTP_R_FAILED_READING_DATA and returns 0, except in OHS_ERROR_CONTENT where end of data checks the accumulated length via check_set_resp_len (which can raise an error) and returns 0; a failed write to mem returns 0 without an error raised. Sending phase: ADD_HEADERS appends the final CRLF, then the header, then request body are copied to wbio in chunks (write failure: retry -1, else state OHS_ERROR and 0), the body is read from rctx->req (read failure: -1 or HTTP_R_FAILED_READING_DATA and 0), then the wbio is flushed (failure: -1 or state OHS_ERROR and 0) and the state moves to OHS_FIRSTLINE. Header phase: lines must be complete and shorter than the buffer, at most max_hdr_lines (otherwise HTTP_R_RESPONSE_TOO_MANY_HDRLINES, line too long, or state OHS_ERROR with return 0, the last without an error raised); the status line sets the next state (200 continue, 301/302 with GET go to redirect, otherwise a header-error state for status < 400 or header reading for status >= 400, with an error for redirect with POST); Location in redirect state stores redirection_url, resets the rbio and returns 0; Content-Type, Connection and Content-Length are parsed and can make it raise errors and return 0 (content type mismatch, unexpected or missing content type, bad content length, server cancelled keep-alive, missing redirect location); after the blank line a header-error state turns into reading the error content (or discards it and returns 0), otherwise it returns 1 in stream mode or goes on to parse the ASN.1 SEQUENCE header and expected length, then returns 1 when that many bytes are buffered. In OHS_ERROR and any other unlisted state, including OHS_STREAM and OHS_ASN1_DONE on a further call, it returns 0.

functions.name: sh_init
functions.prose_contract: Initialises the global secure-heap state sh with an arena of size bytes and a minimum allocation size minsize. Precondition: size must be a non-zero power of two and, when minsize is larger than sizeof(SH_LIST), minsize must be a power of two; violations hit OPENSSL_assert, which aborts the process (the following return paths are fallbacks only reached if assertions are compiled out). A minsize not larger than SH_LIST is replaced by the next power of two at or above sizeof(SH_LIST). It clears sh first, computes bittable and freelist sizes, allocates the freelist and two bit tables with OPENSSL_zalloc (asserting non-NULL), maps arena plus two guard pages with mmap (or VirtualAlloc on Windows), and registers the whole arena as one free block. Return value: 0 if sizes are invalid, the bit table would be empty, an allocation fails or the mapping fails, in which case sh_done() releases whatever was allocated; otherwise 1 when the guard pages were protected, the arena was locked with mlock/mlock2/VirtualLock and madvise(MADV_DONTDUMP) (when available) all succeeded, and 2 when the mapping succeeded but any of the guard-page protection, memory locking or madvise steps failed (the heap is still usable, but not fully locked or protected).

functions.name: CRYPTO_128_unwrap_pad
functions.prose_contract: Unwraps an RFC 5649 padded AES key wrap ciphertext. Precondition: in holds inlen readable bytes (a multiple of 8, at least 16 and below CRYPTO128_WRAP_MAX), out is writable (the documented minimum is inlen - 8 bytes, but the failure paths below clear inlen bytes of it), icv is NULL (use the default A65959A6 value) or 4 readable bytes, block is the block cipher function. Returns 0 without writing when inlen is not a multiple of 8, is below 16 or is at least CRYPTO128_WRAP_MAX. For inlen == 16 it decrypts the two blocks with one block call, takes the first 8 bytes as the AIV and the rest as the 8-byte padded data in out; for longer input it calls crypto_128_unwrap_raw into out and returns 0 (after clearing inlen bytes of out) if the raw routine does not return inlen - 8. Then it returns 0 (clearing out) if the first 4 bytes of the AIV differ from icv or the default value, if the length field in the last 4 AIV bytes is not in (8*(n-1), 8*n], or if the padding bytes after that length in out are not all zero. Otherwise it returns the plaintext length taken from the AIV. On success out holds the unwrapped key followed by the zero padding.

functions.name: WPACKET_fill_lengths
functions.prose_contract: Finalises the length fields of all open sub-packets without closing them. Precondition: pkt->subs non-NULL (ossl_assert failure returns 0). It walks from the innermost sub-packet out through its parents and calls wpacket_intern_close(pkt, sub, 0) on each, returning 0 as soon as one call fails and 1 if all succeed. For each sub, that call fails (returns 0) for a zero-length sub flagged NON_ZERO_LENGTH, for a zero-length sub flagged ABANDON_ON_ZERO_LENGTH (it cannot be handled when not closing), or when the length cannot be encoded. Otherwise, for a sub with length bytes it backfills the length at the reserved position in the buffer (only if a buffer exists), and for a length-prefix-at-end (endfirst) sub that has a parent it appends the length bytes to the written data (plus a length-of-length byte for lengths above 0x7f) instead of backfilling. The sub-packets are not freed or popped. Because the walk stops at the first failure, sub-packets processed before the failing one may already have had their lengths written or appended, so the packet is not left unchanged on failure.

functions.name: WPACKET_close
functions.prose_contract: Closes the innermost open sub-packet of pkt. Precondition: pkt non-NULL; if pkt->subs is NULL or the innermost sub has no parent (only the top-level packet is open) it returns 0 and changes nothing. Otherwise it returns the result of wpacket_intern_close(pkt, pkt->subs, 1). That call returns 0, leaving the sub-packet open, when a zero-length sub has the NON_ZERO_LENGTH flag, when the length cannot be encoded or written, or when appending the length bytes of an endfirst sub fails. For a zero-length sub flagged ABANDON_ON_ZERO_LENGTH it instead removes the reserved length bytes (if they are the last bytes written), writes no length, and succeeds. On success it writes or appends the length (backfilled into the buffer only if a buffer exists, so with no buffer nothing is written), makes the parent the innermost sub, frees the closed sub and returns 1.

functions.name: ossl_param_find_pidx
functions.prose_contract: Machine-generated trie lookup that maps a parameter name to its PIDX_* index. Precondition: s is a non-NULL NUL-terminated string (it is dereferenced without a NULL check). It switches on successive characters of s; a deeper character s[k] is only read after every earlier character was matched to a non-NUL case label, so the reads stay within the string including its terminator. Where the remaining suffix is unique it compares it with strcmp against the rest of the name. A string that exactly equals one of the known parameter names returns the corresponding PIDX_* constant; a string that is a strict prefix of a name, or contains an unmatched character, falls out of the switches and the function returns -1. It has no side effects and does not modify s.

functions.name: ossl_pw_get_passphrase
functions.prose_contract: Central passphrase dispatcher: fills pass (capacity pass_size) with a passphrase from the source configured in data, storing its length in *pass_len. Precondition: pass, pass_len and data non-NULL; params may carry OSSL_PASSPHRASE_PARAM_INFO; verify requests confirmation for UI-based prompts. Order of sources: (1) an explicit passphrase (data type is_expl_passphrase) or, when caching is on and a cached one exists, the cached passphrase: its bytes are copied into pass, silently truncated to pass_size, *pass_len is set to the copied length and the function returns 1 without prompting (no NUL terminator is written to pass here, and no length error is reported for a passphrase larger than pass_size). (2) An OSSL passphrase callback: its return value ret is used. (3) Otherwise a prompt info parameter of the wrong type raises ERR_R_PASSED_INVALID_ARGUMENT and returns 0; a PEM password callback is wrapped in a UI method (wrap failure raises ERR_R_UI_LIB and returns 0), or a configured UI method is used; with neither it raises ERR_R_PASSED_INVALID_ARGUMENT ("No password method specified") and returns 0; else do_ui_passphrase supplies ret and the temporary wrapper method is destroyed. For cases (2) and (3), if ret is non-zero and caching is enabled, the result is copied into data->cached_passphrase (grown with clear-realloc to length + 1 when needed and NUL-terminated); if growing fails the passphrase in pass is cleansed and 0 is returned. The function returns ret, so a callback that returns 0 yields 0 without this function raising an error, and failures other than the cache allocation failure do not cleanse pass.

functions.name: ossl_pw_get_passphrase
functions.prose_contract: Central passphrase dispatcher: fills pass (capacity pass_size) with a passphrase from the source configured in data, storing its length in *pass_len. Precondition: pass, pass_len and data non-NULL; params may carry OSSL_PASSPHRASE_PARAM_INFO; verify requests confirmation for UI-based prompts. Order of sources: (1) an explicit passphrase (data type is_expl_passphrase) or, when caching is on and a cached one exists, the cached passphrase: its bytes are copied into pass, silently truncated to pass_size, *pass_len is set to the copied length and the function returns 1 without prompting (no NUL terminator is written to pass here, and no length error is reported for a passphrase larger than pass_size). (2) An OSSL passphrase callback: its return value ret is used. (3) Otherwise a prompt info parameter of the wrong type raises ERR_R_PASSED_INVALID_ARGUMENT and returns 0; a PEM password callback is wrapped in a UI method (wrap failure raises ERR_R_UI_LIB and returns 0), or a configured UI method is used; with neither it raises ERR_R_PASSED_INVALID_ARGUMENT ("No password method specified") and returns 0; else do_ui_passphrase supplies ret and the temporary wrapper method is destroyed. For cases (2) and (3), if ret is non-zero and caching is enabled, the result is copied into data->cached_passphrase (grown with clear-realloc to length + 1 when needed and NUL-terminated); if growing fails the passphrase in pass is cleansed and 0 is returned. The function returns ret, so a callback that returns 0 yields 0 without this function raising an error, and failures other than the cache allocation failure do not cleanse pass.

functions.name: PKCS7_dataFinal
functions.prose_contract: Finishes a PKCS7 structure after content has been written through bio: computes signatures or digests and attaches the content. Precondition: p7 non-NULL (else PKCS7_R_INVALID_NULL_POINTER, 0) with p7->d.ptr non-NULL (else PKCS7_R_NO_CONTENT, 0); bio is the chain that was set up by PKCS7_dataInit. It allocates a temporary digest context (failure raises ERR_R_EVP_LIB, returns 0) and sets p7->state to PKCS7_S_HEADER. By content type it picks the octet string os (and signer list): data uses p7->d.data; enveloped and signedAndEnveloped use the encrypted data octet string, creating it if absent (ERR_R_ASN1_LIB and error exit on failure); signed and digest need contents (else PKCS7_R_NO_CONTENT) and use the content octet string, which for detached data content is freed and cleared; any other type raises PKCS7_R_UNSUPPORTED_CONTENT_TYPE. Then, for each signer with a private key, it finds the matching digest in the bio chain (failure returns 0), copies the digest context, and either signs the signed attributes (do_pkcs7_signed_attrib) or, with no attributes, allocates a signature buffer of the key size (a zero size or malloc failure returns 0 with no error raised), signs with EVP_SignFinal_ex (ERR_R_EVP_LIB on failure) and stores it in si->enc_digest. For a digest type with no signer list it finalises the digest of the matching digest context and stores it in p7->d.digest->digest. If the structure is not detached, os must be non-NULL (else 0) and, unless it is streaming (NDEF), the memory BIO data are attached to os as a read-only reference (PKCS7_R_UNABLE_TO_FIND_MEM_BIO if there is none). Returns 1 on success and 0 on the first failure; the temporary digest context is freed on all exits after its creation.

functions.name: PKCS7_verify
functions.prose_contract: Verifies a signed PKCS7 structure: signer certificates, certificate chains, then the content digests and signatures. Precondition: p7 non-NULL and of signed type; indata is required when the content is detached; certs, store, out may be NULL. Returns 0 with an error for: NULL p7 (PKCS7_R_INVALID_NULL_POINTER), non-signed type (PKCS7_R_WRONG_CONTENT_TYPE), detached content without indata (PKCS7_R_NO_CONTENT), PKCS7_NO_DUAL_CONTENT set with content present and indata given (PKCS7_R_CONTENT_AND_DATA_PRESENT), and no signer infos (PKCS7_R_NO_SIGNATURES_ON_DATA); and returns 0 when PKCS7_get0_signers finds no signers. Unless PKCS7_NOVERIFY is set it builds an untrusted list from certs (and the included certificates unless PKCS7_NOCHAIN) and verifies each signer chain with X509_verify_cert, loading the smime_sign default parameters unless NOCHAIN (a failure of that call or of the list building goes to the error exit without an error raised here) and the CRLs unless PKCS7_NOCRL; a failed chain verification raises PKCS7_R_CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_ERROR. It then sets up the data BIO chain with PKCS7_dataInit, reads all content through it (writing it to out, or through a memory BIO and SMIME_text when PKCS7_TEXT is set, PKCS7_R_SMIME_TEXT_ERROR on failure; the BIO_write results are not checked) and, unless PKCS7_NOSIGS is set, verifies each signature with PKCS7_signatureVerify (PKCS7_R_SIGNATURE_FAILURE on failure). Returns 1 only if all of these steps succeeded. On all exits after the signer list exists it frees the contexts, buffers, signer and untrusted lists and pops and frees the BIOs it added in front of indata.

functions.name: ossl_method_store_cache_set
functions.prose_contract: Stores, replaces or removes the cached method for (nid, prov, prop_query) in the method store cache. Precondition: store, prop_query non-NULL, nid > 0 and prov non-NULL (these are checked; a violation returns 0 before taking any lock). It takes the store write lock (returning 0 without holding it if that fails), flushes some cache entries first if cache_need_flush is set, and looks up the algorithm entry for nid; if there is none it returns 0 (releasing the lock). If method is NULL it deletes the matching cache entry if one exists (freeing it and decrementing cache_nelem) and returns 1 whether or not an entry existed. Otherwise it allocates a cache element, copies the query string, takes a reference on the method (method_up_ref) and inserts it into the algorithm cache: if an old entry was replaced, the old one is freed and the function returns 1 without changing cache_nelem or cache_need_flush; if a new entry was inserted, cache_nelem is incremented and cache_need_flush set when it reaches IMPL_CACHE_FLUSH_THRESHOLD, and it returns 1. Allocation failure, a failed up_ref (element freed, no reference kept), or a hash table insert error (the method reference is released and the element freed) return 0 with no error raised here. The write lock is released on every return after it was taken.

functions.name: provider_conf_activate
functions.prose_contract: Activates the provider named name from the configuration, once per library context. Precondition: libctx, name, value and cnf valid; path may be NULL; soft selects whether a failure to create the provider is tolerated. It takes the provider-config write lock; if the global data are missing or the lock fails it raises ERR_R_INTERNAL_ERROR and returns -1. If the name is already in the activated list it does nothing and returns 0 (ok stays 0). Otherwise it disables fallback provider loading (failure: unlock, ERR_R_INTERNAL_ERROR, return -1), finds or creates the provider (if neither works it unlocks and returns -1, or, when soft is set, clears the error and returns 0), sets the module path if given, and applies the configuration section with provider_conf_params. If that returns 1, it activates the provider, adds it to the store (deactivating prov again if adding fails), activates the store copy when it differs from prov (freeing that reference on failure), and pushes the result onto the activated list, deactivating and freeing the store copy if the list push fails; success gives 1, any of these failures gives 0. If provider_conf_params returns 0 or a negative value, that value is returned. Whenever the final result is <= 0 the local prov reference is freed with ossl_provider_free (it is not separately deactivated on the params or first-activation failure paths, where it was not activated). The lock is released before returning in every path after it was taken.

functions.name: ossl_provider_add_to_store
functions.prose_contract: Adds prov to the provider store of its library context, or resolves to an already stored provider of the same name. Precondition: prov non-NULL; actualprov may be NULL. If actualprov is non-NULL it is first set to NULL. It returns 0 if the store cannot be obtained or its write lock fails. Under the lock it looks up the provider by name. If none exists, it pushes prov onto the store list (if the push fails it unlocks and returns 0; prov was never added, so nothing is removed), sets prov->store, creates the provider children (on failure it removes prov from the list again, unlocks and returns 0) and, unless retain_fallbacks is set, turns off use_fallbacks. If one exists, the stored one becomes the actual provider. After unlocking, if actualprov is non-NULL it takes a reference on the actual provider (failure raises ERR_R_CRYPTO_LIB and returns 0, and in the already-stored case the passed prov has not yet been deactivated or freed) and stores it in *actualprov. When the name was already in the store, the passed prov is then deactivated (without removing children) and its reference freed, so the caller must use *actualprov afterwards; otherwise (new entry, non-FIPS builds) the decoder cache of the library context is flushed. Returns 1 on success. On the failure paths the passed prov reference is not freed here.

functions.name: pkey_rsa_ctrl
functions.prose_contract: Control dispatcher of the legacy RSA EVP_PKEY method; rctx = ctx->data. Typical results are 1 on success, 0 or -2 on failure. EVP_PKEY_CTRL_RSA_PADDING: for p1 from PKCS1 to PSS padding it returns 0 if check_padding_md rejects the current md; PSS padding needs a sign or verify operation and sets md to SHA-1 if unset; any non-PSS mode is refused if the key is PSS-restricted; OAEP needs an encrypt/decrypt-type operation and sets md to SHA-1 if unset; on success it stores pad_mode and returns 1; otherwise (illegal value or refused) it raises RSA_R_ILLEGAL_OR_UNSUPPORTED_PADDING_MODE and returns -2 (the check_padding_md failure returns 0 without that error). GET_RSA_PADDING returns pad_mode in *p2, result 1. PSS_SALTLEN and GET_PSS_SALTLEN: -2 with error unless pad_mode is PSS; get stores saltlen; set returns -2 without an error for p1 < RSA_PSS_SALTLEN_MAX, for a restricted key it returns -2 with error for AUTO on a verify operation or a non-positive digest size, returns 0 with RSA_R_PSS_SALTLEN_TOO_SMALL for a salt length below min_saltlen, else stores p1 and returns 1. KEYGEN_BITS: -2 below RSA_MIN_MODULUS_BITS. KEYGEN_PUBEXP: -2 unless p2 is an odd BIGNUM other than 1; it frees the old exponent and stores p2 (ownership passes). KEYGEN_PRIMES: -2 outside the allowed prime count. RSA_OAEP_MD and GET_RSA_OAEP_MD: -2 unless pad_mode is OAEP; get/set md. EVP_PKEY_CTRL_MD: 0 if check_padding_md fails; for a restricted key it returns 1 if the digest type is the same and otherwise 0 with RSA_R_DIGEST_NOT_ALLOWED; else stores md. GET_MD stores md. RSA_MGF1_MD and its getter: -2 unless pad_mode is PSS or OAEP; get returns mgf1md or md; set on a restricted key returns 1 for the same digest type else 0, otherwise stores mgf1md. OAEP_LABEL: -2 unless OAEP; frees the old label and stores p2 (ownership passes) if p2 is non-NULL and p1 > 0, else clears it, result 1; GET_OAEP_LABEL returns -2 unless OAEP, 0 if p2 is NULL, else stores the label pointer and returns its length. IMPLICIT_REJECTION: -2 unless PKCS1 padding, else stores p1. DIGESTINIT, PKCS7_SIGN and CMS_SIGN return 1; the PKCS7/CMS encrypt and decrypt commands return 1 unless the key is PSS-type, in which case they and PEER_KEY return -2 with RSA_R_OPERATION_NOT_SUPPORTED_FOR_THIS_KEYTYPE; any other type returns -2.

functions.name: UI_set_result_ex
functions.prose_contract: Stores the user response for the UI string uis. Precondition: ui and uis non-NULL; for string prompts result points to len readable bytes and uis->result_buf has room for result_maxsize + 1 bytes; for boolean prompts result is a NUL-terminated string. It first clears UI_FLAG_REDOABLE in ui->flags. For UIT_PROMPT and UIT_VERIFY: a len below result_minsize or above result_maxsize sets UI_FLAG_REDOABLE, raises UI_R_RESULT_TOO_SMALL or UI_R_RESULT_TOO_LARGE and returns -1 (these checks run before the buffer check, so a NULL result_buf with an out-of-range len also leaves REDOABLE set); otherwise a NULL result_buf raises UI_R_NO_RESULT_BUFFER and returns -1 without setting REDOABLE; otherwise it copies len bytes into result_buf, writes a terminating NUL at result_buf[len] and sets result_len = len, returning 0. For UIT_BOOLEAN: a NULL result_buf raises UI_R_NO_RESULT_BUFFER and returns -1; otherwise result_buf[0] is set to 0, then to the first ok character (if the first character of result found in ok_chars comes first) or the first cancel character according to the first character of result that appears in ok_chars or cancel_chars (it stays 0 if none does), and it returns 0; result_len is not changed. UIT_NONE, UIT_INFO and UIT_ERROR do nothing and return 0.

functions.name: X509V3_add1_i2d
functions.prose_contract: Encodes value as an extension with the given nid and criticality crit and adds it to the extension stack *x according to the operation in flags (the X509V3_ADD_OP_MASK part). Precondition: x non-NULL (it is dereferenced); *x may be NULL (a new stack is created when appending). Unless the operation is APPEND it looks for an existing extension with that nid.
