If one exists: KEEP_EXISTING returns 1 without changing anything; DEFAULT raises X509V3_R_EXTENSION_EXISTS (suppressed by X509V3_ADD_SILENT) and returns 0; DELETE removes and frees it and returns 1 (or -1 if the removal fails). If none exists, REPLACE_EXISTING and DELETE raise X509V3_R_EXTENSION_NOT_FOUND (also suppressed by X509V3_ADD_SILENT) and return 0. In the remaining cases it encodes the extension with X509V3_EXT_i2d; if that fails it raises X509V3_R_ERROR_CREATING_EXTENSION regardless of the SILENT flag and returns 0. If an extension existed it frees the old one and stores the new one in its place (returns 1, or -1 if the set fails, in which case the old one is already freed and the new one is not freed here); otherwise it appends the new extension, creating the stack if *x was NULL, sets *x and returns 1; allocation or push failure frees the new extension (and a newly created stack) and returns -1 without raising an error.

functions.name: r2i_pci
functions.prose_contract: Builds a PROXY_CERT_INFO_EXTENSION from the configuration string value (a list of name:value settings, possibly @section references). Precondition: method may be unused; ctx is the X509V3 context used to look up sections; value is the extension string. It parses the list with X509V3_parse_list, then for every entry: an entry whose name is NULL, or whose name does not start with @ and has no value, raises X509V3_R_INVALID_PROXY_POLICY_SETTING and fails; an entry starting with @ names a section, which must exist (else X509V3_R_INVALID_SECTION) and whose values are each passed to process_pci_value until one fails; any other entry is passed to process_pci_value directly. process_pci_value (read only in part) fills the language, pathlen and policy values. After all entries, the language is mandatory (else X509V3_R_NO_PROXY_CERT_POLICY_LANGUAGE_DEFINED), and a policy together with the Independent or inheritAll language is rejected (X509V3_R_POLICY_WHEN_PROXY_LANGUAGE_REQUIRES_NO_POLICY). It then allocates the extension (ERR_R_ASN1_LIB on failure) and moves the language, policy and path length into it, so the extension owns them. Returns the new extension, or NULL on any failure, in which case the partly collected language, pathlen and policy objects and any allocated extension are freed. The parsed value list is freed on both success and failure.

functions.name: X509_chain_check_suiteb
functions.prose_contract: Checks a certificate chain against the Suite B 128-bit LOS rules; returns X509_V_OK or an X509_V_ERR_SUITE_B_* code. Precondition: if x is NULL then chain must be non-NULL with the end-entity certificate as its first element; perror_depth may be NULL. If flags lacks X509_V_FLAG_SUITEB_128_LOS it returns X509_V_OK immediately. It takes the leaf key from x (or chain[0], starting the walk at index 1). With chain == NULL it only checks the leaf key algorithm and returns that check_suite_b result directly, without writing *perror_depth. Otherwise it returns X509_V_ERR_SUITE_B_INVALID_VERSION for a leaf that is not X.509 v3, then checks the leaf key, then walks the chain checking each certificate version (INVALID_VERSION) and each issuer key against the signature algorithm of the previous certificate, and finally checks the root signature. On a failure it moves the reported depth back by one (when non-zero) for INVALID_SIGNATURE_ALGORITHM and LOS_NOT_ALLOWED errors, and if the error is LOS_NOT_ALLOWED and the check changed the temporary flags (a P-384 certificate signed with P-256) it returns X509_V_ERR_SUITE_B_CANNOT_SIGN_P_384_WITH_P_256 instead. Only in the failing case with non-NULL perror_depth is *perror_depth written; on success it is left untouched. Returns X509_V_OK if all checks passed.

functions.name: build_chain
functions.prose_contract: Builds the certificate chain in ctx->chain, starting from the single leaf certificate, until a trust anchor is reached or no further issuer is found. Precondition: ctx->chain has exactly one element and ctx->num_untrusted equals 1 (otherwise internal error). Return value: 1 when the chain is trusted; 0 when trust was rejected, when a time-validity error was already reported, or when the verify callback returns 0 for a final error; -1 on an internal error (ctx->error = X509_V_ERR_UNSPECIFIED), allocation failure (X509_V_ERR_OUT_OF_MEM) or a trust store lookup failure (X509_V_ERR_STORE_LOOKUP); and, where it reports a final error through verify_cb_cert, the return value of that callback (non-zero only if the application callback chooses to continue). Search policy: it works on a shallow copy of the untrusted certificates (DANE trust anchors from DNS added first), searches the untrusted list unless none was given, and searches the trust store first when TRUSTED_FIRST is set or there is no untrusted list, with optional alternate chains (pruning untrusted certificates one at a time) unless X509_V_FLAG_NO_ALT_CHAINS; DANE without PKIX only disables the trust store search. The chain is extended by at most depth + 1 certificates. Trusted issuers replace or extend the top certificate (a self-signed untrusted certificate is replaced only by an identical trust store certificate, otherwise ignored), untrusted issuers are appended with a reference and removed from the working copy, and trust is re-evaluated with check_trust / check_dane_issuer after each addition. After the loop it tries bare DANE public-key trust and direct leaf trust when the chain is within the depth limit. For an untrusted result it reports, in order, an already recorded time error (returns 0), another preliminary ctx->error via the callback, X509_V_ERR_CERT_CHAIN_TOO_LONG, X509_V_ERR_DANE_NO_MATCH, a self-signed certificate error (DEPTH_ZERO_SELF_SIGNED_CERT for a one-element chain, else SELF_SIGNED_CERT_IN_CHAIN) or UNABLE_TO_GET_ISSUER_CERT / UNABLE_TO_GET_ISSUER_CERT_LOCALLY. The temporary untrusted copy is freed on all exits.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Demo QUIC client that opens several streams on one connection and prints the responses. Precondition: command line "[-6] hostname port" (fewer than 3 arguments, or fewer than 4 with -6, prints usage and ends with EXIT_FAILURE). It creates a QUIC client SSL_CTX with peer verification and default trust paths, an SSL with default stream mode disabled, a socket BIO to the host (IPv4 or IPv6) installed with SSL_set_bio, sets SNI, hostname verification, the ALPN list and the initial peer address, and calls SSL_connect (on failure it prints the verification error if any). It then creates one bidirectional and one unidirectional stream, writes an HTTP GET request on each with write_a_request (failure ends with EXIT_FAILURE), reads and prints everything from stream 1 until SSL_read_ex fails, accepts a server-initiated stream and reads and prints it the same way. After each read loop it inspects SSL_get_error: normal end (SSL_ERROR_ZERO_RETURN) continues; a stream error of type reset or unknown, and any other error, are only printed and execution continues; a connection-closed state jumps to the end with EXIT_FAILURE. Finally it calls SSL_shutdown repeatedly until it returns 1 (a negative result ends with EXIT_FAILURE). The result is EXIT_SUCCESS only if the shutdown loop completes, so a stream read error that is merely printed can still lead to EXIT_SUCCESS. At the end label it prints the OpenSSL error stack if the result is EXIT_FAILURE, frees the SSL objects, the context and the peer address (the BIO is owned by the SSL after SSL_set_bio) and returns the result.

functions.name: run_quic_server
functions.prose_contract: Main loop of the demo HTTP/3-over-QUIC server: accepts QUIC connections on the UDP socket fd and serves one at a time. Precondition: ctx is a server SSL_CTX and fd an open UDP socket. It creates a listener (SSL_new_listener), gives it fd, starts listening and puts it in non-blocking mode (any failure goes to the error exit), sets the nghttp3 callbacks and default memory functions, and then loops forever: it waits for socket activity, reads from the connection streams until the request headers have been received (an error from the wait or from reading, or 25 consecutive timeouts, goes to the error exit; a close by the peer before a request goes to the wait-for-close step), creates the server unidirectional streams if needed, builds a 200 response with content-type and content-length derived from the requested file (a missing file gives a default test page; a file of INT_MAX length uses an endless buffer of A bytes; a file whose data cannot be loaded makes the program abort), submits the response to nghttp3 and writes the stream data out with quic_server_write until nghttp3 has nothing more to send, and then waits for the connection to close, handling new-connection, restart and done events. At the end of each iteration it closes the streams and connection and loops to accept the next connection. A failure of nghttp3_conn_submit_response, of the writes or of the offsets goes to the error exit, which prints the OpenSSL error stack, frees the listener and returns 0. The statement that sets ok = 1 is placed after the infinite loop and no break or return at the loop own level leads to it, so this function is only left through the error exit and returns 0.

functions.name: OSSL_DEMO_H3_CONN_handle_events
functions.prose_contract: Runs one round of event handling for an HTTP/3 connection. Returns 0 if conn is NULL. Step 1: it accepts all pending incoming QUIC streams without blocking and registers each with h3_conn_accept_stream; if registration fails it frees that stream and returns 0. Step 2: it repeatedly asks nghttp3 for outgoing data (nghttp3_conn_writev_stream, up to 8 vectors) until nghttp3 has none; a negative result returns 0, and a stream id that is not in the stream map raises an internal error and returns 0. For each non-empty vector it writes the data to the QUIC stream with SSL_write_ex2 (adding the CONCLUDE flag when nghttp3 reports fin): data for a stream that was already discarded is treated as written; SSL_ERROR_WANT_WRITE is not an error, it counts 0 bytes written and blocks that stream in nghttp3 (so a vector may be only partly or not at all consumed and the function still goes on); any other write failure raises an internal error and returns 0; a successful write unblocks the stream. Whatever number of bytes was written is reported back to nghttp3 with add_write_offset and add_ack_offset (a failure returns 0). For a zero-length stream with fin it calls add_write_offset(0). Step 3: it sets conn->pump_res to 1 and runs h3_conn_pump_stream over all streams (incoming QUIC data to nghttp3); if that clears pump_res it returns 0. Returns 1 otherwise, including when some offered data could not be written because the send buffer was full.

functions.name: capi_dsa_do_sign
functions.prose_contract: DSA signing method of the Windows CryptoAPI engine: signs a 20-byte SHA-1 digest with the CAPI key attached to dsa and returns an OpenSSL DSA_SIG. Precondition: dsa carries a CAPI key in its ex data and its engine carries the CAPI context (neither pointer is checked before use except the key); digest points to dlen bytes. Returns NULL, with a CAPI error raised, if the key is missing (CAPI_R_CANT_GET_KEY), if dlen is not 20 (CAPI_R_INVALID_DIGEST_LENGTH), or if creating the SHA-1 hash object fails. Otherwise it loads the given digest bytes as the hash value (CryptSetHashParam; failure raises CAPI_R_CANT_SET_HASH_VALUE, returns NULL), signs the hash with CryptSignHash into a 40-byte buffer (failure raises CAPI_R_ERROR_SIGNING_HASH, returns NULL), and converts the first 20 bytes into r and the next 20 bytes into s, both read as little-endian numbers (lend_tobn), building a new DSA_SIG that owns r and s; allocation or conversion failure frees r and s and returns NULL. On all paths after the hash object was created, the signature buffer is cleansed and the hash object destroyed. The caller owns the returned DSA_SIG.

functions.name: digest_op
functions.prose_contract: Issues one CIOCCRYPT ioctl on the /dev/crypto descriptor for the digest session of ctx. Precondition: ctx->sess.ses is a valid open session; src points to srclen readable bytes (it may be NULL with srclen 0); res is NULL or a buffer for the digest; flags is a COP_FLAG_* value. It fills a zeroed crypt_op with the session id, length, source pointer, a NULL destination, the mac pointer set to res and the given flags, and returns the ioctl result unchanged: 0 on success and -1 (errno set) on failure, not 1. Whether the digest is written to res depends on the kernel and the flags passed in: the callers in this file use COP_FLAG_UPDATE with res NULL (digest_update, line 777) and COP_FLAG_FINAL with the output buffer (digest_final, line 794). The function itself does not check res or flags and writes nothing else.

functions.name: static inline int RISCV_HAS_##NAME(void)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function RISCV_HAS_<NAME> (from RISCV_DEFINE_CAP(NAME, INDEX, BIT_INDEX, HWPROBE_KEY, HWPROBE_VALUE) at riscv_arch.h:53-58, one static inline function per capability listed in riscv_arch.def). functions.name: SELF_TEST_post
functions.prose_contract: Runs the FIPS module power-on self tests (or re-runs them on demand) and moves the module to the running state on success. Precondition: st holds the module checksum data, file name and BIO callbacks (checked below, except that st is read after the lock); on_demand_test is non-zero when a re-test is requested. It first runs the one-time lock initialisation (failure returns 0). Before taking the lock: if the state is RUNNING and this is not an on-demand test it returns 1; any state other than RUNNING or SELFTEST raises PROV_R_INVALID_STATE and returns 0; these early returns do not change the module error state. It then takes the self-test write lock (failure returns 0). Under the lock it re-reads the state: RUNNING without on-demand unlocks and returns 1, RUNNING with on-demand switches the state to SELFTEST, anything other than SELFTEST unlocks, raises PROV_R_INVALID_STATE and returns 0. Then, with FIPS POST compiled in, it requires st and its checksum data (else PROV_R_MISSING_CONFIG_DATA), creates a self-test event object (failure returns 0), decodes the checksum (PROV_R_INVALID_CONFIG_DATA on failure), verifies the module file integrity (PROV_R_MODULE_INTEGRITY_FAILURE), runs the known-answer tests (PROV_R_SELF_TEST_KAT_FAILURE) and checks that the private RNG was restored (a missing TEST-RAND or an RNG still named TEST-RAND is PROV_R_SELF_TEST_KAT_FAILURE). On success the state becomes RUNNING and it returns 1; on any of these failures it sets the module error state (ossl_set_error_state) and returns 0. The lock is released and temporary objects and the module BIO freed on the paths after the lock was taken. Without FIPS POST it just sets RUNNING, unlocks and returns 1.

functions.name: rsa_decrypt
functions.prose_contract: RSA asymmetric cipher decrypt operation of the provider. Precondition: vprsactx is a PROV_RSA_CTX with an RSA key; outlen is non-NULL; in holds inlen bytes. Returns 0 at once if the provider is not running. If out is NULL it is a size query: in TLS padding mode it sets *outlen to SSL_MAX_MASTER_KEY_LENGTH and returns 1; in other modes it raises PROV_R_INVALID_KEY and returns 0 if the RSA size is 0, else sets *outlen to the RSA size and returns 1. Otherwise outsize must be at least SSL_MAX_MASTER_KEY_LENGTH (TLS padding) or the RSA size, else PROV_R_BAD_LENGTH and 0. For OAEP and TLS padding it decrypts into a temporary buffer with no padding (returning 0 without an error raised here if the allocation fails, and PROV_R_FAILED_TO_DECRYPT and 0 if the raw decryption does not return the full RSA size), then removes the padding: OAEP uses the label, the OAEP digest (fetching SHA-1 if none is set, 0 with ERR_R_INTERNAL_ERROR if that fails) and the MGF1 digest; TLS padding needs client_version > 0 (else PROV_R_BAD_TLS_CLIENT_VERSION and 0) and uses the TLS type 2 check with the client and alternative versions. The temporary buffer is freed on all these paths. Other padding modes decrypt directly into out with RSA_private_decrypt (PKCS#1 v1.5 without implicit rejection when implicit_rejection is 0). In the decrypting cases the final result r is handled in constant time: *outlen is set to r if r is not negative and left unchanged otherwise, and the function returns 1 if r is not negative and 0 if it is negative. Success therefore includes a decrypted length of 0.

functions.name: aes_get_ctx_params
functions.prose_contract: Reports the AES-CBC-HMAC-SHA cipher context parameters requested in params. Precondition: vctx is a PROV_AES_HMAC_SHA_CTX; params is an OSSL_PARAM array. For each parameter present it writes a value and stops at the first failing one, raising PROV_R_FAILED_TO_SET_PARAMETER and returning 0 (earlier parameters in the array may already have been filled). With multiblock support compiled in it provides the multiblock maximum buffer size (asked from the hardware method), the interleave, the AAD packet length and the encrypted length; it also provides, when requested, the TLS AAD padding (tls_aad_pad), key length, IV length, the original IV (oiv) and the updated IV (iv). The two IV parameters are first tried as a copied octet string of ivlen bytes; if that fails they are tried as an octet pointer, in which case the caller receives a pointer into the context (the address of the oiv or iv array), not a copy. Returns 1 if every parameter that is present was set, including the case where none is present.

functions.name: tls1_multi_block_encrypt
functions.prose_contract: Encrypts one large TLS 1.1+ application record as 4*n4x (n4x is 1 or 2) interleaved fragments with AES-CBC and HMAC-SHA1 using the multi-block assembly routines. Precondition: the context holds the key schedule, the MAC key states (md/tail) and the 13-byte AAD set by the multiblock AAD control; inp holds inp_len bytes; out has room for all fragments, each laid out as a 5-byte record header, a 16-byte explicit IV, the data, a 20-byte MAC and 1..16 padding bytes. Returns 0 if drawing 16*4*n4x random IV bytes with RAND_bytes_ex fails (nothing written). Otherwise it splits the input into x4 fragments of size frag (the last of size last, adjusted so the hash blocks line up), writes each IV before its fragment, computes the HMAC-SHA1 of every fragment in parallel starting from the saved inner state, with the sequence number incremented by the fragment index and the length field rewritten to that fragment length, while CBC-encrypting the data in chunks of up to 2048 bytes, then finishes the inner hash with padding, runs the outer hash, copies the remaining plaintext, appends the MAC and the padding, writes each 5-byte record header (type and version bytes from the AAD, length including the IV, MAC and padding) and finally runs the last CBC pass. It cleanses the temporary hash blocks and context, stores the total number of output bytes in ctx->multiblock_encrypt_len and returns that total. No error is raised for the early return.

functions.name: aes_gcm_siv_decrypt
functions.prose_contract: AES-GCM-SIV decryption of len bytes from in to out, and computation of the tag that the plaintext should have; it does not itself compare the tag. Precondition: ctx holds the derived keys, nonce, the user-supplied tag (user_tag), the AAD (aad, aad_len) and the ecb cipher context; in and out have len bytes. It clears generated_tag first. It returns 0 without decrypting if the context has already been used to decrypt (used_dec) and speed mode is off, or if len exceeds 2^36. Otherwise it forms the CTR initial block from user_tag with the top bit of its last byte set, decrypts in to out with the 32-bit counter routine, then computes the POLYVAL hash over the AAD (padded to 16 bytes), the decrypted data (last partial block zero-padded) and the bit lengths of AAD and data, XORs in the nonce, clears the top bit of the last byte, and encrypts the result with AES-ECB into ctx->tag (the locally computed S_s block is only an intermediate). generated_tag is set to 1 if the decryption and tag encryption succeeded, used_dec is set to 1 whether or not an error occurred, and the function returns 1 on success and 0 if the CTR routine or the ECB encryption failed. The plaintext is already in out when it returns; checking ctx->tag against user_tag is done elsewhere.

functions.name: aes_ocb_block_update_internal
functions.prose_contract: Feeds inl bytes of in through the AES-OCB block routine ciph in whole 16-byte blocks, keeping any partial block in buf (with fill count *bufsz). It is used for both data (out non-NULL) and AAD (out NULL, with the AAD buffer). Precondition: buf holds AES_BLOCK_SIZE bytes, *bufsz <= 16; outsize is the room in out. If a partial block is buffered it first tops it up from in (ossl_cipher_fillblock); when that fills a block, it requires outsize >= 16 (else PROV_R_OUTPUT_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL and 0), processes the block with ciph (failure raises PROV_R_CIPHER_OPERATION_FAILED and returns 0), clears *bufsz, counts 16 output bytes and advances out. It then processes the whole blocks that remain in in (requiring outsize to cover the counted bytes, else error 0; ciph failure 0), and stores any trailing partial block in buf via ossl_cipher_trailingdata (its failure returns 0, error already raised). On success *outl is set to the number of bytes counted as processed (bytes written to out for data; for AAD, the AAD bytes consumed, since nothing is written) and the return value is 1 only if all input was consumed (inl == 0 at the end). *outl is not set on any failure path.

functions.name: chacha20_poly1305_aead_cipher
functions.prose_contract: Single entry point of the ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD for AAD, data and final calls (and TLS records). Precondition: bctx holds a PROV_CHACHA20_POLY1305_CTX; outl is non-NULL; in/out/inl select the call type: in != NULL and out == NULL is AAD; in != NULL and out != NULL is data; in == NULL is the explicit final. If the MAC has not been started: in TLS mode (a TLS payload length is set) with out non-NULL it returns 0 when inl is not payload length + 16 (without setting *outl) and otherwise, unless built for small footprint, returns the result of chacha20_poly1305_tls_cipher; else it derives the Poly1305 key from block 0 of the ChaCha20 stream, starts the MAC, resets counters and lengths, and in TLS mode absorbs the TLS AAD. AAD calls feed the MAC, add to the AAD length and finish with *outl = inl although nothing is written. Data calls first pad out the AAD to a block, require inl equal to payload length + 16 in TLS mode (otherwise error exit with *outl = 0 and result 0), and encrypt-then-MAC (encrypt) or MAC-then-decrypt (decrypt) plen bytes, advancing in and out. A final or TLS tag step (when in is NULL or inl differs from plen) pads the data, appends the lengths to the MAC and finishes it: when encrypting the tag is stored in ctx->tag and, for an appended-tag record, copied to out; when decrypting with an appended tag a mismatch zeroes the plen output bytes and takes the error exit with result 0, and a match strips the tag from inl; for an explicit final on decryption the computed tag is compared with the stored tag (mismatch gives the error exit with result 0). On success *outl is set to inl as it stands (for appended-tag decryption the input length minus 16, for other calls the number of bytes processed or consumed) and the result is 1; on the error exit *outl is 0 and the result is 0.

functions.name: tdes_init
functions.prose_contract: Common initialisation for triple-DES encrypt and decrypt contexts. Precondition: vctx is a PROV_CIPHER_CTX of a TDES cipher; key and iv may each be NULL (to keep the previous ones); keylen/ivlen describe them. Returns 0 at once if the provider is not running. Before any other check it resets the partial-block state (num and bufsz to 0) and stores the direction ctx->enc = enc, so these changes remain even if a later step fails. If iv is non-NULL it installs it with ossl_cipher_generic_initiv (failure returns 0, an IV length problem being checked there). If iv is NULL and an IV had been set earlier in CBC, CFB or OFB mode, the working IV is reset from the original IV. If key is non-NULL its length must equal ctx->keylen (else PROV_R_INVALID_KEY_LENGTH and 0), the hardware init sets the key schedule (failure returns 0) and key_set is set to 1. It then applies params through ossl_tdes_set_ctx_params (failure returns 0), and in FIPS builds checks that encryption is approved (failure returns 0). Returns 1 on success, which also happens when key and iv are both NULL (nothing is then installed).

functions.name: ossl_cipher_generic_block_final
functions.prose_contract: Finishes a block-cipher operation by processing the last buffered data. Precondition: vctx is a PROV_CIPHER_CTX; out has outsize bytes; outl is non-NULL. Returns 0 if the provider is not running, 0 with PROV_R_NO_KEY_SET if no key was set, and 0 with PROV_R_CIPHER_OPERATION_FAILED for a TLS-mode context (a TLS-mode context is rejected by this function). Encrypting: with padding enabled it pads whatever number of bytes is buffered (any length from 0 to blocksize-1) to a full block; without padding, an empty buffer gives *outl = 0 and 1, and a buffer that is not exactly one block gives PROV_R_WRONG_FINAL_BLOCK_LENGTH and 0. It then needs outsize >= blocksize (else PROV_R_OUTPUT_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL and 0), encrypts that block into out (failure PROV_R_CIPHER_OPERATION_FAILED, 0), clears bufsz, sets *outl to the block size and returns 1. Decrypting: the buffer must hold exactly one block, except that an empty buffer without padding returns *outl = 0 and 1; any other length raises PROV_R_WRONG_FINAL_BLOCK_LENGTH and returns 0. It decrypts that block in place (failure 0), removes the padding when padding is enabled (failure 0 with the error already raised by the unpad routine), requires outsize to cover the remaining bytes (else PROV_R_OUTPUT_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL and 0), copies them to out, sets *outl to their count, clears bufsz and returns 1. *outl is not set on failure.

functions.name: ccm_cipher_internal
functions.prose_contract: Common AES-CCM cipher entry point covering the message-length, AAD, data and final steps (and TLS records). Precondition: ctx holds the CCM context; padlen is non-NULL. Returns 0 (without setting *padlen) if no key was set. If a TLS AAD was set (tls_aad_len initialised) it returns the result of ccm_tls_cipher, which works in place on a record with 8-byte explicit IV and tag, copies the explicit IV on encryption, sets the CCM IV and message length (so len_set becomes 1), sets the saved AAD, encrypts or decrypts, and reports the output length in *padlen; it does not reset iv_set, tag_set or len_set after a TLS decryption. In the normal path: in == NULL with out != NULL (final, which returns no data) returns 1 with *padlen = 0; otherwise the IV must be set (else error exit). With out == NULL: in == NULL passes the message length len to ccm_set_iv (sets len_set); in != NULL is AAD, which needs the message length to be set when len is non-zero, and is fed to setaad. With out != NULL: if the length is not yet set it is set from len; when encrypting it runs auth_encrypt and sets tag_set; when decrypting the tag must already be set, it runs auth_decrypt against the stored tag and then clears iv_set, tag_set and len_set. A failing step goes to the error exit. On success *padlen = len for AAD, length or data calls, and 1 is returned; on the error exit *padlen = 0 and 0 is returned.

functions.name: gcm_init
functions.prose_contract: Common initialisation of an AES-GCM context for encryption or decryption. Precondition: vctx is a PROV_GCM_CTX; iv and key may each be NULL to leave the current ones unchanged; params may carry further settings. Returns 0 if the provider is not running. It stores the direction ctx->enc = enc before checking anything else, so this change persists even if a later step fails. If iv is non-NULL its length must be between 1 and the size of the internal IV buffer (else PROV_R_INVALID_IV_LENGTH and 0); it is then copied into the context, ivlen is updated and the IV state becomes buffered. If key is non-NULL its length must equal ctx->keylen (else PROV_R_INVALID_KEY_LENGTH and 0), the hardware setkey installs the key (failure returns 0) and the TLS record counter is reset to 0. Finally it returns the result of ossl_gcm_set_ctx_params(ctx, params). Because both iv and key are optional, a successful return does not mean an IV or key was installed by this call. When the IV was already updated and the key check fails, the new IV stays in place.

functions.name: scrypt_alg
functions.prose_contract: Computes the scrypt key derivation (RFC 7914) of pass and salt with cost N, block size r and parallelism p, writing keylen bytes to key, or only validating the parameters when key is NULL. Precondition: N must be a power of two of at least 2, r and p non-zero, sha256 a fetched SHA-256 digest; maxmem is the memory limit in bytes. It returns 0 without raising an error if r or p is 0, N < 2 or N is not a power of two. It returns 0 with EVP_R_MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED if p > (2^30 - 1) / r, if 16*r is small enough and N >= 2^(16*r), if p*128*r exceeds INT_MAX, if the size of the work array 128*r*(N+2) words would overflow, or if the total memory p*128*r + 32*r*(N+2)*4 exceeds maxmem (maxmem is capped at SIZE_MAX). If key is NULL it returns 1 here, having only checked the parameters. Otherwise it allocates one buffer holding B, X, T and V (returning 0 without an error if allocation fails), derives B with one-iteration PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 from pass and salt, runs scryptROMix over each of the p blocks, and derives the output key with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 from pass and the mixed B. A failure of either PBKDF2 call raises EVP_R_PBKDF2_ERROR and returns 0. The work buffer is cleared and freed on all paths after it was allocated. Returns 1 on success.

functions.name: ecxkem_init
functions.prose_contract: Initialises an X25519/X448 KEM (encapsulate or decapsulate) context. Precondition: vecxctx is a PROV_ECX_CTX; vecx is the recipient key (dereferenced without a NULL check by ecx_key_check); vauth is an optional authentication key; operation is EVP_PKEY_OP_ENCAPSULATE or EVP_PKEY_OP_DECAPSULATE. It returns 0 if the provider is not running, and 0 without changing the context if the recipient key fails the check (a key without a private part is only accepted when the operation is not decapsulation). It then replaces the context recipient key: recipient_key_set frees the old recipient key first, looks up the KEM info for the key (returning -2 if the key type has no KEM info, in which case the old key is already released and the new one not stored), sets the KDF name to HKDF, and takes a reference on the new key (returning 0 if the reference cannot be taken); a result <= 0 from this step is returned unchanged. If an authentication key vauth is given, it must match the parameters of the recipient key, must have a private part when the operation is encapsulation, and must be stored by sender_authkey_set (which also frees the old sender key and takes a reference); any of these failing returns 0 (the recipient key set earlier stays in place). Finally it records the operation in ctx->op and returns the result of ecxkem_set_ctx_params(vecxctx, params). A successful return is the result of that last call.

functions.name: ossl_prov_drbg_instantiate
functions.prose_contract: Instantiates a DRBG: gathers entropy and a nonce and calls the DRBG-specific instantiate. Precondition: drbg is valid; strength must not exceed drbg->strength; pers (NULL selects the built-in personalisation string) must not be longer than drbg->max_perslen. The function returns 1 exactly when drbg->state equals EVP_RAND_STATE_READY at the end label, otherwise 0. Early failures jump to the end without changing the state: a requested strength above drbg->strength (PROV_R_INSUFFICIENT_DRBG_STRENGTH) and a too long personalisation string (PROV_R_PERSONALISATION_STRING_TOO_LONG) leave the state as it was; a state other than UNINITIALISED raises PROV_R_IN_ERROR_STATE (state ERROR) or PROV_R_ALREADY_INSTANTIATED and also leaves the state as it was, so for a DRBG that is already READY the function raises that error but still returns 1. Otherwise it sets the state to ERROR and tries to obtain a nonce when min_noncelen > 0 (from the parent nonce callback, by increasing the requested entropy when a parent exists, or from prov_drbg_get_nonce without a parent), computes the next reseed counter, obtains entropy of the required size (PROV_R_ERROR_RETRIEVING_ENTROPY on a size violation) and calls drbg->instantiate (failure raises PROV_R_ERROR_INSTANTIATING_DRBG). The entropy is cleaned up after the instantiate call, and the nonce at the end label. Only on success does it set the state to READY, generate_counter to 1, reseed_time to the current time and publish the reseed counter, so on a failure after the state was set the state stays ERROR and the reseed counter is not advanced.

functions.name: ossl_prov_drbg_reseed_unlocked
functions.prose_contract: Reseeds a DRBG whose lock is already held by the caller. Precondition: drbg valid; ent (may be NULL) is caller-supplied entropy of ent_len bytes within the DRBG entropy length limits; adin/adinlen is optional additional input within max_adinlen. Returns 1 only if the state is READY at the end, otherwise 0. It returns 0 at once if the provider is not running. If the state is not READY it first calls rand_drbg_restart to try to recover (which may change the state); afterwards a state of ERROR raises PROV_R_IN_ERROR_STATE and a state of UNINITIALISED raises PROV_R_NOT_INSTANTIATED, both returning 0 without touching the state further. If ent is given and shorter than min_entropylen or longer than max_entropylen it raises an error, sets the state to ERROR and returns 0. A too long adin raises PROV_R_ADDITIONAL_INPUT_TOO_LONG and returns 0 (state unchanged). From then on the state is set to ERROR and only set back to READY on success. It computes the next reseed counter; if ent was given it is applied with drbg->reseed (in FIPS builds as additional input with no entropy, otherwise as entropy together with adin, after which adin is not used again), a failure raising PROV_R_UNABLE_TO_RESEED and returning 0. It then draws entropy from its own sources (a size violation raises PROV_R_ERROR_RETRIEVING_ENTROPY and goes to the end, returning 0) and reseeds with it. Only on success does it set READY, generate_counter = 1, reseed_time = now, publish the reseed counter and refresh the parent reseed counter; the temporary entropy is cleaned up at the end label.

functions.name: rsa_set_ctx_params
functions.prose_contract: Applies signature context parameters (FIPS indicators, digest and properties, padding mode, PSS salt length, MGF1 digest) to an RSA signature context. Precondition: vprsactx is a PROV_RSA_CTX; params is an OSSL_PARAM array that may be empty. Returns 0 if the context is NULL; returns 1 immediately if params is empty (no defaults are applied then). Otherwise it first processes the four FIPS indicator parameters (any failure returns 0), then reads the digest name and properties (a failed string read returns 0). The pad mode may be given as an integer or a string name; an unknown name or other type returns 0 (an unknown string leaves the current mode); OAEP padding, and PSS padding for a context that is not signing or verifying, are rejected with PROV_R_ILLEGAL_OR_UNSUPPORTED_PADDING_MODE, as are PKCS1, no-padding and X9.31 padding for non-RSA key types (X9.31 has extra FIPS checks). A PSS salt length requires PSS padding to be the selected mode (PROV_R_NOT_SUPPORTED otherwise); it may be an integer or one of the strings digest, max, auto, auto-digestmax or a decimal number; values below RSA_PSS_SALTLEN_AUTO_DIGEST_MAX give PROV_R_INVALID_SALT_LENGTH, and for a PSS-restricted key an auto salt length is only allowed when verifying and a salt length shorter than min_saltlen (or digest size shorter than it) gives PROV_R_PSS_SALTLEN_TOO_SMALL. An MGF1 digest requires PSS padding (PROV_R_INVALID_MGF1_MD otherwise). Only after all these parsing checks pass does it store saltlen and pad_mode in the context; it then defaults the digest to RSA_DEFAULT_DIGEST_NAME when PSS padding is selected and no digest is set, sets up the MGF1 digest if given (failure returns 0), and sets up the digest if one was given or defaulted (failure returns 0), otherwise it checks that the existing digest is compatible with the padding (failure returns 0). Returns 1 on success. An earlier failure leaves saltlen and pad_mode unchanged, but a later failure (MGF1 or digest setup) happens after they were stored.

functions.name: rsa_sign
functions.prose_contract: One-shot RSA signing entry point of the provider signature implementation. Precondition: vprsactx is a PROV_RSA_CTX initialised for signing; sig may be NULL to ask for the signature length; sigsize is the room in sig. It returns 0 without raising an error if the provider is not running or the context is NULL. If the context does not allow one-shot calls (flag_allow_oneshot clear, for example after a streaming update began) it raises PROV_R_ONESHOT_CALL_OUT_OF_ORDER and returns 0. For a message-signing context (EVP_PKEY_OP_SIGNMSG): with sig == NULL it only calls rsa_sign_message_final to obtain the length and does not feed tbs to the digest; otherwise it returns the logical AND of rsa_signverify_message_update(tbs, tbslen) and rsa_sign_message_final(sig, siglen, sigsize), skipping the final step if the update fails. For any other operation it returns the result of rsa_sign_directly (signing the already prepared tbs directly). The return value is that of the delegated function, or 0 for the early failures.

functions.name: file_set_ctx_params
functions.prose_contract: Applies store context parameters to a file store loader context. Precondition: loaderctx is a struct file_ctx_st (dereferenced without a NULL check); params may be empty. It returns 1 at once if params is empty. For a context that is not a directory it replaces the stored property query (OSSL_STORE_PARAM_PROPERTIES) and input type (OSSL_STORE_PARAM_INPUT_TYPE) if present: the old string is freed and set to NULL first and a failed string read returns 0 (leaving that field NULL). For a directory these two parameters are accepted but ignored. OSSL_STORE_PARAM_EXPECT is read into expected_type for every kind of context (failed read returns 0). OSSL_STORE_PARAM_SUBJECT, if present, is only allowed for directories (otherwise it raises PROV_R_SEARCH_ONLY_SUPPORTED_FOR_DIRECTORIES and returns 0); the DER-encoded name is decoded, hashed with X509_NAME_hash_ex and written as an 8-digit hexadecimal string into the directory search name; a failed octet string read or DER decode returns 0, and a hash failure returns 0 after the search name was already written. Failures other than the subject-on-file case raise no error here. Returns 1 if all present parameters were handled.

functions.name: compute_pqueue_growth
functions.prose_contract: Computes a new capacity for the priority queue arrays by repeatedly multiplying current by 8/5 until it reaches target. Parameters are sizes; max_nodes (SIZE_MAX divided by the larger of the heap and element sizes) is a file-level limit. If current >= target it returns current unchanged without looping. Otherwise, while current < target: it returns 0 if current is already at or above max_nodes; it sets current to current*8/5 using the overflow-checked safe_muldiv_size_t and returns 0 if that computation reports overflow; and it clamps current to max_nodes if the product reached or exceeded it. When the loop ends it returns the resulting current, which is then at least target and at most max_nodes. So a target above max_nodes ends with 0 (after clamping, the next iteration sees current >= max_nodes), and a target at or below max_nodes returns a value between target and max_nodes. Caveat: when current is 0 and target is positive, 0*8/5 stays 0, so the loop never terminates; callers must not pass a zero current with a non-zero target.

functions.name: json_undefer
functions.prose_contract: Emits any deferred indentation. If json->defer_indent is not set it returns without doing anything. Otherwise it calls json_indent, which clears defer_indent first (so there is no recursion) and, only in pretty-print mode, writes a newline followed by indentation of depth*4 repetitions of a four-space string, where depth is the number of open containers on the bit stack; that is 16 spaces per level, not 4. When pretty printing is off the flag is simply cleared and nothing is written. Writes go through json_write_char and json_write_str, which do nothing once the encoder is in the error state and raise the error flag if the write buffer rejects a write; json_undefer itself returns nothing.

functions.name: json_pre_item
functions.prose_contract: Prepares the encoder for the next value (the part that writes separators before an item). Returns 0 without raising a new error if the encoder is already in the error state. State PRE_COMMA: it looks at the top of the container stack: if the top is an object (value 0) it raises the error flag and returns 0 (a value was given where a key was expected); if the top is an array (value 1) it writes a comma, returns 0 if that write failed, and then calls json_indent; if the stack is empty (negative result) and sequence mode is on it writes the 0x1E record separator (a write failure here is not checked, so the function can still return 1 after a write error); then the state becomes PRE_ITEM. State PRE_ITEM: nothing to do. State PRE_KEY or any other value: it raises the error flag and returns 0. Returns 1 when the encoder is ready for the item, including when the container stack is empty.

functions.name: composite_end
functions.prose_contract: Closes an object (type 0, char }) or an array (type 1, char ]). Returns without doing anything if the encoder is already in the error state. It clears defer_indent (remembering the old value), then raises the error flag and returns if the container on top of the stack is not of the requested type or the stack is empty (peek differs from type), or if closing an object while the state is PRE_ITEM, i.e. a key has been written but its value is still pending; closing an empty object (state PRE_KEY or PRE_COMMA) is allowed. It then pops the stack (failure raises the error flag and returns), writes an indentation only if the opening bracket was not followed directly by this close (was_defer clear), writes the closing character and runs json_post_item, which sets the state to PRE_COMMA and, for an outermost value in sequence mode, writes a newline. The character writes can themselves raise the error flag.

functions.name: ossl_json_key
functions.prose_contract: Writes an object key. Returns without doing anything if the encoder is already in the error state. It raises the error flag and returns if the top of the container stack is not an object (peek != 0, including an empty stack). If the state is PRE_COMMA (a previous member was written) it writes a comma and moves the state to PRE_KEY. It then writes the indentation (json_indent, which only emits output in pretty mode) and, if the state is not PRE_KEY at that point (for example a key was already written and its value is pending), it raises the error flag and returns. Otherwise it writes the key as a quoted string, then a colon (followed by a space in pretty mode) unless a write error occurred, and sets the state to PRE_ITEM, awaiting the value. It returns nothing; failures are recorded in the encoder error flag.

functions.name: ossl_ackm_on_rx_packet
functions.prose_contract: Records the receipt of a QUIC packet in the acknowledgement manager. Precondition: ackm and pkt are valid and pkt->pkt_space is a valid packet number space. If the packet number is not processable (already processed or written off, as reported by ossl_ackm_is_rx_pn_processable) it returns 1 without changing anything. Otherwise it updates the largest received packet number and its receive time for that space when the new number is larger, remembers whether the number had been implied missing by an earlier ACK frame, and adds the number to the receive history; if adding fails (rx_pkt_history_add_pn returns something other than 1) it returns 0 (the largest-number update has already been applied). For an ack-eliciting packet it then calls ackm_on_rx_ack_eliciting, which may bring forward the ACK flush deadline (immediately if the number was previously missing, subject to that helper). Finally it increments the ECT0, ECT1 or ECN-CE counter of that space according to pkt->ecn (no counter for other values) and returns 1.

functions.name: ch_rx_handle_packet
functions.prose_contract: Processes the single received QUIC packet held in ch->qrx_pkt and returns nothing. Precondition: ch->qrx_pkt is non-NULL (asserted in debug builds). It returns without effect if the channel is not active, or if the packet is of an encrypted type and its encryption level has already been discarded. For the first encrypted packet it records the remote source connection id as the current remote destination id and initial source id, marks that an encrypted packet was received and tells the packet transmitter. For a client it silently ignores a packet whose source address differs from the current peer address, and a packet that carries a source connection id different from the initial one. A packet with a version that is not QUIC version 1 is dropped. A version negotiation packet (version field 0) is ignored if it is malformed or if any packet was processed before it; otherwise the supported versions in it are scanned and if version 1 is listed the packet transmitter version is set and the channel is restarted with ch_restart (an internal protocol error if that fails), else a connection-refused protocol error (unsupported version) is raised. For other packets it marks that a packet was processed, and an encrypted packet with non-zero reserved header bits raises a protocol violation and is dropped. After logging the packet it dispatches by type: a Retry packet is ignored when the channel is already retrying, is a server, has already received an encrypted packet, is too short, or fails the integrity-tag check, and otherwise is handled with ch_retry (an internal error is raised if that fails); a 0-RTT packet is ignored by a client and otherwise does nothing further here; Initial, Handshake and 1-RTT packets cause a server to discard the initial encryption level when a handshake packet arrives, raise a key-update error for a 1-RTT packet with an old key epoch during a pending key update, raise a protocol violation if a client receives an Initial packet carrying a token, and otherwise pass the packet to ossl_quic_handle_frames (result not checked) and run ch_tick_tls if a crypto frame was seen; any other type is unexpected (assertion).

functions.name: ossl_quic_conn_shutdown
functions.prose_contract: Shuts down a QUIC connection in up to three phases and reports whether it is complete. Precondition: s is a QUIC connection SSL (not a stream); the function takes the connection lock itself, so the caller must not hold it. flags select behaviour (no stream flush, no blocking, wait for the peer, rapid); args may be NULL, otherwise it supplies the application error code and reason. Returns -1 if s is not a QUIC object or is a stream object (the latter raises SSL_R_CONN_USE_ONLY). It returns 1 immediately if the channel is already terminated. Phase 1 (only when not waiting for the peer and stream flushing is wanted): it starts the stream flush and, if not finished, waits for it when blocking is allowed (a failed or interrupted wait ends the call with return 0) or else just ticks the reactor if autotick is enabled; if the flush is still not finished it returns 0 (ongoing). Phase 2 (only with wait-for-peer and the channel not yet terminating): it waits for the peer to close (failed wait returns 0) or ticks, and returns 0 if the channel is still not terminating. It then marks the connection as shutting down, requests a local close with the given error code and reason (a no-op if already terminating), sets the TLS object SSL_SENT_SHUTDOWN, and returns 1 if the channel is now terminated. Phase 3: unless no-block or rapid is set (or the connection is non-blocking) it waits for termination (failed wait returns 0), else it ticks if autotick is enabled; the result is whether the channel is terminated (1) or not (0). The lock is released on every return after it was taken.

functions.name: ossl_quic_conn_poll_events
functions.prose_contract: Reports which of the requested poll events currently hold for a QUIC SSL object (connection, stream or listener). Precondition: ssl is a QUIC object (else it returns 0 and p_revents is not written); events is a mask of SSL_POLL_EVENT_* bits; p_revents is non-NULL; the function takes the object lock itself. If the object has a connection that has not been started, only the writable event can be reported: SSL_POLL_EVENT_W is set in the result if it was requested, without testing any predicate, no reactor tick is performed even if do_tick is non-zero, and no other event is examined. Otherwise, if do_tick is non-zero it first runs one reactor tick. For an object with a stream component it then tests the read, read-exception, write and write-exception events requested. For a connection object (not a stream) it tests connection exception, connection exception drain, incoming bidirectional and unidirectional stream availability and outgoing bidirectional and unidirectional stream availability. For a listener it tests listener exception and incoming connection availability. Each bit is set only if it was requested and its test holds. It releases the lock, stores the resulting mask in *p_revents and returns 1.

functions.name: qrx_process_pkt
functions.prose_contract: Processes one packet inside a received datagram: decodes the header, removes header protection, decrypts the body and queues the decrypted packet on the pending list. Precondition: pkt is a PACKET positioned at the start of this packet, pkt_idx is its index in the datagram, urxe is the datagram entry, first_dcid is the destination connection id of the first packet (used for coalesced packets), datagram_len is the full datagram length. Return value: 1 means the packet is deferred (its encryption level is not yet available, or 1-RTT is not yet allowed), after advancing pkt past this packet; 0 means the packet was either queued successfully or dropped as malformed, and the two cases are not distinguished by the return value. Behaviour: a free receive entry is reserved (failure goes to the malformed path); a packet already marked processed, a header that does not decode, or a header failing the early validation is malformed. An unencrypted packet type (such as version negotiation) is copied into a reserved entry, marked processed and appended to the pending list without decryption (a failed reservation is malformed). For encrypted packets the encryption level must exist (otherwise deferral; an error from the level lookup is malformed); for Initial packets the token pointer is relocated after a buffer relocation; the header protection is removed if this has not been done and the header decoded again; the header is validated, an optional message callback is invoked, a buffer for the plaintext is reserved (failure sets the end-of-packet pointer to NULL and goes to the malformed path), the body is decrypted (failure is malformed), and late validation is run (failure is malformed). A 1-RTT packet whose key phase differs from the current epoch triggers a key update initiation. On success the packet is marked processed, the entry receives the decrypted data, key epoch, addresses and receive time, the largest packet number of its space is updated, and it is moved from the free list to the pending list. In the malformed path the packet is marked processed and, if the end of this packet is known, only this packet is skipped; if it is unknown (early allocation failure, undecodable header, or the plaintext-buffer reservation failure) the whole rest of the datagram is skipped.

functions.name: ossl_quic_stream_map_notify_reset_recv_part
functions.prose_contract: Handles a received RESET_STREAM for the receive part of stream qs. Precondition: qsm and qs valid; app_error_code and final_size come from the frame. The result depends on the receive state. If the stream has no receive part (state NONE or any unrecognised state) it returns 0 (caller error). In the states RECV, SIZE_KNOWN and DATA_RECVD it returns 0 if a final size was already known and differs from final_size (the final size may not change); the caller therefore does not have to guarantee equality, it is checked here. Otherwise it moves the state to RESET_RECVD, records the peer reset error code, clears want_stop_sending, frees the receive stream buffer and sets it to NULL, calls ossl_quic_stream_map_update_state, and returns 1. In the states DATA_READ, RESET_RECVD and RESET_READ it ignores the frame and returns 1 without changing anything and without comparing final_size (such a frame may be a reordered or retransmitted one).

functions.name: txp_generate_stream_related
functions.prose_contract: Generates the stream-related frames (STOP_SENDING, RESET_STREAM, MAX_STREAM_DATA and STREAM data) for the streams that need to send something, into the packet under construction. Precondition: txp, pkt valid; have_ack_eliciting and tmp_head non-NULL; the stream map iterator visits streams with pending work. For each stream it first clears the per-packet bookkeeping flags (sent_fc, sent_stop_sending, sent_reset_stream, blocked, new credit consumed). If a STOP_SENDING is wanted it begins a frame (failure returns 0), encodes it (if it does not fit the frame is rolled back, the stream is linked on the temporary list and the loop stops with result 1), commits (failure returns 0) and marks it sent. If a RESET_STREAM is wanted it requires the stream to be in the reset-sent state (else returns 0), gets the final size (a failure returns 0), encodes and commits the frame the same way (rollback, link and stop when it does not fit), marks it sent and computes the flow control credit consumed (returning 0 if the final size is below the stream send window mark). If the receive part is still receiving and a MAX_STREAM_DATA is needed it is encoded and committed in the same manner. If the stream has a send buffer and is not reset it calls txp_generate_stream_frames; a failure links the stream on the temporary list and returns 0, otherwise the consumed connection credit is added up and, when the packet is full, the stream is linked and the loop stops with result 1. At the end of each loop iteration that did not break out the stream is linked on the temporary list. Returns 1 if the loop finished or stopped because a frame did not fit; returns 0 on the allocation, assertion or encoding failures listed. The failures at the begin and commit steps return 0 before the current stream is linked on the temporary list, whereas a failure inside txp_generate_stream_frames links it first.

functions.name: tls_post_encryption_processing_default
functions.prose_contract: Finishes the record packet after the payload was encrypted: accounts for encryption growth, adds the MAC for encrypt-then-MAC, closes the length field, reports the header to the message callback and finalises the packet. Precondition: thispkt holds the record header and the encrypted payload, thiswr describes the record, mac_size is the MAC size (0 if none). Every failing step raises a fatal internal-error alert (SSL_AD_INTERNAL_ERROR) and returns 0. First it reads the packet length origlen and requires that the allowed overhead covers the record length (assertion), that encryption did not shrink the data (origlen <= thiswr->length), and, if the record is longer than origlen, it allocates the extra bytes in the packet (this growth is not added to thiswr->length, which already contains it). If encrypt-then-MAC is in use and mac_size is non-zero, it allocates mac_size bytes, computes the MAC into them and adds mac_size to the record length. It then reads the packet length and closes the length sub-packet. If a message callback is set it reports the record header (and, for TLS 1.3 with encryption active, the inner content type) before the packet is finished. It then finishes the packet and adds the header length (5 bytes, or 13 for DTLS) to thiswr->length. Returns 1 on success.

functions.name: tls_write_records
functions.prose_contract: Record layer write entry point: builds the records for numtempl templates and sends them. Precondition: no earlier pipe buffer is still pending (rl->nextwbuf is past the last pipe or the next buffer has nothing left); otherwise it raises a fatal internal-error alert (ERR_R_SHOULD_NOT_HAVE_BEEN_CALLED) and returns OSSL_RECORD_RETURN_FATAL. It then calls the protocol-specific write_records method to encrypt and frame the templates into the write buffers; if that fails it returns OSSL_RECORD_RETURN_FATAL (the method itself is responsible for raising any error; none is raised here). It sets nextwbuf to 0 and returns the result of tls_retry_write_records, which writes the buffers to the BIO one after another: OSSL_RECORD_RETURN_SUCCESS when all pipes were written (nextwbuf then equals numwpipes, it is not reset to 0), OSSL_RECORD_RETURN_RETRY when the BIO asks for a retry (the position is kept for the next call), OSSL_RECORD_RETURN_FATAL when the BIO write fails without a retry condition (only a system error is queued, no alert), when no BIO is set (SSL_R_BIO_NOT_SET alert), or when a copy of a moving application buffer cannot be allocated, or the value returned by the optional prepare_write_bio hook when that is not success.

functions.name: tls_default_read_n
functions.prose_contract: Reads at least n bytes into the record layer read buffer from the underlying BIO (up to max bytes when read-ahead allows) and sets *readbytes to n on success. Precondition: rl has a read buffer; n > 0 (n == 0 returns OSSL_RECORD_RETURN_NON_FATAL_ERR); extend non-zero means the data continues the current packet; clearold == 1 allows moving the pending data to the start of the buffer. With extend == 0 it starts a new packet: if no bytes are buffered (left == 0) the buffer offset is reset to the aligned start, otherwise the packet starts at the current offset (so it is not necessarily aligned), and the packet pointer is set with length 0. A NULL packet pointer is a fatal internal error. If the packet is not at the aligned start and clearold == 1, the packet and the buffered bytes are moved to the aligned start. For DTLS, an extend request with nothing buffered returns NON_FATAL_ERR (a record header without body) and n is reduced to the buffered amount if that is smaller. If the buffer already holds at least n bytes it takes them (advancing packet_length and offset, reducing left) and returns SUCCESS. If n does not fit in the rest of the buffer it is a fatal internal error. Otherwise it loops reading from the previous BIO (rl->prev) or the main BIO: in TLS without read-ahead it reads at most n bytes, otherwise up to max (capped to the buffer space); a read that would block on the previous BIO frees it and continues with the main BIO; on a retry, end of file or other failure it stores the count already read in rb->left (so the partial bytes stay buffered), releases the buffer in TLS (not DTLS) mode if release-buffers is set and nothing is held, and returns RETRY, EOF or FATAL (no BIO set raises SSL_R_READ_BIO_NOT_SET); for DTLS it stops after one read at the amount received. After enough bytes arrive it updates offset, left and packet_length and returns SUCCESS.

functions.name: ssl3_cbc_copy_mac
functions.prose_contract: Extracts the MAC from the end of a decrypted CBC record in constant time with respect to the (secret) padding length, returning either the real MAC or a random one. Precondition: *reclen is the record length already reduced by the padding that the caller removed (good is all-ones if the padding was valid and 0 otherwise); origreclen is the original record length, recdata the record; origreclen must be at least mac_size and mac_size at most EVP_MAX_MD_SIZE (checked, else return 0); mac and alloced must be non-NULL when block_size != 1 (checked, else 0). If mac_size is 0 it returns 0 when good is 0 and 1 otherwise, touching nothing else. Otherwise it reduces *reclen by mac_size. For block_size 1 (no padding) the MAC position is fixed: it sets *mac to point into recdata at the new *reclen, *alloced to 0 and returns 1. For block ciphers it draws a random MAC with RAND_bytes_ex (failure returns 0), allocates a mac_size output buffer into *mac (failure returns 0) and sets *alloced to 1; it then scans only the last 256+mac_size bytes of the original record (the MAC position can only vary within that window; the scan assumes the MAC start is not before the scan start, which is not checked here), copying the MAC bytes into a rotation buffer with constant-time masks, and rotates them into place so the output is the real MAC when good is set and the random MAC when it is not. Returns 1 on success. The caller owns *mac when *alloced is 1.

functions.name: dtls1_read_bytes
functions.prose_contract: DTLS read entry point: returns data of the requested record type to the caller, and processes alerts, change-cipher-spec records, retransmissions and renegotiation attempts it meets on the way. Precondition: s is a DTLS SSL; type is 0 (any) or application data or handshake; peek only with application data; buf has room for len bytes; readbytes non-NULL. Return values: 1 with *readbytes = n when bytes were copied; 0 for end of connection (received close_notify or fatal alert, shutdown state) or a zero-length request; a negative value for errors (fatal alerts raised for most of them) or retry conditions (rwstate set to reading); handshake function results are passed through. It returns -1 for an invalid type or peek combination (internal error alert) and runs the handshake function first if the connection is still in init (a negative result is returned, 0 becomes -1). In a loop (label start) it handles timeouts (retry the loop, or -1 on error state), reads records from the record layer when none is pending (a failed read goes through dtls1_read_failed, may retry or return its result), resets the alert counter for non-alert data, buffers a record that arrives out of order before ChangeCipherSpec was processed, and returns 0 after releasing a record when the peer shutdown was already received. A record of the requested type (or CCS while a handshake read with recvd_type is requested) is rejected with an alert if it is application data during the first handshake; with len == 0 it returns 0 without consuming, releasing the record only when it is empty (so a non-empty record stays pending); otherwise it copies min(len, available) bytes to buf and releases the consumed bytes (with peek, only an empty record is released and nothing is consumed), then returns 1 after setting *readbytes, except that for SCTP, when a shutdown was received and no message waits, it returns 0 after the bytes were copied into buf without setting *readbytes. Alerts: a malformed alert raises an alert and returns -1; a warning alert is counted (too many gives an alert and -1), close_notify returns 0 (or an SCTP retry -1), no_renegotiation raises a handshake failure and returns -1, other warnings continue the loop; a fatal alert records it, raises a fatal error, marks shutdown received, drops the session and returns 0; an unknown level raises an alert and -1. After SSL_SENT_SHUTDOWN a record is dropped and 0 returned. Change-cipher-spec records are released and the loop continues. A handshake record when not in a handshake: records from another epoch or too short are dropped; a Finished message triggers retransmission handling and, without auto-retry and with no unprocessed data, a retry -1; any other handshake message restarts the handshake function (renegotiation), with the same retry rule, and then continues the loop. Other record types give an unexpected-record alert and -1 (application data while expected otherwise may set in_read_app_data to 2 and return -1).

functions.name: ssl3_write_bytes
functions.prose_contract: SSL/TLS write entry point of the record layer: writes len bytes of buf as records of the given type, resuming a previous partial write if one is pending. Precondition: ssl is a connection; if a write was interrupted the caller retries with the same buffer pointer and a length not smaller than the amount already written (s->rlayer.wnum) and the pending amount. Returns 1 with *written set (the full length, or the part written if partial writes are enabled for application data), or -1 or another non-positive value from a callee on error or retry. It sets rwstate to SSL_NOTHING and reads the resumed offset tot from wnum. A length smaller than wnum or than wnum plus the pending total raises a fatal alert (SSL_R_BAD_LENGTH) and returns -1; in that case, and for an early-data length limit failure, wnum is left unchanged. After those checks it sets wnum to 0, so a later return of 0 or less from the handshake function (which is run when the connection is still in init, a negative value is returned, 0 becomes -1) leaves wnum at 0 and not restored for a retry. It then asks tls_write_check_pending whether a previous write must be retried; a negative result is returned, a positive result retries the pending records (a result of 0 or less stores tot in wnum and returns it), and the pending total is added to tot. If nothing was written yet it records the pending type and buffer. If tot equals len it returns 1. A pending alert is dispatched first (a failure stores tot in wnum and returns it). The maximum and split fragment sizes must be non-zero and consistent (else fatal internal error and -1). In a loop it asks the record layer for the number of pipes, splits the remaining data into one template per pipe (full split-sized fragments if enough data, otherwise an even split), and writes them with write_records; a result of 0 or less stores tot in wnum and is returned; success returns 1 when everything (or, for application data with partial write enabled, whatever was written) is done, setting *written, otherwise it continues with the remainder.

functions.name: ssl3_read_bytes
functions.prose_contract: SSL/TLS read entry point of the record layer: returns data of the requested record type to the caller, and handles alerts, handshake records (including renegotiation), change-cipher-spec and early data on the way. Precondition: type is 0 (any), application data or handshake; peek is only allowed with application data; buf has room for len bytes; readbytes non-NULL. An invalid combination raises an internal-error alert and returns -1. Return values: 1 with *readbytes set when data was delivered, 0 on a clean end (close_notify, fatal alert, shutdown already received, or a zero-length request), and -1 or a callee result for errors and retry conditions. If a handshake read is requested and bytes of a handshake message are buffered in handshake_fragment, it copies up to len of them to buf, removes them from the fragment, sets *recvd_type and *readbytes = n (n is 0 when len is 0) and returns 1. If the connection is still in init outside the handshake function it runs the handshake function first (negative result returned, 0 becomes -1). Then, at label start, it reads records from the record layer when none is pending (a non-positive read result is returned), rejects a TLS 1.3 non-handshake record while a handshake fragment is buffered, resets the alert counter for non-alert data, rejects data between CCS and Finished, and returns 0 if the peer shutdown was already received. A record of the requested type (or CCS for a handshake read with recvd_type, below TLS 1.3) is rejected with an alert for application data during the first handshake or CCS arriving with a pending handshake fragment; with len == 0 it returns 0 without consuming, releasing the record only if it is empty; otherwise it copies data from consecutive records into buf (several records only for application data) until len is reached; without peek the copied bytes are released from the record layer, with peek they are not consumed (only empty records are released); it returns 1 with the total in *readbytes, or loops again if nothing was copied. Alerts: malformed alert gives an alert and -1; warning alerts (or TLS 1.3 user_canceled) are counted, too many gives -1; user_canceled in TLS 1.3 continues; close_notify sets the received-shutdown flag and returns 0; fatal alerts (and any TLS 1.3 alert) record the alert, raise a fatal error, drop the session and return 0; no_renegotiation raises a handshake failure and -1; other warnings continue; unknown levels give -1. After a sent shutdown a handshake record is released and the read retried or reported as retry, and application data gives an alert and -1. Handshake records are copied into handshake_fragment (and released) and the loop continues until the fragment is full (4 bytes); with at least 4 bytes buffered outside the handshake the handshake function is run (renegotiation), returning -1 for early data reading or when auto-retry is off and no data is pending (retry), and otherwise continuing. A CCS record at this point is an alert and -1; other types give an unexpected-record alert and -1, except application data while the state machine allows it (in_read_app_data set to 2, -1), or skipped early data (counted and released, then continue).

functions.name: DEFINE_RUN_ONCE_STATIC(do_wsa_startup)
functions.prose_contract: Windows-only initialiser body (compiled under OPENSSL_SYS_WINDOWS) defined with DEFINE_RUN_ONCE_STATIC(do_wsa_startup); it takes no arguments. It calls WSAStartup requesting Winsock version 2.2 and returns 0 if that call fails (nothing is changed). On success it sets the static wsa_started flag to 1, registers ossl_wsa_cleanup with OPENSSL_atexit (the registration result is not checked) so that WSACleanup runs at exit, and returns 1. The function itself does no once-only protection: it is meant to be called through RUN_ONCE in ensure_wsa_startup (rio_notifier.c:54-57), which runs it at most once per process and returns the stored result on later calls; a direct call would call WSAStartup again and register another atexit handler.

functions.name: ssl_cipher_get_evp
functions.prose_contract: Looks up the EVP cipher, digest, MAC key type and secret size, and compression method that correspond to the cipher of session s. Precondition: ctx is the SSL_CTX (used for fetches); s is a session whose cipher field s->cipher is read; enc, md, mac_pkey_type, mac_secret_size and comp are output pointers, of which enc and md are required unless only comp is wanted. Returns 0 if s->cipher is NULL. If comp is non-NULL it sets *comp to NULL and looks the session compression method up in the registered compression methods, storing the entry if found; if enc and md are both NULL it then returns 1. If either of enc or md is NULL at that point it returns 0. It then fetches the cipher (ssl_cipher_get_evp_cipher, failure returns 0) and the digest/MAC data (ssl_cipher_get_evp_md_mac; failure frees *enc and returns 0). If the result has a cipher and either a digest or an AEAD cipher and a valid MAC (AEAD, no mac_pkey_type pointer, or a defined MAC key type) then it returns 1, after possibly replacing the cipher and digest by a combined stitched implementation: this is skipped (return 1 unchanged) when encrypt-then-MAC is used or the session version is not TLS 1.0 or later TLS 1.x; otherwise for RC4-MD5, AES-128/256-SHA1 and AES-128/256-SHA256 it fetches the matching cbc-hmac cipher and, if found, frees the old cipher and digest, sets *enc to it and *md to NULL. In all other cases (cipher or digest missing, or no valid MAC) it returns 0.

functions.name: SSL_add1_host
functions.prose_contract: Adds a reference host name (or an IP address) to the verification parameters of the connection s. Precondition: s is an SSL; host may be NULL. Returns 0 if the connection object cannot be obtained. If host is non-NULL and parses as an IP address (a2i_IPADDRESS), it is treated as an IP address: if an IP address was already set it raises ERR_R_PASSED_INVALID_ARGUMENT ("IP address was already set") and returns 0 (only one IP address is allowed), otherwise it returns the result of X509_VERIFY_PARAM_set1_ip_asc. Otherwise it returns the result of X509_VERIFY_PARAM_add1_host(param, host, 0), which in add mode does not clear the existing host list: for a NULL or empty host (or one that is only a trailing NUL) it changes nothing and returns 1; a name with an embedded NUL byte, or an allocation failure, returns 0; otherwise a copy of the name is appended to the host list and 1 is returned. Thus 1 does not always mean that something was added.

functions.name: dane_tlsa_add
functions.prose_contract: Adds one TLSA (DANE) record to dane. Precondition: dane has DANE enabled (trecs non-NULL), data non-NULL with dlen bytes. Returns -1 with SSL_R_DANE_NOT_ENABLED if DANE is not enabled. Invalid input returns 0 with an error: a length that does not fit an int (SSL_R_DANE_TLSA_BAD_DATA_LENGTH), usage above DANETLS_USAGE_LAST, selector above DANETLS_SELECTOR_LAST, an unknown matching type (no digest registered for it), a digest-matching record whose data length differs from the digest size, or NULL data (SSL_R_DANE_TLSA_NULL_DATA). Allocation failures of the record or its copy of the data return -1 without an error raised here. For a full-data matching type (0) the data are validated and partly cached: for the certificate selector the data must decode to exactly one X.509 certificate with a usable public key (else SSL_R_DANE_TLSA_BAD_CERTIFICATE, return 0); for usages other than PKIX-TA and DANE-TA the certificate is then discarded; for those two usages it is appended to dane->certs (creating that stack if needed; failure raises ERR_R_CRYPTO_LIB and returns -1, with dane->certs possibly left allocated but empty); for the public key selector the data must decode to exactly one public key (else SSL_R_DANE_TLSA_BAD_PUBLIC_KEY, 0), which is kept in the record only for DANE-TA usage. The record is inserted into dane->trecs at the position that keeps the list sorted by descending usage, then descending selector, then descending digest order; if the insert fails the record is freed, ERR_R_CRYPTO_LIB is raised and -1 is returned, but a certificate already appended to dane->certs remains there. On success dane->umask gets the bit of the usage and the function returns 1.

functions.name: SSL_CTX_ctrl
functions.prose_contract: Control function of an SSL_CTX: gets or sets context settings according to cmd, with larg and parg carrying the arguments. Special cases come first: for SSL_CTRL_SET_GROUPS_LIST with larg == 1 it returns tls1_set_groups_list(ctx, ..., parg) as a syntax check, whether or not ctx is NULL. If ctx is NULL, SSL_CTRL_SET_SIGALGS_LIST and SSL_CTRL_SET_CLIENT_SIGALGS_LIST return tls1_set_sigalgs_list as a syntax check and every other command returns 0. With a non-NULL ctx the return value depends on cmd: read-ahead, max cert list, session cache size and mode set commands return the previous value (max cert list and cache size return 0 and change nothing for negative larg); the matching get commands return the current value; SSL_CTRL_SESS_NUMBER returns the session count and the SESS_* statistics commands return the counters; SSL_CTRL_MODE sets and CLEAR_MODE clears mode bits and return the new mode; SET_MAX_SEND_FRAGMENT returns 0 unless 512 <= larg <= SSL3_RT_MAX_PLAIN_LENGTH, otherwise stores it (lowering split_send_fragment if needed) and returns 1; SET_SPLIT_SEND_FRAGMENT returns 0 if larg is 0 or above the max fragment, else stores it and returns 1; SET_MAX_PIPELINES returns 0 unless 1 <= larg <= SSL_MAX_PIPELINES; CERT_FLAGS sets and CLEAR_CERT_FLAGS clears certificate flags and return the new flags; SET_MIN/MAX_PROTO_VERSION return 1 only if the allowed-version check and ssl_set_version_bound succeed (else 0) and the GET variants return the bounds; SET_MSG_CALLBACK_ARG stores parg and returns 1. Any other cmd is passed, with larg and parg, to ctx->method->ssl_ctx_ctrl and its result returned, so parg is used for those commands.

functions.name: SSL_do_handshake
functions.prose_contract: Performs or continues the TLS/DTLS/QUIC handshake on s. If s is a QUIC object it returns the result of ossl_quic_do_handshake(s) immediately. Returns -1 if the connection object cannot be obtained, and -1 with SSL_R_CONNECTION_TYPE_NOT_SET if no handshake function is set (SSL_set_connect_state or accept state was not called). It returns -1 if ossl_statem_check_finish_init fails. Otherwise it calls the method renegotiate check and, only when the connection is in initialisation or before the handshake, runs the handshake: when the async mode is set and no async job is currently running it starts an async job running ssl_do_handshake_intern and uses the value returned by ssl_start_async_job (for example the job pause or error outcomes, which that function maps to a return value that was not read); otherwise it calls sc->handshake_func(s) directly and returns its result (1 on success, 0 on controlled failure, negative on error or retry). If the connection is neither in init nor before the handshake it does nothing and returns 1.

functions.name: IMPLEMENT_tls_meth_func(version, flags, mask, func_name, s_accept, s_connect, enc_data)
functions.prose_contract: Generated accessor function func_name(void) (from IMPLEMENT_tls_meth_func(version, flags, mask, func_name, s_accept, s_connect, enc_data), ssl_local.h:2343-2382; the sibling macros IMPLEMENT_ssl3_meth_func at 2384 and IMPLEMENT_dtls1_meth_func at 2424 generate the same kind of function with SSLv3 or DTLS tables). It takes no arguments and returns a pointer to a function-local static const SSL_METHOD named func_name_data, which is initialised at compile time with the given version, flags and mask, the generic connection new/free/reset functions, the tls1 new/clear/free functions, the given accept and connect functions, the ssl3 read, peek, write, shutdown, renegotiate, record read/write, alert dispatch, ctrl, cipher lookup, pending and timeout functions, a pointer to enc_data, and the callback ctrl functions. The same non-NULL pointer is returned on every call; the object is constant and has no side effects.

functions.name: ssl_clear_bad_session
functions.prose_contract: Removes the session of connection s from the session cache when it should be treated as bad, and reports whether it asked for the removal. Precondition: s is a connection. If s->session is non-NULL, the SSL_SENT_SHUTDOWN flag is not set, and the connection is neither in the initialisation state nor in the before state, it calls SSL_CTX_remove_session(s->session_ctx, s->session) and returns 1. In every other case it does nothing and returns 0. The return value of SSL_CTX_remove_session is ignored, so a result of 1 means the removal was requested, not that a session was actually removed from the cache.

functions.name: tls_construct_ctos_early_data
functions.prose_contract: Client-side construction of the TLS 1.3 early_data extension in the ClientHello, which also settles which PSK session the client will offer.
