Returns EXT_RETURN_FAIL after a fatal alert on every error, EXT_RETURN_NOT_SENT when early data is not to be offered, and EXT_RETURN_SENT after writing an empty early_data extension. First, if a PSK use-session callback is set it is called (with the handshake digest when a HelloRetryRequest is pending); a callback failure, or a returned PSK session whose version is not TLS 1.3, frees the returned session and fails with SSL_R_BAD_PSK. If no session came back and the older PSK client callback is set (non-OPENSSL_NO_PSK builds) it is called to obtain identity and key: a key longer than the maximum or an identity longer than the maximum fails, and a non-empty key becomes a new session using the TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 cipher (failures set the alert and return, wiping the key but not freeing the half-built session). It then replaces s->psksession by the obtained session (freeing the old one); only when a session exists, it also replaces psksession_id with a copy of the identity (an allocation failure sets the length to 0 and fails), so when there is no PSK session the old identity is left unchanged. If the state is not early-data connecting, or neither s->session nor the PSK session allows early data, it sets max_early_data to 0 and returns NOT_SENT. Otherwise it takes the session that allows early data (s->session preferred over the PSK session), copies its max_early_data, and fails with an alert if its SNI hostname differs from the connection one, if the ALPN protocol it selected is not offered, or if the extension cannot be written; on success it marks early_data as rejected-until-confirmed (early_data = REJECTED, early_data_ok = 1) and returns SENT.

functions.name: read_state_machine
functions.prose_contract: Drives the handshake message reading state machine of a connection (client or server) through the header, body and post-processing states, returning SUB_STATE_FINISHED when the last message of the flight was read and processed, or SUB_STATE_ERROR when it cannot continue now. The selection of the transition, process, size-check and post-process functions depends on s->server. On first use it sets first_packet and clears the first-init flag. In the HEADER state it reads a message header (tls_get_message_header or dtls_get_message; a result of 0 returns SUB_STATE_ERROR leaving read_state unchanged, so a retry resumes at the same place, whether the failure was a retry or an error is determined by the callee), calls the info callback, runs the transition function for the message type (failure returns SUB_STATE_ERROR) and rejects a message larger than the allowed maximum with a fatal alert, then moves to the BODY state. In the BODY state it reads the message body (0 returns SUB_STATE_ERROR), builds a PACKET over it (failure: fatal alert, SUB_STATE_ERROR), resets init_num and calls the process function: MSG_PROCESS_ERROR returns SUB_STATE_ERROR after checking whether a fatal error was already raised; MSG_PROCESS_FINISHED_READING stops the DTLS timer and returns SUB_STATE_FINISHED; MSG_PROCESS_CONTINUE_PROCESSING moves to POST_PROCESS with work state WORK_MORE_A; any other result returns to HEADER. In POST_PROCESS it stores the result of post_process_message in read_state_work: an error (after check_fatal) or a still-pending WORK_MORE_A/B/C returns SUB_STATE_ERROR, so in the pending case the work state has already been advanced for the retry; WORK_FINISHED_CONTINUE returns to HEADER; WORK_FINISHED_SWAP or STOP stop the DTLS timer and return SUB_STATE_FINISHED. An unknown read_state raises an internal-error alert and returns SUB_STATE_ERROR. The function loops until one of these returns.

functions.name: tls_process_server_hello
functions.prose_contract: Client-side processing of a ServerHello (or a TLS 1.3 HelloRetryRequest, which has the ServerHello layout). Returns MSG_PROCESS_CONTINUE_READING for a normal ServerHello, the result of tls_process_as_hello_retry_request (MSG_PROCESS_FINISHED_READING on success) for a HelloRetryRequest, and MSG_PROCESS_ERROR after a fatal alert for any failure; the temporary extension list is freed on the error and normal exits. It parses the version, then the 32-byte random: when the connection is at TLS 1.3, the version field is TLS 1.2 and the random equals the HelloRetryRequest magic value, it is a HRR (a second HRR is an unexpected message; the record protocol version is set), otherwise the random is stored as the server random. It then parses the session id (at most the maximum size), cipher suite bytes, compression byte and the length-prefixed extensions block with no trailing data (a missing extension block is allowed except for a HRR). For a non-HRR it collects the extensions and selects the protocol version (ssl_choose_client_version). For TLS 1.3 or a HRR the compression must be 0 and the returned session id must equal the one the client sent. A HRR sets the cipher suite and continues in the HRR handler. Otherwise it checks the extension contexts, sets hit to 0, and for TLS 1.3 parses the PSK extension first (only on a record boundary) while for earlier versions it applies the session-secret callback if set (failure is fatal) and sets hit when the returned non-empty session id matches the cached session. For a resumed session the session id context must match. For a new session, if the cached session has an id a miss is counted and a new session is started; the session version is set, and, for versions below TLS 1.3 only, the session id length and bytes are copied from the message (in TLS 1.3 the session id is not saved). Then the negotiated version must match the session version, the cipher suite is validated and set, the compression method is checked against the cached or allowed methods, all extensions are parsed, in DTLS-SCTP with a resumed session the SCTP authentication key is derived and installed, and for TLS 1.3 the key block and handshake traffic hash are set up and the handshake write (unless middlebox compatibility or early data is in use) and read cipher states are switched.

functions.name: tls_process_initial_server_flight
functions.prose_contract: Final checks after the server flight has been received (certificate, status, key exchange and done). Returns 1 on success and 0 on failure. It returns 0 if ssl3_check_cert_and_algorithm fails (the alert is raised there). If a certificate status type was requested and the context has an OCSP status callback, the callback is called: a result of 0 raises SSL_R_INVALID_STATUS_RESPONSE (bad certificate status response alert) and returns 0, a negative result raises SSL_R_OCSP_CALLBACK_FAILURE and returns 0, a positive result continues. In builds with certificate transparency support, only when a CT validation callback is set on the connection, ssl_validate_ct is run, and a validation failure returns 0 only if peer verification is requested (SSL_VERIFY_PEER set); with the callback NULL no CT validation is done, and with a validation failure but no SSL_VERIFY_PEER the function continues and returns 1.

functions.name: ossl_statem_client13_write_transition
functions.prose_contract: Chooses the next handshake state when the TLS 1.3 client is writing messages. Returns WRITE_TRAN_CONTINUE after setting st->hand_state to the next state, WRITE_TRAN_FINISHED without changing the state (switch to reading), or WRITE_TRAN_ERROR after a fatal internal-error alert. By current state: TLS_ST_CR_CERT_REQ goes to the compressed-certificate or certificate state when post-handshake authentication was requested, otherwise it requires that a shutdown was already sent (else fatal error, WRITE_TRAN_ERROR) and goes to TLS_ST_OK; TLS_ST_CR_FINISHED records the read time and goes to PENDING_EARLY_DATA_END (early data write retry or finished writing), CW_CHANGE (middlebox compatibility, no HelloRetryRequest), CW_FINISHED (no certificate request), or the compressed certificate or certificate state; TLS_ST_PENDING_EARLY_DATA_END goes to CW_END_OF_EARLY_DATA if early data was accepted and end-of-early-data is used, else behaves like the next case; TLS_ST_CW_END_OF_EARLY_DATA and TLS_ST_CW_CHANGE go to CW_FINISHED, or the (compressed) certificate state when a certificate was requested; TLS_ST_CW_COMP_CERT and TLS_ST_CW_CERT go to CW_CERT_VRFY if a certificate was requested, else CW_FINISHED; TLS_ST_CW_CERT_VRFY goes to CW_FINISHED; TLS_ST_CR_KEY_UPDATE, TLS_ST_CW_KEY_UPDATE, TLS_ST_CR_SESSION_TICKET and TLS_ST_CW_FINISHED go to TLS_ST_OK; TLS_ST_OK goes to CW_KEY_UPDATE if a key update is pending, otherwise it returns WRITE_TRAN_FINISHED without changing the state. Any other state (this function has no case for TLS_ST_BEFORE, TLS_ST_CW_CLNT_HELLO or TLS_ST_EARLY_DATA) is a fatal internal error and returns WRITE_TRAN_ERROR.

functions.name: ossl_statem_client_write_transition
functions.prose_contract: Chooses the next handshake state when the client is writing messages (TLS 1.2 and earlier, DTLS, and the start of a connection). If the connection is at TLS 1.3 it returns the result of ossl_statem_client13_write_transition. Otherwise it returns WRITE_TRAN_CONTINUE after changing hand_state, WRITE_TRAN_FINISHED with the state unchanged, or WRITE_TRAN_ERROR (unknown state: fatal internal-error alert). TLS_ST_OK without renegotiation returns FINISHED, and with renegotiation falls through to TLS_ST_BEFORE; TLS_ST_BEFORE goes to CW_CLNT_HELLO. TLS_ST_CW_CLNT_HELLO goes to CW_CHANGE (middlebox compatibility) or TLS_ST_EARLY_DATA when early data is being connected and it is not a QUIC handshake; in every other case (no early data, or a QUIC handshake) it records the write time and returns FINISHED. TLS_ST_CR_SRVR_HELLO goes to CW_CHANGE (middlebox compatibility and early data not finished writing) or CW_CLNT_HELLO (for a retried ClientHello); TLS_ST_EARLY_DATA records the write time and returns FINISHED; DTLS_ST_CR_HELLO_VERIFY_REQUEST goes to CW_CLNT_HELLO; TLS_ST_CR_SRVR_DONE goes to CW_CERT if a certificate was requested, else CW_KEY_EXCH; TLS_ST_CW_CERT goes to CW_KEY_EXCH; TLS_ST_CW_KEY_EXCH goes to CW_CERT_VRFY if a certificate was requested and certificate verify is not skipped, else CW_CHANGE; CW_CERT_VRFY goes to CW_CHANGE; CW_CHANGE goes to CW_CLNT_HELLO (pending HelloRetryRequest), TLS_ST_EARLY_DATA (early data connecting), CW_NEXT_PROTO (next protocol seen, not DTLS) or CW_FINISHED; CW_NEXT_PROTO goes to CW_FINISHED; TLS_ST_CW_FINISHED goes to TLS_ST_OK when the session was resumed, otherwise returns FINISHED with the state unchanged; TLS_ST_CR_FINISHED goes to CW_CHANGE for a resumed session, else TLS_ST_OK; TLS_ST_CR_HELLO_REQ goes to CW_CLNT_HELLO after a successful renegotiation check and handshake setup (setup failure returns ERROR), otherwise to TLS_ST_OK.

functions.name: dtls1_set_handshake_header
functions.prose_contract: Starts a DTLS handshake message in the packet pkt for message type htype. Returns 1 on success and 0 if a packet write fails. For a ChangeCipherSpec (htype SSL3_MT_CHANGE_CIPHER_SPEC): it copies next_handshake_write_seq into handshake_write_seq, sets the stored message header for the CCS with that sequence number, and writes the single CCS type byte to pkt (failure returns 0); no handshake header space is allocated and no sub-packet is started. For any other message type: it records the message header fields for htype (length and fragment fields zero for now), reserves DTLS1_HM_HEADER_LENGTH bytes at the current position for the header, to be filled in later, and starts a sub-packet for the body; if the header allocation or the sub-packet start fails it returns 0, and if only the sub-packet start fails the header bytes have already been reserved in pkt.

functions.name: tls_finish_handshake
functions.prose_contract: Completes the handshake: frees temporary buffers, resets handshake bookkeeping, updates session caches and statistics, and runs the handshake-done callback. Precondition: s is a connection at the end of a handshake; wst is unused; clearbufs says whether to free the init buffers; stop selects the return value. Returns WORK_ERROR (with an internal-error alert) if freeing the write BIO buffer fails; otherwise WORK_FINISHED_STOP when stop is non-zero, or WORK_FINISHED_CONTINUE when stop is zero. With clearbufs set it frees s->init_buf (except for DTLS without SCTP), frees the write BIO buffer and resets init_num. A TLS 1.3 client that had requested post-handshake authentication moves it to the extension-sent state. Only if the stored cleanuphand flag is set (a handshake, not a post-handshake message, was completed) it resets renegotiate, new_session, cleanuphand and ticket_expected, clears the key block, and: for a server (TLS below 1.3) updates the session cache, counts a good accept and sets handshake_func to ossl_statem_accept; for a client removes the session from the cache in TLS 1.3 when client caching is on (else updates the cache), counts a hit and a good connect, and sets handshake_func to ossl_statem_connect; in DTLS it also resets the handshake sequence numbers and clears the received buffer. It then clears the in-init state, calls the info callback with SSL_CB_HANDSHAKE_DONE when one is set and the handshake was just cleaned up, or the protocol is below TLS 1.3, or this is the first handshake. Finally, when stop is zero it sets the in-init state again and returns WORK_FINISHED_CONTINUE; when stop is non-zero the connection is left out of the init state and WORK_FINISHED_STOP is returned. The stop argument is not used to choose handshake_func.

functions.name: tls_process_client_hello
functions.prose_contract: Parses a ClientHello message on the server into a CLIENTHELLO_MSG and collects its raw extensions, without choosing the protocol version or cipher (that is done later in tls_early_post_process_client_hello). Returns MSG_PROCESS_CONTINUE_PROCESSING on success with s->clienthello set to the new structure, MSG_PROCESS_ERROR (after a fatal alert, freeing the structure and its extension list) for malformed or inconsistent messages, and MSG_PROCESS_FINISHED_READING in two non-error cases. Renegotiation: if this is not the first handshake and renegotiation is not already in progress, a TLS 1.3 connection is an internal error; if renegotiation is not permitted by the options (or the client lacks secure renegotiation binding and unsafe legacy renegotiation is not allowed) it sends a warning alert no_renegotiation and returns MSG_PROCESS_FINISHED_READING (no fatal error); otherwise it sets renegotiate and new_session. It allocates the message (failure is fatal). For an SSLv2-format hello (only allowed in the first handshake and without a pending HelloRetryRequest) it parses the SSLv2 fields (cipher list, session id up to the maximum, challenge) and builds the random from the last up to 32 bytes of the challenge, with a single null compression method. For the normal format it reads the random, the session id, the DTLS cookie (and for DTLS with cookie exchange enabled and an empty cookie it frees the structure and returns MSG_PROCESS_FINISHED_READING so the cookie exchange proceeds), the cipher suites, the compression methods and an optional length-prefixed extensions block with nothing trailing. Length or format errors raise decode-error or illegal-parameter alerts. It copies the compression methods (bounded), collects the raw extensions of the ClientHello (failure returns MSG_PROCESS_ERROR) and stores the message in s->clienthello.

functions.name: rsa_keygen_test
functions.prose_contract: ACVP test case id for RSA key generation with known auxiliary values. It takes the id-th entry of rsa_keygen_data and returns 1 if all steps succeed and 0 otherwise (each step is wrapped in a test assertion that reports the failure). It converts the test xp1, xp2, xp, xq1, xq2 and xq values to BIGNUMs and passes them to the key generation as test parameters built with OSSL_PARAM_BLD; the public exponent is not part of these parameters: it is converted separately and set on the key generation context with EVP_PKEY_CTX_set1_rsa_keygen_pubexp, together with the modulus size. It creates an RSA key generation context, initialises it, applies the parameters and generates the key, then reads back p1, p2, q1, q2, the factors p and q, n and d as byte strings and compares each against the expected values of the test entry (a mismatch fails). On success it prints the values with test_output_memory. All temporaries (BIGNUMs, byte buffers, key, context, parameter list and builder) are released on every exit path after they were allocated.

functions.name: setup_tests
functions.prose_contract: Test registration function of the ASN.1 time tests. It takes no arguments and registers test cases with the test framework through ADD_ALL_TESTS and ADD_TEST (the underlying add_test and add_all_tests functions return void, so there is no registration failure value to check) and then returns 1. It first probes whether time_t is signed and usable with negative values (localtime of -1 non-NULL and time_t not unsigned). It always registers the positive-value table test, the comparison table test, the duplicate test, the ASN.1-to-time_t conversion test and the tm-to-ASN.1 conversion test; it registers the negative-value table test only if negative time_t values are usable; it registers the 64-bit table test when time_t is wider than 32 bits, and in that case also the negative 64-bit table test when negative values are usable and the platform is not HP-UX. A log line is printed when the negative or 64-bit groups are added.

functions.name: setup
functions.prose_contract: Command-line processing for the BIO prefix filter test program; returns 1 if all options were handled and 0 on any error (after printing a message for most errors). It creates text-mode BIOs on stdin, stdout and stderr (asserting that each exists) and then iterates over the options. -n AMOUNT sets the number of prefix filters from a decimal number (trailing characters give an error message and 0; an amount below 1 is rejected) and builds the filter chain with setup_bio_chain (failure prints a message and returns 0). -i [INDEX:]INDENT requires that the chain exists (the -n option came first), parses an optional filter index and the indent value in decimal, rejects an index not below amount, and sets the indentation of that filter with BIO_set_indent (failure returns 0). -p [INDEX:]PREFIX requires the chain, parses an optional index, checks it against amount and sets the prefix string of that filter with BIO_set_prefix (failure returns 0). Any other option, including the error option, returns 0 without a message from this function. The numbers are read with strtoul, which accepts leading white space and a sign, and an empty string is accepted as 0 because the check only looks for trailing characters. If setup_bio_chain fails after it freed the chain, the global chain pointer is not reset, so a later cleanup would free it again.

functions.name: setup_tests
functions.prose_contract: Test registration function of the CMAC tests. It takes no arguments, registers the three test cases test_cmac_bad, test_cmac_run and test_cmac_copy with ADD_TEST and always returns 1. ADD_TEST expands to a call of add_test, which returns void, so no registration failure is reported by the function and the return value does not depend on any registration result.

functions.name: DEFINE_SET_GET_BASE_TEST(PREFIX, SETN, GETN, DUP, FIELD, TYPE, ERR, DEFAULT, NEW, FREE)
functions.prose_contract: Generated test function execute_CTX_<SETN>_<GETN>_<FIELD>(fixture) (from DEFINE_SET_GET_BASE_TEST, cmp_ctx_test.c:357-490) that exercises one setter and getter pair of a CMP context field. It returns 1 only if every check passed (TEST_true(res)), otherwise 0, and it reports each failed check with an error message. It requires that there is no pending error at the start and end. For an exported setter (PREFIX 1) the setter must return an error and queue an error when called with a NULL context; the getter must return the value ERR and queue an error for a NULL context. On the fixture context: the first get must return the default value; the setter is called with a first newly created value; a set0-style setter (SETN 0) takes ownership of it, so that value is not freed by the test afterwards, while a set1-style setter makes a copy; a get1-style getter (GETN 1) returns a value the test must free. After the first set the getter result must equal the stored pointer for SETN 0, or be a non-default value (and a different pointer when DUP is set) for SETN 1. The same is done with a second value, checking that the second set did not reset to the default, matches or copies as appropriate, differs from the first, and for GETN 1 returns a fresh object; a third get must be non-default and consistent (same pointer for GETN 0, a new copy when DUP is set for GETN 1). At the end it frees the values it still owns: the test-created values only when the setter did not take ownership (SETN != 0), and the values returned by get1 getters.

functions.name: DEFINE_SET_GET_BASE_TEST(PREFIX, SETN, GETN, DUP, FIELD, TYPE, ERR, DEFAULT, NEW, FREE)
functions.prose_contract: Generated wrapper test_CTX_<SETN>_<GETN>_<FIELD>(void) (from DEFINE_SET_GET_BASE_TEST, cmp_ctx_test.c:492-497). It takes no arguments, creates a test fixture with set_up (SETUP_TEST_FIXTURE), runs execute_CTX_<SETN>_<GETN>_<FIELD> on it through EXECUTE_TEST with tear_down as the cleanup, and returns the macro result variable (1 if the fixture was created and the executed test passed, 0 otherwise). It is the test case function registered for the setter/getter pair; the ownership handling of the values (SETN 0 versus SETN 1) is done inside the executed function, not here.

functions.name: setup_tests
functions.prose_contract: Test setup for the configuration include tests. It returns 0 if any setup step fails and 1 after registering the tests. It creates a new NCONF object in the global conf (failure returns 0). It then processes the command-line options: the failure option sets expect_failure; the provider-test option sets test_providers (and then falls through to the next label, doing nothing more); the test-cases option does nothing; any other option returns 0. It takes the first non-option argument as the configuration file name and opens it into the global in BIO (a missing argument or an open failure returns 0 after a note). It then changes directory to the file location with change_path because the configuration files use relative names (failure returns 0), and registers the tests test_load_config, test_check_null_numbers and test_check_overflow, plus test_available_providers only when the provider option was given. ADD_TEST expands to a call of add_test, which returns void, so there is no registration failure that could make the function return 0 at this point.

functions.name: setup_tests
functions.prose_contract: Test setup for the CRL tests. It parses the four test certificates (root, leaf, second root, second leaf) from their embedded PEM strings into the globals test_root, test_leaf, test_root2 and test_leaf2, assigning them without freeing any value those globals may already hold. If any parse fails it returns 0 immediately (the already parsed certificates stay in their globals and are not freed here). Otherwise it registers the eight test groups with the test framework: test_no_crl, test_basic_crl, test_bad_issuer_crl, test_crl_empty_idp, test_known_critical_crl, test_get_crl_fn_score as single tests, test_unknown_critical_crl for every entry of the unknown_critical_crls table, and test_reuse_crl for six indices, and returns 1. The registration macros expand to calls of add_test and add_all_tests, which return void, so registration cannot make the function return 0; the only failure return is the certificate parsing.

functions.name: are_ec_nids_compatible
functions.prose_contract: Decides whether two EC curve NIDs name the same curve, where some curves have two equivalent NIDs (the SEC name and the WAP WTLS name). Takes two int NIDs and returns 1 if they are compatible and 0 otherwise; it reads no global state. The result is computed by switching on n1d: for each curve with an alias pair (sect113r1/wtls4, sect163k1/wtls3, sect233k1/wtls10, sect233r1/wtls11, X9.62 c2pnb163v1/wtls5, which exist only when binary-field curves are not disabled, and secp112r1/wtls6, secp160r2/wtls7) it returns 1 when n2d is either member of the pair, whichever member n1d is. For secp224r1/wtls12 the result depends on the build: when the optimised NIST P curves are disabled (OPENSSL_NO_EC_NISTP_64_GCC_128 defined) the pair is symmetric like the others; otherwise only n1d == NID_wap_wsg_idm_ecid_wtls12 is special-cased, and it is compatible only with NID_secp224r1, while n1d == NID_secp224r1 goes to the default case and is compatible only with itself, so the relation is not symmetric there. For every other n1d (the default case) it returns 1 only when n1d == n2d.

functions.name: test_save_restore
functions.prose_contract: Test function taking idx (0 or 1 selects which save API is exercised); it manipulates the calling thread's OpenSSL error queue and returns 1 on success, 0 on the first failed check. It allocates an ERR_STATE with OSSL_ERR_STATE_new() (returns 0 if that fails), raises ERR_R_MALLOC_FAILURE and records ERR_peek_last_error() as mallocfail (returns 0 if that is not greater than 0), for idx == 1 sets a mark with ERR_set_mark() (returns 0 if it does not return 1), raises ERR_R_INTERNAL_ERROR with data "test data" and records its code as interr (returns 0 if it equals mallocfail). For idx == 0 it calls OSSL_ERR_STATE_save() and checks the queue is then empty (last error is 0); for idx == 1 it calls OSSL_ERR_STATE_save_to_mark(), which saves only the entries above the mark, and checks the queue is not empty (the marked malloc-failure entry stays). It then loops twice: OSSL_ERR_STATE_restore() appends the saved entries, the last error must equal interr with data "test data" and flags ERR_TXT_STRING | ERR_TXT_MALLOCED, a second restore duplicates the saved entries, and the queue is drained with ERR_get_error_all() checking each entry (for idx == 0 the saved set is mallocfail then interr, giving mallocfail, interr, mallocfail, interr; for idx == 1 the saved set is only interr, so the queue holds the still-queued mallocfail on the first iteration followed by interr twice, and only interr twice on the second iteration), ending with ERR_get_error() == 0. Any failed check jumps to err, leaving the queue as it is; OSSL_ERR_STATE_free(es) is called on every exit after es is declared (also when allocation failed, where es is NULL). Returns 1 only when all checks pass; success requires the queue to be empty on entry because of the final ERR_get_error() == 0 check.

functions.name: test_EVP_SM2
functions.prose_contract: Test function (no parameters, uses globals testctx and testpropq, and the message kMsg) that exercises SM2 keygen, sign/verify and encrypt/decrypt, returning 1 if every check passes and 0 at the first failure. It creates an SM2 EVP_PKEY_CTX, sets the sm2 curve with EVP_PKEY_CTX_set_ec_paramgen_curve_nid, generates parameters and then a key, creates two EVP_MD_CTX and an EVP_PKEY_CTX for the key shared by both digest contexts, and fetches "sm3". It signs kMsg with DigestSign after setting a 10-byte SM2 id with EVP_PKEY_CTX_set1_id, obtaining the signature size first and allocating the buffer with OPENSSL_malloc, then verifies it with the same id (must return > 0), then re-initialises the verify context and sets a zero-length id and requires DigestVerifyFinal to return exactly 0. It then loops over the digests "SM3" (the entry is NULL and skipped when OPENSSL_NO_SM3 is defined) and "SHA2-256": it frees any previous cctx, creates a new context, encrypts kMsg, decrypts, reads the digest name back, fetches that digest and requires EVP_MD_is_a to match the requested name, requires the decrypted length to equal sizeof(kMsg) and the bytes to equal kMsg. Any failed check goes to done; on every exit at done it frees pctx, kctx, sctx, cctx, the keys, both digest contexts, check_md and sig. Returns 1 only after the loop completes. If creating cctx fails on the second loop iteration, the pointer freed at the top of the loop is freed again at done (lines 2733, 2741-2743, 2796).

functions.name: setup_tests
functions.prose_contract: Test-registration entry point (no parameters) that processes command-line options with opt_next() and then registers test cases with ADD_TEST / ADD_ALL_TESTS; it returns 1 on success and 0 on failure. In the option loop, OPT_CONTEXT creates testctx with OSSL_LIB_CTX_new() (returns 0 if that gives NULL), when STATIC_LEGACY is defined adds the builtin legacy provider (returns 0 if that fails), and loads the "null" provider into the default context and "default" (and, unless OPENSSL_SYS_TANDEM, "legacy") into testctx without checking those load results; OPT_CONFIG_FILE stores opt_arg() and calls test_get_libctx(), returning 0 if it fails; OPT_TEST_CASES does nothing; any other option returns 0. If a config file was given it registers only test_EVP_set_config_properties and returns 1. Otherwise it registers the full set of tests, with many guarded by OPENSSL_NO_* macros; the engine tests (test_signatures_with_engine, test_cipher_with_engine) are registered only if OPENSSL_NO_DYNAMIC_ENGINE is not defined (and OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_3_0 is not) and testctx is NULL. Under OPENSSL_NO_DEPRECATED_3_0 undefined it also creates custom_pmeth with EVP_PKEY_meth_new(0xdefaced, 0), setting its check callbacks and adding it with EVP_PKEY_meth_add0, returning 0 if the creation fails or add0 does not return 1. It returns 1 at the end. It assigns the globals testctx, nullprov, deflprov, lgcyprov and custom_pmeth.

functions.name: rand_test_run
functions.prose_contract: EVP_TEST run callback for DRBG known-answer tests: it reads the parsed RAND_DATA from t->data, allocates got of generate_bits/8 bytes with OPENSSL_malloc (returns 0 if that fails), converts the init controls with ctrl2params when there are any (goto err if that fails, returning 0), and appends the use_df, cipher, digest and "HMAC" mac parameters before calling EVP_RAND_CTX_set_params on expected->ctx. If that set_params call fails, it jumps to err with ret = 1 and t->err = "EVP_RAND_CTX_set_params" when t->expect_unapproved is 0, or returns 0 (t->err untouched) when t->expect_unapproved is non-zero. Otherwise it loops over items 0..expected->n: it instantiates the parent and the ctx (with the test entropy, nonce and personalisation string), optionally sets reseed entropy on the parent and reseeds, optionally sets pr_entropyA/pr_entropyB on the parent, calls EVP_RAND_generate twice (additional inputs A then B), requires the output of the second generate to equal item->output, calls rand_check_fips_approved (returns 0 if the FIPS indicator query fails or check_fips_approved reports a mismatch with t->expect_unapproved), and uninstantiates ctx and parent, verifying zeroization and that the ctx state is EVP_RAND_STATE_UNINITIALISED. Each failed TEST_* check or step jumps to err with ret still 0 (t->err is not set on those paths). If all iterations pass, t->err = NULL and ret = 1. At err it prints the failing case index when i >= 0, frees got and the converted params, and returns ret.

functions.name: test_mod_exp_x2
functions.prose_contract: Test function taking idx that selects the operand size: factor_size is 1024 for idx <= 100, 1536 for 101..200, 2048 for 201..300 and stays 0 for idx > 300 (no early return; the function continues with factor_size 0). It creates a BN_CTX and ten BIGNUMs (returns 0 if any allocation fails), fills a1, b1, a2, b2 with BN_rand and m1, m2 as odd random numbers (the return values of BN_rand are not checked), reduces a1, b1 mod m1 and a2, b2 mod m2 with BN_mod, computes two results with BN_mod_exp_simple and both at once with BN_mod_exp_mont_consttime_x2, and returns 0 if any of those calls does not succeed. It then compares each simple result with the matching x2 result; if either pair differs it prints diagnostics (TEST_info and BN_print_var of all values) and returns 0. It returns 1 when all calls succeeded and both results match. All BIGNUMs and the BN_CTX are freed at err on every return after the first allocation attempt.

functions.name: fake_rsa_dgstvfy
functions.prose_contract: Fake provider one-shot digest-verify callback; ctx is treated as a pointer to a single flag byte and sig, siglen, tbv, tbvlen are not otherwise inspected. It first calls fake_rsa_dgstsgnvfy_update, which returns 0 if ctx is NULL, if the flag byte is 0, or if the FINALISED bit is set, and otherwise sets the UPDATED bit in *ctx. If that update step failed it returns 0. Otherwise it returns the result of fake_rsa_dgstvfy_final, which calls fake_rsa_dgstsgnvfy_final with a NULL siglen: that returns 0 if ctx is NULL, the flag byte is 0 or FINALISED is set (these cannot hold after a successful update step), or if the SIGN bit is set (a sign context with no siglen); the VERIFY bit is not required. In the remaining case it sets the FINALISED bit when the NO_DUP bit is set, does not write to sig (the sign branch is skipped because siglen is NULL), and returns 1.

functions.name: qtest_create_quic_connection_ex
functions.prose_contract: Drives a QUIC client SSL (clientssl, may be NULL for server-only) and a QUIC test server (qtserv) until the client has connected or failed with the wanted error and the server has confirmed the handshake or terminated, and returns 1 only if neither side recorded an error; returns 0 otherwise. With thread support (OPENSSL_THREADS and no CRYPTO_TDEBUG) a non-NULL clientssl resets abortserverthread and client_ready under the mutex. It returns 0 immediately if qtserv is NULL. If clientssl is NULL the client side is treated as done (retc = 1). If clientssl is in blocking mode, with thread support it stores qtserv in globtserv, starts run_server_thread (returns 0 if the thread cannot be started), sets qtserv to NULL and treats the server side as done (rets = 1); without thread support it returns 0. The loop then repeatedly: calls SSL_connect (an error equal to wanterr counts as success for the client, setting retc = 1; with a server thread it instead asks the thread to abort via abortserverthread, otherwise it also sets rets = 1 without checking whether the server confirmed the handshake; any error other than WANT_READ/WANT_WRITE sets clienterr), advances the test time, runs SSL_handle_events and the server tick (waiting for client_ready when threaded), polls the server for termination (servererr) or handshake confirmation (rets), and exits through err (returning 0) if both sides have erred, after MAXLOOPS iterations with a non-NULL clientssl, or if qtest_wait_for_timeout fails. After the loop, if a server thread was used and rets > 0, it signals client_ready, waits for the thread, and returns 0 if wait_for_thread or globserverret is false. It returns 1 if clienterr and servererr are both clear, otherwise 0.

functions.name: create_bare_ssl_connection_ex
functions.prose_contract: Drives the handshake between a client SSL and a server SSL, both supplied by the caller, until both have completed or something stops it, and returns 1 only when the loop ends because SSL_connect on clientssl and the server step (SSL_accept, or DTLSv1_listen followed by SSL_accept) have both returned > 0. It returns 0 immediately, without writing cm_count or sm_count, if listen is non-zero and serverssl is not DTLS, if BIO_ADDR_new fails, or (in a no-sock build) whenever listen is non-zero. Each loop iteration calls SSL_connect (repeating while the error is WANT_WRITE; an error other than WANT_READ sets clienterr after logging) and then, for the server, either DTLSv1_listen (if listen is still set; a positive return clears listen and continues with SSL_accept in later steps; a negative return is treated as SSL_ERROR_SSL) or SSL_accept (an error other than WANT_READ or WANT_X509_LOOKUP sets servererr). It jumps to the exit, returning 0, if want is not SSL_ERROR_NONE and either side's last error code equals want, if both clienterr and servererr are set, if (for DTLS with read set) an SSL_read that is only meant to trigger retransmits unexpectedly returns > 0, or when abortctr reaches MAXLOOPS; for DTLS it sleeps 50 ms every 10th pass for the first 50. At the exit (after the loop starts) it stores the counts of connect and server-step calls in *cm_count and *sm_count when those pointers are non-NULL and frees the BIO_ADDR. The loop condition is only that retc <= 0 or rets <= 0, so a side that has recorded an error does not by itself end the loop.

functions.name: test_hmac_run
functions.prose_contract: Test function with no parameters that exercises the HMAC_CTX API on entries 4, 5 and 6 of the static test table; it returns 1 if all checks pass and 0 at the first failed check. It allocates an HMAC_CTX (returns 0 if that fails) and resets it. It then requires: HMAC_CTX_get_md is NULL, HMAC_Init_ex with NULL key and NULL digest fails, HMAC_Update before init fails, and HMAC_Init_ex with key length -1 and SHA-1 fails. It computes HMAC-SHA1 over test[4] (Init, Update, Final) and compares the hex string with test[4].digest; then requires HMAC_Init_ex with NULL key and SHA-256 to fail (the context was keyed for SHA-1 before); computes HMAC-SHA256 over test[5] (also checking HMAC_CTX_get_md equals EVP_sha256()) and compares with test[5].digest; then initialises with test[6].key and a NULL digest (reusing SHA-256 from the context), updates and finalises over test[6] and compares; and twice more reuses the existing key, once with NULL key and NULL digest and once with NULL key and EVP_sha256(), each over test[6].data and compared with test[6].digest. Each failed check jumps to err, where the context is freed, returning 0; reaching the end returns 1.

functions.name: test_http_method
functions.prose_contract: Test function that runs one mocked HTTP exchange through memory BIOs, selected by do_get (0 means OSSL_HTTP_transfer; non-zero means OSSL_HTTP_get, with do_get > 1 using a "/will-be-redirected" path), do_txt (text/plain request body versus a DER-encoded certificate from the globals x509 and x509_it) and suggested_status (embedded in the request path and consumed by the mock server callback). It builds path, a request BIO req (for do_txt two text strings written to a memory BIO, otherwise ASN1_item_i2d_mem_bio of x509), and the BIOs wbio and rbio; req is set to NULL if the text writes fail. If wbio, rbio or req is NULL it returns 0. It then runs the request (never against the real server, since real_server is always 0) and requires that "suggested_status == HTTP_STATUS_CODES_FATAL_ERROR" has the same truth value as "response is NULL"; if not, it returns 0. When the suggested status is HTTP_STATUS_CODES_FATAL_ERROR (and the response is therefore NULL) it returns 1 without looking at why the response is NULL. Otherwise the response is non-NULL and the result is 1 only if, for do_txt, the first line read from it equals text1, or, for a certificate, d2i_X509_bio yields a certificate that X509_cmp considers equal to x509; the response BIO is freed. At err it frees req, wbio, rbio and the headers stack, and returns res.

functions.name: create_socket
functions.prose_contract: Takes a UDP port number in host byte order (converted with htons) and returns a datagram BIO bound to the IPv6 wildcard address on that port, or NULL on failure. It creates an AF_INET6 SOCK_DGRAM socket with BIO_socket, then, when IPV6_V6ONLY is defined, sets that option to 0 so the socket also accepts IPv4 (failure of setsockopt goes to err); it allocates a BIO_ADDR, fills it with BIO_ADDR_rawmake for AF_INET6 and in6addr_any, binds the fd with BIO_bind, creates the BIO with BIO_new(BIO_s_datagram()) and attaches the fd with BIO_set_fd(sock, fd, BIO_CLOSE) so the BIO owns the descriptor. On success it frees the BIO_ADDR and returns sock. Every failure of those calls prints a message to stderr and goes to err, which frees the BIO_ADDR and the BIO and calls BIO_closesocket(fd) (also when fd is still -1), then returns NULL. Since BIO_set_fd with BIO_CLOSE gives the fd to the BIO, a failure after that point is not possible in this function (the only code after set_fd is the success return).

functions.name: test_tlsext_status_type
functions.prose_contract: Test function with no parameters, using the globals libctx, cert, privkey, ocspcert, cdummyarg, ocsp_client_called and ocsp_server_called, that checks the OCSP status-type settings and callbacks; it returns 1 only if every stage succeeds and 0 otherwise. It returns 0 at once if create_ssl_ctx_pair fails (before the end label, so ocspcert is not touched). Otherwise it checks that the client context's status type is -1 initially, that SSL_new then reports -1, that SSL_set_tlsext_status_type(TLSEXT_STATUSTYPE_ocsp) works on an SSL, and that after setting it on the context new SSLs inherit it. It then installs ocsp_client_cb and ocsp_server_cb with argument &cdummyarg and requires a handshake to succeed with both callbacks having been called (the callbacks set the flags; they were not read here), then resets the flags and cdummyarg to 0 and requires a second handshake to fail with neither flag set, then sets cdummyarg to 2, builds an OCSP_RESPID from the server certificate read from cert (overwriting the global ocspcert with a freshly allocated X509, without freeing any earlier value), hands the stack to the client SSL with SSL_set_tlsext_status_ids (ownership transferred) and requires a third handshake to succeed with both callbacks called. Any failed step jumps to end, which frees the SSL objects, both contexts, any remaining OCSP_RESPID stack and id, the BIO, frees ocspcert and sets it to NULL, and returns testresult (0 unless it reached the final statement).

functions.name: test_early_data_replay_int
functions.prose_contract: Test helper taking idx (passed to setupearly_data_test), usecb (0 no allow-early-data callback, 1 or 2 callback installed) and confopt (when usecb > 0, 0 sets SSL_OP_NO_ANTI_REPLAY directly, otherwise the same through SSL_CONF_cmd "Options" "-AntiReplay"); it resets allow_ed_cb_called to 0 first and uses the globals libctx, cert, privkey, clientpsk and serverpsk. It returns 0 immediately, without freeing or clearing clientpsk and serverpsk, if create_ssl_ctx_pair fails. Otherwise it configures the callback (SSL_CONF_CTX_new failure or a SSL_CONF_cmd result other than 2 goes to end), runs setupearly_data_test, makes a connection that must reuse the session (using up the ticket), shuts down and frees it, creates new SSL objects with the old session, writes early data from the client and checks that SSL_write_early_data wrote all bytes. For usecb <= 1 the server's SSL_read_early_data must return SSL_READ_EARLY_DATA_FINISH with early-data status SSL_EARLY_DATA_REJECTED. For usecb == 2 SSL_read_early_data must return SSL_READ_EARLY_DATA_SUCCESS; if it does not, testresult is set to the return value of check_early_data_timeout(timer) and the function ends there (so it can return 1 on that path); otherwise it checks the data, calls SSL_connect, requires a second SSL_read_early_data to return FINISH with status SSL_EARLY_DATA_ACCEPTED. It then completes the connection and requires SSL_session_reused to be 1 when usecb > 0 (0 otherwise) and allow_ed_cb_called to be 1 when usecb > 0 (0 otherwise). Reaching the end sets testresult = 1. At end (all paths after the first return) it frees sess, clientpsk, serverpsk (setting both globals to NULL), the SSLs and both contexts.

functions.name: virstor_label
functions.prose_contract: gctl handler for the "label" verb: req supplies nargs, hardcode, arg0 (geom name), arg1..arg(nargs-1) (provider names), vir_size and chunk_size; it returns void and reports problems through gctl_error and early return, so some failures leave earlier providers already modified. It returns with an error if nargs < 2, if arg0 is missing, if vir_size or chunk_size is 0, if the providers' sector sizes differ (checked via g_get_sectorsize for each), if no sector size was found, if g_get_mediasize or g_get_sectorsize returns 0 for a provider in the clearing pass, or if g_metadata_clear fails. A provider smaller than the larger of 4 chunks and the map size only gets a gctl_error "Device %s is too small" without returning. It rounds chunk_size up to a multiple of the sector size, rounds the virtual size down (integer division) to a multiple of the chunk size, and if the map byte size (one virstor_map_entry per chunk) is not a multiple of the sector size adds chunks and recomputes the virtual size so the map fits; it prints a warning if the virtual size is below the summed media size. It then opens arg1 (prefixing _PATH_DEV when the name does not start with it; returns an error if open fails), writes a zero-filled allocation map of total_chunks entries in blocks of at most 1 MiB worth of entries (calloc failure or a write error returns after freeing and closing), generates md_id with arc4random, and for each provider fills the metadata (position, provider size, chunk_count reduced by 1 if the last sector would be used, chunk_next, chunk_reserved = 2 * map_chunks and the ALLOCATED and CURRENT flags only for the first provider, provider name only if hardcode), encodes it into a calloc'd sector (the process exits via err(1, ...) if that allocation fails) and stores it with g_metadata_store; a store failure prints a message, calls gctl_error and returns without handling the remaining providers.

functions.name: be_activate
functions.prose_contract: Activates the boot environment named bootenv (relative to the BE root) in handle lbh; temporary selects a one-time activation. It builds be_path with be_root_concat and calls be_exists on it; if be_exists returns non-zero (it fails e.g. when the dataset is missing or its mountpoint is not /), the function returns set_error(lbh, err) for both the temporary and the permanent case. If temporary is true it then returns the result of lzbe_set_boot_device(zpool_get_name(lbh->active_phandle), lzbe_add, be_path) and does not touch bootfs, the previous BE, or origins. If temporary is false: when lbh->bootfs does not start with "-" it calls be_deactivate(lbh, lbh->bootfs, false) and returns -1 if that fails; it sets the pool's bootfs property with zpool_set_prop to be_path (returns -1 on failure); then it loops, opening be_path with zfs_open (returns -1 if that fails), calling be_zfs_promote(zhp, &found_origin) and closing the handle, until found_origin is false; if found_origin is true and the promote returned a non-zero err it returns that err; when the loop leaves with found_origin false and err non-zero it returns -1. Otherwise it returns BE_ERR_SUCCESS. Before the promotion loop fails the bootfs property has already been changed.

functions.name: be_destroy_internal
functions.prose_contract: Destroys the boot environment dataset or snapshot called name (relative to the BE root of lbh, with an optional @snapshot suffix) according to the BE_DESTROY_* flags in options; odestroyer is true when the call is the recursive destruction of an origin snapshot. Error returns go through set_error(lbh, code), which stores the code in lbh->error, optionally prints it, and returns the code itself (a BE_ERR_* value, not -1). Returns BE_ERR_NOENT if the filesystem or snapshot does not exist, BE_ERR_DESTROYACT if the filesystem path equals lbh->rootfs or lbh->bootfs, BE_ERR_ZFSOPEN if zfs_open fails, BE_ERR_NOMEM if strdup of the snapshot name fails, BE_ERR_DESTROYMNT if the filesystem is mounted and BE_DESTROY_FORCE is not set (when it is set the filesystem is unmounted, ignoring the unmount result), and also if be_destroy_cb fails with EBUSY, BE_ERR_UNKNOWN for other be_destroy_cb errors. If the path equals lbh->bootonce it clears the boot-once device with lzbe_set_boot_device. It then calls be_promote_dependent_clones; on error it returns set_error(lbh, err) of that error (for example BE_ERR_HASCLONES), except that when odestroyer is true, the error is BE_ERR_HASCLONES and BE_DESTROY_AUTOORIGIN is set it returns 0 without destroying anything. When BE_DESTROY_WANTORIGIN is set it reads the dataset's origin property, and returns BE_ERR_NOORIGIN if that read fails and BE_DESTROY_ORIGIN is set. If BE_DESTROY_AUTOORIGIN is set and the origin name is an automatic snapshot name it adds BE_DESTROY_ORIGIN. After be_destroy_cb succeeds and the dataset is closed it returns 0 when BE_DESTROY_ORIGIN is not set; otherwise it returns BE_ERR_INVORIGIN if the origin is empty or not longer than root plus one, returns 0 if the origin is not under lbh->root, and otherwise returns the result of the recursive be_destroy_internal on the origin with BE_DESTROY_ORIGIN cleared and odestroyer true. The zfs handle fs is not closed on the DESTROYMNT-unforced, promote-failure and NOORIGIN returns, and the duplicated snapshot name is not freed on the NOORIGIN return.

functions.name: __bt_open
functions.prose_contract: Creates and returns a DB handle for a btree on file fname (an in-memory tree backed by an unlinked temporary file when fname is NULL), or returns NULL with errno set. It copies openinfo (or fills defaults when openinfo is NULL) and fails with EINVAL if openinfo->flags has bits other than R_DUP, if psize is non-zero but below MINPSIZE, above MAX_PAGE_OFFSET + 1 or not indx_t-aligned, if minkeypage is 1, or if lorder is neither BIG_ENDIAN nor LITTLE_ENDIAN after defaulting; it also returns EINVAL for access modes other than O_RDONLY and O_RDWR on a named file (O_RDONLY sets B_RDONLY) and for a non-O_RDWR mode when fname is NULL. It allocates the BTREE and DB (calloc failure returns NULL), sets B_NEEDSWAP when the byte order differs from the machine's, opens the file with flags | O_CLOEXEC (or tmp() with B_INMEM), and fstat()s it. If the file is non-empty it reads a BTMETA; a short read gives EFTYPE, a wrong magic (after byte-swap detection), version, page size outside the allowed range or unknown flags also give EFTYPE; otherwise page size, flags, free list head and record count come from the file. If the file is empty it picks the page size from st_blksize (clamped to MINPSIZE and MAX_PAGE_OFFSET + 1) when none was given, sets B_NODUPS unless R_DUP, bt_free = P_INVALID, nrecs 0 and B_METADIRTY. It rounds the cache size to a multiple of the page size and to at least MINCACHE pages, computes bt_ovflsize, opens the mpool (with __bt_pgin/__bt_pgout filters unless B_INMEM) and calls nroot (failure goes to err). Finally it sets B_DB_LOCK, B_DB_SHMEM and B_DB_TXN from dflags and returns the DB. The err path frees the DB and BTREE and closes the fd if one was opened, but does not close the mpool opened at line 296, so a failure of nroot leaves bt_mp allocated.

functions.name: bt_fast
functions.prose_contract: Fast path for sequential inserts into a btree: tries to place the key at the position remembered from the previous insert (t->bt_last.pgno and t->bt_last.index) without a tree search, and returns &t->bt_cur on a hit or NULL on a miss. It pins the page with mpool_get; if that fails it sets t->bt_order to NOT and returns NULL, leaving bt_cur and *exactp unchanged. Otherwise it stores the page and the remembered index in t->bt_cur (these stay set even on a miss) and treats it as a miss if the free space on the page (upper - lower) is smaller than the space for the new leaf entry plus an index slot. When t->bt_order is FORWARD it is a miss if the page has a next page, if the index is not the last index on the page (NEXTINDEX - 1), or if __bt_cmp of the key against that entry is negative; on a hit it advances t->bt_cur.index by one when the key differs from the entry and records the new index in t->bt_last.index. In the other case (backward order) it is a miss if the page has a previous page, if the index is not 0, or if the key compares greater than the entry; on a hit it sets t->bt_last.index to 0. On a miss it sets t->bt_order to NOT, releases the page with mpool_put and returns NULL (leaving t->bt_cur.page pointing at the released page). On a hit it sets *exactp to 1 when the key compared equal and returns &t->bt_cur with the page still pinned.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Driver for the DB(3) regression script interpreter: options -f file, -i infoarg, -l (adds DB_LOCK to the open flags), -o file (output file, opened with O_TRUNC) and -s are parsed with getopt; an unknown option calls usage(), an unopenable -o file calls the local err(), and exactly two operands must remain (otherwise usage()), the database type (via dbtype) and a script path, where "-" keeps stdin and any other path is reopened as stdin (err on failure). The -i string is split on commas, tabs and spaces and each non-empty piece is passed to setinfo. The database file is $TMPDIR/__dbtest or /var/tmp/__dbtest when no -f is given (unlinked first), or the -f name (unlinked unless -s); dbopen failure calls err. Script lines are then read with fgets: when the output is stdout the trailing newline is removed, and lines that are empty, begin with a whitespace character or with # are skipped. The first character selects a command (c compare, e echo to the output fd, g get, p put, r remove, S sync, s seq, f set flags, o dump, k/K key text or key file, d/D data text or data file); a command, key or data line seen in the wrong state, a K line for recno, a key or data given to a command that does not take it, or an unknown command character calls err(), as does a short write for echo. The commands then call compare, get, getdata, put, rem, synk, seq or dump on the open DB, with the r and s commands acting immediately on the previous key when the flags are R_CURSOR (for s, otherwise when flags are not R_CURSOR). After end of input it calls dbp->close (err on failure), closes the output fd and calls exit(0); main ends by calling exit(0) or through err()/usage(). The local err() prints "dbtest: " and the message and calls exit(1), so each err() call terminates the process with status 1, usage() also exits with 1; allocated keys/data are freed in most branches but not on every error exit.

functions.name: __xuname
functions.prose_contract: Fills namebuf, treated as five consecutive fields of namesize bytes (sysname, nodename, release, version, machine), and returns 0 or -1. For sysname (UNAME_s), release (UNAME_r), version (UNAME_v) and machine (UNAME_m), if the environment variable is set its value is copied into the field with strlcpy (truncated to namesize - 1 characters and NUL-terminated); otherwise the field is read with sysctl (KERN_OSTYPE, KERN_OSRELEASE, KERN_VERSION, HW_MACHINE) and its last byte is forced to NUL. The nodename field has no environment override and is read with sysctl(KERN_HOSTNAME), last byte forced to NUL. A sysctl failure with errno ENOMEM (output truncated) restores the previous errno and is not counted as an error; any other sysctl failure makes the return value -1 (the remaining fields are still processed). In the sysctl path for the version field, after the sysctl each newline or tab within the first len bytes (len as updated by sysctl, or the original namesize if the call failed) is replaced by a space, except that those within the last two of those bytes are replaced by NUL; this replacement is not done when UNAME_v is set. The function returns 0 if no sysctl call failed with an error other than ENOMEM, and -1 otherwise.

functions.name: __fts_read_44bsd
functions.prose_contract: Returns the next entry of the traversal for FTS stream sp, or NULL. If sp->fts_cur is NULL or FTS_STOP is set it returns NULL immediately without changing errno. Otherwise it takes the current node p = sp->fts_cur, saves its fts_instr and resets it to FTS_NOINSTR. For FTS_AGAIN it re-stats p with fts_stat (no follow) and returns the same node. For FTS_FOLLOW on a node whose fts_info is FTS_SL or FTS_SLNONE it re-stats with following; if the result is FTS_D and FTS_NOCHDIR is not set it opens "." to remember the location (on failure the node gets FTS_ERR and fts_errno, otherwise FTS_SYMFOLLOW is set), and returns the same node. If p is a directory in pre-order (FTS_D) it either marks it FTS_DP and returns it (when the instruction was FTS_SKIP, or FTS_XDEV is set and the device differs from the root's; the symlink fd is closed and any cached child list freed), or descends: it discards a cached name-only child list, changes into the directory for a cached child list (on failure it records fts_errno, sets FTS_DONTCHDIR and rewrites the children's access paths) or builds the child list with fts_build(BREAD) (if that returns NULL it returns NULL when FTS_STOP is set and otherwise returns the directory itself), then returns the first child with the path updated. For any other node it moves to the next sibling (freeing the old node): a sibling at root level triggers a change to the root directory (failure sets FTS_STOP and returns NULL) and fts_load; siblings with instruction FTS_SKIP are skipped and FTS_FOLLOW siblings are stat-followed like above. With no sibling it frees the node and moves to the parent: when the parent is the root parent it frees it, sets errno to 0 and returns NULL with fts_cur NULL (normal end); otherwise it terminates the path, changes back to the parent directory (via the root fd, the saved symlink fd, or "..", setting FTS_STOP and returning NULL, with errno from the failed call, if that fails) and returns the parent with fts_info FTS_ERR if it has a non-zero fts_errno and FTS_DP otherwise. Except in the FTS_AGAIN and FTS_FOLLOW cases, which return without updating the path, sp->fts_cur is set to the returned node.

functions.name: __fts_children_44bsd
functions.prose_contract: Returns the list of children of the current entry sp->fts_cur (the caller must have a non-NULL fts_cur; the function dereferences it). If instr is neither 0 nor FTS_NAMEONLY it sets errno to EINVAL and returns NULL. Otherwise it sets errno to 0 and returns NULL if FTS_STOP is set; if the current entry's fts_info is FTS_INIT it returns that entry's fts_link (the root list, still owned by the stream); if fts_info is anything other than FTS_D (a directory visited in pre-order) it returns NULL. It then frees any previous sp->fts_child list (the pointer is not cleared before the next assignment), sets the FTS_NAMEONLY flag when instr is FTS_NAMEONLY (reading names only, BNAMES) and otherwise reads with BCHILD, and builds the list with fts_build. When the current entry is not at the root level, its access path is absolute, or FTS_NOCHDIR is set, it stores and returns the fts_build result in sp->fts_child. Otherwise it opens "." first (returns NULL if that fails), builds the list, then restores the directory with fchdir; if the fchdir fails it closes the fd and returns NULL (leaving sp->fts_child set to the built list); otherwise it closes the fd and returns sp->fts_child. fts_build may return NULL for an empty directory or on error, with errno distinguishing the cases only as the callee leaves it.

functions.name: freebsd11_fts_read
functions.prose_contract: FreeBSD 11 ABI version of fts_read: returns the next FTSENT11 for stream sp, or NULL. If sp->fts_cur is NULL or FTS_STOP is set it returns NULL at once without touching errno. Otherwise it takes p = sp->fts_cur, saves its fts_instr and resets it to FTS_NOINSTR. FTS_AGAIN re-stats p (fts_stat without following) and returns the same node; FTS_FOLLOW on a node with fts_info FTS_SL or FTS_SLNONE re-stats it following the link, and if the result is a directory and FTS_NOCHDIR is not set opens "." (on failure sets FTS_ERR and fts_errno, else sets FTS_SYMFOLLOW) and returns the same node. A pre-order directory (FTS_D) is turned into FTS_DP and returned when the instruction was FTS_SKIP or FTS_XDEV is set and the device differs from the root's (closing a symlink fd and freeing any cached child list). Otherwise it drops a name-only child list, then either changes into the directory for an existing child list (on failure recording fts_errno on the directory, setting FTS_DONTCHDIR and fixing the children's access paths) or builds the list with fts_build(BREAD); if that returns NULL it returns NULL when FTS_STOP is set and otherwise returns the directory node itself; with a non-empty list it returns the first child with the path updated. For other nodes it advances to the next sibling (freeing the old node): a sibling at root level triggers fchdir to the root directory (failure sets FTS_STOP, returns NULL without freeing the old node) and fts_load; FTS_SKIP siblings are skipped and FTS_FOLLOW siblings are stat-followed. With no sibling it moves to the parent: at the root-parent level it frees both nodes, sets errno to 0 and returns NULL with fts_cur NULL (normal end of traversal); otherwise it NUL-terminates the path and changes back to the parent (root fd, saved symlink fd, or ".."), setting FTS_STOP and returning NULL with the failing call's errno if that fails, then frees the old node, sets fts_info to FTS_ERR when the parent's fts_errno is non-zero and FTS_DP otherwise, and returns the parent. Except for the FTS_AGAIN and FTS_FOLLOW returns, sp->fts_cur is set to the returned node.

functions.name: fts_stat
functions.prose_contract: Classifies the entry p of stream sp and returns an FTS_* info code; follow selects link handling (0 no, positive follow, negative follow only if the target is a directory) and dfd is -1 (use p->fts_accpath relative to the current directory) or a directory descriptor (use p->fts_name relative to it). The stat result goes into p->fts_statp, or into a local buffer when FTS_NOSTAT is set. If p has FTS_ISW set it returns FTS_W, first zeroing p->fts_statp and setting st_mode to S_IFWHT only when the stat buffer is the entry's own. When FTS_LOGICAL is set or follow is non-zero it calls fstatat following links; if that fails, or if follow < 0 and the target is not a directory, it retries with AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW; if the retry fails it stores the first errno in p->fts_errno, zeroes the buffer and returns FTS_NS; otherwise it sets errno to 0 and returns FTS_SLNONE when the first stat failed and the second shows a symlink. Without following it does only the no-follow stat and returns FTS_NS with p->fts_errno set (buffer zeroed) on failure. For a directory it sets p->fts_dev, p->fts_ino and p->fts_nlink (also under FTS_NOSTAT), returns FTS_DOT if the name is ".", scans the ancestors for the same device and inode and returns FTS_DC with p->fts_cycle set to the matching ancestor, and otherwise returns FTS_D. It returns FTS_SL for a symlink, FTS_F for a regular file and FTS_DEFAULT for any other type.

functions.name: fts_read
functions.prose_contract: Returns the next FTSENT for stream sp, or NULL. If sp->fts_cur is NULL or FTS_STOP is set it returns NULL at once without touching errno. Otherwise it takes p = sp->fts_cur, saves its fts_instr and resets it to FTS_NOINSTR. FTS_AGAIN re-stats p (fts_stat without following) and returns the same node; FTS_FOLLOW on a node with fts_info FTS_SL or FTS_SLNONE re-stats it following the link, and if the result is a directory and FTS_NOCHDIR is not set opens "." (on failure sets FTS_ERR and fts_errno, else sets FTS_SYMFOLLOW) and returns the same node. A pre-order directory (FTS_D) is turned into FTS_DP and returned when the instruction was FTS_SKIP or FTS_XDEV is set and the device differs from the root's (closing a symlink fd and freeing any cached child list). Otherwise it drops a name-only child list, then either changes into the directory for an existing child list (on failure recording fts_errno on the directory, setting FTS_DONTCHDIR and fixing the children's access paths) or builds the list with fts_build(BREAD); if that returns NULL it returns NULL when FTS_STOP is set and otherwise returns the directory node itself; with a list it returns the first child with the path updated. For other nodes it advances to the next sibling (freeing the old node): a sibling at root level triggers fchdir to the root directory (failure sets FTS_STOP and returns NULL) and fts_load; FTS_SKIP siblings are skipped and FTS_FOLLOW siblings are stat-followed. With no sibling it moves to the parent: at the root-parent level it frees both nodes, sets errno to 0 and returns NULL with fts_cur NULL (normal end); otherwise it NUL-terminates the path and changes back to the parent (root fd, saved symlink fd, or ".."), setting FTS_STOP and returning NULL with the failing call's errno if that fails, then frees the old node, sets fts_info to FTS_ERR when the parent's fts_errno is non-zero and FTS_DP otherwise, and returns the parent. Except for the FTS_AGAIN and FTS_FOLLOW returns, sp->fts_cur is set to the returned node. The caller must not use a node returned by an earlier call after the next call, since nodes are freed when passed.

functions.name: nfcmp
functions.prose_contract: Compares the name-field string nf with the name field at the start of the record rec, where the name field is taken to end at the first colon (included). It scans rec for the first ':' or NUL; if it reaches the NUL without a colon it returns 1 (not a match) and leaves rec unchanged. Otherwise it saves the byte after the colon, temporarily writes a NUL there, calls strcmp(nf, rec) on the truncated string (so the colon is part of the compared text), restores the saved byte and returns the strcmp result, which is 0 when nf equals the record's text up to and including the first colon and non-zero otherwise. rec is modified only temporarily and holds its original contents when the function returns; the byte after the colon must be writable.

functions.name: _CITRUS_BCS_PRED(isspace, _citrus_bcs_isblank(c) || _citrus_bcs_iseol(c) || c == '\f' || c == '\v')
functions.prose_contract: Generated function _citrus_bcs_isspace, a static inline function created by the _CITRUS_BCS_PRED macro with parameter c of type uint8_t. It returns 1 (the value of the condition) when c is a space (32), tab (9), newline (10), carriage return (13), form feed (12) or vertical tab (11), via _citrus_bcs_isblank (space, tab), _citrus_bcs_iseol (newline, carriage return) and the two comparisons, and returns 0 for every other byte value. Unlike ctype.h it has no EOF argument.

functions.name: _CITRUS_BCS_PRED(isalnum, _citrus_bcs_isdigit(c) || _citrus_bcs_isalpha(c))
functions.prose_contract: Generated function _citrus_bcs_isalnum, a static inline function created by the _CITRUS_BCS_PRED macro with parameter c of type uint8_t. It returns 1 when c is an ASCII digit '0' to '9' (48 to 57), an ASCII uppercase letter 'A' to 'Z' (65 to 90) or an ASCII lowercase letter 'a' to 'z' (97 to 122), through _citrus_bcs_isdigit and _citrus_bcs_isalpha, and returns 0 for every other byte value.

functions.name: _CITRUS_BCS_PRED(isxdigit, _citrus_bcs_isdigit(c) || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'F') || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'f'))
functions.prose_contract: Generated function _citrus_bcs_isxdigit, a static inline function created by the _CITRUS_BCS_PRED macro with parameter c of type uint8_t. It returns 1 when c is an ASCII digit (48 to 57), an uppercase letter 'A' to 'F' (65 to 70) or a lowercase letter 'a' to 'f' (97 to 102), and returns 0 for every other byte value.

functions.name: _CITRUS_PROP_READ_UINT_COMMON(num, uint64_t, UINT64_MAX)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function _citrus_prop_read_num_common(ms, result, base, neg), a static function created by the _CITRUS_PROP_READ_UINT_COMMON macro with _type_ uint64_t and _max_ UINT64_MAX. It reads characters from the memory stream ms one at a time with _memstream_getc, converting each (upper-cased) character through the xdigit table to a digit value, and accumulates acc = acc * base + digit. It stops at the first character that is not a digit below base, or at the first digit that would make the value exceed UINT64_MAX (checked with cutoff = UINT64_MAX / base and cutlim = UINT64_MAX % base), so the character it stops on may be a non-digit or an overflowing digit. It then pushes back exactly that last character read with _memstream_ungetc, stores acc in *result (negated modulo 2^64, as -acc, when neg is non-zero, otherwise unchanged) and returns 0. It has no error return: overflow ends the number early rather than failing, and base must be non-zero and at most the length of the xdigit table for the digit test to be meaningful.

functions.name: _EUC_mbrtowc_impl
functions.prose_contract: Restartable EUC multibyte-to-wide-character conversion; ps is a conversion state (_EucState) holding the number of bytes still wanted (want) and the partial value (ch), and cs2/cs2width/cs3/cs3width describe the two single-shift code sets. If es->want is negative or greater than MB_CUR_MAX it sets errno to EINVAL and returns (size_t)-1 with the state unchanged. If s is NULL it behaves as if s pointed at "" with n = 1 and pwc = NULL; then if n is 0 it returns (size_t)-2 without changing the state or errno. When es->want is 0 and the first byte has the high bit clear it stores it in *pwc (when pwc is non-NULL) and returns 0 for NUL, otherwise 1, leaving the state unchanged; a first byte >= 0xa1 starts a 2-byte sequence, a byte equal to cs2 or cs3 starts a sequence of cs2width or cs3width bytes, and any other high-bit byte sets errno to EILSEQ and returns (size_t)-1; for a new sequence es->want is set to the wanted length and es->ch to 0. When es->want is non-zero it continues with want = es->want and the saved es->ch (the continuation bytes are not validated). It then shifts up to MIN(want, n) bytes into the value; if fewer than want bytes were available it saves the remaining count in es->want and the partial value in es->ch, sets errno to EILSEQ and returns (size_t)-2. If the sequence is complete it stores the wide character in *pwc when pwc is non-NULL, sets es->want to 0 (es->ch keeps whatever it held, 0 after a sequence that began in this call) and returns 0 if the value is L'\0', otherwise the sequence length want.

functions.name: setlocale
functions.prose_contract: Queries or sets the program locale for category (LC_ALL or one of the individual categories) and returns a pointer to the resulting locale name, or NULL on error. If category is below LC_ALL or at/above _LC_LAST it sets errno to EINVAL and returns NULL. If locale is NULL it returns current_categories[category] for a single category or currentlocale() for LC_ALL, and changes neither the stored categories nor errno. Otherwise it first copies current_categories into new_categories, then fills new_categories from locale: an empty string takes the names from the environment (__get_locale_env) for every category (LC_ALL) or just the one category, returning NULL with EINVAL if a name is longer than ENCODING_LEN; a non-empty string for a single category is copied (EINVAL and NULL if longer than ENCODING_LEN); for LC_ALL a string without '/' is copied to all categories (same length check), and a string with '/' is split into per-category names (EINVAL and NULL if it consists only of slashes or a component is longer than ENCODING_LEN; names beyond the last category are silently ignored, and categories not given are copied from the previous one). For a single category it then returns loadlocale(category). For LC_ALL it loads each category in turn, saving the old name; if loading category i fails it saves errno, reloads the previously loaded categories 1..i-1 from their saved names (falling back to "C" if that also fails), restores errno and returns NULL; if all succeed it returns currentlocale().

functions.name: _nis_gethostbyaddr
functions.prose_contract: nsswitch dispatch method for reverse host lookup through NIS; rval points to a struct hostent * result slot and ap supplies, in order, addr, len, af, hptr, buffer, buflen, errnop and h_errnop. In every build it first stores NULL in *(struct hostent **)rval. Without YP defined it returns NS_UNAVAIL at once (the NULL stays in the slot). With YP defined it reads the arguments, gets the thread's resolver state, and if __hostent_data_init returns NULL sets the resolver h_errno to NETDB_INTERNAL, stores it in *h_errnop and returns NS_NOTFOUND. It then calls _gethostbynisaddr_r (which formats addr with inet_ntop, returning -1 if that fails, and otherwise looks it up in the hosts.byaddr map for AF_INET or ipnodes.byaddr for other families); if that returns non-zero it stores the current resolver h_errno in *h_errnop and returns NS_NOTFOUND (errnop untouched). If __copy_hostent into hptr and buffer fails it stores errno in *errnop, sets the resolver h_errno to NETDB_INTERNAL, stores it in *h_errnop and returns NS_RETURN with the result slot still NULL. Otherwise it stores hptr in the result slot and returns NS_SUCCESS.

functions.name: link_ntoa_r
functions.prose_contract: Formats the link-level address of sdl as text into obuf (obuf may be NULL; sdl and buflen must be non-NULL, asserted) and reports the space needed through *buflen. The text is the interface name (sdl_nlen bytes, capped at IFNAMSIZ, copied as is), then a ':' only if the name length is greater than 0 and sdl_alen > 0, then each address byte in lowercase hexadecimal, a byte above 0xf as two digits and a byte up to 0xf as one digit without a leading zero, with '.' between bytes. Output is written only while it fits: each piece is checked to leave room for one more byte for the terminating NUL, and once a piece does not fit nothing more is written (rem set to 0, later pieces are skipped even if they would fit). When obuf is non-NULL and the initial *buflen was non-zero it always writes a NUL at the current output position, which is inside the buffer because earlier pieces were only written when room for the NUL remained. *buflen is then set to the total length needed including the NUL (the count stops growing if it would exceed SIZE_MAX). The function returns 0 if obuf was non-NULL, the initial *buflen was positive and every piece fit, and -1 otherwise (including when obuf is NULL, *buflen is 0, or the text was truncated). The initial *buflen is stored in an int.

functions.name: _nsdispatch
functions.prose_contract: Name-service dispatcher: for the database and method_name it tries the configured sources in order (or the NULL-name terminated defaults list when the database has no configured entry), passing the variadic arguments to each source's method, and returns an NS_* result; errno is saved on entry and restored to that value on every return path (the label fin). If the process is threaded it takes the nss_lock read lock; if that fails it returns NS_UNAVAIL (lock not held). It then calls fb_getstate and nss_configure; if either returns non-zero it returns NS_UNAVAIL while the read lock, if it was taken, is still held and without having incremented dispatch_depth. Otherwise it increments the dispatch depth and, when that exceeds the fallback depth, looks up the database's source list and the fallback method. For each source in the list it sets result to NS_NOTFOUND and looks up the method; if one exists it clears errno, calls it (with NS_CACHING compiled in, a "cache" source is handled through the cache read functions, may be skipped when issetugid() is non-zero under NS_STRICT_LIBC_EID_CHECKING, and a later cache write is done for NS_SUCCESS or NS_NOTFOUND results) and stops the loop when the result intersects that source's flags; a result that does not match the flags goes on to the next source. If no method exists, the fallback method (if any) is called with the source name and its result becomes the source's result; the loop does not stop on a fallback result because it is not checked against the flags; with no fallback the source gives NS_NOTFOUND after a debug log. The function returns the result from the last source tried (the matching one, or the last one if none matched); if the source list is empty it returns the 0 from nss_configure. Normal exit releases the read lock when threaded and decrements dispatch_depth.

functions.name: acl_strip_np
functions.prose_contract: Returns a newly allocated ACL holding only the trivial entries of aclp, chosen by the brand of aclp (aclp must be a valid acl_t; _acl_brand is called on it), or NULL with errno set. For ACL_BRAND_NFS4 it calls _nfs4_acl_strip_np(aclp, 0), which allocates a new NFS4-branded ACL with acl_init (ENOMEM and NULL if that fails), derives a mode from aclp with acl_nfs4_sync_mode_from_acl and fills the new ACL with acl_nfs4_trivial_from_mode_libc; recalculate_mask is ignored for this brand. For ACL_BRAND_POSIX it calls _posix1e_acl_strip_np(aclp, recalculate_mask), which duplicates aclp with acl_dup (NULL if that fails), allocates a new ACL (NULL, after freeing the duplicate, if that fails), copies the ACL_USER_OBJ, ACL_GROUP_OBJ and ACL_OTHER entries into it while walking the duplicate with acl_get_entry (the walk simply ends if acl_get_entry stops returning 1, including on an error, and the partial result is then returned), notes whether an ACL_MASK entry existed, and if one existed and recalculate_mask is non-zero calls acl_calc_mask. If acl_get_tag_type, acl_create_entry, acl_copy_entry or acl_calc_mask fails it frees both ACLs and returns NULL, with errno as left by the failing call. On the success path of the POSIX case the duplicate acl_old is not freed. For any other brand it sets errno to EINVAL and returns NULL.

functions.name: __signalcontext
functions.prose_contract: PowerPC64 helper that rewrites the context ucp so that resuming it runs func(sig, siginfo, ucontext) through ctx_wrapper on a fresh frame; it returns 0. If ucp is NULL it calls abort(). It takes the saved stack pointer ucp->uc_mcontext.mc_gpr[1], subtracts sizeof(ucontext_t), aligns down to 16 bytes and copies *ucp (the original context, before it is modified) there as sig_uc; it then subtracts sizeof(siginfo_t), aligns again, zero-fills the siginfo_t there with bzero and sets si_signo to sig; it subtracts a further 48 bytes (6 * sizeof(uint64_t)) for a frame pointer area and aligns the resulting stack pointer down to 16 bytes. It then zeroes ucp->uc_mcontext, sets ucp->uc_link to the copied context sig_uc, removes sig from ucp->uc_sigmask with sigdelset, and fills in the mcontext: version _MC_VERSION, length, mc_srr0 = ctx_wrapper, mc_gpr[1] = the new stack pointer, mc_gpr[3] = func, mc_gpr[4] = sig, mc_gpr[5] = the siginfo pointer and mc_gpr[6] = sig_uc. The stack below the saved stack pointer must have room for the two structures and the 48 bytes; nothing checks this.

functions.name: walk
functions.prose_contract: Core matcher step loop of the regex engine, used in two modes selected by fast; it runs the state set through the subject from start toward stop using step(), starting at strip state startst with stopst as the accepting state. It begins with the state set containing startst (after one NOTHING step); in fast mode it also saves that set as the fresh state. At each position it decodes the next character with XMBRTOWC (the end of subject gives OUT with length 0), applies the BOL/EOL, beginning/end-of-string and word-boundary steps that apply between the previous and current character, then tests whether stopst is in the set: in fast mode that ends the loop, in slow mode it records matchp = p and continues. The loop also ends when the state set is empty, when p equals stop, or when the character length exceeds the remaining bytes; otherwise it steps over the character (fast mode restarts from the fresh state at each position, slow mode from an empty set) and advances p.
