In fast mode, matchp is set to p whenever the state set equals the fresh set at the top of an iteration; at exit it sets m->coldp to matchp and returns p advanced by the length XMBRTOWC reports for the character at p (at least 1, because that helper returns 1 for NUL and for invalid sequences) if stopst is in the set, and NULL otherwise. In slow mode it returns matchp, the last position at which stopst was in the set, or NULL if there was none, and does not change m->coldp.

functions.name: regress
functions.prose_contract: Reads regression-test lines from the open stream in and runs them through try(), then runs five regerror() self-checks; it returns no value and reports failures through the global status and stderr. For each line read with fgets (buffer of 1000 bytes) it first increments the global line counter, so skipped lines are counted too, and skips lines whose first character is '#' or a newline. For other lines it overwrites the last character of the line with NUL (the newline, or the last character if the line was truncated or lacked a newline), prints the line number if debug is set, splits the line with split() into at most 10 fields on tabs, and if there are fewer than 3 fields prints "bad input, line N" and calls exit(1). Fields equal to the two characters "" become empty strings; fields 3 and 4 are set to NULL when absent. It calls try() with the first five fields and the options from the second field; when the second field contains '&' it calls try() a second time with REG_EXTENDED cleared. After end of input it checks regerror(REG_BADPAT) into a 100-byte buffer for the text "invalid regular expression" and its length, a 10-byte truncated version, the REG_ITOA form ("REG_BADPAT") and the REG_ATOI form (a number equal to REG_BADPAT and a consistent length); each failed check prints a message to stderr and sets status to 1.

functions.name: findmust
functions.prose_contract: Computes the "must" string of a compiled regex: the longest run of literal characters (OCHAR operators) that every match must contain, recording it in g->must with its length g->mlen and its offset g->moffset (-1 when the offset is unknown), for use as a quick pre-search. It returns without changing anything if p->error is non-zero, or if MB_CUR_MAX > 1 and the current encoding is not "UTF-8". Otherwise it scans g->strip from element 1 to the OEND element, building runs of OCHAR operators (a wcrtomb failure falls into the "too hard" case) and updating the best run, the mlen and an offset estimate at each operator that breaks a run; alternation/optional constructs are skipped, and if the skip walk meets an element that is not one of the expected branch operators it sets BAD in g->iflags and returns immediately (g->mlen and g->moffset may already be partly updated, g->must untouched). If no OCHAR run was found (g->mlen == 0) it sets g->moffset to -1 and returns. Otherwise it mallocs mlen + 1 bytes for g->must (not freeing any earlier value of g->must, so a non-NULL g->must would be leaked); if malloc fails it sets g->mlen to 0 and g->moffset to -1 and returns; if it succeeds it re-encodes the characters of the chosen run into g->must with wcrtomb and terminates the string with NUL.

functions.name: regexec
functions.prose_contract: Executes the compiled regular expression preg against string, filling pmatch with up to nmatch sub-match offsets, and returns 0 on a match or an REG_* error code. It first reads g = preg->re_g (so preg and preg->re_g must be valid) and returns REG_BADPAT if preg->re_magic is not MAGIC1 or g->magic is not MAGIC2. It then asserts that g->iflags does not have the BAD bit; in a build where asserts are enabled that aborts, and otherwise a BAD pattern makes it return REG_BADPAT. It reduces eflags with GOODFLAGS (only REG_NOTBOL, REG_NOTEOL and REG_STARTEND survive unless REDEBUG is defined). It then calls mmatcher when MB_CUR_MAX > 1, otherwise smatcher when g->nstates fits in the small state-set type (CHAR_BIT * sizeof(states1)) and REG_LARGE is not set, and otherwise lmatcher, returning that matcher's result. In those matchers (engine.c matcher), with REG_STARTEND the subject is the range string + pmatch[0].rm_so to string + pmatch[0].rm_eo (REG_INVARG if the end precedes the start), otherwise string up to its NUL; the matcher result is 0, REG_NOMATCH, REG_INVARG or REG_ESPACE as far as read here.

functions.name: res_nsearch
functions.prose_contract: Resolver search: queries name for the given class and type, applying the search list, and returns the positive response length stored in answer on success or a non-positive value (-1 in all return statements written in this function; the other returns pass on a callee's value) on failure. It clears errno, sets res_h_errno to HOST_NOT_FOUND, counts the dots and notes a trailing dot. If the name has no dots and res_hostalias finds an alias it returns res_nquery for the alias, so that result (and whatever res_h_errno it left, not necessarily NOERROR) is what the caller gets. If the dots reach statp->ndots or there is a trailing dot it first queries the name as is through res_nquerydomain; a positive result or any result when there is a trailing dot is returned directly; if errno is ECONNREFUSED it sets res_h_errno to TRY_AGAIN and returns -1; res_h_errno NO_DATA or HOST_NOT_FOUND (or TRY_AGAIN with rcode SERVFAIL) lets it go on and the code is saved, any other error returns -1 immediately. It then, if there are no dots and RES_DEFNAMES is set or there are dots, no trailing dot and RES_DNSRCH is set, loops over statp->dnsrch calling res_nquerydomain for each domain (skipping the root domain if the name was already tried as is): a positive result is returned; ECONNREFUSED gives res_h_errno TRY_AGAIN and -1; NO_DATA is counted and the search continues, as does HOST_NOT_FOUND and TRY_AGAIN with rcode SERVFAIL (counted); any other error ends the loop, and without RES_DNSRCH the loop ends after one domain. If the final res_h_errno is not NO_DATA/HOST_NOT_FOUND/(TRY_AGAIN with SERVFAIL) it goes to giveup; otherwise it tries the name as is once more unless already tried (or the root is on the list, or no dots with RES_NOTLDQUERY set after a search), returning a positive result. At giveup it sets res_h_errno to the saved as-is error if one was saved, else NO_DATA if any NO_DATA was seen, else TRY_AGAIN if a TRY_AGAIN with SERVFAIL was seen, else leaves it as the last query set it, and returns -1.

functions.name: send_dg
functions.prose_contract: Sends the query datagram buf (buflen bytes) to nameserver number ns over UDP and waits for a matching reply, which it stores in ans (anssiz bytes); the optional kqueue descriptor kq is an extra first parameter when USE_KQUEUE is defined. Return values: the reply length resplen (> 0) when an acceptable reply arrived; 1 when the reply has the TC bit set and RES_IGNTC is not set (v_circuit is set to 1 and the socket is closed, so the caller retries over TCP); -1 when a new socket cannot be created for a reason other than an unsupported protocol/family, or, in a build using select, when the new descriptor is above highestFD (res_nclose is called and errno set to ENOTSOCK before the check), in both cases with *terrno = errno; and 0 in the other failure cases: socket creation failing with EPROTONOSUPPORT, EPFNOSUPPORT or EAFNOSUPPORT (no *terrno), connect, send or sendto failing (socket closed), the timeout expiring (*gotsomewhere set to 1), select/poll/kevent failing with an error other than EINTR (socket closed), recvfrom returning <= 0 (socket closed, *gotsomewhere already set to 1), a reply shorter than HFIXEDSZ (*terrno set to EMSGSIZE, socket closed), a reply with rcode FORMERR when RES_USE_EDNS0 is set (RES_F_EDNS0ERR set in statp->_flags, socket closed), and a reply with rcode SERVFAIL, NOTIMP or REFUSED (socket closed) when statp->pfcode is 0 (if pfcode is non-zero it falls through to the TC check and then returns resplen). It creates and, unless RES_INSECURE1 is set, connects the socket on first use, computes the timeout as (retrans << tries), divided by nscount when ns > 0, at least 1 second, and loops waiting: an EINTR, a reply whose id differs from the query's, a reply from an address that is not one of our servers (unless RES_INSECURE1) or a reply whose question does not match (unless RES_INSECURE2) is ignored and waiting continues until the deadline.

functions.name: __rpc_get_time_offset
functions.prose_contract: Obtains the time difference between a remote host and the local clock: it zeroes *td, finds the server's address, asks rpcbind for its time (RPCB_GETTIME over TCP) or, if that fails, reads the port-37 time service over TCP or UDP, and stores remote minus local seconds in td->tv_sec. It returns 1 if a remote time was obtained and 0 otherwise (the 0 returns leave td zeroed). If *uaddr is NULL: if both srv and thost are non-NULL it prints a message and returns 0; without srv it builds one from thost and netid with get_server (returns 0 if that fails, and frees the endpoints it built on later failures); it picks the TCP endpoint if there is one, else the UDP endpoint, and returns 0 if there is neither; if *uaddr is non-NULL it is used as the address. It then rewrites the address to the form a1.a2.a3.a4.0.111 using sscanf on the first four fields (the sscanf result is not checked), converts it to a sockaddr (return 0 on failure), and creates a TCP client handle to rpcbind (return 0 on failure) and calls RPCBPROC_GETTIME with a 5-second timeout; success marks the time valid. Otherwise it destroys the handle, converts the address to the port-37 form and opens a socket of the chosen type (any failure there jumps to the cleanup with the time invalid), and for UDP sends a datagram and waits up to 20 seconds with select, then receives the 4-byte time; for TCP it connects with a 20-second alarm and reads 4 bytes; the value is converted with ntohl and TOFFSET is subtracted. On the cleanup path it closes any open socket, destroys any client handle, cancels the alarm and restores the old SIGALRM handler. If the time is valid it sets *uaddr to a strdup of the address used when *uaddr was NULL (the result of strdup is not checked), adds 1 to the local gettimeofday seconds when they exceed 500000 (tested on tv_sec, not on tv_usec, so this is not a rounding to the nearest second based on microseconds), stores the signed difference remote minus local in td->tv_sec with td->tv_usec 0, and returns 1; otherwise it prints "unable to get the server's time." and returns 0. Endpoints built by get_server are freed before returning when it allocated them.

functions.name: getnetid
functions.prose_contract: Looks up the netid string for key in the file /etc/netid (NETIDFILE), optionally falling back to NIS, and copies the value into ret (which must be large enough for the value; it is copied with strcpy). It returns 1 when a file record whose first field equals key is found, with its value copied to ret; 2 (only when YP is defined) when a NIS lookup in the netid map succeeded, with the NIS value copied to ret; and 0 otherwise, in which case ret is not modified. If the file cannot be opened the function returns 0 without YP, and with YP it tries NIS once and returns 2 on success or 0 on failure. It reads the file line by line (1024-byte buffer): lines starting with '#' are skipped; a line starting with '+' triggers the NIS lookup (yp_get_default_domain then yp_match on key; on any NIS failure it continues with the next line) when YP is defined, and is skipped when it is not; any other line is split into a key (up to the first space or tab) and the first non-empty value token (delimiters space, tab, '#', newline); a line without a value token prints "Bad record" on stderr and is skipped, and a line whose key equals key stops the search. End of file gives 0. The file is closed before returning if it was opened, and the buffer returned by yp_match is freed after copying.

functions.name: svc_getreq_common
functions.prose_contract: Services pending RPC requests on the transport registered for descriptor fd (fd must be a valid index of __svc_xports); returns nothing. It sets up a local credential area, reads xprt = __svc_xports[fd] under a read lock on svc_fd_lock (the lock is dropped right after the read) and returns without doing anything if that is NULL. Otherwise it loops: if SVC_RECV yields a message it copies program, version, procedure and credentials into a local svc_req and calls _authenticate; if that returns something other than AUTH_OK it sends svcerr_auth(xprt, why) unless why is RPCSEC_GSS_NODISPATCH, in which case it sends nothing, and goes to the end-of-iteration check. Otherwise it searches the registered services (svc_head) for the program and version, calls the matching sc_dispatch(&r, xprt) and goes to the end-of-iteration check; if the program is registered with other versions only it calls svcerr_progvers with the lowest and highest registered versions, and if the program is not registered it calls svcerr_noprog. Only in the cases where SVC_RECV returned false or an error reply was sent (not after a dispatch or an auth failure) does it then take the read lock and leave the loop if __svc_xports[fd] is no longer xprt (the transport was replaced or deregistered during the call). At the end-of-iteration check it calls SVC_STAT: if the transport has died (XPRT_DIED) it calls SVC_DESTROY(xprt) and leaves; otherwise the loop repeats while SVC_STAT returned XPRT_MOREREQS. svc_fd_lock is not held at return.

functions.name: float64_to_int32
functions.prose_contract: Converts the IEEE double a to a 32-bit signed integer, rounding according to the global float_rounding_mode, and returns it. It extracts the fraction, exponent and sign; for a NaN (exponent 0x7FF with a non-zero fraction) the sign is treated as positive; a non-zero exponent adds the implicit leading bit; it shifts the significand right by 0x42C minus the exponent with sticky-bit jamming when that count is positive and leaves it unshifted otherwise, and hands the result to roundAndPackInt32. That function rounds with nearest-even, toward zero, toward negative infinity or toward positive infinity according to float_rounding_mode, sets float_flag_inexact in float_exception_flags when any discarded bits were non-zero, and, when the rounded magnitude does not fit in 32 bits or its sign no longer matches, sets float_flag_invalid and returns 0x7FFFFFFF for a positive (or NaN) input or 0x80000000 for a negative input; an infinity or a NaN therefore gives 0x7FFFFFFF or 0x80000000 with float_flag_invalid. The value -2^31 is returned without the invalid flag.

functions.name: stdc_first_trailing_zero_ul
functions.prose_contract: Takes an unsigned long x and returns an unsigned int: 0 if every bit of x is one (x == ~0UL), otherwise 1 plus the index (counted from 0 at the least significant bit) of the least significant zero bit of x, computed as __builtin_ctzl(~x) + 1; the result therefore lies between 1 and the width of unsigned long when x is not all ones. It reads no memory other than its argument and has no side effects.

functions.name: stdc_trailing_ones_ui
functions.prose_contract: Takes an unsigned int x and returns the number of consecutive one bits starting at the least significant bit. If x == ~0U it returns UINT_WIDTH; otherwise it returns __builtin_ctz(~x), the index of the lowest zero bit of x, so the low result bits of x are one and the next bit is zero. It reads no memory other than its argument and has no side effects.

functions.name: stdc_trailing_ones_ul
functions.prose_contract: Takes an unsigned long x and returns the number of consecutive one bits starting at the least significant bit. If x == ~0UL it returns ULONG_WIDTH; otherwise it returns __builtin_ctzl(~x), the index of the lowest zero bit of x, so the low result bits of x are one and the next bit is zero. It reads no memory other than its argument and has no side effects.

functions.name: stdc_trailing_ones_ull
functions.prose_contract: Takes an unsigned long long x and returns the number of consecutive one bits starting at the least significant bit. If x == ~0ULL it returns ULLONG_WIDTH; otherwise it returns __builtin_ctzll(~x), the index of the lowest zero bit of x, so the low result bits of x are one and the next bit is zero. It reads no memory other than its argument and has no side effects.

functions.name: _fseeko
functions.prose_contract: Repositions stream fp to offset relative to whence (SEEK_SET, SEEK_CUR or SEEK_END) and returns 0 on success or -1 with errno set; ltest, when non-zero, additionally requires the resulting position to fit in a long. Early failures return -1 before touching the stream: ESPIPE if the stream has no seek function; for SEEK_CUR a failing _ftello (its errno is left as is), ESPIPE if the current offset is negative, EOVERFLOW if adding offset would exceed OFF_MAX or (with ltest) exceed LONG_MAX, EINVAL if the sum is negative; EINVAL for a negative SEEK_SET offset or an unknown whence. It then allocates a buffer if none exists and chooses between an optimised path and a "dumb" path (flush, then seek to the requested place). The optimised path is used only for a read-only seekable regular-file stream (otherwise it sets __SNPT and, when first examining the stream, may set __SOPT and the block size) and computes the target for SEEK_END from fstat (EOVERFLOW or EINVAL for an out-of-range target, ltest respected); if the target is inside the current buffer it just moves the read pointer, frees any ungetc pushback, clears __SEOF and resets the multibyte state and returns 0; otherwise it seeks to the block boundary below the target, refills, and positions inside the buffer, also clearing pushback, __SEOF and the conversion state; any seek, refill or short-read problem falls to the dumb path. The dumb path calls __sflush and _sseek (returning -1 with errno from those calls if either fails), fails with EOVERFLOW and sets __SERR when ltest is set and the new position exceeds LONG_MAX, and otherwise frees pushback, empties the buffer, clears __SEOF, resets the multibyte state and returns 0. On failure the stream may already have been altered (flags set, buffer allocated, file offset changed), and errno can come from _ftello, _fstat, __srefill, __sflush or _sseek as well as ESPIPE, EINVAL and EOVERFLOW.

functions.name: _gettemp
functions.prose_contract: Fills in the trailing X characters of the template path (excluding the last slen characters, a suffix) with random characters from padchar and tries to create or check the resulting name, returning 1 on success and 0 on failure with errno set by the failing step. It returns 0 with errno EINVAL if doopen is non-NULL and domkdir is set together, if slen is negative, if oflags has bits other than O_APPEND, O_DIRECT, O_SHLOCK, O_EXLOCK, O_SYNC, O_CLOEXEC and O_CLOFORK, or if the suffix would start at or before the start of path (slen not smaller than strlen(path)) or contains a '/'; ENAMETOOLONG if strlen(path) is MAXPATHLEN or more. It replaces each trailing 'X' before the suffix with arc4random_uniform characters of padchar, then loops: with doopen set it opens the name with _openat(dfd, ..., oflags | O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_RDWR, 0600), storing the descriptor in *doopen and returning 1 on success or 0 on an error other than EEXIST; with domkdir it does mkdir(path, 0700) with the same rule; otherwise it calls lstat and returns whether errno was ENOENT (1 if the name does not exist, 0 for another lstat error; when the name exists it continues). On a collision it saves the initial random characters and increments the characters like an odometer through padchar, returning 0 when every combination has been tried, in which case errno is whatever the last call left (EEXIST after open or mkdir collisions, but not set by this code after a successful lstat), and returning 0 with errno EIO if a template character is not found in padchar.

functions.name: __srefill
functions.prose_contract: Refills the read buffer of stream fp and returns 0 on success or EOF; the caller is expected to hold fp's lock (the function does not lock fp itself, and its flush of fp itself at the line-buffered step is done without locking). It initialises stdio if needed, and ORIENT(fp, -1) only sets the stream orientation to byte if it was unset; it does not fail on a wide-oriented stream and the function does not set EINVAL. It then sets fp->_r to 0 and returns EOF at once if __SEOF is set. If the stream is not in read mode: when it is also not read/write it sets errno to EBADF and __SERR and returns EOF; when it was writing it calls __sflush (returning EOF if that fails), switches it to reading and sets __SRD. If it was already reading and has an ungetc buffer it frees it and, if the saved count _ur is non-zero, restores the read pointer and returns 0 without reading. It allocates a buffer if none exists. For a line-buffered or unbuffered stream it sets __SIGN on fp, calls _fwalk(lflush) to flush line-buffered writers, clears __SIGN, and flushes fp itself with __sflush only if fp is line-buffered and in write mode (the result of that flush is ignored). It then reads up to the buffer size with _sread into the buffer and clears __SMOD (not cleared on the earlier returns). If the read returns 0 it sets __SEOF and returns EOF; if it returns a negative value it sets _r to 0 and __SERR and returns EOF; otherwise it returns 0 with _r holding the byte count.

functions.name: __wcsconv
functions.prose_contract: Converts the wide string wcsarg to a newly malloc'd multibyte string for printf's %ls, limited to prec bytes when prec >= 0 (no limit when prec < 0), and returns it NUL-terminated, or NULL on failure; the caller must free it. With prec < 0 the whole string (up to its terminating NUL) is measured with wcsrtombs; NULL is returned if that fails on an unconvertible character. With 0 <= prec < 128 the buffer size is simply prec bytes without examining the string. With prec >= 128 it counts bytes with wcrtomb from the start, stopping at a NUL wide character, at a conversion error, or at the first character that would take the byte count over prec; that loop reads wide characters up to and including the one at which it stops, so a string without a NUL needs at least one readable wide character beyond the converted prefix. It allocates nbytes + 1 bytes (NULL if malloc fails), then converts with wcsrtombs into that buffer limited to nbytes bytes; if that returns -1 (for prec < 128 this can happen on an unconvertible character within the limit) it frees the buffer and returns NULL; otherwise it NUL-terminates the converted bytes and returns them. For prec >= 128, an unconvertible character found by the counting loop ends the count there, so the result is the truncated prefix before it, not NULL.

functions.name: __svfscanf
functions.prose_contract: Core of scanf for a stream: parses the format fmt0 and reads input from fp (using the locale for wide and floating conversions), storing converted values through pointers fetched from ap, and returns an int count or EOF. It sets the stream orientation to byte if unset. For each format character: end of format returns nassigned; white space in the format skips input white space; an ordinary character (or "%%") must equal the next input byte, otherwise it takes the match_failure exit (input_failure exit if no input can be read). After '%', flags and sizes are parsed (the flags '*' suppress assignment; h, hh, l, ll, j, q, t, z, L; a decimal width; %w<8|16|32|64> with an optional f, any other w width goes to match_failure); a trailing '%' at the end of the format returns EOF at once; an unknown conversion character takes match_failure; %n stores the characters consumed so far (unless suppressed) and does not count as a conversion. The conversions are %d %i %o %u %x %X %b %B %p (read with parseint then strtoimax_l or strtoumax_l and stored by the size flag), %a %A %e %E %f %F %g %G (parsefloat then strtof_l, strtod_l or strtold_l), %s %S, %c %C and %[ (via convert_string, convert_char, convert_ccl and the wide variants). Input white space is skipped before a conversion unless it is %c or %[; hitting end of input at that point or during a conversion that reports a negative count takes input_failure; a parseint or parsefloat count of 0 and an empty %[ match take match_failure. Each completed conversion adds to nconversions and, unless suppressed, nassigned. At input_failure it returns nassigned if at least one conversion was completed and EOF otherwise; at match_failure it returns nassigned (which may be 0, not EOF).

functions.name: __printf_render_float
functions.prose_contract: Renders one floating-point conversion to the output sink io according to pi and returns the sum of the values returned by the __printf_pad and __printf_puts calls it makes (the characters it asked to be written, as reported by those helpers). The value is taken from arg[0] as a double, or as a long double when pi->is_long_double. For %a/%A it uses __hdtoa/__hldtoa hexadecimal digits with a 0x or 0X prefix (dropped for inf/nan), with p/P exponent; for %e/%E, %f/%F and %g/%G it uses dtoa or __ldtoa (default precision DEFPREC when none is given, 1 for %g with precision 0); any other spec value fails the assert(pi->spec == 'f') (in a build with asserts) and otherwise falls to the %f path. The sign is '-' for a negative value, else pi->showsign. A value whose exponent is INT_MAX (infinity or NaN) is printed as inf/nan, or INF/NAN for an upper-case spec, with no sign for NaN. For %g it chooses between fixed and exponent form from the exponent and precision. Output order is: left padding unless zero padding or left justification applies, the sign, the 0x/0X prefix, zero padding up to the width when pi->pad is '0' and not left-justified, then the digits (in fixed form with leading "0.", digit grouping using the locale's thousands separator when pi->alt is set and the locale has grouping, the decimal point from the locale, trailing zero padding; in exponent form the digit, decimal point, remaining digits, zero padding and the exponent string), and finally right padding when pi->left is set. It then calls __printf_flush(io), frees the dtoa buffer if it is non-NULL, and returns the accumulated count.

functions.name: __merge_environ
functions.prose_contract: Re-synchronises the library's internal environment table with the program's environ array when the program has replaced or emptied environ, returning 0 or -1. It does nothing and returns 0 if intEnviron is NULL (no internal copy exists), or if environ equals intEnviron and not (envActive > 0 and environ[0] == NULL). Otherwise, if envActive > 0 it sets origEnviron to NULL and calls __clean_env(false), which deactivates all internal variables, resets envActive to 0 and removes putenv entries; since origEnviron is NULL at that point, __clean_env does not restore or free intEnviron. It then sets origEnviron = environ and, if environ is not NULL, walks its entries: an entry without '=' prints a warning, sets errno to EFAULT and returns -1; each other entry is inserted with __setenv(name, namelen, value, 1) and a -1 return from __setenv is returned as -1 (errno as set by __setenv). A failure leaves the merge partially done. It returns 0 after a complete walk. The function modifies origEnviron and the internal table and reads environ, intEnviron and envActive.

functions.name: __libc_system
functions.prose_contract: Implements system(3): runs command with /bin/sh -c and returns the wait status of the child, or -1. If command is NULL it only tests whether _PATH_BSHELL is executable by the caller (eaccess with X_OK) and returns 1 if so and 0 otherwise, without forking or touching signals. Otherwise, with a spin lock held when the process is threaded, it counts concurrent callers; the first caller sets SIGINT and SIGQUIT to ignore (saving the old actions in static variables), and every caller blocks SIGCHLD, remembering the previous mask. It then forks. If fork fails it saves errno and the return value stays -1. In the child it restores the saved SIGINT/SIGQUIT actions and the saved signal mask and calls _execve on the shell, calling _exit(127) if the exec fails, so a failed exec is seen by the parent as an exit status of 127 inside the wait status. In the parent it calls _wait4 for the child, retrying on EINTR; any other wait4 error saves errno and leaves the return value -1, otherwise the return value is the wait status. Afterwards, under the lock, the last of the concurrent callers restores the saved SIGINT and SIGQUIT actions (an earlier finisher leaves them ignored), and a caller unblocks SIGCHLD only if SIGCHLD was not blocked in the mask it saw when it started. If a fork or wait4 error was saved it sets errno to it before returning the status.

functions.name: MKREFFUNC(name, type)
functions.prose_contract: Test-local macro (defined in stdc_count_ones_test.c and expanded by the stdbit test kernel with the names and unsigned types unsigned char, unsigned short, unsigned int, unsigned long and unsigned long long) that generates a static reference function "static unsigned name(type value)" for stdc_count_ones. Otherwise it builds a mask bit holding the most significant bit of the type by shifting a 1 left until the next shift (cast back to the type) would be 0, then moves the mask right one step at a time, counting from 1, until bit & value is non-zero, and returns that count: the 1-based position of the highest set bit counted from the most significant end. It has no side effects.

functions.name: do_values_test
functions.prose_contract: Test helper taking a writable byte array buf with writable bytes at buf[-1] and buf[len] (so buf must have one byte of slack on each side), the length len, an index i and a character value c; it returns nothing and the caller keeps ownership of buf. It stores c (converted to unsigned char) in the two sentinel bytes buf[-1] and buf[len], fills buf[0..len-1] with c + 1 (converted to unsigned char by memset, so it wraps for c = 255), and if i < len stores c at buf[i] and records a check failure (ATF_CHECK_EQ, which does not abort) unless memrchr_fn(buf, c, len) returns buf + i; if i >= len it records a check failure unless the result is NULL. Nothing is restored afterwards: the sentinels and fill remain in buf.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(badparent, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function badparent_body(tc), the body of an ATF test of cpuset parent assignment; it returns nothing. skip_ltncpu(2, &mask) obtains the CPU mask (the test is skipped on a machine with fewer than two CPUs). It records the calling thread's current cpuset id (origsetid), creates a new cpuset with cpuset(&setid) (which becomes the thread's set), clears the first CPU of the mask, sets the thread's affinity to that reduced mask, then sets the process's cpuset id back to origsetid with cpuset_setid and reads the thread's cpuset id again as finalsetid. Each of these calls must return 0 (ATF_REQUIRE_EQ), and finally finalsetid must equal origsetid; any failure fails the test.

functions.name: token
functions.prose_contract: Reads the next token from the static stream cfile (a netrc-style file) into the static 100-byte buffer tokval and returns a code. It returns 0 immediately, without touching tokval, if feof(cfile) or ferror(cfile) is true on entry. It skips newline, tab, space and comma characters; reaching end of file while skipping returns 0 (tokval untouched). If the first character is '"' it reads up to the closing quote or end of file, otherwise it takes that character and reads up to the next newline, tab, space, comma or end of file; in both forms a backslash makes the following character be taken literally (in the unquoted form not for the first character, which is stored as is), and end of file after a started token still gives a token. It NUL-terminates tokval with no check against its 100-byte size, so a longer token overruns the buffer. If the token is empty (an empty quoted string) it returns 0 with tokval[0] == 0. Otherwise it compares tokval against the table (default 1 DEFAULT, login 2 LOGIN, password and passwd 3 PASSWD, account 4 ACCOUNT, machine 11 MACH, macdef 5 MACDEF) and returns the matching code, or ID (10) for any other token.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(md5, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function md5_body(tc), the body of the ATF test case for the MD5 password hash; it returns nothing. It calls crypt("0.s0.l33t", "$1$deadbeef$0Huu6KHrKLVWfqa4WljDE0"), using the full expected hash as the setting, and records a non-fatal failure (ATF_CHECK_STREQ) if the returned string differs from "$1$deadbeef$0Huu6KHrKLVWfqa4WljDE0". The crypt result is not checked for NULL beforehand.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(invalid, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function invalid_body(tc), the body of the ATF test case checking that a wrong hash does not verify; it returns nothing. It calls crypt("0.s0.l33t", "$1$cafebabe$0Huu6KHrKLVWfqa4WljDE0") and records a non-fatal failure (ATF_CHECK) if strcmp of the returned string and that setting string is zero; a NULL result from crypt would be passed to strcmp unchecked.

functions.name: TEST_P(DevNameTest, TestDevname)
functions.prose_contract: Generated gtest method DevNameTest_TestDevname_Test::TestBody() for the parameterised fixture DevNameTest; it returns nothing. It copies the current DevNameTestParams, builds a string from its evs field, sets the fixture member m_ev to Event::CreateEvent(*m_factory, that string) (m_factory was created by the fixture's SetUp; the result is dereferenced without a NULL check), calls m_ev->DevName(devname) to fill a local string, and records a non-fatal failure (EXPECT_STREQ) if the string differs from the parameter's devname. The fixture's TearDown later deletes m_ev (if non-null) and m_factory.

functions.name: TEST_P(DevNameTest, TestIsDiskDev)
functions.prose_contract: Generated gtest method DevNameTest_TestIsDiskDev_Test::TestBody() for the parameterised fixture DevNameTest; it returns nothing. It copies the current DevNameTestParams, builds a string from its evs field, sets the fixture member m_ev to Event::CreateEvent(*m_factory, that string) (the result is dereferenced without a NULL check) and records a non-fatal failure (EXPECT_EQ) if m_ev->IsDiskDev() differs from the parameter's is_disk. The fixture's TearDown deletes m_ev (if non-null) and m_factory afterwards.

functions.name: parse_dialogrc
functions.prose_contract: Loads the dialog(1) configuration file into the library's globals; it takes no arguments. If the environment variable named by ENV_DIALOGRC is set and non-empty, the path is that value (truncated to PATH_MAX). Otherwise, if ENV_HOME is set, the path is its value, followed (only when the value is non-empty, shorter than PATH_MAX - 1 and does not end in '/') by a '/', and then by DIALOGRC if room remains; an empty HOME gives a path that is just DIALOGRC with no leading slash. If neither variable provides a path it sets errno to ENOENT and returns -1 immediately, without changing use_shadow, use_colors or gauge_color. Otherwise it calls parse_config(dialogrc_config, path, NULL, FIGPAR_BREAK_ON_EQUALS) and keeps its result res; whether or not that call succeeded, it then sets use_shadow and use_colors from the boolean values and copies the gauge_color string value (into the STR_BUFSIZE buffer with snprintf) from dialogrc_config_option's entries, which hold defaults for options not found in the file, and returns res (the result of parse_config).

functions.name: DevPathFromTextDns
functions.prose_contract: Builds a DNS messaging device-path node from TextDeviceNode, a NUL-terminated CHAR16 string of comma-separated server addresses, and returns it, or returns NULL. It first duplicates the string (NULL if that fails) and counts the comma-separated tokens by walking the copy with GetNextParamStr, then frees the copy; if the count is 0 it returns NULL. It allocates a node of length sizeof(EFI_DEVICE_PATH_PROTOCOL) + sizeof(UINT8) + count * sizeof(EFI_IP_ADDRESS) with CreateDeviceNode (NULL if that fails). It scans the original TextDeviceNode for the first '.' or ':' to set IsIPv6 to 0x00 or 0x01 (left as CreateDeviceNode set it when neither character appears). It then calls GetNextParamStr on TextDeviceNode itself for each address, which overwrites each separating comma in the caller's string with a NUL and advances the local pointer, and parses each token with StrToIpv4Address (IPv4 case) or StrToIpv6Address (IPv6 case) into the matching DnsServerIp entry; the parse return values are ignored. It returns the new node. The caller's string is therefore modified (commas become NUL) in the final loop, not read-only.

functions.name: fetch_socks5_init
functions.prose_contract: Performs the SOCKS5 handshake on the open connection conn to ask the proxy to connect to host:port, returning 1 on success and 0 on failure. It logs the request, sends a 3-byte greeting (SOCKS_VERSION_5, SOCKS_CONNECTION, SOCKS_RSV) with fetch_write (failure code SOCKS5_ERR_SELECTION unless exactly 3 bytes were written), reads 2 bytes with fetch_read (SOCKS5_ERR_READ_METHOD unless exactly 2 were read), requires the first byte to be SOCKS_VERSION_5 (SOCKS5_ERR_VER5_ONLY), then fails with SOCKS5_ERR_NOMETHODS if the second byte is SOCKS_NOMETHODS and with SOCKS5_ERR_NOTIMPLEMENTED if it is anything other than SOCKS5_NOTIMPLEMENTED. It then builds the request in the local buffer (version, connect command, reserved byte, address type domain name, the host length byte, the host bytes, and the port in network byte order); a host longer than FQDN_SIZE gives SOCKS5_ERR_HOSTNAME_SIZE (this is an error path, not a precondition), and a write that does not send the whole request gives SOCKS5_ERR_REQUEST. It reads the reply into the BUFF_SIZE buffer and only treats a return of 0 as a failure (SOCKS5_ERR_REPLY); a -1 from fetch_read is not caught, and the buffer's contents are then examined as they are. The first reply byte must be SOCKS_VERSION_5 (otherwise SOCKS5_ERR_NON_VER5_RESP) and the second selects the result: SOCKS_SUCCESS continues, and the other documented status codes and any unknown status each map to a SOCKS5_ERR_* code. Every failure path calls socks5_seterr with the code and returns 0; the success path returns ret, which is 1. The verbose parameter is not used in the function body.

functions.name: hbsdctrl_feature_prohibit_ptrace_capsicum_apply
functions.prose_contract: Stores the requested state of the "prohibit ptrace on Capsicum processes" feature in two extended attributes on the file descriptor *arg1, and returns RES_SUCCESS or RES_FAIL. arg1 points to an int descriptor and arg2 to the feature state; the function returns RES_FAIL immediately if either is NULL, if the descriptor is negative, or if the state's value is not valid. Otherwise it writes a 2-byte buffer whose first byte is '1' if the value is HBSDCTRL_STATE_ENABLED and '0' otherwise to the ATTRNAME_ENABLED attribute in ctx->hc_namespace; if extattr_set_fd does not return 2 it returns RES_FAIL and does not write the second attribute. It then writes the buffer with first byte '1' if the value is HBSDCTRL_STATE_DISABLED and '0' otherwise to ATTRNAME_DISABLED; a result other than 2 returns RES_FAIL after the first attribute was already written. Only the first byte of the buffer is ever set (the second byte is left uninitialised and is written too). On success it sets HBSDCTRL_FEATURE_STATE_FLAG_PERSISTED on the state and returns RES_SUCCESS; the flag is not set on any failure path.

functions.name: hbsdctrl_feature_prohibit_ptrace_capsicum_get
functions.prose_contract: Reads the stored state of the "prohibit ptrace on Capsicum processes" feature from two extended attributes on the file descriptor *arg1 into the state *arg2, and returns RES_SUCCESS or RES_FAIL. It returns RES_FAIL at once if arg1 or arg2 is NULL (there is no check of the descriptor value). It first sets the state value to HBSDCTRL_STATE_SYSDEF. It queries the size of ATTRNAME_ENABLED; if the size is not positive it returns RES_SUCCESS when errno is ENOATTR (nothing stored, the value stays SYSDEF) and RES_FAIL otherwise. Having found the attribute it sets the PERSISTED flag, and returns RES_FAIL with the value INVALID if its size exceeds 2. It reads the attribute into a calloc'd buffer (RES_FAIL if calloc fails, leaving the value SYSDEF; value INVALID and RES_FAIL if the read fails) and takes enabled = (first byte == '1'). It then does the same for ATTRNAME_DISABLED, except that a size of zero or less, a size over 2, or a failed read all give value INVALID and RES_FAIL (a calloc failure gives RES_FAIL without changing the value), and takes disabled = (first byte == '1'). If both enabled and disabled are true the value becomes INVALID and it returns RES_FAIL; otherwise the value becomes ENABLED if enabled and DISABLED if not (also when neither flag was '1'), and it returns RES_SUCCESS. The buffers are freed on each path after allocation.

functions.name: _citrus_EUC_mbrtowc_priv
functions.prose_contract: Restartable conversion of one EUC multibyte character from *s (n bytes available) to a wide character, using the partial-character state psenc; it returns 0 or EILSEQ and reports the byte count or status through *nresult. If *s is NULL it re-initialises psenc with _citrus_EUC_init_state, sets *nresult to 0 and returns 0 without writing *pwc. Otherwise it remembers the previous psenc->chlen, and when no byte is buffered it takes the first byte from the input (if n is 0 it goes to the restart exit); a buffered chlen of 1 or 2 continues; any other chlen is an encoding error. The code set is taken from the first byte and the character length c from ei->count (c == 0 is an encoding error). It then appends bytes from the input until chlen reaches c; if the input runs out it takes the restart exit, which sets *nresult to (size_t)-2, stores the advanced pointer into *s and returns 0, leaving the partial bytes in psenc. When the character is complete it sets *s to the advanced pointer, assembles the wide character (skipping the leading SS2/SS3 byte for code sets 2 and 3), masks it with ei->mask and ei->bits[cs], clears psenc->chlen, writes *pwc when pwc is non-NULL, sets *nresult to the number of bytes consumed in this call for the character (c minus the previously buffered length), or to 0 when the wide character is zero, and returns 0. The encoding-error exit clears psenc->chlen, sets *nresult to (size_t)-1, returns EILSEQ and does not update *s.

functions.name: _ISO2022_sgetwchar
functions.prose_contract: Reads one character from the n bytes at string in an ISO-2022 stream, updating the shift state in psenc, and returns either the decoded wchar_t or _ISO2022INVALID, setting *result (if result is non-NULL) to the position after what it consumed on most returns; ei is unused. It first loops over control sequences, consuming each and continuing: SI/SO set psenc->gl to 0 or 1; the single-shift bytes 0x8e/0x8f set both singlegl and singlegr; a complete escape sequence found in seqtable that designates a character set stores the set's type, final, intermediate and version bytes in psenc->g[i] (an unexpected table type returns _ISO2022INVALID without setting *result); ESC n/o set gl to 2 or 3, ESC ~ } | set gr, ESC N/O set singlegl. A non-ESC byte ends the loop; an unrecognised or incomplete escape sequence ends the loop too, except that a prefix of a known sequence that is the whole remaining input returns _ISO2022INVALID with *result = string (more input needed). With no input left (n < 1) it returns _ISO2022INVALID with *result = string. A control character (iscntl) is returned as is (masked to 0xff), as is any byte for which the selected set is -1; the set is gr (or singlegr) for bytes with the high bit and gl (or singlegl) otherwise. For multibyte sets it returns _ISO2022INVALID with *result = string if fewer than 2 (or 3, when the final byte says three-byte) bytes remain or when the bytes do not all have the same high bit; for single-byte sets if no byte remains. A byte (or byte pair) outside the 94 or 96 range is returned as is, one byte consumed. Otherwise it assembles the wide character from the set's final byte, intermediate byte and the character bytes (special cases for ASCII ('B' with no intermediate) and ISO-8859-1 ('A' with no intermediate)), consumes 1 to 3 bytes, and returns it. In every path that returns a decoded character (as is or assembled) singlegl and singlegr are reset to -1.

functions.name: ifconfig_{*name*}_display(enum {*name*} v)
functions.prose_contract: Function template (in a Lua-processed template, instantiated by sfp.lua once per SFP enum named sfp_<name> whose last value has a display string) that generates ifconfig_<name>_display(enum sfp_<name> v). The generated function looks up v in the enum's metadata table with find_metadata, which scans the table entries until one has value v or the NULL-symbol terminator, and returns NULL if no entry has that value. If an entry is found it returns that entry's display field, a pointer to a static string, or NULL if that entry has no display string (the field is left NULL by the designated initialisers). The returned string must not be freed.

functions.name: _kvm_open
functions.prose_contract: Common open routine for kvm_open and friends: initialises the caller-allocated kd, opens the memory and kernel files, and returns kd on success or NULL on failure (after kvm_close). It sets vmfd, pmfd and nlfd to -1 and vmst, procbase, argspc and argv to NULL; it does not initialise the other fields (arch, rawdump, writable, resolve_symbol and the like), which must already be zero or set by the caller. If uf is NULL it uses getbootfile(); an exec file name of MAXPATHLEN or more characters fails with an error. A flag with bits other than O_RDWR fails with "bad flags arg". The memory file mf defaults to _PATH_MEM; it is opened (with flag | O_CLOEXEC) into pmfd, fstat'ed, and an empty regular file fails with EINVAL. If mf is a character device named _PATH_DEVNULL it opens /dev/null read-only into vmfd (the result is not checked, so vmfd may be -1) and returns kd immediately, and if it is _PATH_MEM it opens _PATH_KMEM into vmfd (failure goes to failed) and returns kd immediately; in both early returns nlfd stays -1 and the ELF header read, architecture probe, resolver check and ka_initvtop are skipped. Otherwise it opens uf into nlfd, calls _kvm_read_kernel_ehdr, sets rawdump and writable when mf starts with _PATH_FWMEM or _PATH_DEVVMM, probes the registered kvm_arch entries with ka_probe to set kd->arch (failure: "unsupported architecture"), fails with "non-native kernel requires a symbol resolver" for a non-native architecture without kd->resolve_symbol, calls ka_initvtop (failure goes to failed) and returns kd. At failed it copies the error buffer to errout (up to _POSIX2_LINE_MAX) when errout is non-NULL, calls kvm_close(kd) and returns NULL.

functions.name: memstat_malloc_zone_used
functions.prose_contract: Reports whether the malloc size class n is marked in the type's size mask: it returns 1 if memstat_get_sizemask(mtp) & (1 << n) is non-zero and 0 otherwise. memstat_get_sizemask returns the 64-bit field mt_sizemask of *mtp (which must be a valid struct memory_type). The shift is done on a plain int constant 1, so the expression is only well defined for n from 0 to 30 (n = 31 shifts into the sign bit, and n >= 32 is undefined), which means the upper 32 bits of the 64-bit mask cannot be tested correctly. It allocates, frees and locks nothing and modifies no state.

functions.name: _pam_exec
functions.prose_contract: Runs the program argv[0] (with arguments argv, argc >= 1) for PAM service function func with the options in *options, collects its output, and returns a PAM error code. Returns PAM_SERVICE_ERR if argc < 1, if the child is killed by a signal, or if the wait status is neither a signal nor a normal exit; PAM_BUF_ERR if reallocarray of the environment list, asprintf or strdup fails; PAM_SYSTEM_ERR if a pipe, fcntl, open of /dev/null, authentication-token fetch, pdfork, poll, read, write (other than EAGAIN) or waitpid (other than EINTR) call fails; otherwise, after a normal exit, the child's raw exit status when return_prog_exit_status is set, or PAM_SUCCESS for exit status 0 and PAM_PERM_DENIED for any other status. It builds the child's environment from pam_getenvlist plus the PAM items, PAM_SM_FUNC and (with return_prog_exit_status) the PAM error-code names; when expose_authtok is set it fetches the authentication token (from the stored item with use_first_pass or in pam_sm_setcred, else with pam_get_authtok) and feeds it to the child through a non-blocking stdin pipe; stdout and stderr go either to pipes (capture_stdout, capture_stderr) whose output is read and passed to pam_prompt as info or error messages, or to /dev/null. It forks with pdfork; the child sets up its descriptors and calls execve, calling _exit(1) if any step fails. The parent closes the child-side pipe ends, polls the process descriptor and the pipes until the process descriptor reports an event, then waits for the child. The cleanup at out preserves errno, closes pd and every pipe descriptor that is still >= 0, frees the environment list and returns pam_err. The descriptors chin[0], chout[1] and cherr[1] are closed after the fork but not reset to -1, so the cleanup closes them a second time (and the cleanup tests cherr[0] but closes cherr[1], so cherr[1] is closed twice when capture_stderr is set and is not closed at all on a failure before the fork when capture_stderr is not set).

functions.name: pam_sm_authenticate
functions.prose_contract: PAM authentication entry point for the Kerberos 5 module: it authenticates the PAM user against the KDC and, on success, stores the credentials in a new in-memory ccache whose name it registers with pam_set_data under "ccache"; it returns PAM_SUCCESS or a PAM error code. It returns pam_get_user's or pam_get_item's (PAM_RUSER) error code immediately if they fail. It then duplicates the service name (PAM_BUF_ERR on failure), initialises the Kerberos context (PAM_SERVICE_ERR on failure), calls verify_krb_v5_tgt_begin (a failure is PAM_SERVICE_ERR unless the allow_kdc_spoof option is set), registers the memory ccache type (an error other than KRB5_CC_TYPE_EXISTS is PAM_SERVICE_ERR), builds the principal (user, or ruser/user with the auth_as_self option; the asprintf and strdup results are not checked for NULL) and parses and unparses it (PAM_SERVICE_ERR on failure). It obtains the password with pam_get_authtok (returning its error code); unless no_user_check is set, a user name containing '@' is mapped to a local name with krb5_aname_to_localname (PAM_USER_UNKNOWN on failure) and stored with pam_set_item, and getpwnam must find the user (PAM_USER_UNKNOWN otherwise). It then allocates credential options (PAM_SERVICE_ERR on failure), sets the forwardable flag if requested, and calls krb5_get_init_creds_password (PAM_AUTH_ERR on failure). With the TGT it creates a unique memory ccache, initialises it and stores the credentials (PAM_SERVICE_ERR on failure), runs verify_krb_v5_tgt (PAM_AUTH_ERR if it returns -1, destroying the ccache), returns PAM_AUTH_ERR (destroying the ccache) if a "ccache" item already exists in the PAM handle, builds the name "type:name" with asprintf (PAM_BUF_ERR if NULL) and registers it with pam_set_data using cleanup_cache (PAM_SERVICE_ERR on failure, destroying the ccache); on success ownership of the name string passes to the PAM framework. The cleanup labels free the credential contents (only on paths after get_init_creds), the principals, the context, the verify state and the duplicated service name, and a non-success result logs a message.

functions.name: pam_sm_authenticate
functions.prose_contract: PAM authentication entry point that authenticates the user with a TACACS+ server and returns a PAM error code. It reads the conf and template_user options, opens a TACACS+ handle with tac_open, reads the configuration with tac_config and creates a login authentication request (each failure logs, closes the handle where one was opened, and returns PAM_SERVICE_ERR). It then passes PAM_USER, PAM_TTY and PAM_RHOST to the server through do_item, which returns the error code of pam_get_item if that fails (in this case the handle is not closed by do_item or by this function, so it leaks) and, when the item is set and the corresponding tac_set_* call fails, closes the handle and returns PAM_SERVICE_ERR; a non-success value from do_item is returned immediately. In the loop it calls tac_send_authen (on -1 it closes the handle and returns PAM_AUTHINFO_UNAVAIL), sets the echo option from the reply flags, and handles the status: PASS closes the handle and returns PAM_SUCCESS, after first, when template_user is set and pam_get_item(PAM_USER) succeeds, replacing PAM_USER by template_user if getpwnam does not find the user (an error from pam_get_item is returned after the close); FAIL closes the handle and returns PAM_AUTH_ERR; GETUSER and GETPASS fetch the server message (NULL gives PAM_SERVICE_ERR without closing the handle), obtain the user or password through pam_get_user or pam_get_authtok (an error closes the handle and is returned) and send it with set_msg (a failure returns PAM_SERVICE_ERR without closing the handle); GETDATA prompts with pam_prompt (error closes the handle and is returned) and sends the answer (set_msg failure returns PAM_SERVICE_ERR without closing); ERROR, RESTART, FOLLOW and any other status log, close the handle and return PAM_AUTHINFO_UNAVAIL. The loop repeats for the statuses that continue.

functions.name: pam_sm_chauthtok
functions.prose_contract: PAM password-change entry point for pam_unix: flags selects the preliminary check (PAM_PRELIM_CHECK, tested first) or the actual update (PAM_UPDATE_AUTHTOK); it returns a PAM code. The user is getlogin() when the auth_as_self option is set (the result is not checked for NULL) and otherwise comes from pam_get_user (its error is returned). If getpwnam does not find the user it returns PAM_AUTHTOK_RECOVERY_ERR. Preliminary round: for uid 0 and a user from the local files (or, with YP, from NIS when ypclnt_havepasswdd reports a password daemon; failures are PAM_BUF_ERR or PAM_SERVICE_ERR) it returns the result of setting PAM_OLDAUTHTOK to "" without checking any old password. Otherwise the old password is "" if the stored hash is empty and the nullok option is set, or comes from pam_get_authtok(PAM_OLDAUTHTOK) (its error is returned); it then returns PAM_PERM_DENIED if the old password is empty and nullok is not set, or if crypt(old, stored hash) differs from the stored hash (so an empty old password only passes when the stored hash is empty too, and the crypt result is not checked for NULL), and otherwise returns PAM_SUCCESS (the pam_get_authtok result). Update round: it gets the old password (error returned) and the new password with pam_get_authtok, repeating while the result is PAM_TRY_AGAIN (other errors returned); a non-root caller with an empty new password and no nullok gets PAM_PERM_DENIED; pw_dup failure gives PAM_BUF_ERR. It sets the crypt format from the login class, sets pw_change from the passwordtime capability, creates a salt and encrypts the new password; for a files-sourced user it runs pw_init, pw_lock, pw_tmp, pw_copy and pw_mkdb, returning PAM_SUCCESS only if all succeed and PAM_SERVICE_ERR otherwise (pw_fini always runs); with YP a NIS-sourced user is changed through ypclnt_passwd (PAM_BUF_ERR, PAM_SERVICE_ERR or PAM_SUCCESS), and any other source gives PAM_SERVICE_ERR. With any other flags it returns PAM_ABORT.

functions.name: get_args
functions.prose_contract: Reads the argument or environment strings of a core-dump process, located through the ps_strings structure at psstrings, and returns a buffer of the strings each followed by a NUL, with *lenp set to the number of bytes stored; type must be PSC_TYPE_ARGV or PSC_TYPE_ENVV (asserted). If args is non-NULL it is the caller's buffer and *lenp must be at least 1 (the capacity is the smaller of ARG_MAX and *lenp); if args is NULL it allocates an ARG_MAX-byte buffer, which the caller must free. It returns NULL, leaving *lenp unchanged, if reading ps_strings fails, if the address or the string count of the selected array is 0, if the count exceeds ARG_MAX (after a warning), or if allocating the temporary pointer array fails. It then reads the pointer array (failure goes to the fail exit) and, if it must allocate the buffer, allocates it (failure goes to the fail exit). For each string pointer it stops at the end of the array or at a NULL pointer, and reads the string in chunks of up to ARGS_CHUNK_SZ bytes, leaving one byte of the capacity spare; the number of bytes asked for in each chunk is treated as valid data (the byte count returned by core_read_mem is only compared with -1, so a short read leaves unread bytes in the length scan), and the string ends at the first NUL within the chunk, which is replaced by a stored NUL. If the capacity is exhausted it stops without terminating the last string. At the normal exit it sets *lenp to the bytes stored and returns the buffer (the caller's or the allocated one). At the fail exit (a failed pointer-array read, a failed buffer allocation or a failed core_read_mem in the loop, which returns -1) it frees the allocated buffer, if any, sets *lenp to the bytes stored so far (0 for the first two) and returns NULL. The temporary pointer array is freed on both exits.

functions.name: check_and_init_rwlock
functions.prose_contract: Resolves the pthread_rwlock_t stored at *rwlock into the actual lock object and stores it in *rwlock_out, returning 0 or an error code. If *rwlock is THR_PSHARED_PTR or is at most THR_RWLOCK_DESTROYED (that is, the static initialiser NULL, the destroyed marker 1, or any other value up to it) it returns the result of init_rwlock(rwlock, rwlock_out); otherwise it stores *rwlock in *rwlock_out and returns 0. In the init_rwlock case the possible errors are EINVAL (process-shared lock whose off-page cannot be found, or a destroyed lock) and ENOMEM (allocation failure while initialising a statically initialised lock); *rwlock_out is only written on a return of 0.

functions.name: init_rwlock
functions.prose_contract: Resolves *rwlock into the actual lock object, performing lazy static initialisation, stores it in *rwlock_out and returns 0, or returns an error and leaves *rwlock_out unchanged. If *rwlock is THR_PSHARED_PTR it looks up the process-shared off-page lock with __thr_pshared_offpage(rwlock, 0) and returns EINVAL if there is none. Otherwise, if *rwlock is at most THR_RWLOCK_DESTROYED: for the static initialiser (NULL) it calls init_static for the current thread, which takes the static-init lock and, if the lock is still uninitialised, allocates and zeroes a lock structure with rwlock_init (NULL attributes), returning ENOMEM if the allocation fails (EFAULT cannot occur on this path), and the error is returned; for THR_RWLOCK_DESTROYED it returns EINVAL; any other small value falls through unchanged; the lock used is then the re-read *rwlock. For any other value it is used as is. It then stores the lock in *rwlock_out and returns 0.

functions.name: rwlock_rdlock_common
functions.prose_contract: Acquires a read lock on *rwlock for the calling thread, optionally waiting until the absolute time abstime (NULL means no timeout), and returns 0 or an error code. It first resolves the lock with check_and_init_rwlock and returns its error (EINVAL for a destroyed lock or an unmappable process-shared lock, ENOMEM when static initialisation fails). If the thread already holds read locks (curthread->rdlock_count non-zero) it requests URWLOCK_PREFER_READER so a recursive read lock cannot deadlock behind a waiting writer. It tries _thr_rwlock_tryrdlock; on success it increments rdlock_count and returns 0. Only if that fails does it check abstime and return EINVAL if tv_nsec is 1000000000 or more or negative. It then loops on __thr_rwlock_rdlock(lock, flags, abstime) in the kernel, retrying in user space with another trylock when the call returns EINTR (so EINTR is not returned); any other result ends the loop. On a return of 0 it increments rdlock_count; any other result (for example ETIMEDOUT or EAGAIN from __thr_rwlock_rdlock) is returned with rdlock_count unchanged.

functions.name: _Tthr_rwlock_rdlock
functions.prose_contract: Implements the read-lock operation without a timeout (the pthread_rwlock_rdlock entry): it calls _thr_check_init() and returns rwlock_rdlock_common(rwlock, NULL). It therefore returns 0 with the calling thread holding a read lock and its rdlock_count incremented, or the error from rwlock_rdlock_common: EINVAL (destroyed lock or unmappable process-shared lock), ENOMEM (static initialisation failed) or an error from the blocking read-lock call such as EAGAIN; no lock is taken on an error return. EFAULT cannot come from static initialisation.

functions.name: _pthread_rwlock_timedrdlock
functions.prose_contract: Implements pthread_rwlock_timedrdlock: it calls _thr_check_init() and returns rwlock_rdlock_common(rwlock, abstime), the absolute-time variant of the read lock. It returns 0 with a read lock held and the thread's rdlock_count incremented, or an error with no lock taken: EINVAL (destroyed lock, unmappable process-shared lock, or an abstime whose tv_nsec is out of range, checked only when the immediate trylock failed), ENOMEM (static initialisation failed), or an error from the blocking call such as ETIMEDOUT or EAGAIN. EFAULT cannot come from static initialisation.

functions.name: _pthread_suspend_np
functions.prose_contract: Suspends the thread given by handle thread, waiting until it is suspended, and returns 0 or an error code. If thread is the calling thread it returns EDEADLK without touching it. Otherwise it takes a reference on the target with _thr_ref_add(curthread, thread, 0) and returns that call's error code if it fails (no reference taken, no signal sent). When the reference is obtained it locks the thread and calls suspend_common(curthread, thread, 1), then unlocks it, drops the reference with _thr_ref_delete and returns 0 (the result of suspend_common is not used). suspend_common loops while the target is not PS_DEAD and not yet marked THR_FLAGS_SUSPENDED: it sets THR_FLAGS_NEED_SUSPEND on the target and, if the target's tid is TID_TERMINATED, returns at once with the flag set and no signal; otherwise it records the thread's cycle counter, sends SIGCANCEL, drops the thread lock, waits on the cycle counter in _thr_umtx_wait_uint (waitok is 1), retakes the lock and re-tests. Hence on a return of 0 the target is either dead, marked suspended, or has THR_FLAGS_NEED_SUSPEND set while its tid is TID_TERMINATED, and no signal is sent in the dead, already-suspended and TID_TERMINATED cases.

functions.name: pt_dbsuspend
functions.prose_contract: Suspends (suspend non-zero) or resumes (suspend zero) the debuggee thread described by th and returns a td_err_e code (P2T converts proc_service errors). It returns pt_validate's error if validation fails. For a thread mapped as a raw LWP (type PT_LWP) it returns P2T of ps_lstop or ps_lcontinue on that lwp and does nothing else. Otherwise it reads the thread's attribute flags, TCB address and the mailbox's tm_lwp from the target with ps_pread, returning P2T of the first failing read. Only when the lwp is non-zero: if attrflags has bit 0x200 set it returns 0 immediately (without touching the mailbox dflags); for a system-scope thread (PTHREAD_SCOPE_SYSTEM) it reads the KSE lock level (and the thread's lock level if the KSE's is not positive) and stops the lwp only when suspending and the lock level is not positive, or continues it when resuming (a failing read or stop/continue returns P2T of the error); for other threads it calls ps_linfo (TD_ERR on failure) and stops the lwp when suspending unless PL_FLAG_BOUND is set in the info, or continues it when resuming (errors returned as P2T). With lwp zero none of that is done. It then reads tm_dflags, sets TMDF_SUSPEND when suspending or clears it when resuming, writes it back and returns P2T of the ps_pwrite result.

functions.name: libusb20_dev_get_port_path
functions.prose_contract: Copies the USB port path of device pdev into the caller's buffer buf (bufsize bytes) and returns the number of bytes written, or LIBUSB20_ERROR_OVERFLOW if the buffer is too small. If pdev->port_level is 0 (a backend without a port path) it returns LIBUSB20_ERROR_OVERFLOW when bufsize < 2 (buf untouched); otherwise it stores the parent address in buf[0] and the parent port in buf[1] and returns 2. If port_level is greater than bufsize it returns LIBUSB20_ERROR_OVERFLOW without writing. Otherwise it copies port_level bytes of pdev->port_path into buf and returns port_level.

functions.name: libusb20_desc_foreach
functions.prose_contract: Safely walks a block of USB descriptors described by pdesc (start pointer ptr and length len): given the current descriptor psubdesc (or NULL to begin) it returns a pointer to the next descriptor, or NULL at the end or when the data is inconsistent. It returns NULL if pdesc is NULL. The candidate is the start of the block when psubdesc is NULL, otherwise psubdesc plus its first byte (its length), which is read before any range check. It returns NULL if the candidate lies outside [start, start + len), if the address of the descriptor after it (candidate plus its own first byte) lies outside [start, start + len] (it may equal the end), or if the candidate's first byte is below 3. Otherwise it returns the candidate. It writes nothing; apart from the first byte of psubdesc it reads only the first byte of the candidate, after the range test.

functions.name: hid_get_item
functions.prose_contract: Returns the next HID item of parser state s in *h, skipping items that do not belong to the selected report, and returns the result of hid_get_item_raw. It loops: each iteration calls hid_get_item_raw(s, h) and leaves the loop as soon as that result r is zero or negative, or s->reportid is -1 (no report selected), or the item's h->report_ID equals s->reportid; otherwise it discards the item and reads the next one. It returns r. In hid_get_item_raw (213-513) the only return values are 1, when an item has been stored, and 0 at the end of data, for a NULL s, for an invalid end collection, or for an invalid push/pop; so hid_get_item returns 1 for a stored item that matches the selected report (or when no report is selected) and 0 otherwise. s->reportid is only dereferenced after r > 0, so a NULL s (for which the raw function returns 0) is not dereferenced here.

functions.name: vcpu_reset
functions.prose_contract: Sets the guest register and descriptor state of virtual CPU vcpu to the x86 power-on reset values using vm_set_register and vm_set_desc, in this order, and returns 0 if every call succeeded; at the first call that returns a non-zero error it stops and returns that error, leaving the earlier registers already written. The values are: RFLAGS 0x2, RIP 0xfff0, CR0 = CR0_NE (not the architectural reset value, as the code comment explains), CR2, CR3 and CR4 zero; CS with base 0xffff0000, limit 0xffff, access 0x0093 and selector 0xf000; SS, DS, ES, FS and GS with base 0, limit 0xffff, access 0x0093 and selector 0; EFER, RAX, RBX, RCX, RSI, RDI, RBP, RSP and R8 to R15 zero and RDX 0xf00; GDTR and IDTR with base 0, limit 0xffff and access 0; TR with base 0, limit 0, access 0x8b and selector 0; LDTR with base 0, limit 0xffff, access 0x82 and selector 0; DR6 0xffff0ff0, DR7 0x400 and the interrupt shadow 0.

functions.name: yppasswd_remote
functions.prose_contract: Asks the NIS password daemon rpc.yppasswdd on ypclnt->server to change the password entry described by pwd, using passwd as the old password (an empty string when passwd is NULL), and returns 0 on success or -1 on failure with a message recorded in ypclnt. It builds a local yppasswd request from pwd's uid and gid and strdup'd copies of its name, passwd, gecos, dir and shell and of the old password; if any strdup fails it records the strerror text with ypclnt_error and returns -1. It then connects with clnt_create to the YPPASSWDPROG/YPPASSWDVERS service over UDP (failure records the clnt_spcreateerror text and returns -1), sets default Unix credentials, calls yppasswdproc_update_1 and checks the RPC status: a status other than RPC_SUCCESS records an error and returns -1; a NULL result or a result that is not 0 records "NIS password update failed" and returns -1. When the call succeeded and the result is 0 it clears the ypclnt error (ypclnt_error with NULL) and returns 0. On every exit it destroys the client's credentials and the client when a client was created and frees the copies, zeroing the copied password and old password strings before freeing them.

functions.name: lgammal_r
functions.prose_contract: Computes log|Gamma(x)| for a 128-bit long double x and stores the sign of Gamma(x) in *signgamp. For an infinity or NaN it sets *signgamp to 1 and returns x*x. Otherwise it sets *signgamp to 1 for a non-negative sign bit and -1 for a negative sign bit (so for -0 and tiny negative x it is -1). For |x| below 2^-116 it returns one/vzero, a division by zero giving +Inf, if x is +-0, and -logl(fabsl(x)) otherwise. For negative x it resets *signgamp to 1, returns one/vzero if |x| >= 2^(112) (all such values are integers) or if sin_pil(x) is zero (negative integers), and otherwise computes nadj = logl(pi / fabsl(sin_pil(x) * x)), sets *signgamp to -1 when sin_pil(x) is negative, and replaces x by -x. It then evaluates log Gamma(|x|): 0 for x exactly 1.0 or 2.0 (for negative x these values were already excluded as negative integers); for x below 2 a polynomial approximation selected by range (with -log(x) added below about 0.9); for x below 8 a rational approximation in the fractional part with a logarithm of the product of the omitted factors added; for x below 2^116 an asymptotic expression (x - 1/2) * (log x - 1) + w(1/x^2); and x*(logl(x) - 1) for larger x. For originally negative x it returns nadj - r, otherwise r.

functions.name: powl
functions.prose_contract: Computes x raised to y for 80-bit long doubles, returning a long double. The special cases are tested in this order: y == 0 gives 1.0 (even for a NaN x); x == 1 gives 1.0 (even for a NaN y); a NaN x or y gives nan_mix(x, y); y == 1 gives x; an infinite y with x == -1 gives 1.0 (a NaN y is caught earlier and does not reach this test); y >= LDBL_MAX gives +INFINITY for x > 1 or x < -1 and +0 for 0 < x < 1 or -1 < x < 0; y <= -LDBL_MAX gives +0 for |x| > 1 and +INFINITY for 0 < |x| < 1; x >= LDBL_MAX gives +INFINITY for y > 0 and +0 otherwise; x <= -LDBL_MAX gives -INFINITY or +INFINITY for y > 0 (negative when y is an odd integer) and -0 or +0 for y < 0 (negative when y is an odd integer). For x == 0 with y < 0 it returns +INFINITY (-INFINITY for -0 and odd integer y) and for y > 0 +0 (-0 for -0 and odd integer y). A negative x with a non-integer y gives NaN ((x-x)/(x-x)). An integer y with |y| < 32768 and an integer-valued x is computed with powil. Otherwise it works on |x| (with a sign flag for negative x), splits x into a mantissa and exponent with frexpl, finds a table entry, and computes the result with a log2/exp2 style extended-precision reduction and a polynomial; the result overflows to huge*huge when the exponent exceeds MEXP and underflows to twom10000*twom10000 when it is below MNEXP; for a negative x raised to an odd integer y the result is negated. Cases beyond the listed special values were read only in outline.

functions.name: avdtpACPHandlePacket
functions.prose_contract: Handles one pending AVDTP acceptor-side signalling packet on cfg->hc and returns the handled signal ID (positive), or a negative errno or callee error code. It reads the packet with avdtpGetPacket; if the packet is not a COMMAND it returns -ENXIO without sending a reject. For AVDTP_DISCOVER and AVDTP_GET_CAPABILITIES it sends the matching response (avdtpSendDiscResponseAudio or avdtpSendCapabilitiesResponseSBCForACP) and returns the signal ID, or the response function's non-zero result on failure; these two do not change cfg->acceptor_state. For AVDTP_SET_CONFIGURATION it requires acceptor_state == acpInitial, parses the SEID and the configuration elements, handles an SBC codec element with avdtpParseSBCConfig (a non-zero result is returned directly, without reject), and treats a packet without a usable SBC configuration as an error; otherwise it sends the accept (failure returned), allocates cfg->handle.sbc_enc with malloc if it is NULL (-ENOMEM on failure, after the accept was sent), zeroes it with memset, sets acceptor_state to acpConfigurationSet and returns AVDTP_SET_CONFIGURATION. AVDTP_OPEN needs acpConfigurationSet and moves to acpStreamOpened; AVDTP_START needs acpStreamOpened or acpStreamSuspended and moves to acpStreamStarted; AVDTP_CLOSE needs acpStreamOpened, acpStreamStarted or acpStreamSuspended and moves to acpStreamClosed; AVDTP_SUSPEND needs acpStreamOpened or acpStreamStarted and moves to acpStreamSuspended; each sends an accept first (a failure is returned without changing the state or rejecting) and returns the signal ID. A state that does not permit the signal, and the signals AVDTP_GET_CONFIGURATION, AVDTP_RECONFIGURE, AVDTP_ABORT and any unknown ID, make it send avdtpSendReject and return -ENXIO.

functions.name: bsd_arp_set
functions.prose_contract: Installs or updates a static ARP (link-layer) entry for the IPv4 address *ia with the hardware address eaddr of len bytes via the routing socket, returning 0 on success, -1 if the routing-socket write fails, or 1 for a lookup problem; getsocket() may call exit(1) if the socket cannot be opened. It copies len bytes of eaddr into the static sockaddr_dl's link-level address (len is not checked against its capacity), clears doing_proxy, flags and expire_time, and sets expire_time to now + 20 minutes. It then sends RTM_GET through rtmsg; if that returns a negative value it logs a warning and returns 1. It interprets the reply as a sockaddr_in followed by a sockaddr_dl: if the reply's address equals the target address and the sockaddr_dl has family AF_LINK, the route is not a gateway route (RTF_GATEWAY clear) and its type is IFT_ETHER, IFT_FDDI, IFT_ISO88023, IFT_ISO88024 or IFT_ISO88025, it switches to RTM_CHANGE and goes on; if the address matches but those conditions do not hold and doing_proxy is 0 (always the case here, since doing_proxy was just cleared) it logs "can only proxy" and returns 1; if the reply's address differs from the target it goes on with RTM_ADD. It then returns 1 with a warning if the reply's sockaddr_dl family is not AF_LINK; otherwise it copies the reply's link type and interface index into the message and returns rtmsg(op), which is 0, or -1 when the routing-socket write fails with an error other than ESRCH (or EEXIST for RTM_ADD); rtmsg returns 0 also when the write fails with a tolerated error or when the read of the reply fails (a warning is logged).

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Entry point of getty: it prepares the terminal line named by argv[2] (or the standard input's tty when argv[2] is missing or "-") using the gettytab entry argv[1] (default "default"), prompts for a login name and execs login (or ppplogin); it does not return. It ignores SIGINT and SIGQUIT, sets the host name, installs a SIGXCPU handler that logs and exits with 1, sets a CPU time limit, and reads the default table. If there is no tty argument it uses ttyname(STDIN_FILENO) (exit 1 if that fails); otherwise it takes /dev/<argv[2]>, and unless argv[0] is "+" changes its owner and mode and calls revoke, reads the gettytab entry, and, when an init chat (IC) or answer chat (AC) is configured, opens the tty non-blocking (exit 1 on failure), runs the init chat (exit 1 if it fails), and for the answer chat waits in select for input for up to RT seconds (exit 0 for a timeout, to recycle the tty for init) and then runs the chat (exit 1 on failure); without a chat it opens the tty with opentty (exit 1 on failure). It then loops forever: after an optional delay it sets the tty mode, switches table for autobaud or port selector and continues, prints the clear-screen string, host edit, issue file and banner, and arms the login timeout (a timeout exits with status 1). The login name comes from the auto-login string AL (copied up to the size of name) or from getname() (which exits with 0 if reading the terminal fails or hits end of file, and returns 0 when the line is interrupted, 2 for a PPP frame). If getname returned 2 or both PL and PP are set it lifts the CPU limit and execs the PPP program PP as "ppplogin" with the tty name (exit 1 if the exec fails). Otherwise, for a non-zero rval or an auto-login string, it flushes output, cancels the alarm, restarts the loop on an empty name or on a name beginning with '-' (after printing a message), restarts on a name without letters or digits (for an auto-login name that is an error: it logs and exits 1), applies the tty flags and tcsetattr (exit 1 on failure), builds the environment, lifts the CPU limit and execs login (with -fp for auto-login, -p otherwise), logging and exiting with 1 if the exec fails. If no name was obtained it cancels the alarm, resets the handlers and optionally switches to the table named NX before the next iteration.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Entry point of pppoed, a PPPoE daemon, returning an exit status. Options are -F (stay in the foreground), -P pidfile, -a acname, -d (debug), -e exec, -l label, -n level (netgraph debug level) and -p provider; the provider defaults to "". It returns usage(prog) for an unknown option, for a number of non-option arguments other than one or two, and when both -e and -l are given. With no -e it takes the label as -l or else the provider (which defaults to "", so the "either a provider, a label or an exec command" check cannot fail), and builds exec as the default exec prefix followed by the label in alloca memory (EX_OSERR if alloca returns NULL). With no -a the access-concentrator name is the host name up to the first dot ("localhost" if gethostname fails). It returns EX_UNAVAILABLE if LoadModules() fails (unless NOKLDLOAD), EX_CANTCREAT if NgMkSockNode fails, the non-zero status from ConfigureNode (after closing both sockets), EX_OSERR if daemon(1, 0) fails (unless -F), and EX_CANTCREAT if the pid file cannot be opened for writing (after closing the sockets); otherwise it writes the pid file, opens the log, installs Farewell on SIGHUP, SIGINT, SIGQUIT and SIGTERM, and loops until a signal is recorded: it receives data on the data socket with NgRecvData and, for a positive size, calls Spawn with the received packet; a size of -1 or 0 sets ret to EX_UNAVAILABLE and ends the loop. It then removes the pid file; if a signal was received it logs it, restores the default action and raises it again (so the process normally ends by that signal) and sets ret to the negative signal number. It returns ret.

functions.name: digest_dynamic
functions.prose_contract: Processes the dynamic section of the object obj in two steps and returns a bool. It calls digest_dynamic1(obj, early, &dyn_rpath, &dyn_soname, &dyn_runpath), which returns void, sets the three local pointers to NULL first, and (when obj->dynamic is not NULL) digests the dynamic entries into obj, recording the DT_RPATH, DT_SONAME and DT_RUNPATH entries it meets in those pointers.
