Otherwise it computes the dump length, checks that the save directory has enough space (stop if not), opens the core file (and a compressing stream when compress is set), writes the info file, for an encrypted dump reads the key (stop on failure), and copies the data with DoTextdumpFile or DoRegularFile (a failure goes to the cleanup that closes everything); it closes the core file, creates the info.last, key.last and core.last symlinks (failures are logged), and, unless keep is set, overwrites the dump header on the device to mark it cleared. It finishes the XML output and returns; the cleanup paths close the files and the device.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Entry point of tunefs, which changes tunable parameters in a UFS superblock; it does not return. With fewer than 3 arguments it calls usage(). It parses the options (-A, -a, -e, -f, -j, -J, -k, -L, -l, -m, -N, -n, -o, -p, -s, -S, -t), counting each in found_arg and validating its value with errx(10, ...) on a bad value (for example enable/disable values, numbers below their minimum, an over-long or invalid volume label, -m outside 0 to 99, -o other than space or time); an unknown option calls usage(). It calls usage() if no option was given or the operand count is not one. It opens the disk with ufs_disk_fillout and reads the superblock (a failure goes to the error exit). If the filesystem is not clean (or has a needs-fsck flag) and more than one option was given or -p is not the only option, it calls errx(1, "... not clean - run fsck"). With -p it prints the current tuning values and exits 0. Otherwise it applies each requested change in turn to the in-memory superblock, printing whether the value changed or stayed the same (some changes can fail with a message, for example enabling journaling on a filesystem that cannot take it). It then writes the superblock with sbwrite; a failure goes to the error exit, which calls errx(11) when the disk has an error message and err(12) otherwise. On success it closes the disk, calls chkdoreload for the mount point and exits 0.

functions.name: readfd
functions.prose_contract: Handles readability of the health-check connection of l4 (an l4cfg_t with descriptor l4_fd). If l4_rw is -2 (the connection is still being established) it calls connectfd(l4) and returns without reading. Otherwise it receives with recv: into the rest of l4_rbuf (l4_rsize - l4_rlen bytes at offset l4_rlen) when a response size is configured, else into a local 80-byte buffer. A recv result of 0 or -1 calls closel4(l4, 1), which closes the socket and (per its argument) removes the NAT rule if the target was alive. For a positive result: with no configured response size (local buffer) the data is NUL-terminated and, if the target was not alive, it is marked alive, addnat(l4) is called and closel4(l4, 0) closes the connection; with a configured response size the received count is added to l4_rlen and, once l4_rlen reaches l4_rsize, the buffer is compared with the expected response: a match marks the target alive and calls addnat if it was not alive already, then closes with closel4(l4, 0); a mismatch calls closel4(l4, 1). Until the whole response has arrived the function returns without closing.

functions.name: parse_req
functions.prose_contract: Parses the first tokens of a control-transfer command line into the global libusb20 setup packet (bmRequestType, bRequest, wValue, wIndex, wLength); argv holds argc tokens. It examines at most seven tokens (idx 0 to 6) and stops early when no tokens remain. Token 0 selects the direction by its first letter: 'i' sets bit 0x80, 'o' leaves it clear, anything else prints a message and returns -1. Token 1 selects the type by its first letter: 's' standard, 'c' class (0x20), 'v' vendor (0x40), otherwise a message and return -1. Token 2 selects the recipient by its first letter: 'd' device, 'i' interface (1), 'e' endpoint (2), 'o' other (3), otherwise a message and return -1; after a valid recipient it stores the accumulated request type in setup.bmRequestType. Token 3 is converted to bRequest with get_req (not read), and tokens 4, 5 and 6 are converted with strtoul (base detected) into wValue, wIndex and wLength. Fields for tokens that are not present are not touched, and bmRequestType is only stored when token 2 is reached. On success it returns the value of argc after the loop, which is the number of tokens left unconsumed (0 when seven or fewer tokens were given), and -1 on any invalid direction, type or recipient.

functions.name: command_bcache
functions.prose_contract: Boot-loader command handler for "bcachestat"; argc and argv come from the command interpreter and argv is unused. If argc != 1 it sets command_errmsg to "wrong number of arguments" and returns CMD_ERROR without printing. Otherwise it prints the block cache statistics (total blocks, block size, read-ahead, unit blocks, cached units, operations, bypasses, hits and misses, from the bcache globals) and returns CMD_OK.

functions.name: autoboot
functions.prose_contract: Counts down and then boots the default kernel, or returns to the loader prompt when interrupted; it sets autoboot_tried to 1 first and returns a CMD_* code. A timeout of -1 means use the "autoboot_delay" environment variable in seconds (10 if unset or unparseable). If the "kernelname" variable is unset it calls loadakernel(0, 0, argv) and, if it is still unset, sets command_errmsg to "no valid kernel found" and returns CMD_ERROR. If the timeout is negative it boots at once; otherwise it prints a prompt (the custom one or the default) and waits for the deadline: it polls the console; in the default build an Enter key sets yes and any other key leaves the loop with yes still 0 (no boot); when the BOOT_PROMPT_123 option is compiled in, Enter boots, and the sequence "1", "2", "3" leaves the loop with yes = 0 (any wrong key restarts the sequence); when the deadline passes yes is set to 1. It prints a countdown once per second. If yes is set it prints the "Booting" message and returns the result of command_boot with "boot"; otherwise it returns CMD_OK after a newline, which hands control to the command prompt.

functions.name: gfx_get_ppi
functions.prose_contract: Returns the pixels-per-inch estimate of the framebuffer: it calls edid_diagonal_squared() and returns 0 if that is 0 (no usable EDID size, so no division by zero happens); otherwise it computes dp = fb_width squared plus fb_height squared (in unsigned arithmetic) from the global gfx_state and returns isqrt(dp / di). It acquires nothing.

functions.name: gfx_get_font
functions.prose_contract: Chooses a font from the global font list for a terminal of rows by cols characters on a screen of height by width pixels; it returns the font bitmap data or NULL. It returns NULL for a text framebuffer (FB_TEXT) and when gfx_get_ppi() is 0. It computes a target font height from the screen's pixels per inch. It then walks the font list (sorted by size): it skips fonts that would not fit rows and cols on the screen; for the first font that fits and where the next font in the list is missing or smaller than the target height it uses it, loading it with its font_load callback if its bitmap is not loaded or it is flagged FONT_RELOAD (the result of font_load, which can be NULL, becomes the returned value), and stops; fonts that fit but are not selected make the candidate NULL again. It returns the candidate (NULL if none was chosen).

functions.name: set_font
functions.prose_contract: Selects the font for a screen of h by w pixels and updates *rows and *cols to the character grid that fits; it returns font bitmap data (never NULL when the default font data is available). It first looks for a font flagged FONT_MANUAL, loading it if needed (a font whose bitmap is still NULL is discarded); if none, it asks gfx_get_font for the best match. When a font is found it sets *rows = h / font height and *cols = w / font width and returns it. Otherwise it scans the font list for the first font that fits the existing rows and cols (or the default font on very large screens), loading it when needed (a failed load skips the font), and on success updates *rows and *cols from it and stops. If still nothing was chosen it tries to load the last font in the list and, failing that, uses the built-in default font; in this case it also updates *rows and *cols from the font and returns it.

functions.name: cons_clear
functions.prose_contract: Clears the framebuffer console: it feeds the two-byte reset sequence ESC 'c' to the teken emulator with teken_input(&gfx_state.tg_teken, clear, 2) and then calls gfx_state.tg_functions->tf_param(&gfx_state, TP_SHOWCURSOR, 0) to hide the cursor. It returns nothing and acquires nothing.

functions.name: setup_font
functions.prose_contract: Chooses a font and applies it to the teken graphics state; it returns nothing. It calls set_font(&state->tg_tp.tp_row, &state->tg_tp.tp_col, height, width), which updates the row and column counts, and calls panic("out of memory") if set_font returns NULL. It then copies the font maps and map counts (VFNT_MAPS of them) from the chosen font into state->tg_font, copies the byte count, height and width, and sets the environment variable "screen.font" to "<width>x<height>" (volatile, no hook, with font_set as the set hook and env_nounset as the unset hook).

functions.name: efi_term_emu
functions.prose_contract: Processes one output character c for the EFI console, emulating a subset of ANSI/cons25 escape sequences when TERM_EMU is defined; it returns nothing. It returns immediately, doing nothing, if boot_services_active is false. When TERM_EMU is not defined it passes c to efi_cons_rawputchar and returns. When it is defined the function is a state machine on the static esc, args and argc: in the normal state (esc 0) an ESC byte only records the state and any other byte goes to efi_cons_rawputchar; after ESC a '[' starts a numeric-argument sequence (args[0] cleared, argc -1) and any other byte calls bail_out(c); within "ESC [" a ';' advances to the next argument (bail_out when there would be more than MAXARGS), 'H' calls HO() with no argument or CM() with exactly one extra argument (otherwise bail_out), 'J' with no argument calls CD() (otherwise bail_out), 'm' applies the colour and attribute arguments to the global foreground and background (0 reset, 1 bold, 4 and 5 bright background, 7 reverse, 22, 24, 25, 30-37, 39, 40-47 and 49) and calls SetAttribute on the console output and end_term(), a digit is accumulated with get_arg, and any other byte calls bail_out(c); any unknown esc state calls bail_out(c). The helpers HO, CM, CD, bail_out, end_term and get_arg were not read, so the memory and console effects of CD (which may allocate and free) are not described here.

functions.name: efi_redirect_exceptions
functions.prose_contract: Installs the loader's own IDT (and, if needed, GDT and TSS) so that CPU exceptions raised while UEFI boot services are active are handled by the loader's handlers, returning 1 on success and 0 on failure (in every failure case after the first allocation it calls free_tables() to release what was set up). It saves the firmware IDT with sidt and allocates pages for the loader IDT (AllocatePages; on failure it prints a message, clears lidt_pa and returns 0) and one page for an exception stack (failure: message, free_tables(), return 0), then copies the firmware IDT contents into the loader IDT. It saves the firmware GDT and task register. If the firmware has no TSS loaded (task register 0) it looks for a free system-segment slot in the firmware GDT; if none, it checks that the table can grow (message, free_tables() and return 0 if all 8190 slots are used), allocates and fills a larger GDT (failure: message, free_tables(), return 0), and sets up a new TSS with efi_setup_tss (failure: free_tables(), return 0); if the firmware has a TSS it validates its descriptor type (a non-TSS descriptor gives a message, free_tables() and return 0) and marks it not busy. It prepares the handlers for the exception vectors 0 to 14 and 16 to 20, chooses an unused IST index (all used: message, free_tables(), clear lidt_pa, return 0), sets that IST in each intercepted IDT entry and stores the exception stack top in the TSS. With interrupts disabled it loads the new GDT (if one was made), the new TSS and the loader IDT, restores the interrupt state and returns 1.

functions.name: fdt_fixup_stdout
functions.prose_contract: If the /chosen node of the loaded device tree has no "stdout" property, sets "stdout" and "stdin" to the path of a matching serial node derived from the console name str; it returns nothing. It sets ptr to the last character of str and then runs a loop that decrements str while ptr > str and the byte before str is a digit (the test reads *(str - 1), i.e. memory before the start of the string, and str moves backwards, not the tail of the name; with a typical name where that byte is not a digit the loop does not run). It returns without changes when ptr == str (which holds for a one-character string whose preceding byte is not a digit), when /chosen cannot be found, or when "stdout" already exists with non-zero length. Otherwise it builds the string "serial" followed by up to three characters copied from ptr (the last character of the original name, for a name like "uart0" giving "serial0"), returns without changes if strlen(ptr) > 3, looks the path up with fdt_path_offset (return if it is not found) and sets both "stdout" and "stdin" in /chosen to that string.

functions.name: ficlNtohl
functions.prose_contract: Returns ntohl(number): the low 32 bits of number are converted from network (big-endian) byte order to host byte order and the result is returned zero-extended as an unsigned long. On a little-endian host this swaps the four low bytes; on a big-endian host it returns the low 32 bits unchanged. The upper bits of number are ignored. It has no side effects.

functions.name: ofCoIm
functions.prose_contract: Compile-time (immediate) word for OF in a FICL CASE ... OF ... ENDOF construct; vm is the FICL virtual machine and the function returns nothing. It asserts that pSys->pBranch0 is set. If the top of the parameter stack is the fallthroughTag (left by a preceding fallthrough), it checks it with matchControlTag and pops its fixup pointer; then it requires a caseTag control frame to follow (matchControlTag) and re-marks it with markControlTag. It then appends the OF-paren runtime cell (pSys->pOfParen) to the dictionary, pushes an ofTag branch fixup with markBranch, and appends a single cell holding the value 2 (dictAppendUNS(dp, 2), one cell). If there was a fallthrough fixup it patches that earlier branch with the distance from it to the current dictionary position (here). The caseTag is expected below the fallthroughTag when both are present, not on top.

functions.name: parse_cmds
functions.prose_contract: Parses the boot command string cmdstr (modified in place: a NUL replaces the separator after each token) and applies option switches, a disk specification and a kernel name; dskupdated is set to 0 on entry and to 1 when a "disk(...)" specification was parsed. Tokens are separated by blanks, tabs and newlines. A token starting with '-' is a list of option letters: 'P' prints the keyboard status (and, when no keyboard is present, sets the dual-console and serial flags), 'S' followed by decimal digits that end the token sets comspeed when the number is positive and ends that token's scan, and any other letter must be one of the letters in optstr, whose flag in opts is toggled (an unknown letter returns -1). After the letters ioctrl is recomputed from the dual and serial flags and, if serial is used, sio_init is called with 115200 / comspeed (on failure the serial bit is dropped). Any other token is a kernel name, optionally preceded by a disk specification "[drive:]xx(unit p part)": a malformed specification (drive digit above 9, name length not 2, an unknown device name, unit above 9 or missing 'p', partition outside 1 to 128, missing ')') returns -1; a valid one sets gdsk.dsk type, unit, part and drive and dskupdated to 1. A remaining name longer than or equal to sizeof(kname) returns -1, otherwise it is copied to kname. The function returns 0 when all tokens are consumed and -1 on the first invalid token.

functions.name: parse_cmd
functions.prose_contract: Parses the global boot command string cmd (no parameters; the string is modified in place) in the ZFS boot loader, applying option switches, listing, a status request, a root dataset and a kernel name; it returns 0 when all tokens were consumed and -1 on a problem or after an informational command. Tokens are separated by blanks, tabs and newlines. A token starting with '-' is a list of option letters: 'P' prints the keyboard status (and sets the dual and serial flags when there is no keyboard), 'S' followed by a positive number that ends the token sets comspeed, any other letter must be in optstr (otherwise -1) and toggles its flag in opts; then ioctrl is recomputed and sio_init(115200 / comspeed) is called when serial is used (failure drops the serial bit). Because the following test is written "} if (c == '?')" rather than "else if", after processing a '-' token control falls on to the final else branch with the rest of the token as if it were a name, so the next steps also run for such tokens. A token starting with '?' lists the files and ZFS datasets at the given path (default "/") and returns -1. Otherwise the token "status" prints the status of all devices through the pager and returns -1; a token that may start with "zfs:" and contain ':' is passed to mount_root (return -1 if that fails) and the part after it is the kernel name; a remaining name of sizeof(kname) or more returns -1, otherwise it is copied to kname.

functions.name: biospnp_call
functions.prose_contract: Calls a PnP BIOS function through the real-mode BIOS entry point and returns the low 16 bits of the BIOS's eax result (the PnP status code). The function number func is packed first as a 16-bit value into a local array of four 32-bit words that starts zeroed, then each variadic argument is packed according to fmt: a 'w' takes a u_int argument stored as 16 bits, an 'l' takes a uint32_t stored as 32 bits, and other format characters are ignored; the BIOS data segment pnp_Icheck->pnp_rmds is appended last as 16 bits (the caller must not pass more than the four words allow; there is no bounds check). It sets the v86 control to a far call to the BIOS entry address (pnp_rmcs:pnp_rmip from pnp_Icheck), runs v86bios with the four packed words as stack arguments and returns v86.eax & 0xffff.

functions.name: spinc_putchar
functions.prose_contract: Output routine of the spinning-cursor console: the character argument c is ignored; instead it draws the next frame of a spinner on the parent console, at most once per second. It reads the current time; if now is less than lasttime + 1 it returns without output or state change. Otherwise, when TERM_EMU is defined and lasttime is non-zero, it first writes a backspace '\b' to the parent; then it sets lasttime to now, writes the low byte of the static tw_chars (initially '|' from the value 0x5C2D2F7C) to the parent with c_out, and rotates tw_chars right by one byte (so the successive characters are '|', '/', '-', '\' and then repeat). The low-byte extraction does not depend on the host byte order because it is a numeric cast. parent must be non-NULL (set by spinc_probe).

functions.name: device_probe_and_attach
functions.prose_contract: Tries to find and attach a driver module for the device dev (whose parent must be set) in the kernel-shim bus framework; it returns 0 on success and ENODEV otherwise. It returns 0 immediately if the device is already attached. Otherwise, for each registered module whose bus_name equals the parent's name, it finds the module's device class; if the device is not already in that class it skips the module when the device has a fixed class, removes the device from its old class and adds it to the new one (skipping the module if the add fails); it then records the module in dev->dev_module and, if DEVICE_PROBE(dev) returns 0 or less, calls device_allocate_softc (a zero-size softc is allowed, in which case nothing is allocated and it still returns 0) and, if that returns 0, DEVICE_ATTACH; when attach succeeds it sets dev_attached to 1 and returns 0. In every other case (probe returned positive, softc allocation failed, or attach failed) it calls device_detach(dev) and tries the next module. After all modules have been tried without success it returns ENODEV, which is therefore also the result when modules matched but failed to probe or attach.

functions.name: delay
functions.prose_contract: Busy-waits for roughly usecs microseconds using the Open Firmware millisecond counter: it computes msecs = usecs / 1000 (C integer division, truncating toward zero, so 1500 microseconds waits 1 ms and a negative or sub-millisecond value gives a wait of 0 or less), records start = OF_milliseconds(), and loops, polling OF_milliseconds(), until OF_milliseconds() - start is no longer less than msecs. It returns nothing, and for msecs <= 0 the loop ends at its first test.

functions.name: getopt
functions.prose_contract: Boot-loader getopt: returns the next option letter from nargv according to the option string ostr, -1 when there are no more options, '?' (BADCH) for an unknown option or a missing argument (or BADARG ':' for a missing argument when ostr starts with ':'). It uses the globals optind, optreset, opterr, optopt and optarg and a static scan pointer place. When optreset is set or the current word is exhausted it restarts at nargv[optind]: if optind >= nargc or the word does not begin with '-' it returns -1; a word "--" advances optind and returns -1. It takes the next letter into optopt; if it is ':' or not found in ostr it advances optind when the word is finished and returns BADCH (printing a message when opterr is set and ostr does not begin with ':'), except that a letter '-' (a lone "-") returns -1 without advancing. For a letter that takes no argument it sets optarg to NULL and advances optind at the end of the word; for one that takes an argument it sets optarg to the rest of the word, or to the next argv word, or, when none is left, returns BADARG or BADCH as above; optind advances past the argument. On success it returns the option letter.

functions.name: gptbootconv
functions.prose_contract: Converts "boot once" GPT partition entries of the table described by hdr into "boot failed" entries and writes the changes back; which names the table (primary or backup) for messages, dskp the disk, and the function returns nothing. It computes entries per sector as DEV_BSIZE / hdr_entsz and walks only the complete sectors of the table (hdr_entries / entries_per_sec sectors; a trailing partial sector of entries is not visited when the entry count is not a multiple). For each entry whose attribute bits, masked to BOOTME, BOOTONCE and BOOTFAILED, equal exactly BOOTONCE (other attribute bits are not considered), it clears BOOTONCE and sets BOOTFAILED. Each sector that contained a changed entry is copied to the scratch buffer secbuf and written with drvwrite (a failure prints a message and the loop goes on). If any entry changed it recomputes the table CRC and the header CRC (with the table CRC stored first), copies the header into a zeroed sector and writes it to hdr_lba_self with drvwrite (a failure prints a message). If no entry changed it returns without writing anything.

functions.name: pkg_seek
functions.prose_contract: Seek method of the package (tar) file system; f is the open file (f_fsdata a struct tarfile), ofs the offset and whence one of SEEK_SET, SEEK_CUR and SEEK_END; it returns the resulting file position tf_fp or -1 with errno set. It returns -1 with EBADF if f_fsdata is NULL, and with EINVAL for any other whence. It computes the signed distance delta to move (from tf_fp for SEEK_SET, ofs itself for SEEK_CUR, relative to the end for SEEK_END). A backward move is allowed only when the data is cached: if tf_cachesz > 0 and tf_fp <= tf_cachesz and the new position is not negative it sets tf_fp to the new position and returns it; in every other backward case (no cache, tf_fp beyond the cache, or a negative target) it returns -1 with ESPIPE. A forward move reads and discards data with pkg_read in chunks of at most 512 bytes until delta is used up or the end of the file is reached; an error from pkg_read is stored in errno and -1 returned. It returns tf_fp, which can be less than the requested position when the end of the file is reached first.

functions.name: kvprintf
functions.prose_contract: Formats fmt with the arguments in ap, sending each output character either to the callback func (called with the character and arg) or, when func is NULL, into the buffer pointed to by arg, and returns the number of characters produced (retval); no NUL terminator is added by this function and the caller must provide a buffer large enough for the whole output. A NULL fmt is replaced by "(fmt null)\n", and a radix below 2 or above 36 is replaced by 10 (the radix is used for %r and %R conversions). The format is scanned character by character: ordinary characters are output; after '%' the flags and modifiers ('#', '+', '-', '0', '.', '*', digits, h, hh, j, l, ll, q, t, z) are accumulated and the conversion is one of b (bit-field print), c, D (hex dump), d, i, n, o, p, r, s, S (16-bit wide string), u, X, x, y, or "%%". Numbers are taken with the size given by the modifiers, converted in the proper base with sign, '#' prefix, padding and precision, and written with left or right adjustment; %s prints "(null)" for a NULL pointer and honours the precision; %n stores the count so far through a pointer of the size selected by the modifiers. A conversion character that is not recognised outputs the text of the directive from its '%' up to and including that character and then sets stop, after which the rest of the format string is output verbatim (the directive arguments are not consumed). The function returns retval when it reaches the NUL at the end of the format.

functions.name: zfs_bootenv
functions.prose_contract: Rebuilds the boot-environment menu for the ZFS dataset name; it sets environment variables and returns 0 on success or an error number. It returns EINVAL if name is NULL or the variable zfs_be_root is unset, and ENOMEM if replacing zfs_be_root with name fails (zfs_be_root is overwritten before the pool lookup, so a later failure leaves it changed). It then empties the list zfs_be_head and the count and splits name into a pool name and dataset name (EINVAL if that fails), finds the pool (ENXIO if unknown), looks up the dataset (returning the lookup's error) and calls zfs_callback_dataset with zfs_belist_add to collect the boot environments; the result of that callback is kept as the return value. It computes the number of pages, stores it in zfs_be_pages (ENOMEM on failure, without freeing the list), parses zfs_be_currpage with strtol (which requires the variable to be set) and resets it to "1" if it exceeds the page count (ENOMEM on failure, again without freeing the list). It calls zfs_set_env() (its result is ignored) and frees all collected entries, then returns the result of the callback. The list is therefore leaked on the ENOMEM returns after the callback and on the early error returns after it was initialised.

functions.name: sys_sigreturn
functions.prose_contract: System call that restores the user context saved by a signal handler frame; uap->sigcntxp points to the user-space ucontext_t and the function returns EJUSTRETURN on success or an errno. It copies the context in (returning the copyin error), returns EINVAL if mc_flags has bits outside _MC_FLAG_MASK, if the new rflags are not EFL_SECURE with respect to the current ones, or if the ss or cs selector fails is_seg_val. If the code segment is not CS_SECURE it posts SIGBUS (BUS_OBJERR, T_PROTFLT, at the current rip) with trapsignal and returns EINVAL, so the thread's signal state is changed on that path. When _MC_HASFPXSTATE is set it returns EINVAL if the extended state length is too large, allocates a save area and copies the user's extended state in (freeing the area and returning the copyin error on failure); otherwise there is none. It then calls set_fpcontext and frees the area, returning its error if non-zero. Only after all of those checks pass does it copy the general registers into the trapframe, update the pcb's fs and gs bases, with COMPAT_43 set or clear SS_ONSTACK from mc_onstack, set the signal mask from uc_sigmask with kern_sigprocmask, and return EJUSTRETURN. Any earlier error return leaves the trapframe, bases and signal mask unchanged.

functions.name: hammer_time
functions.prose_contract: First C function of the amd64 kernel, called once on the boot CPU from locore with modulep (the preload metadata) and physfree (the first free physical address after the loaded kernel and modules); it sets up CPU identification, descriptor tables, per-CPU data, consoles, memory and thread0, and returns the top of thread0's kernel stack (thread0.td_md.md_stack_base) for the assembly caller to switch to. In order it: records the boot-method flags and the BIOS warm-boot word, identifies the CPU and any hypervisor, initialises the CPU caches, reads the PTI, PCID, XSAVE and scheduler tunables, relocates ifuncs, links proc0 and thread0, zeroes the thread0 kernel stack, builds and loads the GDT, sets the FS/GS base registers, initialises the dynamic per-CPU area and the BSP pcpu, initialises the mutexes, fills the IDT with the exception vectors (using the PTI variants when pti is set) and loads it, reads the CPU-mitigation tunables, finishes CPU identification, initialises clocks, the CPU registers, the IST stacks, the task register and the fast system call MSRs, and sets thread0's top of stack. It reads the debug.late_console tunable: when it is not set it initialises the console (cninit) and the kernel debugger (amd64_kdb_init) before sizing memory, and when it is set it does both later (cninit before the PCI quirks and amd64_kdb_init after the interrupt controller setup), so the debugger is initialised on both paths. It then calls getmemsize and init_param2, sets up the interrupt controller, msgbuf and FPU, selects the user segment selectors, loads the data segment registers, clears thread0's pcb flags, copies the "kernelname" environment value, calls the sanitizer and optional FDT initialisers and returns thread0.td_md.md_stack_base.

functions.name: cpu_minidumpsys
functions.prose_contract: Writes an amd64 minidump through the dumper device di; state supplies the msgbuf pointer and the dump bitset; it returns 0 on success or a positive error number. It walks the kernel page tables from km_low up to the kernel virtual-memory end: for every valid 1 GB or 2 MB mapping it adds each dumpable physical page of the mapping to the dump bitset (vm_phys_is_dumpable, vm_page_dump_add), for page-table pages it adds the page-table page itself and every valid 4 KB mapping whose physical address is in the direct map and dumpable, and it counts the size of the page-directory pages that will be written (pmapsize). It then totals the dump size (pmap pages, msgbuf, dump_avail, the bitmap and one header page) and, going through the bitset, adds PAGE_SIZE for each page that is in the direct map and dumpable and removes (vm_page_dump_drop) the others. It fills a minidump header (magic, version, sizes, KERNBASE, direct map range), starts the dump with dump_start and writes in order: the header page, the msgbuf, the dump_avail array, the bitmap, the page-directory pages (a zero page for an invalid 1 GB entry, a synthesised directory for a 1 GB mapping, the real directory page when it is dumpable, otherwise a zero page; each followed by blk_flush), then every page in the bitset, then flushes and calls dump_finish. Any failing step goes to the fail path, which makes a negative error positive; for ENOSPC it retries the whole dump from the start up to dump_retry_count times, for ECANCELED it reports that the dump was aborted, for E2BIG it reports the size needed, and it returns the error.

functions.name: pmap_pkru_update_range
functions.prose_contract: Sets the protection-key (PKRU) field of the page-table entries covering [sva, eva) of pmap to keyidx; the caller must hold the pmap lock (asserted), pm_type must be PT_X86 and keyidx at most PMAP_MAX_PKRU_IDX (both MPASS). It walks the range one top-level region at a time: an invalid PML4 or PDP entry is skipped; a 1 GB mapping gets its key field replaced if it differs, with a KASSERT that the mapping is not partially covered (va_next <= eva); an empty page-directory entry is skipped; a 2 MB mapping whose whole span lies in the range gets its key field replaced, while a partially covered 2 MB mapping is first demoted with pmap_demote_pde (if the demotion fails that region is skipped); and for the 4 KB mappings in the remaining span each valid page-table entry gets its key field replaced if it differs. Whenever any entry was changed it calls pmap_invalidate_range(pmap, sva, eva) once at the end. It returns nothing; the wrap-around of va_next is clamped to eva.

functions.name: pmap_ts_referenced
functions.prose_contract: Counts and clears (where safe) the reference bits of the mappings of the managed page m (asserted not VPO_UNMANAGED) across all pmaps, and returns cleared + not_cleared: the number of mappings found referenced whose bit was cleared plus those found referenced whose bit could not be cleared, so the result can be non-zero when no bit was actually cleared. It takes the page's PV list lock as a write lock itself and releases it before returning (the caller must not hold it). It scans the 2 MB mappings on the page's pv list and then the 4 KB mappings on m's own pv list, locking each pmap (if the trylock fails it drops the PV lock, takes the pmap lock and restarts the scan when the lists changed). For each mapping it marks the page dirty if the entry is both modified and writable; if the referenced bit is set it clears it with atomic_clear_long and invalidates the page when safe_to_clear_referenced allows it, and counts it as cleared; for a 2 MB mapping it clears the bit only for a limited subset of mappings (selected by a hash of the physical address, virtual address and pmap) that are not wired, demoting or removing the 4 KB mapping when it is not safe to clear, and otherwise counts it as not cleared; for a 4 KB mapping that cannot be cleared safely and is not wired it removes the mapping (counted as cleared), and a wired one is counted as not cleared. Visited pv entries are rotated to the tail of their list. The scan stops once cleared + not_cleared reaches PMAP_TS_REFERENCED_MAX (the test is applied after counting, to either kind of count) or when all entries have been visited. It then frees any page-table pages collected and returns the sum.

functions.name: pmap_change_attr
functions.prose_contract: Changes the memory (cache) attribute of the kernel virtual range [va, va + size) to mode: it takes the kernel_pmap lock, calls pmap_change_props_locked(va, size, PROT_NONE, mode, MAPDEV_FLUSHCACHE), releases the lock and returns that function's result (0 on success, or an error number such as EINVAL or ENOMEM produced by pmap_change_props_locked, which was not read; the values are positive errno numbers, not negative ones).

functions.name: pmap_change_prot
functions.prose_contract: Changes the protection of the kernel virtual range [va, va + size) to prot: it returns EINVAL without changing anything if va is below kva_layout.km_low; otherwise it takes the kernel_pmap lock, calls pmap_change_props_locked(va, size, prot, -1, MAPDEV_ASSERTVALID), releases the lock and returns that function's result (0 on success, or an error number produced by the callee, which was not read; positive errno values).

functions.name: read_rflags
functions.prose_contract: Static inline function returning the current RFLAGS register as a u_long: it executes "pushfq; popq %0" in volatile inline assembly, which pushes the flags on the stack and pops them into a register, and returns that value. The stack pointer is temporarily changed by the pushfq/popq pair, which is restored by the pop; there is no other effect on memory. On x86-64 the upper 32 bits of RFLAGS are reserved and read as zero and bit 1 reads as 1 (an architectural property, not enforced by this code).

functions.name: systrace_args
functions.prose_contract: Generated DTrace helper systrace_args(sysnum, params, uarg, n_args): it fills the 64-bit array uarg with the arguments of the Linux system call sysnum read from the matching args structure params, and sets *n_args to the argument count; it returns nothing. It is one large switch with a case per system call number: each case casts params to that call's args structure, stores the arguments in order into slots uarg[0], uarg[1], ... and sets *n_args. Integer-typed and unsigned-typed arguments (int, l_uint, l_ulong, l_size_t and similar) are stored through the int64_t alias iarg (sign-extending per the field type), and pointer arguments are stored through uarg as (intptr_t) values. A system call without arguments, and some calls whose case does not store its arguments, only set *n_args (to 0 for the no-argument calls). A sysnum with no case reaches the default branch, which sets *n_args to 0 and writes nothing to uarg; params is not read in that case. (This slice covers the cases for system call numbers from the middle of the switch in the amd64 Linux table.)

functions.name: systrace_entry_setargdesc
functions.prose_contract: Generated DTrace helper (the real name is systrace_entry_setargdesc, at linux_systrace_args.c:2821-7306) that writes the type description of argument number ndx of Linux system call sysnum into the buffer desc of size descsz; it returns nothing. It switches on sysnum and, for the calls that have arguments, on ndx, setting a local pointer p to a constant type string such as "int", "userland char *" or "l_size_t"; for an unknown sysnum, for an ndx beyond the call's arguments, and for calls with no arguments p stays NULL. Only when p is non-NULL it copies it with strlcpy(desc, p, descsz) (truncated and NUL-terminated to fit descsz); otherwise desc is left unchanged. The slice region contains the cases for calls around number 441 (with arguments 0 to 5) and the empty cases for the later numbers up to 453.

functions.name: pci_docfgregread
functions.prose_contract: Reads a PCI configuration register for (domain, bus, slot, func, reg) with the access width bytes and returns it as a uint32_t. If domain and bus are both 0 and bit slot of pcie_badslots is set (slot must be below 32 for the shift to be defined) it uses the legacy I/O-port method pcireg_cfgread. Otherwise, if cfgmech is CFGMECH_PCIE and pcie_lookup_region finds a memory-mapped region for the domain and bus, it returns pciereg_cfgread on that region. Otherwise, for domain 0 it uses the legacy pcireg_cfgread, and for any other domain it returns -1, which as a uint32_t is 0xFFFFFFFF whatever the width. pcireg_cfgread takes and releases the pcicfg_mtx spin mutex, so the caller must not hold it on the legacy paths.

functions.name: pci_cfgregread
functions.prose_contract: Public read of a PCI configuration register. If reg is PCIR_INTLINE and bytes is 1 it reads the value with pci_docfgregread and returns PCI_INVALID_IRQ (255) when it is 0 or at least 128 (this includes an all-ones failure value), otherwise the value read. For every other register and width it returns pci_docfgregread(domain, bus, slot, func, reg, bytes) unchanged (so a failed access yields 0xFFFFFFFF as in pci_docfgregread). The caller must not hold pcicfg_mtx on the legacy paths.

functions.name: pci_cfgregwrite
functions.prose_contract: Public write of a PCI configuration register (domain, bus, slot, func, reg) with data of width bytes; it returns nothing. If domain and bus are both 0 and bit slot of pcie_badslots is set (slot below 32) it writes with the legacy method pcireg_cfgwrite (which takes and releases the pcicfg_mtx spin mutex) and returns. Otherwise, if cfgmech is CFGMECH_PCIE and a memory-mapped region covers the domain and bus, it writes through pciereg_cfgwrite (this path does not take pcicfg_mtx in this function) and returns. Otherwise it uses pcireg_cfgwrite for domain 0, and for any other domain does nothing.

functions.name: pci_cfgenable
functions.prose_contract: Prepares the legacy PCI configuration mechanism 1 for an access and returns the data port to use, or 0 if the arguments are invalid. When bus <= PCI_BUSMAX, slot <= PCI_SLOTMAX, func <= PCI_FUNCMAX, reg lies in 0..PCI_REGMAX, bytes is not 3 and at most 4, and reg is aligned to the width (reg & (bytes - 1) is 0; for bytes 0 that requires reg == 0), it writes the enable word (bit 31, bus, slot, function and the register number with its low two bits cleared) to CONF1_ADDR_PORT with outl and returns CONF1_DATA_PORT plus the low two bits of reg. In every other case it writes nothing and returns 0. It takes no locks; the callers hold pcicfg_mtx.

functions.name: pcireg_cfgread
functions.prose_contract: Reads a configuration register with the legacy I/O-port mechanism and returns it as an int. It takes the pcicfg_mtx spin mutex, calls pci_cfgenable, and if that returned a non-zero port reads 1, 2 or 4 bytes (inb, inw or inl) according to bytes and calls pci_cfgdisable (which does nothing); for bytes other than 1, 2 and 4 nothing is read even if the port was valid. It then releases the mutex and returns the data, which is -1 when pci_cfgenable rejected the arguments or when bytes was not 1, 2 or 4. A 4-byte read can return any 32-bit value, which as an int may be negative. The caller must not hold pcicfg_mtx.

functions.name: ept_init
functions.prose_contract: Checks that the CPU's EPT/VPID capabilities (MSR_VMX_EPT_VPID_CAP) are sufficient for bhyve and sets the global nested-pmap flags; ipinum is the IPI number that is masked into the flags. It returns EINVAL, without changing ept_pmap_flags or ept_enable_ad_bits, if the capability lacks a 4-level page walk, write-back EPT memory type, INVVPID support with all types, or INVEPT support with all types. Otherwise it sets ept_pmap_flags to ipinum & PMAP_NESTED_IPIMASK, adds PMAP_PDE_SUPERPAGE when the tunable hw.vmm.ept.use_superpages (default 1) is set and the CPU supports 2 MB superpages, sets ept_enable_ad_bits to 1 when hw.vmm.ept.use_hw_ad_bits (default 1) is set and the CPU supports accessed/dirty bits (otherwise it adds PMAP_EMULATE_AD_BITS to the flags), adds PMAP_SUPPORTS_EXEC_ONLY when hw.vmm.ept.use_exec_only (default 1) is set and the CPU supports execute-only mappings, and returns 0.

functions.name: vmcs_snapshot_any
functions.prose_contract: Saves or restores one VMCS field to or from a snapshot buffer: meta->op selects VM_SNAPSHOT_SAVE or VM_SNAPSHOT_RESTORE, ident names the field and running tells whether the vCPU is running; it returns 0 or an error number. For save it reads the field with vmcs_getany (returning its error if that fails) and then stores the value in the snapshot buffer with SNAPSHOT_VAR_OR_LEAVE, which sets ret to the macro's error and jumps to the exit if the buffer copy fails. For restore it first loads the value from the snapshot buffer with SNAPSHOT_VAR_OR_LEAVE (on failure it returns that error and does not write the VMCS) and then writes it with vmcs_setany, returning that call's error if non-zero. For any other meta->op it returns EINVAL. It returns the last value of ret.

functions.name: ppt_setup_msix
functions.prose_contract: Sets up or tears down one MSI-X vector (idx) of a PCI passthrough device identified by (vm, bus, slot, func); addr and msg give the guest MSI address and data and vector_control the vector's control word. It takes PPT_LOCK itself and releases it before returning; it returns 0 or an error number. It returns the error from ppt_find if the device is not found, EBUSY if MSI (not MSI-X) is already in use, ENXIO if the device has no ivars, and for the first call on a device (no MSI-X set up yet) EINVAL if the device has no MSI-X vectors, ENOSPC (after ppt_teardown_msix) if the MSI-X table or PBA BAR resource cannot be allocated, and, if pci_alloc_msix fails, that function's error (or ENOSPC when it succeeded but allocated fewer vectors than requested), also after tearing down. It allocates the resource, cookie and argument arrays on that first call. It returns EINVAL if idx is out of range. If the vector's mask bit in vector_control is clear it tears down any existing interrupt for idx, allocates the IRQ resource (ENXIO if that fails), fills arg[idx] with the device, addr and msg and registers pptintr with bus_setup_intr (on failure it releases the resource and returns ENXIO); if the mask bit is set it only tears down the interrupt for idx. It returns 0 on those paths.

functions.name: vatpit_update_mode
functions.prose_contract: Handles a write of the control byte val to the virtual i8254 PIT mode port (the caller holds the vatpit lock); it returns 0 or -1. It splits val into the select field (channel or read-back), the read/write field and the mode. If the select field is TIMER_SEL_READBACK it returns the result of pit_readback(vatpit, val), which latches counter or status values of the selected channels and so can change channel state. If the read/write field is neither TIMER_LATCH nor TIMER_16BIT it returns -1; if it is not TIMER_LATCH (a mode programming) and the mode is not one of TIMER_INTTC, TIMER_RATEGEN, TIMER_SQWAVE or TIMER_SWSTROBE it returns -1. Otherwise, for the channel selected by sel >> 6, a latch command updates the counter and latches it with pit_update_counter(vatpit, c, true), and a mode programming stores the mode in the channel, clears its output latch byte (olbyte) and sets TIMER_STS_NULLCNT in its status; then it returns 0.

functions.name: vlapic_fire_lvt
functions.prose_contract: Delivers the local-vector-table interrupt lvt of the virtual local APIC vlapic to its vCPU and returns 1 if it was handled as an interrupt or 0 if nothing was delivered. It reads the last value written to the LVT entry (lvt_last[lvt]) with an acquire load. It returns 0 if the mask bit APIC_LVT_M is set. Otherwise it dispatches on the delivery mode: for fixed delivery a vector below 16 records a send-illegal-vector error in the ESR (vlapic_set_error, for the error LVT the flag is passed as such) and returns 0, otherwise vlapic_set_intr_ready is called and vcpu_notify_lapic only if that returned non-zero, and the function still returns 1 even when the interrupt was already pending and no notification was sent; NMI mode injects an NMI with vm_inject_nmi and returns 1; ExtINT mode injects an external interrupt with vm_inject_extint and returns 1; any other delivery mode is ignored and returns 0.

functions.name: vrtc_time_update
functions.prose_contract: Updates the virtual RTC's base time to newtime with the host uptime base newbase; the caller holds the vrtc lock (asserted); it returns 0 or EBUSY. It saves the current alarm fields, always stores newbase in vrtc->base_uptime, and returns 0 at once if newtime equals the old base_rtctime. If newtime is VRTC_BROKEN_TIME it stores that in base_rtctime and returns 0. If the guest has halted RTC updates (rtc_halted) it returns EBUSY, leaving base_rtctime as it was (the base uptime has already been changed). Otherwise it advances base_rtctime toward newtime: when alarm interrupts are enabled and the old time was not VRTC_BROKEN_TIME it steps one second at a time, converting each second to RTC fields and setting the alarm interrupt flag in reg_c whenever the alarm fields match (values of 0xC0 or more are wildcards); in the other cases it sets base_rtctime to newtime directly. After the loop it sets the update-ended interrupt flag in reg_c if that interrupt is enabled, and returns 0.

functions.name: vrtc_set_reg_b
functions.prose_contract: Handles a guest write of newval to the virtual RTC's register B (the vrtc lock is held, asserted); it returns 0, or -1 in one case. It stores newval in reg_b and computes the changed bits. If the HALT bit changed: when HALT is being cleared it reads the guest-programmed time with rtc_to_secs and takes the current uptime as base, and if that time is VRTC_BROKEN_TIME and the tunable rtc_flag_broken_time is set it returns -1 (reg_b has already been updated); when HALT is being set it freezes the current time into the RTC fields (secs_to_rtc), sets the new time to VRTC_BROKEN_TIME and clears RTCSB_UINTR from reg_b (so reg_b can differ from newval). In both HALT cases it then calls vrtc_time_update with the new time and base (whose success is only asserted). If any interrupt-enable bit changed it recomputes reg_c with vrtc_set_reg_c. It then resets the periodic callout with vrtc_callout_reset when the frequency changed, and otherwise calls vrtc_callout_check, and returns 0.

functions.name: vm_run
functions.prose_contract: Runs the guest vCPU vcpu until an exit that must be handled by user space or an error, and returns 0 or an error number. It returns EINVAL if the vCPU's id is not in the VM's active_cpus or is in suspended_cpus. Otherwise it loops: with a critical section entered it records the TSC, sets PCB_FULL_IRET, restores the guest FPU state, requires the vCPU state VCPU_RUNNING, runs the guest with vmmops_run, requires VCPU_FROZEN afterwards, saves the guest FPU state, adds the run time to the statistics and leaves the critical section. If vmmops_run returned 0 it sets retu to false, advances nextrip past the instruction and handles the exit code: request-idle, suspended, rendezvous, HLT, paging, instruction emulation, in/out and debug exits are passed to their handlers (which set the error and may set retu to request return to user space); IOAPIC EOI exits are processed; MONITOR, MWAIT and VMINSN exits inject #UD; any other exit code sets retu to true so user space handles it. Then, if there was no error and the exit code is VM_EXITCODE_IPI, vm_handle_ipi is called (it may set retu). If there is no error and retu is false it restarts the loop. Otherwise (a vmmops_run error, a handler error, or a request to return to user space) it increments VMEXIT_USERSPACE, logs and returns error, which is 0 when the exit is to be handled in user space.

functions.name: emulate_movs
functions.prose_contract: Emulates one iteration of a MOVS (string move, opcode 0xA4 byte or 0xA5 word/dword/qword) instruction for a bhyve guest where one operand is memory-mapped I/O at gpa; the parameters are the vCPU, the decoded instruction vie, the guest paging state, the memread and memwrite callbacks and their argument. It uses opsize 1 for 0xA4 and vie->opsize otherwise. With a REP prefix it reads RCX and returns 0 immediately, doing nothing, when the count (masked to the address size) is 0. It translates the source address (segment override or DS, offset RSI) and, if the translation reports a guest fault or an error, jumps to done (returning the error, or 0 when only a fault was reported so that the guest resumes and takes the fault). If the source can be mapped with vm_copy_setup it reads the value from guest memory and writes it to the I/O address with memwrite (the source is ordinary memory and the destination is the MMIO location); otherwise it translates the destination (ES:RDI), and if that maps it reads the value from the I/O address with memread and copies it out; if neither side maps it translates both to guest-physical addresses and performs memread from the source followed by memwrite to the destination. A fault or error in any of these steps goes to done without updating registers. On success it adjusts RSI and RDI by opsize (decreasing when the direction flag is set, otherwise increasing), and for REP decrements RCX and, if it is still non-zero, calls vm_restart_instruction so that the instruction runs again. It returns 0 or EFAULT (asserted by a KASSERT at done); a guest page fault that must be reflected to the guest also returns 0 (fault is set), not EFAULT.

functions.name: a10_map_to_emac
functions.prose_contract: Maps the Allwinner A10 SRAM block D to the EMAC: if the global softc pointer a10_sramc_sc is NULL it returns ENXIO and touches no hardware; otherwise it reads the 32-bit register SRAM_CTL1_CFG, ORs in 0x5 << 2 (0x14, setting bits 2 and 4), writes it back and returns 0. It takes no locks.

functions.name: a10_map_to_otg
functions.prose_contract: Maps the Allwinner A10 SRAM block D to USB0: if the global softc pointer a10_sramc_sc is NULL it returns ENXIO and touches no hardware; otherwise it reads the 32-bit register SRAM_CTL1_CFG, ORs in CTL1_CFG_SRAMD_MAP_USB0, writes it back and returns 0. It takes no locks.

functions.name: alpine_serdes_eth_mode_set
functions.prose_contract: Sets the SerDes group's Ethernet mode (SGMII or KR); group indexes the global alpine_serdes_eth_group_mode array, whose entry address is computed before the bounds check (the pointer arithmetic happens first, but the entry is only used after the check). It returns EINVAL without touching hardware if serdes_base is NULL or if group >= SERDES_NUM_GROUPS. Otherwise it locks the group's mutex; if the mode was not set before or differs from mode it initialises the group object with al_serdes_handle_grp_init, calls mode_set_sgmii for SGMII or mode_set_kr for any other mode value, and records the new mode and sets mode_set. It unlocks the mutex and returns 0.

functions.name: bp_hardening_action
functions.prose_contract: Per-CPU action (arg unused) that calls handle_bp_hardening(disable_bp_hardening == 0), i.e. it asks for branch-predictor hardening to be enabled unless disable_bp_hardening is non-zero; it returns nothing. handle_bp_hardening (cpuinfo.c:384-490) for an ARM-implemented CPU selects BPIALL (with an ACTLR bit for the Cortex-A8; with no ACTLR bit for A9, A12, A17, A57, A72, A73 and A75) or ICIALLU (Cortex-A15, with ACTLR bit 0) through apply_bp_hardening; an unknown ARM part leaves the kind NONE and the global state unchanged; if apply_bp_hardening fails (the ACTLR bits cannot be written because firmware locked them) it sets the per-CPU kind to NONE, clears spectre_v2_safe and prints a warning; for a Qualcomm CPU or any other implementer it prints a warning (Qualcomm) and sets the per-CPU kind to NONE and spectre_v2_safe to 0; on the normal path it only prints the chosen kind when bootverbose. So enabling can fail or be a no-op, and the resulting state need not match disable_bp_hardening == 0.

functions.name: pmap_preboot_get_vpages
functions.prose_contract: Early-boot allocator: allocates num pages of physical memory with pmap_preboot_get_pages (which returns last_paddr and advances it by num * PAGE_SIZE without any check), takes the next virtual range of the same size from virtual_avail (advancing virtual_avail by num * PAGE_SIZE), maps the pages at that address with pmap_preboot_map_pages, zero-fills the mapped range with bzero and returns the virtual address, which is the value virtual_avail had on entry.

functions.name: sdma_configure
functions.prose_contract: Configures SDMA channel chn on the i.MX6 with the channel configuration conf and starts loading its context; it returns 0 on success or -1. It records conf in the channel, stops the channel (sdma_stop), sets the channel priority to 1, sets bit chn in the event-enable register for conf->event and clears the overrides. If conf->num_bd is greater than MAX_BD it prints an error and returns -1 before touching the buffer descriptors or the context. Otherwise it fills conf->num_bd buffer descriptors (command from conf, status BD_DONE | BD_EXTD | BD_CONT | BD_INTR with BD_WRAP added to the last, count conf->period, buffer address conf->saddr + conf->period * i), sets the channel control block's base and current BD pointers to the physical address of the channel's descriptors, builds a zeroed channel context (program counter from the firmware's mcu_2_app_addr, the event mask in gReg[0] or gReg[1] (conf->event above 32 uses gReg[0] with the event modulo 32), conf->daddr in gReg[6] and conf->word_length in gReg[7]), prepares buffer descriptor 0 to write that context into the SDMA data memory at the channel's offset, starts channel 0 with a write to SDMAARM_HSTART and returns 0 without waiting for or checking the context load (the wait loop is compiled out with #if 0).

functions.name: mv_rtc_gettime
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is the mv_rtc device with an initialized softc, ts points to a writable struct timespec. Postcondition: the function takes the RTC softc lock (MV_RTC_LOCK, line 258), then loops: read RTC_TIME into val, DELAY(100), read RTC_TIME into val_check, and repeat while the unsigned difference (val_check - val) is greater than 1 (line 268). Because the subtraction is unsigned, a second read that is smaller than the first (for example val_check == val - 1) wraps to a huge value and also makes the loop repeat; the loop exits only when val_check equals val or val + 1. It then releases the lock, stores val_check in ts->tv_sec and 0 in ts->tv_nsec, and returns 0 (the only return statement is at line 276). It takes no references and allocates nothing.

functions.name: fdt_win_process
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: child is a phandle of a device-tree node. Postcondition: loops over the soc_nodes table (entries with a non-NULL compat, line 1808). For each entry it skips the entry when ofw_bus_node_status_okay(child) is 0 or the child is not compatible with that entry's compat string; otherwise it calls fdt_win_process_child(child, &soc_nodes[i], 'reg') and returns that call's result at once if it is nonzero (line 1818). If the loop ends without a nonzero result, including when no entry matched, it returns 0 (line 1821). It handles only the one child passed in, not every node of the tree. The nonzero values come from fdt_win_process_child: ENXIO when fdt_addrsize_cells fails on the parent or when the matching entry has a NULL decode_handler (after the entry's valid_handler, if any, accepted), ENOMEM when the parent's address-cells plus size-cells exceed the local 8-cell reg buffer, EINVAL when OF_getprop of 'reg' returns <= 0 or the entry's valid_handler returns 0 (lines 1832-1855). On success the callee also calls the entry's decode_handler (and the dump handler when MV_DUMP_WIN is set and one exists). It allocates no memory and takes no locks in this function.

functions.name: fdt_win_setup
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the device tree is readable. Postcondition: it finds the root node with OF_finddevice('/') and calls panic if that returns -1 (line 1872-1873); it sets the global platform_io_coherent to true when the root is compatible with 'marvell,armada380' (line 1876-1877). It then walks the children of the root, and later of the first simple-bus node and of a nested simple-bus node found under it. For each child it calls fdt_win_process(child) and returns its nonzero result immediately; if the child is compatible with 'marvell,armada-370-pcie' it also calls fdt_win_process_child on each of its children with the PCIe soc_nodes entry and the 'assigned-addresses' property and returns any nonzero result (lines 1886-1902). Returns ENXIO when no simple-bus under the root is found (line 1912); returns 0 when the nested simple-bus search under the first simple-bus finds nothing (line 1923) or when the walk finishes (line 1928). Nonzero values from the child calls are ENXIO, ENOMEM or EINVAL as described for fdt_win_process_child. Side effects of the callees (window decode handlers) are applied to children processed before a failure. No allocation or locking in this function.

functions.name: tegra_bo_create
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: drm is a DRM device, size is the requested size in bytes, res_bo is a writable output pointer. Postcondition: if size == 0 (size is size_t, so the test size <= 0 only catches 0) it returns -EINVAL with no allocation (line 208-209). Otherwise it mallocs a zeroed tegra_bo with M_WAITOK (cannot return NULL), rounds size up to a page multiple, and calls drm_gem_object_init; on nonzero it frees bo and returns that error (215-218). Then drm_gem_create_mmap_offset; on nonzero it calls drm_gem_object_release, frees bo and returns the error (220-223). Then it stores the result of cdev_pager_allocate in bo->cdev_pager (result not checked) and calls tegra_bo_alloc (allocates the page array, contiguous pages and pager pages); on nonzero it calls tegra_bo_free_object(&bo->gem_obj) and returns that error (229-231). tegra_bo_free_object runs drm_gem_free_mmap_offset, drm_gem_object_release, tegra_bo_destruct, frees bo->m and bo. In that failure path tegra_bo_destruct loops over bo->npages looking up pages in the pager (lines 65-72) even when tegra_bo_alloc failed before pages were inserted, so that cleanup is not shown to be correct for a failure of the contiguous allocation or pager init. On success it sets *res_bo = bo and returns 0 (234-235); *res_bo is not written on any error return.

functions.name: tegra_xhci_probe
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is a newbus device with an OFW node. Postcondition: returns ENXIO if ofw_bus_status_okay(dev) is false (line 904-905). Otherwise it calls ofw_bus_search_compatible(dev, compat_data) and checks the ocd_data field of the returned entry (line 907). That helper returns NULL only when its compat argument is NULL; here compat_data is a static non-NULL table ending in a {NULL, 0} entry (tegra_xhci.c:358-362), so when no ocd_str matches the helper returns that terminating entry, whose ocd_data is 0. If ocd_data is nonzero (the matching tegra124-xusb or tegra210-xusb entry) it calls device_set_desc(dev, 'Nvidia Tegra XHCI controller') and returns BUS_PROBE_DEFAULT; otherwise it returns ENXIO (line 911). No other return paths; no memory or locks are touched.

functions.name: rk32xx_start_ap
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: id is the CPU number, node its OFW cpu node, reg points to the first cell of its reg property; it reads and writes the globals running_cpus, psci_mask and pmu_mask. Postcondition, in order: returns false if ofw_bus_node_status_okay(node) is 0 (line 126-127); returns true immediately for id == 0 with no state change (130-131); returns false if running_cpus >= mp_ncpus (133-134); otherwise increments running_cpus (135) and computes mask = 1 << (*reg & 0x0f). Under INVARIANTS only, it prints a warning if the mask already appears in pmu_mask or psci_mask; it does not return false for that. It then reads the 'enable-method' property: if the read length is > 0 and the string equals 'psci', it sets mask in psci_mask first (146), then calls psci_cpu_on(*reg, physical address of mpentry, id); if that does not return PSCI_RETVAL_SUCCESS it prints 'Failed to start CPU' and returns false (so running_cpus and psci_mask have already been updated in that failure case), else returns true. For any other or missing enable-method it sets mask in pmu_mask and returns true (155-156); no PMU start happens in this function.

functions.name: am335x_pwm_config_ecap
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: unit selects an am335x_ecap device, period and duty are signed ints in timer ticks. Postcondition: devclass_get_device(devclass_find(am335x_ecap_driver.name), unit) is tried first and ENXIO is returned if it gives NULL (line 112-114). Then EINVAL is returned if duty > period (signed compare, so a negative duty is not rejected here) or if period == 0 (116-120); no lock is taken and no register is touched on those returns. A negative period is not rejected either (it only fails if duty > period). Otherwise it takes PWM_LOCK on the device softc, reads ECCTL2 and writes it back with the APWM mode, free-run and SYNCO_SEL bits ORed in, writes period - 1 to CAP3, duty to CAP4 and 0 to TSCTR, releases PWM_LOCK and returns 0 (122-139). The function does not check the register writes and has no other return paths.

functions.name: ti_edma3_enable_event_intr
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ch is an unsigned channel number. This function is compiled only under #ifdef notyet (ti_edma3.c:280-296), so it is absent from a normal build. Postcondition: if ch >= TI_EDMA3_NUM_DMA_CHS (64) it returns EINVAL without writing any register (286-287). Otherwise it writes 1 << ch to the shadow-region-0 interrupt-enable-set register TI_EDMA3CC_S_IESR(0) when ch < 32, or 1 << (ch - 32) to TI_EDMA3CC_S_IESRH(0) when ch >= 32, and returns 0 (289-294).

functions.name: ti_edma3_request_dma_ch
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ch, tccn, eqn are unsigned ints; tccn is not used anywhere in the body. Postcondition: if ch >= 64 (TI_EDMA3_NUM_DMA_CHS) it returns EINVAL and writes nothing (303-304). Otherwise it does read-modify-write on hardware registers: sets bit ch of DRAE(0) (ch < 32) or bit ch-32 of DRAEH(0); in DMAQNUM(ch >> 3) clears the 4-bit field for ch and sets it to (eqn & 7) (only the low 3 bits of eqn are used, line 90); in the PaRAM OPT register for ch clears the TCC field and sets it to ch & 0x3F (the TCC is taken from ch, not from tccn, lines 324-327); then returns 0. No locks are taken.

functions.name: ti_edma3_request_qdma_ch
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ch, tccn, eqn are unsigned ints; tccn is not used. Postcondition: if ch >= TI_EDMA3_NUM_DMA_CHS (64, not the QDMA channel count of 8) it returns EINVAL and writes nothing (337-338). Otherwise it ORs 1 << ch into QRAE(0) (a 32-bit shift whose result is undefined in C for ch >= 32, and QDMA channels are only 0-7), ORs (eqn & 7) << (ch * 4) into the QDMAQNUM register without first clearing the old field, and clears then sets the TCC field of PaRAM OPT(ch) to ch & 0x3F, then returns 0 (340-356). The range check therefore admits channel numbers 8-63 that do not name a QDMA channel, and for those the shifts act on bits outside the intended fields.

functions.name: ti_edma3_enable_transfer_manual
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ch is an unsigned channel number. Postcondition: if ch >= 64 it returns EINVAL and writes nothing (362-363). Otherwise it writes the event-set bit for ch to the shadow-region-0 register TI_EDMA3CC_S_ESR(0) (1 << ch) when ch < 32, or 1 << (ch - 32) to TI_EDMA3CC_S_ESRH(0), and returns 0 (366-372).

functions.name: ti_edma3_enable_transfer_qdma
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ch is an unsigned channel number. Postcondition: if ch >= TI_EDMA3_NUM_QDMA_CHS (8) it returns EINVAL and writes nothing (378-379). Otherwise it writes 1 << ch to the shadow-region-0 register TI_EDMA3CC_S_QEESR(0) and returns 0 (381-384).

functions.name: ti_edma3_enable_transfer_event
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ch is an unsigned channel number. Postcondition: if ch >= 64 it returns EINVAL and writes nothing (390-391). Otherwise, in shadow region 0, it writes the bit for ch (1 << ch for ch < 32, 1 << (ch - 32) for ch >= 32) to three registers in this order: SECR (SECRH) to clear the secondary event, EMCR (EMCRH) to clear the event-miss bit, and EESR (EESRH) to set the event-enable bit (395-403). These are write-one-to-act registers, not read-modify-write, so other channels' bits are not affected by the writes; it then returns 0.

functions.name: enable_cpu_feat
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: stage contains only bits in CPU_FEAT_STAGE_MASK (MPASS at line 51, a debug-only assertion); it runs on the current CPU and reads its midr via get_midr(). Postcondition: nothing is returned; it iterates every feature in the cpu_feat_set linker set. For each feature: (1) when stage == CPU_FEAT_EARLY_BOOT and the current CPU id is 0, it fetches the boolean tunable hw.feat.<feat_name> and if present ORs CPU_FEAT_USER_ENABLED or CPU_FEAT_USER_DISABLED into feat_flags (58-70); this happens before the stage test, so it also applies to features of other stages. (2) It then does 'continue' (no further processing and no feat_disabled call) if the feature's stage bits differ from stage (73-74), or if it is CPU_FEAT_SYSTEM scoped and the current CPU id is not 0 (77-79). (3) Otherwise it calls feat_check(feat, midr) if non-NULL, else assumes FEAT_DEFAULT_ENABLE, and jumps to the label next, skipping feat_has_errata and feat_enable, if the status is FEAT_ALWAYS_DISABLE, the user-disabled flag is set, or the status is FEAT_DEFAULT_DISABLE without the user-enabled flag (87-100). (4) Otherwise it starts with ERRATA_NONE, calls feat_has_errata (if non-NULL) and sets ERRATA_AFFECTED when it returns true; if affected and cpu_feat_check_cb is registered, it asks the callback for each listed erratum in order and, on the first result other than ERRATA_UNKNOWN, takes that status and narrows the list to that one erratum (107-133). (5) It calls feat_enable(feat, status, list, count) (not checked for NULL) and sets feat_enabled = true if it returns nonzero (138-140); a zero return leaves feat_enabled unchanged. (6) At label next, if feat_enabled is still false and feat_disabled is non-NULL it calls feat_disabled(feat) (143-144); this runs for features that reached next or finished step 5 but not for those skipped in step 2. It takes no locks and allocates nothing.

functions.name: cpu_minidumpsys
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: di is the dump device, state supplies dump_bitset and msgbufp; the caller is the kernel dump path (live or panic). The function is named cpu_minidumpsys (the packet name minidump_dump does not exist in this file); it uses the file statics kdh, dumpsize, tmpbuffer, fragsz, dump_va. Steps: it starts retry_count at 0 and at label retry (line 161) increments it, zeroes error and pmapsize and snapshots kva_end = kernel_vm_end. Pass 1 walks va from VM_MIN_KERNEL_ADDRESS to kva_end in L2_SIZE steps, adds PAGE_SIZE to pmapsize per step, skips steps where pmap_get_tables fails, and for a 1GB L1 block, 2MB L2 block or an L2 table adds the dumpable pages to state->dump_bitset (a 1GB block also adds 511 extra pages to pmapsize and skips va ahead; L3 pages are added only if in the DMAP range) (176-211). It then computes dumpsize from pmapsize, the msgbuf, dump_avail, the bitmap, one PAGE_SIZE per bitmap page that is in the DMAP range and dumpable (any other bitmap page is removed from the bitmap via vm_page_dump_drop) plus one header page (213-225), calls dumpsys_pb_init, fills mdhdr, calls dump_init_header and dump_start; a nonzero error goes to fail (252-254). It then writes, each followed by goto fail on a nonzero blk_write error: the header page, the msgbuf, the dump_avail page, the bitmap (262-284); then pass 2 over the same va range writing one PAGE_SIZE record per L2 step: a zero page when pmap_get_tables fails, 512 synthesized L3-style pages for a 1GB L1 block, one synthesized page of 512 entries for a 2MB L2 block, otherwise the physical page the L2 entry points to (if it is in the DMAP range and dumpable) or a zero page (288-359); then every page in the bitmap (362-366), then blk_flush and dump_finish (368-374). On success it prints 'Dump complete' and returns 0 (376-377). At fail: a negative error is negated; ENOSPC with retry_count < 5 prints a message and jumps back to retry (rebuilding the bitmap and sizes, so at most 4 re-runs; the bitmap from the failed pass is not cleared), ENOSPC at retry_count >= 5 prints 'Dump failed.', ECANCELED prints 'Dump aborted', E2BIG prints a partition-too-small message, anything else prints the error number; each of these returns the (positive) error (379-399). It takes no locks and allocates no memory; it can leave the dump incomplete on any failure return.

functions.name: wait_for_aps
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: called on the boot CPU after the application processors have been released; reads the globals aps_started and mp_ncpus. Postcondition: loops with i from 0 while i < 2000 and a local started initially 0 (line 142). Each iteration atomically loads aps_started into nstarted and returns true if nstarted == mp_ncpus - 1 (145-147), before any delay. Otherwise, if nstarted > started it resets i to 0 and records started = nstarted (153-156), then calls DELAY(1000) (157). When i reaches 2000 the loop ends and it returns false (160). Hence DELAY(1000) runs on each iteration that does not return true, including iterations that observed progress; the timeout is about 2000 consecutive iterations without a larger count (roughly two seconds of delay plus loop time), not a fixed total. It takes no locks and allocates nothing.

functions.name: start_cpu_fdt
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: node is a CPU node, reg points to addr_size pcells (1 or 2) holding the CPU's MPIDR, id is unused; reads the globals psci_present, fdt_cpuid, vm_ndomains and cpuid_to_pcpu[]. Postcondition: target_cpu = reg[0], or (reg[0] << 32) | reg[1] when addr_size == 2 (653-657); cpuid is 0 if is_boot_cpu(target_cpu), else the current fdt_cpuid (659-662). If PSCI is absent and cpuid != 0 it returns false when OF_getprop_alloc of 'enable-method' returns <= 0 (671-673), or when that property is not the string 'spin-table' (the property buffer is freed with OF_prop_free before that return, 675-678); otherwise the buffer is freed (680), populate_release_addr is called, and if release_addr is still 0 it prints a message and returns false (681-686; no buffer is held at that point). It then calls start_cpu(cpuid, target_cpu, 0, release_addr) and returns false if that fails (689-690), with fdt_cpuid and the domain data unchanged. On success it increments fdt_cpuid unless the CPU is the boot CPU (695-696), sets domain to 0 if vm_ndomains == 1 or if OF_getencprop of 'numa-node-id' returns <= 0, otherwise to the property value (699-701), stores it in cpuid_to_pcpu[cpuid]->pc_domain, adds cpuid to cpuset_domain[domain] only if domain < MAXMEMDOM (702-704), and returns true (705).

functions.name: pmap_kremove_device
