Otherwise it calls scsi_error_action, takes error = err_action & SS_ERRMASK, and the paths then differ: (a) SS_START on a sequential-access device sets *action_string and jumps to the exit with that errno (1696-1701); (b) if the action is SS_START or higher and ccb is a recovery CCB that was a START_STOP_UNIT (for SS_START) or TEST_UNIT_READY (for SS_TUR), err_action is replaced by SS_RETRY|SSQ_DECREMENT_COUNT|EIO and *relsim_flags = RELSIM_RELEASE_AFTER_TIMEOUT, *timeout = 500 are stored (1706-1714); (c) if SSQ_DECREMENT_COUNT is set it decrements retry_count when it is > 0 and the periph is not CAM_PERIPH_INVALID, else sets *action_string 'Retries exhausted' and jumps to the exit with the errno (1721-1728); (d) for SS_START or higher it allocates a recovery CCB with xpt_alloc_ccb_nowait, on NULL sets *action_string 'Can't allocate recovery CCB' and jumps to the exit (1731-1740), else clears CAM_DEV_QFRZN on ccb and copies it into the new CCB keeping the new CCB's alloc_flags (1745-1752); (e) the switch on err_action & SS_MASK: SS_NOP sets *action_string 'No recovery action needed' and error = 0; SS_RETRY sets error = ERESTART; SS_FAIL leaves error as the errno from the sense action; SS_START sets CAM_PERIPH_RECOVERY_INPROG and rewrites ccb into a START STOP UNIT command; SS_TUR sets CAM_PERIPH_RECOVERY_INPROG (and RECOVERY_WAIT with retries = 120 when SSQ_MANY is set and RECOVERY_WAIT_FAILED is not, else retries = 1), sets *action_string ('Polling...' or 'Testing device for readiness'), rewrites ccb into TEST UNIT READY and stores *relsim_flags = RELSIM_RELEASE_AFTER_TIMEOUT and *timeout = 500; any other value panics (1755-1837); (f) for SS_START or higher it lowers the CCB priority, sets CAM_DEV_QFREEZE and saved_ccb_ptr = the copy, stores *orig = the copy and sets error = ERESTART (1839-1852). At the exit (all paths of the non-in-progress branch) *action = err_action is stored (1856). A nonzero return other than ERESTART is the errno from the sense action (for example EIO); it can also be 0 when err_action is SS_NOP.

functions.name: cam_periph_mapmem
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ccb is a CCB owned by the caller, mapinfo is writable; the caller may sleep (M_WAITOK allocations); buffer addresses in the CCB are user addresses. Postcondition (cam_periph.c:806-1000): mapinfo is zeroed first (814). maxmap becomes DFLTPHYS if 0, or maxphys if larger than maxphys (815-818). A switch on func_code builds up to two (pointer, length, direction) buffer descriptors: XPT_DEV_MATCH returns EINVAL if match_buf_len == 0 (821-825), otherwise describes the patterns buffer (if pattern_buf_len > 0, direction out) and matches buffer, and raises maxmap to maxphys (844); XPT_SCSI_IO, XPT_CONT_TARGET_IO, XPT_ATA_IO, XPT_NVME_IO and XPT_NVME_ADMIN return 0 with no work if the direction is CAM_DIR_NONE and EINVAL if the CAM_DATA flags are not CAM_DATA_VADDR, else one buffer; XPT_MMC_IO returns 0 with no work if CAM_DIR_NONE, else two buffers (the mmc_data pointer itself and cmd.data->data, with length cmd.data->len), with no CAM_DATA check; XPT_SMP_IO describes two buffers (request out, response in) with no direction or flag checks; XPT_DEV_ADVINFO returns 0 with no work if bufsiz == 0, else one buffer and maxmap = maxphys; any other func_code returns EINVAL (846-915). It then returns E2BIG, printing a message, if any length exceeds maxmap (923-929). For each buffer it saves the user pointer in mapinfo->orig[i]; for lengths <= periph_mapmem_thresh and func_code != XPT_MMC_IO it mallocs a kernel copy (M_WAITOK), copying the user data in with copyin unless the direction is CAM_DIR_IN (then zeroed); if copyin fails it frees the copy, restores the user pointer and goes to fail (942-955); otherwise it takes a pbuf from pbuf_zone, sets b_iocmd, calls vmapbuf, and on failure frees the pbuf and goes to fail, else stores the mapped b_data into the CCB pointer (961-974). After all buffers it calls BUF_KERNPROC on each mapped pbuf, sets mapinfo->num_bufs_used = numbufs and returns 0 (982-988). At fail, buffers 0..i-1 (those completed before the failing one) are unmapped/freed and their CCB pointers restored to the user values, then it returns EACCES (990-999); mapinfo->num_bufs_used stays 0. On the early EINVAL and E2BIG returns nothing was allocated and no CCB pointer changed. The no-op 0 returns leave num_bufs_used 0 and the CCB untouched. The caller releases a successful mapping with cam_periph_unmapmem.

functions.name: cam_periph_unmapmem
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ccb and mapinfo are the same ones passed to a successful cam_periph_mapmem, with the CCB's func_code, lengths and CCB data pointers not changed (for XPT_MMC_IO the cmd.data pointer must still be valid), unless mapinfo->num_bufs_used is <= 0 (cam_periph.c:1007-1110). Postcondition: if mapinfo->num_bufs_used <= 0 it returns 0 without touching anything (1014-1017). Otherwise it rebuilds the same buffer descriptor list from ccb->ccb_h.func_code (DEV_MATCH, SCSI_IO, CONT_TARGET_IO, ATA_IO, MMC_IO, SMP_IO, NVME_IO, NVME_ADMIN, DEV_ADVINFO); for any other func_code it sets numbufs = 0 and so does nothing and returns 0 (1080-1082; it does not return an error). For each buffer it either (pbuf) calls vunmapbuf and uma_zfree on mapinfo->bp[i], or (malloc copy) if the direction is not CAM_DIR_OUT copies the kernel copy to the saved user address with copyout (recording only the first copyout error, 1094-1100) and then frees the copy; in both cases it sets the CCB pointer back to mapinfo->orig[i] (1106). A copyout failure does not stop the loop, so all remaining buffers are still unmapped, freed and restored. It returns the first nonzero copyout error (typically EFAULT) or 0 (1085-1109). mapinfo->num_bufs_used and the bp/orig arrays are not cleared.

functions.name: ctl_nvme_check_ooa
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: lun->lun_lock is held by the caller (mtx_assert at 11217, debug-only), pending_io is an NVMe or NVMe-admin I/O (CTL_IO_ASSERT at 11215), *starting_io is NULL or the OOA-queue entry at which to start (ooa_io = *starting_io), aborted_io is writable. Postcondition (ctl.c:11210-11295): *aborted_io is set to NULL first (11219). (1) If pending_io has CTL_FLAG_ABORT it returns CTL_ACTION_PASS, leaving *starting_io unchanged (11226-11227). (2) If *starting_io is non-NULL and its FUSE field is NVME_FUSE_FIRST: if pending_io's FUSE field is NVME_FUSE_SECOND it returns CTL_ACTION_FUSED with *starting_io unchanged (11255-11262); otherwise it marks that first-half I/O with ctl_nvme_set_missing_fused_command, sets *aborted_io to it and falls through to the scan in step 4 (11265-11266). (3) Otherwise, with pending_io's FUSE field: NVME_FUSE_FIRST returns CTL_ACTION_SKIP; NVME_FUSE_SECOND (no matching first half) marks pending_io as missing-fused, sets *aborted_io = pending_io and returns CTL_ACTION_SKIP, in both cases leaving *starting_io unchanged; any other fuse value falls through to the scan (11268-11277). (4) The scan walks the OOA list from ooa_io (including the aborted first half itself, if there was one) via LIST_NEXT looking for an entry whose FUSE field is NVME_FUSE_SECOND; if found it stores it in *starting_io and returns CTL_ACTION_BLOCK (11284-11290); if none is found (or ooa_io is NULL) it sets *starting_io = NULL and returns CTL_ACTION_PASS (11293-11294). The lock is neither taken nor released here. So a pending first half only yields SKIP when *starting_io is not itself a first half; when it is, the old first half is aborted and the result is BLOCK or PASS.

functions.name: ctl_check_for_blockage
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: pending_io and ooa_io are SCSI I/Os (CTL_IO_ASSERT, debug-only), serialize_row is the serialize-table row for pending_io, lun->be_lun is valid and the caller holds the LUN lock (not asserted here). Postcondition (ctl.c:11698-11795), checks in this order, each returning at once: (1) CTL_ACTION_OVERLAP if both I/Os are CTL_TAG_UNTAGGED, from the same targ_port and initid, and ooa_io has neither CTL_FLAG_ABORT nor CTL_FLAG_STATUS_SENT; (2) CTL_ACTION_OVERLAP_TAG if both are tagged with equal tag_num, same targ_port and initid, and ooa_io has neither flag; (3) CTL_ACTION_PASS if pending_io has CTL_TAG_HEAD_OF_QUEUE; (4) CTL_ACTION_BLOCK if ooa_io is CTL_TAG_ORDERED or CTL_TAG_HEAD_OF_QUEUE; (5) CTL_ACTION_PASS if ooa_io->scsiio.seridx == CTL_SERIDX_INVLD; then a switch on serialize_row[ooa_io->scsiio.seridx]: CTL_SER_PASS returns PASS; CTL_SER_SEQ returns ctl_seq_check(ooa_io, pending_io) when be_lun->serseq != CTL_LUN_SERSEQ_OFF, else falls through to PASS; CTL_SER_EXTENTOPT returns PASS if the queue algorithm field of MODE_CTRL is SCP_QUEUE_ALG_UNRESTRICTED, else falls through to CTL_SER_EXTENT, which returns ctl_extent_check(ooa_io, pending_io, serseq == CTL_LUN_SERSEQ_ON); CTL_SER_BLOCKOPT returns PASS for the unrestricted queue algorithm, else falls through to CTL_SER_BLOCK, which returns CTL_ACTION_BLOCK; any other table value reaches __assert_unreachable() (11770-11794). ctl_seq_check returns PASS if ooa_io has CTL_FLAG_SERSEQ_DONE, BLOCK if lba1 + len1 == lba2 (lba/len of ooa_io and pending_io), else PASS (11679-11695). ctl_extent_check first calls ctl_extent_check_unmap(ooa_io, ...): for a non-UNMAP ooa_io that returns CTL_ACTION_SKIP and ctl_extent_check goes on to compare the two LBA ranges with ctl_extent_check_lba (BLOCK if they overlap, else PASS; when the seq flag is true and ooa_io lacks SERSEQ_DONE, ooa_io's range is extended by one block); for an UNMAP ooa_io it returns BLOCK if the unmap data is not yet available (no CTL_FLAG_ALLOCATED or null pointer) or any descriptor overlaps pending_io's range, else PASS (11657-11675, 11624-11654). So the function does not return SKIP itself; the earlier return values depend on the tag and flag tests above.

functions.name: ctl_scsi_try_unblock_io
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: lun->lun_lock is held (mtx_assert, debug-only); io is a SCSI I/O; skip says the current blocker no longer counts. If io->io_hdr.blocker is non-NULL, io sits on that blocker's blocked_queue. Postcondition (ctl.c:11862-11955; returns nothing): if io->io_hdr.blocker is NULL it returns at once (11874-11875). Otherwise obio = bio = the blocker, and with skip the check starts at the OOA entry after the blocker (11877-11879). It calls ctl_check_ooa(lun, io, &bio). If that returns CTL_ACTION_BLOCK, io stays blocked: when ctl_check_ooa left bio different from obio, io is moved from obio's blocked_queue to bio's blocked_queue and io_hdr.blocker is set to bio, otherwise nothing is changed (11881-11890). For every other action io is first removed from obio's blocked_queue and its blocker set to NULL (11894-11895), then: CTL_ACTION_PASS or CTL_ACTION_SKIP: if io is FROM_OTHER_SC and ha_mode != CTL_HA_MODE_XFER it clears CTL_FLAG_IO_ACTIVE and sends a CTL_MSG_R2R message to the peer, leaving io on the OOA queue (11902-11910); otherwise it looks up the command entry, runs ctl_scsiio_lun_check and on nonzero calls ctl_done(io), else sets CTL_FLAG_IS_WAS_ON_RTR and calls ctl_enqueue_rtr(io) (11918-11925). CTL_ACTION_OVERLAP and CTL_ACTION_OVERLAP_TAG set the overlapped-command or overlapped-tag sense and go to the error code: for a FROM_OTHER_SC io with ha_mode != CTL_HA_MODE_XFER it calls ctl_try_unblock_others(lun, io, TRUE), removes io from the OOA list, copies the sense data into a CTL_MSG_BAD_JUJU message, sends it with M_WAITOK and frees io with ctl_free_io (not ctl_done) (11937-11949); otherwise it calls ctl_done(io) (11952). Any other action value reaches __assert_unreachable().

functions.name: ctl_isc_mode_sync
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: msg is a received HA message of len bytes, softc is the ctl softc; the caller holds neither softc->ctl_lock nor any lun_lock. Postcondition (ctl.c:1401-1450; returns nothing): if len < offsetof(struct ctl_ha_msg_mode, data[0]) it prints a message, calls ctl_ha_msg_abort(CTL_HA_CHAN_CTL) and returns; the same happens if len < offsetof(struct ctl_ha_msg_mode, data[page_len]) for the message's page_len (1407-1419). Otherwise it takes ctl_lock; if targ_mapped_lun >= ctl_max_luns or the LUN pointer is NULL it releases only ctl_lock and returns (1421-1427); else it takes the lun_lock and drops ctl_lock, and if the LUN has CTL_LUN_DISABLED it releases lun_lock and returns (1428-1433). It scans the LUN's CTL_NUM_MODE_PAGES mode page index for an entry with the same page_code (masked by SMPH_PC_MASK) and subpage; if none matches it releases lun_lock and returns (1434-1443). Otherwise it copies min(the local page_len, msg->mode.page_len) bytes of msg->mode.data into that entry's page_data (1444-1445), computes ctl_get_initindex(&msg->hdr.nexus) and, unless it is (uint32_t)-1, calls ctl_est_ua_all(lun, initidx, CTL_UA_MODE_CHANGE), which takes the sender's initiator index as its 'except' argument, and finally releases lun_lock (1446-1449). Nothing is allocated; page_len is not bounded against the size of msg->mode.data other than by the len check.

functions.name: ctl_ioctl
functions.prose_contract: Slice cut the head and tail: static int ctl_ioctl(struct cdev *dev, u_long cmd, caddr_t addr, int flag, struct thread *td) is at ctl.c:2583-3633. Precondition: dev->si_drv1 is the CTL softc and addr points to the argument structure for cmd, which the function both reads and writes. Postcondition: retval starts at 0 and the function has a switch on cmd. It returns retval at 3632, except that CTL_LUN_MAP returns ENXIO directly (without the lock held) when lm->port is outside [port_min, port_max) or has no port (3496-3501) and when a non-UNSET mapping names a LUN that does not exist (3520-3521). Cases: CTL_IO returns ctl_ioctl_io's result. CTL_ENABLE_PORT, CTL_DISABLE_PORT and CTL_SET_PORT_WWNS walk the port list under ctl_lock: a port is acted on if entry->port_type is CTL_PORT_NONE and targ_port matches (then the loop stops after that port), or if entry->port_type & port->port_type is nonzero; for CTL_SET_PORT_WWNS the second kind of match prints a message, sets retval = EINVAL and stops the loop without changing the port, so a port-type match always gives EINVAL for SET_PORT_WWNS (2615-2670); enable/disable drop ctl_lock around ctl_port_online/ctl_port_offline. CTL_GET_OOA returns EINVAL for alloc_len == 0, alloc_num == 0, alloc_len != alloc_num * sizeof(struct ctl_ooa_entry), or (without CTL_OOA_FLAG_ALL_LUNS) a lun_num out of range or absent (2681-2712); otherwise it allocates entries, fills them via ctl_ioctl_fill_ooa under ctl_lock, sets fill_num = min(found, alloc_num) and fill_len, copies the entries out (retval = the copyout result), then sets cur_bt and dropped_num/status (CTL_OOA_NEED_MORE_SPACE when found > alloc_num, else CTL_OOA_OK) even if the copyout failed, and frees entries (2700-2747). CTL_DELAY_IO sets only delay_info->status: NOT_IMPLEMENTED when CTL_IO_DELAY is not compiled in, else INVALID_LUN (return path leaves it) or OK/INVALID_TYPE then INVALID_LOC, and when the LUN exists and the location is valid the delay type/seconds are stored in the LUN even if the type was invalid (2755-2790); retval stays 0. CTL_ERROR_INJECT returns EINVAL for a bad LUN (2803-2811), otherwise appends a copy of the descriptor to the LUN's error_list, assigns the next error_serial to it and to the caller's copy, retval 0. CTL_ERROR_INJECT_DELETE returns EINVAL for a bad LUN or when no descriptor with the serial exists, otherwise frees all descriptors with that serial (2847-2874). CTL_DUMP_STRUCTS prints PR keys of enabled LUNs, ports and frontends and returns 0. CTL_LUN_REQ finds the backend by name; backend not found, args too long (> CTL_MAX_ARGS_LEN), copyin failure or an nvlist unpack failure set lun_req->status = CTL_LUN_ERROR and an error_str with retval left 0 (2949-2983); otherwise it calls backend->ioctl (retval is its result), destroys the args nvlist, and packs result_nvl out to lun_req->result, with CTL_LUN_ERROR set on pack, size or copyout failure (those error returns do not destroy result_nvl, 2996-3019). CTL_LUN_LIST builds an XML sbuf of fixed size alloc_len under ctl_lock; sbuf allocation failure, or running out of space, sets list->status (CTL_LUN_LIST_ERROR or CTL_LUN_LIST_NEED_MORE_SPACE) and leaves retval 0; on success it copies out and retval is the copyout result (3064-3206); in that loop a LUN whose backend is NULL is skipped with continue at 3106 before the mtx_unlock(&lun->lun_lock) at 3181. CTL_ISCSI and CTL_NVMF forward to the frontend's ioctl or set status to an error when the frontend is missing; CTL_PORT_REQ and CTL_PORT_LIST are analogous to LUN_REQ and LUN_LIST for ports (3242-3490); CTL_LUN_MAP sets up or removes LUN mappings and announces the port (3491-3531); CTL_GET_LUN_STATS and CTL_GET_PORT_STATS copy stats out until alloc_len would be exceeded (3532-3597). Any other cmd sets retval = ENOTTY (3628). Partly read: the bodies of CTL_PORT_REQ (3242-3334) and CTL_PORT_LIST (3335-3490) were only skimmed by their returns, not read line by line.

functions.name: ctl_decode_lun
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: encoded is any 64-bit REPORT LUNS style LUN field. Postcondition: it writes encoded big-endian into an 8-byte array lun[] (so lun[0] holds the top byte) and returns a decoded uint32_t, starting from 0xffffffff (ctl.c:3761-3804). Switch on lun[0] & 0xc0: address method 0x00 (peripheral) returns lun[1] when (lun[0] & 0x3f) == 0 and lun[2..7] are all zero; address method 0x40 (flat) returns ((lun[0] & 0x3f) << 8) + lun[1] when lun[2..7] are all zero; address method 0xc0 (extended) switches on lun[0] & 0x0f: for 0x02 it switches on lun[0] & 0x30: 0x00 returns lun[1] (the other bytes are not checked), 0x10 returns (lun[1] << 16) + (lun[2] << 8) + lun[3] (bytes 4-7 not checked), 0x20 returns (lun[2] << 24) + (lun[3] << 16) + (lun[4] << 8) + lun[5] only when lun[1], lun[6] and lun[7] are zero, and 0x30 and any 0x20 case failing the zero test leave 0xffffffff; for extended address method 0x0f it explicitly sets 0xffffffff and any other extended method leaves 0xffffffff. Method 0x80 (logical unit addressing, RPL_LUNDATA_ATYP_LUN) has no case and yields 0xffffffff. Any shape failing its checks yields 0xffffffff, which is also the value for a malformed input. The shift (lun[2] << 24) is done on an int, so it overflows for lun[2] >= 0x80 (signed overflow in C). No memory, lock or reference is taken.

functions.name: ctl_pro_preempt
functions.prose_contract: Slice cut the head: static int ctl_pro_preempt(softc, lun, res_key, sa_res_key, type, residx, ctsio, cdb, param) is at ctl.c:7910-8164. Precondition: the caller does not hold lun->lun_lock; ctsio is an in-flight PERSISTENT RESERVE OUT with parsed res_key, sa_res_key, type, residx. Postcondition: it takes lun_lock at once (7918) and every return path below releases it first. Branch A (sa_res_key == 0 and lun->pr_res_idx == CTL_PR_ALL_REGISTRANTS): returns 1 after ctl_set_invalid_field and ctl_done when the scope is not SPR_LU_SCOPE or the type is > 8, 2, 4 or 0, without freeing ctsio->kern_data_ptr (7922-7945); otherwise it clears every other registrant's key with a CTL_UA_REG_PREEMPT unit attention, sets pr_key_count = 1, pr_res_type = type, sets pr_res_idx = residx unless the type is one of the all-registrants types, increments pr_generation, unlocks and sends a CTL_PR_PREEMPT HA message, then falls to return 0 (7951-7976, 8163). Branch B (sa_res_key == 0 and not all-registrants): frees kern_data_ptr, sets invalid field, ctl_done, returns 1 (7977-7988). Branch C (sa_res_key != 0 and either all-registrants or no reservation held, 7990): if res_key == sa_res_key it frees kern_data_ptr, sets invalid field, completes and returns 1 (7994-8014); else it clears every key equal to sa_res_key (pr_key_count-- and a unit attention each); if none was found it unlocks, frees kern_data_ptr, sets a reservation conflict, completes the I/O and returns CTL_RETVAL_COMPLETE (0 as the return value, 8026-8031); if found it increments pr_generation, unlocks, sends the HA message and returns 0. Branch D (sa_res_key != 0 and a reservation is held by a specific registrant): if sa_res_key equals that holder's key it checks scope and type as in branch A (invalid-field return 1 without freeing kern_data_ptr, 8052-8074), then clears the key of each registrant other than residx that equals sa_res_key, sends CTL_UA_RES_RELEASE to the rest when the reservation type changes from a registrants-only type, sets pr_res_type = type and pr_res_idx (to residx, or CTL_PR_ALL_REGISTRANTS for the all-registrants types), increments pr_generation, unlocks, sends the HA message and returns 0 (8091-8123); if sa_res_key does not equal the holder's key it clears every matching key, and when none was found it unlocks, frees kern_data_ptr, sets a reservation conflict, completes and returns 1 (8141-8147), else increments pr_generation, unlocks, sends the HA message and returns 0 (8148-8160). So the 'not found' paths return 0 in branch C and 1 in branch D, and the invalid scope/type returns do not free kern_data_ptr.

functions.name: ctl_pro_preempt_other
functions.prose_contract: Slice cut the head: static void ctl_pro_preempt_other(struct ctl_lun *lun, union ctl_ha_msg *msg) is at ctl.c:8167-8231. Precondition: msg is a PERS_ACTION/CTL_PR_PREEMPT HA message from the peer with sa_res_key, res_type and residx; the function takes no lock and has no mtx_assert, so the caller is expected to hold the LUN lock. Postcondition: returns nothing. It decodes sa_res_key and then: (1) if pr_res_idx is CTL_PR_ALL_REGISTRANTS or CTL_PR_NO_RESERVATION, or sa_res_key differs from the key of the current holder (ctl_get_prkey(lun, pr_res_idx)), then (1a) when sa_res_key == 0 it clears the key of every initiator other than msg residx that has a nonzero key and establishes CTL_UA_REG_PREEMPT for it, sets pr_key_count = 1, sets pr_res_type from the message and sets pr_res_idx = msg residx unless the type is one of the all-registrants types (then pr_res_idx is left unchanged) (8182-8195); (1b) when sa_res_key != 0 it loops over all CTL_MAX_INITIATORS slots and, for each slot whose key is not equal to sa_res_key (including slots whose key is 0, i.e. unregistered ones), calls ctl_clr_prkey, decrements pr_key_count and establishes CTL_UA_REG_PREEMPT; it changes neither pr_res_type nor pr_res_idx (8197-8204). (2) Otherwise (sa_res_key equals the holder's key) it loops over initiators other than msg residx with a nonzero key: a key equal to sa_res_key is cleared with pr_key_count-- and CTL_UA_REG_PREEMPT, while other registrants get CTL_UA_RES_RELEASE when the message's type differs from the old pr_res_type and the old type is SPR_TYPE_WR_EX_RO or SPR_TYPE_EX_AC_RO; then pr_res_type is set from the message and pr_res_idx to the message's residx, or to CTL_PR_ALL_REGISTRANTS for the all-registrants types (8207-8227). In all three branches pr_generation is incremented once at the end (8229). It takes no lock, allocates nothing and sends no message.

functions.name: ctl_backend_ramdisk_scsi_config_write
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: io is a SCSI I/O for a ramdisk LUN; the function contains no CTL_IO_ASSERT and does not validate the opcode beforehand (ctl_backend_ramdisk.c:819-872). Postcondition: it switches on io->scsiio.cdb[0] and returns retval, which is 0 except in the default case. SYNCHRONIZE_CACHE and SYNCHRONIZE_CACHE_16 set success and call ctl_config_write_done. START_STOP_UNIT: if any power-condition bits (SSS_PC_MASK) are set it sets success and completes without touching the LUN; otherwise with SSS_START it calls ctl_lun_has_media when SSS_LOEJ is also set and then ctl_start_lun, and without SSS_START it calls ctl_stop_lun and, with SSS_LOEJ, ctl_lun_ejected; it then sets success and calls ctl_config_write_done. PREVENT_ALLOW sets success and calls ctl_config_write_done (853-856). WRITE_SAME_10 and WRITE_SAME_16 call ctl_backend_ramdisk_ws(io) and UNMAP calls ctl_backend_ramdisk_unmap(io); completion of the I/O in those two cases is left to those helpers (I did not check their completion paths here). Any other opcode sets invalid-opcode sense, calls ctl_config_write_done and sets retval = CTL_RETVAL_COMPLETE, whose value is 0 (ctl_private.h:44), so the function returns 0 in every case.

functions.name: sddadump
functions.prose_contract: Slice cut the head: the function is static int sddadump(void *arg, void *virtual, off_t offset, size_t length) at mmc_da.c:2000-2065 (the packet name mmcsd_dump does not exist). Precondition: arg is a struct disk whose d_drv1 is an sdda_part with a valid softc; virtual points to at least (length / MMC_SECTOR_SIZE) * MMC_SECTOR_SIZE readable bytes; called in dump context. Postcondition: it returns ENXIO if softc->state != SDDA_STATE_NORMAL (2018-2019); returns 0 without any I/O if length / MMC_SECTOR_SIZE (a uint16_t count) is 0 (2021-2023), so a length under one sector is not an error here; returns EIO if the softc's currently selected partition is not this part (2025-2026). functions.name: brcmf_fweh_handle_if_event
functions.prose_contract: static void brcmf_fweh_handle_if_event(struct brcmf_pub *drvr, struct brcmf_event_msg *emsg, void *data) at fweh.c:127-191 (slice cut the head); it returns nothing. Precondition: data points to a struct brcmf_if_event. Postcondition: it computes is_p2pdev from the NOIF flag with the P2P-client role, or the STA role while p2pdev setup is ongoing (144-147). It returns without further action when the NOIF flag is set and it is not a p2p device (148-151), when ifidx is not below BRCMF_MAX_IFS (152-155) or when bsscfgidx is not below BRCMF_MAX_IFS (156-160). Otherwise it takes ifp = drvr->iflist[bsscfgidx] (162), which may be NULL. For BRCMF_E_IF_ADD it creates the interface with brcmf_add_if (returning if that gives an error pointer), adds it to the protocol layer unless it is a p2p device, and, when no BRCMF_E_IF handler is registered, attaches the net device and returns if that fails (164-176). For BRCMF_E_IF_CHANGE with a non-NULL ifp it calls brcmf_proto_reset_if (178-179). It then calls brcmf_fweh_call_event_handler with ifp (181-182); that helper invokes the registered handler only when ifp is non-NULL and otherwise just logs (fweh.c:106-116), so for a NULL ifp (for example a DEL or CHANGE for an unknown index) the handler is not called. For BRCMF_E_IF_DEL with a non-NULL ifp it removes the interface with brcmf_remove_interface unless the cfg80211 vif event is armed (184-189).

functions.name: brcmf_pcie_download_fw_nvram
functions.prose_contract: static int brcmf_pcie_download_fw_nvram(struct brcmf_pciedev_info *devinfo, const struct firmware *fw, void *nvram, u32 nvram_len) at pcie.c:1785-1893; the packet name brcmf_pcie_download_fw is not defined in pcie.c (the function is called at pcie.c:2295) and the slice (1797-2047) holds this function plus following ones. Precondition: fw is a loaded firmware image of at least 4 bytes and fits in device RAM; nvram, if non-NULL, was allocated by the firmware loader. Postcondition: it first calls brcmf_pcie_enter_download_state and returns that error immediately if it fails, before copying anything and before release_firmware, so in that case fw (and nvram) are not released here (1798-1800). Otherwise it copies the firmware into device RAM, reads the reset vector from its first four bytes, calls release_firmware(fw) (1811-1812) and zeroes the last RAM word (1817). If nvram is non-NULL it copies it to the top of RAM, frees it with brcmf_fw_nvram_free (1828) and, when devinfo->fwseed is set, writes a random-seed footer and random bytes below it (1830-1851); if nvram is NULL it only logs a message (1853-1855). It records the last RAM word, calls brcmf_pcie_exit_download_state(devinfo, resetintr) and returns its error if it fails, after fw and nvram were already released (1858-1864). It then polls that RAM word every 50 ms for up to BRCMF_PCIE_FW_UP_TIMEOUT until it changes; if it never changes it logs and returns -ENODEV, and a changed value outside the RAM range also returns -ENODEV (1867-1889). Otherwise it returns the result of brcmf_pcie_init_share_ram_info (1892).

functions.name: brcmf_sdio_rxglom
functions.prose_contract: static u8 brcmf_sdio_rxglom(struct brcmf_sdio *bus, u8 rxseq) at sdio.c:1514-1726; the slice (1524-1778) starts mid-function. Precondition: the caller must not already hold the func1 host claim, since the function claims and releases it itself around its bus accesses (1623-1626, 1634-1638, 1648-1651, 1666-1669, 1678-1682). Postcondition: it returns the number of subframes in the superframe that were parsed (num), or 0 on the failure paths below. If bus->glomd (a glom descriptor) is set, it parses the 16-bit sub-frame lengths from it (an empty or odd-length descriptor is treated as length 0, 1533-1541): a sub-frame length that is too small stops the parse (1548-1553), and a failed skb allocation stops it (1570-1575); if the loop ended without a valid packet chain (pnext NULL) it frees the partial glom queue with brcmf_sdio_free_glom and sets num to 0 (1593-1596), which does not call brcmf_sdio_rxfail. The descriptor skb is then freed in either case, bus->glomd cleared and cur_read.len zeroed (1599-1601). If the glom queue is non-empty, it receives the whole chain from the bus with brcmf_sdiod_recv_chain; on an error it calls brcmf_sdio_rxfail(bus, true, false), counts rxglomfail, frees the glom and returns 0 (1630-1639). It parses the super-frame header and each sub-frame header with brcmf_sdio_hdparse; if any parse returns an error it calls brcmf_sdio_rxfail, counts rxglomfail, frees the glom, zeroes cur_read.len and returns 0 (1676-1684). Otherwise it trims each sub-frame to its length, skips its data offset, drops empty ones, and passes the others to brcmf_rx_event (event channel) or brcmf_rx_frame, counting rxglompkts (1689-1720) and rxglomframes (1723). It returns num (1725); num is 0 if there was no glom at all.

functions.name: brcmf_sdio_bus_sleep
functions.prose_contract: static int brcmf_sdio_bus_sleep(struct brcmf_sdio *bus, bool sleep, bool pendok) at sdio.c:965-1018 (slice cut the head). Precondition: none is checked here; this function takes no lock itself. Postcondition: it returns err, 0 unless the KSO control (keep SDIO on) fails (1016). With save-restore enabled (bus->sr_enabled, 975): if the requested state equals bus->sleeping it jumps to end without any KSO change (977-978); otherwise, for sleep it reads CHIPCLKCSR and, if its clock-select bits are zero, writes SBSDIO_ALP_AVAIL_REQ to it (982-990), then calls brcmf_sdio_kso_control(bus, false); for wake it calls brcmf_sdio_kso_control(bus, true) (991-993). If the KSO call returns an error it logs and jumps to done, returning that error with bus->sleeping unchanged, but in the sleep case the ALP_AVAIL_REQ write may already have been made, so the clock request is not necessarily unchanged (995-998). At end (reached by the normal path and by the already-in-that-state jump): for sleep and without save-restore it calls brcmf_sdio_clkctl(bus, CLK_NONE, pendok); for wake it calls brcmf_sdio_clkctl(bus, CLK_AVAIL, pendok) and re-arms the watchdog timer with brcmf_sdio_wd_timer(bus, true) (1004-1010); then it stores bus->sleeping = sleep (1011) and returns 0. Without save-restore the KSO step is skipped entirely, so it returns 0 after the clock control and the flag update.

functions.name: brcms_c_dpc
functions.prose_contract: bool brcms_c_dpc(struct brcms_c_info *wlc, bool bounded) at brcmsmac/main.c:7701-7786 (slice cut the head); the interrupt bottom half. Precondition: wlc is a valid controller; the interrupt handler has stored the pending causes in wlc->macintstatus. Postcondition: if brcms_deviceremoved(wlc) is true it calls brcms_down(wlc->wl) and returns false without servicing anything (7707-7711). Otherwise it takes a copy of wlc->macintstatus and clears the field (7715-7716), and does a WARN_ON if MI_PRQ is set (the probe-request queue is not serviced here, 7721). It then services these bits of the copy in order: MI_TFS (brcms_b_txstatus; if it reports more work it re-sets MI_TFS in wlc->macintstatus, and a fatal result jumps to the fatal label, 7724-7732), MI_TBTT or MI_DTIM_TBTT (brcms_c_tbtt), MI_ATIMWINEND (writes the saved queue-valid mask to maccommand and clears it), MI_DMAINT (brcms_b_recv on RX_FIFO; if more work remains it re-sets MI_DMAINT), MI_BG_NOISE (noise sample), MI_GP0 (logs once and calls brcms_fatal_error), MI_TO (clears the GP timer), MI_RFDISABLE (updates the rfkill state), and MI_BCNTPL (brcms_c_update_beacon) (7734-7778). It returns wlc->macintstatus != 0 (7781), true when TX status or RX work was left over or new causes were set meanwhile. At the fatal label it calls brcms_fatal_error and returns the same expression (7783-7785). Bits not listed above are cleared without action.

functions.name: wlc_lcnphy_a1
functions.prose_contract: static void wlc_lcnphy_a1(struct brcms_phy *pi, int cal_type, int num_levels, int step_size_lg2) at brcmsmac/phy/phy_lcn.c:3589-3782 (an LCN PHY TX IQ/LO coefficient search; the packet item was an unnamed placeholder and the function does exist under this name). Precondition: pi is an initialised LCN PHY; cal_type is 0, 2, 3 or 4 (other values leave the search limit phy_c10 unset at 0, 3670-3683); it has no pointer parameter, ptr is an internal buffer. Postcondition: it returns nothing. It allocates a 131-entry s16 scratch buffer (GFP_ATOMIC) and returns at once on failure, without touching any register (3608-3610); it allocates a 20-entry u16 save area, and on failure frees the scratch buffer and returns, again before touching any register (3612-3616). Otherwise it saves PHY registers 0x6da, 0x6db and radio register RADIO_2064_REG026, writes 0xC0 to PHY register 0x93d (this register is not restored), starts a 3750 tone, sets up the loopback, saves 0x938, 0x4d7 and 0x4d8 and modifies them (3617-3638). A num_levels of 0 becomes 4 (cal_type non-zero) or 9, and a step_size_lg2 of 0 becomes 3 or 8 (3642-3653). Starting from the current coefficient pair for cal_type (wlc_lcnphy_get_cc), it repeats num_levels times (or until the step becomes 0): it adjusts the radio gain field of REG026 by sampling until clipping is seen, evaluates the nine neighbouring coefficient pairs (clamped to a per-type limit) by setting them with wlc_lcnphy_set_cc, capturing 128 samples and computing the correlation power against a stored tone, keeps the pair with the lowest power, sets it as the new centre and halves the step (3667-3768). The last chosen pair is left set as the coefficient for cal_type. Cleanup (3770-3781) then restores the loopback state, stops the tone, writes back 0x6da, 0x6db, 0x938, 0x4d7, 0x4d8 and REG026 to their saved values and frees both internal buffers.

functions.name: iwl_v3_rate_from_v2_v3
functions.prose_contract: static inline u32 iwl_v3_rate_from_v2_v3(__le32 rate, bool fw_v3) at fw/api/rs.h:899-911. It converts a firmware rate_n_flags word to the host's version-3 layout. Precondition: none. Postcondition: if fw_v3 is true it returns le32_to_cpu(rate) unchanged (903-904). Otherwise, for a version-2 word, it clears the version-2 NSS indicator bit RATE_MCS_NSS_MSK_V2 (0x10, bit 4) and ORs that bit's value (0 or 1) into RATE_MCS_NSS_MSK (0x20, bit 5) of the result (906-908). The NSS indicator is a single bit in both layouts (rs.h:663-675: version 2 has MCS in bits 3-0 and NSS==2 in bit 4; version 3 has MCS in bits 4-0 and NSS==2 in bit 5). All other bits are copied, and because the new bit is ORed in without first clearing bit 5, bit 5 of the result is the OR of the input's bit 5 and bit 4; version 2 treats bits 7-5 as reserved (rs.h:679). It has no side effects.

functions.name: iwl_v3_rate_to_v2_v3
functions.prose_contract: static inline __le32 iwl_v3_rate_to_v2_v3(u32 rate, bool fw_v3) at fw/api/rs.h:913-925. It converts a host version-3 rate_n_flags word to the firmware's layout. Precondition: none. Postcondition: if fw_v3 is true it returns cpu_to_le32(rate) unchanged (917-918). Otherwise it clears the version-3 NSS indicator bit RATE_MCS_NSS_MSK (0x20, bit 5) and ORs that bit's value into RATE_MCS_NSS_MSK_V2 (0x10, bit 4) of the little-endian result (920-922). The NSS indicator is a single bit (rs.h:663-675). Because the value is ORed into bit 4 without clearing it first, bit 4 of the result is the OR of the input's bit 4 (a version-3 MCS bit) and bit 5; so for a version-3 word with MCS bit 4 set the version-2 result keeps bit 4 set whatever the NSS bit was. Bit 3 and the other bits are copied unchanged. It has no side effects.

functions.name: iwl_dbgfs_send_hcmd_write
functions.prose_contract: Writes a hex-encoded host command to the firmware. Returns -EIO if iwl_trans_fw_running(fwrt->trans) is false; -EINVAL if count < header_size+1 (21) or count > 4096; -ENOMEM if kmalloc of (count-1)/2 bytes fails; the hex2bin error (non-zero) if the input is not valid hex; -EINVAL (with an IWL_ERR message) if count != header_size + 2*length + 1 where length is the decoded be16 length field; -EPERM if fwrt->ops or ops->send_hcmd is NULL. Otherwise it calls ops->send_hcmd and, if that returns a negative value, returns it. If it returns >= 0 and hcmd.flags has CMD_WANT_SKB it calls iwl_free_resp (so the response buffer is freed only on that non-negative path, not when send_hcmd fails); the final return is the callback value if non-zero (positive values included) or count when it returned 0. The temporary buffer is kfree'd on every path after the kmalloc succeeded (the out label); the earlier returns happen before it exists.

functions.name: iwl_parse_tlv_firmware
functions.prose_contract: Parses a TLV-format firmware image (static int iwl_parse_tlv_firmware, iwl-drv.c:809; the slice began in the middle of the TLV switch). Returns -EINVAL if len < sizeof(*ucode) (830) or the magic is not IWL_TLV_UCODE_MAGIC (836); it then records ucode_ver, human_readable and fw_version in drv->fw and walks TLVs while len >= sizeof(*tlv). A TLV with length greater than the remaining len returns -EINVAL (873). Per-type handlers jump to invalid_tlv_len/tlv_error (both end in -EINVAL after logging and optionally a hex dump) for a wrong fixed size or an invalid value: e.g. a wrong-size probe/flags/capa/evtlog/phy/cpu-count/scan-channel/fw-version/num-stations/num-links/umac-lmac-debug/paging TLV, a bad default-calibration entry (iwl_set_default_calib), num stations > IWL_STATION_COUNT_MAX or links > IWL_FW_MAX_LINK_ID+1. Other direct -EINVAL returns: NUM_OF_CPU outside 1..2 (1082), paging size > MAX_PAGING_IMAGE_SIZE (1247) or not a multiple of FW_PAGING_SIZE (1254), a second CMD_VERSIONS TLV when capa->cmd_versions is already set (1405). A wrong-size FW_DBG_DUMP_LST TLV is only logged and skipped (1219-1222), not an error; a bad/duplicate debug dest, conf or trigger TLV is also logged and skipped; unknown TLV types are ignored. A CMD_VERSIONS length that is not a multiple of the entry size is truncated down, not rejected. Returns -ENOMEM when krealloc of dbg_mem_tlv (1280), kmemdup of iml (1290), cmd_versions, phy_integration_ver, pc_data or kvmemdup of pnvm_data fails. After the loop it returns -EINVAL if the usniffer capability is not unified, a usniffer config was requested and *usniffer_images is zero (1456-1460), and -EINVAL if bytes remain in len (1463-1473); otherwise 0. Fields in drv->fw, drv->trans->dbg, capa and pieces may already have been set when an error is returned, and heap copies made earlier stay referenced from those structures; this function does not free them. Callee bodies (iwl_store_ucode_sec, iwl_set_default_calib) not read.

functions.name: iwl_mld_release_frames_from_notif
functions.prose_contract: Static helper (agg.c:45). If baid equals IWL_RX_REORDER_DATA_INVALID_BAID or baid >= ARRAY_SIZE(mld->fw_id_to_ba) it does WARN_ON_ONCE and returns before taking any lock (57-59). Otherwise it calls rcu_read_lock (61), reads mld->fw_id_to_ba[baid] and, if NULL, logs and jumps to out_unlock. It computes sta_id = ffs(ba_data->sta_mask) - 1 (70, no check that sta_mask is non-zero, so a zero mask gives an out-of-range index into fw_id_to_link_sta), looks up the link_sta and if it is an error pointer/NULL or has no ->sta it WARN_ON_ONCEs and goes to out_unlock. Otherwise it calls iwl_mld_reorder_release_frames(mld, link_sta->sta, napi, ba_data, &ba_data->reorder_buf[queue], nssn) (77); what that callee does with head_sn was not read. rcu_read_unlock is executed at out_unlock on every path after the lock was taken. It does not require the caller to be outside an RCU read section: rcu_read_lock nests and its caller iwl_mld_handle_bar_frame_release_notif already holds it (128).

functions.name: iwl_mld_wowlan_resume
functions.prose_contract: Resume flow after WoWLAN (d3.c:1958). Asserts the wiphy lock (lockdep_assert_wiphy). It reaches the err label (sets mld->fw_status.in_hw_restart = true, ret = 1) if fw_status.in_d3 is false (1976), iwl_mld_get_bss_vif returns NULL (WARN_ON, 1987), the link_conf for the vif's first active link (or link 0) is NULL (WARN_ON, 1997), or iwl_mld_wait_d3_notif returns non-zero (2010; the error is logged, then ret is overwritten with 1). Before the in_d3 check passes nothing is changed; after it passes, resuming is set true and in_d3 cleared. If the zeroed wowlan_status allocation fails (2002) it returns -ENOMEM directly, so fw_status.resuming stays true and in_d3 is already false. If the D3 end flags contain IWL_D0I3_RESET_REQUIRE it sets in_hw_restart and skips the power/regdomain updates but still goes to process_wakeup_results with ret still 0. Otherwise it updates regdomain, MAC power, beacon filter, device power and, if mld->netdetect, calls iwl_mld_scan_stop whose result becomes ret and is returned unchanged at the end (the flow continues even if it is non-zero). In process_wakeup_results: with netdetect it processes the netdetect results and sets mld->netdetect = false (no EMLSR unblock or disconnect there); without netdetect it calls iwl_mld_process_wowlan_status and then iwl_mld_unblock_emlsr(IWL_MLD_EMLSR_BLOCKED_WOWLAN) if that returned true, else ieee80211_resume_disconnect. Both the normal and err paths reach out, which clears fw_status.resuming and frees wowlan_status->wake_packet and wowlan_status when wowlan_status was allocated. Returns 0 on the normal paths (including the RESET_REQUIRE one), 1 on err, -ENOMEM on the allocation failure, or the scan_stop result in the netdetect case.

functions.name: iwl_mld_remove_key
functions.prose_contract: Removes a key from the firmware (key.c:181). Asserts the wiphy lock. It first computes sta_mask and key_flags with iwl_mld_get_key_sta_mask and iwl_mld_get_key_flags. If sta_mask is 0 it returns with nothing else done (191). If key->keyidx is 4 or 5 (IGTK/BIGTK) it uses link_id = key->link_id when that is >= 0, else 0; if iwl_mld_link_dereference_check gives NULL it does WARN_ON and returns without sending the command and without touching hw_key_idx (203-204); otherwise it sets mld_link->igtk = NULL only if it equals key and then decrements mld->num_igtks (the decrement is not conditional on the pointer match). It then calls iwl_mld_remove_key_from_fw, which itself returns without sending anything when CONFIG_PM_SLEEP is set and mld->fw_status.resuming is true (171-172), or when sta_mask is 0 (175); otherwise it sends the SEC_KEY_CMD remove command and ignores its result. Finally it sets key->hw_key_idx = STA_KEY_IDX_INVALID. Returns void.

functions.name: iwl_mld_handle_missed_beacon_notif
functions.prose_contract: Handles a firmware missed-beacons notification (link.c:526). It maps notif->link_id to a link_conf; if NULL it does WARN_ON and returns (544). It takes vif from link_conf, logs missed counts with IWL_DEBUG_INFO, and if vif is NULL does WARN_ON and returns (555; the debug log has already run). It then records the IWL_FW_INI_TIME_POINT_MISSED_BEACONS time point. If missed_bcon >= IWL_MLD_MISSED_BEACONS_THRESHOLD_LONG: it calls ieee80211_connection_loss(vif) and returns when missed_bcon_since_rx >= IWL_MLD_MISSED_BEACONS_SINCE_RX_THOLD, else logs a warning and returns (561-569). Otherwise, if missed_bcon_since_rx > IWL_MLD_MISSED_BEACONS_THRESHOLD it calls ieee80211_cqm_beacon_loss_notify(vif, GFP_ATOMIC) and, only if iwl_mld_emlsr_active(vif) is false, iwl_mld_int_mlo_scan; execution then continues. It returns without EMLSR exit if hweight16(vif->active_links) <= 1, if notif->other_link_id equals FW_CTXT_ID_INVALID, or if the other link does not resolve (IWL_FW_CHECK). Otherwise it calls iwl_mld_exit_emlsr(mld, vif, IWL_MLD_EMLSR_EXIT_MISSED_BEACON, iwl_mld_get_primary_link(vif)) only when one of the three beacon-loss conditions at lines 613-618 is true. It takes no lock and acquires no reference in this function itself (callees not read). Returns void.

functions.name: iwl_mld_low_latency_update_counters
functions.prose_contract: Counts VO/VI frames per rx queue for low-latency detection (low_latency.c:260). It dereferences sta (mld_sta->vif, and the vif's fw_id) before any check, so sta and its vif must be valid. It returns with no counter change if mld->low_latency.pkts_counters is NULL (WARN_ON_ONCE, 272), if fw_id >= ARRAY_SIZE(counters->vo_vi) or queue >= mld->trans->info.num_rxqs (WARN_ON_ONCE, 275; ARRAY_SIZE is a compile-time size, it does not read the uninitialised counters pointer), if mld->low_latency.stopped is set (279), or if iwl_mld_is_vo_vi_pkt(hdr) is false (282). Otherwise it increments pkts_counters[queue].vo_vi[fw_id] under spin_lock_bh(&counters->lock), then, outside that lock, sets window_start[fw_id] to jiffies (or 1 when jiffies is 0) if it is zero, and, if time_is_before_jiffies(timestamp + MLD_LL_PERIOD), queues mld->low_latency.work with delay 0 via wiphy_delayed_work_queue. Returns void.

functions.name: iwl_mld_handle_nan_dw_end_notif
functions.prose_contract: Handles the NAN discovery-window-end notification (nan.c:252; the slice cut the head). It logs the band, then returns early with IWL_FW_CHECK failure reporting if mld->nan_device_vif is NULL (so mld_vif is NULL, 262) or if ieee80211_vif_nan_started on it is false (265); it also returns early (WARN_ON) if mld_vif->aux_sta.sta_id == IWL_INVALID_STA (268). Otherwise it flushes the aux station's TX queues with iwl_mld_flush_link_sta_txqs(mld, sta_id) (274). It then selects chan = ieee80211_get_channel(wiphy, 2437) for IWL_NAN_BAND_2GHZ or 5745 for IWL_NAN_BAND_5GHZ; for any other band it reports through IWL_FW_CHECK and returns (after the flush has already been done, so the flush is not skipped for an invalid band). For the two valid bands it calls cfg80211_next_nan_dw_notif(wdev from ieee80211_vif_to_wdev(nan_device_vif), chan, GFP_KERNEL); chan may be NULL if ieee80211_get_channel finds no such channel (not checked). Returns void; no lock is taken here.

functions.name: iwl_mld_he_mac80211_mcs_to_fw_mcs
functions.prose_contract: Static pure helper (tlc.c:200) converting an HE MCS support code to a firmware MCS bitmask. For mcs equal to IEEE80211_HE_MCS_SUPPORT_0_7 it returns BIT(IWL_TLC_MNG_HT_RATE_MCS7 + 1) - 1 = 0xFF (255), for IEEE80211_HE_MCS_SUPPORT_0_9 it returns BIT(MCS9 + 1) - 1 = 0x3FF (1023), for IEEE80211_HE_MCS_SUPPORT_0_11 it returns BIT(MCS11 + 1) - 1 = 0xFFF (4095), and for IEEE80211_HE_MCS_NOT_SUPPORTED it returns 0. For any other value it executes WARN(1, ...) and returns 0. It reads no global state, takes no lock and allocates nothing.
functions.contract: /*@ requires \true; ensures (mcs == 0 ==> result == 255) && (mcs == 1 ==> result == 1023) && (mcs == 2 ==> result == 4095) && (mcs >= 3 ==> result == 0); */

functions.name: iwl_mvm_ftm_range_resp
functions.prose_contract: Handler for the firmware FTM range-response notification (ftm-initiator.c:1262; the name iwl_mvm_ftm_range_resp_notif in the packet does not exist, the slice cut the head). It takes (mvm, rxb), asserts mvm->mutex is held, and returns void. It returns with no further effect if mvm->ftm_initiator.req is NULL, if iwl_mvm_ftm_resp_size_validation(notif_ver, pkt_len) fails, or if iwl_mvm_ftm_range_resp_valid(...) returns true for the request_id/num_of_aps of the v8 layout (when FTM_NEW_RANGE_REQ API is present) or of the v5 layout (otherwise); that helper returns true on a bad response. Otherwise it loops over i < num_of_aps and i < IWL_TOF_MAX_APS: it picks fw_ap from the v8, v7, v6 or v5 layout; in the new-API, notif_ver >= 8 case it calls iwl_mvm_ftm_pasn_update_pn(mvm, fw_ap) before looking the peer up, so this call also happens for an entry whose bssid is later found unknown. If iwl_mvm_ftm_find_peer finds no peer for fw_ap->bssid it logs IWL_WARN and continues with the next entry. For a known peer it builds a cfg80211_pmsr_result (status and failure reason from measure_status, busy_retry_time from refusal_period for REQUEST_REJECTED, addr, host_time, type FTM, burst_index = the peer's responses[] count, which it then increments, RSSI/RTT values with valid flags, LCI/civic via iwl_mvm_ftm_get_lci_civic, then iwl_mvm_ftm_rtt_smoothing) and passes it to cfg80211_pmsr_report with GFP_KERNEL. After the loop, if last_in_batch (v8 last_report or v5 last_in_batch) is set it calls cfg80211_pmsr_complete and iwl_mvm_ftm_reset. It allocates no memory that it keeps itself (callee iwl_mvm_ftm_get_lci_civic not read).

functions.name: iwl_run_init_mvm_ucode
functions.prose_contract: Runs the INIT firmware and calibrations (fw.c:702). If iwl_mvm_has_unified_ucode(mvm) it returns iwl_run_unified_mvm_ucode(mvm) immediately (711), before the lockdep_assert_held(&mvm->mutex) at 714. Otherwise it asserts mvm->mutex is held, clears rfkill_safe_init_done and registers calib_wait for INIT_COMPLETE_NOTIF/CALIB_RES_NOTIF_PHY_DB. It then, in order: loads the INIT ucode (iwl_mvm_load_ucode_wait_alive), on device family < 8000 sends the BT init config, reads NVM if mvm->nvm_data is NULL, loads the NVM file to the NIC if nvm_file_name is set; each failure sets ret to that callee's value and goes to remove_notif (which removes calib_wait) and then out. If iwl_mvm_is_radio_hw_killed(mvm) is true after the NVM steps it goes to remove_notif with ret still equal to the last successful step's value (0), so it returns 0 without running calibrations. Otherwise it sets rfkill_safe_init_done = true, sends the TX antenna config and PHY config (failures go to remove_notif), then waits for calibration with iwl_wait_notification (timeout MVM_UCODE_CALIB_TIMEOUT): a 0 result goes to out; a non-zero result is reset to 0 if the radio is RF-killed, else it is logged and returned. At out it always sets rfkill_safe_init_done = false, and if mvm->nvm_data is still NULL it kzallocs a small fake NVM (returning -ENOMEM if that fails, overriding ret; otherwise one channel and one bitrate are set up). Returns ret, which is 0, a callee's non-zero result, or -ENOMEM.

functions.name: iwl_mvm_mac_ampdu_action
functions.prose_contract: mac80211 ampdu_action callback (mac80211.c:1017; the name iwl_mvm_ampdu_action does not exist, the slice cut the head). It reads sta->addr for a debug print (sta is dereferenced before any check) and returns -EACCES without taking mvm->mutex if mvm->nvm_data->sku_cap_11n_enable is false (1032). Otherwise it does mutex_lock(&mvm->mutex) and switches on action. RX_START: if the vif's deflink.ap_sta_id equals the station's deflink.sta_id it sets the TCM mac data's opened_rx_ba_sessions = true and cancel_delayed_work on uapsd_nonagg_detected_wk; this happens before and independent of the next check; then if !iwl_enable_rx_ampdu() ret = -EINVAL, else ret = iwl_mvm_sta_rx_agg(..., *ssn, true, buf_size, timeout). RX_STOP calls iwl_mvm_sta_rx_agg with start false and ssn 0. TX_START returns -EINVAL if !iwl_enable_tx_ampdu(), else iwl_mvm_sta_tx_agg_start (which gets the ssn pointer). TX_STOP_CONT calls iwl_mvm_sta_tx_agg_stop; TX_STOP_FLUSH and TX_STOP_FLUSH_CONT call iwl_mvm_sta_tx_agg_flush; TX_OPERATIONAL calls iwl_mvm_sta_tx_agg_oper. Any other action does WARN_ON_ONCE and ret = -EINVAL. If ret is 0 it calls iwl_mvm_ampdu_check_trigger with rx_ba_ssn = *ssn for RX_START and 0 otherwise. It then unlocks mvm->mutex on the way out (the early -EACCES return is the only exit before the lock) and returns ret, which is 0 or whatever the dispatched helper or the -EINVAL cases produced.

functions.name: iwl_mvm_pre_channel_switch
functions.prose_contract: Prepares a channel switch (mac80211.c:5473, static). Asserts mvm->mutex is held; clears mvmvif->csa_failed and csa_blocks_tx and fires the FW_DBG_TRIGGER_CHANNEL_SWITCH debug trigger. AP: returns -EBUSY if mvm->csa_vif is set and its bss_conf.csa_active is true (WARN_ONCE), or if mvm->csa_tx_blocked_vif is set; then it assigns mvm->csa_vif = vif, and returns -EBUSY (WARN_ONCE) if mvmvif->csa_countdown is already set, so csa_vif stays assigned in that case; otherwise it sets csa_target_freq and, only when chsw->block_tx and the HW has HANDLES_QUIET_CSA, sets csa_blocks_tx, sets IWL_MVM_TXQ_STATE_STOP_AP_CSA on the vif txq and blocks station txqs via ieee80211_iterate_stations_atomic. STATION: sets csa_blocks_tx = chsw->block_tx; if the firmware knows CHANNEL_SWITCH_ERROR_NOTIF (notif version non-zero) it breaks out of the switch and skips everything else in this case (no delayed work, no CSA command, no csa_count update). Otherwise it returns -EBUSY if the vif is not associated or has no dtim_period, may schedule csa_work (immediately if chsw->delay > IWL_MAX_CSA_BLOCK_TX, or after IWL_MAX_CSA_BLOCK_TX ms if block_tx and the countdown is long or zero), then on firmware without CHANNEL_SWITCH_CMD capability calls iwl_mvm_old_pre_chan_sw_sta and returns its non-zero error, or else calls iwl_mvm_schedule_client_csa and ignores its result; it then records csa_count = chsw->count and csa_misbehave = false. Other interface types do nothing in the switch. After the switch it sets mvmvif->ps_disabled = true, returns the error from iwl_mvm_power_update_ps if non-zero, and otherwise calls iwl_mvm_teardown_tdls_peers and returns 0.

functions.name: iwl_mvm_mld_vif_cfg_changed_station
functions.prose_contract: Handles station-mode vif config changes (mld-mac80211.c:601, static, returns void). If changes == BSS_CHANGED_IDLE exactly, it returns at once, before the MAC context push and before mvmvif->associated is updated. Otherwise it calls iwl_mvm_mld_mac_ctxt_changed (logging an error on failure but continuing) and sets mvmvif->associated = vif->cfg.assoc. If changes has BSS_CHANGED_ASSOC: when vif->cfg.assoc is true it clears session_prot_connection_loss, requests statistics and periodic system statistics, calls iwl_mvm_sf_update and iwl_mvm_power_vif_assoc (these two calls appear at 634-635 and again at 668-671), zeroes each valid link's beacon_stats, for p2p vifs sets dynamic SMPS per link, and checks under rcu_read_lock whether a link_conf has dtim_period 0; if so and IWL_MVM_STATUS_IN_HW_RESTART is not set it calls iwl_mvm_protect_assoc(mvm, vif, 0). When vif->cfg.assoc is false and iwl_mvm_mld_vif_have_valid_ap_sta is true it calls iwl_mvm_mei_host_disassociated, turns off periodic system statistics and calls iwl_mvm_sf_update, with a WARN_ONCE if that fails and no HW restart was requested. In both cases iwl_mvm_bss_info_changed_station_assoc(mvm, vif, changes) is then called (687), also when disassociating or when no valid ap_sta exists. If changes has BSS_CHANGED_PS it calls iwl_mvm_smps_workaround and iwl_mvm_power_update_mac, logging an error on failure. Callees not read.

functions.name: iwl_mvm_set_mac80211_rx_flag
functions.prose_contract: Decides from the firmware MPDU status word whether an RX frame is kept and what it reports (rx.c:139, static, returns u32). Returns 0 without touching stats or *crypt_len if the frame is not protected or the cipher field is SEC_NO_ENC (145-148), or if it is SEC_ENC_ERR (151-153). For CCM it returns (u32)-1 if MIC_OK is not set; else sets RX_FLAG_DECRYPTED and *crypt_len = IEEE80211_CCMP_HDR_LEN and returns 0. For TKIP: if the DEPRECATE_TTAK API is absent and TTAK_OK is not set it returns 0 leaving stats and *crypt_len untouched (software decrypts); otherwise (TTAK ok, or the API deprecates the TTAK check so the bit is not consulted) it sets *crypt_len = IEEE80211_TKIP_IV_LEN and falls into the WEP case. WEP/TKIP: returns -1 if ICV_OK is not set (for TKIP *crypt_len has already been set); else sets RX_FLAG_DECRYPTED, sets *crypt_len = IEEE80211_WEP_IV_LEN only for WEP, and returns 0. EXT_ENC: returns -1 if MIC_OK is not set, else sets RX_FLAG_DECRYPTED and returns 0 leaving *crypt_len unchanged. Any other cipher value logs an unhandled-algorithm warning (unless monitor_on) and returns 0 with no flag or length change.

functions.name: iwl_mvm_rx_crypto
functions.prose_contract: Checks the firmware's crypto status for a received MPDU (rxmq.c:417, static, returns int). It returns -1 first if the PHY info has IWL_RX_MPDU_PHY_AMPDU, the status cipher field is SEC_UNKNOWN and mvm->monitor_on is false (432-437). If the frame is a management frame without the protected bit it returns whatever iwl_mvm_rx_mgmt_prot(sta, hdr, desc, status, stats) returns (callee not read). If the frame is not protected, or the cipher is SEC_NONE, it returns 0 without setting any flag or *crypt_len (443-446); on FreeBSD an SEC_ENC_ERR cipher also returns 0 untouched (451-453). Then by cipher: CCM or GCM returns -1 on !MIC_OK, else sets RX_FLAG_DECRYPTED | RX_FLAG_MIC_STRIPPED and *crypt_len = IEEE80211_CCMP_HDR_LEN and returns 0. TKIP returns 0 untouched if the DEPRECATE_TTAK API is absent and TTAK_OK is clear; else (gen2 devices without MIC_OK also get RX_FLAG_MMIC_ERROR) it sets *crypt_len = IEEE80211_TKIP_IV_LEN and falls into WEP: returns -1 if ICV_OK is clear, else sets RX_FLAG_DECRYPTED, sets *crypt_len = IEEE80211_WEP_IV_LEN only for WEP, and, if FH_RSCSR_RADA_EN is set in pkt_flags, also RX_FLAG_ICV_STRIPPED (plus RX_FLAG_MMIC_STRIPPED on gen2) and returns 0. EXT_ENC returns -1 if MIC_OK is clear, else sets RX_FLAG_DECRYPTED and returns 0 leaving *crypt_len unchanged. The CMAC/GMAC cipher (break) and any unlisted cipher (default; may log a warning for unicast non-monitor frames) both fall out of the switch and return 0 with no flag change.

functions.name: iwl_mvm_check_running_scans
functions.prose_contract: Decides whether a new scan of the given type can start (scan.c:2628, static). First: if type is IWL_MVM_SCAN_SCHED or IWL_MVM_SCAN_NETDETECT and scan_status has a sched or net-detect scan running, it returns -EBUSY even if scan slots are free (2644-2646). Then, if iwl_mvm_num_scans(mvm) < mvm->max_scans (a slot is free) it returns 0 (2648). Only when no slot is free does it switch on type: REGULAR returns -EBUSY if a regular scan (REGULAR_MASK) is running, else returns the result of iwl_mvm_scan_stop(SCHED, true); SCHED returns -EBUSY if SCHED_MASK is set, else the result of iwl_mvm_scan_stop(REGULAR, true); NETDETECT returns 0 for a non-unified image (no CNSLDTD_D3_D0_IMG capability), and for a unified image returns iwl_mvm_scan_stop of the running regular scan, else of the running sched scan; if neither is running (or for an unknown type) it does WARN_ON(1) and returns -EIO. So the return is 0, -EBUSY, -EIO, or whatever iwl_mvm_scan_stop returns (including an error from it).

functions.name: iwl_mvm_sta_rx_agg
functions.prose_contract: Starts or stops an RX block-ack session (sta.c:2893). Asserts mvm->mutex is held. If start and mvm->rx_ba_sessions >= the session limit (IWL_MAX_BAID with the new TX API, else IWL_MAX_BAID_OLD) it returns -ENOSPC. With the new RX API and start it kzallocs baid_data (returns -ENOMEM on failure). The baid passed to the firmware is mvm_sta->tid_to_baid[tid] when stopping with the new RX API, else -1. It calls iwl_mvm_fw_baid_op unless this is a stop during IWL_MVM_STATUS_IN_HW_RESTART (then baid keeps that initial value, which is -1 with the old RX API). If the resulting baid is negative (a firmware/command error from iwl_mvm_fw_baid_op, or the initial -1) it frees baid_data (kfree, NULL-safe) and returns that negative value (so a stop in a HW restart with the old RX API returns -1). On start success it increments mvm->rx_ba_sessions; with the old RX API it returns 0 there; with the new RX API it fills baid_data (baid, timeout, last_rx, timer, sta_mask, buf_size), stores baid in mvm_sta->tid_to_baid[tid], arms the session timer when timeout != 0, initialises the reorder buffer, WARNs if baid_map[baid] is already set and publishes baid_data with rcu_assign_pointer; returns 0. On stop success it first decrements rx_ba_sessions if it is > 0; with the old RX API it returns 0; with the new API it returns -EINVAL (WARN_ON) if tid_to_baid[tid] is IWL_RX_REORDER_DATA_INVALID_BAID or if baid_map[baid] is NULL (rx_ba_sessions has already been decremented and the map entry left as it was in those cases); otherwise it frees the reorder buffer, shuts down the timer, clears baid_map[baid] and kfree_rcu's baid_data, and returns 0. Callees (fw_baid_op and its variants) not read, so their exact error values are not claimed.

functions.name: iwl_mvm_sta_tx_agg_stop
functions.prose_contract: Stops a TX aggregation session for one tid (sta.c:3358). If IWL_MVM_STATUS_IN_HW_RESTART is set it calls ieee80211_stop_tx_ba_cb_irqsafe and returns 0 right away, without taking the station lock, touching tid_data or asserting the mutex (3370-3373). Otherwise it takes mvmsta->lock (spin_lock_bh), clears the tid bit in mvmsta->agg_tids and calls iwl_mvm_unreserve_agg_queue, which asserts mvm->mutex is held on every call (so the mutex is needed for all paths past the restart check) and on the old TX API frees a RESERVED queue and sets tid_data->txq_id to IWL_MVM_INVALID_QUEUE. Then by tid_data->state: IWL_AGG_ON sets ssn from seq_number, sets ssn to 0xffff and state to IWL_AGG_OFF, drops the lock, calls ieee80211_stop_tx_ba_cb_irqsafe and iwl_mvm_sta_tx_agg(..., false) and returns 0; IWL_AGG_STARTING or IWL_EMPTYING_HW_QUEUE_ADDBA calls ieee80211_stop_tx_ba_cb_irqsafe, sets state to IWL_AGG_OFF, and returns 0 after unlocking; any other state logs errors and returns -EINVAL after unlocking, leaving the state unchanged (the agg_tids bit has already been cleared and unreserve already run in this case).

functions.name: iwl_mvm_sta_tx_agg_flush
functions.prose_contract: Flushes a TX aggregation session (sta.c:3431). It does not check IN_HW_RESTART. It takes mvmsta->lock, records the old tid state, sets tid_data->state = IWL_AGG_OFF, clears the tid bit in agg_tids and unlocks, then calls iwl_mvm_unreserve_agg_queue (which asserts mvm->mutex is held, so the mutex is a precondition on every call). If the old state was >= IWL_AGG_ON it drains the station (iwl_mvm_drain_sta true), flushes the queue (iwl_mvm_flush_sta_tids and iwl_trans_wait_txq_empty with the new TX API, else iwl_mvm_flush_tx_path and iwl_trans_wait_tx_queues_empty) logging but ignoring a flush error, undrains the station and calls iwl_mvm_sta_tx_agg(mvm, sta, tid, txq_id, false). For an older state none of that is done. It returns 0 in every path (no error return exists in this function); it does not call ieee80211_stop_tx_ba_cb_irqsafe.

functions.name: iwl_mvm_redirect_queue
functions.prose_contract: Moves a TX queue to the FIFO of another AC (sta.c:704, static). Returns -EINVAL (WARN_ON) if the new TX API is in use (715). Returns 0 without any change if ac <= mvm->queue_info[queue].mac80211_ac and force is false (726; since AC numbering is flipped, it redirects only to a numerically larger AC, or when force is set). Otherwise it reads the queue's ra_sta_id, tx fifo and tid, notes whether the queue is shared (tid_bitmap has more than one bit), sets IWL_MVM_TXQ_STATE_STOP_REDIRECT on txq and waits for the queue to drain; if the wait fails it returns -EIO via the out label (the queue is not disabled in that case). Otherwise it disables the queue (iwl_trans_txq_disable) and sends SCD_QUEUE_CFG with the disable action; that command's result is stored in ret and an error is only logged, execution continues. It then re-enables the queue config with the ssn, sets queue_info[queue].txq_tid = tid, calls iwl_mvm_reconfig_scd (return value ignored), sets mac80211_ac = ac and, if shared, sets shared mode in the transport. At out it clears STOP_REDIRECT and returns ret, which is -EIO on drain failure, else the result of the SCD disable command (0 or its error), so a failed disable command is returned even though the redirect was carried on.

functions.name: iwl_mvm_stop_roc
functions.prose_contract: Stops a remain-on-channel (time-event.c:1252). It locks mvm->mutex itself (1261). Branch 1: if the device has P2P over aux, or the ROC_CMD version is >= 3 and the vif is not P2P_DEVICE, then if mvmvif->roc_activity < ROC_NUM_ACTIVITIES it sends iwl_mvm_roc_rm_cmd for that activity and sets roc_activity = ROC_NUM_ACTIVITIES (only in that case), then goes to cleanup_roc. Branch 2: else, with the SESSION_PROT_CMD capability: for a P2P_DEVICE vif, if te_data->id >= SESSION_PROTECT_CONF_MAX_ID it logs, unlocks the mutex and returns without any cleanup; else it cancels the session protection; for other vif types it removes the aux ROC time event for hs_time_event_data; then cleanup_roc. Branch 3 (older firmware): te_data = iwl_mvm_get_roc_te; if NULL it warns, unlocks and returns; otherwise it switches to that te_data's vif and removes the time event (P2P_DEVICE) or the aux ROC time event (other types), then falls to cleanup_roc. At cleanup_roc it SETS (not clears) IWL_MVM_STATUS_ROC_AUX_RUNNING if p2p_aux or the vif type is not P2P_DEVICE, else IWL_MVM_STATUS_ROC_P2P_RUNNING, so that iwl_mvm_cleanup_roc does the cleanup even if the ROC had not started; it then calls iwl_mvm_cleanup_roc(mvm), which test-and-clears those bits, removes the p2p bcast/aux station as applicable and itself calls mutex_unlock(&mvm->mutex) (time-event.c:126), so on the cleanup_roc path this function does not unlock separately. Returns void; the mutex is released on every exit.

functions.name: iwl_trans_pcie_start_fw
functions.prose_contract: Starts firmware on a PCIe device (trans.c:1291). It first calls iwl_pcie_prepare_card_hw and returns -EIO if that is non-zero (1301-1304), before trans_pcie->mutex is taken. It then enables the RF-kill interrupt, acks CSR_INT, disables interrupts and synchronizes IRQs, and locks trans_pcie->mutex. With the mutex held it goes to out with: -ERFKILL if HW RF-kill is set and run_in_rfkill is false (1324); -EIO if trans_pcie->is_down (1330); or the non-zero error of iwl_pcie_nic_init. Otherwise it clears the RF-kill/cmd-blocked bits, enables only the firmware-load interrupt (iwl_enable_fw_load_int; the general host interrupts are not re-enabled here), and loads the image with iwl_pcie_load_given_ucode_8000 (device family >= 8000) or iwl_pcie_load_given_ucode, keeping its return value in ret. It then re-reads the HW RF-kill state and, if set and run_in_rfkill is false, overwrites ret with -ERFKILL, even if the load itself failed. At out it unlocks the mutex and returns ret, so the result is 0, -EIO, -ERFKILL, or a callee error from nic_init or the ucode load (callee values not read).

functions.name: mt7603_pre_tbtt_tasklet
functions.prose_contract: Pre-TBTT tasklet of the mt7603 driver (beacon.c:101, void). If dev->mphy.offchannel is set it returns immediately and does nothing (110). Otherwise it flushes the CAB queue by writing MT_WF_ARB_CAB_FLUSH, runs mt76_queue_tx_cleanup on the CAB and BEACON queues, increments dev->beacon_check if the beacon queue still has queued frames and resets it to 0 otherwise, and calls mt7603_mac_stuck_beacon_recovery. Under the beacon queue lock it iterates active interfaces with mt7603_update_beacon_iter (which fetches and queues each beacon; in that helper, if either MT_DMA_FQCR0 poll times out it sets beacon_check to MT7603_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT and skips queueing, and the fetched beacon skb is then neither queued nor freed there) and kicks the queue. It then calls mt76_csa_check; if mdev->csa_complete is set it returns, with no CAB work. Otherwise it collects buffered broadcast/multicast frames from all interfaces via mt7603_add_buffered_bc, repeating while the count keeps growing and stays below 8. If none were collected it returns without queueing anything or starting CAB. Otherwise it clears the more-data flag on the last frame of each interface, queues all collected skbs on the CAB queue under its lock (mt76_tx_queue_skb, then kick), writes the per-BSS CAB counts, and writes MT_WF_ARB_CAB_START.

functions.name: mt7615_mac_adjust_sensitivity
functions.prose_contract: Adjusts the CCK or OFDM energy-detect sensitivity (mac.c:1795, static, void). It selects false_cca, default threshold def_th (-98 for OFDM, -110 for CCK) and a pointer to the stored sensitivity, and gets signal = mt76_get_min_avg_rssi. If that is 0 it calls mt7615_mac_set_default_sensitivity and returns without anything else. Otherwise signal = min(signal, -72). If false_cca > 500: it returns at once if rts_err_rate > MT_FRAC(40,100); else if the sensitivity equals def_th and signal > -90 it sets the sensitivity to -90 (a jump of 8 for OFDM, 20 for CCK), else if sensitivity + 2 < signal it raises it by 2. Else if (0 < false_cca < 50) or rts_err_rate > MT_FRAC(60,100): if sensitivity - 2 >= def_th it lowers it by 2. Then in all non-returning cases, if the sensitivity is above signal it is clamped to signal (so it can drop by more than 2). If anything changed it writes the register value (sensitivity*2+512 for OFDM, sensitivity+256 for CCK) with mt7615_mac_set_sensitivity and records phy->last_cca_adj = jiffies. rts_err_rate is not range-checked; any u32 value is compared as given.

functions.name: mt7915_get_et_stats
functions.prose_contract: Fills the ethtool statistics array for an mt7915 vif (main.c:1514, void). It takes dev->mt76.mutex, calls mt7915_mac_update_stats(phy), and writes the PHY MIB counters sequentially into data[] (tx counters, 15 aggregation-size counters from phy->mt76->aggr_stats, beamforming and AMSDU counters, rx counters, dl_* and ul_hetrig_* counters), advancing ei. It sets wi.initial_stat_idx = ei and iterates all stations with mt7915_ethtool_worker; for each station whose vif idx equals this vif's mt76.idx, mt76_ethtool_worker does sta_count++ and ADDS (+=) that station's per-mode counters into the same worker slots starting at initial_stat_idx (the slots are accumulated across stations, not appended per station; data[] is not zeroed by this function). It then unlocks the mutex. If wi.sta_count == 0 it returns (main.c:1635-1636), so in that case the page-pool statistics are not written. Otherwise it advances ei by wi.worker_stat_count, writes the page-pool stats via mt76_ethtool_page_pool_stats(&dev->mt76, &data[ei], &ei), and logs with dev_err if ei differs from MT7915_SSTATS_LEN + page_pool_ethtool_stats_get_count(). The caller's data buffer must therefore hold that many u64 entries.

functions.name: mt7925e_mac_reset
functions.prose_contract: Resets the mt7925 PCIe MAC (pci_mac.c:70). Sequence: mt792xe_mcu_drv_pmctrl (result ignored); frees pending TX skbs; disables host IRQs and PCIe MAC interrupts; sets MT76_RESET and MT76_MCU_RESET, wakes the MCU waiters and purges the MCU response queue; schedules all txqs; disables the tx worker and, depending on irq_map masks, the main/MCU/WA rx NAPIs and the tx NAPI; puts the TX tokens (mt7925_tx_token_put) and re-initialises the token idr; resets the WPDMA (mt792x_wpdma_reset(dev, true)); re-enables all rx NAPIs and the tx NAPI and schedules them (it does not schedule the tx worker); clears fw_assert and MT76_MCU_RESET; re-enables the host IRQ mask and MT_PCIE_MAC_INT_ENABLE. Then err = mt792xe_mcu_fw_pmctrl(dev); if that fails it returns err immediately (125-126) without reaching the out label, so MT76_RESET stays set and the tx worker stays disabled. Otherwise it runs, stopping at the first failure with err set: __mt792xe_mcu_drv_pmctrl, mt7925_run_firmware, mt7925_mcu_set_eeprom, mt7925_mac_init, __mt7925_start. At out it clears MT76_RESET and re-enables the tx worker (mt76_worker_enable), and returns err (0 on success).

functions.name: mt7996_mac_reset_work
functions.prose_contract: Work function for MCU/L1 SER recovery on mt7996 (mac.c:2520, void; the slice cut the head). If dev->recovery.restart is set it disables the MCU command watchdog interrupt, increments wa_reset_count (if the recovery state has MT_MCU_CMD_WA_WDT) or wm_reset_count, runs mt7996_mac_full_reset, enables MT_INT_MCU_CMD (disabling the rest), re-enables the watchdog mask, sets recovery.state = MT_MCU_CMD_NORMAL_STATE and recovery.restart = false, and returns. Otherwise it returns at once, doing nothing, if the recovery state does not have MT_MCU_CMD_STOP_DMA. Otherwise (L1 SER recovery): it logs a start message, stops any active WED devices, stops the mac80211 queues, sets MT76_RESET and MT76_MCU_RESET, aborts scans, wakes MCU waiters, cancels the WED RRO work, and for each phy aborts ROC, sets MT76_RESET and cancels mac_work synchronously; disables the tx worker and the rx NAPIs (skipping WED RRO queues when WED is active) and the tx NAPI. Then it locks dev->mt76.mutex and, with it held: stops the NPU hw, signals DMA_STOPPED, waits for the RESET_DONE state (result tested only for that one wait), and if that wait returns 0 resets the DMA, puts the TX tokens, re-inits the token idr, signals DMA_INIT and waits for RECOVERY_DONE; then signals RESET_DONE and waits for NORMAL_STATE (this wait result is ignored), restarts DMA, programs the RRO 3.0 emu config when applicable, restarts WED hardware paths when active, clears MT76_MCU_RESET and the per-phy MT76_RESET bits, re-enables and schedules the rx NAPIs, schedules the irq tasklet, re-enables the tx worker, re-enables and schedules the tx NAPI, wakes the queues and updates beacons. The mutex is released only after the beacon update (mac.c:2660); after unlocking it calls mt7996_npu_hw_init, requeues each phy's mac_work with MT7996_WATCHDOG_TIME and logs completion. No return value or error is produced for failures of the individual waits.

functions.name: mt7996_mac_sta_event
functions.prose_contract: Applies an association, authorization or disassociation event to every active link of a station (main.c:1158, static, returns int). It takes dev->mt76.mutex itself (1167; the caller must not hold it) and releases it at the unlock label on every path. For each active link (for_each_sta_active_link) it skips the link (continue) if link_conf, the vif link or the station link structure is NULL. ASSOC: calls mt7996_mcu_add_sta with CONN_STATE_CONNECT and, if that succeeds, mt7996_mcu_add_rate_ctrl, then sets MT_WCID_TX_INFO_SET in wcid.tx_info; the first failing MCU call jumps to unlock and its error is returned, so later links are not processed. AUTHORIZE: mt7996_mcu_add_sta with CONN_STATE_PORT_SECURE; an error is returned the same way. DISASSOC: tears down all TWT flows of the link, then for a non-MLO station calls mt7996_mcu_add_sta with CONN_STATE_DISCONNECT (its result is ignored), or for an MLO station on its last remaining link calls mt7996_mcu_teardown_mld_sta (result ignored), and then SETS msta_link->wcid.sta_disabled = 1 and sets wcid.sta = 0 and removes the link from the local links mask. Returns 0 unless an ASSOC or AUTHORIZE MCU call failed.

functions.name: mt7996_set_radar_background
functions.prose_contract: Starts or stops the background radar (RDD2) detector (main.c:2112, static, returns int). Picks phy = mt7996_band_phy(dev, chandef->chan->band) when chandef is given, else dev->rdd2_phy; if phy is NULL it returns -EINVAL before taking the mutex (2124-2125). It then takes dev->mt76.mutex and, with ret preset to -EINVAL, goes to out (unlock, return ret) if mt76.region is NL80211_DFS_UNSET (returns -EINVAL), or returns -EBUSY via out if dev->rdd2_phy is set to a different phy. It computes running = rdd2_phy set and rdd2_chandef valid and its channel flagged IEEE80211_CHAN_RADAR. If chandef is NULL, or running, or chandef's channel is not a radar channel, it first calls mt7996_mcu_rdd_background_enable(phy, NULL) (error returned via out); if not running it then jumps to update_phy, otherwise it falls through. Otherwise (and in the running fall-through) it calls mt7996_mcu_rdd_background_enable(phy, chandef) (error returned via out). At update_phy it sets dev->rdd2_phy = phy when chandef is non-NULL and NULL otherwise, and copies *chandef into dev->rdd2_chandef only when chandef is non-NULL (rdd2_chandef is left unchanged when chandef is NULL). Returns the last MCU result (0 on success).

functions.name: mt7996_mcu_get_temperature
functions.prose_contract: Queries the firmware temperature (mcu.c:4058; the packet name mt7996_mcu_get_temp does not exist, the slice cut the head). It builds a local request (tag TEMPERATURE_QUERY, action GET_TEMPERATURE, band_idx = phy->mt76->band_idx) and calls mt76_mcu_send_and_get_msg with MCU_WM_UNI_CMD(THERMAL) and wait set. If that returns non-zero the function returns that error and no reply skb is held by it. Otherwise it reads res->temperature (a little-endian u32 at the packed reply layout) from skb->data without checking skb->len, frees the reply skb with dev_kfree_skb, and returns the converted u32 value through the int return type (a value above INT_MAX would read as negative).

functions.name: mt76_testmode_tx_init
functions.prose_contract: Prepares the test-mode TX frame and rate (testmode.c:178, static, returns int). It first calls mt76_testmode_alloc_skb(phy, td->tx_mpdu_len) and returns its error if non-zero: -ENOMEM when the head skb allocation fails (td->tx_skb is left as it was), or -ENOMEM when a fragment allocation fails, in which case that function has already called mt76_testmode_free_skb, so the previous td->tx_skb is freed (not left unchanged); on success td->tx_skb is the newly built skb. If td->tx_rate_mode is above MT76_TM_TX_MODE_VHT it returns 0 with no rate setup. Otherwise max_nss = number of antennas, limited by td->tx_antenna_mask if set; rates[0] gets count 1 and idx = td->tx_rate_idx. By mode: CCK returns -EINVAL if the band is not 2 GHz or idx > 4; OFDM on a non-2 GHz band does no range check and keeps idx as requested, while on 2 GHz it returns -EINVAL if idx > 8 and otherwise adds 4 to idx; HT returns -EINVAL if idx > 8*max_nss unless idx == 32 with channel width >= 40 MHz, and sets IEEE80211_TX_RC_MCS; VHT returns -EINVAL if idx > 9 or td->tx_rate_nss > max_nss, then sets the VHT rate and RC_VHT_MCS flag. Then it sets SHORT_GI, LDPC, STBC when requested, and, for modes HT and above, the 40/80/160 MHz width flag from phy->chandef.width. Returns 0. The -EINVAL returns happen after the new skb was already stored in td->tx_skb, which is not freed on those paths.

functions.name: rtw_bf_assoc
functions.prose_contract: Registers the associated AP as a beamformee (bf.c:30, void). If the chip does not support the 5 GHz band it returns immediately (45-46), before taking rcu_read_lock, so no RCU lock is taken on that path. Otherwise it takes rcu_read_lock and looks up the AP station by bssid; if not found it unlocks, logs a warning and returns. It then takes pointers to the 5 GHz band's VHT capability and the station's deflink.vht_cap, and calls rcu_read_unlock BEFORE using those capability pointers (the station pointer is used after the RCU section ends). If the local device is MU-beamformee capable and the AP is MU-beamformer capable: it returns without changes if bfer_mu_cnt >= chip->bfer_mu_max_num (debug log); else it sets bfee mac_addr, role RTW_BFEE_MU, p_aid and aid (vif->cfg.aid), increments bfer_mu_cnt and calls rtw_chip_config_bfee(..., true); it does not touch su_reg_index or bfer_su_reg_maping.
