Else if SU beamformee/beamformer are both capable: it returns without changes if bfer_su_cnt >= bfer_su_max_num; else it sets mac_addr, role RTW_BFEE_SU, sound_dim from the AP's sounding dimensions, g_id 0 and p_aid, increments bfer_su_cnt, claims the first free bit in bfer_su_reg_maping for bfee->su_reg_index (if none is free su_reg_index is left unchanged), and calls rtw_chip_config_bfee(..., true). If neither case applies it does nothing more.

functions.name: rtw_coex_set_ant_path
functions.prose_contract: Sets the coexistence antenna path for a phase (coex.c:1283, static, void). If force is false and coex_dm->cur_ant_pos_type already equals phase it returns doing nothing. Otherwise it stores phase in cur_ant_pos_type, then calls rtw_coex_check_rfk and logs bt_disabled; these happen before the switch, so they also happen for an unknown phase. Per phase: POWERON sets the coex control owner (true if bt_disabled, else false) and selects ctrl BBSW / pos TO_BT; it does not set the GNT_BT/GNT_WL signals. INIT sets GNT_BT low and GNT_WL high if bt_disabled, else GNT_BT high and GNT_WL low, takes the control owner, ctrl BBSW / pos TO_BT. WONLY sets GNT_BT low, GNT_WL high, owner true, BBSW / TO_WLG. WOFF only releases the control owner (false) and selects ctrl BY_BT / pos NOCARE, with no GNT changes. 2G sets both GNT to HW_PTA, owner true, ctrl BY_PTA / NOCARE. 5G sets GNT_BT HW_PTA and GNT_WL SW_HIGH, owner true, BBSW / TO_WLA. 2G_FREERUN sets GNT_BT HW_PTA, GNT_WL SW_HIGH, BBSW / TO_WLG_BT. 2G_WLBT sets both to HW_PTA, BBSW / TO_WLG_BT. An unknown phase executes WARN(1) and returns without calling the antenna switch. After a known phase, if the selected ctrl and pos types are both valid and coex_rfe->ant_switch_exist, it calls rtw_coex_set_ant_switch(rtwdev, ctrl_type, pos_type).

functions.name: rtw8821c_phy_pwrtrack
functions.prose_contract: Periodic thermal power tracking for the RTL8821C (rtw8821c.c:1092, static, void). It first calls rtw_phy_config_swing_table to fill a local swing table, and only then returns if efuse.thermal_meter[0] == 0xff (1100-1101), so the swing-table call is made even in that early-return case and no thermal read, tracking or IQK check follows. Otherwise it reads the path-A thermal meter, feeds it to rtw_phy_pwrtrack_avg, and then: if dm_info->pwr_trk_init_trigger is set it clears that flag and continues to the power computation even if the thermal value has not changed; else if rtw_phy_pwrtrack_thermal_changed reports no change it skips straight to the IQK check. The power computation gets delta (capped to RTW_PWR_TRK_TBL_SZ - 1) and the new delta_power_index[A] from the swing table; if that equals delta_power_index_last[A] it skips to the IQK check, else it stores it into delta_power_index_last and calls rtw8821c_pwrtrack_set. At the iqk label, if rtw_phy_pwrtrack_need_iqk is true it calls rtw8821c_do_iqk.

functions.name: rtw89_mcc_duration_decision_on_bt
functions.prose_contract: Decides how MCC role durations are adapted to the BT duration (chan.c:1691, static, returns bool). Returns false at once, changing nothing, if mcc->bt_role.duration is 0. If both the reference and auxiliary roles are on 2 GHz it calls rtw89_mcc_mod_duration_dual_2ghz_with_bt (which clamps bt_role.duration and rewrites both role durations) and returns true; this is the only path that returns true. If neither role is on 2 GHz it logs and returns false without changes. If exactly one role is on 2 GHz it calls rtw89_mcc_mod_duration_diff_band_with_bt with the 2 GHz role first and the other second, then returns false. That helper itself returns without changing anything when the non-2 GHz role's duration is already >= the BT duration (chan.c:1665-1668); otherwise it sets the non-2 GHz duration to the BT duration (capped by that role's limit.max_dur if its limit is enabled) and the 2 GHz duration to mcc_interval minus that. So in the exactly-one-2GHz case the durations may or may not be modified, and the result is false either way.

functions.name: rtw89_mcc_fill_role_limit
functions.prose_contract: Fills the MCC time-of-arrival/-of-beacon limit of a P2P GC role from its NoA descriptor (chan.c:881, static, void). It returns immediately if !mcc_role->is_gc (894-895), before any RCU lock is taken. Otherwise it recalculates the once-NoA (rtw89_p2p_noa_once_recalc), takes rcu_read_lock, dereferences the link's bss_conf and scans its P2P NoA descriptors for one with count == 255; if none is found it calls rcu_read_unlock and returns (910-911). If found, it copies start_time, interval and duration and unlocks RCU. It then returns without enabling a limit if the NoA interval differs from the beacon interval in us, if rtw89_mac_port_get_tsf fails (warning), if max_toa_us or max_tob_us is 0 (boundary), or if max_dur_us < max_toa_us. Otherwise it sets limit.max_toa, max_tob (both microseconds divided by 1024), limit.max_dur = max_toa + max_tob and limit.enable = true. The early returns do not write limit.enable or any other limit field; whatever value the role already had is kept, which relies on the caller having cleared the role beforehand.

functions.name: _chk_btc_err
functions.prose_contract: Updates a BTC error counter/flag selected by type (coex.c:1103, static, void). It logs type and cnt, then switches on type; an unlisted type changes nothing. WL_FW_VER_MATCH sets wl->fw_ver_mismatch and error.map.wl_ver_mismatch to whether the high 16 bits of wl->ver_info.fw_coex differ from chip->wlcx_desired (cnt is unused). The hang types RPT, CYCLE, W1, B1 and E2G each compare the passed cnt with the value stored last time in cnt_dm[...]; if equal AND their extra condition holds (RPT: btc->fwinfo.rpt_en_map non-zero; CYCLE: tdma_now.type != CXTDMA_OFF or ext_ctrl == CXECTL_EXT; W1 and B1: tdma_now.type != CXTDMA_OFF; E2G: ext_ctrl == CXECTL_EXT) the matching *_HANG counter is incremented, else reset to 0; the corresponding error.map flag is set when that counter >= BTC_CHK_HANG_MAX and cleared otherwise, and the stored cnt_dm value is updated to cnt. TDMA_NONSYNC and SLOT_NONSYNC increment their counter when cnt != 0, else reset it, and set tdma_no_sync/slot_no_sync when the counter >= BTC_CHK_HANG_MAX (no stored cnt update). BTTX_HANG ignores the passed cnt and uses cx->cnt_bt[BTC_BCNT_LOPRI_TX]: it counts up if that is 0 and bt->link_info.slave_role is set, else resets, and sets error.map.bt_tx_hang at the maximum. BTCNT_HANG likewise ignores cnt and sums the four BT hi/lo-pri rx/tx counters: counts up while the sum is 0, else resets; and calls _update_bt_scbd(rtwdev, false) when the counter has reached the maximum while bt->enable.now is set, or when the counter is 0 while bt->enable.now is clear. WL_SLOT_DRIFT and BT_SLOT_DRIFT count up when cnt >= BTC_CHK_WLSLOT_DRIFT_MAX / BTC_CHK_BTSLOT_DRIFT_MAX, else reset, and set wl_slot_drift/bt_slot_drift at the maximum.

functions.name: rtw89_debugfs_file_read
functions.prose_contract: Generic debugfs read for rtw89 (debug.c:155, static). bufsz is opt->rsize or PAGE_SIZE. If debugfs_priv->rbuf is NULL it allocates it with devm_kzalloc(bufsz); if the buffer is still NULL it returns -ENOMEM. If *ppos is non-zero it uses n = debugfs_priv->rused (the byte count saved by the previous read at position 0) and returns simple_read_from_buffer(userbuf, count, ppos, buf, n), whose result depends on ppos and count and is not itself the cached count. If *ppos is 0 and opt->rlock is set, it calls wiphy_locked_debugfs_read(... rtw89_debugfs_file_read_helper ...), stores its result in rused and returns it directly (that helper copies to userbuf itself). If *ppos is 0 and rlock is clear it calls rtw89_debugfs_file_read_helper(wiphy, file, buf, bufsz, debugfs_priv) with no lock taken by this function, stores the result in rused (a negative result is stored as-is, converted to the rused type) and returns simple_read_from_buffer(userbuf, count, ppos, buf, n) with that n. The helper's callback behaviour was not read, so what a non-positive callback result does is not claimed here.

functions.name: rtw89_debug_mac_dump_dle_dbg
functions.prose_contract: Formats the DLE (WDE/PLE) debug registers into buf (debug.c:1253, static, returns int; the slice cut the head). It first calls rtw89_mac_check_mac_en(rtwdev, 0, RTW89_DMAC_SEL); if that fails it writes '[DLE]  : DMAC not enabled' into buf and returns the bytes written (a non-negative length via the out label). Otherwise it dumps free-page head/tail and public page count for WDE and PLE and then, for each quota id of WDE (up to WDE_QTAID_CPUIO) and of PLE (up to PLE_QTAID_CPUIO), rsv_pgnum and use_pgnum, appending text with scnprintf. Each register read goes through the local macro DLE_DFI_DUMP, which writes the DFI control register and polls it with read_poll_timeout (1000 us interval, 50000 us limit); on timeout the macro logs an error and executes return __ret, so this function then returns the (negative) poll error immediately, with the text appended so far left in buf. If all reads succeed it returns p - buf, the number of bytes written.

functions.name: rtw89_ops_change_vif_links
functions.prose_contract: mac80211 change_vif_links callback (mac80211.c:1645). Asserts the wiphy lock. Returns -EOPNOTSUPP, before any change, if rtw89_can_work_on_links(rtwdev, vif, new_links) is false. When links are being removed (old_links == 0 or some link is cleared) it kzallocs a snapshot of the old bss_conf pointers (-ENOMEM on failure, nothing else done yet) and publishes it in rtwvif->snap_link_confs. It then leaves IPS (rtw89_leave_ips_by_hwflags), aborts a running scan, and calls rtw89_vif_update_fw_links(rtwdev, rtwvif, old_links, true); then clears the idle link if old_links was 0, else clears clr_links if non-empty. If it removed links it resets snap_link_confs to NULL, calls synchronize_rcu and kfrees the snapshot. Then if set_links is non-empty it sets those links (on failure it clears them again) and keeps the error in ret; else if new_links is 0 it sets the idle link (clearing it on failure). If ret is 0 it calls rtw89_vif_update_fw_links(rtwdev, rtwvif, new_links, false). It then re-enters IPS (rtw89_enter_ips_by_hwflags) and returns ret (0 or the set-links error). The effect of the two update_fw_links calls (what is sent to firmware, and whether the ml_trans state set elsewhere is needed) was not read, so no claim about firmware updates is made.

functions.name: get_mcs_ra_mask
functions.prose_contract: Pure static helper (phy.c:53) that builds a rate-adaptation bitmask from a 2-bit-per-stream MCS map. It loops i = 0..3 over the 4 two-bit fields of mcs_map (low field first), with nss starting at 12 and increasing by 12 per field (shift 12, 24, 36, 48). For field value 2 it ORs GENMASK_ULL(highest_mcs, 0) << nss; for 1 it ORs GENMASK_ULL(highest_mcs - gap, 0) << nss; for 0 it ORs GENMASK_ULL(highest_mcs - gap*2, 0) << nss; for 3 (and nothing else) it adds nothing. It returns the accumulated u64. It has no side effects, takes no locks and touches no global state. GENMASK_ULL with a high bit below 0 (when highest_mcs < gap or highest_mcs < 2*gap in the respective case) is not valid, so callers must pass highest_mcs >= 2*gap.

functions.name: rtw89_phy_txpwr_dbm_to_mac
functions.prose_contract: Static inline (phy.h:977) converting a dBm value to the MAC tx-power unit. It computes dbm << rtwdev->chip->txpwr_factor_mac in int (dbm is s8, promoted; shifting a negative dbm left is not well-defined C), converts that int to s16 in clamp_t(s16, ..., -64, 63), so a result outside the s16 range would first wrap, then clamps it to the range -64..63, and returns that as s8. The clamp range includes negative values (-64..-1), so the result is not limited to 0..63. It reads only rtwdev->chip->txpwr_factor_mac; it has no side effects.

functions.name: _dpk_pas_read
functions.prose_contract: Static DPK helper (rtw8851b_rfk.c:2289, returns u8). It does return a value: the final comparison at 2327-2332. It writes the PAS-read configuration registers (R_KIP_RPT1, R_DPK_CFG2, R_DPK_CFG3). If is_check is non-zero it reads two (I,Q) pairs from R_RPT_COM at index 0 and index 0x1f, takes the absolute value of the 12-bit sign-extended I and Q parts, and logs the ratio PAS_delta; if is_check is 0 it only loops over 32 indexes writing R_DPK_CFG3 and logging each report word, and leaves all four value variables at 0. In both cases it then computes sqrt-sum values val1 = I1^2 + Q1^2 and val2 = I2^2 + Q2^2 (both 0 when is_check is 0) and returns 2 if val1 < val2, else 1 if val1 >= val2 * 8 / 5, else 0. So with is_check == 0 it returns 1 (0 >= 0), and with is_check != 0 it returns 2, 1 or 0 by that comparison.

functions.name: _iqk_one_shot
functions.prose_contract: Runs one IQK calibration step on an RTL8852A path (rtw8852a_rfk.c:802, static bool). It picks addr_rfc_ctl = 0x5864 for path A else 0x7864 and always sends the BTC notification BTC_WRFK_ONESHOT_START first (817), before the ktype switch. Per ktype it builds iqk_cmd: ID_TXAGC and ID_RXAGC only build the command (no register writes before the shot); ID_FLOK_COARSE, ID_FLOK_FINE, ID_RXK and ID_NBRXK set bit 0x20000000 of addr_rfc_ctl and write R_IQK_DIF4 (TXT 0x009 for the FLOK types, RXT 0x011 for the RX types); ID_TXK and ID_NBTXK clear that bit and write R_IQK_DIF4 TXT 0x025. For an unknown ktype it returns false right away, after the START notification but without sending STOP, writing the command or clearing addr_rfc_ctl (857-858). For the known types it writes iqk_cmd + 1 to R_NCTL_CFG, sets R_DPK_CTL enable, delays 1 us, takes fail from _iqk_check_cal, optionally reads XYM, FFT, SRAM and (TX CFIR for ID_TXK, RX CFIR for every other ktype) data depending on the iqk_info enable flags, clears bit 0x20000000 of addr_rfc_ctl, sends BTC_WRFK_ONESHOT_STOP and returns fail.

functions.name: _dpk_lbk_rxiqk
functions.prose_contract: Runs the DPK loopback RX IQ calibration for one path (rtw8852b_rfk.c:1832, static void, no return value). It reads the current RX baseband gain (RR_MOD RXBB field) and then: enables MDPK_RX_DCK, zeroes the RXCFIR result field of R_IQK_RES for the path, copies RR_CFGCH into RR_RSV4, sets RR_MOD mode to 0xd, sets RR_RXK PLLEN, sets RR_TXIQK ATT1 to 0x13 if the RXBB value is >= 0x11, 0x00 if it is <= 0x0a, else 0x05, clears RR_XGLNA2 SW and RR_RXKPLL POW, writes 0x80014 to RR_RXKPLL, waits 70 us, sets R_P0_RFCTM_EN and R_IQK_DIF4 RXT = 0x025, runs _dpk_one_shot(LBK_RXIQK), and logs R_RXIQC. Afterwards it clears R_P0_RFCTM_EN (so that bit is restored to 0), clears RR_RXK PLLEN, clears MDPK_RX_DCK_EN and R_KPATH_CFG_ED, sets R_LOAD_COEF DI to 1 and sets RR_MOD mode to 0x5. It does not restore the earlier values of RR_RSV4, RR_TXIQK ATT1, RR_XGLNA2 SW, RR_RXKPLL, R_IQK_DIF4 RXT or the R_IQK_RES RXCFIR field; these keep the values written above. Callee _dpk_one_shot not read.

functions.name: _iqk_one_shot
functions.prose_contract: Runs one IQK step on an RTL8852B path (rtw8852b_rfk.c:815, static bool). For an unknown ktype it returns false immediately (858-859), before writing anything and before clearing B_P0_RFCTM_EN. For known ktypes it builds iqk_cmd: FLOK_COARSE, FLOK_FINE, FLOK_VBUFFER, RXK and NBRXK set B_P0_RFCTM_EN to 1 first; TXK and NBTXK set it to 0 first; RXAGC writes no R_P0_RFCTM_EN value before the shot; NBTXK writes R_IQK_DIF4 TXT 0x011 and NBRXK writes R_IQK_DIF4 RXT 0x011. It then writes iqk_cmd + 1 to R_NCTL_CFG, waits 1 us, sets fail = _iqk_check_cal(rtwdev, path), writes B_P0_RFCTM_EN = 0 and returns fail. So B_P0_RFCTM_EN is cleared after every known-ktype shot (including RXAGC) but not on the unknown-ktype return.

functions.name: rtw89_tas_track
functions.prose_contract: Static bool (sar.c:778) running one TAS (transmit antenna selection power) tracking step. In order: returns false if the TAS dynamic mechanism bit is set in hal->disabled_dm_bitmap; returns false if rtw89_tas_is_active() is false; if rtw89_tas_query_sar_config fails OR tas->block_regd is set it returns the result of __rtw89_tas_state_update(rtwdev, RTW89_TAS_STATE_STATIC_SAR) (so not necessarily false, and the state update happens before the pause check); then returns false if tas->pause is set (this check comes after the query and the block_regd test); otherwise it calls rtw89_tas_window_update and rtw89_tas_history_update and returns rtw89_tas_rolling_average(rtwdev). The meaning of the returned bool beyond these callee results was not read.

functions.name: blake2b_update
functions.prose_contract: Feeds inlen bytes from in into an initialised blake2b_state (blake2b.c:358). It has one return statement, return 0 at line 385, so it returns 0 for every input including inlen == 0 (no pointer or finalised-state check is made). While inlen > 0 it computes left = S->buflen and fill = 2*BLAKE2B_BLOCKBYTES - left. If inlen > fill it copies fill bytes into S->buf, adds the block counter for one block, compresses the first block of the buffer, moves the second block down to the first, subtracts BLAKE2B_BLOCKBYTES from buflen and advances in/inlen by fill. Otherwise (inlen <= fill) it copies the remaining inlen bytes into the buffer after left, increases buflen by inlen and ends. Because compression only happens when input exceeds the space left, after the call S->buflen can equal 2*BLAKE2B_BLOCKBYTES (when the buffer is exactly full), i.e. up to two whole blocks stay buffered and uncompressed; it is never above that. The caller must have initialised S so that buflen <= 2*BLAKE2B_BLOCKBYTES and S->buf has space for 2 blocks.

functions.name: sc25519_reduce
functions.prose_contract: Reduces a 64-byte little-endian scalar modulo the Ed25519 group order l = 2^252 + 27742317777372353535851937790883648493 in place (ed25519_ref10.c:1557, void; the name sc_reduce in the packet is not the real name). It reads s[0..63] (through load_3/load_4 into 24 21-bit limbs s0..s23), performs the fixed sequence of limb multiplications, carries and subtractions of the reference ref10 reduction without any branch or return, and finally stores exactly 32 bytes s[0] .. s[31] (32 byte stores, none to s[32] or higher). On return the first 32 bytes hold the little-endian value of the input mod l; bytes s[32]..s[63] are not written by this function and keep their input values. The caller must supply a writable 64-byte buffer. No allocation, no locks.

functions.name: crypto_generichash_blake2b_final
functions.prose_contract: Thin wrapper (generichash_blake2b.c:100) that does assert(outlen <= UINT8_MAX) (a no-op when NDEBUG is defined) and returns blake2b_final(state, out, (uint8_t) outlen), so outlen is truncated to 8 bits if the assert is compiled out. The callee (blake2b-ref.c:290) calls sodium_misuse() (which does not return) if the 8-bit outlen is 0 or greater than BLAKE2B_OUTBYTES (64); it returns -1 without writing anything if the state is already finalised (blake2b_is_lastblock); otherwise it compresses any extra full block, pads and compresses the last block, writes the first outlen bytes of the 64-byte state hash into out (it does not compare outlen with the digest length stored in the state at init time), zeroes S->h and S->buf with sodium_memzero and returns 0. So the result is 0 or -1, and a state that returned 0 is wiped and must not be reused.

functions.name: GetMacAddrHashCode
functions.prose_contract: Pure static function (memac.c:57) that computes a 6-bit multicast hash from the low 48 bits of ethAddr (a local copy, shifted away; the argument is by value). For i = 0..5 it XORs the 8 bits 8*i .. 8*i+7 of the original value (mask1 takes bit 8i, then XOR with the next 7 bits) and ORs that parity bit into bit (5 - i) of the result. Bits 48..63 of the input are never read. The result is therefore in 0..63 and bit 5 is the parity of the first (lowest) byte and bit 0 the parity of the sixth byte. No side effects, no locks, no allocation.

functions.name: MatchTableSet
functions.prose_contract: Static t_Error (fm_cc.c:4324-4903) that fills in a CC (coarse classification) match-table node p_CcNode from p_CcNodeParam. The slice began in the middle (statistics-mode fix-up at 4363). The function asserts its three arguments non-NULL (ASSERT_COND), mallocs p_GlblMask (CC_GLBL_MASK_SIZE bytes) and memsets it without checking for NULL (4350-4352), copies key counts, mask support and statistics mode into the node, and, if maxNumOfKeys is 0 and the statistics mode is NONE, forces the mode to FRAME (4363-4365). It then obtains the MURAM handle, initialises the lists and a spinlock, and decodes the extraction parameters (by header, non-header, IC etc.) into parseCode, offsets and sizes. From that point every failure first calls DeleteNode(p_CcNode) (or FM_PCD_MatchTableDelete later) and then returns an error: E_INVALID_HANDLE if no MURAM handle (4368-4369, before any DeleteNode), E_NO_MEMORY if the spinlock cannot be created, E_INVALID_STATE / E_INVALID_SELECTION / E_INVALID_VALUE for inconsistent or unsupported extraction parameters (e.g. unknown extraction type, illegal parse code, sizeOfExtraction above FM_PCD_MAX_SIZE_OF_KEY, keySize != sizeOfExtraction, hash-indexed offset+size > 8), the error of CheckParams/IcHashIndexedCheckParams, CalcAndUpdateCcShadow or AllocStatsObjs, and E_NO_MEMORY when MURAM allocation of the temporary AD, key match table or AD table fails. It copies each key (and local mask) into the key table and writes each next-engine AD (with stats objects when statisticsEn is set), handles the miss entry, takes FmPcdLockTryLockAll: if that fails it deletes the table and returns E_BUSY; then applies required actions for each next engine (on failure unlocks, deletes the table and returns the error), unlocks and returns E_OK. So on any error return after the early part the node has already been torn down by this function; on success the caller owns the populated node (it does not return a handle; the node pointer is an argument).

functions.name: FmPcdCcTreeAddIPR
functions.prose_contract: Adds IP-reassembly (IPR) groups to a CC tree (fm_cc.c:5046). Asserts the tree pointer non-NULL. It asks whether the reassembly manip carries an IPv6 header (FmPcdManipIpReassmIsIpv6Hdr). It returns E_INVALID_VALUE if IPv6 is present and tree->numOfEntries > FM_PCD_MAX_NUM_OF_CC_GROUPS - 2, or (for any case) if numOfEntries > FM_PCD_MAX_NUM_OF_CC_GROUPS - 1; so the tree may hold at most MAX-2 entries with IPv6 and at most MAX-1 without. It then tries the root lock (CcRootTryLock); on failure it returns E_BUSY. With the lock held: if tree->h_IpReassemblyManip already equals the given manip it releases the lock and returns E_OK without adding any group or entry (nothing consumed); if a different manip is already set it releases the lock and returns E_INVALID_STATE. Otherwise, for IPv6 it takes the next group id (numOfGrps++), sets that group's base entry to MAX-2, optionally builds the reassembly scheme (createSchemes; on failure it decrements numOfGrps, releases the lock and returns the error) and writes a DONE next-engine AD at entry MAX-2; then for IPv4 it takes the next group id, sets totalBitsMask 0 and base entry MAX-1, optionally builds the IPv4 scheme (on failure it decrements numOfGrps, also again for IPv6 when present with FmPcdManipDeleteIpReassmSchemes, releases the lock and returns the error), writes the DONE AD at entry MAX-1, stores the manip in the tree, releases the lock and returns E_OK.

functions.name: BuildSchemeRegs
functions.prose_contract: Static t_Error (fm_kg.c:1009-1834; the slice 1107-1378 is a middle part) that fills a struct fman_kg_scheme_regs and the software scheme state from a KG scheme parameter block. It memsets the register block to zero, then returns E_INVALID_VALUE if numOfDistinctionUnits exceeds FM_PCD_MAX_NUM_OF_DISTINCTION_UNITS; for a non-alwaysDirect scheme it gets the netEnv id and the matching vector (E_INVALID_STATE if PcdGetUnitsVector fails), else it sets matchVector to SCHEME_ALWAYS_DIRECT and netEnvId to ILLEGAL_NETENV. It returns E_INVALID_STATE if nextEngine is e_FM_PCD_INVALID; E_NOT_SUPPORTED for bypassFqidGeneration on unsupported FM revisions, and E_INVALID_VALUE if bypassFqidGeneration is set with a non-zero baseFqid. For the PLCR next engine it records direct/absolute and returns E_INVALID_STATE for indirect policing with a shared profile; for the CC next engine it queries the tree group (FmPcdCcGetGrpParams, error passed on) and returns E_INVALID_VALUE (not E_INVALID_STATE) when a shared profile is requested in a KG->CC->PLCR flow (fm_kg.c:1219; a different shared-profile check at 1119 does return E_INVALID_STATE). Further E_INVALID_VALUE returns cover fqidOffsetShift too large and numOfProfiles zero or not a power of two, hash and extract parameters out of range, etc.; E_NOT_SUPPORTED, E_FULL (generic registers exhausted), E_INVALID_SELECTION and E_NO_MEMORY returns appear in the extract section. At the end it checks baseFqid fits in 24 bits (E_INVALID_VALUE), sets kgse_fqb, records nextEngine and doneAction in p_Scheme and returns E_OK. Many of the intermediate scheme fields (matchVector, netEnvId, ccUnits, directPlcr, etc.) are therefore already written into p_Scheme when a later error is returned.

functions.name: CheckManipParamsAndSetType
functions.prose_contract: Static t_Error (fm_manip.c:2527-2655) that validates a header-manipulation request and sets p_Manip->opcode (and sometimes muramAllocate). Exactly one branch is taken: remove, else insert, else frag/reassembly. Remove (u.hdr.rmv) is accepted only for rmvParams type BY_HDR / FROM_START: with include set and header CAPWAP_DTLS it sets opcode CAPWAP_RMV_DTLS_IF_EXIST and muramAllocate = TRUE, returns E_INVALID_STATE if insrt is also set, and, if fragOrReasm is set, accepts only non-frag reassembly with header CAPWAP (opcode becomes CAPWAP_REASSEMBLY) and returns E_INVALID_STATE otherwise (frag, or another header); with include clear and header CAPWAP_DTLS or CAPWAP it returns E_INVALID_STATE if fragOrReasm or insrt is set, else sets opcode HMAN_OC_RMV_N_OR_INSRT_INT_FRM_HDR, muramAllocate = TRUE and WRITES p_ManipParams->u.hdr.insrt = TRUE (it modifies the caller's parameter block). Any other remove type, location or header returns E_INVALID_STATE. Insert (only when rmv is not set) supports only the by-template type: opcode INSRT_HDR_BY_TEMPL_N_OR_FRAG_AFTER with muramAllocate = FALSE, changed to CAPWAP_FRAGMENTATION when fragOrReasm with frag and CAPWAP header is requested; other fragOrReasm combinations and insert types return E_INVALID_STATE. Frag/reassembly alone: frag with CAPWAP sets opcode CAPWAP_FRAGMENTATION and muramAllocate FALSE; reassembly alone always returns E_INVALID_STATE. If none of rmv, insrt, fragOrReasm is set it returns E_INVALID_STATE. Because opcode/muramAllocate are assigned before some of the later E_INVALID_STATE returns, a failing call can leave those fields modified in p_Manip. On success it copies insrt and rmv from the params into p_Manip->insrt and p_Manip->rmv (2651-2652) and returns E_OK.

functions.name: FmPcdManipInitUpdate
functions.prose_contract: Static t_Error dispatcher (fm_manip.c:4562-4621) that initialises or updates the AD for a manipulation according to p_Manip->opcode. It first applies SANITY_CHECK_RETURN_ERROR(h_Manip, E_INVALID_HANDLE) (macro: returns the handle error when h_Manip is NULL). The level and h_FmTree arguments are marked UNUSED in this function body (they are passed to a callee only in the FM_CAPWAP_SUPPORT / DPAA_VERSION == 10 block), so no valid tree handle is required by this function itself. By opcode: HMAN_OC_IP_REASSEMBLY calls UpdateInitReasm; HMAN_OC_IP_FRAGMENTATION calls UpdateInitIpFrag; with DPAA_VERSION >= 11, HMAN_OC_CAPWAP_FRAGMENTATION calls UpdateInitCapwapFrag and HMAN_OC_CAPWAP_REASSEMBLY calls UpdateInitReasm; in a DPAA 1.0 CAPWAP build additional cases exist (MV_INT_FRAME_HDR..., INSRT_HDR_BY_TEMPL with a frag handle, CAPWAP_RMV_DTLS_IF_EXIST with h_Frag, CAPWAP_INDEXED_STATS); for the INSRT_HDR_BY_TEMPL case with h_Frag NULL and for CAPWAP_RMV_DTLS_IF_EXIST with h_Frag NULL the function does no callee call and returns E_OK. Any other opcode returns E_OK at once with no effect. Otherwise it returns the callee's error code (E_OK on success). It takes no locks of its own here; callee behaviour was not read.

functions.name: FM_PCD_ManipNodeSet
functions.prose_contract: Public function returning a t_Handle (fm_manip.c:5198-5342; the packet name FM_PCD_ManipNodeCreate is not in this file, the slice cut the head). It applies SANITY_CHECK_RETURN_VALUE on h_FmPcd and p_ManipParams (NULL return with E_INVALID_HANDLE if either is NULL) and calls ManipOrStatsSetNode(h_FmPcd, params, FALSE); a NULL result is returned as NULL. For opcodes HMAN_OC_IP_REASSEMBLY, IP_FRAGMENTATION, HMAN_OC, IPSEC_MANIP (and, for DPAA_VERSION >= 11, CAPWAP_MANIP, CAPWAP_FRAGMENTATION, CAPWAP_REASSEMBLY) it requires FmPcdIsAdvancedOffloadSupported; if not, it reports E_INVALID_STATE, frees p_Manip with XX_Free and returns NULL. It then creates a spinlock (XX_InitSpinlock); on failure it reports an error, calls ReleaseManipHandler, frees p_Manip and returns NULL. It initialises the node list and switches on p_Manip->opcode to the matching setup routine: IpReassembly, IpFragmentation followed by IPManip (stopping at the first error), IPSecManip, CapwapReassembly, CapwapFragmentation, CapwapManip (DPAA >= 11), or CreateManipActionNew for HMAN_OC; extra cases exist under FM_CAPWAP_SUPPORT with DPAA_VERSION == 10; an unknown opcode reports E_INVALID_VALUE, releases the handler, frees p_Manip and returns NULL. If the selected routine returns an error it reports it, calls ReleaseManipHandler, frees p_Manip and returns NULL. On success, if p_ManipParams->h_NextManip is set it stores it in p_Manip->h_NextManip, sets the next manip's previous pointer to p_Manip and increments its owner count (FmPcdManipUpdateOwner(..., TRUE)); it returns p_Manip, owned by the caller. On the failure paths this function does not free the spinlock itself (any release is inside ReleaseManipHandler, not read).

functions.name: BuildProfileRegs
functions.prose_contract: Static t_Error (fm_plcr.c:334-530) that builds the policer profile register image in p_PlcrRegs. It asserts p_FmPcd. It returns E_NOT_AVAILABLE if FmGetTimeStampScale returns 0, and returns the error of SetProfileNia if converting the green, yellow or red next-engine parameters fails (those three NIA values are then stored at the end). pemode starts at FM_PCD_PLCR_PEMODE_PI. Pass-through: sets pecir, pecbs, pepepir_eir, pepbs_ebs, pelts, pects and pepts_ets all to 0 (token buckets are NOT set full), clears the algorithm bits, and for colour-blind mode sets the blind bit and the default colour (E_INVALID_SELECTION for an unknown default colour), for colour-aware clears it; any other colour mode returns E_INVALID_SELECTION. RFC 2698: returns E_INVALID_SELECTION if committedInfoRate > peakOrExcessInformationRate; RFC 2698 and RFC 4115 share the continuation: colour-blind sets the blind bit, colour-aware clears it and selects the override colour (E_INVALID_SELECTION for an invalid value), then the rate mode: byte mode selects frame-length and roll-back selections (E_INVALID_SELECTION for invalid values), packet mode sets the PKT bit, other modes are E_INVALID_SELECTION; then CalcRates fills cir, cbs, pir_eir, pbs_ebs and the floating-point position into the registers, and pepts_ets and pects are set to 0xFFFFFFFF (full buckets) here. Any other algSelection returns E_INVALID_SELECTION. On success it stores pemode and the three NIAs and zeroes the five colour counters pegpc, peypc, perpc, perypc and perrpc (fm_plcr.c:523-527), then returns E_OK. Registers assigned before a later error return stay partly written in p_PlcrRegs.

functions.name: SetPcd
functions.prose_contract: Static t_Error (fm_port.c:1111-1668) that programs a port's PCD (parser/keygen/CC/policer) configuration. Early checks, each returning an error before any register write: SANITY_CHECK E_INVALID_STATE if p_FmPortDriverParam is still set (port not yet initialised), E_INVALID_OPERATION for independent-mode ports and for port types other than RX, RX_10G and offline-parsing, E_INVALID_STATE for pcdSupport NONE or an unknown value, E_INVALID_VALUE if the parser's numOfHdrsWithAdditionalParams exceeds FM_PCD_PRS_NUM_OF_HDRS, and E_INVALID_STATE when the presence of the PRS, KG and CC parameter blocks does not match pcdSupport (the PLCR parameter block is not part of that consistency check). It sets p_FmPort->netEnvId and pcdEngines (written before these later checks fail). With CC it binds the tree (FmPcdCcBindTree, error returned) and writes the CC base register. With KG it requires at least one scheme (E_INVALID_VALUE), calls FmPcdKgSetOrBindToClsPlanGrp (any failure becomes E_INVALID_VALUE), records each scheme in schemesPerPortVector, returns E_INVALID_STATE for a VSPE scheme when the port has no VSPE (DPAA >= 11), and calls FmPcdKgBindPortToSchemes (error returned). The policer parameters p_PlcrParams are dereferenced only for pcdSupport PLCR_ONLY and PRS_AND_PLCR: there h_Profile must be set and valid (E_INVALID_STATE otherwise) and the profile id is written to the parse NIA or ORed into savedBmiNia. CC_ONLY (and the CAPWAP CC variants) require an offline-parsing port (E_INVALID_OPERATION). With PRS it maps firstPrsHdr to a header number (E_NOT_SUPPORTED if illegal), writes the parser NIA according to the pcdSupport combination (PRS_AND_PLCR writes nothing in that switch, a value not handled there gives E_INVALID_STATE, and E_INVALID_VALUE if a direct scheme is not among the port's schemes), configures the parser start offset, the stop/enable bits and the additional header parameters (errors E_INVALID_VALUE from AdditionalPrsParams etc.), and finally writes the initial parse result registers. It returns E_OK at the end. Partial register writes done before a later error are not undone by this function.

functions.name: FmSetNumOfOpenDmas
functions.prose_contract: Sets the number of open DMAs for one FM port (fm_ncsw.c:2808-2953; the slice cut the head). p_NumOfOpenDmas and p_NumOfExtraOpenDmas are in/out: their values are read as the request at entry (2818) and, in two paths, overwritten with the values read from the registers (2868-2869 and 2906-2907). Asserts 1 <= hardwarePortId <= 63. Guest with no mapped registers but an IPC session: it sends an FM_SET_NUM_OF_OPEN_DMAS IPC message, returns the IPC error (MINOR) if sending fails, E_INVALID_VALUE if the reply length is wrong, else the reply's error code, and does nothing else. Otherwise the behaviour depends on build options: with FM_HAS_TOTAL_DMAS any non-master guest returns E_NOT_SUPPORTED; without it a non-master guest with mapped registers and FM major revision >= 6 either (when the requested count is 0) reads the current counts from the registers into the two output pointers, or writes the requested counts with fman_set_num_of_open_dmas, and continues; any other non-master guest returns E_NOT_SUPPORTED (so E_NOT_SUPPORTED is returned in more than the no-IPC/no-register case). Then, if !initialConfig it reads the current per-port values; with FM_NO_GUARANTEED_RESET_VALUES and a requested count of 0 it takes the register values into the pool/accumulated counters and the output pointers and returns E_OK. Otherwise it raises extraOpenDmasPoolSize if the new extra count exceeds the current one, checks the total against the limit (E_NOT_AVAILABLE when FM_HAS_TOTAL_DMAS and rev < 6 exceed maxNumOfOpenDmas, or rev >= 6 exceeds DMA_THRESH_MAX_COMMQ + 1, except rev 6.0 when the A006981 errata macro is defined); if within limits it updates accumulatedNumOfOpenDmas (minus the current value, plus the request) and writes the DMA counts to the registers. Returns E_OK at the end, or the errors above.

functions.name: qman_retire_fq
functions.prose_contract: Static t_Error (qm_portal_fqr.c:274-330) that retires a frame queue. It returns E_INVALID_STATE (via SANITY_CHECK_RETURN_ERROR) unless p_Fq->state is parked or sched, and E_INVALID_VALUE if QMAN_FQ_FLAG_NO_MODIFY is set, both before taking any lock and without touching *p_Flags. It then takes the portal lock (NCSW_PLOCK) and the FQ lock; if QMAN_FQ_STATE_CHANGING is set or the state is retired or oos it goes to out with E_BUSY, also without writing *p_Flags. Otherwise it starts a management command, fills the fqid (and, when drain is true, context_b with the FQ pointer), commits ALTER_RETIRE (or ALTER_RETIRE_CTXB when draining) and busy-waits for the result. On QM_MCR_RESULT_OK it sets QMAN_FQ_STATE_NE / ORL flags from the result's fqs bits and sets state = retired; on PENDING it sets QMAN_FQ_STATE_CHANGING; any other result prints an error and sets err = E_INVALID_STATE. After the result handling (including the failure case) it stores p_Fq->flags into *p_Flags if p_Flags is non-NULL. At out it releases the FQ lock and the portal lock and returns err (E_OK for OK and PENDING). So *p_Flags is written only on the paths that actually issued the command.

functions.name: run_rec_check_impl
functions.prose_contract: Static int (raidz_test.c:470-584) that tests one reconstruction function fn (index into the rec_tgts table: P, Q, R, PQ, PR, QR, PQR) over combinations of data columns and returns the number of failing combinations (err, starting at 0; it is a count, not an errno). It copies the three target indexes for fn from rec_tgts. For fn < RAIDZ_REC_PQ it loops over one data column x0 < opts->rto_dcols; for fn < RAIDZ_REC_PQR over pairs x0 < x1; otherwise over triples x0 < x1 < x2; columns at or beyond rr_cols - parity of row 0 are skipped (continue). In each iteration it first checks rto_opts.rto_should_stop and returns the current err immediately if set (so it can return before any column of that call was corrupted), then sets the data-column targets (tgtidx[2], tgtidx[1..2], or tgtidx[0..2], as x + parity) and corrupts exactly those data columns in rm (1, 2 or 3 columns depending on the branch) with corrupt_colums; the parity columns named in tgtidx are not corrupted here. Unless opts->rto_sanity is set it calls vdev_raidz_reconstruct(rm, tgtidx, 3), then compares with cmp_data and increments err when it returns non-zero. Return value: err after all combinations, or the partial err at an early stop. Side effects: modifies rm (its column data) and logs; the contents of rm after the call are the last reconstruction attempt, not restored.

functions.name: zfs_process_add
functions.prose_contract: Static void (zfs_mod.c:197-596; the slice cut the head) that handles a device-add event for one vdev of a pool; it has no return value and every exit is a plain return. It returns without action if the vdev has no path, if its vdev stats say VDEV_STATE_HEALTHY, or if it is offline and not faulted. It computes fullpath (the guid as a decimal string, or the path, with the partition stripped for a whole disk; returning if the strip allocation fails), then tries zpool_vdev_online (with CHECKREMOVE|UNSPARE, plus SPARE for spares): if that succeeds and the new state is HEALTHY or DEGRADED it logs and returns. Unless pool autoreplace is on AND the disk is a whole disk (or multipath whole disk) AND physpath is known, it tries ZFS_ONLINE_FORCEFAULT and returns. It builds a by-path or by-vdev raw path; if realpath fails and it is not a multipath whole disk, it FORCEFAULTs and returns (so a realpath failure on a multipath whole disk does not return here). It returns if the vdev state is not one of degraded, faulted, removed or can't-open. Then: for a multipath whole disk it calls zpool_prepare_disk (on failure frees the output and returns); else for an unlabeled disk it calls zpool_prepare_and_label_disk (on failure frees output, FORCEFAULTs and returns; on success it mallocs a pending-device record (exit(EXIT_FAILURE) if malloc fails), appends it to g_device_list and returns, to resume at the later partition event); else (labeled) it looks up and removes the matching pending device from g_device_list (if not found it FORCEFAULTs and returns) and may rewrite path for by-id paths. On the paths that continue it builds nvroot/newvd nvlists (returning if allocation or an nvlist_add fails, after freeing), waits for the partition link (zpool_label_disk_wait; on failure frees nvroot and returns), calls zpool_vdev_attach(replace) with rebuild, retries without rebuild if it fails, logs the result and frees nvroot. So it ends in attach in only some paths; the others return as listed.

functions.name: zfs_retire_recv
functions.prose_contract: Static void event handler (zfs_retire.c:366-634; the slice cut the head). It reads the vdev state from the payload and handles three groups of classes. (1) 'resource.fs.zfs.removed', or 'statechange' with state REMOVED/FAULTED: it notes whether the vdev type is spare or l2cache; returns if the vdev guid is missing or 0; for a spare it calls find_and_remove_spares and returns; returns if the pool guid is missing or find_by_guid fails; returns if the vdev is OFFLINE, and returns if the vdev is already REMOVED and the event state is REMOVED unless the class is 'removed' carrying 'by_kernel' (then skip_removal is set); unless skip_removal, for an l2arc vdev or a 'removed' class it calls zpool_vdev_remove_wanted; if it is not an l2arc and that call gave 0 and either spare_on_remove is off or replace_with_spare returns false, it logs 'no spare'; it frees devname, closes the pool and returns. (2) The resolved class returns at once; 'statechange' to HEALTHY and 'sysevent.fs.zfs.vdev_remove' call zfs_vdev_repair and return. (3) Otherwise it clears saved data, sets is_repair for the repaired class, returns if there is no suspect fault list, and for each fault: skips it if its retire flag is false; fault.fs.zfs.vdev.io sets fault_device, vdev.checksum and vdev.slow_io set degrade_device, fault.fs.zfs.device sets neither, fault.io.* is marked is_disk and then skipped (continue) without any action, other classes are skipped; for ZFS-scheme faults it needs the resource, pool guid and, unless is_repair (then vdev_guid becomes 0), the vdev guid, and a matching pool (else continue); a vdev_guid of 0 does zpool_clear on the whole pool and closes it (this also happens for a repair event with a missing vdev guid); a repair with a vdev guid clears that vdev and sets repair_done; otherwise it faults or degrades the vdev as flagged, calls replace_with_spare (its result ignored; a spare is only attempted) and closes the pool. Finally, for the repaired class with repair_done and a suspect UUID it calls fmd_case_uuresolved.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Entry point of the ZFS event daemon (zed.c:220-311; the slice cut the head). It initialises logging and the configuration, parses options, switches stderr logging to LOG_INFO when verbose, and calls zed_log_die (which terminates) if the effective uid is not 0 or chdir('/') fails. It closes descriptors above stderr and sets umask 0. The initial zed_conf_scan_dir(&zcp) result is checked: a negative value does exit(EXIT_FAILURE) (line 243-244); the later rescan on SIGHUP inside the main loop (line 292) ignores the result. Unless foreground it starts daemonizing and opens syslog; it installs signal handlers, optionally locks memory, writes the pid file (exit(EXIT_FAILURE) if that fails and force is not set), finishes daemonizing, logs the version, opens and reads the state file (each failure exits with EXIT_FAILURE). At the idle label it loops: zed_event_init, break if that returns false (non-zero success means retry after sleep(30) while idle mode is on and no exit was requested). If _got_exit is set at that point it jumps to out, so zed_event_fini is not called on that path. Otherwise it seeks to the saved event and runs while !_got_exit: on _got_hup it rescans the directory, and it calls zed_event_service, leaving the loop if that returns non-zero. After the loop it logs 'Exiting', calls zed_event_fini, and if do_idle is set and no exit was requested it goes back to idle; otherwise at out it destroys the conf, finalises logging and exits with EXIT_SUCCESS. It never returns from main normally; all paths end in exit or zed_log_die.

functions.name: wait_for_children
functions.prose_contract: Reaps zed's child processes (zed_exec.c:200-273, void). It first sets _reap_children_stop = B_FALSE and loops while that flag stays false (the flag is set elsewhere, not in this function). Each iteration locks _launched_processes_lock and calls wait4(0, ..., wait ? 0 : WNOHANG, &usage). If wait4 returns 0 or -1 it unlocks and then: for pid 0 or errno == ECHILD it calls pause() when do_pause is set; for any other errno except EINTR it logs a warning (and does not pause); then, if do_pause is false, it returns (so with do_pause false the function returns at the first iteration where wait4 reported no child, an error, or EINTR). If wait4 returned a pid it looks it up in the launched-process tree, copies and removes the node if found (freeing the tree node), unlocks, increments _launched_processes_limit atomically, adds system time to user time in usage, logs a 'Finished' line with exit status, signal or raw status, frees node.name (a NULL name when the pid was not found) and continues the loop, also when do_pause is false. So it returns only when do_pause is false and wait4 gave no child, or when the stop flag is set during the loop; with do_pause true it does not return on ECHILD or pid 0 but pauses and loops until the flag is set.

functions.name: share_mount_one
functions.prose_contract: Static int (zfs_main.c:7163-7390) that mounts or shares one filesystem and returns 0 or 1. Most checks return 0 quietly when explicit is false and print a message and return 1 when explicit is true: dataset zoned and we are in the global zone, or not zoned but in a non-global zone; op share with both sharenfs and sharesmb 'off' (legacy share); mountpoint 'legacy' or 'none'; canmount == off; encryption key unavailable (unless MS_CRYPT is in flags); an inconsistent dataset with a receive-resume token; a redacted dataset without MS_FORCE; and, for share, a filesystem already shared according to the nfs/smb combination; for mount, one already mounted without a remount option. The canmount == noauto case is special: only when !explicit, op mount returns 0 and op share on an unmounted filesystem calls zfs_unshare (result ignored) and returns 0, so a skipped noauto share does still call zfs_unshare; with explicit set, noauto passes through and does not return 1. After the checks: share (OP_SHARE) mounts the filesystem first if it is not mounted (return 1 if zfs_mount fails) and then calls zfs_share (return 1 on failure); mount (OP_MOUNT) calls zfs_mount with the given options and returns 1 on failure. Otherwise it returns 0.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: The slice is the tail of main (zinject.c:914-1527; no function named zinject_parse_args exists). In this tail, after the option loop (lines 914-1289, not read), main picks the injection mode and validates it, with every error path calling libzfs_fini(g_zfs) before returning: raw (-b) mode returns 2 (after usage()) if combined with other options or if argc != 1, returns 1 if error == ENXIO or the -e option is used with a delay command, or if translate_raw fails; panic (-p) returns 2 for incompatible options or when argc is not 1 or 2; import/export delay returns 2 for incompatible options or when argc != 1 or zi_duration <= 0 (so an invalid duration -s <= 0 is exit status 2, not 1); ignore-writes (-I) returns 2 for incompatible options, for nowrites == 0, for both -s and -g, or for argc != 1; with no type (TYPE_INVAL) it returns 2 if flags is 0 or if there are extra arguments (unless a pool name is given with ZINJECT_UNLOAD_SPA); otherwise (data/object injection) it returns 2 if argc != 1, and returns 1 for error types ENXIO/EILSEQ, for -C combined with decrypt/decompress errors, for -e combined with delay injection, for decrypt errors on non-data types, or if translate_record fails. Next, when a dataset was selected and domount is set, it opens it and unmounts it (return 1 if zfs_open or zfs_unmount fails). It then stores the error in the record, calls ret = register_handler(pool, flags, &record, quiet); if the dataset was unmounted it then re-mounts and OVERWRITES ret with (zfs_mount(...) != 0), so a failed registration is reported as 0 when the re-mount succeeds. Finally it calls libzfs_fini and returns ret. (The re-mount happens only when dataset[0] != 0 and domount.)

functions.name: zpool_do_wait
functions.prose_contract: Implements 'zpool wait' (zpool_main.c:13472-13624; the slice cut the head). It initialises a wait_data_t (scripted, exact, headers_once, should_exit all false; mutex and condition variable initialised; every wait activity enabled) and parses options with getopt using the option string 'HpT:t:' (the 'n' case in the switch cannot be reached through that string): H scripted, p exact, T timestamp, t a comma-separated activity list (an unknown name prints 'invalid activity' and calls usage()); '?' prints 'invalid option' and calls usage(). It then calls get_interval_count; a non-zero count, a missing pool argument or more than one pool argument print a message and call usage(B_FALSE). A non-zero interval turns verbose on. It opens the pool and returns 1 if zpool_open fails (the mutex and cv created above are not destroyed on that return). In verbose mode it creates the status thread; if pthread_create fails it prints a message, closes the pool and returns 1 without destroying the mutex and condition variable (13570-13576). Then it loops: for each enabled activity it calls zpool_wait_status, stopping the inner loop on an error or a missing pool; the outer loop ends when error != 0, missing is set, or no activity was waited for. It closes the pool; in verbose mode it sets wd_should_exit under the mutex, signals the cv, joins the status thread and, if the thread's status is non-zero, replaces error with it. It then destroys the mutex and cv (only on this path) and returns error (0 on success).

functions.name: zpool_do_online
functions.prose_contract: Implements 'zpool online [-e] [--power] pool device...' (zpool_main.c:7985-8102). Options: -e sets ZFS_ONLINE_EXPAND, --power (or the environment variable ZPOOL_AUTO_POWER_ON_SLOT) sets is_power_on; an invalid option prints a message and calls usage(B_FALSE). A missing pool name or missing device name prints a message and calls usage(B_FALSE). It returns 1 if zpool_open fails (after printing a message). For each device argument: if is_power_on it calls zpool_power_on_and_disk_wait and, for a non-zero rc (printing a message when ENOTSUP), returns rc immediately without calling zpool_close (so the pool handle is leaked on that path and the return value is the errno-style rc, not 0 or 1). It then looks the vdev up with zpool_find_vdev; if not found it prints a message, sets ret = 1 and continues to the next device. It reads the vdev's old state, calls zpool_vdev_online: on failure it prints the error and sets ret = 1; on success, if the new state is not HEALTHY it prints a warning with a hint (use 'zpool clear' for faulted, 'zpool replace' otherwise), and if -e was given it also prints an error or warning about expansion, with ret = 1 and a break out of the device loop only when the old state was >= VDEV_STATE_DEGRADED (degraded or healthy, i.e. not faulted). After the loop it calls zpool_close and returns ret (0 or 1).

functions.name: zstream_do_dump
functions.prose_contract: Implements 'zstream dump' (zstream_dump.c:209-813; the packet name main does not exist in this file, the slice cut the head). It allocates a SPA_MAXBLOCKSIZE buffer (safe_malloc) and parses options -v (twice gives very verbose), -C (no checksum check), -d (dump: sets verbose and very verbose); a missing option argument or an invalid option prints a message and calls zstream_usage(). It opens the stream from the named file (exit(1) if fopen fails) or uses stdin (exit(1) with a message when stdin is a terminal). It then reads headers in a loop (read_hdr): on the first record a byte-swapped magic selects byte-swap mode, any other bad magic prints 'Invalid stream (bad magic number)' and exit(1)s; a record type >= DRR_NUMTYPES prints 'INVALID record found' / 'Aborting.' and exit(1)s. For each valid record it counts per-type record number, adds the header size to the overhead and processes it in a per-type switch (BEGIN, END, OBJECT, FREEOBJECTS, WRITE, WRITE_BYREF, FREE, SPILL, WRITE_EMBEDDED, OBJECT_RANGE, REDACT; byte-swapping fields when needed); the printing of record contents depends on verbose (for example REDACT and OBJECT_RANGE print only when verbose), so not every record is printed; with very verbose each record other than BEGIN also prints its checksum line. It accumulates the payload sizes. After the loop it frees the buffer and, after fletcher_4_fini, prints a SUMMARY with the per-type counts and byte counts, total records, payload size, header overhead and stream length (these totals are printed regardless of verbosity), and returns 0. Only the exits listed above terminate with a non-zero status. Not read in detail: the per-type switch bodies (lines 353-739, I checked only their control flow and the verbose gating of the last cases).

functions.name: zstream_do_recompress
functions.prose_contract: Implements 'zstream recompress [-l level] type' (zstream_recompress.c:67-382; the packet name main does not exist, the slice cut the head). It parses -l (calls zstream_usage() if the level is unparsable) and requires exactly one argument (the compression type) else zstream_usage(). The type is 'off' or a name found in zio_compress_table; an unknown type or one without a compress function prints a message and exit(2)s. A terminal on stdin prints an error and exit(1)s. It then reads dmu_replay_record_t records from stdin in a loop, re-emitting each through dump_record to stdout; BEGIN resets the stream checksum, requires only one BEGIN (VERIFY), reads the payload (growing the buffer with realloc, err(1) if realloc fails); END replaces a non-zero checksum with the running stream checksum; OBJECT, SPILL, WRITE_EMBEDDED payloads are read into the buffer unchanged; FREEOBJECTS, FREE and OBJECT_RANGE have no payload; WRITE_BYREF prints 'Deduplicated streams are not supported' and exit(1)s; an unknown record type prints a message and hits assert(B_FALSE). For DRR_WRITE: an encrypted record (non-zero salt) is passed through unchanged; otherwise an invalid compression type in the stream exit(3)s, a stream type without a decompress function is treated as uncompressed, the payload is decompressed if needed (decompression failure exit(4)s) and, when the target type is not 'off', recompressed at the requested level and stored compressed only if the rounded compressed size is smaller than the logical size (else stored uncompressed with compression type and compressed size set to 0). When the target type is 'off' the decompressed data is written directly into buf (dbuf aliases buf), the record's compression type and compressed size are set to 0 and the payload is therefore the uncompressed data. EOF or error on stdout exits with status 1. After the loop it frees the buffer, shuts the subsystems down and returns 0 (also if dump_record returned non-zero, which only breaks out of the loop).

functions.name: raidz_scratch_verify
functions.prose_contract: Static void (ztest.c:3964-4050) that checks the RAIDZ-expansion scratch state in the uberblock. It asserts raidz_expand_pause_point == RAIDZ_EXPAND_PAUSE_NONE (ASSERT) and returns at once if ztest_scratch_state->zs_raidz_scratch_verify_pause is 0 (no further effect). Otherwise it initialises the kernel in read mode (kernel_init(SPA_MODE_READ)), looks the test pool up in the namespace under spa_namespace_enter/exit, sets ZFS_IMPORT_SKIP_MMP in spa_import_flags, opens it with spa_open (VERIFY0), and asserts RRSS_GET_OFFSET(&spa->spa_uberblock) != UINT64_MAX; this assertion is made whether or not spa_raidz_expand is set. It then takes ztest_vdev_lock and the SCL_ALL config lock as reader. If spa->spa_raidz_expand is NULL it skips the state checks (goto out); otherwise it looks up the top-level vdev, reads the uberblock scratch offset and state, computes logical_size = P2ALIGN(VDEV_BOOT_SIZE, 1 << ashift) * children and asserts, by state: NOT_IN_USE offset == 0; VALID, INVALID_SYNCED and INVALID_SYNCED_ON_IMPORT offset == logical_size; INVALID_SYNCED_REFLOW offset >= logical_size. At out it releases the config lock and the vdev lock, sets zs_raidz_scratch_verify_pause = 0, closes the pool and calls kernel_fini. The checks are ASSERTs (abort on failure in builds where they are enabled), so the function has no return value.

functions.name: ztest_fault_inject
functions.prose_contract: ztest test function (ztest.c:6419-6718; the packet name ztest_vdev_fault_inject does not exist, the slice cut the head); zd and id are unused and it returns void. It allocates two path buffers, takes ztest_vdev_lock itself and jumps to out (unlock, optional scrub, free buffers) if device removal is active, a raidz expansion is in progress (spa_raidz_expand set), the pool has not yet been scrubbed, maxfaults is 0 after the offline/online step, open of the chosen leaf file fails, or the mirror count changed during the loop (that case closes fd first). With ztest_name_lock (read) and SCL_STATE held it picks, with probability 1/2, a data/slog leaf from the top-level vdevs: if that vdev was found and maxfaults != 1 and it needs no resilver (or its resilver txg is non-zero) it randomly either closes the vdev's file descriptor (sets f_fd = -1), sets vdev_cant_read, or sets vdev_cant_write; these unreadable/unwritable/fd-close actions happen only in this data/slog branch. Otherwise it picks a cache (l2cache) device, returning via out if there are none (after releasing both locks), uses that device's path and sets maxfaults = INT_MAX; cache devices are never marked unreadable/unwritable here, they only take the later offline/online and bad-word injection. After the locks are released, if (maxfaults >= 2 or the vdev is a log) and a guid was chosen, then with 60 percent chance it offlines that vdev (temporary at random; VERIFY it is not EBUSY; for a log vdev under the write lock of ztest_name_lock) and otherwise brings it online. It then opens the leaf path and up to 999 times writes the 8-byte pattern at a random offset (skipping label areas for even/odd leaves), calling fatal() if pwrite fails, then closes fd. At out it unlocks, and if something was injected and zo_raid_do_expand is set it starts a scrub and waits while it runs; finally it frees both buffers.

functions.name: ztest_spa_import_export
functions.prose_contract: Static void (ztest.c:7443-7525) that exercises export and re-import of a pool under a new name. It first destroys any pool called newname (spa_destroy, result ignored), so newname does not need to be free beforehand. It opens oldname (VERIFY0), at random starts a scrub (result ignored), records the pool guid and closes it, exports the pool (VERIFY0, capturing its config), checks that spa_tryimport(config) returns a config (ASSERT, then frees it), and imports the config as newname: a non-zero error dumps the config and calls fatal(B_FALSE, ...), which is the only path that uses fatal. It then VERIFYs that importing again as newname and importing as oldname each return EEXIST, that spa_open(oldname) returns ENOENT, and that spa_open(newname) succeeds with the same guid (ASSERT3U), then closes the pool and frees the config. All VERIFY/ASSERT conditions panic (abort the process via the assertion handler), they do not call fatal(); the function has no return value and does not free the config on the fatal path.

functions.name: pam_sm_chauthtok
functions.prose_contract: PAM password-change hook (pam_zfs_key.c:902-993, returns a PAM status). It returns PAM_PERM_DENIED if the effective uid is not 0, PAM_SERVICE_ERR if the config cannot be loaded or the user's uid is outside [uid_min, uid_max] (config freed in the second case). It then fetches the old token and, in an inner block, calls pam_zfs_init (PAM_SERVICE_ERR on failure, config freed), gets the dataset name (PAM_SERVICE_ERR if NULL), requires a non-null old token (PAM_SERVICE_ERR, frees the dataset), and decrypt_mount(old token, B_TRUE): on -1 it logs 'old token mismatch', frees dataset, ZFS handle (pam_zfs_free) and config and returns PAM_PERM_DENIED. If that check succeeds, the dataset string and the ZFS state from this first block are still held afterwards. Without PAM_UPDATE_AUTHTOK (the other branch) it only calls zfs_key_config_free and returns PAM_SUCCESS, so on that path the first-block dataset string is not freed and pam_zfs_free is not called (the first-block dataset is leaked and the ZFS handle stays initialised). With PAM_UPDATE_AUTHTOK: a missing new token, a NULL dataset (second lookup) or a failed decrypt_mount of the old key (when the key was not already loaded) each call pam_zfs_free and zfs_key_config_free, clear the stored passwords and return PAM_SERVICE_ERR; otherwise it calls change_key with the new token, unmounts/unloads again if it had to load the key, frees the second dataset string, calls pam_zfs_free and frees the config, clears both stored passwords and returns PAM_SERVICE_ERR if either clear or change_key failed, else PAM_SUCCESS. On update paths the first-block dataset string is also not freed.

functions.name: nv_alloc_sys
functions.prose_contract: Static allocator callback (nvpair_alloc_system.c:35-38) that returns kmem_alloc(size, (int)(uintptr_t)nva->nva_arg). It dereferences nva (so nva must be non-NULL) and uses its nva_arg as the kmem flags: the two statics defined in this file pass KM_SLEEP (nv_alloc_sleep) and KM_NOSLEEP (nv_alloc_nosleep). It adds no checks of its own: whatever kmem_alloc returns (a pointer, or NULL if the underlying allocator fails, which is only a possible outcome for KM_NOSLEEP in typical implementations) is returned unchanged, and for size 0 the result is whatever kmem_alloc gives for that size (not examined here). It has no other side effect and takes no locks of its own.

functions.name: nfs_enable_share_impl
functions.prose_contract: Writes the exports lines for one share to tmpfile (nfs.c:119-161, static, returns an int SA_* code). The share options are used as 'sa_shareopts', with the literal 'on' replaced by an empty string. It escapes the mountpoint with nfs_escape_mountpoint and returns that call's non-SA_OK code at once (nothing allocated yet). It then strdup's the options; if that fails it returns SA_SYSTEM_ERR directly, without freeing the escaped mountpoint, so that string leaks when need_free is set. Otherwise it splits the copy on ';': for each option set it sets fnd_semi once any ';' has been seen (s != NULL) and, while fnd_semi is true, skips (continue) a set consisting only of tabs/spaces; so an empty or whitespace-only set is skipped only when it is followed by a ';' or comes after one, while a single set with no ';' (including the empty string from 'on') is still written. For each set that is kept it writes the mountpoint, a tab, the translated options (translate_opts) and a newline; if any of those four writes fails, including translate_opts failing because its malloc returned NULL (it returns EOF), it prints 'failed to write to temporary file', sets rc = SA_SYSTEM_ERR and breaks out of the loop. It then frees the duplicated options, frees mp only if need_free, and returns rc (SA_OK or SA_SYSTEM_ERR).

functions.name: changelist_gather
functions.prose_contract: Builds a prop_changelist_t for dataset zhp and property prop (libzfs_changelist.c:654-814; the slice is only the tail and the packet name changelist_add does not exist). Steps: zfs_alloc the list; for prop NAME, ZONED, MOUNTPOINT, SHARENFS or SHARESMB it reads the mountpoint property and sets legacy if it is 'legacy' or 'none'; it creates the AVL pool (compare by name when legacy, else by mountpoint) and tree, returning NULL after reporting EZFS_NOMEM and changelist_free if either creation fails. It maps prop to cl_prop: NAME gives MOUNTPOINT with cl_alldependents, ZONED gives MOUNTPOINT with cl_allchildren, CANMOUNT and VOLSIZE give MOUNTPOINT, other props are used as is, and stores cl_realprop. If cl_prop is not MOUNTPOINT, SHARENFS or SHARESMB it returns the (empty) list immediately, without adding zhp. Otherwise it sets cl_shareprop to the other share property for the share cases and gathers dependent datasets: with MOUNTPOINT and CL_GATHER_ITER_MOUNTED via zfs_iter_mounted(changelist_add_mounted), else with cl_alldependents via zfs_iter_dependents_v2, else for non-MOUNTPOINT props zfs_iter_filesystems_v2, else zfs_iter_children_v2 with change_one; any non-zero iteration result frees the list and returns NULL. It then re-opens zhp by name (zfs_open; NULL result frees the list and returns NULL), allocates a node with the new handle, cn_mounted (CL_GATHER_MOUNT_ALWAYS or zfs_is_mounted), cn_shared (zfs_is_shared), cn_zoned and cn_needpost = B_TRUE, and inserts it into the tree unless a node with the same key exists, in which case it frees the node and closes the extra handle. Finally, if cl_prop is MOUNTPOINT and the mountpoint was legacy/none, it sets cl_waslegacy unless canmount is noauto, and returns clp.

functions.name: make_dataset_handle_common
functions.prose_contract: Static int (libzfs_dataset.c:440-476). It first calls put_stats_zhdl(zhp, zc) and returns -1 if that returns non-zero. It then sets zfs_head_type from the dataset type: DMU_OST_ZVOL gives VOLUME and DMU_OST_ZFS gives FILESYSTEM; DMU_OST_OTHER sets errno = EINVAL and returns -1; only for any other type value, if dds_inconsistent is set, it sets errno = EBUSY and returns -1 (so an inconsistent ZVOL or ZFS dataset does not return EBUSY here), and otherwise (any remaining type) it calls abort(). It then sets zfs_type to SNAPSHOT if dds_is_snapshot, else VOLUME or FILESYSTEM by dds_type (abort() for anything else), and sets zhp->zpool_hdl = zpool_handle(zhp), returning -1 if that is NULL. Returns 0 on success. It has no locks and does not free zhp on failure (that is left to the caller).

functions.name: zfs_show_diffs
functions.prose_contract: Runs 'zfs diff' (libzfs_diff.c:747-830; the slice is only the tail, the head is cut). It calls setup_differ_info; on failure it tears down the differ info and returns -1. It creates a pipe (pipe2 with O_CLOEXEC): failure sets an aux message, tears down and returns zfs_error(EZFS_PIPEFAILED). It sets the display flags and the two fds, starts the differ thread: if pthread_create fails it closes both pipe ends, tears down and returns zfs_error(EZFS_THREADCREATEFAILED). It then issues the ZFS_IOC_DIFF ioctl with the write end of the pipe. If the ioctl fails it sets an aux message by errno (EPERM and EXDEV special texts; other errors except EPIPE-with-differ-error), closes the write end, cancels and joins the thread, tears down and returns zfs_error(EZFS_DIFF, di.errbuf) when the differ recorded an error other than EPIPE, else zfs_error(EZFS_DIFFDATA, errbuf); read end pipefd[0] is not closed in this function on that path (it may be closed by the differ thread, not read). If the ioctl succeeds it closes the write end, joins the thread, and if di.zerr is non-zero returns zfs_error(EZFS_DIFF, di.errbuf) WITHOUT calling teardown_differ_info (the final di.zerr path at 824-827); otherwise it tears down the differ info and returns 0. The zfs_error values are -1 style return codes of that function (not read).

functions.name: zpool_initialize_impl
functions.prose_contract: Static int (libzfs_pool.c:2478-2558) that starts, cancels or suspends initialisation on vdevs. It translates the vdev names to guids with zpool_translate_vdev_guids; if that fails (err non-zero) it goes to list_errors. Otherwise it calls lzc_initialize; on failure, if the returned errlist has an ZPOOL_INITIALIZE_VDEVS member it goes to list_errors with that per-vdev list; otherwise it sets an aux message for EINVAL with POOL_INITIALIZE_UNINIT, reports zpool_standard_error('operation failed') and goes to out (so per-vdev error translation is not used for these failures). If the call succeeded and wait is set, it calls lzc_wait_tag for each vdev guid and on the first failure reports zpool_standard_error_fmt and goes to out. list_errors prints, for each entry of the per-vdev error list, 'cannot initialize <path>' via zfs_error_fmt using xlate_init_err on the stored error (the path comes from guids_to_paths or the guid string). out frees vdev_guids, guids_to_paths and, if set, vd_errlist (the errlist returned by lzc_initialize is not freed here). The return value is 0 if err is 0 and -1 otherwise; the raw errno-like err is never returned.

functions.name: dump_snapshot
functions.prose_contract: Static iterator callback (libzfs_sendrecv.c:1150-1293) that sends one snapshot of the iterated dataset; it takes ownership of zhp and, on most paths, closes it. thissnap is the part after '@'. If the 'from' snapshot has not been seen and this is it: it gathers holds, sets seenfrom, copies the name into prevsnap, records prevsnap_obj, closes zhp and returns 0 without sending anything (so sdd is changed but this snapshot is not sent). If seento is already set or seenfrom is not yet set, it closes zhp and returns 0. Otherwise it notes whether this is the 'to' snapshot (sets seento), builds the lzc flags from sdd, and for a snapshot that is neither from nor to and not doall, excludes it (exclude = TRUE when not replicating, or when replicating and the snapshot is not a clone origin found through fsavl); if excluded or filter_cb returns false it closes zhp and returns 0. Otherwise it gathers holds, and when verbosity is non-zero estimates the size and prints it (adding to sdd->size). Unless dryrun, it fills the progress args and starts send_progress_thread: if pthread_create fails it closes zhp and returns that error; else it runs dump_ioctl and then send_progress_thread_exit; if that exit call fails it returns -1 immediately without closing zhp and without updating prevsnap. On the normal path it copies thissnap into prevsnap, stores prevsnap_obj, closes zhp and returns err (the dump_ioctl result, or 0 for a dry run).

functions.name: recv_incremental_replication
functions.prose_contract: Static int (libzfs_sendrecv.c:3521-3819) that makes the local filesystem hierarchy under tofs match the stream's names and origins before an incremental replication receive. If flags->dryrun is set it returns 0 immediately, before reading anything or changing anything locally (so in a dry run the local hierarchy is not adjusted). Otherwise it reads fromsnap and the recursive flag from stream_nv and enters the 'again' pass: it allocates the deleted-guid list and gathers the local nvlist/avl with gather_nvlist, returning that call's non-zero error value directly if it fails. For each local filesystem it finds the matching stream entry; when the origin guids differ it may call recv_promote (progress = TRUE on success) and sets needagain, or, if created_before returns -1, it frees the local lists and returns -1; with flags->force it destroys local snapshots/filesystems missing from the stream via recv_destroy (failure sets needagain, success sets progress and records the guid in deleted); it renames filesystems with recv_rename when the parent or name differ (failure sets needagain, success sets progress), and may skip entries when parents are not yet in place (goto doagain / needagain). After the pass it frees the lists; if needagain and progress were both set it repeats from 'again'. Final return is the boolean (needagain || error != 0), so 0 or 1: individual destroy, rename and promote failures are not returned as their errno values (error holds only the last callee result and is only compared with 0). Hence the function returns 0, 1, -1 (created_before failure) or a gather_nvlist error value.

functions.name: zfs_setproctitle_init
functions.prose_contract: Void function (zutil_setproctitle.c:159-218) that prepares the process-title area. It returns without changing anything if argc < 0 or argv[0] is NULL. It sets nul to the end of argv[0] and end to the byte after it, then extends end across following argv strings that are contiguous in memory (the loop reads argv[i] for i >= argc until a NULL entry, so argv must be NULL-terminated, i.e. have argc+1 valid pointers) and then across contiguous envp strings, counting envp entries (envp must be NULL-terminated). It then duplicates argv[0] into SPT.arg0 (on strdup failure sets SPT.error = errno and returns), duplicates the program name and calls setprogname with it (same error handling), calls spt_copyenv(envc, envp) and spt_copyargs(argc, argv); a non-zero result from either is stored in SPT.error and the function returns. Only if everything succeeded does it set SPT.nul, SPT.base and SPT.end. It never sets SPT.error to 0 on success (it leaves the earlier value) and it does not itself rebuild environ; any environ change is inside spt_copyenv (not read). Resources already duplicated before a failure (arg0, progname) are not freed.

functions.name: sha2_mac_final
functions.prose_contract: Finishes an HMAC-SHA2 operation (sha2_mod.c:458-537, static). It asserts ctx->cc_provider_private != NULL, then selects the digest length from hc_mech_type: only SHA512_HMAC_MECH_INFO_TYPE is accepted (digest_len = SHA512_DIGEST_LENGTH); any other mechanism returns CRYPTO_ARGUMENTS_BAD at once. If mac->cd_length is 0 or less than digest_len it sets mac->cd_length = digest_len and returns CRYPTO_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL. Both of these early returns leave the provider context allocated and unchanged (it is not freed or zeroed). Otherwise it finishes the inner hash (SHA2Final into a local digest), feeds it to the outer context, and by mac->cd_format: CRYPTO_DATA_RAW writes the outer digest into the raw buffer at cd_offset (directly, or via a local copy if digest_len differs from sha_digest_len); CRYPTO_DATA_UIO calls sha2_digest_final_uio and takes its result; any other format sets ret = CRYPTO_ARGUMENTS_BAD. After that it sets mac->cd_length = digest_len when ret is CRYPTO_SUCCESS and 0 otherwise, zeroes and kmem_frees the hmac context (sha2_hmac_ctx_t), sets ctx->cc_provider_private = NULL and returns ret, so these cleanup steps run on both the success and the failure outcome of the format switch.

functions.name: lua_next
functions.prose_contract: Lua API function (lapi.c:1113-1127) that advances a table traversal. It takes the state lock, resolves idx to a stack slot (index2addr) and api_check-s that it is a table (a check that is active only when API checking is compiled in). It calls luaH_next(L, table, L->top - 1), which uses the key on the top of the stack as the current position and, when there is a next entry, replaces that key slot with the next key and writes the value above it; if that call returns non-zero the function does api_incr_top(L) so the stack ends up one slot larger than before the call (the popped key is replaced by key and value). If luaH_next returns 0 (no more elements) it removes the key with L->top -= 1, so the stack is one slot smaller. It then releases the lock and returns the luaH_next result (zero or non-zero; the code returns it as is). The behaviour of luaH_next for an invalid key (it may raise a Lua error) was not read.

functions.name: nvlist_snprintf
functions.prose_contract: Formats an nvlist as text into buf of size bytes (nvpair.c:3753-3943) and returns the length that the full output would have (the sum of the snprintf return values, like snprintf, excluding any terminator), or a negative snprintf result immediately. If list is NULL it returns 0 without writing anything to buf. Otherwise, for each nvpair it calls snprintf into the remaining space (the NVP/NVPA macros and the explicit cases for boolean, boolean value, nvlist, nvlist array and the default 'bad config type' message), adds each rc to len, and after each write reduces size by rc (not below 0) and moves buf forward, or sets buf to NULL once size reaches 0, so later writes only count characters. Nested nvlists and nvlist-array members are formatted by recursive calls with the remaining buffer. A negative rc from any snprintf or recursive call is returned at once, abandoning the rest. With size 0 on entry nothing is written (no NUL is stored), and with a non-zero size each snprintf terminates its own piece, but a truncated output ends at buf_end with whatever snprintf stored (the function itself never stores a final NUL beyond that). The return value can exceed size - 1 when the output was truncated.

functions.name: zfs_readdir
functions.prose_contract: Reads directory entries into the caller's uio (zfs_vnops_os.c:1682-1931; the slice cut the head). It enters the filesystem with zfs_enter_verify_zp and returns that error if it fails; it looks up the parent object with sa_lookup (on failure it calls zfs_exit and returns the error). If eofp is NULL it uses a local variable instead (so eofp may be NULL). It returns EINVAL if the first iov length is 0, and returns 0 with *eofp = TRUE if the directory is unlinked (z_unlinked), both after zfs_exit. It allocates the zap attribute and a cursor (fresh for offsets <= 3, serialized otherwise) and chooses the output buffer: the iov itself for a single kernel-space iov, otherwise a kmem_alloc'd temporary; if ncookies is non-NULL it also malloc's a cookie array. The loop emits '.', '..', optionally the .zfs control directory entry, then ZAP entries until bytes_wanted is reached: a ZAP retrieve error sets *eofp for ENOENT and ends the loop, or any other error jumps to update; an entry with unexpected integer size/count sets ENXIO; if an entry does not fit and nothing has been output yet it sets EINVAL, else the loop stops. After the loop it clears the prefetch flag, trims *ncookies, and for the single kernel-space iov advances the iov and resid directly, else copies with zfs_uiomove (an error there is kept and the offset is re-read from the uio). At update it finishes the cursor, frees the attribute and temporary buffer, converts ENOENT to 0, updates the access time, stores the offset in the uio, calls zfs_exit, frees the cookie array and zeroes *ncookies/*cookies when error != 0 and cookies was given, and returns error.

functions.name: zfs_setattr
functions.prose_contract: Applies vattr changes to a znode (zfs_vnops_os.c:2291-2981; the slice is the tail, the head is cut). Before the zfs_enter_verify_zp it returns 0 if the mask is empty and EINVAL if AT_NOSET is set; after entering it returns (with zfs_exit) EINVAL for FUID-incompatible requests or AT_SIZE on non-regular/non-FIFO files, EISDIR for AT_SIZE on a directory, EPERM for immutable files, EOVERFLOW for out-of-range times, EOPNOTSUPP for project-id requests when unsupported, EINVAL for an invalid project id, EROFS on a read-only filesystem, any error from zfs_freesp (AT_SIZE is applied first), policy/permission errors (zfs_zaccess, policy checks), and EPERM for AT_XVATTR/XAT_REPARSE. Then, for uid/gid/project changes it looks up and locks the xattr directory znode (attrzp), and returns EDQUOT (via out2, before any transaction) if a quota check fails; for AT_MODE it builds the ACL, EPERM in restricted mode (via out). It then creates the dmu transaction and assigns it (DMU_TX_WAIT); an assign error goes to out. After assignment it updates the in-memory fields and the bulk attribute arrays under z_acl_lock: uid/gid, mode/ACL, times, size, project id (the project id is set both on zp->z_projid and, when attrzp exists, on attrzp->z_projid, 2821-2826 and 2895-2899), and the xvattr flags.
