At the out label: on err == 0 with attrzp it applies the xattr bulk update; it frees the ACL and fuid info; on err it aborts the transaction (and vput's attrzp), but on success it applies the bulk update to zp, commits the transaction, and for attrzp may call zfs_setattr_dir (its error becomes the function's error AFTER the commit) and vput's attrzp. Finally (out2) if err == 0 and the objset sync is ALWAYS it sets err = zil_commit(zilog, 0), calls zfs_exit and returns err. So a zfs_setattr_dir or zil_commit failure is reported after the transaction was already committed.

functions.name: zfs_do_rename_impl
functions.prose_contract: Static int (zfs_vnops_os.c:3316-3548) that performs the rename; it enters the filesystem itself (zfs_enter_verify_zp on tdzp, zfs_verify_zp on sdzp, szp and tzp), so the caller must not have entered it already; a verify failure after the enter calls zfs_exit and returns that error. Failures that jump to out (so zfs_exit still runs, after the optional ZFS_SYNC_ALWAYS commit): EILSEQ for an invalid UTF-8 target name; success (error = 0, nothing done) if source and target vnode are the same; EXDEV if either is a directory with a mount on it; EINVAL if source and target dirs differ in XATTR-ness; EXDEV on project-id inheritance mismatch; the error of zfs_zaccess_rename; for a directory source EINVAL when renaming '.', sdzp == szp or an ISDOTDOT component, or the error of zfs_rename_check; for an existing target EEXIST if AT_RENAME_NOREPLACE, ENOTDIR (dir onto non-dir) or EISDIR (non-dir onto dir). It then begins vn_seqc writes, fires the vnevents, builds and assigns a transaction (a dmu_tx_assign failure aborts the tx and goes to out_seq). With the tx assigned it destroys an existing target link, creates the new link (ZRENAMING), updates the source flags, destroys the old link and logs the rename; if the old-link destroy fails it removes the just-created new link (VERIFY0) and keeps that error; on success with the namecache it updates it. It always commits the transaction after assignment (dmu_tx_commit at 3532, also when error is non-zero), then ends the seqc writes. At out, if error == 0 and the objset sync property is ALWAYS it assigns error = zil_commit(zilog, 0) (the source assigns that result; the reviewer's claim that zil_commit returns void conflicts with this line), then zfs_exit and returns error.

functions.name: zfs_symlink
functions.prose_contract: Creates a symbolic link (zfs_vnops_os.c:3613-3743; the slice cut the head). It returns ENAMETOOLONG for a too-long name before entering the filesystem, then enters with zfs_enter_verify_zp (returns its error). After the enter every early failure calls zfs_exit and returns: EILSEQ for an invalid UTF-8 name, ENAMETOOLONG if the link target length exceeds MAXPATHLEN, the error of zfs_acl_ids_create, of zfs_dirent_lookup(ZNEW) (name already exists), or of zfs_zaccess(ACE_ADD_FILE), and EDQUOT on overquota; the acl ids are freed on those after they were created. Then getnewvnode_reserve() is called and a transaction is built and assigned; if dmu_tx_assign fails it frees the acl ids, aborts the tx, drops the getnewvnode reserve, exits and returns the error. (So the getnewvnode reserve is dropped only on that path and on the final path, not on the early returns before it was taken, which never took it.) With the tx assigned it makes the znode (zfs_mknode), writes the link text (sa_update when the znode is SA, else zfs_sa_symlink; the sa_update result is overwritten by the later error value), sets the size, and calls zfs_link_create; if that fails it deletes the new znode, unlocks and releases it; otherwise it logs the symlink. It then frees the acl ids, commits the transaction (also on a zfs_link_create failure), drops the getnewvnode reserve, and on success stores the new znode in *zpp (so *zpp is written only on success) and, if the objset sync is ALWAYS, sets error = zil_commit(zilog, 0). It calls zfs_exit and returns error (0 or the zfs_link_create/zil_commit/earlier error).

functions.name: zfs_lookup
functions.prose_contract: Directory lookup (zfs_vnops_os.c:751-1004; the slice cut the head). Without LOOKUP_XATTR it returns ENOTDIR if dvp is not a directory and EIO if the dnode's SA handle is NULL; these two returns, and a failing zfs_enter_verify_zp, happen before *vpp is assigned, so *vpp is left untouched there (it is not set to NULL on them). After the enter it sets *vpp = NULL. With LOOKUP_XATTR it returns EOPNOTSUPP if xattrs are unsupported, EINVAL if the directory is itself an xattr dir, or the zfs_get_xattrdir error; otherwise it sets *vpp to the xattr dir vnode, checks execute permission on it and on a zaccess failure vrele's it and returns the error (while *vpp still holds that pointer). Otherwise, unless cached, it checks execute permission (error returned, zfs_exit called) and returns EILSEQ for an invalid UTF-8 name. For '..' at the root of a snapshot-mounted zfsvfs it goes through the control-directory root and the 'snapshot' entry and returns that result. For the '.zfs' name in a dataset with a ctldir it returns ENOENT if the snapdir is disabled, ENOTSUP if it is the last component of a non-lookup operation, else the control root. Otherwise it loops: zfs_dirlook, zfs_exit, lock the found vnode (zfs_lookup_lock; on failure *vpp = NULL and return); for non-dotdot it stops; for dotdot it re-enters, reads the parent and repeats until the found vnode is not the directory's parent or an error occurs. On any error *vpp is set to NULL. For the last component of CREATE/RENAME, ENOENT becomes EJUSTRETURN; the dotdot seqc check may clear MAKEENTRY; it adds a negative cache entry for ENOENT and a positive entry on success, when the namecache is enabled and not replaying; it returns error.

functions.name: define_ddi_strtox(type, valtype)
functions.prose_contract: Macro (spl-generic.c:212-280) that generates ddi_strtol, ddi_strtoull and ddi_strtoll (invoked with (l, long), (ull, unsigned long long) and (ll, long long)); the generated function is int ddi_strto<type>(const char *str, char **endptr, int base, valtype *result). Behaviour of the generated function: it skips leading characters found in the set ' \t\n\r\f' with strchr(set, *ptr); because strchr also matches the terminating NUL of the searched set when *ptr is '\0', the skip loop does not stop at the end of str, so an empty or all-whitespace string is walked past its terminator (an out-of-bounds read) until some non-whitespace byte is found; the subsequent 'strlen(ptr) == 0 returns EINVAL' test therefore only triggers if the loop ended on a NUL. It then accepts one '-' (sets minus) or '+'. If base is 0 it detects the base from str[0] (the original string start, not the post-sign pointer): '0x' followed by a hex digit gives base 16 (ptr += 2), '0' followed by 0-7 gives base 8 (ptr += 1), a leading '0' with anything else returns EINVAL, otherwise base 10. It then accumulates digits (decimal digits and letters, stopping at the first character whose digit value is >= base or at a non-alphanumeric); it returns ERANGE if the accumulated value decreases ('last_value > value', a wrap-around test), which is only a reliable overflow test for the unsigned variant. At least one digit is not required: with no digits it stores 0 and returns 0. It stores minus ? -value : value in *result, sets *endptr (if non-NULL) to the first unparsed character, and returns 0. On the EINVAL and ERANGE returns *result and *endptr are not written.

functions.name: zone_dataset_attach
functions.prose_contract: Attaches a dataset name to the zone (user namespace) given by userns_fd (spl-zone.c:183-231). Without CONFIG_USER_NS it returns ENXIO immediately. With it: it returns the error of zone_dataset_cred_check (credential check), of zone_dataset_name_check (name check, also yields dsnamelen) or of user_ns_get (resolves the fd to a user namespace), in that order and before taking the lock. It then takes zone_datasets_lock and holds it until the end: it looks up the zone's dataset list by user_ns_zoneid; if none exists it kmem_allocs a new zone_datasets_t, initialises its lists, stores the userns, takes a reference with get_user_ns and adds it to the global zone_datasets list; if one exists and already contains the dataset name it releases the lock and returns EEXIST (nothing else is added; whether the reference from user_ns_get is released on this path is not handled in this function). Otherwise it kmem_allocs a zone_dataset_t sized for the name, copies the name with strlcpy and appends it to the zone's dataset list, releases the lock and returns 0. The lock is therefore held across the allocations, the strlcpy and get_user_ns as well as the list lookup and update.

functions.name: zfs_zaccess_common
functions.prose_contract: Common access check (zfs_acl.c:2483-2537). It first sets *working_mode = v4_mode and *check_privs = B_TRUE. If v4_mode is 0 or the filesystem is replaying (z_replay) it sets *working_mode = 0 and returns 0. If zfs_zaccess_dataset_check(zp, v4_mode) returns non-zero it sets *check_privs = B_FALSE and returns that error with *working_mode still equal to v4_mode. If skipaclchk is set it sets *working_mode = 0 and returns 0. If v4_mode contains data-write bits, zp is not a directory and ZFS_READONLY is set in z_pflags it returns EPERM, leaving *working_mode equal to v4_mode and *check_privs TRUE. If ZFS_ACL_TRIVIAL is set it returns zfs_zaccess_trivial(zp, working_mode, cr, mnt_ns); otherwise it returns zfs_zaccess_aces_check(zp, working_mode, B_FALSE, cr, mnt_ns). Those last two return values are passed through unchanged and may be whatever those callees return (the reviewer reports -1 from the ACE check); in those two cases *working_mode is the callee's output.

functions.name: zfsctl_snapdir_mkdir
functions.prose_contract: Creates a snapshot by mkdir in .zfs/snapshot (zfs_ctldir.c:1012-1047). It returns EACCES immediately if the zfs_admin_snapshot tunable is off (nothing allocated). Otherwise it kmem_allocs a dataset-name buffer and: returns EILSEQ (via out) if dirname fails zfs_component_namecheck; fills dsname from the objset; returns the error of zfs_secpolicy_snapshot_perms(dsname, cr) if non-zero; calls dmu_objset_snapshot_one(dsname, dirname) and returns its error if non-zero; otherwise it calls zfsctl_snapdir_lookup(dip, dirname, ipp, ...) and returns its result. So if the snapshot was created and the following lookup fails, the error is returned although the snapshot remains in existence. out frees the name buffer. The admin-snapshot setting and the dirname validity are not preconditions: they are checked here, giving EACCES and EILSEQ.

functions.name: zfs_remove
functions.prose_contract: Removes a non-directory name from directory dzp (zfs_vnops_os.c:992-1211; the slice cut the head). It returns EINVAL if name is NULL, enters with zfs_enter_verify_zp (returns its error), then zfs_dirent_lock the entry: on failure it frees realnmp, exits and returns the error. Past that, failures that go to out: the error of zfs_zaccess_delete, EPERM if the target is a directory. It then builds a transaction (holds on the dir, the znode, possibly its blocks, xattr dir and external ACL when the object may be deleted now); dmu_tx_assign failure unlocks the dirent lock and, for ERESTART, aborts the tx, releases zp and xzp and retries from top; for any other error it aborts, releases zp/xzp, exits and returns the error. After assign, zfs_link_destroy runs; if it fails it commits the tx and goes to out. On success, if the znode became unlinked it is added to the unlinked set (when it cannot be deleted immediately) or deleted now (delete_now, including the unlinked xattr dir); otherwise (the object still has other hard links, unlinked false) neither happens and the znode is simply released. The transaction is committed and at out the name buffer and the dirent lock are released, zp is released with zrele when delete_now else zfs_zrele_async, xzp is released async if present, and with ZFS_SYNC_ALWAYS and no error the result of zil_commit becomes the return value; zfs_exit then runs and error is returned.

functions.name: zfs_mkdir
functions.prose_contract: Creates a directory (zfs_vnops_os.c:1235-1407; the slice cut the head). It returns EINVAL if FUIDs are unavailable but needed, or dirname is NULL (before entering), then zfs_enter_verify_zp (error returned); after entering, each failure calls zfs_exit and returns: EINVAL if dzp is an xattr dir, EILSEQ for an invalid UTF-8 name, the error of secpolicy_xvattr or of zfs_acl_ids_create. At 'top' it takes the dirent lock (zfs_dirent_lock with the new-name flag): failure frees the acl ids, exits and returns its error. Then access check on ACE_ADD_SUBDIRECTORY (error: frees acl ids, unlocks, exits, returns) and EDQUOT if over quota (same cleanup). It builds and assigns a transaction: on a dmu_tx_assign failure it unlocks the dirent lock and, for ERESTART, aborts the tx and retries from top; for other errors it frees the acl ids, aborts the tx, exits and returns the error. With the tx assigned it makes the znode (zfs_mknode) and zfs_link_create; if that fails it deletes the znode, removes the inode from the hash and goes to out; otherwise it syncs fuids and writes the create log record. At out it frees the acl ids, commits the transaction (also after a link failure), unlocks the dirent lock; on error it releases zp, else it returns the new znode through *zpp and applies zil_commit when the objset sync is ALWAYS (its result becomes the return value); then zfs_exit and return error.

functions.name: zfs_rmdir
functions.prose_contract: Removes a directory (zfs_vnops_os.c:1426-1537). It returns EINVAL if name is NULL (before entering the filesystem; zfs_exit is not called there), and enters with zfs_enter_verify_zp itself (so the caller must not have entered it already; failure returns its error without holding anything). It takes the dirent lock (zfs_dirent_lock): on failure it exits and returns the error, no zp to release. After that, failures go to out: the error of zfs_zaccess_delete, ENOTDIR if the target is not a directory, EINVAL if the target is cwd. It then takes the target's z_name_lock and z_parent_lock as writer, creates and assigns a transaction (on failure it releases both locks and the dirent lock; for ERESTART it aborts, releases zp and retries from top; otherwise it aborts, releases zp, exits and returns the error), calls zfs_link_destroy and, if that succeeded, writes the log record, commits the transaction and releases both rw locks. At out it unlocks the dirent lock, releases zp (zrele), applies zil_commit when the sync property is ALWAYS and error is 0 (the result becomes error), calls zfs_exit and returns error. EEXIST is not produced by this function's own checks.

functions.name: zpl_xattr_set
functions.prose_contract: Sets or removes (value == NULL) an extended attribute (zpl_xattr.c:600-673, static). It holds a cred reference and marks fstrans, enters with zpl_enter_verify_zp (on failure it skips the lock and returns that error), and takes z_xattr_lock as writer. It finds where the attribute currently lives (__zpl_xattr_where, a bitmask of XATTR_IN_SA / XATTR_IN_DIR). If that call fails with an error other than -ENODATA it returns that error; for -ENODATA (attribute absent) it returns -ENODATA when XATTR_REPLACE is set, returns 0 (nothing to remove) when value is NULL, and otherwise continues with error 0; if the attribute exists it sets -EEXIST and returns it when XATTR_CREATE is set, otherwise continues. If the file system uses SA and the znode is SA-based and (xattr=sa is set, or this is a removal of an SA attribute) it tries zpl_xattr_set_sa; on success it removes any directory copy (zpl_xattr_set_dir with a NULL value, whose result is ignored) and returns 0; if the SA attempt fails it falls through. Otherwise it calls zpl_xattr_set_dir with the value; on success, if the attribute was previously in SA it clears the SA copy with zpl_xattr_set_sa(NULL) and ignores that result. At out it releases the lock, exits, drops fstrans and the cred, asserts error <= 0 and returns error (0 or a negative errno). So after a successful set exactly one location is written, but a failure to clear the other copy is not reported; after a successful removal the attribute is cleared in the location(s) the code tried and errors of clearing the second location are ignored.

functions.name: abd_raidz_gen_iterate
functions.prose_contract: Walks the parity abds and the data abd in lock step and calls func_raidz_gen on each mapped chunk (abd.c:1057-1133). It asserts parity <= 3; for each parity abd it checks off + csize <= abd_size and initialises an iterator at off; if dsize > 0 it asserts dabd is set, that off + dsize <= dabd->abd_size, and initialises the data iterator (c_dabd). It enters a critical section and loops while csize > 0 (the parity length controls the loop, not dsize): it maps each parity iterator, takes len = min(csize, the parity map sizes); if dsize > 0 it also maps the data iterator, takes len = min(len, data map size) and dlen = len (not clamped to the remaining dsize), otherwise it uses daddr = NULL and dlen = 0. It asserts len > 0 and that len is a multiple of 512, calls func_raidz_gen(caddrs, daddr, len, dlen), unmaps and advances the data iterator by dlen and subtracts dlen from dsize (only when dsize > 0), then unmaps and advances each parity iterator by len and subtracts len from csize. So dsize may be smaller than csize (later calls then get daddr NULL and dlen 0 once dsize reaches 0) and dsize may be larger than csize (the loop ends when csize is 0 and the rest of dsize is not consumed). It exits the critical section and returns void.

functions.name: arc_change_state
functions.prose_contract: Moves an ARC header between arc states and adjusts size accounting (arc.c:2430-2622, void). It asserts the hash lock is held and new_state != old_state. If the header has an L1 part it reads old_state, the reference count, and update_old (buf, pabd or raw data present); otherwise old_state is arc_l2c_only, refcnt 0 and update_old false. update_new starts equal to update_old, and both become TRUE when the old or new state is a ghost state respectively. If refcnt == 0: for a non-anon, non-l2c-only old state it removes the header from that state's multilist (and decrements evictable space) only if its list node is active, and for a non-anon, non-l2c-only new state it inserts it into the new state's multilist and increments evictable space. If new_state is arc_anon and the header is in the hash table it removes it with buf_hash_remove. Then, for update_new (and new state not l2c_only) it adds the header's sizes to new_state->arcs_size (logical size for ghost states, otherwise each non-shared buf, the pabd and the raw data), and for update_old (old state not l2c_only) removes the sizes from the old state in the same way. Finally, only if the header HAS an L1 part it sets hdr->b_l1hdr.b_state = new_state, and, if it also has an L2 header and new_state is not l2c_only, it decrements the l2 arcstats for the old state, sets b_l2hdr.b_arcs_state = new_state->arcs_state and increments the stats. A header with no L1 part does not get b_state or b_l2hdr.b_arcs_state written. Returns void.

functions.name: l2arc_evict
functions.prose_contract: Evicts L2ARC buffers from the area about to be overwritten (arc.c:9125-9340, void). dev must be a valid pointer (it is dereferenced at entry to read l2ad_vdev, even when all is set); vd and l2ad_spa may be NULL only when all is TRUE (ASSERTs). At top it sets taddr to dev->l2ad_hand + distance, or to l2ad_end with rerun = TRUE when that sum would pass l2ad_end. If !all: when dev->l2ad_first is set it jumps to out without evicting anything (l2ad_evict is not advanced and l2ad_first is not cleared here); otherwise it optionally trims the freed range (dropping and retaking the SCL_L2ARC config lock around vdev_trim_simple) and raises l2ad_evict to at least taddr. Under l2ad_mtx it frees log-block pointer entries from the tail of l2ad_lbptr_list that are no longer valid (all of them when all is TRUE), then walks the buffer list from the tail: it try-locks each header's hash lock (on contention it drops l2ad_mtx, waits on that lock, and restarts at retry), stops the walk (break) when !all and the header's device address is outside [l2ad_hand, l2ad_evict), and otherwise evicts the header: an L2-only header is moved to arc_anon and destroyed; a header that has an L1 part is flagged L2_EVICTED if it is being read and its l2hdr is destroyed. It then unlocks l2ad_mtx. At out, if !all and rerun is set it resets l2ad_hand and l2ad_evict to l2ad_start, clears l2ad_first and repeats from top (so the wrap-around case evicts in two passes); then, if !all, it asserts hand + distance <= l2ad_end and hand <= l2ad_evict when not l2ad_first. Returns void.

functions.name: dbuf_dirty
functions.prose_contract: Marks a dbuf dirty in the transaction's txg and returns its dirty record (dbuf.c:2322-2578; the slice cut the head). The caller must hold a reference on db (ASSERT on db_holds) and the tx must have an assigned txg; the caller does NOT have to hold the dnode entered: dbuf_dirty itself calls DB_DNODE_ENTER(db) near the top and DB_DNODE_EXIT before returning. It takes db_mtx and, if the dbuf already has a dirty record for tx->tx_txg, releases the lock and returns that existing record with no change (2374-2379). Otherwise it creates a new dirty record (the lines between 2405 and 2478, including arc_release or data copy for level-0 non-bonus buffers, freed-range cleanup and dirtycnt update, were only skimmed), drops db_mtx, and for bonus and spill buffers it links the record to dn_dirty_records[txgoff] under dn_mtx, calls dnode_setdirty and returns the record. For other buffers it takes dn_struct_rwlock as reader if not already held for write, and, if the block is not the top level, finds or holds the parent dbuf (dbuf_hold_level), drops the rwlock if it took it, re-takes db_mtx, and links the record into the parent's dr_children only if the dbuf's first dirty record is still dr or the object is the meta dnode (this guards against dbuf_undirty having changed the list while db_mtx was dropped; if that test fails the record is not linked to the parent, 2553-2561), then releases the parent hold and db_mtx. For a top-level block (the dnode's own block pointers) it links the record directly into dn_dirty_records[txgoff] under dn_mtx and drops the rwlock if taken. It returns the record in all of these paths.

functions.name: receive_object
functions.prose_contract: Applies one DRR_OBJECT record on the receive side (dmu_recv.c:1913-2195). Before any transaction exists it returns EINVAL for an invalid or inconsistent record: a DMU_OT_NONE or invalid type/bonus type, oversized block size or bonus length, raw-stream field mismatches (object below or outside or_firstobj etc.), non-raw streams with raw fields or flags, and for a dmu_object_info result other than 0, ENOENT or EEXIST; it also returns the error of dmu_free_long_object (or of dmu_object_info in the slot loop) without a transaction. When the object exists (err == 0) it may free its old contents with dmu_free_long_object and return that error; for EEXIST it returns EINVAL if the object still exists; for ENOENT it records that a sync is needed. For objects needing several dnode slots it checks and frees the following slots (errors other than ENOENT/EEXIST are returned). It then creates a transaction and assigns it: a dmu_tx_assign failure aborts the tx and returns that error. With the tx assigned it claims a new object, reclaims an existing one with changed properties, or removes a stale spill block; if that fails it commits the transaction (not aborts) and returns EINVAL. With crypt params it sets them up (failure: commit the tx and return EINVAL); for raw streams it sets blocksize, nlevels and max blkid (VERIFY0); if a bonus buffer was sent it holds the dnode and bonus, copies the bonus data (byteswapping when needed) and releases them. It records the resume state, commits the transaction and returns 0. Errors after objects/ranges have been freed return without undoing that freeing, so partial state can remain.

functions.name: receive_process_record
functions.prose_contract: Dispatches one receive record to its handler (dmu_recv.c:3142-3263; the slice is the middle of it). It asserts bytes_read does not go backwards and stores rrd->bytes_read in rwa->bytes_read. In heal mode, for any record that is not DRR_WRITE it frees rrd->abd (or else the payload) and returns 0 without processing. In normal mode, for any record that is not DRR_WRITE it first flushes the pending write batch (flush_write_batch); if that fails it frees the abd or payload and returns the error. Then by type: OBJECT calls receive_object and frees the payload; FREEOBJECTS, FREE, OBJECT_RANGE, REDACT call their handlers; WRITE calls receive_process_write_record and then frees rrd->abd when in heal mode, or when the result is not EAGAIN (an EAGAIN result leaves the abd to the batch); WRITE_EMBEDDED calls its handler and frees the payload; SPILL calls receive_spill, frees the abd if it failed, and clears both abd and payload pointers. The default case (unknown record type) sets err = EINVAL and does not free rrd->abd or rrd->payload. If err is non-zero it logs with dprintf_drr. It returns err, so the abd and payload are not freed on every non-EAGAIN path: the unknown-type EINVAL path leaves them to the caller, and some handlers' results are returned without any free of fields they did not take.

functions.name: dmu_recv_end_sync
functions.prose_contract: Sync-task callback that finishes a receive (dmu_recv.c:3671-3823, void). It logs 'finish receiving' in the pool history and clears os_raw_receive. Heal mode (drc_heal): it only frees drc_keynvl; no snapshot is created and DS_FLAG_INCONSISTENT is not cleared in this branch. Non-heal, existing filesystem (!drc_newfs): it holds the origin head, with drc_force destroys the snapshots newer than the received one, applies a raw key if drc_keynvl is set (then frees it), swaps the clone with the origin head, snapshots the origin head under drc_tosnap, sets that snapshot's creation time and guid from the stream header, clears DS_FLAG_INCONSISTENT on both the new snapshot and the head, records newsnapobj, releases the head and destroys the temporary receive dataset. Non-heal, new filesystem: it snapshots the dataset, sets the snapshot's creation time and guid, clears DS_FLAG_INCONSISTENT on the snapshot and the dataset, removes the saved resume state (ZAP fields) if present and records newsnapobj. After the branches, if not heal, raw and drc_ivset_guid != 0 it zapifies the new snapshot object and stores DS_FIELD_IVSET_GUID (so the IVSET GUID is not stored in the heal case); for a non-raw receive into an encrypted dataset it removes the keystore mapping; finally, for all three branches including heal, it disowns the dataset and sets drc->drc_ds = NULL.

functions.name: dmu_redact_snap
functions.prose_contract: Creates or resumes a redaction bookmark and runs the redaction (dmu_redact.c:1004-1204; the packet name dsl_redact does not exist, the slice cut the head). It returns the error of dsl_pool_hold directly if that fails. Then it allocates the bookmark-name buffer, holds snapname (error goes to out), long-holds it and returns EINVAL (via out) if it is not a snapshot or its objset cannot be opened, EALREADY if it already has the redacted-datasets feature active. For each name in redactnvl it holds the dataset and objset and requires it to be earlier than snapname (EINVAL otherwise) and not already redacted (EALREADY); the first error goes to out. It builds '<snapname>#<redactbook>'; if that does not fit, it releases the pool, frees the name buffer and args and returns ENAMETOOLONG directly, WITHOUT releasing the long-held and held target dataset or the redaction-snapshot holds (this is the only path that skips out's dataset release). If the bookmark already exists: EEXIST if it is not a redaction bookmark or if it was already fully completed (last blkid and object UINT64_MAX), EIO if its redaction list cannot be held, ESRCH if the snapshot list does not match (count or guids); then it resumes. Otherwise it releases the pool and creates the redaction bookmark with dsl_bookmark_create_redacted (error goes to out). It starts one traverse thread per redaction snapshot and a merge thread and calls perform_redaction(os, new_rl, rmta), keeping its result in err; then it destroys the queue and frees rmta. At out it frees the name buffer, releases the redaction list holds, each redaction snapshot's long hold and hold, the args array, the pool (if still held) and the target dataset's long hold and hold, and returns err.

functions.name: dump_dnode
functions.prose_contract: Emits a DRR_OBJECT record for one dnode (dmu_send.c:713-805, static). If object < dscp->dsc_resume_object it returns 0 immediately (ASSERTing the distance fits within one dnode block) and sends nothing. If dnp is NULL or its type is DMU_OT_NONE it returns the result of dump_freeobjects(dscp, object, 1). Otherwise, if an operation is pending it flushes it with dump_record(dscp, NULL, 0): failure returns EINTR, success clears the pending op. It then zeroes the record, fills the object fields from dnp (type, bonus type/len, block size clamped to SPA_OLD_MAXBLOCKSIZE unless the large-blocks feature is set, dn_slots, checksum, compress, toguid); for a raw send it asserts the bp is encrypted, may set DRR_RAW_BYTESWAP, copies maxblkid, indblkshift, nlevels and nblkptr, and, only when the rounded bonus length is non-zero, returns EINVAL if the bonus length exceeds DN_MAX_BONUS_LEN or else sets raw_bonuslen and uses it as the bonus length. It sets DRR_OBJECT_SPILL when the dnode has a spill block pointer. It then calls dump_record with the bonus buffer (failure returns EINTR) and dump_free for the object's whole data range (failure returns EINTR), and finally returns EINTR if dscp->dsc_err is non-zero, else 0.

functions.name: dmu_tx_try_assign
functions.prose_contract: Static int (dmu_tx.c:1050-1151) that tries once to assign the tx to an open txg. It asserts tx_txg == 0. It returns EIO if tx_err is set, ESHUTDOWN if the pool is suspended, and ERESTART (setting tx_wait_dirty) if the tx is not already dirty-delayed and the pool needs a write-log delay or a dirty-data delay; all of these happen before a txg is held, so tx_txg is still 0. Then it takes tx_txg = txg_hold_open(...) and walks the holds: for each hold with a dnode it takes dn_mtx and, if the dnode was assigned to the previous txg (tx_txg - 1), releases the mutex, records the hold in tx_needassign_txh and returns ERESTART with tx_txg already set and the earlier holds' dnode references still taken; otherwise it sets dn_assigned_txg if it is 0 and adds a dn_tx_holds reference; it sums the space-to-write and memory-to-hold counters. It computes the worst-case asize and, if tx_dir is set and asize != 0, calls dsl_dir_tempreserve_space; a non-zero result is returned as is, again with tx_txg set and the dnode holds in place (it does not undo anything here, the caller's dmu_tx_unassign releases the txg hold and the dnode holds, but it does not clear tx_tempreserve_cookie). On success it bumps a statistic and returns 0. The throttle delay checks are skipped when tx_dirty_delayed is already set, so the delay returns are not unconditional.

functions.name: dmu_tx_assign
functions.prose_contract: Assigns a transaction to a txg (dmu_tx.c:1232-1323). It asserts tx_txg == 0, valid flags (DMU_TX_WAIT, NOTHROTTLE, SUSPEND; SUSPEND requires WAIT), not in syncing context, and that the dsl pool config lock is not held when WAIT is set. NOTHROTTLE sets tx_dirty_delayed; unless SUSPEND is set it sets tx_break_on_suspend. It then loops on dmu_tx_try_assign: for each non-zero result it calls dmu_tx_unassign (which drops the txg hold and the dnode holds but does not clear tx_tempreserve_cookie), maps ESHUTDOWN to ERESTART (SUSPEND, or WAIT without continue failmode...) or EIO (WAIT with the pool failmode CONTINUE) per the flags, and returns the error unless it is ERESTART and WAIT was requested (so the returned errors are those allowed by the ASSERT: EDQUOT, ENOSPC, ERESTART or EIO). For ERESTART with WAIT it clears tx_break_on_suspend if the pool was suspended, calls dmu_tx_wait, restores tx_break_on_suspend (unless SUSPEND) and tries again. On success (try_assign returned 0) it calls txg_rele_to_quiesce(&tx->tx_txgh), which releases the quiesce hold, and returns 0. The txg itself stays held for syncing until the later dmu_tx_commit/abort (txg_rele_to_sync), so on success the transaction is still assigned. There is no explicit monotonic-txg guarantee in this function.

functions.name: dmu_zfetch_prepare
functions.prose_contract: Decides prefetching for a read at [blkid, blkid + nblks) (dmu_zfetch.c:470-689, returns a zstream_t pointer or NULL). It returns NULL at once if prefetch is globally disabled or the objset prefetch mode is NONE; for mode METADATA it only sets fetch_data = FALSE (it does not return). It returns NULL if indirect vdevs are not yet loaded, and if !have_lock and blkid == 0. If !have_lock it takes dn_struct_rwlock as reader; if the dnode's maxblkid < 2 it releases that lock (if it took it) and returns NULL. It then takes zf_lock and scans the streams: an exact or one-off match goes to hit; otherwise it looks for a stride/future/past match: stride and future matches go to future, an overlapping earlier stream goes to hit, and a recent 'past' match refreshes the stream's atime and exits via out (return NULL). With no match it creates a new stream when end_blkid < maxblkid (dmu_zfetch_stream_create), drops zf_lock and, WITHOUT returning a stream, falls to the prescient section; there it issues indirect-block prefetches (dbuf_prefetch at level 1 for the computed range), releases dn_struct_rwlock if it took it, counts the issued I/Os and returns zs, which is NULL on this miss path. On hit/future paths it updates the stream's atime, returns NULL via out if no blocks remain or the stream reached the end (removing the stream if end_blkid >= maxblkid), otherwise it grows the prefetch distance (data distance only when fetch_data is true; with fetch_data false pf_nblks is 0 but the indirect prefetch distance still advances), takes a reference on the stream (zs_refs and zs_callers), drops zf_lock, runs the same prescient prefetch and returns the stream (non-NULL) even when fetch_data is false. The dn_struct_rwlock is released on the return paths only when this function took it (have_lock false).

functions.name: spa_keystore_change_key_sync
functions.prose_contract: Sync-task function that changes a dataset's wrapping key (dsl_crypt.c:1540-1633, void). It holds the dataset (VERIFY0) and asserts it is not a snapshot. For DCP_CMD_NEW_KEY it takes the wrapping key from the params and sets its ddobj; for DCP_CMD_FORCE_NEW_KEY it uses keylocation 'prompt' and has no wrapping key (wkey stays NULL). For these two commands it sets the keylocation property locally only if keylocation is non-NULL (for NEW_KEY that is only when cp_keylocation was supplied; for FORCE_NEW_KEY it is always set to 'prompt'), and takes the current encryption root as the old root and the dataset's own dir as the new root. For the inherit commands (DCP_CMD_INHERIT holds the parent's wrapping key in wkey; FORCE_INHERIT does not) it clears the keylocation property (source NONE), takes the dataset's dir as old root and the parent's encryption root as new root. It then takes sk_wkeys_lock as writer, calls spa_keystore_change_key_sync_impl(old root, dd_object, new root, wkey, B_FALSE, tx), removes and frees any cached wrapping key for this dataset's ddobj (asserting its refcount is 0), and inserts the new key into the keystore AVL tree only for DCP_CMD_NEW_KEY (FORCE_NEW_KEY and the two inherit commands insert nothing); for DCP_CMD_INHERIT it releases the parent key hold taken above. It releases the lock and the dataset hold. The function returns void.

functions.name: spa_do_crypt_abd
functions.prose_contract: Encrypts or decrypts one block held in abds (dsl_crypt.c:2808-2896; the packet name zio_do_crypt does not exist, the slice cut the head). It asserts the encryption feature is active and looks up the key for zb->zb_objset in the keystore; if that fails it returns EACCES at once, before touching any buffer or the salt/iv/mac outputs. It borrows the plain and cipher buffers (the input one by copy). When encrypting a non-intent-log, non-dedup block it fills the salt (zio_crypt_key_get_salt) and a random IV; when encrypting a dedup block it derives the IV and salt from an HMAC of the plaintext; a failure of either goes to error. For decryption (and for encrypting ZIL blocks, whose salt/iv were generated at allocation) it uses the caller-provided salt and iv. It then calls zio_do_crypt_data with the key, mac and no_crypt; and, if fault injection is enabled, for a successful decryption of a non-DNODE object it may replace the result with zio_handle_decrypt_injection(..., ECKSUM). A non-zero result goes to error; on success it returns the buffers (the output buffer by copy-back), releases the key hold with spa_keystore_dsl_key_rele and returns 0. At error, when encrypting it zeroes the salt, iv and mac outputs, returns the buffers the same way, releases the key hold and returns the error value; when decrypting it returns the buffers and releases the key hold. Return value: 0, EACCES, or the callee's or injected error.

functions.name: dsl_scan_check_suspend
functions.prose_contract: Decides whether the scan should suspend now (dsl_scan.c:1643-1720, returns boolean_t). In order: returns B_FALSE if zb is non-NULL and zb_object (as signed) is negative, even if scn_suspending is already set; returns B_TRUE if scn_suspending is already set (without changing the bookmark); returns B_FALSE if the saved scn_bookmark is not zero (resuming); returns B_FALSE if zb is non-NULL and its level is neither 0 nor ZB_ROOT_LEVEL. Otherwise it computes scan time, sync time and the dirty-data threshold, and if any suspend condition holds (scan time over the minimum and (dirty data at or above the threshold, or a txg sync is waiting, or the sync time reached zfs_txg_timeout), or the spa is shutting down, or strict memory limiting wants a clear, or the DDT walk is not ready) it records where to resume: for a root-level zb it sets the bookmark to (objset, 0, 0, 0), for another non-NULL zb it copies *zb into scn_bookmark, and for a NULL zb (DDT suspend) it leaves scn_bookmark unchanged (it only logs the DDT bookmark in debug builds); in all three cases it then sets scn_suspending = B_TRUE and returns B_TRUE. If no suspend condition holds it returns B_FALSE.

functions.name: dsl_scan_sync
functions.prose_contract: Per-txg scan sync entry point (dsl_scan.c:4354-4669, void). Beginning: if spa_resilver_deferred it activates the RESILVER_DEFER feature if needed and computes restart_early (defer disabled, or fewer blocks issued than the configured percent of the to-examine count). It returns at once if spa_sync_pass > 1. If the scan is restarting (dsl_scan_restarting) or restart_early is set it ends the current scan with dsl_scan_done(scn, B_FALSE, tx) and starts a new scrub, or resilver when a vdev needs one, with dsl_scan_setup_sync (this dirties scan state) and then continues. It then returns if the pool is shutting down, if the sync txg is before spa_first_txg + zfs_import_defer_txgs, or if async destroys are not stalled and no scan is active. Past those, it resets the per-txg statistics counters, clears scn_suspending, records scn_sync_start_time and sets spa->spa_scrub_active = B_TRUE (so these are done before the following early returns). It runs dsl_process_async_destroys and returns if that gave an error; returns if no scan is running or the scrub is paused; and, if zfs_scan_suspend_progress is set, it waits (in one-second delays) until the minimum time passes, a txg sync is waiting or the pool shuts down, and returns. Otherwise it optionally reports statistics every zfs_scan_report_txgs, sets the checkpoint state, then, when the scan is not clearing and not done, it traverses (the main scan work branch: DDT scan then dsl_scan_visit with prefetch tasks and bookkeeping, reporting stats), else for a sorted scan with queues pending it issues the queued I/O, else when scn_done_txg is reached it finishes the scan. The remaining work-branch details (lines 4549-4669) were only skimmed for structure.

functions.name: metaslab_activate
functions.prose_contract: Activates a metaslab for an allocator (metaslab.c:3591-3665). The caller must hold ms_lock (ASSERT). An already-active metaslab is accepted: if ms_weight has an active bit set it asserts the metaslab is loaded and returns 0 immediately, without checking the allocator or activation weight. Otherwise it calls metaslab_load; on error it resorts the metaslab in its group with weight 0 and returns that error (what state metaslab_load leaves the metaslab in on failure was not read). If, after loading (the lock may have been dropped during load), the metaslab became active, it returns EBUSY if ms_allocator differs from allocator or if the active weight bits do not include activation_weight, else (after an EQUIV assertion about the primary flag) returns 0. If ms_weight is 0 it asserts the allocatable range tree is empty and returns ENOSPC. Otherwise it calls metaslab_activate_allocator(group, msp, allocator, activation_weight) and returns its error if non-zero, else asserts the metaslab is loaded and active and returns 0.

functions.name: metaslab_should_condense
functions.prose_contract: Static boolean_t (metaslab.c:3836-3862) with one parameter, msp. It asserts ms_lock held, the metaslab loaded, a space map present and sync pass 1. It returns B_TRUE at once if the allocatable range tree has no segments or ms_condense_wanted is set. Otherwise it computes record_size = MAX(sm_blksz, vdev_blocksize), where vdev_blocksize is a local variable set to 1ULL << vd->vdev_ashift (it is not a parameter of this function), object_size = space_map_length(sm) and optimal_size = space_map_estimate_optimal_size(sm, ms_allocatable, SM_NO_VDEVID), and returns B_TRUE only if object_size >= optimal_size * zfs_condense_pct / 100 AND object_size > zfs_metaslab_condense_block_threshold * record_size; otherwise B_FALSE. No state is modified.

functions.name: spa_wait_tag
functions.prose_contract: Thin wrapper (spa.c:11577-11581) that returns spa_wait_common(pool, activity, B_TRUE, tag, waited). The slice mostly shows spa_wait_common (spa.c:11510-11570), whose behaviour is: with use_tag it returns EINVAL unless the activity is ZPOOL_WAIT_INITIALIZE or ZPOOL_WAIT_TRIM, and returns EINVAL for an activity outside the valid range, before touching the pool; it opens the pool (returning spa_open's error), takes spa_activities_lock, increments spa_waiters and closes the pool handle. It sets *waited = B_FALSE and loops: it calls spa_activity_in_progress; it leaves the loop if that returned an error, if the activity (or, with a tag, that tag) is not in progress (this includes a tag that is absent), or if spa_waiters_cancel is set (so it can return 0 without the activity having finished); otherwise it sets *waited = B_TRUE and waits on spa_activities_cv, returning EINTR if the wait was interrupted. It then decrements spa_waiters, signals spa_waiters_cv, drops the lock and returns error (0 when it left because of no activity in progress or because of the cancel flag, an errno otherwise). So the tag need not be in progress and *waited stays false when no wait happened.

functions.name: spa_ld_select_uberblock
functions.prose_contract: Selects the uberblock to use during pool load (spa.c:4720-4884, returns int). Early return: if the current uberblock has a checkpoint txg and the pool is being imported read-only from its checkpoint it calls spa_ld_select_uberblock_done and returns 0 immediately, skipping the label search and the feature recording. Otherwise it loads the best uberblock and label with vdev_uberblock_load and returns spa_vdev_err(VDEV_AUX_CORRUPT_DATA, ENXIO) if no valid uberblock (txg 0) was found (freeing the label). It logs the chosen txg (and the raidz reflow info if set) and runs the multihost activity check when required: a failure maps through spa_ld_activity_result, frees the label and returns that error; when not required it records MMP result ESRCH. It returns spa_vdev_err(VDEV_AUX_VERSION_NEWER, ENOTSUP) if the on-disk version is unsupported (label freed); for versions with feature flags it requires the label to exist and have the features-for-read nvlist (otherwise ENXIO via spa_vdev_err), and stores a duplicate of that list in spa_label_features. It frees the label, then returns spa_vdev_err(VDEV_AUX_UNSUP_FEAT, ENOTSUP) with the unsupported feature list recorded in spa_load_info if any feature in the label is unsupported. If not assembling and a config split is in progress, it takes the config lock as writer, calls spa_try_repair (which has no return value here) and clears spa_config_splitting. Finally it calls spa_ld_select_uberblock_done and returns 0.

functions.name: spa_export_common
functions.prose_contract: Common export/destroy path (spa.c:7652-7845, returns int). It sets *oldconfig = NULL if given. Without the namespace lock held by the caller (it takes spa_namespace_lock itself, so the caller must not hold it) it returns, before any state change or async suspend: EROFS if the global mode is not writable, ENOENT if the pool does not exist, ZFS_ERR_EXPORT_IN_PROGRESS if another export of the pool is running. It then marks spa_is_exporting, takes a reference, drops the namespace lock, suspends async tasks, removes zvol minors, retakes the lock and records the export thread. If the pool is UNINITIALIZED it jumps to export_spa. Otherwise it waits for a sync when sync is on; goes to fail with EBUSY if the pool is still referenced or has injection references; drops the namespace lock; if sync is on: with !force and EXPORTED it goes to fail with EXDEV if an active shared spare exists (after retaking the namespace lock); otherwise stops initialize, trim, autotrim, rebuild and the L2ARC rebuild, unless hardforce (or new state UNINITIALIZED) it marks the new state and dirties the vdev config, flushes the sync-time logger and log space maps when appropriate and, unless hardforce, sets spa_final_txg. At export_spa it runs spa_export_os, sends the destroy or export event, unloads and deactivates the pool unless uninitialised, copies the config into *oldconfig when asked and present, applies the export-delay injection, retakes the namespace lock and, for new states other than UNINITIALIZED, writes the cache file (skipped when hardforce) and calls spa_remove; for UNINITIALIZED it only clears spa_is_exporting and spa_export_thread. It broadcasts the namespace condition, drops the lock and returns 0. The fail label clears spa_is_exporting and the export thread, resumes async tasks, broadcasts and returns the error; the early EROFS, ENOENT and EXPORT_IN_PROGRESS returns do none of that (they have not suspended async work or set the flags).

functions.name: vdev_offline_locked
functions.prose_contract: Offlines a leaf vdev (vdev.c:4551-4659, returns int, every return goes through spa_vdev_state_exit). It enters vdev state with SCL_ALLOC and looks the vdev up by guid: ENODEV if not found, ENOTSUP if it is not a leaf or is a dRAID spare. If the vdev is not already offline: for a non-log, non-aux vdev whose DTL is required it returns EBUSY; for a log (slog) vdev with a metaslab group it passivates the group, leaves vdev state, calls spa_reset_logs, sets the error to ZFS_ERR_CHECKPOINT_EXISTS if the log top vdev has a non-empty checkpoint space map, re-enters vdev state and, if there was an error or the config generation changed, re-activates the group and either returns that error (including an error from spa_reset_logs or ZFS_ERR_CHECKPOINT_EXISTS) or, when only the generation changed, retries from the top. It then sets vdev_offline and reopens the top vdev; for a non-log, non-aux vdev if the top vdev is then dead it clears vdev_offline, reopens and returns EBUSY. On the success path for a slog it re-activates the metaslab group (vdev.c:4652-4653), so the group is not left passivated. Finally, in all non-error cases it sets vdev_tmpoffline from ZFS_OFFLINE_TEMPORARY and returns the result of spa_vdev_state_exit(spa, vd, 0), which is 0 on success.

functions.name: vdev_prop_get
functions.prose_contract: Fills outnvl with vdev properties (vdev.c:6308-6799; the slice cut the head). It asserts vd and the meta objset are set, then returns EINVAL if innvl lacks ZPOOL_VDEV_PROPS_GET_VDEV (the vdev guid), and EINVAL if the vdev's property object id cannot be found. The ZPOOL_VDEV_PROPS_GET_PROPS list in innvl is optional: its absence is not an error. With spa_props_lock held it handles two modes. If a property list was given, it processes each requested name: for each property that has a value for this vdev it adds an entry to outnvl and continues; some properties are only added when applicable and otherwise skipped without an error, e.g. name when no string, path, devid, physpath, enclosure path and fru when NULL, parent when there is no parent, children when there are none, RAIDZ_EXPANDING only for raidz vdevs, SIT_OUT only for leaf vdevs with the required conditions, TRIM_SUPPORT only for leaf vdevs, ALLOCATING/AUTOSIT conditional parts, and the stored user/comment properties are read from the ZAP (a stored integer of size 8 gives EINVAL, a missing one an error); an unknown property name sets err = ENOENT; the first non-zero err stops the loop. Without a list it iterates the whole property ZAP of the vdev, adding string-valued and integer-valued stored properties (user properties as local source). It then releases spa_props_lock and returns err if it is non-zero and not ENOENT, else 0, so an ENOENT result (unknown or missing property) is not reported as an error. Properties that are not present for the vdev are skipped, not added with a default.

functions.name: vdev_inuse
functions.prose_contract: Decides whether a device label shows the device is in use (vdev_label.c:891-1016, returns boolean_t). It first sets *spare_guid and *l2cache_guid to 0 if those pointers are non-NULL. It returns B_FALSE if the label cannot be read, if the pool state or device guid is missing, or, for non-spare non-l2cache labels, if the pool guid or pool txg is missing. For a non-spare, non-l2cache label it returns B_FALSE if neither the pool guid pair nor a spare nor an l2cache with that device guid is known, and returns B_TRUE if txg == 0 and the label's create txg equals crtxg (this B_TRUE case requires that the label state is not spare or l2cache). If the device guid is a known spare (spa_spare_exists or spa_has_spare) it sets *spare_guid = device_guid (even if the function then returns B_FALSE) and, depending on reason, returns B_TRUE for CREATE, (!spa_has_spare || spare_pool != 0) for REPLACE, spa_has_spare for SPARE, or falls through for other reasons. Likewise for a known l2cache device it sets *l2cache_guid and returns B_TRUE for CREATE, !spa_has_l2cache for REPLACE, spa_has_l2cache for L2CACHE, or falls through. Finally, for non-spare non-l2cache labels whose pool is found by guid and open read-only, the state is treated as ACTIVE; it returns state == POOL_STATE_ACTIVE. So *spare_guid / *l2cache_guid can be non-zero even when the return is B_FALSE.

functions.name: MUL_x2_DEFINE(x)
functions.prose_contract: Macro (vdev_raidz_math_avx512f.c:249-251) that generates 'static void mul_x2_<x>(void)' for x = 0..35 (invoked at lines 254-262): each function expands _MUL_PARAM(x, 21, 22 as input, 23, 24 as accumulator), emitting inline AVX-512 instructions that multiply the data held in the register pair zmm21, zmm22 (two 512-bit vectors) by the constant x in GF(2^8) and leave the product in the pair zmm23, zmm24. The expansion is decided at compile time from x: bit 0 of x selects COPY(in, acc) versus ZERO(acc) for the accumulator; each further multiplication by 2 (MUL2 on the input pair) is performed only if x has a higher bit set, and each XOR(in, acc) is done if the corresponding bit of x is set. So for x = 0 only the accumulator is zeroed (input untouched), and for x = 1 the input is copied to the accumulator and the input registers are not modified; for x >= 2 the input pair zmm21/zmm22 is overwritten by the successive doublings (MUL2 also uses scratch registers, including zmm25 and zmm26, and the constants set up by MUL2_SETUP, which the caller must have prepared). The generated function takes no arguments, has no return value and acts only on the zmm registers; it does not access memory.

functions.name: spa_vdev_noalloc
functions.prose_contract: Marks a top-level vdev as no-allocate (vdev_removal.c:306-336, returns int). It asserts the namespace lock is not held on entry and the pool is writeable, then calls spa_vdev_enter(spa) (which takes the namespace lock and returns a txg). It looks the vdev up by guid: error ENOENT if not found; ZFS_ERR_VDEV_NOTSUP if the vdev has no metaslab group; if the vdev is not already noalloc, error = vdev_passivate(vd, &txg) (which may return an error such as EINVAL, not read; vdev_noalloc may already have been set by it before the exit step); if it is already noalloc the error stays 0. If error is 0 (including the already-noalloc case) it dirties the DTL leaves and the vdev config. Finally it returns spa_vdev_exit(spa, NULL, txg, error), so the value returned is the result of that call, which passes the error through and can itself return a different error (for example a failure of its transaction wait) even after the vdev was changed; the failure state is therefore not guaranteed unchanged.

functions.name: get_special_prop
functions.prose_contract: Static int (zcp_get.c:224-453; the packet name zcp_get_ds_prop does not exist, the slice cut the head and also shows get_zap_prop) that looks up a dataset property by special-case code and pushes value and source onto the Lua stack. It allocates a ZAP_MAXVALUELEN string buffer and a setpoint buffer. For ZFS_PROP_CLONES it builds the clone list with get_clones_stat_impl: on success it pushes that list as a Lua table through zcp_nvlist_to_lua (VERIFY0) and then pushes nil as the source and returns 0; on failure it pushes nothing (so no table is left on the stack by this function), frees the list and buffer and returns the error. For the other properties it computes numval or strval in a big switch (ds accessors, objset/ZAP lookups for VERSION, VOLSIZE, VOLBLOCKSIZE, IVSET_GUID, RECEIVE_RESUME_TOKEN, encryption properties, etc.; unmatched properties are looked up in the dsl_dir with get_dsl_dir_prop). A non-zero error from that switch frees the buffer and returns the error with nothing pushed. Otherwise, depending on the property type, it pushes the number, the string, or, for index properties, the index string (zfs_prop_index_to_string; if that fails it frees the buffer and returns the error with nothing pushed), then frees the buffer, pushes the source with get_prop_src and returns 0. On success exactly two values are pushed (value then source) in the normal path and, for CLONES, the table and nil.

functions.name: zfs_set_prop_nvlist
functions.prose_contract: Applies a list of property settings to dataset dsname (zfs_ioctl.c:2766-2936; the slice cut the head). It returns the last error seen in rv (0 if none); errlist may be NULL, in which case errors are only reflected in the return value. For each pair it extracts the value (an nvlist wrapper must contain ZPROP_VALUE else EINVAL), validates the type against the property (for inherit the value must be a boolean; user properties must be strings and userquota ones uint64 arrays; others must match the property type, an index value must be a valid index else ZFS_ERR_BADPROP), then calls zfs_check_settable and, unless inheriting, zfs_prop_set_special. A result of -1 (not special) puts the pair into genericnvl; another non-zero result from zfs_prop_set_special in the first pass puts the pair into retrynvl, and that nvlist_add result overwrites err, so such a failure is not recorded in rv or errlist in that pass. Validation and settable errors are recorded immediately (added to errlist if given, and rv = err). After the first pass, if retrynvl is non-empty it loops again over retrynvl; failures there are recorded (errlist, rv) and are not queued again, while a retry that succeeds leaves rv and errlist untouched. If genericnvl is non-empty it calls dsl_props_set once; on failure it falls back to setting each property one by one (string, inherit or integer), recording each failure in errlist and rv. namespace-related properties set should_update_mount_cache, which triggers zfs_ioctl_update_mount_cache at the end. It frees both temporary nvlists and returns rv.

functions.name: zfs_replay_write2
functions.prose_contract: Replays a TX_WRITE2 log record by only extending the file size (zfs_replay.c:880-926, static int). It asserts the record length, byteswaps the record when asked, and returns the error of zfs_zget(lr_foid) if the znode cannot be obtained. At top it computes end = offset + length; if end is greater than zp->z_size it creates a transaction and sets zp->z_size = end BEFORE the transaction is assigned (so the size is changed in memory even if the assignment later fails), holds the SA, and assigns it with DMU_TX_WAIT. If the assign fails it releases the znode (zrele) and, for ERESTART, waits, aborts the tx and jumps back to top with zp already released (the retry then uses and releases zp a second time); for any other error it aborts the tx and returns the error (zp already released). On success it updates the SA size (result ignored), marks the log replay on the tx (zil_replaying) and commits. After the optional extension it releases the znode with zrele and returns error, which is 0 on the paths that reach the end.

functions.name: zil_check_log_chain
functions.prose_contract: Dataset-iteration callback (zil.c:1264-1329) that checks that a dataset's intent-log chain can be walked. It ignores dp and asserts tx is NULL. It opens the objset with dmu_objset_from_ds; if that fails it logs a warning and returns 0 (the failure is handled here, so the objset is not required to be openable by the caller). It reads the log header's block pointer; if it is not a hole it takes SCL_STATE as reader only in this case (the lock is not taken when the log pointer is a hole), looks up the top-level vdev of the first DVA and, for a dead log vdev, computes validity with vdev_log_state_valid; an invalid result returns 0 without parsing. It also returns 0 if the pool has a checkpoint txg and the log header was never claimed (zh_claim_txg == 0). Then it calls zil_parse(zilog, zil_claim_log_block, zil_claim_log_record, tx, claim_txg, B_FALSE) with claim_txg = -1ULL when the header has already been claimed, else spa_min_claim_txg(), and returns 0 if the result is ECKSUM or ENOENT, otherwise the zil_parse error value (0 on success).

functions.name: zio_write_compress
functions.prose_contract: ZIO pipeline stage that compresses a write and sets up its block pointer (zio.c:1913-2131). It returns NULL (zio stopped) if zio_wait_for_children says it must wait for logical/gang children; returns zio unchanged (no compression, no transform, psize and compression untouched) if the zio is not an allocating write. It calls io_children_ready for parent blocks, and for a block already allocated in this txg (rewrite in syncing context) sets pass from the sync pass and turns compression off at or beyond zfs_sync_pass_dont_compress. If compression is on and the zio is not a raw-compress write, it computes psize: 0 for an all-zero buffer, lsize for ZIO_COMPRESS_EMPTY, else the result of zio_compress_data. psize 0 or psize >= lsize turns compression off (freeing the compressed abd when psize >= lsize); a result small enough for an embedded block (not encrypted, level 0, no fill, feature enabled) builds an embedded block pointer, frees the abd, sets the birth txg, sets the interlock pipeline and returns zio at once; otherwise the compressed size is rounded up to the allocation size, and if the rounded size is not smaller than lsize compression is turned off and psize = lsize (abd freed), else the buffer is zero-padded, psize = rounded and the compressed buffer is pushed as a transform. After a compression attempt it clears io_bp_override and restores io_bp_orig and the original pipeline. For raw-encrypted DNODE writes psize is 0 (and compression off) for an all-zero buffer, else lsize; for raw-compress non-encrypted writes it pads the data up to the rounded allocation size via a transform when that differs from psize; otherwise it asserts psize != 0. Then it either converts the zio to a rewrite (same txg, same psize, pass >= zfs_sync_pass_rewrite) or zeroes the bp and uses the write pipeline. If psize is 0 it sets a hole bp when the original had a birth and the hole-birth feature is active, and uses the interlock pipeline; otherwise it sets the bp's lsize, type, level, psize, compress, checksum, dedup and byteorder, and only if zp_dedup is set switches to the DDT write pipeline, and only if zp_nopwrite is set adds the NOP_WRITE stage. It returns zio.

functions.name: zio_vdev_io_done
functions.prose_contract: ZIO pipeline stage run after the vdev I/O completes (zio.c:4811-4857). It returns NULL (zio stopped) if zio_wait_for_children indicates it must wait for vdev children. Otherwise it asserts the zio type (read, write, flush or trim) and converts a non-zero io_delay start time into an elapsed time. If the zio's vdev exists, is a leaf and is not a dRAID spare: for non-flush zios it calls vdev_queue_io_done; with fault injection enabled and no error yet it may set io_error from device and label injection (any zio type); and only for an error on a zio that is not a FLUSH or TRIM it sets io_error to ENXIO when the vdev is not accessible, else it flags an unexpected error. It then calls the vdev ops' io_done (for a NULL vdev the mirror ops). If an unexpected error was flagged and vdev_remove_wanted is false it calls vdev_probe (result VERIFY0P-asserted to be NULL). It returns zio. So the ENXIO conversion and the probe apply only to read and write errors, not to flush or trim errors.

functions.name: zvol_init_impl
functions.prose_contract: Initialises the zvol subsystem (zvol.c:2144-2227, returns int). It computes zvol_actual_threads: MAX(max_ncpus, 32) when zvol_threads is 0, else zvol_threads clamped to 1..1024. It picks the number of taskqs, MIN(max_ncpus, zvol_num_taskqs), or, when that is 0, 1 + max_ncpus/6 reduced while num_tqs squared exceeds the thread count; the threads per taskq are the rounded-up share. It sets zvol_taskqs.tqs_cnt, allocates the taskq pointer array (KM_SLEEP) and creates each taskq; if a taskq_create returns NULL it destroys the ones already created, frees the array and sets it to NULL and returns SET_ERROR(ENOMEM), which is the positive value ENOMEM (12), not -ENOMEM; zvol_taskqs.tqs_cnt keeps the attempted count and zvol_state_list, zvol_state_lock and zvol_htable have not been initialised at that point. On success it creates zvol_state_list, initialises zvol_state_lock, allocates and initialises the ZVOL_HT_SIZE hash heads of zvol_htable and returns 0. It reads module parameters and writes global state.

functions.name: HUF_compress_internal
functions.prose_contract: Static size_t (huf_compress.c:638-725) that Huffman-compresses src into dst, returning a compressed size, 0 (store uncompressed), 1 (single-symbol RLE) or a ZSTD error code. Checks in order: workspace not 4-byte aligned gives ERROR(GENERIC), workspace smaller than HUF_WORKSPACE_SIZE gives ERROR(workSpace_tooSmall); srcSize == 0 or dstSize == 0 returns 0; srcSize > HUF_BLOCKSIZE_MAX gives ERROR(srcSize_wrong); huffLog or maxSymbolValue above their maxima give tableLog_tooLarge / maxSymbolValue_tooLarge errors; zero maxSymbolValue and huffLog take defaults. If preferRepeat is set, repeat is non-NULL and *repeat is HUF_repeat_valid it immediately returns HUF_compressCTable_internal with the old table (this reuse path can return 0 or a size and is taken before any histogram, so it can precede the single-symbol check). Otherwise it counts symbols (a histogram error is returned), returns 1 after writing the single byte to ostart when one symbol makes up the whole input (this return does not update *repeat or oldHufTable), returns 0 if the data is judged not compressible (largest <= srcSize/128 + 4). If *repeat is HUF_repeat_check and the old table does not validate for the symbol range it sets *repeat = HUF_repeat_none. If preferRepeat and *repeat is not none it reuses the old table (compress-with-old-table return). Else it builds a new Huffman tree (errors from HUF_buildCTable_wksp or HUF_writeCTable are returned), writes the table header; with a usable old table it compares estimated sizes and may return the old-table compression, and it returns 0 if the header size plus 12 is not smaller than srcSize; otherwise it advances past the header, sets *repeat = HUF_repeat_none, saves the new table into oldHufTable if provided and returns HUF_compressCTable_internal with the new table.

functions.name: ZSTD_compressBegin_usingCDict_advanced
functions.prose_contract: Starts a compression frame using a prepared dictionary (zstd_compress.c:3539-3571, returns size_t). It returns an error (dictionary_wrong via RETURN_ERROR_IF) if cdict is NULL. Otherwise it copies cctx->requestedParams and chooses cParams: the dictionary's own parameters (ZSTD_getCParamsFromCDict) when the attach preference is not ZSTD_dictForceLoad and (pledgedSrcSize is below the cutoff, or below dictContentSize times the multiplier, or unknown, or the dictionary level is 0); else parameters recomputed from the dictionary level, the pledged size and the dictionary size. Only when pledgedSrcSize is known does it raise windowLog to at least ceil(log2(min(pledgedSrcSize, 2^19))) (the source size is capped at 2^19, so the window log is raised by at most that much, not enough to cover larger sources; with an unknown size windowLog is not raised). It sets params.fParams = fParams and returns ZSTD_compressBegin_internal(cctx, NULL, 0, ZSTD_dct_auto, ZSTD_dtlm_fast, cdict, &params, pledgedSrcSize, ZSTDb_not_buffered), so the result is 0 or an error code from that call.

functions.name: ZSTD_compressStream_generic
functions.prose_contract: Static size_t (zstd_compress.c:3804-3943) running the streaming compression state machine. It asserts that the input and output buffers and the stream buffers are set and the positions are within their sizes. It loops while there is more work, switching on zcs->streamStage: zcss_init returns the error init_missing at once (so a stream that was not initialised is an error handled here, not a precondition); zcss_load either, for ZSTD_e_end with enough output capacity and an empty input buffer, compresses the whole remaining input directly (ZSTD_compressEnd, error forwarded), sets frameEnded and resets the session, or copies input into the internal buffer, ends the loop for ZSTD_e_continue when the buffer is not yet full or for ZSTD_e_flush when nothing new is buffered, else compresses one block (ZSTD_compressEnd for the last block, otherwise ZSTD_compressContinue; errors are forwarded), compressing straight into the caller's output when it has room, else into the internal output buffer and moving to zcss_flush; zcss_flush copies as much of the buffered output as fits, stops when output is full, and after a full flush either ends the frame (resetting the session) or returns to zcss_load. Errors (FORWARD_IF_ERROR, init_missing) are returned before input->pos and output->pos are updated. On normal exit it stores input->pos and output->pos, and returns 0 if zcs->frameEnded is set, else ZSTD_nextInputSizeHint(zcs).

functions.name: ZSTD_window_update
functions.prose_contract: MEM_STATIC U32 (zstd_compress_internal.h:938-972) that registers a new source segment in the match-finder window and returns whether it is contiguous with the previous one. If srcSize == 0 it returns 1 immediately and changes nothing (nextSrc is not updated). Otherwise it asserts window->base and dictBase are set. If src differs from window->nextSrc (a non-contiguous segment) it saves the old position as the extDict: lowLimit = old dictLimit, dictLimit = distance of nextSrc from base, dictBase = old base, base = ip - distance; if the extDict is smaller than HASH_READ_SIZE it sets lowLimit = dictLimit; and the return value becomes 0. It then sets window->nextSrc = ip + srcSize. If the new input overlaps the extDict (ends after dictBase + lowLimit and starts before dictBase + dictLimit) it RAISES lowLimit to min(dictLimit, the input's end index relative to dictBase), so lowLimit only increases there. It returns contiguous (1 unless the non-contiguous branch was taken).

functions.name: ZSTD_selectEncodingType
functions.prose_contract: Chooses the symbol-compression mode for a sequence table (zstd_compress_sequences.c:143-221, returns symbolEncodingType_e: set_basic, set_rle, set_repeat or set_compressed) and updates *repeatMode. If mostFrequent == nbSeq (a single symbol) it sets *repeatMode = FSE_repeat_none and returns set_basic when defaults are allowed and nbSeq <= 2, else set_rle. For strategies below ZSTD_lazy with defaults allowed: it returns set_repeat if *repeatMode is FSE_repeat_valid and nbSeq < 1000 (leaving *repeatMode unchanged, so it stays valid), or set_basic (setting *repeatMode = none) when nbSeq is below the dynamic minimum or mostFrequent is below nbSeq >> (defaultNormLog-1); without defaults allowed this branch selects nothing and falls to set_compressed. For lazier strategies it computes the bit cost of the default table (if allowed), of the previous table (when *repeatMode is not none, which reads prevCTable, so prevCTable must be valid whenever *repeatMode is FSE_repeat_check or valid) and of a new compressed table, and returns set_basic (repeatMode = none) if the default is no more costly than both, else set_repeat (repeatMode unchanged) if the repeat cost is no more than the new table, else falls through. All paths that fall through set *repeatMode = FSE_repeat_check and return set_compressed. So after a set_repeat return *repeatMode can remain FSE_repeat_valid.

functions.name: ZSTD_compressBlock_lazy_generic
functions.prose_contract: Static size_t (zstd_lazy.c:626-868) implementing the greedy/lazy/lazy2 match finder for one block; it appends sequences to seqStore and returns the number of trailing literal bytes (iend - anchor) that were not covered by a stored sequence. It reads the repeat offsets itself: offset_1 = rep[0], offset_2 = rep[1] (so the caller supplies rep[] as in/out, but does not have to prepare anything else beyond valid values). In ZSTD_noDict mode it zeroes any repeat offset that exceeds the current window (keeping one in savedOffset); in dictMatchState mode it asserts both repeat offsets are within dict plus prefix length. It chooses the search function by search method and dict mode and loops while ip < ilimit (iend - 8): at each position it first tries the repeat-offset match, then searchMax; with depth > 0 it runs the lazy search for a better match at ip + 1 (and ip + 2 for depth 2) and keeps the best; only the finally selected match for each iteration is stored with ZSTD_storeSeq (the other candidates found during the lazy search are discarded, not stored). After storing a match it also loops over immediate repeat-offset matches (stored with zero literals). When the loop ends it writes back rep[0] = offset_1 (or savedOffset if it was zero) and rep[1] = offset_2 (or savedOffset), and returns iend - anchor. It does not copy the final literals itself; the caller does.

functions.name: ZSTD_decodingBufferSize_min
functions.prose_contract: Computes the minimum decoding ring-buffer size (zstd_decompress.c:1485-1494, size_t). blockSize = MIN(windowSize, ZSTD_BLOCKSIZE_MAX); neededRBSize = windowSize + blockSize + WILDCOPY_OVERLENGTH * 2 computed in unsigned long long (WILDCOPY_OVERLENGTH is 32 in zstd_internal.h:257, so the constant added is 64); neededSize = MIN(frameContentSize, neededRBSize). The result is neededSize converted to size_t; if that conversion changes the value (possible only where size_t is narrower than 64 bits) the function returns the error code frameParameter_windowTooLarge via RETURN_ERROR_IF, otherwise it returns minRBSize. There is no check against overflow of the unsigned long long addition itself, and no global state is read.

functions.name: ZSTD_estimateDStreamSize
functions.prose_contract: Estimates the memory needed by a streaming decompressor (zstd_decompress.c:1496-1502, size_t). With blockSize = MIN(windowSize, ZSTD_BLOCKSIZE_MAX), inBuffSize = blockSize and outBuffSize = ZSTD_decodingBufferSize_min(windowSize, ZSTD_CONTENTSIZE_UNKNOWN), it returns ZSTD_estimateDCtxSize() (= sizeof(ZSTD_DCtx), zstd_decompress.c:87) + inBuffSize + outBuffSize. The error return of ZSTD_decodingBufferSize_min is not checked, so an error code from it would be added into the sum like an ordinary size. The WILDCOPY_OVERLENGTH * 2 term inside outBuffSize is 64 with WILDCOPY_OVERLENGTH = 32.

functions.name: load_tests
functions.prose_contract: Parses a crypto test vector file into a linked list (crypto_test.c:199-505; the packet name parse_test_file does not exist, the slice cut the head). It opens filepath (error message and failure if fopen fails), derives the base file name for messages, and reads lines with getline. A header section must give 'algorithm' (AES-GCM or AES-CCM) and 'tests' (a number); duplicates, unknown header keys, bad values or an incomplete header produce an error message and failure. Test records are key/value lines (id, comment, flags, result valid/invalid, and the hex fields iv, key, msg, ct, aad, tag); an unknown key, a duplicate key, an odd-length value or a non-hex character is an error. A blank line or end of file closes the test in progress: the test is committed to the list only if it has a non-zero id, all six hex fields and a result, otherwise it prints 'incomplete test' and fails, so completeness IS validated before committing. A read error (errno set) also fails. On any failure it frees the line buffer, closes the file and returns NULL (the tests parsed so far are not freed and *algp is not set). On success it frees the buffer, closes the file, prints 'no tests' if the list is empty, sets *algp = alg and returns the list head (which can be NULL when the file contains no tests).

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Program entry (manipulate_user_buffer.c:245-335). It calls parse_options(argc, argv) itself (so options need not be parsed by the caller), then opens the target file with O_DIRECT plus O_WRONLY|O_CREAT for a write test or O_RDONLY otherwise; open failure prints a message and exit(2)s. It allocates a page-aligned buffer of blocksize bytes with posix_memalign (exit(2) on error). For a write test it fills the buffer with the repeated data pattern '0xdeadbeef' or, with randompattern, random bytes. It starts the buffer-manipulating thread and then the writer or reader thread; a pthread_create failure prints a message and exit(2)s (so thread creation success is not assumed, it is handled by exiting). It joins both threads, asserts args.entire_file_completed == 1 (an assert, so this check is absent when NDEBUG is defined), closes the file, frees the buffer and returns 0. All error exits use status 2.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Program entry (xattrtest.c:669-715). It calls parse_args and returns its non-zero result immediately. If value_is_random is set it fills xattrbytes with get_random_bytes; the test 'rc < rndsz' compares an int with a size_t, so a negative rc would be converted to a large unsigned value and would not take the error branch; a non-negative short result prints an error and the function returns that rc, which can be 0 for a zero-length read, so this path can return 0 without having run any phase. Otherwise (value not random) it memsets xattrbytes to 'x'. It then runs the selected phases in order, each only when phase is ALL or that phase: create_files, setxattrs, getxattrs, and (unless keep_files is set) unlink_files; the first non-zero return of a phase is returned at once and later phases are not run. Returns 0 when all selected phases returned 0.

functions.name: pcg_output_xsh_rr_16_8
functions.prose_contract: Static inline pure function (pcg_variants.h:140-143) mapping a 16-bit PCG state to an 8-bit output ('xorshift high, random rotation'). It computes x = ((state >> 5) ^ state) >> 5 (done in int after promotion, so the intermediate is at most 16 bits wide), passes the low 8 bits of x as the value to pcg_rotr_8, and uses state >> 13 (a value 0..7) as the rotate count, returning the 8-bit result (value rotated right by that count; pcg_rotr_8 is (value >> rot) | (value << ((-rot) & 7)), or an equivalent rorb on clang x86). It reads only its argument, has no side effects and no failure result.

functions.name: pcg_output_xsh_rr_32_16
functions.prose_contract: Static inline pure function (pcg_variants.h:145-148) mapping a 32-bit PCG state to a 16-bit output. It computes x = ((state >> 10) ^ state) >> 12, takes the low 16 bits of x as the value and uses state >> 28 (0..15) as the rotate count in pcg_rotr_16, returning the rotated 16-bit value (pcg_rotr_16 is (value >> rot) | (value << ((-rot) & 15)), or rorw on clang x86). No side effects, no failure result.

functions.name: pcg_output_xsh_rr_64_32
functions.prose_contract: Static inline pure function (pcg_variants.h:150-153) mapping a 64-bit PCG state to a 32-bit output. It computes x = ((state >> 18) ^ state) >> 27, takes the low 32 bits of x as the value and uses state >> 59 (0..31) as the rotate count in pcg_rotr_32, returning the rotated 32-bit value (pcg_rotr_32 is (value >> rot) | (value << ((-rot) & 31)), or rorl on clang x86). No side effects, no failure result.

functions.name: krping_wlat_test_server
functions.prose_contract: Static void (krping.c:1295-1327) server side of the write-latency test. It spins calling krping_cq_event_handler until cb->state reaches RDMA_READ_ADV, formats and posts the send of the start DMA address (ib_post_send; on a non-zero result it prints an error and returns). It then polls the completion queue with 'while ((ret = ib_poll_cq(cb->cq, 1, &wc) == 0));': because of operator precedence ret receives the boolean value of the comparison (ib_poll_cq(...) == 0), so the loop ends when ib_poll_cq returns any non-zero value, including a negative error, and then ret is 0; the following 'ret < 0' check can therefore never be true and a negative poll result is not reported, leaving wc unset when the loop was left by an error. If wc.status is non-zero it prints a send-completion error and returns. Otherwise it runs wlat_test(cb) and then waits interruptibly until cb->state == ERROR. It returns nothing.

functions.name: krping_bw_test_server
