functions.prose_contract: Static void (krping.c:1329-1362) server side of the bandwidth test, with the same structure as the write-latency server: it calls krping_cq_event_handler until cb->state reaches RDMA_READ_ADV, posts the send of the start DMA address (print and return on a non-zero ib_post_send result), then polls with 'while ((ret = ib_poll_cq(cb->cq, 1, &wc) == 0));', which stores the boolean (poll == 0) in ret, so the loop is left by any non-zero poll result including a negative error and the later 'ret < 0' check can never fire, leaving wc unset in the error case. A non-zero wc.status prints a send-completion error and returns. Then, only if cb->duplex is set, it runs bw_test(cb); finally it waits interruptibly until cb->state == ERROR. It returns nothing.

functions.name: vchiq_arm_force_suspend
functions.prose_contract: Forces the videocore to suspend (vchiq_arm.c:2132-2240, returns VCHIQ_STATUS_T). It returns VCHIQ_ERROR straight away (out label, only the trace log) if there is no arm_state. Otherwise it takes susp_res_lock for writing and calls block_resume; if that fails it jumps to unlock with its status, WITHOUT calling unblock_resume. If the state is already VC_SUSPEND_SUSPENDED it sets VCHIQ_SUCCESS and jumps to unlock (resume stays blocked). If the state is idle or lower it stops the suspend timer and: when videocore is not wanted it calls vchiq_arm_vcsuspend (its status, which may be a failure, is kept); else if autosuspend_override is below FORCE_SUSPEND_FAIL_MAX it returns success without suspending (letting videocore go idle); else it calls vchiq_arm_vcsuspend. In any other state (suspend in progress) it sets success. A non-success status from this step jumps to unblock_resume (so a vchiq_arm_vcsuspend failure ends with unblock_resume and that status). It then waits (dropping the lock) for vc_suspend_complete with a timeout: an interrupted wait gives VCHIQ_ERROR via unblock_resume; a timeout (once repeated if suspend is in progress) increments autosuspend_override, reports a timeout and returns VCHIQ_RETRY via unblock_resume. After the wait, if the state is not SUSPENDED it logs, resets the state to IDLE if it was an error state and returns VCHIQ_RETRY via unblock_resume. On success it jumps to unlock without unblock_resume, so resume remains blocked after a successful suspend. unblock_resume (when reached) runs under the lock, then the lock is released and the status returned.

functions.name: service_callback
functions.prose_contract: Callback delivering vchiq service events to a user instance (vchiq_arm.c:272-378, returns VCHIQ_STATUS_T). It maps the handle to the service (BUG_ON if none), reads the user_service and its instance, and returns VCHIQ_SUCCESS at once, doing nothing, if the instance is NULL or closing. Only when header is non-NULL and the service is a VCHI service does it queue the message: under msg_queue_spinlock, while the message queue is full it drops the lock, inserts an extra MESSAGE_AVAILABLE completion if none is pending (a failure of add_completion is returned), waits on remove_event (an interrupted wait returns VCHIQ_RETRY; if the instance started closing it returns VCHIQ_ERROR) and retakes the lock; it then stores header in the queue, advances msg_insert, may set skip_completion if a MESSAGE_AVAILABLE is already pending or a dequeue is waiting (clearing dequeue_pending), unlocks, ups insert_event and sets header = NULL. If skip_completion is set it returns VCHIQ_SUCCESS without a completion. Otherwise it returns add_completion(instance, reason, header, user_service, bulk_userdata): with the header pointer cleared if it was queued, or with the original header when the service is not VCHI or header was NULL (in that case the header is passed straight to add_completion and not queued in the message queue).

functions.name: vchiq_ioctl
functions.prose_contract: The slice is the VCHIQ_IOC_AWAIT_COMPLETION case (vchiq_arm.c:790-961) of the ioctl handler vchiq_ioctl (vchiq_arm.c:425-1156, returns int); there is no function named after the case. In this case: it returns -ENOTCONN if the instance is not connected. It copies the user args, takes completion_mutex and, while the completion queue is empty and the instance is not closing, drops the mutex and waits on insert_event; an interrupted wait sets ret = -EINTR and leaves the wait loop. If ret is still 0 it copies up to args.count completions to the user buffer: it stops at the first empty slot; for a completion with a message header it needs args.msgbufsize >= header size plus header struct (else it logs, WARNs, sets ret = -EMSGSIZE only if nothing was copied yet, and stops), needs a free user message buffer (msgbufcount), copies the buffer pointer from user space and the message into it (-EFAULT only if count is 0, otherwise it just stops), releases the message and replaces the header pointer with the user buffer; for a closed service whose close is not delivered separately it calls unlock_service; it copies the completion record to the user (an -EFAULT is recorded only if ret is still 0, then it stops) and advances completion_remove. It writes back the updated msgbufcount and count to the user args when they changed. If at least one completion was returned it ups remove_event; if ret is 0 and the instance is closing it sets ret = -ENOTCONN; a positive ret is reset to 0; the mutex is released. After the switch the common code of vchiq_ioctl converts a status of VCHIQ_ERROR/RETRY into -EIO/-EINTR when ret is 0 and returns ret.

functions.name: vchiq_ioctl
functions.prose_contract: The slice is the VCHIQ_IOC_DEQUEUE_MESSAGE case (vchiq_arm.c:962-1020) of the ioctl handler vchiq_ioctl. It copies the user args and looks the service up with find_service_for_instance: -EINVAL if not found, or if the service is not a VCHI service (is_vchi == 0). Under msg_queue_spinlock, if the message queue is empty: a non-blocking call unlocks and returns -EWOULDBLOCK; a blocking call sets dequeue_pending and loops, dropping the lock and waiting on insert_event (interrupted: -EINTR) until a message arrives. It then takes the header at msg_remove, increments msg_remove, unlocks and ups remove_event. A NULL header gives -ENOTCONN; a header larger than args.bufsize logs, WARNs and gives -EMSGSIZE (the message stays dequeued); otherwise it copies the data to the user buffer when a buffer is given (a failed copy gives -EFAULT and the message is not released), stores the size in args, writes args back and releases the message. The case itself does not call unlock_service: the looked-up service is unlocked by the common code after the switch (vchiq_arm.c:1123-1124, 'if (service) unlock_service(service)'), which runs for every case that set the local service pointer, including the early -EINVAL breaks.

functions.name: queue_message_sync
functions.prose_contract: Sends a message through the single synchronous slot (vchiq_core.c:1007-1110, static, returns VCHIQ_STATUS_T). Unless the message type is VCHIQ_MSG_RESUME it takes state->sync_mutex with lmutex_lock_interruptible and returns VCHIQ_RETRY if that is interrupted; for RESUME it does not take the mutex (the caller is expected to hold it, since the function unlocks it below). It waits for the local sync_release event, reads the sync slot header (logging an error if its msgid is not PADDING) and, if a service is given, copies the elements from user/kernel space into the header data with vchiq_copy_from_user: on a failed copy it unlocks sync_mutex (also for RESUME), increments the service error count and returns VCHIQ_ERROR; on success it updates the service tx statistics. Without a service it memcpy's the single element when size != 0 (with a WARN_ON if count and size are inconsistent). It then sets header->size and msgid, issues a write barrier, signals the remote sync_trigger and unlocks sync_mutex unless the message type is VCHIQ_MSG_PAUSE (for PAUSE the mutex stays locked after a successful return, for RESUME the unlock releases a mutex that this function did not take). It returns VCHIQ_SUCCESS.

functions.name: x86emuOp32_opcFF_word_RM
functions.prose_contract: Static void (x86emu.c:4085-4120) emulating the 32-bit opcode 0xFF group: INC (reg field 0), DEC (1) and PUSH (6) on a 32-bit r/m operand. It does not decode the modrm byte itself (the dispatcher must already have set emu->cur_mod and cur_rh, since this function never calls fetch_decode_modrm). For a memory operand (cur_mod != 3) it computes the address with decode_rl_address and ALWAYS fetches the 32-bit value from memory (fetch_data_long), whatever the reg field is; then for reg 0 it increments the value with inc_long and stores it back, for reg 1 it decrements with dec_long and stores it back, for reg 6 it pushes the value with push_long, and for any other reg value it does nothing further (the memory read still happened). For a register operand (cur_mod == 3) it gets the 32-bit register pointer and does the same three operations in place (inc, dec, push) and nothing for other reg values. Flags are updated by inc_long/dec_long (not read).

functions.name: rcl_byte
functions.prose_contract: Static function (x86emu.c:6703-6767) returning the 8-bit result of rotate-left-through-carry of d by s positions (the slice is the preceding part). It starts with res = d and cnt = s % 9. If cnt is 0 it returns d unchanged and touches no flag. Otherwise it takes the new carry cf as bit (8 - cnt) of d, builds res = (d << cnt) & 0xff, ORs in (d >> (9 - cnt)) masked to cnt-1 bits, and, if the CF flag is currently set, sets bit (cnt - 1) of res. It then sets CF to cf and sets OF only when cnt == 1 (OF = XOR of the new CF and the new top bit; for cnt != 1 OF is cleared by CONDITIONAL_SET_FLAG with a false condition, i.e. it is explicitly written, not left unchanged). SF, ZF, PF and AF are not modified. It returns (uint8_t) res.

functions.name: rol_byte
functions.prose_contract: Static function (x86emu.c:6969-7007) returning the 8-bit result of rotating d left by s positions (s is a count that can be 0 to 8 or larger). It starts with res = d; if cnt = s % 8 is non-zero it computes res = (d << cnt) | ((d >> (8 - cnt)) & ((1 << cnt) - 1)) and sets OF with CONDITIONAL_SET_FLAG(s == 1 && XOR2(...)), i.e. the OF flag is written (cleared unless s == 1 and the XOR condition holds) in that branch only. Then, if s != 0 (not s % 8 != 0) it sets CF from the low bit of res. So for s == 8 (cnt == 0) the value is returned unchanged and OF is left untouched, but CF is still set from bit 0 of d; for s == 0 no flag is modified. Other flags are not touched. It returns (uint8_t) res.

functions.name: xz_dec_bcj_run
functions.prose_contract: Runs the BCJ filter on top of the LZMA2 decoder (xz_dec_bcj.c:417-525, returns enum xz_ret). First, if filtered bytes are pending in the temp buffer it flushes them with bcj_flush; if some remain it returns XZ_OK, and if none remain and the stored result is XZ_STREAM_END it returns XZ_STREAM_END. Then, if the temp buffer fits in the free output space (or is empty), it copies the temp bytes to the output and advances out_pos (without changing s->temp.size at that moment), runs xz_dec_lzma2_run into the output, and returns the lzma2 result immediately if it is neither XZ_STREAM_END nor XZ_OK, or is XZ_OK in single_call mode; in that early return s->temp.size still holds its old value even though those bytes were already copied out. Otherwise it applies bcj_apply to the new output, returns XZ_STREAM_END at the end of stream, saves the unfiltered tail of the output into the temp buffer (sets s->temp.size, moves out_pos back and copies the tail) and returns XZ_OK if the output buffer has room left after that. If output space remains afterwards it decodes into the temp buffer with the output pointers swapped, restores them, returns any error code (not XZ_OK/XZ_STREAM_END), applies bcj_apply to the temp buffer, marks everything filtered at stream end, flushes, and returns XZ_OK if filtered bytes remain. Finally it returns s->ret (XZ_OK or XZ_STREAM_END).

functions.name: xz_dec_microlzma_run
functions.prose_contract: Runs the MicroLZMA decoder (xz_dec_lzma2.c:1215-1291, returns enum xz_ret). If the sequence is not yet SEQ_LZMA_RUN: in SEQ_PROPERTIES it returns XZ_OK when no input is available, returns XZ_DATA_ERROR if lzma_props rejects the (inverted) properties byte, and moves to SEQ_LZMA_PREPARE; then it returns XZ_DATA_ERROR if the compressed size is below RC_INIT_BYTES or above 3U << 30, returns XZ_OK if rc_read_init needs more input, subtracts RC_INIT_BYTES, switches to SEQ_LZMA_RUN and resets the dictionary. In single-call mode it limits dict.end to the free output space. It then loops: it sets the dictionary limit to the smaller of the free output space and the remaining uncompressed size, runs lzma2_lzma (a false result returns XZ_DATA_ERROR), flushes the dictionary and subtracts the flushed bytes from the uncompressed count. When the uncompressed count reaches 0 it returns XZ_STREAM_END, but only when pedantic_microlzma is set does it first require compressed == 0, lzma.len == 0 and a finished range coder (otherwise XZ_DATA_ERROR); without pedantic mode those checks are not made. Otherwise it returns XZ_OK if the output buffer is full or if the input is exhausted while the compressed bytes still needed exceed the temp buffer, else loops again.

functions.name: deflate_rle
functions.prose_contract: Compression strategy for Z_RLE (deflate.c:2086-2151, local block_state). It loops: when lookahead is at most MAX_MATCH it calls fill_window (which may modify s->insert and other window state); after that, if lookahead is still at most MAX_MATCH and flush == Z_NO_FLUSH it returns need_more (so need_more is returned only for Z_NO_FLUSH with insufficient lookahead); if lookahead is 0 it leaves the loop to flush. It sets match_length to 0 and, if lookahead >= MIN_MATCH and strstart > 0, scans the window for a run of the byte before strstart (up to MAX_MATCH, capped at lookahead). A run of at least MIN_MATCH is emitted as a distance-1 match (_tr_tally_dist, advancing strstart and reducing lookahead), otherwise one literal is emitted. When the tally says the block is full it does FLUSH_BLOCK(s, 0), a macro that can itself return need_more or finish_started when the output buffer is full. After the loop it sets s->insert = 0; for Z_FINISH it flushes the final block (FLUSH_BLOCK(s, 1), again possibly returning finish_started) and returns finish_done; otherwise, if there are pending symbols it flushes a block (FLUSH_BLOCK(s, 0)) and returns block_done.

functions.name: fill_window
functions.prose_contract: Local void (deflate.c:252-376) that refills the deflate sliding window from the input. It asserts lookahead < MIN_LOOKAHEAD, then loops (do/while). Each iteration computes the free space 'more' at the end of the window. When strstart has reached at least wsize + MAX_DIST it slides the window: the upper half (wsize - more bytes) is copied down by wsize, match_start, strstart and block_start are reduced by wsize, s->insert is lowered to strstart if it was larger, the hash tables are slid (slide_hash), and more grows by wsize. If strm->avail_in is 0 it leaves the loop; otherwise it reads up to 'more' bytes with read_buf into the window after the lookahead and adds the count to lookahead. If lookahead + insert is at least MIN_MATCH it initialises ins_h from the bytes at strstart - insert and inserts pending hash entries (decrementing s->insert for each one until lookahead + insert falls below MIN_MATCH). The loop repeats while lookahead < MIN_LOOKAHEAD and input remains. After the loop, if high_water < window_size it zeroes memory beyond the data to avoid uninitialised reads: when high_water is below the current data end (curr = strstart + lookahead) it zeroes up to WIN_INIT bytes starting at curr (not at high_water) and sets high_water = curr + that count; otherwise, when high_water is below curr + WIN_INIT, it zeroes from high_water for the missing bytes (bounded by the window size) and advances high_water. It asserts strstart <= window_size - MIN_LOOKAHEAD at the end. Returns void.

functions.name: deflate
functions.prose_contract: Public int ZEXPORT deflate(z_streamp strm, int flush) (deflate.c:981-1290). It returns Z_STREAM_ERROR without setting strm->msg if the stream/state check fails or flush is outside 0..Z_BLOCK. With ERR_RETURN (which sets strm->msg to the error text before returning) it returns Z_STREAM_ERROR for next_out NULL, avail_in != 0 with next_in NULL, or a finished stream called with a flush other than Z_FINISH, and Z_BUF_ERROR if avail_out == 0. It records old_flush, stores the new flush in s->last_flush, and if pending output exists it calls flush_pending: if avail_out is then 0 it sets s->last_flush = -1 (not flush) and returns Z_OK; else if there is no input and the flush level does not exceed the previous one (and is not Z_FINISH) it returns Z_BUF_ERROR; a finished stream with more input also returns Z_BUF_ERROR. It writes the zlib or gzip header (states INIT, GZIP, EXTRA, NAME, COMMENT, HCRC), returning Z_OK with last_flush = -1 whenever flushing the header leaves pending bytes. Then, if there is input, lookahead, or a non-NO_FLUSH request on an unfinished stream, it runs the strategy function (deflate_stored, deflate_huff, deflate_rle or the table function for the level): finish_started/finish_done set the FINISH state; need_more or finish_started return Z_OK (with last_flush = -1 if avail_out is 0); block_done emits the alignment or empty stored block for PARTIAL, SYNC or FULL flush (clearing the hash for Z_FULL_FLUSH), flushes pending and returns Z_OK with last_flush = -1 when avail_out is 0. If flush is not Z_FINISH it returns Z_OK; if the stream has no wrapper (wrap <= 0) it returns Z_STREAM_END; otherwise it writes the gzip or zlib trailer, flushes, makes wrap negative so the trailer is written once, and returns Z_OK if output is still pending, else Z_STREAM_END.

functions.name: inflate
functions.prose_contract: Public int ZEXPORT inflate(z_streamp strm, int flush) (inflate.c:474-1153); this slice covers the early part of it (header, dictionary, stored blocks, dynamic table setup) before the decoding loop. It returns Z_STREAM_ERROR immediately, with no counters updated, if the state check fails, next_out is NULL or next_in is NULL with avail_in != 0. Otherwise it loads the stream into local variables and runs a state machine on state->mode. Header states (HEAD, FLAGS, TIME, OS, EXLEN, EXTRA, NAME, COMMENT, HCRC, DICTID) read the zlib or gzip header; invalid headers, bad window sizes, header checks or flags set the mode to BAD with a message (reported as Z_DATA_ERROR). In the DICT state without a preset dictionary it restores the stream pointers and returns Z_NEED_DICT directly (no counter or check updates). Block states (TYPE, STORED, COPY, TABLE, LENLENS, CODELENS) handle block headers, stored blocks and Huffman table construction, and set BAD on invalid data. Input or output exhaustion (no input, or no output space) and the Z_BLOCK / Z_TREES flush modes jump to inf_leave. The mode MEM returns Z_MEM_ERROR directly and SYNC or an unknown mode returns Z_STREAM_ERROR directly. Normal exits go through inf_leave, which stores the pointers back, updates the window (a failure of updatewindow sets mode MEM and returns Z_MEM_ERROR), updates total_in, total_out, the running check and strm->adler, sets data_type, and turns Z_OK into Z_BUF_ERROR when no progress was made (in == 0 and out == 0) or flush == Z_FINISH. So the return values are Z_OK, Z_STREAM_END, Z_NEED_DICT, Z_DATA_ERROR, Z_MEM_ERROR, Z_BUF_ERROR or Z_STREAM_ERROR. After Z_DATA_ERROR (BAD) or Z_MEM_ERROR (MEM) the stream is in a terminal state and cannot be resumed.

functions.name: inflate
functions.prose_contract: Public int ZEXPORT inflate(z_streamp strm, int flush) (inflate.c:474-1153); this slice covers the middle part: block-table reading and the decoding of codes and copying of matches. Within it a code table or length error sets the mode to BAD (message set, later returned as Z_DATA_ERROR); running out of input or output goes to inf_leave; Z_BLOCK and Z_TREES flush values stop at block boundaries (inf_leave) when requested. Whatever the path, the exits of the whole function are: Z_STREAM_ERROR before any counter update (invalid stream, or the default/SYNC mode), Z_NEED_DICT returned from the DICT state after restoring pointers but before totals and checks are updated, Z_MEM_ERROR returned directly in mode MEM or after a failed updatewindow, and otherwise the normal inf_leave path which updates total_in, total_out, state->total, the check value and adler (only when output was produced and wrap & 4), data_type, and converts a Z_OK without progress (or with flush == Z_FINISH) to Z_BUF_ERROR. Consumed input is not always matched by produced output: header, table and trailer bytes are consumed without producing output.

functions.name: HUF_setMaxHeight
functions.prose_contract: Static U32 (huf_compress.c:376-498) that limits the Huffman code length to targetNbBits. The caller must supply huffNode sorted by decreasing count (so nbBits is non-decreasing along the array, the largest length at lastNonNull). It returns largestBits unchanged and does nothing else if the largest code length is already <= targetNbBits. Otherwise it computes totalCost by clamping every code longer than targetNbBits to targetNbBits (walking down from lastNonNull), converts the cost to units of 2^-targetNbBits, then repays that cost by lengthening (nbBits++) symbols that have fewer bits than the target, chosen by the rankLast table (the rank with the cheapest increase in total count); if the repayment overshoots (totalCost < 0) it shortens some symbols again (nbBits-- on the symbols just after the last rank-1 one). When it finishes the Kraft sum (the sum of 2^-nbBits) is again 1 under the assumption that the input satisfied it, and it returns targetNbBits. The function modifies huffNode[*].nbBits in place; it asserts (debug builds only) divisibility and positivity of totalCost and rank validity, and it does not check the sortedness or the Kraft precondition itself.

functions.name: ZSTD_buildBlockEntropyStats_sequences
functions.prose_contract: Static size_t (zstd_compress.c:3759-3789) that computes the FSE encoding choices for the sequences of a block. It derives nbSeq from the sequence store and splits the workspace: the first (MaxSeq + 1) unsigned values are counts and the remainder, of size wkspSize - (MaxSeq + 1) * sizeof(unsigned), is the entropy workspace; the caller must therefore pass wkspSize of at least that count area (the size_t subtraction would underflow otherwise; the code does not check it). If nbSeq != 0 it calls ZSTD_buildSequencesStatistics (which fills the FSE tables in nextEntropy and writes table headers into fseMetadata->fseTablesBuffer); if nbSeq == 0 it calls ZSTD_buildDummySequencesStatistics(nextEntropy), which only sets the three repeat modes of nextEntropy to FSE_repeat_none and returns set_basic for all three types with size 0 and does not build any FSE table. A non-zero error in stats.size is returned through FORWARD_IF_ERROR before anything is stored in fseMetadata. On success it stores the three symbol encoding types and lastCountSize in fseMetadata and returns stats.size (the number of header bytes written, 0 in the dummy case).

functions.name: ZSTD_compressContinue_internal
functions.prose_contract: Static size_t (zstd_compress.c:4792-4851) that compresses one chunk or block, returning the number of bytes written to dst or an error code. It returns the stage_wrong error if the context stage is ZSTDcs_created (not initialised). If frame is set and the stage is ZSTDcs_init it writes the frame header (error forwarded), advances dst, reduces dstCapacity and sets the stage to ZSTDcs_ongoing; the stage change therefore happens only in that case (not for non-frame calls or after the header was already written). If srcSize == 0 it returns fhSize right away (0 when no header was written), without generating a block and without updating consumedSrcSize or producedCSize. Otherwise it updates the match-state window (and the LDM window when enabled), for non-frame calls runs overflow correction, then compresses with ZSTD_compress_frameChunk (frame) or ZSTD_compressBlock_internal (not frame); an error is forwarded before any counter changes. It then adds srcSize to consumedSrcSize and cSize + fhSize to producedCSize, and, when a source size was pledged, returns the srcSize_wrong error if the consumed size exceeds the pledge. On success it returns cSize + fhSize.

functions.name: ZSTD_compressStream_generic
functions.prose_contract: Static size_t (zstd_compress.c:6103-6287), the newer streaming state machine that supports buffered and stable input/output buffers. Before the loop, in stable input mode it rewinds input->pos and ip by the bytes left unconsumed by the previous call (stableIn_notConsumed) and clears that counter; the other preconditions on the buffers are assertions. Loop on streamStage: zcss_init returns the error init_missing immediately (so an uninitialised stream is handled here by an error, not assumed away); zcss_load either compresses the whole remaining input directly with ZSTD_compressEnd_public when flushMode is ZSTD_e_end and the output has room (or the output buffer mode is stable), sets frameEnded and resets the session, or, in buffered input mode, copies input into the internal buffer (stopping for ZSTD_e_continue when the block is not yet full, or for ZSTD_e_flush when nothing new is buffered), or, in stable input mode, stops for ZSTD_e_continue when fewer than blockSizeMax bytes remain (recording them in stableIn_notConsumed and pretending they were consumed) or for ZSTD_e_flush when the input is empty; it then compresses one block (ZSTD_compressEnd_public for the last block, else ZSTD_compressContinue; errors are forwarded), directly into the output when it has room or in stable output mode, else into the internal buffer followed by the zcss_flush stage, which copies buffered output out, stops when the output is full, and after a full flush either ends the frame (reset session) or returns to zcss_load. On the normal exit it stores the input and output positions and returns 0 when frameEnded is set, else ZSTD_nextInputSizeHint(zcs). Error returns happen before the positions are written back.

functions.name: ZSTD_decompressContinue
functions.prose_contract: Public size_t ZSTD_decompressContinue(ZSTD_DCtx* dctx, void* dst, size_t dstCapacity, const void* src, size_t srcSize) (zstd_decompress.c:1275-1432), the buffer-less streaming decoder step; it returns the number of bytes written to dst (0 for header or checksum steps) or an error code, not a count of bytes consumed. It first returns the srcSize_wrong error, before touching any state (processedCSize is not yet updated), if srcSize is not exactly the size the context expects next. It then checks continuity of dst, adds srcSize to processedCSize, and switches on dctx->stage: getFrameHeaderSize detects a skippable frame (copies the bytes, sets expected and stage decodeSkippableHeader) or reads the frame header size (a header size error is returned, after processedCSize was already increased), copies the bytes and sets stage decodeFrameHeader; decodeFrameHeader parses the header (errors forwarded) and sets expected to the block header size; decodeBlockHeader reads the block size (error if it exceeds the block size maximum; both errors can leave expected/stage as they were or partly changed); an empty block either ends the frame (to the checksum or a new frame header stage) or advances to the next block header; decompressBlock/LastBlock handles compressed, raw and RLE blocks (an invalid block type, a decode error, or a block larger than the maximum returns an error, in some cases after dctx->expected was changed), adds the produced size to decodedSize, updates the checksum, sets previousDstEnd, and returns the produced size; at the last block it checks the frame content size (corruption_detected on mismatch) and moves to checksum or the next frame; checkChecksum compares the stored 32-bit checksum when validating (checksum_wrong on mismatch) and finishes the frame returning 0; decodeSkippableHeader and skipFrame only advance the stage and return 0; an unknown stage returns the GENERIC error.

functions.name: COVER_buildDictionary
functions.prose_contract: Static size_t (cover.c:727-777) that fills a dictionary buffer from the best segments and returns tail, the offset in dictBuffer where the filled region starts (the dictionary occupies dictBuffer[tail .. capacity)). It starts with tail = dictBufferCapacity, computes the epoch layout with COVER_computeEpochs and a limit maxZeroScoreRun = MAX(10, MIN(100, epochs.num >> 3)). It loops epoch by epoch (cycling) while tail > 0: it selects the best segment of the epoch (COVER_selectSegment); a segment with score 0 increments the zero-score run and ends the loop (break) when that run reaches the limit, else moves to the next epoch; a non-zero score resets the run. It sizes the segment as MIN(segment.end - segment.begin + d - 1, tail) and breaks out of the loop if that size is smaller than parameters.d (this includes the case where the remaining tail is smaller than d, not only the case of a short selected segment). Otherwise it subtracts the size from tail and copies the segment from the samples to dict + tail (the buffer is filled from the back). The loop ends when tail reaches 0, when too many consecutive zero-score epochs occur, or when the size is below d, so the returned tail is 0 only when the dictionary was filled completely; in the other two exits it is greater than 0. It prints progress (display level) and returns tail.

functions.name: ss_mintrosort
functions.prose_contract: Static void (divsufsort.c:400-531) that sorts the suffix-array range [first, last) by multikey introsort, comparing the characters T[PA[*x] + depth] starting at the given depth and continuing to deeper characters (it does not stop after the first depth characters). It uses an explicit local stack of pending ranges (STACK_PUSH / STACK_POP) instead of recursion, so subranges of equal characters are re-sorted inside the same call at depth + 1; the function returns (through the STACK_POP macro when the stack is empty) only when all pending ranges have been sorted. Small ranges (<= SS_INSERTIONSORT_THRESHOLD) are finished with ss_insertionsort, a range whose depth-limit counter reaches zero is handled with ss_heapsort, and otherwise a pivot is chosen with ss_pivot, the range is three-way partitioned around the pivot character, and the less-than, equal (next depth) and greater-than parts are pushed or processed. Elements of the range of PA indices are permuted in place (the sort moves entries of the range; T and PA are only read). It returns nothing and has no failure result.

functions.name: HUF_readStats
functions.prose_contract: Static size_t (zstd_v02.c:1481-1557) reading a Huffman weight table header. It returns ERROR(srcSize_wrong) for empty input. The first byte iSize selects the format: >= 242 is an RLE header (oSize from a 14-entry table, all hwSize bytes of huffWeight set to 1, iSize = 0, with no check that oSize is smaller than hwSize); 128..241 is an uncompressed 4-bit header (oSize = iSize - 127; returns srcSize_wrong if the packed bytes do not fit in srcSize and corruption_detected if oSize >= hwSize, then unpacks the nibbles); below 128 the weights are FSE-compressed: srcSize_wrong if iSize + 1 > srcSize, otherwise FSE_decompress into at most hwSize - 1 weights (an FSE error is returned as is). It then zeroes rankStats, counts the weights and sums weightTotal = sum of (1 << w) >> 1, returning corruption_detected if any weight is >= HUF_ABSOLUTEMAX_TABLELOG, if weightTotal is 0, or if the derived tableLog (highbit(weightTotal) + 1) exceeds HUF_ABSOLUTEMAX_TABLELOG. It then derives the implied last weight from rest = 2^tableLog - weightTotal: corruption_detected unless rest itself is a power of two (it is the remaining total rest, not weightTotal, that must be a power of two); the last weight is stored at huffWeight[oSize] and counted. Finally corruption_detected unless rankStats[1] is at least 2 and even. On success it sets *nbSymbolsPtr = oSize + 1 and *tableLogPtr = tableLog and returns iSize + 1, the number of header bytes consumed.

functions.name: HUF_decompress4X2
functions.prose_contract: Static size_t (zstd_v02.c:1752-1763) wrapper that decodes a 4-stream single-symbol Huffman block. It builds a decoding table on the stack with HUF_readDTableX2 from the start of cSrc and returns that call's error if it fails; the non-error result is the number of header bytes consumed. If the header consumed cSrcSize bytes or more it returns ERROR(srcSize_wrong) (so this error can be returned before the size check inside the callee). Otherwise it skips the header and returns HUF_decompress4X2_usingDTable(dst, dstSize, ip, cSrcSize - header, DTable). That callee (zstd_v02.c:1656-1750) returns corruption_detected if the remaining input is smaller than 10 bytes (a jump table plus one byte per stream), returns any error of the four BIT_initDStream calls, returns corruption_detected on overflow of the fourth stream length, on stream pointers crossing their segments, or when the bit streams are not fully consumed at the end, and otherwise returns dstSize (all dstSize bytes decoded).

functions.name: HUF_decompress4X6_usingDTable
functions.prose_contract: Static size_t (zstd_v02.c:2373-2468) decoding a 4-stream quad-symbol Huffman block with a prepared table. It returns ERROR(corruption_detected) if cSrcSize < 10 (jump table plus one byte per stream). It reads the three 16-bit stream lengths from the jump table, derives the fourth length as cSrcSize - (length1 + length2 + length3 + 6) and returns corruption_detected if that wrapped around. It initialises the four bit streams with BIT_initDStream and returns that call's error code as is (not forced to corruption_detected; for example srcSize_wrong is possible). Four streams are decoded in an interleaved loop while all streams are unfinished and the output position is far enough from the end; then it returns corruption_detected if any of the first three output pointers passed the start of the next segment, finishes the tails with the per-stream decoders and returns corruption_detected unless all four streams ended exactly at their end; otherwise it returns dstSize.

functions.name: BIT_reloadDStream
functions.prose_contract: MEM_STATIC BIT_DStream_status (zstd_v03.c:404-434) that refills the bit container of a backward bit stream and reports its status. If bitsConsumed exceeds the container width in bits it returns BIT_DStream_overflow immediately, without refilling. If ptr is at least one container width above start, it moves ptr back by the whole consumed bytes, keeps the remaining bit count (bitsConsumed &= 7), reloads the container from memory and returns BIT_DStream_unfinished. Otherwise, if ptr == start it returns BIT_DStream_endOfBuffer when fewer than a full container of bits was consumed, else BIT_DStream_completed, again without refilling. In the remaining case (ptr strictly between start and start + container size) it computes nbBytes = bitsConsumed >> 3; if ptr - nbBytes would go below start it limits nbBytes to ptr - start and the result becomes BIT_DStream_endOfBuffer; when ptr - nbBytes equals start exactly the result stays BIT_DStream_unfinished. It then moves ptr back by nbBytes, reduces bitsConsumed by nbBytes * 8, reloads the container and returns the result. So the container is refilled only in the unfinished/short-buffer paths, not in the overflow, completed, or ptr == start returns.

functions.name: ZBUFFv05_decompressContinue
functions.prose_contract: Buffered streaming decompression step (zstd_v05.c:3842-3994, returns size_t: a size hint or an error). In/out parameters *srcSizePtr and *maxDstSizePtr are the available input and output on entry and the consumed and produced bytes on a normal exit (written at 3986-3987); they are NOT updated on the early returns. It loops over zbc->stage: ZBUFFv05ds_init returns ERROR(init_missing); readHeader calls ZSTDv05_getFrameParams on the input (error returned), and if the header is not complete it copies the input bytes into headerBuffer, sets stage loadHeader and returns headerSize - hPos without writing any output and without updating *srcSizePtr; loadHeader appends more input to the header buffer and, if the header is still incomplete, returns the remaining count with the stage unchanged (loadHeader) and *srcSizePtr not updated; once the header is complete decodeHeader allocates the input and output buffers (ERROR(memory_allocation) on failure), copies any buffered header bytes into the input buffer and goes to load, else to read; read gets the next needed input size (0 means end of frame: stage back to init and exit the loop), decodes directly from the caller's input when enough is available (error returned), or switches to load; load fills the input buffer (corruption_detected if the request does not fit), exits the loop to wait for more input when it has too little, and decodes (a zero decoded size means a header only); flush copies decoded bytes to the output and either returns to read or exits the loop when the output is full; an unknown stage returns ERROR(GENERIC). On loop exit it stores the consumed and produced sizes and returns the next input size hint (including the block header size, minus the bytes already loaded).

functions.name: HUFv06_readStats
functions.prose_contract: MEM_STATIC size_t (zstd_v06.c:1798-1865) with the same structure as the v02 HUF_readStats: it returns ERROR(srcSize_wrong) for empty input; reads iSize from the first byte; for iSize >= 242 it uses an RLE header (oSize from a 14-entry table, all hwSize bytes of huffWeight set to 1, iSize = 0, no check of oSize against hwSize); for 128..241 an uncompressed 4-bit header (srcSize_wrong if the packed bytes do not fit, corruption_detected if oSize >= hwSize); below 128 an FSE-compressed header (srcSize_wrong if iSize + 1 > srcSize, otherwise FSEv06_decompress into at most hwSize - 1 weights, an FSE error being returned). It zeroes rankStats, accumulates the counts and weightTotal, returning corruption_detected for a weight >= HUFv06_ABSOLUTEMAX_TABLELOG, for weightTotal == 0 and for tableLog above the maximum. It writes *tableLogPtr = tableLog at that point, before the remaining checks, so the output is written even when a later check fails. It then requires the remaining total rest = 2^tableLog - weightTotal to be a power of two (corruption_detected otherwise, it is rest and not weightTotal that is tested), stores the implied last weight at huffWeight[oSize] and counts it, and returns corruption_detected unless rankStats[1] is at least 2 and even. On success it sets *nbSymbolsPtr = oSize + 1 and returns iSize + 1 (the header bytes consumed).

functions.name: ZSTDv07_decodeSeqHeaders
functions.prose_contract: Static size_t (zstd_v07.c:3393-3441) that decodes the sequences section header: the sequence count and the three FSE table descriptions. It returns ERROR(srcSize_wrong) if srcSize < MIN_SEQUENCES_SIZE. It reads the first byte as the sequence count: 0 stores *nbSeqPtr = 0 and returns 1 at once; 1..127 is the count itself; 128..254 uses a second byte, and 255 uses a 16-bit value plus LONGNBSEQ (srcSize_wrong if those extra bytes are missing). *nbSeqPtr is written before the later checks, so it is set even if an error follows. It then requires four more bytes (srcSize_wrong otherwise), reads the three 2-bit table types, and builds the literal-length, offset and match-length decoding tables with ZSTDv07_buildSeqTable; any error from a table build is converted to ERROR(corruption_detected) (the original error is not returned). On success it returns the number of header bytes consumed (ip - istart), which is 1 for a zero count and at least 2 otherwise (count byte plus the type byte when all three tables are RAW/RLE-free, i.e. no table bytes), not at least 4.

functions.name: ZSTDv07_execSequence
functions.prose_contract: size_t (zstd_v07.c:3534-3609) that executes one decoded sequence (copies litLength literals, then matchLength bytes of match) at op, returning the sequence length litLength + matchLength on success or an error code. Checks before any copy: ERROR(dstSize_tooSmall) if the literal length plus WILDCOPY_OVERLENGTH does not fit in the remaining output, or if litLength + matchLength does not fit; ERROR(corruption_detected) if litLength exceeds the remaining literal buffer (litLimit - *litPtr). It then wild-copies the literals, advances op and *litPtr (so on a later error *litPtr has already been advanced and the literals already written). If the match offset reaches before the current prefix (offset > oLitEnd - base) it returns corruption_detected unless the match lies in the dictionary segment (offset <= oLitEnd - vBase); a match entirely inside the dictionary is copied with memmove and returned; a match crossing from the dictionary into the prefix copies the first part, then continues with the rest (byte by byte near the end of the buffer or when the remainder is shorter than MINMATCH). For a normal in-prefix match it copies the first 8 bytes using the dec32/dec64 tables for offsets below 8 (overlapping copy), then either copies the rest byte by byte up to oMatchEnd when close to the buffer end (using wildcopy while it is still safe), or uses ZSTDv07_wildcopy for the remainder. In all success paths it returns the sequence length (litLength + matchLength) and leaves op conceptually at oMatchEnd (op is a local copy; the caller advances its own pointer by the returned length).

functions.name: ZSTDv07_decompressContinue
functions.prose_contract: Public size_t ZSTDv07_decompressContinue(ZSTDv07_DCtx* dctx, void* dst, size_t dstCapacity, const void* src, size_t srcSize) (zstd_v07.c:3933-4029), the buffer-less streaming step; it returns the number of bytes written to dst (0 for header steps) or an error code. It returns ERROR(srcSize_wrong) at once, with no state change, if srcSize differs from dctx->expected; if dstCapacity is non-zero it checks continuity. By stage: getFrameHeaderSize (srcSize_wrong if not the minimal header size) detects a skippable-frame magic (copy, stage decodeSkippableHeader) or computes the full header size (error returned), and goes to decodeFrameHeader unless the minimal header is already complete (then it falls through with expected 0); decodeFrameHeader copies the rest of the header, decodes it (error returned) and sets expected to the block header size; decodeBlockHeader reads the block size (error returned); for an end block it checks the 22-bit checksum if the frame has one (checksum_wrong on mismatch), sets expected = 0 and stage getFrameHeaderSize; otherwise it records the block type and size and moves to decompressBlock; decompressBlock handles compressed and raw blocks; an RLE block or an unknown type returns ERROR(GENERIC) BEFORE the stage and expected are reset, so those two paths leave the stage as decompressBlock; for the compressed and raw paths the stage is set back to decodeBlockHeader and expected to the block header size BEFORE the error check of rSize, so a decode error returns an error with the stage and expected already reset (they are not left unchanged). On success it updates previousDstEnd, the checksum and returns rSize. The skippable stages only advance the stage and return 0; an unknown stage returns ERROR(GENERIC).

functions.name: BMK_benchMemAdvancedNoAlloc
functions.prose_contract: Static BMK_benchOutcome_t (benchzstd.c:410-777; the packet name BMK_benchMemAdvanced_Internal does not exist and the slice is the middle and tail of this function, ending where BMK_benchMemAdvanced starts at 779). It benchmarks compression and decompression of a set of blocks with caller-provided buffers and returns a BMK_benchOutcome_t that is either an error outcome or a valid result. In decode-only mode it first sums the decompressed size of every file (frame content sizes): an unknown or erroneous content size, a size_t overflow, or a failed allocation of the result buffer returns an error outcome through RETURN_ERROR (the result buffer is freed and replaced first). It then splits the source into blocks, prepares the per-block sizes, and, when multi-threaded measurements are unsupported but several workers were requested, adjusts the worker count. It repeats compression and decompression runs until both are completed, keeping the best speeds: a failed run returns an error outcome ('compression error' / 'decompression error'). After the runs, in compress-and-decompress mode it compares a checksum of the decompressed data with the original and, on mismatch, searches for the first differing byte and prints diagnostic context (this path is reported but is not turned into an error outcome in the part of the code that I read). It prints the result line depending on the display level and returns BMK_benchOutcome_setValidResult(benchResult).

functions.name: z_inflateReset
functions.prose_contract: Wrapper for inflateReset (zstd_zlibwrapper.c:663-674, ZEXTERN int ZEXPORT z_inflateReset). It logs, and if the wrapper is forced to use zlib (g_ZWRAPdecompressionType == ZWRAP_FORCE_ZLIB) or the stream is not a zstd-wrapped stream (!strm->reserved) it simply returns zlib's inflateReset(strm) (so it does fall back to the zlib reset in those cases). Otherwise it calls ZWRAP_inflateReset_keepDict(strm) and returns its error code if that is not Z_OK; in the zstd branch that helper (lines 641-658) returns Z_STREAM_ERROR if the state pointer is NULL, otherwise re-initialises the ZWRAP decompression context, sets its state to ZWRAP_useReset, zeroes totalInBytes, total_in and total_out and returns Z_OK; it does not call inflateReset itself in this branch, so inflateReset's error cannot be returned from the zstd branch. After the helper succeeds it fetches the state again (returning Z_STREAM_ERROR if NULL, though the helper already checked) and sets decompState to ZWRAP_useInit, then returns Z_OK.

functions.name: db_command
functions.prose_contract: Static void (db_command.c:378-526) that parses and runs one ddb command line. The first token decides: tEOL repeats *last_cmdp with address db_next, no address and count 1; tEXCL runs db_fncall and returns; any non-identifier token prints 'Unrecognized input' and flushes the line. For an identifier it searches cmd_table (then sub-tables via cmd->more): no match prints 'No such command', an ambiguous name prints 'Ambiguous', and help prints the help text; each of these flushes the lexer and returns without executing; if a table has subcommands and the next token is not an identifier it prints a hint and returns. The loop is skipped when cmd_table is NULL, in which case cmd stays NULL and the code after the loop dereferences cmd->flag (a NULL cmd_table with an identifier token would crash), so a non-NULL cmd_table is needed. For commands without CS_OWN it parses '[/modifier] [addr] [,count]': a bad modifier returns; when an address expression parses, db_dot and db_last_addr are set to it immediately (so a later parse failure such as 'Count missing', which flushes and returns, leaves db_dot and db_last_addr already modified); count defaults to -1; unless CS_MORE it skips to end of line. After parsing it sets *last_cmdp = cmd (only on this path; the early returns above do not update it), optionally lets MAC veto the command (prints a message and returns), enables or disables the pager according to dopager, calls (*cmd->fcn)(addr, have_addr, count, modif) when cmd is non-NULL, and finally sets db_dot from db_prev or db_next for CS_SET_DOT commands, else db_next = db_dot.

functions.name: db_check_interrupt
functions.prose_contract: Void function (db_input.c:419-458) that polls the console for pending input during ddb output. It loops: if ddb_prioritize_control_input is false and the raw input buffer has no space (db_raw_space() false) it returns immediately without reading; otherwise it reads one character with cncheckc(): -1 (no character) returns; Ctrl-C calls db_do_interrupt('^C'); Ctrl-S enters a wait loop that keeps calling cncheckc() until it returns Ctrl-Q (a Ctrl-C in that loop also calls db_do_interrupt; a return value of -1 does not leave the loop, it just polls again, so this loop can only be left by Ctrl-Q or by db_do_interrupt); any other character is pushed into the raw buffer with db_raw_push if there is space, else it is dropped and a one-time '--Exceeded input buffer--' message is printed (db_raw_warned). So when the raw buffer is full the pending characters are not all buffered: control characters are processed (if prioritising) and other characters are discarded.

functions.name: db_stop_at_pc
functions.prose_contract: bool function (db_run.c:71-189) deciding whether the debugger should stop at a trap. It first sets *is_breakpoint and *is_watchpoint from the trap type/code (IS_BREAKPOINT_TRAP / IS_WATCHPOINT_TRAP), reads pc, clears single-step, breakpoints and watchpoints, and (where defined) fixes the pc after a breakpoint trap. It looks up a debugger breakpoint at pc: if one exists, it decrements its count; when the count reaches 0 it resets the count to init_count, sets *is_breakpoint = true and returns true; otherwise it returns false (the countdown continues) with *is_breakpoint left at its initial trap classification value (it is not cleared on this path). If no breakpoint is registered at pc and the trap looked like a breakpoint, BKPT_SKIP is applied when defined. In every other path *is_breakpoint is then set to false ('might be a breakpoint, but not ours'). Then, where IS_SSTEP_TRAP is defined: STEP_CONTINUE with a single-step trap returns false, and a non-continue run mode without a single-step trap prints 'Stepping aborted' and returns true. By run mode: STEP_INVISIBLE sets STEP_CONTINUE and returns false; STEP_COUNT returns false; STEP_ONCE returns false (optionally printing the location) while db_loop_count stays above zero after decrement; STEP_RETURN returns false until a return or trap-return instruction (tracking call depth); STEP_CALLT returns false unless the instruction at pc is a call, return or trap return. Otherwise it returns true. It has side effects on the debugger run-mode, loop count, call depth and the breakpoint list.

functions.name: aac_map_command_sg
functions.prose_contract: Static bus_dmamap callback (aac.c:1549-1636; the slice cut the head, and the packet name aac_map_command does not exist) that finishes setting up a command once its data is mapped. The error argument is ignored. If cm->cm_sgtable is non-NULL it fills the scatter/gather table from segs according to the FIB command type: for RawIo it sets SgCount = nseg and writes address and byte count with Next, Prev and Flags zeroed, for non-64-bit controllers it fills the 32-bit table, otherwise the 64-bit table; in each case it then increases fib->Header.Size by nseg times the entry size (the table must have room for nseg entries, no bound is checked here). It then sets Header.SenderFibAddress = cm_index << 2, ReceiverFibAddress = low 32 bits of cm_fibphys and SenderData = cm_index, performs PREREAD and/or PREWRITE bus_dmamap_sync according to cm_flags, and sets AAC_CMD_MAPPED. With AAC_FLAGS_NEW_COMM it loops calling AAC_SEND_COMMAND until it returns 0, waiting DELAY(5) per attempt; when the retry counter (10,000,000) reaches 0 it unmaps the command, sets AAC_QUEUE_FRZN and requeues the command to the ready queue, but the loop has no exit at that point, so it keeps trying to send (the counter continues to decrease). Otherwise it enqueues the FIB on cm_queue; if aac_enqueue_fib returns EBUSY it unmaps the command, sets AAC_QUEUE_FRZN and requeues it. It returns nothing.

functions.name: aac_container_special_command
functions.prose_contract: Static void (aacraid_cam.c:502-837; the packet name aac_cam_action is the caller, the slice is the middle of aac_container_special_command) that answers SCSI commands for a container (logical drive) directly in the driver. It asserts aac_io_lock is held, looks the container up by target id; if it is missing or the LUN is not 0 it sets CAM_DEV_NOT_THERE, calls xpt_done and returns. Then, by SCSI opcode (cmdp): INQUIRY builds standard inquiry data (or the supported-pages and serial number VPD pages; an unsupported page code sets a check-condition error through aac_set_scsi_error, calls xpt_done and returns); REPORT_LUNS, TEST_UNIT_READY, REQUEST_SENSE, READ_CAPACITY, SERVICE_ACTION_IN, MODE_SENSE_6 and SYNCHRONIZE_CACHE fill in the data and set CAM_REQ_CMP (errors for an unsupported service action or mode page set a check condition and return after xpt_done); START_STOP with power management support allocates a command: if allocation fails it freezes the SIM queue, sets CAM_RESRC_UNAVAIL, and queues an AAC_EVENT_CMFREE event (aac_cam_event) and returns without xpt_done (the ccb is completed later by the event), and if the event allocation fails it prints a warning and returns without xpt_done or a queued event; otherwise it builds a container-config FIB (start or stop unit) and waits for it with aacraid_wait_command; and finally CAM_REQ_CMP; unknown opcodes also get CAM_REQ_CMP (the CAM_REQ_INVALID alternative is commented out). Paths that fall out of the switch call xpt_done(ccb) once at the end.

functions.name: acpi_fujitsu_update
functions.prose_contract: Static int (acpi_fujitsu.c:649-758) refreshing the cached Fujitsu hotkey state. It asserts the driver serial lock. If the 'gsif' method exists it computes changed = gsif.value & acpi_fujitsu_method_get(GHKS), else 0. For each of gvol (volume), gmou (pointer), gbls (P8XXX brightness) and gbll (brightness) that exists, it reads the current value with acpi_GetInteger; a failed query prints a message and returns FALSE immediately (the later features are not refreshed and lastValChanged is not updated). Only when the matching changed bit is set does it process the value: volume updates bIsMuted, keeps the setting bits and notifies FN_MUTE or FN_VOLUME with a log line (the volume value is not written back with acpi_fujitsu_method_set); pointer updates bIntPtrEnabled, masks the value, writes it back with acpi_fujitsu_method_set(METHOD_GMOU) and notifies FN_POINTER_ENABLE; P8XXX brightness masks the value, writes it back with method_set(METHOD_GBLS) and notifies FN_LCD_BRIGHTNESS; brightness (gbll) masks the value and notifies FN_LCD_BRIGHTNESS (no write-back). The cached value fields are overwritten by the query for every feature that exists, but the masking and write-back happen only when changed. At the end it stores lastValChanged = changed and returns TRUE.

functions.name: acpi_hp_sysctl_set
functions.prose_contract: Static int (acpi_hp.c:776-848) applying a sysctl write for the HP laptop driver; it returns 0 on success and -EINVAL when a WMI command fails. It asserts the serial lock. For every method except CMI_DETAIL and VERBOSE it first normalises arg to 0 or 1. Nothing is done (and 0 is returned) when arg equals oldarg. Otherwise by method: WLAN_ENABLED, BLUETOOTH_ENABLED and WWAN_ENABLED send a WMI wireless command (acpi_hp_exec_wmi_command with the enable/disable code for that radio), and return -EINVAL if the command returns non-zero (so these three *_ENABLED methods are written to the hardware, not read-only); ALS sends the ambient-light-sensor WMI command (-EINVAL on failure); the *_ENABLE_IF_RADIO_ON and *_DISABLE_IF_RADIO_OFF methods store the flag in the softc and call acpi_hp_evaluate_auto_on_off; CMI_DETAIL stores the value and resets cmi_order_size to -1 if the SHOW_MAX_INSTANCE bit changed; VERBOSE stores the value. A method code not listed does nothing. Because there is no default case, a read-only or unknown method with arg != oldarg stores nothing, issues no WMI command, and still returns 0.

functions.name: EcSpaceHandler
functions.prose_contract: ACPI operation-region handler for the Embedded Controller (acpi_ec.c:772-843, returns ACPI_STATUS). It returns AE_BAD_PARAMETER if Function is neither ACPI_READ nor ACPI_WRITE, or if Width is not a multiple of 8, Value is NULL or Context is NULL; it returns AE_BAD_ADDRESS if Address + Width / 8 exceeds 256. A Width of 0 passes these checks (the do/while loop then still performs one single-byte transfer). When cold, rebooting or suspending it may run the EC query handler directly if the SCI bit is set and no query is pending. It then takes the EC lock (EcLock; a failure is returned), tries to enable burst mode (a failure is ignored; the burst flag is set only if the data register returns the burst ack), sets *Value = 0 for reads, and transfers byte by byte over Width / 8 addresses (at least one byte): EcRead into the value buffer or EcWrite from it, stopping at the first failing status. It then disables burst mode if it was active, unlocks and returns the status of the last transfer (the failing one, or the last success).

functions.name: acpi_pwr_switch_consumer
functions.prose_contract: Switches a power consumer to ACPI D-state `state` (acpi_powerres.c:295-513, returns ACPI_STATUS). It returns AE_NOT_FOUND for a NULL consumer. With the powerres serial lock held it finds or registers the consumer (a registration failure goes to out with that status; a missing consumer after registering panics). If the consumer is already in `state` it returns AE_OK. It returns AE_BAD_PARAMETER (via out) when the current state is D3hot and the request is neither D0 nor D3cold, when the current state is D3cold and the request is neither D0 nor D3hot, and for a state value that is not D0..D3cold. Method and resource list names are _PS0/_PR0 ... _PS3/_PR3 (D3cold uses _PS3 and no resource list). If neither the method nor the resource list exists: for D0 it records D0 and returns AE_OK; a D3cold request is converted to D3hot; any state other than D3hot then goes to out with the status left at AE_BAD_PARAMETER; for D3hot it needs _PR0: without _PR0 it returns AE_NOT_FOUND, if _PR0 cannot be evaluated it returns that error, and a _PR0 that is not a valid package gives AE_TYPE; a valid _PR0 is evaluated only to validate it and freed. If a resource list exists it is evaluated (an evaluation error or a non-package type, AE_TYPE, returns). It then dereferences the old resources, references the new list, and calls acpi_pwr_switch_power (a failure is returned). If a _PSx method exists it is evaluated; on failure the recorded state becomes ACPI_STATE_UNKNOWN and the error is returned. On success it records the state, which for a requested D3cold with no _PS3 and no _PR3 is D3hot (converted at 393-394), not the requested state, and returns AE_OK. The lock is released and the evaluated buffer freed on all paths after the lock was taken.

functions.name: abtn_receive_packet
functions.prose_contract: ADB receive callback for the hotkey device (adb_buttons.c:109-156, returns u_int, always 0 by its single return). It reads the first data byte (data[0] is read without checking len, so the caller must supply at least one byte) as cmd and switches on it: 0x0a sends a devctl 'brightness notify=down'; 0x09 sends 'brightness notify=up'; 0x08 and 0x01 send 'mute'; 0x07 and 0x02 send 'volume notify=down'; 0x06 and 0x03 send 'volume notify=up'; 0x0b sends 'eject'; 0x0c (mirror display) and 0x7f (numlock) do nothing; any other value does nothing unless DEBUG is defined, in which case a value with the high bit clear prints 'unknown ADB button 0x%x'. The status, command, reg and len arguments are not used. It returns 0 in all cases.

functions.name: adlink_ioctl
functions.prose_contract: Character device ioctl handler (adlink.c:193-360, returns int). It reads the argument u = *(u_int *)data (data is dereferenced for every command) and switches on cmd. SETDIVISOR returns EBUSY if running, EINVAL if u is odd, else stores the divisor. SETCHUNKSIZE returns EBUSY unless the state is RESET, EINVAL if u is not a multiple of PAGE_SIZE, and EINVAL if ringsize != 0 and ringsize % u is non-zero; for u == 0 the test 'u % PAGE_SIZE' passes and 'ringsize % u' with a non-zero ringsize divides by zero (not guarded); otherwise it stores chunksize. SETRINGSIZE returns EBUSY unless RESET, EINVAL if u is not page-multiple or chunksize != 0 and u % chunksize is non-zero, else stores ringsize. START returns EBUSY if running; if the state is RESET it applies defaults (chunksize 4 pages, ringsize 16 chunks, divisor 4), computes nchunks and returns EINVAL if nchunks is 0 or if the generation array plus the page-0 header would not fit in one page (nchunks * sizeof(sample) + sizeof(*p0) > PAGE_SIZE); it then allocates the chunk descriptor array (M_WAITOK) and a contiguous buffer for each chunk, linking them in a ring. For any state other than RUN it clears all sample generation words, programs the device registers, sets the state to RUN, loads the first chunk address and size and starts the hardware, then returns 0. STOP does nothing if the state is RESET, otherwise sets state = EINTR and sleeps in a loop (tsleep) until the generation word of the next chunk becomes non-zero. Any other command returns ENOIOCTL. So the possible returns are 0, EBUSY, EINVAL and ENOIOCTL (plus the possible trap on the zero divisor).

functions.name: ahci_timeout
functions.prose_contract: Callout handler for a command timeout on one AHCI slot (ahci.c:1856-1932, void). It returns at once if the slot is below AHCI_SLOT_RUNNING. If the slot is RUNNING but not yet EXECUTING it reads the port's SACT and current command slot: if the slot's bit is set in SACT, or it is the current command slot, or FBS is enabled, or wrongccs is already set, it marks the slot EXECUTING; else if the current slot is not one of our running slots it sets ch->wrongccs and marks it EXECUTING; then it re-arms the callout for half of the ccb timeout (ahci_timeout again) and returns. Otherwise (a real timeout) it prints diagnostics. If a frozen ccb exists it takes it, sets its status to CAM_REQUEUE_REQ | CAM_RELEASE_SIMQ (this assignment overwrites any earlier status bits), then, because CAM_DEV_QFRZN is never set at that point, it always freezes the device queue and sets CAM_DEV_QFRZN, and completes the ccb with ahci_done (so the queue freeze is unconditional, not conditional on the old status). Then if FBS is not enabled and wrongccs is not set it takes the single-command path: it sets fatalerr, ends the timed-out slot's transaction with AHCI_ERR_TIMEOUT and ends every other running slot with AHCI_ERR_INNOCENT; otherwise (FBS enabled, or wrongccs set even without FBS) it freezes the SIM queue the first time, adds the slot to toslots, calls ahci_process_timeout if no other running slots remain outside toslots, else prints that it is waiting for the remaining slots (the slot is not ended immediately on this path).

functions.name: ahd_handle_scsiint
functions.prose_contract: SCSI interrupt handler for the AIC79xx (aic79xx.c:1523-1792, void; the slice cut the head). It selects SCSI mode, reads SSTAT0/1/3, LQISTAT1, LQOSTAT0 and SSTAT2, masks the selection bits with SIMODE0, finds the current SCB (NULL if the sequencer reports NOT_IDENTIFIED), then handles exactly one condition in this priority order (an else-if chain): IOERR (transceiver mode change: clears it, resets channel A, re-runs the iocell workaround with pause/unpause); OVERRUN (message, correctable-error accounting, channel reset); SCSIRSTI (message, reset channel without initiating, uncorrectable-error accounting); SCSIPERR (clears the critical section, ahd_handle_transmission_error); lqostat0 non-zero (prints it and only clears the LQO interrupt bits, with no pause/unpause or restart); SELTO (stops selection, clears message and interrupt state, finds the waiting SCB, marks it CAM_SEL_TIMEOUT and runs ahd_handle_devreset, or reports an uncorrectable error if there is no SCB; then clears the SCSI interrupt, re-initialises the iocell and unpauses); SELDI/SELDO (iocell first selection, unpause); status3 non-zero (prints a cell parity error, counts a correctable error with AHD_CORRECTABLE_ERROR, and clears the status bits, with no unpause); LQI phase errors (clear critical section, ahd_handle_lqiphase_error); LQICRCI_NLQ (only clears that interrupt bit); BUSFREE or LQOBUSFREE (clears selection, decides whether the busfree was packetized, calls ahd_handle_pkt_busfree or ahd_handle_nonpkt_busfree, clears the busfree status, optionally the FIFO and message state and the SCSI interrupt, then restarts the sequencer if the handler said so, else unpauses); if none of the conditions matches it prints 'Missing case', dumps the card state, clears the interrupt status and unpauses. Only some branches restart, reset or unpause the controller; the lqostat0, status3 and LQICRCI_NLQ branches only clear status.

functions.name: ahd_handle_nonpkt_busfree
functions.prose_contract: Handles a non-packetized bus free (aic79xx.c:2164-2435, returns int; the slice cut the head). It reads the last phase and the saved SCSI id and LUN, builds the initiator devinfo, finds the current SCB (NULL if NOT_IDENTIFIED), and sets printerror = 1. If the last phase was MESGOUT it checks which message was just sent: an abort/abort-tag message aborts the SCB(s) (and returns 1 early, restarting the sequencer, when there is no SCB); a bus-device-reset message runs ahd_handle_devreset; a sent PPR, WDR or SDTR message reverts or applies transfer settings (ahd_set_width / ahd_set_syncrate) as appropriate; expected IDE or QAS-reject busfree flags are recognised; each handled case clears printerror. If printerror is still set, the last phase was a message phase and a PPR busfree was expected, it freezes the devq, marks the SCB CAM_REQUEUE_REQ and freezes it, then either aborts the SCBs of that target (when the IU requirement changed) or calls ahd_done(ahd, scb) on this SCB (so ahd_done can be called here), and clears printerror. If printerror is still set, it prints the unexpected-busfree report, aborts the SCBs for the target when an SCB was identified (CAM_UNEXP_BUSFREE), counts an uncorrectable error, dumps the card state and, unless the last phase was P_BUSFREE, forces renegotiation. The function has no return 0: every path, including the early one, returns 1 (restart the sequencer).

functions.name: ahd_init
functions.prose_contract: Initialises an AIC79xx controller (aic79xx.c:6225-6464, returns int; the slice is its middle and tail). It probes the stack size and mallocs saved_stack, returning ENOMEM if that fails. It then builds the DMA resources in stages, each stage incrementing ahd->init_level only after that stage succeeded: the buffer DMA tag (ENOMEM on failure, init_level unchanged), the shared-data tag (ENOMEM on failure), the shared-data memory allocation (ENOMEM on failure); after mapping the shared memory it sets up the queued hscb and increments init_level, and then ahd_init_scbdata is called AFTER that increment (so on its failure, which returns ENOMEM, init_level has already been counted for the previous stage). It then clears AHD_RESET_BUS_A if the initiator role is off, calls ahd_platform_init and ahd_chip_init, and, if AHD_CURRENT_SENSING is set, probes the termination current-sensing through the flexport registers; any timeout in that probe prints a message and jumps to init_done (it is not an error return). At init_done it calls ahd_restart, restarts the statistics timer and returns 0. So the only error returns are ENOMEM from the allocation steps; everything after ahd_init_scbdata returns 0.

functions.name: ahd_action
functions.prose_contract: CAM SIM action entry point (aic79xx_osm.c:462-728, void; the slice is the middle of it). It finds the softc from the sim and dispatches on ccb->ccb_h.func_code. With AHD_TARGET_MODE: XPT_ACCEPT_TARGET_IO is queued on the LUN's accept_tios list (status CAM_REQ_INPROG, no xpt_done here) and the target queue FIFO is run if it was blocked; XPT_CONT_TARGET_IO is not queued but turned into an SCB: if the target device lookup fails it is routed to the black-hole LUN, and the common SCB-setup code below then runs (fall-through) with our_id and target_id swapped. XPT_SCSI_IO, XPT_RESET_DEV and the continued target I/O share the SCB path: when the initiator role is off it completes the ccb with an error (xpt_done, return); it fetches an SCB, and if none is available it sets the status to resource-unavailable, freezes the queue as needed, calls xpt_done and returns; otherwise it fills the SCB (reset-device message, tag/disconnect flags, target-mode status flags) and hands it on for DMA setup and execution (error from the mapping completes the ccb via xpt_done). XPT_EN_LUN is completed immediately through xpt_done. XPT_ABORT, XPT_SET_TRAN_SETTINGS, XPT_GET_TRAN_SETTINGS, XPT_CALC_GEOMETRY, XPT_RESET_BUS, XPT_TERM_IO and XPT_PATH_INQ fill in their results and complete with xpt_done; an unknown function code sets an error status and completes with xpt_done. So not all requests are completed by this function itself: the accepted target IO is queued, and SCSI I/O completes asynchronously after the SCB runs.

functions.name: ahc_parse_msg
functions.prose_contract: Parses one incoming SCSI message for the AIC7xxx (aic7xxx.c:3058-3473, returns the loop state: MSGLOOP_IN_PROG, MSGLOOP_MSGCOMPLETE or MSGLOOP_TERMINATED; the slice is its middle). It starts with done = MSGLOOP_IN_PROG, response = FALSE, reject = FALSE and switches on msgin_buf[0]: DISCONNECT, SAVEDATAPOINTER, CMDCOMPLETE, RESTOREPOINTERS and IGN_WIDE_RESIDUE give MSGLOOP_TERMINATED (handled elsewhere); MESSAGE_REJECT calls ahc_handle_msg_reject and its result becomes response, then (falls through) NOOP gives MSGLOOP_MSGCOMPLETE; MSG_EXTENDED waits for enough bytes (index checks leave done as IN_PROG), then by the extended message type: SDTR (wrong length rejects) takes the period and offset, filters them with ahc_devlimited_syncrate and ahc_validate_offset and DOES apply them with ahc_set_syncrate (active and goal, aic7xxx.c:3150); if the SDTR was a reply to our own request an offset that changed rejects it, else it constructs an SDTR reply (response = TRUE); WDTR and PPR messages are handled similarly (validate, set width and sync rate, reject when the settings were widened relative to what was sent or the length is wrong, construct a reply when initiated by the target); an unknown extended message sets reject; BUS DEVICE RESET and the abort messages run ahc_handle_devreset or clean up the target-mode LUN state and give MSGLOOP_TERMINATED (the abort messages reject unless acting as a target); any other message sets reject. If reject is set it prepares a MESSAGE_REJECT reply (msgout), sets done = MSGLOOP_MSGCOMPLETE and response = TRUE. If done is not IN_PROG and there was no response it clears the message-in index; it returns done.

functions.name: ahc_reset
functions.prose_contract: Resets the AIC7xxx chip (aic7xxx.c:4094-4194, returns int). It calls ahc_pause itself, so the caller does not need to have paused the chip. It saves SXFRCTL1 of channel A (and, on an AIC7770, channel B by selecting it through SBLKCTL), writes CHIPRST to HCNTRL and waits up to 1000 iterations of 1000 us for CHIPRSTACK (printing a warning if the reset did not finish but continuing anyway), then restores HCNTRL to the paused value. It determines the channel configuration from SBLKCTL (SELBUSB cleared for PCI chips): a single narrow channel needs nothing, wide sets AHC_WIDE, twin sets AHC_TWIN; any other combination prints 'Unsupported adapter type' and returns -1 immediately, BEFORE the saved SXFRCTL1 values are written back, so on that path SXFRCTL1 is not restored. Otherwise it writes back SXFRCTL1 (channel B first for twin channel chips, then channel A), and returns 0, or, if reinit is non-zero, the result of ahc->bus_chip_init(ahc).

functions.name: ahc_handle_en_lun
functions.prose_contract: Handles an XPT_EN_LUN ccb (enable or disable target-mode LUN) (aic7xxx.c:7268-7634, void; the packet name ahc_enable_lun does not exist). It reports its result by setting ccb->ccb_h.status and does not call xpt_done itself. It first looks the target/LUN state up with ahc_find_tmode_devs (a failure becomes the ccb status and returns). It validates the requested target id against our id and the chip's multi-role/multi-tid features (CAM_TID_INVALID), and, if target role is not enabled yet, refuses with CAM_BUSY when commands are pending, or tries to switch the chip to target mode (a failure gives CAM_FUNC_NOTAVAIL). Enable path: CAM_LUN_ALRDY_ENA if the LUN already exists; CAM_REQ_INVALID for a non-zero group-6 CDB length; CAM_RESRC_UNAVAIL if the target state, the LUN state (malloc) or its CAM path cannot be allocated (the LUN state is freed when the path creation fails); otherwise it pauses the chip, registers the target id in the TARGID registers (or via SCSIID/SBLKCTL on chips without multi-tid), updates SCSISEQ for the black-hole LUN, unpauses and sets CAM_REQ_CMP. Disable path: CAM_LUN_INVALID if the LUN does not exist; it rejects with CAM_REQ_INVALID if a CONT_TARGET_IO ccb is still pending on that path, aborts all pending accept-TIO and immediate-notify ccbs (CAM_REQ_ABORTED, each completed with xpt_done), and if the status is still CAM_REQ_CMP it frees the LUN path and state, pauses the chip, frees an empty target state and its TARGID bit, restores SCSISEQ when no LUNs remain enabled, and unpauses. Paths that return early leave the chip state as it was at that point.

functions.name: al_eth_change_mtu
functions.prose_contract: Static int (al_eth.c:3011-3025) applying a new MTU to the adapter. It performs no validation of new_mtu. It computes max_frame = new_mtu + ETHER_HDR_LEN + ETHER_CRC_LEN + ETHER_VLAN_ENCAP_LEN, calls al_eth_req_rx_buff_size(adapter, new_mtu) (which chooses the receive buffer size, not examined here, so what size adapter->rx_mbuf_sz ends up with is decided there), logs a debug message, calls al_eth_rx_pkt_limit_config with the frame range AL_ETH_MIN_FRAME_LEN..max_frame, and al_eth_tso_mss_config with an MSS of new_mtu - 100 (so a new_mtu below 100 gives a negative argument converted to the callee's parameter type). It returns 0 in every case; errors of the callees are not examined.

functions.name: al_eth_lm_link_detection
functions.prose_contract: Link-manager step that checks the link and detects a mode change (al_init_eth_lm.c:1147-1270, returns int: 0 or the error of module detection). lm_context, old_mode and new_mode must be non-NULL (al_assert); link_fault may be NULL. If lm_pause is configured and returns true it sets *new_mode = DISCONNECTED, sets *link_fault (when given) to false if the link state is UP, else true, and returns 0 at once; on this path *old_mode is NOT written and lm_context->link_state is not updated from hardware. Otherwise it sets *old_mode and *new_mode to the current mode and *link_fault to true, then by link_state: UP reads the hardware status; if the link is up it clears *link_fault, sets the LED on and returns 0; otherwise it moves the state to DOWN (local fault) or DOWN_RF and continues; DOWN_RF reads the status: a local fault moves to DOWN and continues, else, with no remote fault, it moves the state to UP, and in this branch (whether or not it moved to UP) it returns 0 immediately, leaving *link_fault true and *new_mode equal to the current mode (not a newly detected one); DOWN continues. After that it turns the LED off and detects the module: with sfp_detection it calls al_eth_module_detect (an error is logged and returned) and stores the result in lm_context->mode and *new_mode, else it uses default_mode. If the mode changed it logs it, marks rx/tx parameters dirty, sets new_port and, if a LED configuration callback exists and the new mode is not DISCONNECTED, calls it with the speed for the mode (an unknown mode logs an error but the callback is still called). Returns 0.

functions.name: ale_dma_alloc
functions.prose_contract: Allocates the DMA tags, rings and maps of the Atheros AR81xx driver (if_ale.c:999-1281, returns int; the slice is the middle of it). It computes the page size from the guard size (jumbo or normal frame length) and starts with lowaddr = BUS_SPACE_MAXADDR. It creates parent and per-ring tags (Tx ring, Rx pages, Tx CMB, Rx CMBs), allocates and loads the ring, page and CMB memory, and, for each load, treats 'error != 0 || ctx.ale_busaddr == 0' as a failure: it prints a message and jumps to fail. Because fail only returns the current value of error, a load whose callback left ale_busaddr at 0 while the bus_dmamap_load error was 0 returns 0 (success) even though the allocation failed. After the ring allocations, if lowaddr is not already 32-bit it calls ale_check_boundary: if the 4 GB boundary was crossed it prints a message, frees everything with ale_dma_free, sets lowaddr to 32-bit and restarts from the 'again' label (once). It then creates the Tx buffer parent tag and Tx tag and a DMA map for each Tx ring entry (a failure prints a message and goes to fail). Nothing is freed on the fail path here (the caller cleans up); the function returns error, which is 0 on full success or the last bus_dma error (or 0 in the busaddr == 0 case above).

functions.name: ale_watchdog
functions.prose_contract: Static void (if_ale.c:1898-1921) run from the periodic tick, with the driver lock asserted. It returns without doing anything if the watchdog timer is 0 or, after being decremented, is still non-zero. When the timer reaches 0 it checks the link flag: if there is no link it prints 'watchdog timeout (lost link)' first, then increments the OERRORS counter, clears IFF_DRV_RUNNING, calls ale_init_locked and returns without restarting the send queue. With a link it prints 'watchdog timeout -- resetting', increments OERRORS, clears IFF_DRV_RUNNING, calls ale_init_locked, and, if the interface send queue is not empty, calls ale_start_locked to restart transmission.

functions.name: ata_interrupt_locked
functions.prose_contract: Interrupt handler body for an ATA channel (ata-all.c:356-388, void). If the channel has a hw.status callback and it reports no interrupt for this device (returns false) the function returns at once. It returns if there is no running request. If the channel state is ATA_IDLE it prints 'interrupt on idle channel ignored' with device_printf (a diagnostic is emitted) and returns without further effect. Otherwise it calls ch->hw.end_transaction(request); only when that returns ATA_OP_FINISHED it clears ch->running, sets the state to ATA_IDLE only if it was ATA_ACTIVE (other states are left unchanged), and calls ata_cam_end_transaction(ch->dev, request); any other return value of end_transaction leaves the request running and changes nothing here.

functions.name: ata_begin_transaction
functions.prose_contract: Starts an ATA/ATAPI transaction (ata-lowlevel.c:82-237, returns ATA_OP_FINISHED or ATA_OP_CONTINUES, not an errno; errors are stored in request->result). It first clears ATA_R_DMA from the request flags for channels that cannot do ATAPI DMA (or ATAPI DMA reads only). By (ATAPI, DMA) flags: PIO (default): issues the command with ch->hw.command (on failure prints a message, result = EIO, finish); an ATA_DEVICE_RESET command is a finished path that polls status for up to about 10 s, reads the error register if the error bit is set, reads the task file and finishes with request->result left unchanged (0), i.e. a success result with ATA_OP_FINISHED; for a PIO write it waits for READY|DRQ (timeout: message, EIO, finish) and writes the first data block; then it continues.
