DMA: loads the DMA map (error: message, result = error, finish), starts DMA before or after the command depending on ATA_DMA_BEFORE_CMD, with EIO and finish on a command or DMA-start error; then continues. ATAPI PIO and ATAPI DMA: a POLL_DSC request selects the drive, waits 10 us and sets result = EBUSY if DSC is not set, then finishes (the request status and error fields are not updated on this path); otherwise it issues the packet command (and for DMA loads and starts DMA), with EIO or the load error on failures; then continues. A value falling outside the switch prints 'ata_begin_transaction OOPS!!!' and falls into the finish label. On every finish path it unloads the DMA map if there is an unload method and returns ATA_OP_FINISHED; on the continue path it arms the request callout (timeout * hz, ata_timeout) and returns ATA_OP_CONTINUES.

functions.name: ata_nvidia_status
functions.prose_contract: Static int (ata-nvidia.c:281-307) reading and acknowledging the NVIDIA SATA interrupt status for one channel. The register offset is 0x0440 when the chip config has the NV4 flag and 0x0010 otherwise (NV4, not NVQ, selects the offset); the per-channel bit shift is ch->unit shifted left by 4 when the NVQ flag is set (NVQ selects the register width, 32-bit versus 8-bit and the shift width) and by 2 otherwise. It reads the status with a 32-bit read for NVQ chips or an 8-bit read otherwise, calls ata_sata_phy_check_events(dev, -1) if any of the 0x0c bits for this channel (the shifted mask) are set, writes back the acknowledge value (0x0f << shift, with 0x00f000f0 ORed in for the 32-bit case; the write clears the channel's bits) and returns istatus & (0x01 << shift), the raw masked bit value, which is 0 or (1 << shift), not necessarily 1.

functions.name: ar5212AniLowerImmunity
functions.prose_contract: Static void (ar5212_ani.c:809-881) that lowers one ANI immunity setting by one step, performing at most one adjustment per call (each branch returns after one ar5212AniControl call). It asserts ANI is enabled. If RSSI-based ANI is enabled (ANI_ENA_RSSI) it reads the beacon RSSI and: for RSSI above the high threshold it takes no action in this block (falls to the spur and noise steps below); for RSSI above the low threshold it first re-enables OFDM weak-signal detection (ar5212AniControl(HAL_ANI_OFDM_WEAK_SIGNAL_DETECTION, AH_TRUE), i.e. it can ENABLE detection, not lower it) if it is currently off and returns, else lowers the first-step level by one if it is above 0 and returns; for RSSI at or below the low threshold it lowers the first-step level if above 0 and returns. If RSSI-based ANI is disabled, that whole block is skipped (the first-step level is not touched by it). Then, if nothing returned: it lowers the spur immunity level by one if above 0 (return), else lowers the noise immunity level by one if above 0. If every level is already 0 it does nothing.

functions.name: ar5212SetCapability
functions.prose_contract: Sets a hardware capability on an AR5212 (ar5212_misc.c:930-1047, returns HAL_BOOL AH_TRUE/AH_FALSE). By type: TKIP_MIC sets or clears the MIC-enable bit in the saved STA_ID1 defaults and returns AH_TRUE; TKIP_SPLIT returns AH_FALSE if the chip lacks TX/RX MIC key support, else updates ah_miscMode, ORs it into AR_MISC_MODE and returns AH_TRUE; DIVERSITY switches on `capability`: 0 returns AH_FALSE; 1 (setting) updates the CCK-detect antenna fast-diversity bit only when the PHY is powered and capability equals HAL_CAP_STRONG_DIV, stores ah_diversity, and returns AH_TRUE regardless of whether the PHY is powered; HAL_CAP_STRONG_DIV returns AH_FALSE when the PHY is off, else writes the diversity gain control field and returns AH_TRUE; any other value returns AH_FALSE. DIAG writes AR_DIAG_SW; TPC sets ah_tpcEnabled; MCAST_KEYSRCH sets or clears a STA_ID1 bit; TPC_ACK and TPC_CTS add the TX power index offset, cap the value at 63, update the TPC register fields and write AR_TPC (all return AH_TRUE); INTMIT maps `capability` (0..6) to an ANI command and returns the result of ah_aniControl (which may be AH_FALSE), or AH_FALSE for an out-of-range capability; TSF_ADJUST sets or clears the TX_ADD_TSF bit and returns AH_TRUE only if the chip supports it, otherwise it falls through into the default case (there is no break or return), which calls ath_hal_setcapability(ah, type, capability, setting, status) and returns its result; the default case does the same.

functions.name: ar5212GetNf
functions.prose_contract: Reads, filters and re-loads the noise floor for a channel (ar5212_reset.c:1390-1474, returns int16_t). If the AGC NF-calibration bit is still set (calibration not complete) it stores h->privNF (the most recent value) into ichan->rawNoiseFloor, returns it and changes no register. Otherwise it reads the noise floor nf; if a threshold exists and nf > threshold it marks the channel CWINT and sets nf = 0, and if no threshold is available it also sets nf = 0. It adds nf to the history buffer. During the warm-up phase (h->first_run): an nf below AR5212_CCA_MIN_BAD_VALUE or above AR5212_CCA_MAX_HIGH_VALUE (including the nf = 0 set above) is replaced by AR5212_CCA_MAX_GOOD_VALUE and the invalid counter is reset; otherwise the counter is decremented and, when it reaches 0, first_run is cleared and nf and privNF become the median of the history buffer; before that nf is AR5212_CCA_MAX_GOOD_VALUE. After warm-up (first_run clear) nf and privNF are always set to the median of the history buffer, so an out-of-range reading no longer produces AR5212_CCA_MAX_GOOD_VALUE but the median. It then loads nf into AR_PHY(25), toggles the AGC NF control bits to start a calibration, waits for it to complete (a timeout only prints a debug message), loads a fixed -50 dBm into the register, re-enables NF updates and starts another calibration, and returns ichan->rawNoiseFloor = nf.

functions.name: ar5416ProcessRadarEvent
functions.prose_contract: Converts a radar PHY-error frame into a DFS event (ar5416_radar.c:233-420, returns HAL_BOOL; the packet name dfs_process_phy_err does not exist). It returns AH_FALSE unless rs_phyerr is HAL_PHYERR_RADAR or HAL_PHYERR_FALSE_RADAR_EXT. It reads the capability flags (ext channel, enhanced DFS, combined RSSI), selects rssi (combined or control chain 0) and ext_rssi, and zeroes either one if its top bit (0x80) is set. With ext-channel DFS support it needs at least 3 bytes of data (AH_FALSE if datalen < 3) and reads the primary pulse length, extension pulse length and bandwidth info from the last three bytes of buf (buf is indexed by datalen); it returns AH_FALSE if pulse_bw_info is 0. Without ext-channel support it takes the duration from buf[0] (0 if there is no data) and returns AH_FALSE when both the duration and rssi are 0. With ext-channel support it picks the pulse: radar found on both channels sets is_dc and uses the longer pulse; early-extension, primary-only or extension-only cases select the corresponding duration and flags. With enhanced DFS it adjusts rssi by the pulse_bw_info case (zeroing it or taking ext_rssi, using 3 dB and 12 dB margins); with ext-channel support but not enhanced DFS it uses ext_rssi if larger (and below 128). It fills event->re_full_ts, re_ts, re_rssi, re_dur and re_flags (PRICH, EXTCH, EXTEARLY, ISDC as applicable) and returns AH_TRUE.

functions.name: ar5416ResetTxQueue
functions.prose_contract: Programs the hardware registers of one TX queue (ar5416_xmit.c:1243-1497, returns HAL_BOOL; the slice cut the head and the function is not unnamed). It returns AH_FALSE (with a debug message) if q is not below the chip's total queue count, and returns AH_TRUE without touching any register if the queue is HAL_TX_QUEUE_INACTIVE. Otherwise it computes cwMin (the default contention window from the channel type, rounded up to 2^n - 1, when tqi_cwmin is HAL_TXQ_USEDEFAULT, else the configured value) and writes the DCU local IFS (cwmin, cwmax, aifs), the retry limits (initial short/long station retries and the queue's long/short frame retry values), and the other DCU/QCU control registers (misc, backoff threshold, ready time, scheduling flags); then, by queue type, applies type-specific settings: beacon queues get beacon-specific QCU/DCU flags and timers, CAB queues set the ready-time handling (defaulting a ready time when the driver supplied none), PS-poll and UAPSD queues set their QCU flags, and other types add nothing. It enables the queue's interrupt bits as needed and returns AH_TRUE.

functions.name: ar9280Attach
functions.prose_contract: Attaches an AR9280 (Merlin) chip (ar9280_attach.c:149-423, returns struct ath_hal * or AH_NULL; the slice cut the head). It allocates the HAL state (on failure sets *status = HAL_ENOMEM and returns AH_NULL), installs the 9280-specific method pointers and calibration tables, resets the chip (ar5416SetResetReg) and wakes it (ar5416SetPowerMode), and selects the INI register tables for Merlin 2.0 or later versus earlier revisions. It then runs the chip reset and self-test, reads the PHY revision, and checks the analog 5 GHz revision (unsupported chips give HAL_ENOTSUPP); it sets up the RF (ar9280RfAttach), reads the EEPROM power-table and clock settings, and, for Merlin 2.0, selects the RX gain INI table and the TX gain INI table from the EEPROM gain type. For an unknown RX or TX gain type the code does HALASSERT(AH_FALSE) and then jumps to the bad label (so in a build without assertions the attach fails with ecode as it stood, instead of continuing; the comment says 'try to continue' but the code does not). It then fills the capability information (failure: HAL_EEREAD), checks the final ecode, sets the misc mode, ANI and noise-floor limits for 2 GHz and 5 GHz, and returns ah. Every failure path goes to bad, which calls ah->ah_detach(ah) if ah is set, stores ecode in *status if status is non-NULL and returns AH_NULL. The status pointer is dereferenced only on failure paths after the allocation (a NULL status is tolerated at bad).

functions.name: _ath_power_setpower
functions.prose_contract: Void function (if_ath.c:299-342) that records a target power state and applies it if allowed. It asserts the ATH lock, logs a debug line, and always stores power_state in sc->sc_target_powerstate. It then acts only if (the power-save reference count is 0 or the requested state is HAL_PM_AWAKE) and the requested state differs from sc_cur_powerstate: it stores the new current state and calls ath_hal_setpower(sc->sc_ah, power_state) (this call happens whenever that outer condition holds, whether or not selfgen is non-zero); and if selfgen is non-zero, the current state is now awake, and sc_target_selfgen_state is not awake, it also calls ath_hal_setselfgenpower with the target selfgen state. If the outer condition is false (reference count held and a sleep request, or no change of state) only the target state was updated and the hardware is left alone. file and line are used only for the log message.

functions.name: ath_newstate
functions.prose_contract: net80211 state-change method of the ath driver (if_ath.c:5815-6256, returns int; the slice is the early to middle part). It sets the LED for the new state, requests awake power (ath_power_setselfgen unless going to SLEEP, and the power state), and, for the SCAN state, restores awake power and enables the global interrupts before continuing. It computes the RX filter and a 'stamode' flag (STA, AHDEMO or IBSS); only when stamode is true AND the new state is RUN does it set sc_curaid and sc_curbssid from the node and call ath_hal_setassocid; so the association id and bssid are updated in those modes only, not on every successful change. It installs the RX filter and, for non-STA modes, updates the MAC address of valid key cache entries. It then calls the vap's saved av_newstate (an error goes to bad, restoring power state and returning the error). For the RUN state, by opmode: HOSTAP, IBSS, MBSS and AHDEMO (the latter only with TDMA capability) stop beacon DMA, allocate the beacon (ath_beacon_alloc, error goes to bad) and then, for an IBSS node with a current TSF, defer beacon timer setup (sc_syncbeacon = 1), else if beacons are not yet configured call ath_tdma_config (TDMA) or ath_beacon_config and set sc_beacons; the STA mode defers beacon configuration to the next beacon (so STA does not allocate a beacon here); other modes do nothing. It then updates noise-floor processing, power, and the calibration callout. INIT, SLEEP and SCAN states stop timers, interrupts or calibrations as appropriate. At the end it restores the power state with ath_power_restore_power_state and returns error.

functions.name: ath_node_set_tim
functions.prose_contract: Sets or clears the TIM bit for a node (if_ath.c:6778-6887, returns int: whether the TIM changed). It has two builds. Without ATH_SW_PSQ it returns 0 if the vap's av_set_tim hook is NULL and otherwise returns av_set_tim(ni, enable) (the NULL check is present here too). With ATH_SW_PSQ it takes ATH_TX_LOCK itself (it must not be called with that lock held), stores an_stack_psq = enable, and if av_set_tim is NULL unlocks and returns 0. Then: if enable is set and an_tim_set is already 1 it only logs, unlocks and returns 0 (the request is ignored, an_tim_set stays 1); if enable is set otherwise it sets an_tim_set = 1, unlocks and returns av_set_tim(ni, enable); if enable is clear and the software queue depth is 0 it clears an_tim_set, unlocks and returns av_set_tim(ni, 0); if enable is clear, the queue is not empty and the node is no longer in power save it also clears an_tim_set and calls av_set_tim; otherwise (clear requested, packets queued, node asleep) it unlocks, logs and returns 0 without changing the TIM. The av_set_tim call is made after the lock is dropped.

functions.name: ath_lna_rx_comb_scan
functions.prose_contract: Void function (if_ath_lna_div.c:704-1010; the packet name ath_ant_div_comb_scan does not exist, the slice is the later half of ath_lna_rx_comb_scan) called for received frames to drive the LNA/antenna diversity combining scan. It decodes the main and alternate RSSI and antenna configuration from the rx status and returns at once if LNA diversity is not enabled (sc_dolnadiv) or the TX antenna is not HAL_ANT_VARIABLE. It accumulates packet and RSSI totals per antenna when both RSSI values are positive. It decides short_scan (when scanning with a good alternate: the short-scan interval elapsed, or the short-scan packet count was reached with a low alternate ratio) and returns without changes if fewer than the maximum number of packets has been collected (or the frame is part of an aggregate) and no short scan is due. Otherwise it computes the alternate-antenna ratio and the average RSSI per antenna, reads the current diversity configuration from the HAL (ath_hal_div_comb_conf_get), increments the scan counter and, when it reaches the maximum, evaluates whether the alternate antenna is good (ath_lnaconf_alt_good_scan) and starts the scan (scan = true, scan_not_start = true). Outside a scan it switches the main and alternate LNA configurations when the alternate ratio is high or by the current main set, and goes to div_comb_done in those cases; during a scan it steps through the LNA1/LNA2/ADD/SUB configurations by the current alternate set and the measured RSSI values, and finally adjusts the fast diversity bias (ath_ant_adjust_fast_divbias). At div_comb_done it writes the new configuration back to the HAL when changed, logs the changes, resets scan_start_time to ticks and zeroes the packet and RSSI counters.

functions.name: proc_synaptics
functions.prose_contract: Processes one Synaptics TouchPad absolute-mode packet (psm.c:3264-3677, returns int; the packet name psm_process_synaptics_packet does not exist, the slice is the middle of proc_synaptics). It returns 0 immediately if synaptics support is disabled, and -1 (discard) if the packet's framing bits are wrong (ipacket[0] & 0xc8 != 0x80 or ipacket[3] & 0xc8 != 0xc0). It starts from ms->button = ms->obutton, decodes the finger count (W value, extended-W codes for multi-finger and fuzzy-finger reports, keeping some state in static variables) and the button bits (physical, extended/guest buttons, clickpad). For the extended-W packets it records the extra finger info and jumps to SYNAPTICS_END (skipping position processing). If sc->syninfo.touchpad_off is set it also jumps to SYNAPTICS_END (psm.c:3453-3454), skipping the finger tracking, palm detection and gestures. Otherwise it runs psmpalmdetect on the first finger; when no palm is detected it runs gesture detection, then smooths every finger's position into x and y. If a palm was detected it sets *x = *y = *z = 0, restores ms->button = ms->obutton and returns 0 immediately (this palm early return is separate from the touchpad_off path). Otherwise it ORs the extended and guest buttons into ms->button. At SYNAPTICS_END it turns the extra buttons 4-7 into a scroll-wheel value in *z (-1, 1, -2, 2, else 0), clears those button bits from ms->button and returns 0.

functions.name: proc_elantech
functions.prose_contract: Processes one Elantech touchpad packet (psm.c:4389-4842, returns int: 0 processed or ignored, -1 for an out-of-sync/invalid packet; the packet name elantech_get_packet does not exist, this slice is the early part of proc_elantech). It returns 0 at once if elantech support is disabled. It classifies the packet: a debounce packet is NOP; a track-point packet (when the hardware has one) is TRACKPOINT; otherwise by hardware version: v2 returns -1 unless the packet looks like v2 (then 2-finger or common), v3 returns -1 unless it is a v3 head or tail packet (then V3), v4 distinguishes status/head/motion packets by byte 3 and returns -1 for an unknown code, and an unknown hardware version returns -1. Then the per-format decoding: V2 common/2-finger read the finger positions and buttons; V3 head and tail packets assemble multi-finger positions across two packets and return 0 early when more data is needed; V4 status packets track the finger-count bitmask and return 0 early for a repeated status; V4 head packets fill one finger's position (returning 0 early under some conditions) and V4 motion packets update positions of several fingers.

functions.name: proc_elantech
functions.prose_contract: Later part of proc_elantech (psm.c:4389-4842, returns int). After the per-format decoding of the packet types (V4 head, V4 motion, track-point, NOP), the track-point packet reports its relative movement and buttons and returns 0 early; a NOP packet returns 0 and an unknown packet type returns -1 (the default case, which is reached only after the earlier classification code has accepted the packet, so it is a defensive return). The remaining code, for touchpad packets, applies palm detection (psmpalmdetect) and, if no palm is found, gesture handling (psmgestures), smooths the finger positions into *x, *y, converts the buttons (including the clickpad button and the left/right/middle bits), and, when a palm was detected, zeroes the motion and returns 0 (psm.c:4824); otherwise it sets *z and the button state in ms and returns 0 at the end (4841).

functions.name: BHNDB_IO_MISC(_type, _ptr, _op, _size)
functions.prose_contract: Macro (bhndb.c:1823-1833) that generates one static void bus method 'bhndb_bus_<op>_<size>(device_t dev, device_t child, struct bhnd_resource *r, bus_size_t offset, _type _ptr datap, bus_size_t count)'; BHNDB_IO_METHODS instantiates it for read_multi, write_multi, their _stream variants, set_multi, set_region, read_region, write_region and their _stream variants, for 1, 2 and 4 byte types (BHNDB_IO_METHODS(uint8_t, 1), (uint16_t, 2), (uint32_t, 4)). Each generated function does the common setup (BHNDB_IO_COMMON_SETUP(sizeof(_type) * count)): it takes the softc, locks the bhndb softc lock (BHNDB_LOCK), asks bhndb_io_resource for a dynamic window resource covering offset .. offset + sizeof(type) * count of the child's resource (possibly 'stealing' a window, recording the restore address), takes the parent resource, and KASSERTs that the child resource is not a direct resource and that the window resource is active (these checks only exist when KASSERT is compiled in). It then performs the corresponding bus_<op>_<size> on the window resource at the translated offset, and the common teardown: if a window was stolen it returns it (bhndb_dw_return_stolen with the saved restore address) and always unlocks. The generated functions return nothing; they have no error path of their own, and a failure to obtain a window is handled inside bhndb_io_resource (not read).

functions.name: bhndb_attach
functions.prose_contract: Generic bhndb(4) attach helper (bhndb.c:509-607, returns int; the packet name bhndb_generic_attach does not exist, and the slice also shows the following detach/suspend/resume functions). It copies dev, the parent device, the bridge core and chip id into the softc and initialises the service registry (its error is returned immediately, with nothing else set up). It initialises the softc lock, looks up a hardware spec for the core list (if none is found it prints a message and uses the parent's generic hwcfg), allocates the bridge resources (NULL gives ENOMEM, via failed), adds the 'bhnd' child bus device (NULL gives ENXIO), marks its dinfo as bridged, allocates an EROM parser over a new iores (failure: finalises the I/O object and ENXIO), obtains the hardware priority table and initialises the region configuration (an error is printed and returned). On success it frees the EROM, sets it to NULL and returns 0. The failed label destroys the softc lock, frees the bridge resources if allocated, frees the EROM if allocated, finalises the service registry and returns the error. Note that the child bus device added with BUS_ADD_CHILD is not deleted on the failure paths.

functions.name: bhnd_pmu_spuravoid_pllupdate
functions.prose_contract: Static int (bhnd_pmu_subr.c:2976-3316) that reprograms the PMU PLL for spur avoidance mode `spuravoid` and returns 0 or ENODEV. It treats a BCM6362 revision 0 as a BCM43224. Per chip group it programs PLL control registers through BHND_PMU_PLL_WRITE: for BCM6362 (asserting rev != 0), BCM5357, BCM4749, BCM43235..43238, BCM43234, BCM43237 and BCM53572 it selects p1div/ndiv for NONE, M1 or M2 and writes PLLCTL0 and PLLCTL2 (offset +6 for BCM5357); BCM4331 writes PLLCTL0 and PLLCTL2 constants for NONE, M1 and M2; the BCM43224/43225/43226/43421 group writes PLLCTL0-5 for NONE and M1 only; BCM43111/43112/43222/43420, BCM4716/4748/47162, BCM4322/43221/43231/4342, BCM4336 and BCM43131/43227/43228/43428 each have their own constant sets (some modes unsupported); the BCM4319 case performs no PLL register writes at all and leaves pmuctrl 0. A mode that a chip group does not support returns ENODEV immediately, after possibly having written nothing, and an unknown chip logs 'unknown spuravoidance settings' and returns ENODEV without changing the PLL. After the switch it ORs the update bits (PLLCTL_UPD, or NOILP_ON_WAIT and others for the 4716 group) into BHND_PMU_CTRL if pmuctrl is non-zero (so BCM4319 does not update that control register) and returns 0.

functions.name: bhnd_nvram_ident_num_string
functions.prose_contract: Static bool (bhnd_nvram_value_fmts.c:968-1050) that checks whether the ilen bytes at inp are a valid integer string and reports the base. It returns false for an empty string, for a string that ends right after an optional leading '-' or '+', and for a string that ends right after a '0x'/'0X' prefix. The prefix is recognised and skipped only when base is 16 or 0 (setting base to 16); when base is 0 and no hex prefix was seen, a leading '0' selects base 8 and any other start selects base 10. It then checks every remaining byte: it must be a decimal or hexadecimal digit (any other character returns false) whose value is below base (otherwise false), counting digits; it returns false if no digit was counted. On success, if obase is non-NULL it stores the (possibly detected) base in *obase and returns true; *obase is not written on a false return. No leading whitespace is skipped and no overflow check is made; the code does not validate the base argument itself, so a base other than 0, 8, 10 or 16 is accepted as long as every digit is below it (a base of 0 is the only value that triggers detection).

functions.name: bhnd_nvram_val_vprintf
functions.prose_contract: Formats an NVRAM value with a printf-style format (bhnd_nvram_value_prf.c:209-879, returns int; the slice is its tail, with the 's' and 'c' conversions and the epilogue). It takes the output limit from *olen when outp is non-NULL (else 0), walks the format string and the value's elements and produces output with the WRITE_CHAR macro, which stores a byte only while limit > nbytes but always counts it. The 's' conversion first asks bhnd_nvram_val_encode_elem for the string length (error returned), drops the trailing NUL from the length, writes right-adjust padding, encodes the string directly into the output buffer when space remains (an ENOMEM result is tolerated, any other error is returned), adds the length to nbytes (returning EFTYPE on size_t overflow) and writes left-adjust padding. The 'c' conversion encodes the element into a local char c (error returned) and asserts the encoded size is 1, writes right-adjust padding, but then calls WRITE_CHAR(padc), i.e. it writes the pad character instead of the encoded character c (the encoded value is never output), then the left-adjust padding. At the end it appends a terminating NUL if limit > nbytes, increments nbytes (EFTYPE if it would overflow), stores the required size nbytes in *olen, and returns ENOMEM if the limit is smaller than the required size and outp is non-NULL, else 0 (a NULL outp with a size query returns 0).

functions.name: bnxt_queue_remap
functions.prose_contract: Static int (bnxt_dcb.c:198-241) that remaps traffic classes to hardware queues so lossless classes land on lossless queues; it returns 0 or the error of an HWRM configuration call. First loop: for each traffic class i < max_tc whose bit is set in lltc_mask it scans the receive queue info with index j for a queue whose profile is lossless (BNXT_LLQ), assigns tc_to_qidx[i] = j and marks j used in qmap; the scan over j has no upper bound check against the number of queues (it relies on enough lossless queues existing, so with too few lossless queues j can run past the array and the loop may not terminate within max_tc queues), and a lossless queue index above max_tc - 1 is recorded in tc_to_qidx but cannot be marked in a bitmap of only max bits meaningfully for the second pass. Second loop: for each class not in lltc_mask it takes the next zero bit of qmap in 0..max-1 (find_next_zero_bit(&qmap, max, j)) and assigns it, so tc_to_qidx is a permutation of 0..max_tc-1 only if every lossless class found a lossless queue with index below max_tc; otherwise it is not guaranteed to be a permutation. Then, if softc->ieee_ets is set, it configures the CoS bandwidth (bnxt_hwrm_queue_cos2bw_cfg) and the priority-to-CoS map (bnxt_hwrm_queue_pri2cos_cfg); the first non-zero result is printed and returned (tc_to_qidx has already been changed by then). It returns 0 otherwise.

functions.name: bnxt_qplib_post_send
functions.prose_contract: Posts one send work request to a QP's send queue (qplib_fp.c:1941-2291, returns int; the slice is the early to middle part). It returns -EINVAL (via done) if the QP state is neither RTS nor ERR, and -ENOMEM if the SQ does not have room for the needed slots plus the full-queue delta (messages are logged). Otherwise it takes the next software WQE entry, records the wr_id, type, flags, slot count and start PSN, and sets the signal-completion flag when the QP is signalled-by-default or the WQE asks for it. If the QP's current state is ERR (cur_qp_state) it does not write any WQE headers or data: it sets sch_handler and jumps to queue_err, which still advances the software queue entry, the hardware producer index and wqe_cnt, and the function returns 0 (the WQE is queued so that poll_cq can complete it in error). For a normal QP it zeroes the base and extension headers of the WQE, then puts the data: inline data (bnxt_qplib_put_inline) or the SGE list; a negative data_len (for example inline data that does not fit) jumps to queue_err WITHOUT setting rc, so the headers have already been zeroed and the work request is still counted and queued and the function returns 0 on that path. It then fills the headers by wqe->type (send, RDMA write/read, atomic, local invalidate, bind MW); an unknown type returns -EINVAL via done without advancing the queue. The PSN search/MSN entry is filled when needed, and queue_err/the tail advances the swq and producer index and increments wqe_cnt. At done, if sch_handler is set, it allocates nq_work (GFP_ATOMIC) and queues bnxt_qpn_cqn_sched_task on the CQ's workqueue; an allocation failure logs and sets rc = -ENOMEM (overriding 0). It returns rc.

functions.name: bnxt_qplib_cq_process_req
functions.prose_contract: Static int (qplib_fp.c:2911-3033) that turns one requester CQE into software CQEs for the send queue. It returns -EINVAL if the CQE's QP handle is NULL. It returns 0 without producing anything or advancing the queue if the SQ is already flushed, or if, for an error CQE on a variable-size WQE, the reported SQ consumer slot cannot be found (the lookup failure goes to done with rc still 0). Otherwise it walks the software WQE list from swq_last up to the consumer index reported by the CQE while the CQE budget is non-zero: it stops at the end index; for each entry it builds a CQE (opcode, qp handle, src qp, wr_id; a fence WQE produces no CQE); for the last WQE, if the hardware status is not OK, it reports an error CQE with the hardware status REGARDLESS of whether that WQE was signalled, consumes one budget unit and calls bnxt_qplib_mark_qp_error(qp); otherwise on chips before gen P5/P7 it runs the legacy 9060 workaround (which may stop the walk by jumping to out with *lib_qp set), and only for a signalled WQE emits an OK CQE and decrements the budget. Each processed WQE advances the hardware consumer and swq_last; with sq->single set it handles only one WQE per call. It stores the advanced CQE pointer in *pcqe. If swq_last has not reached the CQE's index (out of budget, a single-step pass, or the workaround exit) it returns -EAGAIN (so -EAGAIN is not only for budget exhaustion, also for sq->single and the workaround path); otherwise it clears sq->single and returns 0.

functions.name: bwi_led_blink_start
functions.prose_contract: Static void (if_bwi.c:3941-3959) that starts blinking the activity LED. It reads the GPIO control register, applies bwi_led_onoff(led, val, 1) to turn the LED on (for an active-low LED, BWI_LED_F_ACTLOW, bwi_led_onoff inverts the request so the GPIO mask bit is CLEARED rather than set, if_bwi.c:3837-3842) and writes the register back. If the LED has the BWI_LED_F_SLOW flag it applies BWI_LED_SLOWDOWN to both on_dur and off_dur, which sets each to (dur * 3) / 2, i.e. lengthens each by about 50 percent (if_bwivar.h:64). It then sets sc_led_blinking = 1, stores off_dur in sc_led_blink_offdur and arms the blink callout to call bwi_led_blink_next(sc) after on_dur ticks. It returns nothing.

functions.name: bwn_phy_lp_rccal_r12
functions.prose_contract: Static int (if_bwn_phy_lp.c:1813-1930) performing the RC calibration of an LP PHY with an rev 1/2 radio; it returns 0 in every case. It switches to channel 7 (a failure only prints a message and the function continues), saves whether TX override is active (txo) and the current bbmult and, if txo, the TX gain, and saves seven PHY registers (RF_OVERRIDE_0 and _VAL_0, AFE_CTL_OVR and _OVRVAL, RF_OVERRIDE_2 and _2_VAL, LP_PHY_CTL). It turns TX power control off, sets the receiver deaf and the TR switch override and writes a long list of override bits. It runs the loopback measurement (bwn_phy_lp_loopback); if that returns -1 it jumps to done without calibrating. Otherwise it sets the RX gain index and for each capacitor value i in 128..159 writes it to the B2062 RXBB calibration register and, for each of 21 tone frequencies j, turns on the DDFS tone and runs bwn_phy_lp_rx_iq_est: a failed estimate jumps to done (skipping bwn_phy_lp_ddfs_turnoff); otherwise it accumulates the squared difference between the table power and the measured power and stores the best i in plp->plp_rccap. At done it clears the deaf state, masks the RF_OVERRIDE_0 and _2 registers to their low bits, writes back the seven saved registers, restores bbmult, the TX gain (if txo was set) and the TX power control mode, and calls bwn_phy_lp_set_rccap if plp_rccap is non-zero. Registers that were written with fixed values and are not restored: PS_CTL_OVERRIDE_VAL0..2, TX_GAIN_CTL_OVERRIDE_VAL, RX_GAIN_CTL_OVERRIDE_VAL, the RX gain index and the B2062 RXBB calibration register (the last is left at the final probed value unless set_rccap rewrites it).

functions.name: bxe_init_locked
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc is a valid softc and the core lock is held (BXE_CORE_LOCK_ASSERT). Postcondition: returns 0 immediately if IFF_DRV_RUNNING is already set; returns ENXIO immediately, without touching IFF_DRV_RUNNING, if sc->state is BXE_STATE_ERROR and recovery_state is BXE_RECOVERY_FAILED. Otherwise it sets power state D0; for a PF with a pending reset or parity attention it may attempt leader recovery, and if that does not complete it moves the device to D3hot, sets recovery_state to BXE_RECOVERY_FAILED and goes to the common exit with rc = ENXIO. If no recovery failure occurs it sets recovery_state to BXE_RECOVERY_DONE and calls bxe_nic_load(sc, LOAD_OPEN), keeping its return code as rc. At the common exit any nonzero rc (ENXIO from the recovery failure, or whatever bxe_nic_load returned) is logged and IFF_DRV_RUNNING is cleared; rc is returned and the core lock stays held.

functions.name: bxe_prev_unload_common
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc is a valid softc for a device whose path may have been left loaded by a previous function. Postcondition: if bxe_prev_is_path_marked(sc) is true it returns bxe_prev_mcp_done(sc) right away, with no MAC close, BRB drain or common reset (but bxe_prev_mcp_done itself runs). Otherwise it reads MISC_REG_RESET_REG_1; only if the RST_BRB1 bit is set does it close the MAC Rx paths and the LLH filters, check for UNDI (when RST_DORQ is set and DORQ_REG_NORM_CID_OFST reads 0x7, it clears that offset), and poll BRB1_REG_NUM_OF_FULL_BLOCKS until empty or until the timer runs out (logging "Failed to empty BRB" on timeout). Then in both remaining cases it calls bxe_reset_common, rewrites any saved xmac/umac/emac/bmac register values that were recorded, and calls bxe_prev_mark_path(sc, prev_undi); if that returns nonzero it calls bxe_prev_mcp_done(sc), ignores its result and returns the marking error; otherwise it returns bxe_prev_mcp_done(sc).

functions.name: bxe_nic_unload
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc is a valid softc and the core lock is held (BXE_CORE_LOCK_ASSERT). It first clears IFF_DRV_RUNNING, zeroes each fastpath watchdog_timer and briefly takes and releases each fastpath TX lock, and for a PF with the shmem2 capability flag clears the LOADED_L2 bit. It then returns -1 (after logging an error) when sc is a PF whose recovery_state is not BXE_RECOVERY_DONE and whose state is BXE_STATE_CLOSED or BXE_STATE_ERROR; only in CHIP_4_PORT_MODE does that path first set recovery_state to BXE_RECOVERY_DONE, clear is_leader and release the leader lock. Otherwise, if state is CLOSED or ERROR it returns 0 with no further teardown. Otherwise it sets state to CLOSING_WAITING_HALT, disables TX, sets rx_mode to none, for a PF without grcdump_done drives the driver pulse and stops and saves statistics, drains the TX queues, then: for a VF does nothing here; for unload_mode other than UNLOAD_RECOVERY it calls bxe_chip_cleanup unless grcdump_done is set; for UNLOAD_RECOVERY it sends the unload request, disables the PF on non-E1x chips, disables and detaches interrupts and reports unload done. A PF then squeezes the queueable objects. For all device types it clears sp_state and port.pmf, frees the fastpath buffers and firmware stats memory, and sets state to BXE_STATE_CLOSED; bxe_free_mem is called only for a PF. A PF then checks parity attention (setting reset-in-progress and possibly reset-global) and may disable the close-the-gate; finally it reports the link and returns 0. The function contains no call that releases the core lock.

functions.name: bxe_interrupt_alloc
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc is an initialized softc whose interrupt_mode selects the first mode to try (INTR_MODE_MSIX, INTR_MODE_MSI or INTR_MODE_INTX) and whose devinfo.pcie_cap_flags and num_queues are set. If interrupt_mode is positive it first reads the MSI-X and MSI vector counts from the bus when the capability flags are set. It then runs three sequential attempts, each skipped unless interrupt_mode equals its own mode: MSI-X (needs the capability and msix_count >= 2; requests min(num_queues + 1, msix_count) vectors; fewer than 2 granted is treated as failure; on success sets intr_count to the number granted and num_queues to that number minus one, and maps one IRQ resource per vector starting at rid 1), then MSI (needs the capability and msi_count >= 1; requests one vector, requires exactly one granted; sets intr_count and num_queues to 1 and maps rid 1), then INTx (sets intr_count and num_queues to 1 and maps rid 0 with RF_SHAREABLE). When an MSI-X or MSI attempt fails after vectors were allocated, it releases the already mapped IRQ resources (MSI-X) and calls pci_release_msi, resets intr_count and num_queues to 0 where they had been set, sets interrupt_mode to the next mode and falls through to it. If the INTx resource cannot be mapped it sets intr_count and num_queues to 0 and interrupt_mode to -1. Returns 1 if interrupt_mode is -1 at the end (and logs the failure) and 0 otherwise. If interrupt_mode on entry matches none of the three modes, no allocation is attempted and the function still returns 0 unless it was -1.

functions.name: elink_init_fpga
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: params and vars point to valid structures and params->sc is a softc for an FPGA configuration. It sets vars->duplex to DUPLEX_FULL and vars->flow_ctrl to ELINK_FLOW_CTRL_NONE; if the chip is not E1 it instead sets flow_ctrl to TX|RX and ORs the TX/RX flow-control-enabled bits into vars->link_status. On an E3 chip it copies params->req_line_speed[0] into vars->line_speed; ELINK_SPEED_AUTO_NEG is changed to 2500 and falls through to the 2500 case; 2500, 1000, 100 and 10 assign vars->link_status the corresponding full-duplex link constant (an assignment, so the flow-control bits set earlier are overwritten); any other speed returns ELINK_STATUS_ERROR immediately (leaving line_speed at the requested value and link_up unchanged). It then ORs in LINK_STATUS_LINK_UP and calls elink_umac_enable with the loopback argument 1 if loopback_mode is ELINK_LOOPBACK_UMAC, else 0. On a non-E3 chip it sets line_speed to ELINK_SPEED_10000, link_status to LINK_STATUS_LINK_UP|ELINK_LINK_10GTFD and calls elink_emac_enable with loopback 1 if loopback_mode is ELINK_LOOPBACK_EMAC, else 0. After either branch it sets vars->link_up to 1, calls elink_pbf_update when the chip is E1x, writes 0 to NIG_REG_EGRESS_DRAIN0_MODE + port*4, calls elink_update_mng with vars->link_status, and returns ELINK_STATUS_OK.

functions.name: elink_ets_e3b0_sp_set_pri_cli_reg
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: params->sc and params->port are valid and sp_pri_to_cos points to at least max_num_of_cos bytes, where max_num_of_cos is ELINK_DCBX_E3B0_MAX_NUM_COS_PORT1 if params->port is nonzero, else ELINK_DCBX_E3B0_MAX_NUM_COS_PORT0. The function builds register values in locals first: the first loop takes each entry that is not DCBX_INVALID_COS as a strict-priority COS, and returns ELINK_STATUS_ERROR if the entry is >= ELINK_DCBX_MAX_NUM_COS or if its COS bit was already consumed (duplicate or out of the port's range); the second loop appends every COS index in increasing order that was not used as strict priority. If the number of priorities assigned does not equal max_num_of_cos it returns ELINK_STATUS_ERROR. Only after all checks pass does it write registers: for port 1 the low 32 bits to NIG_REG_P1_TX_ARB_PRIORITY_CLIENT2_LSB and the PBF value to PBF_REG_ETS_ARB_PRIORITY_CLIENT_P1; for port 0 the low 32 bits and bits 32-35 to the P0 NIG LSB and MSB registers and the PBF value to PBF_REG_ETS_ARB_PRIORITY_CLIENT_P0; then it returns ELINK_STATUS_OK. No register is written on any of the three error returns.

functions.name: ciss_periodic
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: arg is the ciss_softc pointer that the periodic callout was armed with, and sc->ciss_cfg is mapped. If sc->ciss_cfg->heartbeat equals the saved sc->ciss_heartbeat it increments ciss_heart_attack; when that counter reaches exactly 3 it logs ADAPTER HEARTBEAT FAILED, calls ciss_disable_adapter and returns without sending a NOP, restarting notify or rescheduling the callout. If the heartbeat differs it saves the new value and resets ciss_heart_attack to 0. In every case that did not return early (heartbeat changed, or unchanged for the first or second time), if the global ciss_nop_message_heartbeat is nonzero and ciss_get_request succeeds it fills in a NOP message command with completion routine ciss_nop_complete and calls ciss_start; a nonzero ciss_start result is only logged and the request is not released here, and a ciss_get_request failure is silently ignored. Then if CISS_FLAG_NOTIFY_OK is not set in sc->ciss_flags it calls ciss_notify_event, and it finally calls callout_reset to run itself again after CISS_HEARTBEAT_RATE * hz ticks.

functions.name: aw_clk_np_register
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: clkdom and clkdef are valid pointers to a clock domain and an aw_clk_np_def. It calls clknode_create with aw_np_clknode_class and the generic clknode definition inside clkdef; if that returns NULL it returns 1 and nothing is copied or registered. Otherwise it copies offset, the n field (shift, width, value, flags) and the p field (shift, width, value, flags), gate_shift, lock_shift, lock_retries and flags from clkdef into the node's softc, computes n.mask and p.mask as ((1 << width) - 1) << shift (int arithmetic, so a width of 31 or more is not safe), calls clknode_register(clkdom, clk), and returns 0.

functions.name: t3_aq100x_phy_prep
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: pinfo points to an initialised port_info whose adapter is valid, phy_addr selects the PHY and mdio_ops gives the MDIO accessors. It initialises pinfo->phy with cphy_init (aq100x_ops, supported-feature mask, "1000/10GBASE-T"), toggles a GPIO bit (F_GPIO10_OUT_VAL if phy_addr is nonzero, else F_GPIO6_OUT_VAL) low then high to hard-reset the PHY with msleep delays, waits 1000 ms, then polls the PMA/PMD MII_BMCR register until BMCR_RESET clears (up to 500 polls of 10 ms). If that BMCR read returns an error or the value 0xffff it logs a warning and jumps to done; if BMCR_RESET is still set after the polling it logs a timeout warning and jumps to done. Otherwise it reads the firmware version, the BMCR power-down bit and the XAUI/1000-X settings, emitting CH_WARN warnings only when they look wrong, calls aq100x_set_defaults and discards its result. The value returned (at done) is the variable err, which is only ever assigned by the mdio_read inside the polling loop; so it returns that read's error code if one occurred, and 0 in all other cases, including the 0xffff-read and the reset-timeout exits (which are meant to let adapter preparation succeed). No locks are taken.

functions.name: t4_write_flash
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: data points to at least n readable bytes. Returns -EINVAL immediately, before touching the hardware, if addr is >= adapter->params.sf_size or if (addr & 0xff) + n exceeds SF_PAGE_SIZE. Otherwise it sends a write-enable and then the page-program command with the byte-swapped address through sf1_write, then feeds the data to sf1_write in chunks of up to 4 bytes (each chunk assembled most significant byte first into a word, and passed through cpu_to_be32 only when byte_oriented is zero), then calls flash_wait_op with 8 attempts. If any of those sf1_write or flash_wait_op calls returns nonzero, it writes 0 to A_SF_OP (releasing the serial flash) and returns that code; the page may then be partly programmed. On success of the programming steps it writes 0 to A_SF_OP, reads the whole page back with t4_read_flash (same byte_oriented value) and returns that call's error code if it fails; then compares the n bytes at addr's offset in the page with the supplied data, logging an error and returning -EIO on mismatch, else returning 0. The serial flash is unlocked (A_SF_OP written 0) on every return after the -EINVAL check, but not on the -EINVAL return, where it was never locked.

functions.name: ktls_act_open_cpl_size
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: none; isipv6 may be true or false. Returns sizeof(struct cpl_t6_act_open_req6) if isipv6 is true, otherwise sizeof(struct cpl_t6_act_open_req); no other value is returned and it has no side effects.

functions.name: cudbg_collect
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: handle points to a struct cudbg_private whose dbg_init (dbg_bitmap, adap, verbose, print, use_flash) is set up, outbuf is writable for *outbuf_size bytes and outbuf_size is writable. It writes the global cudbg_hdr at the start of outbuf, and treats the call as extended mode (flag_ext) if cudbg_hdr->data_len is nonzero when read after those writes. If use_flash is set and t4_get_flash_params fails, use_flash is cleared. If *outbuf_size is smaller than sizeof(struct cudbg_entity_hdr) * CUDBG_MAX_ENTITY it returns CUDBG_STATUS_SMALL_BUFF without updating *outbuf_size. Otherwise it loops over the entity numbers 1 to CUDBG_MAX_ENTITY-1 selected by the bitmap (or all, if the CUDBG_ALL bit is set), skipping the EXT entity: it obtains an entity header (in ext mode via get_next_ext_entity_hdr, whose nonzero return makes the function return that code immediately; in normal mode via get_entity_hdr, whose nonzero result is only stored in cudbg_hdr->hdr_flags), skips large entities when the remaining buffer is at most BUFFER_WARN_LIMIT (recording them for a retry) and firmware-dependent entities when firmware is not attached, and otherwise runs the entity's process function. If an entity fails, its header size is set to 0 and the offset is restored to its start; its hdr_flags, sys_err and sys_warn are recorded in its header, sys_err turning the status into CUDBG_SYSTEM_ERROR, and none of this is returned to the caller. A second loop retries the entities that were skipped as large, with the same header handling and the same early return on a get_next_ext_entity_hdr failure. In normal mode total_size grows by each entity size; it then sets cudbg_hdr->data_len and *outbuf_size to total_size, adds ext_size to *outbuf_size in ext mode, and returns 0, so per-entity failures do not change the return value. Entities are optionally written to flash through wr_entity_to_flash when use_flash is set.

functions.name: process_socket_event
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ep points to a valid c4iw_ep with com.so set. It reads ep->com.state once into a local. If the state is DEAD it only logs a trace message and returns. If the state is CONNECTING it calls process_connected and returns. If the state is LISTEN it takes the listen socket lock, then loops: solisten_dequeue(listen_so, &new_so, SOCK_NONBLOCK); if that returns an error it returns at once without calling SOLISTEN_UNLOCK itself (the code comment says solisten_dequeue returns with the lock released); otherwise it calls process_newconn(lep, new_so), re-takes the listen lock and repeats while listen_so->sol_qlen is nonzero, and finally unlocks and returns. For other states: if so->so_error is set it calls process_conn_error and returns; else if the receive side has SBS_CANTRCVMORE set and the saved state is <= CLOSING it calls process_peer_close and returns unless SS_ISDISCONNECTED is also set, in which case it continues; then if SS_ISDISCONNECTED is set it calls process_close_complete and returns; else if the receive buffer has data (sbused) it calls process_data and returns. If none of those apply, then in a kernel built with INVARIANTS the MPASS asserts the state is MPA_REQ_RCVD or MORIBUND (and panics otherwise); when assertions are compiled out and the state is neither MPA_REQ_RCVD nor MORIBUND, an Unprocessed socket event error is logged; no handler is called. The function returns nothing.

functions.name: send_mpa_reply
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ep points to a valid endpoint with mpa_attr, ird, ord and com.so set, and pdata points to at least plen bytes when plen is nonzero. It sizes the MPA message as sizeof(struct mpa_message) + plen, plus sizeof(struct mpa_v2_conn_params) when mpa_attr.version is 2 and enhanced_rdma_conn is set. It returns -ENOMEM if the M_NOWAIT malloc of that buffer fails, with ep unchanged. It then fills the key (MPA_KEY_REP), flags (MPA_CRC if crc_enabled, MPA_MARKERS if the global markers_enabled), revision and private_data_size; in the v2 enhanced case it also sets MPA_ENHANCED_RDMA_CONN, adds the v2 parameter size, fills ird and ord from ep->ird and ep->ord, adds the peer-to-peer model bit and an RDMA-write or read RTR bit only when the global peer2peer is set, ep->mpa_attr.p2p_type is not disabled and the global p2p_type is the matching value, copies the v2 parameters into private_data, and copies plen bytes of pdata after them only if ep->plen is nonzero (the condition tests ep->plen, the copy length is the argument plen). In the other case it copies plen bytes of pdata when plen is nonzero. It then allocates an mbuf chain with m_getm (M_NOWAIT); if that fails it frees the MPA buffer and returns -ENOMEM before changing ep. Otherwise it copies the message into the mbufs, frees the MPA buffer, sets ep->com.state to MPA_REP_SENT, adds the message length to ep->snd_seq, calls sosend with MSG_DONTWAIT passing the mbuf, and returns the negated sosend return value (0 on success). State and snd_seq are updated before sosend is called and are not rolled back if it fails.

functions.name: poll_cq
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: cq is a valid t4_cq and wq is either NULL or the t4_wq of the QP that owns the next CQE; cqe, cqe_flushed, cookie and credit point to writable storage. It sets *cqe_flushed and *credit to 0, then calls t4_next_cqe(cq, &hw_cqe); if that returns nonzero it returns that value and consumes nothing. Once a CQE has been fetched, every later path ends at skip_cqe, which consumes it (t4_swcq_consume for a software CQE, otherwise t4_hwcq_consume) and returns ret. Paths with ret = -EAGAIN and no completion copied: wq is NULL; wq->flushed and the CQE is not a software CQE; FW_RI_TERMINATE opcode; a read-response CQE of type 1, an unsolicited one (WRID_STAG 1) or one for an unsignaled read (each of the first two also marks the wq in error when CQE_STATUS is nonzero); an RQ completion when the receive queue is empty (also marks the wq in error); and a send completion whose SQ index differs from wq->sq.cidx, which is stored in the software SQ entry and followed by flush_completed_wrs. For a C4IW_DRAIN_OPCODE CQE it sets *cookie to the drain cookie, copies the CQE to *cqe and returns 0 without consuming any SQ or RQ entry. Otherwise, if the CQE status is nonzero or the wq is in error it sets *cqe_flushed to 1 only when the status is T4_ERR_SWFLUSH (else 0) and marks the wq in error; an RQ completion whose MSN differs from wq->rq.msn is marked with T4_ERR_MSN and the wq is put in error. On the proc_cqe path it copies the CQE to *cqe, and for an SQ completion adjusts sq.in_use, sets sq.cidx, sets *cookie to the stored wr_id, consumes the SQ entry and calls flush_completed_wrs; for an RQ completion it sets *cookie to the RQ wr_id and consumes the RQ entry. Those proc_cqe paths return 0.

functions.name: c4iw_modify_qp
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: rhp, qhp and attrs are valid and the caller does not hold qhp->mutex. The function takes qhp->mutex and, after releasing it at the out label, runs deferred actions outside the lock. If mask has C4IW_QP_ATTR_VALID_MODIFY: it returns -EIO if the QP is not in C4IW_QP_STATE_IDLE; otherwise it applies the RDMA read/write/bind flags, and returns -EINVAL if max_ord exceeds c4iw_max_read_depth or max_ird exceeds cur_max_read_depth(rhp) (attributes are stored into qhp->attr only after all checks pass). If C4IW_QP_ATTR_NEXT_STATE is not in mask, or the current state already equals next_state, it returns the current ret (0 after a successful attribute update) with no state change. It returns -EINPROGRESS if the current state is ERROR or later and the requested state is TERMINATE. Then by current state: IDLE accepts RTS (needs both C4IW_QP_ATTR_LLP_STREAM_HANDLE and C4IW_QP_ATTR_MPA_ATTR else -EINVAL; sets the mpa attributes, endpoint and RTS state, takes an endpoint reference with c4iw_get_ep, calls rdma_init and goes to the err path if it fails) and ERROR (sets ERROR and flush_qp), other targets give -EINVAL. RTS accepts CLOSING (rdma_fini, err path on failure; for a non-internal call it also takes an extra endpoint reference and schedules a disconnect), TERMINATE (sets state and error codes; non-internal calls schedule terminate and disconnect, internal calls call rdma_fini and go to the err path on failure, otherwise return normally), and ERROR (always takes the err path, which for a non-internal call also schedules an abort-disconnect), other targets give -EINVAL. CLOSING returns -EINVAL for a non-internal call unless it is a kernel QP (no uobject) going to ERROR; it accepts IDLE (flush_qp, state IDLE, drops the endpoint with c4iw_put_ep) and ERROR (err path), other targets give -EINVAL via the err path. ERROR accepts only IDLE, and only if the SQ and RQ are empty (else -EINVAL). TERMINATE: a non-internal call gets -EINVAL, an internal call takes the err path; any unknown state gives -EINVAL via the err path. The err path clears llp_stream_handle and qhp->ep, forces state ERROR, flushes the QP, wakes waiters, and sets flags so that the endpoint is aborted and dereferenced (one c4iw_put_ep for the QP's reference, and for a scheduled disconnect another one after __c4iw_ep_disconnect). The return value is ret: 0 on success and on the no-op cases, or the negative error above; the err path leaves ret as it was, so it can return 0 while moving the QP to ERROR.

functions.name: update_hw_clip_table
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller holds clip_db_lock (asserted with mtx_assert). It calls begin_synchronized_op(sc, NULL, HOLD_LOCK, "t4clip") and returns its error if nonzero, in which case no synchronized operation is open. Otherwise, if hw_all_ok(sc) is false it ends the synchronized operation and returns 0 with sc->clip_pending untouched. Otherwise it processes sc->clip_pending from the head until the queue is empty or it stops. For an entry with clip_idx == -1 (pending add): if both ce->refcount and cde->krn_ref are 0 it removes and frees the entry (and frees the database entry when its adp_ref reaches 0); otherwise it calls add_lip: FW_ENOMEM makes it stop and return 0 leaving that entry (and the later ones) queued, any other nonzero error is logged, stops the loop and is returned with the entry still queued, and on success the entry is dequeued and marked not pending. For an entry with a valid clip_idx (pending delete): if both counts are 0 it calls del_lip, logs a nonzero result, treats FW_EPROTO as success, returns any other error leaving the entry queued, and otherwise removes and frees the entry as above; if either count is nonzero it just dequeues the entry and clears pending. On every return after a successful begin_synchronized_op it calls end_synchronized_op(sc, LOCK_HELD); clip_db_lock is still held on return. It returns 0 if the queue was drained or it stopped on FW_ENOMEM or on hw_all_ok being false, and otherwise the error from add_lip or del_lip.

functions.name: toe_capability
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller holds the adapter's synchronized-operation lock (ASSERT_SYNCHRONIZED_OP) and vi is a VI of the adapter. It returns ENODEV if the adapter is not offload capable and ENXIO if hw_all_ok fails. When enable is true: in a KERN_TLS build, if KERN_TLS_ON is set on a T6 adapter it counts the interfaces with IFCAP_TXTLS enabled and returns EAGAIN if any, otherwise calls t6_config_kern_tls(sc, false) and returns its error if nonzero; this happens before the check for TOE already being enabled, so it also runs when TOE is already on. Then if IFCAP_TOE is already set on vi->ifp it returns 0 with no counter change. Otherwise it runs vi_init on vi and on the port's first VI if their VI_INIT_DONE flags are not set (returning a failure code), and if offload_map already has the port's bit set it increments pi->uld_vis and returns 0. Otherwise it activates the TOM ULD if it is not active (logging when the error is EAGAIN and returning any nonzero error), tries to activate the iWARP and iSCSI ULDs ignoring their results, then increments pi->uld_vis and sets the port's bit in offload_map if the count was previously 0, and returns 0. When enable is false: if IFCAP_TOE is not set it returns 0; otherwise it decrements pi->uld_vis and clears the port's offload_map bit when the count reaches 0, then returns 0. The MPASS checks assert expected states only in builds with assertions.

functions.name: service_iq_fl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: iq is a valid ingress queue in IQS_BUSY state with IQ_HAS_FL set. Only when INET or INET6 is compiled in, if IQ_ADJ_CREDIT is set it clears the flag and checks the descriptor at cidx: if its generation bit does not equal iq->gen it flushes all LRO state, writes the SGE GTS register crediting one descriptor, and returns 0 without refilling the freelist; if it matches, the count of consumed descriptors starts at 1. It then processes descriptors while their generation bit equals iq->gen, with limit = budget if budget is nonzero, else iq->qsize / 16. For a free-list-buffer response it may advance to the next rx buffer, and when the hardware consumer index has moved by more than 4 since the snapshot it refills the freelist (64 buffers) under the FL lock; a CPL_RX_PKT is passed to eth_rx and any other one gets its payload from get_fl_payload and then goes to the CPL handler table; if eth_rx returns nonzero or get_fl_payload returns NULL the loop is left without consuming the current descriptor. A CPL-type response calls the CPL handler for its opcode. An interrupt-type response panics if its qid is below 1024, otherwise calls t4_an_handler. An unknown response type triggers KASSERT and logs an error (continuing if assertions are off). Each processed descriptor advances cidx, wrapping and flipping the generation bit at sidx. When the consumed count reaches limit, it writes the GTS register with that count and, if LRO is enabled, not sorted-before-LRO and sc->lro_timeout is nonzero, flushes inactive LRO entries; with a nonzero budget it then returns EINPROGRESS directly (no freelist refill at that point); with budget 0 it resets the count to 0 and continues. At the common exit (generation mismatch or the early exits) when IQ_LRO_ENABLED is set it holds back one credit and sets IQ_ADJ_CREDIT if the count is positive and more than 8 LRO mbufs are pending, otherwise flushes all LRO state; it writes the GTS register with the remaining count, refills the freelist with 64 buffers under the FL lock, adds the freelist to the starved list if refill_fl reports starvation, and returns 0.

functions.name: do_peer_close
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: called as the CPL_PEER_CLOSE handler with m == NULL (KASSERTed) and a tid that lookup_tid maps to a toepcb with a valid inp. It returns 0 on every path. If toep->flags has TPF_SYNQE it returns immediately without taking any lock. Otherwise it enters the vnet and network epoch and write-locks the inp. If TPF_ABORT_SHUTDOWN is set it skips to the common exit. Otherwise, when the ULP mode is TCPDDP it takes DDP_LOCK and calls handle_ddp_close only if a DDP buffer is active, then releases DDP_LOCK; it calls socantrcvmore on the socket and sets tp->rcv_nxt from the CPL (the old and new values are compared only in a KASSERT, and not for RDMA or T6+ iSCSI modes). Then by TCP state: SYN_RECEIVED sets t_starttime and, like ESTABLISHED, moves to CLOSE_WAIT; FIN_WAIT_1 moves to CLOSING; FIN_WAIT_2 restores the socket protocol, detaches the toepcb from the tcpcb, calls tcp_twstart, exits the epoch and vnet, takes the inp write lock again, calls final_cpl_received(toep) and returns 0 without passing through the common exit; any other state only logs an error. All paths other than the FIN_WAIT_2 one reach the common exit, which drops the inp write lock, exits the epoch and restores the vnet before returning 0.

functions.name: insert_ddp_data
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller holds the inp write lock and the DDP lock of toep (both asserted), and n bytes of data were placed by DDP before the connection fell out of DDP. It adds n to tp->rcv_nxt and, unless USE_DDP_RX_FLOW_CONTROL is defined, KASSERTs tp->rcv_wnd >= n and subtracts n from tp->rcv_wnd. Then while toep->ddp.active_count > 0 it takes the active buffer. In DDP_RCVBUF mode it places min(n, remaining space of the buffer), queues that many bytes with queue_ddp_rcvbuf_mbuf if nonzero, calls complete_ddp_buffer and reduces n by the amount placed. Otherwise it takes the buffer's AIO job, places min(n, bytes still wanted by the job), counts statistics, and: if the cancel function can no longer be cleared (a cancel is in progress) it only adds the placed amount to job->aio_received; else if some data was received in total (copied + placed != 0) it completes the job with that byte count; else it tries to put the job back at the head of the pending queue (incrementing waiting_count) and cancels it if that is not possible; then it reduces n by the amount placed and calls complete_ddp_buffer. After the loop MPASS(n == 0) asserts (in INVARIANTS builds only) that all n bytes were placed; in other builds a nonzero n would be left unplaced and the function returns nothing.

functions.name: t4_pmtu_update
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller holds the inp write lock (asserted), mtu is positive (MPASS) and seq is in network byte order, snd_una and snd_max being in host order. It converts seq to host order. It returns without changing anything if the ULP mode is ULP_MODE_NONE and seq is outside [tp->snd_una, tp->snd_max) (the range check is skipped for other ULP modes), or if the MTU index chosen as the largest table entry not above mtu is not smaller than toep->params.mtu_idx (the path MTU is never raised), or if start_wrq_wr for the control queue fails (in which case it logs an error). Otherwise it builds and commits an atomic compound work request with two SET_TCB_FIELD operations (one setting the T_MAXSEG field to the new index, one clearing the timestamp field to trigger a retransmit), then sets toep->params.mtu_idx to the new index, sets tp->t_maxseg to the table MTU minus the IPv6 or IPv4 header and TCP header sizes, and sets toep->params.emss to that value minus TCPOLEN_TSTAMP_APPA when TF_RCVD_TSTMP is set. It then calls send_mss_flowc_wr, which logs an error and sends nothing if tx credits or tx sdesc entries are insufficient or the work request cannot be allocated, and otherwise sends a flowc work request carrying the new emss. Finally, if sc->tt.update_hc_on_pmtu_change is nonzero it calls tcp_hc_updatemtu with the foreign address and fib number and the requested mtu. It returns nothing.

functions.name: cyapa_attach
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is a newbus device whose softc is a cyapa_softc not yet attached. It sets sc->reporting_mode to 1 first, then calls init_device(dev, &cap, 0); if that returns nonzero it returns ENXIO (reporting_mode has already been set, but no mutex, knlist, evdev, hook or device node exists yet). Otherwise it initialises the softc mutex and the selinfo knlist on it, stores dev, computes the X/Y resolution and physical size and the button mask from the capability data, prints a summary line, fills in the hw and mode structures (PS/2 protocol, packet size, rate 100, resolution 4) and sets the interrupt hook function to cyapa_start with dev as argument. With EVDEV_SUPPORT it allocates an evdev, sets its name, phys, id, flags and supported events/keys/axes, and registers it; if evdev_register fails it destroys the mutex and returns ENOMEM (the evdev is not freed on that path and the knlist is not destroyed). It then calls config_intrhook_establish; if that fails it frees the evdev (with EVDEV_SUPPORT), destroys the mutex and returns ENOMEM (the knlist is not destroyed). On success it creates the /dev/cyapa<unit> node with owner root, group wheel, mode 0600, sets si_drv1 to the softc, and returns 0.

functions.name: dc_rxeof
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc is a valid dc_softc and the caller holds the softc lock (DC_LOCK_ASSERT). Starting at sc->dc_cdata.dc_rx_prod it loops over RX descriptors while IFF_DRV_RUNNING is set on the interface. The loop is left, and the current index stored into sc->dc_cdata.dc_rx_prod, when (with DEVICE_POLLING and IFCAP_POLLING enabled) sc->rxcycles is not positive, when a descriptor still has DC_RXSTAT_OWN set, or when IFF_DRV_RUNNING has been cleared; sc->rxcycles is decremented once per descriptor examined in polling mode. Each descriptor examined past the ownership check increments rx_npkts, including PNIC-workaround fragments, errored frames, and frames that are dropped. On PNIC-bug hardware (DC_PNIC_RX_BUG_WAR) a non-whole-frame descriptor is skipped until its last fragment, then dc_pnic_rx_bug_war repairs it. For a descriptor with DC_RXSTAT_RXERR that is not a giant frame without another error flag, it increments IFCOUNTER_IERRORS (and IFCOUNTER_COLLISIONS if DC_RXSTAT_COLLSEEN) and calls dc_discard_rxbuf; if DC_RXSTAT_CRCERR is set it continues with the next descriptor, otherwise it clears IFF_DRV_RUNNING, calls dc_init_locked(sc) and returns rx_npkts immediately without storing dc_rx_prod. For a good frame it subtracts ETHER_CRC_LEN and either (on __NO_STRICT_ALIGNMENT) replaces the ring buffer with dc_newbuf, or on dc_newbuf failure discards the buffer and increments IFCOUNTER_IQDROPS, or (strict alignment) copies it with m_devget and discards the original buffer, counting IFCOUNTER_IQDROPS if m_devget returns NULL. A delivered frame increments IFCOUNTER_IPACKETS and is passed to if_input with the softc lock dropped around the call and re-taken afterwards. The function returns rx_npkts; the softc lock is held on return.

functions.name: pnphy_service
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc, mii and mii->mii_media.ifm_cur are valid. For MII_MEDIACHG with the interface not IFF_UP it falls out of the switch; with the interface up, a current subtype of IFM_100_TX or IFM_10_T sets mii_media_active to IFM_ETHER plus that subtype (adding IFM_FDX if the entry has it), calls MIIBUS_STATCHG and returns 0 without calling PHY_STATUS or mii_phy_update; any other subtype returns EINVAL with no media state changed. For MII_TICK with the interface not IFF_UP it returns 0 immediately without calling PHY_STATUS or mii_phy_update; with the interface up, and for MII_POLLSTAT, MII_MEDIACHG while down, or any other cmd value, it calls PHY_STATUS(sc) and mii_phy_update(sc, cmd) and returns 0.

functions.name: qman_portals_fdt_attach
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is a newbus device with an OFW node. It reads the address/size cell counts of the parent node and of its own node with get_addr_props, then loads the "ranges" property. If the property has fewer than addr + paddr + size cells it returns ENXIO at once without calling OF_prop_free on the ranges buffer and without setting sc->sc_dp_pa or sc_dp_size. Otherwise it decodes the property into portal physical address (the child base plus parent base) and size, frees the buffer with OF_prop_free, and stores sc_dp_pa and sc_dp_size. It then iterates the child nodes, stopping once mp_ncpus portals have been counted; children not compatible with "fsl,qman-portal" are skipped, as are children for which no CPU handle can be found (neither the cpu-handle property nor qman_portal_find_cpu gives a positive value). If the CPU node's "reg" cannot be read it prints a message and returns ENXIO immediately, without calling qman_portals_detach. After counting the CPU, a child whose devinfo setup, "reg" or "interrupts" processing fails is skipped (after freeing the resource list and destroying the devinfo where they had been created). If dpaa_portal_alloc_res fails it frees the resource list, destroys the devinfo, calls qman_portals_detach(dev) and returns ENXIO. After the loop it destroys the devinfo and returns the result of qman_portals_attach(dev).

functions.name: drm_context_switch
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is a valid DRM device. It atomically tests and sets bit 0 of dev->context_flag; if the bit was already set it logs "Reentering" and returns -EBUSY, leaving the bit set. Otherwise it logs the switch and, if new equals dev->last_context, clears bit 0 again; in every case that reaches this point it returns 0 (when new differs from dev->last_context the flag is left set). It does not itself change dev->last_context.

functions.name: drm_switchctx
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev, data (a struct drm_ctx) and file_priv are valid. It logs ctx->handle and returns drm_context_switch(dev, dev->last_context, ctx->handle) unchanged: -EBUSY if dev->context_flag bit 0 was already set (flag left as it was), otherwise 0, with the bit cleared again when ctx->handle equals dev->last_context and left set otherwise.

functions.name: drm_crtc_helper_set_config
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller holds the mode config lock as the DRM code expects (not checked here). Returns -EINVAL if set is NULL, set->crtc is NULL, or set->crtc->helper_private is NULL. If set->mode is NULL it sets set->fb to NULL; if set->fb is then NULL it returns drm_crtc_helper_disable(set->crtc) directly, before allocating any backup, so the crtc is disabled and nothing else in this function runs. Otherwise it allocates zeroed backup arrays for all crtcs, encoders and connectors (M_NOWAIT), returning -ENOMEM and freeing what was allocated if any allocation fails, with nothing modified; it copies the current crtc/encoder/connector structs into them and works out whether the change is a full mode set (mode_changed: no current fb, different depth or bits per pixel, a different mode, a changed encoder or crtc binding, or a flip needed without a mode_set_base hook) or only a flip (fb_changed: same-format fb or changed x/y). It rebinds connectors to encoders using best_encoder for the connectors named in set; a NULL best_encoder, or an encoder that cannot work with the new crtc (drm_encoder_crtc_ok), leads to failure with -EINVAL. If mode_changed, it sets crtc->enabled from drm_helper_crtc_in_use; only if the crtc is in use does it call drm_crtc_helper_set_mode (failure restores the old fb and gives -EINVAL) and turns the listed connectors' DPMS on; in both cases it then calls drm_helper_disable_unused_functions. Else if fb_changed it updates x, y and fb and calls crtc_funcs->mode_set_base; a nonzero return restores the old fb and fails with that code. If neither flag is set nothing is applied. On success it frees the three backups and returns 0. On any failure it copies the saved crtc/encoder/connector structs back, tries to restore the old mode with drm_crtc_helper_set_mode when mode_changed was set (only logging an error if that fails), frees the backups and returns the error.

functions.name: drm_wait_vblank
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev and data (a union drm_wait_vblank) are valid; file_priv is used only on the event path. Returns -EINVAL without taking a vblank reference if dev->irq_enabled is not set, if the request type has _DRM_VBLANK_SIGNAL set, if it has bits outside the supported type/flags/high-crtc mask, or if the selected crtc (high-crtc field if nonzero, else 1 for _DRM_VBLANK_SECONDARY, else 0) is >= dev->num_crtcs. It then calls drm_vblank_get and returns its error if nonzero. With the reference held and the current count read, a relative request has seq added to the requested sequence; an absolute request is left; any other type value gives -EINVAL and goes to done. If _DRM_VBLANK_EVENT is set it returns drm_queue_vblank_event(dev, crtc, vblwait, file_priv) directly, without calling drm_vblank_put here, since the reference is kept for the event (what that function does on its failures was not read). Otherwise, with _DRM_VBLANK_NEXTONMISS and a requested sequence already passed it moves the request to seq + 1, records last_vblank_wait, then under vblank_time_lock sleeps with msleep (PCATCH, 3 second timeout) until the vblank count reaches the requested sequence or irq_enabled clears; a nonzero sleep result ends the wait and is returned negated (ERESTART becomes -ERESTARTSYS; a timeout gives -EWOULDBLOCK, a signal -EINTR). Unless the result is -EINTR it fills reply.sequence, reply.tval_sec and reply.tval_usec from drm_vblank_count_and_time. At done, on every non-event path after drm_vblank_get succeeded, it calls drm_vblank_put and returns ret (0 on a completed wait).

functions.name: drm_setmaster_ioctl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev and file_priv are valid and file_priv->minor is non-NULL (it is dereferenced); data is unused. It returns 0 immediately if file_priv->is_master is already set. It returns -EINVAL if file_priv->minor->master is set and differs from file_priv->master, if file_priv->master is NULL, or if file_priv->minor->master is set at all. Otherwise, holding DRM_LOCK(dev), it stores drm_master_get(file_priv->master) into file_priv->minor->master and sets file_priv->is_master to 1; if dev->driver->master_set exists and returns nonzero it sets is_master back to 0 and drops the master reference with drm_master_put on minor->master. The result of master_set is not returned: after the lock is released the function returns 0 in every case that passes the checks.

functions.name: ttm_bo_handle_move_mem
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: bo and mem are valid and the caller has bo reserved as the TTM code expects (not checked here). If either region is PCI-mapped or the old and new caching placements share no bit, it takes the old memory type manager's io lock (an error from that lock goes to out_err), unmaps the bo's virtual mappings and releases the lock. If the new memory type is not fixed it creates the bo->ttm if absent (ttm_bo_add_ttm), sets its caching with ttm_tt_set_placement_caching and, when the target is not TTM_PL_SYSTEM, binds it with ttm_tt_bind; any failure of these goes to out_err without any move_notify call. If bo currently lives in TTM_PL_SYSTEM it then calls the driver move_notify (if any), sets bo->mem = *mem, clears mem->mm_node and skips the move. Otherwise it calls move_notify (if any) and performs the move with ttm_bo_move_ttm when neither old nor new type is fixed, else with the driver move hook if present, else ttm_bo_move_memcpy. If the move fails and move_notify exists it calls move_notify again with the memory regions swapped around the call (bo->mem is the same value after the swap sequence), and goes to out_err. On success: if bo->evicted it calls invalidate_caches (a failure is only printed) and clears evicted; if bo->mem.mm_node is non-NULL it sets bo->offset from bo->mem.start and the manager's gpu_offset and bo->cur_placement from bo->mem.placement, else it sets only bo->offset to 0 and leaves cur_placement alone; it returns 0. At out_err it takes the memory type of the current bo->mem and, if that type is fixed and bo->ttm exists, unbinds and destroys the ttm and sets bo->ttm to NULL; it returns the error code. The io lock is released on all paths where it was taken.

functions.name: e1000_set_d0_lplu_state_82575
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hw is a valid e1000_hw. If hw->phy.ops.read_reg is NULL it touches no register and returns E1000_SUCCESS. Otherwise it reads IGP02E1000_PHY_POWER_MGMT and returns that error if the read fails. If active is true it sets the D0_LPLU bit and writes the register back (returning the write error if any), then reads IGP01E1000_PHY_PORT_CONFIG, clears the SmartSpeed bit and writes it back; the status of that port-config read is overwritten by the write's status, so only the write error is returned in this branch (the cleared bit is written even if the read failed, using whatever data holds). If active is false it clears D0_LPLU and writes the power-management register; if phy->smart_speed is e1000_smart_speed_on or e1000_smart_speed_off, that write's status is overwritten by the next port-config read and a read or write failure there is returned after setting or clearing the SmartSpeed bit accordingly; for any other smart_speed value no further access is made and the status of the power-management write is returned. The function returns E1000_SUCCESS or the status described above.

functions.name: e1000_update_nvm_checksum_ich8lan
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hw is an initialised e1000_hw with NVM acquire, release and reload operations set. It first calls e1000_update_nvm_checksum_generic and returns its error if nonzero (that call may itself modify shadow RAM words). If nvm->type is not e1000_nvm_flash_sw it returns the generic call's result (0) without acquiring the NVM, committing to flash or resetting the shadow cache. Otherwise it calls nvm->ops.acquire (result ignored), detects the valid bank (a detection failure is not returned: bank 0 is assumed), erases the opposite flash bank (an erase error goes to release), then writes each of the E1000_SHADOW_RAM_WORDS words to the new bank byte by byte (a modified shadow word is used, otherwise the word is read from the old bank), with the signature word forced to have bits 15:14 set; a read or write error stops the loop. After a failed copy it releases the NVM and returns the error. After a successful copy it reads back the new bank's signature word and writes its high byte with bit 14 cleared, then writes 0 to the high byte of the old bank's signature word; an error in these steps goes to release. Only when everything succeeded does it clear every shadow_ram entry to unmodified and value 0xFFFF. It always calls nvm->ops.release on the flash path; if the result is zero it then calls nvm->ops.reload and waits 10 ms; on error the NVM is released but not reloaded and the shadow cache is left as it was. It returns the first nonzero status, logging it, or 0.

functions.name: e1000_kmrn_lock_loss_workaround_ich8lan
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hw is an initialised e1000_hw with ich8lan device-specific data. If dev_spec->kmrn_lock_loss_workaround_enabled is false it returns E1000_SUCCESS immediately without any hardware access. Otherwise it calls e1000_phy_has_link_generic(hw, 1, 0, &link) (which accesses the PHY; its return value is ignored) and returns E1000_SUCCESS if link is false.
