With link up it makes up to 10 attempts: each reads IGP3_KMRN_DIAG twice through phy.ops.read_reg, returning that read's error code if either read fails; if the second read has the PCS lock-loss bit clear it returns E1000_SUCCESS; otherwise it calls phy.ops.reset and waits 5 ms and tries again. If all 10 attempts show lock loss it sets E1000_PHY_CTRL_GBE_DISABLE and E1000_PHY_CTRL_NOND0A_GBE_DISABLE in E1000_PHY_CTRL, calls e1000_gig_downshift_workaround_ich8lan, and returns -E1000_ERR_PHY.

functions.name: e1000_config_fc_after_link_up_generic
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hw is an initialised e1000_hw with mac, phy and fc fields valid. First step: if mac->autoneg_failed is set and the media is fiber or internal serdes, or if it is clear and the media is copper, it calls e1000_force_mac_fc_generic and returns its error if nonzero (so for copper with autoneg_failed set, and for fiber/serdes without autoneg_failed, nothing is forced here). Copper with mac->autoneg: it reads PHY_STATUS twice (returning a read error if either fails); if MII_SR_AUTONEG_COMPLETE is clear it returns E1000_SUCCESS without changing hw->fc.current_mode (the MAC flow-control bits may already have been programmed by the first step); otherwise it reads the advertisement and link-partner registers (returning any read error), derives hw->fc.current_mode from the PAUSE/ASM_DIR bits (full or rx_pause if both PAUSE bits are set, depending on fc.requested_mode; tx_pause, rx_pause or none in the asymmetric cases), calls mac->ops.get_link_up_info (error returned) and forces current_mode to e1000_fc_none on half duplex, then calls e1000_force_mac_fc_generic (error returned). Internal serdes with mac->autoneg: it reads PCS_LSTAT; if auto-negotiation is not complete it returns E1000_SUCCESS without changing current_mode or the PCS/MAC bits; otherwise it derives current_mode from the PCS advertisement and link-partner registers the same way (without the half-duplex override), sets E1000_PCS_LCTL_FORCE_FCTRL in PCS_LCTL and calls e1000_force_mac_fc_generic (error returned). In all other cases it returns E1000_SUCCESS.

functions.name: e1000_check_for_serdes_link_generic
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hw is an initialised e1000_hw with mac->txcw set. It reads CTRL, STATUS and RXCW. If the link-up status bit is clear and no /C/ is being received: on the first such observation (mac->autoneg_failed false) it sets mac->autoneg_failed to true and returns E1000_SUCCESS immediately without touching serdes_has_link; on later observations it clears the autoneg-enable bit in TXCW, sets SLU and full-duplex in CTRL and calls e1000_config_fc_after_link_up_generic, returning that call's error if nonzero. Otherwise, if CTRL has SLU set and /C/ is being received, it restores TXCW to mac->txcw, clears SLU in CTRL and sets mac->serdes_has_link true. Otherwise, if autoneg is currently disabled in TXCW (forced link), it waits 10 us and re-reads RXCW: with sync and no invalid codeword it sets serdes_has_link true, with no sync it sets it false, and with sync plus invalid codeword it leaves it unchanged. After that, if autoneg is enabled in TXCW it re-reads STATUS and, depending on the link-up bit and the RXCW sync and invalid-codeword bits after a 10 us wait, sets serdes_has_link true (up, synced, no invalid codeword) or false (any other combination). It returns E1000_SUCCESS at the end of those steps; the only other return value is the error from e1000_config_fc_after_link_up_generic.

functions.name: e1000_load_firmware
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hw is an initialised e1000_hw and buffer holds at least length readable bytes. Returns -E1000_ERR_CONFIG if hw->mac.type is below e1000_i210 or if HICR lacks the host-enable or memory-base-enable bit; returns -E1000_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT if length is 0, not a multiple of 4, or above E1000_HI_FW_MAX_LENGTH. Otherwise it reads ICR_V2, sets the FW reset-enable and FW reset bits in HICR, and polls ICR_V2 up to 2 * E1000_HI_COMMAND_TIMEOUT times (1 ms apart) for E1000_ICR_MNG; it returns -E1000_ERR_HOST_INTERFACE_COMMAND if the loop index equals exactly E1000_HI_COMMAND_TIMEOUT afterwards (so the check is on that index value, not on the loop having run out). It then polls FWSM up to E1000_HI_COMMAND_TIMEOUT ms for FW valid with the host-interface-enable-only mode, returning -E1000_ERR_HOST_INTERFACE_COMMAND on timeout. It writes the buffer as 32-bit words into the host interface RAM, setting HIBBA at each block boundary, sets the E1000_HICR_C bit in HICR and polls up to E1000_HI_COMMAND_TIMEOUT ms for it to clear; if it does not clear it returns -E1000_ERR_HOST_INTERFACE_COMMAND, else E1000_SUCCESS. No locks are taken.

functions.name: e1000_reset_hw_vf
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hw and its mailbox ops (check_for_rst, write_posted, read_posted) are set up. It sets the reset bit in CTRL, then polls mbx->ops.check_for_rst(hw, 0) every 5 us until it reports a reset or E1000_VF_INIT_TIMEOUT iterations pass. If the poll ran out (timeout is 0) it returns the initial value -E1000_ERR_MAC_INIT with perm_addr unchanged. Otherwise it sets mbx->timeout to E1000_VF_MBX_INIT_TIMEOUT, posts a one-word E1000_VF_RESET message (the write_posted result is ignored), waits 10 ms, and calls read_posted for 3 words. If read_posted returns nonzero that error code is returned as is (not necessarily -E1000_ERR_MAC_INIT) and perm_addr is unchanged. If it succeeds and the first word equals E1000_VF_RESET | E1000_VT_MSGTYPE_ACK, the 6 bytes following that word are copied into hw->mac.perm_addr and 0 is returned; otherwise it returns -E1000_ERR_MAC_INIT without copying.

functions.name: reset_system
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: none beyond type being an enum efi_reset value. Returns EINVAL if type is not EFI_RESET_COLD, EFI_RESET_WARM or EFI_RESET_SHUTDOWN. Returns ENXIO if the global efi_runtime is NULL. Otherwise it builds a zeroed efirt_callinfo for the "rt_reset" runtime service with four arguments (type, 0, 0, NULL) and the physical address of the runtime reset method, calls efi_call on it, and returns efi_call's return value unchanged. The function takes no locks itself.

functions.name: ena_update_buf_ring_size
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: adapter is a valid ENA adapter and new_buf_ring_size is the requested TX buf_ring size. It saves the old size, stores the new one in adapter->buf_ring_size, records whether ENA_FLAG_DEV_UP was set, calls ena_down, frees all I/O ring resources and re-initialises the rings with ena_init_io_rings_advanced. In a DEV_NETMAP build it then calls ena_reinit_netmap and returns its code immediately if nonzero (device left down, no reset triggered, no revert). If the device was up it calls ena_up; if that fails it logs, restores the old size, frees and re-initialises the rings again, (in a DEV_NETMAP build calls ena_reinit_netmap again and returns its code if nonzero), sets ENA_FLAG_DEV_UP_BEFORE_RESET and triggers a device reset with ENA_REGS_RESET_OS_TRIGGER; ena_up is not retried. The return value is rc: in a build without DEV_NETMAP it is the ena_up error in the failure case (0 on success); in a DEV_NETMAP build the successful second ena_reinit_netmap call overwrites rc, so after a failed ena_up it returns 0 once the reset has been triggered.

functions.name: ena_update_queue_size
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: adapter is a valid ENA adapter and new_tx_size and new_rx_size are the requested ring sizes. It stores the old and new requested TX and RX ring sizes, records whether ENA_FLAG_DEV_UP was set, calls ena_down and re-initialises the basic I/O rings (ena_init_io_rings_basic). In a DEV_NETMAP build it calls ena_reinit_netmap and returns its code immediately if nonzero (device left down with the new sizes, nothing reverted, no reset). If the device was up it calls ena_up; if that fails it logs, restores the old requested sizes, re-initialises the basic rings, (with DEV_NETMAP calls ena_reinit_netmap again and returns its code if nonzero), then calls ena_up a second time; if that second call fails it logs, sets ENA_FLAG_DEV_UP_BEFORE_RESET and triggers a device reset with ENA_REGS_RESET_OS_TRIGGER. It returns rc, which at that point is the result of the last ena_up call: 0 if the first ena_up succeeded or the retry with the old sizes succeeded (the first failure is then not reported), nonzero if the retry failed.

functions.name: ena_attach
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: pdev is a PCI device whose softc (struct ena_adapter) was allocated by the bus. It initialises defaults in the adapter, allocates a zeroed ena_com_dev (M_WAITOK) and stores it in adapter->ena_dev, and allocates the register BAR. If the register BAR allocation fails it returns ENOMEM after freeing only the ena_com_dev (label err_dev_free; no PCI resources, no ena_bus). It then allocates the separate MSI-X table BAR if its rid differs, returning ENOMEM through err_pci_free (which releases PCI resources and frees ena_dev) on failure. It allocates ena_dev->bus and stores the register tag and handle; if the handle is 0 it returns ENXIO via err_bus_free (frees the bus, releases PCI resources, frees ena_dev). ena_map_llq_mem_bar failure returns its code via err_bus_free; ena_device_init failure returns ENXIO via err_bus_free. After reading features and computing queue sizes, if ena_calc_io_queue_size fails or the maximum IO queue count is not positive it returns EFAULT via err_com_free, which additionally destroys the admin queue, host info and MMIO read request. TX and RX DMA tag setup failures return their codes via err_com_free and err_tx_tag_free (which frees the TX tag first); failure of ena_enable_msix_and_set_admin_interrupts returns its code via err_io_free (frees io ring resources and the RX DMA tag, then continues down through the labels below); failure of ena_com_allocate_customer_metrics_buffer returns its code via err_msix_free (frees stats, resets the device with ENA_REGS_RESET_INIT_ERR, frees the management IRQ and disables MSI-X); failure of ena_sysctl_allocate_customer_metrics_buffer returns its code via err_metrics_buffer_destroy (deletes the metrics buffer, then falls through the remaining labels). Each error path falls through all the later labels, so it performs the cleanup listed for its label and those below it. On success it also allocates stat counters, adds sysctl nodes, sets up the ifnet, creates and starts the reset and metrics taskqueues, with DEV_NETMAP attaches netmap (failure returns its code via err_detach, which detaches the ifnet, removes the media, frees customer_metrics_array and then falls through all the cleanup above), clears IFF_DRV_RUNNING and sets IFF_DRV_OACTIVE, sets ENA_FLAG_DEVICE_RUNNING, resets the timer and returns 0. On every failure path adapter->ena_dev is left pointing at freed memory once free(ena_dev) has run, and the taskqueues and ifnet created before the netmap step are not torn down except for the ifnet detach on the netmap failure path.

functions.name: _vnic_dev_cmd2
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: vdev->devcmd2 is an initialised devcmd2 controller (wq_ctrl, cmd_ring, result ring, posted, next_result, color, result_size), cmd is a devcmd word and wait is the number of poll iterations of 100 microseconds each; for write-direction commands the arguments are in vdev->args. It reads the TX fetch index and returns ENODEV if it is 0xFFFFFFFF. It returns EBUSY (after logging that the work queue is full) if advancing the posted index would equal the fetch index. Otherwise it fills the command ring slot at the posted index (cmd, flags, with DEVCMD2_FNORESULT set for _CMD_FLAGS_NOWAIT commands, and for _CMD_DIR_WRITE commands copies VNIC_DEVCMD_NARGS args from vdev->args), writes the new posted index to TX_POSTED_INDEX and stores it in dc2c->posted. If the slot has DEVCMD2_FNORESULT set it returns 0 immediately. Otherwise it takes the result entry at next_result and the current color, advances next_result (wrapping to 0 and flipping color at result_size), and polls up to wait times, 100 us apart, for the result entry's color to match: when it matches and result->error is nonzero it logs it (except for ERR_ECMDUNKNOWN on CMD_CAPABILITY) and returns that error value; when it matches with no error it copies VNIC_DEVCMD2_NARGS result words into vdev->args for _CMD_DIR_READ commands and returns 0. If no match is seen it logs a timeout and returns ETIMEDOUT. The ring slot and result cursor stay advanced in the ETIMEDOUT and error cases. No locks are taken here.

functions.name: evdev_mt_reassign_id
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: evdev and evdev->ev_mt are valid and slot is a valid MT slot index. If id is -1 or the EVDEV_FLAG_MT_KEEPID flag is set, it stores id in mt->tracking_ids[slot] and returns id. Otherwise it reads the slot's current ABS_MT_TRACKING_ID value with evdev_mt_get_value; if that value is not -1 it returns it without changing state (a KASSERT, effective only in kernels with INVARIANTS, requires id to equal mt->tracking_ids[slot] in that case). If the current value is -1 it stores id (not the generated value) in mt->tracking_ids[slot], then repeatedly takes nid = mt->tracking_id++ until no slot in the mt->touches bitmap has an ABS_MT_TRACKING_ID value equal to nid (the loop macro reuses the variable slot as its iterator), and returns that nid. No locks are taken.

functions.name: EXCA_ACCESSOR(slot, SLOT, uint32_t)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function exca_get_slot: a static inline int function taking (device_t dev, uint32_t *t) defined by the EXCA_ACCESSOR(slot, SLOT, uint32_t) invocation, whose body is the single statement return BUS_READ_IVAR(device_get_parent(dev), dev, EXCA_IVAR_SLOT, (uintptr_t *)t). It returns whatever the parent bus's read-ivar method returns for EXCA_IVAR_SLOT (100); on success that method stores the slot value through the cast pointer, which is a uintptr_t pointer aimed at a uint32_t location, so the width written is that of uintptr_t. It performs no checks of its own and takes no locks.

functions.name: pcx_draw
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: adp is a valid video adapter and pcx_info (zlen, zdata, width, height, bpsl, palette) holds a decoded PCX image. Returns 1 immediately if pcx_info.zlen < 1. Otherwise it loads the palette, clears every bank of the framebuffer window by stepping the window origin through the screen (origin < height * bytes-per-scanline) with vidd_set_win_org and bzero, computes the centred position x,y and the window origin and in-window offset pos for it, and then, for each of pcx_info.height scanlines, run-length decodes up to pcx_info.bpsl bytes from zdata into a local line buffer of MAXSCANLINE bytes; it returns 1 if a run header is at the end of the data or a run would exceed pcx_info.bpsl. After decoding a scanline it advances the window by banksize if pos > banksize; then if pos + pcx_info.width exceeds banksize it copies the first banksize - pos bytes, advances origin by banksize, subtracts banksize from pos, repositions the window with vidd_set_win_org and copies the remaining pcx_info.width - j bytes to the window base; otherwise it copies pcx_info.width bytes at pos. After the loop it returns 0. No bound is checked between pcx_info.bpsl or width and MAXSCANLINE in this function.

functions.name: vesa_set_mode
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: adp is a video adapter and mode is a requested mode number. If adp is not vesa_adp it returns the previous driver's set_mode result unchanged. Otherwise it maps the mode number with vesa_map_gen_mode_num. If the current mode is a VESA mode, the new mode is not a VESA mode and the previous driver's get_info accepts it, it resets the DAC to 6 bits if V_ADP_DAC8 was set, calls int10_set_mode(adp->va_initial_bios_mode) and, if the current mode info has V_INFO_LINEAR, unmaps the old linear buffer; this happens before the following steps and is not undone if they fail. If the new mode is not a VESA mode and the previous driver's set_mode returns 0 it returns 0. Otherwise it calls vesa_get_info and returns 1 if that fails. It then resets a 8-bit DAC if V_ADP_DAC8 is set, drops V_INFO_LINEAR for non-graphics modes, sets bit 0x4000 for a linear mode and calls vesa_bios_set_mode(mode | 0x8000), returning 1 if that fails (before the adapter state fields below are updated). On success it may switch the DAC to 8 bits (sets V_ADP_DAC8), unmaps the old linear buffer if the adapter's previous info had V_INFO_LINEAR, then updates va_mode (9 bits), the color flag, va_crtc_addr, va_line_width, the buffer, window, window size and granularity (mapping the linear frame buffer with pmap_mapdev_attr for a linear mode, otherwise using the BIOS window), va_buffer_size, window origin, display start and va_info, moves the hardware cursor off-screen with set_hw_cursor(-1, -1), and returns 0.

functions.name: vesa_save_state
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: adp is a video adapter, p a caller buffer of size bytes (size 0 queries the needed size). It returns the previous driver's save_state(adp, p, size) result if adp is not vesa_adp, or if size is 0 and vesa_state_buf_size is 0. Otherwise it computes bsize = offsetof(adp_state_t, regs) + vesa_state_buf_size; if size is 0 it returns bsize; if vesa_state_buf_size > 0 and size < bsize it returns EINVAL. Otherwise it frees any existing vesa_vmem_buf; then, only if the current mode is a VESA mode and adp->va_buffer is non-NULL, it tries to allocate adp->va_buffer_size bytes (M_NOWAIT) into vesa_vmem_buf and copies the frame buffer into it when the allocation succeeds (on failure vesa_vmem_buf stays NULL and the save continues). Finally if vesa_state_buf_size is 0 it returns the previous driver's save_state result, else it stores V_STATE_SIG in p and returns the result of vesa_bios_save_restore(STATE_SAVE, p->regs).

functions.name: fdt_foreach_mem_region
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: cb is a callback taking (struct mem_region *, void *arg) and OF/FDT accessors are usable. It returns ENXIO if the /memory node cannot be found; returns the error from fdt_addrsize_cells for the parent node if nonzero; returns ERANGE if the parent address cell count is more than 2, or if the length of the reg property is not positive or exceeds the local buffer; returns ENXIO if OF_getprop of reg returns <= 0. Otherwise it calls fdt_data_to_res on each complete (addr_cells + size_cells) tuple, returning its error immediately if nonzero (without calling cb for that tuple), and calls cb(&mr, arg) for each successfully converted tuple, ignoring cb's return value; trailing cells not forming a complete tuple are ignored; it returns 0 after the loop.

functions.name: sbp_recv1
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller holds the sbp softc lock (SBP_LOCK_ASSERT) and xfer->sc is the sbp_softc. It jumps to done0 without processing any status if xfer->resp is nonzero, the payload is NULL, the received packet is not a FWTCODE_WREQB write request, the target number from the destination address is >= SBP_NUM_TARGETS, or the LUN is out of range or has no sbp_dev. Otherwise it selects the OCB by status source: for src 0 or 1 it takes the target's current management OCB if it matches the status (stopping the management timeout and clearing mgm_ocb_cur), else dequeues one with sbp_dequeue_ocb (which may find none); src 2 (unsolicited) and unknown values leave ocb NULL. It computes status_valid0 (src < 2, response complete, not dead) and status_valid, logs unexpected statuses, and if the dead bit is set freezes the device queue (when it has a path, incrementing sdev->freeze) and sets reset_agent. If ocb is NULL it goes to done. Otherwise, for a standard-format ORB: a management OCB (OCB_ACT_MGM) clears reset_agent and then acts on the ORB function: login parses the login response and on valid status calls sbp_busy_timeout, else sets the device status to SBP_DEV_RESET; reconnect on valid status calls sbp_scan_dev if the device is attached, else sbp_agent_reset, and on failure calls sbp_login; logout sets the status to SBP_DEV_RESET; ORB_FUN_RST only calls sbp_busy_timeout; LUR, ATA and ATS call sbp_agent_reset; other values are logged; then it calls sbp_mgm_orb(sdev, ORB_FUN_RUNQUEUE, NULL). A command OCB (OCB_ACT_CMD) clears sdev->timeout and, if it has a ccb, sets the CAM status from the SCSI status (sbp_scsi_status when the status length is > 1, else CAM_REQ_CMP or CAM_REQ_CMP_ERR from the response), fixes INQUIRY data for INQUIRY commands and calls xpt_done. NOP and VED format ORBs do nothing. If use_doorbell is off the OCB is then freed with sbp_free_ocb. At done, if reset_agent is still set it calls sbp_agent_reset. At done0 (reached from all paths) it sets xfer->recv.pay_len to SBP_RECV_LEN and then, if NEED_RESPONSE is defined, builds a write response and sends it with fw_asyreq, otherwise appends the xfer to sbp->fwb.xferlist. The function returns nothing.

functions.name: sbp_probe_target
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: target is a valid sbp_target with a valid fwdev. It records whether the firewire device is alive (SBP_FWDEV_ALIVE), calls sbp_alloc_lun(target) to (re)build the LUN array, and then walks target->num_lun slots, skipping NULL slots. For a LUN whose status is not SBP_DEV_DEAD while the device is alive: if it has a path it freezes the device queue (incrementing sdev->freeze); it calls sbp_probe_lun and sbp_show_sdev_info; it takes the sbp lock only around sbp_abort_all_ocbs(sdev, CAM_SCSI_BUS_RESET); then if its status is SBP_DEV_RESET it calls sbp_login only when auto_login is set (otherwise it does nothing more), and for every other status (TOATTACH, PROBE, ATTACHED, RETRY and any other value) it sends an ORB_FUN_RCN management ORB with sbp_mgm_orb. For a LUN when the device is not alive or the LUN's status is SBP_DEV_DEAD: SBP_DEV_ATTACHED freezes the queue if it has a path (incrementing freeze), sets the status to SBP_DEV_RETRY, calls sbp_cam_detach_sdev and sbp_free_sdev and sets the slot to NULL; SBP_DEV_PROBE and SBP_DEV_TOATTACH are only set to SBP_DEV_RESET; SBP_DEV_RETRY, SBP_DEV_RESET and SBP_DEV_DEAD are left unchanged. The function returns nothing.

functions.name: scmi_virtio_poll_msg
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is an attached scmi_virtio device, msg is a message submitted for polling, and tmo_ms is a timeout in milliseconds. It sets a loop budget N = tmo_ms / SCMI_VIRTIO_POLLING_INTERVAL_MS. The loop condition decrements the budget first and then, only if the budget was nonzero, checks msg->poll_done; each iteration calls virtio_scmi_message_poll; if no message is available it delays for the polling interval and continues; otherwise it maps the returned buffer to its message, sets that message's poll_done to 1 if its polling flag is set, leaves the loop if the returned message is msg, and for any other message that is not a polling one passes it to scmi_rx_irq_callback. The function returns 0 if the budget left after the loop is greater than zero and ETIMEDOUT otherwise. Consequently: when msg is returned by the poll on the k-th iteration it returns 0 only if k < N (returns ETIMEDOUT if it arrives on the last allowed iteration); when the loop ends because msg->poll_done was seen nonzero at the loop test it returns 0 only if at least two iterations of budget were left at that point; if N is 0 (tmo_ms below the interval) no poll is made, poll_done is not examined and it returns ETIMEDOUT.

functions.name: inphy_service
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc is an attached inphy softc, mii its mii_data. For MII_MEDIACHG it calls mii_phy_setmedia(sc) only if the interface has IFF_UP set; when IFF_UP is clear it skips the media set but still continues to the status update below. For MII_TICK it returns 0 immediately if mii_phy_tick(sc) returns EJUSTRETURN, with no status update; otherwise it continues. For MII_POLLSTAT and for any other cmd value it continues without other action. On the continuing paths it calls PHY_STATUS(sc) and mii_phy_update(sc, cmd). It returns 0 in all cases.

functions.name: gpio_check_flags
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: caps and flags are arbitrary uint32_t values; no memory, lock or state is touched. It first masks flags with caps, then returns EINVAL if the masked value has both GPIO_PIN_INPUT and GPIO_PIN_OUTPUT, or both GPIO_PIN_PULLUP and GPIO_PIN_PULLDOWN, or GPIO_PIN_OUTPUT together with any bit of GPIO_INTR_MASK, or more than one bit of GPIO_INTR_MASK, or GPIO_INTR_ATTACHED; otherwise it returns 0.

functions.name: hmt_intr
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: context is the hmt_softc and buf points to len readable bytes of a HID input report (len must be at least 1 when sc->report_id is nonzero). When built with IICHID_SAMPLING and sc->iichid_sampling is set, a zero-length report clears sc->prev_touch and sc->timestamp, calls evdev_sync and returns. Otherwise, if sc->report_id is nonzero it reads the first byte as the report id and returns without action when it differs from sc->report_id, else strips that byte. It reads the contact count (1 if the device has none) and, if the count is nonzero, stores it in sc->nconts_todo. It then processes MIN(sc->nconts_todo, sc->nconts_per_report) contacts: for each it extracts the usage values, maps the contact id to an evdev MT slot and skips the contact (with a debug message) if no slot is available (slot == -1); otherwise, if the tip switch is nonzero and the confidence usage (when present) is not zero, it sets sc->touch, computes distance, orientation, major and minor from width and height and pushes the slot data; else it pushes the slot with NULL data. It subtracts the processed count from sc->nconts_todo. When sc->do_timestamps is set and sc->nconts_todo has reached 0 it updates sc->timestamp from the scan time (delta computed only when sc->prev_touch was set), pushes MSC_TIMESTAMP, sets sc->prev_touch from sc->touch, clears sc->touch and zeroes sc->timestamp if there is no touch. When sc->nconts_todo is 0 it also pushes BTN_LEFT (from the internal and left buttons) and the other configured buttons and calls evdev_sync. The function returns nothing; no locks or memory are acquired or released here.

functions.name: hpt_default_ioctl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: lpInBuffer and lpOutBuffer point to buffers of the sizes given in nInBufferSize and nOutBufferSize (these sizes are checked per code, the buffer contents are trusted), and lpBytesReturned is NULL or writable. It switches on dwIoControlCode and returns -1 for an unknown code. Per code, returning -1 on a wrong size or a failing helper: GET_VERSION needs input size 0 and output size sizeof(DWORD) and stores HPT_INTERFACE_VERSION; GET_CONTROLLER_COUNT needs output size sizeof(DWORD); GET_CONTROLLER_INFO, GET_CHANNEL_INFO, GET_DEVICE_INFO and GET_DEVICE_INFO_V2 need exact input and output sizes (the device-info ones also reject INVALID_DEVICEID and zero the output first) and fail when the helper returns nonzero; GET_LOGICAL_DEVICES needs an input of one DWORD and an output of at least (1 + max) DWORDs and stores the helper's count. Under SUPPORT_ARRAY only: CREATE_ARRAY and CREATE_ARRAY_V2 need exact input size and output size sizeof(DEVICEID) and fail if the created id is INVALID_DEVICEID; SET_ARRAY_INFO, SET_DEVICE_INFO and ADD/REMOVE_SPARE_DISK need exact input size and output size 0; SET_DEVICE_INFO_V2 needs input at least the struct size and output 0; ADD_DISK_TO_ARRAY reads the two ids from the input before checking sizes, then needs exact input size and output size 0; SET_BOOT_MARK needs input size sizeof(DEVICEID) and walks every adapter's top-level devices, returning -1 if a device's vbus differs from the current vbus, clearing or setting the boot mark and calling SyncArrayInfo on the matching top device. GET_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES needs output size at least sizeof(DRIVER_CAPABILITIES). GET_CONTROLLER_VENID finds the adapter with the given index (-1 if none or if output size is under 4), writes (pciConfigDeviceId << 16) | 0x11AB and returns 0 directly without setting *lpBytesReturned. EPROM_IO finds the adapter by index (-1 if none), checks the input size (16 bytes plus length for a write) and output size (length for a read), returns -1 if too small, otherwise performs sx508x_flash_access for read or write and returns 0 directly without setting *lpBytesReturned. For all other codes that succeed, if lpBytesReturned is non-NULL it is set to nOutBufferSize and the function returns 0.

functions.name: hpt_create_array_v2
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: pParam is non-NULL; when pParam->nDisk is 0 the code still reads Members[0] (line 584), which is not checked, so nDisk should be at least 1. It first returns INVALID_DEVICEID, before allocating anything, if nDisk > MAX_MEMBERS, if any member fails check_VDevice_valid, is itself an array or is not online, if the members are not all on one vbus, or if the first member's vbus pointer is NULL. It then allocates an array table with mArGetArrayTable and returns INVALID_DEVICEID if that gives NULL. By ArrayType it sets the device type: JBOD; RAID0 and RAID5 (both need BlockSizeShift within [MinBlockSizeShift, MaxBlockSizeShift], else go to error; RAID5 also sets rf_need_rebuild unless CAF_CREATE_R5_NO_BUILD is given); RAID1 (with at most 2 disks a plain mirror, otherwise a RAID0 of nDisk/2 RAID1 child arrays built from pairs of members); any other type goes to error. It fills the array fields, attaches the members (setting their parent and serial number and unregistering them, except the first member in a CAF_CREATE_AND_DUPLICATE RAID1), sets each member's pfnDeviceFailed, and for CAF_CREATE_AND_DUPLICATE RAID1 transfers the boot flags and, if the first member was found in the vbus slot table, installs the array in that slot (so RegisterVDevice is skipped), otherwise clears boot flags on all disks and zeroes sector 0 of each with fDeReadWrite. It then marks the array online and computes VDeviceCapacity per type (RAID0, RAID1, JBOD, RAID5), sets the command and failure callbacks, calls SyncArrayInfo, calls RegisterVDevice unless the array was installed in the vbus slot, and returns VDEV_TO_ID(pArray). At the error label (reached from the block-size, unknown type and capacity switch failures after the table was allocated) it frees each member entry that is not a single disk with mArFreeArrayTable, frees the array table and returns INVALID_DEVICEID; the earlier validation and allocation failures return INVALID_DEVICEID without calling mArFreeArrayTable.

functions.name: pmc_save_user_callchain
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: tf is a user-mode trap frame (KASSERTed with TRAPF_USERMODE), cc points to storage for the samples. It always writes the trap frame PC to cc[0], even when maxsamples is 0 or 1, and returns 1 if maxsamples <= 1. Otherwise it takes fp from the trap frame and returns 1 if either the PC or the frame pointer is not in user space (PMC_IN_USERSPACE). Then, starting with count 1, while count < maxsamples it reads the saved return address at fp + sizeof(uintptr_t) with copyin and stops if the copy fails or the value is not in user space; otherwise it appends it to cc; it then reads the previous frame pointer from fp with copyin and stops if the copy fails, if the new fp is below the old fp (equal is allowed) or if it is not in user space; otherwise count is incremented and the loop continues. The function returns count; because the count is incremented only at the end of a complete iteration, when the loop stops after a return address has been appended (failed fp copy or bad new fp) the returned count is one less than the number of entries written to cc.

functions.name: hvsock_canread_check
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: pcb may be NULL; if non-NULL, pcb->so is valid and pcb->chan may be NULL. Returns 0 if pcb is NULL; returns 0 after setting pcb->so->so_error to EIO if pcb->chan is NULL; returns the pending pcb->recv_data_len if it is greater than 0. Otherwise it sets advance to the length of the previous packet when pcb->rb_init is set, else 0, and reads the readable byte count of the channel ring. If rb_init is set and exactly advance + 8 bytes are readable it advances the ring index by advance with vmbus_chan_recv_idxadv: on error it returns 0 (rb_init unchanged); on success it clears rb_init, zeroes recv_data_len and recv_data_off, re-reads the readable count, returns 0 if nothing is readable, else resets advance to 0. It returns 0 if fewer than advance + sizeof(struct hvs_pkt_header) + 8 bytes are readable, or if vmbus_chan_recv_peek of the header fails. It validates the peeked header (header length at least the channel packet header size, not above total length, total length at least data length plus the header size); if invalid it sets so_error to EIO and returns 0. Otherwise it sets rb_init to true, sets so_error to ESHUTDOWN when the data length is 0 (FIN), stores the data length in recv_data_len, sets recv_data_off to 0 and returns the data length (0 for a FIN).

functions.name: hv_hid_receive
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc is an initialised hv_hid_sc and pkt is a received inband channel packet whose payload begins with an hv_hid_msg. It returns nothing. It returns at once if msg->type is not HV_HID_MSG_DATA, and after printing a message if the payload length is not greater than sizeof(hv_hid_pmsg). Otherwise by sub-message type: SH_PROTO_RESP calls vmbus_xact_ctx_wakeup with the packet payload if sc->hs_xact_ctx is non-NULL, else does nothing. SH_DEVINFO builds an ack and calls vmbus_xact_get(sc->hs_xact_ctx, ...); if that returns NULL it stops (without parsing the device info); otherwise it sends the ack on sc->hs_chan (result ignored) and releases the transaction, then stops if sc->rdesc is already non-NULL, if hdesc->bLength is 0, or if the report descriptor length is 0 (in which last case sc->hdi has already been zeroed and has rdescsize 0); otherwise it fills sc->hdi (name, bus, vendor, product, version), allocates a zeroed buffer of rdescsize bytes with M_WAITOK, copies the report descriptor into it, and under sc->mtx stores it in sc->rdesc and calls wakeup(sc). SH_INPUT_REPORT takes sc->mtx and, if sc->intr is non-NULL and sc->intr_on is set, calls sc->intr with the report buffer and size, then releases sc->mtx. Any other sub-message type does nothing.

functions.name: iavf_asq_send_command
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hw is a valid iavf_hw, desc points to a descriptor in ordinary memory, buff is NULL or points to buff_size bytes, cmd_details is NULL or valid. It takes hw->aq.asq_spinlock and releases it on every return path, sets asq_last_status to IAVF_AQ_RC_OK, and sends nothing and returns an error in these cases: IAVF_ERR_QUEUE_EMPTY if asq.count is 0, or if the head register value is >= num_asq_entries; then (after copying or clearing the command details and applying details->flags_dis and flags_ena to desc->flags and setting the cookie when given) IAVF_ERR_INVALID_SIZE if buff_size > asq_buf_size, IAVF_ERR_PARAM if postpone is set without async, and IAVF_ERR_ADMIN_QUEUE_FULL if iavf_clean_asq finds no free descriptor. Otherwise it copies desc into the ring descriptor at next_to_use, copies the buffer (when given) into the matching DMA buffer and sets datalen and the buffer address, advances next_to_use with wrap, writes the tail register unless postpone is set, and unless async or postpone is set polls iavf_asq_done every 50 us until done or asq_cmd_timeout. If the command is done it copies the descriptor (and the buffer, when given) back to the caller, takes the descriptor's return value (masked to 8 bits if nonzero), sets asq_last_status to it and returns IAVF_SUCCESS for IAVF_AQ_RC_OK, IAVF_ERR_NOT_READY for IAVF_AQ_RC_EBUSY and IAVF_ERR_ADMIN_QUEUE_ERROR otherwise. If details->wb_desc is set the ring descriptor is copied to it after queueing. If not done and neither async nor postpone is set, it returns IAVF_ERR_ADMIN_QUEUE_CRITICAL_ERROR when the ATQCRIT bit is set in the length register and IAVF_ERR_ADMIN_QUEUE_TIMEOUT otherwise; if not done with async or postpone it returns IAVF_SUCCESS.

functions.name: iavf_process_adminq
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc and its hw are valid, sc->aq_buffer is at least IAVF_AQ_BUF_SZ bytes, and pending is non-NULL (it is dereferenced in the loop test). If IAVF_STATE_RESET_PENDING is set it sets status IAVF_ERR_ADMIN_QUEUE_ERROR; otherwise if iavf_check_aq_errors reports an error it sets IAVF_ERR_ADMIN_QUEUE_CRITICAL_ERROR; in both cases it skips to the interrupt re-enable without taking the VC lock and without writing *pending. Otherwise it clears sc->aq_buffer, takes the VC lock and loops: it calls iavf_clean_arq_element(hw, &event, pending) and breaks with that status if nonzero, otherwise calls iavf_vc_completion with the message opcode, return value, buffer and length and clears the buffer; the loop continues while *pending is nonzero and loop++ < IAVF_ADM_LIMIT, so it can handle up to IAVF_ADM_LIMIT + 1 elements per call. It releases the VC lock, and on every path reaches the label that sets the IAVF_VFINT_ICR0_ENA1_ADMINQ_MASK bit in IAVF_VFINT_ICR0_ENA1. It returns the status (IAVF_SUCCESS if the loop ended with the last clean call succeeding, or the failing status).

functions.name: ice_bitmap_from_array32
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dst points to a bitmap of at least size bits, src points to an array of u32 words with ceil(size / 32) readable entries. It first calls ice_zero_bitmap(dst, size) (what that call clears was not read), then for each of the size / 32 full words in src it sets, with ice_set_bit, every dst bit at index word * 32 + j for which bit j of the word is set. If size % 32 is nonzero it then reads the next word src[size / 32] and sets the dst bits for its lowest size % 32 bits that are set. The function returns nothing and takes no locks; src is not modified.

functions.name: ice_clean_rq_elem
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hw, cq and e are valid, the caller does not hold cq->rq_lock, e->msg_buf (if non-NULL) has room for e->buf_len bytes, and pending is NULL or points to a u16. It zeroes e->desc first, then takes cq->rq_lock. If cq->rq.count is 0 it returns ICE_ERR_AQ_EMPTY without writing *pending. It reads the hardware head (masked by head_mask); if it equals next_to_clean it returns ICE_ERR_AQ_NO_WORK with the ring state unchanged and *pending still updated when pending is non-NULL. Otherwise it takes the descriptor at next_to_clean; if its ICE_AQ_FLAG_ERR flag is set it records ICE_ERR_AQ_ERROR and logs, but continues; it copies the descriptor into e->desc, sets e->msg_len to MIN(datalen, e->buf_len), copies that many bytes from the ring buffer to e->msg_buf when msg_buf is non-NULL and msg_len is nonzero, then zeroes the ring descriptor and rewrites its flags (ICE_AQ_FLAG_BUF, plus ICE_AQ_FLAG_LB for large buffers), datalen and buffer address, writes next_to_clean to the tail register, advances next_to_clean with wrap at num_rq_entries and sets cq->rq.next_to_use to the head value read. In every case except ICE_ERR_AQ_EMPTY it sets *pending (when non-NULL) to the number of descriptors still pending computed from a fresh head read. It releases cq->rq_lock on every return and returns 0, ICE_ERR_AQ_ERROR (after full processing of the descriptor), ICE_ERR_AQ_NO_WORK or ICE_ERR_AQ_EMPTY.

functions.name: ice_sched_add_rl_profile
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hw is an ice_hw whose scheduler lock is held by the caller (not checked here), and rl_type, bw and layer_num select the profile. It returns NULL, with nothing allocated, if hw is NULL, if layer_num >= hw->num_tx_sched_layers, or if rl_type is not ICE_MIN_BW, ICE_MAX_BW or ICE_SHARED_BW (mapped to profile types CIR, EIR and SRL). It then scans hw->rl_prof_list[layer_num] and returns the first existing entry whose profile type matches and whose bw equals bw, without changing that entry (prof_id_ref is not touched here). Otherwise it allocates a new element (NULL on failure), converts bw into a profile with ice_sched_bw_to_rl_profile, sets bw, profile.level = layer_num + 1, profile.flags = the profile type and profile.max_burst_size from hw->max_burst_size, and calls ice_aq_add_rl_profile for exactly one profile. If the conversion fails, the AQ call fails, or profiles_added is not 1, it frees the new element and returns NULL. On success it sets prof_id_ref to 0, adds the element at the head of hw->rl_prof_list[layer_num] and returns it. The returned pointer is owned by the list.

functions.name: ice_add_mac_with_sw_marker
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hw is valid with hw->switch_info and hw->port_info set; f_info describes the filter. It returns ICE_ERR_PARAM if f_info->fltr_act is not ICE_FWD_TO_VSI, the lookup type is not ICE_SW_LKUP_MAC, sw_marker is ICE_INVAL_SW_MARKER_ID or the vsi_handle is not valid; otherwise it sets f_info->fwd_id.hw_vsi_id and calls ice_add_mac_rule: ICE_ERR_ALREADY_EXISTS marks the entry as pre-existing, any other nonzero result is returned at once. It then takes the MAC recipe's filt_rule_lock and looks up the entry. It reaches the error exit if the entry is not found, if its counter_index is valid (ret = ICE_ERR_PARAM), if its sw_marker_id already equals sw_marker (ret = ICE_ERR_ALREADY_EXISTS), if ice_alloc_res_lg_act fails (ret is its error), if the allocated lg_act_id equals ICE_INVAL_LG_ACT_INDEX (ret keeps its previous value), or if ice_add_marker_act fails. On success of ice_add_marker_act it releases the lock and returns 0. At the error exit it releases the lock and, if the filter was added by this call (not pre-existing), returns the result of ice_remove_mac instead of the earlier error; if the filter pre-existed it returns the value ret has at that point, which is ICE_ERR_ALREADY_EXISTS when the entry is not found, and 0 when the lg_act_id was invalid. So the function can return 0 without installing the marker (pre-existing filter and invalid lg_act_id), and a failed marker installation on a newly added filter returns the removal status, which may be 0.

functions.name: ice_poll_for_media_avail
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc is a valid ice_softc with hw->port_info set. On an E830 device with ICE_STATE_PHY_FW_INIT_PENDING set: if GL_MNG_FWSM_FW_LOADING_M is set in GL_MNG_FWSM it clears ICE_STATE_PHY_FW_INIT_PENDING and continues, otherwise it returns immediately. Then if ICE_STATE_NO_MEDIA is not set it does nothing more (the E830 step may already have cleared the pending state). If ICE_STATE_NO_MEDIA is set it sets pi->phy.get_link_info to true and calls ice_get_link_status, which refreshes sc->link_up and the link info whether or not media is available. If the link info then has ICE_AQ_MEDIA_AVAILABLE set: when ICE_STATE_LINK_ACTIVE_ON_DOWN is set or the interface has IFF_UP, it calls ice_apply_saved_phy_cfg(sc, ICE_APPLY_LS_FEC_FC) (result ignored) and ice_add_media_types, printing an error message if the latter fails; in either case it then clears ICE_STATE_NO_MEDIA. If media is not available, ICE_STATE_NO_MEDIA stays set. The function returns nothing and takes no locks itself.

functions.name: icintr
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is an ic(4) device with softc sc; the caller does not hold sc->ic_lock (the function takes it with mtx_lock on entry and releases it before returning). event is dispatched: INTR_GENERAL and INTR_START reset the input pointer and transfer count and set IC_IFBUF_BUSY; INTR_STOP clears IC_IFBUF_BUSY and wakes a buffer waiter if only IC_BUFFER_WAITER is set among the busy/waiter flags; then if error count ic_iferrs is nonzero or the transferred length is at most ICHDRLEN (but nonzero) it logs the errors, resets ic_iferrs and increments IFCOUNTER_IERRORS; a zero-length transfer is ignored; otherwise it increments IFCOUNTER_IPACKETS and IBYTES, taps BPF, builds an mbuf with m_devget and, only if that succeeds, drops the lock around netisr_dispatch(NETISR_IP) inside the network epoch and re-takes it (if m_devget fails, the counters have still been incremented and the frame is dropped silently). INTR_RECEIVE stores one byte from *ptr and advances unless the transfer count is already at least MTU + ICHDRLEN, in which case it only increments ic_iferrs. INTR_NOACK does nothing. INTR_TRANSMIT writes 0xff to *ptr. INTR_ERROR increments ic_iferrs. Any other event panics. For all handled events it releases the lock and returns 0.

functions.name: ds1307_sqw_freq_sysctl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: arg1 points to an initialised ds1307 softc; oidp and req are the sysctl handler arguments (arg2 is unused). It reads the control register with ds1307_ctrl_read and returns the error if that fails. It takes the RS field of sc_ctrl as an index into the table {1, 4096, 8192, 32768} (clamped to the last entry if out of range) and passes that frequency to sysctl_handle_int(oidp, &freq, 0, req); if that returns an error or the request has no new value (newptr is NULL) it returns that result without writing the device. If the new value differs from the current table frequency, it picks the largest table index whose frequency is <= the new value (index 0, 1 Hz, if the value is below 1), replaces the RS bits in sc_ctrl, and writes the control register with ds1307_ctrl_write, returning its error if nonzero (sc_ctrl has already been modified in that case). If the value is unchanged it returns 0 without a write.

functions.name: ds1775_sensor_sysctl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: arg1 is the device_t of an attached ds1775 whose softc is valid; oidp and req are the sysctl handler arguments. It reads the temperature with ds1775_sensor_read(sc); if the value is negative it returns EIO without calling sysctl_handle_int. Otherwise it calls sysctl_handle_int(oidp, &temp, 0, req) and returns that call's result. It takes no locks itself.

functions.name: irdma_sc_suspend_resume_qps
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: vsi is a valid irdma_sc_vsi whose qos[i].qos_mutex and qplist are initialised for i < IRDMA_MAX_USER_PRIORITY. For each user priority it takes qos[i].qos_mutex, walks every qp on that priority's list, and releases the mutex before the next priority. For op == IRDMA_OP_RESUME, a qp that is not suspended is skipped; for a suspended one it calls qp->dev->ws_add(vsi, i): if ws_add returns 0 (success) it sets qp->qs_handle from irdma_get_qp_qs and issues the CQP resume, clearing qp->suspended only if the CQP call returns 0 (qs_handle stays updated even if the CQP call fails); if ws_add returns nonzero it still issues the CQP resume (clearing suspended only on CQP success, qs_handle unchanged) and then calls irdma_modify_qp_to_err(qp). For op == IRDMA_OP_SUSPEND, only a qp in IRDMA_QP_STATE_RTS or IRDMA_QP_STATE_RTR gets a CQP suspend, and only if that returns 0 does it increment vsi->qp_suspend_reqs and set qp->suspended. For any other op value nothing is changed, but the lists are still walked under the mutexes. The function returns nothing and holds no mutex on return.

functions.name: sati_inquiry_translate_command
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sequence, scsi_io and ata_io are valid and the CDB of scsi_io can be read. If the EVPD bit in CDB byte 1 is clear and the page code (byte 2) is nonzero, it builds CHECK CONDITION sense data (ILLEGAL REQUEST, invalid field in CDB) and returns SATI_FAILURE_CHECK_RESPONSE_DATA. Otherwise it sets sequence->allocation_length from CDB bytes 3 and 4 (this happens before the EVPD branch, so also on the supported-pages and unsupported-page paths). If EVPD is set: the supported-pages page sets sequence->type to SATI_SEQUENCE_INQUIRY_SUPPORTED_PAGES, builds the response data with sati_inquiry_supported_pages_translate_data and returns SATI_COMPLETE without constructing an ATA command; the unit serial number, device ID and block device pages set the corresponding sequence type; the ATA information page, when sequence->state is SATI_SEQUENCE_STATE_INCOMPLETE, constructs an EXECUTE DEVICE DIAGNOSTIC command in ata_io and sets type SATI_SEQUENCE_INQUIRY_EXECUTE_DEVICE_DIAG, otherwise sets type SATI_SEQUENCE_INQUIRY_ATA_INFORMATION; any other page code builds the same ILLEGAL REQUEST sense data and returns SATI_FAILURE_CHECK_RESPONSE_DATA. If EVPD is clear the type is set to SATI_SEQUENCE_INQUIRY_STANDARD. For all those non-returning cases it then calls sati_ata_identify_device_construct(ata_io, sequence) (also after the EXECUTE DEVICE DIAGNOSTIC construction in the incomplete ATA-information case) and returns SATI_SUCCESS.

functions.name: scic_controller_set_mode
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: controller is a controller handle. If the controller state machine is in SCI_BASE_CONTROLLER_STATE_INITIALIZING or SCI_BASE_CONTROLLER_STATE_INITIALIZED, then for operating_mode SCI_MODE_SPEED it sets each of remote_node_entries, task_context_entries, the unsolicited frame buffer count, completion_event_entries and completion_queue_entries to the minimum of its current value and the speed-mode constants (SCI_MAX_REMOTE_DEVICES, SCU_IO_REQUEST_COUNT, SCU_UNSOLICITED_FRAME_COUNT, SCU_EVENT_COUNT, SCU_COMPLETION_QUEUE_COUNT), rebuilds the memory descriptor table and returns SCI_SUCCESS; for SCI_MODE_SIZE it does the same with the size-mode constants (SCI_MIN_REMOTE_DEVICES, SCI_MIN_IO_REQUESTS, SCU_MIN_UNSOLICITED_FRAMES, SCU_MIN_EVENTS, SCU_MIN_COMPLETION_QUEUE_ENTRIES) and returns SCI_SUCCESS; for any other mode it returns SCI_FAILURE_INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE without changing the controller. In any other controller state it returns SCI_FAILURE_INVALID_STATE without changing the controller.

functions.name: scic_sds_abort_reqests
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: controller is non-NULL; remote_device and port may each be NULL. request_count starts as remote_device->started_request_count when remote_device is non-NULL, else port->started_request_count when port is non-NULL, else SCI_MAX_IO_REQUESTS. It scans controller->io_request_table from index 0 while index < SCI_MAX_IO_REQUESTS and request_count > 0. For each non-NULL entry it tests whether the request's target_device equals remote_device, or the target_device's owning_port equals port (this dereferences target_device whenever the first test is false, so target_device must be non-NULL in that case), or both remote_device and port are NULL; for each match it calls scic_controller_terminate_request(controller, target_device, request), remembers the last non-SCI_SUCCESS status it returned, and decrements request_count. Matching entries are terminated whether or not they were started, and matching entries beyond the first request_count matches are not visited once request_count reaches 0. It returns SCI_SUCCESS if no terminate call failed (including when none was made), otherwise the last failing status. It takes no locks.

functions.name: scic_sds_phy_starting_substate_await_iaf_uf_frame_handler
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: this_phy is a valid phy in the AWAIT_IAF_UF starting substate and frame_index names an unsolicited frame of the controller. It obtains the frame header with scic_sds_unsolicited_frame_control_get_header; if that returns an error it returns that error at once and does not release the frame. Otherwise it byte-swaps header word 0 (this happens before the frame-type test). If the address frame type is 0 (identify frame) it also byte-swaps words 1 to 5, copies the frame into this_phy's identify_address_frame_buffer, and changes the starting substate to FINAL if the frame's protocols have the SMP target bit set, or to AWAIT_SAS_POWER otherwise. If the type is non-zero it only logs a warning and copies nothing and does not change the substate. In both of those cases it releases the frame with scic_sds_controller_release_frame and returns SCI_SUCCESS (the value from get_header).

functions.name: scic_remote_device_da_construct
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: remote_device was set up with scic_remote_device_construct and has a valid owning port. It records the port's attached protocols in target_protocols, sets is_direct_attached to TRUE, sets is_atapi (unless DISABLE_ATAPI is defined), and sets device_port_width to the number of bits set in the port's phy_mask; these happen before the allocation. It then calls scic_sds_controller_allocate_remote_node_context; if that returns a status other than SCI_SUCCESS it returns that status, and the remote node index, device address, ready substate machine, connection rate and the final port width of 1 are not set (but the protocols, direct-attached flag, atapi flag and phy-mask port width were already changed). On SCI_SUCCESS it stores the allocated index in the RNC, copies the port's attached SAS address into device_address, then sets has_ready_substate_machine to FALSE for an SSP target, or to TRUE and constructs the STP ready substate machine for an STP target, or the SMP one for an SMP target (checked in that order; if none of the three target bits is set the flag is not changed), sets connection_rate to the port's maximum allowed speed, sets device_port_width to 1 and returns SCI_SUCCESS.

functions.name: scic_remote_device_ea_construct
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: remote_device is a constructed device with a valid owning port and discover_response points to an SMP DISCOVER response for the attached target. It fills the device's target information from the response with scic_sds_remote_device_get_info_from_smp_discover_response, then calls scic_sds_controller_allocate_remote_node_context passing the address of this_device->rnc->remote_node_index; if that returns a status other than SCI_SUCCESS it returns that status and does nothing more (the discover-response information has already been recorded). On SCI_SUCCESS it sets has_ready_substate_machine to FALSE for an SSP target, or to TRUE and constructs the SMP ready substate machine for an SMP target, or the STP one for an STP target (checked in that order; if no bit is set the flag is unchanged), sets connection_rate to the minimum of the port's maximum allowed speed and the response's negotiated physical link rate, sets device_port_width to 1 and returns SCI_SUCCESS.

functions.name: scic_sds_stp_remote_device_ready_substate_start_request_handler
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: device is a valid STP remote device in a READY substate and request is a valid request. It calls the owning port's start_io_handler; if that returns a status other than SCI_SUCCESS it returns that status and does nothing else. If it succeeds it calls scic_sds_remote_node_context_start_task on the RNC, and, only if that succeeds, the request's parent start_handler. Only when both succeed (status is SCI_SUCCESS) does it set working_request to the request, change the ready substate to CMD, and suspend the RNC (SCI_SOFTWARE_SUSPENSION) and resume it with scic_sds_remote_device_continue_request as the callback. In every case where the port's start_io succeeded (including when the RNC start or the parent start failed) it then calls scic_sds_remote_device_start_request(this_device, this_request, status) with the current status, and returns SCI_FAILURE_RESET_DEVICE_PARTIAL_SUCCESS.

functions.name: scic_cb_io_request_complete
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: controller, remote_device and io_request each have an associated framework object (sci_object_get_association). It calls the request's state_handlers->complete_handler. If that returns anything other than SCI_SUCCESS nothing further happens. If it returns SCI_SUCCESS: when the request's protocol_complete_handler is non-NULL it is called with the controller, device, request and a pointer to completion_status (the handler may change completion_status), and its result becomes status; when the handler is NULL, status stays SCI_SUCCESS. If status is SCI_SUCCESS, a request that is not high priority and not waiting for the abort task set is completed to the user with scif_cb_io_request_complete using completion_status; a request that is not high priority but is waiting for the abort task set is left untouched; a high-priority request is passed to scif_sas_controller_complete_high_priority_io (regardless of the abort-task-set flag). If status is SCI_WARNING_SEQUENCE_INCOMPLETE the IO is continued with scif_sas_io_request_continue. For any other status nothing more is done. The function returns nothing.

functions.name: isp_fclink_test
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: chan is a valid channel and usdelay is the firmware-ready wait in microseconds. It returns -1 if the channel's loop state is below LOOP_HAVE_LINK, and 0 at once (doing nothing) if it is already at or beyond LOOP_LTEST_DONE. Otherwise it repeatedly reads the firmware state (sleeping 1 ms between tries) until it is FW_READY or about usdelay microseconds have passed; if the loop state drops below LOOP_HAVE_LINK during this wait it logs and returns 1; if the firmware state is not FW_READY afterwards it returns -1. It then issues MBOX_GET_LOOP_ID, returning -1 if the command does not complete. It records the topology (set to TOPO_PTP_STUB if the reported value is outside the range TOPO_NL_PORT..TOPO_PTP_STUB), the port ID, and, for a non-fabric topology the loop ID, or for a fabric topology other than F port the loop ID found by looking up the ALPA in alpa_map if found. It sets the loop state to LOOP_TESTING_LINK. For TOPO_F_PORT or TOPO_FL_PORT it queries the fabric controller port database; if that query fails or gives port ID 0 it forces topology to TOPO_PTP_STUB and skips the fabric steps; otherwise it stores the fabric params and SNS handle and tries the FC4 type, FC4 feature, port name and node name registrations in turn: if the loop state falls below LOOP_TESTING_LINK after any of them it logs and returns 1, and if one of the first three returns nonzero it skips the remaining registrations (the registration failure does not change the topology and the function can still return 0). It then sets isp_gbspeed to 1 and updates it from the MBOX_GET_SET_DATA_RATE reply when that command completes. If the loop state is below LOOP_TESTING_LINK at that point it logs and returns 1; otherwise it sets the loop state to LOOP_LTEST_DONE, logs the link information and returns 0.

functions.name: isp_reset
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: isp is a valid softc for a 24xx-or-later FC adapter with register access; do_load_defaults selects whether defaults are loaded at the end. The function returns nothing; it returns early at many points after logging (or silently), leaving the adapter in whatever state it reached, with isp_state left at ISP_NILSTATE (it is set to ISP_RESETSTATE only at the end). It sets isp_state to ISP_NILSTATE, disables interrupts and pauses the RISC, stops DMA (polling up to 100000 x 10 us and only logging if it does not stop), soft-resets the chip and polls OUTMAILBOX0 up to 10000 times for it to leave 0x4: returns after logging if the value is 0x4 (ROM busy), 0xf (board configuration error) or an unknown value. It then resets and releases the RISC and repeats that OUTMAILBOX0 check with the same three early returns. It zeroes the request, response and ATIO indices and the queue pointer registers (the priority request pointers only when not a 26xx). It runs MBOX_NO_OP (return if it does not complete) and the mailbox register test (return if the command fails or, after logging, if any register value mismatches), then ISP_MBOXDMASETUP (return after logging on failure). Next it sets up the flash addresses, firmware version strings and, unless ISP_CFG_NORELOAD is set, tries firmware_get for the ispfw module. It decides whether to download: on 27xx via isp_load_risc (success means firmware already loaded; abort or, with ispfw present, other failures mean download), on others only if ispfw was obtained. If downloading, it loads each firmware fragment into RAM (return after logging on a load failure; the firmware reference is not released on that path) and, after all succeed, calls firmware_put with FIRMWARE_UNLOAD on the ispfw reference. If firmware was loaded it verifies the checksum (return on failure), else on 26xx asks the RISC to load from flash (return on failure). It then issues MBOX_EXEC_FIRMWARE (return if not complete), records the ability mask, issues MBOX_ABOUT_FIRMWARE (return if not complete), stores firmware revision and attributes, logs them, issues MBOX_GET_RESOURCE_COUNT (return if not complete; sets isp_maxcmds), limits isp_nchan to 1 for firmware without multi-ID or VP0 decoupling support, calls ISP_MBOXDMASETUP again and ISP_IRQSETUP (return after logging on failure), enables interrupts, sets each channel's firmware state to FW_CONFIG_WAIT, sets isp_state to ISP_RESETSTATE and, if do_load_defaults, calls isp_setdfltfcparm for each channel.

functions.name: isp_gdt
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: arg is a pointer to a valid struct isp_fc whose gtask task has been initialised (TASK_INIT with isp_gdt_task), and the structure stays valid until the task runs. This is the callout function: it only calls taskqueue_enqueue(taskqueue_thread, &fc->gtask) and returns nothing. It does not take the ISP lock, scan the port database or re-arm the callout itself; those actions are done later by the separate task function isp_gdt_task.

functions.name: iwi_notification_intr
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc is a valid iwi softc whose ic has at least one vap (the first vap is dereferenced in several branches) and notif points to a firmware notification whose payload is at least as long as the structure implied by notif->type. The function returns nothing and dispatches on notif->type. SCAN_CHANNEL only sets sc->sc_state_timer to 3. SCAN_COMPLETE ends the IWI_FW_SCANNING state; in monitor mode it queues sc->sc_monitortask, otherwise if scan->status is IWI_SCAN_COMPLETED it calls ieee80211_scan_next(vap). AUTHENTICATION: IWI_AUTH_SUCCESS calls ieee80211_new_state(vap, IEEE80211_S_ASSOC); IWI_AUTH_FAIL clears IWI_FLAG_ASSOCIATED and, if the vap is not in RUN state, counts is_rx_auth_fail and ends IWI_FW_ASSOCIATING, else counts is_rx_deauth, then calls ieee80211_new_state to SCAN; IWI_AUTH_SENT_1, IWI_AUTH_RECV_2 and IWI_AUTH_SEQ1_PASS do nothing; IWI_AUTH_SEQ1_FAIL counts is_rx_auth_fail and ends IWI_FW_ASSOCIATING; other states print an unknown-state message. ASSOCIATION: IWI_AUTH_SUCCESS does nothing; IWI_ASSOC_SUCCESS sets IWI_FLAG_ASSOCIATED, ends IWI_FW_ASSOCIATING, calls iwi_checkforqos with the association frame and calls ieee80211_new_state to RUN; IWI_ASSOC_INIT clears IWI_FLAG_ASSOCIATED and, depending on sc->fw_state, ends IWI_FW_ASSOCIATING and moves to SCAN (association failed), or ends IWI_FW_DISASSOCIATING, counts is_rx_disassoc and moves to SCAN, and does nothing else for other firmware states; other states print an unknown-state message. BEACON: for a beacon-miss state whose count is at least vap->iv_bmissthreshold it counts is_beacon_miss and queues sc->sc_disassoctask. CALIBRATION and NOISE only produce a debug print. LINK_QUALITY calls iwi_notif_link_quality. An unknown type only produces a debug print.

functions.name: iwn_attach
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is a probed iwn PCI device with its softc zeroed by the bus, called once from attach. It reads the debug resource value, then calls pci_find_cap for PCI Express and returns its error directly (without iwn_detach) if nonzero; it enables bus mastering and allocates the memory BAR, returning ENOMEM directly (without iwn_detach) if that fails. It then tries to allocate one MSI vector and allocates the IRQ resource (shared when MSI was not obtained); from that point every failure jumps to the fail label, which calls iwn_detach(dev) and returns the saved error: IRQ allocation failure (ENOMEM), then after the lock init and hardware-specific attach, errors from iwn_config_specific, iwn_hw_prepare, iwn_alloc_fwmem, iwn_alloc_kw, iwn_alloc_ict (not done for the 4965), iwn_alloc_sched, any iwn_alloc_tx_ring, iwn_alloc_rx_ring, iwn_read_eeprom, taskqueue_start_threads and bus_setup_intr. On the success path it also clears pending interrupts, fills in the ieee80211com capabilities (HT capabilities only when IWN_FLAG_HAS_11N is set), calls ieee80211_ifattach and saves/overrides the ampdu, addba, wme and other net80211 callbacks, attaches radiotap, initialises the three callouts and the rftoggle, panic and xmit tasks and the transmit mbuf queue, creates and starts the taskqueue, attaches sysctls, installs the interrupt handler, optionally announces the device, creates the debug character device (if make_dev returns NULL only a message is printed; otherwise si_drv1 is set to the softc) and returns 0.

functions.name: iwn_scan
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc, vap (with valid iv_bss and iv_ifp) and ss are non-NULL: ss is tested against NULL once when copying the SSID, but it is dereferenced unconditionally later (ss->ss_nssid when setting the channel flags and when computing the dwell time), so a NULL ss would fault. The argument c is ignored: it is replaced by ic->ic_curchan. If sc->sc_is_scanning is already set it prints a message and returns EAGAIN with no other effect. Otherwise it sets sc->rxon to &sc->rx_on[IWN_RXON_BSS_CTX], then allocates the scan buffer (M_NOWAIT); on failure it returns ENOMEM (sc->rxon has already been assigned). It builds the scan header, a TX template with a broadcast probe request (SSID, rates and, if HT, HT capabilities) and one channel entry for the current channel with active or passive flags and dwell times, sets sc->sc_is_scanning to 1, sends the command with iwn_cmd(sc, IWN_CMD_SCAN, buf, buflen, 1), frees the buffer, arms sc->scan_timeout for 5 seconds only if iwn_cmd returned 0, and returns iwn_cmd's result. In this function sc_is_scanning is not reset if iwn_cmd fails, so it stays 1 after any path that got past the buffer allocation. No lock is taken or released here.

functions.name: iwx_run_init_mvm_ucode
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller holds the softc mutex (sc_mtx is used with msleep) and readnvm says whether the NVM should be read. If IWX_FLAG_RFKILL is set and readnvm is 0 it prints a message and returns EPERM. Otherwise it clears sc_init_complete, calls iwx_load_ucode_wait_alive and returns its error if nonzero. It then sends the init-extended-config command and the NVM-access-complete command with iwx_send_cmd_pdu, returning the error of the first one that fails (before any wait for the init-complete flag). Only then does it wait: while IWX_INIT_COMPLETE is not set in sc_init_complete it calls msleep on sc_init_complete (with sc_mtx, 2 second timeout) and returns the msleep error (for example a timeout) if nonzero. If readnvm is nonzero it then calls iwx_nvm_get (returning its error after printing a message) and copies the NVM hardware address into ic_macaddr. It returns 0 otherwise. The mutex is dropped during msleep and held again on every return.

functions.name: ixgbe_bp_set_state
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: arg1 is the ixgbe_softc and req is a valid sysctl request. It reads control page 0 with hw->mac.ops.bypass_rw while holding the bypass mutex (released right after) and returns that error if nonzero; it stores the status bits ((value >> BYPASS_STATUS_OFF_SHIFT) & 0x3) in a function-static variable and passes it to sysctl_handle_int; it returns that call's error, or 0 when the request carries no new value. A new value other than BYPASS_NORM, BYPASS_BYPASS or BYPASS_ISOLATE returns EINVAL. Otherwise, holding the bypass mutex, it calls bypass_set(hw, BYPASS_PAGE_CTL0, BYPASS_MODE_OFF_M, state): because of operator precedence in the assignment, a nonzero result of that call makes error equal 1 (not the driver's error code) and it skips the second call; if it succeeds it calls bypass_set again with BYPASS_AUTO and returns that call's error code. The mutex is released at the out label on both of these paths, followed by a 6 ms delay, and the function returns error.

functions.name: ixgbe_setup_mac_link_smartspeed
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hw is a valid ixgbe_hw. It reads AUTOC once at entry, sets hw->phy.autoneg_advertised from the 10G, 1G and 100M full-duplex bits of speed, and sets smart_speed_active to false. Then for up to IXGBE_SMARTSPEED_MAX_RETRIES rounds it calls ixgbe_setup_mac_link_82599 and polls ixgbe_check_link 5 times at 100 ms intervals; an error from either call, or link up, ends the function immediately and returns that status (IXGBE_SUCCESS when link came up) with smart_speed_active false. If no link came up in those rounds and the AUTOC value read at entry lacks KR support or lacks KX4/KX support, it returns the last status (IXGBE_SUCCESS) without any further attempt (no link may exist). Otherwise it sets smart_speed_active to true, calls ixgbe_setup_mac_link_82599 again (an error is returned with smart_speed_active still true) and polls ixgbe_check_link 6 times at 100 ms: an error or link up returns that status with smart_speed_active still true. If still no link it sets smart_speed_active back to false, calls ixgbe_setup_mac_link_82599 once more and returns its status. A message is logged if the link is up at 1 Gb/s.

functions.name: ixgbe_identify_sfp_module_generic
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hw is a valid ixgbe_hw with mac and phy ops set. It remembers the current sfp_type. If the media type is not fiber it sets phy.sfp_type to not_present and returns IXGBE_ERR_SFP_NOT_PRESENT (phy.id and phy.type are not changed on this path). Otherwise it calls set_lan_id and reads the identifier byte over I2C; if any of the checked I2C reads (identifier, 1G and 10G compliance codes, cable technology, and the three vendor OUI bytes when phy.type is not ixgbe_phy_nl) returns nonzero it goes to a common error exit that sets sfp_type to not_present, zeroes phy.id and sets phy.type to ixgbe_phy_unknown unless phy.type is ixgbe_phy_nl, and returns IXGBE_ERR_SFP_NOT_PRESENT (not the read's own error code). If the identifier is not IXGBE_SFF_IDENTIFIER_SFP it sets phy.type to ixgbe_phy_sfp_unsupported and returns IXGBE_ERR_SFP_NOT_SUPPORTED. Otherwise it sets phy.sfp_type from the cable type and compliance codes (on 82598 only DA passive, SR, LR or unknown; on others core 0 or core 1 variants depending on lan_id; the cable-spec read for active DA cables is not checked), sets sfp_setup_needed if sfp_type changed, sets multispeed_fiber, and unless phy.type is ixgbe_phy_nl records the identifier as phy.id and sets phy.type from the vendor OUI. Then: a DA passive or active cable returns IXGBE_SUCCESS; a module with 10G compliance 0 whose sfp_type is not one of the 1G types sets phy.type to ixgbe_phy_sfp_unsupported and returns IXGBE_ERR_SFP_NOT_SUPPORTED; an 82598 returns IXGBE_SUCCESS; otherwise it reads the device caps and, unless IXGBE_DEVICE_CAPS_ALLOW_ANY_SFP is set or the type is a 1G type, accepts only Intel modules (IXGBE_SUCCESS) or, when hw->allow_unsupported_sfp is true, accepts with a one-time warning; else sets phy.type unsupported and returns IXGBE_ERR_SFP_NOT_SUPPORTED. All remaining cases return IXGBE_SUCCESS.

functions.name: ixgbe_check_mac_link_vf
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hw, speed and link_up are valid pointers (autoneg_wait_to_complete is unused). It sets mac->get_link_status to true if check_for_rst (mailbox ops[0]) returns 0 or mbx->timeout is 0. If get_link_status is false it skips to the exit. Otherwise it reads VFLINKS and exits if the link-up bit is clear; for the 82599 VF it re-reads VFLINKS five times at 100 us and exits if the link-up bit clears at any point. Past those checks it sets *speed from the speed bits of the last VFLINKS value (10G, or 2.5G on X550 or later with the non-standard bit; 1G; 100M, or 5G on X550/E610 VF with the non-standard bit; 10M on X550 or later for the X550EM_A 10M code; otherwise IXGBE_LINK_SPEED_UNKNOWN). It then reads one mailbox word with ixgbe_read_mbx: if that fails, get_link_status is cleared only when hw->api_version >= ixgbe_mbox_api_15, and the function exits with ret_val unchanged (IXGBE_SUCCESS); if the reply lacks IXGBE_VT_MSGTYPE_CTS it sets ret_val to IXGBE_ERR_MBX only when the FAILURE bit is also set, else leaves IXGBE_SUCCESS, and exits; if CTS is present and mbx->timeout is 0 it sets ret_val to IXGBE_ERR_TIMEOUT and exits; otherwise it clears get_link_status. At the exit it sets *link_up to !mac->get_link_status and returns ret_val. *speed is written only on the path that reached the speed decode; on other paths it is left unchanged.

functions.name: i40e_aq_debug_dump
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hw is a valid hardware structure; ret_buff_size, ret_next_table and ret_next_index may each be NULL. It returns I40E_ERR_PARAM, without sending anything, if buff_size is 0 or buff is NULL. Otherwise it fills a default descriptor for the i40e_aqc_opc_debug_dump_internals opcode, sets the buffer flag (and the large-buffer flag when buff_size > I40E_AQ_LARGE_BUF), writes cluster_id, table_id and the little-endian start_index into the command, sets datalen to buff_size, and sends it with i40e_asq_send_command using buff as the data buffer. It returns that call's status. Only when the status is zero (I40E_SUCCESS) does it write each non-NULL output: *ret_buff_size from the descriptor's returned datalen, *ret_next_table from the response table_id and *ret_next_index from the response idx; on any error status none of them is written.

functions.name: i40e_remove_pd_page
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hw and hmc_info are valid pointers and idx is a valid index into hmc_info->sd_table.sd_entry; hmc_info is dereferenced by the callee, so it must not be NULL. It calls i40e_prep_remove_pd_page(hmc_info, idx). If that does not return I40E_SUCCESS it returns I40E_SUCCESS (the initial value) without calling the second step; the prep call itself returns I40E_ERR_NOT_READY without changing anything when the pd table's ref_cnt is nonzero, and on success marks the sd entry invalid and decrements the sd table reference count. If the prep succeeded it returns the status of i40e_remove_pd_page_new(hw, hmc_info, idx, TRUE), whose effects on registers and entries were not read.

functions.name: i40e_remove_sd_bp
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hw and hmc_info are valid pointers and idx is a valid index into hmc_info->sd_table.sd_entry; hmc_info is dereferenced by the callee, so it must not be NULL. It calls i40e_prep_remove_sd_bp(hmc_info, idx). That call decrements the sd entry's backing-page reference count first and, if the count is still nonzero, returns I40E_ERR_NOT_READY (the decrement stays applied); otherwise it decrements the sd table reference count, marks the entry invalid and returns I40E_SUCCESS. If prep does not return I40E_SUCCESS, i40e_remove_sd_bp returns I40E_SUCCESS (its initial value) without calling the second step; if prep succeeds it returns the status of i40e_remove_sd_bp_new(hw, hmc_info, idx, TRUE), whose effects were not read.

functions.name: jedec_dimm_attach
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is a jedec_dimm device whose parent is an smbus device; the softc is zeroed by this function. It zeroes the softc and stores dev, smbus, spd_addr and tsod_addr, then reads the SPD DRAM-type byte; on a read error it prints a message and returns that error. DDR3 and DDR4 set type_str and the per-type offsets; any other type prints a message and returns EINVAL. It then fills capacity_mb, the manufacturing year and week, the part number and the serial number, returning the error of the first of jedec_dimm_capacity, jedec_dimm_mfg_date or jedec_dimm_field_to_str that fails, and reads the TSOD-present byte, returning its error if the read fails. On all of these error returns no sysctl has been added and the device description is unchanged, but the softc already holds the fields set so far. If the TSOD-present byte has bit 0x80 set it reads the TSOD manufacturer and device ID words; a failure of either read prints a message and is treated as TSOD absent with rc 0 (not an error); otherwise it looks up a known TSOD name. It then adds the type, capacity, part, serial, mfg_year and mfg_week sysctls; adds the temp sysctl only if a TSOD is present and its IDs matched a known device; if a slotid hint exists it stores a strdup(M_DEVBUF) copy in sc->slotid_str and adds a slotid sysctl; and if a TSOD name or slotid exists it extends the device description with them. It returns 0.

functions.name: kbd_realloc_array
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: Giant is held (GIANT_REQUIRED) and the global keyboard array and its size keyboards are consistent. It computes newsize = rounddown(keyboards + ARRAY_DELTA, ARRAY_DELTA) and allocates a zeroed array of that many keyboard_t pointers with M_NOWAIT; if the allocation fails it returns ENOMEM and leaves the old array and keyboards unchanged. Otherwise it copies the old keyboards entries into the new array, frees the old array only if keyboards > 1 (so that the initial static array is not freed), stores the new array in the global keyboard, sets keyboards to newsize, prints the new size when bootverbose is set and returns 0.

functions.name: lio_get_set_intr_coalesce
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: arg1 is the struct lio, arg2 selects the coalescing parameter (LIO_USE_ADAPTIVE_RX/TX_COALESCE, LIO_RX_COALESCE_USECS, LIO_RX/TX_MAX_COALESCED_FRAMES, the packet-rate, low/high trigger and sample-interval parameters), req is a sysctl request. For an unrecognised arg2 it returns EINVAL. For each parameter it first loads the current value into both new_val and old_val only under a condition that depends on the parameter: the adaptive-enable flags and the low/high/rate/interval parameters are loaded only when adaptive rx (or tx for the TX ones) is enabled, and the plain RX_COALESCE_USECS and the two MAX_COALESCED_FRAMES parameters only when the corresponding adaptive mode is disabled; otherwise old_val and the value shown remain 0. It calls sysctl_handle_64; if that returns an error or req->newptr is NULL it returns that error (or 0). It returns 0 without changes when the new value equals old_val (so with old_val still 0 a written value of 0 is also treated as no change). Otherwise it applies the value: the adaptive flags are set to 1 or 0; the plain usecs/frames values are held for the hardware step below; the rate, trigger and interval fields are stored in intrmod_cfg only if adaptive rx (or tx, or either for the two rate parameters and the interval) is enabled. It then refreshes rx_usecs, rx_frames and tx_frames in intrmod_cfg from the device configuration and calls lio_set_intrmod_cfg (a failure only logs a message). If adaptive rx is disabled it programs the hardware with lio_intrmod_cfg_rx_intrtime and lio_intrmod_cfg_rx_intrcnt (using the saved values from oct when no new one was given) and returns the first nonzero return value; if adaptive rx is enabled it copies the configured rx values into oct. Likewise if adaptive tx is disabled it calls lio_intrmod_cfg_tx_intrcnt and returns its nonzero result, else copies the configured tx value into oct. It returns 0 if nothing failed.

functions.name: mana_poll
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: arg is a valid struct mana_cq with a valid gdma_cq (pending is unused). It sets cq->work_done to 0 and cq->budget to MANA_RX_BUDGET for a receive queue (MANA_CQ_TYPE_RX) or MANA_TX_BUDGET otherwise.
