It then loops at most MANA_POLL_BUDGET times; on the last allowed iteration it first sets cq->budget to CQE_POLLING_BUFFER + 1; each iteration calls mana_cq_handler(cq, cq->gdma_cq) and leaves the loop if cq->work_done < cq->budget, otherwise it resets cq->work_done to 0 and continues. mana_cq_handler polls the RX or TX completions and then always calls mana_gd_ring_cq on the queue, with the arm bit set only when work_done < budget and cq->do_not_ring_db is false (otherwise it rings with arm bit 0). The function returns nothing.

functions.name: mfi_dump_blocks
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc is a valid softc, len is nonnegative, and virt points to len readable bytes (the data is sent to the device, flags MFI_CMD_DATAOUT). It returns EBUSY if mfi_dequeue_free returns no command, without touching anything else. Otherwise it zeroes the command frame (keeping its context), fills an MFI_CMD_LD_WRITE I/O frame for target id with lba, header data_len = howmany(len, MFI_SECTOR_LEN) (a sector count) and sets cm_data = virt, cm_len = len, and flags MFI_CMD_POLLED | MFI_CMD_DATAOUT. It calls mfi_mapcmd; if that returns nonzero it prints a message. Then in all cases it syncs cm_dmamap with BUS_DMASYNC_POSTWRITE, unloads the DMA map, releases the command and returns the result of mfi_mapcmd (0, or the nonzero error, in which case the write may not have been performed).

functions.name: mfi_linux_ioctl_int
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev->si_drv1 is an initialised mfi softc and arg is a user pointer to a packet whose type depends on cmd. For MFI_LINUX_CMD_2: it copies in a mfi_linux_ioc_packet (returning the copyin error), returns EINVAL if lioc_sge_count > MAX_LINUX_IOCTL_SGE, and returns EBUSY if no free command can be dequeued (these three returns happen before any command, buffer or lock is held). It copies the frame into the command, allocates a zeroed kernel data buffer of the header data_len when a data direction flag is set, and for data-out commands copies each scatter-gather segment from the user iov_base addresses into it (a copyin failure goes to the exit). It takes the config lock for DCMD commands, then under mfi_io_lock calls mfi_check_command_pre and mfi_wait_command (an error from either goes to the exit). For data-in commands it copies the data back out to each segment's user iov_base; if lioc_sense_len is nonzero it copies the command's sense data to the user address taken from the sense offset in the user packet; then it copies the one-byte command status into the user packet's frame header. Any copyout failure goes to the exit. At the exit it unlocks the config lock, frees the data buffer if any, releases the command under mfi_io_lock and returns the error (0 on success). For MFI_LINUX_SET_AEN_2: it copies in the mfi_linux_ioc_aen (returning the copyin error without allocating anything), prints a message, allocates an AEN entry, and under mfi_io_lock inserts it into sc->mfi_aen_pids and calls mfi_aen_register; if that fails the entry is removed and freed; it returns mfi_aen_register's result. For any other cmd it prints a message and returns ENOENT without touching arg.

functions.name: atphy_service
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc, mii and mii->mii_media.ifm_cur are valid. MII_POLLSTAT does nothing before the common status update. MII_MEDIACHG: for IFM_AUTO or IFM_1000_T it calls atphy_setmedia and then falls to the common status update; for IFM_100_TX or IFM_10_T it programs the ANAR, clears the gigabit control register when the PHY has gigabit extended capabilities, and writes BMCR with the speed, duplex and reset/autoneg/restart bits; for IFM_NONE it writes BMCR with BMCR_ISO set; any other subtype returns EINVAL immediately with no status update. MII_TICK: if the current media subtype is not IFM_AUTO it sets mii_ticks to 0 and continues; for IFM_AUTO it reads BMSR twice and if the link is up it sets mii_ticks to 0 and continues; if the link is down, the first such tick (mii_ticks was 0) continues without further action, later ticks return 0 immediately, skipping the status update, while mii_ticks (after incrementing) is at most mii_anegticks, and once mii_ticks exceeds mii_anegticks it resets mii_ticks to 0, calls atphy_setmedia and continues. Every path that continues, including all MII_MEDIACHG paths except EINVAL, then calls PHY_STATUS(sc) and mii_phy_update(sc, cmd) and returns 0.

functions.name: e1000phy_service
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc, mii and mii->mii_media.ifm_cur are valid. MII_POLLSTAT does nothing before the common update. MII_MEDIACHG: for IFM_AUTO it calls e1000phy_mii_phy_auto; otherwise it chooses the speed from the subtype and returns EINVAL for IFM_1000_T when MIIF_HAVE_GTCR is not set, for IFM_1000_SX when the PHY has neither 1000BASE-X full nor half duplex extended capability, and for any unlisted subtype; IFM_NONE writes E1000_CR with the isolate and power-down bits set and skips the rest; the other speeds write the gigabit control, advertisement and control registers with a reset. MII_TICK: for a non-IFM_AUTO media it sets mii_ticks to 0; for IFM_AUTO it reads BMSR twice, sets mii_ticks to 0 if link is up, and if link is down it increments mii_ticks and acts only once mii_ticks exceeds mii_anegticks, in which case it sets mii_ticks to 0, calls PHY_RESET and e1000phy_mii_phy_auto. Every path that does not return EINVAL then calls PHY_STATUS(sc) and mii_phy_update(sc, cmd) and returns 0. mii_ticks is modified only on the MII_TICK path.

functions.name: gentbi_service
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc and mii are valid; cmd is the service command. For MII_POLLSTAT nothing is done before the common update. For MII_MEDIACHG it calls mii_phy_setmedia(sc) and then also continues to the common update. For MII_TICK it calls mii_phy_tick(sc) and returns 0 immediately, skipping the status update, if that returns EJUSTRETURN; otherwise it continues. For any other cmd it continues. On every path that continues it calls PHY_STATUS(sc) and mii_phy_update(sc, cmd), and returns 0. The function returns 0 on all paths.

functions.name: mlx4_master_process_vhcr
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is a master device, slave a valid slave index, and in_vhcr is either NULL (the vhcr is then read from the slave by DMA with mlx4_ACCESS_MEM and the result is written back to the slave) or a caller-supplied vhcr command buffer. It allocates a software vhcr, returning -ENOMEM if that fails. If in_vhcr is NULL and the DMA read fails it frees the software vhcr and returns that error without writing a status. It decodes the vhcr fields and looks up the command in cmd_info; an unknown opcode sets status CMD_STAT_BAD_PARAM and goes to out_status. For commands with an inbox it allocates a mailbox (failure: CMD_STAT_BAD_SIZE) and reads it from the slave (failure: status CMD_STAT_INTERNAL_ERR, and ret keeps the nonzero DMA error); a failing verify function gives CMD_STAT_BAD_OP; an outbox allocation failure gives CMD_STAT_BAD_SIZE (all of these go to out_status). It then runs the command through its wrapper or, if none, through __mlx4_cmd; an error is converted with mlx4_errno_to_status into vhcr_cmd->status and goes to out_status. On success, if the command has an outbox and status is 0, it DMA-writes the outbox back to the slave; a failure there logs an error and goes to the out label, skipping the vhcr result write-back and returning that error. At out_status, only when in_vhcr is NULL, it DMA-writes the vhcr result back to the slave, overwriting ret with that result (an error is only logged) and generates a command-completion EQE if the e_bit is set and the write-back succeeded. At out it frees the software vhcr, inbox and outbox and returns ret. So command failures are reported through vhcr_cmd->status and the return value is usually 0, but it is nonzero when the initial read, the outbox write-back or the final result write-back fails, and also when an inbox read failure occurred and in_vhcr was non-NULL.

functions.name: mlx4_master_do_cmd
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is a master device with priv->mfunc.master.slave_state allocated and slave is a valid index; the caller holds neither slave_state_lock nor cmd.slave_cmd_mutex. It first flips slave_state[slave].comm_toggle and builds reply with the new toggle in bit 31. If the toggle argument differs from the new comm_toggle it goes to the reset_slave path. If cmd is MLX4_COMM_CMD_RESET it clears active, old_vlan_api and vst_qinq_supported, deactivates the slave admin state and resets each event_eq entry (eqn -1, token 0); if the slave last_cmd is MLX4_COMM_CMD_FLR it then jumps straight to inform_slave_state, skipping the resource deletion, the shutdown event and the last_cmd update; otherwise it dispatches MLX4_DEV_EVENT_SLAVE_SHUTDOWN, adds the comm version to reply and goes to reset_slave. For a non-RESET cmd received while last_cmd is MLX4_COMM_CMD_FLR it logs a warning and returns without writing a reply. Otherwise it handles the command in sequence: VHCR0 (requires last_cmd RESET) starts vhcr_dma and clears the cookie; VHCR1 and VHCR2 (each requiring the previous command as last_cmd) add the next address parts; VHCR_EN (requires last_cmd VHCR2) completes vhcr_dma, calls mlx4_master_activate_admin_state (failure goes to reset_slave), sets active and dispatches MLX4_DEV_EVENT_SLAVE_INIT; VHCR_POST (requires last_cmd VHCR_EN or VHCR_POST) calls mlx4_master_process_vhcr(dev, slave, NULL) with slave_cmd_mutex held and released again (a nonzero return goes to reset_slave); an out-of-sequence or unknown command goes to reset_slave. After a handled command it takes slave_state_lock (irqsave) and sets last_cmd to cmd unless the slave is going down, in which case it logs and returns without writing a reply; otherwise it writes reply (just the new toggle bit) to priv->mfunc.comm[slave].slave_read followed by mmiowb. At reset_slave it deletes all resources for the slave if the interface state is UP, adds COMM_CHAN_EVENT_INTERNAL_ERR to reply when cmd is not RESET, sets last_cmd to MLX4_COMM_CMD_RESET unless the slave is going down, then at inform_slave_state zeroes the first sizeof(struct mlx4_slave_event_eq_info) bytes of event_eq, writes reply to slave_read and issues wmb. The function returns nothing.

functions.name: mlx4_master_do_cmd
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is a master device with priv->mfunc.master.slave_state allocated and slave is a valid index; the caller holds neither slave_state_lock nor cmd.slave_cmd_mutex. It first flips slave_state[slave].comm_toggle and builds reply with the new toggle in bit 31. If the toggle argument differs from the new comm_toggle it goes to the reset_slave path. If cmd is MLX4_COMM_CMD_RESET it clears active, old_vlan_api and vst_qinq_supported, deactivates the slave admin state and resets each event_eq entry (eqn -1, token 0); if the slave last_cmd is MLX4_COMM_CMD_FLR it then jumps straight to inform_slave_state, skipping the resource deletion, the shutdown event and the last_cmd update; otherwise it dispatches MLX4_DEV_EVENT_SLAVE_SHUTDOWN, adds the comm version to reply and goes to reset_slave. For a non-RESET cmd received while last_cmd is MLX4_COMM_CMD_FLR it logs a warning and returns without writing a reply. Otherwise it handles the command in sequence: VHCR0 (requires last_cmd RESET) starts vhcr_dma and clears the cookie; VHCR1 and VHCR2 (each requiring the previous command as last_cmd) add the next address parts; VHCR_EN (requires last_cmd VHCR2) completes vhcr_dma, calls mlx4_master_activate_admin_state (failure goes to reset_slave), sets active and dispatches MLX4_DEV_EVENT_SLAVE_INIT; VHCR_POST (requires last_cmd VHCR_EN or VHCR_POST) calls mlx4_master_process_vhcr(dev, slave, NULL) with slave_cmd_mutex held and released again (a nonzero return goes to reset_slave); an out-of-sequence or unknown command goes to reset_slave. After a handled command it takes slave_state_lock (irqsave) and sets last_cmd to cmd unless the slave is going down, in which case it logs and returns without writing a reply; otherwise it writes reply (just the new toggle bit) to priv->mfunc.comm[slave].slave_read followed by mmiowb. At reset_slave it deletes all resources for the slave if the interface state is UP, adds COMM_CHAN_EVENT_INTERNAL_ERR to reply when cmd is not RESET, sets last_cmd to MLX4_COMM_CMD_RESET unless the slave is going down, then at inform_slave_state zeroes the first sizeof(struct mlx4_slave_event_eq_info) bytes of event_eq, writes reply to slave_read and issues wmb. The function returns nothing.

functions.name: mlx4_init_slave
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is a slave function with its comm channel mapped; the caller does not hold priv->cmd.slave_cmd_mutex. It returns -EAGAIN without taking the mutex if the global pf_loading is nonzero. Otherwise it takes slave_cmd_mutex, sets max_cmds to 1 and checks mlx4_comm_check_offline; if the channel is offline it releases the mutex and returns -EIO without sending any command. It then resets the VF support state and sends MLX4_COMM_CMD_RESET with mlx4_comm_cmd: if that returns MLX4_DELAY_RESET_SLAVE (the slave is in FLR) it releases the mutex and returns -EAGAIN without sending a further command; any other nonzero result goes to the error exit. It then compares the interface revision from the comm channel with its own and goes to the error exit on a mismatch, and sends VHCR0, VHCR1, VHCR2 and VHCR_EN carrying the 64-bit VHCR DMA address in four parts, going to the error exit if any fails. On success it releases the mutex and returns 0. The error exit sends another MLX4_COMM_CMD_RESET (timeout 0, result ignored), releases the mutex and returns -EIO. So -EIO is returned when the channel is offline (no RESET sent), when the first RESET fails for a reason other than FLR delay, on revision mismatch, or when any VHCR command fails (the last three after a second RESET).

functions.name: __mlx4_qp_modify
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev, qp and context are valid; mtt must be valid for the RST-to-INIT transition (it is not used otherwise). It returns -EINVAL, issuing nothing, if cur_state or new_state is MLX4_QP_NUM_STATE or more, or if the static op table has no command for that pair. If the command is MLX4_CMD_2RST_QP it issues it directly with mlx4_cmd (no mailbox is allocated on this path) and then, if the device is a master, cur_state is neither MLX4_QP_STATE_ERR nor MLX4_QP_STATE_RST and the QP is the master or proxy QP0 (is_master_qp0), it clears the matching proxy_qp0_active or qp0_active flag of port (qpn & 1) + 1; it then returns the mlx4_cmd result, whether or not the command succeeded. For other commands it allocates a command mailbox and returns PTR_ERR of it on failure. For RST to INIT it fills the MTT base address and log page size in the context; for RTR to RTS it sets roce_entropy when MLX4_DEV_CAP_FLAG2_ROCE_V1_V2 is set. It writes optpar and a copy of the context with local_qpn = qp->qpn into the mailbox and issues the command (op[cur_state][new_state]) with mlx4_cmd. Afterwards, if the device is a master and the QP is a master or proxy QP0, it clears the qp0/proxy_qp0 active flag when the new state is ERR from a state other than ERR or RST, or sets it when the new state is RTR; these updates are made regardless of whether the command succeeded. It frees the mailbox and returns the mlx4_cmd result.

functions.name: mlx4_QP_FLOW_STEERING_ATTACH_wrapper
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev, slave, vhcr, inbox, outbox and cmd describe a flow-steering attach command from the slave; inbox->buf holds a mlx4_net_trans_rule_hw_ctrl followed by the rule header. It returns -EOPNOTSUPP if dev->caps.steering_mode is not MLX4_STEERING_MODE_DEVICE_MANAGED, and -EINVAL if mlx4_slave_convert_port returns a value <= 0 for the control port (otherwise it stores the converted port in the control block). It reads the QP number, takes a reference on the QP resource with get_res and returns its error if that fails (nothing to release yet). It maps the rule header id. If the slave is the device's own function (slave == dev->caps.function) it skips all header checks and goes straight to executing the command. Otherwise by header id: for Ethernet it returns -EINVAL (after releasing the QP) when validate_eth_header_mac fails; IB is accepted; IPv4, TCP and UDP rules get an Ethernet header added with add_eth_header (failure is -EINVAL) and vhcr->in_modifier is increased by the Ethernet header size in 4-byte units; any other id returns -EINVAL. It then issues MLX4_QP_FLOW_STEERING_ATTACH with mlx4_cmd_imm, placing the rule id in vhcr->out_param (a failure returns that error after releasing the QP reference, with no detach). On success it registers the rule as a RES_FS_RULE owned by the slave and bound to qpn with add_res_range, looks it up with get_res, allocates a mirror copy of the inbox in that resource (-ENOMEM on failure), swaps the mirror's port (1 becomes 2, anything else becomes 1), calls mlx4_do_mirror_rule when the device is bonded and increments the QP ref_count. A failure of add_res_range, of the second get_res, or of the allocation, after the attach command succeeded, sends MLX4_QP_FLOW_STEERING_DETACH for the new rule id; this function does not call rem_res_range for a RES_FS_RULE that was already registered. The RES_FS_RULE reference is released with put_res when it was taken, and the QP reference taken by get_res is released with put_res on every path after the QP lookup succeeded. It returns 0 on success or the error described.

functions.name: mlx4_ib_mcg_work_handler
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: work is the work member of a valid mcast_group on which a reference is held for this scheduled work; the caller does not hold group->lock. It takes group->lock and starts with a release count rc = 1 (for the scheduled work). If group->state is MCAST_RESP_READY it cancels the timeout work; if the response TID differs from last_req_tid it logs, restores state to prev_state and skips to request processing; otherwise: for a nonzero response status, if the method is GET_RESP and a pending request exists it replies to the slave with that status, removes and frees the first pending request and increments rc (if none exists it only logs), while a DELETE_RESP during demux flushing increments rc; for a zero status it computes the response and current join states, decrements rc for a GET_RESP that moves the group from no joined state to a joined one, increments rc for a non-GET_RESP whose response join state is 0, and in both cases copies the response record into group->rec. After a matching response it sets state to MCAST_IDLE. Then, while the pending list is non-empty and the state is MCAST_IDLE, it takes the first request and adds to rc the return value of handle_leave_req (for a DELETE request) or handle_join_req (otherwise); those values depend on the request and may be 0 or more than 1. If the state is still MCAST_IDLE it computes the join state to leave with get_leave_state; if nonzero it clears those bits in group->rec and sends a leave to the wire: on a send failure it restores the state and increments rc, else the state becomes MCAST_LEAVE_SENT. If requests are still pending and the state is MCAST_IDLE it repeats the request processing. It then releases group->lock and calls release_group(group, 0) rc times (rc can be below 1 after the decrement above, in which case fewer releases are made). The function returns nothing.

functions.name: create_qp_common
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev, pd, init_attr and caller_qp are valid; *caller_qp is NULL (the function allocates the QP) or a preallocated QP; for a user PD udata holds the create-QP command. It first classifies the QP type; a tunnel QP request whose proxy type is not SMI or GSI, or made on a non-master device, returns -EINVAL. If *caller_qp is NULL it allocates an sqp or qp structure (-ENOMEM on failure, returning at once). It sets up the RQ size (set_rq_size); then for a user PD copies the create command (-EFAULT on failure), sets the SQ size, pins the buffer with ib_umem_get (PTR_ERR on failure), and initialises and writes the MTT; for a kernel PD it handles the NETIF flag (if IB_QP_CREATE_NETIF_QP is requested but device-managed steering is not supported it jumps to the err label with err still 0, i.e. it returns 0 without creating a QP, freeing a QP allocated here), sets the kernel SQ size, allocates the doorbell, the QP buffer (with a smaller-alignment retry) and the MTT, and the sq/rq wrid arrays (-ENOMEM on failure). For a special QP number (sqpn) of proxy SMI, SMI owner or GSI type it allocates proxy buffers with alloc_proxy_bufs (-ENOMEM on failure); otherwise it reserves a QP number (steering-managed for NETIF). It then calls mlx4_qp_alloc, sets the doorbell QPN, sets *caller_qp if it was NULL, and under the reset-flow resource lock adds the QP to the device list and the send and receive CQ lists, and returns 0. Failures after the buffers exist unwind through labels: err_qpn releases the reserved QPN when sqpn is 0; err_proxy frees proxy buffers only when the QP type is MLX4_IB_QPT_PROXY_GSI (proxy SMI and SMI owner buffers allocated at 841 are not freed on these paths); then the doorbell mapping or wrid arrays, the MTT, the buffer or umem, and the doorbell are released as applicable; at err a QP allocated by this call (*caller_qp NULL) is freed. The function returns the saved negative errno (or 0 on success or the NETIF-unsupported path).

functions.name: try_add_to_existing_fg
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ft is a flow table, match_head lists the candidate flow groups, ft_version is the table version snapshot taken before the search; the caller holds the node references the mlx5 flow-steering code expects. It allocates a scratch fte with alloc_fte; if that fails it returns ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM) (whatever alloc_fte's error was). Unless FLOW_ACT_NO_APPEND is set it first searches the groups for an existing fte matching the spec: if one is found (lookup_fte_locked) it calls add_rule_fg on it, releases the found fte's lock and reference, frees the scratch fte and returns add_rule_fg's result, which can be a rule or an ERR_PTR. If no existing fte is used, it returns ERR_PTR(-EAGAIN) (freeing the scratch fte) when the table version has changed; if the group list version changed since the search it retries the search with write locking. Then for each active group it tries insert_fte(g, fte): on -ENOSPC it goes on to the next group; on any other error it frees the scratch fte and returns ERR_PTR(err); on success it calls add_rule_fg on the inserted fte (the scratch fte now being the inserted one and not freed) and returns that result, and if add_rule_fg returned an error it also drops the inserted fte with tree_put_node. If no group accepted the fte it frees the scratch fte and returns ERR_PTR(-ENOENT).

functions.name: init_one
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: pdev is a PCI device being probed by this driver and id is NULL or the matching pci_device_id. It allocates the softc with kzalloc_node and does not check the result for failure before using it. It stores the NUMA node and pci_dev_data, falls back to the default profile if mlx5_prof_sel is out of range, sets the device description, initialises the sysctl context and adds several scalar sysctls (return values ignored), then creates the pme_stats, pme_stats errors and caps (with current and max subnodes) sysctl nodes; if any of those node creations returns NULL it sets err = -ENOMEM and jumps to clean_sysctl_ctx (which frees the sysctl context and the softc). The opaque capability sysctls (SYSCTL_ADD_OPAQUE) and the counters are added without checking for failure. It then initialises lists, locks and the dump_lock, and calls mlx5_pci_init, mlx5_health_init, mlx5_pagealloc_init, mlx5_fs_core_alloc and mlx5_load_one in order; a nonzero error from mlx5_pci_init, mlx5_health_init, mlx5_fs_core_alloc or mlx5_load_one is logged and the matching cleanup labels run in reverse (flow steering freed, page allocator and health cleaned up, PCI closed, dump lock destroyed, sysctl context freed, softc freed with kfree) and the error is returned. On success it calls mlx5_fwdump_prep and mlx5_firmware_update (results not used); under PCI_IOV, when the vport group manager capability is set it reads the SR-IOV VF total, calls mlx5_eswitch_init, and only if that succeeds sets up the IOV schemas and calls pci_iov_attach; dev->iov_pf is set true only if pci_iov_attach also succeeds, and failures of either are only logged. It then calls pci_save_state and returns 0.

functions.name: mlx5e_create_ethtool
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: priv is an initialised mlx5e_priv whose mdev, params and sysctl_ctx are set up; the function returns nothing and takes no locks. It fills priv->params_ethtool from priv->params and the device capabilities, and, when the disable_local_lb_mc or disable_local_lb_uc capability is set, queries the multicast and unicast local loopback state (a failed query leaves that field unchanged). It then creates the "conf" sysctl node and returns immediately if that returns NULL; otherwise it registers one read-only or read-write handler per entry of mlx5e_params_desc (read-only for names containing _max or _mtu). It creates the "fec" node and returns immediately if that is NULL; if mlx5e_fec_update returns 0 it registers the FEC mode and mask sysctls. It registers debug_stats and the PCI device-name string, calls mlx5e_create_diagnostics, and creates the "qos" node, returning immediately if that returns NULL. Under qos it registers tc_max_rate only when mlx5e_getmaxrate returns 0, tc_rate_share only when mlx5e_get_max_alloc returns 0, prio_0_7_tc only when mlx5e_get_prio_tc returns 0, and, when mlx5e_get_dscp returns 0, the dscp_%d_%d_prio sysctls for i = 0, 8, ... below MLX5_MAX_SUPPORTED_DSCP and trust_state; it registers buffers_size, buffers_prio and cable_length only when mlx5e_port_query_buffer returns 0, and hw_temperature when mlx5e_hw_temperature_update returns 0. The results of the individual SYSCTL_ADD_* calls other than the three node creations are not checked, and the registered entries belong to priv->sysctl_ctx.

functions.name: mlx5e_sq_tls_xmit
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sq, parg and *ppmb are valid and the mbuf has a packet header. It returns MLX5E_TLS_CONTINUE without touching parg if the mbuf has no CSUM_SND_TAG flag or its send tag type is not TLS (or TLS rate-limit when RATELIMIT is built). It computes the full header size and returns MLX5E_TLS_FAILURE if the size is 0 or no TCP header is found. If the whole packet is just headers, or mlx5e_sq_tls_populate returns 0 (no TLS record header could be filled in), it sets parg->tisn to 0 and parg->ihs to the header size and returns MLX5E_TLS_CONTINUE. Otherwise it takes the tag lock only around a state check: an INIT tag releases the lock and returns MLX5E_TLS_FAILURE; a SETUP tag becomes TXRDY with expected_seq forced to a value different from the packet sequence; the lock is released in every case before continuing. If expected_seq differs from the TCP sequence number of the packet (out of order) it calls sbtls_recover_record: a NULL result counts a tx error and returns MLX5E_TLS_FAILURE; otherwise, when the recovered data starts a record it sets the initial record number, sends the static and progress parameter work requests and, if the recovered mbuf carries no data, sends a NOP, sets expected_seq to the packet sequence and returns MLX5E_TLS_LOOP. In the other out-of-order cases it sets parg->tisn and parg->mst and sends the recovered data with mlx5e_sq_dump_xmit: on failure it frees the recovered mbuf, sets expected_seq to the recovered record start sequence and returns MLX5E_TLS_FAILURE (parg->tisn and parg->mst have already been changed); on success it sets expected_seq to the packet sequence and returns MLX5E_TLS_LOOP. In the in-order case it counts statistics, advances expected_seq by the payload length, sets parg->tisn, parg->ihs and parg->mst and returns MLX5E_TLS_CONTINUE.

functions.name: update_buffer_lossy
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: priv, buffer (an array of MLX5E_MAX_PRIORITY priority-to-buffer entries), port_buffer and change are valid. For each of MLX5E_MAX_BUFFER buffers it counts the priorities mapped to it and how many of them have their bit clear in pfc_en, and sets the lossy flag to 1 if all mapped priorities are non-PFC (a buffer with no priorities mapped also gets lossy = 1), else 0, updating port_buffer->buffer[i].lossy and noting whether any flag changed. If none changed it returns 0 and leaves *change unmodified. If at least one changed it calls update_xoff_threshold(priv, port_buffer, xoff): a nonzero result is returned with *change not set (the lossy flags in port_buffer have already been modified); otherwise it sets *change to true and returns 0. The mtu argument is not used.

functions.name: mlx5e_port_manual_buffer_config
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: priv is a valid mlx5e_priv; change is a bit mask of MLX5E_PORT_BUFFER_* flags; pfc must be non-NULL when MLX5E_PORT_BUFFER_PFC is set, buffer_size must point to MLX5E_MAX_BUFFER entries when MLX5E_PORT_BUFFER_SIZE is set, and prio2buffer to MLX5E_MAX_PRIORITY entries when MLX5E_PORT_BUFFER_PRIO2BUFFER is set. It computes xoff with calculate_xoff, queries the current port buffer (returning the error), and per flag: CABLE_LEN marks an update and recomputes the xoff thresholds; PFC queries the priority-to-buffer map, sets priv->sw_is_port_buf_owner to true and calls update_buffer_lossy with pfc->pfc_en; PRIO2BUFFER marks a priority-map update, queries the current PFC enable and calls update_buffer_lossy with the new map; SIZE sets each buffer size from buffer_size, returning -EINVAL if a non-lossy buffer has size 0 or if the total exceeds port_buffer.port_buffer_size, marks an update and recomputes the thresholds. Each failing step returns its error at once (earlier steps may already have changed port_buffer in memory and sw_is_port_buf_owner). If no buffer update is pending and xoff differs from priv->dcbx.xoff it recomputes the thresholds and marks an update. It then stores xoff into priv->dcbx.xoff (before any hardware write), and if an update is pending sets sw_is_port_buf_owner to true and calls port_set_buffer (returning its error, with dcbx.xoff already updated), then, if a priority-map update is pending, sets sw_is_port_buf_owner to true and returns the result of mlx5e_port_set_priority2buffer; otherwise it returns err, which is 0 at that point.

functions.name: mlx5e_rl_sysctl_handler
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: arg1 is the mlx5e_rl_priv_data (with a valid priv) and arg2 indexes rl->param.arg. It takes PRIV_LOCK(priv) for its whole body (released at the done label on every path) and reads the stored value under the RL read lock. If req is non-NULL it calls sysctl_handle_64 and returns without changes (with that error, or 0) if the call failed, req->newptr is NULL, or the value equals the stored one; if req is NULL it does not return early: the stored value is used and it continues. It then returns ENXIO if priv->gone is set. Otherwise it records whether the rate-limit workers are open and whether cq_period_mode_modify is supported, and by parameter: tx_worker_threads_def, tx_channels_per_worker_def and tx_rates_def are clamped to [1, their max] and stored; tx_coalesce_usecs and tx_coalesce_pkts are clamped to [0, field max] (values below 1 become 0), stored, and if the workers are open the error of mlx5e_rl_refresh_channel_params is returned; tx_coalesce_mode is normalised to 0 or 1 and stored, and if the workers are open it either closes and reopens them (when mode modification is unsupported) or returns the refresh error (when supported); tx_queue_size is clamped to [1 << MLX5E_PARAMS_MINIMUM_LOG_SQ_SIZE, tx_queue_size_max], rounded to a power of two, stored with the workers closed and reopened if they were open, and the completion factor resynced; tx_completion_fact is stored the same way; tx_limit_add and tx_limit_clr return the error from mlx5e_rl_tx_limit_add / mlx5e_rl_tx_limit_clr; tx_allowed_deviation and tx_burst_size are clamped to their min and max and stored under the RL write lock; any other index changes nothing. The error variable is returned (0 except where a branch set it).

functions.name: mlx5e_rl_worker
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: arg is an initialised mlx5e_rl_worker (mutex, condvar, priv, channels, process_head and index_list_head valid) and the thread holds neither the worker lock nor the rate lock. It raises the thread priority, takes the worker lock, then for each of tx_channels_per_worker_def channels (skipping FREE channels unless HAVE_RL_PRE_ALLOCATE_CHANNELS is defined) it drops the worker lock, opens a send queue with mlx5e_rl_open_channel under the RL read lock, re-takes the worker lock, stops the loop after logging at the first failure, and otherwise sets the channel's rate to init_rate (the result of that rate setting is ignored). It then loops: it waits on the condvar while the process queue is empty and leaves the loop when worker_done is nonzero; it takes the first queued channel: for state MODIFY it sets the state to USED, then opens an SQ (logging an error, or incrementing tx_open_queues on success) if the channel has none, else resumes its SQ, and then sets the rate to new_rate * 8 (an error is logged); for state DESTROY it sets the rate to 0 (an error is logged), drains the SQ if there is one, inserts the channel at the head of index_list_head, sets the state to FREE and decrements tx_active_connections; other states are ignored. After the loop it goes through all tx_channels_per_worker_def channels: it copies last_rate to init_rate, sets the rate to 0 (result ignored), and closes the SQ (with the lock dropped) and decrements tx_open_queues if the channel has an SQ; the channel state is not changed. Finally it clears worker_done, broadcasts the condvar, releases the worker lock and calls kthread_exit.

functions.name: syndrome_to_errno
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: none; syndrome is an enum mlx5_ipsec_response_syndrome value and any integer is accepted. It returns 0 for MLX5_IPSEC_RESPONSE_SUCCESS (value 0), -EINVAL for MLX5_IPSEC_RESPONSE_ILLEGAL_REQUEST (value 1), -EEXIST for MLX5_IPSEC_RESPONSE_SADB_ISSUE (value 2), -EIO for MLX5_IPSEC_RESPONSE_WRITE_RESPONSE_ISSUE (value 3), and -EIO for every other value. It has no side effects.

functions.name: mlx5_fpga_device_reload
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: fdev is an initialised mlx5_fpga_device with a valid mdev. It reads fdev->fdev_state under state_lock: MLX5_FDEV_STATE_NONE gives -ENODEV and IN_PROGRESS gives -EBUSY (returned without taking the interface mutex). Otherwise it takes mdev->intf_state_mutex and holds it until return. For image MLX5_FPGA_IMAGE_RELOAD it returns the result of mlx5_fpga_device_reload_cmd without unregistering the device or changing MLX5_INTERFACE_STATE_UP. For any other image it clears MLX5_INTERFACE_STATE_UP, unregisters and stops the device, sets fdev_state to IN_PROGRESS and re-initialises load_event; then for image <= MLX5_FPGA_IMAGE_FACTORY it calls mlx5_fpga_load, for MLX5_FPGA_IMAGE_RESET it issues the reset control operation (a failure of either returns that error), and for any other image it logs an unknown command and returns err, which is 0 at that point. After a load or reset it calls wait_for_completion_timeout on load_event; if the value assigned to err is negative it sets fdev_state to MLX5_FDEV_STATE_FAILURE and returns it (a timeout, which returns 0, is not treated as an error). It then calls mlx5_fpga_device_start (a nonzero result is returned) and mlx5_register_device; if registration fails it sets fdev_state to FAILURE, stops the fpga device and returns the error; otherwise it sets MLX5_INTERFACE_STATE_UP and returns 0. In none of the paths is fdev_state set to MLX5_FDEV_STATE_SUCCESS by this function. The mutex is released on all paths after it was taken.

functions.name: mlx5_ib_poll_cq
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ibcq is a valid completion queue, num_entries is nonnegative and wc has room for num_entries completions. It takes cq->lock with interrupts saved and releases it on every path. If the core device state is MLX5_DEVICE_STATE_INTERNAL_ERROR it calls mlx5_ib_poll_sw_comp (software completions from the attached QPs) and returns the number it reports, without touching cq->wc_list and without polling hardware. Otherwise, if cq->wc_list is non-empty it polls soft completions with poll_soft_wc (count soft_polled), then calls mlx5_poll_one for up to num_entries - soft_polled entries, stopping at the first call that returns nonzero; each call that returns 0 increments npolled; if npolled is nonzero it updates the CQ consumer index with mlx5_cq_set_ci. It returns soft_polled + npolled, which is at most num_entries as far as the loop bounds show.

functions.name: mlx5_query_mad_ifc_port
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ibdev is a valid mlx5_ib device, port a 1-based port number, props a caller-owned writable struct ib_port_attr. It returns -EINVAL (props untouched) if port is below 1 or above the num_ports capability. It allocates an input and an output MAD (-ENOMEM, props untouched, if either allocation fails; both buffers are freed on every return after allocation). It zeroes *props, issues a PortInfo query for the port with mlx5_MAD_IFC and returns that error (with *props left zeroed) if it fails. Otherwise it fills lid, lmc, sm_lid, sm_sl, state, phys_state, port_cap_flags, gid_tbl_len, max_msg_sz, pkey_tbl_len (from mdev->port_caps[port - 1]), the counters, widths, speed, MTU, subnet_timeout, max_vl_num and init_type_reply from the response. If the extended-speeds capability flag is set it replaces active_speed with 16 (extended speed code 1) or 32 (code 2). If active_speed is 4 and the port's extended capability includes MLX_EXT_PORT_CAP_FLAG_EXTENDED_PORT_INFO, it issues a second MAD (extended port info); if that fails it returns the error with *props already filled from the first response; if bit 0 of its data byte 15 is set it sets active_speed to 8. It returns 0 on success.

functions.name: reg_umr
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: pd and umem are valid, order is a valid cache order index, and npages, page_shift and the other arguments describe the region. It tries once to take a cached MR with alloc_cached_mr(dev, order); if none is available it calls add_keys for one key (a failure other than -EAGAIN is only logged) and does not retry, so if the cached MR is still NULL it returns ERR_PTR(-EAGAIN). It then maps the page address list with dma_map_mr_pas; on failure it frees the cached MR with free_cached_mr and returns ERR_PTR of that error (umrc->sem has not been taken yet). Otherwise it prepares the UMR work request, takes umrc->sem, posts it with ib_post_send; if the post fails it goes to unmap_dma with err set; otherwise it waits for the completion and sets err to -EFAULT if the completion status is not IB_WC_SUCCESS. After a successful post (whether or not the completion succeeded) it sets mmkey.iova, mmkey.size, mmkey.pd and marks mr->live = 1. At unmap_dma it releases umrc->sem, unmaps the DMA buffer and frees the temporary page list. If err is nonzero it frees the cached MR with free_cached_mr and returns ERR_PTR(err); otherwise it returns the MR.

functions.name: mlx5_ib_update_mtt
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: mr is a live MTT-mode MR with a valid umem, and start_page_index and npages describe a range inside it; the caller keeps mr and its umem alive. It first rounds start_page_index down to a multiple of MLX5_UMR_MTT_ALIGNMENT / 8 (growing npages by the difference) and rounds the page count up to that alignment. If the aligned range would exceed MLX5_MAX_UMR_PAGES it returns -EINVAL immediately, before allocating anything. Otherwise it gets a zeroed page with get_zeroed_page(GFP_ATOMIC) as the page buffer; if that fails it falls back to a static emergency buffer of MLX5_UMR_MTT_MIN_CHUNK_SIZE bytes, taking mlx5_ib_update_mtt_emergency_buffer_mutex. It maps the buffer for DMA; if the mapping fails it returns -ENOMEM after freeing the page or releasing the mutex. It then processes the range in chunks that fit the buffer: for each chunk it copies the page addresses for the chunk from the umem into the buffer unless zap is set (with zap the buffer's existing contents, zero, are used), posts a UMR work request to update the MTT under umrc->sem (taken and released per chunk), and waits for its completion. A failed ib_post_send ends the loop with its error; a completion status other than IB_WC_SUCCESS ends it with -EFAULT; chunks before the failing one have been written and later ones not. After the loop it unmaps the DMA buffer. At the exit it frees the page buffer or, if the emergency buffer was used, releases the emergency mutex, and returns 0 or the error.

functions.name: create_raw_packet_qp
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev, qp, in and pd are valid and pd->uobject is non-NULL with a ucontext (it is dereferenced at the start to obtain the user context's transport domain number tdn). If qp->sq.wqe_cnt is nonzero it creates the TIS and then the SQ (a TIS failure returns its error at once; an SQ failure destroys the TIS) and sets sq->base.container_mibqp = qp. If qp->rq.wqe_cnt is nonzero it sets rq->base.container_mibqp = qp, creates the RQ (on failure it destroys the SQ and TIS if the send queue exists) and then the TIR (on failure it destroys the RQ, and then the SQ and TIS if the send queue exists). If everything succeeded it sets qp->trans_qp.base.mqp.qpn to the SQ's qpn when a send queue exists, otherwise the RQ's qpn, and returns 0. On failure it returns the error from the failing create helper after destroying the objects this call created, in reverse order.

functions.name: mlxfw_firmware_flash
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: mlxfw_dev has valid ops (fsm_lock, fsm_state_wait path, fsm_activate, fsm_release) and firmware points to a readable image. It returns -EINVAL if the image is not an MFA2 file and returns PTR_ERR of mlxfw_mfa2_file_init if the file cannot be parsed (neither case locks anything). Otherwise it calls fsm_lock: if that fails it finalises the MFA2 file with mlxfw_mfa2_file_fini and returns the error without calling fsm_release. After a successful lock it waits for the LOCKED state, flashes all components, calls fsm_activate and waits for LOCKED again; if any of these steps fails it calls fsm_release, finalises the MFA2 file and returns that error. If all succeed it calls fsm_release, logs completion, finalises the MFA2 file and returns 0.

functions.name: mmc_switch_status
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: timeout (in microseconds) is nonzero (KASSERTed, effective only in kernels with INVARIANTS). It polls the card status with mmc_send_status, retrying a send that returns MMC_ERR_BADCRC up to 10 times in a row; any other send error, or a BADCRC on the tenth try, ends the loop and is returned. When the status shows the TRAN state the loop ends with err = MMC_ERR_NONE. If the state is not TRAN it computes the deadline (timeout microseconds after the first non-TRAN check) and keeps polling until the current time passes it, then ends the loop with MMC_ERR_TIMEOUT. After the loop, only if err is MMC_ERR_NONE and the last status has R1_SWITCH_ERROR set (which can only be the TRAN-state case), it returns MMC_ERR_FAILED; otherwise it returns err (MMC_ERR_NONE, a send_status error, or MMC_ERR_TIMEOUT). A status with R1_SWITCH_ERROR set but not in the TRAN state does not end the loop and ends in MMC_ERR_TIMEOUT if the card never reaches TRAN.

functions.name: mpi3mr_process_op_reply_desc
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc is a valid softc, reply_desc is a reply descriptor from an operational reply queue and reply_dma points to writable storage; the descriptor's host tag indexes sc->cmd_list. It sets *reply_dma to 0 and decodes the descriptor by type: a status descriptor supplies the host tag and IOC status (and log info when the status bits are set); an address-reply descriptor supplies the reply frame address in *reply_dma, maps it with mpi3mr_get_reply_virt_addr (if that is NULL it logs and goes to out without touching a ccb) and then takes host tag, IOC status, SCSI status and state, transfer count, sense count and the sense buffer from the reply frame; a success descriptor supplies only the host tag. It takes the command cm from sc->cmd_list[host_tag] and goes to out if its state is MPI3MR_CMD_STATE_FREE. Otherwise, when sc->iot_enable is set, it works on the I/O throttling state: for a command whose block count is at least sc->io_throttle_data_length on a throttle-enabled target it subtracts the block count from sc->pend_large_data_sz and, if the target has a throttle group, from the group's counter, and clears the group's (or, for a target without a group, the target's) io_divert flag (and sets the divert flags of the group's volumes) when the pending counts are at or below the low-water marks; a target that is diverting but does not meet the first condition gets a similar low-water check. A success descriptor sets CAM_REQ_CMP and goes to out_success. For others, a data underrun with zero transferred bytes and a BUSY, RESERVATION_CONFLICT or TASK_SET_FULL SCSI status is treated as IOC success; valid sense data with a nonzero count and a sense buffer is copied into csio (with sense_resid) and CAM_AUTOSNS_VALID is set. The CAM status then depends on the IOC status: BUSY and INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES give CAM_REQUEUE_REQ; SCSI_DEVICE_NOT_THERE gives CAM_REQ_CMP for a volume (targ->devinfo == 0) else CAM_DEV_NOT_THERE; the three terminated codes give CAM_SCSI_BUSY; DATA_OVERRUN sets resid 0 and CAM_DATA_RUN_ERR; DATA_UNDERRUN sets resid to the command length minus the transfer count and, like RECOVERED_ERROR and SUCCESS, with no reply frame gives CAM_REQ_CMP for IOC success or CAM_REQ_CMP_ERR otherwise, and with a reply frame is decided by the SCSI state and status (CAM_REQ_CMP_ERR for no-status or terminated states, CAM_AUTOSENSE_FAIL, CAM_REQ_ABORTED for command-terminated or task-aborted status, CAM_REQ_CMP for GOOD status, else CAM_SCSI_STATUS_ERROR, with sense copied when the sense state is valid); INVALID_SGL gives CAM_UNREC_HBA_ERROR; EEDP, protocol, internal-error and every other IOC status set resid to the command length and CAM_REQ_CMP_ERR. At out_success, if the ccb status is not CAM_REQ_CMP it sets CAM_DEV_QFRZN and freezes the device queue; it decrements the target's outstanding count, completes the command with mpi3mr_cmd_done and decrements sc->fw_outstanding. At out, if a sense buffer was found it reposts it to the controller. The function returns nothing.

functions.name: mpi3mr_pel_wait_complete
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: drvr_cmd is the completed PEL wait command; if MPI3MR_CMD_REPLYVALID is set in its state, drvr_cmd->reply points to a valid reply. If MPI3MR_CMD_RESET is set it only resets the command (state MPI3MR_CMD_NOTUSED, callback NULL, retry_count 0) and leaves sc->pel_wait_pend unchanged. If no valid reply is present it logs, clears sc->pel_wait_pend and resets the command (no retry). Otherwise, if the IOC status is not success or the PEL log status is neither success nor aborted, it retries: while retry_count is below MPI3MR_PELCMDS_RETRYCOUNT it increments it, calls mpi3mr_issue_pel_wait(sc, drvr_cmd) and returns (the command is not reset by this function; whether the reissue succeeds was not read); after the retries are used up it clears pel_wait_pend and resets the command. If the status is success or aborted it calls mpi3mr_app_send_aen and, unless sc->pel_abort_requested is set, clears sc->pel_cmds.retry_count and calls mpi3mr_send_pel_getseq(sc, &sc->pel_cmds); in this success case drvr_cmd itself is not reset and pel_wait_pend is not cleared by this function.

functions.name: mpi3mr_pel_getseq_complete
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: drvr_cmd is the completed PEL get-sequence command; if MPI3MR_CMD_REPLYVALID is set its reply points to a valid reply. If MPI3MR_CMD_RESET is set it only resets the command (state NOTUSED, callback NULL, retry_count 0) and leaves sc->pel_wait_pend unchanged. If no valid reply is present it logs, clears sc->pel_wait_pend and resets the command. If the IOC status is not success or the PEL log status is not success it retries: while retry_count is below MPI3MR_PELCMDS_RETRYCOUNT it increments it, calls mpi3mr_send_pel_getseq(sc, drvr_cmd) and returns (no reset is done by this function; the outcome of the resend was not read); after the retries it clears pel_wait_pend and resets the command. On success it sets sc->newest_seqnum to the little-endian Newest value from sc->pel_seq_number plus one, clears retry_count and calls mpi3mr_issue_pel_wait(sc, drvr_cmd).

functions.name: mpi3mr_app_construct_sgl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc has an ioctl chain SGE buffer; mpi_request is a writable request frame (MPI3MR_AREQ_FRAME_SZ bytes when is_rmc is 0, or a management passthrough request when is_rmc is nonzero); dma_buffers has bufcnt entries; num_datasges is the number of data SGEs to build. It first computes the total number of SGEs needed. For is_rmc it writes the CommandSGL pointing at the first buffer, sets the SGL position inside that buffer after user_buf_len, and returns -1 if the needed SGEs exceed the room in it; it then marks the chain as already in use (so no chain SGE is ever created for this case), writes the ResponseSGL from the next buffer when is_rmr is set or a zero-length ResponseSGL otherwise, and builds the data SGEs if num_datasges is nonzero. For is_rmc zero it returns -1 if sgl_offset is not below MPI3MR_AREQ_FRAME_SZ or no SGE slot fits. If num_datasges is 0 it writes a zero-length SGE and returns 0. For an SMP passthrough function it returns -1 if more than 2 SGEs are needed or more than are available, else writes one last-flagged simple SGE per non-skipped buffer and returns 0. Otherwise it builds simple SGEs from each buffer's descriptors (skipping buffers whose data direction is MPI3MR_APP_DDN and writing a zero-length SGE for buffers without descriptors), with end-of-buffer on each buffer's last SGE and end-of-list on the very last. When the initial frame is down to one free slot and more than one SGE is still needed it switches to a chain: it returns -1 if the chain buffer is too small, writes a last-chain SGE pointing at sc->ioctl_chain_sge, zeroes the chain buffer and continues there. When the chain (or, for is_rmc, the management buffer) runs out of slots it returns -1. It returns 0 on success. On a -1 return the SGEs already written (the command and response SGLs, any chain SGE and the zeroed chain buffer) stay as written. No locks are taken.

functions.name: mpi3mr_app_mptcmds
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: uarg points to a kernel copy of a struct mpi3mr_ioctl_mptcmd whose user pointers (mpi_msg_buf, buf_entry_list, and each buffer entry's user buffer) are user addresses; dev, cmd, flag and td are unused in what was read; the caller may sleep. The initial return value is EINVAL. It returns ENODEV if no adapter matches karg->mrioc_id, ENOMEM if the ioctl SGE DMA memory was not allocated, raises karg->timeout to at least MPI3MR_IOCTL_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT, returns EINVAL (nothing allocated) if mpi_msg_size or buf_entry_list_size is zero or mpi_msg_size * 4 exceeds MPI3MR_AREQ_FRAME_SZ, and returns ENOMEM if the request frame allocation fails. After that all failures go to the out label, which frees kern_erb, the buffer list, the MPI request frame, the per-buffer DMA descriptors and the dma_buffers array and the reply buffer when allocated, and returns the code. It copies in the MPI request (EFAULT on failure) and the buffer entry list (ENOMEM if its allocation fails, EFAULT on copyin failure), validates the entries and sets up the kernel and DMA buffers (EINVAL for an empty or invalid entry list or invalid sizes, ENOMEM for allocation failures, EFAULT for copyin failures; the exact checks in this stretch, lines 836-1004, were only checked by their return statements). It then returns EAGAIN if an ioctl command is already pending, if a reset is in progress or if ioctls are blocked, and EFAULT if the controller is in an unrecoverable state. For non-NVMe functions it builds the SGL with mpi3mr_app_construct_sgl (EAGAIN on failure); the NVMe-encapsulated branch has its own checks returning ENOMEM or EINVAL. For a SCSI task-management request other than abort-task it looks up the target by device handle (ENODEV if not found) and increments its block_io count. It marks the ioctl command pending, posts it with mpi3mr_submit_admin_cmd (a nonzero result is returned after the out_failed cleanup) and waits for completion with the timeout; on a timeout it returns EAGAIN and, unless the command was already reset, requests a soft reset. On completion it copies the MPI reply, the sense data and the data-in buffers back to user space (ENOMEM if a reply buffer cannot be allocated, EFAULT on copyout failure), and returns 0. out_failed also decrements the target's block_io count if one was taken and clears the ioctl command state before falling to out.

functions.name: mpr_user_pass_thru
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc is an initialised mpr_softc whose lock the caller does not hold, and data is a kernel copy of an mpr_pass_thru_t whose pointers are user addresses. It takes the softc lock; if MPR_FLAGS_BUSY is already set it releases the lock and returns EBUSY with nothing else touched; otherwise it sets MPR_FLAGS_BUSY and releases the lock. It checks the direction: valid combinations are DataSize 0 with direction NONE, or a nonzero DataSize with READ, WRITE, or BOTH with a nonzero DataOutSize; for a valid BOTH request the direction is rewritten to READ, for other valid ones DataOutSize is set to 0; an invalid combination returns EINVAL. It returns EINVAL if RequestSize exceeds sc->reqframesz, copies the request in (returning the copyin error). For a SCSI task-management request it allocates a TM command (EINVAL if none), finds the target by DevHandle, and if the target is unknown or mpr_wait_command fails sets EIO; with a reply it copies up to MIN(reply size, ReplySize) bytes of the reply to the user and returns the copyout result; the TM command is freed. For other requests it allocates a command (ENOMEM if none), copies in the request, sets up the data buffer, copying in the data-out (or write) data (a copyin failure goes to the cleanup), checks the SCSI I/O handle fields (EINVAL cases at lines 1007 and 1035) and waits for completion with mpr_wait_command (30 s); on an error or a NULL command it returns the error. On completion it syncs and unloads the DMA map, copies data-in to the user, copies the reply (up to MIN of the reply size and ReplySize), copies SCSI sense data for SCSI I/O functions when autosense is valid, and copies the NVMe error response for NVMe-encapsulated functions, where a NULL error response buffer only logs and the function proceeds to the cleanup with the err value it had. At the end it clears MPR_FLAGS_BUSY with the lock held, frees the command (and its data buffer if any) and the request copy, releases the lock and returns err (the first copyout error, the wait error, or 0).

functions.name: mps_read_config_page
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc and params are valid and params->hdr describes the page; the caller holds the softc lock as the mps code requires (not checked here). It returns EBUSY without touching params if MPS_FLAGS_BUSY is set or mps_alloc_command returns NULL. Otherwise it builds a CONFIG request (action, page address, and the standard or extended header fields from params->hdr), sets cm_data and cm_length from params->buffer and params->length (with a data-in simple SGE when the buffer is non-NULL) and records params in cm_complete_data. If params->callback is non-NULL it sets mps_config_complete as the completion routine and returns the result of mps_map_command (0, EINPROGRESS or an error); params->status and the header are filled in later by mps_config_complete, and the page data is written into params->buffer by the hardware through DMA. If params->callback is NULL it calls mps_wait_command with no timeout and CAN_SLEEP: on a nonzero error it logs, frees the command if cm is still non-NULL, and returns that error; on success it calls mps_config_complete directly and returns 0. mps_config_complete syncs and unloads the buffer DMA map, sets params->status to MPI2_IOCSTATUS_BUSY if the command had error flags or no reply, else to the reply IOCStatus and copies the reply page header into params->hdr; it frees the command and calls params->callback if non-NULL.

functions.name: mps_mapping_check_devices
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: data is the mps_softc and sc->mps_mtx is held (asserted); it is the device_check_callout handler. It first sets sc->track_mapping_events to 0. If the callout is pending or not active it returns at once without touching the callout. Otherwise it deactivates the callout and looks at the IOC page 8 mapping mode. In enclosure-slot mapping mode it scans the enclosure table, in device-persistence mapping mode the device mapping table, for an entry with init_complete set; if none is found (or the mode is neither) it re-arms the callout to run again after MPS_MISSING_CHECK_DELAY seconds and returns. Otherwise in enclosure-slot mode, for every enclosure entry not yet init_complete it increments missing_count (if below MPS_MAX_MISSING_COUNT, committing the entry with _mapping_commit_enc_entry when its dpm_entry_num is valid) and sets init_complete; it then returns if the firmware is not IR firmware, else it takes the IR map range of the mapping table. In persistence mode it uses the whole mapping table. It returns if the end index is 0. Over the selected mapping-table range, an entry with MPS_DEV_RESERVED set and physical_id 0 only gets init_complete set; an entry with MPS_DEV_RESERVED set and a nonzero physical_id that is not init_complete gets missing_count incremented (if below the cap, committed with _mapping_commit_map_entry when its dpm_entry_num is valid) and init_complete set; entries without MPS_DEV_RESERVED are left unchanged. The function returns nothing.

functions.name: mps_mapping_enclosure_dev_status_change_event
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc and event_data are valid objects. The function returns nothing and has an exit label that always flushes pending DPM pages with _mapping_flush_dpm_pages and decrements sc->pending_map_events if it is nonzero. If the IOC page 8 mapping mode is not enclosure-slot mapping it goes straight to that exit. For an MPI2_EVENT_SAS_ENCL_RC_ADDED event: zero reported slots goes to the exit; it looks the enclosure up by logical ID and phy bits; if an entry exists and is init_complete with missing_count 0 it goes to the exit; otherwise it updates the existing entry's handle and start slot, ORs in the phy bits and, if the missing count was nonzero or the phy bits changed, clears missing_count and (when DPM is enabled and the entry has a DPM slot and that DPM entry has a missing count or the phy bits changed) rewrites the DPM entry and marks it for flushing. If no entry exists it takes the next free table index, or, if the table is full, evicts the entry with the highest missing count (adding its DPM entry to the removal table and clearing it); only when no entry can be evicted does it log that the table is full and go to the exit. A new entry is filled from the event (handle, logical ID, slots, start slot, phy bits, BAD indexes for start_index and dpm_entry_num). For both existing and new entries it then sets init_complete. For an MPI2_EVENT_SAS_ENCL_RC_NOT_RESPONDING event it finds the entry by handle (logging and going to the exit if none), increments missing_count up to MPS_MAX_MISSING_COUNT, rewrites its DPM entry with the slot count and missing count when DPM is enabled and the entry has a DPM slot, marks it for flushing and sets init_complete. Other reason codes change nothing.

functions.name: mpssas_ir_shutdown
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc is an attached mps softc with initialised mapping_table, sassc and target arrays; the caller does not hold the mps lock (the function takes and releases it around the wait); howto holds the reboot flags. If IR firmware is loaded it computes the volume index range from the IOC page 8 volume mapping mode (starting at 0, or 1 when target ID 0 is reserved, for the low-volume mapping, else at max_devices - max_volumes) and scans the mapping_table indexes from the start up to but not including start + max_volumes - 1 for an entry with a nonzero physical_id and missing_count 0. If such a volume is found it allocates a command (printing a message and skipping the request if that fails), builds a RAID action request with action MPI2_RAID_ACTION_SYSTEM_SHUTDOWN_INITIATED, waits for it with mps_wait_command (5 second timeout, sleeping allowed) under the mps lock, ignores the reply, and frees the command if it is still held. Whether or not any of this happened, it then walks all max_devices targets: for each target with a nonzero handle and supports_SSU set it sets stop_at_shutdown according to sc->enable_ssu: MPS_SSU_DISABLE_SSD_DISABLE_HDD gives FALSE; MPS_SSU_DISABLE_SSD_ENABLE_HDD gives TRUE except for SATA SSDs, which get FALSE; MPS_SSU_ENABLE_SSD_ENABLE_HDD gives TRUE; MPS_SSU_ENABLE_SSD_DISABLE_HDD and any other value give TRUE only for SATA SSDs. Finally it calls mpssas_SSU_to_SATA_devices(sc, howto). It returns nothing.

functions.name: mps_do_diag_action
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc is a valid mps softc, diag_action is a user address, and return_code points to the caller's code. It saves the incoming *return_code and sets *return_code to MPS_FW_DIAG_ERROR_SUCCESS. By action: REGISTER sets MPS_FW_DIAG_ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER and MPS_DIAG_FAILURE when length is 0, otherwise copies in a whole diag_register structure (sizeof, regardless of length) and returns MPS_DIAG_FAILURE if that copyin fails; UNREGISTER, QUERY and RELEASE set INVALID_PARAMETER and failure when length is smaller than their structure, else copy in the structure (MPS_DIAG_FAILURE on copyin failure) and call the corresponding handler, QUERY also copying the result out after a successful handler (copyout failure returns MPS_DIAG_FAILURE); READ_BUFFER copies in the read-buffer structure first (copyin failure returns MPS_DIAG_FAILURE), sets INVALID_PARAMETER and failure if length is less than BytesToRead, otherwise calls mps_diag_read_buffer and on success copies out all but the PtrDataBuffer member (copyout failure returns MPS_DIAG_FAILURE); any other action sets INVALID_PARAMETER and failure. A copyin or copyout failure returns MPS_DIAG_FAILURE immediately with *return_code still MPS_FW_DIAG_ERROR_SUCCESS. At the end, if the status is failure, the incoming *return_code was MPS_FW_DIAG_NEW and the new *return_code is not MPS_FW_DIAG_ERROR_SUCCESS, the status is changed to MPS_DIAG_SUCCESS. It returns the status.

functions.name: mps_user_pass_thru
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc is a valid mps softc whose lock the caller does not hold, and data is a kernel copy of an mps_pass_thru_t with user pointers. It takes the lock; if MPS_FLAGS_BUSY is already set it releases the lock and returns EBUSY, leaving the flag alone; otherwise it sets MPS_FLAGS_BUSY and releases the lock. It returns EINVAL (after the common cleanup) for an invalid DataSize/DataDirection/DataOutSize combination, or if RequestSize exceeds sc->reqframesz; it copies the request from user space and returns the copyin error. For a task-management request it takes the lock, allocates a TM command (EINVAL if none), looks up the target by DevHandle (an unknown target or a failed mps_wait_command both end as EIO), copies the reply to the user when there is one (up to MIN of the reply size and ReplySize; the result of the copyout becomes the return value) and frees the TM command. For other requests it allocates a command (ENOMEM if none), sets up the request and data buffer, and copies in the data-out (or write) data: the result of that copyin is stored in err but no check or jump follows in the lines read, so it can be overwritten by later steps. For SCSI I/O requests with DevHandle 0 it returns EINVAL. It then waits for completion with mps_wait_command (30 s) and, on an error or a NULL command, goes to cleanup with that error. After a successful wait it copies data-in to the user, the reply (up to MIN of reply size and ReplySize) and, for SCSI I/O, the autosense data, each copyout result replacing err. At the end it clears MPS_FLAGS_BUSY with the lock held, frees the command and its data buffer if any and the request copy, releases the lock and returns err. On every path except the initial EBUSY the busy flag is cleared and the request buffer freed.

functions.name: mpt_wait_db_ack
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: mpt is a valid mpt_softc. It loops i from 0 to MPT_MAX_WAIT - 1: it reads the interrupt status register with mpt_rd_intr; if the doorbell is not busy (MPT_DB_IS_BUSY false) it records i in the global maxwait_ack if i is larger than the stored value and returns MPT_OK immediately, with no delay after that successful read; otherwise it calls DELAY(200) and polls again. After MPT_MAX_WAIT polls it returns MPT_FAIL.

functions.name: mpt_wait_db_int
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: mpt is a valid mpt_softc. It loops i from 0 to MPT_MAX_WAIT - 1: it reads the interrupt status register with mpt_rd_intr; if a doorbell interrupt is asserted (MPT_DB_INTR true) it records i in the global maxwait_int if larger and returns MPT_OK immediately without a delay; otherwise it calls DELAY(100) and polls again. After MPT_MAX_WAIT polls it returns MPT_FAIL.

functions.name: mpt_wait_state
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: mpt is a valid mpt_softc. It loops i from 0 to MPT_MAX_WAIT - 1: it reads the doorbell register with mpt_rd_db; if MPT_STATE of the value equals state it records i in the global maxwait_state if larger and returns MPT_OK immediately without a delay; otherwise it calls DELAY(100) and reads again. After MPT_MAX_WAIT reads it returns MPT_FAIL.

functions.name: mpt_fc_els_reply_handler
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: mpt is an initialised adapter, req the request the reply belongs to, reply_frame the reply message. The function returns TRUE on every path that was read. If the IOC status is not success it logs, sets mpt->disabled to 1 when the status is MPI_IOCSTATUS_INVALID_STATE, and returns TRUE. For a MPI_FUNCTION_FC_LINK_SRVC_RSP reply it finds req in mpt->els_cmd_ptrs (a KASSERT, effective only with INVARIANTS, requires it to be there), removes it from mpt->request_pending_list, marks it done instead of queued and reposts it with mpt_fc_post_els. For a MPI_FUNCTION_FC_PRIMITIVE_SEND reply it removes req from the pending list, marks it done, and frees it if it timed out or nobody is waiting for it (otherwise it is left for the waiter); then returns. Any function other than LINK_SRVC_BUF_POST logs and returns. For a buffer-post reply with MsgLength <= 5 it logs and returns, as it does when MPI_LS_BUF_POST_REPLY_FLAG_NO_RSP_NEEDED is set. Otherwise it takes the request at mpt->els_cmd_ptrs[TransactionContext] and decodes R_CTL, type and command: for an ELS PRLI it builds an accept payload in the ELS buffer (target/initiator role bits set from mpt->role), removes the request from the pending list, marks it done and sends the response with mpt_fc_els_send_response (20 bytes), without reposting; PRLO is handled the same with a different payload; other ELS commands only log and are reposted. For an ABTS frame it logs, and if the RX_ID is in range, mpt->tgt_cmd_ptrs is non-NULL, the target command has a back pointer, and its context id and initiator tag match RX_ID and OX_ID, it logs the target state and calls mpt_abort_target_cmd (logging if that cannot be started); in every ABTS case (including the mismatch cases that skip the abort) it rewrites the frame's R_CTL to BA_ACC and sends a 12-byte response through mpt_fc_els_send_response. Any other R_CTL/type is logged. Unless a response was sent, the request is removed from the pending list, marked done and reposted with mpt_fc_post_els.

functions.name: mpt_scsi_tgt_atio
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: req is a target request whose mpt_tgt_state is TGT_STATE_LOADED (otherwise the function dumps the state and panics), reply_desc is a valid reply descriptor, and req->req_vbuf offset by MPT_RQSL(mpt) holds the FC, SAS or SPI target command buffer. It zeroes the target state, sets it to TGT_STATE_IN_CAM and records reply_desc and the tag id. Then by transport: for FC, a nonzero task-management byte selects a task management function (query task set, abort task set, clear task set, query async event, LUN reset, target reset or clear ACA); an unrecognised value sends SCSI_STATUS_OK with mpt_scsi_tgt_status and returns before tgt->itag and tgt->resid are set; otherwise the tag action is derived from the control byte, and tgt->resid (data length), the CDB, LUN and tgt->itag (OX_ID) are taken from the FCP buffer; for SAS and SPI the CDB, LUN and tgt->itag are taken from their buffers and tgt->resid is left at zero. It then picks a LUN resource: if the LUN is out of range, target mode is disabled or the LUN is not enabled, the wildcard resource is used when mpt->twildcard is set, else (when no task management function is pending) it answers locally: INQUIRY (with EVPD clear) and REQUEST SENSE are answered with mpt_scsi_tgt_local and return; REPORT_LUNS returns without sending any status; every other command, and INQUIRY with EVPD set, gets SCSI_STATUS_CHECK_COND with sense data built in the function; if a task management function is pending and no resource is available the function answers SCSI_STATUS_OK. A task management function with a resource is passed to mpt_scsi_tgt_tsk_mgmt. Otherwise it takes the first ATIO queued on the LUN resource; if none is queued it sends SCSI_STATUS_QUEUE_FULL (or SCSI_STATUS_BUSY when target mode is disabled); else it removes the ATIO, fills in LUN, tag id, initiator id, the 16-byte CDB and the tag action and completes it with xpt_done. The function returns nothing.

functions.name: mpt_scsi_tgt_reply_handler
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: mpt is a valid softc, req a valid request and reply_frame either NULL (a context/turbo reply) or a valid reply message. If reply_frame is NULL it switches on the target state of req: TGT_STATE_LOADED calls mpt_scsi_tgt_atio; MOVING_DATA with no associated request panics, with no associated CCB and is_local zero panics, with no CCB and is_local set it frees the associated request and sends status with mpt_scsi_tgt_status and returns; with a CCB it clears the timeout, counts the transfer, frees the associated request and, if the CCB has no CAM_SEND_STATUS flag, completes the CCB with CAM_REQ_CMP and sets state TGT_STATE_IN_CAM (releasing the SIM queue if outofbeer), else sends the status; SENDING_STATUS and MOVING_DATA_AND_STATUS (panic if there is no associated request) complete the CCB if there is one (CAM_REQ_CMP, CAM_SENT_SENSE if sense was sent), free the associated request, repost the target command buffer with mpt_post_target_command and call xpt_done on the CCB; TGT_STATE_NIL sets TGT_STATE_LOADED; other states only log. It returns TRUE. If reply_frame is non-NULL it logs and switches on the function: for MPI_FUNCTION_TARGET_CMD_BUFFER_POST a non-success status leaves req unchanged, a success asserts (INVARIANTS only) that the state is TGT_STATE_LOADING, assigns a serial number and sets state TGT_STATE_LOADED; for TARGET_ASSIST and TARGET_STATUS_SEND it logs, removes req from the pending list and frees it; for TARGET_MODE_ABORT it logs the abort completion, removes req from the list and frees it; other functions are only logged. It returns TRUE.

functions.name: mrsas_aen_handler
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc may be NULL. If sc is NULL it prints "invalid instance!" and returns; if remove_in_progress or reset_in_progress is set it prints a message and returns; if sc->evt_detail_mem is NULL it prints "invalid evt_detail" and returns (so these returns are not free of side effects: each prints a message). Otherwise it acts on the event code in evt_detail_mem: MR_EVT_PD_INSERTED and MR_EVT_PD_REMOVED call mrsas_get_pd_list and scan sim_1 if it succeeds (a failure jumps to the end without registering a new AEN); MR_EVT_LD_OFFLINE, MR_EVT_CFG_CLEARED and MR_EVT_LD_DELETED scan sim_0; MR_EVT_LD_CREATED calls mrsas_get_ld_list and scans sim_0 (failure skips AEN registration); MR_EVT_CTRL_HOST_BUS_SCAN_REQUESTED, MR_EVT_FOREIGN_CFG_IMPORTED and MR_EVT_LD_STATE_CHANGE set a flag that makes it call get_pd_list then scan sim_1 and get_ld_list then scan sim_0 (any failure skips registration); MR_EVT_CTRL_PROP_CHANGED calls mrsas_get_ctrl_info (failure skips registration); any other code does nothing. If none of those failed it computes seq_num = the event's seq_num + 1, returns if sc->aen_cmd is non-NULL, and otherwise registers a new AEN for locale ALL and class DEBUG with mrsas_register_aen under sc->aen_lock, printing an error if registration returns nonzero. The function returns nothing.

functions.name: msk_watchdog
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller holds the interface lock (MSK_IF_LOCK_ASSERT). If msk_watchdog_timer is 0 it returns with nothing changed. Otherwise it decrements the timer, and if the decremented value is still nonzero it returns (the timer has been decremented but nothing else changed). When the timer reaches 0: if MSK_FLAG_LINK is not set it counts one IFCOUNTER_OERRORS, clears IFF_DRV_RUNNING and calls msk_init_locked, then returns without calling msk_start_locked; if the link flag is set it prints a watchdog message, counts one output error, clears IFF_DRV_RUNNING, calls msk_init_locked and then calls msk_start_locked if the send queue is not empty. The function returns nothing.

functions.name: mthca_alloc_srq
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev, pd, attr and srq are valid; attr->max_wr and attr->max_sge are the requested sizes; udata is non-NULL for a userspace SRQ and NULL for a kernel SRQ. It returns -EINVAL if attr->max_wr or attr->max_sge exceeds the device limits, or, on a non-mem-free device, if the descriptor size exceeds dev->limits.max_desc_sz. It sets the SRQ size (one more than requested; rounded up to a power of two on mem-free devices) and allocates an SRQ number with mthca_alloc, returning -ENOMEM if none is available. On mem-free devices it takes the ICM table entry (mthca_table_get; error returned) and, for a kernel SRQ, allocates a doorbell (-ENOMEM if that fails). It then allocates a mailbox (PTR_ERR on failure) and the SRQ buffer with mthca_alloc_srq_buf, initialises the lock, refcount (1), waitqueue and mutex, builds the SRQ context and calls mthca_SW2HW_SRQ; a nonzero result unwinds and is returned. It then inserts the SRQ in the SRQ table under the table lock; if mthca_array_set fails it calls mthca_HW2SW_SRQ and then unwinds, and the value returned is that of mthca_HW2SW_SRQ (a HW2SW failure is only logged), which can be 0 even though creation failed. On success it frees the mailbox, sets first_free to 0 and last_free to max - 1, writes the actual max_wr (max - 1) and max_sge back into attr and returns 0. The unwinding releases, in reverse order, the SRQ buffer (kernel SRQs), the mailbox, the doorbell (kernel SRQ on mem-free devices), the ICM table reference (the mthca_table_put call is not conditioned on mem-free in the code) and the SRQ number.

functions.name: mvs_reset
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is an mvs channel device with consistent softc and slot arrays; the global dumping flag may be set. It freezes the SIM queue once, and if a reset countdown is active (ch->resetting nonzero) it clears it, stops the reset callout and releases one queue freeze. It requeues frozen CCBs, turns EDMA off, writes 0 to DMA_C and ends every slot at or above MVS_SLOT_RUNNING with mvs_end_transaction(..., MVS_ERR_INNOCENT). It completes every held CCB with xpt_done and decrements numhslots, releases the SIM queue if ch->toslots is nonzero, clears eslots, toslots, fatalerr and fake_busy, announces AC_BUS_RESET and resets the controller (EDMA interrupt mask written 0, ATA reset pulse, mvs_errata) and the SATA PHY. If the PHY reset finds no device it sets ch->devices to 0, clears the SATA error register, clears the EDMA interrupt cause, writes the EDMA interrupt mask register as ~EDMA_IE_TRANSIENT (so all non-transient EDMA interrupts are unmasked, not masked off), releases the SIM queue and returns. Otherwise it waits for BSY and DRQ to clear (31000 ms when dumping, else without a wait); if the wait fails, in dump mode it only prints a message and in normal mode it sets ch->resetting to 310. It then sets ch->devices to 1, clears the SATA error and EDMA interrupt cause registers, writes the interrupt mask as ~EDMA_IE_TRANSIENT, and if ch->resetting is set starts the reset callout (hz / 10, mvs_reset_to) instead of releasing the SIM queue, otherwise releases the SIM queue; so in dump mode the queue is released even if the device was not ready.

functions.name: mvs_legacy_intr
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is an mvs channel device handling a legacy (non-EDMA) PIO or ATAPI interrupt; slot 0 is the PIO slot. The function returns nothing. It reads the status; if slot 0 is below MVS_SLOT_RUNNING it returns without doing anything else. If the status is BUSY it returns at once when poll is nonzero, otherwise it re-reads the status after DELAY(100) and again after DELAY(1000) and returns if still BUSY. If the error bit is set it ends the transaction with MVS_ERR_TFE. For an ATA PIO command it stores the status, and for a data command reads (data-in, waiting for DRQ for up to 1000 ms; a timeout prints, freezes the SIM queue, sets the slot's bit in ch->toslots and ends with MVS_ERR_TIMEOUT) and advances donecount; if more data remains it, for a write, waits for DRQ (same timeout handling), writes the next chunk and returns, and for a read returns to wait for the next interrupt; if no more data remains, or for no-data commands, it ends the transaction with MVS_ERR_NONE. For an ATAPI command with basic DMA it sets MVS_ERR_TFE if the device-write-fault bit or the DMA error bit is set, clears DMA_C and ends the transaction. For an ATAPI PIO command it decodes the interrupt reason and status: the command-out phase prints and returns without ending the transaction; the write and read data phases transfer the data, update donecount and transfersize and return (a write phase on a data-in command, or a read phase on a data-out command, ends with MVS_ERR_TFE); DONEDRQ prints a warning, moves one chunk if the direction is in or out (MVS_ERR_TFE otherwise) and then falls through to the end handling of the done phase; the abort and done phases end with MVS_ERR_TFE if the error or write-fault bit is set, else MVS_ERR_NONE; an unknown phase ends with MVS_ERR_TFE. The transaction is ended with mvs_end_transaction(slot, et).

functions.name: mwl_watchdog
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: arg is a valid mwl_softc and this is the watchdog callout. It first re-arms the callout to run again after hz ticks on every call.
