If sc_tx_timer is 0 it returns; otherwise it decrements the timer and returns if the new value is still above 0. When the timer reaches 0 and sc_running is set and sc_invalid is clear, it calls mwl_hal_setkeepalive: if that returns nonzero it prints "transmit timeout (firmware hung?)", otherwise it prints "transmit timeout"; it then increments ic_oerrors by one and mst_watchdog. If sc_running is clear or sc_invalid is set, nothing is printed and no counter is changed.

functions.name: mxge_attach
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is a device bound to this driver with a zeroed softc; the function creates its own taskqueue, parent DMA tag, ifnet, mutexes and callout. It fetches tunables, creates the taskqueue and a parent DMA tag (error from bus_dma_tag_create goes to abort_with_tq, which only drains and frees the taskqueue and returns the error). It then allocates the ifnet, initialises the command and driver mutexes, sets up PCI config space and maps the memory BAR (ENXIO if it cannot be mapped, via abort_with_lock, or if the computed SRAM size exceeds the mapped size, via abort_with_mem_res). It reads and parses the EEPROM strings (mxge_parse_strings error returned), enables write combining and allocates DMA memory for the command buffer, zero-pad and dmabench areas (each failing allocation unwinds the earlier ones and returns its error), selects the firmware (mxge_select_firmware), probes slices, allocates slices (mxge_alloc_slices), resets the NIC (mxge_reset), allocates rings (mxge_alloc_rings) and adds the interrupt (mxge_add_irq); each failure unwinds in reverse through the abort labels (rings, slices, dmabench, zeropad and cmd DMA, memory resource and bus mastering, mutexes, ifnet free, parent DMA tag, taskqueue) and returns the error. On success it sets the ifnet capabilities and handlers, initialises and probes the media, calls ether_ifattach, changes the MTU if mxge_initial_mtu differs from ETHERMTU (the result of mxge_change_mtu is ignored), adds sysctls, sets the transmit and flush functions, starts the taskqueue thread (the return value of taskqueue_start_threads is not checked), arms the tick callout and returns 0.

functions.name: netmap_ioctl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: priv is the netmap_priv_d of the calling file, data points to the argument for cmd (a struct nmreq_header for NIOCCTRL, otherwise the legacy argument). The function returns an errno-style value (0 on success). NIOCCTRL: it returns EINVAL for an out-of-range API version (before copying anything), copies the request in with nmreq_copyin (returning that error), and dispatches on the request type, each case storing the callee's result in error: REGISTER (takes NMG_LOCK; EBUSY if the file is already registered; resolves the port with netmap_get_na, using a memory allocator when an id is given and EINVAL for an unknown memory id; EBUSY if the port is kernel-owned; EIO for a virtio-net header mismatch; calls netmap_do_regif, validates a CSB option with netmap_csb_validate, reads memory info with netmap_mem_get_info and checks the options with nmreq_checkoptions; releases NMG_LOCK), PORT_INFO_GET, VALE_ATTACH and DETACH (netmap_bdg_attach and netmap_bdg_detach), PORT_HDR_SET and GET (ENXIO if the port cannot be found, EINVAL for a bad header length), VALE_LIST, VALE_NEWIF and DELIF (nm_vi_create and nm_vi_destroy), VALE_POLLING_ENABLE and DISABLE (nm_bdg_polling), POOLS_INFO_GET (netmap_mem_finalize and netmap_mem_pools_info_get), CSB_ENABLE (EINVAL if the file is already in a state that does not allow it, else netmap_csb_validate), SYNC_KLOOP_START and STOP (netmap_sync_kloop and netmap_sync_kloop_stop); an unknown request type gives EINVAL. At the end of NIOCCTRL it writes the reply header back with nmreq_copyout(hdr, error) and returns the resulting error (the copyout can add an EFAULT). NIOCTXSYNC and NIOCRXSYNC: ENXIO if the port is not registered, EBUSY if the CSB mode is active, and for each ring tried, a failed nm_kr_tryget is converted to EIO if it reported an error and to 0 (success, the ring is skipped) if it did not. Any other cmd is handed to netmap_ioctl_legacy and its result returned.

functions.name: netmap_bwrap_bdg_ctl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hdr and na are valid and na is a bridge-wrapper adapter. For hdr->nr_reqtype == NETMAP_REQ_VALE_ATTACH: it returns EINVAL if the request's registration ring id is nonzero or its mode is neither NR_REG_ALL_NIC nor NR_REG_NIC_SW; returns EBUSY if NETMAP_OWNED_BY_ANY(na) is true; returns 0 without any change if bna->na_kpriv is already set (the code checks this after the EBUSY test, so a set na_kpriv with NAF_BUSY and no way for NETMAP_OWNED_BY_ANY to be false makes this branch rarely reachable); otherwise it allocates a private netmap_priv_d (ENOMEM on failure), sets its np_ifp, calls netmap_do_regif and, on failure, deletes the private data, restores the hardware adapter's memory with netmap_mem_restore and returns the error; on success it stores the private data in bna->na_kpriv, sets NAF_BUSY in na->na_flags and returns 0. For any other request type (detach): it returns EINVAL without changes if na->active_fds is 0; otherwise it deletes bna->na_kpriv, sets it to NULL, clears NAF_BUSY, restores the hardware adapter's memory and returns 0.

functions.name: netmap_mem_finalize
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: nmd is a valid allocator and na a valid adapter; the caller does not hold the allocator lock. If nm_mem_check_group(nmd, na->pdev) is negative it returns ENOMEM immediately without locking the allocator. Otherwise it takes NMA_LOCK and calls netmap_mem_config; if that returns nonzero it jumps to the exit without incrementing nmd->active and without calling nmd_finalize, and the value returned is whatever nmd->lasterr currently holds. If the config succeeds it increments nmd->active, calls ops->nmd_finalize(nmd, na) and stores its result in nmd->lasterr, and when that is zero and NETMAP_MEM_NOMAP is clear it maps the buffer pool with netmap_mem_map and stores that result in lasterr. At the exit it copies nmd->lasterr to a local, releases the lock, calls netmap_mem_deref(nmd, na) if that value is nonzero, and returns it.

functions.name: netmap_get_pipe_na
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hdr is a netmap request whose nr_body is a register request, na is an output pointer, the caller holds NMG_LOCK. It looks for '{' (master) or '}' (slave) in the port name; if neither is present the name is not a pipe and it returns 0 without touching *na. It returns EINVAL if the pipe id after the bracket is empty or the bracket is at the start, or if the register mode is not NR_REG_ALL_NIC or NR_REG_ONE_NIC. It then looks up the parent port with netmap_get_na (on an ENXIO error it tries once to create a persistent VALE port with the NMG_LOCK temporarily released, otherwise it returns the error). If the parent is owned by the kernel it releases it with netmap_unget_na and returns EBUSY. If a pipe with that id already exists it picks the endpoint with the requested role (or its peer), releases the parent reference with netmap_unget_na and goes to found. If not found and create is 0 it releases the parent and returns ENODEV. Otherwise it allocates a master and a slave pipe adapter (ENOMEM on allocation failure), registers them with netmap_attach_common (an error frees what was built, removes the master from the parent with netmap_pipe_remove and releases the parent through netmap_unget_na) and netmap_pipe_add, links them as peers, takes references on the parent and on ifp (if non-NULL) and a peer reference on the opposite endpoint. At found it sets *na to the requested endpoint, takes a reference on it and returns 0.

functions.name: ntsync_wait_check_ready
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller holds the owner's private lock (NTSYNC_PRIV_ASSERT) and state is a valid wait state. If state->ready is already true it returns without doing anything. For an 'all' wait it calls ntsync_wait_all_prepare: if that returns true (and, asserted with MPASS, stop is false) it calls ntsync_wait_all_commit, sets state->ready to true and calls ntsync_wait_post_commit; if it returns false with stop set, this function does nothing more (what the prepare step already changed in state, for example an index, was not read); if it returns false without stop and an alert event exists, it asks the alert object whether it is signaled at index obj_count - 1 and, if so, sets state->index to that index, consumes it, runs its post_commit and sets state->ready to true. For an 'any' wait it calls ntsync_wait_any(state) and sets state->ready to true if that returns true (the internals of that call, including whether it consumes the signaled object, were not read); if it returns false state->ready stays false. The function returns nothing.

functions.name: nvmft_controller_lun_changed
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ctrlr is a valid controller with an initialised lock and changed_ns list; the caller does not hold ctrlr->lock. It computes new_nsid = lun_id + 1 and takes ctrlr->lock. If the changed-namespace list is not already marked full (ns[0] != 0xffffffff) it scans the sorted list: if new_nsid is already present it releases the lock and returns without reporting anything. Otherwise, if the last list slot is non-zero (the list is full) it resets the list and sets ns[0] to the full marker 0xffffffff; else it inserts new_nsid at its sorted position (shifting later entries). Whether it inserted, reset the list, or found the list already marked full, it then checks changed_ns_reported: if it is already true it releases the lock and returns; otherwise it sets it to true, releases the lock and calls nvmft_report_aer for an NS attribute change event (log page NVME_LOG_CHANGED_NAMESPACE), which may itself drop the event depending on the AER mask and pending state. The lock is released on every path and no memory is allocated.

functions.name: update_cc
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ctrlr and ctrlr->np are valid and the caller does not hold ctrlr->lock. It sets *need_shutdown to false and takes the lock. It returns false (with the lock released and ctrlr->cc unchanged) if ctrlr->shutdown is already set or if _nvmf_validate_cc(np->max_io_qsize, np->cap, ctrlr->cc, new_cc) fails. Otherwise it records the changed bits, stores new_cc in ctrlr->cc, and: if the SHN field changed and new_cc has a nonzero SHN, it sets CSTS.SHST to the shutdown-occurring value, clears CC.EN in ctrlr->cc (so ctrlr->cc then differs from new_cc), sets ctrlr->shutdown and *need_shutdown to true and logs; if the EN bit changed, a new EN of 0 logs a reset request and sets ctrlr->shutdown and *need_shutdown to true, while a new EN of 1 sets CSTS.RDY. It releases the lock and returns true.

functions.name: _nvmf_validate_cc
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: none; it only reads its arguments and has no side effects. It returns false if any of these hold for new_cc: its IOCQES field is nonzero and not 4; its IOSQES field is nonzero and not 6; with STRICT_CHECKS defined, either of those two fields is nonzero while max_io_qsize is 0 (max_io_qsize is otherwise unused); its SHN field is 3; its AMS field is nonzero; its MPS field is below the CAP MPSMAX field or above the CAP MPSMIN field (as coded, in this order of comparison); its CSS field is neither 0 nor 7; or the CC.EN bit is set in old_cc and the AMS, MPS or CSS field differs between old_cc and new_cc. Otherwise it returns true.

functions.name: nvmf_receive_capsule
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: arg is the host qpair, nc a received completion capsule; the caller does not hold qp->lock. It sets sc->ka_active_rx_traffic to 1 if keep-alive traffic tracking is enabled. If the completion's CID is greater than qp->num_commands it logs, calls nvmf_disconnect, frees the capsule and returns before taking qp->lock and before updating the submission queue head. Otherwise it takes qp->lock and updates qp->sqhd (from the completion if flow control is on and the field is valid, else by incrementing it modulo num_commands + 1). If qp->qp is NULL (the queue pair is shut down) it logs, releases the lock, frees the capsule and returns without invoking any callback and without disconnecting. If no active command exists for the CID it releases the lock, logs, calls nvmf_disconnect, frees the capsule and returns. Otherwise it takes the command's request: if no requests are pending it clears the CID's active slot, returns the command to the free list and releases the lock; if requests are pending it binds the first pending request to the command and calls nvmf_dispatch_command (the lock is not released in this function on that branch; whether nvmf_dispatch_command releases it was not read). Finally it calls the completed request's callback with the CQE, frees the capsule and frees the request.

functions.name: ocs_add_new_tgt
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: node and fcp are valid and fcp->sim is a valid SIM; the target table fcp->tgt has OCS_MAX_TARGETS entries. It looks for the first slot i with state OCS_TGT_STATE_NONE; if there is none, i is left equal to OCS_MAX_TARGETS (the code does not check this and goes on to use i as the target id, and then calls ocs_update_tgt with that index, which would index past the table if it uses it as a table index; ocs_update_tgt was not read). It allocates a ccb with xpt_alloc_ccb_nowait; if that fails it prints a message and returns (uint32_t)-1 (the function returns uint32_t, so -1 becomes 0xFFFFFFFF). It creates a path for the SIM with target id i and the wildcard LUN; if that fails it prints a message, frees the ccb and returns (uint32_t)-1. Otherwise it calls ocs_update_tgt(node, fcp, i), queues a rescan of the path with xpt_rescan(ccb) and returns 0. On the two failure returns no target slot has been changed.

functions.name: ocs_target_io
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ocs and ccb are valid and ccb is a target SCSI I/O ccb whose csio.tag_id identifies an IO in the driver's IO table. It looks the IO up with ocs_scsi_find_io; if none is found it sets the ccb status to CAM_REQ_CMP_ERR and panics (the following return 1 is not reached). If the IO already has OCS_CAM_IO_F_ABORT_RECV set it also sets OCS_CAM_IO_F_ABORT_CAM and returns 1: with CAM_SEND_STATUS set it sets CAM_REQ_CMP and frees the IO with ocs_target_io_free; without it it sets CAM_REQ_ABORTED and leaves the IO allocated. Otherwise it records the ccb in the IO, sets the ccb status to CAM_REQ_INPROG with CAM_SIM_QUEUED, and then: if CAM_SEND_STATUS is set and the transfer length is 0 it sets IO state RESP and calls ocs_scsi_send_resp (with sense data when CAM_SEND_SENSE is set); else if the transfer length is nonzero it sets state DATA, builds the SGL and, if the SGL has entries, calls ocs_scsi_send_rd_data for CAM_DIR_IN or ocs_scsi_recv_wr_data for CAM_DIR_OUT (any other direction sets CAM_REQ_INVALID and rc = 1), while an SGL build that gives no entries sets CAM_REQ_CMP_ERR and rc = 1; if neither condition holds (no status and no data) it sets CAM_REQ_INVALID and rc = 1. The completion callback registered with the hardware calls is ocs_scsi_target_io_cb. If rc is nonzero (including the value returned by the send/recv calls) it then sets the ccb status to CAM_REQ_CMP_ERR (overwriting a previous CAM_REQ_INVALID), clears CAM_SIM_QUEUED, sets the IO state to OCS_CAM_IO_DATA_DONE and, when CAM_SEND_STATUS was set with zero transfer length, frees the IO. It returns rc: 0 when the IO was handed to the hardware, otherwise 1 or the nonzero code from the hardware calls.

functions.name: ocs_scsi_recv_tmf
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: tmfio and tmfio->node->sport are valid; abortio must be non-NULL when cmd is OCS_SCSI_TMF_ABORT_TASK (it is dereferenced there without a check). It returns 1 if the sport's tgt_data is NULL. It picks the target resource for the LUN (the enabled per-LUN entry if lun < OCS_MAX_LUN, else the enabled wildcard entry, else none) and takes the first immediate-notify ccb (INOT) queued on it. If there is no INOT it logs, completes abortio (if non-NULL) and tmfio with ocs_scsi_io_complete and returns -1. Otherwise it stores abortio in tmfio, removes the INOT from the queue, fills in tag, sequence id, initiator id and status CAM_MESSAGE_RECV and the LUN, and by cmd: ABORT_TASK sets the abort message and the abort-task tag and sets the OCS_CAM_IO_F_ABORT_RECV and ABORT_NOTIFY flags on abortio; ABORT_TASK_SET, CLEAR_TASK_SET, QUERY_ASYNCHRONOUS_EVENT, LOGICAL_UNIT_RESET, CLEAR_ACA and TARGET_RESET set the corresponding message in the INOT; QUERY_TASK_SET logs that it is unsupported, puts the INOT back at the tail of the queue, completes tmfio and returns -1; any other cmd logs, puts the INOT back and returns -1 without completing tmfio. For the supported commands it sets rc to 0, prints a trace and passes the INOT to CAM with xpt_done, and if abortio is non-NULL it sets OCS_CAM_IO_F_ABORT_DEV on it and returns the result of ocs_scsi_tgt_abort_io(abortio, ocs_io_abort_cb, tmfio); otherwise it returns 0.

functions.name: __ocs_domain_wait_alloc
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ctx is a domain state-machine context in the wait-alloc state, evt a domain event, arg the per-event argument (passed only to __ocs_domain_common). The handler returns NULL on every path. For OCS_EVT_DOMAIN_ALLOC_OK: it reads the optional wwn_bump property, takes domain->sport (ocs_assert returns NULL, logging, if it is NULL), copies the service parameters from the domain DMA buffer into domain->service_params and sport->service_params (and into flogi_service_params when femul_enable is set), writes the port and node names from sport->wwpn and sport->wwnn into the sport's service parameter block (XORing them with wwn_bump when it is nonzero), then: for a loop domain that is not an NL port it transitions to __ocs_domain_allocated and calls __ocs_domain_attach_internal(domain, sport->fc_id); otherwise it looks for the fabric controller node: if one exists it logs and breaks out of the case without any transition; else it allocates a fabric node (a failure is only logged) and, if allocated, pauses or transitions it to __ocs_fabric_init, then sets domain->req_accept_frames to 1 and transitions to __ocs_domain_allocated (also after an allocation failure). For OCS_EVT_DOMAIN_ALLOC_FAIL it logs and sets domain->req_domain_free to 1. OCS_EVT_DOMAIN_FOUND does nothing. OCS_EVT_DOMAIN_LOST logs and transitions to __ocs_domain_wait_domain_lost. Any other event is passed to __ocs_domain_common.

functions.name: __ocs_p2p_wait_domain_attach
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ctx is the state-machine context of a transient point-to-point node. The handler returns NULL on every path. OCS_EVT_ENTER holds the node's frames (ocs_node_hold_frames) and OCS_EVT_EXIT accepts them again (ocs_node_accept_frames). OCS_EVT_DOMAIN_ATTACH_OK first asserts that sport->p2p_winner is set (ocs_assert returns NULL, logging, if not), then looks for a node with fc_id sport->p2p_remote_port_id: if one exists it is left untouched (asserted to be a different node than this one); otherwise it allocates a new remote node (on failure it logs and returns NULL immediately, leaving the transient node neither reinitialised nor shut down), calls ocs_fabric_notify_topology(node) and transitions the new node to __ocs_p2p_rnode_init. After that, if this node's rnode.fc_id is 0 it reinitialises the node for device login with ocs_node_init_device(node, FALSE), otherwise it sets the shutdown reason to OCS_NODE_SHUTDOWN_DEFAULT and calls ocs_fabric_initiate_shutdown(node). Any other event is passed, with arg, to __ocs_fabric_common.

functions.name: ocs_hw_set_persistent_topology
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hw is an initialised ocs_hw_t with a ready SLI context; topology is OCS_HW_TOPOLOGY_AUTO, OCS_HW_TOPOLOGY_NPORT or OCS_HW_TOPOLOGY_LOOP; opts is OCS_CMD_POLL or anything else (treated as the no-wait, semaphore-waiting mode). It builds a set-features parameter: AUTO becomes P2P-with-failover on a Lancer ASIC and P2P-only otherwise, NPORT becomes P2P-only, LOOP becomes FC-AL-only; any other topology logs and returns -1 before any command is built. It initialises a semaphore, builds the SET_FEATURES persistent-topology mailbox command and, for OCS_CMD_POLL, submits it with ocs_hw_command in polling mode, returning that function's nonzero result (after logging) if it fails. In the other mode it submits it with OCS_CMD_NOWAIT and the callback ocs_hw_set_persistent_topolgy_cb (which stores the completion status and posts the semaphore), returns the nonzero ocs_hw_command result if submission fails, waits on the semaphore forever (returning -ENXIO if the wait fails) and returns -EFAULT if the callback stored a nonzero status. When no error occurred it records the topology in the SLI context with sli_config_persistent_topology and returns the (zero) result code. No locks are taken here.

functions.name: ocs_hw_get
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hw is an initialised ocs_hw_t and value is NULL or a writable uint32_t. If value is NULL it returns OCS_HW_RTN_ERROR without dereferencing it (hw is not checked for NULL in the part read). Otherwise it sets *value to 0 and switches on prop, returning OCS_HW_RTN_SUCCESS with *value set from the matching configuration, SLI or link field for each recognised property, except: OCS_HW_AUTO_XFER_RDY_BLK_SIZE returns OCS_HW_RTN_ERROR (with *value 0) for an unrecognised block-size code; OCS_HW_TOPOLOGY returns OCS_HW_TOPOLOGY_NONE with success when hw->link.speed is 0 whatever the topology field holds, and otherwise maps the link topology to NPORT, LOOP or NONE, returning OCS_HW_RTN_ERROR with *value left 0 for any other topology value; OCS_HW_LINK_CONFIG_SPEED maps the configured speed to 0 (auto), 2000, 4000, 8000, 10000, 16000 or 32000 and returns OCS_HW_RTN_ERROR (value 0) for any other configured speed; OCS_HW_RESET_REQUIRED calls sli_reset_required and returns OCS_HW_RTN_ERROR if that is negative; any unrecognised prop logs and returns OCS_HW_RTN_ERROR with *value 0. It takes no locks.

functions.name: ocs_hw_io_abort
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hw and io_to_abort are valid, hw->state is OCS_HW_STATE_ACTIVE and io_to_abort has a live reference. It returns OCS_HW_RTN_ERROR for NULL arguments or a state other than OCS_HW_STATE_ACTIVE, and OCS_HW_RTN_IO_NOT_ACTIVE if ocs_ref_get_unless_zero on the IO's reference fails (nothing taken). After taking a reference it returns OCS_HW_RTN_IO_NOT_ACTIVE (dropping the reference) if the IO has no work queue, and OCS_HW_RTN_IO_ABORT_IN_PROGRESS (dropping its own reference but leaving the flag that another abort set) if abort_in_progress is already set. Otherwise, under io_abort_lock, it sets abort_in_progress, stores the callback and argument, and allocates a request tag with ocs_hw_reqtag_alloc; if that fails it returns OCS_HW_RTN_NO_RESOURCES without dropping the reference and without clearing abort_in_progress. With a tag, if the IO's WQE is still on the work queue's list it marks the WQE as needing an abort submission (storing send_abts, id and abort tag) and returns 0 with the reference and abort_in_progress retained. Otherwise it builds the ABORT WQE with sli_abort_wqe (failure sets rc to OCS_HW_RTN_ERROR and frees the tag), selects a work queue if the IO had none and writes the WQE with hw_wq_write (a positive result is treated as 0). If the final rc is not OCS_HW_RTN_SUCCESS it clears abort_in_progress under the lock and drops the reference; it returns rc (0 after a successful submission, in which case the reference is held until the abort completes).

functions.name: ocs_hw_init
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hw is an ocs_hw_t that has been set up (ocs_hw_setup) or reset. Under cmd_lock it returns OCS_HW_RTN_ERROR immediately if the cmd_head or cmd_pending lists are not empty. It frees the receive buffers with ocs_hw_rx_free and rebuilds the IO free lists. The remaining steps each return on failure: a sequence of sub-steps (auto xfer ready configuration, SLI init, health check, queue initialisation and count checks against the SLI maxima, header template registration, rnode memory allocation, RQ buffer and sequence pool allocation, rpi_ref set-up, FCFI/MRQ registration, reqtag and IO set-up) returns either OCS_HW_RTN_ERROR, OCS_HW_RTN_NO_MEMORY (for the allocation failures at the lines near 755, 795 and 809) or the failing sub-step's rc; earlier-allocated resources are not released on those returns, except that rnode_mem is freed on one failure path and payload_memory on another. After that it initialises queue history, queries the link configuration, sets the Ethernet license if applicable (failure only logged), and on a Lancer-type interface calls ocs_hw_set_dif_seed: a failure returns the current rc (which can still be OCS_HW_RTN_SUCCESS) at once, before any queue is armed or the state is made active; on a BE3-type interface with DIF capability ocs_hw_set_dif_mode is called and a failure returns its rc. It then arms every event queue and every completion queue (sli_queue_arm), adds receive, work and completion queues to the lookup hashes (the receive and work queues are not armed here), sets hw->state to OCS_HW_STATE_ACTIVE, initialises the rqpair (failure only logged), starts the WQE timer if configured, allocates the send-frame IOs (failures logged), configures the watchdog if requested (failures logged), allocates domain_dmem and fcf_dmem (OCS_HW_RTN_NO_MEMORY if either fails) and loop_map (a failure there is only logged), and returns OCS_HW_RTN_SUCCESS.

functions.name: ocs_hw_wq_process_io
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: arg is a valid ocs_hw_io_t with a valid hw pointer, cqe is the work-queue completion entry for it and status its completion status; for an OCS_HW_IO_TARGET_RSP IO that is port-owned, io->axr_buf is valid and the caller does not hold io->axr_lock. The function returns nothing. It handles quarantine: if the IO is in its first quarantine phase it sets io->quarantine from the CQE and re-queues it with ocs_hw_io_quarantine, clears quarantine_first_phase, and does the same for a secondary IO that is still quarantined. It removes the IO's timed WQE, clears io->xbusy if the CQE's XB bit is 0, and derives len (and ext for ELS requests) from the CQE according to io->type; for a port-owned target response it takes io->axr_lock (recording that) and notes whether the out-of-order AXR command and data callbacks are flagged. If status is nonzero it reads the extended status and may call ocs_hw_io_abort: for an originator IO with config.i_only_aab when an abort is needed (abort with send_abts TRUE), or for a non-originator IO whose XB bit is set (send_abts FALSE); if the abort returns OCS_HW_RTN_SUCCESS it saves status, ext and len in io->saved_* with status_saved set and jumps to the exit, skipping everything below (no sec_hio free, no done callback, no AXR callbacks); any other result, including OCS_HW_RTN_IO_ABORT_IN_PROGRESS, is only logged and processing continues. Next it frees io->sec_hio if present and clears it; if io->done is non-NULL it clears io->done, replaces status, len and ext with the saved values if status_saved was set (clearing it), restores the SGL and calls done once. Then, only if the out-of-order AXR command flag was set, it delivers the command sequence to the bounce callback (when config.bounce is set and a bounce callback exists) or to the unsolicited callback, and, only inside that same block, if the AXR data flag was also set, delivers the data sequence the same way. At the exit label it releases io->axr_lock if it was taken.

functions.name: ocs_hw_cb_fip
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ctx is a valid ocs_hw_t and e a valid sli4_fip_event_t (both ocs_hw_assert-ed). Before the switch, for every event type, it looks up a domain: for SLI4_FCOE_FIP_FCF_CLEAR_VLINK it scans the sport list of each non-NULL domain in hw->domains for a sport whose indicator equals event->index; for all other types it uses ocs_hw_domain_get_indexed(hw, event->index). Then by type: SLI4_FCOE_FIP_FCF_DISCOVERED calls ocs_hw_read_fcf(hw, event->index) (the domain found is not used); SLI4_FCOE_FIP_FCF_DEAD calls hw->callback.domain with OCS_HW_DOMAIN_LOST and the domain if both the domain and the callback are non-NULL; SLI4_FCOE_FIP_FCF_CLEAR_VLINK does the same after setting domain->req_rediscover_fcf to TRUE; SLI4_FCOE_FIP_FCF_MODIFIED makes the same callback (when domain and callback are non-NULL) and then always calls ocs_hw_read_fcf(hw, event->index); any other type is only logged. The function returns 0 on every path and takes no locks.

functions.name: ocs_xport_control
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: xport is a valid transport with xport->ocs non-NULL (both are ocs_assert-ed and return -1 if not); cmd is an OCS_XPORT_* command and the variable arguments match the command. OCS_XPORT_PORT_ONLINE calls ocs_hw_port_control(OCS_HW_PORT_INIT) and sets xport->configured_link_state to cmd on success; its result is the returned code (nonzero on failure). OCS_XPORT_PORT_OFFLINE calls the port shutdown control and sets configured_link_state on success; a failure is only logged and the function returns 0. OCS_XPORT_SHUTDOWN reads OCS_HW_RESET_REQUIRED (treated as 0 if the query fails); if a reset is required it calls ocs_xport_force_free and leaves the case at once, without registering the domain-list callback, without calling ocs_vport_del_all and with rc still 0. Otherwise it registers the domain-list-empty callback, issues the port shutdown (a failure calls ocs_xport_force_free), else waits on the semaphore for OCS_FC_DOMAIN_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_USEC (a timeout makes rc the nonzero wait result and calls ocs_xport_force_free); it then unregisters the callback and calls ocs_vport_del_all. OCS_XPORT_POST_NODE_EVENT returns -1 if the node or node->ocs is NULL (asserted) or the node state machine has no current state, otherwise posts the event with ocs_hw_async_call and waits for its semaphore forever: -1 if the async call or the wait fails, else 0. OCS_XPORT_WWNN_SET and WWPN_SET store the 64-bit value in xport->req_wwnn or req_wwpn and return 0. An unrecognised cmd returns 0. rc is a uint32_t returned through an int32_t.

functions.name: otus_set_key_cb
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: arg points to an otus_cmd_key. The function is inside an #ifdef notyet block in if_otus.c (lines 2948-3046), so it is not compiled in a normal build; in that block its non-group branch refers to a variable ni that is not declared in the function. It clears a ar_cmd_ekey; for a group key it uses the key id as uid and our own address with bit 0x80 set in the first byte as MAC, otherwise it uses OTUS_UID(associd) and ni->ni_macaddr. It sets kix to 0, maps the key cipher (WEP40, WEP104, TKIP, CCMP) to the hardware cipher and returns without sending anything for any other cipher. It copies up to 16 bytes of the key and sends AR_CMD_EKEY with otus_cmd; if that returns an error, or the cipher is not TKIP, it returns. For TKIP it then sets kix to 1, copies the next 16 key bytes (the MIC key) and sends a second AR_CMD_EKEY, ignoring its result. It returns nothing.

functions.name: p2sb_get_port
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is unused. It compares unit with the number of entries in the static table lbg_communities (6 entries) and returns EINVAL if unit is not below that count (a negative unit is converted to a large unsigned value in the comparison and also returns EINVAL); otherwise it returns lbg_communities[unit], which is 0xAF, 0xAE, 0xAD, 0xAC, 0xAB or 0x11 for units 0 to 5. It has no side effects.

functions.name: PCCARD_ACCESSOR(vendor, VENDOR, uint32_t)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function pccard_get_vendor: a static inline int function taking (device_t dev, uint32_t *t), defined by that macro invocation in pccardvar.h, whose body is the single statement return BUS_READ_IVAR(device_get_parent(dev), dev, PCCARD_IVAR_VENDOR, (uintptr_t *)t). It returns whatever the parent bus read-ivar method returns for that ivar; on success that method stores the vendor id through the cast pointer, which is a pointer to uintptr_t aimed at an object of type uint32_t, so the width written is that of uintptr_t. The function itself makes no checks and takes no locks.

functions.name: pci_set_powerstate_method
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: child is a PCI device whose ivars hold a valid pci_devinfo. Postcondition: returns EOPNOTSUPP, before any config read or write, if the device has no power management capability (pp_location == 0); returns 0 without a config write or delay if the current power state from pci_get_powerstate equals state; otherwise it reads the power status register (a config read that happens before the state is validated), then returns EOPNOTSUPP without writing if state is D1 or D2 and the matching D1SUPP or D2SUPP capability bit is clear, or EINVAL without writing if state is not one of D0, D1, D2, D3; for a supported state it optionally prints a message when bootverbose, writes the power status register with the old non-state bits kept and the new state bits set, busy-waits 10000 us when the higher of the old and new states is D3, 200 us when it is D2, none otherwise, and returns 0.

functions.name: pci_dw_init
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is a DesignWare PCI host-bridge device; the glue driver is expected to have set sc->dbi_res before the call (this function does not allocate it). Postcondition: sets sc->dev and sc->node, initializes sc->mtx, sets bus_start 0, bus_end 255, root_bus 0, sub_bus 1, reads coherent and num-lanes from the OFW node (num_lanes defaults to 1), then returns 0 if every step succeeds. Steps and failures: num_lanes not 1, 2, 4 or 8 sets num_lanes to 0 and returns ENXIO; missing 'config' in reg-names returns ENXIO; failure to allocate the config memory resource returns ENXIO; bus_dma_tag_create, ofw_pcib_init, pci_dw_decode_ranges, pci_dw_detect_out_atu_regions and pci_dw_setup_hw return their nonzero error unchanged. If pci_dw_detect_atu_unroll reports unroll mode, the 'atu' entry in reg-names is looked up: found means the resource is allocated (ENXIO if NULL) with offset 0; ENOENT means iatu_ur_res aliases dbi_res with the default DBI offset and size; any other lookup error returns ENXIO. On success it calls device_add_child for 'pci', whose result is ignored, and returns 0. Every error goes to label out, which returns rv with no cleanup (XXX Cleanup), so the mutex, resources and dma tag already created are left in place.

functions.name: pcib_pcie_hotplug_task
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: used as a taskqueue handler with context pointing to the pcib_softc; the caller does not hold the hotplug lock. Postcondition: takes PCIB_HP_LOCK, then calls pcib_hotplug_present(sc). If it returns nonzero and sc->child is NULL, it sets sc->child to the result of device_add_child(dev, 'pci', DEVICE_UNIT_ANY) (which may be NULL on failure) and calls bus_attach_children(dev); if it returns nonzero and sc->child is already set, nothing changes. If it returns zero and sc->child is non-NULL, it calls device_delete_child and clears sc->child only when that returns 0; if it returns zero and sc->child is NULL, nothing changes. It then releases the lock and returns nothing (void). The pending argument is unused.

functions.name: pci_ioctl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev, data and td are valid for cmd, with data pointing at the command-specific structure, and the caller does not hold the bus topology lock. Behavior: if flag lacks FWRITE and cmd is not one of PCIOCGETCONF (and its 32-bit, FreeBSD14 and FreeBSD6 compat variants when compiled), PCIOCGETBAR or PCIOCLISTVPD, it returns EPERM before taking any lock; so PCIOCREAD, PCIOCWRITE, PCIOCATTACHED, PCIOCBARMMAP, PCIOCBARIO and unknown commands get EPERM on a read-only descriptor. Otherwise it takes the bus topology lock, dispatches on cmd, each case ends in break, then releases the lock and returns error. Results: PCIOCGETCONF initializes error to 0 and returns 0 for the list-changed and past-the-end cases with a status code, EINVAL when pattern sizes are inconsistent, when only one of num_patterns or pat_buf_len is nonzero, or when copyin of the patterns fails, the copyout error if copying a match out fails, otherwise 0; it frees its temporary buffers. PCIOCREAD and PCIOCWRITE (and the FreeBSD6 forms) return EINVAL for a width other than 1, 2 or 4 or for a negative or misaligned register, ENODEV when the device is not found (except FreeBSD6 read with COMPAT_FREEBSD4, which stores -1 and returns 0), else 0 after the config read or write. PCIOCGETBAR returns ENODEV, EINVAL (no such BAR) or 0. PCIOCATTACHED returns ENODEV or 0. PCIOCLISTVPD returns ENODEV or the result of pci_list_vpd. PCIOCBARMMAP returns ENODEV or the result of pci_bar_mmap (the inner EPERM check for read-write mapping without FWRITE is unreachable on a read-only descriptor because it is rejected earlier). PCIOCBARIO returns ENODEV or the pci_bar_io result. Any other command returns ENOTTY.

functions.name: dmUpStreamDiscover2ExpanderPhy
functions.prose_contract: Handles one SAS2 DISCOVER response for the phy oneExpander->discoveringPhyId during upstream discovery; returns void. Precondition: dmRoot, onePortContext, oneExpander (with oneExpander->dmDevice set) and pDiscoverResp are valid. Behavior: if dmDiscoverCheck returns agTRUE it returns at once with no change. If pDiscoverResp->phyIdentifier differs from oneExpander->discoveringPhyId it calls dmDiscoverDone(dmRoot, onePortContext, DM_RC_FAILURE) and returns, without recording sasAddressIDDiscoverError and without incrementing discoveringPhyId. Otherwise it stores the response's routing attribute in oneExpander->routingAttribute[phyId]. If the expander's device is a fanout expander and the routing attribute is subtractive, it records the device's SAS address and the phy id in onePortContext->discovery.sasAddressIDDiscoverError, calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) and returns; a fanout expander with any other routing attribute does nothing further in this step. For a non-fanout expander with an attached device and subtractive routing: it calls dmExpanderUpStreamPhyAdd. If hasUpStreamDevice was already set, an upstream SAS address that differs from the attached address while the attached device is an edge or fanout expander makes it record the error address and call dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) without returning. If hasUpStreamDevice was not set, it sets it and the upstream SAS address; when the attached address is not the port's local address it looks the attached device up with dmPortSASDeviceFind: if found and an edge expander, it either links oneExpander->dmUpStreamExpander to that expander when its upstream address matches this device, or else records the error address and calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE); if found and not an edge expander, it only logs a debug message and calls neither dmDiscoverDone nor records an error; if not found it adds the device with dmPortSASDeviceAdd (STP type for STP target or SATA, otherwise SAS type, link rate the minimum of the port's rate and the reported one; in non-full-start discovery first trying dmFindRegNValid), and if the add produced a device it allocates and registers an expander for an attached edge or fanout expander (setting oneExpander->dmUpStreamExpander) or, for an end device, sets that device's dmExpander to oneExpander and clears dmUpStreamExpander; a failed device add or a failed expander allocation calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) without recording sasAddressIDDiscoverError. Every path that did not return early then increments oneExpander->discoveringPhyId; if the discovery status is still DISCOVERY_UP_STREAM it either calls dmDiscoverSend (more phys remain) or dmUpdateAllAdjacent, dmDiscoveringExpanderRemove and dmUpStreamDiscovering; otherwise it just returns.

functions.name: dmDownStreamDiscoverExpanderPhy
functions.prose_contract: Handles one SAS 1.1 DISCOVER response for oneExpander->discoveringPhyId during downstream discovery; returns void. Behavior: returns at once with no change if dmDiscoverCheck returns agTRUE. If pDiscoverResp->phyIdentifier differs from discoveringPhyId it calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) and returns without recording sasAddressIDDiscoverError and without incrementing discoveringPhyId. Otherwise it stores the response's routing attribute in oneExpander->routingAttribute[phyId] and sets oneExpander->discoverSMPAllowed to agTRUE. When the response reports an attached device: direct routing to an attached edge or fanout expander records the expander's SAS address and the phy id in onePortContext->discovery.sasAddressIDDiscoverError, calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) and returns without incrementing discoveringPhyId. Otherwise, if the attached SAS address differs from the port's local address it looks up the device with dmPortSASDeviceFind. If not found and the routing is subtractive with an attached edge or fanout expander, it records the error address and sets onePortContext->discovery.DeferredError to agTRUE without calling dmDiscoverDone; if not found otherwise it adds the device with dmPortSASDeviceAdd (STP type for STP target or SATA, otherwise SAS type, at the minimum of the port link rate and the reported rate; in non-full-start discovery it first tries dmFindRegNValid) and sets its dmExpander to oneExpander; for table routing with an attached fanout expander it records the error and calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE), with an attached edge expander it allocates an expander, adds the up and down phys and queues it, or calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) if allocation fails. If the device was already known, the checks on subtractive and table routing can record the error and call dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) without returning. No attached device, or an attached address equal to the local address, adds nothing. Each path that did not return early then increments discoveringPhyId; if the status is still DISCOVERY_DOWN_STREAM it either calls dmDiscoverSend (discoveringPhyId < numOfPhys) or dmUpdateAllAdjacent, dmDiscoveringExpanderRemove and dmDownStreamDiscovering; otherwise it returns.

functions.name: dmDownStreamDiscoverExpanderPhy
functions.prose_contract: Handles one SAS 1.1 DISCOVER response for oneExpander->discoveringPhyId during downstream discovery; returns void. Behavior: returns at once with no change if dmDiscoverCheck returns agTRUE. If the response's phy id differs from discoveringPhyId it calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) and returns without recording sasAddressIDDiscoverError and without incrementing discoveringPhyId. Otherwise it stores the routing attribute in oneExpander->routingAttribute[phyId] and sets discoverSMPAllowed to agTRUE. With an attached device, direct routing to an edge or fanout expander records the error address and phy id in onePortContext->discovery.sasAddressIDDiscoverError, calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) and returns without incrementing discoveringPhyId. Other cases add or look up the attached device (dmPortSASDeviceFind, dmPortSASDeviceAdd, dmFindRegNValid), allocate and queue an attached edge expander, or on topology errors (subtractive routing with no recorded upstream device or an upstream address mismatch, table routing to a fanout expander, and similar) record the error address and call dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) without returning; a subtractive-routed unknown expander instead sets DeferredError to agTRUE. After those, the paths that did not return early reach the increment of discoveringPhyId (line 2119) and check the status: if it is still DISCOVERY_DOWN_STREAM it calls dmDiscoverSend when discoveringPhyId < numOfPhys, else dmUpdateAllAdjacent, dmDiscoveringExpanderRemove and dmDownStreamDiscovering; if the status is no longer DISCOVERY_DOWN_STREAM it only returns.

functions.name: dmDownStreamDiscover2ExpanderPhy
functions.prose_contract: Handles one SAS2 DISCOVER response for oneExpander->discoveringPhyId during downstream discovery; returns void. Behavior: returns at once with no change if dmDiscoverCheck returns agTRUE. If the response's phy id differs from discoveringPhyId it calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) and returns, without recording sasAddressIDDiscoverError. Otherwise it stores the routing attribute in oneExpander->routingAttribute[phyId] and sets discoverSMPAllowed to agTRUE (both before the direct-routing check). With an attached device: direct routing to an attached edge or fanout expander records the SAS address and phy id in onePortContext->discovery.sasAddressIDDiscoverError, calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) and returns. Otherwise, when the attached SAS address differs from the port's local address, it looks up the device with dmPortSASDeviceFind; if not found it computes the connection rate as the minimum of the port link rate and the reported logical rate and adds the device with dmPortSASDeviceAdd (STP type for STP target or SATA, otherwise SAS type; in non-full-start discovery it first tries dmFindRegNValid), and if a device results sets its dmExpander to oneExpander. A phy with no attached device or one attached to the local address adds nothing and sets no failure. A failed device add is handled later in the function by dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) (2681) without recording an error address. The remaining effects of this slice's range (table or subtractive routing to an expander and the configurable-expander routing entry) are in the continuation of the function.

functions.name: dmDownStreamDiscover2ExpanderPhy
functions.prose_contract: Handles one SAS2 DISCOVER response for oneExpander->discoveringPhyId during downstream discovery; returns void. Behavior: returns at once if dmDiscoverCheck returns agTRUE; a phy-id mismatch calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) and returns; otherwise it stores the routing attribute and sets oneExpander->discoverSMPAllowed to agTRUE, and a direct-routed phy attached to an edge or fanout expander records the error address and calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) and returns. If the attached device is not yet known and was added: for table routing, an attached fanout expander records the error address and calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE); an attached edge expander gets an allocated expander registered (with up and down phys set, hasUpStreamDevice true, dmUpStreamExpander set) or dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) if allocation fails; a subtractive-routed attached edge or fanout expander is allocated the same way (dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) on allocation failure). If discovery is still DISCOVERY_DOWN_STREAM and ConfiguresOthers is agFALSE, it finds a configurable expander and, when one is found with no duplicate configured SAS address, updates dmCurrentDownStreamExpander, currentDownStreamPhyIndex and dmReturnginExpander and calls dmRoutingEntryAdd. If the device add itself failed it calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) without an error record. If the attached device was already known: a subtractive phy with no upstream device recorded records the error and calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE); a subtractive phy whose upstream address differs from the attached address records the error address and sets DeferredError to agTRUE without terminating discovery; table routing to a fanout expander records the error and calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE); table routing to an edge expander whose upstream address differs from this device either, when both expanders support table-to-table (TTTSupported) and dmSAS2SAS11ErrorCheck does not flag a problem, sets UndoDueToTTTSupported and clears DeferredError, or records the error and calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE); otherwise it adds the up and down phys and queues the attached expander. The tail then increments discoveringPhyId and, if the status is still DISCOVERY_DOWN_STREAM, sends the next phy (dmDiscoverSend) or runs dmUpdateAllAdjacent, optionally dmDiscoveringUndoAdd, dmDiscoveringExpanderRemove and dmDownStreamDiscovering.

functions.name: dmSMPCompleted
functions.prose_contract: SMP completion callback for the discovery manager; returns void. It reads the dmSMPRequestBody from agIORequest->osData and works on the request's device and port contexts. Early exits: if the device has valid and valid2 both agFALSE, a NULL dmPortContext and the request's port context is not valid (everything was reset), or the port context or the old port context is NULL, the request body is put on dmAllShared->freeSMPList and so is the indirect response body when it is non-NULL (without DIRECT_SMP), then it returns. Otherwise it decrements onePortContext->discovery.pendingSMP; if the request's port context differs from the old one it stops the discovery SMP timers for discovery-type SMP functions (report general, discover, report phy sata, configure routing), calls dmCleanAllExp on the old context, frees the bodies and returns; if the port is invalid, discovery completed or aborted it stops timers, frees the bodies, may clean up expanders when pendingSMP is 0, and returns. For a live port it stops the SMP timers, and then dispatches on whether the expander is SAS 1.1 or SAS2 (oneExpander->SAS2) and on agIOStatus. OSSA_IO_SUCCESS: for report general, discover, report phy sata, configure routing and phy control, a response length mismatch calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE), frees the bodies and returns, otherwise the matching per-function handler (dmReportGeneralRespRcvd or dmReportGeneral2RespRcvd, dmDiscoverRespRcvd or dmDiscover2RespRcvd, dmReportPhySata2Rcvd, dmConfigRoutingInfo(2)RespRcvd, dmPhyControl(2)RespRcvd) is called and the function breaks to the common tail; SMP functions the switch does not list do nothing. OSSA_IO_ABORTED and OSSA_IO_INVALID_LENGTH only log. OSSA_IO_ERROR_INTERNAL_SMP_RESOURCE resubmits with saSMPStart: on AGSA_RC_SUCCESS it increments pendingSMP, re-arms the discovery timer for discovery functions and returns without freeing; on AGSA_RC_BUSY a discovery function starts dmSMPBusyTimer and SMP_PHY_CONTROL calls dmPhyControlFailureRespRcvd; on failure a discovery function calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) and SMP_PHY_CONTROL calls dmPhyControlFailureRespRcvd. In the SAS2 branch OSSA_IO_OPEN_CNX_ERROR_ZONE_VIOLATION calls dmHandleZoneViolation. Other statuses: for the IT-nexus-loss and non-operational statuses the device is set operational with saSetDeviceState; for a connection-rate-unsupported error with dmAllShared->RateAdjust it lowers the rate via saSetDeviceInfo or, at 1.5G, reports discovery or phy-control failure; otherwise it retries with saSMPStart while retries < SMP_RETRIES (on success or busy it increments pendingSMP and retries, starts a timer and returns), and once retries are used up it calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) for discovery functions (and for phy control only with the clear-affiliation operation). Paths that reach the common tail free the request body and, when non-NULL, the indirect response body to freeSMPList and return.

functions.name: dmSMPCompleted
functions.prose_contract: SMP completion callback for the discovery manager; returns void. It first handles the device or port having gone away (valid and valid2 both agFALSE with a NULL dmPortContext and an invalid request port context, or a NULL port context: frees the request body, and when non-NULL the indirect response body, to dmAllShared->freeSMPList and returns), decrements discovery.pendingSMP at line 2436, stops discovery SMP timers for discovery functions, and returns early with the bodies freed when the port context changed or the port is invalid, completed or aborted. For a live port it then branches on SAS 1.1 versus SAS2 expander and on agIOStatus: OSSA_IO_SUCCESS parses the SMP response header and, after a response-length check that calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) and frees the bodies on a mismatch, hands the response to the per-function handler; OSSA_IO_ABORTED and OSSA_IO_INVALID_LENGTH only log; OSSA_IO_ERROR_INTERNAL_SMP_RESOURCE resubmits through saSMPStart (success: pendingSMP++, discovery timer, return; busy: dmSMPBusyTimer for discovery functions or dmPhyControlFailureRespRcvd for phy control; failure: dmDiscoverDone or dmPhyControlFailureRespRcvd); OSSA_IO_OPEN_CNX_ERROR_ZONE_VIOLATION calls dmHandleZoneViolation; other statuses mark the device operational for the nexus-loss and non-operational statuses, optionally lower the connection rate (saSetDeviceInfo, with discovery or phy-control failure reported at 1.5G), or retry with saSMPStart while the request's retries is below SMP_RETRIES (success or busy: pendingSMP++, retries++, a timer is started and the function returns), and once retries are used up call dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) for discovery functions (and for phy control only with the clear-affiliation operation). SMP functions the handlers do not list are not handled and only fall to the common tail. Unless a path returns earlier, the tail frees the request body and, when non-NULL, the indirect response body to freeSMPList.

functions.name: dmSMPCompleted
functions.prose_contract: SMP completion callback for the discovery manager; returns void. Slice-relevant behavior: this part is the end of the SAS2 branch (OSSA_IO_* statuses other than success, aborted, resource-error and zone violation) and the common tail. For statuses not handled by the earlier branches (after the nexus-loss/non-operational device-state and the rate-adjust handling), the retry logic is: if the request's retries is below SMP_RETRIES it re-issues the request with saSMPStart; on AGSA_RC_SUCCESS it increments pendingSMP and retries, (for discovery functions) re-arms the discovery SMP timer, and returns without freeing anything; on AGSA_RC_BUSY it increments pendingSMP and retries and, for a discovery function, starts dmSMPBusyTimer and returns, for SMP_PHY_CONTROL it calls dmPhyControlFailureRespRcvd, and for any other function it takes no reporting action and falls through to the common tail; on AGSA_RC_FAILURE it calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) for discovery functions or dmPhyControlFailureRespRcvd for SMP_PHY_CONTROL, and does nothing else for other functions. When retries has reached SMP_RETRIES, discovery functions call dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE), and SMP_PHY_CONTROL calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) only for the clear-affiliation operation (other phy-control operations take an else branch at 3646 that was not read). Every path that falls out of the status handling reaches the tail at 3662: the request body goes to dmAllShared->freeSMPList, and the indirect response body too when it is non-NULL, then the function returns. Earlier in the function, early exits for an invalid device, NULL port contexts or a changed or aborted port also free the bodies and return after decrementing discovery.pendingSMP.

functions.name: dmReportGeneralRespRcvd
functions.prose_contract: Handles the SAS 1.1 Report General response for an expander device; returns void. Precondition: oneDeviceData has a port context, and, when the function result is accepted, a non-NULL dmExpander. It reads the response from the frame (the indirect response body when DIRECT_SMP is not defined), then returns at once with no further change if dmDiscoverCheck(dmRoot, onePortContext) returns agTRUE. If frameHeader->smpFunctionResult is SMP_FUNCTION_ACCEPTED it stores numOfPhys in oneDeviceData and routingIndex, configReserved (0), configRouteTable and configuring in the expander; then, if oneExpander->SAS2 was 0 and the response is a long response, it sets oneExpander->SAS2 to the long-response value, calls dmReportGeneralSend and returns; otherwise, if the expander is configuring it increments discovery->retries and either, when retries reached dmAllShared->MaxRetryDiscovery, resets retries to 0 and calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE) or else starts dmDiscoveryConfiguringTimer; if it is not configuring it resets retries to 0 and calls dmDiscoverSend. If the function result is anything else it calls dmDiscoverDone(DM_RC_FAILURE). It then returns.

functions.name: siHDAMode
functions.prose_contract: Forces the SPC controller into HDA mode and loads firmware images through the boot ROM; returns AGSA_RC_SUCCESS or AGSA_RC_FAILURE. Parameters: agRoot, HDAMode (when it is 0 the function first calls siSpcSoftReset and reads the HDA status, returning AGSA_RC_FAILURE if the status is not BOOTTLOADERHDA_IDLE), userFwImg. It returns AGSA_RC_FAILURE at once if userFwImg is NULL; with SA_EXCLUDE_FW_IMG defined it also returns failure if any of the aap1, ila, iop or istr image pointers or lengths is missing. Image pointers taken from userFwImg are used as given when both the pointer and length are non-zero. The function then polls the boot ROM, copies the ISTR image (siBar4Cpy), the ILA image, the AAP1 image and the IOP image in that sequence, polling each step; any failed siBar4Cpy returns AGSA_RC_FAILURE, an HDAR_BAD_IMG or HDAR_BAD_CMD response returns AGSA_RC_FAILURE, and a poll timeout returns AGSA_RC_FAILURE except that two of the polls first jump to the label TryAfterReset when the HDA reset has not been done yet (the code at 1532-1538 and 1653-1659). It returns AGSA_RC_SUCCESS only after all four image copies and polls complete and mpiWaitForConfigTable(agRoot, &mainCfg) does not return AGSA_RC_FAILURE; a failure there returns AGSA_RC_FAILURE.

functions.name: siBar4Cpy
functions.prose_contract: Copies array_size bytes from parray to controller memory at offset via the BAR4 window in 64 KB pieces; returns AGSA_RC_SUCCESS or AGSA_RC_FAILURE. The window shift address is (GSMSM_AXI_LOWERADDR+offset) & SHIFT_MASK and the first piece starts at offset & OFFSET_MASK inside the window. The loop is a do-while, so even for array_size 0 it shifts BAR4 once and calls siPciMemCpy with zero dwords. Each iteration calls siBar4Shift for the current window and returns AGSA_RC_FAILURE immediately if that fails (earlier pieces stay copied and later ones are not copied). It then copies cpy_size bytes (the rest of the 64 KB window, or all remaining bytes if they fit) through siPciMemCpy as CEILING(cpy_size,4) little-endian dwords written to PCIBAR2, so up to 3 bytes beyond the end of the last piece may be read from parray and written to the card; it then advances to the next 64 KB window. After the loop it shifts BAR4 back to 0 and returns AGSA_RC_FAILURE if that final siBar4Shift fails (all bytes were already copied then), otherwise AGSA_RC_SUCCESS.

functions.name: siHDAMode_V
functions.prose_contract: Loads firmware into an SPCv controller via the HDA boot-ROM DMA protocol; returns AGSA_RC_SUCCESS or AGSA_RC_FAILURE (returnVal starts as AGSA_RC_FAILURE). Precondition: agRoot->sdkData points to a valid agsaLLRoot_t whose memoryAllocated.agMemory array holds memoryAllocated.count entries. Behavior: it calls siScratchDump(agRoot) first, then returns AGSA_RC_FAILURE if userFwImg is NULL (before reading the HDA response register). It reads the HDA response status register and finds the largest allocated memory chunk (biggest), whose DMA address it uses as the transfer buffer; if aap1Len, ilaLen or iopLen exceeds biggest it returns AGSA_RC_FAILURE. Then for each enabled step (HDA_STEP_2 to HDA_STEP_8 are all defined as 1) it zeroes the buffer, copies the ILA, AAP1 or IOP image into it only when that image's length is less than biggest (an image whose length equals biggest is not copied, but the command is still issued with that length), issues the HDA DMA command or scratchpad request and polls for completion; a timeout in the ILA, AAP1 or IOP polls returns AGSA_RC_FAILURE or jumps to fw_err (which also returns the failure value); a step-5 response other than SPC_V_HDAR_EXEC jumps to bootrom_err, which returns returnVal (AGSA_RC_FAILURE at that point). Only step 8 sets returnVal to AGSA_RC_SUCCESS; there a timeout of the IOP0 state poll sets it back to AGSA_RC_FAILURE, an ILA or RAAE poll timeout is only logged, and a scratchpad-1 error state afterwards sets AGSA_RC_FAILURE and goes to fw_err. It returns returnVal at the end. It takes no locks and the caller keeps ownership of the images.

functions.name: siHDAMode_V
functions.prose_contract: Loads firmware into an SPCv controller via the HDA boot-ROM DMA protocol; returns AGSA_RC_SUCCESS or AGSA_RC_FAILURE (returnVal starts as AGSA_RC_FAILURE). In the range of this slice (steps 2 to 5): after the entry checks (userFwImg NULL, or aap1Len, ilaLen or iopLen larger than the largest allocated chunk, each returning AGSA_RC_FAILURE) it zeroes the DMA buffer, copies the ILA image into it only when ilaLen is below the buffer size, and, if the HDA status reads idle, builds an HDAC DMA command (ILA length, destination 0x1e200000) with an incremented sequence id and writes it. Steps 2, 3 and 5 each poll for command completion and return AGSA_RC_FAILURE if the poll times out (returns at 2088, 2148, 2288); after the step-5 poll completes the status must equal SPC_V_HDAR_EXEC, otherwise it jumps to bootrom_err, which returns returnVal (AGSA_RC_FAILURE at that point). A step-5 poll that sees the wrong sequence id counts as not complete and so takes the timeout return. The function then continues to steps 6 to 8, where only step 8 sets returnVal to AGSA_RC_SUCCESS.

functions.name: siHDAMode_V
functions.prose_contract: Loads firmware into an SPCv controller via the HDA boot-ROM DMA protocol; returns AGSA_RC_SUCCESS or AGSA_RC_FAILURE (returnVal starts as AGSA_RC_FAILURE). In the range of this slice (steps 6 to 8 and the exit): the entry checks have already returned AGSA_RC_FAILURE for a NULL userFwImg or for any of aap1Len, ilaLen or iopLen larger than the biggest allocated chunk (1979-1998), so oversized images do not continue. Step 6 zeroes the buffer, copies the AAP1 image only when aap1Len is below the buffer size, writes the AAP1 address and length into host scratchpad registers and polls; a poll timeout jumps to fw_err and returns the failure value. Step 7 zeroes the buffer, copies the IOP image only when iopLen is below the buffer size, writes the IOP address and length (ILAHDAC_IOP_IMG_DONE) to scratchpad 3/4/5, optionally (hostDirectAccessMode & 2) does extra work, then polls for ILAHDA_IOP_IMG_GET for up to 2 s; a timeout returns returnVal, still AGSA_RC_FAILURE at that point. Step 8 sets returnVal to AGSA_RC_SUCCESS, polls scratchpad 1 for the PCIe, ILA, RAAE and IOP0 states; the ILA and RAAE timeouts are only logged, but an IOP0 timeout sets returnVal to AGSA_RC_FAILURE (2562). If the scratchpad-1 error state is set it sets AGSA_RC_FAILURE and goes to fw_err. Otherwise it returns returnVal.

functions.name: siIODone
functions.prose_contract: Completes a successfully finished IO request; returns void. Precondition: pRequest is non-NULL (SA_ASSERT only, no runtime check). If pRequest->valid is not agTRUE it only logs. If valid, it takes pDevice from the request and switches on requestType & AGSA_REQTYPE_MASK. SSP: calls pRequest->completionCB(agRoot, pIORequestContext, OSSA_IO_SUCCESS, 0, agNULL, (bit16)(sspTag & SSPTAG_BITS), 0) unconditionally, then under LL_IOREQ_LOCKEQ_LOCK removes the request from pDevice->pendingIORequests, sets valid to agFALSE and adds it to saRoot->freeIORequests. SATA: calls the SATA completion callback with OSSA_IO_SUCCESS only if pIORequestContext is non-NULL; then under the lock removes it from pendingIORequests and adds it to saRoot->freeIORequests; sets valid to agFALSE after releasing the lock. SMP: calls the SMP completion callback with OSSA_IO_SUCCESS only if pIORequestContext is non-NULL; then under the lock removes it from pendingIORequests and adds it to saRoot->freeReservedRequests if that list has fewer than SA_RESERVED_REQUEST_COUNT entries, otherwise to saRoot->freeIORequests; sets valid to agFALSE after releasing the lock. An unrecognised request type only logs, leaving the request valid and on the pending list. The status argument is not used; the completion callbacks called here are given OSSA_IO_SUCCESS.

functions.name: mpiHWevent
functions.prose_contract: Handles a hardware-event outbound message; returns AGSA_RC_SUCCESS or AGSA_RC_FAILURE. It returns AGSA_RC_FAILURE if agRoot->sdkData (saRoot) is NULL, if the decoded port id exceeds saRoot->phyCount and the port state is not OSSA_PORT_NOT_ESTABLISHED, for OSSA_HW_EVENT_PORT_RECOVERY_TIMER_TMO when no port context is available, and for OSSA_HW_EVENT_PHY_START_STATUS when the IOMap entry for the event's tag holds no request (no callback and no free in that case); the other paths I read return AGSA_RC_SUCCESS. It decodes phy id, port id and port state, looks up the port context from saRoot->PortMap, then switches on Event: most events call ossaHwCB with the event, the phy id or port context and event-specific parameters (and some, such as PHY_DOWN and PORT_RECOVERY_TIMER_TMO, update port or phy state first); OSSA_HW_EVENT_PHY_STOP_STATUS calls siPhyStopCB (not ossaHwCB) after reading the request and context from the IOMap, then clears the IOMap entry (Tag, IORequest, agContext) and, under LL_IOREQ_LOCKEQ_LOCK, returns the request to saRoot->freeReservedRequests when that list has fewer than SA_RESERVED_REQUEST_COUNT entries, otherwise to saRoot->freeIORequests; OSSA_HW_EVENT_PHY_START_STATUS calls ossaHwCB first and only afterwards clears the IOMap entry, then under the lock marks the request invalid and frees it to the same two lists; OSSA_HW_EVENT_IT_NEXUS_LOSS and any unknown event only log.

functions.name: ossaSATAEvent
functions.prose_contract: SATA event callback of the SM layer; returns void and uses the global gsmRoot (smIntRoot and smAllShared are derived from it with no NULL check). On OSSA_IO_XFER_ERROR_ABORTED_NCQ_MODE it scans smAllShared->MainDeviceList for the device whose agDevHandle equals agDevHandle: it returns if a list entry object is NULL, if no device matches, or if the matching device's valid flag is agFALSE. If the device's satDriveState is SAT_DEV_STATE_NORMAL it sets it to SAT_DEV_STATE_IN_RECOVERY and allocates an internal IO resource for READ LOG EXT page 10h; if allocation fails it sets satAbortAfterReset to agTRUE and returns; otherwise it fills the internal IO context and calls smsatSendReadLogExt, and if that does not return SM_RC_SUCCESS it frees the internal IO resource, sets satAbortAfterReset to agTRUE and returns; on success the recovery continues in the READ LOG EXT completion. If the drive is already not in the NORMAL state it only logs. On OSSA_IO_OPEN_CNX_ERROR_STP_RESOURCES_BUSY it takes the smIORequestBody from agIORequest->osData and returns if it, its smDevHandle or the device data is NULL; then, only if smAllShared->FCA is set, it does one SMP hard reset through smPhyControlSend when oneDeviceData->SMNumOfFCA is not positive (incrementing SMNumOfFCA) and otherwise only logs; with FCA clear it does nothing. All other events listed (command frame issued, PIO setup error, IT-nexus-loss variants, DEK key tag mismatch, NAK received, DMA activate timeout) and unknown events only log. It returns no value.

functions.name: smsatTestUnitReadyCB
functions.prose_contract: Completion callback for the internal ATA command (SAT_GET_MEDIA_STATUS or SAT_CHECK_POWER_MODE) that implements SCSI TEST UNIT READY; returns void. It marks the internal request ioCompleted and not ioStarted and finds the original request through satIntIo. If agIOStatus is OSSA_IO_ABORTED it completes the original request with tdsmIOCompletedCB(smIOFailed, smDetailAborted), decrements the pending IO count (smsatDecrementPendingIO), frees the internal IO resource and returns. If agFirstDword is NULL and the status is not success it sets NOT_READY sense, completes the original with SCSI_STAT_CHECK_CONDITION, decrements pending IO, frees the internal resource and returns. If the status is otherwise not success, a failure FIS is examined; an aborted status goes through smsatProcessAbort (not tdsmIOCompletedCB), and then per command: SAT_GET_MEDIA_STATUS sets NOT_READY sense (medium-not-present when the NM bit of the ATA error register is set), SAT_CHECK_POWER_MODE sets NOT_READY with logical-unit-does-not-respond, and any other command sets NOT_READY; each case completes the original with SCSI_STAT_CHECK_CONDITION via tdsmIOCompletedCB, decrements pending IO and frees the internal resource. On success: SAT_GET_MEDIA_STATUS decrements pending IO and frees the internal resource, allocates a new internal IO and issues smsatTestUnitReady_1 (SAT_CHECK_POWER_MODE); if the allocation fails (nothing new to free) it completes the original with CHECK_CONDITION and returns; if smsatTestUnitReady_1 does not return SM_RC_SUCCESS it frees the new internal IO and completes the original with CHECK_CONDITION; if it succeeds no completion is made here and the original stays pending for the next callback. SAT_CHECK_POWER_MODE success decrements pending IO, frees the internal resource and completes the original with SCSI_STAT_GOOD and no sense. Any other command on the success path completes the original with CHECK_CONDITION, decrements pending IO and frees the resource.

functions.name: smsatStartStopUnitCB
functions.prose_contract: Completion callback for the internal ATA command issued as part of SCSI START STOP UNIT (flush cache, standby, read verify sectors or media eject); returns void. It locates the original request through satIntIo (returning at 3395 on one early path) and then, if agFirstDword is NULL and the status is not success, sets ABORTED COMMAND sense (a deferred sense when the CDB IMMED bit is set, otherwise normal sense), completes the original with SCSI_STAT_CHECK_CONDITION and returns. For other non-success statuses it examines the failure FIS; an aborted status is handled separately (3500-3513) and returns; otherwise a per-command error switch (flush cache, standby, read verify sectors, media eject: ABORTED COMMAND sense, deferred when IMMED is set; default: NO_SENSE sense, not deferred and independent of IMMED) completes the original with CHECK_CONDITION, then returns. On success the command switch is: SAT_FLUSH_CACHE or SAT_FLUSH_CACHE_EXT decrements pending IO, frees satIntIo, allocates a new internal IO and sends a follow-up standby via smsatStartStopUnit_1; if allocation fails or the send does not return SM_RC_SUCCESS it sets ABORTED COMMAND sense (deferred when IMMED is set), completes the original with CHECK_CONDITION and returns (freeing the new IO when it was allocated and the send failed); if the send succeeds the original stays pending for the follow-up. SAT_STANDBY decrements pending IO, frees satIntIo, completes the original with SCSI_STAT_GOOD only when the IMMED bit is clear, and sets satStopState to agTRUE. SAT_READ_VERIFY_SECTORS(_EXT) does the same completion rule and sets satStopState to agFALSE. SAT_MEDIA_EJECT decrements pending IO, frees satIntIo and completes with GOOD only when IMMED is clear. Any other command sets NO_SENSE sense, completes with CHECK_CONDITION, decrements pending IO and frees satIntIo.

functions.name: ossaHwCB
functions.prose_contract: Hardware-event callback of the TISA layer (a very large switch on event); returns void. This description covers only the cases in the range read. OSSA_HW_EVENT_PHY_DOWN: decodes PhyID, link rate and PortState from eventParm1; if agPortContext is NULL it returns immediately; if agPortContext->osData is NULL it only logs; otherwise the tdsaPortContext_t from osData, if NULL, causes an immediate return, else it clears onePortContext->PhyIDList[PhyID], computes whether every phy of the port is down, and then by PortState: OSSA_PORT_VALID calls tdsaUpdateMCN(dmRoot, onePortContext) only when FDS_DM is compiled in and otherwise does nothing further; OSSA_PORT_LOSTCOMM and OSSA_PORT_IN_RESET record the event in tdsaAllShared->eventSource[PhyID] (EventValid agTRUE, port context, event, param), set onePortContext->eventPhyID and set valid to agFALSE; OSSA_PORT_INVALID does the same recording and additionally issues ostiPortEvent (tiPortStopped for the initiator driver, tiPortLinkDown for the target driver), calls tdssReportRemovals (initiator) or ttdssReportRemovals (target), and sets Ports[i].portContext to agNULL for each phy still flagged in PhyIDList. OSSA_HW_EVENT_PHY_START_STATUS only logs by status value. OSSA_HW_EVENT_PHY_STOP_STATUS with PhyStatus 0 takes the port context from the event parameters (immediate return if NULL), clears PhyIDList[PhyID] and, for PortState OSSA_PORT_INVALID, sets eventSource[PhyID].EventValid to NO_ACK, sets valid to agFALSE, issues the ostiPortEvent and removal calls and clears Ports[i].portContext as above; other PhyStatus values only log. OSSA_HW_EVENT_RESET_START and RESET_COMPLETE (in the range) act on new_status and, for RESET_COMPLETE, call ostiPortEvent. Other event types are handled by the rest of the function.

functions.name: tiCOMMgntIOCTL
functions.prose_contract: Management IOCTL dispatcher of the TISA layer; returns a bit32 status (IOCTL_CALL_SUCCESS, IOCTL_CALL_PENDING, IOCTL_CALL_FAIL, IOCTL_CALL_INVALID_CODE, IOCTL_CALL_INVALID_DEVICE or a handler's status) and also writes agIOCTLPayload->Status and Length. status starts as IOCTL_CALL_INVALID_CODE; if agIOCTLPayload->Signature is not PMC_IOCTL_SIGNATURE it returns IOCTL_CALL_INVALID_CODE at once. Otherwise it switches on MajorFunction. Cases visible in the range read: IOCTL_MJ_INI_DRIVER_IDENTIFY returns IOCTL_CALL_SUCCESS; IOCTL_MJ_GET_DEVICE_LUN returns IOCTL_CALL_PENDING when its handler returned success, otherwise the handler's value; IOCTL_MJ_GET_EVENT_LOG1/2 with IOCTL_MN_FW_GET_TRACE_BUFFER: when the log length is not greater than the offset it sets Status IOCTL_ERR_STATUS_NO_MORE_DATA (IOCTL_ERR_FW_EVENTLOG_DISABLED when the event log option is 0), Length 0 and returns IOCTL_CALL_SUCCESS immediately, otherwise it sets ReadLength = MIN(remaining, requested), Status OK and returns success; IOCTL_MJ_FW_INFO and IOCTL_MJ_GET_FW_REV with a requested length of 0 set NO_MORE_DATA and return success, else Status OK and success; IOCTL_MJ_GET_CORE_DUMP on non-SPC sets Status IOCTL_ERR_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED and success; IOCTL_MJ_GPIO returns IOCTL_CALL_INVALID_DEVICE for vendor id 0x9005, and otherwise IOCTL_CALL_PENDING when the setup succeeded or the setup's status when it did not; IOCTL_MJ_PHY_DETAILS fills the PhyDetails array and returns IOCTL_CALL_SUCCESS; IOCTL_MJ_PHY_GENERAL_STATUS returns IOCTL_CALL_FAIL when Length is smaller than agsaPhyGeneralState_t or when tdsaGetPhyGeneralStatusIoctl returns AGSA_RC_FAILURE, sets Status NOT_SUPPORTED and returns IOCTL_CALL_SUCCESS when it returns IOCTL_ERR_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED, else IOCTL_CALL_PENDING; IOCTL_MJ_LL_TRACING: reset-index and buffer-info set Status OK and return IOCTL_CALL_SUCCESS, IOCTL_MN_LL_GET_TRACE_BUFFER leaves the case without setting Status or status when the low fence or high fence check fails (status then keeps its current value, normally IOCTL_CALL_INVALID_CODE) and otherwise sets Status OK and success; IOCTL_MJ_PORT_START and IOCTL_MJ_PORT_STOP call tiCOMPortStart or tiCOMPortStop, set Status OK or IOCTL_ERR_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR and return IOCTL_CALL_SUCCESS; IOCTL_MJ_GET_DRIVER_VERSION sets Status OK and returns success. The default case sets Status to IOCTL_ERR_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED and returns the unchanged status, IOCTL_CALL_INVALID_CODE. The remaining major functions delegate to per-function handlers whose results become the return value.

functions.name: smHandleDirect
functions.prose_contract: Handles the identify data of a directly attached SATA device; returns void. Precondition: tiRoot, agRoot, oneDeviceData and IDdata (agsaSATAIdentifyData_t) are valid. It saves oneDeviceData->phyID, then walks tdsaAllShared->MainDeviceList; if an entry converts to a NULL device it returns immediately with nothing changed. It stops at the first entry whose DeviceType is TD_SATA_DEVICE and whose stored identify serialNumber (20 bytes), firmwareVersion (8 bytes) and modelNumber (40 bytes) all equal IDdata's. If such an existing record is found it sets that record's valid and valid2 to agTRUE, sets its agRoot to the agRoot parameter, takes over oneDeviceData's agDevHandle (setting agDevHandle->osData to the existing record), tdPortContext and phyID, calls saDeregisterDeviceHandle(agRoot, ...) on oneDeviceData->agDevHandle unconditionally, calls saRegisterNewDevice for the existing record only if its registered flag is agFALSE, fills oneDeviceData's stored identify data with 0xFF and moves oneDeviceData from MainDeviceList to tdsaAllShared->FreeDeviceList. If no record matches, oneDeviceData's identify data is set to a copy of *IDdata. In both cases it then calls ostiPortEvent(tiPortLinkUp, tiSuccess) on tdsaAllShared->Ports[PhyID].tiPortalContext, plus a tiPortDiscoveryReady event when INITIATOR_DRIVER is defined, and returns.

functions.name: tdsmIDCompletedCB
functions.prose_contract: Completion callback for the SATA identify-device request; returns void. It takes the tdIORequestBody from smIORequest->tdData and the device from smDeviceHandle. If smDeviceHandle is NULL it frees the request memory and returns without touching IDPending. Otherwise it clears oneDeviceData->satDevData.IDPending and kills the ID timer if it is running. It then returns after freeing the request memory (and for some paths reporting the device removed) in these early cases: NULL port context (frees only, no removal report); pid in the request differing from the port context id, and NULL portal context (both report removal directly or via smReportRemoval then free); NULL agRoot (frees only). For smIOSuccess it sets IDDeviceValid to agTRUE and, for a directly attached device, calls smHandleDirect and copies serial number, firmware version and model into onePortContext->remoteName, while for an expander-attached device it signals tiDeviceArrival through ostiInitiatorEvent when the port discovery state is ITD_DSTATE_COMPLETED; the request memory is then freed. For smIORetry: if the device is no longer valid, registered and attached to a port context it frees the request and sets IDDeviceValid to agFALSE; otherwise while reTries <= SM_RETRIES it restarts smIDStart: on failure it frees the request and calls smReportRemoval, on success it increments reTries, sets IDPending to agTRUE and re-arms the ID timer, keeping the request; when retries are exhausted it frees the request, clears IDDeviceValid and calls smReportRemoval. For smIOSTPResourceBusy it frees the request, clears IDDeviceValid, and when FCA is set and SMNumOfFCA is not positive increments SMNumOfFCA and sends an SMP hard reset, when FCA is set otherwise calls smReportRemoval, and when FCA is not set takes the remaining else branch (not checked beyond its control flow). For any other status it frees the request and returns if the device is not valid and registered; otherwise when tdsaAllShared->IDRetry is set and reTries <= SM_RETRIES it restarts smIDStart (failure: free, clear IDDeviceValid, report removal; success: reTries++, IDPending true, request retained), else it frees the request, clears IDDeviceValid, and either sends a hard reset (saLocalPhyControl for directly attached, tdsaPhyControlSend otherwise) once while SMNumOfID <= 0 or reports removal.

functions.name: itdssSMPCompleted
functions.prose_contract: SMP completion callback for the initiator discovery code (the TD_DISCOVER build; a second definition at 2044 for builds without TD_DISCOVER is a separate stub). Returns void. It takes the request body from agIORequest->osData, its device and port context, and decodes the SMP function of the original request (from the payload with DIRECT_SMP, else by reading the request header).
