If the device's port context is NULL, or the request's remembered old port context is NULL, it frees the request body (and, without DIRECT_SMP, the indirect request and response buffers) and returns. Otherwise it decrements onePortContext->discovery.pendingSMP; if the port context changed, or the port is no longer valid, it kills the discovery SMP timers for discovery functions, may clean up expanders, frees the bodies and returns. For a live port it stops the timers and dispatches on agIOStatus. OSSA_IO_SUCCESS: for report general, discover, report phy sata, configure routing, phy control and report manufacturer information, a response-length mismatch calls tdsaSASDiscoverDone or tdsaSATADiscoverDone(tiError), frees the bodies and returns; otherwise the matching handler (tdsaReportGeneralRespRcvd, tdsaDiscoverRespRcvd, tdsaConfigRoutingInfoRespRcvd, tdsaPhyControlRespRcvd, tdsaReportManInfoRespRcvd, SATA report) runs and the function falls through to the common tail; unlisted SMP functions do nothing. OSSA_IO_ABORTED and OSSA_IO_INVALID_LENGTH only log. OSSA_IO_ERROR_INTERNAL_SMP_RESOURCE resubmits with saSMPStart: success (pendingSMP++, timer for discovery functions) returns without freeing; busy starts tdsaSMPBusyTimer for discovery functions or calls tdsaPhyControlFailureRespRcvd for phy control; failure calls tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiError) for discovery functions or tdsaPhyControlFailureRespRcvd for phy control. Other statuses: while retries < SMP_RETRIES it marks the device operational for the nexus-loss statuses and calls saSMPStart again, increments pendingSMP and retries and returns without freeing; once retries are used up it handles non-operational and in-recovery states and reports discovery failure (tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiError)) for discovery functions, and for phy control handles the clear-affiliation and hard-reset operations. All other paths reach the tail that frees the request body and, without DIRECT_SMP, the indirect buffers, then returns.

functions.name: tdsaSASFullDiscover
functions.prose_contract: Starts a full SAS discovery on a port context; returns tiError or tiSuccess. If onePortContext->valid is agFALSE it calls tdsaSASDiscoverAbort and returns tiError. Otherwise it walks tdsaAllShared->MainDeviceList and, for each device whose tdPortContext is this port and only when onePortContext->nativeSATAMode and onePortContext->directAttatchedSAS are both agFALSE, sets valid and processed to agFALSE (so with a direct-attached SAS port or native SATA mode no device is invalidated). It sets onePortContext->DiscoveryState to ITD_DSTATE_STARTED. If nativeSATAMode is agFALSE it enables spin-up notification (saLocalPhyControl with AGSA_PHY_NOTIFY_ENABLE_SPINUP, TD_MAX_NUM_NOTIFY_SPINUP times) on the first phy flagged in PhyIDList, but only when the port's identify frame is a SAS end device with an SSP target; it then adds the directly attached device with tdsaPortSASDeviceAdd; if that returns a device that is not yet registered it starts tdsaDeviceRegistrationTimer, if it is registered it calls tdsaSASUpStreamDiscoverStart, and if the add returns NULL nothing more happens. If nativeSATAMode is agTRUE it calls tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiRoot, onePortContext, tiSuccess). In every non-abort path it returns tiSuccess.

functions.name: tdssReportRemovals
functions.prose_contract: Reports device removals for a port after a port event; returns void. Precondition: onePortContext->eventPhyID indexes tdsaAllShared->eventSource (the code reads eventSource[PhyID].EventValid before it tests PhyID != 0xFF). Behavior: if eventSource[PhyID].EventValid is agTRUE, onePortContext->RegisteredDevNums is 0 and PhyID is not 0xFF, it acknowledges the hardware event with saHwEventAck (only logging a non-success result) and clears EventValid; then if onePortContext->valid is agFALSE it moves every MainDeviceList device of this port to FreeDeviceList (filling its identify data with 0xFF, under TD_DEVICE_LOCK), reinitializes the port context with tdsaPortContextReInit and moves it from the main list to FreePortContextList under TD_PORT_LOCK; if valid is agTRUE (still inside that outer condition) it returns immediately if MainDeviceList is empty, and otherwise recycles those devices of this port that have valid, valid2 and registered all agFALSE into FreeDeviceList. When the outer condition is false none of that is done. After that, in all cases that did not return, it returns immediately if MainDeviceList is empty and otherwise visits every device of this port: for registered devices that are SSP, STP, SATA or SMP targets it calls tdsaAbortAll, for other registered devices it calls saDeregisterDeviceHandle, then it sets valid, valid2 and registered to agFALSE and NumOfFCA to 0 for every device of the port and, when flag is agTRUE, sets tdPortContext to agNULL; it records a removal when a device that was valid and registered is an SSP target, STP target or SATA device, and finally issues one ostiInitiatorEvent(tiIntrEventTypeDeviceChange, tiDeviceRemoval) for the port if any such removal was recorded. A NULL device object in the list returns immediately. TD_DEVICE_LOCK and TD_PORT_LOCK are released in each place they are taken.

functions.name: tdsaSASUpStreamDiscoverExpanderPhy
functions.prose_contract: Handles one SMP DISCOVER response for oneExpander->discoveringPhyId during upstream discovery; returns void. If onePortContext->valid is agFALSE it calls tdsaSASDiscoverAbort and returns. If pDiscoverResp->phyIdentifier differs from discoveringPhyId it calls tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiError) and returns, recording no error address. Otherwise it stores the response's routing attribute in oneExpander->routingAttribute[phyId]. If the expander's device is a fanout expander and the routing is subtractive it records the device's SAS address and phy id in onePortContext->discovery.sasAddressIDDiscoverError, calls tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiError) and returns; for a fanout expander with other routing nothing more happens in this step. For a non-fanout expander with an attached device and subtractive routing only: it adds the upstream phy (tdsaSASExpanderUpStreamPhyAdd); if hasUpStreamDevice was already set and the upstream address differs from the attached address it records the error address and calls tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiError); otherwise it sets hasUpStreamDevice and the upstream address, and when the attached address differs from the port's local address it looks the device up with tdsaPortSASDeviceFind: found as an edge expander gives either oneExpander->tdUpStreamExpander = that expander (upstream addresses consistent) or error-address recording plus tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiError); not found, it adds the device with tdsaPortSASDeviceAdd (STP type for STP target or SATA, otherwise SAS; in non-full-start discovery first looking for a registered valid one), and if that produced a device it allocates and queues an expander for an attached edge or fanout expander (setting tdUpStreamExpander, or tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiError) on allocation failure with no error address) or for an end device sets its expander link and clears tdUpStreamExpander, and if no device was produced it calls tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiError) with no error address. An edge expander with an attached device but non-subtractive routing, or with no attached device, only has its routing attribute stored. All paths that do not return early then increment discoveringPhyId; if discovery.status is DISCOVERY_UP_STREAM it either sends the next phy (tdsaDiscoverSend) or finishes the expander (adjacent update, tdssSASDiscoveringExpanderRemove, tdsaSASUpStreamDiscovering).

functions.name: tdsaSASDownStreamDiscoverExpanderPhy
functions.prose_contract: Handles one SMP DISCOVER response for oneExpander->discoveringPhyId during downstream discovery; returns void. If onePortContext->valid is agFALSE it calls tdsaSASDiscoverAbort and returns. It then calls tdsaFindUpStreamConfigurableExp and tdsaFindDownStreamConfigurableExp. If the response's phy id differs from discoveringPhyId it calls tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiError) and returns without recording an error address. Otherwise it stores the routing attribute in oneExpander->routingAttribute[phyId] and sets discoverSMPAllowed to agTRUE. With an attached device: direct routing to an attached expander records the error address and phy id in onePortContext->discovery.sasAddressIDDiscoverError, calls tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiError) and returns; otherwise, if the attached SAS address differs from the port's local address and the device is not yet known, subtractive routing to an attached expander records the error address and calls tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiError), and otherwise the device is added (STP or SAS type; in non-full-start discovery a registered valid one is reused first); for an added device, table routing to a fanout expander records the error address and calls tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiError), table routing to an edge expander allocates an expander and, if oneExpander->configRouteTable is set, sets up routing, with an allocation failure calling tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiError) without an error address; a failed device add also calls tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiError) without an error address. If the discovery status is still DISCOVERY_DOWN_STREAM it finds a configurable expander and, only when one exists and tdsaDuplicateConfigSASAddr does not report a duplicate, records its current downstream phy index and returning expander and adds a routing entry with tdsaSASRoutingEntryAdd; a duplicate address simply skips the routing entry (no error call). If the device was already known: subtractive routing with no upstream device recorded, or an upstream address mismatch, table routing to a fanout expander, and certain edge-expander upstream mismatches record the error address and call tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiError) without returning. Every path that did not return early then increments discoveringPhyId; if the status is still DISCOVERY_DOWN_STREAM it sends the next phy (tdsaDiscoverSend) when phys remain, otherwise it removes the expander from the discovering list and continues downstream discovery.

functions.name: tdsaConfigRoutingInfoRespRcvd
functions.prose_contract: Handles the response to an SMP CONFIGURE ROUTE INFORMATION request for an expander device; returns void. Precondition: oneDeviceData has a port context and a tdExpander; frameHeader holds the SMP response header. If onePortContext->valid is agFALSE it calls tdsaSASDiscoverAbort and returns. If frameHeader->smpFunctionResult is neither SMP_FUNCTION_ACCEPTED nor PHY_VACANT it calls tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiRoot, onePortContext, tiError). Otherwise it takes DownStreamExpander = oneExpander->tdCurrentDownStreamExpander; if that is non-NULL it increments its currentUpStreamPhyIndex; it increments oneExpander->currentDownStreamPhyIndex; then only if DownStreamExpander is non-NULL: if its currentUpStreamPhyIndex is below numOfUpStreamPhys it adds a routing entry (tdsaSASRoutingEntryAdd) for that upstream phy with oneExpander's configSASAddressHi/Lo, with no condition on oneExpander->tdUpStreamExpander; otherwise it looks up the upstream expander and a configurable expander and, if the upstream expander is non-NULL, checks for a duplicate configured SAS address: when a configurable expander exists and the address is not a duplicate it sets UpStreamExpander->tdCurrentDownStreamExpander to oneExpander, updates the configurable expander's currentDownStreamPhyIndex and sets its tdReturnginExpander to oneExpander->tdReturnginExpander, resets DownStreamExpander->currentUpStreamPhyIndex to 0 and adds a routing entry on the configurable expander's current downstream phy; otherwise it takes ReturningExpander = oneExpander->tdReturnginExpander, resets DownStreamExpander->currentUpStreamPhyIndex to 0 and, if ReturningExpander is non-NULL, sets discovery.status to DISCOVERY_DOWN_STREAM and, when the returning expander's discoveringPhyId is below its device's numOfPhys, calls tdsaDiscoverSend if its discoverSMPAllowed is agTRUE (then clearing it), else (all phys done) sets discoverSMPAllowed to agTRUE, removes it from the discovering list and calls tdsaSASDownStreamDiscovering. When DownStreamExpander or the upstream expander is NULL the corresponding branch does nothing (apart from the increments above). It then returns.

functions.name: tdsaSMPBusyTimerCB
functions.prose_contract: Timer callback that retries an SMP request after a busy indication; returns void. timerData1, timerData2 and timerData3 are the port context, the device data and the SMP request body. It starts with status = AGSA_RC_FAILURE, increments discovery->SMPRetries, and only if SMPRetries is still below SMP_BUSY_RETRIES calls saSMPStart for the request on tdsaAllShared->SMPQNum with ossaSMPCompleted as completion. Then: if status is AGSA_RC_SUCCESS it resets SMPRetries to 0 and kills discovery->SMPBusyTimer if running (discovery is not completed here); if status is AGSA_RC_FAILURE (including the case where no call was made because the retry limit was reached) it resets SMPRetries to 0, calls tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiRoot, onePortContext, tiError) and kills the busy timer if running; otherwise (AGSA_RC_BUSY from the call) it either, when SMPRetries is >= SMP_BUSY_RETRIES, resets SMPRetries, calls tdsaSASDiscoverDone(tiError) and kills the busy timer, or re-arms the busy timer through tdsaSMPBusyTimer. It returns nothing.

functions.name: ossaSATAEvent
functions.prose_contract: SATA event callback of the TISA initiator layer; defined only when FDS_SM is not defined (#ifndef FDS_SM at 10986). Returns void. Precondition for the NCQ path: agDevHandle and its osData point to valid device data (not checked). On OSSA_IO_XFER_ERROR_ABORTED_NCQ_MODE: if the device's satDriveState is SAT_DEV_STATE_NORMAL it sets it to SAT_DEV_STATE_IN_RECOVERY and allocates an internal IO resource for READ LOG EXT page 10h; if the allocation returns NULL it sets satAbortAfterReset to agTRUE and returns (the device reset is inside #ifdef NOT_YET and not compiled); otherwise it prepares the internal IO context and calls satSendReadLogExt; if that does not return tiSuccess it frees the internal IO resource, sets satAbortAfterReset to agTRUE and returns; on success the recovery continues in the READ LOG EXT completion. If the drive is not in the NORMAL state it only logs. For the other listed events (command frame issued, PIO setup error, IT-nexus-loss variants, DEK key tag mismatch, DIF mismatch with a frame read that returns early on a NULL agParam or too-short length) it only logs or reads the DIF details. For any other event it takes the request body from agIORequest->osData and, if the event is OSSA_IO_OPEN_CNX_ERROR_STP_RESOURCES_BUSY and tdsaAllShared->FCA is set, sends one SMP hard reset through tdsaPhyControlSend when NumOfFCA is not positive (incrementing it), else, when the device is registered and ResetInDiscovery is 0, aborts all IO on it (tdsaAbortAll), marks it invalid, not registered, and reports a device-removal event with ostiInitiatorEvent.

functions.name: satWriteSame10CB
functions.prose_contract: Completion callback of the ATA command used to emulate SCSI WRITE SAME(10) in pieces; returns void. It locates the original request: if satIntIo is NULL the request itself is the original; otherwise the original context comes from satIOContext->satOrgIOContext, and if that is NULL the function returns immediately, before marking the request body completed. It then sets tdIORequestBody->ioCompleted to agTRUE and ioStarted to agFALSE. If agFirstDword is NULL and agIOStatus is not OSSA_IO_SUCCESS it sets NO_SENSE/no-additional-info sense, completes the original with SCSI_STAT_CHECK_CONDITION through ostiInitiatorIOCompleted, decrements pending IO, frees the internal IO resource and returns. If agIOStatus is not success and the FIS type is not REG_DEV_TO_HOST or SET_DEV_BITS, or the ATA status has the ERR or DF bit set: an OSSA_IO_ABORTED status goes through satProcessAbort (the original is not completed by this function), otherwise the original is completed with CHECK_CONDITION and NO_SENSE sense; in both cases it then decrements pending IO, frees the internal IO resource and returns (the command-specific switch at 6197 only logs). Otherwise (success) it decrements pending IO and frees the internal IO resource, takes the LBA and transfer length from the original CDB, computes the sector count (a zero transfer length means up to 0x0FFFFFFF-1 minus lba), and, depending on how many sectors satSectorDone already covers, completes the original or allocates a new internal IO and issues the next satWriteSame10_1 for the next LBA range, completing the original with an error and returning if the allocation or issue fails.

functions.name: satLogSense
functions.prose_contract: SAT translation of SCSI LOG SENSE; returns tiSuccess (when it completes the request itself) or the status of the lower call it delegates to. With NACA or LINK set in cdb[9] it sets ILLEGAL REQUEST / INVALID FIELD IN CDB, completes with SCSI_STAT_CHECK_CONDITION and returns tiSuccess. AllocLen is computed as (bit8)((cdb[7] << 8) + cdb[8]), so only the low 8 bits of the allocation length are kept. When AllocLen is 4 it writes only a 4-byte page header into the caller's buffer for the supported-pages page (length 1, 2 or 3 depending on SMART support), the self-test-results page (length 0x190) or the information-exceptions page, without checking SMART support, and completes with SCSI_STAT_GOOD; any other page code completes with CHECK_CONDITION / INVALID FIELD IN CDB. For other allocation lengths: the supported-pages page writes the header and list (0x00, plus 0x10 when SMART is supported, plus 0x2F when SMART self-test is supported), copies MIN(AllocLen, list size) bytes, and completes with tiIOUnderRun and residual AllocLen - lenRead when AllocLen is larger, otherwise with SCSI_STAT_GOOD; the self-test-results page completes with CHECK_CONDITION / INVALID FIELD IN CDB when SMART self-test is not supported, otherwise returns satLogSenseAllocate's status (LOG_SENSE_0 when SMART is not enabled, with 512 bytes LOG_SENSE_1 when 48-bit addressing is supported, else LOG_SENSE_2); the information-exceptions page completes with INVALID FIELD IN CDB when the SMART feature set is absent, with ABORTED COMMAND / ATA DEVICE FEATURE NOT ENABLED when SMART is not enabled, and otherwise builds a SMART RETURN STATUS FIS, sets satCompleteCB to satLogSenseCB and returns sataLLIOStart's status; an unknown page code completes with CHECK_CONDITION / INVALID FIELD IN CDB. After the switch (for the paths that completed inline) it returns tiSuccess.

functions.name: satSendDiagnostic
functions.prose_contract: SAT translation of SCSI SEND DIAGNOSTIC; returns tiSuccess when it completes inline or the status of sataLLIOStart when it submits an ATA FIS. At entry it sets pSatDevData->satVerifyState to 0 and satBGPendingDiag to agFALSE. It completes with SCSI_STAT_CHECK_CONDITION and ILLEGAL REQUEST / INVALID FIELD IN CDB (returning tiSuccess) when the PF, DEVOFFL or UNITOFFL bit is set or the parameter list length bytes cdb[3] and cdb[4] are not both 0, when NACA or LINK is set in cdb[5], or when the self-test bit is clear and SMART self-test is not supported; it completes with CHECK_CONDITION and ABORTED COMMAND / ATA DEVICE FEATURE NOT ENABLED when the self-test bit is clear, SMART self-test is supported and SMART is not enabled. When the self-test bit is set and SMART self-test is unsupported, or supported but SMART not enabled, it builds a non-data READ VERIFY SECTORS (EXT form when 48-bit addressing is supported) FIS for one sector at LBA 0 and returns sataLLIOStart's status. When the self-test bit is set and SMART self-test and SMART are both enabled it builds a SMART EXECUTE OFF-LINE IMMEDIATE FIS and returns sataLLIOStart's status. When the self-test bit is clear and both SMART self-test and SMART are enabled it switches on the self-test code (cdb[1] bits >> 5): codes 1 and 2 set satBGPendingDiag to agTRUE, first complete the request with SCSI_STAT_GOOD through ostiInitiatorIOCompleted and then build and submit a SMART EXECUTE OFF-LINE IMMEDIATE FIS; code 4 completes with CHECK_CONDITION if the parameter length is nonzero or if no background test is pending, otherwise submits the FIS; codes 5 and 6 build and submit an FIS; other codes (0, 3, 7, default) fall out and complete with SCSI_STAT_GOOD, returning tiSuccess. The satCompleteCB for submitted FISes is satSendDiagnosticCB.

functions.name: agtiapi_EncryptionIoctl
functions.prose_contract: Handles an encryption-management ioctl for the card; returns IOCTL_CALL_SUCCESS or IOCTL_CALL_FAIL. Precondition: pCard and pIoctlPayload are valid; user blob pointers in the payload are user addresses. It first sets pIoctlPayload->hdr.Status to IOCTL_ERR_STATUS_INVALID_CODE, points pCard->ioctl_data at the payload body, reinitializes pCard->ioctl_completion and only prints a warning if encrypted IO is outstanding. It then switches on the minor function: GET_INFO, SET_MODE and DEK_INVALID call the corresponding tiCOMEncrypt* function and store its result in rc; KEK_ADD copies the KEK blob from user space (returning IOCTL_CALL_FAIL if access_ok or copy_from_user fails), calls tiCOMEncryptKekAdd, and if that returned tiSuccess records the KEK in the local table with agtiapi_AddKek (returning IOCTL_CALL_FAIL if that fails, after the chip was already updated); DEK_ADD copies the DEK blob, adds it to the local table (agtiapi_AddDek), maps it to its KEK (agtiapi_MapDekKek) and then calls tiCOMEncryptDekAdd, returning IOCTL_CALL_FAIL when a copy or local step fails (leaving earlier local updates in place); KEK_NVRAM sets rc to tiError; DEK_ASSIGN maps the DEKs locally (IOCTL_CALL_FAIL with Status INVALID_CODE on failure) and otherwise sets rc to tiSuccess, skip_wait to 1 and the body status to tiSuccess; ERROR_QUERY clears the query structure, and if no error events are queued and the query flag requests blocking it waits interruptibly (returning IOCTL_CALL_FAIL if interrupted); once events or the non-blocking flag allow it, it sets rc tiSuccess, skip_wait 1 and status tiSuccess; an unrecognized minor function sets Status INVALID_CODE and returns IOCTL_CALL_FAIL. After the switch: rc == tiSuccess waits for pCard->ioctl_completion unless skip_wait is set, then sets hdr.Status to ioctl_data->status; rc == tiNotSupported sets hdr.Status to IOCTL_ERR_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED with no wait; any other rc sets IOCTL_ERR_STATUS_INVALID_CODE with no wait; it then returns IOCTL_CALL_SUCCESS.

functions.name: ostiInitiatorEvent
functions.prose_contract: Initiator event callback of the FreeBSD adapter; returns void. It switches on eventType. CnxError, TransportRecovery and the default case only print a message. Discovery: sets AGTIAPI_CB_DONE in the card flags; for tiDiscOK it sets AGTIAPI_DISC_COMPLETE in the portal status and, unless AGTIAPI_INIT_TIME is set (the test is replaced by TRUE when HOTPLUG_SUPPORT is defined), calls agtiapi_GetDevHandle, sets AGTIAPI_DISC_DONE | AGTIAPI_PORT_LINK_UP and re-arms the IO_timer callout with agtiapi_CheckIOTimeout; for tiDiscFailed it calls agtiapi_GetDevHandle and clears AGTIAPI_DISC_DONE. DeviceChange: calls agtiapi_GetDevHandle unless AGTIAPI_INIT_TIME is set (without HOTPLUG_SUPPORT). TaskManagement: takes the ccb from ((tiIORequest_t *)parm)->osData; if TASK_TIMEOUT is set it frees the TM ccb with agtiapi_FreeTMCCB; otherwise it sets AGTIAPI_CB_DONE, for tiTMOK sets TASK_SUCCESS and, for a DEV_RESET ccb whose IO has not completed (startTime != 0), starts a local abort with tiINIIOAbort, and then frees the TM ccb (agtiapi_FreeTMCCB) whatever the event status. LocalAbort: takes the ccb from parm->osData and sets AGTIAPI_CB_DONE for every event status; for tiAbortOK with TASK_MANAGEMENT set it allocates a TM ccb (logging and skipping when none is available), marks it DEV_RESET and issues tiINITaskManagement(AG_TARGET_WARM_RESET), freeing the new TM ccb if that fails, and then frees the abort ccb; tiAbortOK without TASK_MANAGEMENT, and tiAbortFailed (which only logs), leave the abort ccb allocated.

functions.name: lp_intr
functions.prose_contract: Receive interrupt handler of the PLIP parallel-port network interface; returns void. Precondition: the caller holds the ppbus lock (asserted with ppb_assert_locked) and arg is the lp_data. It handles one received frame in one of two modes. With IFF_LINK0 set it reads length bytes and then the frame with clpinbyte; otherwise it reads nibbles while the LPIP_SHAKE status bit is set (if that bit is initially clear it returns after the loop without doing anything). A timeout, a bad or oversized length, a missing/short frame (not longer than the header) all go to the error label err. For a frame longer than the header it clears sc_iferrs, subtracts the header length and increments IFCOUNTER_IPACKETS by 1 and IFCOUNTER_IBYTES by the payload length, both before calling m_devget; if m_devget returns a mbuf it releases the ppbus lock, calls lptap, sets the FIB and queues the packet to netisr (NETISR_IP), then retakes the lock; if m_devget returns NULL nothing is queued, no error is counted, and the function still returns with the lock held. The err label writes 0 to the data register, increments IFCOUNTER_IERRORS and sc_iferrs, and when sc_iferrs exceeds LPMAXERRS prints a message, writes 0 to the control register, clears IFF_DRV_RUNNING and resets sc_iferrs to 0. The lock is held again on every return.

functions.name: ppb_peripheral_negociate
functions.prose_contract: Peripheral-side IEEE 1284 negotiation; returns 0 or an errno. Precondition: the caller holds the ppbus lock; mode is a mode ppb_request_mode accepts (another mode panics there). It sets the bus mode to PPB_COMPATIBLE and the 1284 state to PPB_PERIPHERAL_NEGOCIATION, computes request_mode, then spins up to 10 iterations (1 us delay each) while nBUSY is set. If the SELECT status line is not set or the spin ran out it sets error ENODEV and goes to the error label without calling ppb_1284_set_error. Otherwise it reads the data register r: if r equals the requested mode byte or NIBBLE_1284_NORMAL it drives the control lines; for NIBBLE_1284_NORMAL it calls ppb_1284_set_error(PPB_MODE_UNSUPPORTED) and takes the error label with EINVAL; for any other matching byte it sets the state to PPB_PERIPHERAL_IDLE, switches the ppbus mode to PPB_BYTE only when r is BYTE_1284_NORMAL (other accepted modes leave the mode at PPB_COMPATIBLE) and returns 0. If r matches neither, it drives the control lines, latches PPB_MODE_UNSUPPORTED through ppb_1284_set_error (recorded only if no error was already latched and the state is not already PPB_ERROR) and takes the error label with EINVAL. The error label calls ppb_peripheral_terminate(bus, PPB_WAIT) and returns the error code.

functions.name: ppb_1284_negociate
functions.prose_contract: Host-side IEEE 1284 negotiation; returns 0 or an errno. Precondition: bus is the ppbus device; mode is one of PPB_NIBBLE, PPB_PS2, PPB_ECP, PPB_EPP (another mode panics in ppb_request_mode, or in the final switch). It first terminates a peripheral-side negotiation if the state is at least PPB_PERIPHERAL_NEGOCIATION, terminates the 1284 link if the state is not PPB_FORWARD_IDLE, sets the bus mode to PPB_COMPATIBLE, resets the error to PPB_FORWARD_IDLE, writes the requested mode byte and drives the handshake lines. If the status-line wait for the peripheral's response fails it records PPB_NOT_IEEE1284 and returns ENODEV; if the nACK wait times out it records PPB_TIMEOUT and returns EBUSY; each of these goes through the error label, which calls ppb_1284_terminate and returns the code. If options has PPB_EXTENSIBILITY_LINK set it calls ppb_1284_terminate and returns 0 without entering any of the mode states below. Otherwise it checks the peripheral's answer lines (for NIBBLE and otherwise): a mismatch records PPB_MODE_UNSUPPORTED and returns ENODEV via the error label. On success it sets the state to PPB_REVERSE_IDLE for PPB_NIBBLE and PPB_PS2; for PPB_ECP it sets PPB_SETUP, drives the control lines and waits for the ECP status lines (a timeout records PPB_TIMEOUT and returns ENODEV via the error label), then sets PPB_ECP_FORWARD_IDLE; for PPB_EPP it sets PPB_EPP_IDLE. Finally it sets the bus mode to mode and returns 0.

functions.name: ppb_MS_microseq
functions.prose_contract: Interprets a ppbus microsequence; returns 0 or an errno. Precondition: the caller holds ppb->ppc_lock (mtx_assert). If ppb->ppb_owner is not dev it returns EACCES. Otherwise it loops over the microinstructions starting at msq: MS_OP_PUT or MS_OP_GET looks up the transfer description with mode2xfer; when it has no loop sequence, a PUT writes arg[1] bytes from arg[0] with PPBUS_WRITE and returns that call's error if nonzero, and a GET panics; when it has a loop sequence the function runs the internal init sequence and then the loop sequence by recursive calls, returning the error from either if nonzero. MS_OP_RET stores arg[0].i in *ret when ret is non-NULL and returns 0. Any other opcode is executed by PPBUS_EXEC_MICROSEQ on the parent bus, which may advance the instruction pointer, and a nonzero error is returned. It does not itself construct a sequence from an opcode (that is ppb_MS_exec).

functions.name: puc_bfe_attach
functions.prose_contract: Attach routine of the puc multi-port serial/parallel bus front end; returns 0 or an errno. It sets every BAR's b_rid to -1 and initialises the ioport, iomem and irq resource managers in turn; if one rman_init fails it finalises the ones already initialised and returns that error at once (before any allocation or the fail label). It then gives the rmans description strings, reads the port count with puc_config(PUC_CFG_GET_NPORTS) (a nonzero error is only KASSERTed, not returned), allocates the zeroed sc_port array with M_WAITOK, manages the irq region 1..nports, and runs puc_config(PUC_CFG_SETUP). For each port it sets p_nr, queries type, BAR rid (puc_get_bar returning NULL gives ENXIO), offset and length, tries to reserve the port's register range (a NULL p_rres is not an error: only when it is non-NULL is its bus handle and tag set from the BAR subregion), reserves an irq entry (NULL gives ENXIO), reads the clock and adds a child device, setting its ivars if the child was created. A failed rman_manage_region, puc_config call, puc_get_bar or irq reservation jumps to fail, which deletes the children, releases each port's p_rres and p_ires and each BAR resource, finalises the three rmans, frees their descriptions and the port array and returns the error. After the ports it reads PUC_CFG_GET_ILR (error goes to fail), allocates the shared IRQ resource and sets up the interrupt handler, first as a filter handler (setting sc_fastintr on success) and retrying as an MPSAFE ithread handler on failure; if the interrupt cannot be set up it releases the IRQ and, with no IRQ resource, sets sc_polled. It then probes and attaches each child that exists, deleting and clearing any child whose device_probe_and_attach fails, calls bus_teardown_intr if sc_serdevs is 0 (this call is not conditioned on sc_ires being non-NULL), and returns 0.

functions.name: LacSymKey_KeyGenSslTls_GenCommon
functions.prose_contract: Common path that builds and submits a QAT SSL3/TLS/HKDF key-derivation request; returns a CpaStatus. Parameters: instance handle, callback and its tag, lacCmdId (SSL3 derive, TLS v1.1/v1.2/v1.3 derive, HKDF extract/expand/label variants), the op data, hashAlgCipher and the output flat buffer. If pKeyGenCb is NULL it returns LacSymKey_SslTlsSync(...) (the synchronous wrapper) without doing anything else. Otherwise it takes a cookie from pService->lac_sym_cookie_pool: a NULL result gives CPA_STATUS_RESOURCE (after a log message) and the retry marker gives CPA_STATUS_RETRY (cookie set to NULL). With a cookie it stores the instance, callback, tag, op data and output pointers in it, builds a nested-mode hash setup (SSL3: SHA1 inner, MD5 outer and digest size of MD5 with empty prefixes; TLS v1.1 and v1.2 and the HKDF cases choose the hash and secret/label prefix lengths from the op data, handling a pre-master secret longer than the fixed maximum by computing the hash key through computeHashKey when precompute applies), initializes the content descriptor (LacSymQat_HashContentDescInit), and populates the request header, mid and footer for the selected protocol: SSL3 uses LacSymQat_KeySslRequestPopulate and KeySslKeyMaterialInputPopulate (a user-defined label whose virtual-to-physical translation is 0 sets CPA_STATUS_FAIL after a log message); TLS v1.1/1.2 use the hash-state, prefix/AAD and request-parameter helpers and LacSymQat_KeyTlsRequestPopulate (with the same label translation check giving CPA_STATUS_FAIL); HKDF extract/expand/label use the HKDF variants and a switch on hashAlgCipher for the cipher constants. A zero physical address of the output buffer sets CPA_STATUS_FAIL. If status is still CPA_STATUS_SUCCESS it writes the content descriptor header, common header and mid, and submits the message with icp_adf_transPutMsg on pService->trans_handle_sym_tx, taking its status. If the final status is not CPA_STATUS_SUCCESS and a cookie was obtained it frees the cookie with Lac_MemPoolEntryFree. It returns the status.

functions.name: check_accel_unit_config
functions.prose_contract: Validates the configured accelerator-unit split for a c4xxx device; static int, returns 0 or an errno. Parameters are the counts of cy, dc and inline accel units (u8). It reads the ADF_SERVICES_ENABLED value from the general section and returns EFAULT, without printing anything, if that read fails. It then splits the value into service tokens: each token that starts with the CY, SYM, ASYM, DC or INLINE service name ORs the matching service bit into a local service mask (for 'asym' only when num_inline_au is less than the total number of units, so 'asym;inline' with all units inline does not set the crypto bit) and ORs in the result of check_svc_to_hw_capabilities, which prints a message and returns EPERM when the hardware lacks the capability; tokens that match none of these names are ignored. If any capability check failed it prints a message and returns EFAULT. It then returns EFAULT (with printed messages) if dc units are configured but the compression bit is not in the mask, if cy units are configured but the crypto bit is not, or if inline units are configured but the inline bit is not. After those three checks pass it stores the mask in hw_data->service_mask; the later checks can still return EFAULT after that store: the sum of the three unit counts differing from get_num_accel_units, or a zero cy, dc or inline unit count when the corresponding service bit is set (messages printed). Otherwise it returns 0.

functions.name: ecore_hw_lock
functions.prose_contract: Takes a hardware resource lock through the PF's lock register; returns an ecore status. Parameters: p_hwfn, p_ptt, resource (bit mask) and block. The lock register address is MISCS_REG_DRIVER_CONTROL_0 plus rel_pf_id times the register size. It reads the register; if the resource bit is already set it logs a notice and returns ECORE_BUSY without writing a request. Otherwise it writes the resource to the register at +4 bytes (the lock request) and polls the register up to HW_LOCK_MAX_RETRIES times: if the resource bit is set it returns ECORE_SUCCESS immediately, leaving the request in place, so the lock is held; if the bit is not set and block is false it sets ECORE_BUSY and leaves the loop after the first poll; otherwise it sleeps 5 ms and polls again. If the loop ran to HW_LOCK_MAX_RETRIES it logs a notice and sets ECORE_TIMEOUT. After a non-success loop exit (non-blocking miss or timeout) it writes the resource to the register at the base address (clearing the pending request) and returns the saved status (ECORE_BUSY or ECORE_TIMEOUT).

functions.name: ecore_iwarp_mpa_complete
functions.prose_contract: Handles the firmware's MPA handshake completion for an iWARP endpoint; static void. Precondition: ep is valid; on RDMA_RETURN_OK ep->qp is used and so must be non-NULL. It sets params.event to ECORE_IWARP_EVENT_ACTIVE_COMPLETE for an active endpoint and ECORE_IWARP_EVENT_PASSIVE_COMPLETE otherwise; for an active endpoint whose mpa_reply_processed is false it parses the private data first; it sets params.cm_info to &ep->cm_info and params.ep_context to ep. A passive endpoint whose state is not ECORE_IWARP_EP_MPA_OFFLOADED logs an error, has its state set to ECORE_IWARP_EP_CLOSED and returns with no callback and no further cleanup; a passive endpoint whose state is ECORE_IWARP_EP_ABORTING returns at once with its state unchanged and no callback. Otherwise it sets ep->state to ECORE_IWARP_EP_CLOSED and switches on fw_return_code: RDMA_RETURN_OK copies cm_info.ord and ird into the QP's max_rd_atomic_req and max_rd_atomic_resp, moves the QP to RTS with ecore_iwarp_modify_qp, sets ep->state to ECORE_IWARP_EP_ESTABLISHED and params.status to ECORE_SUCCESS; MPA timeout gives ECORE_TIMEOUT; reject, FIN, insufficient IRD, RTR mismatch, invalid packet, local error and terminate give ECORE_CONN_REFUSED; MPA reset and any other code give ECORE_CONN_RESET. It then calls ep->event_cb(ep->cb_context, &params) if it is non-NULL. For a non-OK fw_return_code it sets ep->tcp_cid to ECORE_IWARP_INVALID_TCP_CID and then either, for a passive endpoint with no QP, returns the endpoint with ecore_iwarp_return_ep, or removes the endpoint's list entry from the iWARP ep_list while holding iw_lock (spin lock, released after the removal).

functions.name: ecore_ll2_acquire_connection
functions.prose_contract: Acquires a free LL2 connection slot and sets it up; returns an ecore status. Precondition: cxt is the ecore_hwfn and data points to a valid acquire-data structure. It returns ECORE_INVAL, with no side effects, if data->p_connection_handle is NULL or p_hwfn->p_ll2_info is NULL. It scans the slots 0..ECORE_MAX_NUM_OF_LL2_CONNECTIONS-1, taking each slot's mutex around the test, and marks the first slot with b_active clear as active; if all are active it logs and returns ECORE_BUSY. It copies data->input into the slot; for a tx_dest value other than NW, LB or DROP it returns ECORE_INVAL at that point, leaving the slot marked active (it is not released). Otherwise it translates tx_dest, sets main_func_queue to false for the OOO connection type or a secondary queue and true otherwise, defaults tx_max_bds_per_packet to CORE_LL2_TX_MAX_BDS_PER_PACKET when 0 and clamps it to that value otherwise, then installs the callbacks, acquires the Rx, Tx and OOO resources in that order (each failing step logs and goes to q_allocate_fail). It registers the Rx and Tx completion callbacks (the OOO ones for the OOO type) with ecore_int_register_cb when rx_num_desc or tx_num_desc is nonzero, stores the slot index in *data->p_connection_handle and returns the final rc, which is ECORE_SUCCESS at that point. q_allocate_fail calls ecore_ll2_release_connection for the slot and returns ECORE_NOMEM regardless of which step failed. No slot mutex is held at return.

functions.name: qlnx_tpa_start
functions.prose_contract: Handles a TPA (LRO) start completion on a receive queue; returns void. Precondition: cqe is a TPA start CQE for rxq and the ring slots used below hold posted buffers. If cqe->tpa_agg_index is >= ETH_TPA_MAX_AGGS_NUM it increments fp->err_rx_tpa_invalid_agg_num and returns with the rings untouched. Otherwise it syncs and takes the mbuf mp at sw_rx_ring[sw_rx_cons]. If mp is NULL it increments err_rx_mp_null, advances sw_rx_cons by one and returns without changing agg_state. If the CQE parse flags carry CQE_FLAGS_ERR it increments err_rx_hw_errors, reuses the buffer with qlnx_reuse_rx_data, increments IERRORS and returns. If qlnx_alloc_rx_buffer fails it increments err_rx_alloc_errors and IQDROPS, swaps the current buffer into tpa_info[agg_index].rx_buf and the old tpa buffer into the ring slot at sw_rx_prod, produces and consumes one rx BD, reuses a slot for each nonzero entry of ext_bd_len_list, sets agg_state to QLNX_AGG_STATE_ERROR and returns. If tpa_info[agg_index].agg_state is not QLNX_AGG_STATE_NONE it increments IQDROPS, frees a previously stored mpf chain, stores mp as mpf with mpl NULL, advances the ring, reuses a slot per nonzero ext_bd_len_list entry, sets agg_state to QLNX_AGG_STATE_ERROR and returns. Otherwise it consumes the rx BD, then for each nonzero ext_bd_len_list entry takes the next ring mbuf (a NULL mbuf or a failed refill frees the chain built so far, sets agg_state to QLNX_AGG_STATE_ERROR and skips that entry) and chains the good ones. If agg_state is still not QLNX_AGG_STATE_NONE at that point it increments IQDROPS, stores mp as mpf (mpl NULL) and returns. Otherwise it records placement_offset, sets mp's length and links the extension chain (mpf = mp with mpl the chain tail, or mp alone), sets M_PKTHDR, rcvif, flowid = rss_hash and the hash type (RSS IPv4, TCP IPv4, IPv6, TCP IPv6, otherwise M_HASHTYPE_OPAQUE), csum_flags CSUM_IP_CHECKED|CSUM_IP_VALID|CSUM_DATA_VALID|CSUM_PSEUDO_HDR with csum_data 0xFFFF, the VLAN tag and M_VLANTAG when the CQE has one, sets agg_state to QLNX_AGG_STATE_START and returns.

functions.name: qla_sec_to_hz
functions.prose_contract: Static inline helper in qla_os.h that converts a number of seconds into scheduler ticks; returns int. It builds a struct timeval with tv_sec = sec and tv_usec = 0 and returns tvtohz() of it. By the kernel's tvtohz: a negative sec gives 1; a value at or above tick_seconds_max gives INT_MAX; otherwise the result is the tick count for that time plus one (so sec == 0 gives 1, not 0). It takes no locks and touches no other state.

functions.name: ql_parse_template
functions.prose_contract: Walks the firmware minidump template and captures each entry into the minidump buffer; static int that returns 0. It reads the template header from ha->hw.mdump_template and records sane_start when the header entry_type is TLHDR. It sets template_hdr->saved_state_array[QL_OCM0_ADDR_INDX] to the template's own ocm_window_array[ha->pci_func] (the template header's array, not ha->hw), saved_state_array[QL_PCIE_FUNC_INDX] to ha->pci_func and template_hdr->driver_capture_mask to ha->hw.mdump_capture_mask. It then visits num_of_entries entries starting at first_entry_offset, advancing by each entry's entry_size: an entry whose entry_capture_mask does not intersect the capture mask gets QL_DBG_SKIPPED_FLAG in driver_flags and is skipped; an entry whose entry_capture_size is nonzero and would not fit in the remaining buffer (buff_level + size > hw.mdump_buffer_size) is flagged skipped and skipped. Otherwise by entry_type: RDNOP does nothing; RDEND increments sane_end; RDCRB, POLLRD, POLLRDMWR, L1DAT/L1INS, RDOCM, RDMEM, BOARD/RDROM, RDMUX, RDMUX2 and QUEUE call their read helper to write into mdump_buffer at buff_level, then apply ql_entry_err_chk and advance buff_level by the returned size; L2ITG/L2DTG/L2DAT/L2INS call ql_L2Cache and, if it returns -1, flag the entry skipped without advancing, otherwise handle it like the other read helpers; CNTRL calls ql_cntrl and flags the entry skipped when it returns nonzero; unrecognized types are flagged skipped. After the walk it prints a 'Template configuration error' message with device_printf if sane_start is 0 or sane_end is greater than 1, and then returns 0 (its only return statement).

functions.name: qls_mbx_cmd
functions.prose_contract: Sends a mailbox command to the QLogic 8100-series MPI and waits for the reply; returns 0 or nonzero (-1 or a register-access error). ret starts as -1. It reads Q81_CTL_HOST_CMD_STATUS and, if the HTR interrupt bit is set, prints a message and goes to the exit with -1. It then takes the NIC-receive process-address semaphore with qls_sem_lock (failure prints a message and exits with -1 without unlocking), clears mbx_done, writes the i_count command words through qls_mbx_wr_reg (a failed write prints, releases the semaphore and exits with that nonzero error), sets the host-to-RISC interrupt bit, releases the semaphore, sets ret to -1 and clears mbx_done again. It then polls up to 50 iterations. With interrupts disabled (ha->flags.intr_enable == 0) each iteration checks the PI bit in Q81_CTL_STATUS (if clear it sleeps 100 ms and continues); otherwise it reads mailbox register 0: a value with high nibble 0x4000 is a command response, stored in out_mbx[0] with out_mbx[1..o_count-1] read with qls_mbx_rd_reg (a failed read prints and leaves its nonzero error in ret) and the loop is left; a value with nibble 0x8000 is an asynchronous event: the poll count is reset to 50 and the RTH interrupt is cleared; any other nibble just continues polling. With interrupts enabled it checks ha->mbx_done each iteration and, when set, copies ha->mbox[1..o_count-1] into out_mbx[1..o_count-1] (out_mbx[0] is not written), sets ret to 0 and leaves the loop. After each iteration that does not exit it sleeps 1000 ms. If the polling ends by exhaustion, ret holds the last status assigned, so it may be 0 (a register read that succeeded with an unrecognised nibble or after an event) with out_mbx not filled, or -1. At the exit label, when interrupts are disabled it clears the RTH interrupt, and when ret is nonzero it sets ha->qla_initiate_recovery to 1; it returns ret.

functions.name: rt2560_prio_intr
functions.prose_contract: Handles completed entries of the rt2560 priority (management) transmit ring; static void, called from the interrupt path with the softc lock held by the caller (the function itself neither takes nor releases it). It first syncs the descriptor map for POSTREAD, then loops from sc->prioq.next: it stops at the first descriptor whose RT2560_TX_BUSY flag is set or whose RT2560_TX_VALID flag is clear. For each finished entry it prints a debug message for success, success-after-retry and too-many-retries results (DPRINTFN only), and uses device_printf for RT2560_TX_FAIL_INVALID, RT2560_TX_FAIL_OTHER and any other result; it syncs the data map POSTWRITE and unloads it, takes the mbuf and node out of the entry (setting data->m and data->ni to NULL), clears RT2560_TX_VALID in the descriptor, decrements prioq.queued, advances prioq.next modulo RT2560_PRIO_RING_COUNT, calls ieee80211_process_callback with the failure bits when the mbuf has M_TXCB set, frees the mbuf with m_freem and releases the node with ieee80211_free_node. After the loop it syncs the descriptor map for PREWRITE, sets sc->sc_tx_timer to 0 when both prioq.queued and txq.queued are 0, and calls rt2560_start(sc) when prioq.queued is below RT2560_PRIO_RING_COUNT. Returns void.

functions.name: rt2860_init_locked
functions.prose_contract: Brings up an rt2860 wireless device; static void. Precondition: the caller holds the RAL lock (RAL_LOCK_ASSERT; the function neither takes nor releases it). If the board has a hardware radio switch that reads off, it only prints a message (the stop-and-return is under #ifdef notyet). It disables DMA, resets DMA indexes and the PBF, loads the 8051 microcode with rt2860_load_microcode and, if that fails, prints a message, calls rt2860_stop_locked and returns. It then writes per-rate TX power registers, waits up to 100 ms for the TX/RX DMA busy bits to clear (timeout: rt2860_stop_locked and return), programs the default MAC registers, sets RT2860_PCIE in sc->sc_flags when the PCI_CFG register shows a non-PCI bus, waits for the MAC to become ready (timeout: rt2860_stop_locked and return), calls rt2860_bbp_init (nonzero: rt2860_stop_locked and return), waits for DMA idle again (timeout: stop and return), initializes RF with rt5390_rf_init for mac_ver >= 0x5390 or rt3090_rf_init for mac_ver >= 0x3071 (a nonzero return from rt3090_rf_init: stop and return), configures antenna chains, then calls rt2860_txrx_enable (nonzero: stop and return). On the success path it clears pending interrupts, sets INT_MASK to 0x3fffc, sends the power-save level command when RT2860_ADVANCED_PS is set, sets RT2860_RUNNING in sc_flags and arms the watchdog callout (hz ticks, rt2860_watchdog); on each failure path above RT2860_RUNNING is not set and the watchdog is not armed.

functions.name: fxrng_event_processor
functions.prose_contract: Mixes one harvested entropy event into the FenestrasX pools; void. Precondition: event->he_size <= sizeof(he_entropy) (ASSERT_DEBUG only). first_time is true when he_size > 0 and this is the first observation of the source (atomic test-and-set of its bit in fxrng_seen). On first_time it takes FXENT_LOCK and the root BRNG lock; if the root BRNG generation is greater than 0 it releases FXENT_LOCK and calls fxrng_brng_src_reseed(event), which handles the BRNG lock, and returns; otherwise it unlocks the BRNG, hashes the event counter and entropy into pool 0, for a high-quality source adds he_size to fxrng_preseed_ent only if the addition would not overflow ULONG_MAX (it skips the addition on overflow rather than saturating), releases FXENT_LOCK and returns. Otherwise it evaluates first_32: he_size > 0, the source is high quality, more than one pool is active and the source's pool-0 eligibility check passes. If first_32 it takes FXENT_LOCK; if the source has already given FXENT_HI_SRC_POOL0_BYTES bytes it goes to the round-robin step, else it computes rem = MIN(remaining budget, he_size), adds rem to fxrng_reseed_seen[src], hashes the last rem bytes of the entropy into pool 0, and if rem equals he_size also hashes the counter, releases the lock and returns; otherwise it reduces he_size by rem and goes to round robin. If not first_32 it takes FXENT_LOCK. Round robin: it picks pool = he_destination % fxent_nactpools, hashes the entropy (he_size bytes) and the counter into it, and for a high-quality source while the root generation is still 0 adds he_size to fxrng_preseed_ent with the same overflow guard, then releases FXENT_LOCK and returns. Events with he_size == 0 skip the first-time and pool-0 branches (both require he_size > 0).

functions.name: rtsx_mmcbr_update_ios
functions.prose_contract: Applies the cached MMC ios settings to the Realtek card reader; returns 0 or the first nonzero error. Each ios cache field rtsx_ios_bus_width, power_mode, timing, clock and vccq is negative when its value still has to be applied. In this order: if rtsx_ios_bus_width < 0 it stores ios->bus_width in the cache and calls rtsx_set_bus_width, returning its error if nonzero; if rtsx_ios_power_mode < 0 it stores ios->power_mode and calls rtsx_bus_power_off for power_off or rtsx_bus_power_on for power_up and power_on, returning its error if nonzero; then, whether or not the previous steps ran, it sets sc->rtsx_double_clk to true and sc->rtsx_vpclk to false (these two assignments are skipped when the bus-width or power-mode step returned an error); then timing (rtsx_set_sd_timing), clock (rtsx_set_sd_clock) and vccq (rtsx_mmcbr_switch_vccq) in the same pattern. Each cache field is updated before its hardware call, so a failing step returns its error with the cache already marked as applied and the later steps are not run. If no step fails it returns 0.

functions.name: rtwn_newstate
functions.prose_contract: net80211 state-change method for an rtwn vap; static int. Precondition: the caller holds the net80211 com lock (IEEE80211_LOCK(ic)) on entry. If vap->iv_bss->ni_chan is IEEE80211_CHAN_ANYC and the transition is INIT to RUN, it first calls uvp->newstate(vap, nstate, arg) and returns its error at once if nonzero (com lock still held), else remembers early_newstate = 1. If the old state is IEEE80211_S_CSA it cancels the CSA beacon timeout task and clears vap->iv_csa_count (before the com lock is released). It then releases the com lock and takes the driver lock. If leaving CSA it writes 0 to R92C_TXPAUSE (unblocking Tx queues). If the old state is CSA, or the old state is RUN and the new state is not CSA, it decrements sc->vaps_running, sets the port to NOLINK, stops the IBSS TSF-sync callout for IBSS vaps, disables beaconing and station beacon, resets the TSF unless uvp->id == 0 with monitor vaps running, stops the power-mode init callout and sets power mode 0 for port 0 when IEEE80211_C_PMGT is set (without RTWN_WITHOUT_UCODE), recalculates basic rates when non-monitor vaps remain, and when vaps_running equals monvaps_running stops calibration, zeroes the Rx filter maps and resets EDCA parameters, turning the link LED off only when vaps_running is 0. A RUN-to-CSA transition does not decrement vaps_running. It then handles the new state: IEEE80211_S_SCAN with no vaps running pauses the AC Tx queue; IEEE80211_S_RUN calls rtwn_run, printing a message and keeping the error on failure, and incrementing vaps_running on success; IEEE80211_S_CSA pauses the AC, MGT and HIGH Tx queues. It releases the driver lock and retakes the com lock, returns the error if rtwn_run failed, and otherwise returns 0 when the early path already ran uvp->newstate, else uvp->newstate(vap, nstate, arg).

functions.name: r12a_handle_c2h_report
functions.prose_contract: Handles a C2H (firmware-to-host) report for the RTL8812A in builds with the microcode support (RTWN_WITHOUT_UCODE not defined; in the other build the function only prints a 'called' message). Precondition: buf points at the start of an Rx descriptor (struct r92c_rx_stat) and len is the total length of the buffer; sc->sc_priv is an r12a_softc. It skips the Rx descriptor (buf += sizeof(struct r92c_rx_stat), len -= the same). If fewer than 2 bytes remain it prints a 'C2H report too short' message and returns. Otherwise it subtracts 2 from len and switches on buf[0] (the command id): R12A_C2H_TX_REPORT hits KASSERT(0) (only effective with INVARIANTS; otherwise nothing further), R12A_C2H_IQK_FINISHED clears R12A_IQK_RUNNING in rs->rs_flags, and any other id prints a 'was not handled' message. Returns void.

functions.name: r12au_attach
functions.prose_contract: USB attach hook for the RTL8812AU; static void. It takes sc = &uc->uc_sc and sets uc->uc_align_rx to r12au_align_rx and uc->tx_agg_desc_num to 1; sets sc->sc_flags to RTWN_FLAG_EXT_HDR (replacing, not OR-ing); fills the softc's operation hooks (channel, Tx descriptor, radiotap, RSSI, interrupt classification, Tx and C2H report handlers, ROM parsing, power on and off, LLT, calibration, beacon, temperature, aggregation, EDCA, BB/RF init, antenna selection and so on) with r12a_*, r88e_*, r92c_*, r12au_* or rtwn_nop_* functions, with the firmware reset, download-enable and power-mode or media-status hooks chosen by whether RTWN_WITHOUT_UCODE is defined; and sets the chip data: the three 5 GHz channel lists and counts, the MAC, BB, AGC and RF programming tables (rtl8812au_*), name 'RTL8812AU', fwname 'rtwn-rtl8812aufw', fwsig 0x950, page and packet-buffer counts, page size, ack timeout 0x80, Tx descriptor length, efuse and Rx DMA sizes, MACID, CAM and firmware size limits, temperature delta, beacon status registers, RCR flags, two Tx and two Rx chains and sc_ht40 = 1. It finishes by calling r12a_attach_private(sc), whose result is not checked, and returns nothing.

functions.name: safe_attach
functions.prose_contract: Attach routine of the safe(4) crypto accelerator driver; returns 0 or ENXIO. It maps the register BAR (sc_sr, sc_st, sc_sh), allocates and sets up the shared IRQ with safe_intr as MPSAFE handler, obtains a crypto driver id (sc_cid), creates two DMA tags (sc_srcdmat, sc_dstdmat), allocates the packet-engine ring (sc_ring, sc_ringtop, sc_front, sc_back; zeroed, with sc_ringmtx initialized), the source and destination particle rings (sc_spring/sc_spfree and sc_dpring/sc_dpfree; zeroed), prints the chip's capabilities, resets and initializes the board (safe_reset_board, safe_init_pciregs, safe_init_board), and, when SAFE_NO_RNG is not defined and the chip reports SAFE_DEVINFO_RNG, sets SAFE_FLAGS_RNG, installs the harvest function, calls safe_rng_init and arms the sc_rngto callout. It then logs a deprecation notice and returns 0. Failures print a message and return ENXIO: no register BAR (bad), IRQ not allocated (bad1), interrupt not established (bad2), no driver id (bad3), DMA tag creation or ring allocation failure (bad4). The labels unwind in order: bad4 crypto_unregister_all, bad3 bus_teardown_intr, bad2 releases the IRQ, bad1 releases the memory BAR. The failure paths do not free all DMA tags: a failed destination-tag creation leaves sc_srcdmat created; a failed ring allocation or source-particle allocation destroys sc_srcdmat but not sc_dstdmat; a failed destination-particle allocation destroys sc_dstdmat but not sc_srcdmat; the ring and particle allocations made before the failing step are freed and sc_ringmtx destroyed where those steps are reached.

functions.name: sdhci_card_task
functions.prose_contract: Taskqueue handler that reconciles the slot's registered card state with the card-detect state; static void. Precondition: arg is a struct sdhci_slot *; pending is unused. It takes the slot lock, then tests whether a card is present with SDHCI_GET_CARD_PRESENT(slot->bus, slot). If a card is present and none is registered (MMCCAM: card_present == 0; otherwise slot->dev == NULL): with MMCCAM it sets card_present to 1, starts discovery with mmccam_start_discovery and unlocks the slot; otherwise it unlocks the slot, takes the bus topology lock, sets slot->dev to the result of device_add_child(slot->bus, 'mmc', DEVICE_UNIT_ANY) and only if that is non-NULL sets the slot as ivars and calls device_probe_and_attach (result ignored), then releases the topology lock. If no card is present and one is registered: with MMCCAM it sets card_present to 0, restarts discovery and unlocks; otherwise it sets slot->dev to NULL, removes the tuning bits from intmask and writes it to SDHCI_INT_ENABLE and SDHCI_SIGNAL_ENABLE, clears SDHCI_TUNING_ENABLED, unlocks the slot, drains the retune callout and deletes the child device under the bus topology lock. In the remaining cases (no state change) it just unlocks the slot. The slot lock is released on each of these paths. Returns void.

functions.name: sdhci_fdt_gpio_get_readonly
functions.prose_contract: Returns whether the SD slot is write protected according to the FDT-described write-protect GPIO; int result. If gpio->wp_disabled is set it returns false. If gpio->wp_pin is NULL it returns the value of sdhci_generic_get_ro(gpio->slot->bus, gpio->slot->dev). Otherwise it calls gpio_pin_is_active(gpio->wp_pin, &pinstate), ignoring its return value, and returns pinstate XOR gpio->wp_inverted (so pinstate is used even if the GPIO call failed and left it unset). It takes no locks.

functions.name: ef10_ev_rx_packed_stream
functions.prose_contract: Handles one packed-stream (or equal-stride super-buffer) Rx event; static boolean_t returning the callback's abort flag. It extracts the low bits of the global packet counter, the queue label and the ROTATE (new buffer) bit, and selects eersp = &eep->ee_rxq_state[label]. It computes pkt_count as (pkt_count_lbits - eers_rx_stream_npackets) masked with the ESF_DZ_RX_DSC_PTR_LBITS field mask and adds it to eers_rx_stream_npackets. If the event has the new-buffer bit it sets EFX_PKT_PACKED_STREAM_NEW_BUFFER in flags, increments eers_rx_packed_stream_credits only when EFSYS_OPT_RX_PACKED_STREAM is compiled in, and increments eers_rx_read_ptr. current_id is eers_rx_read_ptr masked with eers_rx_mask. A truncation error or an Ethernet CRC error counts the matching statistic, sets EFX_DISCARD and delivers; an incomplete parse sets EFX_PKT_PACKED_STREAM_PARSE_INCOMPLETE and delivers; otherwise IPv4 header and TCP/UDP checksum errors only count statistics. At deliver it counts EV_RX_OK when EFX_DISCARD is not set, asserts eecp->eec_rx_ps is non-NULL (EFSYS_ASSERT), calls eecp->eec_rx_ps(arg, label, current_id, pkt_count, flags) and returns its result.

functions.name: ef10_ev_rx
functions.prose_contract: Handles a regular EF10 Rx completion event; static boolean_t returning whether the event loop should abort. It counts EV_RX and returns B_FALSE at once, without calling the Rx callback, if enp->en_reset_flags has EFX_RESET_RXQ_ERR, EFX_RESET_TXQ_ERR or EFX_RESET_HW_UNAVAIL. It takes the queue label and eersp = &eep->ee_rxq_state[label]. When packed-stream or super-buffer support is compiled in and eersp->eers_rx_packed_stream is set it returns ef10_ev_rx_packed_stream(...) before any other decoding (so the drop-event check below does not apply to those queues). Otherwise it decodes the byte count, continuation bit, descriptor-pointer low bits and the ethernet/L3/L4 classes; if ESF_DZ_RX_DROP_EVENT is set it returns B_FALSE (no callback). It sets EFX_PKT_CONT for a continued event and EFX_PKT_UNICAST for a unicast MAC class, advances eers_rx_read_ptr by the number of descriptors consumed (modulo the LBITS mask) and, when more than one descriptor was consumed, counts EV_RX_BATCH and sets EFX_PKT_PREFIX_LEN. last_used_id is (read_ptr - 1) & eers_rx_mask. A truncation error or CRC error counts the statistic, sets EFX_DISCARD and delivers; an incomplete hardware parse delivers without further classification; otherwise it sets EFX_PKT_VLAN_TAGGED for VLAN tag classes, classifies IPv4 and IPv6 (setting EFX_PKT_IPV4/IPV6, EFX_CKSUM_IPV4 when the IP checksum is good, EFX_PKT_TCP or EFX_PKT_UDP from the L4 class, and counting statistics) and sets EFX_CKSUM_TCPUDP for TCP or UDP without a checksum error. At deliver it counts EV_RX_OK when not discarded, asserts eecp->eec_rx is non-NULL and returns the result of eecp->eec_rx(arg, label, last_used_id, size, flags).

functions.name: ef10_filter_reconfigure
functions.prose_contract: Reconfigures all EF10 unicast, multicast and encapsulated hardware filters; returns an efx_rc_t. The caller is expected to serialize access to the filter table. If table->eft_default_rxq is NULL it deletes every unicast, multicast and encapsulation filter with ef10_filter_delete_internal (ignoring errors), sets their counts to 0 and returns 0. Otherwise it marks all existing unicast, multicast and encapsulation filters as auto-old, sets the unicast count to 0, inserts the specific unicast filter for mac_addr and, if all_unicst is true or that insertion failed, inserts the all-unicast filter; if both insertions failed it goes to fail1. It then calls ef10_filter_get_workarounds (an error goes to fail2). If the all-multicast setting changed (table->eft_using_all_mulcst != all_mulcst) and the bug26807 workaround is enabled it removes the old filters first. For all_mulcst true it inserts the all-multicast filter, and if that fails inserts the multicast list without rollback (failure goes to fail3). For all_mulcst false it inserts the multicast list with rollback; on failure it removes old filters when the workaround is enabled and all-multicast was not in use, tries the all-multicast filter, and if that also fails tries the multicast list without rollback (failure goes to fail4). When tunnel encapsulation is supported it inserts encapsulation filters, ignoring errors; it removes the remaining auto-old filters, and returns ENOTSUP if all_unicst was requested and the all-unicast insertion failed or all_mulcst was requested and the all-multicast insertion failed, otherwise the value of rc (0 on the paths reached). The fail labels clear the auto-old mark on every entry that has it (they do not delete those entries) and return rc.

functions.name: efx_build_signed_image_write_buffer
functions.prose_contract: Builds the NVRAM partition layout for a signed image in a caller buffer; returns 0 or an errno. It returns EINVAL if bufferp or infop or headerpp is NULL or buffer_size is 0, if infop is not EFX_IMAGE_FORMAT_SIGNED with a non-NULL image and header, if the header lies before the image or the image is too small, or if any of the located source chunks (CMS header, image header, code, trailer, signature) does not fit within buffer_size by the size/offset check. It then fills the buffer with 0xFF and writes, in the partition order, a chunk header followed by the copied data for the reflash trailer, the CMS header, the reflash header (setting *headerpp to the copy of the image header inside the buffer), the code, and the signature; ENOSPC is returned if the buffer cannot hold a chunk header or a chunk's data (the checks before each copy), in which case the buffer may be partly written and *headerpp may or may not have been set. It takes no locks and the caller keeps ownership of the buffer.

functions.name: ef10_mac_stats_update
functions.prose_contract: Reads the MAC statistics from the DMA stats buffer into stat[]; returns 0 or an errno. Parameters: enp, esmp (stats DMA memory), stat (array of EFX_MAC_NSTATS counters), generationp (optional). It returns ENOSPC if encp->enc_mac_stats_nstats is smaller than MC_CMD_MAC_NSTATS or the buffer is smaller than nstats 64-bit counters. Otherwise it syncs the buffer for the kernel, reads the generation-end counter from the last counter (index nstats - 1), then reads every counter group the firmware reports (extra groups only when nstats is at least the V3 or V4 count) into stat[] with EFSYS_STAT_SET_QWORD, re-syncs and reads the generation-start counter (MC_CMD_MAC_GENERATION_START). If start and end differ it returns EAGAIN (the stat[] array has already been written by then); otherwise it stores the low dword of the generation-start counter in *generationp when generationp is non-NULL and returns 0.

functions.name: efx_bootcfg_write
functions.prose_contract: Writes a DHCP-format boot configuration block into this function's sector of the BOOTROM_CFG NVRAM partition; returns 0 or an errno. The sector number is enc_pf on Huntington-family adapters and 0 otherwise. It gets the partition size (efx_nvram_size) and the sector offset and length (efx_bootcfg_sector_info), limits the sector length to BOOTCFG_MAX_SIZE, and returns EFBIG if the sector would end beyond the partition. It verifies data with efx_dhcp_verify (returning its error) and requires the verified block to be at least 2 bytes with its last byte equal to EFX_DHCP_END (ENOENT otherwise) and no longer than MIN(sector_length, BOOTCFG_MAX_SIZE) (ENOSPC otherwise). It allocates a buffer for the whole partition (ENOMEM on failure), starts a read-write NVRAM session, reads the whole partition into the buffer, zeroes the sector region, copies the block in, subtracts the block checksum from the first byte of the sector, erases the partition, writes the buffer back and finishes the session, then frees the buffer and returns 0. Errors after the session started finish the session and free the buffer; errors before it only return the code.

functions.name: sfxge_ev_qpoll
functions.prose_contract: Polls an event queue and re-primes it; returns 0 or an errno. It takes the event queue lock. If evq->init_state is neither SFXGE_EVQ_STARTING nor SFXGE_EVQ_STARTED it unlocks and returns EINVAL without touching the queue. Otherwise it syncs the event memory (POSTREAD), asserts (KASSERT) that rx_done, tx_done and txq are clear, calls efx_ev_qpoll(evq->common, &evq->read_ptr, &sfxge_ev_callbacks, evq), which can advance read_ptr, resets rx_done and tx_done to 0, calls sfxge_ev_qcomplete(evq, B_TRUE) to complete the pending Rx and Tx work, then calls efx_ev_qprime(evq->common, evq->read_ptr). If the prime fails it unlocks and returns that error, with the polled events already consumed, read_ptr advanced and the completions already done; otherwise it unlocks and returns 0.

functions.name: tso_fill_packet_with_fragment
functions.prose_contract: Adds one DMA descriptor for the current TSO fragment to the transmit queue's pending list; static void. Precondition: txq and tso are valid; the in_len and packet_space values are non-negative. If tso->in_len or tso->packet_space is 0 it returns without doing anything. It saves dma_addr = tso->dma_addr before updating the state. For firmware-assisted TSO v2 (SFXGE_FATSOV2) it takes n = tso->in_len, subtracts n from out_len, adds n to seqnum, sets in_len to 0, and either (n < packet_space) decreases packet_space by n and decrements segs_space, or recomputes packet_space as seg_size - (n - packet_space) % seg_size and segs_space as EFX_TX_FATSOV2_DMA_SEGS_PER_PKT_MAX - 1 minus 1 if packet_space is not a whole seg_size; tso->dma_addr is not changed in that mode. Otherwise it takes n = min(in_len, packet_space) and subtracts it from packet_space, out_len and in_len and adds it to tso->dma_addr. It computes eop as true when out_len, packet_space or segs_space is 0, then appends a descriptor to txq->pend_desc (incrementing n_pend_desc) with efx_tx_qdesc_dma_create using the saved (pre-update) dma_addr, length n and eop.

functions.name: sfxge_tx_init
functions.prose_contract: Initializes the transmit side of the sfxge driver; returns 0 or an errno. Precondition: the interrupt state is SFXGE_INTR_INITIALIZED (KASSERT). It first validates the tunables: sfxge_tx_dpl_get_max <= 0, sfxge_tx_dpl_get_non_tcp_max <= 0 or sfxge_tx_dpl_put_max < 0 each log a message and return EINVAL before any other state is changed (sc->txq_count is not reset on these returns). It then sets sc->txq_count = SFXGE_EVQ0_N_TXQ(sc) - 1 + intr.n_alloc, computes sc->tso_fw_assisted from the tunable minus the FATSOV1 and FATSOV2 bits the NIC does not support or has not enabled, and creates the 'txq' sysctl node (ENOMEM on failure, with txq_count set to 0). When sc->txq_dynamic_cksum_toggle_supported is false it initializes the NON_CKSUM and IP_CKSUM queues with sfxge_tx_qinit; it then initializes the IP_TCP_UDP_CKSUM queues, one per event queue. On success it calls sfxge_tx_stat_init and returns 0. If a queue init fails, the unwind frees the queues already initialized: after a TCP/UDP queue failure it finalizes the earlier TCP/UDP queues and then also the IP_CKSUM and NON_CKSUM queues, even when the dynamic toggle skipped initializing those two; a failure at the IP_CKSUM or NON_CKSUM init finalizes the earlier ones; failures after the txq_count assignment set txq_count to 0 and return the error.

functions.name: siis_timeout
functions.prose_contract: Callout handler for a command timeout on a SIIS slot; static void. Precondition: the channel mutex is held (mtx_assert). If the slot's state is below SIIS_SLOT_RUNNING it returns. If the command is an ATA control command with the reset bit (ATA_A_RESET) set, it freezes the SIM queue for ch->numrslots, ends the transaction with SIIS_ERR_TFE through siis_end_transaction and returns, without modifying ch->toslots itself (siis_end_transaction may clear this slot's bit). Otherwise it prints diagnostic register values and 'Timeout on slot', freezes the SIM queue once when ch->toslots was empty (xpt_freeze_simq(ch->sim, 1)), sets this slot's bit in ch->toslots, and if all running slots are now timed out ((ch->rslots & ~ch->toslots) == 0) calls siis_process_timeout(dev), else prints which slots it is still waiting for.

functions.name: sk_intr_bcom
functions.prose_contract: Handles a Broadcom PHY interrupt for an SK network interface; static void. It clears the XMAC TX and RX enable bits in XM_MMUCMD, reads the PHY interrupt status register (BRGPHY_MII_ISR) to clear pending interrupts, and if IFF_DRV_RUNNING is not set it calls sk_init_xmac(sc_if) and returns without setting the TX/RX enable bits again. Otherwise, only when the status has BRGPHY_ISR_LNK_CHG or BRGPHY_ISR_AN_PR set, it reads the aux status: if the link is down while sk_link was set it calls mii_mediachg, turns the link LED off and clears sk_link; else if LNK_CHG is set it writes the interrupt mask register 0xFF00, calls mii_tick, sets sk_link and turns the link LED on; else (AN_PR only) it calls mii_tick and reschedules the sk_tick callout in hz ticks. With neither status bit set it does none of that. At the end of the running path it sets the XMAC TX and RX enable bits again and returns.

functions.name: pqi_process_firmware_features
functions.prose_contract: Negotiates firmware features with the smartpqi controller through the PQI configuration table; static void, no return value. First pass over the local pqi_firmware_features[] list: an entry for PQI_FIRMWARE_FEATURE_UNIQUE_SATA_WWN is skipped (nothing recorded, no callback) when softs->sata_unique_wwn is not set; for every other entry, if the controller reports the feature as supported (pqi_is_firmware_feature_supported) it marks the entry supported and counts it; otherwise it logs a warning, calls pqi_firmware_feature_update for it and, if the entry is the PQI_FIRMWARE_FEATURE_MAX_KNOWN_FEATURE bit, stops scanning. If no feature is supported it returns. It then requests each supported feature in the firmware features table with pqi_request_firmware_feature, except that with DEVICE_HINT defined it skips features for which check_device_hint_status returns nonzero. It calls pqi_enable_firmware_features; if that fails it logs an error, calls pqi_firmware_feature_update for every supported entry and returns. Otherwise it checks each supported entry with pqi_is_firmware_feature_enabled: enabled ones get enabled = true, the others log a warning, and pqi_firmware_feature_update is called for each supported entry.

functions.name: pqisrc_sis_wait_for_db_bit_to_clear
functions.prose_contract: Waits for a doorbell bit to clear in the legacy SIS interface; returns PQI_STATUS_SUCCESS, PQI_STATUS_FAILURE or PQI_STATUS_TIMEOUT. It loops: it reads the host-to-IOA doorbell register (LEGACY_SIS_IDBR) and exits with success when (db_reg & bit) is 0; otherwise, if the firmware status shows PQI_CTRL_KERNEL_PANIC it logs and exits with PQI_STATUS_FAILURE; otherwise, once loop_cnt has reached SIS_DB_BIT_CLEAR_TIMEOUT_CNT (checked before each increment) it logs that the bit was not cleared and exits with PQI_STATUS_TIMEOUT; otherwise it sleeps 500 (OS_SLEEP(500)) and repeats. It returns the result code. No locks are taken.

functions.name: pqisrc_get_tag
functions.prose_contract: Pops a free tag from the lock-free tag stack; returns the tag index or INVALID_ELEM. It compiles only when LOCKFREE_STACK is defined. It loops: it copies stack->head; if the head's top index is 0 (stack empty) it returns INVALID_ELEM; otherwise it builds a new head with seq_no incremented and index equal to stack->next_index_array[cur_head.top.index], and tries to install it with os_atomic64_cas on stack->head.data, retrying if the compare-and-swap fails. After a successful swap it sets next_index_array[cur_head.top.index] to 0, decrements stack->num_elem (a plain, non-atomic update) and returns cur_head.top.index.

functions.name: smb_ioctl
functions.prose_contract: ioctl handler of the smb character device; returns 0 or an errno. It reads the smbcmd from data; if the device minor has bit 0x0400 set it overrides s->slave with the low 10 bits of the minor. It returns EINVAL if the slave address is odd (s->slave & 1). It requests the SMBus bus with smbus_request_bus (SMB_DONTWAIT for O_NONBLOCK, otherwise SMB_WAIT | SMB_INTR) and returns that error if nonzero. Under COMPAT_FREEBSD32 it first converts the 32-bit command structure into a local smbcmd for the *32 command codes. It then dispatches on cmd: quick write/read, send byte, receive byte (stores into s->cmd), write byte/word call the matching smbus_* call and convert the SMBus error with smbus_error; read byte, read word and process call, if their smbus call succeeded and s->rbuf is non-NULL with s->rcount large enough (1 or 2), copyout the 1 or 2 result bytes to s->rbuf (error from copyout kept) and set s->rcount to the size copied; block write returns EINVAL for a negative wcount, clamps wcount to SMB_MAXBLOCKSIZE, copies the data in (copyin error kept) and calls smbus_bwrite; block read returns EINVAL for a negative rcount, clamps it to SMB_MAXBLOCKSIZE, calls smbus_bread, shortens rcount to the byte count read and copies the data out; any other command gives ENOTTY. For compat 32-bit commands the results are copied back to the 32-bit structure: cmd for SMB_RECVB32; only rdata.word for the read-byte, read-word and process-call variants (not rcount); and rdata.word (when rbuf is NULL) plus rcount for SMB_BREAD32. It releases the bus with smbus_release_bus and returns the error, including after a failed smbus request (that path returns before the release).

functions.name: smbus_error
functions.prose_contract: Converts an SMBus error bit mask to a unix errno; int. If smb_error equals SMB_ENOERR it returns 0. Otherwise it tests the bits in this order: SMB_ENOTSUPP gives ENODEV; else SMB_ENOACK gives ENXIO; else SMB_ETIMEOUT gives EWOULDBLOCK; else SMB_EBUSY gives EBUSY; else any of SMB_EABORT, SMB_EBUSERR or SMB_ECOLLI gives EIO; any other nonzero value gives EINVAL. When several bits are set the first match in that order wins.

functions.name: atiixp_chan_trigger
functions.prose_contract: Trigger callback for an ATI IXP audio channel; static int, returns 0. If the trigger is not one of the common PCMTRIG start/stop/abort values (PCMTRIG_COMMON false) it returns 0 at once. Otherwise it takes the softc lock. PCMTRIG_START: flushes and rebuilds the scatter/gather table, writes the link pointer register (0 then the table address with ATI_REG_LINKPTR_EN) and enables the DMA; when sc->polling is nonzero it resets ch->ptr and prevptr, computes pollticks from hz, the block size and the buffer format (a quarter of the block period, clamped to between 1 and hz) and, only if no channel was running or pollticks is less than sc->poll_ticks, stores it in sc->poll_ticks and arms the poll timer callout; it then sets ATI_IXP_CHN_RUNNING. PCMTRIG_STOP and PCMTRIG_ABORT: disable and flush the DMA, clear ATI_IXP_CHN_RUNNING and, when polling, stop the poll timer and reset poll_ticks to 1 if no channel remains active, or recompute the tick count from the remaining running channel and, if it is larger than poll_ticks, store it and re-arm the timer. Any other trigger value unlocks and returns 0 without further work. For START, STOP and ABORT it then reads ATI_REG_IER and sets or clears ATI_REG_IER_SET_BUS_BUSY according to whether the command register has any of the send, receive or S/PDIF-out enable bits, writes it back, releases the lock and returns 0.

functions.name: emu_init
functions.prose_contract: Initializes an EMU10K1/Audigy sound chip (emu10k1.c); returns 0 or -1. It programs the hardware configuration and interrupt registers, clears the record buffer registers and the clean/solo interrupt enables, resets all NUM_G voice channel registers and the software voice table (vnum, slave, busy, etc.), sets pnum and rnum to 0, writes the default S/PDIF channel status word to EMU_SPCS0..2, and for non-Audigy chips calls emu_initefx (for Audigy 2 it also adjusts the S/PDIF sample-rate register and writes two port pairs). It initializes the page table: SLIST_INIT of mem.blocks, allocates ptb_pages (returning -1 if it fails) and a silent page (freeing ptb_pages and returning -1 if that allocation fails), fills every page table entry with the silent page address and sets EMU_PTB, EMU_TCB, EMU_TCBS and the per-voice map registers. It then enables audio: for Audigy chips it writes the HCFG value, calls audigy_initefx and sets audio enable and clears the GP output (Audigy 2 also unmutes analog); for the original EMU10K1 it writes HCFG with the audio-enable, lock-tank and auto-mute bits (plus joystick enable when sc->rev >= 6) and then probes the S/PDIF (TOS link) state: sc->tos_link is set to 0 and set to 1 only in this non-Audigy branch when the GP inputs indicate it and a probe write changes the register. It returns 0.

functions.name: emu_rate_to_pitch
functions.prose_contract: Converts a sample rate to an EMU10K2 pitch register value (emu10kx.c); static uint32_t. If rate is 0 it returns 0.
