Otherwise it multiplies rate by 11185 in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic (which wraps for rate above about 383990), then scans bit positions from 31 down to 1 for the first set bit of the shifted value, shifting it left each step. At the first set bit i it returns ((i - 15) << 20) + logMagTable[(rate >> 24) & 0x7f] + ((rate >> 17) & 0x7f) * logSlopeTable[(rate >> 24) & 0x7f], using the shifted value; if no bit from 31 down to 1 is set (for example when the product is 0 or has only bit 0 set) it returns 0. It uses two static tables of 128 entries and takes no locks.

functions.name: envy24htchan_trigger
functions.prose_contract: Trigger callback for an Envy24HT PCM channel; returns 0 or -1 as error. It takes sc->lock and selects slot 0 for playback and 1 for record. PCMTRIG_START: if neither slot is running it sets the card speed with envy24ht_setspeed(ch->speed) and pins the min and max speed of both capability entries; otherwise a channel speed that is nonzero and differs from the card speed gives error -1 (goto fail); a zero channel speed takes the card speed. It increments run[slot]; for the first channel in the slot it resets ch->offset and sets blk[slot] = ch->blk, otherwise it computes ch->offset from the hardware pointer and lowers blk[slot] if ch->blk is smaller. For a playback channel it runs ch->emldma and envy24ht_setvolume; for both directions it calls envy24ht_updintr(sc, ch->dir) and, for the first running channel in the slot, envy24ht_start(sc, ch->dir); then sets ch->run = 1. PCMTRIG_EMLDMAWR and PCMTRIG_EMLDMARD require ch->run == 1 (else error -1) and call ch->emldma. PCMTRIG_ABORT, if the channel is running, clears ch->run, decrements run[slot], mutes the volume for playback, and when run[slot] reaches 0 calls envy24ht_stop(sc, ch->dir) and sets sc->intr[slot] = 0. Other values do nothing. It releases the lock at the fail label and returns the error.

functions.name: fm801_wrcd
functions.prose_contract: Writes an AC97 codec register on an FM801 (ac97 write method); returns 0 or -1. Parameters: devinfo is the fm801_info, regno the codec register, data the 16-bit value to write. It first polls the FM_CODEC_CMD register's BUSY bit up to TIMO times with a 10 ms DELAY; if the codec is still busy it prints 'fm801 wrcd: read codec busy' and returns -1 without writing. Otherwise it writes data to FM_CODEC_DATA and regno to FM_CODEC_CMD (both 16-bit writes), then polls the BUSY bit again up to TIMO times with 10 ms delays; if it never clears it prints the same message and returns -1 (the write has already been issued), else it returns 0.

functions.name: tr_wrcd
functions.prose_contract: Writes an AC97 codec register on a Trident-family sound chip; returns 0 or -1. It selects the codec write register and busy-status bit by tr->type: SPA, ALI and TDX use their own register and status-bit constants and TNX adds the secondary-codec bit when bit 8 of regno is set; for any other type it prints '!!! tr_wrcd defaulted !!!' and returns -1 without touching hardware. It masks regno with 0x7f, takes tr->lock, and for the ALI chip polls the busy bit up to TR_TIMEOUT_CDC times and then, if the poll did not time out, reads register 0xc8 twice and polls until the two values differ (up to the timeout again). For non-ALI chips, or for ALI when the previous waits did not time out, it polls the busy bit again (up to TR_TIMEOUT_CDC reads); for an ALI chip with tr->rev above 0x01 it sets 0x0100 in the status mask, then it writes (data << TR_CDC_DATA) | regno | status-bit to the codec write register, even if that last poll timed out. It releases the lock, prints a timeout message when the poll counter reached 0 and returns 0 when the counter is above 0, else -1; so a timed-out last poll returns -1 although the write was issued, and an ALI chip whose first wait timed out returns -1 without writing.

functions.name: chn_syncdestroy
functions.prose_contract: Removes a channel from its sync group if it has one; returns int. Precondition: the caller holds the sync group list mutex (PCM_SG_LOCKASSERT(MA_OWNED)). It starts with sg_id = 0. If c->sm is non-NULL it takes the member sm and its group sg, sets c->sm to NULL, removes the member from sg->members and frees it; if the group's member list is then empty it removes the group from the global snd_pcm_syncgroups list, records sg->id in sg_id and frees the group. It returns sg_id, which is non-zero only when the removed member was the last one of its group (so the caller can release the group id after dropping the lock), and 0 otherwise, including when c had no sync member.

functions.name: dsp_oss_engineinfo
functions.prose_contract: Handler body for SNDCTL_ENGINEINFO: fills an oss_audioinfo for an audio engine (a channel) by index; returns 0 or EINVAL. If ai->dev is -1 and the ioctl came on a device that is not a dsp device (i_dev->si_devsw != &dsp_cdevsw) it returns EINVAL. It takes the bus topology lock and iterates over the registered pcm units (pcm_devclass), locking each device and walking its pcm channels with a running channel index nchan; for each channel it locks it and stops at the first channel for which either ai->dev is -1 and devfs_foreach_cdevpriv with dsp_oss_engineinfo_cb reports the channel as owned by the opened device, or ai->dev equals nchan; other channels are unlocked and counted. When a channel was found it zeroes *ai and fills it: ai->dev is the channel index nchan (not the pcm unit), name, busy state (OPEN_WRITE or OPEN_READ when the channel is busy), pid and command, capability flags, the natively supported formats (stored in oformats for playback and iformats for record) and the minimum and maximum channel counts from the channel caps, card_number, port_number and legacy_device set to the pcm unit, mixer_dev (the unit when the device has a mixer, else -1), /dev/dsp<unit> as devnode, enabled from device_is_attached, min and max rates (from the capabilities for an exclusive or bitperfect channel, else from feeder_rate_min and feeder_rate_max), the rates list from chn_getrates limited to OSS_MAX_SAMPLE_RATES, and next_play_engine and next_rec_engine as 0. It then unlocks the channel and device, releases the bus topology lock and returns 0. If no channel matched in any unit it releases the bus topology lock and returns EINVAL. This function has no 'unavailable' branch.

functions.name: z_resampler_set
functions.prose_contract: Sets a resampler feeder parameter and re-runs the setup; static int. what selects FEEDRATE_SRC, FEEDRATE_DST, FEEDRATE_QUALITY or FEEDRATE_CHANNELS; any other value returns EINVAL. For SRC and DST a value outside feeder_rate_min..feeder_rate_max returns E2BIG; a value equal to the current rsrc or rdst returns 0 unchanged; otherwise the field is changed. For QUALITY a value outside Z_QUALITY_MIN..Z_QUALITY_MAX returns EINVAL, an unchanged value returns 0, otherwise the quality is changed and z_resampler_setup(f) is called: if that returns 0 the function returns 0, if it fails the old quality is restored and the function falls through to the final call, so it then returns the result of z_resampler_setup(f) with the old quality (which may be 0). For CHANNELS a value outside SND_CHN_MIN..SND_CHN_MAX returns EINVAL, an unchanged value returns 0, else the channel count is changed. For SRC, DST and CHANNELS the new value stays stored even when the final z_resampler_setup(f) returns an error, and that error is returned.

functions.name: mixer_setrecsrc
functions.prose_contract: Selects the recording source of a mixer; static int. It gets the sound device d = device_get_softc(mixer->dev); if d is NULL it returns -1. It decides whether it must drop the mixer lock: dropmtx is 1 when the device is not SD_F_MPSAFE and the mixer lock is currently owned by the caller, else 0 (so the lock need not be held). It masks src with mixer->recdevs; if the result is 0 it tries in order the microphone, monitor and line bits of recdevs, and if still 0 while recdevs is non-zero it uses the lowest set bit of recdevs. It then releases the mixer lock (when dropmtx), calls MIXER_SETRECSRC(mixer, src) to let the driver apply it, retakes the lock (when dropmtx), stores the driver's returned mask in mixer->recsrc and returns 0.

functions.name: ste_intr
functions.prose_contract: Interrupt handler of the Sundance ST201 (ste) Ethernet driver; static void. It takes STE_LOCK. With DEVICE_POLLING defined and IFCAP_POLLING enabled it unlocks and returns before reading any status. Otherwise it reads STE_ISR_ACK (acknowledging the status); if IFF_DRV_RUNNING is not set it unlocks and returns without servicing events and without rewriting STE_IMR. If the status is 0xFFFF or has no bit in STE_INTRS it jumps to the end (the label inside the running block) and rewrites STE_IMR with the current mask, without servicing any event. Otherwise, if Rx interrupt moderation is active (ste_int_rx_act > 0) it drops the Rx-DMA-done bit from the status and mask; for a SOFTINTR or RX_DMADONE status it calls ste_rxeof(sc, -1) and, if still running with ste_int_rx_mod nonzero, arms the countdown timer and masks Rx-DMA-done (setting ste_int_rx_act = 1) or, when the status did not carry RX_DMADONE, unmasks it and clears ste_int_rx_act. While still running it then handles TX_DMADONE (ste_txeof), TX_DONE (ste_txeoc) and STATS_OFLOW (ste_stats_update); a HOSTERR status clears IFF_DRV_RUNNING, calls ste_init_locked, unlocks and returns without re-enabling interrupts here; otherwise it starts transmission with ste_start_locked when the send queue is non-empty, writes the interrupt mask register STE_IMR with the updated mask and unlocks.

functions.name: sym_prepare_setting
functions.prose_contract: Computes the SCSI controller's software settings from its features, saved registers and NVRAM; static int, returns 0 (its only return statement). It sets np->maxwide from FE_WIDE; the clock multiplier (4 for FE_QUAD, 2 for FE_DBLR, else 1) and clock_khz (40 or 80 MHz times the multiplier, calling sym_getclock when it is not 40000); the SCNTL3 value from the divider table (zeroed on FE_C10); minsync and maxsync from the clock, raised to at least 25 or 12 depending on the Ultra feature bits; the DT sync limits for FE_C10|FE_ULTRA3 at 160 MHz; the CCNTL0/CCNTL1 flags from FE_DAC and FE_NOPM and an erratum on the 53C1010; the burst length from the saved registers and limits; the DMODE, DCNTL, CTEST3, CTEST4, CTEST5 and SCNTL0 bits from the features and the setup options (parity checking, prefetch, cache-line, write-and-invalidate), clearing FE_WRIE, FE_ERL and FE_ERMP for a 53C810 erratum case; the host SCSI id (from the NVRAM or the SCID register, default SYM_SETUP_HOST_ID); the SCSI mode (single-ended or differential, setting the HVD bit); the LED feature; the IRQ mode bit; and for every target the default user period, offset and width, with FE_ULTRA3 DT-capable limits, and tags. It prints the controller summary when sym_verbose is set and returns 0.

functions.name: daemon_saver
functions.prose_contract: Screen-saver callback that draws a bouncing daemon picture and moving host-name text; returns 0 or EAGAIN. It finds the softc with sc_find_softc (EAGAIN if NULL) and uses sc->cur_scp. If blank is non-zero: in a graphics video mode (V_INFO_GRAPHICS) it returns EAGAIN; on the first call (blanked == 0) it clears the screen text buffer, hides the hardware cursor, sets the border to black and zeroes the clip lengths; it returns 0 for the first two calls (blanked++ < 2) and then sets blanked = 1. On later calls it erases the previously drawn daemon and string (clear_daemon, clear_string). The daemon position moves only on every other call: moved_daemon is pre-incremented and the movement block runs when the result is non-zero (the block sets moved_daemon back to -1). In that block it computes min and max for the x position from the screen width (when the screen is not wider than the picture it uses min = xsize - DAEMON_MAX_WIDTH - 10 and max = 10, so positions may be negative), flips dxdir at the limits, does the same for y, advances dxpos and dypos by their directions and computes the x and y offsets and lengths: a position at or beyond the screen edge gives length 0, a negative position sets the offset to -pos and a position that overruns the screen edge shortens the length; the offset is not subtracted from the length. Every call (not only on movement) updates the message position txpos/typos with the same kind of clamping and clipping (toff, tlen) and then draws the daemon and the string. If blank is 0 it sets blanked to 0. It returns 0.

functions.name: gfb_cursor
functions.prose_contract: Draws, moves or hides the text cursor on a generic framebuffer console; static void. Two variants exist in the file. Variant for SC_OFWFB builds: if scp->curs_attr.height <= 0 (cursor disabled) it returns without changing any status; with blink set it sets VR_CURSOR_BLINK, and when on is set sets VR_CURSOR_ON and moves the hardware cursor to at (column at % xsize, row at / xsize), otherwise hides the hardware cursor if VR_CURSOR_ON was set and clears VR_CURSOR_ON; without blink it clears VR_CURSOR_BLINK and, when on is set, sets VR_CURSOR_ON, redraws the character at cursor_oldpos from the screen buffer and draws the character at position at with swapped foreground and background nibbles (an inverse-video cursor by software), or when on is clear and VR_CURSOR_ON was set redraws the character at at normally and clears VR_CURSOR_ON. Other builds: after the same disabled-cursor early return, if on is set and blink is 0 it sets VR_CURSOR_ON and positions the hardware cursor at at; if on is set with blink it increments pxlblinkrate and, when bit 2 of it is set, resets it, toggles VR_CURSOR_ON and moves the hardware cursor to at or hides it (-1, -1); if on is clear it moves the hardware cursor to at when VR_CURSOR_ON was set and clears VR_CURSOR_ON; finally it sets or clears VR_CURSOR_BLINK according to blink. The flip argument is unused.

functions.name: scsplash_saver
functions.prose_contract: Screen-saver callback that shows or removes the splash image (DEV_SPLASH); static void. It uses a static busy flag: if busy is already TRUE it returns immediately without touching it; otherwise it sets busy to TRUE, works on sc->cur_scp and sets busy to FALSE at the end, so every path after the first check clears it. With show set and SC_SAVER_FAILED not set it blanks the screen (set_scrn_saver_mode) if the screen is not already blanked and calls splash(sc->adp, TRUE): result 0 does nothing more; EAGAIN restores the saver mode (restore_scrn_saver_mode(scp, FALSE)) and touches the screen saver timer, without setting SC_SAVER_FAILED; any other result sets SC_SAVER_FAILED, clears the sticky splash, restores the mode (restore_scrn_saver_mode(scp, TRUE)) and prints 'scsplash_saver(): failed to put up the image'. With show clear and the splash not sticky, if the screen is blanked and splash(sc->adp, FALSE) returns 0 it restores the saver mode with TRUE. busy is cleared after those cases.

functions.name: sc_switch_scr
functions.prose_contract: Requests a switch to another virtual terminal; returns 0 or an errno. If sc->cur_scp is NULL it returns 0. If SC_SCRN_VTYLOCK is set it rings the bell and returns EPERM. If the screen is blanked or a write or blink is in progress it records delayed_next_scr = next_scr + 1, touches the screen saver and returns 0 (the switch is delayed); otherwise it clears delayed_next_scr and raises spl. While a switch is already in progress and the current vty is in VT_PROCESS mode with a controlling process, it checks whether that process died: if so a pending WAIT_REL finishes the previous switch with finish_vt_rel(TRUE) and returns EINVAL, a pending WAIT_ACQ is completed with finish_vt_acq and execution continues, otherwise it only logs; if the process is alive but not answering, in WAIT_REL the switch_in_progress counter is incremented and on the fourth and later calls it forces finish_vt_rel(FALSE) and returns EINVAL (the second call resends the release signal), and in WAIT_ACQ it resends the acquire signal on the second call and forces finish_vt_acq on the fourth and later. It then returns EINVAL (with a bell) if next_scr is outside first_vty..first_vty+vtys or a switch is still in progress; EINVAL for leaving a graphics-mode VT_AUTO vty that is open, unless the target is the same vty; EINVAL if the target is not the kernel console and its tty is not open; EINVAL if the debugger is active and the target is not the console and is in VT_PROCESS mode (this check is skipped when next_scr is the console vty). It then sets switch_in_progress, old_scp and new_scp; if both are the same it clears switch_in_progress, wakes up waiters unless kdb_active and returns 0. Otherwise it signals the old vty's release (returning 0 if the process must answer first), exchanges screens with exchange_scr, wakes up waiters unless kdb_active, signals acquisition (returning 0 if the process must answer), and otherwise clears switch_in_progress, announces console availability when this is the console unit and returns 0.

functions.name: ns8250_divisor
functions.prose_contract: Computes the 16-bit baud rate divisor for an 8250-family UART; static int. It returns 0 if baudrate is 0. Otherwise divisor = (rclk / (baudrate << 3) + 1) >> 1, i.e. rclk / (16 * baudrate) rounded, and it returns 0 if the divisor is 0 or at least 65536. It computes actual_baud = rclk / (divisor << 4) and the error in percent as (((actual_baud - baudrate) * 2000 / baudrate) + 1) / 2 (a rounded percentage), returning 0 if the error is below -UART_DEV_TOLERANCE_PCT or above UART_DEV_TOLERANCE_PCT. Otherwise it returns the divisor. It reads and writes no global state; the multiplications and the shift use int arithmetic, so large rclk or baudrate values can overflow.

functions.name: ufshci_pci_setup_interrupts
functions.prose_contract: Chooses and sets up the controller's interrupt scheme (MSI-X, then MSI, then INTx); static int, returns 0 or an errno. With the tunable hw.ufshci.force_intx set it goes straight to INTx. If the device reports no MSI-X vectors it goes to MSI. Otherwise it derives num_io_queues from the tunables (hw.ufshci.num_io_queues clamped to 1..mp_ncpus, per_cpu_io_queues, min_cpus_per_ioq) and the available vector count minus one, rounds it down to a multiple of vm_ndomains when larger, and requests min(num_io_queues + 1, MSI-X count) vectors. If pci_alloc_msix fails it logs, clears msi_count and falls back to MSI. If exactly 1 vector was granted it returns ufshci_pci_setup_shared(ctrlr, 1) (which can return ENOMEM or the bus_setup_intr error); if a different number than requested was granted it releases the MSI, sets num_io_queues to granted - 1 and retries the request; when the request was granted in full it sets num_io_queues and returns 0 without installing any handler here (the multi-vector handlers are installed elsewhere). The MSI path requests min(MSI count, 2) MSIs: a failure clears msi_count and falls to INTx; a grant of 2 sets num_io_queues = 1 and returns 0 without installing a handler; otherwise it falls to the INTx step, which returns ufshci_pci_setup_shared(ctrlr, rid) with rid 1 when MSI count is above 0 and rid 0 otherwise.

functions.name: dwc_otg_data_tx
functions.prose_contract: Device-mode (peripheral) IN data transmit step for a dwc_otg endpoint; static uint8_t returning 0 for complete and 1 for not complete. It loops at most 3 times (to starts at 3). For endpoint 0 with a pending last RX status for channel 0: a packet status that is neither SETUP data nor SETUP complete is acknowledged with dwc_otg_common_rx_ack; otherwise the transfer was cancelled by the host, td->error_any is set to 1 and it returns 0. If td->tx_bytes is non-zero it reads DIEPTSIZ to find how many packets the FIFO has consumed, computes the space left (up to max_buffer, or one max-size packet when max_buffer is 0), copies up to that many bytes into the FIFO with dwc_otg_write_fifo and updates tx_bytes, remainder, offset and npkt; if bytes are still pending it returns 1; if remainder is 0 and the transfer was short it returns 0 (complete). If the repeat budget is used up it returns 1. If DIEPTSIZ still shows packets pending it returns 1. Otherwise it programs the next burst: with a nonzero max_buffer and a max packet size multiple of 4 it computes the packet count (limited to min(max_buffer / max_packet_size, 0x3FE) and a byte count up to 0x7FFFFF) and sets short_pkt for a trailing short or zero-length packet; else it sends one packet; it writes DIEPTSIZ, flips the data PID bit for isochronous endpoints, writes DIEPCTL with EPENA and CNAK, sets tx_bytes to the byte count, and returns 0 if no bytes and no remainder are left and the packet was short, else repeats. The early returns (cancel, still-pending, not-complete) skip the DIEPTSIZ and DIEPCTL programming.

functions.name: dwc_otg_update_host_transfer_schedule_locked
functions.prose_contract: Re-schedules host-mode transfers when a new (micro)frame has started; static uint8_t returning 0 if HFNUM is unchanged from sc_last_frame_num and 1 otherwise. It reads the frame number (masked) and returns 0 if it equals sc_last_frame_num; else it stores it. When (frame & 7) == 0 it clears the TT info and walks the transfer queue (intr_q) in passes, moving each newly scheduled transfer to a temporary list and recording its start slot: isochronous transfers with a split (hcsplt != 0) not yet scheduled, first those whose direction is not IN (isochronous IN endpoints are skipped in that pass, and only scheduled if dwc_otg_compute_isoc_rx_tt_slot gives a slot <= 3), then those that are IN (start slot = frame); then interrupt transfers (subject to dwc_otg_host_rate_check_interrupt; those without a split are only flagged scheduled); then control transfers. Then, for (frame & 7) < 6, it does the same for bulk transfers. Each pass sets sc_needsof = 1 for the transfers it examines. It then, for every new frame, appends the temporary list to the queue, reorders the queue so entries with a split (hcsplt != 0) come first, and moves entries without a split that are not isochronous to the end. When (frame & 7) == 0 it finally adjusts the SOF interrupt mask: if SOFMSK is set and sc_needsof is 0 it clears the bit, if it is clear and sc_needsof is non-zero it sets it, writes GINTMSK in either case, and resets sc_needsof to 0. It returns 1.

functions.name: dwc_otg_interrupt
functions.prose_contract: Interrupt handler of the dwc_otg USB controller; static void. It takes the USB bus lock and spin lock, reads GINTSTS and writes back status & DWC_OTG_MSK_GINT_THREAD_IRQ to clear only the thread-level interrupt bits (other status bits are not cleared by this write). It then handles: GINTSTS_USBRST (sets device-mode and connect-change flags, clears the SOF interrupt mask and notifies the root hub); GINTSTS_ENUMDONE (marks the bus reset ended, reinitializes the FIFOs for device mode, sets address 0, records the enumerated speed, disables resume and SOF interrupts, enables suspend and notifies the root hub); GINTSTS_PRTINT (reads HPRT, writes back the HPRT change bits together with sc_hprt_val, updates the flags for connection, enable, over-current, power and speed, calls dwc_otg_suspend_irq or dwc_otg_resume_irq, notifies the root hub and updates the host frame interval); GINTSTS_WKUPINT (resume) or else GINTSTS_USBSUSP (suspend); and, when any of USBSUSP, USBRST, OTG or SESSREQ is set, reads GOTGCTL and calls dwc_otg_vbus_interrupt with whether a session is valid. Finally, if sc_xfer_complete is non-zero it clears it and calls dwc_otg_interrupt_complete_locked(sc). It releases both locks and returns void. Status bits outside these cases are only read, not acted on.

functions.name: ehci_non_isoc_done
functions.prose_contract: Completes a non-isochronous EHCI transfer; static void. It takes the QH for the current DMA set and invalidates its page cache, then starts from xfer->td_transfer_first. For a control transfer with a header stage it processes that stage with ehci_non_isoc_done_sub (its error kept), sets aframes to 1 and jumps to done if the transfer descriptor cache became NULL. It then loops over the data frames while aframes != nframes, calling ehci_non_isoc_done_sub for each, incrementing aframes and jumping to done if the descriptor cache became NULL. If it is a control transfer without an active data stage (control_act clear) it processes the status stage with ehci_non_isoc_done_sub. At done it calls ehci_device_done(xfer, err) with the last error code. The function itself invalidates the QH page cache, so the caller does not need to do that; the err of earlier frames is overwritten by later ones.

functions.name: musbotg_host_ctrl_status_rx
functions.prose_contract: Host-mode control transfer IN status stage for the MUSB controller; static uint8_t, returns 0 for complete and 1 for not yet complete. It allocates a channel when td->channel is -1 (musbotg_channel_alloc) and returns 1 if none is available. It selects endpoint 0 (EPINDEX). On the first call (transaction_started clear) it programs the device address, hub address and port and the transfer type, sets the NAK limit, marks the transaction started, disables PING in RXCSRH and writes TXCSRL with the STATUSPKT and REQPKT bits, then returns 1. On later calls it reads TXCSRL: if RXPKTRDY is set it clears it, frees the channel and returns 0; if the NAK-timeout bit is set it clears the STATUSPKT and REQPKT and NAKTIMO bits (two writes) and sets td->error = 1; if the RXSTALL or ERROR bit is set it writes TXCSRL = 0 and sets td->error = 1. Then, if td->error is non-zero (set now or earlier, even when none of the bits above are set), it frees the channel and returns 0; otherwise it returns 1.

functions.name: musbotg_dev_ctrl_data_rx
functions.prose_contract: Device-mode control transfer OUT data stage receive for the MUSB controller; static uint8_t, 0 means complete and 1 not complete. It selects endpoint 0, writes any pending sc->sc_ep0_cmd to TXCSRL and clears it, then reads TXCSRL. If SETUPEND or SENTSTALL is set it returns 0, with no error when td->remainder is 0 (a complete transfer followed by the next SETUP) and with td->error = 1 otherwise. If RXPKTRDY is not set it returns 1. Otherwise it reads the byte count; a count below td->max_frame_size marks a short packet (td->short_pkt = 1 and a local got_short), a count above it sets td->error = 1 and returns 0; a count greater than td->remainder also sets td->error = 1 and returns 0. It copies the bytes from the FIFO into the transfer's pages (through the bounce buffer when the destination is not 4-byte aligned), reducing remainder and advancing offset. Finally, if td->remainder is 0 or this packet was short: when td->short_pkt is set it stores MUSB2_MASK_CSR0L_RXPKTRDY_CLR in sc->sc_ep0_cmd (to be written on the next call) and returns 0; when td->short_pkt is not set (remainder reached 0 on a full-size packet) it falls to the common tail. The common tail writes RXPKTRDY_CLR to TXCSRL immediately and returns 1, so a full-size final packet leaves the transfer not complete (a zero-length packet is still expected).

functions.name: ohci_non_isoc_done
functions.prose_contract: Completes a non-isochronous OHCI transfer; static void. It starts with err = 0 and td_transfer_cache = td_transfer_first. For a control transfer with a header stage it runs ohci_non_isoc_done_sub (storing its result in err), sets aframes to 1 (without incrementing it per call here) and jumps to done if the transfer descriptor cache became NULL. It then loops while aframes != nframes: err = ohci_non_isoc_done_sub(xfer), aframes++, and a jump to done when the cache became NULL. For a control transfer whose data stage is not active (control_act clear) it runs one more ohci_non_isoc_done_sub for the status stage, again overwriting err. At done it calls ohci_device_done(xfer, err). err is overwritten by each sub-scan, not aggregated, so the error of an earlier stage is lost when a later scan runs; the status-stage scan does not increment aframes.

functions.name: xhci_configure_reset_endpoint
functions.prose_contract: Re-initializes an endpoint on the xHCI controller after its transfer ring was reset; static usb_error_t. It derives the endpoint id from the descriptor (a control endpoint is treated as direction IN) and returns USB_ERR_NO_PIPE if the id is 0. It takes the command lock and calls xhci_configure_endpoint_by_xfer; if that fails it unlocks and returns that error. It then gets the endpoint into the stopped state according to its state: Disabled or Stopped needs nothing (drop = 0); Halted sends a reset-endpoint command and sets drop when it fails; any other state sends a stop-endpoint command and sets drop when it fails. It then sends set-TR-dequeue-pointer for the stream with the endpoint's ring address (a failure is only logged). Only when drop is set and the endpoint type is neither control nor isochronous does it configure a drop (xhci_configure_mask and configure-endpoint command), clearing the endpoint's bit in ep_configured on success (a failure is only logged). It then configures the slot and endpoint context: when the endpoint's bit in ep_configured is clear it sends a configure-endpoint command and sets the bit if that succeeded, otherwise it sends an evaluate-context command; a failure is only logged. It unlocks the command lock and returns 0 (USB_ERR_NORMAL_COMPLETION) in all those cases: errors from the stop, reset, dequeue-pointer and configure commands are not returned.

functions.name: fg_add_new_strokes
functions.prose_contract: Creates new strokes from the unmatched pressure spans of one sensor frame in the atp touchpad driver; static void. It copies the spans whose matched flag is false from pspans_x and pspans_y into local arrays and counts them (nspans[X], nspans[Y]). If the two counts are equal it adds one stroke per index pair with fg_add_stroke(spans[X][i], spans[Y][i]). Otherwise the axis with fewer unmatched spans is the repeat axis (repeat_axis = (nspans[X] > nspans[Y]) ? Y : X), repeat_count is the absolute difference of the counts, and on that axis it picks the span with the largest cumulative pressure (repeat_index). It then pairs spans index by index with fg_add_stroke until either axis runs out, and while repeat_count > 0 it repeats the span at repeat_index (decrementing the loop index of the repeat axis) at most repeat_count additional times, so that the repeated span is paired with exactly enough spans of the other axis to make up the difference, not with every span of the other axis. fg_add_stroke allocates a stroke with atp_alloc_stroke and returns without adding one when none is available.

functions.name: ukbd_read_char_locked
functions.prose_contract: Reads one keyboard character or scan code from the USB keyboard (locked variant); returns an int32/uint32 code, NOKEY or ERRKEY. Precondition: the keyboard lock is held (UKBD_LOCK_ASSERT). It returns NOKEY if the keyboard is not active. At next_code, if a composed character is pending and the compose flag is not set it returns that character, after clearing sc_composed_char, as ERRKEY when it is above 0xFF. With UKBD_EMULATE_ATSCANCODE and K_RAW mode it first returns buffered scan codes (an E0/E1 prefix first). Otherwise it fetches a key with ukbd_get_key (blocking when wait is true): -1 gives NOKEY; any real key increments kbd->kb_count, even if the following translation yields no key. The usb code is translated to a keycode (AT scancode emulation or the translation table); NN gives NOKEY. In K_RAW mode it returns the scan code or usb code. A left-alt (0x38) key press sets the compose flag and clears the composed char, and its release clears the flag and, if sc_composed_char is above 0xFF, resets it to 0. K_CODE mode returns the keycode (with the release bit for releases). In compose mode the keypad digit keys accumulate decimal digits in sc_composed_char (releases of those keys continue with the next key; an overflow past 0xFF continues to next_code), and any other key while sc_composed_char > 0 clears the compose flag and the composed char and returns ERRKEY. Otherwise genkbd_keyaction translates the key; NOKEY continues with the next key (goto next_code), else the action is returned.

functions.name: ums_intr_callback
functions.prose_contract: USB interrupt-transfer callback of the ums mouse driver; static void. It gets the transfer length with usbd_xfer_status. In USB_ST_TRANSFERRED: it truncates len to sizeof(sc_temp); a zero length goes to tr_setup; it copies the data out, takes the report id from the first byte when sc_iid is set (reducing len) or, for UMS_FLAG_SBU devices without report ids, ignores packets whose first byte is 0x14 or 0x15 (goto tr_setup). For each ums_info it accumulates the w, x, y, z, t axis deltas and the button bits that appear in the report, keeps button bits not found in the report from the previous state, and if any delta is non-zero or the buttons differ from sc_status.button it updates sc_status (button, dx, dy, dz; t is not exported) and, for an SBU device with an all-zero report, only arms a 50 ms callout, else stops the callout, queues the event with ums_put_queue and (with EVDEV_SUPPORT) pushes it with ums_evdev_push. With a report in which the wheel axis t is non-zero it first queues the previous button state and sets button bits 5 or 6. If there was no change nothing is queued. It then falls through to USB_ST_SETUP (tr_setup), which, when the receive FIFO has no room (usb_fifo_put_bytes_max == 0) and no evdev client is open (or EVDEV_SUPPORT is not built), breaks without resubmitting; otherwise it sets the frame length to the maximum and submits the transfer. In the error default case, a cancelled transfer does nothing; any other error sets the stall and goes to tr_setup, so it is resubmitted unless the same FIFO-full condition applies.

functions.name: usbhid_intr_out_callback
functions.prose_contract: USB interrupt-OUT transfer callback of the usbhid driver; static void. For USB_ST_TRANSFERRED and USB_ST_SETUP it takes len = xfer_ctx->req.intr.maxlen. If len is 0: in polling mode (USB_IN_POLLING_MODE_FUNC) it sets xfer_ctx->error to 0; in all cases it returns without calling the callback. Otherwise it copies len bytes from xfer_ctx->buf into the transfer's frame, sets the frame length, submits the transfer, sets req.intr.maxlen to 0 and, in polling mode, returns; otherwise it sets xfer_ctx->error to 0 and calls the completion callback xfer_ctx->cb(xfer_ctx) (ignoring its result), so the callback is also called after a successful non-polling submission. In the error case: an error other than USB_ERR_CANCELLED sets the stall and retries from the setup code; USB_ERR_CANCELLED sets xfer_ctx->error to EIO and calls the callback, also in polling mode.

functions.name: uled_ioctl
functions.prose_contract: ioctl handler of the uled USB LED device; returns 0 or an errno. It takes the softc mutex (sc_mtx) and switches on cmd. ULED_GET_COLOR copies the stored sc_color into *addr (it writes the caller's structure) and returns 0. ULED_SET_COLOR reads the colour from *addr, stores red, green and blue in sc->sc_color before sending anything (so the stored colour changes even if the USB request fails), builds an 8-byte report (for ULED_FLAG_BLINK1 devices: 0x01, 'n', red, green, blue and zeros; otherwise red, green, blue, three zeros, 0x1a, 0x05) and sends it with uled_ctrl_msg as a class interface SET_REPORT request (value 0x200); the result of uled_ctrl_msg is the return value. Any other command returns ENOTTY. The mutex is released before returning.

functions.name: mos_bulk_write_callback
functions.prose_contract: USB bulk-OUT (transmit) callback of the mos Ethernet driver; static void. In USB_ST_TRANSFERRED it increments IFCOUNTER_OPACKETS by 1 and then continues into the setup code. In USB_ST_SETUP (and after a completed transfer) it dequeues one mbuf from the interface send queue; if there is none it returns without submitting anything. Otherwise it copies the frame into the transfer's first frame, sets the frame length to m_pkthdr.len, passes a copy to BPF (BPF_MTAP), frees the mbuf, submits the transfer, increments IFCOUNTER_OPACKETS again at submit time (so a completed transfer followed by another queued packet is counted twice, once at completion and once at the new submission) and returns. On a USB error it increments IFCOUNTER_OERRORS; if the error is not USB_ERR_CANCELLED it sets the stall and retries through the setup code, else it returns.

functions.name: umb_up
functions.prose_contract: Advances the MBIM modem's bring-up state machine by one step; static void. It switches on sc->sc_state: UMB_S_DOWN calls umb_open; UMB_S_OPEN, when UMBFLG_FCC_AUTH_REQUIRED is set: with sc_cid == -1 calls umb_allocate_cid and leaves the switch; with a CID already allocated calls umb_newstate(sc, UMB_S_CID, UMB_NS_DONT_DROP) and then falls into the UMB_S_CID case, which calls umb_send_fcc_auth (so two actions in that case); without the flag it calls umb_radio(sc, 1); UMB_S_CID calls umb_send_fcc_auth; UMB_S_RADIO sends a subscriber-ready-status query; UMB_S_SIMREADY calls umb_packet_service(sc, 1); UMB_S_ATTACHED resets sc_tx_seq to 0 and calls umb_connect; UMB_S_CONNECTED calls umb_qry_ipconfig; UMB_S_UP only, if IFF_DRV_RUNNING is not yet set, sets it, clears IFF_DRV_OACTIVE and calls umb_rx(sc); it does not start any other state-advancing action. After the switch (including after the allocate-CID break) it re-arms sc_statechg_timer with umb_statechg_timeout when sc_state is still below UMB_S_UP, and stops that timer otherwise. Returns void.

functions.name: usb_alloc_device
functions.prose_contract: Allocates and enumerates a new USB device on a bus port; returns the new struct usb_device or NULL. It finds the first free device index starting at USB_ROOT_HUB_ADDR and returns NULL if the bus has no free index (devices_max reached) or the hub depth is above 0x10, and returns NULL if the device structure allocation fails. It initializes the device (mutex, speed, mode, parent hub, hub transaction-translator information and so on), calls the host controller's device_init method if present (a failure goes to the done label with the error), moves the device to USB_STATE_POWERED and, in host mode, sets the device address with usbd_req_set_address (errors are ignored, with the address taken from the device index if the request did not set it); in device mode it sets up the USB template (failure goes to done). It then sets the state to USB_STATE_ADDRESSED, reads the device descriptor with usbd_setup_device_desc, retrying through usbd_req_re_enumerate twice on failure (a further failure goes to done). It applies quirks, and in host mode selects a configuration index and calls usbd_set_config_index, retrying through re-enumeration or other configuration indexes in several cases (including the CD-ROM and mass-storage auto-quirk handling); a failure for a device with no configurations is cleared. At config_done it registers the device on its bus port with usb_bus_port_set_device, with USB_HAVE_UGEN creates the symlink and prints the attach line, with USB_HAVE_DEVCTL sends the ATTACH notification and returns udev. At done, if err is non-zero it frees the device and all its sub-devices with usb_free_device(udev, 0) and sets udev to NULL; it returns udev.

functions.name: uhub_reattach_port
functions.prose_contract: Re-enumerates the device on a hub port; static usb_error_t, 0 on success or the error of a failed control request. It first clears UHF_C_PORT_CONNECTION on the port (an error goes to the error label), frees any existing child device on the port with usb_free_device and re-reads the port status (an error goes to the error label). With USB_HAVE_DISABLE_ENUM, if enumeration is disabled globally or for this hub it goes to the error label with err still 0; if the port has no connected device it also goes to the error label with err 0 (nothing is reset and no speed is determined). Otherwise, when the port is in host mode it clears a still-set suspend feature, waits for the power-up delay, resets the port with usbd_req_reset_port (an error is logged and goes to the error label), re-reads the status, and if the connect-change bit is set or the device is no longer connected it repeats the whole sequence once (timeout flag) and on the second occurrence gives up through the error label with err 0. It then derives the device speed from the hub's speed and the port status bits (for a SuperSpeed hub with U1/U2 timeouts it calls usbd_req_set_hub_u1_timeout and usbd_req_set_hub_u2_timeout, whose errors are only logged and do not change the return value), chooses the device mode and allocates the child with usb_alloc_device; if that returns NULL it goes to the error label, otherwise it returns 0. The error label frees a child device if one exists; when err is 0 and the port status shows the port enabled it clears UHF_PORT_ENABLE with usbd_req_clear_port_feature (so the no-device and enumeration-disabled exits do clear port enable when it was set), logs 'device problem' with the error code if there is one, and returns err.

functions.name: usb_do_clear_stall_callback
functions.prose_contract: USB transfer callback that clears the halt condition of stalled endpoints, one at a time; static void. It takes the USB bus lock itself on entry and releases it before returning (it drops and retakes it around usbd_transfer_submit). It starts from udev->ep_curr. In USB_ST_TRANSFERRED it resets clear_stall_errors to 0 and, unless ep_curr is NULL (device unconfigured, which goes to the setup code), for an endpoint that has a descriptor and is marked stalled it clears toggle_next and is_stalled, calls usbd_clear_stall_locked and restarts the pending transfer of every stream queue, then advances to the next endpoint and falls into USB_ST_SETUP. In SETUP, if the device has no endpoints it does nothing; otherwise it wraps the endpoint pointer to the first endpoint when out of range and scans forward (at most endpoints_max positions) for the next endpoint with a descriptor that is stalled; for that endpoint it builds a CLEAR_FEATURE(ENDPOINT_HALT) device request for its address, sets one frame and submits the transfer, and stops scanning. At exit, udev->ep_curr is set to the endpoint last examined (the stalled endpoint just submitted, not the next one). On an error: a cancelled transfer does nothing; otherwise, unless usb_no_cs_fail is set or the error is USB_ERR_STALLED (both treated as success, so the stalled endpoint is cleared locally), it counts the failure: a timeout re-enumerates the device and sets clear_stall_errors to USB_CS_RESET_LIMIT, other errors increment the counter and re-enumerate when it reaches the limit; it then retries through the setup code, which does nothing further when the counter is at the limit.

functions.name: usbd_do_request_flags
functions.prose_contract: Performs a USB control request on a device and waits for completion; returns a usb_error_t. The timeout is clamped to 50..30000 ms. It returns USB_ERR_NOT_CONFIGURED if the device state is below USB_STATE_POWERED and zeroes *actlen if non-NULL. Without USB_HAVE_USER_IO a request with USB_USER_DATA_PTR returns USB_ERR_INVAL at once (before it touches the caller's mutex). If mtx is non-NULL and not Giant it unlocks it (and it is relocked at done). It takes the control-transfer serialization lock (usbd_ctrl_lock). If the device has a handle-request function (device mode or a root hub) it uses it instead of a transfer: a write with non-zero length gives USB_ERR_INVAL; the function's error is returned; a returned descriptor shorter than the requested length gives USB_ERR_SHORT_XFER (with *actlen left at 0 and nothing copied) unless USB_SHORT_XFER_OK is set, in which case the length is cut to what was returned; the data are copied to the caller (copyout failure gives USB_ERR_INVAL), *actlen is set and it goes to done. Otherwise it sets up the control transfer (USB_ERR_NOMEM if it cannot), sets the manual-status and short-transfer flags from flags and the timeout, copies the setup packet into frame 0 and loops: each pass sets the data frame length (at most the transfer maximum), copies write data in, starts the transfer and waits for completion (cv_wait), takes xfer->error, copies read data out, advances the data pointer, updates *actlen and stops at an error, a timeout (USB_ERR_TIMEOUT when the elapsed time exceeds the timeout), or when no data remains. On error it stops the transfer. At done it releases the control lock if it took it, relocks the caller's mutex and, for any error other than normal completion, short transfer, stall or cancel, sleeps hz/16 for transaction-translator cleanup before returning the error.

functions.name: usbd_req_reset_port
functions.prose_contract: Resets a hub port and waits for the reset to finish; returns a usb_error_t. It first tries to clear UHF_C_PORT_RESET (any error is ignored), then sets UHF_PORT_RESET (an error is returned). It then polls: pause usb_port_reset_delay ms, add that to a counter n, read the port status (an error is returned); if the port is no longer connected it returns the current err value, which is 0, so a vanished device is reported as success; if the reset-change bit is set it leaves the loop; if the reset bit is no longer asserted (a VM workaround) it leaves the loop; if n exceeds 1000 ms it sets n to 0 and leaves the loop. After the loop it clears UHF_C_PORT_RESET again and returns that error if nonzero (so a failed clear after a timeout returns the clear error, not USB_ERR_TIMEOUT); then it returns USB_ERR_TIMEOUT if n is 0 (the wait timed out). Otherwise it pauses usb_port_reset_recovery ms and returns 0.

functions.name: usbd_req_warm_reset_port
functions.prose_contract: Performs a warm (BH) reset on a SuperSpeed hub port; returns a usb_error_t. It reads the port status (an error is returned). Only when the link state is U3, compliance mode, loopback or SS.Inactive does it continue; for any other link state it logs and returns 0 without doing anything. It tries to clear UHF_C_BH_PORT_RESET (error ignored), sets UHF_BH_PORT_RESET (error returned), then polls the status every usb_port_reset_delay ms: a status read error is returned; if the device is no longer connected it returns the current err, which is 0; if the BH reset change bit is set it leaves the loop; if the accumulated wait n exceeds 1000 ms it sets n to 0 and leaves. After the loop it clears UHF_C_BH_PORT_RESET and returns that error if nonzero (so that error wins over a timeout), then returns USB_ERR_TIMEOUT if n is 0, else pauses usb_port_reset_recovery ms and returns 0.

functions.name: usbd_callback_wrapper
functions.prose_contract: Runs the callback of the transfer at the head of a transfer queue (the 'done' queue command); static void. Precondition: the USB bus lock is held. If the queue is being recursed (recurse_3 != 0) or the transfer's xfer_mtx is not owned by the caller, and the system is not in polling mode, it postpones the work by signalling the done process (usb_proc_msignal) and returns, still holding the bus lock. Otherwise it clears done_q.curr, sets doing_callback, drops the bus lock and then: if the transfer is not transferring it sets usb_state to USB_ST_SETUP and, if it was not started, retakes the bus lock and goes to done without calling the callback; if it is transferring it calls usbd_callback_wrapper_sub(xfer); a nonzero result retakes the bus lock and goes to done without calling the callback; otherwise it releases the power reference (USB_HAVE_POWERD), clears transferring, sets usb_state to USB_ST_ERROR or USB_ST_TRANSFERRED and syncs DMA after a successful transfer. It then (with USB_HAVE_PF) taps the transfer when the state is not SETUP and calls xfer->callback(xfer, xfer->error). It retakes the bus lock; if the transfer is not open, is started and the state is USB_ST_ERROR (it was started after being cancelled) it clears doing_callback, requeues the transfer on done_q with usb_command_wrapper and returns without the drain check. At done it clears doing_callback, and if the transfer is draining and not transferring it clears draining and broadcasts cv_drain, then runs the next queued command with usb_command_wrapper(&info->done_q, info->done_q.curr) and returns.

functions.name: usbd_callback_wrapper_sub
functions.prose_contract: Post-processes a transfer before its callback is called; static uint8_t returning 1 to wait for a new callback or 0 to call the callback now. If the transfer is not open and not yet closed it calls the endpoint's close method under the bus lock, sets did_close and returns 1. If xfer->error is non-zero, the DMA delay has not been done, and the error is USB_ERR_CANCELLED or USB_ERR_TIMEOUT or the bus has a start_dma_delay method (so any error when that method exists), it sets did_dma_delay, clears can_cancel_immed, gets the DMA delay for the device and, when it is non-zero, starts the bus's DMA-delay handler or a timeout calling usb_dma_delay_done_cb and returns 1. It then limits aframes to nframes (panicking only if the error is 0), sums frlengths into actlen, zeroes the length of frames not transferred, and limits actlen to sumlen (panicking only if the error is 0). If there is an error it clears control_act, requests a TT buffer reset for errors other than normal completion, short transfer, stall or cancel (USB_HAVE_TT_SUPPORT), and for a non-cancel error on a pipe_bof transfer jumps to done and returns 0 without starting the next transfer. Without an error: a short actual length clears control_act and, when short transfers are not allowed, sets xfer->error to USB_ERR_SHORT_XFER (jumping to done and returning 0 for pipe_bof); a full-length transfer in the middle of an active control transfer (control_act) jumps to done and returns 0. Otherwise, if this transfer is the current one of its endpoint queue (stream_id), it runs the queue's command to start the next transfer and, when the queue is empty, clears the endpoint's is_synced flag. It returns 0.

functions.name: usbd_xfer_get_isochronous_start_frame
functions.prose_contract: Computes the next isochronous frame number at which the first packet of a transfer should be queued and updates the endpoint's schedule; uint8_t, returning non-zero when a discontinuity occurred and 0 in normal operation. delta = (endpoint->isoc_next - frame_curr) & frame_mask. If the endpoint is not synced (is_synced == 0), or delta is smaller than frame_ms + frame_min, or delta is larger than frame_mask / 2 (a negative delta), it resets isoc_next to (frame_curr + 2 * frame_ms + frame_min) & frame_mask, sets is_synced to 1 and returns 1; otherwise it returns 0. If p_frame_start is non-NULL it stores isoc_next & frame_mask in it (after the possible reset). It then computes the frame offset delta again (in units of frame_ms, with the current frame rounded down), selects shift = 3 for a full-speed device and usbd_xfer_get_fps_shift(xfer) otherwise, computes duration = ((nframes << shift) + 7) / 8, sets xfer->isoc_time_complete to the expanded current time plus the delta plus the duration, advances endpoint->isoc_next by duration * frame_ms (masked with frame_mask) and returns the retval computed above.

functions.name: mtw_fw_callback
functions.prose_contract: USB bulk-OUT callback used to download firmware to the MediaTek mtw chip, one chunk at a time; static void. It clears the transfer's private pointer. USB_ST_TRANSFERRED: adds actlen to sc->sc_sent and zeroes the first actlen bytes of the current firmware buffer txd_fw[sc_idx]; if actlen is below 0x2c44 and sc_idx is 0 it returns without submitting anything; if sc_idx is 3 it writes the interrupt vector block (mtw_write_ivb, logging a failure), waits 10 ms and polls the MCU DMA address register up to 100 times (10 ms apart) for MTW_MCU_READY: when ready it sets fwloading to 1 and stops polling, if the 100 tries are used up it sets fwloading to 0; it then wakes up waiters on fwloading and returns; otherwise if actlen equals 0x2c44 it increments sc_idx and delays 1 ms, and then continues into USB_ST_SETUP. USB_ST_SETUP: takes dlen from the length field of txd_fw[sc_idx], writes the MCU DMA address (0x40 + sc_sent) and length registers, sets frame 0 to the firmware buffer with length dlen and submits the transfer. On an error it prints a message, sets fwloading to 0 and wakes waiters; it does not resubmit. It returns void.

functions.name: mtw_vap_create
functions.prose_contract: Creates a net80211 vap for the mtw driver; returns the vap or NULL. It returns NULL (after a message) if sc->rvp_cnt is already at or above MTW_VAP_MAX. For IEEE80211_M_STA (also adding IEEE80211_CLONE_NOBEACONS), IBSS, monitor, hostap and mesh modes it returns NULL if the interface already has any vap; for WDS it needs an existing hostap vap (clearing the clone-BSSID flag) and otherwise returns NULL with a message; any other mode prints a message and returns NULL. It allocates the mtw_vap (M_WAITOK, zeroed) and calls ieee80211_vap_setup, freeing it and returning NULL if that fails. It then sets iv_update_beacon, iv_max_aid, the RX A-MPDU limit (both branches choose the 64K value) and density, the key set and delete hooks, saves the original iv_newstate in rvp->newstate and installs mtw_newstate (for IBSS it also hooks iv_recv_mgmt), initializes rate control (1 s interval) and calls ieee80211_vap_attach. It then takes the first free index of sc->rvp_bmap as rvp_id, increments rvp_cnt (setting ic_opmode to the mode for the first vap), sets cmdq_run to MTW_CMDQ_GO for hostap and returns the vap.

functions.name: rsu_rx_event
functions.prose_contract: Handles a firmware event received by the rsu driver; static void with the event code, buffer and length. It uses the first vap of the interface, which may be NULL. R92S_EVT_SURVEY calls rsu_event_survey. R92S_EVT_SURVEY_DONE logs and: if sc_extra_scan is 1 it clears it and, when a vap exists and rsu_site_survey(sc, NULL) fails, drops the lock and cancels the scan (ieee80211_cancel_scan) and in any case then ends the case without calling scan_done; otherwise, when a vap exists, it drops the lock and calls ieee80211_scan_done(vap); with a NULL vap it does nothing further. R92S_EVT_JOIN_BSS calls rsu_event_join_bss only when vap->iv_state is IEEE80211_S_AUTH (vap is dereferenced without a NULL check). R92S_EVT_DEL_STA logs and, when the vap is in RUN state and the event's address equals the BSS id, drops the lock and moves the vap to IEEE80211_S_SCAN (also dereferencing vap unchecked). R92S_EVT_WPS_PBC only logs; R92S_EVT_FWDBG terminates the buffer at byte 60 and logs it; R92S_EVT_ADDBA_REQ_REPORT calls rsu_event_addba_req_report; any other code prints 'unhandled code'.

functions.name: rum_newstate
functions.prose_contract: net80211 state-change method for a rum vap; static int. Precondition: the caller holds the net80211 com lock; the function releases it, takes the driver lock, and retakes the com lock before returning. It stops the rate-control callout. If leaving IEEE80211_S_SLEEP in station mode it clears the ACK/CTS power-management and auto-wakeup bits and sets power state 0 (errors ignored). Then by new state: INIT aborts the TSF sync if the old state was RUN; RUN (unless it comes from SLEEP, already handled) refs the BSS node and, for non-monitor vaps, fails with EINVAL when the BSS channel or the node channel is IEEE80211_CHAN_ANYC, otherwise updates slot time, MRR, TX preamble, basic rates and max retry and sets the BSSID; for hostap and IBSS it calls rum_alloc_beacon (nonzero result becomes the return value and ends the case); for non-monitor, non-ahdemo vaps it calls rum_enable_tsf_sync (a nonzero result is likewise returned), else rum_enable_tsf; when the channel's unicast rate is not fixed it starts rate control; SLEEP, for station vaps only, sets the auto-wakeup and ACK/CTS power-management bits (a USB error gives EIO) and calls rum_set_power_state(sc, 1) whose nonzero result is returned. It then releases the driver lock, retakes the com lock and returns ret if non-zero, else the result of the saved rvp->newstate(vap, nstate, arg).

functions.name: urtw_8187b_cmd_reset
functions.prose_contract: Resets the RTL8187B command register block; static usb_error_t. It reads URTW_CMD, keeps bit 0x2 and sets URTW_CMD_RST, writes it back, then polls up to 20 times (2 ms pause each) reading URTW_CMD until the reset bit clears; if it is still set after 20 tries it prints 'reset timeout'. The register accessors set the local error variable and jump to the fail label on a USB error, and the fail label returns error. The function therefore returns the error of the last register access: the USB error code if a read or write failed, and the value of the last successful access (0) otherwise, so the reset timeout case also returns 0 (the message is only printed).

functions.name: vge_attach
functions.prose_contract: Attach routine of the VIA Velocity (vge) Ethernet driver; returns 0 or an errno. It initializes the softc mutex and watchdog callout, maps the memory BAR (ENXIO if it cannot), looks up the PCI Express and power-management capabilities, tries to allocate a single MSI (falling back to INTx), allocates the IRQ (ENXIO if it cannot), resets the chip, waits up to VGE_TIMEOUT iterations for the EEPROM reload bit to clear, reads the station address from the EEPROM, allocates the DMA resources with vge_dma_alloc (an error goes to fail), sets up the ifnet, attaches the PHY with mii_attach (an error goes to fail), calls ether_ifattach and sets up the interrupt handler with bus_setup_intr (an error goes to fail). Every failure reaches the fail label, which, when error is non-zero, calls vge_detach(dev) to release whatever was acquired so far, and then returns the error; vge_detach checks each resource before releasing it, but it does not free the sysctl nodes created earlier in attach.

functions.name: vge_poll
functions.prose_contract: DEVICE_POLLING handler of the vge driver; returns the number of received packets from the first receive pass (rx_npkts). It takes the softc lock. If IFF_DRV_RUNNING is not set it goes to done and returns 0. Otherwise it runs vge_rxeof(sc, count) (its result is the return value), vge_txeof, and vge_start_locked when the send queue is non-empty. For cmd == POLL_AND_CHECK_STATUS it reads VGE_ISR: a value of 0xFFFFFFFF goes to done; a non-zero status is written back to VGE_ISR to acknowledge it (a zero status is not written); a TX or RX DMA stall clears IFF_DRV_RUNNING and re-initializes the chip with vge_init_locked; an RX overflow or no-descriptor status runs a second vge_rxeof(sc, count), whose packet count is ignored (not added to the return value) and restarts the receive queue. It unlocks and returns rx_npkts.

functions.name: edid_parse
functions.prose_contract: Parses a 128-byte EDID block into a struct edid_info; int, returns 0 on success or -1. It returns -1 without writing anything if edid_is_valid(data) returns non-zero (invalid EDID). Otherwise it fills the vendor id string, product id, vendor and product names (from the lookup tables, or empty strings), the serial number string, manufacture week and year, EDID version and revision, video input, maximum horizontal and vertical size, gamma, features, the chromaticity coordinates (note that ec_redy is assigned EDID_CHROMA_REDX(data), not REDY, so the red-y value is wrong), and the extension block count. It builds the mode list: the established timings (looked up in the standard mode list), the standard timings (each not already present), and the detailed timing and descriptor blocks with edid_block, trims trailing whitespace from the name, serial and comment strings, computes the maximum pixel clock over the modes and, when the monitor has range limits, raises er_max_clock to cover it, and returns 0.

functions.name: vmd_attach
functions.prose_contract: Attach routine of the Intel VMD (volume management device) bridge; returns 0 or ENXIO. It zeroes the softc, sets the PCI domain to PCI_DOMAINMAX minus the unit and enables bus mastering. It allocates up to VMD_MAX_BAR memory BARs (stepping over the high half of 64-bit BARs); a failure prints 'Cannot allocate resources' and goes to fail. It finds the device entry for the vendor and device id, computes the bus range (restricting the start bus to 0, 128 or 224 when the device has the BUS_RESTRICT capability and the config register says so, failing on an unknown offset) and sets up the bus-number rman and the memory-window rman from the BARs (each failure goes to fail). It then sets the MSI-X handling: when vmd_bypass_msi is set and the device can bypass MSI it sets vmd_msix_count to 0 and enables MSI bypass; otherwise, if pci_alloc_msix succeeds it allocates an irq entry per vector, allocating each IRQ and setting up vmd_intr on it (a failure goes to fail) and disables MSI bypass; if pci_alloc_msix fails it neither installs handlers nor enables bypass and attach continues. It then sets the DMA tag, adds the pci child, attaches children and returns 0. The fail label calls vmd_free(sc) and returns ENXIO.

functions.name: get_memseg
functions.prose_contract: Returns information about a bhyve memory segment; static int. It calls vm_get_memseg(sc->vm, mseg->segid, &mseg->len, &sysmem, NULL); this call can write mseg->len, including on a path where it then fails. If it returns an error, or the segment length is 0, it returns that error (0 for a zero length) without touching mseg->name. For a non-system-memory segment it searches the softc's devmem list for the entry with the same segid; the entry is only asserted to exist (KASSERT, active only in debug builds): there is no EINVAL return for a missing entry, and without the assertion the following dsc->name access would use a NULL pointer. It then copies the device name into mseg->name with copystr (at most len bytes, result returned). For a system memory segment it zeroes len bytes of mseg->name. It returns the resulting error.

functions.name: vmci_queue_pair_alloc_guest_work
functions.prose_contract: Allocates or attaches to a guest-side VMCI queue pair; returns VMCI_SUCCESS or a VMCI error code. It returns VMCI_ERROR_NO_ACCESS if priv_flags is not VMCI_NO_PRIVILEGE_FLAGS. It takes the guest endpoints mutex. If the guest is hibernating and the flags do not include VMCI_QPFLAG_LOCAL it returns VMCI_ERROR_UNAVAILABLE (this check precedes the lookup of an existing entry). If an entry for the handle already exists: for a local queue pair with ref_count above 1 it returns VMCI_ERROR_UNAVAILABLE; if the sizes or flags (ignoring ATTACH_ONLY) do not match it returns VMCI_ERROR_QUEUEPAIR_MISMATCH; otherwise it notifies the peer locally, and on success it reuses the existing queues swapped (produce and consume exchanged) and jumps to out; for a non-local existing entry it returns VMCI_ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS. Without an entry it allocates the produce and consume queues (VMCI_ERROR_NO_MEM on failure), creates the endpoint, and allocates the PPN set; for a local pair it checks the handle's context and peer against the current context (VMCI_ERROR_NO_ACCESS) and rejects ATTACH_ONLY (VMCI_ERROR_NOT_FOUND), for a non-local pair it makes the allocation hypercall; failures free the endpoint or the queues and return the code. It then adds the entry to the list, and at out increments ref_count, stores the handle and the queue pointers for the caller, initializes the queue headers for a newly created local pair (ref_count 1), releases the mutex and returns VMCI_SUCCESS. The error_keep_entry exits keep the existing entry.

functions.name: vt_parse_rgb_triplet
functions.prose_contract: Parses a colour given as '#rrggbb' or as three decimal components; int, 0 on success or -1. If the string starts with '#' its total length must be exactly 7 (otherwise -1); the 6 characters after '#' are parsed with strtoul base 16 and must be consumed completely (a non-empty end remainder gives -1), so strtoul's own conventions apply (a leading sign, white space or 0x prefix inside those 6 characters is accepted when it fits); r, g and b are set from bits 23-16, 15-8 and 7-0 and it returns 0. For the decimal form it parses three numbers with strtoul base 10 separated by commas or spaces: if a number has no digits or is above 255 it returns -1 (a negative number wraps to a large unsigned value and fails, except '-0' or '-00', which parse as 0); *r is stored after the first number and *g after the second, before the later parts are checked, and *b after the third, so on a later failure (including trailing garbage after the third number) the earlier outputs may already have been written. After the third number only spaces are skipped and any other remaining character gives -1; otherwise it returns 0.

functions.name: vt_mouse_event
functions.prose_contract: Handles a mouse event for the vt console; void. It uses the main device's current window and font. It returns without doing anything if the window has VWF_MOUSE_HIDE or VWF_GRAPHICS set or has no font (text mode). If vw_mouse_level > 0 it first forwards the event to the terminal with vt_mouse_terminput. For MOUSE_ACTION and MOUSE_MOTION_EVENT it adds x and y to the stored pointer position, clamps it to the screen size (columns times font width, rows times font height) in vd_mx/vd_my, extends the selection mark with VTB_MARK_MOVE when button 1 or the extend button is down, resumes the flush timer and returns (without touching vd_mstate). For MOUSE_BUTTON_EVENT it handles event: MOUSE_BUTTON1DOWN chooses a mark from cnt % 4 (end, start, word, row); VT_MOUSE_PASTEBUTTON, for non-zero cnt, calls vt_mouse_paste and sets a start mark at the pointer, and in every case returns before updating vd_mstate; VT_MOUSE_EXTENDBUTTON chooses VTB_MARK_EXTEND (or VTB_MARK_NONE for a release while button 1 is down); other events return. For the button and extend events it sets or clears the event bit in vd_mstate according to cnt > 0, applies the mark with vtbuf_set_mark at the pointer cell, and, if that returns 1, resumes the flush timer, then for end, word, row and extend marks continues, else returns; it takes the marked length and returns if it is 0 or less, grows the paste buffer when needed (M_WAITOK) and extracts the marked text into it, setting the paste length.

functions.name: vtterm_ioctl
functions.prose_contract: Terminal ioctl handler of the vt console; returns 0, an errno or ENOIOCTL. It first maps a set of old-style ioctl numbers (_IO('v', 4..6), _IO('K', ...), _IO('c', ...)) to their current commands, then switches on cmd. Keyboard-map and keyboard-info commands (KDSETRAD after a range check, GIO/PIO_KEYMAP, dead keys, function keys, KDGKBINFO, KDGKBTYPE, repeat rates, KBADDKBD, KBRELKBD) are passed to the current keyboard with kbdd_ioctl and its error returned (ENODEV for KDGKBTYPE with no handler). KDGKBSTATE, KDSKBSTATE, KDGETLED, KDSETLED, KDGKBMODE and KDSKBMODE read or update the window's saved keyboard state, LEDs or mode, validating the values (EINVAL for bits outside the mask or an unknown mode) and updating the hardware keyboard when the window is the current one. FBIO_* commands go to the driver's vd_fb_ioctl when present; CONS_* commands handle blank time, history size (EINVAL out of range), clear history, window info (EINVAL for a wrong vid_info size), bell type, version, mode info and mouse control (EINVAL for an unknown operation). PIO_VFONT returns ENOTSUP in text mode, otherwise loads and applies a font; GIO_SCRNMAP fills an identity map; KDSETMODE switches between text and graphics; KDENABIO requires PRIV_IO and a securelevel check; CONS_SETKBD, CONS_RELKBD, VT_ACTIVATE (EINVAL for a bad window number), VT_GETACTIVE, VT_GETINDEX, VT_LOCKSWITCH (EINVAL for values other than 1 and 2), VT_OPENQRY (EINVAL when none is free), VT_WAITACTIVE (EINVAL for a too large index) and the VT_SETMODE, VT_GETMODE and VT_RELDISP screen-switch commands are handled as shown: VT_SETMODE to VT_AUTO sets VT_AUTO and calls finish_vt_rel and finish_vt_acq, ignoring their results, and returns 0; VT_SETMODE to VT_PROCESS validates the signals (EINVAL) and the owning process (EPERM); VT_RELDISP returns EINVAL when the window is not the current VT_PROCESS window and EPERM for another process, and otherwise returns the error of finish_vt_rel or finish_vt_acq. Unknown commands return ENOIOCTL.

functions.name: vt_window_switch
functions.prose_contract: Makes the given window the current vt window; returns 0 or EINVAL. If a window switch is already in progress and the kernel has panicked it returns 0 immediately. It sets inside_vt_window_switch. If the debugger is active it does not take locks: for a window that is neither opened nor the console it clears the flag and returns EINVAL; otherwise it sets vd_curwindow to the window, marks the device VDF_INVALID, calls the driver's vd_postswitch if present, clears the flag and returns 0, without suspending or resuming the flush timer, broadcasting the window-switch condition variable or updating the keyboard state. Otherwise it takes VT_LOCK: if the window is already the current one it only calls vd_postswitch when the debugger is active or the kernel has panicked, then unlocks, clears the flag and returns 0 (no VDF_INVALID and no switch); if the window is neither opened nor the console it unlocks, clears the flag and returns EINVAL; else it suspends the flush timer, sets vd_curwindow, marks VDF_INVALID, broadcasts vd_winswitch, unlocks, calls vd_postswitch, resumes the flush timer, and under Giant saves the old window's keyboard state (when its kbd mode is K_XLATE) and updates the keyboard mode and state for the new window; it clears the flag and returns 0.

functions.name: vt_processkey
functions.prose_contract: Processes one key code from the keyboard for the current vt window; returns 0. It feeds the code to the random harvester. With VT_ALT_TO_ESC_HACK, a key release (RELKEY): for the left Alt, or for the right Alt when vt_enable_altgr is 0 (the right Alt case falls through into the left Alt case), it clears ALKED in vd_kbstate; for the right Alt with altgr enabled it breaks without clearing; every release then returns 0 without further processing. A key press of the left Alt (or right Alt with altgr disabled) sets ALKED. Without the hack any release simply returns 0. It then calls vt_machine_kbdevent(vd, c); if that consumes the key it returns 0. In scroll mode (VWF_SCROLL) it passes the key to vt_scrollmode_kbdevent and returns 0. For special keys (SPCLKEY): the window-select keys switch to the corresponding window through vt_proc_window_switch and return 0, NEXT and PREV switch to the next or previous window (modulo VT_MAXWINDOWS) and return 0, SLK toggles scroll-lock mode of the window (saving the keyboard state, enabling or disabling scroll mode and scrolling to the end on disable), and back-tab, function and cursor keys are sent to the terminal as special keys. For an ordinary key (no flags): in K_XLATE mode it sends ESC first when ALKED is set (with the hack), calls kdb_alt_break when KDB is defined and sends the character with terminal_input_char; in the other modes it passes the raw code with terminal_input_raw. It returns 0.

functions.name: wg_decrypt
functions.prose_contract: Decrypts one received WireGuard data packet; static void. It takes the remote from the packet's keypair and the owning peer from it, reads the nonce from the data header and strips that header with m_adj, then calls noise_keypair_decrypt; a failure goes to out with state WG_PACKET_DEAD. A decrypted packet of length 0 is a keepalive: it logs and goes to out with state WG_PACKET_CRYPTED, without trimming or resetting the mbuf. Otherwise determine_af_and_pullup sets the address family: for IPv4 it looks up the allowed peer from the source address, takes the IP length from the header and trims the mbuf to it with m_adj only when that length is at least the IP header size and smaller than the packet length; for IPv6 it looks up the source address, computes payload length plus header and trims only when that is smaller than the packet length; a packet that is neither IPv4 nor IPv6 logs and goes to out as dead. It releases the reference on the allowed peer's remote if one was returned; if the allowed peer is not the sending peer it logs 'unallowed src IP' and goes to out as dead; otherwise it resets the mbuf (wg_mbuf_reset) and sets state WG_PACKET_CRYPTED. At out it stores the mbuf in pkt->p_mbuf, publishes the state with a release store, enqueues the peer's receive group task and drops the reference on the remote.

functions.name: wg_peer_send_staged
functions.prose_contract: Encrypts and sends the packets staged on a WireGuard peer; static void. It takes all packets off the peer's stage queue into a local list (wg_queue_delist_staged); if the list is empty it returns. It gets the peer's current keypair; if there is none, or if assigning the next nonce to any packet fails (noise_keypair_nonce_next), it releases the keypair (when held) and puts all the packets back on the stage queue (wg_queue_enlist_staged) and calls wg_timers_event_want_initiation(peer), so the stage queue is not left empty on that path. Otherwise it gives every packet a reference on the keypair and queues it on both the encrypt-parallel and the peer's encrypt-serial queue with wg_queue_both; a packet for which that fails is dropped (the OQDROPS counter is incremented) and is not returned to the stage queue and does not trigger an initiation. It then calls wg_encrypt_dispatch(sc), releases the keypair and returns.

functions.name: noise_consume_response
functions.prose_contract: Processes a received WireGuard handshake response on the initiator side; returns 0 or an errno (EINVAL initially). It looks up the remote by its local index r_idx (returning EINVAL if not found), takes the identity lock for reading and fails if the local identity is not set. It reads the handshake under the handshake read lock: the handshake state must be HANDSHAKE_INITIATOR (otherwise error) and it copies the pre-shared key and the handshake state. It then mixes in the ephemeral key, performs the two Diffie-Hellman mixes (a failed mix goes to error_zero), mixes the PSK and decrypts the (empty) payload with its tag (failure goes to error_zero). It then takes the handshake write lock and, only if the state is still HANDSHAKE_INITIATOR and the local index still equals r_idx, stores the new handshake state and the remote index s_idx and calls noise_begin_session; ret is that call's result (so a failing begin_session returns its own error code rather than EINVAL), and on success *rp is set to a new reference on the remote. If the state check at that point fails ret stays EINVAL. In all exit paths after the lookup it wipes the secret material, releases the identity lock and drops the lookup reference on r with noise_remote_put (also on success, where *rp holds its own reference).

functions.name: xdma_process
functions.prose_contract: Builds a scatter/gather list from the queued xdma requests; int, returns the number of segments added to sg (n) or -1. Precondition: the channel is locked (XCHAN_ASSERT_LOCKED) and sg points to an array of struct xdma_sglist entries. It asks the DMA controller for its capacity with XDMA_CHANNEL_CAPACITY; a non-zero result prints a message and returns -1. It then walks the channel's input queue: for an mbuf request it defragments it (xdma_mbuf_defrag) when the channel has XCHAN_CAP_NOSEG or the previous segment count exceeds maxnsegs, other request types count as 1 segment; it stops when the engine capacity is not larger than (count + n) or when n + count + maxnsegs reaches XDMA_SGLIST_MAXLEN; it loads the request's data into a local bus_dma_segment array (xdma_load_data), stopping if no segments result, adds those segments to sg[n] with the request pointer (xdma_sglist_add), and moves the request from queue_in to the processing queue under their locks. It returns n (0 when nothing could be queued).

functions.name: xl_start_locked
functions.prose_contract: Starts transmission on a 3Com 3c90x (xl) Ethernet interface in the non-90xB descriptor mode; static void. Precondition: the driver lock is held (XL_LOCK_ASSERT). It returns at once unless IFF_DRV_RUNNING is set and IFF_DRV_OACTIVE is clear. If there is no free transmit descriptor it runs xl_txeoc and xl_txeof to reclaim descriptors, and if there is still none sets IFF_DRV_OACTIVE and returns. It then dequeues packets while the send queue is non-empty and descriptors remain: for each it calls xl_encap into the next free descriptor; on an encapsulation error it undoes that descriptor and either stops (mbuf consumed) or sets IFF_DRV_OACTIVE, puts the mbuf back at the head of the send queue and stops; on success it removes the descriptor from the free list, links it to the previous one (software and hardware next pointers) and passes the frame to BPF. If no packet was queued it returns. It sets the download-interrupt bit in the last descriptor, stalls the download engine (XL_CMD_DOWN_STALL, xl_wait), and appends the chain to the existing transmit list (clearing the interrupt request in the old tail) or starts a new list; it syncs the DMA map for PREWRITE, writes XL_DOWNLIST_PTR with the start of the chain if that register is 0, unstalls the download engine, selects register window 7, sets xl_wdog_timer to 5 and enqueues xl_task on the software-interrupt taskqueue (to flush the receive ring).

functions.name: xl_setmode
functions.prose_contract: Selects the transceiver and duplex for a 3Com xl adapter; static void. Precondition: the softc lock is held (XL_LOCK_ASSERT). It reads the media status register (register window 4) and the internal config register (window 3). Then, for each media option the card reports in sc->xl_media, if the requested media subtype matches: 10baseT (XL_MEDIAOPT_BT, IFM_10_T) sets xl_xcvr to 10BT, rewrites the connector bits of icfg and sets the link-beat and jabber-guard bits and clears SQE enable; 100baseFX (XL_MEDIAOPT_BFX, IFM_100_FX) sets xl_xcvr to 100BFX, the connector bits, sets link-beat and clears SQE enable; AUI (IFM_10_5) or 10baseFL (IFM_10_FL) with XL_MEDIAOPT_AUI or 10FL set xl_xcvr to AUI, the connector bits, clear link-beat and jabber-guard and set mediastat |= ~XL_MEDIASTAT_SQEENB (an OR with the complement, which sets every bit except SQE enable); 10base2 (XL_MEDIAOPT_BNC, IFM_10_2) sets xl_xcvr to COAX, the connector bits and clears link-beat, jabber-guard and SQE enable (its message string is 'AUI port'). The code has no branches for 10baseT4, MII or 100baseTX, and when nothing matches the message string stays empty (it does not say 'unknown'). It then writes the MAC duplex bit through window 3: set for full duplex or 100baseFX, cleared otherwise; issues XL_CMD_COAX_START for 10base2 and XL_CMD_COAX_STOP otherwise; writes icfg to the internal config register and mediastat to the media status register (window 4), waits 800 us, selects window 7 and prints 'selecting <media>, <full|half> duplex' with the chosen strings.

functions.name: gdb_trap
functions.prose_contract: Command loop of the GDB remote stub once the kernel debugger has stopped on a trap; returns 1 when the target should resume or the connection ended, and 0 when the packet loop ends. It saves the current kdb jump buffer with kdb_jmpbuf(jb); if a longjmp back to this setjmp happens (an error in the receive path) it sets gdb_listening to 0, restores the saved jump buffer and returns 1. It clears gdb_listening, sends the stop reply with the signal for (type, code) and records the stop reason, then reads packets while gdb_rx_begin() returns 0.
