'?' replies with the signal; 'c' and 'C' (the latter only when the signal and ';' parse) set the PC register when an address was given, set gdb_listening to 1 and return 1; 's' and 'S' do the same for single stepping and return 1; 'D' replies OK, calls gdb_handle_detach and returns 1; 'k' calls gdb_handle_detach and returns 1; 'g' and 'p' return register values; 'G' and 'P' write registers (EINVAL for a bad format, OK otherwise); 'H' selects a thread (EINVAL for a bad id, ENOENT when not found, OK otherwise); 'm' reads memory (EINVAL for a bad command, EIO when the read fails); 'M' writes memory (EINVAL for a bad command, EIO when the write fails); 'q' answers queries or an empty reply when the CPU-specific query does not handle it; 'Q' handles StartNoAckMode (OK or empty reply depending on a feature flag) and otherwise an empty reply; 'T' replies OK if the thread exists and ENOENT otherwise (EINVAL for a bad id); 'z' and 'Z' remove and insert watchpoints; end of input and unknown commands get an empty reply. When gdb_rx_begin() returns non-zero it restores the saved jump buffer (kdb_jmpbuf(prev_jb)) and returns 0.

functions.name: pax_enforce_tpe
functions.prose_contract: Checks Trusted Path Execution for a program being executed; returns 0 or an errno. It returns EDOOFUS if td, vn or path is NULL. It returns 0 if TPE is disabled in the thread's prison or _pax_tpe_active says TPE does not apply to the thread (exempt flag, or the group test with tpe_all, tpe_gid and tpe_negate). It finds the last '/' in path: EDOOFUS if there is none, and 0 if the slash is the last character (strlen of the part from the slash is below 2, i.e. empty file name). It copies the text before the last slash into parent_path, locks vn shared (the VOP_LOCK error is returned) and reads its attributes: a VOP_GETATTR error is returned with vn still locked; otherwise vn is unlocked and the attributes are checked with _pax_tpe_vap(..., S_IWGRP | S_IWOTH), whose EPERM (root-owned and user-owned rules, owner-write bit for non-root owners, group/other write bits) is returned. It then looks up the parent directory with namei (LOOKUP, FOLLOW | LOCKLEAF), returning its error, gets the parent's attributes and applies the same check, unlocks the parent vnode and frees the path buffer, and returns the error of that check (0 when all pass). after parent_path is allocated, every return path frees it.

functions.name: pax_segvguard_segfault
functions.prose_contract: Records a segmentation fault of the process's executable for the segvguard feature; returns 0 or EFAULT. It returns 0 at once if segvguard is not active for the process. It returns EFAULT if td->td_proc->p_textvp is NULL. Otherwise it takes the current uptime, looks the vnode up in the segvguard table (pax_segvguard_lookup, which fills a vattr with VOP_GETATTR and may fail, returning NULL, in which case the vattr is only partly filled), and: if there is no entry it calls pax_segvguard_add(td, v, sbt, &vap), whose result is ignored (the allocation uses M_NOWAIT and can fail, in which case no entry is inserted); if an entry exists and both its expiry and its suspension deadline are in the past it logs, resets the crash count to 1, sets a new expiry and clears the suspension, and returns 0 at that point; otherwise it increments the crash count and, when it reaches pax_segvguard_maxcrashes, logs, sets the suspension deadline, zeroes the crash count and clears the expiry. It returns 0. The hash-bucket lock is taken and released inside the lookup and add helpers, not here.

functions.name: acpi_sleep_machdep
functions.prose_contract: Machine-dependent part of entering an ACPI sleep state on i386; returns -1, 0 or 1. It returns -1 immediately when sc->acpi_wakeaddr is 0 (no wake memory could be allocated). With SMP it prepares the set of other CPUs to suspend (all CPUs but the current one). It acquires the speaker timer when acpi_resume_beep is non-zero, sets the firmware waking vector to sc->acpi_wakephys, calls intr_suspend and saves the context into the first suspend pcb with savectx. In the branch taken when savectx returns non-zero it saves the FPU state, suspends the other CPUs (printing 'Failed to suspend APs' and returning 0 if that fails), patches the wake code variables (resume beep, reset video, EFER when NX is supported, CR4, pcb pointer, GDT limit and base), remaps low memory with pmap_remap_lowptdi(true) and enters the sleep state (AcpiEnterSleepStateS4bios when state is S4 and sc->acpi_s4bios is set, otherwise AcpiEnterSleepState), printing a message and returning 0 on failure. If the sleep call returns and acpi_susp_bounce is set it calls resumectx(pcb); otherwise it spins in a pause loop waiting for the system to power down. The other branch (reached after the machine resumes through the saved context) re-initializes the console with cnresume, restores the FPU state and returns 1 (woken up successfully).

functions.name: bios16
functions.prose_contract: Calls a 16-bit BIOS entry point from i386 protected mode; returns an errno or the value returned by bios16_call. The fmt string describes the variadic arguments: 'p' (32-bit pointer, also tracks the lowest and highest pointer and sets the args flag), 'i' (32-bit integer), 'U', 'D' and 'C' (16-bit selectors for the BIOS utility, data and code segments) and 's' (16-bit integer); any other character returns EINVAL (in either pass over fmt). In the first pass it computes the stack size needed starting 32 bytes below the page end (padding the top of the stack). If a pointer argument was given and the span between the lowest and highest pointer exceeds 16 pages it returns EACCES; otherwise it sets the args segment base to the lowest pointer and limit 0xffff, sets the 32-bit code segment base from bios16_jmp, enters the BIOS pmap with pmap_bios16_enter and, in the second pass, builds the argument frame on that stack (pointers become offsets from the lowest pointer plus the args selector). It sets the BIOS selectors, loads the call vector with the entry offset and the 16-bit code selector, calls bios16_call(&args->r, stack_top), leaves the BIOS pmap and returns the call's value.

functions.name: bios_oem_strings
functions.prose_contract: Collects OEM identification strings from the BIOS ROM area into buffer; returns the string length or a negative code. It returns -1 if oem or buffer is NULL or maxlen is below 2, -2 if there is no signature list, and -3 if the search range is empty or outside the BIOS area (BIOS_START to BIOS_START + BIOS_SIZE). For each signature (anchor, offset, totlen) it returns -4 after printing a message if the offset range is outside the BIOS area, or -5 after printing a message if the string would not fit in maxlen - 1 bytes. It scans the BIOS memory for the anchor text from the start of the range up to to - len, and for the first match copies tot bytes starting at the given offset into buffer, replacing characters outside 0x20-0x7E by spaces, dropping leading spaces and collapsing runs of spaces. After all signatures it removes one trailing space (when more than one character was stored), terminates the buffer with NUL and returns idx, the number of characters stored.

functions.name: initializecpu
functions.prose_contract: Applies CPU-specific initialization on i386 for the CPU being brought up; void. It switches on the detected cpu type: the old 486-class parts call their init routines (init_bluelightning, init_486dlc, init_cy486dx, init_5x86, init_6x86, and for a 486 on a 386 init_i486_on_386); 586-class parts depend on the vendor (AMD K5/K6 write-allocate enabling and a TSC-through-suspend MSR bit for family 0xa0, Centaur init_winchip, Transmeta init_transmeta, Rise init_rise); 686-class parts depend on the vendor (Intel init_ppro or init_mendocino for specific steppings, AMD optional SSE enabling via the HWCR MSR for some models and, for families 0xf and 0x10 without a hypervisor, setting cpu_amdc1e_bug, Centaur init_via, Transmeta init_transmeta); other types do nothing. It then, for all CPUs that have SSE and FXSR, sets CR4_FXSR | CR4_XMM and sets cpu_fxsr and hw_instruction_sse to 1; if elf32_nxstack is set it sets EFER_NXE in the EFER MSR; and if the CPU has RDTSCP or RDPID it writes MSR_TSC_AUX with cpu_auxmsr(), which asserts (KASSERT) that interrupts are disabled and returns the CPU id. Interrupts need to be disabled only for that last step (the assertion), not for the rest.

functions.name: __CONCAT(PMTYPE, pinit0)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function pmap_pae_pinit0 or pmap_nopae_pinit0 (named by the __CONCAT(PMTYPE, pinit0) definition head): initializes the pmap of process 0 (statically allocated, already using the boot page directory); void. It initializes the pmap mutex (PMAP_LOCK_INIT), sets pm_pdir to IdlePTD (and, in the PAE build, pm_pdpt to IdlePDPT), initializes the page-table-page radix tree, clears pm_active, initializes the pv chunk list, zeroes pm_stats and calls pmap_activate_boot(pmap). It allocates no memory and returns nothing.

functions.name: __CONCAT(PMTYPE, pinit)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function pmap_pae_pinit or pmap_nopae_pinit (named by the __CONCAT(PMTYPE, pinit) head): initializes a preallocated, zeroed pmap; returns 1 on success and 0 if the page-directory kernel virtual address cannot be allocated. Only when pmap->pm_pdir is NULL it allocates NBPTD bytes of KVA for it (returning 0 if that fails), in the PAE build allocates the PDPT from pdptzone (M_WAITOK|M_ZERO, with debug assertions on alignment and 4 GB placement), and initializes the page-table-page radix tree; when pm_pdir is already set it only asserts (KASSERT) that the radix tree is empty. It then allocates the NPGPTD page-directory pages (wired, zeroed, VM_ALLOC_WAITOK, so they cannot fail), fills the PDPT entries for PAE, maps the pages at pm_pdir with pmap_qenter, in the PAE build flushes the PDPT from the cache when the CPU has no PAT, copies the TRPTDI kernel page-directory entry from PTD, clears pm_active, initializes the pv chunk list, zeroes pm_stats and returns 1.

functions.name: __CONCAT(PMTYPE, growkernel)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function pmap_pae_growkernel or pmap_nopae_growkernel (named by the __CONCAT(PMTYPE, growkernel) head): grows the kernel page tables so kernel virtual addresses up to addr are mapped; returns KERN_SUCCESS or KERN_RESOURCE_SHORTAGE. Precondition: the kernel map's system mutex is held (mtx_assert). It rounds addr up to a multiple of NBPDR and limits it to vm_map_max(kernel_map). While kernel_vm_end is below addr: if the page-directory entry for kernel_vm_end is already present it advances kernel_vm_end by one NBPDR (limited to the map maximum, ending the loop there) and continues; otherwise it allocates a wired, zeroed page table page (VM_ALLOC_INTERRUPT | NOFREE | WIRED | ZERO), returning KERN_RESOURCE_SHORTAGE if none is available, sets its pindex, increments nkpt, installs the new page-directory entry in the kernel page directory and in all pmaps with pmap_kenter_pde, and advances kernel_vm_end (again limited to the map maximum). It returns KERN_SUCCESS when the loop ends.

functions.name: __CONCAT(PMTYPE, protect)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function pmap_pae_protect or pmap_nopae_protect (head __CONCAT(PMTYPE, protect)): reduces the access permissions of the mappings in [sva, eva) of a pmap; void. With prot == VM_PROT_NONE it calls pmap_remove(pmap, sva, eva) and returns. Otherwise, in the PAE build it returns without changes when both write and execute are requested; in the non-PAE build it returns without changes when write is requested (such a request would not reduce permissions). If the pmap is not the current one it takes the global pv-list lock and pins the thread. For each page-directory range it skips absent page directory entries; for a large (PG_PS) mapping it protects it as a unit with pmap_protect_pde when the range covers the whole large page, otherwise it takes the pv lock (restarting the whole operation if it cannot be taken without blocking) and demotes the mapping, continuing if the demotion destroyed the mapping. For each valid PTE it clears PG_RW and PG_M when write is not requested (calling vm_page_dirty first for a managed, modified, writable page); in the PAE build it sets the NX bit when execute is not requested and i386_read_exec is not set; if the entry changed it stores it with an atomic compare-and-set (retrying on conflict), invalidates the page at once when it was a global mapping, and otherwise remembers that TLB entries must be flushed (flushed for the whole pmap at the end). It releases the pmap lock, unpins and releases the pv lock when it was taken.

functions.name: __CONCAT(PMTYPE, enter_object)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function pmap_pae_enter_object or pmap_nopae_enter_object (head __CONCAT(PMTYPE, enter_object)): maps the resident pages of an object, starting at m_start, into [start, end) of a pmap with the given protection; void. Precondition: the caller holds the object's lock (asserted with VM_OBJECT_ASSERT_LOCKED on m_start->object); the lock stays held. It iterates the object's pages from m_start->pindex up to a limit of m_start->pindex + atop(end - start) (the page at the limit pindex is not included), taking the global pv-list lock and the pmap lock for the whole loop. For each page it computes va = start + ptoa(pindex - m_start->pindex); if va is large-page aligned, a whole large page fits below end, the page has psind 1 and super pages are enabled, it tries pmap_enter_4mpage: on KERN_SUCCESS or KERN_NO_SPACE it jumps NBPDR / PAGE_SIZE pages ahead in the iterator (so on KERN_NO_SPACE the skipped pages are not mapped individually); otherwise it maps the single page with pmap_enter_quick_locked, passing the previous page-table page as a hint, and steps to the next page. Only resident pages found by the iterator are mapped (holes are skipped). It then releases the pmap and global locks.

functions.name: __CONCAT(PMTYPE, enter_quick)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function pmap_pae_enter_quick or pmap_nopae_enter_quick (head __CONCAT(PMTYPE, enter_quick)): quickly maps one resident page m at va in a pmap with the given protection; void. It takes the global pv-list write lock and the pmap lock, calls pmap_enter_quick_locked(pmap, va, m, prot, NULL), ignoring its result, and releases both locks. The mapping is created only if the helper succeeds: pmap_enter_quick_locked returns NULL without mapping (and drops the page-table-page reference it took) when a large page already covers the address, when allocating a page table page fails (no sleeping), when the PTE already holds a mapping, or when a pv entry cannot be inserted for a managed page; otherwise it builds a valid, read-only (user-accessible for non-kernel pmaps) PTE, optionally sets NX in the PAE build when execute is not requested and i386_read_exec is not set, and may attempt superpage promotion.

functions.name: __CONCAT(PMTYPE, kenter_temporary)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function pmap_pae_kenter_temporary or pmap_nopae_kenter_temporary (head __CONCAT(PMTYPE, kenter_temporary)): makes a temporary kernel mapping for a physical address, meant for crash dumps; returns the base of the crash dump map area as a void pointer (crashdumpmap, not the mapped page itself unless i is 0). It computes va = crashdumpmap + i * PAGE_SIZE, maps pa there with pmap_kenter, invalidates the TLB entry for va with invlpg and returns (void *)crashdumpmap.

functions.name: __CONCAT(PMTYPE, object_init_pt)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function pmap_pae_object_init_pt or pmap_nopae_object_init_pt (head __CONCAT(PMTYPE, object_init_pt)): pre-maps a large device or scatter-gather object region with large pages; void. Precondition: the object is write-locked and is OBJT_DEVICE or OBJT_SG (asserted). Only when super pages are enabled and both addr and size are multiples of the large page size does it do anything: it populates the object (returning if that fails), takes the first page, aborts (returns) if the first page's physical address is not large-page aligned, and aborts if any following page is not physically contiguous or has a different PAT memory mode. Otherwise it locks the pmap and, for each large page in the range, stores a PG_PS | PG_M | PG_A | PG_U | PG_RW | PG_V page directory entry when the pde is currently 0 (existing entries are left as they are), adding the page count to resident_count and counting pmap_pde_mappings, and unlocks. In every other case it does nothing.

functions.name: __CONCAT(PMTYPE, unwire)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function pmap_pae_unwire or pmap_nopae_unwire (head __CONCAT(PMTYPE, unwire)): clears the wired attribute on all mappings in [sva, eva); void. If the pmap is not the current one it takes the global pv-list write lock and pins the thread; it locks the pmap. For each page-directory range it skips invalid page directory entries; for a large page it panics if PG_W is not set, clears PG_W and reduces wired_count by NBPDR / PAGE_SIZE when the range covers the whole large page, otherwise it demotes the mapping (taking the pv lock with a try-lock and restarting the operation if it would block; a failed demotion panics). For each valid PTE in the range it panics if PG_W is not set and clears PG_W atomically and decrements the pmap's wired count (the clearing code follows the displayed lines). Invalid entries are ignored. No TLB invalidation is done because PG_W is not a hardware bit. It releases the locks it took.

functions.name: __CONCAT(PMTYPE, set_nx)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function pmap_pae_set_nx or pmap_nopae_set_nx (head __CONCAT(PMTYPE, set_nx)): enables no-execute support for the PAE pmap; void. In the PAE build it returns without doing anything when the CPU has no NX capability (AMDID_NX clear in amd_feature); otherwise it sets pg_nx to PG_NX and sets elf32_nxstack to 1. In the non-PAE build the function does nothing.

functions.name: __CONCAT(PMTYPE, bootstrap)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function pmap_pae_bootstrap or pmap_nopae_bootstrap (head __CONCAT(PMTYPE, bootstrap)): brings the pmap module in sync with the page tables built by pmap_cold; void. It sets virtual_avail to firstaddr and virtual_end to VM_MAX_KERNEL_ADDRESS, initializes the statically allocated kernel pmap (mutex, pm_pdir = IdlePTD, pm_pdpt = IdlePDPT in PAE, pm_active set for all CPUs, resident_count from the pages used by bootstrap, pv chunk list, radix tree) and the global pv lock. It then carves reserved kernel virtual addresses and PTEs with the SYSMAP macro starting at virtual_avail: this CPU's cmap pages and qmap address, CMAP3 (boot memory test), the crash dump maps, ptvmmap, the message buffer, the KPTD/KPTmap area (filling KPTD[i] for the NKPT initial page tables), and the PMAP1, PMAP2 and PMAP3 temporary mappings, initializes the PMAP2 mutex, sets virtual_avail to the end of those reservations and calls pmap_init_pat().

functions.name: i386_set_ldt
functions.prose_contract: Implements the i386_set_ldt system call to set, allocate or clear user LDT entries; returns 0 or an errno and sets td_retval[0] to the start index on success except in the clear case. If descs is NULL: for start == 0 and num == 0 it selects the whole user range (NLDT to MAX_LD); under dt_lock it returns 0 when the process has no LDT or start is beyond its length, else zeroes the descriptors in the range (clipped to the LDT length) and returns 0 without setting td_retval[0]. For descriptors supplied: unless the call is the auto-allocation request (start == LDT_AUTO_ALLOC and num == 1) it returns EINVAL if start is not below MAX_LD or start + num exceeds MAX_LD. It then checks every descriptor: SDT_SYSNULL entries have their present bit cleared in the caller-supplied descriptor (so descs is modified); system types (TSS, LDT, task and interrupt/trap/call gates) return EACCES; conforming code segment types require the present bit (EACCES otherwise); ordinary data and code types are accepted; any other type returns EINVAL; a present descriptor whose privilege level is not SEL_UPL returns EACCES. For the auto-allocation request it takes dt_lock, grows the LDT if there is none, scans from NLDT for the first free (SDT_SYSNULL) slot, growing the LDT by one entry and retrying when none is free, sets uap->start to that slot and stores the descriptor with i386_set_ldt_data; otherwise it takes dt_lock, grows the LDT to start + num and stores the descriptors. On success it sets td_retval[0] to uap->start; on error it returns the error.

functions.name: vm86_emulate
functions.prose_contract: Emulates one privileged instruction trapped in vm86 mode; int, returning 0, a signal number (SIGTRAP when the trap flag was set, SIGBUS when the instruction cannot be emulated, SIGKILL for a fatal STI) or the retcode. If curpcb->pcb_ext is 0 it returns SIGBUS (so pcb_ext non-zero is not a precondition). retcode starts as SIGTRAP when PSL_T is set in the frame's eflags, else 0. It fetches the opcode at cs:ip, skipping an address-size prefix; the operand-size prefix is handled separately. With the CPU's virtual-mode-extensions (vm86_has_vme): an operand-size-prefixed PUSHF pushes the flags with the virtual interrupt flag (VIF) reflected as the interrupt flag, advances ip and returns retcode; POPF pops the flags, sets or clears VIF, advances ip and returns retcode unless a virtual interrupt is pending (VIP), in which case it falls out to return SIGBUS; any other operand-size-prefixed opcode and INT n fall out to SIGBUS; STI sets VIF, advances ip and returns SIGKILL if VIP was not set (printing 'fatal sti'), else falls out to SIGBUS; POPF and IRET pop their values, update the flags and VIF and return retcode unless VIP is pending (then SIGBUS); other opcodes return SIGBUS. Without VME the emulation uses the vm86 structure's own virtual eflags: operand-size-prefixed PUSHF and POPF, CLI, STI, PUSHF, INTn (using the interrupt redirection bitmap: a set bit falls out to SIGBUS; otherwise it pushes flags, cs and the return ip, loads the vector from the real-mode table, clears TF and VIF), IRET and POPF are emulated and return retcode; STI, POPF and IRET with VIP pending fall out to SIGBUS; an operand-size-prefixed opcode other than PUSHF/POPF, and unknown opcodes, return SIGBUS.

functions.name: vm86_emulate
functions.prose_contract: Emulates one privileged instruction trapped in vm86 mode; int, returning 0, a signal number (SIGTRAP when the trap flag was set, SIGBUS when the instruction cannot be emulated, SIGKILL for a fatal STI) or the retcode. If curpcb->pcb_ext is 0 it returns SIGBUS. retcode starts as SIGTRAP when PSL_T is set in the frame's eflags, else 0. It fetches the opcode at cs:ip, skipping an address-size prefix. With virtual-mode extensions (vm86_has_vme) it emulates operand-size-prefixed PUSHF and POPF, STI (SIGKILL when no virtual interrupt is pending, else SIGBUS), POPF and IRET, and returns SIGBUS for INT n, other prefixed opcodes and unknown opcodes, and for POPF/IRET/STI when a virtual interrupt is pending. Without VME it emulates, using the vm86 structure's virtual eflags, operand-size-prefixed PUSHF and POPF, CLI, STI, PUSHF, INT n (a set bit in the interrupt redirection map falls out to SIGBUS), IRET and POPF, each returning retcode on success and falling out to SIGBUS when VIP is pending after STI, POPF or IRET; an operand-size-prefixed opcode other than PUSHF/POPF and any unknown opcode return SIGBUS.

functions.name: ATOMIC_CMPSET(int, "r")
functions.prose_contract: Generated function atomic_cmpset_int(volatile u_int *dst, u_int expect, u_int src), produced by the ATOMIC_CMPSET macro for TYPE int with the "r" constraint. It executes lock cmpxchg: if *dst equals expect it atomically stores src into *dst; the zero flag is captured with sete, and the function returns 1 if the exchange happened and 0 if *dst did not equal expect (in which case *dst is left unchanged). The asm has a memory clobber, so it also acts as a compiler barrier, and the locked instruction is a full hardware barrier. It does not report the value it saw on failure.

functions.name: ATOMIC_CMPSET(int, "r")
functions.prose_contract: Generated function atomic_fcmpset_int(volatile u_int *dst, u_int *expect, u_int src), produced by the ATOMIC_CMPSET macro for TYPE int. It executes lock cmpxchg with the expected value taken from *expect: if *dst equals *expect it atomically stores src into *dst and returns 1. If they differ, it returns 0, leaves *dst unchanged and (because *expect is the in/out EAX operand) writes the value found in *dst back into *expect, so a retry loop can use it. The asm has a memory clobber and the locked instruction is a full barrier.

functions.name: ATOMIC_LOADSTORE(int)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function atomic_load_acq_int(const volatile u_int *p), produced by ATOMIC_LOAD(TYPE) inside ATOMIC_LOADSTORE(int). It reads *p into a local with a plain load, then issues a compiler barrier (__compiler_membar) and returns the value. On i386 no fence instruction is emitted; the acquire ordering relies on x86's load ordering plus the compiler barrier.

functions.name: outw
functions.prose_contract: Static inline helper that writes the 16-bit value data to I/O port port with the x86 outw instruction (value in AX, port in DX via the 'Nd' constraint); returns void and has no C-level side effects other than the port write.

functions.name: read_eflags
functions.prose_contract: Static inline helper that returns the current EFLAGS register as a u_int, read with pushfl followed by popl into a register.

functions.name: rdmsr
functions.prose_contract: Static inline helper that executes the privileged rdmsr instruction for model-specific register number msr (in ECX) and returns the 64-bit value from EDX:EAX; if the MSR is not valid or the caller lacks privilege the CPU raises an exception rather than returning.

functions.name: rdmsr32
functions.prose_contract: Static inline helper that executes rdmsr for model-specific register msr and returns only the low 32 bits (EAX); the high half in EDX is discarded (clobbered). Invalid MSRs raise a CPU exception as for rdmsr.

functions.name: rdpmc
functions.prose_contract: Static inline helper that executes rdpmc for performance counter number pmc (in ECX) and returns the 64-bit counter value from EDX:EAX.

functions.name: rdtsc
functions.prose_contract: Static inline helper that executes rdtsc and returns the 64-bit time-stamp counter from EDX:EAX; it does not serialize the instruction stream.

functions.name: rdtsc_ordered_lfence
functions.prose_contract: Static inline helper that issues lfence and then returns rdtsc(), so the counter read is ordered after earlier loads.

functions.name: rdtsc_ordered_mfence
functions.prose_contract: Static inline helper that issues mfence and then returns rdtsc(), so the counter read is ordered after earlier loads and stores.

functions.name: rdtscp
functions.prose_contract: Static inline helper that executes rdtscp and returns the 64-bit time-stamp counter from EDX:EAX; the auxiliary value in ECX is discarded (ECX is declared clobbered).

functions.name: rdtscp_aux
functions.prose_contract: Static inline helper that executes rdtscp, returns the 64-bit time-stamp counter, and stores the auxiliary value from ECX (IA32_TSC_AUX) in *aux; aux must be a valid pointer.

functions.name: rdtsc32
functions.prose_contract: Static inline helper that executes rdtsc and returns only the low 32 bits (EAX) of the time-stamp counter; EDX is declared clobbered.

functions.name: rdtscp32
functions.prose_contract: Static inline helper that executes rdtscp and returns only the low 32 bits (EAX) of the time-stamp counter; ECX and EDX are declared clobbered, so the auxiliary value is discarded.

functions.name: write_eflags
functions.prose_contract: Static inline helper that loads the EFLAGS register with the value ef using pushl followed by popfl; returns void. Flags that the current privilege level cannot change are not changed by popfl.

functions.name: wrmsr
functions.prose_contract: Static inline helper that executes the privileged wrmsr instruction, writing the 64-bit newval (EDX:EAX) to model-specific register msr (ECX); returns void. An invalid MSR or value makes the CPU raise an exception.

functions.name: load_cr0
functions.prose_contract: Static inline helper that writes the value data to control register CR0 with a mov instruction (privileged); returns void.

functions.name: rcr0
functions.prose_contract: Static inline helper that returns the current value of control register CR0 as a u_int.

functions.name: rcr2
functions.prose_contract: Static inline helper that returns the current value of control register CR2 (the faulting linear address of the last page fault) as a u_int.

functions.name: load_cr3
functions.prose_contract: Static inline helper that writes data to control register CR3 (the page-directory base), which also flushes the non-global TLB entries; the asm declares a memory clobber. Returns void.

functions.name: rcr3
functions.prose_contract: Static inline helper that returns the current value of control register CR3 as a u_int.

functions.name: load_cr4
functions.prose_contract: Static inline helper that writes data to control register CR4 with a mov instruction (privileged); returns void.

functions.name: rcr4
functions.prose_contract: Static inline helper that returns the current value of control register CR4 as a u_int.

functions.name: rxcr
functions.prose_contract: Static inline helper that executes xgetbv for extended control register number reg (ECX) and returns the 64-bit value assembled as low | (high << 32) from EAX and EDX.

functions.name: load_xcr
functions.prose_contract: Static inline helper that executes xsetbv, writing the 64-bit val (split into low 32 bits in EAX and high 32 bits in EDX) to extended control register reg (ECX); returns void.

functions.name: invltlb
functions.prose_contract: Static inline helper that flushes the non-global TLB entries by reloading CR3 with its current value: load_cr3(rcr3()).

functions.name: invlpg
functions.prose_contract: Static inline helper that invalidates the TLB entry for the page containing linear address addr with the invlpg instruction (memory clobber); returns void.

functions.name: rfs
functions.prose_contract: Static inline helper that returns the current value of the FS segment selector as a u_short.

functions.name: rgdt
functions.prose_contract: Static inline helper that returns the contents of the global descriptor table register as a uint64_t, stored with the sgdt instruction into a local 64-bit variable.

functions.name: linux_ptrace
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: td is the calling thread and uap points to the Linux ptrace arguments (req, pid, addr, data). Postcondition: dispatches on uap->req and returns an errno (0 when the selected sub-operation succeeded). TRACEME, POKETEXT, POKEDATA, KILL and ATTACH are passed to kern_ptrace; DETACH, SINGLESTEP and CONT are passed with addr (void *)1 and the signal mapped by map_signum. PEEKTEXT/PEEKDATA call kern_ptrace and, only if it returned 0, copy an l_int-sized td_retval to uap->data; td_retval[0] is restored in every case. GETREGS and GETFPREGS call kern_ptrace into a local BSD buffer, convert and copyout to uap->data; SETREGS and SETFPREGS copyin from uap->data, convert and call kern_ptrace; a copyin/copyout failure is returned. GETFPXREGS/SETFPXREGS (SET first copies in; its failure is returned): EIO on a size mismatch of linux_pt_fpxreg and savexmm (a message is printed once); ESRCH when pfind finds no process; with the process locked, ESRCH if exiting, the p_candebug error, EINVAL for a system process, EPERM if not traced, EBUSY if p_pptr is not the caller or the process is not stopped and waited for; each of these exits unlocks p. Otherwise the first thread's FP/XMM registers are read (then copied out) or written (after masking mxcsr with 0xffbf) through linux_proc_read_fpxregs/linux_proc_write_fpxregs, with a hold on the process and the process lock released before the copyout. PEEKUSR/POKEUSR start with EIO and stop there if uap->addr is negative or not l_int aligned or lies in neither the linux_pt_reg range nor [LINUX_DBREG_OFFSET, LINUX_DBREG_OFFSET+LINUX_DBREG_SIZE]; in the register range they use PT_GETREGS (PEEK copies the l_int at that offset to uap->data; POKE stores (l_int)uap->data, the value itself, then PT_SETREGS); in the debug range uap->addr is reduced by LINUX_DBREG_OFFSET and PT_GETDBREGS/PT_SETDBREGS are used the same way. LINUX_PTRACE_SYSCALL and any other request print a message and return EINVAL.

functions.name: systrace_args
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: uarg points to an array of uint64_t slots large enough for the arguments of sysnum, n_args points to a writable int, and for a syscall number that takes arguments params points to that syscall's argument structure. Postcondition: the function (void) switches on sysnum; for a case with arguments the fields of the argument structure are stored in order into slots 0, 1, ... of uarg and *n_args is set to the argument count; fields typed as pointers are stored as (intptr_t) through uarg, and the generator stores some integer-like fields (for example int, clockid_t and l_size_t such as ssize in case 414) through the int64_t alias iarg and others (for example uint32_t nfds in case 414, u_int, size_t) through uarg, so the choice follows the generated per-field code and not a single rule. Cases for syscalls without arguments (and the default branch) set *n_args to 0 and write nothing to uarg, and params is not read for those. The function returns nothing and changes no state other than uarg and *n_args.

functions.name: systrace_entry_setargdesc
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sysnum is a syscall number, ndx an argument index, desc a writable buffer of descsz bytes. Postcondition: the function starts with p == NULL; for a sysnum case in its big switch it sets p to a constant string naming the type of argument ndx (for example "l_int") when ndx matches a case of the inner switch, and leaves p NULL otherwise (including for a sysnum with no case, a no-argument syscall or an ndx beyond the last argument); at the end, only if p is not NULL, it copies the string into desc with strlcpy truncated to descsz. It returns nothing, and desc is not touched when p is NULL.

functions.name: systrace_args
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: uarg points to an array of uint64_t slots large enough for the arguments of sysnum, n_args points to a writable int, and for a syscall number that takes arguments params points to that syscall's argument structure. Postcondition: the function (void) switches on sysnum; for a case with arguments the fields are stored in order into slots 0, 1, ... of uarg and *n_args is set to the argument count; pointer fields are stored as (intptr_t) through uarg, and the generator stores each other field either through the int64_t alias iarg (for example int and several l_* typed fields) or through uarg (for example u_int and uint32_t), following the type comment of the generated line, so unsigned-looking types are not uniformly stored through uarg. Cases for syscalls without arguments, and the default branch, set *n_args to 0 and write no slot. The function returns nothing and changes only uarg and *n_args.

functions.name: hostap_input
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ni is a valid node (non-NULL, asserted) with valid ni_vap and ni_ic, m is an mbuf holding a received 802.11 frame, rxs may be NULL. Postcondition: returns the frame type (the value is held in a uint8_t, initially -1 so it returns 255 when the frame was rejected before the type was read, e.g. too short or bad version), and in the paths that reach the common exit (label out, or err then out) the mbuf, if still non-NULL, is radiotap-tapped when it was not already tapped and the vap is tapping, and then freed with m_freem. Frames flagged M_AMPDU_MPDU skip validation and jump into the data path at resubmit_ampdu. Otherwise too-short frames, a bad version (goes to err), a wrong BSSID while not scanning, and failed sequence checks are dropped with statistics. Data frames are dropped (some via err, which also counts an interface input error, others via out without it) for wrong direction, unassociated or unknown source, unauthorized 4-address frames, privacy off with a protected frame, crypto decap/demic failure, defrag not complete, decap failure, unauthorized port with non-EAPOL, or unencrypted frames when DROPUNENC is set. 4-address frames from a node without a WDS vap are handed to ieee80211_dwds_discover and the function returns the type without freeing m itself. A-MPDU reorder that takes the frame, decap_amsdu or decap_fastframe returning NULL return the data type directly without the common exit. Successful data frames are delivered to ni->ni_wdsvap (4-address with a WDS vap) or hostap_deliver_data and the function returns IEEE80211_FC0_TYPE_DATA without freeing. Management frames are checked for direction, length, multicast source and protection, optionally decrypted, tapped, passed to iv_recv_mgmt and then fall to out where m is freed; control frames matching the vap go to iv_recv_ctl and then to out; an unknown type falls into err.

functions.name: hostap_auth_shared
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ni is a node whose vap is in IEEE80211_S_RUN (asserted), frm..efrm bounds the information elements of a received authentication frame, seq and status come from that frame. Postcondition: returns nothing. If privacy is disabled it goes to bad with status IEEE80211_STATUS_ALG without counting an error; if ni_authmode is neither AUTO nor SHARED it counts is_rx_bad_auth and goes to bad (ALG); only the first information element (if frm+1 < efrm) is examined: if its length overruns efrm it counts is_rx_bad_auth and goes to bad (CHALLENGE), if its id is the challenge element it is taken as the challenge. For seq CHALLENGE or RESPONSE a missing challenge or a challenge length other than IEEE80211_CHALLENGE_LEN counts is_rx_bad_auth and goes to bad (CHALLENGE). For seq REQUEST the node is duplicated from vap->iv_bss when ni is the bss (returns silently if the dup fails) or referenced if not already AREF; AREF and ASSOCID are set, RSSI and noise updated, a challenge buffer allocated (returns silently on failure) and filled with random bytes; if a RADIUS ACL policy is in force it only calls ieee80211_notify_node_auth and returns without sending a response; otherwise an auth response with seq+1 is sent. For seq RESPONSE it returns silently when ni is the bss; goes to bad (CHALLENGE) when no challenge is recorded (counting is_rx_bad_auth) or on mismatch (counting is_rx_auth_fail); on match it authorizes the node and sends an auth response with seq+1. Any other seq counts is_rx_bad_auth and goes to bad with status SEQUENCE. The bad label calls ieee80211_send_error with (seq+1) and the status.

functions.name: ieee80211_ampdu_reorder
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ni is an HT node, m is an A-MPDU frame (M_AMPDU set, M_AMPDU_MPDU clear; both asserted) whose first mbuf holds the QoS header, rxs may supply A-MSDU flags. Postcondition: returns 0 (PROCESS, caller keeps m and handles it) or 1 (CONSUMED, caller must not touch m). Returns 0 without changing state when the frame is not QoS data, when addr1 is multicast, or when the TID's reorder state does not have IEEE80211_AGGR_XCHGPEND set. A frame with fragment bits in the sequence field is counted (is_ampdu_rx_drop), freed, and returns 1. Otherwise rxa_nframes is incremented, and if WAITRX was set it is cleared and the window start taken from the frame. If the frame's sequence equals rxa_start: with frames already queued, the frame is dispatched and the queue dispatched and it returns 1; with none queued it advances rxa_start by one (unless it is an A-MSDU subframe that is not the last, in which case the window is not advanced) and returns 0. If the frame lies inside the window (offset < rxa_wnd) and queued frames are older than ieee80211_ampdu_age, the queue is flushed (counted in is_ampdu_rx_age), the window start is advanced as above and it returns 0; otherwise the frame is stored in its slot (starting the age timer when the queue was empty) and it returns 1. If the offset is beyond the window but below IEEE80211_SEQ_BA_RANGE, is_ampdu_rx_move is counted, frames below rxseq - rxa_wnd + 1 are flushed with ampdu_rx_flush_upto and the sequence is re-examined from the top. Beyond that range the frame is counted dropped, freed, and it returns 1.

functions.name: ieee80211_recv_bar
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ni is a node and m0 holds a received BAR control frame (header at least ieee80211_frame_bar sized; the frame is not otherwise validated, see the XXX at 1245). Postcondition: returns nothing and does not free m0. If ieee80211_recv_bar_ena is clear, or the BAR's TID has no pending BA exchange (IEEE80211_AGGR_XCHGPEND clear), it increments is_ampdu_bar_bad and returns with the reorder state unchanged. Otherwise it increments is_ampdu_bar_rx; if the BAR's sequence number equals the window start it returns with nothing else changed. Otherwise, when the offset from the window start is below IEEE80211_SEQ_BA_RANGE it increments is_ampdu_bar_move and calls ampdu_rx_flush_upto(ni, rap, rxseq), which dispatches queued MSDUs with sequence numbers before rxseq (it may continue past rxseq while a contiguous run of queued frames follows) and moves the window start; if the offset was at least rxa_wnd it then sets rxa_start to rxseq explicitly. An offset at or beyond the range is counted in is_ampdu_bar_oow, noted in the node's rx_drop statistic, and leaves the window unchanged.

functions.name: hwmp_recv_prep
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: vap has mesh and HWMP state, ni is the neighbour the PREP arrived from, wh is the received frame header and prep a parsed PREP element. Postcondition: returns nothing. It returns early with no route change when the PREP's originator address is not our own address (or is a proxied route not proxied by us) and mesh forwarding (IEEE80211_MESHFLAGS_FWD) is off. It looks up or adds the route to prep_targetaddr (counting is_mesh_rtaddfailed and returning if the add fails). If that route is already VALID it returns without updating when the PREP's target sequence is older than hr_seq, or when it is not newer than hr_seq and the new metric (prep_metric plus the path metric of ni) is greater than the route's metric. Otherwise the route's sequence, next hop (ni_macaddr), metric, hop count (prep_hopcount + 1) and lifetime are set, DISCOVER is cleared and VALID set, and hwmp_update_transmitter is called. If the originator is not us and ttl > 1 and hopcount < hs_maxhops, the PREP is forwarded with hop count and metric increased and ttl decreased through hwmp_send_prep to the originator route's next hop, but the function returns without sending when no route to the originator exists (which also skips the steps below). If the AE flag is set, a proxy route for the external target address is found or added (returning with is_mesh_rtaddfailed counted if the add fails) and its fields overwritten with flags PROXY|VALID, gate = prep_targetaddr, next hop = wh->i_addr2. Finally frames staged for the target (or external) address are taken from ic_stageq and each is passed to ieee80211_vap_xmitpkt.

functions.name: ieee80211_parse_beacon
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ni and m are valid, m's first mbuf holds an 802.11 management header followed by a beacon or probe-response body, rxchan is the receive channel, scan is writable. The pointers stored in scan point into m's data, so they are valid only while that data is unchanged. Postcondition: the function returns scan->status. If fewer than 12 bytes follow the header it sets scan->status to IEEE80211_BPARSE_BADIELEN and returns, leaving the rest of scan as it was. Otherwise scan is zeroed and filled with tstamp (pointer), bintval, capinfo, bchan, chan (initially bchan), ies and ies_len; the information elements are then walked and pointers or values recorded per element id (ssid, rates, xrates, country, csa, quiet, tim and timoff, erp as a value, ht/vht/rsn/mesh elements, vendor WPA/WME/Atheros/TDMA elements, and the pre-draft HT vendor elements if IEEE80211_FHT_HTCOMPAT is set), with fhdwell/fhindex/erp stored as values, chan taken from the FH or DS parameter element, and unknown ids counted in is_rx_elem_unknown. If an element's length overruns the frame, the walk returns BADIELEN at that point with scan zeroed and only partly filled. After a complete walk status bits are or-ed for invalid rates, xrates, ssid, mesh id, bad beacon interval, an off-channel mismatch (chan != bchan on a non-FH phy), and a CSA element of the wrong length; a too-short country element, HT or VHT element is not flagged but its pointer is set to NULL. Status 0 means no problem was detected.

functions.name: setcurchan
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: vap is a valid vap with valid iv_ic and iv_bss, and c is IEEE80211_CHAN_ANYC or a channel of the com. Postcondition: if c is not ANYC it returns EBUSY for a radar channel; on a HOSTAP vap EINVAL for a NOHOSTAP channel or a channel inconsistent with iv_des_mode; on an IBSS vap EINVAL for a NOADHOC channel; and 0 without storing anything when the vap is in RUN or SLEEP state and iv_bss->ni_chan already equals c. Otherwise vap->iv_des_chan is set to c, and: for a monitor vap with a real channel, if the interface is up and running the com channel is switched with ieee80211_setcurchan and iv_bss->ni_chan updated, else ic_curchan and the rate table are set directly; for other vaps, if the vap is up and running and iv_roaming is AUTO (IS_UP_AUTO) a transition to IEEE80211_S_SCAN is requested, otherwise (when c is not ANYC) ic_curchan and the rate table are set directly. It then returns 0 (the local error stays 0 on all paths that reach the end).

functions.name: ieee80211_ioctl_setappie_locked
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller holds the com lock of vap->iv_ic (asserted with IEEE80211_LOCK_ASSERT) and fc0 selects an application IE slot; ireq gives the length and user data. Postcondition: the function does not release the lock. It switches on the subtype in fc0: BEACON (HOSTAP or IBSS vap only, else EINVAL) replaces iv_appie_beacon through setappie and, if that returned 0, calls ieee80211_beacon_notify(IEEE80211_BEACON_APPIE); PROBE_RESP and PROBE_REQ replace their slots; ASSOC_RESP (HOSTAP only) and ASSOC_REQ (STA only) replace theirs, else EINVAL; the WPA appie subtype replaces iv_appie_wpa, and when that succeeded iv_wpa_ie and iv_rsn_ie are cleared and re-derived from the new blob (setwparsnie, which checks the lengths of up to two IEs), after which the result is ENETRESET on a HOSTAP or IBSS vap (including when the appie was deleted with i_len 0). Any other subtype returns EINVAL. setappie itself returns 0 (with i_len 0 deleting and freeing the old IE), EINVAL when i_len is nonzero but outside 2..IEEE80211_MAX_APPIE, ENOMEM when allocation fails, or a copyin error, in which case the old IE is left in place. The function returns that error value.

functions.name: ieee80211_ioctl_set80211
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: vap and ireq are valid, and for request types that take user data ireq->i_data points to a user buffer of ireq->i_len bytes. Postcondition: the function switches on ireq->i_type; each case validates and applies one configuration item and the function returns an errno. Many cases return directly (EINVAL for out-of-range values, EOPNOTSUPP when the capability is missing), skipping the post-processing; the others leave a value in error and fall to the tail. Several cases copy data in with copyin (SSID, WEP key, BSSID, ...) and return its error (e.g. EFAULT). Many cases delegate to helpers (channel, key, MLME, scan request, WME, appie, txparams, regdomain and others), whose errno values are propagated; unknown types go to ieee80211_ioctl_setdefault, which returns EINVAL if no registered handler accepts the type. The old IEEE80211_IOC_SCAN_REQ (23) case starts a scan or moves an INIT vap into SCAN and ignores the return value of ieee80211_start_scan. After the switch, an error of ERESTART becomes the result of vap->iv_reset when the interface is up and running and 0 otherwise, and an error of ENETRESET calls ieee80211_init when the vap is up with auto roaming, and is then replaced by 0. So ENETRESET and ERESTART are not returned to the caller; EINPROGRESS can be returned from the scan request path.

functions.name: mesh_input
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ni is a valid node on a mesh vap, m is an mbuf holding a received 802.11 frame whose ownership passes to the function, and the TX lock is not held (asserted). Postcondition: returns the frame type held in a uint8_t (initially -1, so 255 when the frame was rejected before the type was read, i.e. too short or bad version), or IEEE80211_FC0_TYPE_DATA from two paths. The inactivity timer is reloaded first. Frames shorter than the minimum header or with a bad version are dropped (the bad-version one counts an interface input error); while not scanning, RSSI and noise are updated and for sequenced frames a failed duplicate check drops the frame. Data frames: dropped if ni is the vap's bss node, if the peer link is not ESTABLISHED, for a direction other than FROMDS or DSTODS (counts an input error), for a non-QoS subtype or missing mesh-control bit (input error), after defragmentation fails, when the mesh source address taken from addr3 or addr4 equals our own address, when mesh_checkpseq reports a duplicate; otherwise the frame is routed to mesh_recv_indiv_data_to_me, mesh_recv_group_data or mesh_recv_indiv_data_to_fwrd, whose negative result counts an error and positive result drops the frame without that count, and a zero result goes on to radiotap, mesh_decap (a NULL result is dropped, without an error count for null-data subtypes), optional A-MSDU decap (returning DATA when it yields NULL), and ieee80211_deliver_data, after which the function returns the type without freeing m. Management frames are checked for direction and length, protected frames are discarded, and others are handed to iv_recv_mgmt and then fall to out. Control frames are counted and dropped. Unknown types go to the error exit. At the common exit (err then out) a still-owned m is tapped to radiotap if it was not yet tapped and then freed with m_freem.

functions.name: ieee80211_beacon_update
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller does not hold the com lock (the function takes and releases it), ni and m describe an already-constructed beacon whose offsets in the vap's beacon-offsets structure match the mbuf, and the mbuf has contiguous room for a maximal TIM bitmap and for a CSA element. Postcondition: the com lock is taken on entry and released before each of the four returns. It returns 1 immediately, after rebuilding the whole beacon with ieee80211_beacon_construct, when the CSA flag is set and the vap's CSA count equals ic_csa_count (the vap's count is reset, and ieee80211_csa_completeswitch is called first if ic_csa_newchan is set), or when the QUIET_IE flag state differs from iv_quiet (the flag is toggled to match). Otherwise it assigns the beacon sequence number, rewrites the capability field, handles WME aggressive-mode switching and the WME element, HT info, TDMA and mesh beacon updates, and for HOSTAP/MBSS vaps updates the TIM (moving the trailing elements and the stored offsets when the bitmap length changes, which sets the return value to 1), counts the DTIM countdown and the multicast bit, inserts the CSA element when the vap's CSA count is 0 (growing the mbuf lengths, without setting the return value) or decrements its count otherwise, adds the quiet element when DFS and quiet apply, and updates ERP and Atheros elements when flagged. A pending APPIE update that changes the application IE length moves the trailer and sets the return value to 1. The function returns 1 if the beacon length changed by those TIM or APPIE adjustments and 0 otherwise.

functions.name: ieee80211_csa_cancelswitch
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller holds the com lock (checked with IEEE80211_LOCK_ASSERT); the function does not check that a channel switch is actually pending. Postcondition: it calls the static csa_completeswitch, which sets ic_csa_newchan to NULL, clears IEEE80211_F_CSAPENDING and moves every vap currently in IEEE80211_S_CSA to IEEE80211_S_RUN through ieee80211_new_state_locked (vaps in other states are left alone). Unlike ieee80211_csa_completeswitch it does not call ieee80211_setcurchan and does not update any vap's iv_bss->ni_chan, so the current channel and BSS channels are not changed by this function. It returns nothing.

functions.name: ieee80211_alloc_countryie
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ic is a valid com with a valid ic_bsschan, channel table (ic_channels, ic_nchans) and regdomain. Postcondition: returns a newly allocated zeroed ieee80211_appie owned by the caller (to be freed with IEEE80211_FREE), or NULL after printing a message when the allocation of IEEE80211_COUNTRY_MAX_SIZE bytes fails (the only NULL return). The country element's id is IEEE80211_ELEMID_COUNTRY, its country code is rd->isocc, or two blanks (with a message printed) when isocc[0] is '\0', and its third character is 'I' or 'O' when rd->location says so and a blank otherwise. The channel table is walked once: channels whose ic_ieee was already seen (duplicates) or whose flags match the skip set for the BSS channel's mode and band (turbo, half/quarter, the other band, and for FH also OFDM/CCK/DYN) are ignored; each remaining channel starts a new run of (first channel, count 1, ic_maxregpower) unless its number is the one after the previous channel and its maxregpower equals that of the current run, in which case the run's count is incremented. If a new run would exceed IEEE80211_COUNTRY_MAX_BANDS a message is printed and the loop stops, so the element is truncated. The element length is set from the data written, padded with one zero byte when odd, and ie_len is set to the total size.

functions.name: sta_roam_check
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: vap is a station vap (the sole caller sta_age checks this) with valid iv_ic and iv_bss, ss->ss_priv is the sta_table, and the vap's iv_roamparms rate and rssi for the phymode of ic_bsschan are nonzero (KASSERT). Postcondition: returns nothing. If the scan cache has no entry for the BSS node's MAC address it returns with nothing changed. Otherwise it takes the roam thresholds for the BSS channel's mode, the current RSSI from ic_node_getrssi, and the current rate (the node's tx rate when the unicast rate is not fixed, else a value equal to the roam rate so the rate test cannot fire). Only when the current rate is below the roam rate or the current RSSI is below the roam RSSI (either one is enough) does it go on: if the scan cache is older than iv_scanvalid it may start a background scan (not when the current channel is dynamic turbo, and only with scan offload or after iv_bgscanidle of no data) and returns without selecting; otherwise it stores the current RSSI into the matching cache entry's se_rssi, runs select_bss, and when that returns a different entry it calls ieee80211_sta_join on that entry's channel (demoted from 11g to 11b when STA_DEMOTE11B is set) and ignores the join result. In all other cases nothing further is modified.

functions.name: sta_add
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller does not hold the scan-table lock; ss, curchan, sp, wh, subtype, rssi and noise describe one received beacon or probe response from wh->i_addr2, with sp->rates non-NULL and sp->rates[1] (and sp->xrates[1] if xrates is non-NULL) at most IEEE80211_RATE_MAXSIZE, and when the chosen channel is VHT or HT but the frame lacks the corresponding capability a non-VHT or non-HT channel with the same frequency must exist (the KASSERTs would fire otherwise). Postcondition: returns 0 with the table lock released when allocation of a new entry fails and nothing was inserted; otherwise it returns 1 after the lock is released. The table entry for the sender MAC is found or created (zeroed, appended to the list and hash bucket, RSSI average at the dummy marker) and updated: ssid (copied when the new ssid is non-empty and the frame is a probe response or the entry has no ssid), rates, extended rates (length cleared when absent), bssid from addr3, on-channel RSSI average and noise (not updated when the frame was off-channel), timestamp, beacon interval, capability info, mesh id if present. se_chan is set to curchan for an on-channel frame; for an off-channel frame it is set to the channel found from sp->chan, else kept if already set, else set to curchan. It is then demoted to a non-VHT channel if the frame has no VHT capability and then to a non-HT channel if it has no HT capability. FH, ERP, TIM offset, DTIM period and country code are copied; a country mismatch with 11d active triggers at most one notification per scan generation; the IEs are copied with ieee80211_ies_init (its result ignored); the failure count is cleared after STA_FAILS_AGE; last-update time, se_seen and not-seen count are updated and st_maxrssi for the beacon channel raised. After unlocking, if PICK1ST is set and no pick has yet been made and match_bss accepts the entry, IEEE80211_SCAN_GOTPICK is set.

functions.name: tdma_update
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: vap is a TDMA vap (IEEE80211_C_TDMA set in iv_caps, asserted), tdma points to a received TDMA parameter element, ni is the sending node. The function takes no reference on ni. Postcondition: returns 0, with no runtime state, beacon, driver callback or join/leave notification changed (apart from the rate-limited diagnostic bookkeeping in tdma_lastprint/tdma_fails), when the received slot count, slot length (le16toh(tdma_slotlen)*100) or beacon interval differs from the current value and is not valid, or when pickslot is nonzero and no free slot above 0 is found in the in-use bitmap (a message is printed). Otherwise it computes which of slot count, slot length, beacon interval and slot differ (the slot is changed only when pickslot is nonzero and the picked slot, the highest free one, differs; with pickslot zero ts->tdma_slot is unchanged), forces all four updates when ni is not the current peer, stores the changed values and calls ieee80211_beacon_notify(IEEE80211_BEACON_TDMA) when any changed, calls ic_tdma_update(ni, tdma, update) only if the vap is in RUN state, and when ni differs from ts->tdma_peer calls ieee80211_notify_node_leave on vap->iv_bss (only if a previous peer was recorded, and on iv_bss, not on that peer), then ieee80211_notify_node_join(ni, 1) and records ni as the peer. It then returns 1.

functions.name: ieee80211_create_wds
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: vap has IEEE80211_F_DESBSSID set and is in IEEE80211_S_RUN state (both KASSERTs), with iv_des_bssid holding the peer address. Postcondition: in non-legacy mode (IEEE80211_FEXT_WDSLEGACY clear) it looks up the node for iv_des_bssid in the station table under the node-table lock; if none is found ni stays NULL and nothing is linked; if the found node already has ni_wdsvap set (to any vap, possibly this one) it is left untouched and nothing is linked; otherwise the vap's bss is replaced with that node through iv_update_bss, ni_wdsvap is set to vap, and after unlocking the previous bss node is freed. In legacy mode a new WDS node for iv_des_bssid on chan is created with ieee80211_node_create_wds; if that succeeds it is installed as the vap's bss (with an extra reference, flag AREF set, the old bss freed), the driver ic_newassoc and the authenticator's ia_node_join are called when present, the node is authorized only if its ni_authmode is not IEEE80211_AUTH_8021X, and a join notification is sent. In both modes, when ni is non-NULL wds_flush is then called to send pending frames for it. It returns ENOENT when ni is NULL (node not found in non-legacy mode, node creation failed in legacy mode) and 0 otherwise, including the non-legacy case where a node was found but owned by another WDS vap and no link was made.

functions.name: wds_input
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ni is the WDS peer node (non-NULL, asserted) of a WDS vap, m is an mbuf holding a received 802.11 frame whose ownership passes to the function, rxs may be NULL. Postcondition: returns the frame type held in a uint8_t (initially -1, so 255 when rejected before the type was read), or IEEE80211_FC0_TYPE_DATA from some data paths. Frames flagged M_AMPDU_MPDU skip validation and enter the data path at resubmit_ampdu. Otherwise: frames shorter than the minimum header are dropped; ni_inact is reloaded for a non-multicast addr1; a bad version goes to the error exit (counts an interface input error); frames shorter than a 4-address header, or whose addr1 is neither our address nor the broadcast address are dropped; RSSI and noise are updated and for sequenced frames a failed rx-sequence check drops the frame. Data frames are dropped if the direction is not DSTODS, if the vap is not in legacy WDS mode, after A-MPDU reorder consumes the frame, for privacy off with a protected frame, crypto decap or demic failure, incomplete defragmentation, decap failure (error exit, except null-data subtypes), an unauthorized port with non-EAPOL, or an unencrypted frame when IEEE80211_F_DROPUNENC applies; A-MSDU or fast-frame decap returning NULL returns the DATA type directly; otherwise the frame is delivered with ieee80211_deliver_data and the function returns the DATA type without freeing it. Management frames are counted, checked for direction, length and protection, handed to iv_recv_mgmt, and then freed at the common exit; control frames are counted and freed; unknown types go to the error exit. At the common exit a non-NULL m is tapped to radiotap if not yet tapped and freed.

functions.name: ng_hci_process_command_status
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: unit is a valid HCI unit and e is an mbuf holding a Command_Status event; the function takes ownership of e. Postcondition: if the pullup of the ng_hci_command_status_ep header fails (the pullup macro then releases the mbuf and e is NULL) it returns ENOBUFS at once, without calling ng_hci_send_command. Otherwise it stores the controller's number of command packets in the unit buffer info; if the opcode is 0x0000 (NOOP) it skips matching; otherwise complete_command is tried (EINVAL when no command is pending, the queue is empty or the first queued opcode differs, ETIMEDOUT when the command timeout cannot be cancelled), and on success the opcode is converted to host order and dispatched by OGF: link control, link policy and LE go to process_link_control_status, process_link_policy_status and process_le_status, whose return values (which these helpers decide, and which can be other errnos) become the result and which take care of the dequeued command packet; BT_LOGO and VENDOR free it and give 0; any other OGF frees it and gives EINVAL. After the pullup succeeded, the code reaches the out label on every path of this function, where e is freed with NG_FREE_M and ng_hci_send_command(unit) is called, and the error value is returned.

functions.name: con_compl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: unit is a valid HCI unit and event is an mbuf holding a Connection_Complete event; the function takes ownership of event. Postcondition: if the pullup of the ng_hci_con_compl_ep header fails it returns ENOBUFS (the macro having released the mbuf). Otherwise it looks for a descriptor with the same link type and address in state NG_HCI_CON_W4_CONN_COMPLETE. If none exists and ep->status is nonzero, it does nothing further and returns 0; if none exists and status is 0 a new descriptor is created (ENOMEM if that fails) and given the address. If one exists its timeout is cancelled, and a nonzero return from ng_hci_con_untimeout is returned without updating the descriptor. Otherwise the descriptor receives the connection handle and encryption mode, ng_hci_lp_con_cfm reports the status to the upper layers, and with a nonzero status the descriptor is freed, while with status 0 it becomes NG_HCI_CON_OPEN and, for an ACL link, a Write_Link_Policy_Settings command is built from the unit's features (if an mbuf can be allocated), queued, and sent when no command is pending. In every path after a successful pullup the event mbuf is freed, and the error value returned is 0 except for the ENOMEM and untimeout cases.

functions.name: ng_btsocket_l2cap_process_l2ca_con_req_rsp
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: msg holds an ng_l2cap_l2ca_con_op in its data and header.token identifies a socket pcb; rt is not used. Postcondition: returns EMSGSIZE, taking no lock, when arglen differs from sizeof(op); otherwise takes ng_btsocket_l2cap_sockets_mtx, finds the pcb by token (ENOENT if none), takes the pcb mutex, and returns ENOENT without other effects when the pcb is not in NG_BTSOCKET_L2CAP_CONNECTING. It then cancels the pcb timeout. For op->result NG_L2CAP_PENDING it re-arms the timeout and returns 0. For NG_L2CAP_SUCCESS: on an ATT or SMP channel it stores encryption and cid and either moves to W4_ENC_CHANGE (re-arming the timeout) when encryption is needed but absent, or to OPEN with soisconnected; on other channels it stores cid and encryption and sends a config request, and if that send fails it sends a disconnect request with token 0, sets the state to CLOSED and calls soisdisconnected and the function returns that send error, while on success it sets CFG_IN_SENT, state CONFIGURING and re-arms the timeout, returning 0. For any other result it stores the errno converted from the result in so_error, sets CLOSED and calls soisdisconnected, returning 0. Both mutexes are released before the return in all paths where they were taken.

functions.name: ng_btsocket_l2cap_process_l2ca_con_ind
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: msg holds an ng_l2cap_l2ca_con_ind_ip and rt is the route the indication came from; ng_btsocket_l2cap_sockets_mtx is not held. Postcondition: returns EMSGSIZE immediately, with no lock taken, when arglen differs from sizeof(*ip). Otherwise it takes the sockets mutex and looks for a listening pcb by (rt->src, psm). If there is none the result code is NG_L2CAP_PSM_NOT_SUPPORTED. If there is one it creates a socket with sonewconn; failure gives result NG_L2CAP_NO_RESOURCES, success creates a new pcb whose source address is the listener's when that is not BDADDR_ANY and rt->src otherwise, with dst, psm, cid, route taken from the indication and imtu, oflow and flush_timo copied from the listener. In all these cases, ng_btsocket_l2cap_send_l2ca_con_rsp_req is then called (carrying the new pcb's token, or 0 if none, and the result, which is 0 when the new pcb was made) and its return value is the function's return value. When a new pcb was created, a send error sets its so_error, state CLOSED and soisdisconnected, and a send success sets state CONNECTING, soisconnecting and arms its timeout. The new pcb's mutex, then the listener's mutex (if taken), then the sockets mutex are released before returning.

functions.name: ng_btsocket_l2cap_process_l2ca_cfg_rsp_rsp
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: msg holds an ng_l2cap_l2ca_cfg_rsp_op and the caller does not hold the sockets mutex. Postcondition: returns EMSGSIZE (no lock taken) when arglen differs from sizeof(*op); takes the sockets mutex and finds the pcb by token (ENOENT if none), takes the pcb mutex, and returns ENOENT with no other effect if the pcb is not in NG_BTSOCKET_L2CAP_CONFIGURING. If op->result is not NG_L2CAP_SUCCESS it goes to the disconnect exit: the timeout is cancelled, a disconnect request with token 0 is sent, the state becomes CLOSED, soisdisconnected is called and 0 is returned. If the result is success, CFG_OUT_SENT is cleared and CFG_OUT set; if cfg_state is then CFG_BOTH the timeout is cancelled, the state becomes OPEN and soisconnected is called and it returns 0; otherwise, if CFG_IN_SENT is not yet set, an incoming-path config request is sent: on failure it takes the disconnect exit and returns that send error, on success it sets CFG_IN_SENT and returns 0; if CFG_IN_SENT is already set nothing more is done and it returns 0. The pcb and sockets mutexes are released before every return after they were taken.

functions.name: ng_btsocket_l2cap_raw_control
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: so is a socket whose raw L2CAP pcb may or may not exist, cmd is an ioctl command and data points to the command-specific structure. Postcondition: returns EINVAL before taking any lock when the pcb or the global ng_btsocket_l2cap_raw_node is NULL. Otherwise it takes the pcb mutex and returns EHOSTUNREACH if the pcb has no route, or EBUSY if pcb->token is nonzero (a request already pending; that token is left set). It then switches on cmd. GET_FLAGS, GET_DEBUG, GET_AUTO_DISCON_TIMO use the synchronous send helper and return its error; SET_DEBUG and SET_AUTO_DISCON_TIMO send a message to the route's hook only if the pcb has NG_BTSOCKET_L2CAP_RAW_PRIVILEGED and otherwise give EPERM; GET_INFO also requires the privileged flag (EPERM). The list and ping/info commands validate arguments (EINVAL for bad counts, NULL buffers or echo sizes; ENOMEM if the message cannot be allocated), allocate a message with a fresh token stored in pcb->token, send it to the hook, and sleep with msleep for the reply; a send error, a msleep error (including interruption or timeout) or a copyin error is returned with pcb->token cleared; a reply whose command differs from the one sent or is missing gives EINVAL; otherwise the reply data is copied out to user space (copyout errors, such as EFAULT, are returned) and the reply message is freed. In the ping case the pcb mutex is dropped around copyin and retaken. An unknown cmd gives EINVAL. In the return paths read (all of the cases up to GET_INFO and the common exit) the pcb mutex is released before returning; the function returns 0 only when the selected command's steps completed without error.

functions.name: ng_btsocket_rfcomm_receive_sabm
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller holds s->session_mtx (asserted with mtx_assert) and dlci is the DLCI of the received SABM frame. Postcondition: for dlci 0 in session state CONNECTED or OPEN it sends a UA command; on success the session becomes OPEN and ng_btsocket_rfcomm_connect_cfm is called and 0 is returned, and on failure the session state is set CLOSED, ng_btsocket_rfcomm_session_clean is called and the send error is returned. For dlci 0 in any other session state it changes nothing and returns EINVAL. For dlci other than 0 it returns EINVAL, changing nothing, when the session is not OPEN. Otherwise, if a pcb with that DLCI exists: when it is not in NG_BTSOCKET_RFCOMM_DLC_CONNECTING (any other state, including DISCONNECTING) it returns ENOENT without changing it; when it is CONNECTING its timeout is cancelled, UA and then an MSC are sent, and on success the pcb becomes DLC_CONNECTED and soisconnected is called (return 0), on failure ng_btsocket_rfcomm_pcb_kill(pcb, error) is called and the error returned; the pcb mutex is released before the return. If no pcb exists for the DLCI, ng_btsocket_rfcomm_connect_ind is asked for a pcb for the server channel: if it returns one, its dlci is set and the same UA, MSC, CONNECTED or kill sequence follows (returning 0 or the error); if it returns NULL a DM command is sent and the function returns the result of that send (0 on success), with no pcb changed.

functions.name: ng_btsocket_rfcomm_receive_sabm
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller holds s->session_mtx (asserted with mtx_assert) and dlci is the DLCI of the received SABM frame. Postcondition: for dlci 0 in session state CONNECTED or OPEN it sends a UA command; on success the session becomes OPEN and ng_btsocket_rfcomm_connect_cfm is called and 0 is returned, and on failure the session state is set CLOSED, ng_btsocket_rfcomm_session_clean is called and the send error is returned. For dlci 0 in any other session state it changes nothing and returns EINVAL. For dlci other than 0 it returns EINVAL, changing nothing, when the session is not OPEN. Otherwise, if a pcb with that DLCI exists: when it is not in NG_BTSOCKET_RFCOMM_DLC_CONNECTING (any other state, including DISCONNECTING) it returns ENOENT without changing it; when it is CONNECTING its timeout is cancelled, UA and then an MSC are sent, and on success the pcb becomes DLC_CONNECTED and soisconnected is called (return 0), on failure ng_btsocket_rfcomm_pcb_kill(pcb, error) is called and the error returned; the pcb mutex is released before the return. If no pcb exists for the DLCI, ng_btsocket_rfcomm_connect_ind is asked for a pcb for the server channel: if it returns one, its dlci is set and the same UA, MSC, CONNECTED or kill sequence follows (returning 0 or the error); if it returns NULL a DM command is sent and the function returns the result of that send (0 on success), with no pcb changed.

functions.name: ng_btsocket_rfcomm_pcb_kill
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller holds pcb->pcb_mtx and the session mutex of pcb->session (both asserted with mtx_assert), and pcb->session is non-NULL (the function calls panic if it is NULL). Postcondition: returns nothing. Any pending DLC timeout is cancelled, the pcb is removed from the session's dlcs list and pcb->session is set to NULL, pcb->state becomes NG_BTSOCKET_RFCOMM_DLC_CLOSED, so_error is set to error, soisdisconnected is called and sleepers on pcb->state are woken. If the session's dlcs list is then empty and the session is the initiator (INITIATOR(s)): in session state CLOSED or DISCONNECTING nothing changes; in state OPEN a DISC command is sent on the multiplexor channel and, if the send succeeds, the session becomes DISCONNECTING, otherwise (and also for CONNECTING and CONNECTED) the session becomes CLOSED; any other session state calls panic. When that branch is taken ng_btsocket_rfcomm_task_wakeup is called. When dlcs is not empty or the session is not the initiator the session state is left unchanged.

functions.name: ng_btsocket_rfcomm_connect
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: so, nam and td come from the connect system call; the function does not hold any of the module's mutexes on entry. Postcondition: returns EINVAL if the socket has no pcb or nam is NULL, then EAFNOSUPPORT if the family is not AF_BLUETOOTH, EINVAL if the length is not sizeof(struct sockaddr_rfcomm) or the channel is above 30, EDESTADDRREQ if the channel is 0 or the destination bdaddr is BDADDR_ANY. It then creates an L2CAP socket with socreate (the result is saved in error and not checked yet), takes the sessions mutex, and looks up a session for (pcb->src, destination). With no session: if no L2CAP socket exists it returns the socreate error; otherwise it creates a session, returning its error (and closing the L2CAP socket) on failure. With an existing session the new L2CAP socket, if any, is closed. It then locks the session and pcb, computes the DLCI, and returns EBUSY if that DLCI already exists on the session. If the session state is CONNECTING, CONNECTED or OPEN, the pcb is given the destination, channel and DLCI, linked into the session, timeout armed and soisconnecting called; in session state OPEN it also takes the session mtu and source, sets the state to DLC_CONFIGURING and sends a PN command (its error, or that of the task wakeup, becomes the result and the pcb stays linked in CONFIGURING), else the state is W4_CONNECT; in the W4_CONNECT case error is not reset, so it can still hold the earlier socreate error when an existing session was found and socreate failed. Any other session state returns ECONNRESET without linking the pcb. All three mutexes are released before the final return.

functions.name: nga_rcvmsg
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: node is a ng_async node whose private data is its softc sc, and item carries a control message. Postcondition: for typecookie NGM_ASYNC_COOKIE the command is handled: GET_STATS allocates a response and copies sc->stats into it (ENOMEM if the allocation fails); CLR_STATS zeroes sc->stats; GET_CONFIG allocates a response and copies sc->cfg into it (ENOMEM on failure); SET_CONFIG returns EINVAL when arglen differs from sizeof(struct ng_async_cfg) or either MRU is outside NG_ASYNC_MIN_MRU..NG_ASYNC_MAX_MRU, otherwise normalizes cfg->enabled to 0 or 1, replaces sc->abuf with a larger buffer when smru grows and sc->sbuf with a larger buffer when amru grows (ENOMEM if an allocation fails; when the second one fails the first buffer has already been replaced and sc->cfg is not updated), resets the receive mode to HUNT with slen 0 when the sync buffer is reallocated or the config is disabled, and copies the new config into sc->cfg. Any other command or cookie gives EINVAL. The code then reaches the done label (directly or through ERROUT): NG_RESPOND_MSG(error, node, item, resp) is called, with resp non-NULL only for a successful GET_STATS or GET_CONFIG, the message is freed with NG_FREE_MSG, and the variable error is returned (0 on success, otherwise the errno chosen above; the macro's own effect on error was not read).

functions.name: ng_apply_item
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: node and item are non-NULL (asserted), the item's hook (if any) carries a reference taken for this call, and the caller has entered the node's read side when rw is NGQRW_R or its write side otherwise. Postcondition: the item's stored hook is taken out of the item. For a data item, an invalid hook or node frees the item and gives EIO; with neither a hook nor a node-type receive-data method the item is freed and 0 is returned; otherwise the receive-data method is called and its result returned (it owns the item). For a message item, an invalid hook is dropped (reference released and hook set to NULL); an invalid node frees the item and gives EINVAL; a generic-cookie message that is not a response goes to ng_generic_msg; with no receive-message method the item is freed and 0 returned; otherwise the method's result is returned. For function items (FN, FN2) an invalid node gives EINVAL and frees the item unless the function is ng_rmnode, and an invalid hook gives EINVAL and frees the item unless the function is ng_con_part2, ng_con_part3 or ng_rmhook_part2; a plain function item is run and freed (error stays 0), an FN2 item is run and its result returned. In all cases the hook reference (if any still held) is released, the read or write side of the node is left, and if the item carried an apply structure: when its depth was 1 and the error is nonzero apply->error is set, and when the last reference to apply is dropped its callback is called with apply->error. The function returns the error value.

functions.name: ng_deflate_decompress
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: node's private data holds an initialized inflate context and DEFLATE_BUF_SIZE inbuf/outbuf buffers, m is a mbuf chain given up to this function, and resultp points to writable storage. Postcondition: *resultp is set to NULL first. If the packet is longer than DEFLATE_BUF_SIZE it counts an error, frees m, resets the sequence number to 0 and returns ENOMEM. m_unshare is then applied (on a NULL result an error is counted and ENOMEM returned, and *resultp stays NULL), the packet is copied into inbuf and the protocol field read (one byte if its low bit is set, else two).
