For the compressed protocol the received sequence number must equal priv->seqnum, otherwise the packet is freed, the sequence number reset and EPIPE returned; otherwise inflate with Z_SYNC_FLUSH is run into outbuf+1 and any result other than Z_OK or Z_STREAM_END frees m, resets the sequence number and returns ENOMEM (Z_MEM_ERROR), EIO (Z_DATA_ERROR) or EINVAL (other); on success the output (with a zero byte placed in front when the first decompressed byte has its low bit set, so that the protocol field is two bytes, and used as is otherwise) is written back into m with m_copyback and m is trimmed with m_adj, or, if m could not hold it, freed with ENOMEM and the sequence number reset. For an uncompressed protocol the first inflate call (a stored-block header) has its return value overwritten and ignored, a second inflate over the packet (without its leading zero protocol byte if present) must return Z_OK or the packet is freed, the sequence number reset and EINVAL returned, and m itself (unmodified) is returned. On success *resultp is set to m, the sequence number is incremented and 0 is returned.

functions.name: ng_l2tp_seq_rack_timeout
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: arg is the node pointer, the caller holds the sequence lock (SEQ_LOCK_ASSERT), seq->xwin[0] is non-NULL and the rack timer is active and not pending (all asserted). Postcondition: returns nothing. It enters the network epoch and the node's vnet, increments xmitRetransmits, and increments seq->rexmits, calling ng_l2tp_seq_failure when the value before the increment was already >= conf.rexmit_max (execution continues afterwards). It re-arms the rack timer with a delay of hz times min(2^rexmits, 2^12 when rexmits > 12, conf.rexmit_max_to), then sets ns to rack, ssth to (cwnd + 1) / 2, cwnd to 1 and acks to 0. It then copies the head packet xwin[0] (L2TP_COPY_MBUF): if the copy fails it releases the sequence lock and increments memoryFailures and nothing is retransmitted; otherwise it calls ng_l2tp_xmit_ctrl(priv, m, seq->ns++), where the post-increment is done by this function as the argument is evaluated, and ng_l2tp_xmit_ctrl itself releases the sequence lock. The vnet and epoch are then left.

functions.name: nglmi_newhook
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: node has a softc and name is a NUL-terminated hook name. Postcondition: for the hook named NG_LMI_HOOK_DEBUG it sets the hook's private pointer to NULL and returns 0 even if the node is already connected, setting no protocol state. Otherwise, when the softc already has SCF_CONNECTED it returns EINVAL with nothing changed. For the hooks annexA, annexD and groupof4 it records the hook (lmi_annexA, lmi_annexD or lmi_group4), sets the hook's private pointer to the softc, sets protoID (8, 8, 9), the LMI type and protoname, and calls nglmi_startup_fixed, which marks the softc fixed and connected, stores the channel hook and starts the ticker; for auto0 and auto1023 it records the channel hook, sets protoname to NAME_NONE (and not protoID or the LMI type), sets the hook's private pointer, and calls nglmi_startup_auto (marking auto and connected, resetting the poll state) only when the other auto hook is already present. An unknown name returns EINVAL. All accepted names return 0.

functions.name: ng_mppc_decompress
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: *datap is an mbuf chain owned by the caller, node private data holds the receive-direction state (history, key, rc4 state, coherency count). Postcondition: m_unshare is applied first and when it returns NULL the function returns ENOMEM leaving *datap unchanged (the chain's fate was not verified here). A packet shorter than the 2-byte MPPC header is freed and EINVAL returned. The header (flags and 12-bit coherency count) is read and stripped, numLost is computed; with the FLUSHED flag the decompression history is reset, and for MPPE the lost count (or lost count divided by the update period) is compared with mppe_max_rekey: above it the packet is freed, EINVAL returned (and the node's receive side disabled when mppe_block_on_max_rekey is set); otherwise keys are updated up to the received count, d->cc is set to the received count and numLost cleared. A nonzero remaining numLost, an encrypted packet when MPPE is not configured, an unencrypted packet when MPPE is configured, or a compressed packet when MPPC is not configured frees the packet and returns EINVAL. An encrypted packet is rc4-decrypted in place (updating the key first in stateless mode or at an update boundary), d->cc is incremented, and a compressed packet is decompressed with MPPC_Decompress into a temporary buffer (ENOMEM with the packet freed if a temporary buffer cannot be allocated, EINVAL with it freed if decompression fails or fills the buffer) and written back into the chain, which becomes NULL if it could not hold the result. On every path that reaches the end *datap is set to the resulting chain and the function returns ENOBUFS if that chain is NULL and 0 otherwise. In the error returns above *datap is not updated.

functions.name: ng_nat_rcvmsg
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: item carries a control message for a ng_nat node whose private data is priv. Postcondition: the message is freed at the end, NG_RESPOND_MSG(error, node, item, resp) is called and the variable error is returned (what the macro does with resp was not read). For typecookie NGM_NAT_COOKIE the cmd is handled: SET_IPADDR (arglen at least sizeof(struct in_addr) else EINVAL) sets the libalias address and the ADDR_DEFINED flag; SET_MODE (arglen check, EINVAL) calls LibAliasSetMode and gives ENOMEM if it returns negative; SET_TARGET sets the target address; REDIRECT_PORT, REDIRECT_ADDR and REDIRECT_PROTO check arglen (EINVAL), allocate an entry (ENOMEM), create the libalias link (ENOMEM and the entry is freed if it is NULL), copy the parameters and description (NUL-terminated), assign the next id, count and append it to the redirect list, and then allocate a response holding the id, giving ENOMEM if that allocation fails after the entry was already added; REDIRECT_DYNAMIC and REDIRECT_DELETE look up an entry by id (ENOENT if absent) and either call LibAliasRedirectDynamic (ENOTTY if it returns -1, entry kept) or LibAliasRedirectDelete, and on success the entry is removed from the list and freed; ADD_SERVER finds the entry by id (ENOENT) and calls LibAliasAddServer (ENOMEM if it returns -1, otherwise lsnat is incremented); LIST_REDIRECTS and LIBALIAS_INFO build a response (ENOMEM if it cannot be allocated); PROXY_RULE needs arglen at least 6 (EINVAL) and gives ENOMEM when LibAliasProxyRule returns nonzero; SET_DLT requires arglen exactly 1 byte equal to DLT_EN10MB or DLT_RAW (EINVAL otherwise). Unknown commands and unknown cookies give EINVAL. A response is attached only for the three redirect-creation commands, LIST_REDIRECTS, LIBALIAS_INFO and the GET_DLT case; otherwise resp is NULL.

functions.name: ng_parse_skip_value
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: s is a NUL-terminated string, off0 is an offset in it, and lenp points to a writable int. Postcondition: it scans tokens from off0 with ng_parse_get_token (which also skips leading white space), counting nested brackets and braces, and stops after the first token if that token is not an opening bracket or brace, or after the token that brings both counts back to zero. On this normal exit it stores in *lenp the distance from off0 to the end of the last scanned token (white space included) and returns 0. It returns EINVAL, without writing *lenp, if the first or any later token is the end of the string (T_EOF), including when an opened bracket or brace is not closed, or if a closing bracket or brace is met while the matching open count is zero (the counts are not cross-checked between brackets and braces except that each type is counted separately). A token that the tokenizer reports as an error (for example an unterminated string, T_ERROR) is not treated specially: its length is whatever the token routine left in the local length (possibly 0), the scan goes on from there, and the function can return 0 with *lenp covering only the preceding white space.

functions.name: ng_pptpgre_rcvdata_lower
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hook is the node's lower (IP/GRE) hook and item carries an mbuf starting with an IP header; no session lock is held on entry. Postcondition: increments receive counters, then returns EINVAL (item freed at the done label) for a packet shorter than the IP and GRE headers or than the headers implied by hasSeq/hasAck (recvRunts), for a negative computed extra length or wrong GRE init bits (recvBadGRE), for an unknown, hookless or disabled session (recvBadCID, found by call id), for a late or duplicate sequence number (with the lock released), and for a duplicate already in the reorder queue. A failed m_pullup (counted in memoryFailures) sets the item's mbuf to NULL and returns ENOBUFS (item freed). With the session lock held, an ack (if present) is validated (an ack beyond what was sent, or not newer than recvAck, is ignored), updates recvAck and, when windowing is enabled, the round-trip estimates, send window and ack timers. A packet without a sequence number is counted as a lone ack, the lock released and 0 returned (item freed). For a data packet, the headers and any padding are trimmed; a packet with sequence recvSeq + 1 goes directly to a stack send queue and recvSeq advances; otherwise it is placed in the sequence-ordered reorder queue if the queue length is below reorder_max (stats recvOutOfOrder), and when the queue is full either the current packet goes to the send queue (if it would sit at the head) or the queue head is moved to the send queue and the current packet is queued (recvReorderOverflow). If the queue entry cannot be allocated the queued packets up to the current sequence are flushed to the send queue, ack and the send queue are processed, the current packet is forwarded on the session hook and ENOMEM is returned. In the normal case contiguous entries from the reorder queue are appended to the send queue, the reorder timer is stopped or started depending on whether the queue is empty, and if the send queue is non-empty the lock is dropped by ng_pptpgre_ack and ng_pptpgre_sendq delivers the packets; the function then returns 0. If the send queue is empty it releases the lock and returns 0 with the item held in the reorder queue.

functions.name: ipsec_chkreplay
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sav and sav->replay are non-NULL (asserted), seqhigh points to a writable uint32_t, seq is the received 32-bit sequence number. Postcondition: returns 1 (accept) or 0 (reject). With replay->wsize == 0 it returns 1 before taking the replay lock and without touching *seqhigh. Otherwise, with the replay lock held, it returns 0 when seq is 0 and replay->last is 0. Otherwise window top tl and th are taken from replay->last and the bottom bl = tl - window + 1: when seq lies in the current window subspace it sets *seqhigh to th and returns 0 if seq <= tl and check_window finds it already seen, else 1. In the other cases: if tl is 0xffffffff and ESN is not enabled, replay->overflow is incremented and, unless SADB_X_EXT_CYCSEQ is set, the wrap statistic is incremented and 0 returned (with CYCSEQ a warning is logged and processing continues); if tl < window - 1 and seq >= bl (previous subspace) it returns 0 when th is 0, else sets *seqhigh to th - 1 and returns 0 if check_window reports a duplicate, otherwise 1; in the remaining (next subspace) case *seqhigh is set to th + 1 (which may be 0 when th is 0xffffffff, in which case overflow is incremented and, unless CYCSEQ is set, it returns 0 after counting the wrap statistic, while with CYCSEQ a warning is logged) and 1 is returned. The replay lock is released before every return after it was taken. The function does not update the replay window.

functions.name: key_flush_sad
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the SAD is initialized and now is the current time; the caller holds no SAHTREE lock. Postcondition: returns nothing. Under the SAHTREE read lock it collects candidates with an extra reference: SAHs with no larval and no alive SAs (empty), larval SAs older than V_key_larval_lifetime (drain), alive SAs whose hard lifetime (addtime, usetime or bytes) has expired (hard-expired), and alive SAs in state MATURE whose soft lifetime has expired or, without ESN, whose replay count or last exceeds 80 percent of the 32-bit space (soft-expired). If nothing was collected it returns. Otherwise under the write lock: drain candidates no longer LARVAL are moved to a free list, the others are unlinked from the larval list and SPI hash and marked DEAD; hard-expired ones already DEAD go to the free list, the others are unlinked from the alive list and SPI hash and marked DEAD; soft-expired ones already DEAD go to the free list, the others are only marked DYING; empty-SAH candidates that now are DEAD or no longer empty simply have their extra reference released with key_freesah (not moved to the free list), and the others are unlinked from the tree and hash and marked DEAD. After unlocking, hard-expired SAs get key_expire(sav, 1) and have the SAH reference and two SA references released, soft-expired SAs get key_expire(sav, 0) and their extra reference released, drained SAs have the SAH reference and two SA references released, free-list SAs have their extra reference released, and empty SAHs have two references released.

functions.name: key_updateaddresses
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: so, m, mhp, sav and saidx come from a parsed SADB_UPDATE message; sav is a referenced SA that has not been cloned (SADB_X_EXT_F_CLONED clear, asserted) and is MATURE or DYING (asserted), and saidx is the caller's copy of the SA index. Postcondition: new source and destination addresses found in the message overwrite saidx (ports set to 0). If either new address is present the function returns the error of key_checksockaddrs if it fails, finds the SAH for the new saidx or creates one (ENOBUFS if creation fails); if neither is present it returns EINVAL unless the SA's protocol is ESP and the NAT-T type, sport and dport headers are all present, and then reuses sav's SAH. It allocates a new SA (ENOBUFS), copies sav up to its chain field into it, sets natt NULL, sah to the chosen SAH and state MATURE, and runs key_setnatt on it. Under the SAHTREE write lock it returns ESRCH if sav is already DEAD, otherwise unlinks sav from its SAH and the SPI hash and marks it DEAD, inserts the new SA into the SAH's alive tree ordered by creation time and into the SPI hash, links a newly created SAH into the tree and hash, copies the counters and marks sav CLONED. After unlocking it releases the caller's last reference to sav, builds a reply from m (key_getmsgbuf_x1; ENOBUFS if that fails, after sav has already been replaced, with m not freed) and otherwise frees m, sends the reply up to all sockets and returns 0. The errors returned before the new SA is allocated (checksockaddrs, SAH creation, missing headers) release nothing because nothing was taken yet; the errors after the allocation (allocation failure, key_setnatt error, ESRCH) go to the fail label, which releases the SAH reference (when one was taken or created) and frees the new SA and its natt, leaving the old SA unchanged.

functions.name: key_setnatt
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sav->natt is NULL (asserted), sav->sah->saidx is initialized, mhp holds the parsed PF_KEY extension headers. Postcondition: returns 0 without changing anything when the SA protocol is not ESP, or when any one of the SADB_X_EXT_NAT_T_TYPE, SPORT or DPORT headers is absent. When all three are present it returns EINVAL if any of their lengths is wrong, or if the NAT-T type is not UDP_ENCAP_ESPINUDP; it then allocates sav->natt (ENOBUFS and the no-memory statistic on failure) and stores sport and dport, returning EINVAL if either is 0 (the allocation stays attached to sav in that case). The optional OA-initiator and OA-responder headers, when present, must have the right header size (else EINVAL); in non-tunnel mode each is checked for a supported family and length (EINVAL otherwise), stored in natt->oai or natt->oar with the IPSEC_NATT_F_OAI or _OAR flag set only when its address differs from the SA index source or destination respectively (an equal address is ignored), and the one's-complement checksum adjustment of the differing addresses is accumulated and stored in natt->cksum; in tunnel mode the OAI and OAR headers are only length-checked and natt->cksum is left 0. It returns 0 after the checks pass.

functions.name: key_acqreset
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: seq is a 32-bit sequence number; the function takes and releases the ACQ lock itself. Postcondition: it searches the ACQ sequence hash bucket for seq under the ACQ lock; if an entry with acq->seq equal to seq is found, its count is set to 0 and its created time to time_second, and the function returns 0; if none is found no state is changed and it returns ESRCH. No other value is returned and no memory or reference passes to or from the caller.

functions.name: esp_output
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: m is an mbuf chain for an outbound packet with at least skip bytes before the payload and a protocol byte at protoff, sp and sav are referenced policy and SA objects, sav->tdb_encalgxform is non-NULL (asserted), idx is the transform index; the destination family of the SA is not required to be supported because the function checks it. Postcondition: it computes the ESP header length, padding and authentication length and returns EPFNOSUPPORT when the SA destination family is neither AF_INET nor AF_INET6, or EMSGSIZE when skip + hlen + rlen + padding + alen exceeds IP_MAXPACKET or IPV6_MAXPACKET. It then makes the chain unshared (ENOBUFS on failure), makes room for the ESP header (ENOBUFS), writes the SPI and, when sav->replay exists, increments the replay count and writes the sequence number and saves its high part, copies the counter for CTR/GCM/ChaCha SAs, appends padding and the ICV space with m_pad (ENOBUFS; m_pad frees the chain on failure), fills in padding bytes per the SA's padding mode, the pad length and the original next-protocol byte, and sets the protocol byte to IPPROTO_ESP. It then allocates a crypto request and an xform_data block (ENOBUFS and a crypto statistic on failure), builds the IV, sets up payload, digest and AAD (allocating a separate AAD buffer when the session needs it, ENOBUFS on failure) and dispatches the request, returning the value of crypto_dispatch or crypto_dispatch_async (the chain, sp and sav then belong to the callback esp_output_cb via the xform_data). In each of the error returns listed before the dispatch, the chain (if not already freed) is freed and the references on sav and sp are released with key_freesav and key_freesp.

functions.name: nl_soreceive
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: mp is NULL and uio is non-NULL (asserted), so is a netlink socket with an attached pcb. Postcondition: before taking the receive lock it stores a duplicate of an empty AF_NETLINK source address in *psa when psa is non-NULL, and a NETLINK_MSG_INFO control mbuf in *controlp when controlp is non-NULL and NLF_MSG_INFO is set. It then returns the error of SOCK_IO_RECV_LOCK if the I/O lock cannot be taken, EWOULDBLOCK (after releasing both locks) if the receive queue is empty and the socket is nonblocking (SS_NBIO, MSG_DONTWAIT or MSG_NBIO), or the error of sbwait if waiting for data fails (both locks released); each of these three returns happens without calling nl_on_transmit. Otherwise it scans the queued buffers and counts how many whole netlink messages fit in uio->uio_resid, handling a first oversized message (truncation with MSG_TRUNC, or a partial buffer) and, unless peeking, advances the queue and reduces sb_acc and sb_ccc; with the buffer lock dropped it copies the data with uiomove (once an error occurs it stops copying but still frees the consumed buffers unless peeking), adjusts uio_resid for truncation, adds the message count to the thread's ru_msgrcv, updates *flagsp when flagsp is non-NULL, releases the I/O lock, calls nl_on_transmit and returns the uiomove error (0 if none).

functions.name: smb_t2_reply
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: t2p is an initialized TRANS2 request with a request t2p->t2_rq that has been enqueued. Postcondition: the function first calls smb_rq_reply(rqp), which waits for a reply, and returns its error if it fails. If SMBT2_ALLSENT is clear (an interim response to a multi-packet request), it skips to the next record under SMBRQ_SLOCK and returns 0 without placing any data or setting SMBT2_ALLRECV. Otherwise it loops over reply fragments: it reads the word count (ENOENT if below 10), the total parameter and data counts (keeping the smaller values seen), the parameter and data counts, offsets and displacements, returning the error of a failed read, EINVAL when a nonempty parameter or data fragment is not at the expected displacement, then skips the remaining words and byte count and places the data and parameter fragments into t2_rdata and t2_rparam with smb_t2_placedata, returning its error if it fails. When the accumulated parameter and data totals reach the totals, SMBT2_ALLRECV is set and 0 returned; otherwise it moves to the next record under the lock, calls smb_rq_reply again and returns its error if it fails, and repeats.

functions.name: smb_t2_request_int
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: t2p points to an initialized TRANS2 request with t2_vc, t2_cred and t2_source valid and with parameter and data chains (possibly empty) in t2_tparam and t2_tdata. Postcondition: it returns EINVAL, before allocating any request and without touching the reply chains, when the parameter or data length exceeds 0xffff, and returns the error of smb_rq_alloc, likewise with no request and nothing torn down, if allocation fails. Otherwise it builds the first TRANSACTION or TRANSACTION2 request carrying as much of the parameters (or parameters and data) as fits in the transmit maximum, enqueues it, sets SMBT2_ALLSENT if everything fit, and calls smb_t2_reply. If data remains it then builds and queues secondary requests in a loop, setting SMBT2_SECONDARY, until everything is sent, then sets SMBT2_ALLSENT and re-initializes the reply chains for reading. Errors from building a fragment, smb_rq_enqueue (skipping smb_iod_removerq as it was not enqueued), smb_t2_reply, smb_rq_new or smb_iod_request are returned. In every path after the request was allocated (success included) the request is released with smb_rq_done (after smb_iod_removerq on paths that got past enqueue), and when an error occurred SMBT2_RESTART is set if the request had SMBR_RESTART and both reply chains are freed with md_done. t2p->t2_rq is left pointing to the request that has been released in those paths.

functions.name: nbssn_rq_request
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: nbp has a transport socket in nbp_tso, valid nbp_paddr and nbp_laddr names, and a timeout in nbp_timo. Postcondition: it builds and sends a NetBIOS session request (returning the error of mb_init or nb_sosend, with the state unchanged; on send success nbp_state becomes NBST_RQSENT). It then waits for the socket with selsocket: a timeout gives ETIMEDOUT and any other wait error is returned; the reply is read with nbssn_recv and its error returned. For a positive session response it sets nbp_state to NBST_SESSION and NBF_CONNECTED in nbp_flags and returns 0. A reply code that is neither positive nor retarget, or a retarget whose length is not 6, gives ECONNABORTED. For a retarget response it reads the address and port, sets nbp_state to NBST_RETARGET, disconnects, connects to the new address with nb_connect_in and, if that succeeded, recurses into nbssn_rq_request; if either the connect or the recursive call fails it disconnects again and returns that error, and if the recursive call succeeds it returns 0 with the state left by the recursive call (NBST_SESSION after a positive response). The reply chain is freed with md_done when one was received, and the working structures are freed on all returns.

functions.name: bootpc_init
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: called once during boot (SYSINIT SI_SUB_ROOT_CONF) in a thread context with the network stack initialized. Postcondition: returns nothing. It returns at once, changing nothing, if nfs_diskless_valid is already nonzero, or if the environment variable vfs.root.mountfrom is set to a value not starting with "nfs:" (a message is printed and the string freed). Otherwise it allocates a global context and, in the normal build, counts broadcast Ethernet-style interfaces; with none it prints a warning and goes to the cleanup label without trying BOOTP. It allocates per-interface contexts, fills them from the interfaces found (panicking if an interface has no link-level hardware address), retrying with pauses until a timeout when none is usable and then calling panic ("no suitable interface") when the timeout expires with no usable interface. It creates a UDP socket (panicking on error), sets up the interfaces, composes and sends the queries with bootpc_call (a failure only prints a message), decodes replies for resolved interfaces, and with the BOOTP_NFSROOT option panics when no root path was offered and there are no root overrides. It adjusts the interfaces, closes the socket, and picks the interface that has a root path, else a resolved one; if none it goes to cleanup. If a root path was received it sets boot.netif.name, adds a default route, mounts the root with md_mount (on failure it panics unless a root override exists, in which case it goes to cleanup), and sets rootdevnames[0] to "nfs:" and nfs_diskless_valid to 3. It then copies the chosen interface's address, broadcast, mask and gateway into the diskless structure. The cleanup label frees the interface contexts and the global context.

functions.name: bootpc_received
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: gctx holds a received packet of gctx->replylen bytes in gctx->reply, ifctx is the interface context whose state and dhcpquerytype are initialized. Postcondition: returns 0 without modifying ifctx when the packet has a bad option, when its DHCP message type does not suit the query (for DHCP_DISCOVER: not DHCP_OFFER and, unless BOOTP_FORCE_DHCP is defined, not DHCP_NOMSG; for DHCP_REQUEST: not DHCP_ACK), or when ifctx is already in state IF_BOOTP_RESOLVED, or its query type is DHCP_DISCOVER and its state is IF_DHCP_OFFERED or IF_DHCP_RESOLVED, and either the reply stored in ifctx already has a root-path tag or the new reply has none (IF_DHCP_RESOLVED does not count for a DHCP_REQUEST query). Otherwise it copies the packet into ifctx->reply and updates replylen, then moves the state: IF_BOOTP_UNRESOLVED to IF_BOOTP_RESOLVED; IF_DHCP_UNRESOLVED with a DISCOVER query to IF_DHCP_OFFERED when the reply is an offer and to IF_BOOTP_RESOLVED otherwise; IF_DHCP_OFFERED with a REQUEST query to IF_DHCP_RESOLVED; other states are left as they are (so a repeated message can return 1 with the state unchanged). If the query is DHCP_DISCOVER and the state is not IF_BOOTP_RESOLVED it records the DHCP server id when a 4-byte one is present (setting or clearing gotdhcpserver) and returns 1. Otherwise it sets gotrootpath, gotgw and gotnetmask from the tags of the stored reply and returns 1.

functions.name: nlm_setlock
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: host, ext, vers, timo, vp, op, fl, fh, svid, fhlen and size describe a lock request, flags may contain F_WAIT, reclaim says whether this is a reclaim, and retries is the number of RPC retries allowed. Postcondition: it returns the error of nlm_init_lock if building the lock arguments fails. In its retry loop it returns ENOLCK when no RPC client can be obtained (also inside the cancel loop); when the lock RPC does not succeed it deregisters the wait handle (if blocking) and either retries (decrementing retries) or returns EINVAL when retries are used up. For a denied-grace-period reply it sleeps with tsleep (doubling the delay up to 30 seconds) and loops, returning the tsleep error if it is not EWOULDBLOCK. For a blocking request answered nlm4_blocked it waits with nlm_wait_lock: on EWOULDBLOCK it lengthens the delay and loops; on another error it sends cancel requests (repeating with pauses until the RPC succeeds, ENOLCK if no client) and the error from the wait is kept as the result, except that a cancel answered nlm_denied sets the result to 0 on the assumption that the lock was granted. For any other reply the result is nlm_map_status of the status. When the result is 0 and reclaim is false the lock is recorded locally with nlm_record_lock and nlm_host_monitor is called; the function then returns the result.

functions.name: cm_sidr_req_handler
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: work is a CM work item whose received MAD is a SIDR REQ, with a valid port and device. Postcondition: it creates a new CM id with ib_create_cm_id and returns that call's error (PTR_ERR) if it fails. Otherwise it fills in the id's address vector from the work completion (cm_init_av_for_lap), the remote id and tid from the request, and increments its work count. Every failure after the id was created takes the out label, which destroys the new id and returns -EINVAL (not the underlying error): a cm_init_av_for_lap failure, a duplicate remote SIDR id (cm_insert_remote_sidr found one; the CM_RECV_DUPLICATES counter for SIDR REQ is incremented), and no listener matching the service id (the request is first answered with cm_reject_sidr_req(IB_SIDR_UNSUPPORTED)). On a match the id's state is IB_CM_SIDR_REQ_RCVD, references are taken on both the new id and the listener, the listener's handler and context are copied into the new id with the service id and mask, the event is formatted, the work is processed by cm_process_work, the listener reference is dropped and 0 is returned.

functions.name: cm_enter_timewait
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: cm_id_priv is a valid cm_id_private with a non-NULL timewait_info. Postcondition: returns nothing. If ib_get_client_data returns NULL for the id's device it returns at once, leaving id.state and cm_id_priv->timewait_info unchanged. Otherwise, under cm.lock, it calls cm_cleanup_timewait on the timewait info (not read here) and appends timewait_info->list to cm.timewait_list, then releases the lock. After the lock is released it sets id.state to IB_CM_TIMEWAIT and converts the address-vector timeout to milliseconds; it takes cm.lock again and, unless the cm_device is going down, queues the timewait work on cm.wq with a delay of that many milliseconds, releases the lock and finally sets cm_id_priv->timewait_info to NULL (also outside any lock).

functions.name: cma_port_from_service_id
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: service_id is a 64-bit big-endian value. Postcondition: returns (u16)be64_to_cpu(service_id), the low 16 bits of the host-order number obtained by converting service_id from big-endian. On a big-endian host this is service_id & 0xffff; on a little-endian host it is the byte-swapped upper 16 bits of the stored value (bswap16(service_id >> 48)). It reads no memory and takes no locks.

functions.name: cma_ib_handler
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: cm_id->context is a valid rdma_id_private whose handler_mutex is initialized. Postcondition: it takes handler_mutex and, if the event is not IB_CM_TIMEWAIT_EXIT and the state is not RDMA_CM_CONNECT, or the event is TIMEWAIT_EXIT and the state is not RDMA_CM_DISCONNECT, it releases the mutex and returns 0 without calling the user handler. It then builds an RDMA CM event from the IB CM event: REQ/REP errors give UNREACHABLE with -ETIMEDOUT; REP_RECEIVED gives CONNECT_ERROR or CONNECT_RESPONSE for SDP according to sdp_verify_rep, and otherwise ESTABLISHED or CONNECT_ERROR from cma_rep_recv when a QP exists, or CONNECT_RESPONSE when none, with the REP data attached; RTU_RECEIVED and USER_ESTABLISHED give ESTABLISHED; DREQ_ERROR (with -ETIMEDOUT), DREQ_RECEIVED and DREP_RECEIVED require cma_comp_exch from CONNECT to DISCONNECT (else it returns 0 without dispatch) and give DISCONNECTED; TIMEWAIT_EXIT gives TIMEWAIT_EXIT; REJ_RECEIVED moves the QP to error and gives REJECTED with the reject data. MRA_RECEIVED and unexpected events (a message is printed for the latter) return 0 without dispatch. The user's event_handler is then called; if it returns nonzero, id_priv->cm_id.ib is set to NULL, the state is exchanged to RDMA_CM_DESTROYING, the mutex is released, the id is destroyed with rdma_destroy_id, and the handler's nonzero value is returned. Otherwise the mutex is released and 0 is returned.

functions.name: rdma_resolve_addr
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: id is a valid rdma_cm_id and dst_addr is a valid sockaddr (src_addr may be NULL). Postcondition: if the id is in RDMA_CM_IDLE it first calls cma_bind_addr and returns its error if it fails (the state then is whatever that call left, not changed by this function). It returns -EINVAL when the id's address family differs from dst_addr->sa_family or when the state cannot be moved from RDMA_CM_ADDR_BOUND to RDMA_CM_ADDR_QUERY. After that move it takes an extra reference, copies dst_addr, and resolves it: through cma_resolve_loopback for an any address, cma_resolve_ib_addr for AF_IB, otherwise cma_check_linklocal followed by rdma_resolve_ip with addr_handler as callback. It returns 0 when that step succeeded, with the id in RDMA_CM_ADDR_QUERY and the extra reference to be released by the asynchronous handler; when that step returned an error, the state is set back to ADDR_BOUND (cma_comp_exch from ADDR_QUERY), the reference is dropped and the error of cma_resolve_loopback, cma_resolve_ib_addr, cma_check_linklocal or rdma_resolve_ip is returned.

functions.name: cma_remove_id_dev
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: id_priv is a valid rdma_id_private registered with the device being removed. Postcondition: the state is exchanged to RDMA_CM_DEVICE_REMOVAL with cma_exch; if the previous state was RDMA_CM_DESTROYING the function returns 0 at once (handler_mutex was never taken, nothing cancelled and no handler called). Otherwise it calls cma_cancel_operation for the previous state, takes handler_mutex, and if the state is no longer RDMA_CM_DEVICE_REMOVAL it releases the mutex and returns 0 without calling the handler; otherwise it calls id_priv->id.event_handler with an RDMA_CM_EVENT_DEVICE_REMOVAL event, releases the mutex and returns the handler's return value (the caller cma_process_remove destroys the id when this is nonzero).

functions.name: iw_cm_listen
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: cm_id is a valid iw_cm_id embedded in an iwcm_id_private; a backlog of 0 is replaced by default_backlog. Postcondition: it first calls alloc_work_entries for the backlog, before looking at the state, and returns its error if it fails (the state is not changed and nothing else is done). It then takes the id lock and, if the state is IW_CM_STATE_IDLE, sets it to IW_CM_STATE_LISTEN, drops the lock, calls iw_cm_map and, when that succeeds, the device's create_listen with the backlog; if either fails the state is set back to IW_CM_STATE_IDLE and the error (negative errno) is returned, otherwise 0 is returned. If the state is not IDLE it returns -EINVAL, after the work entries were already allocated. The lock is released before the return in the paths where it was taken.

functions.name: process_rmpp_ack
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: agent is a valid MAD agent private and mad_recv_wc holds a received RMPP ACK MAD. Postcondition: returns nothing. A nonzero rmpp_status calls abort_send and nack_recv with IB_MGMT_RMPP_STATUS_BAD_STATUS and returns; newwin < seg_num does the same with IB_MGMT_RMPP_STATUS_W2S. Otherwise, under the agent lock, it looks up the matching send: with none, an ACK with seg_num 0 is passed to process_ds_ack and the function then returns (any other unmatched ACK just returns). If last_ack equals the segment count and the timeout is set (a repeated ACK for a DS transaction) the lock is dropped and ack_ds_ack is called. If last_ack equals the segment count, or no timeout is set, or the send status is not success, the ACK is ignored. If seg_num exceeds the segment count or the current newwin of the send, the lock is dropped and abort_send and nack_recv are called with IB_MGMT_RMPP_STATUS_S2B. An old ACK (newwin smaller than the recorded newwin, or seg_num below last_ack) is ignored. Otherwise, only when seg_num is greater than last_ack, last_ack is advanced and retries_left reset; newwin is then stored. If last_ack now equals the segment count the send is completed (when the buffer has no timeout the MAD is marked done and completed with success) or the timeout is reset and ack_ds_ack called; otherwise, when the send's refcount is 1 and more segments can be sent within the window, the next segment is sent with send_next_seg and, if that succeeds, refcount is incremented and the send moved to the tail of the agent's send list. The agent lock is released before each return after it was taken.

functions.name: uapi_merge_def
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: uapi and ibdev are valid; def_list is NULL or an array of uapi_definition entries terminated by an entry of kind UAPI_DEF_END. Postcondition: a NULL def_list returns 0 at once. Otherwise the entries are processed in order and the function returns 0 when UAPI_DEF_END is reached. A CHAIN entry recurses on its chained list and returns its error if nonzero; a CHAIN_OBJ_TREE entry gives -EINVAL after a WARN_ON when the entry's object id differs from the tree's id, else it sets the current object key and returns the error of uapi_merge_obj_tree if nonzero; the IS_SUPPORTED_DEV_FN and IS_SUPPORTED_FUNC entries do nothing when the device supports the function and otherwise call uapi_disable_elm, returning its error if nonzero; OBJECT_START sets the current object key and adds the object element with uapi_add_get_elm, returning its error (PTR_ERR) on failure; WRITE calls uapi_create_write with the current keys and returns its error if nonzero; an unknown kind gives -EINVAL after a WARN_ON. The function returns the first nonzero error encountered, leaving earlier merges in place.

functions.name: __ipoib_ib_dev_flush
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: priv is a valid IPoIB device private structure with an initialized vlan_mutex and child_intfs list, level is an ipoib_flush_level value. Postcondition: returns nothing. Under vlan_mutex it first calls itself for every child interface with the same level and then releases the mutex. It then returns without doing anything more if IPOIB_FLAG_INITIALIZED is clear or IPOIB_FLAG_ADMIN_UP is clear. For IPOIB_FLUSH_HEAVY: if ib_find_pkey fails it clears IPOIB_PKEY_ASSIGNED, brings the device down and stops it and returns if ipoib_pkey_dev_delay_open returns true; otherwise (including after a find failure when delay_open is false) it sets IPOIB_PKEY_ASSIGNED with test_and_set_bit and returns without further work if that bit was already set and new_index equals priv->pkey_index (this return cannot happen right after a failed find, because the bit was just cleared), else it stores new_index as pkey_index (after a failed find new_index is whatever ib_find_pkey left it). For IPOIB_FLUSH_LIGHT it marks paths invalid and flushes the multicast state; for levels at or above NORMAL it calls ipoib_ib_dev_down; for HEAVY it also stops and reopens the device. Finally, if ADMIN_UP is still set it calls ipoib_ib_dev_up for levels at or above NORMAL and runs ipoib_mcast_restart_task.

functions.name: sdp_connect_handler
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sk is a listening SDP socket, id is the incoming rdma_cm_id and event->param.conn.private_data points to a readable struct sdp_hh (its max_adverts, bsdh.bufs and localrcvsz fields are read without a NULL or length check). Postcondition: returns -EINVAL without creating a child when h->max_adverts is 0, -ENOMEM when sonewconn fails, and the error of sdp_init_qp(child, id) when that fails, in which case the child socket created by sonewconn is not released here and the function does not touch the new ssk. On success it takes the child's write lock, sets id->context to the child's sdp_sock, ssk->id, ssk->socket and a held credential, copies the remote port and address and only the local port (lport) from the id's route (the local address is not set here), sets max_bufs and the tx credits from the hello header, min_bufs as a quarter of the credits, xmit_size_goal from localrcvsz less the BSDH size, initializes the buffers with rcvbuf_initial_size, sets the state to TCPS_SYN_RECEIVED, releases the lock and returns 0.

functions.name: sdp_cma_handler
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: id and event are the rdma_cm callback arguments; id->context is NULL or an sdp_sock whose socket and id fields may themselves be NULL. Postcondition: if id->context is NULL, or its socket or id is missing, it returns -EINVAL for RDMA_CM_EVENT_CONNECT_REQUEST and 0 for any other event, changing nothing. Otherwise it dispatches on event->event and sets rc: ADDR_RESOLVED (-ENETUNREACH if only IB link layers are allowed and the port's is not, else rdma_resolve_route's result); ADDR_ERROR (-ENETUNREACH); ROUTE_RESOLVED (sdp_init_qp, then builds a hello and rdma_connect); ROUTE_ERROR (-ETIMEDOUT); CONNECT_REQUEST (sdp_connect_handler; on failure rdma_reject; on success builds a hello-ack and calls rdma_accept, and if that fails clears ssk->id, id->qp and id->context of the new child sdp_sock); CONNECT_RESPONSE (sdp_response_handler, with rdma_reject on error, else rdma_accept); CONNECT_ERROR (-ETIMEDOUT); UNREACHABLE (-ENETUNREACH); REJECTED (-ECONNREFUSED); ESTABLISHED (sdp_connected_handler); DISCONNECTED (clears qp_active, rdma_disconnect, and, unless the state is TCPS_TIME_WAIT, rc = -EPIPE if sdp_disconnected_handler returns nonzero); TIMEWAIT_EXIT (sdp_disconnected_handler's result); DEVICE_REMOVAL (-ENETRESET); anything else prints a message and gives -ECONNABORTED. If rc is nonzero afterwards the function takes the socket's write lock and, only when ssk->id still equals id, clears ssk->id, id->qp and id->context and calls sdp_notify(ssk, -rc) (which, when it returns nonzero, leaves the lock released by itself), otherwise releases the lock; it returns rc.

functions.name: sdp_wait_rdmardcompl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ssk->tx_sa is non-NULL, timeo_p points to the remaining timeout, the caller holds the socket lock (which is dropped while sleeping through posts_handler_put and re-taken with posts_handler_get). Postcondition: the function loops while ssk->qp_active is set. In the loop it breaks with -ETIME and TX_SA_TIMEDOUT set when *timeo_p is 0; with -EINVAL and TX_SA_ERROR set when bytes_acked exceeds bytes_sent; with -EAGAIN when TX_SA_SENDSM is set in the abort flags; and, when ignore_signals is 0, with -EINTR and TX_SA_INTRRUPTED if a signal is pending, or with -ETIME and TX_SA_CROSS_SEND if ssk->rx_sa is set while bytes_acked < bytes_sent. Otherwise it sleeps (sk_wait_event on a local copy of the timeout) and breaks with err 0 when bytes_acked equals bytes_sent after waking. After the loop, if ssk->qp_active is clear it returns -EINVAL (whatever err was, and without setting any abort flag); otherwise it returns err. *timeo_p is not modified by this function.

functions.name: crypto_cursor_advance
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: cc is an initialized crypto buffer cursor and amount does not exceed the bytes left in its buffer (asserted with MPASS only for CRYPTO_BUF_CONTIG and CRYPTO_BUF_SINGLE_MBUF; the other types rely on the caller). Postcondition: returns nothing and advances the cursor by amount bytes according to cc_type. CONTIG: cc_buf advances and cc_buf_len decreases by amount. MBUF: cc_offset grows within the current mbuf when amount is smaller than the bytes left in it; otherwise whole mbufs are consumed (cc_mbuf moved to m_next with cc_offset 0) until the amount is used up; cc_buf_len is not modified. SINGLE_MBUF: cc_offset += amount (cc_mbuf unchanged). VMPAGE: cc_buf_len is decreased by amount for a partial advance within a page, or by the bytes left in each page consumed (cc_vmpage incremented, offset 0), stopping when amount is used up or cc_buf_len reaches 0. UIO: cc_offset grows within the current iovec for a partial advance without changing cc_buf_len; for each whole iovec consumed cc_buf_len is decreased by its remaining bytes, cc_iov is incremented and cc_offset set to 0. For an invalid type it panics under INVARIANTS and does nothing otherwise.

functions.name: crypto_done
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: crp is a completed request whose crp_session, crp_callback and crp_retw_id are valid and whose crp_flags and crp_seq were set by the submitter. Postcondition: returns nothing. If crp_etype is nonzero the error statistic is incremented. If CRYPTO_F_ASYNC_ORDERED is clear and either CRYPTO_F_CBIMM is set or CRYPTO_F_CBIFSYNC is set and the session is synchronous, crp->crp_callback(crp) is called directly in this context. Otherwise the request is queued on its return worker under the worker's lock: with CRYPTO_F_ASYNC_ORDERED it is inserted into crp_ordered_ret_q in ascending crp_seq order (after the last entry with a smaller sequence found scanning from the tail, or at the head if none) and the worker is woken if crp_seq equals reorder_cur_seq; without it, it is appended to the tail of crp_ret_q and the worker is woken if that queue was empty. The lock is released after the optional wakeup_one.

functions.name: ktls_ocf_tls_cbc_encrypt
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: tls->sync_dispatch is true (asserted), outiovcnt + 1 <= m->m_epg_npgs + 2 (asserted), m is an unmapped TLS record mbuf; with INVARIANTS and an implicit IV the caller must not run another encryption on this session at once (asserted) and m->m_epg_seqno must equal os->next_seqno. Postcondition: under INVARIANTS with an implicit IV a sequence mismatch prints a message and returns EINVAL with nothing else changed; otherwise in_progress is set. It computes the MAC over the pseudo-header and record payload with the MAC session; if that dispatch fails the error is returned with the record not modified yet (the padding has not been written), after clearing in_progress under INVARIANTS. Otherwise it writes the TLS CBC padding bytes into the trailer after the MAC, then dispatches the CBC encryption of the payload and trailer, in place or, when outiov is non-NULL, to the output iovecs, with the IV taken from os->iv (implicit IV) or from the record header (explicit IV). For an implicit IV the function afterwards copies the last AES block of the record's trailer (read from the mbuf's trailer buffer, not from outiov) into os->iv, and under INVARIANTS sets os->next_seqno to m_epg_seqno + 1 and clears in_progress; this happens whether or not the encryption dispatch returned an error. It returns the error of the encryption dispatch (0 on success).

functions.name: moea_pte_spill
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: addr is a virtual address; the caller does not hold moea_table_mutex. Postcondition: increments moea_pte_spills and takes moea_table_mutex, releasing it before each return. It computes the primary PTEG index from the segment register and addr, picks a pseudo-random slot i (low bits of the time base) in that PTEG, and scans that PTEG's pvo list. For the first pvo whose PTE matches addr it calls moea_pte_insert: if that returns a slot (>= 0) the pvo's PTEG index is set, moea_pte_overflow is decremented and it returns 1 immediately; otherwise that pvo becomes the source. It also looks for a victim pvo whose PTE equals the PTE currently in slot i (only when that PTE is in the primary hash). If no source pvo was found it returns 0 with no change. If a source was found but no victim in the primary list, it panics when slot i's PTE is not a secondary-hash entry and otherwise searches the secondary PTEG's list for the victim, panicking if none exists. With a source and a victim it clears the HID bit in the source's PTE, unsets the victim's PTE in slot i, sets the source's PTE there, clears the victim's PTEG index, sets the source's index to i, increments moea_pte_replacements and returns 1.

functions.name: mmu_radix_advise
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: pmap is a valid pmap and [sva, eva) a range of its addresses. Postcondition: for any advice other than MADV_DONTNEED or MADV_FREE it returns at once without taking the pmap lock or changing anything. Otherwise it holds the pmap lock while walking the range by 1GB, 512GB and 2MB steps, skipping invalid upper-level entries. A valid non-managed 2MB leaf mapping is skipped; a valid managed one is demoted with pmap_demote_l3e_locked: if the demotion fails (the mapping was destroyed, nothing removed) the range is skipped; if it succeeds and the old mapping was not wired, the PTE of the last page of the range within that 2MB region is removed with pmap_remove_pte (and anychanged set). Then each PTE of the range that is both managed and valid is processed: if it is modified and writable, then for MADV_DONTNEED its page is first marked dirty, and for either advice the modified and accessed bits are cleared; else if only the accessed bit is set it is cleared; other PTEs are left alone. If anything changed, pmap_invalidate_all(pmap) is called. The lock is released before returning.

functions.name: mmu_radix_dev_direct_mapped
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: pa and size describe a physical address range. Postcondition: returns the value of mem_valid(pa, size) (mem_valid was not read here; the previous text assumed it returns 0 or EINVAL). The function takes no locks and has no other side effects apart from a trace macro.

functions.name: mmu_radix_change_attr
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: va and size describe a kernel virtual address range, mode is a memory attribute. Postcondition: it takes the kernel_pmap lock, calls pmap_change_attr_locked(va, size, mode, true), releases the lock and returns that function's result, which can be 0, EINVAL, ENOMEM or an error of a recursive direct-map call. The lock is released before the return and nothing is returned to the caller except that status.

functions.name: pmap_change_attr_locked
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller holds the kernel_pmap lock (asserted), va and size describe a kernel address range, mode is a memory attribute, flush says whether to flush caches. Postcondition: the range is rounded to whole pages. It returns EINVAL if the rounded base is below DMAP_MIN_ADDRESS. A first pass over the range returns EINVAL if an L2, L3 or PTE entry is absent or zero, skips 1GB and 2MB leaf mappings that already have the requested attribute or are fully covered, and demotes other large leaf mappings (ENOMEM if a demotion fails); demotions made before a later failure stay in place. A second pass sets the attribute bits of each leaf, L3 and PTE entry whose attribute differs (recording that something changed) and collects runs of kernel-virtual physical ranges below dmaplimit, applying pmap_change_attr_locked recursively to the corresponding direct-map addresses; an error from a recursive call stops the pass (partial changes remain) and is returned, and a last pending run is also applied if no error occurred. If anything changed it calls pmap_invalidate_all(kernel_pmap) and, when flush is true, flushes the cache range from the base to the last address reached, also when a recursive call failed. It returns 0 only when no error occurred.

functions.name: mpc74xx_l2_enable
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: runs on an MPC74xx-class CPU with access to SPR_L2CR; l2cr_config is the desired L2CR value. Postcondition: it chooses the in-progress bit to wait on from the processor version (L2CR_L2IP for MPC7400 and MPC7410, L2CR_L2I otherwise). If the current L2CR value already has L2CR_L2E set, it returns that current L2CR value and writes nothing. Otherwise it writes (l2cr_config with L2CR_L2E cleared) ORed with L2CR_L2I to L2CR to start an invalidate, spins until the chosen in-progress bit reads as clear (a hardware condition that this function cannot itself guarantee), issues powerpc_sync, writes l2cr_config to L2CR, issues powerpc_sync and returns l2cr_config. The L2 is therefore enabled by the final write only if l2cr_config itself has L2CR_L2E set; the function does not set that bit.

functions.name: DB_SHOW_COMMAND(tlb0, tlb0_print_tlbentries)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function (debugger command "show tlb0", defined with DB_SHOW_COMMAND(tlb0, tlb0_print_tlbentries)). Precondition: called from the kernel debugger on a Book-E PowerPC CPU where the MAS registers and tlbre can be used. Postcondition: prints "TLB0 entries:" and then, for each way from 0 to TLB0_WAYS-1 and each entry index from 0 to TLB0_ENTRIES_PER_WAY-1, writes MAS0 (TLB select 0 and the way) and MAS2 (the entry index), executes isync and tlbre, reads MAS1, MAS2, MAS3 and MAS7, computes the table index with tlb0_tableidx(mas2, way) and calls tlb_print_entry with it and those registers. It returns nothing and changes MAS0 and MAS2 as a side effect.

functions.name: fpu_execute
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: tf is the trap frame of the faulting thread, fe is an FP emulator state whose fe_fpstate points to the thread's FPU state, insn points to the instruction word to emulate. Postcondition: it first copies the FPSCR word from fe_fpstate into fe_fpscr. For load/store opcodes (the D-form lfs..stfdu range and the X-form opcode 31 forms) the effective address is computed from tf->fixreg; stfiwx stores a word with copyout; the other X-form opcode-31 forms must be recognized FP load/store ones or it returns NOTFPU; an update form with RA = 0 returns NOTFPU. A store copies out with copyout (single precision values are converted first), a load copies in with copyin into the FP register (single precision values converted to double); a faulting copyin or copyout returns FAULT; on success an update form writes the address back to tf->fixreg[ra] and 0 is returned immediately, without the FPSCR write-back below. For opcode 59 and 63 FP instructions the function decodes the operation (compare, round, convert to integer, FPSCR moves, negate, abs, move, select, add, subtract, multiply, divide, sqrt, reciprocal estimates, fused multiply forms), writes results or FPSCR/CR fields as the instruction requires, and returns NOTFPU for an unrecognized extended opcode; any other primary opcode returns NOTFPU. After a recognized FP instruction the result (if any) is imploded into the destination FP register, the FPSCR exception bits in fe_cx are merged into the new FPSCR value (FX, FEX, FPRF, VX), CR1 or the selected CR field is updated when the instruction asks for it, the new FPSCR word is stored into fe_fpstate, and the function returns FPE when the FEX bit is set in it and 0 otherwise.

functions.name: fpu_sqrt
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: fe is an FP emulator state whose first operand fe_f1 holds an exploded (unpacked) floating-point number. Postcondition: returns a pointer to the result number. For a NaN operand it sets FPSCR_VXSNAN in fe->fe_cx and returns &fe->fe_f1 unchanged; for a zero operand it sets FPSCR_ZX in fe_cx, changes the operand's class to infinity and returns it; for a negative operand it sets FPSCR_VXSQRT and returns the pointer from fpu_newnan(fe); for an infinity it returns &fe->fe_f1 unchanged. Otherwise it halves the exponent (doubling the mantissa first when the exponent is odd), computes the square root of the 4-word mantissa one bit at a time into fp_mant[0..3] of fe_f1, sets fp_sticky to the OR of the remaining remainder words, and returns &fe->fe_f1. It takes no locks and modifies only *fe (the operand, fe_cx).

functions.name: ATOMIC_STORE_LOAD(long)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function atomic_load_acq_long, produced by the macro invocation ATOMIC_STORE_LOAD(long) in the powerpc64 build (the macro is defined at atomic.h:503-520, invoked at 528). Precondition: p points to a readable, suitably aligned u_long. Postcondition: it reads the whole u_long *p into a local, then executes powerpc_lwsync(), and returns the value read. It takes no lock and has no error return. On 32-bit powerpc the same name is instead a separate inline function (atomic.h:536-541) that returns atomic_load_acq_int of the pointer cast to u_int, widened to u_long.

functions.name: ATOMIC_STORE_LOAD(long)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function atomic_store_rel_long, produced by the macro invocation ATOMIC_STORE_LOAD(long) in the powerpc64 build (macro at atomic.h:503-520). Precondition: p points to a writable, suitably aligned u_long. Postcondition: it executes powerpc_lwsync() and then stores the whole u_long v to *p (the store statement is on the stripped line 519 of the macro, read from the macro's shape). It returns nothing, takes no lock, and has no error return. On 32-bit powerpc the same name is a separate inline function (atomic.h:543-548) that calls atomic_store_rel_int with the pointer cast to u_int and the value truncated to u_int.

functions.name: pmac_therm_manage_fans
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the global sensors and fans lists are well-formed with valid read and set callbacks. Postcondition: returns nothing. If enable_pmac_thermal is zero it returns at once without touching any sensor or fan. Otherwise, for each sensor it calls the read callback and replaces last_val with the result only when it is positive (otherwise the previous last_val is kept); if last_val exceeds the sensor's max_temp it increments critical_count, prints a warning and, when critical_count reaches MAX_CRITICAL_COUNT, prints a message and calls shutdown_nice(RB_POWEROFF); otherwise it decrements critical_count when it is above zero. Then for each fan it computes for every sensor the excess of the (max_temp-capped) temperature over target_temp as a percentage, clamped at 0, tracking the sum over all sensors and the maximum over sensors in the fan's zone; with no sensors the fan's set callback is called with default_rpm and the fan is skipped; otherwise the zone maximum (or the average when the zone has no sensor), capped at 100, is converted to a speed between min_rpm and max_rpm; when that speed is at least the fan's last_val the speed is adopted and the hysteresis timer reset, otherwise the timer is decremented and the speed adopted only when the timer reaches 0; finally the fan's set callback is called with fan->last_val.

functions.name: opalpci_read_config
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is a valid opalpci device whose softc holds phb_id; bus, slot, func, reg and width describe the configuration access. Postcondition: the configuration address is built from bus, slot and func. For width 1, 2 or 4 it calls OPAL to read that many bytes, converting widths 2 and 4 from big-endian to host order (the width-1 byte is returned as is); for any other width no OPAL read is made, the value becomes 0xffffffff and width is treated as 4. If the OPAL call returned an error, or the value equals the all-ones mask for the width (0xff, 0xffff or 0xffffffff), and the error is not OPAL_HARDWARE, it queries the EEH freeze status of the default PE and clears the freeze (OPAL_EEH_ACTION_CLEAR_FREEZE_ALL) when the status is not OPAL_EEH_STOPPED_NOT_FROZEN. If the OPAL call returned an error the result is 0xffffffff (for every width); otherwise the result is the value read, so an all-ones read of width 1 or 2 is returned as 0xff or 0xffff, not 0xffffffff, while an unsupported width returns 0xffffffff (after the same EEH check).

functions.name: native_bs_rs_8
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: bsh plus ofs denotes a mapped, readable 8-byte device location. Postcondition: it computes the address with __ppc_ba(bsh, ofs), reads the 64-bit value from that volatile address, executes powerpc_iomb() (an I/O memory barrier) and returns the value. Unlike native_bs_rs_1, _2 and _4 it does not emit a KTR trace. It takes no locks and allocates nothing.

functions.name: REMAP(copyinstr)
functions.prose_contract: Generated-name function copyinstr, defined with the REMAP(copyinstr) wrapper. Precondition: udaddr is a user-space address of the current process, kaddr a kernel buffer of at least len bytes, len a byte count, done NULL or a writable size_t. Postcondition: it installs a fault handler (pcb_onfault) and copies the string byte by byte, mapping the user range in chunks with pmap_map_user_ptr. The result starts as ENAMETOOLONG: it returns 0 as soon as a NUL byte has been copied (that NUL is counted as transferred); it returns EFAULT if a mapping call fails or a fault occurs during the copy (the count is the bytes copied so far); and it returns ENAMETOOLONG when len bytes were copied without a NUL, which includes len == 0 (nothing is copied and no other error value is used for it). The fault handler is cleared before returning, and when done is non-NULL *done is set to the number of bytes counted as transferred in every case.

functions.name: powerpc_get_irq
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: node is a device-tree node handle (0 means none), pin an interrupt pin number. Postcondition: when node is 0 it returns pin immediately, without taking the lock. Otherwise it takes intr_table_lock and looks through piclist: if a PIC with that node already exists (real or earlier fake) it releases the lock and returns that PIC's base plus pin. If none matches it writes a new fake PIC entry at piclist[npics] (no device, the node, 124 irqs, 4 ipis, base = nirqs), adds 1 << 25 to nirqs, increments npics, then asserts npics < MAX_PICS (a KASSERT, checked after the entry was written and counted, so the write itself is not guarded), releases the lock and returns the new base plus pin. Sums are u_int arithmetic and may wrap.

functions.name: bounce_bus_dmamap_create
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dmat is an initialized bus_dma tag and mapp points to a writable bus_dmamap_t variable. Postcondition: if the tag's segment array is NULL it allocates it (M_NOWAIT) and returns ENOMEM if that fails. It then allocates a new map into *mapp and returns ENOMEM when that fails (*mapp is NULL in that case). If the tag could bounce (BF_COULD_BOUNCE) it creates the tag's bounce zone when missing (on failure it frees the new map and returns that error, leaving *mapp pointing at the freed map), sets DMAMAP_COULD_BOUNCE on the map, and, when BF_MIN_ALLOC_COMP is not yet set or the zone has maps and fewer than the maximum bounce pages, computes a page count and calls alloc_bounce_pages: a short allocation sets error to ENOMEM, which is kept when the minimum allocation had not yet completed (BF_MIN_ALLOC_COMP is set only if that first attempt succeeded) and cleared to 0 otherwise; bz->map_count is incremented in any case. If error is 0, dmat->map_count is incremented and 0 is returned with *mapp being the new map; on a nonzero error the new map is freed (*mapp left dangling) and the error returned.

functions.name: parse_metadata
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: early boot, with preload metadata reachable through preload_kmdp after preload_initkmdp(true); the ENVP, DDB symbol and FDT records may be absent. Postcondition: it calls preload_initkmdp(true) and sched_instance_select, sets boothowto from MODINFOMD_HOWTO, reads the kernel end address from MODINFOMD_KERNEND (the value it returns), and fetches the environment pointer: a non-NULL one initializes the static kernel environment from it, otherwise from the built-in static_kenv buffer. With DDB it fetches the symbol table bounds and registers them with db_fetch_ksymtab. With FDT it calls try_load_dtb and, when no environment pointer was supplied, parses the FDT bootargs into boothowto. It then calls parse_boot_hartid, which takes the boot hart from the MODINFOMD_BOOT_HARTID metadata when present and below UINT32_MAX, else from /chosen boot-hartid (FDT builds), panics if the boot hart is still invalid, and sets the per-CPU hart. It returns lastaddr.

functions.name: pmap_promote_l2
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the pmap lock is held (asserted), l2 points to the pmap's level-2 entry for va whose page-table page has been filled, ml3 is the page-table page or NULL, lockp is the caller's PV lock slot. Postcondition: returns false at once when superpages are not enabled for the pmap. The L2 entry must have none of the PTE_RWX bits set (asserted; its valid bit is not checked here, the function dereferences the page it points to). It returns false, counting pmap_l2_p_failures, when the physical address of the first L3 entry is not 2MB-aligned, when any other L3 entry (scanned from the last to the second) does not map the expected consecutive physical page, when its promotion attributes differ from the first entry's, or when pmap_insert_pt_page fails for the page-table page. During the scan the write bit is cleared with an atomic compare-and-set on entries that are writable and not yet dirty, so a failure can leave some L3 entries with PTE_W cleared. On success the accessed bit of the new entry is kept only if it was set in every L3 entry, the page-table page is recorded, PV entries are promoted with pmap_pv_promote_l2 when the mapping is managed, the new superpage entry is stored in *l2, pmap_l2_promotions is incremented and true is returned. On every false return *l2 is unchanged.

functions.name: do_trap_user
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: frame is the current thread's trap frame and the trap came from user mode with SPP and SIE clear in sstatus and SUM clear (all asserted with KASSERT). Postcondition: returns nothing. If scause has the interrupt bit set it calls intr_irq_handler(frame, INTR_ROOT_IRQ) and returns without calling intr_enable. Otherwise it calls intr_enable and dispatches on the exception code: access faults give SIGBUS (BUS_ADRERR) and misalignment SIGBUS (BUS_ADRALN) through call_trapsignal followed by userret; page faults go to page_fault_handler(frame, 1); a user ecall advances sepc by 4 and calls ecall_handler; an illegal instruction from a thread whose FP state has not been started clears the FP state, marks sstatus FS clean and sets PCB_FP_STARTED (lazy FPU enable) and otherwise delivers SIGILL (ILL_ILLTRP) and calls userret; a breakpoint delivers SIGTRAP (TRAP_BRKPT) and userret; any other exception dumps the registers and panics.

functions.name: jh7110_gpio_pin_setflags
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is a JH7110 GPIO device, pin and flags are arbitrary uint32_t values. Postcondition: returns EINVAL without taking the lock or touching any register when pin >= GPIO_PINS. Otherwise, holding the driver mutex: when GPIO_PIN_INPUT is set it sets PAD_INPUT_EN and PAD_HYST in the pad register IOMUX_SYSCFG_288 + PAD_OFFSET(pin); it always clears the ENABLE_MASK field at the pin's position in the GP0_DOEN_CFG register (whatever flags say) and, when GPIO_PIN_INPUT is set, then sets DIROUT_DISABLE in that field; when GPIO_PIN_OUTPUT is set it clears the same ENABLE_MASK-wide field in GP0_DOUT_CFG and sets its low bit to 1, and clears PAD_INPUT_EN, PAD_PULLUP, PAD_PULLDOWN and PAD_HYST in the pad register. It releases the mutex and returns 0.

functions.name: clnt_dg_call
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: cl is a datagram RPC client handle whose socket has the clnt_dg upcall installed (cu_socket->so_rcv.sb_upcallarg is the cu_socket state), ext is NULL or a callextra, args is the argument mbuf chain (NULL allowed for an async call), utimeout is the caller's timeout. Postcondition: returns an enum clnt_stat. If the client is closing or closed it returns RPC_CANTSEND immediately (the lock released, the request freed, nothing stored in the error structure). Otherwise it counts itself in cu_threads, selects the error structure (ext->rc_err, else cu->cu_error), connects the socket on first use (RPC_CANTSEND with errno on failure), and loops: encodes the call header, procedure and AUTH_MARSHALLed arguments (RPC_CANTENCODEARGS sets only re_status), waits for congestion window space (RPC_INTR for EINTR/ERESTART or RPC_CANTSEND for other msleep errors), queues a request record and sends the datagram with sosend (RPC_CANTSEND on send error), then waits for the reply for the retransmit interval: a request-record error gives RPC_CANTRECV with that errno, a timeout of 0 gives RPC_TIMEDOUT, an interrupted or failed wait gives RPC_INTR or RPC_CANTRECV, total time over the timeout gives RPC_TIMEDOUT with errno EWOULDBLOCK, and at each retransmit time the congestion window is halved, the feedback callback is called, and the request is sent again with an increased backoff (RPC_CANTRECV with ESHUTDOWN if the client closed meanwhile). On a reply it updates the round-trip estimates, decodes it with xdr_replymsg (RPC_CANTDECODERES on failure), and for an accepted SUCCESS reply validates the verifier with AUTH_VALIDATE, giving RPC_SUCCESS or RPC_AUTHERROR (a retransmitted RPCSEC_GSS call with an invalid verifier waits again instead); other replies go through _seterr_reply (which stores its details in cu->cu_error) and an authentication error triggers up to two credential refreshes and a repeat of the call with a new xid. On any exit through the out label it frees an unsent request mbuf and an unused reply chain, decrements cu_threads (waking the closer if closing), releases the lock, calls AUTH_VALIDATE(auth, xid, NULL, NULL) when the status is not RPC_SUCCESS, frees the request record and returns the status. The cs_lock is not held on return.

functions.name: clnt_dg_control
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: cl is a datagram client, request is a CLSET_/CLGET_ opcode and info points to storage of the type the request needs (it may be NULL only for CLSET_FD_CLOSE and CLSET_FD_NCLOSE). Postcondition: it takes the socket's cs_lock and releases it before every return. CLSET_FD_CLOSE and CLSET_FD_NCLOSE set cu_closeit to TRUE or FALSE and return TRUE even with a NULL info. For any other request a NULL info returns FALSE. CLSET_TIMEOUT and CLSET_RETRY_TIMEOUT return FALSE when time_not_ok rejects the timeval, otherwise store it in cu_total or cu_wait; CLGET_TIMEOUT and CLGET_RETRY_TIMEOUT copy those fields out; CLGET_SVC_ADDR copies the server address out and CLSET_SVC_ADDR copies a new one in; CLGET_XID reads, and CLSET_XID writes (as *info minus 1), the global rpc_xid, not a per-client field; CLGET_VERS, CLSET_VERS, CLGET_PROG and CLSET_PROG read or write the version and program words of the saved call header in network order; CLSET_ASYNC, CLSET_CONNECT, CLSET_WAITCHAN and CLSET_INTERRUPTIBLE set the matching cu fields (the last one sets cu_waitflag to PCATCH or 0) and CLGET_WAITCHAN and CLGET_INTERRUPTIBLE read them back; any other request returns FALSE. All the successful operations return TRUE.

functions.name: clnt_reconnect_connect
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: cl is a reconnect CLIENT whose cl_private is an initialized rc_data. Postcondition: returns an enum clnt_stat. Under rc_lock it waits while another thread is connecting (rc_connecting), returning RPC_INTR if the wait is interrupted (it changes no flag then), returns RPC_CANTSEND if the client is closed (even when rc_client is set), and returns RPC_SUCCESS if rc_client is already set. Otherwise it sets rc_connecting, switches the thread credentials to rc_ucred, and creates a socket (RPC_TLIERROR in rpc_createerr if that fails), optionally binds a reserved port, and creates a datagram client for connectionless transports, or for others sets SO_SNDTIMEO when a positive timeout is configured (RPC_CANTSEND with the errno if that fails) and creates a stream client; with TLS configured it runs rpctls_connect and on failure sets the status to the returned status or RPC_FAILED, closes and releases the new client. If no client was created it closes the socket, copies rpc_createerr's error into rc_err and returns rpc_createerr.cf_stat (which may be any status left by clnt_dg_create or clnt_vc_create). On success it configures the new client (connect mode, timeouts, wait channel, interruptibility, backchannel) and the status is RPC_SUCCESS. At the common exit it takes rc_lock again, stores newclient in rc_client unless the client was closed meanwhile (in which case the new client is closed and released and the returned status is still the one computed, possibly RPC_SUCCESS), clears rc_connecting, wakes waiters and returns the status.

functions.name: clnt_vc_close
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: cl is a stream RPC client with a valid ct_data and the caller does not hold ct->ct_lock. Postcondition: returns nothing. If the client is already closed it returns at once without further effect; if it is closing it waits until closing ends and returns (neither early path wakes anyone). Otherwise, when ct_socket is non-NULL it sets ct_closing, clears the socket's receive upcall (and calls clnt_vc_upcallsdone) if one is installed, marks every pending request with xid 0 and error ESHUTDOWN and wakes it, and waits until ct_threads reaches zero; when ct_socket is NULL none of that is done. In the non-early path it then sets ct_closing to FALSE and ct_closed to TRUE, wakes sleepers on ct_tlsstate and on ct, and releases ct_lock. The socket itself is not closed here (that is done by clnt_vc_destroy).

functions.name: rpc_gss_init
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: auth is an RPCSEC_GSS handle whose private data gd is protected by gd_lock, options_ret points to writable result storage, and the vnet is set (asserted). Postcondition: under gd_lock it waits until gd_state is RPCSEC_GSS_START or RPCSEC_GSS_ESTABLISHED; if it is ESTABLISHED it releases the lock and returns TRUE without writing options_ret. Otherwise it sets the state to RPCSEC_GSS_CONTEXT and starts a new context negotiation: gc_proc becomes RPCSEC_GSS_INIT and gc_seq 0, a client credential is acquired from gd_clntprincipal for Kerberos when configured (a failure records the GSS status in options_ret and goes to the failure exit), the service principal name is imported (same failure handling), and the function loops calling gss_init_sec_context (the lucid variant for MIT Kerberos) with the thread credentials temporarily set to gd_ucred. A failing GSS status other than COMPLETE or CONTINUE_NEEDED, a failing RPC (CLNT_CALL_EXT of NULLPROC with the token), a server reply whose major status is neither COMPLETE nor CONTINUE_NEEDED, or a failed verification of the server's window MIC ends the loop with the GSS status stored in options_ret (a verify failure with an expired context also destroys the context and sets an RPC_GSS_ER_SYSTEMERROR/EPERM error). The server's handle and token replace the previous ones between rounds and gc_proc becomes CONTINUE_INIT. On GSS_S_COMPLETE with a verified window, options_ret receives the status, version and context, gc_proc becomes RPCSEC_GSS_DATA, gd_seq 1 and gd_win the server's window. At the out label, if gc_proc is not RPCSEC_GSS_DATA, rpc_createerr.cf_stat is set to RPC_AUTHERROR, a GSS error is recorded, any context is deleted, gd_state returns to RPCSEC_GSS_START, waiters are woken and FALSE is returned; otherwise gd_state becomes RPCSEC_GSS_ESTABLISHED, waiters are woken and TRUE is returned.

functions.name: svc_rpc_gss_accept_sec_context
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: client is a client record (cl_sname may be NULL), rqst a request whose argument decodes as a gss_buffer_desc, gr and gc writable. Postcondition: the function first determines the Kerberos implementation (once) and, for MIT, presets the credential uid/gid to 65534. If svc_getargs of the token fails it sets cl_state to CLIENT_STALE and returns FALSE before taking any lock. Otherwise it takes svc_rpc_gss_lock exclusively around the accept call only: with no cl_sname it finds the server name matching rqst->rq_prog and rq_vers, runs gss_accept_sec_context (retrying after rpc_gss_acquire_svc_cred when the credentials expired and could be reacquired) and records the matching name in cl_sname, or, when no server name matches, frees the token, releases the lock and returns FALSE without changing cl_state; with an existing cl_sname it accepts with that name's credentials. It releases the lock and frees the token. If the GSS result in gr is neither GSS_S_COMPLETE nor CONTINUE_NEEDED it logs, sets cl_state to CLIENT_STALE and returns TRUE (the caller reads gr). Otherwise it fills gr's handle and window and the client's mechanism and qop; for GSS_S_COMPLETE it sets the credential expiration (capped by svc_rpc_gss_lifetime_max, 24 hours when indefinite), then for non-MIT exports the client name with gss_export_name and returns FALSE if that fails (the cl_cname name is left unreleased on that path), builds the raw credentials and ucred, sets the flavor and releases cl_cname. The function returns TRUE after that, or TRUE for CONTINUE_NEEDED.

functions.name: xprt_active
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: xprt->xp_group and xprt->xp_pool are valid. Postcondition: returns nothing. It takes grp->sg_lock and releases it before returning. If xp_registered is FALSE it returns without changing the transport. Otherwise, only when xp_active was FALSE, it sets xp_active to TRUE and, when xp_thread is NULL, appends xprt to grp->sg_active if request space is not available for the pool, or if xprt_assignthread finds no idle thread; xprt_assignthread, when an idle thread exists, removes it from the idle list, takes a reference on xprt, sets xp_thread and the thread's transport and signals the thread, and when none exists may set grp->sg_state to SVCPOOL_THREADWANTED (if the group is ACTIVE, the last thread creation was before the current time and the thread count is below the maximum). A transport that already has xp_active TRUE, or a non-NULL xp_thread, is otherwise left unchanged.

functions.name: smist_set
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev has a smist softc whose two settings sets[0] and sets[1] are filled; set->freq should match one of them. Postcondition: returns EINVAL when set->freq matches neither sets[0].freq nor sets[1].freq (CPUFREQ_CMP). Otherwise it calls getset_state with GET_STATE and ignores the return value; getset_state writes the reported state (low bit of the value returned by the SMI) into its state argument before it checks for errors, so state is set even when it returns ENXIO, but its input value, which is passed to the SMI, is an uninitialized int in this function. If that state equals the requested state it returns 0. Otherwise it calls getset_state with SET_STATE up to three times, delaying 200 microseconds after each failure; because getset_state stores the reported state into its argument, req_state itself is overwritten by each SET_STATE call before the next retry. It returns 0 as soon as getset_state returns 0, or the last nonzero value (ENXIO, or EINVAL for a bad function) after three failures.

functions.name: smist_type
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is the device and type is a pointer that may be NULL. Postcondition: returns EINVAL without writing when type is NULL; otherwise it stores CPUFREQ_TYPE_ABSOLUTE through type and returns 0. It takes no locks.

functions.name: msix_release
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: irq is an interrupt source number; the caller does not hold msi_lock (the function takes it). Postcondition: it takes msi_lock, looks up the source for irq and returns ENOENT (lock released) if there is none, or EINVAL (lock released) if the source is not an MSI-X message.
