Otherwise (the message must be owned, asserted with KASSERT) it, in an IOMMU build, drops msi_lock around iommu_unmap_msi_intr(msi_dev, msi_remap_cookie) and takes it again, then clears msi_first, msi_dev, calls apic_free_vector for the message's cpu, vector and irq, clears msi_vector, msi_msix, msi_count and msi_maxcount, releases msi_lock and returns 0.

functions.name: xenbusb_write_ivar
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: child is a xenbus device child with valid ivars. Postcondition: for XENBUS_IVAR_STATE it takes ivars->xd_lock exclusively and releases it before returning. If xd_state already equals the requested state it returns 0 with no xenstore access. Otherwise it runs a xenstore transaction that reads the node's "state" entry and rewrites it (retrying on EAGAIN, restarting the transaction while xs_transaction_end reports failure). Any error aborts the transaction (xs_transaction_end with abort when error is nonzero, after logging a fatal device error for a write failure unless the new state is Closing); in that case xd_state is not changed. On a committed transaction it sets xd_state, and if XDF_CONNECTING is set and the new state is Closed or Connected it clears that flag and releases the config hook, then wakes sleepers on xd_state. The result for the STATE case is the error, except that ENOENT is converted to 0 (so that return can happen with xd_state not updated). XENBUS_IVAR_NODE, TYPE, OTHEREND_ID and OTHEREND_PATH return EINVAL (read-only); any other index returns ENOENT.

functions.name: cponfork_notes_check
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: kq is an open kqueue descriptor of a KQUEUE_CPONFORK queue and clofd the descriptor of another kqueue that was closed on fork; the parameters are not validated. Postcondition: it takes the expected-event mask from cponfork_notes_mask(true), which is RECV_TIMER | RECV_VNODE (0x03) because the parent-only RECV_CLOREAD bit is excluded in the child, registers a one-shot 4 second EVFILT_TIMER with ident TIMER_TIMEOUT and returns RECV_ERROR (0x80) if that kevent call fails. It then loops while the received bits do not cover the mask, waiting for one event at a time with kevent: a failing wait returns RECV_ERROR; a wait that returns 0 ends the loop; an EVFILT_TIMER event with ident TIMER_TIMEOUT returns the bits received so far ORed with RECV_ERROR; any other timer event sets RECV_TIMER; an EVFILT_VNODE event sets RECV_VNODE (its ident is not checked); an EVFILT_READ event whose ident is not clofd returns received ORed with RECV_ERROR, otherwise it sets RECV_CLOREAD; other filters are ignored. When the loop ends it returns the received bits, which include RECV_TIMER and RECV_VNODE and, if that event arrived before the loop ended, also RECV_CLOREAD (0x03 or 0x07), or fewer bits if the wait returned 0.

functions.name: test_kevent_vnode_disable_and_enable

Postcondition: it announces the test, checks there are no pending kevents, adds an EVFILT_VNODE watch for NOTE_ATTRIB on vnode_fd with EV_ADD | EV_ONESHOT and immediately disables it with EV_DISABLE, touches ./kqueue-test.tmp through system() and checks that no kevent is delivered, re-enables the watch with EV_ENABLE, touches the file again and waits (without a timeout) for one kevent, which must have ident vnode_fd, filter EVFILT_VNODE and fflags NOTE_ATTRIB. It returns the descriptor when the loop ends. Any failing ATF_REQUIRE ends the test case, in which case the function does not return.

functions.name: printblk
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: fs is a valid struct fs; the callers pass blocks in increasing logical block number order for ordinary blocks (lastlbn > 0), -level (<= 0) for indirect blocks and 0 for the final flush. The function keeps a run of blocks in static state (seq, totfrags, firstblk, lastblk, lastindirblk) across calls. Postcondition: returns nothing. With lastlbn > 0: if no run is active (seq == 0) it starts one from this block and returns without printing; if lbn == 0 it resets the static state (seq, totfrags, lastblk, firstblk, lastindirblk) to start a new run from this block and returns without printing the old run; if lbn < lastlbn and the block continues the run (both holes, both BLK_NOCOPY, both BLK_SNAP, or blkno equals firstblk + seq * fs_frag) it extends the run and returns. Otherwise (or when lastlbn <= 0) it flushes: if a run is active it prints one line for it, "lbn a[-b] hole|nocopy|snapblk" for sentinel runs or "lbn a[-b] blkno x[-y]" plus the distance from lastblk for real blocks (updating lastblk), where the run's last block number is derived from lbn; then, when lastlbn > 0 or blkno == 0, it starts a new run from the current block and returns. Otherwise it falls to the indirect-block print, which updates lastindirblk, prints "<level>-level indirect, blkno a-b" with the distance, updates lastindirblk (and lastblk when fs_metaspace is 0), and sets seq to 0.

functions.name: dowordfile
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: fname is a non-NULL NUL-terminated file name. Postcondition: it opens the file for reading and returns -1 if that fails (nrandwords and randwords unchanged). It sets nrandwords to the number of fgets calls with a 64-byte buffer needed to read the whole file (a line longer than 63 bytes is counted once per chunk, so this is not strictly the number of lines). It returns -1 after closing the file if ferror is set or rewinding with fseek fails (nrandwords then holds that count and randwords is unchanged), or if calloc of nrandwords pointers returns NULL. Otherwise it reads the file again with the same chunking, strips the first CR or LF and everything after it from each chunk (strcspn at the first occurrence, so not only a trailing newline) and stores a strdup copy in randwords[i]; a failed strdup calls err(1, ...) and exits the process. The second pass stops after the counted number of entries. It then sets nrandwords to that counted number (also if fewer were read, leaving the remaining entries NULL), closes the file and returns 0.

functions.name: recv_loop_with_match
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sock is a datagram socket, group and source point to sockaddrs, source is asserted to be AF_INET, and the global timeout is a number of seconds. Postcondition: returns 0 at once when timeout is 0. It resolves group and source to numeric host strings with getnameinfo and returns that call's nonzero error code (after printing it) if either fails. Otherwise it prints a waiting message, installs signal_handler for SIGINT and SIGALRM, sets an alarm of timeout seconds, and loops under setjmp calling recvfrom (its return value is not checked, and the address length argument is the uninitialized from.sa.sa_len); a datagram whose IPv4 source address equals the blocked source's address breaks out of the loop, any other datagram is counted. After the loop it reports the count when doverbose is set and sets the result from the setjmp value: SIGALRM gives 0, SIGINT prints "interrupted" and gives 20, a break out of the loop (value 0) prints a FAIL message and gives EX_IOERR, any other value prints a warning and gives EX_OSERR. It restores SIGINT and SIGALRM to SIG_DFL and returns the result.

functions.name: test_fcntl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: none; the function opens its own descriptors (it relies on /etc/passwd, a PF_LOCAL stream socket and SHM_ANON shared memory being available). Postcondition: it returns PASSED or FAILED (the success variable, which the REQUIRE, CHECK_* and FAIL macros, not read here, update). It opens the file, the socket and the shared-memory object, makes a capability for each with rights CAP_READ | CAP_FCNTL (cap_new), requires every descriptor to be valid, enters capability mode, and then for each of the six descriptors (the three raw ones and the three capabilities) requires fcntl(F_GETFL) to succeed, makes a new capability from it with only CAP_READ, and, provided a plain fcntl(F_GETFL) on the descriptor itself did not fail, checks that fcntl(F_GETFL) on the new CAP_READ-only capability fails with ENOTCAPABLE. None of the descriptors are closed before returning.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: none; main takes no arguments. Postcondition: if modfind("accf_data") returns -1 it prints "1..0 # SKIP ..." and calls _exit(0) without returning. Otherwise it prints "1..12" and runs the accept-filter steps on a loopback TCP socket bound to port 8080: socket, getsockopt(SO_ACCEPTFILTER) before and after bind (must fail with EINVAL), a setsockopt before listen (must fail), a getsockopt after that (EINVAL), listen, getsockopt before installing (EINVAL), setsockopt of the filter after listen (must succeed), getsockopt returning the filter name, a non-blocking accept sequence with a connected client (an accept before data must not succeed and after writing one byte must succeed), and a reset connection accepted with ECONNABORTED. Every failed check calls errx(-1, "not ok N ..."), which exits the process with status 255 and does not return. The printed plan says 12 but 13 ok lines are printed.

functions.name: main

The test helper functions were not read.

functions.name: bind_test
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: directory_path is a NUL-terminated directory name. Postcondition: returns 0 only after all steps succeed, otherwise -1 after printing a warning and closing the sockets it holds. It creates a PF_UNIX stream socket, composes directory_path "/" SOCK_NAME_ONE (-1 if it does not fit in PATH_MAX or sun_path), binds the socket to it, and records the path with push_path (which calls err(-1, ...) and exits the process when unwind_len is already UNWIND_MAX). The socket file is left on disk (and in the unwind list) from the first successful bind on, so on the success path it exists again after the final bind and on later failures it may or may not exist.

functions.name: t_cmsg_len_client
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: fd is an open socket descriptor; the uc_cfg and sync infrastructure is initialized. Postcondition: it first calls uc_sync_recv and returns -2 at once if that fails (nothing is allocated yet). Otherwise it sets the result to -2, allocates CMSG_SPACE(sizeof(struct cmsgcred)) bytes and returns -2 (through the cleanup label) if malloc fails, initializes a message with one SCM_CREDS control message, and returns -2 if uc_socket_connect fails. The control buffer is freed on all paths after its allocation attempt, and the function returns the result (0 when all sends with a too-short cmsg_len failed, -1 when one succeeded).

functions.name: t_sockcred_1
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the global uc_cfg harness state is initialized and the process may fork. Postcondition: it forks with uc_client_fork. In the child (case 0) it runs up to two client passes: each creates a socket (a failure gives -2), runs t_sockcred_client(1, fd), closes the socket (a failed close gives -2), and stops at the first nonzero result; the child then calls uc_client_exit with that result. In the parent (case 1) it creates a socket (a failure sets -2 and the child is not waited for), runs t_sockcred_server(1, fd) and, if that returned 0, t_sockcred_server(3, fd), then reaps the child with uc_client_wait; the result becomes the client's result when the server result is 0, or when it is -2 and the client result is nonzero (a server result of -1 is kept as -1), and a failed close of the socket sets -2. A fork failure returns -2. The function returns 0, -1 or -2 in the parent and, in the child, the call to uc_client_exit does not return (assumed from its name; not read).

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc and argv are the command line. functions.name: open_1
functions.prose_contract: Sets errno to 0 and calls iconv_open("nonexisting", "foobar"). If the call returned (iconv_t)-1 and errno equals EINVAL it returns 0. In every other outcome it calls iconv_close on the returned descriptor (including a (iconv_t)-1 result with a different errno) and returns 1.

functions.name: open_2
functions.prose_contract: Sets errno to 0 and calls iconv_open("ASCII", "UTF8") in a loop of at most 1025 iterations, storing each descriptor in a local array. On the first call that returns (iconv_t)-1 it sets the result to 0 if errno is ENFILE or EMFILE (the result stays 1 for any other errno), stores NULL in that slot and stops. It then calls iconv_close on slots i down to 1, where i is the failed index or 1024 if no call failed; slot 0 is never closed, and a NULL slot is passed to iconv_close when a failure occurred at index 1 or later. Returns 1 if all 1025 opens succeeded, 0 only in the ENFILE/EMFILE case.

functions.name: close_1
functions.prose_contract: Calls iconv_close on the invalid descriptor (iconv_t)-1. If it returns -1 the condition assigns EBADF to errno (the test uses '=' not '==', so the assignment is evaluated only when the call returned -1) and the function returns 0; if iconv_close returns anything other than -1 the function returns 1 and errno is not assigned.

functions.name: conv_ebadf
functions.prose_contract: Sets errno to 0 and calls iconv on the descriptor (iconv_t)-1 with NULL input and output pointers and zero byte counts. Returns 0 when iconv returned (size_t)-1 with errno equal to EBADF, and 1 otherwise.

functions.name: conv_2big
functions.prose_contract: Opens an "ASCII" to "ASCII" conversion descriptor; if iconv_open fails it returns 1. Otherwise it sets errno to 0 and calls iconv with a 16-byte input and an 8-byte output buffer. It returns 0 only when the input pointer advanced by 8 bytes, inbytesleft is 8, outbytesleft is 0, the output pointer advanced by 8 bytes, errno is E2BIG and iconv returned (size_t)-1; otherwise it returns 1. The descriptor is not closed on any path, and the input buffer is uninitialised.

functions.name: conv_einval
functions.prose_contract: Opens a "UTF-32" from "BIG5" conversion descriptor; if iconv_open fails it returns 1. Otherwise it sets errno to 0 and calls iconv on a 2-byte input (the uint16_t value 0xEA42) with a 16-byte output buffer. It returns 0 only when the input pointer advanced by 1 byte, inbytesleft is 1, outbytesleft is 8, the output pointer advanced by 8 bytes, errno is EINVAL and iconv returned (size_t)-1; otherwise it returns 1. The descriptor is never closed.

functions.name: conv_eilseq
functions.prose_contract: Opens a "Latin2" from "UTF-16LE" conversion descriptor; if iconv_open fails it returns 1. Otherwise it sets errno to 0 and calls iconv with the pointer to a 2-byte buffer holding the uint16_t 0x8AC0 but with inbytesleft set to 4, so iconv is told there are two more bytes than the buffer holds, and with a 16-byte output buffer. It returns 0 only when no input was consumed (pointer offset 0, inbytesleft 4), nothing was produced (outbytesleft 16, pointer offset 0), errno is EILSEQ and iconv returned (size_t)-1; otherwise it returns 1. The descriptor is not closed.

functions.name: random_int
functions.prose_contract: Returns arc4random() % (ma - mi + 1) + mi. arc4random() returns an unsigned 32-bit value and the divisor (int ma - mi + 1) is converted to unsigned for the modulo, so the remainder is non-negative. When mi <= ma and ma - mi + 1 does not overflow int, the remainder is in [0, ma - mi] and the result lies in [mi, ma]. If ma == mi - 1 the divisor is 0 (division by zero); if ma < mi - 1 the divisor wraps to a large unsigned value and the result is not confined to a meaningful range. No locks or memory are touched beyond the arc4random call.
functions.contract: /*@ requires mi <= ma && ma - mi < 2147483647; ensures result >= mi && result <= ma; */

functions.name: test
functions.prose_contract: Creates a Unix stream socket pair in the static sv; if socketpair fails it calls err(1) and the process exits. It then forks. In the child (fork returned 0) it runs writer(), which allocates bufsize bytes (err(1) in the child if malloc fails), fills them with ascending ints and writes them to sv[1] in a loop until a write fails; a write failing with EPIPE makes writer return and the child calls _exit(EXIT_SUCCESS), any other write failure calls err(1) in the child only. In the parent (pid > 0) it runs reader(), which allocates bufsize bytes (err(1) in the parent on malloc failure), reads from sv[0] until read returns 0 or done_testing becomes nonzero (err(1) in the parent if read returns a negative value), then closes sv[0]; the parent then sends SIGINT to the child and returns 0, without waiting for the child or closing sv[1]. If fork fails it calls err(1). bufsize is set by setup() (static, zero before setup runs).

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Entry point of indent_wrapper (the name process_diff does not exist in the file; the slice is the tail of main). It installs a SIGPIPE handler, parses options with getopt (-v verbosity, -t diff tool, -g/-d/-D/-s/-c choose the command whose output is the diff; any other option calls usage()), and calls usage() if no command was selected. It runs that command into a block list, splits the diff into a pre-image list diff_a_head and a post-image list diff_b_head, and then makes passes over diff_a_head: (1) any non-printable ASCII byte other than tab, CR, LF and space makes errx(EX_SOFTWARE) end the process, bytes with the high bit get the BLOCK_MASK flag; (2) comments and (3) preprocessor lines and strings are masked; (4) text inside braces or parentheses is masked, and unbalanced nesting or an unterminated string ends the process via errx(EX_SOFTWARE); (6) for each run of lines carrying the added flag that is not masked, it copies the run into indent_in_head, pipes it through the fixed indent and sed command line via cmd_block_process into indent_out_head, compares the two with diff_tool (when -t was given) or diff_block, sets retval to 1 if the comparison reports a difference, and frees both temporary lists. It returns retval (0 initially, 1 if any region differed). The diff lists, the command buffer and the diff_head list are not freed. Details of the head (lines 368-436) and the diff-splitting loop (436-526) were read only in outline.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Entry point of kttcp (slice cut the head; whole function is kttcp.c:102-306). Options are parsed with getopt: -4/-6 (a second family option calls usage()), -b (buffer size, errx(1) if above INT_MAX), -n, -p, -q, -r/-t (a second direction option calls usage()), -v; -w is in the getopt string but has no case so it falls into usage(), as does any unknown option. usage() is called if neither -r nor -t was given, and in send mode if no host argument follows. It opens the kttcp device, resolves the address with getaddrinfo, creates a stream socket from the first usable address, then either (send) connects and sets SO_SNDBUF or (receive) sets SO_REUSEADDR, binds, listens, accepts one connection and sets SO_RCVBUF on it; failures of open, getaddrinfo, socket, connect, setsockopt, bind, listen, accept and the kttcp ioctl exit with err/errx status 2. It takes rusage before and after the ioctl (their return values are not checked), prints byte and bit rates, a CPU-time line when verbose > 1 and a user/sys/real line, then closes the kttcp socket, the listening socket in receive mode and the device (close results unchecked), calls freeaddrinfo and returns 0. The code divides by the kernel-reported elapsed microseconds and, with -v, by the CPU time delta, without checking for zero.

functions.name: handle_rtmsg
functions.prose_contract: Handles one routing message; msglen is unused. If rtm_version differs from RTM_VERSION it logs an error and returns. For RTM_IFANNOUNCE it logs an arrival (debug) or a departure and, on departure, calls wds_destroy with the announced interface name; other announce kinds do nothing. For RTM_IEEE80211 it switches on the event kind: DISASSOC is ignored unless discover_on_join is set and then falls into LEAVE; LEAVE, if checkifnet(ifan_name, 1) is true, logs 'station leave' and calls wds_leave with the event address, otherwise does nothing; JOIN, REJOIN, ASSOC and REASSOC are ignored unless discover_on_join is set and then fall into WDS; WDS logs '[addr] wds discovery' unconditionally, then, only if checkifnet succeeds, calls wds_discovery with the interface name and address. Other event kinds and other message types are ignored. It returns nothing; the wds list is changed only through wds_destroy, wds_leave and wds_discovery.

functions.name: update_ip6
functions.prose_contract: Copies the IPv6 and UDP headers out of pkt, steps the source then possibly destination address/port fields inside a single-pass do-while(0), adjusts the UDP checksum and copies both headers back into pkt. Source stage: one 16-bit group of the source address (index g->src_ip.ipv6.sgroup) and the UDP source port. With OPT_RANDOM_SRC both are replaced with nrand48 values and the stage ends (the destination is not touched). Otherwise, if the source port is below src_ip.port1 it is incremented and the stage ends with the address unchanged; if not, the port is reset to port0 and, if the address group is below the configured end group value, the group is incremented and the stage ends; otherwise the group is reset to the start value and the destination stage runs. In that case the source delta (address and/or port, when they changed) is first accumulated into udp_sum. Destination stage (egroup and UDP destination port): with OPT_RANDOM_DST both get nrand48 values; else the port is incremented if below dst_ip.port1, else reset to port0 and the group incremented if below its end value, else reset to its start value. After the loop the delta of the last stage reached (destination if the destination stage ran, source otherwise) is added to udp_sum, so when the destination stage runs the checksum delta covers both source and destination changes; if udp_sum is nonzero the UDP checksum is adjusted by it. No return value.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Entry point of syscall_timing (slice cut the head; function is syscall_timing.c:1017-1167). It parses -i iterations (>=1), -l loops (1..100000), -p path, -s alarm seconds (1..3600); a bad number, an unknown option, no test name, or a test name not found in tests[] calls usage(). alarm_timeout starts at 1, so the 'iterations < 1 && alarm_timeout < 1' check at 1068 cannot trigger; if -i is not given iterations becomes UINT64_MAX (bounded by the alarm). In the validation loop, for each named test with FLAG_PATH when -p was not given it does strdup, mkdtemp and asprintf (err(1) on failure), overwriting tmp_dir/tmp_path each time, so with several such tests only the last temporary directory is remembered. It asserts clock_getres succeeds, prints the clock resolution and header, then for each named test: if tmp_path is set it opens/creates it, ftruncate to 1000000 and closes it (err(1) on failure) and uses it as the path for that and every later test; it runs the test once as warmup, then loops times, printing the elapsed time, call count and per-call nanoseconds (divides by the returned call count without checking for zero). At the end, if tmp_path is set it unlinks that file (warning on failure other than ENOENT) and rmdir's the last tmp_dir (warning on failure), and returns 0; earlier temporary directories from the validation loop are not removed.

functions.name: vhbarptluns_act
functions.prose_contract: Real name vhbarptluns_act (static, vhba_rptluns.c:117-364; slice cut the head). Zeroes csio->sense_data, then handles one SCSI command and queues the CCB on vhbas->vhba->done by TAILQ_INSERT_TAIL on every return path (the early returns at 134-135, 146-147, 167-168 and the final insert at 363); each path inserts it once. target_id >= MAX_TGT: status CAM_SEL_TIMEOUT, queued, return. LUN is attached if target_lun < MAX_LUN and its bit is set in vhbas->rpbitmap; if it is not attached and the opcode is not INQUIRY, REPORT_LUNS or REQUEST_SENSE, it calls vhba_fill_sense(ILLEGAL_REQUEST, asc 0x25), queues and returns. Switch on cdb[0]: MODE_SENSE/MODE_SENSE_10 with a page code other than format-device, geometry, cache, control or all-pages fills ILLEGAL_REQUEST (asc 0x24) and returns; otherwise it builds mode data in a local 128-byte buffer (block descriptor unless the DBD bit is set, then the requested pages), computes data_len = min(allocation length from the CDB, dxfer_len, built length), copies that many bytes to csio->data_ptr and sets resid = dxfer_len - data_len (the length byte is stored at the end of the built data rather than at the start of the buffer). READ_6/10/12/16 and WRITE_6/10/12/16: if vhba_rwparm returns nonzero it fills ILLEGAL_REQUEST (asc 0x24) and leaves the switch; otherwise a nonzero data_len is copied between data_ptr and vhbas->disk at the computed offset (read when (cdb[0] & 0xf) == 8, else write) with resid = dxfer_len - data_len, and a zero data_len sets resid = dxfer_len. READ_CAPACITY: if any of CDB bytes 2-5 (the LBA field) is nonzero it fills UNIT_ATTENTION sense (asc 0x24) and leaves the switch; otherwise it writes the last block number (0xffffffff when the PMI bit is set or the last block does not fit in 32 bits) and the block size into the first 8 bytes of data_ptr. Any other opcode is handed to vhba_default_cmd. Paths leaving the switch then clear the CAM status bits and set CAM_SCSI_STATUS_ERROR (plus CAM_AUTOSNS_VALID if scsi_status is CHECK CONDITION) when scsi_status is not OK, or set scsi_status OK and CAM_REQ_CMP when it is. vhba_default_cmd and vhba_fill_sense were read only for what they set (fill_sense sets CHECK CONDITION, vhba.c:154-164); vhba_default_cmd was not read.

functions.name: vhba_rwparm
functions.prose_contract: Defined in tools/tools/vhba/vhba.c, not in this file. Decodes the starting block (lba) and block count (cnt) from a READ/WRITE CDB according to cdb[0] (16-byte, 12-byte, 10-byte and 6-byte forms; in the 6-byte form a count of 0 means 256 and only the low 5 bits of byte 1 are used). For any other opcode it returns -1 with *offset and *tl untouched. If lba + cnt is greater than nblks it returns -1 with *offset and *tl untouched (the sum is computed in 64 bits and is not checked for wraparound). Otherwise it stores *tl = cnt << blk_shift (32-bit shift) and *offset = lba << blk_shift and returns 0.

functions.name: nextjob
functions.prose_contract: Opens ATJOB_DIR ".SEQ" with fopen mode "r+". If that succeeds it scans one value with fscanf("%5lx"): on success it rewinds, sets jobno = (1 + jobno) % 0xfffff (C remainder, so a negative scanned value, which %lx accepts as a signed field of at most 5 characters such as -ffff, gives a negative result), writes it back with fprintf "%05lx\n" (without truncating and without checking the write), closes the file and returns jobno; if the scan does not yield 1 it closes the file and returns EOF (-1) with no write. If the "r+" open fails it tries fopen mode "w" (which truncates an existing file it can open for writing); on success it writes "00001\n", closes the file and returns 1; if that also fails it returns EOF. For a scanned value in 0..0xfffff the returned value is in 0..0xffffe; with a negative scanned value as low as -0xffff it is in -0xfffe..-1 or 0. Return values of fprintf and fclose are not checked, and a legitimate return of -1 cannot be told apart from EOF.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Entry point of at/atq/atrm/batch (slice cut the head; usr.bin/at/at.c:731-914). It records the real/effective ids with RELINQUISH_PRIVS, takes the basename of argv[0] as the program name and picks the mode from it: atq -> ATQ (options "q:v"), atrm -> ATRM (options ""), batch -> BATCH ("f:q:mv"), anything else AT. getopt then handles: -v (verify), -m (mail), -f (input file), -q (queue; usage() if the argument is longer than one character or not a letter), -r and -d (-d warns, then both: usage() unless the mode is AT, then mode ATRM), -t (usage() unless mode is AT, then timer = ttime(arg)), -l (usage() unless mode AT, then ATQ with options "q:"), -b (usage() unless mode AT, then BATCH), -c (sets mode CAT with no mode check, so it is accepted whatever the current mode is), and any other option calls usage(). If check_permission() fails it calls errx(EXIT_FAILURE). It then runs the selected mode: ATQ reduces privileges to DAEMON_UID/GID, builds a job list from the remaining arguments when no queue was given with -q and calls list_jobs; ATRM reduces privileges to DAEMON_UID/GID and calls process_jobs(..., ATRM); CAT calls process_jobs(..., CAT) without a REDUCE_PRIV call in main; AT takes the time from -t or parsetime(argc, argv), optionally prints it with -v and calls writefile; BATCH upper-cases the queue given with -q or uses DEFAULT_BATCH_QUEUE, uses parsetime if arguments remain or the current time otherwise, optionally prints it, and calls writefile; any other mode value calls panic(). After the handler it calls exit(EXIT_SUCCESS). The callees (list_jobs, process_jobs, writefile, parsetime) can themselves exit. Main does not return.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Entry point of banner (usr.bin/banner/banner.c:1017-1161, slice cut the head). Options: -d (debug), -t (trace), -w width where atoi(optarg) must be in 1..DWIDTH (else errx(1)); any other option calls usage(), which exits 1. It marks which of the DWIDTH columns are printed for the chosen width. The message is the remaining arguments joined by single spaces in a malloc'd buffer (err(1) if malloc fails), or, if there are no arguments, a MAXMSG buffer read with fgets after printing "Message: " to stderr (empty message on EOF; a trailing newline is removed). With -d it dumps the asc_ptr and data_table arrays. Each message character must be below NCHARS and have a nonzero asc_ptr entry; for each bad one it prints a warning, and if any were bad it calls exit(1). Then for each character it runs a small interpreter over data_table starting at asc_ptr[ch]: bytes >= 128 emit (x & 63) output rows (and end the character when x > 192), other bytes pair as (start, length) of '#' cells on the current row; if the program counter is below 0 or above NBYTES it prints "bad pc" and exit(1). Writes into line[] (x+y) and the print[] index linen are not range-checked against DWIDTH in the code. At the end it frees the message buffer (line 1159) and calls exit(0); it does not return.

functions.name: sppd_write
functions.prose_contract: Writes buffer to fd in a loop while size > 0. A write returning -1 with errno other than EINTR makes the function return -1 immediately (bytes already written are not reported); -1 with EINTR and a 0 return are both retried, so a write that keeps returning 0 makes the loop spin without progress. A positive write result advances the buffer pointer, reduces size and adds to the running count. When size reaches 0 it returns the number of bytes written, which equals the original size when the original size was positive, and 0 when the original size was 0 or negative (no write is made). The caller must supply at least size readable bytes at buffer (the buffer is only read). It acquires no locks and allocates no memory.

functions.name: zwrite
functions.prose_contract: Write callback of the compress stream (usr.bin/compress/zopen.c:231-317; slice cut the head). If num == 0 it returns 0 at once (line 241) without touching the state. Otherwise, if the state is not yet S_MIDDLE (first call) it sets the state to S_MIDDLE before doing anything else, writes the 3-byte magic header (magic bytes then maxbits|block_compress) with fwrite and returns -1 if either fwrite is short, then initialises the output/hash state, takes the first input byte *bp as the current prefix code and clears the hash table. A later call goes straight to the 'middle' label. The loop consumes the remaining input bytes, looking each up in the hash table (primary then secondary probing); a miss calls output() for the current prefix (return -1 on failure), adds a table entry while free_ent < maxmaxcode, else, once in_count reaches the checkpoint and block compression is on, calls cl_block() (return -1 on failure). It returns num when all bytes were consumed. After a -1 return the already-consumed input is not rolled back; because the state was set to S_MIDDLE before the header was written, a failed header write leaves a later call skipping header and initialisation, so the state is not safe to retry. It allocates no memory.

functions.name: PF_funcs
functions.prose_contract: Scans the global input stream inf for Fortran/Pascal-style declarations (usr.bin/ctags/fortran.c:44-126). It loops, storing ftell(inf) in lineftell, reading a line into lbuf with fgets and returning pfcnt (true if at least one declaration reached pfnote, else false) as soon as fgets returns NULL (end of file or error); there is no other return. Per line: lineno is incremented, lbp points at lbuf, an initial '%' and following whitespace are skipped, and an empty remainder skips the line. An optional type keyword is matched case-insensitively by cicmp (complex, character, integer, logical, real, each followed by takeprec which consumes an optional '*' and digits; or 'double', then whitespace, which must be followed by 'precision' or the line is skipped, and for double precision takeprec is not called). The type keyword is optional: a line starting with function, program, procedure or subroutine is accepted without one, and no whitespace is required after the keyword match. After the keyword (function, program or procedure, or subroutine) and whitespace, a name must follow whose first character is accepted unchecked and whose remaining characters are consumed while intoken() holds; a one-character name is rejected (line skipped). The name is cut with EOS in lbuf, copied with strlcpy into tok (truncated to the buffer size), then get_line() and pfnote(tok, lineno) are called and pfcnt is set. It holds no locks and allocates nothing. get_line, pfnote, intoken were not read.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Entry point of ctlstat (usr.bin/ctlstat/ctlstat.c:846-1007; slice cut the head). Defaults: waittime 1, count -1, 3 devices, CPU and header shown. It reads sysctl kern.cam.ctl.max_luns into ctl_stat_bits (1024 if the sysctl fails), allocates the item bitmask with bit_alloc (err(1) on failure), and parses options. -c sets count and -w the wait time with atoi (no validation); -l and -p add one LUN or port to the mask, with errx(1) only if the number is greater than ctl_stat_bits (negative values and a value equal to ctl_stat_bits are not rejected here) ; -n sets the device count; -P selects Prometheus mode; the default (unknown option) branch calls usage(1) and exit(1). After parsing: -l together with -p is errx(1); in Prometheus mode, if count != -1, waittime != 1, ports were requested or totals were requested, it calls errx(1), otherwise sets count to 1 (so -c 1 or -w 1 passed explicitly are not detected). If neither LUNs nor ports were selected it selects ports when totals are on, else LUNs. It opens CTL_DEFAULT_DEV (err(1) on failure), prints an HTTP/1.1 200 header in Prometheus mode, then loops while count != 0: in Prometheus mode it calls get_and_print_stats twice (LUNs then ports), otherwise once with the ports flag from the context; it prints a blank line, flushes, clears the first-run flag, sleeps waittime unless count == 1, and decrements count if it is positive. A negative count (the default) loops forever; count 0 skips the loop. After the loop it calls exit(retval), which is 0 unless the usage branch set it; get_and_print_stats (not read) can itself terminate the process. The fd is not closed explicitly.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Entry point of diff (usr.bin/diff/diff.c:138-483; slice cut the head). It parses the option letters and long options into globals; options that conflict with an already chosen output format call conflicting_format(), invalid arguments (for example --tabsize or --color values, the context count) call usage() after a warning, -X calls read_excludes_file (which exits 2 through err if the file cannot be opened), --version prints diff_version and exit(0), and several branches call usage(). It defaults the format to D_NORMAL (D_CONTEXT if the prototype flag is set and no format chose), sets colour codes when do_color() and DIFFCOLORS is present, and (OpenBSD builds only) calls pledge. If the operand count is not 2 it calls usage(). It compiles the ignore and most-recent patterns with checked_regcomp (errx(2) on failure), stats or fstats the two operands ('-' means stdin); a failing stat is err(2) unless -N was given and errno is ENOENT, in which case that side is treated as empty; if both are empty it warns and exit(2). Comparing stdin to a directory is errx(2). If both operands are directories it errors out with status 2 when -D is in use, else calls diffdir; otherwise a directory operand is replaced by splice(dir, other) and re-stat'd (err(2) on failure) and diffreg is called and reported through print_status. It then flushes stdout (err(2) if that fails) and calls exit(status) with the global status accumulated by the comparison routines (0 when no differences were reported, 1 when differences were found, 2 when errors were recorded). It does not return. Usage() and the callees were not read in full.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Entry point of dpv (usr.bin/dpv/dpv.c:250-476; slice cut the head). It records argv[0], mallocs and zeroes a dpv_config (errx(EXIT_FAILURE) if out of memory) and parses options. -a, -p, -b and -t copy their argument into malloc'd storage (errx(EXIT_FAILURE) on malloc failure); -D and -X choose the display type; -d sets debug; -h and any unknown option call usage(); -i/-I set status formats (later overwritten, see below); -k keeps the tite; -l selects line mode; -m multiple-file mode; -N, -T, -w set option bits; -o and -x set the output file or shell command; -L, -n, -P and -U take strtol(optarg, NULL, 10) results (a negative -L/-P below -1 becomes -1, a negative -n becomes -1), and the check 'value == 0 && errno == EINVAL' calls errx(EXIT_FAILURE) only if errno was already EINVAL, because strtol does not set EINVAL for a non-numeric string; such an argument normally just yields 0. The remaining arguments are turned into a linked list of file nodes (malloc and zero each, errx on failure): a leading 'number:' is parsed with sscanf into the node's length and stripped from the name, otherwise the length is -1; with -m each label must be followed by a path argument (errx(EXIT_FAILURE) if missing), without -m only the first argument is used and the loop stops after one node. If no label was given it warns and calls usage(). With the default libdialog display it installs sig_int for SIGINT (the sigaction struct's mask and flags are not initialised). The status line formats are then set unconditionally for line or byte mode (overwriting -i and -I) together with the action callback. It calls dpv(config, file_list), warns only if that returns nonzero and -d was given, calls end_dialog() unless -k was given, calls dpv_free() and exit(EXIT_SUCCESS). usage() (490-543) exits with EXIT_FAILURE, printing the text only when debug is off. Main does not return; the config and file nodes are not freed here.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Entry point of elfdump (usr.bin/elfdump/elfdump.c:504-708; slice cut the head). Options set bits in flags (-a sets flags = ED_ALL and -E sets flags = ED_IS_ELF, both replacing earlier bits; the others OR in a single bit); -w opens the named file for writing as the output stream (err(1) if it cannot be opened or its rights cannot be limited to CAP_FSTAT and CAP_WRITE); an unknown option calls usage(). usage() is also called if no operand remains, if no flag was set, or if -E is combined with more than one operand, other flags or -w; extra operands beyond the first are otherwise ignored (only *av is used). It opens the first operand read-only and fstat's it (err(1) on failure; the descriptor is not closed later); a file smaller than an Elf32_Ehdr exits 1 (silently with -E, errx 'not an elf file' otherwise). It limits rights (CAP_MMAP_R on the file, none on stdin, stdout/stderr limits) and enters capability mode, each failure being err(1), then maps the whole file read-only with MAP_SHARED (err(1) on MAP_FAILED). If the magic check fails it exits 1 (errx otherwise); with -E on a valid ELF it exit(0)s without printing. Otherwise it reads header offsets and counts from the mapped image, locates the section header string table and the .strtab and .dynstr section data (offsets and indices taken from the file are not checked against the file size), prints the ELF header, program headers and section headers if requested, walks the program headers (printing the interpreter if requested) and the section headers dispatching to the print routines by section type under the corresponding flag bits, and returns 0. The mapping is never unmapped. Because it never returns nonzero, all error exits are exit/err/errx/usage calls. The print routines were not read.

functions.name: do_printf
functions.prose_contract: Real name do_printf (usr.bin/find/printf.c:159-348; the packet name was truncated and the slice cut the head). It runs plan->c_data through escape(), which may set a flush request and a warned flag (F_HAS_WARNED is set on the plan if warned), and then walks the escaped string. Ordinary characters are copied to fout with putc. After '%', the next character selects the field: the literal percent, path (%p), file name (%f), directory part of the path or '.' if there is no '/' (%h), group and user names or numbers (%g %G %u %U), octal mode (%m), ls-style mode (%M), blocks and sizes (%k %b %s %S, %S printing blocks*512/size as a float), depth (%d), device (%D), link target (%l, printing nothing if readlink returns 0 or fails), inode, link count, file type (%y; %Y follows a symlink with stat and prints L, N or ? when stat fails with the loop, missing or other errors), and the access, change, modification time forms (%a %c %t with ctime, %A %C %T taking the next format character for strftime, %B likewise for birth time but printing nothing when st_birthtime is 0 or the system lacks it); %Z prints nothing. %P, %H and %F, the numeric modifier characters and '.', and any unknown character call errx(1, ...) without returning (the escaped buffer is then not freed). At the end it fflush(fout) if the flush flag was set, frees the escaped copy and returns nothing. The format-taking cases (%A, %B, %C, %T) consume the next format character even if it is the terminating NUL, after which the loop reads past the end of the string. escape(), fp_ctime and fp_strftime were not read in full.

functions.name: print_pts_info
functions.prose_contract: Static function (usr.bin/fstat/fstat.c:498-517) taking a procstat handle and a filestat. It calls procstat_get_pts_info into local pts and errbuf variables (not caller storage). If that returns nonzero it prints "* error" (no newline) and returns. Otherwise it prints "* pseudo-terminal master ", then, when the -n flag (nflg) is set or pts.devname is the empty string, the device number pts.dev as %#10jx, else pts.devname as %10s, and finally calls print_access_flags(fst->fs_fflags). Its only effect is output on stdout; it keeps no pointer to its locals.

functions.name: MCParse
functions.prose_contract: Reads the catalog source from fd line by line with get_line until it returns NULL, then returns (no value). Lines starting with '$': '$set N' calls MCAddSet(atoi) and resets msgid to 0; '$delset N' calls MCDelSet(atoi); '$quote' sets the local quote character to the first non-blank character after it, or to 0 if there is none (this is local state only, nothing is added to the catalog); a '$' followed by whitespace is ignored; any other '$' line gives an 'unrecognized line' warning if text remains. Other lines: an empty line is skipped; a line not starting with a digit gets a warning and is skipped; otherwise msgid = atoi, the id digits and following blanks are skipped, and if nothing remains MCDelMsg(msgid) is called, else getmsg(fd, text, quote) builds the message (backslash escapes, an optional leading quote character, a closing quote character ending the text when followed only by whitespace to the end of the line, otherwise warned about and kept) and MCAddMsg(msgid, str) is called. An unterminated quote simply ends at the end of that line, with no error. getmsg calls error() (which terminates the program) if a trailing backslash is followed by end of file; the callees MCAddSet, MCDelSet, MCAddMsg, MCDelMsg and get_line can also terminate the program via error(), which was not read here. getmsg's message buffer is static and reused between calls.

functions.name: procmatch_match
functions.prose_contract: Static helper (usr.bin/grep/util.c:203-244) called for a matching line. First, independently of mc->printmatch: if mc->doctx is set, it prints "--\n" when first_match is false and either mc->same_file is false or mc->last_outed > 0, calls printqueue() when Bflag > 0, and sets mc->tail = Aflag. Then, if mc->printmatch is set, it calls printline(pc, ':', &last_out); while pc->matchidx >= MAX_MATCHES it resets matchidx to 0, re-runs procline(pc) and calls printline again if that returned !vflag, otherwise leaves the loop; if the last printline did not terminate the line it calls printline once more; finally it sets first_match = false, mc->same_file = true and mc->last_outed = 0. If printmatch is not set, none of the printing or the first_match / same_file / last_outed updates happen, but the doctx separator, queue flush and tail update still do when doctx is set. No return value.

functions.name: litexec
functions.prose_contract: Literal-string matcher (usr.bin/grep/util.c:437-487, compiled only with WITH_INTERNAL_NOSPEC). It uses strcasestr when cflags has REG_ICASE, else strstr. The search region is taken from pmatch[0]: ofs = rm_so, stringlen = rm_eo. If ofs >= stringlen it returns REG_NOMATCH without touching pmatch. It copies the first stringlen bytes of string with strndup (so the copy stops at an embedded NUL) and returns REG_ESPACE if that fails. The loop stops when pat->len exceeds the remaining text, when no occurrence is found, or, when nmatch == 0, after the first occurrence (pmatch is not written in that case). When nmatch > 0 each occurrence is recorded in pmatch[idx] as absolute offsets (rm_so = ofs + offset, rm_eo = rm_so + pat->len) and idx is incremented; the loop ends when idx reaches nmatch; otherwise the next search start is computed as pmatch[idx].rm_so + 1 after idx was incremented, i.e. from the entry that has not been written yet (its prior content), not from the match just found, so searching for further occurrences uses whatever the caller left in that entry. The copy is freed on every path after allocation. If at least one occurrence was found and nmatch > 0, the unused entries pmatch[idx..nmatch-1] are set to -1/-1. It returns 0 if at least one occurrence was counted, else REG_NOMATCH.

functions.name: printline
functions.prose_contract: Real name printline (usr.bin/grep/util.c:774-856; slice cut the head). It starts with a = *last_out and terminated = true. If oflag and matchall are both set it returns true immediately, without printing, without writing *last_out and without incrementing pc->printed. If (oflag || color) and (pc->printed > 0 || pc->matchidx > 0): with color and not -o it prints the line metadata once when nothing was printed yet; for each of the first matchidx matches that is not zero-length it (with -o) sets pc->ln.boff to the match start and prints the metadata, or (without -o) writes the text from a up to the match start; wraps the match text in color escapes when color is set, sets a to the match end, and with -o writes a newline. Then it stores a in *last_out (which equals the old *last_out if no non-empty match was processed, so its value is unchanged in that case). Without -o and when matchidx != MAX_MATCHES it writes the remaining tail (and sets *last_out = ln.len) if any, then a newline and fflush; without -o and with matchidx == MAX_MATCHES it prints no newline and sets terminated = false; with -o it just fflushes. In the other case (neither -o nor color, or no match and nothing printed yet) it calls grep_printline(&pc->ln, sep). In every non-early path it then increments pc->printed and returns terminated, which is false only for the no -o / MAX_MATCHES case above. It also modifies pc->ln.boff in the -o case.

functions.name: gz_uncompress
functions.prose_contract: Decodes a gzip stream from descriptor in (starting with the prelen bytes in pre, which may be 0) to descriptor out (usr.bin/gzip/gzip.c:718-1055). The comment above says it closes the input, but the code never calls close on in (not at any label), so the caller keeps the descriptor. It allocates two BUFLEN buffers; if malloc fails maybe_err prints (unless -q) and exit(2)s (the later goto labels are reached only through that call, which does not return). It then runs a byte-driven state machine over the header (magic 0, magic 1 (also accepts the old-magic byte), method must be Z_DEFLATED, flags, 6 skipped bytes, optional extra field, original name, comment and header CRC), inflateInit2 with raw deflate, inflate with Z_FINISH writing each output chunk to out unless -t (tflag) is set and updating the CRC and the member length, then checks the trailer CRC and length against the decoded member and loops back to the first magic state for the next member. Read errors, bad magic1, unknown method, inflate errors, write_retry failure, truncated trailer or input, CRC or length mismatch, and a decompression error code all end with out_tot = -1 after a warning. At the start of a member, a first byte that is not the gzip magic byte stops the loop and keeps the count so far, with a 'trailing garbage ignored' warning and exit_value = 2, because in_tot is already greater than 0 at that point whenever any byte has been read or passed in (so even a non-gzip first byte takes this path rather than 'input not gziped (MAGIC0)'); end of input exactly at a member boundary also stops normally. After the loop it calls inflateEnd when the state is past the init state, frees both buffers, stores in_tot (prelen plus all bytes read) in *gsizep if gsizep is non-NULL, and returns out_tot, the total uncompressed bytes counted (0 if no member was decoded) or -1 on failure.

functions.name: dump_line
functions.prose_contract: Flushes the current label, code and comment buffers to the output stream (usr.bin/indent/io.c:60-221). First, if ps.procname is non-empty it clears it and sets ps.ind_level to 0. If all three buffers are empty it either decrements suppress_blanklines when that is positive or sets ps.bl_line and increments n_real_blanklines, and prints nothing. Otherwise, if inhibit_formatting is false it clears suppress_blanklines and ps.bl_line, adjusts the pending blank-line count and prints it, counts a code line when a label or code is present, and prints: the label (first closing an open comment with a ".*/" line, trimming trailing blanks, padding, and handling #else/#endif tails), then the code (closing an open comment first, adjusting ps.paren_indents entries for the paren levels, padding and copying characters, with the 0200 marker expanded to a number), then the comment section if present (placed at ps.com_col plus delta, moved to a new line when the cursor is already past the target, trailing space trimmed; an open comment is not closed by this section), then a newline or form feed and ps.out_lines is incremented. When the line is non-empty but inhibit_formatting is set, nothing is written. On every path (including the empty-line and inhibit_formatting paths) it then sets ps.decl_on_line, ps.ind_stmt, ps.use_ff = false and ps.dumped_decl_indent = 0, empties the three buffers (the comment buffer restarts at combuf + 1), reloads ps.ind_level and ps.paren_level from ps.i_l_follow and ps.p_l_follow, sets paren_target from ps.paren_indents when ps.paren_level > 0, and sets not_first_line to 1.

functions.name: parse
functions.prose_contract: Feeds one token code tk to indent's construct parser (usr.bin/indent/parse.c:52-221). First, while the top of ps.p_stack is ifhead and tk is not elselit, it rewrites that entry to stmt and calls reduce() (this happens before the switch, also for a tk that is later rejected). The switch then does: decl pushes one decl entry if the top is not already decl (setting break_comma, ps.il, and with ljust_decl recomputing ps.ind_level and ps.i_l_follow) and sets ps.search_brace; ifstmt (popping an elsehead entry first when 'else if' is enabled), dolit and forstmt push the token, set ps.ind_level and ps.il from ps.i_l_follow and increment ps.i_l_follow; lbrace pushes lbrace and stmt entries and adjusts ps.i_l_follow or ps.ind_level; whilestmt either matches a pending dohead or pushes a while loop entry; elselit turns an ifhead into elsehead, and otherwise only calls diag2(1, "Unmatched 'else'") without changing the stack; rbrace pops back to the matching lbrace and stores stmt, and otherwise (ps.tos == 0 or the entry below the top is not lbrace) only calls diag2(1, "Statement nesting error"); swstmt pushes swstmt and updates case_ind and ps.i_l_follow; semicolon pushes stmt. Any other tk calls diag2(1, "Unknown code to parser") and returns without reaching the checks below. For all other cases, including the two diagnosed ones, control falls out of the switch: if ps.tos >= STACKSIZE - 1 it calls errx(1, "Parser stack overflow"); otherwise reduce() is called, which can still change the stack, and the function returns. The array index ps.tos is not checked before the pushes in the switch, only after.

functions.name: kernel_wait
functions.prose_contract: Polls the iSCSI driver until all sessions are connected (usr.bin/iscsictl/iscsictl.c:553-607). Each poll reallocs the states buffer to nentries entries (xo_err(1) and exit on realloc failure) and issues the ISCSISLIST ioctl on iscsi_fd; if it fails with EMSGSIZE, nentries is multiplied by 4 and the call is repeated; any other failure prints a warning via xo_warn and returns the ioctl's nonzero result (the ioctl failure value, -1). On success it scans the isl_nentries entries returned and returns 0 if every one has iss_connected set (also 0 when the list is empty). Otherwise it sleeps one second; if timeout > 0 it decrements it and returns 1 when it reaches 0 (so a positive timeout allows that many polls); a timeout of 0 or below never reaches that test and polls forever. The states buffer is not freed on any return path. The function has no formal contract because it works through a file descriptor and ioctl.

functions.name: yyparse
functions.prose_contract: Generated byacc LALR parser for the lex input grammar (usr.bin/lex/initparse.c:719-1843; the head is the YYPARSE_DECL() definition, here yyparse(void)). It resets yynerrs, yyerrflag, yychar (to YYEMPTY) and the state, allocates the initial stack through yygrowstack if none exists (a failure goes to yyoverflow), then loops: it takes the default reduction for the state if there is one, else reads a token with YYLEX when yychar < 0 (a negative value becomes YYEOF), shifts it (growing the stack when full; growth failure goes to yyoverflow) or reduces by the grammar rule; the rule actions (lines 845-1810, which run the semantic code for the lex grammar) were not read. On a syntax error it calls YYERROR_CALL("syntax error") (unless already recovering), increments yynerrs (also for the YYERROR action), and tries to pop states to one that accepts the error token, with yyerrflag = 3; if the stack is exhausted or the next token is YYEOF during recovery it goes to yyabort. On yyoverflow it calls YYERROR_CALL("yacc stack overflow") and falls through into yyabort (so the function does not return 2). Both yyabort and yyaccept call yyfreestack (freeing the state and value stacks) before returning: yyabort returns 1 and yyaccept (reached by a reduction in the final state when yychar is YYEOF) returns 0. The stack is therefore freed on every return, and the caller must not free it. yygrowstack (665-702) returns YYENOMEM only to its caller within yyparse.

functions.name: YY_DECL
functions.prose_contract: Generated function flexscan (YY_DECL at initscan.c:1914-1915 expands to 'int flexscan(void)'; the function body runs from line 2191 to 4282; the packet called it yylex, which does not exist here). It is the flex scanner for flex's own input. On its first call it sets yy_init, the start state, yyin/yyout to stdin/stdout when unset and creates the first buffer. It then loops, matching the longest rule with the DFA tables, backing up to the last accepting state if needed, and runs the selected rule action. Rule actions return a token code (for example '<', '^', '"', '$', '\n', BEGIN_REPEAT_POSIX or BEGIN_REPEAT_FLEX, EOF_OP, as in rules 139-151) or just update scanner state (linenum, sectnum, bracelevel, start conditions via BEGIN, output via ACTION_ECHO) and continue the loop. yyterminate() (return 0 / YY_NULL) is used at the end-of-file action of SECT2PROLOG (after mark_prolog and sectnum = 0, line 3156), by rule 152 (the %% line that starts section 3, which sets sectnum = 3, selects SECT3 or SECT3_NOESCAPE and writes a comment, line 3340), and at other EOF actions (lines 2623, 4042, 4051), so it also returns 0 at a section boundary, not only at real end of input. Rule 153 reports 'Input line too long' via synerr and calls FLEX_EXIT(EXIT_FAILURE) when the matched text is not shorter than MAXLINE. Only this slice (rules 130-153), the entry code and the DFA matching loop were read; the other rules and the buffer-refill code were not read, so other return values and exits are not enumerated.

functions.name: end_order
functions.prose_contract: Closes the current collation order entry (usr.bin/localedef/collate.c:605-693). It saves pri = nextpri and switches on currorder. T_CHAR: for each of the NUM_WT weights it resets order_weights[i] to -1 after setting currchar->ref[i] either to pri with RESOLVED (when the weight was negative, get_pri(ref) is NULL, or the referenced priority is -1) or to the given ref with REFER; then ellipsis_start = currchar->wc + 1 and currchar = NULL. T_ELLIPSIS: copies order_weights into ellipsis_weights and resets order_weights to -1; nothing is resolved. T_COLLELEM: if currelem is NULL it prints an internal fault message (INTERR only prints, it does not exit) and sets no weights; otherwise the same RESOLVED/REFER logic is applied to currelem->ref[i]. T_UNDEFINED: the same logic but an unspecified weight sets pri_undefined[i] to -1 with RESOLVED (not to nextpri). T_SYMBOL: the same logic applied to currundef->ref[i] (currundef is dereferenced without a NULL check). Any other currorder value prints the internal fault message and sets nothing. After the switch nextpri is incremented by one on every path (the INTERR cases do not return early).

functions.name: start_order_symbol
functions.prose_contract: Calls get_collundef(name) and stores the result in currundef, then calls start_order(T_SYMBOL). get_collundef (collate.c:549-570) looks name up in the collundefs tree; if it is absent it callocs an entry, strdups the name, gives each of NUM_WT refs a new priority and inserts it, and if calloc or strdup fails it prints 'out of memory', frees the entry and returns NULL (currundef is then NULL and add_charmap_undefined is not called); in all non-failing cases (new or existing entry) it then calls add_charmap_undefined(name), which either frees name or records it in the charmap as an undefined symbol (with a warning), so the caller's name must not be used afterwards. start_order sets lastorder to the old currorder, currorder to T_SYMBOL, prints 'character value expected' if the old currorder was T_ELLIPSIS, resets all COLL_WEIGHTS_MAX order_weights to -1 and sets curr_weight to 0.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Entry point of lock (usr.bin/lock/lock.c:81-255). Options: -t minutes (errx(1) if atoi gives <= 0), -p (use the user's own PAM authentication; errx(1) if getpwuid fails), -n (no timeout), -v (lock the vty), anything else calls usage() (exit 1). Without -p it drops privileges with setuid(getuid()) (errx(1) on failure). It then exit(1)s if tcgetattr on fd 0 fails, errx(1) if ttyname(0) fails, records the time, installs quit for SIGINT/SIGQUIT and turns terminal echo off. With -p it calls pam_start; failure is err(1) and the process exits with echo still off (the terminal is not restored there). Without -p it prompts twice for a key: if the first fgets fails or the line is just a newline it calls quit(0); if the two keys differ it prints a message, restores the terminal and exit(1). It then installs hi for SIGINT/SIGQUIT/SIGTSTP and bye for SIGALRM, starts the interval timer unless -n, and with -v issues the VT_LOCKSWITCH ioctl (on failure it restores the terminal and err(1)). It prints the lock banner and loops: with -p it calls pam_authenticate, leaving the loop on PAM_SUCCESS and otherwise (logging unexpected errors to syslog) going to the tryagain code; without -p it reads a key (on read failure it clears stdin's error, calls hi(0) and goes to tryagain) and leaves the loop if it equals the stored key; each wrong key counts a failure (syslogged when root) and the loop then calls tcgetattr, which exit(1)s on failure other than EINTR (without restoring the terminal), sleeps one second and repeats. After the loop it syslogs a root unlock, calls pam_end with -p and calls quit(0), which restores the terminal attributes, unlocks the vty if locked and exit(0)s. The function does not return normally. The signal handlers can end the process too: bye (SIGALRM, only when a timeout is on) restores the terminal and exit(1)s; hi only prints.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Entry point of login (usr.bin/login/login.c:155-667; slice cut the head). It ignores SIGQUIT/SIGINT/SIGHUP, sets a SIGALRM timeout handler (via setjmp/longjmp: on timeout it logs a failed attempt if any, prints 'Login timed out' and calls bail(NO_SLEEP_EXIT, 0), exit status 0), parses -f, -h host (errx(1) unless root or if the name is too long), -p; other options call usage(). A user name operand is copied with strdup (err(1) on failure). It closes descriptors from 3, finds the tty name with ttyname(0) (a '??' name under _PATH_TTY is used if that fails, so stdin need not be a tty), reads login class parameters, then loops: asks for the name if needed, runs pam_start/pam_set_item (failure: pam_syslog and bail(NO_SLEEP_EXIT, 1)), looks the user up, and either accepts -f for root or the same user or calls auth_pam(); a success with a valid passwd entry leaves the loop; otherwise it prints 'Login incorrect', counts failures and, after the backoff count, sleeps or, at the retry limit, calls badlogin and bail(SLEEP_EXIT, 1). After success it cancels the alarm, installs bail_sig for SIGHUP/SIGTERM, calls pam_setcred (failure: bail(NO_SLEEP_EXIT, 1)), changes to the home directory (refused()/bail if requirehome or the root directory is unusable, else falls back to '/'), picks the shell with strdup (bail(SLEEP_EXIT, 1) on failure), fixes tty ownership, builds the environment, calls setusercontext (bail(NO_SLEEP_EXIT, 1) on failure), pam_setcred reinitialise and pam_open_session (bail(NO_SLEEP_EXIT, 1) on failure) and forks. fork failure is err(1). The parent waits for the child and then calls bail(NO_SLEEP_EXIT, 0), exiting with status 0. The child does export_pam_environment, pam_end, setlogin (bail(NO_SLEEP_EXIT, 1) on failure), the rest of setusercontext (plain exit(1) on failure), sets environment variables, prints the motd and mail notice unless quiet, resets signals, builds arg0 (errx(1) if the shell path is too long, err(1) if asprintf fails) and calls execlp(shell, arg0, NULL); if that returns it calls err(1). bail/bail_internal run pam_cleanup (closing any established session and credentials), sleep the requested seconds and exit(eval). Main never returns.

functions.name: macro
functions.prose_contract: Main m4 input loop (usr.bin/m4/main.c:350-521; returns nothing). It reads characters with gpbc() in an endless loop and handles: an opening quote (nested quotes are counted; the quote delimiters are stripped except nested ones, and the text goes directly to the output when not inside a macro call (sp < 0) or is saved on the string stack otherwise; end of input inside the quote prints 'unclosed quote' (with the count) via warnx, dumps the quote stack and calls exit(1)); a comment start when not inside a macro (copied through to the end delimiter or EOF); an identifier, looked up with inspect(): if it is not a macro, or is a macro needing arguments that is not followed by '(', its name is output (to the string stack when sp >= 0), otherwise a call frame is pushed and, with no '(' and parenthesis level 0, the macro is evaluated immediately with eval(), and sp, fp and ep are restored to their earlier values; an overflow of the macro stack there or later is errx(1, "internal stack overflow") with no stack dump; EOF: if not mimic_gnu and a macro call is still open at the top input level (sp > -1 and ilevel <= 0) it warns 'unexpected end of input, unclosed parenthesis', dumps the paren stack and exit(1)s; otherwise at the top level (ilevel <= 0) the loop ends and the function returns, and at a nested input level the input is released and the loop continues; any other character is output directly when sp < 0, and inside a macro call '(' , ')' and ',' manage argument collection (')' at level 0 evaluates the call and restores sp/fp/ep) and other characters, including comments, are saved on the string stack. The function returns only at EOF with ilevel <= 0; the exit paths above do not return. eval, inspect and the output helpers were not read.

functions.name: mail1
functions.prose_contract: Sends the message on standard input to the recipients in hp (usr.bin/mail/send.c:282-414; returns nothing). It calls collect(); if that returns NULL it increments senderr and returns. In interactive mode it may prompt for Cc/Bcc or print EOT. If the collected file is empty and dontsendempty is set it jumps to out (message dropped silently); an empty body otherwise just prints a notice. It then sets senderr = 0 (so a collect failure count is reset only on this path), expands bcc/to/cc through usermap (NULL prints 'No recipients specified' and increments senderr), runs outof() (which can write to files named in recipients), and saves a dead letter with savedeadletter(mtf) if senderr is nonzero at that point. It elides the list; if no recipients remain it goes to out. With recordrecip it copies the original To name list; fixhead is applied, infix() builds the full message file and the function returns without closing the file if infix returned NULL (infix returns its input or the new file and never NULL, so that branch is not reachable). It builds the sendmail argument list; with debug set it prints the arguments and goes to out without delivering or recording. Otherwise it records the message with savemail (to a file named after the first recipient for recordrecip, or to the 'record' file), forks (on failure: warning, dead letter, out), and the child blocks several signals, uses the temp file as stdin and execv's sendmail (the 'sendmail' option or _PATH_SENDMAIL), calling _exit(1) if the exec fails; the parent waits for the child when 'verbose' is set, else calls free_child. At out it closes the message file with Fclose. The only path that returns without closing it is the NULL result of collect (no file) and the unreachable infix failure.

functions.name: image_init
functions.prose_contract: Initialises the image module (usr.bin/mkimg/image.c:734-755). It empties the chunk list (TAILQ_INIT), sets image_nchunks and image_swap_size to 0 and image_swap_pgsz to getpagesize(). It then calls atexit(image_cleanup); if that fails it returns errno (image_swap_file and image_swap_fd are not touched at that point). Otherwise it builds the template "<dir>/mkimg-XXXXXX" in the static image_swap_file buffer with snprintf, where dir is $TMPDIR (or _PATH_TMP if TMPDIR is unset or empty; a long path is truncated by snprintf), and calls mkstemp on it. If mkstemp fails (returns -1) it returns errno, leaving image_swap_fd at -1 (the atexit handler is already registered, and the handler later unlinks image_swap_file); on success mkstemp has replaced the XXXXXX in image_swap_file with the actual temporary file name and image_swap_fd holds the open descriptor, and it returns 0. The chunk list, counters and page size are set in all cases that reach line 745, that is all cases.

functions.name: parse_part
functions.prose_contract: Real name parse_part (static, usr.bin/mkimg/mkimg.c:247-329; mkimg_parse_spec does not exist). If spec is exactly "-" it increments nparts and returns 0 without allocating or touching partlist. Otherwise it callocs a struct part (ENOMEM and return if that fails), finds the first ':' in spec (EINVAL if none or if it is the first character), mallocs and copies the text before it as part->alias (ENOMEM on failure), and requires the character after the ':' to be ':' (size), '=' (file) or '-' (pipe), else EINVAL. The rest of the string is strdup'ed as part->contents (ENOMEM on failure; it may be empty). If the alias contains a '/', it is split there: an empty alias or empty label gives EINVAL, otherwise the label is strdup'ed (ENOMEM on failure). On success it sets part->index to the old nparts, appends the part to the tail of partlist, increments nparts and returns 0. On any failure after the part allocation it frees part->alias and the part and returns the error, so partlist and nparts are unchanged; part->contents (and the label if it had been allocated, which only matters for a failure that occurs after it) is not freed, so contents leaks when the later alias/label checks fail.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Entry point of msgs (usr.bin/msgs/msgs.c:145-607; slice cut the head; ends with exit(0) at 606 and never returns). It drops privileges with setuid(getuid()) (err(1) on failure), handles SIGINT, and scans arguments: a leading digit gives the starting message, a digit in the second position a backward offset, otherwise it reads flag letters (c clean, only root or the daemon user else errx(1); f hush; h headers; l local; o; p pager; q query; s send; unknown letters call usage()). Unless send mode, the bounds file under _PATH_MSGS must be stat-able, otherwise err(errno) (or exit(1) with -f). It reads firstmsg/lastmsg from the bounds file and closes it. If cleaning or the bounds file could not be opened it rescans the _PATH_MSGS directory (err(errno) if it cannot be opened), computing first and last message numbers and, when cleaning, unlinking writable messages older than the cutoff, never lowering the old upper bound; unless send mode it then rewrites the bounds file (err(errno) if it cannot be opened). In send mode it opens the bounds file for writing and message lastmsg+1 for writing (err(errno) on failure), writes the new bounds, closes the bounds file (the new message file stays open until exit), copies stdin into the message (prompting for the Subject when stdin is a tty), and calls exit(ferror(stdin)) (or exit(1) when OBJECT is defined and no Subject was seen). With -c it then exit(0)s. For display it needs a non-empty HOME (else prints an error and exit(1)), reads and updates the .msgsrc next-message number, and loops over message numbers from firstmsg to lastmsg: it opens each message (skipping unreadable ones), prints the header lines, a line count, and in header mode only the headers; with -q it prints 'There are new messages.' and exit(0)s at the first (local, if -l) message; otherwise it reads the user's command (x exits 0; q prints '--Postponed--' and exits 0; others skip, replay or go to a numbered message) and updates the .msgsrc number as messages are passed; each message file is closed with fclose after processing. After the loop it may offer the last message again (with the 'o' flag on a tty), prints 'No new messages.' if nothing was shown and neither -f nor -q was given, and calls exit(0). The .msgsrc stream opened for update is not closed before exit.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Entry point of netstat (usr.bin/netstat/main.c:241-621; slice cut the head). It calls xo_parse_args (exit(EXIT_FAILURE) on a negative result) and parses options with getopt, setting global flags; invalid fib numbers, unknown address families and unknown protocols call xo_errx(EX_DATAERR, ...), a missing jail option argument or bad interval calls usage(), 'Jail support is not compiled in' is EX_UNAVAILABLE. After options it takes an optional interval and wait argument, attaches to a named jail (EX_UNAVAILABLE if not found or the attach fails), sets live = no -N/-M, loads kvm symbols for non-live use, and rejects -x together with -T (EX_USAGE). Then the first matching report is produced and the program finishes with xo_finish and exit(EX_OK) (exit(EX_IOERR) via xo_err when xo_finish fails): -B (usage() unless live, bpf_stats), -m (mbpr; when not live it is called only if kread(0, NULL, 0) == 0, otherwise nothing is printed, still exit(EX_OK)), -Q (netisr_stats with the same kread condition), -i without -s (intpr), -r (route statistics with -s, else routepr), -o (nhops_print), -O (nexthop groups), -g (setfib, EX_DATAERR on failure, then multicast route stats or tables per address family), -p (one protocol via printproto), and otherwise all protocol tables for the selected address family via printproto plus unixpr when the family is unix or unspecified and -s is not set. The code never returns from main; every path ends in exit or an exit-calling helper. The kvm-loading and routing branches (lines 462-465, 495-548) and the called report functions were not read in detail.

functions.name: addgroup
functions.prose_contract: Switches the process to the group named or numbered by grpname, keeping the old effective gid as a supplementary group (usr.bin/newgrp/newgrp.c:145-243; pwd is the file-static passwd entry). It saves egid, looks grpname up with getgrnam, else as a positive decimal id with getgrgid; if neither works it warns 'bad group name' and returns with nothing changed. The user counts as a member when pwd->pw_gid equals the group's gid or the name is in gr_mem. A non-member, if the group has a non-empty password and getuid() != 0, is prompted with getpass: a NULL result returns silently (no message), a NULL crypt result or a mismatch prints 'Sorry' and returns. It then mallocs sysconf(_SC_NGROUPS_MAX) gids (err(1) if malloc fails), calls getgroups (warning and cleanup/return on failure at label end), and, if the requested gid differs from egid and is in the list, removes it and calls setgroups under PRIV_START/PRIV_END (a failure warns and goes to end, skipping the setgid). It then calls setgid(grp->gr_gid) (warning and end on failure, so the gid is unchanged), and if the old egid is not in the list appends it with setgroups unless the list is full (prints 'too many groups') or setgroups fails (warning). Finally the buffer is freed (also at end) and the function returns nothing. Failures in the privilege helpers PRIV_START/PRIV_END may terminate the program (not read).

functions.name: another_hunk
functions.prose_contract: Reads the next hunk from the patch file pfp (usr.bin/patch/pch.c:536-1203; slice cut the head) and stores it in the global arrays p_line/p_char/p_len in context-diff layout. It first frees the previous hunk's lines p_end down to 0, skipping the fake-copied range (p_bfake..p_efake, where p_end jumps to p_bfake) so shared lines are not freed twice, and resets p_efake. Then by diff_type: for a context diff it expects a line starting with '********' (otherwise next_intuit_at(line_beginning, p_input_line) and return false), reads lines up to the maximum hunk size, records the '***' and '---' header lines and line counts (malformed(), fatal() or grow_hunkmax() on bad numbers, hunks over MAXHUNKSIZE, duplicate or misplaced '---', or end of file; end of file or a premature '***'/'********' is accepted without fatal() only when the replacement part is absent and may be missing), and fills omitted old or new context lines from the other half; a diff of the old style may be re-labelled NEW_CONTEXT_DIFF. For a unified diff it reads the header (returning false after next_intuit_at if no valid '@@' header is found, malformed() on bad numbers) and the lines, where an end of file when fewer than three lines of space remain is treated as chopped blank lines and otherwise is fatal('unexpected end of file'). For a normal diff it reads the command line (next_intuit_at and return false if none), builds the '***'/'---' lines, and reads '<' and '>' lines, with fatal() on end of file or a wrong marker. When savestr runs out of memory (out_of_mem) it returns false after setting p_end to just before the failing entry (it frees partially built lines only in the unified branch); otherwise, if reverse is set it calls pch_swap and only prints 'Not enough memory to swap next hunk!' if that fails, stores a '^' stopper in p_char[p_end+1] when p_end + 1 < hunkmax, and returns true. Malformed input and truncated files normally end in malformed() or fatal(), which do not return. The unified and normal branches (lines 900-1180) were read only in outline.

functions.name: create
functions.prose_contract: Subcommand 'create' (usr.bin/posixmqcontrol/posixmqcontrol.c:424-518; q_creation is passed by value). It builds an mq_attr from q_creation.depth and size and adds O_NONBLOCK to the open flags and the attribute flags when q_creation.block is false. It first tries mq_open(queue, flags) without O_CREAT; if that succeeds the queue exists (exists = true) and its depth and size are not changed. If it fails, it runs validate_size() and validate_depth() (which print their own warnings) and, only if both pass, clears set_mode and calls mq_open with O_CREAT, the requested mode and the attributes; if a validator fails no second open is made. If the handle is invalid it prints 'mq_open(create)' with warnc using errno as it is at that point (which the validators may have changed) and returns that errno. On FreeBSD builds only (__FreeBSD__): it obtains the descriptor with mq_getfd_np and does fstat (failure: warnc, mq_close, return the errno); if a user or group was given it applies fchown with the unset one taken from the stat result (for new and existing queues; failure: warnc, mq_close, return errno); and for an existing queue with set_mode set whose mode bits differ from the requested ones it applies fchmod (failure: warnc, mq_close, return errno). On other platforms those ownership and mode steps are compiled out. Finally it returns the value of mq_close(handle), which is 0 on success and -1 (not an errno value) if mq_close fails. It allocates nothing that it returns to the caller.

functions.name: inln
functions.prose_contract: Reads one input line (or one buffer-full of it) from inf into buf (usr.bin/pr/pr.c:1012-1104; slice cut the head). It reads characters with getc while a limit counter lim (decremented before each read) stays non-negative. When the global ingap (tab expansion width) is non-zero and the character equals inchar, the tab is replaced by spaces up to the next tab stop computed from the column *cps + characters already stored; if the expansion would not fit (col > lim) it first tries ungetc of the tab, and if ungetc fails it returns 1 immediately (that tab is consumed, *cps and *mor are not updated).
