If ungetc succeeds the function still writes spaces until lim is used up and then finishes as a too-long line, so the tab is read again by the next call. A newline ends the line without being stored. After the loop: if the last character read was EOF it sets *mor = 0 and *cps = 0 and returns -1 when nothing was stored, else the stored count; if it was a newline it sets *mor = 0, *cps = 0 and returns the count; otherwise (limit reached) with trnc set it reads and discards characters through the next newline or EOF and sets *cps = 0, *mor = 0, and with trnc zero it adds the count to *cps and sets *mor = 1. It returns the number of characters stored. With lim <= 0 the loop does not read at all (ch starts as EOF), so it returns -1 with *mor = *cps = 0, as if at EOF, without consuming input. Characters read are consumed except a tab pushed back by ungetc.

functions.name: setup
functions.prose_contract: Real name setup (static, usr.bin/pr/pr.c:1589-1849; the slice is only its tail). It parses pr's options and sets the global layout variables, returning 1 on failure and 0 on success. If stdout is a tty it tries to defer diagnostics into a tmpfile() stream stored in err; if tmpfile fails it sets err to stderr, prints 'Cannot defer diagnostic messages' to stderr and returns 1; otherwise err is stderr. egetopt then handles the page number (+), columns (-#, a value below 1 returns 1), -a, -d, -e, -F, -f, -h, -i, -L, -l, -m, -n, -o, -p, -r, -s, -t, -w and an unknown option (return 1); most invalid values print a message to err and return 1, and the unknown-option case returns 1 without a message. After options it defaults the column count (taking it from the number of operands with -m, or CLCNT), rejects -a with a single column and -a with -m, sets the default page width, defaults the tab characters and gaps when -m or multiple columns are used, rejects -m with multiple columns, computes the column width and page width (a column width below 1 prints 'page width is too small' and returns 1), and defaults lines to LINES. If lines <= HEADLEN + TAILLEN it increments nohead, else if nohead is zero it subtracts the header and trailer length from lines. For double spacing, lines == 1 clears dspace; otherwise addone is incremented when lines is odd and lines is halved. It sets the LC_TIME locale from -L or the environment, sets d_first from the locale's day/month order and sets timefrmt to a strdup of the day-first or month-first format (the strdup result is not checked) and returns 0.

functions.name: mulmod
functions.prose_contract: Static helper (usr.bin/primes/spsp.c:33-52) computing a * b mod n for unsigned 64-bit a, b and n with n > 0, using binary double-and-add so the product is never formed in a wider type. It starts with x = 0 and an = a % n, and loops while b is non-zero: if the low bit of b is set it adds an to x, subtracting n if the sum wrapped around or reached n (so x stays below n); it then doubles an modulo n (using wraparound-aware subtraction when an + an overflows 64 bits or is >= n) and shifts b right. It returns x, which is in [0, n-1] and equals the product of a and b reduced modulo n computed on the unsigned values. n == 0 is not allowed (a % n would divide by zero). It reads no globals and writes no memory.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Entry point of renice (usr.bin/renice/renice.c:55-123; slice cut the head). It walks the arguments in order. Before a '--' delimiter, the arguments -g, -u and -p change the target kind (process group, user, process) and -- sets the delimiter; these can appear at any position before the delimiter, including between targets and after the priority. '-n' (once, only before the priority, and needing a following argument, else usage(), which exits 1) marks the priority as an increment and then the next argument is read as the priority. The first other argument is the priority, parsed with getnum; a priority that is not an integer or is out of range prints a message and makes main return 1 immediately (exit status 1, remaining arguments unprocessed). Each later argument is a target: for -u it is looked up with getpwnam and otherwise parsed as a numeric uid; for the other kinds it is parsed as a number; a parse failure or a negative value prints a message, increments errs and skips donice. For each valid target it calls donice, which reads the current priority with getpriority, applies the increment if requested, clamps to PRIO_MIN..PRIO_MAX, calls setpriority and prints old and new priority to stderr; a getpriority or setpriority failure warns and counts as an error. When all arguments are consumed, if no priority was given it calls usage() (exit 1); otherwise it calls exit(errs != 0), so status 0 only when no target errored and status 1 otherwise. A bad priority also yields status 1.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Entry point of rpcinfo (usr.bin/rpcinfo/rpcinfo.c:152-301; slice cut the head). It parses options with getopt: each function-selecting option (-p portmap dump, -t tcp ping, -u udp ping, -a address ping (sets address), -b broadcast, -d delete, -l rpcb address list, -m rpcb statistics, -s short rpcb dump) sets function only if none was chosen yet (a second one sets errflg), -T sets netid, and with PORTMAP -n parses a port number (errx(1) if it is not a number); an unknown option sets errflg. If errflg is set, or -a was used without a netid, it calls usage(). If no function was chosen it defaults to PROGPING when more than one operand remains and otherwise to RPCBDUMP. It then calls the matching routine with the remaining operands (-p with a port number also calls usage()), and returns 0. The routines it calls (pmapdump, ip_ping, brdcst, deletereg, addrping, progping, rpcbdump, rpcbgetstat, rpcbaddrlist) were not read and can themselves exit, so a 0 return is the only normal return of main.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Entry point of sdiff (usr.bin/sdiff/sdiff.c:208-470; slice cut the head). It allocates diffargv and the single-character flag string (err(2) on failure), parses options (-w/-W width via strtonum, -t, -l, -s, -I, -o, -v help which prints the help text and calls exit(0), tabsize via strtonum, diff program name, ...), calling errx(2) for invalid widths or tab sizes and usage() for unknown options. If no single-letter diff flags were used it removes the placeholder argument and frees flagv. It requires exactly two operands (otherwise usage()), opens the output file if -o was given (err(2) on failure), and, when an operand is not a regular file or both names are equal, copies it into a temporary file through mktmpcpy and uses that name instead. It opens both files (err(2) on failure) and, if either is not a text file, returns the result of bindiff (0 if identical, 1 after printing 'Binary files ... differ', 2 on a read error) after the cleanup at done. For text files it sets up a pipe and forks diff (pipe failure is err(2), fork failure is err(1), in the child a dup2 or exec failure ends with _exit(2)), reads the diff output through parsecmd until EOF, closes the pipe, waits for the child and calls errx(2, "diff exited abnormally") if waitpid fails, the child did not exit normally or its status is 2 or more; otherwise ret is diff's exit status (0 or 1). It then enqueues the remaining common lines, closes both inputs and calls processq(). At done it unlinks and frees any temporary copies (warning if unlink fails), frees diffargv and, when single-letter flags were used, flagv, and returns ret (0, 1 or 2 as above). The width check errx(2, "width is too large") and other errors exit rather than return.

functions.name: monthcoll
functions.prose_contract: Real name monthcoll (static, usr.bin/sort/coll.c:1272-1318; mislabelled monthcmp in the packet). Comparison function for month sort (-M) of two key_value entries. With debug_sort set it prints both keys. For each entry whose hint status is HS_UNINITIALIZED it stores bws_month_score(key) in hint->v.Mh.m and sets the status to HS_INITIALIZED, remembering that the key was read. For each entry whose hint is HS_INITIALIZED (including one just initialised) it takes the score from hint->v.Mh.m; for an entry whose status is neither value it computes bws_month_score(key) directly without storing it. It then returns 0 if the two scores are equal, -1 if the first is smaller and +1 otherwise. The offset parameter is unused. Side effects are limited to the hint writes (and debug output); an already initialised hint is left unchanged.

functions.name: split1
functions.prose_contract: Splits the input descriptor ifd into output files of bytecnt bytes each (usr.bin/split/split.c:210-266). It does not return: it loops on read(ifd, bfr, sizeof bfr) and ends the process with exit(0) when read returns 0, or err(EX_IOERR, "read") when read returns a negative value; every short or failed write also calls err(EX_IOERR, "write"). Per chunk read: if no output file is open (file_open is 0) and chunks is 0 or the local count nfiles (a local counter, starting at 0) is below chunks, it calls newfile() and increments nfiles. If the data would complete the current file (bcnt + len >= bytecnt) it writes the bytes needed to fill it, then writes each further whole bytecnt-sized block, calling newfile() before each when chunks is 0 or nfiles < chunks (otherwise the block is written to the current output file), then writes any remaining partial block, again after newfile() when allowed, or sets file_open to 0 when the remainder is exactly zero, and sets bcnt to the remainder. Otherwise it writes the whole read to the current file and adds len to bcnt. Once chunks files have been created no more are opened and further data is appended to the last output file (ofd). The globals bytecnt, chunks, ifd, ofd and file_open are used; newfile() was not read in full (it closes the previous file and opens the next name, exiting on error).

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Entry point of su (usr.bin/su/su.c:136-546; slice cut the head). Options: -f, -l, -m, -s, -c class; any other option calls usage(). The target user defaults to "root" (so a missing user argument is not a usage error) and is argv[optind] when present; the 'user == NULL' usage() test cannot trigger. It errx(1)s if the effective uid is not 0 ('not running setuid'), if the user name is longer than MAXLOGNAME - 1, on malloc failure for the new argument vector, if the invoking user cannot be determined ('who are you?'), and on strdup failure (err). It runs PAM for the target: pam_start (failure: syslog and errx(1)), sets PAM_RUSER and PAM_TTY, pam_authenticate (failure: syslog 'BAD SU' and errx(1, "Sorry")), re-reads the user from PAM, looks it up with getpwnam (errx(1, "unknown login") if absent), and pam_acct_mgmt (an expired token leads to pam_chauthtok; any other failure is errx(1, "Sorry")). It selects the login class (-c only for a real uid of 0, unknown class errx(1)), checks the shell for -m when not root, chooses the shell and csh-ness, restores the priority, calls setusercontext for the group (err(1) on failure), pam_setcred (errx(1) on failure) and, for -l, pam_open_session (errx(1) on failure). It then ignores SIGINT/SIGQUIT/SIGPIPE, creates a pipe (err(1) on failure) and forks (err(1) after PAM_END on failure). The parent waits for the child (handling stop/continue), then calls PAM_END and exit(WEXITSTATUS(status)), with err(1) if waitpid fails. The child waits for the parent via the pipe, restores signals, calls setusercontext for the rest (err(1) on failure), builds the environment (for -l it replaces the environment and chdirs to the home directory, errx(1, "no directory") if that fails), logs the su to syslog for a non-root caller, and execv's the shell; if execv returns it calls err(1). Main does not return.

functions.name: cmdiolat
functions.prose_contract: Handles a systat command for the iolat display (usr.bin/systat/iolat.c:328-350; args is unused). It prints "CMD IS '<cmd>'" to stderr, then tests cmd with prefix(s1, s2), which is true when s1 is a prefix of s2 (cmds.c:183-192). cmd is tested as a prefix of "trim", "read", "write" and "color" in that order (so any abbreviation, including the empty string, matches the first of these it prefixes, i.e. "trim"): the matching one toggles flags by XOR with OP_TRIM_MASK, OP_READ_MASK or OP_WRITE_MASK, or inverts docolor. Otherwise, if "high" is a prefix of cmd (cmd begins with "high") it calls doublecmd(cmd, &high_thresh), and if "med" is a prefix of cmd it calls doublecmd(cmd, &med_thresh). doublecmd (306-322) overwrites the threshold only when cmd contains '=' followed by text sscanf can read as a double; otherwise it leaves the threshold unchanged without a message. If one of these branches was taken (including a high/med command whose value was missing or malformed) it clears the window, calls labeliolat() and refresh() and returns 1. If nothing matched it returns 0 without changing state.

functions.name: keyboard_dispatch
functions.prose_contract: Processes one character typed on the systat command line (usr.bin/systat/keyboard.c:116-176) using the globals col (cursor position in the line buffer) and line. If ch == ERR it returns 0 when errno == EINTR and otherwise calls exit(1). A letter A-Z is lowercased. If col == 0: CTRL-L redraws the screen (wrefresh(curscr)) and returns 0, CTRL-G calls status() and returns 0, any character other than ':' returns 0, and ':' clears the command line and continues. Then, in order: if ch == erasechar() and col > 0, it returns 0 with no change when col == 1 and line[0] == ':', else decrements col, clears from col to the end of the line and returns 0. If ch == CTRL-W and col > 0 (tested before the kill character, so it applies even when killchar() is CTRL-W), it moves col back over trailing blanks and then over the preceding word; if that scan reaches index 0 while line[0] == ':' it returns 1 immediately with col at 0 and the screen unchanged, otherwise it clears from the new col and returns 0. If ch == killchar() and col > 0 it sets col to 0 (or 1 if line[0] == ':'), clears the rest of the line and returns 0. A printable character or space is stored at line[col] (no bounds check here) and echoed, and col is incremented. Finally it returns 0 if col == 0 or ch is not CR or LF, and returns 1 for CR or LF when col > 0 (the character itself is not stored). The caller treats a return of 1 as 'command complete' and runs the command in line + 1.

functions.name: cmdmode
functions.prose_contract: Handles the 'mode' and 'reset' commands (usr.bin/systat/mode.c:62-95). prefix(s1, s2) is true when s1 is a prefix of s2, so cmd matches when cmd is an abbreviation of "mode" (including the empty string) and args matches a mode when args is an abbreviation of "rate", "delta", "since" or "absolute". If cmd is a prefix of "mode": with empty args it moves to the command line, clears it and prints the current mode name; otherwise it sets currentmode to display_RATE, display_DELTA, display_SINCE or display_ABS for the first of those words that args is a prefix of, or, if none matches, prints "unknown mode `<args>'" with printw and leaves currentmode unchanged; in all these cases it returns 1. Else if cmd is a prefix of "reset" it calls curcmd->c_reset() (curcmd must be valid and have a non-NULL c_reset, no check is made) and returns 1; currentmode is not changed. Otherwise it returns 0.

functions.name: cmdkre
functions.prose_contract: Handles systat vmstat commands (usr.bin/systat/vmstat.c:530-591). Each test uses prefix(cmd, word), true when cmd is a prefix of the word (so abbreviations, including the empty string, match the first word tried, "run"). 'run': copies s2 into s1 (copyinfo(&s2, &s1)), calls devstat_getdevs; on a -1 result it calls errx(1, devstat_errbuf) and ends the process; on a result of 1 it updates num_devices and generation from run_dev and sets retval to dscmd("refresh", NULL, MAXDRIVES, &cur_dev), calling labelkre() if that is 2; on other results (no change) retval stays 1; then it sets state = RUN and returns retval. 'boot': sets state = BOOT, copies z into s1 and returns 1. 'time': sets state = TIME and returns 1. 'zero': retval is 1; only if state == RUN it re-reads s1 with getinfo and repeats the same devstat_getdevs/refresh sequence (errx(1) on -1, dscmd status and labelkre() when 2 on a result of 1); the state is not changed; it returns retval (1 unless the refresh branch ran). Any other command returns the result of dscmd(cmd, args, MAXDRIVES, &cur_dev), after calling labelkre() when that result is 2. The case labels for the devstat_getdevs results were read from the structure only.

functions.name: follow
functions.prose_contract: Implements 'tail -f/-F' (usr.bin/tail/forward.c:305-433). First, for each entry in files whose fp is non-NULL it marks active, prints the file name header when -v is set (or when more than one file is given and -q is not), and calls forward() to print the initial tail. If -F is not set and no file is active it returns immediately; this is the only return. Otherwise it sets last to the final entry, creates a kqueue (err(1) on failure), mallocs the kevent array (err(1) on failure) and calls set_events, which registers read (and, for -F, delete/rename) events on each open file, and which switches action to USE_SLEEP instead of failing when a file is on a non-local filesystem or when its kevent registration call fails. Then it loops forever: with -F it reopens files whose fp is NULL and checks the others (a file that cannot be reopened or stat'ed is shown, closed and counted as a change; a different inode/device or zero link count means the old file is shown to its end, closed and replaced by the new one), then it calls show() on every open file (a read error closes it and counts as a change), re-runs set_events when anything changed, and waits: in kqueue mode kevent() is called with a one-second timeout when -F is set (without a timeout otherwise), retried while it fails with EINTR and err(1) on other errors, with an lseek to the end if a read event reports negative data (a seek failure reports an error and continues); in sleep mode it usleeps 250000 microseconds. It never exits the loop normally; forward() (read in part) can itself call exit(1).

functions.name: cour_dialer
functions.prose_contract: Dials a number on a Telebit Courier modem (usr.bin/tip/libacu/courier.c:59-113; num and acu are strings, the modem descriptor is the global FD). It sets HUPCL on the tty, then calls coursync(); if that fails it prints 'can't synchronize with courier' (and logs it when ACULOG is defined) and returns 0. It writes "AT E0\r", sleeps one second, flushes the tty and writes the configuration string; if cour_swallow("\r\nOK\r\n") fails (a mismatching reply or a timeout, in which case dialtimeout may be set by the alarm handler) it goes to the same 'can't synchronize' path and returns 0 without calling cour_disconnect. Otherwise it writes "AT D", replaces every '=' in num with ',' in place (modifying the caller's string), writes num and a carriage return, and sets connected = cour_connect(). If dialtimeout is then non-zero (a timeout during the connect wait) it logs it when ACULOG is defined and calls cour_disconnect(), which pulses DTR, resets the modem and closes FD. It returns connected: 1 only when cour_connect returned 1, and 0 when it returned 0 for any reason (timeout, read error, non-CONNECT line, CONNECT with an unknown baud suffix, overlong line).

functions.name: cour_connect
functions.prose_contract: Waits for the modem's connect result after dialing (static, usr.bin/tip/libacu/courier.c:188-255). It first calls cour_swallow("\r\n"); if that fails it returns 0 at once (without printing; the SIGALRM handler is whatever cour_swallow left, which is SIG_DFL after a mismatch and the previous handler after a timeout). Otherwise it installs the cour_connect SIGALRM handler and, at label again, clears the 64-byte line buffer and dialtimeout and reads up to 63 characters, one per read(), each with an alarm of DIALTIMEOUT seconds. A timeout (handler longjmp), a read returning <= 0, or filling the buffer ends the loop. A '\r' ends the line: it calls cour_swallow("\n") (break if that fails); an empty line goes back to again; a line equal to "RINGING" goes back to again when VERBOSE is set (otherwise it is treated as a non-CONNECT line and ends the loop); a line not starting with CONNECT ends the loop; for a line starting with CONNECT it compares the rest with the baud table ("", " 1200", " 2400", " 9600", " 9600/ARQ") and on a match sets the tty input and output speed to that baud rate, restores the previous SIGALRM handler and returns 1. After a loop exit other than that match (including an unknown suffix) it prints the accumulated dialer_buf line, restores the previous SIGALRM handler and returns 0.

functions.name: df_dialer
functions.prose_contract: Static dialer shared by df02 and df03 modems (usr.bin/tip/libacu/df.c:58-108; the descriptor is the global FD, acu is unused, df03 selects the df03 variant). It sets HUPCL on the tty (TCSANOW). It arms a setjmp point: if the alarm handler later does longjmp, the function prints 'connection timed out', calls df_disconnect() and returns 0 without restoring any terminal speed. Where TIOCMSET is defined and df03 is non-zero, it reads the output speed, and if it is not B1200 sets input and output speed to B1200 (TCSAFLUSH) and clears the ST modem line, else sets the ST line. It then installs alrm_timeout for SIGALRM, arms alarm(5 * strlen(num) + 10), flushes the tty, writes byte 1, sleeps one second, writes byte 2, writes num, and reads one byte c (read result not checked, c is '\0' if nothing was read). Where TIOCMSET is defined, with df03 and a saved speed other than B1200, it restores the saved speed on input and output. It returns 1 if c == 'A', else 0. The alarm is not cancelled and the SIGALRM handler stays installed on return. When TIOCMSET is not defined the speed handling is compiled out.

functions.name: hay_sync
functions.prose_contract: Tries to synchronise with a Hayes modem on the global descriptor FD (static, usr.bin/tip/libacu/hayes.c:288-312). It loops with retry++ <= MAXRETRY, i.e. at most MAXRETRY+1 attempts. Each attempt writes "AT\r", sleeps one second, asks FIONREAD how many bytes are waiting (the ioctl result is not checked, so len is uninitialised if it fails), and, if len is non-zero, reads min(len, DUMBUFLEN) bytes into the global dumbuf (the read result is stored in len and not checked, and no terminating NUL is added). If strchr finds '0' in dumbuf, or finds both 'O' and 'K', it returns 1 at once. With DEBUG defined it then stores a NUL at dumbuf[len] (out of range if len == DUMBUFLEN or -1) and prints the buffer. At the end of every attempt that did not return (including the last) it clears and sets DTR with TIOCCDTR and TIOCSDTR. If no attempt succeeded it prints "Cannot synchronize with hayes..." and returns 0. The strchr scan relies on dumbuf being NUL-terminated, which is not guaranteed when a read fills it or when stale bytes remain; no memory is allocated or released.

functions.name: t3000_sync
functions.prose_contract: Tries to bring a Telebit T3000 modem on the global descriptor FD into sync (static, usr.bin/tip/libacu/t3000.c:276-319). It loops while already++ < MAXRETRY, so at most MAXRETRY iterations (none if MAXRETRY <= 0). Each iteration flushes the tty, writes "\rAT Z\r" with t3000_write (one byte at a time with 50 ms naps), zeroes the 40-byte local buf, sleeps two seconds and calls FIONREAD (result not checked), setting len to 1 if it is 0, so a read of up to sizeof(buf) bytes is always attempted; read's result is assigned to len and not checked. If strchr finds '0' in buf, or finds both 'O' and 'K', it returns 1 immediately, without executing the rest of the iteration. Otherwise it sleeps one second, writes "+++", sleeps, clears DTR (TIOCCDTR), sleeps and sets DTR (TIOCSDTR), then starts the next iteration. If the loop ends without success it writes a final "\rAT Z\r" and returns 0. The scan relies on buf being NUL-terminated, which holds only when fewer than 40 bytes were read, and with DEBUG defined buf[len] is written (out of range if len is 40 or -1). It leaves FD open and allocates nothing.

functions.name: con
functions.prose_contract: Makes the tip connection (usr.bin/tip/tip/acu.c:58-152; returns a string describing an error, or NOSTR for success; all returned strings are literals). If DU is false (a direct line) it writes CM to FD when CM is set, logs 'call completed' and returns NOSTR without touching conflag. Otherwise it installs acuabort for SIGINT and SIGQUIT and sets a setjmp point; if an interrupt arrives later it ignores both signals, prints and logs 'call aborted', and, when the static acu is not NOACU, turns VERBOSE off and calls disconnect(NOSTR) if conflag is true or the dialer's acu_abort otherwise, then returns "interrupt". It looks up the ACU type AT in acutable: if it is not found it returns "unknown ACU type" (the SIGINT/SIGQUIT handlers stay installed). With a PN not starting with '@' it splits the comma-separated numbers, skipping empty ones, and for each calls the dialer (*acu_dialer)(number, CU), assigning the result to conflag and stopping on a true result, else logging 'call failed' and counting the attempt in tried. With PN starting with '@' it opens the phone file PH (printing the file name and returning "can't open phone number file" if that fails), reads lines whose first field equals HOST, and tries each non-empty number the same way, closing the file afterwards. After the loop: if conflag is true it writes CM when set, logs 'call completed' and returns NOSTR; else if no number was tried it logs and returns "missing phone number"; else it calls acu_abort and returns "call failed". conflag is a global that is assigned only from dialer results, so it is not reset on entry: if it was already true from an earlier call and no number was dialled, the function can return NOSTR (using phnum which may then be uninitialised in the log call) instead of "missing phone number".

functions.name: transmit
functions.prose_contract: Sends the open file fp to the remote line (static, usr.bin/tip/tip/cmds.c:294-385). It signals the tipout process with SIGIOT, clears stop, installs stopsnd for SIGINT, sets the terminal to defchars and reads one byte from repdes[0] into ccc (a blocking read, result unchecked). If command is non-NULL it sends each of its characters, then with ECHOCHECK reads one byte back, else drains the line and sleeps five seconds. It then reads fp with getc, one logical line at a time: EOF or a stop request ends the transfer; a DEL (0177) is skipped unless RAWFTP; characters below space are filtered unless RAWFTP, with newline sent as carriage return (outside RAWFTP) and tabs optionally expanded to spaces (TABEXPAND, outside RAWFTP); lastc records the last accepted character. After each line, with VERBOSE it prints a line counter and with ECHOCHECK it arms alarm(ETIMEOUT) and waits for the PROMPT character, jumping to the end if the alarm sets timedout (printing 'timed out at eol') or a stop was requested. At the end (label out), if the last character recorded is not '\n' and RAWFTP is off (also when nothing was read) it sends a '\r', then it sends every character of eofchars when that is non-NULL, closes fp, restores the previous SIGINT handler, prints the transfer time with VERBOSE, writes the saved ccc byte to fildes[1] and restores the terminal settings (term). The routine returns nothing and does not report errors from send/read/write.

functions.name: variable
functions.prose_contract: Implements the tip ~s (set) command (usr.bin/tip/tip/cmds.c:744-796; c is unused). It calls prompt("[set] ", buf, 256); if that returns non-zero (interrupted or failed) it returns at once, before vlex and without touching any CHANGED flag. Otherwise vlex(buf) parses and assigns the variables, and then it checks a fixed list of vtable entries in this order, each tested by its CHANGED bit: BEAUTIFY (clear flag, kill(tipout_pid, SIGSYS)); SCRIPT (clear flag, setscript(), and if RECORD's CHANGED bit is also set, clear that bit without calling any RECORD action); RECORD (if still changed: clear flag and call setscript() only when SCRIPT is true); TAND (clear, tandem on or off by the variable); LECHO (clear, HD = the variable); PARITY (clear, setparity(NOSTR)); HARDWAREFLOW (clear, hardwareflow on or off); LINEDISC (clear, linedisc(NOSTR)). CHANGED bits of variables not in this list are left set. It returns nothing.

functions.name: vassign
functions.prose_contract: Static helper that assigns a new value to a tip variable (usr.bin/tip/tip/value.c:113-148). If vaccess(p->v_access, WRITE) fails it prints 'access denied' and returns with the entry unchanged. Otherwise it switches on the variable type. STRING: if the current value exists and equals v it returns unchanged; otherwise it frees the old value unless the entry is flagged ENVIRON or INIT, then stores strdup(v); if strdup fails it prints 'out of core' and returns with p->v_value NULL (the old value is already freed) and CHANGED not set, else it clears the ENVIRON and INIT type flags. NUMBER: v is not a string here but an integer cast to char * (the callers at lines 185 and 348 pass (char *)(intptr_t)atoi(...)); if number(v) equals the stored number it returns unchanged, else the number is stored. BOOL: the new boolean is (*v != '!') (v is a string); an equal value returns unchanged, else it is stored. CHAR: the new value is *v; an equal value returns unchanged, else it is stored. After a successful change of any type it sets CHANGED in p->v_access. Every unchanged or error return leaves CHANGED as it was.

functions.name: next
functions.prose_contract: Produces the next character of a tr string expansion (usr.bin/tr/str.c:55-130). It switches on s->state. EOS: returns 0. INFINITE: returns 1 without changing s->lastch, s->str, s->cnt or s->state (the caller keeps using lastch). NORMAL: looks at *s->str: a NUL byte sets state = EOS and returns 0; a backslash stores backslash(s, &is_octal) in s->lastch; a '[' tries bracket(s) (for [:class:], [=equiv=] or [c*n] forms) and, if it consumed a construct, returns next(s) recursively, otherwise (and for any other character) it decodes one multibyte character with mbrtowc into s->lastch and advances s->str (an invalid, incomplete or zero-length sequence calls errc(1, EILSEQ)); afterwards, if the following character is '-' and genrange succeeds the range state is set up and next(s) is returned recursively, else it returns 1. RANGE and SEQUENCE: when the repeat count is exhausted (cnt-- == 0) the state returns to NORMAL and next(s) is returned, otherwise RANGE increments s->lastch (SEQUENCE leaves it) and both return 1. CCLASS, CCLASS_UPPER and CCLASS_LOWER: increment cnt, take the next character of the class with nextwctype(lastch, cclass); if none (-1) the state returns to NORMAL and next(s) is returned, else lastch is set and 1 is returned. SET: takes the next entry of s->set at s->cnt++; OOBCH ends the set (state NORMAL, recursive next), else lastch is set and 1 is returned. Any other state value returns 0. The helpers genclass (errx(1) on an unknown class), genequiv, genrange (may malloc and err(1) on failure) and genseq (errx(1) in string1) can end the process, so it does not always return.

functions.name: tsort
functions.prose_contract: Topologically sorts the global graph and prints node names (usr.bin/tsort/tsort.c:289-348; remove_node prints each name followed by a newline). While graph is non-NULL it repeatedly removes every node whose n_refcnt is 0 (remove_node prints the name, decrements the refcount of each successor and detaches the node), repeating until a pass removes nothing or the graph is empty; if the graph is empty it stops. Otherwise a cycle exists: the first time it counts the nodes and mallocs cycle_buf and longest_cycle of that many pointers (err(1, NULL) if either allocation fails). For each remaining node not flagged NF_ACYCLIC it calls find_cycle(n, n, 0, 0); a non-zero length means a cycle through n: unless quiet is set it prints 'cycle in data' and the node names of the longest cycle with warnx, and in all cases it removes n (printing its name) and clears the cycle marks and restarts the main loop; a zero length marks n NF_ACYCLIC. If the scan ends without finding any cycle (n == NULL) it calls errx(1, "internal error -- could not find cycle"). The function returns only when the graph has become empty, with all names printed once; cycles do not terminate it. remove_node's list unlinking (lines 361-365) and clear_cycle were not read in full.

functions.name: cnt
functions.prose_contract: Counts one input for wc (static, usr.bin/wc/wc.c:202-351; slice cut the head). With file == NULL it uses descriptor 0 and the name stdin_filename; otherwise fileargs_open, and on failure it warns '<file>: open' via xo_warn and returns 1 (nothing to close). If words are wanted or multibyte counting is on in a multibyte locale it goes to the 'word' loop. Otherwise, when neither lines nor longest line are wanted it fstat's the descriptor (warn, close and return 1 on failure) and, for a regular file with st_size > 0, does not read it: it takes the character count from st_size, prints it with show_cnt, adds it to tcharct (unconditionally), closes the descriptor and returns 0. Otherwise (unstattable or empty/special file, or lines wanted) it reads the descriptor to EOF in blocks, counting characters and, if lines or longest line are wanted, newlines and the longest line; a read error warns '<file>: read', closes the descriptor and returns 1 with the running totals not yet updated; show_cnt is called during reading when siginfo is set. The 'word' loop reads to EOF, decoding multibyte characters with mbrtowc when applicable (an invalid sequence warns once per file via xo_warn with EILSEQ, resets the shift state and counts the byte as a character; an incomplete sequence at the end of a block breaks out of the inner loop), counting characters, lines, words (transitions from space to non-space using iswspace) and the longest line; a read error warns, closes and returns 1. On normal completion it adds to the totals (tlinect when doline, twordct when doword (word path), tcharct when dochar (non-word path) or dochar/domulti (word path), tlongline when larger), calls show_cnt, closes the descriptor (even if it is standard input) and returns 0. At the end of the word loop it can also warn once if a trailing incomplete multibyte sequence is found and no warning was given.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Entry point of install(1) (usr.bin/xinstall/xinstall.c:163-419; slice cut the head). It parses options with getopt: -m uses setmode (errx(EX_USAGE) on an invalid mode), -l parses the link-type letters (errx(1) on an invalid letter), -N calls setup_getid (err(EX_OSERR) on failure), -U sets dounpriv, and an unknown option calls usage(). It then rejects -s together with -d or -l (usage()), frees the parsed mode set, honours DONTSTRIP, and calls usage() if no operands remain or only one is given without -d. It maps the -h digest name to a digest type (none, md5, rmd160, sha1, sha256, sha512; an unknown name warns and calls usage()). Unless dounpriv is set it resolves the group, owner and file flags: an unknown group or user that is not numeric calls errx(1), and an invalid flag string calls errx(EX_USAGE); with -U these three are skipped, so errors there cannot occur. If a metafile is named it opens it for append (a failure only produces a warning via warn), else digests are disabled. With -d it calls install_dir for each operand and exit(EX_OK). Otherwise the last operand is the target: if it exists as a directory then, with a symbolic link requested (-l s), it lstat's it (err(EX_OSERR) if that fails); if it is itself a symlink then argc must be 2 (otherwise errc(EX_CANTCREAT, ENOTDIR)) and the single source is installed over the symlink itself; in the other cases every operand but the last is installed into the directory (install() with the DIRECTORY flag) and it exits EX_OK. Otherwise exactly two operands are required (else a warning and usage()); when the target exists and no link is requested it stat's the source (err(EX_OSERR) on failure), requires the target to be a regular file (errc(EX_CANTCREAT, EFTYPE)) and rejects the same device and inode (errx(EX_USAGE)); finally it installs the file and calls exit(EX_OK). The function does not return. install(), install_dir and the digest code were not read here.

functions.name: ac
functions.prose_contract: Reads the wtmp log named by file and accumulates connect time (usr.sbin/ac/ac.c:403-507). It opens the log itself with setutxdb(UTXDB_LOG, file), calling err(1, "%s", file) if that fails, and reads records with getutxent until NULL, then endutxent. For each record it copies usr->ut_tv into a local ut_timecopy and raises it to prev_secs if it is earlier (so ut_timecopy never goes backwards), updates prev_secs, and records the first time seen in FirstTime. With AC_D, when the local day-of-year changes it calls show_today with midnight of the new day. By record type: OLD_TIME stores clock_shift = ut_timecopy; NEW_TIME subtracts ut_timecopy from clock_shift (timersub) and shifts every current user's login time by clock_shift; BOOT_TIME and SHUTDOWN_TIME call log_out(usr) and set FirstTime = ut_timecopy; USER_PROCESS calls log_in(usr) unless the line is a pts/ line with an empty host; DEAD_PROCESS calls log_out(usr). log_in and log_out take the record itself, so they use the record's own, unclamped usr->ut_tv rather than ut_timecopy. After the loop it builds a fake SHUTDOWN_TIME record whose time is ut_timecopy with AC_W or the current time otherwise, prints the last day's total under AC_D when the day changed, and calls log_out on it to close all remaining sessions. Finally, with AC_D it calls show_today(now); otherwise it prints the per-user list when AC_P is set and then always calls show("total", Total) (the grand total is not printed under AC_D). It returns nothing. If the log has no records, ut_timecopy is used uninitialised in the AC_W and AC_D paths.

functions.name: audio_record
functions.prose_contract: Real name audio_record (usr.sbin/bhyve/audio.c:257-281; the packet name audio_read_full does not exist). It asserts that aud and buf are non-NULL, that aud->dir is false (a recording stream) and that aud->fd is not -1 (these assert calls disappear if NDEBUG is defined). It then calls read(fd, buf + total, count - total) in a loop until total reaches count. A read returning a negative value logs a debug message (which says 'write') and makes the function return -1 immediately, leaving a partial prefix in buf and errno from that read; a read returning 0 adds nothing to total, so the loop keeps calling read and never ends if the descriptor stays at end of file. When count is 0 no read is made. It returns 0 once exactly count bytes have been read. It allocates nothing and keeps no references to aud or buf.

functions.name: blockif_open
functions.prose_contract: Opens a block backing file described by the nvlist nvl and returns a new context, or NULL (usr.sbin/bhyve/block_if.c:476-677; slice cut the head). It runs blockif_init once, reads the booleans nocache (O_DIRECT), nodelete, sync/direct (O_SYNC) and ro, an optional 'sectorsize' ('N' or 'N/M' via strtol; a bad string goes to err), and an optional 'bootindex' (atoi). A missing 'path' goes to err. It opens the file read-write (or read-only with ro), and if the read-write open fails retries read-only and sets ro; an open failure (warn) or fstat failure goes to err. With Capsicum it limits the descriptor rights (rights failure: errx(EX_OSERR)). For a character device it fetches the media size and sector size with ioctl (failure: perror and err), asserts both are non-zero, and reads the optional stripe size and offset, the GEOM candelete attribute (unless nodelete) and the provider name with ioctls whose failures are ignored; for other files the physical sector size is st_blksize and candelete comes from fpathconf. With Capsicum it limits the ioctl set (failure: errx(EX_OSERR)). If a sector size was given it must be a power of two with 512 <= ssopt <= pssopt and pssopt a power of two (else err), and for a character device ssopt must be at least the device sector size and a multiple of it (else err); the given sizes then replace the detected ones. It callocs a blockif_ctxt (perror and err on failure), fills in the fields (magic BLOCKIF_SIG, fd, ischr, isgeom, candelete, rdonly, size, sector sizes, bootindex), initialises its mutex and condition variables and the three request queues with all BLOCKIF_MAXREQ requests on the free queue, creates BLOCKIF_NUMTHR worker threads named blk-<ident>-<i> (pthread_create results are not checked), and returns the context. On every err path it closes the descriptor if one was opened and returns NULL. The returned context owns the descriptor and must be released with blockif_close.

functions.name: mevent_add_state
functions.prose_contract: Registers an event with the bhyve mevent loop (usr.sbin/bhyve/mevent.c:283-356). If tfd < 0 or func is NULL it returns NULL immediately, before running mevent_init (via pthread_once) and before taking the queue lock. Otherwise it calls pthread_once(mevent_init), takes the queue lock and rejects (jumps to exit and returns NULL) a duplicate: for a type other than EVF_TIMER, an entry with the same me_fd and type already on global_head or change_head; timers are not checked for duplicates. It callocs a struct mevent (NULL on failure), stores for a timer me_msecs = tfd and a new me_timid, otherwise me_fd = tfd, and records type, func, param, state and fflags. It builds a kevent with mevent_populate and registers it synchronously with kevent(mfd, ...); on failure it frees the new struct and returns NULL. On success it clears EV_ADD from me_state (other bits such as EV_DISABLE are kept), inserts the entry at the head of global_head and returns it. The queue lock is held from after the first two returns to exit (released at exit on every path that took it).

functions.name: qemu_loader_finish
functions.prose_contract: Real name qemu_loader_finish (usr.sbin/bhyve/qemu_loader.c:245-274; the slice is its tail). It counts the entries in loader->list and sets len to that count times sizeof(struct qemu_loader_entry). If the list is empty (len == 0) it prints a warning and returns EFAULT without allocating anything. Otherwise it callocs len bytes; if that fails it prints a warning and returns ENOMEM. It then copies each list element's entry into the buffer in list order and returns the value of qemu_fwcfg_add_file(loader->fwcfg_name, len, data) (0 on success, otherwise that function's error code). The buffer is not freed in this function on any path, so after a successful registration it is owned by the fwcfg file table, and on an error return from qemu_fwcfg_add_file it is not freed here (qemu_fwcfg_add_file was read only at its first lines, where it returns EINVAL and ENOMEM without freeing data).

functions.name: rfb_send_screen
functions.prose_contract: Sends the changed parts of the framebuffer to the VNC client on cfd (usr.sbin/bhyve/rfb.c:691-871). It first tries to set rc->sending from false to true atomically; if another thread already holds it, it returns 1 without touching any state (the sending flag is not cleared by this call). Once it owns the flag, every later path leaves through done, which sets rc->sending = false and returns retval (initially 1). It atomically clears rc->pending and, if it was already false, goes to done with 1. If update_pixfmt was set it recomputes the pixel adjustment, refreshes the console and takes the console image, and resets the CRC cache when the image size changed. If the size differs from the client's size it stores the new size and, when enc_resize_ok is set, sends a resize message: a negative result makes it return -1, otherwise it sets update_all and returns 1. If update_all was set it clears it and returns the result of rfb_send_all. Otherwise it computes CRC32 per 32x32 cell and marks the cells that changed; if none changed it sets rc->pending back to true and returns 1; if the changed percentage is at least RFB_SEND_ALL_THRESH it returns rfb_send_all(...); else it writes an update header (a result <= 0 returns -1) and sends each changed cell with rfb_send_rect, returning nwrite as soon as one returns <= 0 (so 0 or a negative value, not necessarily -1), and returning 1 when all cells were sent. The values returned by rfb_send_all and rfb_send_rect (not read) are passed through.

functions.name: umouse_request
functions.prose_contract: Real name umouse_request (usr.sbin/bhyve/usb_mouse.c:325-690; the packet name umouse_request_handler does not exist). It first walks all xfer->ndata blocks in the ring starting at xfer->head, setting bdone = 0 and processed = 1 on every block and picking the first block for which USB_DATA_OK is true as data (and its buf as udata). If xfer->ureq is NULL it goes to done with USB_ERR_NORMAL_COMPLETION. Otherwise it decodes wValue, wIndex and wLength and switches on request and type: GET_CONFIG, GET_DESCRIPTOR (device, config, string, BOS; descriptors are copied into the data buffer and blen/bdone set, a nonzero low byte of the value for device/config, an unknown descriptor type or an out-of-range string index gives USB_ERR_STALLED; a string index out of range uses a bare goto done), GET_DESCRIPTOR for the interface (report descriptor only), GET_INTERFACE (index must be 0 else STALLED), GET_STATUS for device/interface/endpoint, the no-op writes SET_ADDRESS, SET_CONFIG, SET_DESCRIPTOR, SET_INTERFACE, ISOCH_DELAY, SET_SEL and SYNCH_FRAME, CLEAR_FEATURE/SET_FEATURE on the device (only UF_DEVICE_REMOTE_WAKEUP changes sc->hid.feature), the same two on an interface or endpoint (STALLED), and the HID class requests GET_REPORT (STALLED unless report type 1 and length large enough), GET_IDLE, GET_PROTOCOL, SET_REPORT (no-op), SET_IDLE and SET_PROTOCOL (store the upper byte of wValue in sc->hid.idle / sc->hid.protocol). Read requests without a data block break out with no data written. Any other request sets USB_ERR_STALLED. At done: for a write request that completed normally with a data block, data->blen is set to 0; otherwise, if a read reply left bytes unsent (eshort, i.e. blen > 0), the result becomes USB_ERR_SHORT_XFER. It returns the error code (normal completion, stalled or short transfer). No locks are taken.

functions.name: bhyvectl_opts
functions.prose_contract: Real name bhyvectl_opts (usr.sbin/bhyvectl/amd64/bhyvectl_machdep.c:1112-1333; the slice is its tail, and the packet called it an unnamed option-array builder). It builds the long-option table for getopt_long. It asks cpu_vendor_intel() which vendor table applies, computes optlen as count * sizeof(struct option) plus the size of common_opts plus the size of intel_opts or amd_opts plus the size of the terminating null_opt (in an int, with no overflow check), and mallocs that many bytes, calling err(1, "malloc") if it fails. It then copies, in order, the caller's count options, common_opts, the Intel or AMD specific options and the null terminator entry into the new block, and returns the block. The caller owns the returned allocation. It does not modify its input array.

functions.name: kbd_process_keys
functions.prose_contract: Compares the keys in the current HID report (s->keys1) with the keys pressed before (s->keys2) and emits release and press events (usr.sbin/bluetooth/bthidd/kbd.c:339-413; s->vkbd and s->ukbd are file descriptors). It always returns 0. It finds the first set bit f1 of keys1 and f2 of keys2. If keys1 is empty: when keys2 is non-empty it writes release events (make = 0) for the keys in keys2 to vkbd and ukbd and clears keys2; return 0. If keys2 is empty (and keys1 is not): it copies keys1 into keys2, writes press events (make = 1) for the keys in keys1 and clears keys1; return 0. If both are non-empty: it builds a diff bitmap of keys that were in keys2 but are not in keys1 (clearing them from keys2), then, for each key in keys1, sets it in keys2 if it was not there (a new press, kept in keys1) or clears it from keys1 if it was already pressed. It writes release events for the diff keys when the first diff bit index is greater than 0, and press events for the remaining keys1 bits (and then clears keys1) when the first remaining bit index is greater than 0; a key with bit index 0 therefore produces no event in this branch, and keys1 is not cleared if only bit 0 remains. Afterwards keys2 holds exactly the currently pressed keys (it is not a union with the released ones, which were removed). Nothing is allocated; the diff bitmap is a local.

functions.name: bnep_recv_setup_connection_req
functions.prose_contract: Handles a BNEP setup-connection request (static, usr.sbin/bluetooth/btpand/bnep.c:303-375). It returns 0 (consuming nothing) if size < 1, or, after reading the length byte len, if size < len * 2 + 1. If the channel state is neither CHANNEL_WAIT_CONNECT_REQ nor CHANNEL_OPEN it logs 'ignored' and returns len * 2 + 1 without sending a response or changing the state. Otherwise len must be 2, 4 or 16 (else the response code is BNEP_SETUP_INVALID_UUID_SIZE); the destination UUID is compared with the NAP, GN and PANU UUIDs (offset 2 for 16-bit UUIDs) and its class must equal the global service_class, else the code is BNEP_SETUP_INVALID_DST_UUID. The source UUID is then compared with the same three UUIDs; the response is BNEP_SETUP_INVALID_SRC_UUID when the source matches none (src == 0) or when neither the destination nor the source is PANU (the source is not compared with service_class). If all checks pass the response is BNEP_SETUP_SUCCESS, the channel state becomes CHANNEL_OPEN and channel_timeout(chan, 0) is called. In every case after the state check (success or any error code) it sends a BNEP_SETUP_CONNECTION_RESPONSE control message with that code via bnep_send_control and returns len * 2 + 1. The state is changed only on success.

functions.name: __event_dispatch
functions.prose_contract: Runs one round of the btpand event loop (static, usr.sbin/bluetooth/btpand/event.c:85-209; returns 0 normally, -1 only when select fails). It clears the fd sets, initialises the global current queue (TAILQ_INIT, discarding anything left in it from an earlier round) and sets a default 10 second select timeout. It then drains the pending queue: each event is removed from pending with event_del, its timeout (time left until expire, zero if already expired) lowers the select timeout when smaller, its fd is added to the read and/or write sets according to EV_READ/EV_WRITE (when fd >= 0), and it is appended to current. It calls select; if select returns a negative value it returns -1 at that point, with the events still on the current queue and not on pending (they are not re-armed). Otherwise it processes the current queue in order, removing each event from it: if nfd > 0 (the remaining ready count) and the fd is ready in the read or write set, a persistent event is re-added with event_add (with its saved timeout if it had one), nfd is decremented once and the callback is called with the fd and its READ/WRITE flags; a non-persistent ready event is not re-added. If the event was not dispatched that way (not ready, or nfd had already reached 0): an event without a timeout is re-added with no timeout; an event whose timeout has expired is re-added first if persistent and then its callback is called (non-persistent ones are not re-added); an event whose timeout has not expired is re-linked into pending. Because nfd is decremented once per dispatched event, several events sharing a ready fd can exhaust the count so that some are not dispatched in this round. It then returns 0, and the current queue is empty after a successful round. Callbacks may add or delete events. The callers (event_dispatch) loop on a 0 result.

functions.name: hci_write_le_host_support
functions.prose_contract: Real name hci_write_le_host_support (static, usr.sbin/bluetooth/hccontrol/host_controller_baseband.c:1515-1562; hci_write_le_host_supported does not exist). It starts with both command fields zero. With argc == 2 it first parses argv[1] with sscanf("%d") as the simultaneous_le_host value, which must be 0 or 1, else it prints '-ARGC2: <n>' (n may be uninitialised if sscanf failed) and returns USAGE, then falls through to the argc == 1 case, which parses argv[0] as le_supported_host (0 or 1), printing '+ARGC1: <n>' and returning USAGE on a bad value. Any argc other than 1 or 2 returns USAGE without a message. It then sends the Write_LE_Host_Supported command with hci_request on socket s, returning ERROR if that fails; if the reply status is non-zero it prints 'Status: <text> [code]' to stdout and returns FAILED; otherwise it returns OK. No HCI command is sent on a USAGE return. The size returned in n is not checked against the reply buffer. It allocates nothing.

functions.name: server_prepare_service_search_attribute_response
functions.prose_contract: Real name server_prepare_service_search_attribute_response (usr.sbin/bluetooth/sdpd/ssar.c:177-379; the slice was an unnamed excerpt of it). It parses srv->req as a ServiceSearchAttribute request. It returns SDP_ERROR_CODE_INVALID_REQUEST_SYNTAX if the parameters are shorter than 13 bytes, if the ServiceSearchPattern sequence length is not positive (a first byte that is not a SEQ8/16/32 type counts as length 0), if the pattern runs past the request or the 2-byte MaximumAttributeByteCount is missing or is not positive, if the AttributeIDList header is missing or its length is not positive, or if the ContinuationState length byte is missing; a non-zero continuation length must be 2 and exactly 2 bytes must remain, otherwise the same error. A continuation length of 0 sets cs = 0 and any bytes after it are not rejected. If the request's continuation state differs from srv->fdidx[fd].rsp_cs it returns SDP_ERROR_CODE_INVALID_CONTINUATION_STATE; if a response is already pending (rsp_size > 0) it returns 0 without touching it. Otherwise, starting at rsp + 3, for each UUID in the search pattern (16-bit, 32-bit or 128-bit; a truncated or unknown UUID type returns INVALID_REQUEST_SYNTAX, leaving a partly built response in the buffer with rsp_size not set) it walks the providers whose address matches the requesting bdaddr and, for each provider whose profile UUID equals the search UUID, or which matches the public browse group, or in which server_search_uuid finds the UUID, appends the attribute list produced by server_prepare_attr_list (a negative result returns SDP_ERROR_CODE_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES). Then it sets rsp_limit to omtu - sizeof(sdp_pdu_t) - 2 lowered to the requested maximum, rsp_size to the number of bytes built, rsp_cs to 0, writes a SEQ16 header with length rsp_size - 3 at the start of the response and returns 0.

functions.name: child_leader_run
functions.prose_contract: Real name child_leader_run (usr.sbin/bsdinstall/runconsoles/child.c:220-386; the slice 263-386 is its tail). Runs in the forked console leader process and does not return (all exits are through exit/err). It sets the process title, acquires reaper status with procctl (err(EX_OSERR) on failure), installs handlers for SIGCHLD, SIGALRM, SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGQUIT (each failure is err(EX_OSERR)), unmasks signals with the saved oset, and creates the start-grandchild, wait-grandchild and wait-all-descendants barriers (err(EX_OSERR) on failure). If new_session is true it calls setsid (err(EX_OSERR) on failure), otherwise it puts itself in a new process group with setpgid (err(EX_OSERR) on failure). It then waits on the start-children barrier, dup2's the console fd onto stdin, stdout and stderr (err(EX_IOERR) naming the console on failure), makes the console its controlling terminal with tcsetsid or the foreground group with tcsetpgrp (err(EX_IOERR) on failure), blocks all signals and forks. A fork failure is err(EX_OSERR). In the child of that fork (the grandchild) it destroys the two wait barriers, waits on the start-grandchild barrier and calls grandchild_run, which does not return here. In the leader it records grandchild_pid, registers kill_wait_all_descendants_err_exit as the exit hook, restores the signal mask, signals the start-grandchild barrier and waits via wait_grandchild_descendants. If the grandchild was killed by a signal it re-raises that signal death via reproduce_signal_death; if it exited normally it calls exit with its status; otherwise exit(EXIT_FAILURE).

functions.name: op_begemot_stp
functions.prose_contract: Real name op_begemot_stp (usr.sbin/bsnmpd/modules/snmp_bridge/bridge_if.c:1190-1395; op_begemot_bridge_stp does not exist). SNMP handler for the bridge STP leaves, keyed by a bridge index. It first refreshes the bridge list with bridge_update_all_ifs() if the cached data is older than bridge_get_data_maxage(). GET and GETNEXT find the bridge row (SNMP_ERR_NOSUCHNAME when there is none; GETNEXT also appends the index) and then return the selected leaf: read-only fields from the bridge_if structure, with SNMP_ERR_GENERR if bridge_get_time_since_tc fails for the topology-change age, string_get's result for the designated root, and SNMP_ERR_NOERROR otherwise; an unknown leaf ends in abort(). SET finds the row (NOSUCHNAME if absent), then for the writable leaves (Priority, BridgeMaxAge, BridgeHelloTime, BridgeForwardDelay, Version, TxHoldCount) checks the range (Priority must be a multiple of 4096 and at most the maximum; Version must be STP-compatible or RSTP) and returns SNMP_ERR_WRONG_VALUE if it fails, else saves the old value in ctx->scratch->int1, calls the matching bridge_set_* function, and returns SNMP_ERR_GENERR if that returns a negative value or SNMP_ERR_NOERROR; the read-only leaves return SNMP_ERR_NOT_WRITEABLE, and any other leaf reaches abort(). ROLLBACK finds the row (NOSUCHNAME if absent) and calls the matching bridge_set_* with the saved scratch value (its result is ignored) and returns SNMP_ERR_NOERROR (for leaves not listed it does nothing). COMMIT returns SNMP_ERR_NOERROR. Any other operation value reaches abort().

functions.name: op_begemot_bridge_config
functions.prose_contract: SNMP handler for the three bridge configuration leaves (usr.sbin/bsnmpd/modules/snmp_bridge/bridge_snmp.c:164-247). GET: the default bridge interface leaf returns string_get's result for bridge_get_default_name(); DataUpdate stores bridge_data_maxage in val and DataPoll stores bridge_poll_ticks / 100, both returning SNMP_ERR_NOERROR; an unknown leaf reaches abort(). GETNEXT always reaches abort(). SET: DefaultBridgeIf first saves the current name into ctx->scratch (bridge_default_name_save: ptr1 gets a malloc'd IFNAMSIZ copy and int1 its length; failure returns SNMP_ERR_RES_UNAVAIL), then calls bridge_set_default_name with the new octets and returns SNMP_ERR_BADVALUE if that fails (the saved copy is then not freed here) or SNMP_ERR_NOERROR; DataUpdate returns SNMP_ERR_WRONG_VALUE if the value is outside the MIN/MAX data max-age range, else saves the old bridge_data_maxage in scratch int1, stores the new value and returns SNMP_ERR_NOERROR; DataPoll returns SNMP_ERR_WRONG_VALUE for an out-of-range interval, else stores the new value (not the old one) in scratch int1 and changes nothing else (the timer is applied at COMMIT); other leaves reach abort(). ROLLBACK: DefaultBridgeIf restores the default name from scratch and frees the copy, DataUpdate restores the saved max age, DataPoll does nothing; it returns SNMP_ERR_NOERROR in all cases. COMMIT: DefaultBridgeIf frees the saved copy, DataPoll calls bridge_set_poll_ticks(scratch int1 * 100) (which restarts the repeating update timer), DataUpdate does nothing; it returns SNMP_ERR_NOERROR. Any other op reaches abort().

functions.name: camdd_worker
functions.prose_contract: Thread body for one camdd device (usr.sbin/camdd/camdd.c:1676-1878; arg is the struct camdd_dev). It locks dev->mutex, sets CAMDD_DEV_FLAG_ACTIVE and loops. In each pass, for a reading device (write_dev == 0) it computes the queue depths and byte counts and calls camdd_queue(dev, NULL) while either the combined queue depths are below the combined target depths or the queued bytes (ours plus the peer's) are below three times the peer's block size; a return of 1 ends the queuing, any other nonzero return sets error_exit and goes to bailout. If the run queue is non-empty it calls dev->run while the target queue depth exceeds cur_active_io (-1 sets CAMDD_DEV_FLAG_EOF and error_exit and stops, another nonzero value just stops). If CAMDD_DEV_FLAG_EOF or PEER_EOF is set: a writer exits when its work queue is empty, num_run_queue is 0 and cur_active_io is 0; a reader exits immediately when PEER_EOF is set (without draining), else when EOF is set and the peer work and done queues, active I/O and run queue are all empty. Otherwise it waits in kevent (with the device mutex released) using a zero timeout for a reader with no active I/O and fewer queued peer bytes than the peer block size, and no timeout otherwise; a kevent error warns and goes to bailout; EVFILT_READ calls dev->fetch if set (-1 sets error_exit and exits), EVFILT_SIGNAL exits on SIGINT, EVFILT_USER feeds work_queue buffers to camdd_queue (-1 sets error_exit and exits) and passes peer_done_queue buffers to camdd_peer_done, and an unknown filter just warns. At bailout it clears CAMDD_DEV_FLAG_ACTIVE, unlocks the mutex, sets need_exit, posts camdd_sem and returns NULL; resources are not cleaned up here.

functions.name: camdd_file_run
functions.prose_contract: Runs one queued transfer on a file-type camdd device (usr.sbin/camdd/camdd.c:2384-2591; slice cut the head). The caller holds dev->mutex; the function releases it only around the actual I/O and the temporary double-buffer copy (lines 2434-2510) and takes it again before every exit path, so it returns with the mutex held. If the run queue is empty it sets no_resources and goes to bailout with no buffer. If the device is a reader whose EOF or EOF_SENT flag is already set, it removes the first buffer from the run queue, sets its status to CAMDD_STATUS_EOF, counts an error and goes to bailout. For a writer it builds the scatter/gather list; if that fails it sets no_resources and goes to bailout with the buffer still on the run queue. Otherwise it removes the buffer from the run queue, may copy a multi-segment write into the device's temporary buffer (callocing blocksize bytes the first time; on failure the buffer status is CAMDD_STATUS_ERROR, an error is counted and it goes to bailout after retaking the mutex), and performs pread/pwrite/pwritev (seekable files) or read/write/writev with the buffer. After retaking the mutex: a result of at least fill_len sets status OK (if it was NONE), resid 0 and adds to bytes_transferred; -1 warns, sets status ERROR, resid = fill_len and counts an error; 0 sets status EOF, resid = fill_len and counts an error; a short positive result sets SHORT_IO (if NONE) and resid. At bailout, if a buffer is held: if its status is EOF the device gets CAMDD_DEV_FLAG_EOF and every buffer still on the run queue is marked EOF; then camdd_complete_buf(dev, buf, &error_count) is called, including for the already-EOF case and for the scatter/gather failure case, where the buffer is still on the run queue. It returns -1 if error_count != 0, else 1 if no_resources, else 0.

functions.name: do_option
functions.prose_contract: Brings the option header file for the option name up to date (usr.sbin/config/mkoptions.cc:137-281). It computes the file name with tooption(name) and walks the global opt list: for every entry with that name it increments op_ownfile and takes its value as the wanted value (an entry with no value counts as "1"; a later entry with a different value than an earlier one prints a 'redefined' warning and the last entry wins). If the option is not in the list the wanted value stays NULL. It then registers the file with remember(). If the file cannot be opened for reading it is created (fopen "w"; err(1) if that fails) and a single "#define <name> <value>" line is written when the value is non-NULL, else the file is left empty, and the function returns. If it can be read, it parses the existing '#define NAME VALUE' triples into a list, dropping with a warning unknown options and options that now belong to a different file (and counting that as tidy work), replacing the value of name when it is found (the replacement is the wanted value, which is NULL when the option was removed, so its define is then not written) and calloc'ing list entries (err on failure). If nothing needed tidying and the old and new values for name are equal (both absent, or both present and equal), the file is left untouched and the list is freed. Otherwise a missing name with a value is added, and the file is rewritten with fopen "w" (err(1) on failure) containing one "#define name value" line for each retained entry that has a value. The temporary list is freed. It returns nothing.

functions.name: replace_cmd
functions.prose_contract: Real name replace_cmd (static, usr.sbin/cron/crontab/crontab.c:489-623; replace_crontab does not exist). Installs the new crontab held in the global NewCrontab stream as the spool file for User. Returns 0 on success, -1 on a syntax error in the crontab, -2 on an install error. It allocates the environment with env_init() (a NULL result warns 'cannot allocate memory' and returns -2); it builds the temporary name tmp.<Pid> and its spool path (a path that does not fit prints 'path too long' and returns -2), and opens the temp file with fopen "w+" (warn and -2 on failure). It writes the three-line DO NOT EDIT header, then copies NewCrontab (rewound) to it, truncates, flushes and rewinds it; a stream error warns, closes and unlinks the temp file and returns -2. It then parses the temp file with load_env and load_entry (using check_error) until an error is counted or the end is reached; if CheckErrorCount is non-zero it warns 'errors in crontab file', closes and unlinks the temp file and returns -1. It then chowns the file to ROOT_UID (group unchanged), chmods it 0600 (each failure warns, closes and unlinks the temp file and returns -2; the chmod failure message says 'chown'), closes it (an fclose failure warns, unlinks and returns -2), builds the spool path for User (a path that does not fit unlinks the temp file and returns -2), and renames the temp file onto it (failure: warn, unlink, -2). On success it logs 'REPLACE', sleeps one second, calls poke_daemon (which only warns if utime on the spool directory fails) and returns 0. The environment array is not freed by this function on any path. On every -1 and -2 return after the temp file was created, the temp file has been closed and unlinked, so the spool file for User is not touched.

functions.name: cctl_error_inject
functions.prose_contract: Real name cctl_error_inject (static, usr.sbin/ctladm/ctladm.c:866-1099; the packet's 'unnamed error-inject handler' is this function and it was dropped, but it exists). It issues a CTL error-injection request for LUN lun using the options in combinedopt and returns 0 on success or 1 on any error (all error paths set retval = 1 and go to bailout, which just returns). It parses options: -c (continuous), -d id (delete by serial), -i type (once only: a repeated -i is an error; getoption must find a unique match, else 'ambiguous' or 'not found' errors), -p pattern (OR'ed into error_pattern, same matching rules), -r lba,len (strdup'ed and split with strsep; a missing len is an error; the duplicated string is not freed correctly, because strsep advances the pointer that is later passed to free), and -s n (n must be positive and is capped at SSD_FULL_SIZE; the sense bytes come from the following arguments through cget/buff_encode_visit, or from stdin when the first argument starts with '-'). If -d was given it issues CTL_ERROR_INJECT_DELETE with that serial and returns (1 if the ioctl fails). Otherwise it requires an error type (-i) and, for a custom error, -s, else it warns and returns 1. -c adds CTL_LUN_INJ_CONTINUOUS. With sense data from stdin it reads exactly sense_len bytes (a read error returns 1; a read that returns 0 at end of file keeps looping without progress). It requires a pattern (-p), adds CTL_LUN_PAT_RANGE and the range when len != 0, and issues CTL_ERROR_INJECT, printing 'Error injection succeeded, serial number is N' on success or warning and returning 1 if the ioctl fails. Lines 907-921 (the -i/-p lookups) were read only in outline.

functions.name: isns_req::receive
functions.prose_contract: Reads one iSNS message from descriptor s into ir_buf (usr.sbin/ctld/isns.cc:175-199). It resizes ir_buf to the header size and does one read() of the header; if that returns fewer bytes than the header (including a read error), it clears ir_buf and returns false. It then returns false, leaving ir_buf holding only the header, if the big-endian version is not ISNS_VERSION or if the FIRST and LAST flags are not both set. Otherwise it takes len from the header's 16-bit length field, resizes ir_buf to header size plus len, and does one read() of len bytes after the header. If that read returns fewer than len bytes (or fails) it returns false; ir_buf has already been resized to the full header-plus-len size, so it is not truncated and only its first part holds received bytes. If it returns exactly len bytes (including len == 0) it returns true. Only a single read() call is made for each part, so a short read on a stream socket gives false. The caller keeps ownership of s.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Entry point of fdformat (usr.sbin/fdformat/fdformat.c:139-360; slice cut the head, the packet named it format_and_verify_floppy). Options: -F fill byte, -f size in KB (a non-numeric argument prints a message and calls usage()), -n (no verify), -q, -s format string, -v (verify only, verify on), -y (no confirmation); other options or an operand count other than one call usage(). The device operand is used as given if it exists, or with _PATH_DEV prepended (a malloc failure is errx(EX_UNAVAILABLE)); it is opened O_RDWR|O_NONBLOCK (err(EX_OSERR) on failure), FD_GTYPE failing is errx(EX_OSERR) 'not a floppy disk', FD_GDTYPE failing is err(EX_OSERR). With -f it looks up the format for the drive type (errx(EX_USAGE) if unknown); with -s it parses the format string. It sets the type with FD_STYPE and clears O_NONBLOCK with fcntl (each failure is err(EX_OSERR)). Unless -v, -q or -y was given it prints the format prompt, and if the answer is not yes it prints 'Not confirmed.' and returns EX_UNAVAILABLE. It then, for each track, formats it (unless verify-only) and, if verifying, calls verify_track; a failing verify sets the local progress flag error, and only when errs < MAXPRINTERRS and errno == EIO is the FDC status fetched (an FD_GSTAT failure is errx(EX_IOERR)) and errs incremented. After the loop it prints the collected errors (not with -q) and returns errs != 0, so a verify failure with an errno other than EIO, or beyond MAXPRINTERRS recorded errors, does not change the return value. The device is not closed explicitly.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Entry point of fwcontrol (usr.sbin/fwcontrol/fwcontrol.c:729-1090; both packet slices, 559-859 and 860-1090, are parts of this one function). With fewer than two arguments it loops over boards 0..9, opening /dev/fw<board>.0 with open_dev and listing each device; if the open fails it calls usage() and err(EX_IOERR) for board 0 and returns EIO for any other board (the loop opens the device although open_needed is false). When all ten open it falls through to option parsing, finds no command and takes the usage path below. Options are parsed with getopt: -b, -f, -g, -o and -s validate numeric ranges with errx(EX_USAGE) (-o and -s call str2node with fd still -1 at that time); -c and -d, -R and -S malloc and copy their argument (err(EX_SOFTWARE) on failure; -c runs strtol on the new buffer before the string is copied into it); -l loads a CROM file; -m resolves an EUI-64 (errx(EX_USAGE) if invalid) and sets open_needed to false; -p, -r, -t, -u and -M set flags (an unrecognised -M method is errx(EX_USAGE)); an unknown option prints usage, a warning and returns 0. If no command was given and no board display was requested it also prints usage and a warning and returns 0. If open_needed it opens /dev/fw<current_board>.0 (err(EX_IOERR) on failure). The requested actions then run in this order: list board, PHY registers, bus reset (ioctl failure err(EX_IOERR)), display CROM (and free its string), display CROM in hex (and free it), priority budget, root node, gap count, show the CROM loaded from file, set the fwmem target through sysctl, link-on, reset-start, topology map, receive (-R: if no method was chosen it detects one using fd and closes fd, then it reopens the device without closing an earlier fd when a method was set and open_needed was true, so that descriptor leaks; err(EX_IOERR) on failure; the data string is freed) and send (-S, dvsend; string freed). Finally it closes fd if it is greater than 0 and returns 0. Strings from repeated options are not freed. The helper functions were not read.

functions.name: dvsend
functions.prose_contract: Real name dvsend (usr.sbin/fwcontrol/fwdv.c:252-415; the packet called it main and the slice is the whole body). Sends a DV file over the isochronous channel on descriptor d. It opens filename read-only (err(EX_NOINPUT) on failure), mallocs DSIZE*TNBUF bytes for the read buffer (the result is not checked and not freed), sets the tx buffer parameters with ioctl FW_SSTBUF and the stream channel and tag (the low 6 bits and bits 6-7 of ich) with FW_STSTREAM (err(1) on either failure), and prepares the CIP packet headers. It then loops: it reads up to DSIZE*TNBUF bytes (repeating read until the buffer is full); a read returning <= 0 with nothing yet read ends the loop (a negative result prints a warning, zero prints 'end of file') and goes to send_end, but a read error or end of file after some data was read just breaks out of the inner read loop, so the partial buffer is sent and the next pass reads again. For each DSIZE block it fills in CIP headers, inserting an empty packet when the padding accumulator requires; at the start of a frame it detects the DV system (PAL or NTSC) on first use, prints a frame digit, and if count > 0 and the frame count exceeds count it stops (leaving the loop with the current iovecs unsent). It sends each batch with writev on d: EAGAIN prints '(EAGAIN) - push Play?' and retries, any other write error is err(1). At send_end it prints frame count, elapsed time and frames per second to stderr and closes the input file; it returns nothing.

functions.name: gssd_init_sec_context_lucid_v1_1_svc
functions.prose_contract: RPC service routine for the MIT Kerberos build (usr.sbin/gssd/gssd.c:546-743; the earlier definition at line 445 is the Heimdal variant that just reports GSS_S_UNAVAILABLE). It always returns TRUE, reporting problems through result->major_status. It zeroes result and picks the credential-cache name: FILE:<GSSD_CREDENTIAL_CACHE_FILE> when hostbased_initiator_cred is set, argp->cred is non-zero and argp->uid is 0; else, with -s (ccfile_dirlist non-empty) and no cred, it searches the directory list for a cache file for argp->uid, and if none is found it sets GSS_S_CREDENTIALS_EXPIRED and returns TRUE before KRB5CCNAME is set; otherwise FILE:/tmp/krb5cc_<uid> (logging when a cred is given for a non-root uid). It then sets KRB5CCNAME with setenv. It looks up the credential, context and name resources from the ids in argp (a missing cred gives GSS_S_CREDENTIALS_EXPIRED, a missing ctx GSS_S_CONTEXT_EXPIRED, a missing name GSS_S_BAD_NAME, each returning at once), calls gss_init_sec_context, and replaces a non-NULL actual_mech_type with GSS_KRB5_MECH_OID_X. On GSS_S_COMPLETE or GSS_S_CONTINUE_NEEDED it sets result->ctx to argp->ctx if given, else a new resource id from gssd_make_resource. On GSS_S_COMPLETE it also exports the context with gss_krb5_export_lucid_sec_context (overwriting major_status with that call's status) and deletes the resource id; result->ctx still holds the id. If the export succeeds with a non-NULL lucid context it copies the fields into result->lucid: protocol 0 gives the RFC 1964 sign/seal algorithms and the context key, protocol 1 gives have_subkey, the context key and, only when have_subkey is non-zero, the subkey (otherwise subkey_type 0, length 0, value NULL); key buffers are mem_alloc'ed (not checked) for the caller, and the lucid context is freed. If the export fails or returns no context it only logs. The credential release at 653 only runs if gotcred is non-zero, which it never is here.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Entry point of i2c (usr.sbin/i2c/i2c.c:740-908; slice cut the head). It sets defaults (device I2C_DEV, 8-bit width, one byte, read direction, transfer mode). A first getopt pass over all letters records the single mode letter among -a, -i, -r, -s (a second mode letter calls usage()); -h calls usage(); other letters are ignored in this pass. If no mode was chosen it calls usage(). It then restarts getopt with the letter set for that mode (-a: a:f:d:w:o:c:m:bv; -i: iv; -r: rf:v; -s: sf:n:v) and parses the values: -a (hex, 1..7f, shifted left one), -c, -d (r or w), -f (device), -m (no, ss, rs, tr), -n, -o, -w and flags; bad values call usage() and an unlisted option prints 'Illegal -x option' and calls usage(NULL). With -i it returns instruct_bus(i2c_opt, argc, argv) at once, passing any remaining arguments to it (they are not rejected). For the other modes any leftover argument calls usage('Too many arguments'). It then calls encode_offset for the width and offset (a message goes to stderr and EX_USAGE is returned on error), opens the device read-write (a failure prints a message and returns EX_NOINPUT), and runs access_bus for -a (printing the settings first with -v), scan_bus for -s or reset_bus for -r, closes the descriptor (asserted to succeed) and returns that operation's result. The mode-NOTSET fix-up block at 865-870 cannot change anything because the mode defaults to I2C_MODE_TRANSFER.

functions.name: next_command
functions.prose_contract: Advances jail j to its next command and starts it (usr.sbin/jail/command.c:102-172). If paralimit is 0 (no process slots) it requeues j on the runnable queue (at the head if it came from the run queue, else at the tail) and returns 1 without advancing anything. Otherwise it clears JF_FROM_RUNQ and loops: when j->comstring is NULL it moves j->comparam one step forward (one step backward if the jail failed to create and is not stopping) and handles the new parameter: IP__NULL ends the list and the function returns 0; mount parameters that are not enabled and parameters with no value are skipped; the operation and stop-timeout markers use a dummy string; otherwise comstring becomes the first (or, when going back or stopping with a reversed parameter, the last) string of the parameter. When comstring is already set it moves to the next or previous string (or to NULL from the dummy string). Empty strings, an exhausted string list and the create-phase commands after a failed create are skipped. Each remaining command is passed to run_command(j): a result of -1 calls failed(j) and returns 1, a result of 1 returns 1, and a result of 0 (nothing left to wait for) continues the loop with the next command.
